issues.title: Windows Computer Use: capture access and gold/yellow display border remain open after screenshot-producing turn completes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Incident package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1021.3705.0`, Windows x64 MSIX. This version was obtained from the installed package path, not the About dialog.
Computer Use / unified-computer-use plugin: `26.1021.31345`.
Bundled CUA runtime directory identifier: `1fb7137c46617d50`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64, OS-reported version `Microsoft Windows 10.0.26200`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A gold/yellow border remained around the user's display after a Codex chat had finished its native desktop capture work. Investigation found the Windows Computer Use helper still running and its Windows capture-access record still open approximately five hours after the screenshot-producing turn completed.

The request is for capture resources to be released when their owning work ends, while preserving Computer Use for other chats that actually need it.

#### Verified incident timeline

Times below are UTC, with America/New_York (UTC-04:00) equivalents. Incident date was October 25, 2026 locally.

| UTC | Local time | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-25 19:58:05.097 | Oct 25, 15:58:05 | The originating chat called `driveClient.getScreenshot()` on a Google Drive desktop window during an authorized backup/restore verification. |
| 2026-10-25 19:58:07.456 | Oct 25, 15:58:07 | Windows CapabilityAccessManager's entry for this helper records capture-access start. |
| 2026-10-25 20:02:51.338 | Oct 25, 16:02:51 | Another `driveClient.getScreenshot()` call occurred in the same turn. |
| 2026-10-25 20:04:50.622 | Oct 25, 16:04:50 | The local transcript records `task_complete` for that screenshot-producing turn. |
| Before 2026-10-26 01:04:26 | Before Oct 25, 21:04:26 | The user reported the persistent gold display border. The helper remained running; its capture-access stop time was still zero. Latest inspected turns of active chats were using files, APIs, or browser automation, with no current native desktop-capture calls found in those turns. |
| 2026-10-26 01:04:26.466 | Oct 25, 21:04:26 | Only the positively identified stale `codex-computer-use.exe` helper was terminated. Windows then recorded a nonzero capture-access stop time. |

The completion timestamp comes from the original transcript's lifecycle event, not an assumption based on the chat appearing idle.

#### Process and Windows evidence

- The retained process was `codex-computer-use.exe`, PID 34140, directly parented by the main `ChatGPT.exe` process, PID 48532.
- Its command line was the bundled helper path followed by `--parent-pid 48532`.
- Loaded modules included `GraphicsCapture.dll`, `Windows.Graphics.dll`, `d3d11.dll`, and `dwmapi.dll`.
- A separate `codex-computer-use-swift.exe` helper was present and was left untouched.
- The relevant Windows record was under:
  `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder\NonPackaged\<encoded-helper-path>`.
- Before cleanup: `LastUsedTimeStart = 134374318874561759`, `LastUsedTimeStop = 0`.
- After cleanup: `LastUsedTimeStop = 134374502664667304`, corresponding to `2026-10-26T01:04:26.4667304Z`.
- After cleanup, the old helper was absent; no replacement `codex-computer-use.exe` was observed in the follow-up checks. The main app and both checked Codex agent-server processes remained running, and ongoing chats continued.
- No app restart, broad process kill, plugin disablement, or Windows permission change was used.

The user-visible border was reported by the user. The verified post-cleanup result is helper termination plus Windows recording capture access as ended; no new desktop screenshot was taken merely to verify the border.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is one observed incident sequence, not a verified deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Run multiple chats in the Windows desktop app with Computer Use enabled.
2. Have one chat capture a native application window using Computer Use.
3. Let the screenshot-producing chat turn complete, and continue ordinary work in other chats.
4. Observe whether the gold/yellow capture border and native helper persist after native desktop work has ended.
5. Check the helper's Windows capture-access record for an unset stop time.
6. In this incident, terminating only the identified stale native capture helper caused Windows to record the end of capture access while the app and other chat agents remained running.

Please do not use a blanket helper-killing rule as the product fix: another chat may legitimately be using the same helper.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Release native capture sessions, cached frames, and associated graphics resources promptly when the owning chat finishes or relinquishes desktop use.
- Remove the Windows capture indicator when no capture remains needed.
- Preserve any other chat's active native operation.
- Allow a later authorized Computer Use task to acquire a fresh session normally.
- Handle ordinary completion, interruption, errors, disconnects, and concurrent chats.

### Additional information

#### Existing cleanup and a possible lifecycle ordering gap

Local, read-only inspection found that cleanup mechanisms are already present:

- User configuration already had a `notify = [<bundled codex-computer-use.exe>, "turn-ended"]` entry.
- The installed unified-computer-use MCP configuration included its hidden `turn_ended` tool.
- The shipped Windows client registers an `addTurnEndedHandler` and sends an `end_turn` request.
- The shipped desktop JavaScript tracks active turns by native-pipe socket. Its `end_turn` path removes matching active-turn entries. Separately, `closeActiveTurn` first checks that tracking map and returns without closing the helper transport if the turn is no longer present.

**Hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause:** if the end-turn request removes ownership tracking before the outer `turn/completed` cleanup checks it, the later cleanup could skip closing the helper transport, allowing cached capture resources to outlive the turn. Please investigate the interaction between the end-turn callback, socket/turn ownership tracking, helper transport closure, and the native capture cache.

This was static inspection of the installed JavaScript plus process/registry observations. No instrumented race reproduction or native decompilation established the exact defect.

#### Scope and limitations

- The persistent border, retained graphics-capture helper, original turn-completion timestamp, open Windows access record, and successful targeted cleanup are the evidence being reported.
- The registry record alone does not prove continuous frame acquisition, video recording, uploading, or continuous model access to the display. No such claim is made here.
- Later native activity in other turns is not exhaustively ruled out. At diagnosis, no current native capture calls were found in the latest turns inspected.
- No full transcripts, screenshots, credentials, account email addresses, personal usernames, or unrelated project content are included.

Related, but a different primary symptom: #56941 reports a retained helper after Computer Use on the same desktop package version, with system-wide UI lag. This report concerns the lingering capture indicator and capture-access lifecycle; a common cause is not established.

Also related: #46675 describes the takeover overlay remaining until the entire agent turn ends on an older build. The present incident includes a verified completed screenshot-producing turn and Windows capture access remaining open afterward, rather than only an overlay persisting during the same active turn.

issues.body:
## Description

When copying a multiline PowerShell code block from the ChatGPT Windows desktop application and pasting it using the mouse into PowerShell 7, the commands appear in reverse order.

The issue is reproducible and may cause commands to execute in an unintended sequence.

## Relevant Environment

- Operating system: Windows 11
- Source: ChatGPT Desktop for Windows
- PowerShell: 7.6.9
- Console: Windows Console Host (`conhost.exe`)
- Paste method: Mouse right-click

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open PowerShell 7.6.9 in Windows Console Host.
2. Open ChatGPT Desktop for Windows.
3. Copy the following code block:

```powershell
Write-Host "TEST_1";
Write-Host "TEST_2";
Write-Host "TEST_3";
```

4. Right-click inside PowerShell to paste the code.

## Actual Behavior

The commands are pasted in reverse order:

```text
PS C:\Windows\System32> Write-Host "TEST_3";
>> Write-Host "TEST_2";
>> Write-Host "TEST_1";
TEST_3
TEST_2
TEST_1
```

## Expected Behavior

The commands should retain their original order:

```text
TEST_1
TEST_2
TEST_3
```

## Troubleshooting Performed

- Confirmed that PowerShell 7.6.9 executes commands correctly.
- Verified that the Windows clipboard preserves text order and CRLF line endings.
- Tested with PSReadLine enabled and disabled.
- Disabled clipboard filtering in Windows Console Host.
- Reinstalled PowerShell 7.6.9.
- Confirmed that pasting works correctly in Windows Terminal.

The issue persists in the traditional Windows Console Host.

## Impact

Reversing command order can cause:

- Incorrect execution sequences.
- Script failures.
- Unexpected system modifications.
- Potential risks when executing administrative commands.

## Requested Fix

Please investigate why multiline PowerShell code copied from ChatGPT Desktop is pasted in reverse order when using mouse right-click in Windows Console Host.

The original command order must be preserved.

**Status:** Reproducible — unresolved.

**Root cause:** Not confirmed.

## Summary
On November 17, 2026, at approximately 09:53 CET, remote Codex sessions on two Linux hosts stopped being accessible from macOS and iOS clients, despite having worked earlier that morning without any client updates. A Linux client continues to connect to and execute development tasks on the same remote hosts successfully.

## Symptoms
- macOS: remote devices show **Waiting for device** / unavailable; attempting to connect produces `Codex app-server initialize handshake timed out`.
- iOS: the same remote hosts/sessions are unavailable, including while on cellular data (separate network from the Mac).
- Web: remote sessions also appeared unavailable when tested from the affected client environment.
- Linux ChatGPT/Codex client: remote hosts show online, and remote development tasks execute successfully.
- A new Codex CLI conversation created on one remote host appeared in the Mac app's recent conversations, suggesting some conversation synchronization works despite live connectivity failures.

## Remote environment
- Two Linux remote hosts (one x86_64, one aarch64).
- Codex CLI and managed app-server version `0.169.0` observed.
- Remote CLI sessions also run inside systemd-started tmux sessions.
- On one host, `codex remote-control start --json` returned `status: connected`, `timedOut: false`, and an already-running managed daemon.
- On the other host, the same command initially returned `app server is running but is not managed by codex app-server daemon`; process inspection showed a standalone app-server alongside the daemon helper and SSH proxy. This may be a separate local issue, and does not explain why the first host remains accessible from Linux but not macOS/iOS.
- SSH to the hosts works; an interactive fish login-shell readiness test emitted the expected marker without extra output.

## Troubleshooting performed
- Restarted the managed daemon and retried connection; no improvement on macOS/iOS.
- Signed out and reauthenticated the affected clients; no improvement.
- Reauthenticated the remote devices; no improvement reported.
- Confirmed remote daemon status, socket symlink and listening Unix socket.
- Confirmed DNS resolution and outbound HTTPS reachability on the remote host (a HEAD request to `api.openai.com` returned HTTP 421, which does not establish API health).
- Daemon stderr contained a bubblewrap fallback warning and an earlier model-refresh timeout, but no clear ongoing remote-control error.
- macOS and iOS failures occurred across different networks.

## Expected behavior
Remote hosts and their sessions remain available from macOS, iOS, web and Linux clients, independent of whether the CLI terminal is open.

## Actual behavior
Linux can execute remote work, but macOS and iOS cannot connect to the same remote sessions, with a device-waiting state and app-server initialization handshake timeout.

## Request
Please investigate remote-device presence/discovery and app-server handshake routing across client platforms, including possible account/workspace or relay synchronization issues. Are there known service-side regressions or recovery steps that do not require deleting projects or sessions?

No account IDs, hostnames, SSH addresses, environment IDs, tokens, or private repository details are included.

## Summary
ChatGPT Work on macOS is unable to use the built-in browser and cannot complete network-dependent development/deployment work. Read-only diagnostics on October 20 and 21, 2026 reproduced missing browser availability and restricted shell networking. A shared root cause has not been established.

## Environment
- ChatGPT desktop: 26.1013.40934, build 20770
- macOS: 27.0.1
- Surface: Work/local tasks on a connected, attached, authorized Mac
- User reports public internet access is enabled in Work settings.

## Observed results
1. Browser inventory returns an empty list. Selecting the built-in browser returns `Browser is not available: iab`, before any website can be inspected.
2. The shell environment reports `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1`. On October 20, DNS lookups for github.com and learn.chatgpt.com failed with `[Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known`.
3. Existing development-task results also recorded loopback `EPERM` and database-host `ENOTFOUND`. These denied operations were not repeated in the read-only diagnostic.
4. A documentation fetch on October 20 returned `Client error: exec-server transport disconnected`. This particular error did not recur during the October 21 check; permanent recovery is not established.
5. Basic shell commands/file reads, desktop artifact listing, and an authenticated GitHub connector lookup succeeded. This is not evidence of a Mac-wide internet outage. The network-disabled environment variable alone does not establish that every managed network route is unavailable.

## Troubleshooting already performed
- User reports quitting/restarting the app and enabling public internet access.
- A fresh local diagnostic task was started on October 20; missing IAB and shell networking problems persisted.
- Rechecked that diagnostic on October 21 at approximately 13:28 UTC: browser inventory still empty, same IAB error, network-disabled flag still present, app version unchanged. Public HTTPS was not retried under the reported restriction.
- No destructive reset, access-control bypass, deployment, or database mutation was performed.

## Expected behavior
Authorized Work tasks should expose the supported built-in browser and accurately reflect effective network access. If workspace or execution policy overrides an enabled setting, the UI should clearly identify that restriction and provide a supported resolution.

## Impact
Browser-based verification and network-dependent coding/deployment workflows are blocked. Ordinary chat and some read-only tools still work.

## Related reports
- #51290: matching built-in-browser availability failure, including an October 20 comment on this exact app version/build.
- #53278: similar network-setting/effective-policy mismatch on Windows; related symptoms, not proof of the same cause.
- https://community.openai.com/t/chatgpt-work-on-mac-chrome-file-access-blocked-operation-not-permitted-new-threads-temporarily-help/1407805

Please investigate browser-provider availability and the discrepancy between the enabled network setting and actual execution behavior, or route these symptoms to the appropriate team. A supported recovery path that preserves existing chats, files, and project work would be appreciated.

This report was prepared with assistant help and submitted with the user's explicit approval. Private project names, file paths, account details, chat history, credentials, and raw logs have been omitted.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a plugin with a root `plugin.json` (`extensions.com.openai.interface` set) and this `mcp.json`, which follows [Package your plugin](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins) for a remote server with a pre-registered OAuth client:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json",
  "mcpServers": {
    "foo-bar": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      "extensions": {
        "com.openai": {
          "auth": {
            "type": "oauth",
            "client": {
              "mode": "provided",
              "clientId": "example-client-id",
              "tokenEndpointAuthMethod": "client_secret_basic"
            },
            "baseScopes": ["openid", "offline_access"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

2. ZIP it and upload it in the ChatGPT admin console (Plugins → Add → Upload plugin).
3. Install the plugin in the Codex App.
4. Open Settings → MCP servers. The server isn't listed under *From plugins*, and the warning above is in the log.

The same plugin without the `extensions` block loads, but then it can't declare its OAuth client.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex accepts the `extensions` object on a server entry, as documented, and either uses `extensions.com.openai.auth` or ignores what it doesn't support. The server shouldn't be dropped.

### Additional information

`AgentPluginMcpServer` in [`codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/agent_plugin_config.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ab82af0/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/agent_plugin_config.rs#L46-L69) is declared with `#[serde(tag = "type", deny_unknown_fields)]`. The `StreamableHttp` variant has only `url` and `headers`, so any `extensions` key fails to deserialize. Both the docs and the Agent Plugins schema allow `extensions` on HTTP server entries. The upload pipeline keeps the block, and the generated `.mcp.json` in the plugin cache still contains it.

Please investigate whether the missing catalog entries arise from client-version compatibility, account/workspace availability, or model-catalog delivery. Also clarify whether `up_to_date` is expected for this installed desktop version. The root cause has not been established; successful `model/list` alone does not prove the upstream catalog is unfiltered.

issues.body:
### Environment
ChatGPT Work Mode with Codex on Windows. Primary runtime package version 26.1110.973.0. The session reports a managed workspace-write policy. Windows build and active sandbox implementation are unverified.

### Reproduction
1. Open a local project on a secondary Windows drive as a Codex workspace. Verify the exact project path is a writable root.
2. In the sandboxed PowerShell, run Get-Item and Get-ChildItem with -LiteralPath and -ErrorAction Stop against the project.
3. Compare with Get-Item in ordinary Windows PowerShell.

### Observed
- Both sandboxed commands fail with "Access to the path 'D:\<project>' is denied." The error ID prefix is ItemExistsUnauthorizedAccessError for both cmdlets.
- Ordinary Windows PowerShell can read the project.
- An independently granted D:\workspace also fails in the same session. The sandboxed shell can list the C: user temp directory.
- (Get-Location).Path resolves to the packaged runtime's dependencies\native\powershell directory even when the tool call explicitly requests the project as its working directory.
- The user reproduced the problem on both exFAT and NTFS drives. The read failure prevented the write probe.

### Expected
The sandbox should read and write explicitly authorized project directories on secondary drives and launch commands in the requested workspace.

Please investigate the Windows sandbox's effective path access and working-directory handling. Related external-drive reports include #51513 and #55718.

Subject: Formal complaint — 

Date: 27 October 2026
Timezone: Australia/Sydney (AEDT)
Product: Codex desktop for Windows
Desktop version recorded in logs: 26.1021.31345
Windows package version: 26.1021.3705.0
Subscription: Pro 

On opening Codex, I received this error:

“ChatGPT configuration could not be loaded”
C:\Users\[username]\.codex\config.toml:1:7635:
key with no value, expected '='

I deleted config.toml to get the application running. Afterwards, all my local projects disappeared from the Projects tree.

The latest original configuration backup found during recovery was config.toml.vexp-bak, dated 4 October 2026. No newer original configuration backup was found in the locations searched.

The recovery investigation found that 20 original project records still existed in state_5.sqlite, while the separate “local-projects” list in .codex-global-state.json was empty. The desktop startup log reported loading the project records, but the sidebar remained empty.

During troubleshooting, the assistant made several unsuccessful changes and repeatedly asked me to restart Codex. It presented unverified explanations with excessive certainty. These attempts included changing migration flags, modifying chat-to-project assignments and the desktop catalog, and creating a temporary recovery project.

The successful recovery was performed with Codex fully closed. A launcher:

1. Backed up the current global state and databases.
2. Restored the 20 saved sidebar project entries from an older global-state snapshot.
3. Matched those entries to existing database project IDs and restored associated sidebar metadata.
4. Removed the temporary recovery project and corrected unintended remote-host catalog assignments from an earlier attempt.
5. Verified the restored records before I reopened Codex.

I confirmed that the projects returned after this recovery.

## Summary

In the macOS ChatGPT desktop app, new Work conversations accept text, but neither Enter nor clicking the visible send arrow submits a short message. No error is displayed. Regular Chat can send messages.

## Scope observed

- The failure reproduces in Work across two projects.
- Restarting the app did not resolve it.
- A short-message test in a new Work conversation also failed.

## Diagnostic clue

The app log recorded `Local Work executor rendezvous unavailable` with `reason=read_error` at 2026-10-07 09:28:04 UTC and `reason=websocket_error` at 09:28:05 UTC. These warnings are a clue only; no causal link to the composer failure has been established.

## Expected behavior

A short prompt in a new Work conversation should submit with Enter or the send button. If submission is blocked, the app should show an actionable error.

## Summary

On macOS, a user selected Work and reported that the only available Work mode was their local mode. The active task nevertheless received a Linux execution environment with native computer access unavailable. It could generate and retain documents in hosted storage but could not create a folder or place those files in the user's Finder folder.

Please investigate whether this is an execution-routing/capability mismatch or a missing/unclear local-computer connection state. The cause is unconfirmed.

## Environment

- Client metadata supplied to the conversation: `Codex Desktop/26.930.21537 (Mac OS; arm64)`.
- Subscription reported in client context: ChatGPT Pro.
- Observation window: October 2, 2026, approximately 13:01–13:18 America/Los_Angeles (20:01–20:18 UTC).
- Agent shell: `uname -s` returned `Linux`.
- Working-directory structure: `/workspace/scratch/<redacted>`.
- Native computer APIs were advertised as unavailable in the task's computer-use capability description.
- No macOS version, local app logs, device connection diagnostics, or screenshot were collected. The build above comes from client metadata, not an inspected About dialog.

## Observed sequence

1. In the macOS desktop conversation, ask Work to organize project documents into an existing local research folder.
2. The agent creates documents in its hosted workspace and ChatGPT file storage, initially mistaking that destination for the requested folder.
3. The user reports that no new files appear in Finder and clarifies that the destination is a Mac Finder folder.
4. The user explicitly instructs the agent to access the local computer, create the project folder, and place the files there.
5. The agent checks its execution environment: the shell returns Linux, and no native Mac filesystem/computer connection is available through the exposed tools.
6. The user states: "I already did that. I switched to Work, and there is only one Work mode, which is my local mode."
7. Subsequent turns remain unable to complete the local write. The user cannot reconcile the selected Work experience with the agent's reported cloud-only capabilities.

This is the sequence observed in one conversation, not a proven deterministic reproduction across installations.

## Expected behavior

A desktop task intended to work locally should receive the authorized local file/computer capabilities, or present a clear, actionable explanation that the local connection is unavailable before attempting the task. The actual execution target and local connection state should be consistent and visible to both user and agent.

A request to save into a Finder folder should produce a verifiable local path. Hosted artifact retention should not be reported as completion of that local write.

## Actual behavior and impact

- The local folder operation remains blocked despite the user's repeated local-computer instructions and reported Work selection.
- Hosted files exist, but no files were placed in the requested Finder destination.
- The agent first gave a misleading completion statement, then offered generic mode-switching guidance that did not match the user's reported UI.
- Repeated clarification did not expose a usable local connection or a diagnostic explaining why it was absent.

The incorrect destination/completion statement is an agent failure observed alongside the potential execution/capability issue; the report does not assume they share a root cause.

## Requested investigation

1. Correlate the selected desktop Work target with the executor and capabilities delivered to the conversation.
2. Check local-computer connection availability and capability provisioning on this macOS build.
3. Show explicit connection/execution-target diagnostics when local tasks receive cloud-only capabilities.
4. Ensure recovery guidance reflects the controls actually available in the user's build.
5. Prevent local-save completion claims when the produced files exist only in hosted storage.

Possibly related: #49488 reports missing computer capabilities in Windows dot/Work tasks. Its platform and diagnostic evidence differ; a common cause has not been established.

## Privacy and evidence limits

This report includes only relevant technical observations and minimal task context. It excludes private document contents, account/session identifiers, credentials, and private local paths. No screenshots or local logs are attached.

issues.body:
## Environment

- macOS, arm64; desktop app 26.1027.30824, build 22943, production channel.
- Configured app updater reports up_to_date on 31 October 2026.
- Bundled in-app browser and supported CUA/browser APIs. No Chrome fallback.

## Problem A: a newly created background chat lacks its browser owner

1. Create a normal local chat through the supported create_thread tool and let it run without selecting it.
2. Ask it to open a neutral HTTPS page in its own hidden in-app browser.
3. It fails with "Browser is not available: iab" and inventory lacks an IAB endpoint for that chat.
4. Select that chat once. Desktop logs show browser owner-sync capturing its route before a page webview exists.
5. The unchanged tool runtime then discovers IAB and opens/reads the neutral page successfully.

Observed twice in existing normal chats. In the independent diagnostic chat, conversation-stream ownership preceded browser-route ownership by several minutes. No restart, runtime reset, or permission change was used for recovery.

## Problem B: completing a subagent removes the browser connection, and followup_task does not recreate it

Three separate diagnostic subagents each opened and read a neutral HTTPS page successfully, then ended a turn with one of these states:

- Only tab explicitly closed; empty tab inventory verified before completion.
- Temporary tab left open without a retention mark.
- Tab marked with markHandoff; presence verified after marking and before completion.

All three lost IAB on followup_task. The preserved browser binding failed, and inventory lacked IAB. In the first two cases, one fresh IAB tab-creation attempt also failed. The marked-tab case did not attempt fresh creation; logs establish that its whole route was disposed and its marked tab closed.

An additional completed file-only turn did not repair the first agent: another resumed turn failed both the preserved binding and one fresh IAB creation attempt.

## Controls

- The ordinary parent survived its own completed turn with zero tabs and the same browser binding, then created and read a fresh page.
- That parent remained usable while the resumed child tests failed.
- Closing the final tab during an active turn returns a valid empty list; a replacement can be created through the existing binding.
- A stale closed-tab handle produces a tab-specific error while another tab remains usable.
- Reading a page with panel visibility false succeeds.

## Read-only packaged-code trace

- The active host browser hook captures child routes on initial subAgentActivity kind="started". Saved followup_task activities are kind="interacted", which this hook ignores.
- Child routes use disposeAfterSessionActivity=true. endSessionActivity disposes the route/backend independently of tab handoff marks. Logs show no route recapture before failed resumes.
- A broader renderer registration hook exists, but its manager initializer has an unconditional false gate in this build.
- The active host thread/started registration path requires a child source with a parent. The ordinary chats' source is "vscode", so that branch performs no registration.
- Selecting a chat invokes browser-sidebar-owner-sync -> syncOwner -> bindSessionRouteOwner, supplying the missing ordinary-chat route.
- Eighteen isolated tests of extracted installed functions support these findings. Those tests use mocked dependencies; the live reproductions above are separate evidence.

## Requested correction and verification

1. Register and await an exact, trusted window/owner association before the first browser-capable turn of an ordinary background chat.
2. Ensure a resumed child's browser route exists at actual turn admission/start using its verified parent association. Preserve handoff-marked tabs when ending a child turn. Recreating an empty route alone cannot restore an already destroyed tab.
3. Preserve per-chat isolation. A generic "interacted" event can also be messaging, so it is not by itself a reliable new-turn boundary.
4. Verify never-selected background creation, all three child cases, an intervening file-only turn, retained original-tab survival, and unaffected parent/unrelated-chat tabs.

Discovery warning counts are not failure counts: probing wrong-session endpoints can produce "No ChatGPT browser route is available" alongside a successful matching endpoint in the same pass.

Related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/58419 reports IAB discovery failure on the same macOS app version, but its cause and equivalence to these two reproductions are not established.

## Scope and privacy

No installed application files, permissions, security checks, profiles, or unrelated chats were changed. No app restart was performed. Test tabs were cleaned up. This report omits usernames, local paths, chat/session/tab identifiers, private websites, account details, raw logs, screenshots, transcripts, credentials, and proprietary source excerpts. No permanent repair has been applied or verified.

prs.title: Run reviews without unfinished MCP servers
prs.body:
## Summary

Review child sessions currently take the same MCP initialization path as normal sessions. If the parent session's MCP clients are still starting, launching a review can therefore wait on OAuth discovery and client startup even though the review does not require those unfinished servers.

This PR makes MCP availability a launch-time policy for the review child. We snapshot whether the parent MCP connection manager has finished starting every configured client and pass that decision through the child session and turn context as `McpAccess`. A review launched after startup settles keeps the normal MCP path, including when an optional server failed; a review launched while any client is pending uses disabled MCP access for its lifetime.

In disabled mode, the child skips MCP auth discovery and connection startup, uses an ephemeral empty MCP runtime for each model step, and suppresses Apps, configured and plugin-provided MCP tools, resource tools, MCP skill-dependency installation, and tool suggestions. Plugin policy hooks remain active, and the child never mutates or replaces the parent's shared MCP runtime. The decision does not change underneath an in-flight review, while a later review can use MCP once parent startup has completed.

## Stack

This is PR 1 of 2 and provides the safe core behavior after a review has been launched. On its own, it does not make `/review` available while the TUI reports MCP startup; it only guarantees that any client which launches a review at that point will not wait for unfinished MCP servers.

#30509 is PR 2 of 2. It changes the TUI's activity state and command gating so `/review` can actually launch while MCP startup remains in the background. It depends on this PR so that launching early produces a review without unfinished MCP rather than a review that still waits for it.

**Goal:** To significantly improve the reliability, visibility, and actionability of our project's internal (non-benchmark) evaluations.

**Problem:** Our current small project evals are inconsistent ("bleed"), making it difficult to trust their results, track quality trends, and quickly address regressions. This slows down development and impacts confidence in changes.

**Vision:** A streamlined evaluation system where internal project evals are stable, provide clear signals, and enable rapid feedback loops. Developers can confidently rely on these evals to catch issues early and understand the impact of their changes.

**Key Outcomes:**

- Reduced flakiness and increased reliability of existing project evals.
- Clear visibility into eval results and historical trends.
- Faster detection and easier debugging of regressions.
- Basic automation to flag issues and guide developers.
- "Approve" button to increase visibility and reduce excessive runs

**Out of Scope:**

- Large-scale benchmark evals (e.g., SWE-bench, terminal-bench).
- Overhauling the entire testing infrastructure beyond the scope of these specific project evals.

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
This EPIC tracks a series of investigations as to whether there is value in AST aware file read, search, or codebase mapping.

AST aware tools can be used to 1) more precisely read method bounds with a single tool call, reducing turns from misaligned reads, and reducing noise in tokens, 2) navigate to usages and definitions of syntax elements via syntax aware search (AST grep), and 3) compress high level context about the codebase, such as the location of specific classes and their members by collapsing code down to just top level classes and types and their children's signatures.

```
 1. tilth (Rust)
  tilth is built specifically to generate a structural outline of a codebase. It uses Tree-sitter under the hood but ships as a single binary. It gives you an
  immediate map of the repository's symbols.
   * Installation: cargo install tilth (or download the binary from their releases)
   * Usage:
       * tilth map . (Prints a tree-like overview of the whole codebase structure)
       * tilth read <file> (Prints the structural outline of a specific file)


  2. glyph (Go)
  glyph is another single-binary tool designed to generate clean, multi-file symbol maps. It's excellent if you want to quickly see the skeleton of a
  directory of source code.
   * Installation: go install github.com/benmyles/glyph@latest
   * Usage: glyph cli './**/*.go' (Prints a tree of functions, structs, and methods)


  3. ast-grep (sg) (Rust)
  While primarily known as a structural search-and-replace tool, ast-grep is the industry standard for distributing Tree-sitter as a fast, single binary. You
  can use it to extract landmarks via the command line.
   * Installation: brew install ast-grep or cargo install ast-grep
   * Usage: You can write quick one-liners to extract specific symbols (like all function declarations) and format the output.


  4. The Classic: Universal Ctags (C)
  If you truly want zero modern dependencies, u-ctags is the classic UNIX approach. It uses a hybrid regex/parser approach rather than full AST generation, so
  it's incredibly fast and supports over 100 languages out of the box.
   * Installation: brew install universal-ctags
   * Usage: ctags -R --output-format=json .
   * Note: It outputs a flat list of symbols (or JSON) rather than a visual tree, but it is the most robust and portable way to extract codebase landmarks.
```

labels.name: priority/p1
labels.description: Important and should be addressed in the near term.

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Issues related to Core Agent, Tools, Memory, Sub-Agents, Hooks, Agent Quality

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.name: workstream-rollup
labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

issues.body:
### What happened?

**Summary**: `codebase_investigator` subagent reports `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` even though its own result says it hit the maximum turn limit before doing any analysis.

While using Gemini CLI to investigate two local repositories (`t3code` and `superset`), the agent invoked the `codebase_investigator` subagent and it failed immediately without doing any analysis.

I ran the Gemini CLI on these two local repositories with an objective asking it to understand their architectures and AI agent integrations. The saved session log shows:

- The main agent called `codebase_investigator` with a valid, concrete objective.
- The tool result was reported with `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.
- The embedded result text simultaneously says the investigation was interrupted because the "maximum number of turns was exceeded" before any specific task was identified or initiated.
- `RelevantLocations` was empty and no actual codebase analysis was performed.

This looks incorrect because:

1. The subagent appears to have exhausted its turn budget before performing any actual analysis.
2. The termination metadata is internally inconsistent: the parent tool call is surfaced as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`, but the embedded payload describes a limit-induced early termination with no findings.

Relevant evidence from the session log:

```text
session file: session-2026-03-09T18-34-10479ef5.json

line 50: "name": "codebase_investigator"
line 53: objective: "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset..."
line 61: "Termination Reason: GOAL"
line 61: "The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded)..."
line 61: "\"RelevantLocations\": []"
line 66: "status": "success"
line 79: "The `codebase_investigator` was unable to complete its analysis due to a turn limit..."
```

Full snippet from the saved session:

```json
{
  "id": "codebase_investigator_1773081420202_0",
  "name": "codebase_investigator",
  "args": {
    "objective": "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset, focusing on AI agent integrations.\nSpecifically:\n1. In t3code, how is 'Codex' integrated? Where is the core logic for agent interaction?\n2. In superset, what are the different agent/harness integrations (e.g., Mastra, MCP, Claude, etc.) and how are they implemented?\n3. What are the common patterns or interfaces used in superset that could be adapted for t3code to support multiple harnesses?\n\nIdentify key files, symbols, and architectural patterns in both repositories."
  },
  "result": [
    {
      "functionResponse": {
        "response": {
          "output": "Subagent 'codebase_investigator' finished.\nTermination Reason: GOAL\nResult:\n{\n  \"SummaryOfFindings\": \"The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded) before any specific task could be identified or initiated. As a result, no codebase analysis was performed, and no relevant locations or insights could be gathered.\",\n  \"ExplorationTrace\": [\n    \"Received system notification that the maximum number of turns was exceeded.\",\n    \"Followed emergency termination protocol as instructed.\"\n  ],\n  \"RelevantLocations\": []\n}"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "status": "success"
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected one of these outcomes:

- `codebase_investigator` should actually explore the repositories and return findings.
- If it truly hits a turn limit, it should do so after some visible work, and the tool invocation should be surfaced as a failure or explicit limit condition, not as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.

At minimum, the CLI should not report a contradictory success state for a subagent that says it exceeded its turn budget before beginning analysis. If the subagent hits a system-imposed turn limit before doing useful work, the tool result should be reported as a failure or explicit limit condition (e.g. `status: "error"` with a clear error code), not as a successful `GOAL` completion.


### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Run `gemini` to enter the interactive CLI, then run the `/about` command.

```console
> /about
Gemini CLI package version: 0.32.1
Platform: Windows
OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
Node.js: v20.20.0
PowerShell: 5.1.26100.7920
```

</details>

### Login information

Google Account, Pro tier from students promotion

### Anything else we need to know?

- After the failed `codebase_investigator` call, the main agent continued with manual file exploration and eventually produced an implementation plan. So the overall conversation did not fully crash, but the specialized investigator tool clearly failed.
- My current inference is that this may be either:
  - turn-budget state leaking into a fresh subagent invocation, or
  - an incorrect mapping of a subagent limit/error state into a successful `GOAL` termination in the parent session.
- If useful, I can provide the full saved session JSON or a redacted version of it.

issues.body:
# [BUG] Browser Agent ignores `settings.json` overrides (e.g., `maxTurns`)

## What happened?
The Browser Agent completely ignores any configuration overrides provided in the global or project-level `settings.json`. While the `AgentRegistry` correctly reads and merges these settings during initialization, the `BrowserAgentInvocation` and its factory (`browserAgentFactory.ts`) skips the registry and recreate the agent definition from scratch with hardcoded defaults.

## What did you expect to happen?
The Browser Agent should respect settings overrides like `maxTurns`, `maxTimeMinutes`, etc., just like other sub-agents (e.g., `codebase_investigator`). For example, setting `maxTurns: 0` in `settings.json` should cause the agent to terminate immediately upon invocation.

## Client information
<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Platform: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
Gemini CLI Version: 0.35.0-nightly.20260311.657f19c1f

</details>

## Login information
Google Account (OAuth)

## Anything else we need to know?
### Root Cause
The Browser Agent's unique invocation flow skips the `AgentRegistry` where settings overrides are maintained. Instead of using the pre-merged definition from the registry, it re-instantiates a fresh definition using hardcoded defaults.

**Relevant Files & Code Snippets:**

1.  **`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`**
    The Browser Agent is explicitly branched out of the standard flow that uses `LocalSubagentInvocation`:
    ```typescript
    if (definition.name === BROWSER_AGENT_NAME) {
      return new BrowserAgentInvocation(this.config, ...);
    }
    ```

2.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentInvocation.ts`**
    The `execute` method calls `createBrowserAgentDefinition`, passing the `config` object but omitting the merged definition from the registry.

3.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentFactory.ts`**
    The factory re-runs the `BrowserAgentDefinition` constructor, which returns hardcoded defaults (e.g., `maxTurns: 50`):
    ```typescript
    const baseDefinition = BrowserAgentDefinition(config, !visionDisabledReason);
    ```

### Suggested Fix
Update `browserAgentFactory.ts` to attempt to retrieve the existing definition from the `AgentRegistry` before falling back to creating a fresh one.

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The `browser_agent` (specifically `BrowserManager.ts`) currently employs a restrictive "fail-fast" strategy when encountering a locked browser profile (e.g., when `sessionMode: 'persistent'` is used and an existing instance or orphaned process is active):


```json
{
  "success": false,
  "summary": "The task could not be completed because the browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile.",
  "fullErrorMessage": "The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use --isolated to run multiple browser instances.\nCause: The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use a different userDataDir or stop the running browser first."
}
```

I propose to make it more resilient with the following capabilities:

1.  **Automatic Session Takeover:** If `persistent` mode fails due to a profile lock, the agent should automatically attempt to connect to the existing instance (as if `sessionMode: 'existing'` were specified). This requires a graceful "fallback-and-probe" mechanism in `BrowserManager.connectMcp()`.
2.  **Orphaned Process Recovery:** If an `existing` connection is not feasible but the profile remains locked, the `BrowserManager` should proactively detect orphaned `chrome` or `chrome-devtools-mcp` processes associated with the Gemini CLI profile and offer (or automatically execute) a "Self-Healing" routine (process termination + lock file removal).
3.  **Intelligent Error Remediation:** Replace the current static error messages with an interactive recovery flow. Utilizing the `ask_user` tool, the agent should present the user with a "Choice" menu featuring numbered options to resolve the lock (e.g., **1. Attempt Session Takeover**, **2. Force Termination & Reset**, or **3. Launch Isolated Session**). 
### Why is this needed?

Forcing the user to manually `pkill` processes or close browser windows is a friction point that degrades the autonomous agent experience. The agent has sufficient context (profile path, PIDs) to resolve this internally without user intervention.


### Additional context

### What happened?

This is purely anecdotal, but IME Gemini does not use custom skills and sub-agents on its own, basically at all.  It will if I instruct it to explicitly, but won't when it's doing something very related.

For example, I have "gradle" and "git" skills with descriptions like:
> Executes and manages Gradle builds authoritatively with high-performance background orchestration 
  and surgical failure analysis. This skill is the STRONGLY PREFERRED way 
  to run any Gradle task, providing superior reliability through managed background processes, 
  task-specific output capturing, and deep diagnostic integration. Use it for executing core 
  lifecycle tasks like 'build' or 'assemble', starting persistent development servers, 
  or performing complex build troubleshooting. Do NOT use for specialized test diagnostics 
  (use running_gradle_tests).

and 
> Audits Git repository status, examines history, and implements non-interactive modifications. Processes surgical staging, descriptive commits, and multi-file diff analysis. Use for repository introspection and history-based truth verification. NEVER stages or commits without explicit user directives. Avoids interactive prompts via --no-pager.

that never ever get called when using the relevant tools.

I even have this in my `GEMINI.md` in the "priority rules" section:
> 4. **Agent & Tool Hierarchy:** Whenver considering how to approach a task or do anything, ALWAYS follow the hierarchy of preference: **Sub-Agents** > **Skills** > **Specialized MCP Tools** (NOT a Shell tool or similar) > **General/Builtin Tools** (e.g., `run_shell_command`, `grep_search`, `read_file`).
> 5. **Intentionality Protocol:** Before starting ANY task, you MUST stop and consider which agent, skill, or tool is most appropriate for the specific context. If your plan involves using the shell (even via a tool like `run_shell_command`), you MUST stop and reconsider if a more specialized tool or skill exists to handle the task more reliably.

I expected Gemini to use related skills when working on tasks that match the skill description.  Same for sub-agents.

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

## Objective
Ensure the Gemini CLI understands its own mechanics well enough to act as its own expert guide. The agent must be able to provide users with accurate facts about how it works, its hotkeys, and the exact CLI flags needed to run itself for specific workflows.

## The Problem
Users rely on the CLI to learn how to use the CLI. If the agent hallucinates flags (like suggesting the deprecated `--yolo` instead of `--approval-mode=yolo`) or forgets UI hotkeys (like `Double Esc` for `/rewind`), it blocks progress and creates friction. The agent needs strict grounding in its own documentation to accurately guide users.

### Why is this needed?

1. **Accurate Internal Facts:** The agent (specifically the `cli_help` subagent) must have flawless recall of its own UI keyboard shortcuts, slash commands, and settings hierarchy.
2. **Flag Construction:** It must be able to tell users exactly how to run it from the terminal for various use cases (e.g., suggesting `gemini -i "prompt" --sandbox --output-format json` for safe, headless scripting).
3. **Self-Execution & Guidance:** It should be able to write the exact commands needed to run itself, restart itself, or execute sub-tasks with the correct environment variables and flags.

issues.body:
## Description
Gemini 3 models are fundamentally trained to operate as native bash users, chaining standard POSIX tools (`grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`) to explore codebases and edit files. To make full use of the model's native and preferred capabilities without compromising user security or UX, we need to allow the model to use these tools directly to interact and make changes.

## Prior Art
Historically, we have attempted to force models to use custom tools (such as `replace`, `grep_search`, `write_file`, etc.). However, these methods fight the model's core training. Malicious prompts or complex scripts are inherently hard to control and catch via parsing, and forcing custom tools creates significant downstream UX and security issues.

## The Challenge & Value Proposition
Because the model strongly favors raw bash calls even when nudged towards custom tools, it frequently outputs large, complex bash scripts to accomplish tasks. Under our current security model, these scripts require explicit user confirmation. 

This creates a critical point of failure: users are frequently presented with dense, hard-to-read bash messages to evaluate. This leads to severe prompt fatigue, causing users to either blindly confirm the execution or enter "yolo mode" (auto-approving all actions). This behavior is highly detrimental to security and degrades the overall user experience. 

**Value Proposition:** By safely embracing the model's native bash tendencies, we can eliminate confirmation fatigue, prevent unsafe "yolo mode" habits, and drastically improve both the UX and our underlying security posture. 

## Proposed Solution
A highly viable solution is to utilize a secure sandbox. ALL standard shell commands will execute within a zero-dependency, kernel-enforced sandbox. Instead of trying to predict intent before execution (which led to the parsing challenges described above), we can safely observe and handle the results *after* execution.

### Method
By running commands in a sandboxed replica of the workspace, we achieve three distinct UX lanes:
1. **Reads:** Commands that do not mutate the filesystem (e.g., `ls`, `grep`) are auto-approved. We must ensure this does not read from protected spaces or outside our trusted workspaces.
2. **Edits:** Commands that mutate the sandboxed filesystem (e.g., `sed -i`, `>`) trigger a post-execution Diff UI before the changes are synced back to the host, allowing for a seamless "Edit" tool experience using the model's preferred mechanisms. 
3. **Side-Effects:** A dynamic command router will handle commands requiring host credentials or network access (e.g., `git`, `gh`), completely bypassing the sandbox but requiring strict upfront user confirmation (i.e., stays the same as today, utilizing the policy engine to execute or ask for user confirmation).

## Architectural Mandates
In order to support this properly, we must explore, investigate, and implement the proper sandboxing for all major platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Epic
This is an epic that tracks this investigation and implementation. It will contain subtasks used to track progress towards its overall completion. After initial investigation, if this is not a feasible route, the epic can be marked as closed.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Current context baseline is approximately 36.6k tokens per turn. Large file reads often 'firehose' the context, leading to bloat (previously observed at +15k tokens/turn). 

The goal of 'Tactful Extraction' is to establish a surgical code-discovery hierarchy:
1. **grep_search**: Primary scout for locating symbols.
2. **shell/sed**: scalpel for semantic block extraction (preferred for specific line ranges).
3. **read_file**: surgical range-reading (migrated to 1-based start/end lines).

Telemetry indicates that making ~2.1% more targeted tool calls results in a ~6.9% reduction in total input tokens.

## Changes

- **read_file migration**: Switched from 0-based 'offset'/'limit' to 1-based 'start_line'/'end_line' for better model alignment.
- **Surgical Guidance**: Updated tool descriptions and system prompts to mandate 'token-frugal' behavior.
- **Tool Hierarchy**: Emphasized the use of 'grep_search' and 'sed' via 'run_shell_command' for efficient context management.

## Status

This work is temporarily sidelined in favor of other priorities but remains a key architectural goal for efficiency.

issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: fix(core,cli): parse PowerShell commands asynchronously to prevent UI spinner freeze
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes a multi-second UI freeze on Windows where the Thinking spinner and elapsed-time counter stop updating before the Shell tool panel appears when Gemini CLI validates or executes PowerShell commands.

## Details

- **Root cause:** PowerShell AST command parsing (`parsePowerShellCommandDetails` in `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`) used blocking `child_process.spawnSync('powershell.exe', ...)` without per-invocation caching, stalling the Node.js event loop up to 14 times (~200–500ms per spawn) across policy evaluation, taint/build-file checks, confirmation generation, Windows sandbox checks, and React UI renders.
- **Scoped async parsing (`@google/gemini-cli-core`):**
  - Added `CommandParseCache` + `AsyncLocalStorage` (`shell-parse-cache.ts`) to reuse completed parses (including `null` failure results) and deduplicate concurrent in-flight parses within a single `PolicyEngine.check()` or `ShellToolInvocation` lifecycle without introducing an unbounded process-wide cache.
  - Added non-blocking `parsePowerShellCommandDetailsAsync` (`child_process.spawn` with `windowsHide: true` and `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']`) and async shell helpers while preserving all existing PowerShell AST and command-substitution fallback safeguards.
  - Updated `PolicyEngine`, `Scheduler`, `ShellToolInvocation`, `untrustedContextTracker`, and Windows sandbox safety checks to parse asynchronously and share cached results across validation, `ProceedAlways` policy updates, and execution.
- **Non-blocking UI (`@google/gemini-cli`):**
  - Precomputed optional `hasRedirection` on `exec` confirmation details so `ToolConfirmationMessage` and `useGeminiStream` (`AUTO_EDIT` transitions) avoid synchronous re-parsing.
  - Updated `useTurnActivityMonitor` to resolve unconfirmed PowerShell redirection checks asynchronously via `hasRedirectionAsync` instead of calling `hasRedirection` synchronously during React render.
  - Updated `useExecutionLifecycle` (`!` Shell Mode) to fast-path non-`gemini` and obvious interactive `gemini` commands in-process and disambiguate remaining PowerShell commands via `isInteractiveGeminiCommandAsync`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30249

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted unit and integration test suites (verifying scoped cache isolation, 15ms timer responsiveness during simulated PowerShell startup latency, and zero `spawnSync` calls across Core and CLI UI):
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/shell-parse-cache.test.ts src/tools/shell-powershell-parsing.integration.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/powershellUiParsing.test.tsx src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run full preflight validation:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. On Windows PowerShell, start Gemini CLI interactively and ask the model to run:
   ```powershell
   Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name,Length,LastWriteTime
   ```
   as well as a redirected command (`Get-ChildItem > out.txt`), and confirm the Thinking spinner and elapsed-time counter remain smooth and responsive before and during the Shell confirmation prompt.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS

  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx

prs.title: fix(core): stop overriding core.sshCommand with an empty string
prs.body:
## Summary

`getSafeGitEnv()` (and the sandboxed shell defaults) set `core.sshCommand` to an empty string. Git executes that config value, so any operation that needs SSH fails before ssh is even attempted:

```
error: cannot run : No such file or directory
fatal: unable to fork
```

`GIT_SSH_COMMAND` was already set to a BatchMode ssh command, but the empty `core.sshCommand` config override takes precedence over it and breaks the operation.

## Reproduction

```console
$ git remote add origin ssh://localhost/nonexistent/repo.git
$ GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.sshCommand GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0= git fetch origin
error: cannot run : No such file or directory
fatal: unable to fork
```

Without the override the same command reaches ssh instead (`Host key verification failed.`).

## Fix

Pin `core.sshCommand` to a real, non-interactive command instead of an empty string:

- `getSafeGitEnv()` uses the command it already computed for `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, so the config override and the environment variable can no longer disagree, and BatchMode handling (including plink) is unchanged.
- The sandboxed shell defaults use the inherited `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, falling back to `ssh -o BatchMode=yes`.

Keeping the override (rather than dropping it) means a `core.sshCommand` in the user's gitconfig still cannot bypass the non-interactive setting.

`core.fsmonitor` and `core.hooksPath` are deliberately left empty: Git does not execute those values, and an empty `core.hooksPath` keeps repository hooks disabled. `core.editor`/`sequence.editor` are also unchanged, since they only matter for operations that would otherwise open an interactive editor.

## Tests

- New unit test: `core.sshCommand` always matches `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` and is never empty (default env, custom `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, plink).
- New integration test: `git fetch` against an SSH remote with the sanitized env must not report `cannot run` / `unable to fork`. Both new assertions fail before the fix.
- Updated the two existing assertions that pinned the empty override.
- `packages/core`: `gitUtils.test.ts` 18/18, `shellExecutionService.test.ts` 93/93, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier clean.

Fixes #30328

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve MCP env values containing = and empty values
prs.body:
## Summary

`gemini mcp add -e KEY=value` parsed each `-e` entry with `curr.split('=')` and destructured `[key, value]`. That silently corrupted values and still exited 0:

- `TOKEN=abc=def==` was stored as `"abc"` (everything from the second `=` on was dropped).
- `EMPTY=` was dropped entirely, because `value` was `''` (falsy).

Base64 tokens, connection strings and other values that legitimately contain `=` were mangled at add time, and the MCP server then failed authentication with no hint that the configured environment had been altered.

## Details

Split each entry on the **first** `=` only (`indexOf` + `slice`), keep the remainder of the string including any further `=`, and allow an empty value. Entries with no `=` or an empty key are still ignored, matching the previous behaviour for malformed input.

```ts
const separator = curr.indexOf('=');
if (separator <= 0) {
  return acc;
}
acc[curr.slice(0, separator)] = curr.slice(separator + 1);
```

## Testing

Added two cases to `packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/add.test.ts`:

- `should preserve env values containing = and empty values` — `-e TOKEN=abc=def== -e EMPTY=` must produce `{ TOKEN: 'abc=def==', EMPTY: '' }`. This fails on `main` (`env: { TOKEN: 'abc' }`).
- `should ignore env entries without a key or separator` — `-e NOVALUE -e =bar` still produces `{}`.

Verification on this branch:

- `vitest run src/commands/mcp` — 4 files, 53 tests passed.
- `vitest run src/commands/mcp/add.test.ts` with only the fix reverted — the new preservation test fails, the other 24 pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/cli` — clean.
- `eslint` and `prettier --check` on both changed files — clean (also via the repo's pre-commit hook).

## Related Issues

Fixes #30329

prs.title: fix(cli): make auth URL clickable when terminal wraps it
prs.body:
Fixes #29430

## Problem
During sign-in, Gemini CLI prints the long Google login link. On a narrow terminal that link wraps, and terminal URL detection only grabs the visible chunk, so query details like response_type get chopped off and Google answers Error 400 ("Access blocked: Authorization error"). Manually copying the full URL works, which confirms the generated URL itself is correct.

## What changed
- packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts: at the web-login print site, the auth URL is now also sent as an OSC 8 terminal hyperlink behind the short label "Open authentication page", with the full plain URL still printed underneath for copying and for terminals without OSC 8 support. Guards return the URL unchanged for empty, already-wrapped, or control/whitespace-containing URLs.
- packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.ts and InlineMarkdownRenderer.tsx: the TUI text cleaning now preserves exactly one kind of hyperlink through both sanitiser layers (HistoryItemDisplay escaping and RenderInline stripping). The allowlist is narrow: no OSC 8 parameters, label exactly "Open authentication page", target https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with no userinfo or fragment, response_type=code, and a loopback redirect_uri (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oauth2callback) only. Every other OSC 8 link is still escaped/stripped as before, so model or tool output cannot inject a clickable link to another domain.
- This is deliberately narrower than the earlier #29460 attempt, which was closed by a bot for staleness (14 days without a help-wanted label), not by a maintainer technical rejection.

## Tests
- oauth2.test.ts: 5 new tests, full file 46 passed.
- textUtils.test.ts: 9 new allowlist tests passed (preservation, plus rejection of non-allowlisted domains, non-loopback redirects, a different label, and links with parameters).
- HistoryItemDisplay.test.tsx: new end-to-end TUI pipeline test renders the full auth message through HistoryItemDisplay -> InfoMessage -> RenderInline -> Ink and asserts the raw Ink output carries the complete OSC 8 target with no literal escaped form. Passed.
- Prettier and ESLint clean on all touched files. One pre-existing "Thinking..." snapshot failure in HistoryItemDisplay is unrelated to this change.

## Not yet verified
A real mouse click in a real terminal and a live /auth sign-in run were not performed; the evidence is Ink raw output carrying the full OSC 8 target on every wrapped row.

prs.title: fix(core,cli): prevent $-pattern expansion in custom command and prompt substitutions
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where custom command `{{args}}` and system prompt substitutions (`${AgentSkills}`, `${SubAgents}`, `${AvailableTools}`) expand JavaScript `$` replacement patterns (such as `$$`, `$&`, `$'`, `$` `, and `$1`), corrupting user arguments and template text.

Fixes #30105

## Details
In `packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts` and `packages/core/src/prompts/utils.ts`, user input and dynamic system prompt variables were passed as replacement strings directly into `String.prototype.replaceAll` and `String.prototype.replace`. In JavaScript, string-based replacements treat `$` sequences as special patterns (e.g. `$$` collapses to `$`, and `$&` inserts the placeholder itself).

This fix:
- Replaces direct replacement strings with replacer callbacks (`() => value`) across `shellProcessor.ts` and `applySubstitutions` in `utils.ts`, ensuring literal string interpolation without pattern interpretation.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests in `shellProcessor.test.ts` (verifying `$` patterns in both raw `{{args}}` and inside/outside `!{}` shell injection blocks).
- Adds unit tests in `utils.test.ts` (verifying `$` patterns in `${AgentSkills}` and `${AvailableTools}`).

## Related Issues
Fixes #30105

## How to Validate
Run the test suites in `packages/cli` and `packages/core`:
```bash
npx vitest run src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.test.ts --coverage false
npx vitest run src/prompts/utils.test.ts --coverage false
```
Expected: All tests pass, including the new tests asserting literal preservation of `$$`, `$&`, `$'`, and `$1`.

## Pre-Merge Checklist
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [x] Windows (npm run)

prs.title: fix(acp): record tool calls on active chat to prevent 400 on compressed session reload
prs.body:
## Summary

Record completed and failed tool calls through the active chat instance rather than the initial pre-compression chat in ACP sessions. This prevents post-compression tool calls from being attached to removed model messages and avoids 400 errors upon session reload.

## Details

In ACP mode (`gemini --acp`), when automatic chat compression triggers, `GeminiClient` creates a new chat instance with its own `ChatRecordingService`. Previously, `Session` retained a reference to the initial `chat` passed at construction and recorded tool calls via `this.chat.recordCompletedToolCalls(...)`.

When compression ran mid-session, later tool calls were recorded against the old chat's last message (which was removed from the active conversation). On subsequent `session/load`, the rebuilt message history had mismatched function call and response counts, causing requests to fail with HTTP 400.

This introduces `getChat()` on `Session` to dynamically query `this.context.geminiClient.getChat()` (falling back to `this.chat`), aligning with the implementation in `nonInteractiveCli.ts` and `useGeminiStream.ts`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30103

## How to Validate

```bash
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp/acpSession.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
```

Verified that all 55 tests pass in `acpSession.test.ts`, including two new unit tests verifying success and error tool calls record to the active chat after chat instance updates.

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

prs.title: test(core): add unit tests for isApiError and isStructuredError
prs.body:
## Summary

`packages/core/src/utils/quotaErrorDetection.ts` exposes the error-classification
type guards `isApiError` and `isStructuredError` used when handling API/quota
errors, but had no unit coverage. This adds `quotaErrorDetection.test.ts`
covering their behavior:

- `isApiError`: accepts a well-formed `ApiError` (numeric `code`, string
  `message`, string `status`); rejects missing fields, non-numeric `code`,
  missing `error` property, and null/non-object input.
- `isStructuredError`: accepts a message-only error and a numeric `status`
  (including `0` and `undefined`); rejects a non-number defined `status`
  (e.g. `"500"` or `null`), a non-string `message`, a missing `message`, and
  null/non-object input.

## Test plan

```
cd packages/core && npm test -- quotaErrorDetection
```

Pure, deterministic assertions (no I/O), so they run in the normal vitest
collection for `packages/core`.

## Notes

- No production code changed — test-only addition.
- License header matches repo convention.

Updates `lycheeverse/lychee-action` from 2.6.1 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from lycheeverse/lychee-action's releases.

v2.9.0

Summary

This release updates the default lychee version from v0.23.0 to v0.24.2.

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee 0.24.x release artifacts. Starting with lychee v0.24.0, the archive layout changed, and the lychee binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. lychee-action now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows.

If you use:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2

you will get the new version once the floating v2 tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0

What’s new from lychee v0.24.x

Better diagnostics

lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports.

Text fragment checking

lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing #:~:text=.... This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text.

Sitemap support

lychee can now read sitemap.xml inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate.

JUnit output

lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML.

Redirect and remap visibility

lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier.

Multiple config files

lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings.

Timeout handling

lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints.

Fixes and reliability improvements

prs.title: ci: pre-pull triage image and clear Docker login in dedup workflows
prs.body:
## Summary

Pre-pulls the pinned issue triage MCP server image in the automated and
scheduled issue deduplication workflows, and removes the Docker client login
state when the pre-pull step exits.

The GHCR login is only needed to pull the image, so it no longer persists for
the rest of the job.

## Details

- Adds one step, `Pre-pull Triage Image and Scrub Credentials`, between the
  GHCR login step and the `run-gemini-cli` step in
  `gemini-automated-issue-dedup.yml` and `gemini-scheduled-issue-dedup.yml`.
- The image reference is defined once per workflow as a job-level
  `TRIAGE_IMAGE` environment variable. The pre-pull step and the MCP server's
  `docker run` arguments both use it, so the two cannot drift apart.
- The step registers an `EXIT` trap that deletes `~/.docker/config.json`, then
  runs `docker pull "${TRIAGE_IMAGE}"`. The file is removed whether or not the
  pull succeeds.
- The MCP server's `docker run` uses the default pull policy, so it starts from
  the local image.
- The login step is kept because the image requires an authenticated pull. It
  now sets `logout: false`, because the Docker client config is already removed
  by the time the post-job logout would run.
- Both workflows use `shell: bash`, so a failed pull fails the step and the
  remaining steps are skipped.

## Related Issues

N/A

## How to Validate

1. In `google-gemini/gemini-cli`, run `gemini-automated-issue-dedup.yml` via
   `workflow_dispatch` with an existing issue number. In the `find-duplicates`
   job, confirm that:
   - The new pre-pull step pulls the image and succeeds.
   - `Find Duplicate Issues` starts the `issue_deduplication` MCP server and
     calls the `duplicates` tool.
2. Run `gemini-scheduled-issue-dedup.yml` via `workflow_dispatch`. In the
   `refresh-embeddings` job, confirm that:
   - The new pre-pull step pulls the image and succeeds.
   - `Run Gemini Issue Deduplication Refresh` starts the `issue_deduplication`
     MCP server and calls the `refresh` tool.
3. In both runs, confirm that the job completes successfully, including its
   post-job steps.
4. Run the workflow linters locally and confirm that all checks pass:

   ```bash
   node scripts/lint.js --setup
   node scripts/lint.js --actionlint --yamllint --check-github-actions-pinning
   ```

## Pre-Merge Checklist

CI workflow-only change; no product code, documentation or tests are affected.
