prs.title: fix(ide): use per-user discovery directory and atomic port file writes
prs.body:
## Summary

    Scopes IDE companion discovery files on POSIX systems to a per-user temporary directory (`${os.tmpdir()}/gemini-ide-${uid}`) with `0700` permissions and updates the VS Code companion server to write port discovery files atomically via an exclusive `0600` temporary file and rename.

## Details

    - **Per-user discovery path (`packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts`):** Added `getIdeConnectionDir()` returning `${baseTmpDir}/gemini-ide-${process.getuid()}` on POSIX systems and `${baseTmpDir}\gemini\ide` on Windows, avoiding directory ownership collisions on shared POSIX hosts.
    - **Atomic port file persistence (`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts`):**
      - Added `ensurePortDir()` to create the discovery directory with mode `0700` and validate via `lstat` that it is a regular directory owned by the current UID.
      - Replaced sequential `fs.writeFile` + `fs.chmod` calls with `writePortFileAtomically()`, which opens an exclusive `0600` temporary file (`wx`), writes the JSON config, closes the descriptor, and renames it to the target discovery filename across both initial startup and `syncEnvVars()` updates.
    - **Discovery reader validation & compatibility (`packages/core/src/ide/ide-connection-utils.ts`):**
      - Checks the per-user discovery directory first (`lstat` regular directory, UID, and `0700` mode check) and falls back to the legacy `${os.tmpdir()}/gemini/ide` path if no connection file is present in the primary directory.
      - Opens discovery files on POSIX using `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and verifies regular-file type, UID ownership, and file mode bits before reading.
    - **Tests & companion spec:** Updated unit and integration tests across `packages/vscode-ide-companion` and `packages/core`, added filesystem persistence tests in `ide-server-port-file.test.ts`, and updated `docs/ide-integration/ide-companion-spec.md`.

## Related Issues

N/A

## How to Validate

    1. Build and run the VS Code companion unit and filesystem persistence tests:
       ```bash
       npm test -w gemini-cli-vscode-ide-companion
       ```
    2. Run the core IDE discovery and path utility test suites:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/paths.test.ts src/ide/ide-connection-utils.test.ts src/ide/process-utils.integration.test.ts src/ide/ide-client.test.ts src/ide/ide-client.sandbox.test.ts
       ```
    3. Run the CLI sandbox IDE bridge test suite:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/ideBridge.test.ts
       ```
    4. Run full repository preflight validation:
       ```bash
       npm run preflight
       ```

prs.title: fix(cli): detect local git clone from CLI path instead of cwd
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes auto-update misclassifying a local Gemini CLI source checkout as a global `npm` installation when run from outside the clone root (including other directories, other git repositories, `npm link`, `packages/cli` aliases, or subdirectories within the clone).
Previously, running a source build from outside the clone root caused `handleAutoUpdate()` to spawn `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@<channel>` in the background—polluting the user's global npm prefix or overwriting an `npm link` symlink.

## Details

- Updated `getInstallationInfo()` in `packages/cli/src/utils/installationInfo.ts` to detect a local git clone from the CLI executable's resolved path (`realPath`) rather than `process.cwd()` / `projectRoot`:
  - Checks `!realPath.includes('/node_modules/')`, verifies `realPath` matches a source checkout entrypoint (`/packages/cli/`, `/packages/cli`, or `/bundle/`), and calls `isGitRepository(path.dirname(realPath))`.
  - Evaluates explicit package-manager cache/global path checks (`npx`, `pnpx`, `Volta`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bunx`, `bun`) before the local git clone check so installs under an ancestor git repository (e.g., `$HOME/.git` dotfiles repos with `bunx` cache bundles that lack `/node_modules/`) are never misclassified as a local git clone, while still avoiding the macOS `brew --prefix` subprocess for local clones.
- Added unit tests in `packages/cli/src/utils/installationInfo.test.ts` covering out-of-clone, cross-repo, `npm link`, `packages/cli` alias, clone-subdirectory, Windows, and package-manager regression cases.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30209

## How to Validate

```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/installationInfo.test.ts
```
- Source checkout invoked from a non-git directory outside the clone, a different git repository, and a subdirectory inside the clone.
- Source checkout invoked via `npm link` symlink and `packages/cli` directory entrypoint from outside the clone.
- Package-manager installs (`npm`, local `node_modules`, Homebrew, `bunx`) under an ancestor git repository remain unaffected.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS

## Summary

This PR keeps the `ASK_USER` decision for shell commands whose arguments bash
rewrites before they run. `PolicyEngine.applyShellHeuristics()` classifies a
command from its unexpanded text and upgrades the default `ASK_USER` decision to
`ALLOW` when the command is read-only. When the text contains brace expansion,
parameter expansion, ANSI-C or locale quoting, arithmetic expansion,
substitutions, or unquoted globs, bash runs a different argument list than the
one that was classified. With this change, those commands keep the confirmation
prompt, and the decision matches the arguments that run.

## Details

The change adds one helper, one early return in the policy engine, and one
condition in each `isStrictlyApproved()` function. It doesn't add dependencies,
change `shellParse()`, or modify runtime shell flags.

- **New helper:** `hasUnresolvedShellExpansion(command)` in
  `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts` walks the tree-sitter-bash syntax
  tree through the existing `parseCommandTree()` path.
  - It reports `simple_expansion`, `expansion`, `ansi_c_string`,
    `arithmetic_expansion`, `command_substitution`, `process_substitution`, and
    `brace_expression` nodes, plus the `$` token followed by a `string` node
    that tree-sitter-bash 0.25.0 produces for `$"..."`.
  - It checks the unquoted text of `word` and `concatenation` nodes for `{a,b}`
    and `{a..c}` groups and for `*`, `?`, and `[...]`. Text in `raw_string` and
    `string` nodes and backslash-escaped characters are literal, so `'*.md'`,
    `"{a,b}"`, `\*.md`, `{}`, and `{id}` aren't reported. Tilde expansion isn't
    reported, because the existing path checks already handle it.
  - It returns `true` when the parser isn't available, parsing times out, or the
    tree has errors. It returns `false` when the configured shell isn't bash, so
    PowerShell behavior doesn't change.
- **Policy engine:** `applyShellHeuristics()` calls the helper right before the
  known-safe upgrade. When the helper returns `true`, the decision stays
  `ASK_USER`, and a debug line records it:
  `Command contains unresolved shell expansion, preserving ASK_USER`. The `DENY`
  early return, the workspace and Git checks, and YOLO handling are unchanged.
- **Sandbox approval:** both `isStrictlyApproved()` functions
  (`sandbox/utils/commandUtils.ts` and `sandbox/utils/commandSafety.ts`) apply
  the helper only to the `isKnownSafeCommand()` fallback. A command whose root
  tools are all in `approvedTools` stays approved, because that list is an
  explicit approval.
- **Unchanged:** explicit `ALLOW` rules, rules with `commandPrefix` or
  `argsPattern`, and the `plan`, YOLO, and non-interactive modes.

The following table shows example decisions with the default `run_shell_command`
rule in the `default` and `autoEdit` approval modes.

| Command                                                 | Before  | After      |
| :------------------------------------------------------ | :------ | :--------- |
| `echo {1..3}`                                           | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls *.md`                                               | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls ${d:-/etc}`                                         | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls "$HOME"`                                            | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `echo $'x'`                                             | `allow` | `ask_user` |
| `ls -la`, `find . -name '*.md'`                         | `allow` | `allow`    |
| `ls '*.md'`, `echo "{a,b}"`, `grep -E 'a{1,3}' f.txt`   | `allow` | `allow`    |
| `ls *.md` with an explicit `ALLOW` rule for shell tools | `allow` | `allow`    |

**Behavior change:** read-only commands that use unquoted globs, brace groups,
or variables, such as `ls *.md`, now show a confirmation prompt instead of
running automatically. Quoted arguments keep auto-approval. If you want these
commands to run without a prompt, you can add an explicit `ALLOW` policy rule.

**Tests:** this PR adds 117 tests. They only ask for a policy decision or a
boolean result, and they never run the commands.

- `policy/shell-argument-expansion.test.ts` (new): 70 tests with the real
  parser, the real `NoopSandboxManager`, and a temporary workspace, in the
  `default` and `autoEdit` approval modes.
- `utils/shell-utils.test.ts`: 40 tests for the helper, including syntax errors,
  a parse timeout, an unavailable parser, and PowerShell.
- `sandbox/utils/commandUtils.test.ts` (new) and
  `sandbox/utils/commandSafety.test.ts`: 7 tests for both `isStrictlyApproved()`
  functions.
- `policy/policy-engine.test.ts`: the existing `shell-utils` mock in this file
  doesn't load the parser, so it now also mocks `hasUnresolvedShellExpansion` to
  return `false`. No assertion changed.

## Related Issues


## How to Validate

You can validate the change with the unit tests and with a short interactive
check.

1.  Install the dependencies:

    ```bash
    npm ci
    ```

2.  Run the focused suites:

    ```bash
    npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- \
      src/policy/shell-argument-expansion.test.ts \
      src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts \
      src/sandbox/utils/commandSafety.test.ts \
      src/sandbox/utils/commandUtils.test.ts \
      src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts \
      src/policy/shell-safety.test.ts \
      src/policy/shell-safety-regression.test.ts \
      src/policy/shell-substitution.test.ts
    ```

    Expected result: all tests pass. Some `shell-utils.test.ts` tests are
    skipped on Linux and macOS because they only run on Windows.

3.  Run the static checks:

    ```bash
    npm run lint
    npm run typecheck
    ```

    Expected result: both commands exit with code `0`.

4.  Optional: check the behavior interactively on Linux or macOS.
    1.  Start Gemini CLI in a test folder with `--approval-mode default` and
        `--debug`.
    2.  Ask Gemini CLI to run `ls -la` unchanged. It runs without a confirmation
        dialog.
    3.  Ask Gemini CLI to run `ls *.md` unchanged. The **Confirm Shell Command**
        dialog appears, and the debug console shows
        `Command contains unresolved shell expansion, preserving ASK_USER`.
    4.  Ask Gemini CLI to run `ls '*.md'` unchanged. It runs without a
        confirmation dialog.

Edge cases that the tests cover:

- Quoted text stays literal: `echo '{red,green}.txt'`, `cat 'file{1,2}.txt'`,
  and `awk '{print $1}' f.txt`.
- An explicit `ALLOW` rule without `argsPattern` keeps `allow`.
- PowerShell returns `false` for any command.
- A parse error, a parse timeout, or an unavailable parser keeps `ASK_USER`.

Local results on Linux (Node.js 26.1.0): the full `@google/gemini-cli-core`
suite passed (8,955 tests, 57 skipped), and a run that mirrors CI (clean,
install, build, lint, typecheck, all workspace tests, bundle, and a bundle smoke
test) passed.

prs.title: fix(cli): disclose canonical link path and default consent prompt to no
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
This change updates the `gemini extensions link` command and non-interactive extension consent flow to resolve target extension paths to their canonical filesystem locations via `fs.realpathSync`, explicitly disclose the resolved canonical path and live symbolic link behavior in the confirmation prompt, and default the confirmation prompt to No (`[y/N]`) while failing closed in non-TTY environments.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->

- **Target Path Canonicalization (`packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/link.ts`)**: Normalized the input extension path in `handleLink` using `fs.realpathSync(path.resolve(workspaceDir, args.path))` prior to confirmation output and extension registration, and logged `LINK_WARNING_MESSAGE` alongside `INSTALL_WARNING_MESSAGE` when `--consent` is provided.
- **Canonical Path & Live Symbolic Link Disclosure (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/consent.ts`, `packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.ts`)**: Added `LINK_WARNING_MESSAGE` and updated `extensionConsentString` and `maybeRequestConsentOrFail` to accept `linkedSourcePath` when `installMetadata.type === 'link'`. When linking, the prompt header displays `Linking extension "<name>" from canonical path "<realpath>".` and includes a warning explaining that linking creates a live symbolic link to `<canonical_path>` where any future changes made to code, MCP servers, hooks, or prompts inside that directory take effect automatically upon CLI startup without further warnings.
- **Default-No (`[y/N]`) Confirmation & Non-TTY Guard (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/consent.ts`)**: Updated `requestConsentNonInteractive` and `promptForConsentNonInteractive` from `[Y/n]` (`defaultValue = true`) to `[y/N]` (`defaultValue = false`) so pressing `<Enter>` aborts the operation unless `y` or `yes` is explicitly entered, and added a `process.stdin.isTTY` check so non-TTY invocations without `--consent` fail closed (`return false`).
- **Unit Test Coverage (`packages/cli/src/commands/extensions/link.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/consent.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.test.ts`)**: Added and updated unit tests covering canonical path and live-symlink warning disclosure, symlink and relative segment resolution via `fs.realpathSync`, default-No (`<Enter>`) prompt cancellation, non-TTY fail-closed behavior, and successful linking upon explicit `'y'` confirmation.

## Related Issues

<!-- Use keywords to auto-close issues (Closes #123, Fixes #456). If this PR is
only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->
N/A

## How to Validate

<!-- List exact steps for reviewers to validate the change. Include commands,
expected results, and edge cases. -->


1. Run the extension link, consent, and manager unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/commands/extensions/link.test.ts src/config/extensions/consent.test.ts src/config/extension-manager.test.ts
   ```

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}
    

    /* New output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

    This change was contributed by @​BPJEnnova.

  • Additional minification of switch statements (#4176, #4359)

    This release contains additional minification patterns for reducing switch statements. Here is an example:

    // Original code
switch (x) {
  case 0:
    foo()
    break
  case 1:
  default:
    bar()
}

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

... (truncated)

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

function foo() {

  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

Release notes

Sourced from @​simple-git/argv-parser's releases.

@​simple-git/argv-parser@​3.0.0

Major Changes

  • df13aeb: Remove the vulnerabilityCheck export, use parseArgv(...tokens).vulnerabilities and parseEnv(env).vulnerabilities instead. Each vulnerability now also carries the configKey or envKey that triggered it.

Minor Changes

  • df13aeb: Add the allowConfig and strict options. Configuration keys outside the built-in list of known-safe keys (SAFE_CONFIG_KEYS) and the keys named in allowConfig now emit a one-off SIMPLE_GIT_UNLISTED_CONFIG warning, or are rejected when strict: true is set. Known-unsafe keys can now be permitted individually through allowConfig, and environment variables through allowEnvironment, deprecating the unsafe.allowUnsafe* options that only covered configuration keys or environment variables (they continue to work as before).

  • a996f0f: Thanks to @​manus-pi and @​eliteaja11-dev for submitting CVE proposals that contributed to these changes.

    When the recommended checks are enabled (with unsafe.recommended: true or strict: true), HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME supplied through .env() with a value other than the one in process.env require allowUnsafeConfigPaths (or naming them in allowEnvironment), as git reads the global configuration from $HOME/.gitconfig and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config in the same way as GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL. Passing the inherited value through is unaffected, and neither is removed from the inherited environment.

    parseEnv accepts the inherited environment as an optional second argument, used to compare HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME against.

    isGuardedEnvKey is now exported from @simple-git/argv-parser, identifying the environment variables (GIT_* and the others git reads, such as EDITOR and PAGER) that simple-git removes from an inherited environment.

  • c8ee6bb: Vulnerability reports:

    • allowUnsafePager now also covers interactive.diffFilter, the shell command that git add -p and the other --patch commands pipe their diff through.

    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeWebServerConfig option covering the instaweb.httpd, instaweb.modulePath and instaweb.gitwebDir keys used by git instaweb.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeBrowser option covering the browser.<tool>.path, browser.<tool>.cmd, man.<tool>.path and man.<tool>.cmd keys used by git help and git instaweb to open a browser or man page viewer. browser.<tool>.cmd and man.<tool>.cmd were previously covered by allowUnsafeCommandBinaries.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeSignatureTrust option covering gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile, gpg.ssh.revocationFile and gpg.minTrustLevel, which decide which signatures pass verification.

  • df13aeb: Add templateArgv, isTemplateStringsArray, remoteUrl and refName for building a git argv from a tagged template literal, where every interpolated value is treated as untrusted data. simple-git uses these for git.cmd.

prs.title: chore(deps): update workspace dependencies and sandbox runtime packages
prs.body:
## Summary

Updates workspace npm dependencies and refines the Stage 2 sandbox container `Dockerfile` runtime setup so system packages, the global `npm` toolchain, and workspace dependency `overrides` stay aligned.

## Details

- Updates direct and workspace dependencies (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `@opentelemetry/*`, `@grpc/grpc-js`, `glob`, `js-yaml`, `picomatch`, `shell-quote`, `simple-git`, `systeminformation`, `tar`, `undici`, `ws`) along with root `package.json` `overrides` and `package-lock.json`.
- Updates `BatchLogRecordProcessor` initialization in `packages/core/src/telemetry/sdk.ts` to pass `{ exporter: logExporter }`, matching the `@opentelemetry/sdk-logs` `0.222.0` constructor options signature.
- Updates Stage 2 of `Dockerfile` to:
  - Run `apt-get dist-upgrade` during base runtime package installation.
  - Update the base image's global `npm` installation to `npm@^11` (retaining Node 20 engine compatibility) along with its `glob` and `minimatch` sub-packages.
  - Install the packed `@google/gemini-cli` and `@google/gemini-cli-core` tarballs through a temporary `package.json` under `/usr/local/share/npm-global/lib` carrying root `overrides` before linking `/usr/local/share/npm-global/bin/gemini` and cleaning up temporary manifests and caches.

## Related Issues

N/A

## How to Validate

1. Run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run lint` across workspaces.
2. Run unit tests:
   - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/telemetry/sdk.test.ts src/tools/glob.test.ts src/services/gitService.test.ts`
   - `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/sandboxConfig.test.ts`
3. Pack `@google/gemini-cli` and `@google/gemini-cli-core` and build/verify the sandbox container (`npm run build:sandbox`), confirming `/usr/local/share/npm-global/bin/gemini --version` succeeds and workspace `overrides` are applied to the installed dependency tree.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}
    

    /* New output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

... (truncated)

prs.title: refactor(core): use re2js for linear-time policy argsPattern evaluation
prs.body:
## Summary

Policy `argsPattern`, `commandRegex`, and `commandPrefix` rules are now compiled
and evaluated with [`re2js`](https://github.com/le0pard/re2js) through a new
`SafeRegExp` wrapper instead of the built-in `RegExp`. Pattern evaluation time
is linear in the length of the tool arguments, and every policy pattern goes
through one compile path with one regex dialect (RE2).

## Details

- **`SafeRegExp`** (`packages/core/src/policy/safe-regex.ts`) wraps `re2js` and
  exposes `compile()`, `test()`, `source`, and `programSize`. It is the only
  module that imports `re2js`, and it is exported from
  `@google/gemini-cli-core`.
- **Types.** `PolicyRule.argsPattern` and `SafetyCheckerRule.argsPattern` are
  `SafeRegExp`. `PolicyEngine` rejects any other value in its constructor,
  `addRule`, and `addChecker`.
- **Validation.** `compileArgsPattern` is the entry point for pattern text from
  TOML files and `UPDATE_POLICY` messages. It keeps the existing length limit
  and nested-quantifier check and adds a compiled size limit of 2,000
  instructions. The largest built-in pattern compiles to 56.
- **Loader.** A pattern that doesn't compile, or that exceeds the size limit, is
  reported as a `regex_compilation` error and its rule is skipped, as for any
  invalid pattern today. Other rules in the file still load.
- **Command prefixes.** `buildArgsPatterns` spells out the whitespace set that
  may follow a prefix, because `\s` is ASCII-only in RE2. Prefix rules match the
  same commands as before. `escapeRegex` escapes ASCII whitespace only, because
  RE2 rejects a backslash in front of a non-ASCII character.
- **Dependency.** `re2js@2.9.0`: MIT, pure JavaScript, no native build step, no
  transitive dependencies. The bundle grows by about 238 KB.
- **Docs.** The policy engine reference describes the pattern dialect and how it
  differs from JavaScript regular expressions.

### Breaking changes

- Code that builds `PolicyRule` or `SafetyCheckerRule` objects must pass
  `SafeRegExp.compile(pattern)` instead of a `RegExp`.
- Policy patterns use RE2 syntax. Lookahead, lookbehind, backreferences,
  `\uXXXX` escapes, a backslash in front of a non-ASCII character, and
  repetition counts above 1,000 aren't supported. A rule that uses them is
  skipped with a `regex_compilation` error.
- `\s` matches ASCII whitespace only, and `.` matches every character except a
  newline.
- A pattern that compiles to more than 2,000 instructions is rejected. Examples:
  `.{1000}.{1000}` and `.{0,1000}`.

## Related Issues

None.

## How to Validate

1. Install and run the policy tests:

   ```bash
   npm ci
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/policy
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/agents/registry.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/scheduler/policy.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: all pass. `safe-regex.test.ts`, `toml-loader.test.ts`, and
   `policy-engine.test.ts` include timing checks for nested quantifier and
   alternation patterns and for 1 MB arguments. `safe-regex.test.ts` also checks
   that every built-in pattern, and patterns generated from command prefixes,
   match the same arguments as the JavaScript engine.

2. Run the static checks and the bundle:

   ```bash
   npm run typecheck
   npm run lint
   npm run bundle
   npm run check:lockfile
   ```

3. Edge cases to try with a policy file:
   - `argsPattern = '"command":"git (?!push)'` reports "Invalid regex pattern"
     with a note about RE2 syntax at startup, and the other rules still load.
   - `argsPattern = '.{1000}.{1000}'` reports "Regex pattern exceeds the size
     limit".
   - `commandPrefix = "git status"` with `decision = "allow"` still allows
     `git status --short`.
   - `/policies list` shows the args patterns.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [ ] Linux
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker

Local validation so far: unit tests, typecheck, lint, and bundle on macOS. The
platform matrix above has not been exercised.

prs.title: fix(acp): surface BeforeAgent hook denial and stop reasons (#30114)
prs.body:
Fixes #30114, #30132

### Problem
When Gemini CLI is running in ACP mode (`gemini --acp`), if a `BeforeAgent` (or `AfterAgent`) hook denies a prompt or stops execution (`continue: false` / `AgentExecutionStopped` / `AgentExecutionBlocked`), the ACP stream consumer in `acpSession.ts` dropped these events in the `switch (event.type)` default block. As a result, the ACP client received an empty turn ending with `end_turn` and no message or explanation.

### Solution
- Handle `GeminiEventType.AgentExecutionStopped` and `GeminiEventType.AgentExecutionBlocked` in `acpSession.ts`.
- Emit an `agent_message_chunk` with the effective reason or `systemMessage` so the ACP client/IDE clearly sees why execution stopped or was blocked.
- Added unit regression tests in `acpSession.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(core): respect active YOLO mode in taint and build file checks
prs.body:
## Summary

Respect active, trusted YOLO mode (`--approval-mode=yolo` / `-y`) in shell taint/build-file risk checks and `PolicyEngine` build file protection so autonomous interactive and headless YOLO runs are no longer interrupted by confirmation prompts or hard-denied (`POLICY_VIOLATION`) when editing build configuration files or running commands referencing external context.

All indirect prompt-injection protections remain fully enforced in `default` and `auto_edit` modes, in untrusted folders (`!isTrustedFolder()`), when YOLO mode is administratively disabled (`disableYoloMode` / `isYoloModeDisabled()`), and when higher-tier user/admin policy rules explicitly require `ask_user` or `deny`.

## Details

1. **`ShellToolInvocation` (`packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`)**:
   - Added `isActiveYoloMode()` verifying both `ApprovalMode.YOLO` and `!isYoloModeDisabled()`.
   - Updated `shouldConfirmExecute()` to skip forcing confirmation for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` when active YOLO mode is enabled (unless `forcedDecision === 'ask_user'` from an explicit policy rule or hook).
   - Updated `isCommandSubstitutionAllowed()` so active YOLO mode delegates command substitution checks to `PolicyEngine` (`yolo.toml` sets `allowCommandSubstitution = true`) rather than unconditionally blocking on `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()`.
   - Preserved the `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` guard in `getPolicyUpdateOptions()` so tainted commands never persist permanent `"Always allow"` rules.
2. **`Scheduler` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts`)**:
   - Skipped escalating `PolicyDecision.ALLOW` to `ASK_USER` (interactive) or `DENY` (non-interactive/headless) for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` when active YOLO mode (`!isYoloModeDisabled()`) is enabled.
3. **`PolicyEngine` (`packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts`)**:
   - Skipped the hardcoded `Build File Protection` downgrade (`ASK_USER` / `DENY` on `package.json`, `Makefile`, `BUILD.bazel`, etc.) when running in trusted YOLO mode (`this.approvalMode === ApprovalMode.YOLO && this.isTrustedFolder()`). `auto_edit` mode, `default` mode, untrusted workspaces, and explicit user/admin rules remain protected.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29682
Fixes #29680
Related to #29687
Related to #30004

## How to Validate

1. Run targeted unit test suites:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/shell.test.ts src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts
   ```
2. Run typecheck and lint:
   ```bash
   npm run typecheck
   npm run lint
   ```
3. Manual / headless reproduction:
   - Run `gemini --approval-mode=yolo -p "Update a script in package.json and run npm test"` in a trusted workspace -> executes without `DENY` (`Modifying build configuration files requires explicit user confirmation`) or interactive confirmation prompts.
   - Run in `--approval-mode=auto_edit` or in an untrusted workspace -> build file edits and untrusted flags still require explicit user confirmation.

type.name: Feature

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

I've been trying to understand how long sessions behave in Copilot CLI, especially once `/compact` or auto-compaction kicks in.

Right now, it seems like compaction goes through Copilot CLI's own summary/checkpoint flow even when the active model is OpenAI-backed and already using the Responses stack. I'd love to see the CLI prefer native Responses API compaction in those cases, and only fall back to the current Copilot compaction when native support is not available.

### Proposed solution

If the selected provider/model supports native compaction through the Responses API, use that path by default. If not, keep the current Copilot compaction as the fallback.

That feels like the best of both worlds: the current implementation keeps working everywhere, but OpenAI-backed sessions can preserve more of the provider's native behavior during very long runs.

A small config switch would also be nice, something along the lines of `auto | native | copilot`, but even just making `auto` prefer native compaction would already be a big improvement.

### Example prompts or workflows

- Long debugging sessions with lots of shell commands, edits, and tool calls
- Extended GPT-5 / Codex workflows where `/compact` may run more than once
- Research-heavy sessions that build up a lot of intermediate state over time
- Comparing the same workflow between Copilot CLI and other Responses-based harnesses

### Additional context

This is not a request to remove the current compaction/checkpoint system. That still makes sense as a universal fallback.

The request is mainly about letting OpenAI-backed sessions take advantage of provider-native compaction when it's already available.
