issues.title: Expose stable runtime turn IDs to built-in plugins

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Problem

Browser Use needs one exact agent-owned turn identity at both ends of a turn so it can return only the User Tabs claimed by that turn.

The current integration does not provide that correlation:

- MCP `tools/call` may contain `_meta["com.github.copilot/turnId"]`, but only when an SDK caller supplied the optional, caller-controlled `clientTurnId`.
- Built-in Copilot CLI and Copilot App sessions can issue MCP calls without that field.
- `agentStop` carries the session identity and timestamp, but not the agent turn identity that produced the corresponding MCP calls.

A timestamp is not a turn identity. Delayed or reordered hooks force built-in plugins to infer which turn stopped, or to fall back to session-scoped and idle cleanup.

Related Browser integration work: #397 and #398.

## Request

Expose the agent loop's real, opaque turn ID through a new agent-owned field on both:

1. every final MCP `tools/call` request made by that turn; and
2. the matching `agentStop` payload.

The Copilot CLI built-in-plugin path and the Copilot SDK session path should both expose the turn ID already owned by their respective runtimes. The built-in plugin should not generate, inject, or remember this ID through `preMcpToolCall`.

This should be a new field rather than a compatibility extension of `clientTurnId`:

- `clientTurnId` is optional and caller-controlled;
- `agentTurnId` is always agent-runtime-controlled and identifies the actual executing turn;
- no equality or fallback relationship between them is required.

Proposed field names and payloads follow.

### MCP tool call

```json
{
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "browser-use/manage_user_tab",
    "arguments": {
      "action": "claim",
      "tabId": "candidate-tab-id"
    },
    "_meta": {
      "com.github.copilot/agentTurnId": "agent-turn-opaque-id"
    }
  }
}
```

The agent runtime, not a hook or plugin, stamps this field after hook metadata processing so a hook cannot accidentally remove or replace it.

### Agent Stop

Command-hook payload:

```json
{
  "hookEventName": "agentStop",
  "sessionId": "session-opaque-id",
  "agentTurnId": "agent-turn-opaque-id",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-18T05:00:00.000Z",
  "stopReason": "end_turn"
}
```

The `agentTurnId` in `agentStop` must be exactly the same value stamped on MCP calls from the turn that emitted that Stop event. It must not be looked up from whichever turn is current when the hook is delivered.

## Browser Use outcome

With this contract, Browser Use can directly correlate:

```text
tools/call(sessionId, agentTurnId)
...
agentStop(sessionId, agentTurnId)
→ cancel/drain that turn's Browser work
→ return only the User Tabs claimed by that turn
```

This removes the need for Browser-specific generated turn IDs, timestamp-to-turn lookup, cross-process lifecycle locks, and replay/cleanup bookkeeping while preserving exact per-turn User Tab reclamation.

## Acceptance criteria

- A built-in Copilot CLI integration test asserts that MCP calls and `agentStop` receive the same agent-owned turn ID.
- A Copilot SDK integration test asserts the same behavior for an SDK-created session without `clientTurnId`.
- Tests cover multiple MCP calls in one turn, two sequential turns, and a delayed Stop from the earlier turn.
- Tests verify that `preMcpToolCall` output cannot remove or replace the agent-owned field.

issues.title: In 1.0.113, plugin extensions are stopped and started again a few seconds after an interactive session starts

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In 1.0.113, a few seconds after an interactive session starts, the CLI stops every running plugin extension and starts it again. Each extension's startup code runs twice. An extension that logs a message when it loads shows that message twice in the timeline, and any setup it does at startup happens twice.

1.0.112 starts each extension once. Both versions run a `plugin_change` reload of the MCP host shortly after startup, and in both the plugin fingerprint differs from the one used at startup. Only 1.0.113 stops and relaunches the extensions during that reload.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.113 (1.0.112 is not affected)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Enable a plugin from a local `directory` marketplace (`extraKnownMarketplaces` and `enabledPlugins` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`) whose extension logs a message when it loads, like this `com.github.copilot/extensions/probe/extension.mjs`:

   ```js
   import { joinSession } from '@microsoft/copilot-sdk/extension';
   const session = await joinSession({});
   await session.log('probe: loaded', { ephemeral: true });
   ```

2. Start an interactive session.
3. The timeline shows `probe: loaded`, and a few seconds later shows it again.

### Expected behavior

Each extension starts once per session. A reload that ends with the same set of extensions leaves the running extension processes alone, as 1.0.112 does.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- I ran 1.0.112 and 1.0.113 from the same install and config in short interactive sessions and sampled the process list. With four plugin extensions enabled, 1.0.112 started one process per extension and kept it. 1.0.113 started one process per extension, then a few seconds later started a second process for each of the same extension paths.
- The 1.0.113 debug log shows this order: `MCP host start (trigger=startup, ...)`, plugin reconciliation generations 1 and 2, `MCP host start (trigger=plugin_change, ...)` with a different `pluginFingerprint`, `Discovering project extensions`, then `sdk extension cleanup {"phase":"terminate"}` for every running extension, followed by a second discovery and new launches. The 1.0.112 log has the same `plugin_change` start with a changed fingerprint, but no `terminate` until the session exits.
- The plugins' files didn't change while the session ran.
- I couldn't check user and project extensions on 1.0.113, because the ones I have import `@github/copilot-sdk` and fail to load there (#5492).
- Possibly related: the 1.0.113 release notes say the managed setting `features.browserUse` now applies "including in running sessions", which may have added this reload path. Also #4892 (extension hosts re-enumerated on an hourly reload cycle).

issues.title: Computer Use: ChatGPT desktop app (OpenAI.Codex) blocked by built-in safety policy on Windows, Claude app allowed

labels.name: triage:needs-human
labels.description: Auto-triage could not classify this issue confidently. Remove the label to re-queue it.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, Computer Use in the GitHub Copilot app rejects every action on the ChatGPT desktop app, including a read-only `getApp` that only reads the accessibility tree:

```
# action rejected
# reason: actions are blocked for this application by built-in safety policy
```

The Claude desktop app is readable in the same session. I couldn't find this built-in block documented anywhere, or any way for a user or enterprise admin to allow the app. The docs only describe the Computer Use on/off switch, **Always allow**, and permission deny rules.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot app 1.4.2 (Windows). Standalone `copilot --version` reports 1.0.112, but I reproduced this in the app, not the standalone CLI.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Enable Computer Use in the GitHub Copilot app, and open the ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps.
2. In a session, call `cua.listWindows()`. Both windows are listed:
   - `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App`, title "ChatGPT"
   - `Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`, title "Claude"
3. Call `cua.getApp({windowId: <ChatGPT window>, app: "OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App"})`. It fails with the error above.
4. Call `cua.getApp({windowId: <Claude window>, app: "Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"})`. It returns the accessibility tree.

Seen in three separate sessions on this machine, including one where launching ChatGPT through Computer Use was also denied by a safety policy.

### Expected behavior

Either Computer Use can observe and control the ChatGPT app behind the normal per-app approval prompt, as it does for Claude, or the block is documented with its reason and any supported way to allow the app.

Questions for maintainers:

1. Is blocking the ChatGPT (`OpenAI.Codex`) package intended? If so, what makes it different from the Claude app?
2. Is there a supported user or enterprise setting that allows an app on the built-in block list?
3. If the block stays, could the docs list the apps blocked by default so users don't spend time debugging it?

### Additional context

- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26100, x64
- ChatGPT desktop: Microsoft Store package `OpenAI.Codex` 26.1111.2228.0
- Claude desktop: package `Claude` 5.11492.5.0
- Computer Use is enabled and works with other apps. I found no Copilot permission deny rules in local settings.
- Related: #5123 reports the same `built-in safety policy` rejection for Windows Terminal.
- Use case: we test the same agent skills in Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot, and want Copilot to run end-to-end checks in both desktop apps instead of someone doing them by hand.

issues.title: Nested/scoped instructions are only discovered after `view`, so edits, new files and shell changes skip them

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

**Summary**
With `enableOnDemandInstructionDiscovery` on, nested `AGENTS.md` and `applyTo` instructions load only after a successful `view` of a file. An agent that changes files without viewing them gets no scoped rules and no warning. Nothing tells the agent that rules exist and were skipped.

**Environment**
- `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.8, running the same runtime as the CLI. I did not test the interactive CLI.
- Flag on. One model, small test repo with a nested `AGENTS.md` and a scoped `*.instructions.md`.

**Observed**
1. After a successful `view` of a nested file, a `system.notification` with `kind.type: "instruction_discovered"` and `triggerTool: "view"` fires, and the rules reach the agent.
2. `edit` without a prior `view`: no rules, no error.
3. `create` of a new file: no discovery trigger.
4. `bash` (for example `cat` or `sed`): no discovery trigger.
5. Neutral prompts, with no instruction about viewing (4 tasks × 2 runs):

| Task | Rules applied |
|---|---|
| Edit one existing file | 4 of 4: the agent viewed first |
| Create a new file | 1 of 2: one run missed the rules |
| Change every `packages/*/f.ts` | 0 of 2: the agent used `glob` and `bash head`, then edited blind |

Overall, 3 of 8 runs ignored scoped rules.

**Expected**

**Why it matters**
Apps built on the SDK cannot rely on the flag. They need their own pre-tool hook to guarantee delivery, which is fragile because it must parse tool arguments, including shell commands.

**Suggestions**
- Trigger discovery on `edit`, `create` and patch paths, before the tool runs.
- Or add a mode, such as `"beforeWrite"`, that loads rules for the target path on the first write.
- Or emit an event when a write happens in a directory that has undiscovered instructions.

### Affected version

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

_No response_

### Expected behavior

Scoped rules for a path should load before any tool that changes that path (`edit`, `create`, patch, and ideally shell writes), not only after a `view`.

### Additional context

**Related**
- #3051 (recursive nested `AGENTS.md` discovery)
- #4687 (repo-level instructions not preserved across `/compact`)
- #4822 (discovery walks every ancestor and follows symlinks)

issues.title: Repo instruction files are skipped on Windows when the repo is on a volume with no drive letter ("customization path changed to a reparse point")

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
**Bug:** No repo instruction files load when the repo is on a volume that has no drive letter and is reached through a folder mount point. The repo's own files are regular files. The CLI shows no error in the session.

**Environment:** Windows, Copilot CLI 1.0.113.

**Setup:**
- The repo is at `C:\workspace\worktree\<project>\<repo>`.
- `C:\workspace` is a separate NTFS volume with no drive letter. It is mounted at that folder only.
- `.github`, `.github\instructions` and `.github\copilot-instructions.md` are regular files and directories. `Get-Item` shows no `LinkType` for them.

**Actual:** The session log (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`) has this warning for every instruction file in the repo: `.github\copilot-instructions.md` and every `.github\instructions\*.instructions.md` file. None of them loaded. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are also not loaded.

```
[WARNING] [rust:rt_customization_loader::repo_instruction_discovery] Cannot read contained instruction file {"path":"C:\\workspace\\worktree\\<project>\\<repo>\\.github\\copilot-instructions.md","error":"customization path changed to a reparse point"}
```

**Repro:** Use a spare NTFS volume that has no drive letter.
1. Mount it at a folder: `Add-PartitionAccessPath -DiskNumber <n> -PartitionNumber <m> -AccessPath C:\mnt-test`.
2. Copy `.github\copilot-instructions.md` and a few `.github\instructions\*.instructions.md` files into `C:\mnt-test\repo`, then run `git init` there.
3. Run `copilot instruction list` from that folder. The repo's own instructions are missing.
4. Add a drive letter to the same volume: `Add-PartitionAccessPath -DiskNumber <n> -PartitionNumber <m> -AccessPath Z:\`. Change nothing else, and run the same command again. The instructions now load.
5. Remove the letter again. They go missing again.

I repeated this several times. The result changed with the letter each time. A real `copilot -p` session logged the warning above when there was no letter, and logged none when there was one. Results for identical content:

| Location | Instructions listed? |
|---|---|
| Plain folder on `C:` | Yes |
| Volume mounted at `C:\mnt-test`, no drive letter | **No** |
| Same volume and same path, drive letter added | Yes |
| Same volume with a drive letter only (`Z:\repo`), no mount folder | Yes |

The failure did not depend on how deep the repo is or which mount folder is used. It also affected `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.

**Expected:** Instruction files load. A volume without a drive letter is a normal setup, and it should not fail the containment check.

**Impact:** The model silently lacks all repo instructions. The only evidence is in the log file.

**Workaround:** Give the volume a drive letter. I confirmed this on a spare volume. I have not tried it on the volume that holds my repo.

**Suggested fix:** Resolve the repo root once, then check containment against the resolved path. Also show a visible warning when instruction files are skipped.

**Not tested:** Dev Drive, other file systems, or other causes tied to the volume.

issues.title: Fusion judge rejects completed cross-session actions after failing to find their evidence

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Fusion's judge rejected a completed session-ownership transfer because it could not establish that the release, recipient acknowledgment, and follow-up messages existed. The sender and recipient logs record those actions before the rejection.

This case had a nonempty solver answer and no context rollover during the Fusion run: it does not depend on the [empty-result-after-rollover problem](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5493). The failure sends completed coordination work into repair.

## Affected version

The independent transfer case records `copilotVersion: "1.0.103-unstable.r41379698026.g3219c66"`. A second, checkpoint-related case records `"1.0.108-0"`.

Both used the Copilot runtime hosted by VS Code on a Linux SSH host, with Fusion Cascade, Claude Opus 5.5 as solver, and GPT-6 Sol as judge.

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

Observed workflow from historical logs, not a minimal or deterministic reproduction:

1. Transfer a task to another session through `send_message` and obtain the recipient's acknowledgment.
2. Later, ask the outgoing session to reconcile a stale message that still assigns ownership to it.
3. The solver checks the successor's state, sends corrections, and reports the completed transfer.
4. The judge checks older handoff files and searches logs, but rejects the answer for lack of evidence of the release, acknowledgment, and queued messages.

## Expected behavior

Review should verify completed cross-session actions against their recorded results and recipient responses. Failing to locate evidence through a limited filesystem search should not establish that a required action remains undone.

## Additional context

<details>
<summary>Independent case: recorded actions precede the rejection</summary>

All times below are UTC on November 5, 2026:

| Time | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 03:54:32 | Sender issues an explicit ownership release; the send succeeds. |
| 03:54:33 | Recipient records the release as an incoming message. |
| 03:55:06 | Recipient answers: "Release accepted." |
| 04:01:45 | Sender queues two corrective messages; both sends succeed. |
| 04:01:54 | Solver completes with a 2,264-character answer describing the transfer and messages. |
| 04:02:13 | Judge rejects with score 2, saying the inspected record does not establish the release, acknowledgment, or queued messages. |

The judge inspected handoff files, searched for session-URI identifiers as filenames, and searched the sender's log with limits of 12 and 15 matches. It did not inspect the recipient's log. The required evidence existed; this does not demonstrate that it was inaccessible.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Second case: a checkpoint exists outside ordinary filesystem discovery</summary>

On November 12, a solver successfully wrote its checkpoint through `session_artifacts` and had sent the required parent acknowledgment. After rollover, the judge rejected the work for a missing checkpoint and missing acknowledgment.

The judge used filesystem reads and globs, including `**/checkpoint.md`, but did not call `session_artifacts`. The reserved recovery object is stored as JSON, not as a filesystem file named `checkpoint.md`. This case is also affected by the separate rollover defect, so it is not the independent reproduction.

</details>

The review path needs reliable references to non-file side effects, including message receipts and the correct session-artifact scope. These logs show failed evidence discovery, not a proven blanket inability to access those resources.

*Prepared with Copilot assistance from my session logs; task details, paths, and identifiers omitted.*

issues.title: Fusion Cascade judges an empty solver result when new_context requests continuation

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

In a Fusion (Max) session, `new_context` ended an unfinished solver phase instead of continuing it before review. The judge then rejected an empty solver result and escalated to repair. The recovery prompt reached the repair model only after that rejection.

This interrupts long-running work at a context boundary and sends unfinished work through the failure/repair path. In the example below, the judge also requested an already-saved checkpoint and an already-sent parent acknowledgment.

## Affected version

The affected session records `copilotVersion: "1.0.108-0"`. This was the Copilot runtime hosted by VS Code on a Linux SSH host, not a standalone terminal CLI session. Fusion resolved to `hydrafusion-max`, pattern `cascade`, with Claude Opus 5.5 as solver and GPT-6 Sol as judge.

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

Observed sequence from an actual session; I have not reduced it to a standalone test:

1. Run an unfinished task in Fusion (Max), with routing resolved to Cascade.
2. Have the solver save its recovery checkpoint using `session_artifacts`, then call `new_context`.
3. Observe the solver phase complete with `status: "succeeded"` and `content: ""`.
4. The judge runs before the fresh-context continuation. It rejects the result, triggering repair.

## Expected behavior

Resume the unfinished task from its checkpoint before judging its answer. A context rollover should not itself count as solver completion or trigger repair.

## Additional context

<details>
<summary>Recorded sequence and corroborating observations</summary>

All times below are UTC on November 12, 2026:

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 22:00:59 | Solver saves its checkpoint through `session_artifacts`. |
| 22:01:00.884 | `session.context_cleared`, `messagesCleared: 80`. |
| 22:01:00.944 | `assistant.fusion_phase_completed`: primary succeeded, empty content and empty projection. |
| 22:01:18.003 | Judge completes with score 1, verdict `reject`. |
| 22:01:18.007 | `session.fusion_handoff` selects the repair model. |
| 22:01:19.375 | The fresh-context recovery prompt is delivered during repair. |

The solver had run for about 88 minutes and 33 model requests before rollover. Its stop hook reported `end_turn`; only 60ms elapsed between clearing context and completing the primary phase.

A local-log scan found 26 judged Fusion runs with rollover and empty primary output: 25 were rejected, one accepted. Those rejections are not all independently verified as false; the problem is judging before continuation.

For comparison, an inspected single-pattern Fusion run committed its staged tool messages and then started a new Fusion run with the recovery prompt. That trace does not show permanent loss of continuation. The demonstrated Cascade defect is premature review and escalation.

</details>

The sequence suggests rollover's `end_turn` is being treated as a finished solver answer. I have not verified the implementation cause.

Related: [judge evidence-discovery failures also occur without rollover](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5494).

*Prepared with Copilot assistance from my session logs; paths and identifiers omitted.*

issues.title: 1.0.113: extensions importing @github/copilot-sdk fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; SDK renamed to @microsoft/copilot-sdk with no alias or release note

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In Copilot CLI **1.0.113**, the extension SDK package was renamed from `@github/copilot-sdk` to `@microsoft/copilot-sdk`. There is no alias for the old name and no mention in the 1.0.113 release notes, so any existing extension that imports `@github/copilot-sdk` fails to load:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@github/copilot-sdk'
```

A second breaking change ships in the same release: provider settings registered with the flat `providers` / `models` shape are now silently ignored. 1.0.113 requires them to be wrapped in an `inference` object, while 1.0.112 requires the flat shape. No warning or error is emitted, so BYOK models just disappear from the model picker.

Together these break every BYOK/custom-provider extension written against 1.0.112, and fixing one problem only reveals the other.

### Affected version

1.0.113 (1.0.112 works)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create `~/.copilot/extensions/<name>/extension.mjs` that imports `@github/copilot-sdk/extension` and registers a BYOK provider and model using flat `providers` / `models` settings.
2. On CLI 1.0.112, start a session: the extension loads and the model appears in `/model`.
3. On CLI 1.0.113, start a session: the extension fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
4. Change the import to `@microsoft/copilot-sdk/extension`: the extension loads, but the flat settings are silently ignored and the model does not appear.

### Expected behavior

- Keep `@github/copilot-sdk` resolvable as an alias for a deprecation period, or document the rename with migration steps in the release notes.
- Either accept the previous flat settings shape, or log a clear warning/error when settings are ignored.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows x64
- Current workaround in extensions: try importing `@microsoft/copilot-sdk/extension`, fall back to `@github/copilot-sdk/extension`, and pass settings in the shape expected by whichever SDK loaded.

issues.title: `plugins.marketplaces.add`: large marketplaces download the whole repository with no progress, ignore cancellation, orphan git on exit and leave staging folders behind

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Adding a Git marketplace clones its entire repository (`git clone --depth 1 --progress`, then a full checkout) into `<COPILOT_CACHE_HOME>/marketplaces/.copilot-clone-*`, only to read one `marketplace.json`. For a large catalog this takes many minutes, and the operation cannot be observed, cancelled or cleaned up:

1. **Whole-repository download.** A marketplace with thousands of plugins, most of them stored as folders inside the marketplace repository, has a `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` of a few MB, but adding it downloads a pack of several hundred MB and then checks out tens of thousands of files (well over a GB on disk). On a typical connection the download alone took about 11 minutes, and an earlier attempt was still checking out after 22 minutes.
2. **No progress.** The runtime passes `--progress` to git but exposes nothing through `plugins.marketplaces.add` or any event, so SDK hosts can only show an open-ended spinner.
3. **Cancellation is ignored.** The .NET SDK sends `$/cancelRequest` when the caller cancels `Rpc.Plugins.Marketplaces.AddAsync(...)`. The call returns immediately on the client, but the runtime keeps running git (the same git processes were still downloading 30 seconds later). A second `plugins.marketplaces.add` for the same source does not start its own clone while the first one runs (it appears to wait on the marketplace lock).
4. **git outlives the runtime.** When the runtime process exits (for example the host app closes, or the SDK client is disposed) during an add, its git processes keep running as orphans and keep downloading into the staging folder.
5. **Interrupted clones are never cleaned up.** The staging folder of an interrupted add stays in the cache indefinitely; later adds and refreshes do not remove it. A failed add also leaves its `<name>.lock` file even though the marketplace was never registered.

When git exits with an error while the runtime is alive (for example a network failure), the runtime does report the failure and removes the staging folder, so the cleanup path exists; it is just not reached on cancellation or exit.

### Affected version

1.0.111 (also through GitHub.Copilot.SDK 1.0.33). The 1.0.113 runtime ships the same marketplace clone code (the same `git clone --depth 1` arguments, with no partial or sparse clone options).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. With an isolated `COPILOT_HOME` and `COPILOT_CACHE_HOME`, run `copilot plugin marketplace add <owner/repo>` for a marketplace repository that holds its plugins as folders and is several hundred MB.
2. Observe a single `git clone --depth 1 --progress ... <cache>/marketplaces/.copilot-clone-XXXX/repo` and no progress output until it finishes.
3. From an SDK host, call `plugins.marketplaces.add` with a cancellation token and cancel it after 30 seconds: the request completes as cancelled, but the git processes keep running and the staging folder keeps growing.
4. Start another add and stop the runtime process while git is downloading: git keeps running under no parent, and `.copilot-clone-XXXX` remains after it ends. Adding another marketplace later does not remove it.

### Expected behavior

- Adding a marketplace fetches only what browsing needs: the manifest (and, if needed, manifest-relative metadata), using a partial and sparse clone (`--filter=blob:none --sparse`) or the GitHub contents API. Plugin folders are fetched when a plugin is installed.
- `plugins.marketplaces.add` honors `$/cancelRequest`: it stops git, removes the staging folder and releases the lock.
- The add reports progress (phase, bytes or objects received), for example as notifications the SDK can surface.
- The runtime stops the git processes it started when it exits (a job object on Windows, a process group or `kill_on_drop` elsewhere).
- The runtime removes stale `.copilot-clone-*` folders and orphan lock files of marketplaces that were never registered, for example at startup or before the next clone.

### Additional context

- Windows 11, x64.
- Related: #2463 (sparse checkout for marketplace clones), #2399 (sparse checkout for plugin installs) and #4690 (checkout of a large marketplace fails on long paths).
- The add needs only the manifest, which is a few MB for this marketplace, so nearly all of the download and checkout is unnecessary at add time.
- Hosts currently have to work around this by finding the runtime's `git clone` child from its command line to show progress and stop it, which depends on runtime internals.

Calling `extensions_reload` in a session where a running extension registers external tools leaves that extension permanently failed. The new process fails at `session.resume` because the old connection still holds the tool names. Only restarting the app or session recovers it.

peer-closed-before-ready

- A second `extensions_reload` fails the same way. The extension does not recover on its own.

1.0.106-8

### Expected behavior

The old process exits and releases its tool registrations. The new process starts and reaches `ready`, and its tools can be called.

issues.title: Emit structured warning/session event when <available_skills> is truncated by SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

When a session has enough active skills that the `<available_skills>` catalog exceeds `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET` (30,000 characters by default), the Copilot runtime stops emitting full `<skill><name>...</name><description>...</description></skill>` entries and collapses the remaining skills into a name-only line (`Additional skills available (invoke by name): ...`).

Today, this happens silently in the event stream:
- `session.skills_loaded` still lists all discovered skills with `enabled: true` and no indication that any skill's description was dropped from the prompt.
- No `session.warning` or structured truncation event is emitted.

As a result:
1. **CLI users** have no visibility that skills were degraded/cut or that raising `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET` fixes it (see #2314 and #1464).
2. **SDK integrators and evaluation frameworks** (such as Vally ? microsoft/vally#1452) cannot reliably warn users when a tested skill lost its description without resorting to brittle regex parsing of `system.message` XML, which breaks if prompt formatting changes or dynamic skill retrieval is used.

### Proposed solution

Emit a structured signal from the runtime whenever `<available_skills>` prompt assembly truncates or degrades skills due to `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET` (aligned with existing events like `session.warning`, `session.truncation`, `session.skills_loaded`, and `session.mcp_servers_loaded`):

1. **Emit a `session.warning` event** (for human/timeline visibility in Copilot CLI and SDK consumers):
   - `warningType`: e.g. `"skill_budget"` (alongside existing `"subscription"`, `"policy"`, `"mcp"`)
   - `message`: clear summary including how many skills kept full descriptions vs. lost descriptions and naming the affected skills (or preview)
   - `remediation` / tip: mention `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET` (with current effective budget and total catalog size)

2. **Expose machine-readable truncation metadata** (so SDK clients don't have to parse `message` prose or `system.message` XML), via one of:
   - **Option A ? Extend `session.skills_loaded`** (`SkillsLoadedData` / `SkillsLoadedSkill`) or emit a companion event (e.g., `session.skills_truncated` / `session.skills_prompt_built`) with:
     ```jsonc
     {
       "charBudget": 30000,
       "totalChars": 58004,
       "fullSkillCount": 46,
       "totalSkillCount": 92,
       "truncatedSkills": ["skill-47", "..."] // or per-skill promptVisibility: "full" | "name-only" | "omitted"
     }
     ```
   - **Option B ? Structured optional fields on `session.warning`** (when `warningType === "skill_budget"`) carrying the same `charBudget`, `totalChars`, and `truncatedSkills` fields.

*(Note: because skill discovery can happen before system-prompt assembly, emitting the event/metadata when the prompt's `<available_skills>` block is constructed ensures it accurately reflects what the model actually saw.)*

### Example prompts or workflows

1. **Interactive CLI user with 40?90 skills installed:** Starts a session and immediately sees a non-fatal timeline warning listing which skills lost their descriptions and suggesting `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET`, instead of wondering why Copilot fails to auto-select an installed skill or trying to remove MCP servers.
2. **Agent evaluation harness (e.g. Vally / CI skill evals):** Runs a skill-invocation eval with 90 active skills, listens for the typed SDK truncation event, checks whether the eval's target skill is in `truncatedSkills`, and surfaces an explicit warning before/alongside a `0` score.
3. **Observability & token/prompt-budget tooling (#3326):** Tracks `charBudget` vs. `totalChars` across sessions to identify repositories or teams whose skill descriptions need tightening or a higher `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET`.

### Additional context

- **Reproduced on `@github/copilot-sdk` (runtime `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET` default 30,000):**
  - With 90 custom skills (~500-char descriptions each) + 2 built-in skills (92 total, ~58k chars):
    - Default `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET`: `system.message` `<available_skills>` is capped at `30,005` chars with only **46 / 92** full `<skill>` blocks; the remaining 46 (including a late-sorting target skill) are relegated to `Additional skills available (invoke by name): ...`, `session.skills_loaded` still reports **92** skills, no `session.warning` is emitted, and the model fails to invoke the target skill.
    - With `SKILL_CHAR_BUDGET=100000`: all **92 / 92** skills receive full `<skill>` blocks (`58,004` chars) and the target skill is invoked reliably.
- Related issues: #2314, #1464, #3326, microsoft/vally#1452.

issues.body:
### Summary
The permission prompt ("Do you want to allow this?") numbers its choices (1. Yes, 2. Yes, and remember..., 3. No), and pressing `1`, `2` or `3` selects one at once. Single-select questions in the `ask_user` form do not: they show a list with a preselected default and an "Other (type your answer)" row, and every non-default choice needs arrow keys plus Enter.

### Example
A skill asks one question per bug report: "What should I look up?" with the choices None, Both (Jira and code), Jira only, Code only. Today the user presses the arrow keys and Enter. With numbered choices, pressing `3` would pick "Jira only" in one key press.

### Why
- Quality of life: the same key habit as the permission prompt works everywhere.
- Speed: workflows that ask several short questions in a row (yes/no, pick one of a few) become much faster, especially for skills that collect input through `ask_user`.
- Fewer mistakes: a number key is harder to mis-select than arrowing past the intended row.

### Suggested behavior
Render `enum` (single-select) fields with numbered rows, and let the number key select and submit the row, exactly like the permission prompt. Keep the "Other (type your answer)" row as the last number, or keep it on a separate key. Multi-select could stay as it is.

### Environment
Copilot CLI 1.0.111, Windows, PowerShell.

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

Repeated model-side MCP tool discovery reports "Found 0 tools" for a namespace whose tool definitions were already loaded. This misleading result caused the agent to declare a working integration unavailable and skip a required workflow step.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.84-2
- Windows
- Local stdio MCP server exposing four tools

## Reproduction

1. In a fresh session, discover the configured MCP namespace. In this case, the call was `api_tool.list_resources({"paths":["pr-copilot"]})`.
2. Observe "Found 4 tools" and all four tool definitions being loaded.
3. Repeat the identical discovery call without changing MCP configuration.
4. Observe "Found 0 tools", despite the previously loaded definitions remaining in context.

This was reproduced in a separate session after investigating the original failure.

## Actual behavior and impact

The affected session already had all four schemas in its request history. Two later discovery responses completed with `tools: []`. The agent then reported: "The PR-monitor integration currently exposes no tools, so I can't start it."

The empty responses were real; the incorrect inference was that no tools were available. This report concerns model-side discovery, not a claim that the MCP server's raw `tools/list` returned an empty list. No stateful monitor invocation was needed to reproduce the discovery behavior.

## Expected behavior

A repeated lookup should either return the existing tool definitions or explicitly report that the tools are already loaded, including their names/count. "No additional definitions to load" must be distinguishable from "no matching or available tools", so the agent does not abandon an available integration.

---
🤖 m-nash-copilot

issues.title: Sub-agents cannot run `hydrafusion` or `hydrafusion-max`, both offered by the `task` tool

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In an interactive 1.0.109 session with experimental features on, the `task` tool's `model` parameter lists `hydrafusion` and `hydrafusion-max` among its values, and `/model` with an unsupported name lists both under "Available models:". A sub-agent launched with either one does not run HydraFusion:

- In 1.0.109, the launch fails before the sub-agent makes any model request, with `Model "hydrafusion" is not available.`
- In 1.0.105 and 1.0.108, the sub-agent completes, but its request goes to the saved default model from `settings.json`. Its `subagent.completed` event reports `"model":"hydrafusion"` and names the default model only in `firstDispatchedModel`. The `task` tool result does not mention the substitution.

With the same account, `hydrafusion` works as the session model in 1.0.109: `copilot --experimental --model hydrafusion -p "..."` returns an answer.

The 1.0.109 changelog entry "Show an error when a selected or saved model is unavailable instead of silently switching to another model" seems to explain why 1.0.109 reports an error where 1.0.105 and 1.0.108 substituted the default model.

### Affected version

1.0.109 (error); 1.0.105 and 1.0.108 (substitution). Linux x86-64.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run a prompt-mode session launching one sub-agent with the model under test:

   ```sh
   copilot --experimental --model claude-haiku-4.5 --no-custom-instructions --no-auto-update --available-tools task --output-format json -p 'Call the task tool exactly once with these arguments: agent_type "general-purpose", name "probe", description "model probe", mode "sync", model "hydrafusion", prompt "Reply with exactly one word: ok". Then output the tool result verbatim and stop. Do not call any other tool and do not retry.'
   ```

2. On 1.0.109, the `subagent.failed` event in the output has these fields, among others:

   ```json
   {"error": "Model \"hydrafusion\" is not available.", "model": "hydrafusion", "explicitModelOverride": "hydrafusion", "modelSelectionSource": "explicit_override", "totalToolCalls": 0, "durationMs": 40}
   ```

   With `model "hydrafusion-max"` the launch fails the same way. With `model "gpt-6-luna"` the sub-agent completes and returns `ok`.

3. For the earlier builds, I ran that command with three environment variables: `COPILOT_CLI_DIST_DIR` set to the cached 1.0.105 or 1.0.108 package under `~/.cache/copilot/pkg/linux-x64/`, `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false`, and `COPILOT_HOME` set to a directory holding only a `settings.json` with `{"model":"gpt-6.1-sol","experimental":true}`. Adding `--usage-output-file <path>` shows the models used. On both builds, the `subagent.completed` event had `"model":"hydrafusion"` and `"firstDispatchedModel":"gpt-6.1-sol"`, and the usage file listed one request to `gpt-6.1-sol` next to the session model's two requests. With `model "hydrafusion-max"` on 1.0.105, the event had `"model":"hydrafusion-max"` and the same `firstDispatchedModel`.

4. With `"model":"gemini-3.8-flash"` in that `settings.json`, on 1.0.108, the request went to `gemini-3.8-flash` instead, for `hydrafusion` and for `hydrafusion-max`. On 1.0.109 with the same directory, the `hydrafusion` launch fails as in step 2.

5. On 1.0.109, I also tried `fusion` (the Copilot Fusion alias) and `auto`. Neither is in the `task` tool's list in the interactive session, so I added this sentence to the prompt after the argument list: `Pass the model value exactly as given even if it is not among the listed values.` With `model "fusion"` the launch fails the same way (`Model "fusion" is not available.`), although `--model fusion` returns an answer as the session model. With `model "auto"` the sub-agent completes with one request to `gpt-6-luna`, so absence from the list does not by itself cause the rejection.

### Expected behavior

Either a sub-agent can run HydraFusion, or the `task` tool does not offer `hydrafusion` and `hydrafusion-max` and the documentation states the limitation. The [HydraFusion documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/early-access/copilot/hydrafusion) says only that "HydraFusion works separately from subagents and doesn't start them", without saying whether a sub-agent can run HydraFusion.

### Confirmed unresolved

Edit (2026-11-17): Confirmed in 1.0.113: sub-agent launches for both hydrafusion and hydrafusion-max fail with Model "..." is not available.

issues.title: web_fetch rejects public domains resolved to Surge Fake-IP addresses on macOS (CLI 1.0.98)

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS with Surge Enhanced Mode enabled, Copilot CLI's built-in `web_fetch` rejects public HTTPS URLs because system DNS returns Surge Fake-IP addresses in `198.18.0.0/15`.

This makes ordinary public documentation browsing fail even though the domain is intended to be reached through Surge. This report concerns the CLI specifically; a similar report exists for Copilot App in github/app#1867.

### Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI: `1.0.98` (`copilot --version`)
- OS: macOS
- Proxy: Surge for Mac, Enhanced Mode / Fake-IP DNS
- System HTTP and HTTPS proxy enabled
- DNS resolver list includes Surge's `198.18.0.2`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Surge Enhanced Mode with Fake-IP DNS on macOS.
2. Confirm that a public hostname resolves to a Fake-IP address through the system resolver, for example:
   ```bash
   python3 -c 'import socket; print(socket.gethostbyname("lobehub.com"))'
   ```
   Observed result in this environment: `198.18.2.212`.
3. Ask Copilot CLI to fetch `https://lobehub.com/skills/vinitu-macos-music-skill` using its built-in `web_fetch` tool.
4. The tool fails before retrieving the page.

### Actual behavior

```text
WebFetchBlockedUrlError: web_fetch URL "https://lobehub.com/skills/vinitu-macos-music-skill" resolves to blocked address 198.18.2.212. URLs must not target loopback, private, or link-local addresses.
```

The same problem was observed for other public sites, including `docs.github.com` and `context7.com`, when they resolved to Surge Fake-IP addresses.

### Expected behavior / requested improvement

Please provide or document a supported, security-preserving way for `web_fetch` to work in Fake-IP proxy environments without requiring users to change system-wide DNS behavior.

Potential approaches to evaluate include explicit trusted-proxy integration that safely handles target validation, or a narrowly scoped compatibility mechanism for synthetic DNS mappings. The implementation should continue protecting real loopback, private, link-local, metadata-service destinations, and redirects to unsafe destinations; this is not a request to disable SSRF protection globally.

If an existing setting already supports this setup, please document the exact configuration and whether target-address validation still uses the system resolver.

### Current workaround and limitations

Surge supports `always-real-ip` under `[General]`, allowing selected domains to resolve to real IPs while retaining Enhanced Mode. However:

- Per-domain configuration needs maintenance as the agent visits new public sites.
- `always-real-ip = *` changes DNS behavior for all domains and loses the benefits of Fake-IP resolution.

CLI help documents `proxyUrl` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` and URL permissions, but I could not find a documented Fake-IP compatibility setting. Whether configuring an explicit proxy alone fixes this particular validation failure has **not** been verified.

### Related issues

- github/app#1867 — same Fake-IP failure reported in Copilot App.
- #3731 — request for controlled access to private networks; related target-address restrictions, but this report involves public domains mapped to synthetic proxy addresses.

issues.title: /cleanup slash command — detect and resolve orphaned, stale, and hung processes from previous sessions

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

When a Copilot CLI session crashes, is force-killed, or exits uncleanly, it can leave behind a range of residual state: orphaned child processes, hanging MCP server processes, stale lock files, lingering worker or sub-agent processes, and session database files in an inconsistent state. Currently there is no built-in way to detect or resolve any of this. Users who experience repeated crashes or unexpected behaviour across sessions have no tool to audit or clean up leftover state — they must either reboot, hunt for processes manually, or live with the side effects.

The fix must be **lightweight and token-free** — a pure local operation that does not invoke the LLM, consume API quota, or count as a premium request.

### Proposed solution

Introduce a **`/cleanup`** slash command that performs a fast, local-only scan of all residual state from previous sessions and presents a concise, actionable report — without invoking the model or consuming any API quota.

**What it scans:**

| Category | What it looks for |
|---|---|
| **Orphaned processes** | Child processes (MCP servers, sub-agents, worker tasks) whose parent session PID no longer exists |
| **Hung / unresponsive processes** | Copilot CLI processes that are running but not responding (detectable via PID status + lock file age) |
| **Stale lock files** | `.lock` or session mutex files left behind by crashed instances |
| **Inconsistent session state** | `session.db` files from sessions that never cleanly closed (no clean-exit marker) |
| **Abandoned log files** | Oversized or orphaned log files from sessions that did not rotate cleanly |
| **Zombie sub-agents** | Background agent processes that are still alive but whose parent session is gone |

**Output format — compact, structured, actionable:**

```
/cleanup — Session Health Check

  ✖  2 orphaned MCP server processes (playwright PID 18842, git PID 19001)
  ✖  1 stale lock file  (~/.copilot/session-state/813d.../session.lock  age: 4h 12m)
  ⚠  1 inconsistent session DB  (~/.copilot/session-state/813d.../session.db)
  ✔  No hung Copilot CLI processes found
  ✔  No zombie sub-agent processes found

  Found 3 issue(s).  Resolve all? (Y/n)  — or press Enter to review individually
```

**Resolution options (per item or all-at-once):**
- **Kill** orphaned/hung processes (`SIGTERM` → grace period → `SIGKILL` / `Stop-Process` on Windows)
- **Delete** stale lock files
- **Archive or delete** inconsistent session DBs (with option to attempt recovery first — see #1780)
- **Rotate** oversized log files

**No LLM involvement — this is entirely a local process/filesystem operation.** It must not trigger any API call, token usage, or premium request.

**Additional flags for automation:**
```
/cleanup --dry-run    # Report issues without taking any action
/cleanup --force      # Resolve everything without confirmation prompts
/cleanup --stale-only # Only target lock files and session state, skip processes
```

### Example prompts or workflows

1. User returns after a machine sleep that killed their session. Runs `/cleanup` — two orphaned MCP servers and a stale lock file are found and resolved in seconds, zero tokens spent.
2. User notices a new session starts slowly. `/cleanup --dry-run` reveals a hung Copilot CLI process from a previous crash is still holding resources.
3. CI/CD script runs `/cleanup --force` before starting a fresh session to guarantee a clean environment with no residual state from a previous run.
4. User runs `/cleanup` and finds an inconsistent session DB. Chooses to attempt recovery (hands off to #1780 queue recovery flow) rather than delete it.
5. `/cleanup` finds nothing — outputs `✔ All clear. No orphaned or stale state found.` and exits immediately, consuming no time or tokens.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows 11 Pro (Build 26200 / 24H2)
- Shell: PowerShell 7.5.4
- Copilot CLI: 0.0.420 (win32-x64)
- **This command must never invoke the LLM** — it is a local diagnostic and remediation tool only. No API calls, no token usage, no premium requests consumed under any circumstances.
- `/diagnose` already handles connectivity checks — `/cleanup` is the complementary local health check for process and session state.
- On Windows, process termination should use `Stop-Process` / `TerminateProcess`; on Unix, `SIGTERM` followed by `SIGKILL` after a grace period.
- The session state directory (`~/.copilot/session-state/`) and log directory (`~/.copilot/logs/`) are the primary scan targets — both are already well-defined locations.
- Related: #1780 (queue recovery from crashed sessions) — `/cleanup` and queue recovery are complementary; `/cleanup` handles processes and locks, #1780 handles prompt data.

issues.title: 1.0.98: Copilot Enterprise account routed to api.business.githubcopilot.com — 401 on model catalog, 'Authentication failed' despite valid token

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

issues.body:
## Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.98 (installed via official `gh.io/copilot-install` script, Linux x64, headless — no system keychain, token stored in plaintext `~/.copilot/config.json`)
- Auth via `copilot login --device-code` on github.com (not a GHEC data-residency tenant, `GH_HOST` unset)
- Account shape: personal account whose GitHub Copilot access is provided by a **GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization with a Copilot Enterprise seat** (org Copilot management page shows "GitHub Copilot Enterprise", seat assigned and listed under "members with access to Copilot")

## Symptom

Every `copilot -p "<prompt>"` invocation fails immediately:

```
Error: Authentication failed (Request ID: ...)

Your GitHub token may be invalid, expired, or lacking the required permissions.
```

CLI log (same run):

```
[ERROR] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { status_code: 401 ... })
[WARNING] MCP OAuth authorization failed; reporting the server as needing auth {"server":"github-mcp-server","error":"Browser-based OAuth required for https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly"}
[ERROR] Error loading models: Error: 401 "Unauthorized"
```

The model-catalog fetch and the built-in `github-mcp-server` both target **`api.business.githubcopilot.com`** for this account.

## The token is valid

The stored token returns `200` on `GET https://api.github.com/user` with the correct account, so "invalid/expired token" is not the cause.

## Host matrix (same token, `GET <host>/models`)

| Host | Result |
|---|---|
| `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` | **401** `Unauthorized` (x-copilot-service-request-id: 717f9174-81b4-4f3d-a2bb-816f5b9e0d0b) |
| `https://api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com/models` | **200** — full model catalog returned |
| `https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` | **200** — full model catalog returned |

So the account is authorized on the enterprise (and generic) Copilot API hosts, but the CLI routes this Copilot **Enterprise**-seat account to the **business** host, where it is rejected with 401. The CLI appears to classify the account as Copilot *Business* rather than *Enterprise* when resolving the Copilot API base (`authGetCopilotApiUrl`).

## Impact

CLI is completely unusable for Copilot Enterprise accounts with a valid seat: the first authenticated call (model catalog) 401s, before any prompt can run. The error message is misleading — it suggests a token problem, but the token is fine; only the target host is wrong.

## Reproduction

1. Have a personal account whose Copilot is provided by a GitHub Enterprise Cloud org with a Copilot Enterprise seat.
2. `copilot login` (device code flow).
3. `copilot -p "hi"` → `Error: Authentication failed`.
4. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <stored token>" https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` → 200, while the CLI's business host → 401.

## Related

- #4527 — prompt-mode model-catalog fetch hit the wrong host (fixed for GHEC data-residency tenants); same defect class for enterprise-routed accounts.
- #4408 — enterprise-routed accounts resolve the Copilot API base to `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`; for this account the CLI resolves it to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` instead, and that host 401s.

issues.title: Local sandbox 'Authenticate gh' silently uses an unrelated cached fine-grained PAT instead of active gh OAuth session, with no visibility into which credential is chosen

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With local sandboxing enabled (`/sandbox enable`) and the "Authenticate gh" auth setting on (default), the `GH_TOKEN` exported into the sandboxed environment did not correspond to my active `gh` session.

- `gh auth status` (run on the host, outside the sandbox) showed I was logged in via the OAuth device flow, with a `gho_...` token and scopes `admin:public_key`, `gist`, `read:org`, `repo` — i.e. full private repo access.
- Inside a Copilot CLI sandboxed session, `echo $GH_TOKEN` / `gh repo list <org> --visibility private` showed access to only **one** private repository in my org, via a token in the fine-grained PAT format (`github_pat_...`).
- After investigating, I found the actual token being used: an old fine-grained PAT I had created previously and scoped intentionally to a single, unrelated repository (not the repo I was actively working in).
- This PAT is neither the active `gh auth status` OAuth session (keyring-stored `gho_` token) nor the GitHub App `ghu_` token found in `~/.config/github-copilot/auth.db`.

I was unable to determine, from inside a Copilot CLI session or from documentation, **why this specific cached PAT was selected** over my active OAuth login, or where exactly it was being read from/cached. The lack of visibility made this very difficult to diagnose — I only found the answer by manually checking GitHub's "Active tokens" org admin page and recognizing a token I had created weeks earlier for unrelated purposes.

### Expected behavior

When "Authenticate gh" is enabled for the local sandbox, I would expect one of the following:
1. The sandbox's `GH_TOKEN` to be derived from the currently active `gh auth status` account/session (respecting `gh auth switch`), not from some other cached credential, OR
2. If Copilot CLI intentionally uses a different/cached credential for the sandbox (e.g. a previously-supplied `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` env var), this should be clearly surfaced to the user — e.g. via `/sandbox` or `/env`, showing *which* token/account is being exported into the sandbox and why, without requiring the user to manually diff PAT prefixes and check GitHub's org "Active tokens" page.

### Reproduction steps

1. Log in normally via `gh auth login` (OAuth device flow), confirm with `gh auth status` that the active session has broad `repo` scope.
2. Separately, at some earlier point, create (or have previously created) a fine-grained PAT scoped to only one specific repository, for an unrelated purpose.
3. Launch `copilot`, enable local sandboxing (`/experimental on` if needed, then `/sandbox enable`), leave "Authenticate gh" at its default (on).
4. Inside the Copilot CLI session, ask the agent to run `gh repo list <org> --visibility private` or inspect `$GH_TOKEN`.
5. Observe that the token exported into the sandbox matches the old, narrowly-scoped fine-grained PAT from step 2 — not the active OAuth session from step 1 — with no indication in the CLI of which credential was selected or why.

### Additional context

- `/env` and `/sandbox` do not currently surface which specific token/account was selected for `GH_TOKEN` in the sandbox, making this essentially undiagnosable without manual, external investigation (comparing token prefixes, checking org "Active tokens" pages, etc.).
- Docs reference (`Configuring local sandbox settings` → Auth tab): "Authenticate gh: Export GH_TOKEN so that GitHub CLI ... works inside the sandbox without reaching its stored credentials (configuration directory or OS keychain), which the sandbox blocks." This explains *that* a substitute token is exported, but not how that substitute is selected when multiple credentials (OAuth session, GitHub App ghu_ token, cached fine-grained PATs) exist on the host.
- Related open issues that touch on adjacent auth-scoping concerns: #1460 (no scoped-auth workflow vs `gh auth login`), #953 (default OAuth grants excessive scope).

### Suggested improvement

- Add a way to inspect, from within a session (e.g. `/sandbox` Auth tab or `/env`), exactly which token/account is currently selected for sandboxed `gh`/git operations, including its origin (active `gh auth status` session vs. a manually-set `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` env var vs. some other cached credential) and its repository scope.
- Consider making the sandboxed `GH_TOKEN` follow the currently active `gh auth status` account by default, rather than silently preferring a possibly-stale `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` env var or other cached credential.

issues.title: MCP OAuth: Entra rejects 127.0.0.1 callback (AADSTS50011); no localhost host override found

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Remote HTTP MCP servers protected by Microsoft Entra ID fail to authenticate in Copilot CLI 1.0.91 with `AADSTS50011`. The authorization request uses a loopback callback such as `http://127.0.0.1:54335/`, with a different port on subsequent attempts.

With four affected MCP servers enabled, starting Copilot opens four browser tabs that fail with this error. Authentication does not complete, and the prompts recur on subsequent startups.

Our identity support team suggested configuring the client to use `localhost` instead of `127.0.0.1`, as they had encountered a similar issue with another CLI. I could not find a supported callback-host setting in Copilot.

This is an interoperability report, not a claim that using `127.0.0.1` or ephemeral ports violates OAuth. The server-side registration may also need changes.

### Affected version

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.91.
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a remote HTTP MCP server protected by Entra ID, whose app registration rejects the callback below. Sanitized configuration:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "example-entra-mcp": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

   `mcp.example.com` is a placeholder, not a public reproducer.
2. Start Copilot and allow the MCP authentication flow to open the browser.
3. The browser shows an error like this (application ID redacted):

   ```text
   AADSTS50011: The redirect URI 'http://127.0.0.1:54335/' specified in the
   request does not match the redirect URIs configured for the application
   '<application-id>'.
   ```

4. Start Copilot again. Authentication is attempted again with another loopback port and fails.

### Expected behavior

Provide a supported way to select `localhost` as the MCP OAuth callback hostname, consistently for the authorization request and token exchange, while keeping the listener loopback-only and retaining PKCE/state validation.

Alternatively, document a supported configuration or workaround for Entra-backed MCP servers requiring a compatible registered callback. It would also help to avoid repeatedly opening failed authentication tabs on startup without an explicit retry.

### Additional context

- OS: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Four private HTTP MCP servers exhibit the symptom; other configured MCP servers authenticate successfully.
- Checked `copilot help config`, `copilot help environment`, and `copilot mcp add --help`: no callback-host override found.
- The installed SDK/API schema exposes `auth.redirectPort` for a fixed callback port, but no callback-host field. A fixed port does not itself change the hostname.
- Microsoft's [redirect URI guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reply-url#localhost-exceptions) describes port-insensitive matching for `localhost` and separately discusses registering HTTP `127.0.0.1` callbacks. Registering `localhost` should not be assumed to match a `127.0.0.1` request.
- We have **not** tested a host override or confirmed that switching to `localhost` alone resolves this environment. We also have not independently inspected the Entra app registrations.
- Related: #4968 (closed after a CIMD redirect-port fix) and #1965 (Power BI re-authentication/redirect mismatch). This report concerns an Entra app-registration rejection on initial authentication and the lack of a callback-host override, rather than asserting the CIMD fix regressed.

Internal endpoints, tenant/application identifiers, and OAuth credentials are intentionally omitted.

issues.title: Copilot CLI grep compaction corrupts filenames and line numbers, and merges distinct files

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The built-in rg tool returns incorrect filenames and line numbers when output compaction interprets numeric filename suffixes or directory components as grep field delimiters. Standalone ripgrep output launched in bash is correct.

This can misattribute search results during debugging. Distinct files can also be merged into one reported file.

### Affected version

1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Create a directory whose absolute path reaches at least 64 characters, then place the attached rg-compactor-repro.log-3.txt file into that directory and rename it to rg-compactor-repro.log-3 (strip the '.txt', I couldn't attach the file without adding that to the end). Start a new copilot session and tell it :

```
Validate a suspected Copilot CLI grep-output compaction bug using this existing file:
/path/to/rg-compactor-repro.log-3

Do not modify the file. Use its full absolute path: output length affects whether compaction activates. The file contains 20 identical RG_REPRO lines.

Perform these checks using the built-in rg tool (functions.rg), NOT shell ripgrep or another search tool:

1. Control: pattern="RG_REPRO", paths="<file_path>, output_mode="content", head_limit=19, -n=true.
2. Reproduction: use exactly the same arguments, except head_limit=20.

Then independently obtain the correct baseline using Bash:
rg -H -n -m 20 RG_REPRO <file_path>

Compare the literal tool responses, without silently correcting filenames or line numbers.

On the affected CLI 1.0.105 build, the control retains the filename ending in .log-3 and actual line numbers 1 through 19. The reproduction instead groups results under rg-compactor-repro.log (losing -3), gives every result apparent line number 3, and moves the real line number into the text, such as "3: 1:RG_REPRO". The Bash baseline retains .log-3 and actual line numbers 1 through 20.

Report REPRODUCED only if that corruption is observed. Otherwise report NOT REPRODUCED or INCONCLUSIVE and explain the actual results. Merely grouping results is not a failure if filenames and line numbers remain correct. Preserve the tool responses as evidence; do not assume a different CLI version has the same defect.
```

Ensure you update /path/to to whatever path you actually used. 

What this test does it demonstrate that the built in rg tool is returning corrupt/different results than using ripgrep directly in bash.

Additional confirmed impact

• Numeric directory components can trigger the same corruption.
• Disabling line-number output still produces fabricated line numbers.
• Two files,  plain.log  and  plain.log-3 , containing 32 matching lines each, are incorrectly reported as 64 matches across one file.

### Expected behavior

built in rg tool shouldn't produce corrupt results pointing to non-existent files.

### Additional context

_No response_
