issues.title: userPromptSubmitted: only the last plugin's additionalContext reaches the model (sessionStart was fixed in #3589)

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When two or more plugins each return `additionalContext` from a `userPromptSubmitted` hook, only the text of the plugin that is loaded **last** reaches the model. The other plugins' hooks do run, but their text is dropped silently: it does not appear anywhere in the session's `events.jsonl`.

This is the same last-writer-wins behaviour that #3589 reported for `sessionStart`/`subagentStart`, which was fixed in v1.0.88 ("Session and subagent start hooks combine successful additional-context contributions within the hook-output limit"). `userPromptSubmitted` still behaves the old way.

What I observed, with two minimal plugins `alpha` and `beta` (one run per case):

| plugin order (`--plugin-dir`) | `sessionStart` context injected | `userPromptSubmitted` context injected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| alpha, beta | alpha **and** beta (combined) | **beta only** |
| beta, alpha | alpha **and** beta (combined) | **alpha only** |
| alpha, beta — beta's hook prints nothing | — | alpha |
| alpha, beta — beta's hook prints `{}` | — | alpha |

So an empty answer does not override an earlier one, but a non-empty one replaces it instead of being added. A small log written by each hook confirms that both hooks ran in every case.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95 (`copilotVersion` in `events.jsonl`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create two plugins, each with a `hooks/hooks.json` that registers a `UserPromptSubmit` (and, for comparison, a `SessionStart`) command hook.
2. Each hook prints a different marker, e.g.
   `{"additionalContext": "Probe marker from alpha: COBALT", "hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit", "additionalContext": "Probe marker from alpha: COBALT"}}`
3. Run `copilot -p "Reply with every probe marker word given to you in this conversation's context, comma-separated." --plugin-dir ./alpha --plugin-dir ./beta`
4. Only the last plugin's `UserPromptSubmit` marker is reported, and only that one appears in `events.jsonl`. Swap the `--plugin-dir` order and the other one wins. Both `SessionStart` markers always appear.

### Expected behavior

`userPromptSubmitted` contributions from several hooks are combined, in execution order, the same way `sessionStart` contributions now are.

### Additional context

This matters for anyone who ships more than one plugin: today, two plugins that both add per-prompt context silently cancel each other out, and which one survives depends on load order.

issues.title: Resuming a session does not restore the custom agent (regression of #917)

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When a session is resumed, the custom agent it was started with is not restored.
Neither its `mcp-servers:` block nor its `tools:` allow-list is reapplied, so the
session silently continues as if no agent had been selected at all.

This is the behaviour reported in #917, which was closed on 2026-07-04.

It affects both ways of resuming:

- the `/resume` slash command inside a running process
- the `--resume=<id>` flag at startup, when `--agent` is not repeated

Passing `--agent <name>` together with `--resume` works correctly, so the agent
machinery itself is fine. What is missing is that the resume path does not
remember which agent the session belonged to.

### Affected version

Reproduced on 1.0.82-1, 1.0.81-11 and 1.0.80 alike, so this is not a regression
of the last few builds. The behaviour appears to have been present continuously,
which suggests the fix for #917 either did not cover this path or was lost some
time ago.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an agent `my-agent` that declares one MCP server and a `tools:`
   allow-list which does **not** include `github-mcp-server`:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: my-agent
   description: repro
   tools:
     - read
     - my-server/*
   mcp-servers:
     my-server:
       type: stdio
       command: npx
       args: ["-y", "@playwright/mcp@latest"]
       tools: ["*"]
   ---
   Repro agent.
   ```

2. Start it and note the connected servers:

   ```
   copilot --agent my-agent --log-level debug
   ```

3. Type `/resume` and pick any earlier session. Alternatively, exit and run
   `copilot --resume=<id>` without `--agent`.

4. Compare the connected servers.

### Expected behavior

The resumed session runs under the same agent as before: `my-server` connected,
`github-mcp-server` suppressed by the allow-list.

### Actual behavior

`my-server` is gone and `github-mcp-server` is present. The latter is the
clearest signal: it is filtered out by the agent's `tools:` allow-list during
normal operation, so its appearance proves the allow-list is no longer applied,
not merely the server block.

Measured on a real setup with 8 servers declared in the agent and 2 declared
globally in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:

| how the session was resumed | `--agent` passed | servers connected |
|---|---|---|
| `/resume` slash command (interactive) | n/a | 4 |
| `--resume=<id>` | no | 4 |
| `--resume=<id>` | yes | 12 |

The 4 remaining servers are exactly the globally configured ones plus the
built-in and plugin servers. Everything contributed by the agent is lost.

Server counts were read from the `signature` field of the MCP reconcile entries
in the debug log, not from the model's own account of its tools.

This is not #2630: the two `--resume` runs above both used `--prompt`, and the
one that passed `--agent` connected all agent-declared servers correctly.

### Why this is worse than an inconvenience

The `tools:` allow-list is a safety boundary, not a convenience feature. In a
setup where it restricts a business system to read-only operations, the write
tools of that same server become available again after a resume, silently, with
no indication to the user. Anyone relying on an allow-list to keep an agent
inside a safe subset of tools loses that guarantee on resume.

There is also a visible inconsistency: the CLI prints a resume hint after every
run which omits the agent:

```
Resume     copilot --resume=<id>
```

Following the CLI's own suggestion reproduces the bug.

### Possible fix

Persist the agent name in the session record and reapply it on the resume path,
the same way #917 was addressed. Where the agent cannot be resolved (renamed or
deleted), warn instead of silently falling back to no agent.

### Workaround

Always repeat the agent when resuming:

```
copilot --agent my-agent --resume
```

`--resume` without a value opens the same session picker as the slash command,
so this keeps the normal workflow. The slash command has no equivalent
workaround.

issues.title: includeCoAuthoredBy: false is not inherited by task subagents; their commits still get the Co-authored-by trailer

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`includeCoAuthoredBy: false` in `~/.copilot/settings.json` is respected by the interactive session, but **is not inherited by `task`-tool subagents**. Commits created by subagents still get the `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>` trailer.

This is a follow-up to #3181, which added the opt-out. The setting works for the main session — it just doesn't reach spawned subagents.

Beyond silently ignoring the setting, subagents appear to be *told* the trailer is mandatory. During a plan-execution run, one subagent amended an otherwise-finished commit purely to add it, and logged:

> `note: amended cleanup commit to <sha> to add the required Co-authored-by trailer; no file changes.`

That "required" wording suggests the subagent's system prompt carries the coauthor instruction unconditionally, rather than gated on `coauthorEnabled`.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Set the opt-out in `~/.copilot/settings.json`:
   ```json
   { "includeCoAuthoredBy": false }
   ```
2. Start an interactive session in a git repo.
3. Ask the main session to make a commit directly (e.g. via a shell `git commit`). ✅ No trailer — setting respected.
4. Now delegate committing work to a subagent, e.g. via the `task` tool with `agent_type: "general-purpose"`, instructing it to implement a change, commit it, and stop.
5. Inspect the resulting commit:
   ```
   git log -1 --format='%b'
   ```
6. ❌ The message contains `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`.

In my case 8/8 commits created by subagents carried the trailer, while every commit made directly from the main session had none. Stripping them across the branch required:

```
git rebase <base> --exec "git log -1 --pretty=%B | grep -v '^Co-authored-by:' | git commit --amend --quiet -F -"
```

### Expected behavior

`includeCoAuthoredBy: false` should apply to **all** commits produced by the CLI, including those created by subagents — the setting reads as global, not session-scoped.

### Additional context

- The setting key itself is correct and current: `app.js` computes `coauthorEnabled: T.includeCoAuthoredBy !== false`, and `includeCoAuthoredBy?: boolean` is declared in `sdk/index.d.ts`. (The changelog entry for #3181 calls it `include_coauthor`, which no longer matches the settings.json key — minor doc drift, possibly worth fixing too.)
- Ruled out as causes in my repo: no git hooks, `core.hooksPath` unset, and `commit.template` pointed at an empty file. Raw `git commit` from the main session never adds the trailer.
- `settings.json` had `includeCoAuthoredBy: false` for ~2 weeks before the affected session, so this isn't a case of the setting being applied late.
- Environment: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh, iTerm2/agterm.

issues.title: Task tool does not recognize new agents added after conversation start (hot-reload gap)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

When a new `.agent.md` file is added to `.github/agents/` during an active conversation, the `task` tool's `agent_type` enum does not update - even after `session.agent.reload` successfully rescans the disk and the server's agent registry is refreshed. Users must start a new conversation (`/clear`) for the task tool to recognize newly added agents.

## Expected Behavior

After `session.agent.reload` is triggered (via extension or other mechanism), the `task` tool should recognize newly loaded agents within the same conversation - no restart required.

## Actual Behavior

The task tool captures its agent list once in a closure at creation time and never refreshes it. Even though `session.agent.reload` RPC exists, works, and the server emits `session.custom_agents_updated` event, the task tool's closure remains stale.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Start a Copilot CLI conversation in a repo with `.github/agents/`
2. Create a new agent file: `.github/agents/my-new-agent.agent.md`
3. Trigger reload (via extension calling `session.agent.reload` RPC, or manually)
4. Try to use `task` tool with `agent_type: "my-new-agent"` - fails validation
5. Run `/clear` and try again - now it works

## Root Cause

`taskTool.ts` builds the `allAgentNames` array in a closure when the tool is first created. There is no mechanism to rebuild this closure when agents change. The `refreshTools` path only handles `externalToolsVersion` changes (extension tools), not agent list mutations.

## Proposed Fix

When `session.custom_agents_updated` is emitted (after reload), the task tool's agent enum should be refreshed. Options:

1. **Lazy validation** - Instead of validating against a static enum, query the current agent registry at invocation time
2. **Tool rebuild** - Re-create the task tool when agents change, similar to how `refreshTools` handles extension tool changes
3. **Event subscription** - Have the task tool subscribe to `session.custom_agents_updated` and update its internal list

Option 1 (lazy validation) is simplest and most resilient.

## Additional Context

- `session.agent.reload` is defined in the schema with stability: experimental
- Node SDK 1.0.10 does not expose `agent.reload()` in typed client - must use raw `connection.sendRequest`
- Extensions CAN trigger reload successfully; the gap is only in the task tool's stale closure
- This blocks agent hot-reload workflows where developers iterate without restarting conversations

## Environment

- Copilot CLI (latest as of 2025-07)
- @github/copilot SDK 1.0.10
- Windows 11

issues.title: MCP Sampling is Always Declined in Non-Interactive Mode

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

MCP sampling (#1748) works in interactive mode, but the same MCP server reaches a denied permissions prompt in `-p` non-interactive mode, even when `--allow-all` is enabled.

With `--allow-all`, the CLI does invoke the MCP tool in `-p` mode. The tool starts, the server receives `CallToolRequest`, and then the sampling call back into the CLI fails with `Method not found`.

The same server, config, CLI version, and prompts work in interactive mode. In that control case, the CLI logs `Received sampling request from sampling-repro` and the tool returns successfully.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.31

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


### 1. Create a minimal FastMCP server that uses sampling

**`sampling_server.py`**
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal FastMCP server that exercises sampling/createMessage."""

from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context, FastMCP
from mcp.types import SamplingMessage, TextContent


mcp = FastMCP("sampling-repro")


async def sample_text(ctx: Context, prompt: str, system_prompt: str) -> str:
    result = await ctx.session.create_message(
        messages=[
            SamplingMessage(
                role="user",
                content=TextContent(type="text", text=prompt),
            )
        ],
        max_tokens=256,
        system_prompt=system_prompt,
    )

    parts = getattr(result, "content", None)
    if isinstance(parts, list):
        text = "".join(
            part.text for part in parts if getattr(part, "type", None) == "text"
        ).strip()
        if text:
            return text

    text = getattr(getattr(result, "content", None), "text", None)
    if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip():
        return text.strip()

    raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected sampling response: {result!r}")


@mcp.tool()
async def summarize(text: str, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Summarize the given text in one sentence."""
    summary = await sample_text(
        ctx,
        prompt=f"Summarize in exactly one sentence:\n\n{text}",
        system_prompt="You are a concise summarizer. Reply with exactly one sentence.",
    )
    return f"Summary: {summary}"


@mcp.tool()
async def duplicate(text: str, ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Repeat the given text exactly twice with a separator."""
    repeated = await sample_text(
        ctx,
        prompt=(
            "Repeat the following text exactly twice, separated by ' | ', and add no "
            f"other words:\n\n{text}"
        ),
        system_prompt="Return only the duplicated text.",
    )
    return repeated


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
```

### 2. Create a minimal MCP config file

**`mcp-config.json`**
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sampling-repro": {
      "command": "/path/to/python3",
      "args": [
        "/path/to/sampling_server.py"
      ],
      "env": {}
    }
  }
}
```

### 3. Run the same prompts in `-p` mode

**Summarize example**
```bash
copilot \
  --log-level=all \
  --log-dir /path/to/logs \
  --additional-mcp-config @/path/to/mcp-config.json \
  --disable-builtin-mcps \
  --no-custom-instructions \
  --allow-all \
  -p "Use the summarize tool from the sampling-repro MCP server exactly once to summarize this text: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This sentence contains every letter of the alphabet and is often used for typing practice.'"
```

**Duplication example**
```bash
copilot \
  --log-level=all \
  --log-dir /path/to/logs \
  --additional-mcp-config @/path/to/mcp-config.json \
  --disable-builtin-mcps \
  --no-custom-instructions \
  --allow-all \
  -p "Use the duplicate tool from the sampling-repro MCP server exactly once with this text: 'alpha beta'"
```

### 4. Check the outputs

Both non-interactive runs fail the same way:

```text
✗ summarize (MCP: sampling-repro) · text: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This senten…
  └ MCP server 'sampling-repro': Error executing tool summarize: Method not found
```

```text
✗ duplicate (MCP: sampling-repro) · text: "alpha beta"
  └ MCP server 'sampling-repro': Error executing tool duplicate: Method not found
```

Redacted log excerpt from the `-p` summarize run:

```text
[DEBUG] Tool calls count: 2
[ERROR] [mcp server sampling-repro stderr] ... Processing request of type CallToolRequest
[DEBUG] Tool invocation result: Error executing tool summarize: Method not found
```

### Expected behavior

If `--allow-all` is set, `sampling/createMessage` should work in `-p` mode the same way it works in interactive mode.

The non-interactive session cannot show approval prompts, but `--allow-all` already bypasses tool, path, and URL confirmations. Once the tool call is allowed to run, the CLI should expose the sampling handler to the MCP server instead of returning `Method not found`.

### Control: interactive mode works

Run the same prompts in interactive mode:

```bash
copilot \
  --log-level=all \
  --log-dir /path/to/logs \
  --additional-mcp-config @/path/to/mcp-config.json \
  --disable-builtin-mcps \
  --no-custom-instructions \
  --allow-all \
  -i "Use the duplicate tool from the sampling-repro MCP server exactly once with this text: 'alpha beta'"
```

```bash
copilot \
  --log-level=all \
  --log-dir /path/to/logs \
  --additional-mcp-config @/path/to/mcp-config.json \
  --disable-builtin-mcps \
  --no-custom-instructions \
  --allow-all \
  -i "Use the summarize tool from the sampling-repro MCP server exactly once to summarize this text: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This sentence contains every letter of the alphabet and is often used for typing practice.'"
```

These succeed with the same server and config:

```text
duplicate (MCP: sampling-repro) · text: "alpha beta"
  └ {"result":"alpha beta | alpha beta"}
```

```text
summarize (MCP: sampling-repro) · text: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This sentence c…"
  └ {"result":"Summary: \"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog\" is a pangram containing every letter of the alphabet and is commonly used for typing practice."}
```

### Expected behavior

MCP sampling should be allowed through non-interactive sessions when using `-p` and `--allow-all`.

### Additional context

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Process log (redacted) | [process-1776747687370-23478-redacted.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26940309/process-1776747687370-23478-redacted.log) |
| CLI version | GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.31 |

issues.title: [Bug] GPT-6.2 compaction fails with "Compaction summary did not match the required template"

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
### Description

Compaction fails for `gpt-6.2-sol` with:

```
compaction.failed: Compaction summary did not match the required template
```

The model does return text: the failed compaction records show 2,787-3,133 output tokens. The returned text just does not contain a line matching any of the `SUMMARY_TEMPLATE` headings.

This reproduces on a brand-new session with two short prompts and no model switch, so it is not an old checkpoint or a model-switch issue. Setting `agents.compaction.model` to `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max` makes compaction succeed while the chat model stays `gpt-6.2-sol`.

### Environment

- OpenCode 2.3.0 (bundled with OpenChamber 2.7.2), Windows 11.
- Model `gpt-6.2-sol`, variant `xhigh`.
- Provider configured with `package: aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai` and a Responses-compatible `baseURL`.
- No `settings.compaction` override.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new session with `gpt-6.2-sol` (`xhigh`).
2. Send two short prompts that need no tools, for example "Reply OK only" and "Reply DONE only".
3. Trigger compaction with `/compact` or `POST /api/session/{id}/compact`.
4. Compaction fails with the template error.

### What I checked

- v2.3.0 and v2.3.2 `packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts` are identical in the relevant places: `SUMMARY_TEMPLATE`, `filled()`, `NUDGE`, and the error string are unchanged. The 2.3.2 `/responses/compact` change is about the cached prefix, not template validation.
- Native compaction requires `context.model.compaction?.type === "native"` and a route with a compact endpoint. `aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai` routes have `compact: undefined`, so setting `settings.compaction.type: "native"` fails at model load with `UnsupportedCompactionError`.
- On this provider, `/responses/compact` returns 400 `model_retired` for `gpt-6.2-sol`; the error references a different model, `gpt-5.5`. So the native path cannot be used here.
- A direct request with the same `SUMMARY_TEMPLATE` prompt, the build agent's system prompt, a short history, and no tools returns the expected `## Objective` headings. So the model can follow the template in a clean request; the failure seems specific to the compaction request context, such as the session tools or the long history.

### Related

- #57828: `SUMMARY_TEMPLATE` is English-only and `filled()` only accepts English headings; a localized heading fails.
- #53242 and #53370: the compaction request still exposes session tools; the open PR sets `toolChoice: "none"`.
- #63439: commentary phase text from Responses models can be kept in the summary.

Is this a known issue? Is there a recommended configuration for GPT-6.2 on a Responses-compatible provider, or should compaction disable tool calls and/or use a dedicated compaction system prompt?

issues.title: desktop: session tabs are lost after a PC reboot (strip pruned before the bundled server registers)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/desktop
labels.description: Desktop app

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Description

After a **cold reboot of Windows**, the Desktop app opens with an empty session tab strip. The sessions themselves are intact (they are in the sidebar / session search), and pulling the app apart shows the tab state was written to disk — so this is not "state never saved": the strip is pruned on startup and the pruned (empty) list is written back, so the tabs never return.

The strip survives a normal "quit + relaunch" of the app. It is lost on a real machine reboot, which is also the path an auto-update takes (`background service starting { reason: 'missing' }`).

## Plugins

None (no plugins configured in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`).

## OpenCode version

2.3.2, desktop, windows x64 (channel `latest`). Also seen on 2.3.0 before the update.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In Desktop, open several sessions as tabs.
2. Reboot Windows (cold boot).
3. Start Desktop.
4. The session tab strip is empty; "Recently closed" still contains older entries.

## Screenshot

N/A (tab strip is simply empty; no error is shown).

## Operating System

Windows 11 10.0.26300.9974

## Terminal

Desktop app, no terminal.

## Additional context

The tab strip is persisted per window in the desktop's `drafts.sqlite` (`%APPDATA%/ai.opencode.desktop/drafts.sqlite`, table `state`):

- `opencode.window.<id>.dat | tabs` (JSON array of `{type:"session", server:"sidecar", sessionId}`)
- `opencode.window.<id>.dat | tabs.info`, `tabs.recent`, `tabs.panes`, `tabs.closed`

Right after a good start these keys hold a full strip (28 entries in my case, updated seconds after launch), so the write path works.

The startup timing looks like the trigger. From `logs/<timestamp>/main.log` (`<user>` and paths redacted):

```
[09:56:54.224] (main) main window visible { window: '...' }
[09:56:54.227] (main) starting v2 background service
[09:57:01.247] (main) v2 CLI background service starting { reason: 'missing' }
[09:57:02.827] (main) v2 CLI background service ready { version: '2.3.0', url: 'http://127.0.0.1:28894' }
```

and from `renderer.log` of the same launch:

```
[09:57:05.003] [warn] [server-request-queue] server thrashing detected [object Object]
[09:57:05.897] [debug] [tabs] update persisted session info [object Object]
[09:58:04.688] [warn] [server-request-queue] server thrashing detected [object Object]
```

In the renderer, the strip is filtered against the currently known servers and the filtered array is written back immediately:

```ts
M(() => {
  if (!tabsReady() || !infoReady() || !serversReady()) return
  const keys = knownServerKeys()               // servers.list + plugin servers
  const next = tabs.filter((tab) => keys.has(tab.server))
  if (next.length !== tabs.length) for (const tab of tabs) if (!keys.has(tab.server)) { dropInfo(tab); dropPanes(tab) }
  setTabs(() => next)                          // persisted right away
})
```

`server.list` in `opencode.global.dat` is persisted as `[]` — the bundled `sidecar` server is only added at runtime when the background service registers. So if `serversReady()` becomes true before the sidecar is registered (a cold boot, where the service is `missing` and needs ~8 s, is exactly that window), every tab is dropped and an empty array is persisted. When the sidecar appears a moment later there is nothing left to restore.

There is a second, related path: tabs whose session cannot be resolved are removed for good (the `abandon` event), which is the same symptom when the session lookup races the server start.

"Recently closed" (`tabs.closed`) is kept separately, so the only recovery is reopening tabs from there by hand.

Happy to test a build that waits for the bundled server (or that never prunes servers it has not seen yet) before rewriting the strip.

issues.title: browser: intermittent `ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED` on some hosts

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/desktop
labels.description: Desktop app

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

The in-app browser intermittently fails to load specific hosts with `ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED (-111)`. No proxy is configured on the machine. Failures are host-specific and inconsistent between runs: a host that loads can fail minutes later, while static content pages keep working.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.7
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26100 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: terminal environment variables are not set
- Shell: cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. Open the in-app browser to a plain content page (`https://example.com/`) - loads.
2. Navigate the same tab to a webmail sign-in host - fails with `ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED (-111)`.
3. Open 5-6 tabs at once to mixed hosts - some fail, some succeed.
4. Retry the failing hosts later in the same session - some now succeed, others keep failing.

## Expected Behavior

Any publicly reachable HTTPS host loads, or fails with an ordinary DNS/TLS error.

## Actual Behavior

`ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED (-111)`, which Chromium emits for a failed proxy `CONNECT` - but there is no proxy configured:

- WinHTTP: `Direct access (no proxy server)`
- WinINET `ProxyEnable`: `0`
- env: only `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost,::1`
- Chromium process command line: no `--proxy-server`

## Additional Context

Observed host matrix in one session:

| Host | Result |
|---|---|
| control content site | pass (failed once earlier, passed later) |
| webmail provider A sign-in | fail |
| webmail provider B portal | passed on first visit, failed on later attempts |
| provider C apex domain | pass |
| provider C `login.` subdomain (same apex) | fail |

Notes:

- Apex/static pages of one provider load while its `login.` subdomain fails, which points away from DNS and toward the browser's network bridge.
- Two sign-in flows loaded successfully early in the session, then began failing.
- Reading public content pages in the same browser continued to work throughout.
- Workaround: perform auth flows in a regular browser.

Frequency: intermittent, not tied to a single site. Reproduces within a few navigation attempts.

issues.title: shell: Store PowerShell fails with 0xC0070005 in Windows pipe mode

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/service
labels.description: Background service and server

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
### Description

### Description

After updating OpenCode from 2.2.7 to 2.3.0 on Windows, shell tool calls using Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 fail before executing even a one-line command:

```text
failed to spawn C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\pwsh.EXE:
OS Error -1073283067 (FormatMessageW() returned error 317) (os error -1073283067)
```

`-1073283067` is `0xC0070005`. Expected: the command executes and returns its output. Actual: process creation fails, in both a project directory and a separate temporary directory.

#### Isolated Win32 reproduction

A standalone C# P/Invoke probe, independent of OpenCode/plugins, called `CreateProcessW` for the same packaged executable with `-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "exit 0"` and `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Changing only the job attachment strategy produced:

| Creation strategy | Store PowerShell 7.7 | Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No explicit job attribute | Success, exit 0 | Success, exit 0 |
| `STARTUPINFOEXW` + `EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT` + `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` containing one newly created unnamed job | Fails: `0xC0070005` | Success, exit 0 |
| Normal creation, then `AssignProcessToJobObject` | Success, assignment succeeds, exit 0 | Success, exit 0 |

Three additional consecutive rounds reproduced the same Store executable results. Normal `ProcessStartInfo` creation also succeeds for both the real packaged EXE and its app-execution aliases. `Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell` reports Status=Ok and IsPartiallyStaged=False.

At the failing timestamps, **Microsoft-Windows-AppModel-Runtime/Admin** records:

- Event 212, `0x80070005`: cannot add the process to the package's Desktop AppX container.
- Event 208, `0x80070005`: cannot create the package process while configuring its runtime, `[FinishPackageActivation]`.

#### Relevant implementation

The running shell process is launched through `opencode-pty` **0.5.2**, in pipe mode. [The current Windows pipe implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.0/packages/process-daemon/src/service/pipe/windows.rs) supplies `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` during `CreateProcessW`.

Its jobless retry only accepts raw `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (`5`); the packaged EXE returns `0xC0070005`, so that retry is skipped. The standalone probe returns `5` when given the app-execution alias instead of the real packaged path. This error-code distinction appears relevant to the missed fallback.

The [2.2.7 shell service](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.7/packages/core/src/shell.ts) directly spawned commands; [2.3.0](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.3.0/packages/core/src/shell.ts) delegates local commands to the process daemon. Related introduction: #63196; follow-up: #63346. The previous 2.2.7 binary was not rerun during this diagnosis, so the version boundary is based on observed upgrade history and source comparison, not a binary bisect.

This differs from closed #62512: that issue returned exit 0 with empty output through the Store alias; this one fails to create the real packaged process.

Workaround verified: explicitly selecting Windows PowerShell 5.1 restores shell execution. MSI/ZIP PowerShell 7 was not installed or tested. No WindowsApps ACL changes or package repairs were made.

### Plugins

`@tarquinen/opencode-dcp@latest`, `oh-my-opencode-slim`. OpenCode itself was not retested with plugins disabled; the standalone Win32 probe has no plugin dependency.

### OpenCode version

`opencode v2.3.0`, latest/release channel, installed through Scoop; managed `serve --service` process. Process daemon: `opencode-pty` 0.5.2.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, use Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 (observed package: `Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`), with OpenCode 2.3.0 selecting that shell.
2. Ask the shell tool to run `Write-Output 'probe'`.
3. Observe the spawn failure above, before any command output. Changing the working directory does not help.
4. For an API-level comparison, create that same EXE with and without `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST`, as described in the table.

### Operating System

Windows x64, `Windows_NT 10.0.26300` (`[Environment]::OSVersion`: `10.0.26300.0`). Store PowerShell reports 7.7.0. System Windows PowerShell reports 5.1.26100.9818.

### Terminal

Exact frontend terminal application unavailable. Shell-tool environment has `TERM=xterm-256color` (injected by OpenCode); `TERM_PROGRAM`, `COLORTERM`, and `WT_SESSION` are unset. `ComSpec=C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`.


### Plugins

_No response_

### OpenCode version

2.3.0

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

_No response_

### Terminal

_No response_

### Description

On the desktop app, the default **One list** vertical sidebar (`general.sidebarOrganize = "list"`) has no way to pin a session: there is no **Pin** item in the row menu, and no **Pinned** section is rendered. Pinning only exists after switching to **Projects** or **Recent**, so the default sidebar mode cannot keep sessions at the top at all. Sessions pinned in Projects/Recent are also not shown while One list is selected.

## Expected Behavior

**One list** should offer the same **Pin/Unpin** session action and **Pinned** group as **Projects** and **Recent**.

## Actual Behavior

**One list** renders the plain tab strip (`TitlebarTabStrip`) without `tabMenu` or `leading`, so there is no Pin menu item and no Pinned section.

## Additional Context

Source references (`packages/app/src` on `dev`):

- `shell/titlebar/titlebar.tsx`: `sidebarOrganize === "list"` falls through to `verticalTabStrip`, called without `grouped`, so `tabMenu`/`leading` are `undefined`.
- `shell/titlebar/sidebar-organized.tsx`: passes `PinMuteMenuItems` as `menuItems` and renders `createPinnedSessions` (the Pinned group).
- `shell/titlebar/sidebar-customized.tsx`: renders `ProjectSessionRow` without `menuItems`, so the new **Customize** mode also has no pin action.

@tarquinen/opencode-dcp, -opencode.fork-notice

2.3.2 (desktop app OpenCode.app 2.3.2, ai.opencode.desktop)

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the desktop app, open Settings → "Organize vertical sidebar" and choose **One list** (this is the default).

issues.title: core: concurrent first start on a new opencode.db fails with "database is locked" / CREATE TABLE error
issues.body:
When two processes create a new `opencode.db` at the same time, one or both die at boot. The bootstrap lock is an in-process semaphore, so it does not serialize across processes.

**Version:** 2.0.24, macOS arm64

**Repro** (new `$R` each run):
```sh
for w in a b; do
  ( exec 0< <(sleep 15)
    XDG_DATA_HOME=$R/dt XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$R/$w/cfg XDG_STATE_HOME=$R/$w/st OPENCODE_PASSWORD=x \
      opencode serve --stdio --port 0 >$R/$w.out 2>$R/$w.err ) &
done
```
In 6 of 8 runs at least one server failed: `SQLiteError: database is locked` or `Failed query: CREATE TABLE ...`.

**Expected:** both start. **Actual:** the loser exits (`orDie`).

**Source:** `packages/core/src/database/database.ts:49,57-64`

**Fix:** run the bootstrap inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and re-check for the session table, or use a lock file next to the DB.

issues.title: session: apply per-item model and agent selection when a queued prompt is delivered

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
### Description

Thank you for your continued work on OpenCode! Currently, when queuing follow-up prompts (`delivery: "queue"`) while a session is busy, there is no way to bind a specific model (or agent/variant) to an individual queued item and have the session automatically switch to that model only when the queued item is promoted and delivered.

Because model and agent selection only exist as mutable session-wide state (`session.model` and `session.agent`) that `SessionRunner` re-reads at every `step` boundary, both current client approaches have significant drawbacks:

#### Drawbacks of the Current Approach (Step & Turn Boundaries)

In `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts` (`advanceToStep` / `prepareContext`), a single turn often spans multiple steps (e.g., Step 1 calls a tool, Step 2 processes tool output, Step 3 continues generation or runs auto-compaction). At the start of **every step**, `prepareContext(sessionID)` calls `context.select(sessionID)` and `context.load(selected)`, which resolves the model from the session-global `session.model` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts`). Meanwhile, at mid-turn step boundaries (`!entering && continuing`), `SessionInbox.promote` only promotes `"steer"` items while `"queue"` items wait in `session_inbox` until all steps of the current turn finish.

Because there is no per-inbox-item model binding applied at promotion time, clients are forced into one of two broken behaviors:

1. **Calling `switchModel` immediately when queuing (current TUI behavior in `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx`):**
   - **Mid-turn step hijacking:** Mutating `session.model` (and `session.agent`) at queue admission takes effect on the very next `step` of the **currently running turn**. If Model A is on Step 1 (running a tool) and the user queues a follow-up with Model B, Step 2 and all remaining steps of Model A's turn immediately switch to Model B—even though the queued prompt is still waiting in `session_inbox`.
   - **Queue overwrite across multiple items:** If the user queues Prompt 1 with Model B and then queues Prompt 2 with Model C while the current turn is still running, `session.model` is overwritten with Model C before Prompt 1 is ever promoted, so Prompt 1 never runs with Model B.

2. **Skipping `switchModel` when queuing (current Web app behavior in `packages/app/src/composer/submit.ts`):**
   - **Ignored selection on promotion:** To avoid reconfiguring the remaining steps of the active turn, the Web app skips `applySelection` when `delivery === "queue"` and only records the chosen model in `metadata.model`. However, when the active turn finishes all its steps and `SessionInbox.promote` delivers the queued item to start a new turn (`step = 1`), nothing in `SessionInbox` or `SessionRunner` applies `metadata.model` to `session.model`. Consequently, `prepareContext` for `step = 1` of the new turn still resolves the old `session.model`, and the queued prompt executes all of its steps with the previous model.

3. **Why client-side coordination cannot solve this:**
   - Clients may close or disconnect immediately after submitting queued items. Even when connected, racing a client-initiated `switchModel` RPC against the server's internal `advanceToStep` / `SessionInbox.promote` transition cannot atomically target the boundary between the final `step` of the finishing turn and `step = 1` of the newly promoted queued prompt.

#### Expected Behavior

- All remaining steps (Step 2, Step 3, etc.) of the currently running turn continue using **Model A**.
- When the current turn finishes and the first queued prompt is promoted/delivered from `session_inbox`, the session atomically switches to **Model B** before `prepareContext` runs for `step = 1` of that new turn.
- When the second queued prompt is subsequently promoted/delivered, the session switches to **Model C** for `step = 1` of its turn.

#### Actual Behavior

- **Web App:** `switchModel` is skipped for queued prompts (`submit.ts`), and `SessionInbox.promote` does not apply `metadata.model`. The promoted turns start `step = 1` under **Model A** instead of switching to **Model B** / **Model C**.
- **TUI:** `switchModel` is called immediately at queue admission (`prompt/index.tsx`), causing the remaining steps (Step 2+) of the active turn to switch to the queued model prematurely, and causing later queued selections (**Model C**) to overwrite earlier ones (**Model B**) before they run.

#### Additional Context

- Persisting optional `model` (`providerID`, `id`, `variant`) and `agent` on `session_inbox` items—and applying them to the session atomically during `SessionInbox.promote` when a queued item is delivered (before `prepareContext` resolves the context for `step = 1`)—would allow the Web app, TUI, and SDK callers (see #48356) to isolate model selection per turn without corrupting in-flight steps.
- Note that PR #54779 previously implemented deferred `agent` and `model` selection on `Session.Inbox.UserPayload` and passed `opencode-agent` verification, but was automatically closed by the 1-month reaction cleanup bot, while PR #59290 currently only covers `agent` and does not include `model`.

### Plugins

@eficy/opencode2-plugin, @tencent/runmark-opencode-plugin, @yee94/opencode-profile@0.4.0, opencode-magpie-plugin, opencode2-wakatime

### OpenCode version

v2.3.2 (latest)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a multi-step prompt (e.g., one that invokes tools across multiple steps) in a session using **Model A**.
2. While Step 1 of **Model A** is still running, select **Model B** in the composer and submit a follow-up prompt with `delivery: "queue"`.
3. Optionally select **Model C** and queue a second follow-up prompt.
4. Observe the model used for the remaining steps (Step 2+) of the active turn and for `step = 1` of each queued prompt when promoted from `session_inbox`.

### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS Darwin 25.5.0 (arm64)

### Terminal

issues.title: models: catalog cache does not refresh; stale registry hides newly released models until the service is restarted

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/providers
labels.description: Providers and model lists

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

The model catalog is served from a cached registry that does not refresh on its own. On this machine the cache was **154.9 hours (6.5 days) old**, so `opencode models` (and the desktop model list) omitted models released that week. Nothing refreshed it until the background service was restarted manually.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.7
- OS: Darwin 24.2.0 arm64 (macOS)
- Terminal: xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest (desktop app + CLI, shared background service)
- Active plugins: none found

## Reproduction

1. Let `~/.cache/opencode/models.json` age (observed: `mtime` 154.9 h old).
2. Run `opencode models`, or open the desktop model selector.
3. Note that models published to models.dev / OpenRouter in the meantime are absent. In this case `openrouter/inclusionai/ling-3.2-flash:free`, released 3 days earlier, did not appear.
4. Delete the cache file:
   `rm ~/.cache/opencode/models.json && opencode models`
   **The file is not recreated and the list does not change** — the service is serving its own copy.
5. Restart the background service:
   `opencode service restart`
6. Run `opencode models` again — the new model now appears, and the catalog is current.

## Expected Behavior

Opening the app, or starting the background service, should refresh the model catalog (or refresh it on a short TTL). A catalog should not stay frozen for days while the machine is in daily use, and removing the cache file should force a refetch rather than silently fall back to the in-memory copy.

## Actual Behavior

- The catalog stays at the state it had when the service started; `mtime` on `~/.cache/opencode/models.json` is the only visible clue.
- Deleting the cache file does not invalidate the service's in-memory catalog, so a user cannot force a refresh without restarting the service.
- No warning is shown that the catalog is stale, so newly available models are invisible with no indication.

## Additional Context

- Restarting the service is the only reliable workaround found. It works, but it is not discoverable: `opencode models` reports success while serving a week-old list.
- Related, minor: `opencode models --verbose` errors with `Unrecognized flag: --verbose in command opencode models`. Not a blocker, but it was the invocation a script in our repo used to read the catalog, and the failure was silent enough that the script fell back to hardcoded model ids for weeks.
- Impact here: an agent-routing script selected models from memory instead of from the live registry, which put a paid model on a "free only" ladder and kept an unreliable model in rotation. A stale catalog is a correctness problem, not only a convenience one.

issues.body: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Restore Foreground Subagent Execution Since subagents are now forced to run in the background, the parent agent gets flooded with unnecessary status updates, repeated completion checks, and messages like "I'm waiting for subagent X to finish." This pollutes the parent agent's context, wastes tokens, and distracts it from the actual task. Please consider restoring the ability to choose between foreground (synchronous) and background (asynchronous) execution. Background execution is useful for parallel tasks, but synchronous execution is equally important when the parent agent needs the result immediately. Let the agent choose how to execute subagents instead of forcing every subagent to run in the background.

issues.title: Code Mode: model writes tool call markup as plain text — call is dropped and the step ends idle
issues.body:
## Summary

In Code Mode, the model intermittently writes its tool call as **plain
assistant text** (Anthropic-style `<invoke>` / `<parameter name="…">` markup)
instead of emitting a structured tool call. OpenCode does not parse or execute
that text: no `tool` part is created, the step finishes with `idle`, and the
intended tool call is silently lost. The session then stalls and only proceeds
when another turn is issued.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.32 (latest release, Oct 16 2026)
- OS: Linux 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Agent: `build`, Code Mode
- Provider/model: `opencode/big-pickle`, variant `default`
- Plugins: none (no `opencode.json` / `.opencode/opencode.json`)

## Reproduction

1. Run a long multi-step `build` task in Code Mode.
2. Observe the last assistant message of a step. Instead of a structured tool
   call it contains prose followed by raw call markup, and no `tool` part.

Concrete transcript from session `ses_ea9cd281cffe9pJbrBsyPQSpup` (read-only
query against `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`):

```text
10:50:33  assistant  [text, TOOL:grep:completed, TOOL:shell:completed]   <- real calls, fine
10:50:36  assistant  [text*MK*]                                          <- only text, NO tool part
10:50:39  idle                                                           <- step ends
10:52:03  user                                                            <- new turn needed to continue
```

The `text*MK*` message body looks like:

```text
Let me look at `get_deployed_stems` and `_refresh_deployed_flag` — this is the core of the bug.
<parameter name="path">/root/zorq-sigma-bridge/app/…
```

The read it asks for never runs in that step; the same read is repeated and
executed only in the following turn.

## Expected Behavior

The intended tool call should not be dropped. Either:

- parse the text-form call and execute it (a text fallback parser), or
- immediately re-prompt the model to emit a real tool call instead of ending
  the step and leaving the session idle,

and in all cases surface why the step ended.

## Actual Behavior

No `tool` part is created, the step ends with `idle`, the call is lost, and the
session needs an extra turn to move on — effectively stalling long agent runs.

Occurrences (text parts containing call markup, excluding transcripts where the
agent itself quotes the markup while discussing it):

| session | text-parts with markup | window |
|---|---|---|
| `ses_eaea51780ffex7kzsnKf1s1lak` | 7 | 19 Oct 23:02 |
| `ses_eaa3947b1ffeexwKdX3g4RKT3t` (fork of the above) | 36 | 19 Oct 23:02 → 20 Oct 01:04 |
| `ses_ea9cd281cffe9pJbrBsyPQSpup` (new session) | 6 | 20 Oct 10:40 → 10:54 |

9 other sessions on the same provider/model/version never produced it, so it
is intermittent and session-dependent.

## Additional Context

- **Prompt-level workarounds do not help.** A repo `AGENTS.md` rule was added
  that forbids emitting this markup (initially listing the forbidden tokens as
  examples, then rewritten to avoid mentioning them at all). The rules were
  removed from the instructions before the last reproduction: session
  `ses_ea9cd281…` was created at 01:05 on 20 Oct, after the instruction files
  were already clean, and still reproduced at 10:40–10:54. Its recorded
  instruction blob contains no markup tokens.
- **Not a skills/plugins issue.** All installed skill files were scanned for
  `<invoke` / `<parameter name=` / `antml:` / `function_calls` — no matches;
  no plugins are configured.
- The markup always appears in the **final** assistant message of a step,
  immediately before the `idle` message, and is interleaved with normal
  structured `tool` calls earlier in the same step.
- A separate issue in the same environment is a recurring
  `AI.Error: Rate limit exceeded` (`provider.quota`, `FreeUsageLimitError`) on
  the free tier; it is independent of the markup problem and is not
  contributing to the reports above.

## Related

- #43385 — model outputs function-call syntax as plain text (closed against 1.x, invitation to re-file for 2.0)
- #25644 — raw `<tool_calls>` markup in reasoning breaks tool calls
- #27871 — invalid tool arguments leave the session interrupted

issues.body: ### Description OpenCode 1.19.5 can exit with `database is locked` before answering ACP `initialize` when two processes open an already initialized database whose WAL needs recovery. This reproduces without OAR, login, or model prompts: 5 of 12 opens failed in six concurrent pairs. Serializing only spawn through the initialize response gave 0 of 12 failures with the same executable and WAL preparation. The native SQLite layer runs `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` before the database layer installs `busy_timeout = 5000`. In a failing strace, process A holds the WAL recovery write locks; process B gets EAGAIN on the writer/recovery lock bytes and closes the database immediately. Could the busy timeout be installed before that first pragma? Source: [sqlite.bun.ts nativeLayer](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/810c0eba1a7348036f8bdf61e6632d0c36c6876c/packages/core/src/database/sqlite.bun.ts), [database.ts](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/810c0eba1a7348036f8bdf61e6632d0c36c6876c/packages/core/src/database/database.ts). ### Plugins No user plugins; default plugins disabled. ### OpenCode version 1.19.5 (unmodified Linux x64 executable from opencode-ai). ### Steps to reproduce Use a disposable HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME, never a real account database. 1. Open one `opencode acp` process, send `initialize` and `session/new`, then close stdin and wait for exit. This initializes the schema. 2. Using Python sqlite3 on that fixture's `opencode/opencode.db`, disable WAL autocheckpoint, create an extra test table, insert a 64 MiB zeroblob, commit, then call `os._exit(0)`. This deliberately leaves committed WAL pages without a clean connection shutdown. 3. Start two `opencode acp` processes concurrently with the same environment. Send each `initialize` and then `session/new`; send no prompt. One may exit with code 1 and `database is locked` before initialize. 4. Repeat the WAL preparation before each pair. An ordinary warmed database without that preparation passed 60 opens in separate shared-directory, separate-directory and serial controls. The WAL preparation is a controlled trigger, not a claim that normal prompts write that test table. We also saw the same error in warmed-schema CI on Linux/macOS ([OAR #876](https://github.com/botiverse/oar/issues/876)); the exact failing operation in those CI logs is not known. Possibly related: #53879 (first start on a new database); this report is about recovery of an existing database's WAL. ### Screenshot Selected strace, times relative to the first listed lock (same database SHM file): ```text A +0.000000s F_WRLCK offset=120 len=1 -> 0 A +0.000267s F_WRLCK offset=121 len=2 -> 0 B +0.017573s F_WRLCK offset=120 len=1 -> EAGAIN B +0.017608s F_RDLCK offset=122 len=1 -> EAGAIN B +0.0188s closes database; subsequently exits 1 A +0.386s releases recovery lock ``` A separate experimental binary copy replacing only the redundant early WAL pragma with `busy_timeout=5000` passed 12/12 recovery opens; the later WAL pragma remained. This is a diagnostic counterfactual, not a built or released source fix. Reproduction script and selected results: https://github.com/botiverse/oar/tree/6d3410cc97a32c0118119964507075c96a832b41/experiments/opencode-database-lock ### Operating System Linux x64 (Ubuntu, exe.dev VM). ### Terminal Node.js 24.19.0 child_process pipes, no terminal UI. --- Agent Cindy wrote this for @xxchan through Stamp (grant cgr_0a427a0749428a5c521774a30edf08b7)

labels.name: type/bug

issues.body:
## Summary

After updating the OpenCode desktop app to 2.3.0 (which ran a large batch of database migrations on first launch), the projects panel only lists directories that were opened *after* the update. All other historical projects disappeared from the panel, even though their sessions are fully intact in the database. Inspection shows the migration backfilled `project` rows but left `project.name` NULL for every row and the `project_directory` mapping table completely empty.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0 (desktop app `@opencode-aidesktop`, embedded CLI `ai.opencode.desktop\cli\2.3.0-x64\opencode-cli.exe`)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Desktop app (TUI inside OpenCode.exe), plus Windows Terminal for CLI checks
- Shell: cmd.exe / PowerShell
- Install/channel: latest (desktop channel; a separate legacy npm `opencode` 1.18.31 also exists on PATH but is unrelated)
- Active plugins: oh-my-opencode-slim, opencode-acp@stable (fails to load on 2.3.0), opencode-goal-plugin

## Reproduction

1. Use OpenCode desktop with many pre-existing project directories (17 directories, 338 sessions accumulated over ~3 months).
2. Update the desktop app to 2.3.0. On first launch, the server runs a long series of database migrations (all logged as completed successfully).
3. Open the projects panel.
4. Only the 1–2 directories opened after the update appear; all other historical projects are gone from the list.

## Expected Behavior

The projects panel should continue listing all historical projects. Either the migration should backfill `project.name` and `project_directory` rows for pre-existing sessions, or the panel should aggregate project entries from `session.directory` values.

## Actual Behavior

- The projects panel shows only directories opened after the update (a project reappears once you start opencode inside that directory again).
- Database state after migration (read-only inspection of `opencode.db`):
  - `project`: 18 rows (17 directory-derived + `global`); `time_created` all stamped at the migration moment (batch backfill), `time_active` preserved from original sessions — but `name` is NULL on every row.
  - `project_directory`: 0 rows.
  - `session` / `session_v2`: 338 / 343 rows, `directory` and `project_id` intact — data is not lost, only the project listing is broken.
- Sessions are still reachable via `opencode session list` and by launching from the original directory, which confirms this is a listing/migration issue, not data loss.

## Additional Context

- Migration log excerpt (all migrations succeeded, no errors): dozens of `database migration completed` entries between `20260805200742_import_legacy_credentials` and `20261030054400_job`.
- Project directories contain non-ASCII (Chinese) path segments on this machine, in case encoding is relevant to the directory-mapping backfill.
- Workaround: start opencode from each historical project directory once — the project then reappears in the panel. Painful with many projects.
- Unrelated but observed on the same launch: plugin `opencode-acp@stable` fails to load with `Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function`.
- Frequency: consistently reproducible since the update; happens on every launch.

issues.body:
## Summary

`opencode.db` has grown to **12.7 GB** on a machine used daily for about three weeks, and during a 12-minute window on 17 November the database threw **474 `SQLiteError: disk I/O error`** failures across reads and writes — including session, project and config queries. Splitting this out of #64489 at the maintainer's suggestion, since the catalog staleness there may be a symptom of it.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.7
- OS: Darwin 24.2.0 arm64 (macOS), survives sleep/wake
- Terminal: xterm-256color
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest (desktop app + shared background service)
- Active plugins: none found

## Observed

```
$ ls -la ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db
-rw-------@ 12711698432  Nov 18 09:17  opencode.db

$ grep -c "disk I/O" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log
474

first: 2026-11-17T06:56:29.543Z  run=1a4a69c6
last:  2026-11-17T07:08:45.707Z  run=1a4a69c6
by hour: 06:xx → 257   07:xx → 217   (none outside that window)
```

During that window the same process also logged `failed to reload config` twice with `EffectDrizzleQueryError`, and failed `select ... from "session"`, `select "worktree" from "project"` and `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master`.

## Expected Behavior

The database should not reach GB scale in weeks of normal single-user use, and a transient disk error should be retried or surfaced rather than failing unrelated reads (session list, project lookup, config reload).

## Actual Behavior

12.7 GB database; a burst of 474 I/O errors in twelve minutes that broke config reload and session/project queries; a service restart cleared it. Related reports referenced by the maintainer: #54810 (slow startup and heavy disk use), #41739 (startup failing on a large SQLite database).

## Additional Context

Nothing here was manually sized or configured; this is default behaviour on one machine. I can provide a breakdown of table sizes (`dbstat`) or run with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` if that would help, but I will not attach the database itself.

issues.body:
## Summary

In the default TUI keymap, `<leader>q` (`Ctrl+X`, then `Q`) is bound twice: to `app.exit` and to `session.queued_prompts`. Pressing it quits OpenCode and returns to the shell instead of opening the **Queued prompts** dialog.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.0
- OS: Windows 11 (`Windows_NT 10.0.26200`, win32 x64)
- Terminal: Windows console window running PowerShell. Exact terminal emulator: Unavailable (terminal env vars are not exposed to the agent process)
- Shell: PowerShell (TUI launched from PowerShell; `COMSPEC=C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`)
- Install/channel: npm global install of `@opencode/cli` 2.3.0 (`%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\@opencode\cli`), stable/latest channel
- Active plugins: none configured, none found under `~/.config/opencode/plugin` or `~/.config/opencode/plugins`. One MCP server is configured

## Reproduction

1. Use a clean CLI config with no `keybinds` overrides in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`.
2. Run `opencode` 2.3.0 in a project.
3. Press `Ctrl+X`, release, then `Q`.

No queued prompt is required: the two default bindings collide on their own.

## Expected Behavior

The **Queued prompts** dialog opens. At minimum, the shipped default keymap should not bind the same chord to both quitting the app and opening a dialog.

## Actual Behavior

OpenCode exits immediately and drops the user back to the shell. The queued-prompts dialog is never shown.

Reproducible consistently. This is not terminal-specific: the defaults themselves are duplicated, and the `app.exit` handler wins.

## Additional Context

Defaults shipped in 2.3.0, extracted from the installed binary:

```js
"app.exit": c("ctrl+c,ctrl+d,<leader>q", "Exit the application"),
"session.queued_prompts": c("<leader>q", "Manage queued prompts"),
```

The published keybind reference lists the same two defaults in the Application and Sessions tables: <https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/keybinds>

Workaround used by the reporter, which keeps the default exit key intact:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json",
  "keybinds": {
    "session.queued_prompts": "<leader>p"
  }
}
```

Suggestion: drop `<leader>q` from `app.exit` (`ctrl+c,ctrl+d` is enough), or give the queued-prompts dialog a distinct default such as `<leader>k`.

Related: #56152 (`ctrl+d` bound to both `app.exit` and `session.delete`) is the same class of default-keybind collision.

issues.body:
### Description

This is #49673 on OpenCode 2. That issue (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: "output=0, finish=stop … the chat stops after tool calls with no answer at all") was closed only because it was filed against OpenCode 1; the maintainer asked to reopen it if it was still relevant on 2.0, and that never happened. We reproduced the same symptom on 2.0.29 with Gemini.

When the model ends a step with reasoning tokens only (no text, no tool call, `finish_reason: "stop"`), OpenCode settles the turn as a normal completion and shows nothing. The agent just stops right after a tool result, with no error.

The streamed response for that step:

```json
{
  "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
               "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": []}}],
  "usage": {"completion_tokens": 24,
            "completion_tokens_details": {"text_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 24}}
}
```

All the output tokens are reasoning, nothing else comes back, and the turn ends.

**Expected:** a step with no text and no tool call is not settled as a successful turn: retry it, or surface it as an error so the user knows to continue.

### Plugins

N/A

### OpenCode version

2.0.29

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic:

1. Use a Gemini model (seen with `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) in an agentic session with tool calls.
2. Occasionally the step right after a tool result streams back only reasoning, then `finish_reason: "stop"`.
3. OpenCode ends the turn with no visible output and waits for the user as if it had answered.

### Screenshot and/or share link

The tool output is shown, and then nothing: no message, no error.

### Operating System

Linux

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

I checked #7659 and #56285. Both report being pulled back down **after scrolling up**. This is a different request: a setting for the case where the reader never scrolls at all.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

While a long turn streams (a large reasoning block, or a multi-minute tool-heavy run), the desktop timeline keeps the viewport pinned to the end. Reading anything above the newest line is impossible without first scrolling, and every new token slides the text the reader is on further up the screen. On a long reasoning block this reads as the view "jumping to the bottom" every few seconds.

The current answer is "scroll up once and it detaches". That is not enough for this workflow:

- The reader is reading, not scrolling. Touching the wheel or a key to pause the follow is a state change they have to make, and then undo.
- After a detach, resuming the follow requires a separate action (the **Jump to latest** button). So "pause following while I read" and "resume following when I am done reading" cost two explicit actions per turn.
- There is no way to express "keep the newest content visible, but do not move my reading position" as a preference. It is only expressible as a transient gesture, and the gesture is forgotten on the next session.

So: **a persisted setting that decides whether a timeline starts out following the end.**

Suggested shape: `Settings > Timeline > Follow streamed output`, default **on** (current behavior).

Behavior when **off**:

- A session's timeline starts `detached` instead of `following`.
- New streamed content, tool output, and row measurement changes do not move the viewport.
- The **Jump to latest** button stays available and still works, so following can be resumed for the current session on demand — the setting only decides the initial state, not whether the button exists.
- Sending a prompt keeps the current scroll position.

Behavior when **on**: exactly what happens today.

### Why this is low risk

The follow behavior is already an explicit state machine, not scattered scroll writes. `packages/app/src/session/timeline/machine.ts` defines `FollowState` with a `detached` variant, and every anchoring decision in `packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx` is already gated on `input.follow.following()`. The only thing missing is a way to start a session in `detached`.

Concretely, from `dev`:

1. `packages/app/src/session/timeline/machine.ts` — `createFollowState()` currently hardcodes `return FOLLOWING`. Take the preference as an argument and return `DETACHED` when it is off.
2. `packages/app/src/session/timeline/follow.ts` — `createTimelineFollow(sessionKey)` builds the signal from `createFollowState()`; it needs to read the setting there (the memo already re-runs on `sessionKey`, so a per-session reset still works).
3. `packages/app/src/settings/model.tsx` — add `followStreaming: Schema.Boolean` to `generalSchema`, plus its default in `defaultSettings.general` and a setter next to `setWrapCodeBlocks`.
4. `packages/app/src/settings/general/general.tsx` — one `SettingsRow` + `Switch` in the Timeline section, next to **Wrap code blocks**.
5. `packages/app/src/runtime/i18n/en.ts` — `settings.timeline.row.followStreaming.title` / `.description`.

No change to `detached`'s own rules is needed: the existing scroll-intent, pointer, touch and end-probe paths already handle a view that is not following.

### Additional context

- OpenCode version: 2.3.2 (desktop, Windows)
- The same problem exists in the TUI, where `#7648` proposed `tui.auto_scroll` and `#7651` implemented it. A desktop setting would not cover that, but the two could share a name.
- I am not asking to change the default. Following is the right default for short turns; it is long streaming turns where it hurts.

prs.title: feat(app): support building the web app under a base path
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #7624

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Lets the web app be built to run under a path prefix, e.g. behind a reverse proxy at `https://host/opencode/`:

```sh
VITE_BASE_URL=/opencode bun --cwd packages/app build
```

Picks up the idea from #18209 (thanks @Ark-kun), ported to `dev`, where a straight port would break the PWA and the routes:

- **Vite `base`** comes from `VITE_BASE_URL`, normalised so `/opencode`, `opencode/` and `/opencode/` all work.
- **Routing:** Solid Router's own `base` leaves `useLocation().pathname` with the prefix in it, which breaks every place that compares or navigates to it (current route, tabs, cursor hash nav, titlebar history…). Builds with a base use a small `BasePathRouter` that maps browser paths to and from base-free app paths. Root builds keep the stock `Router`.
- **Server URL** is `location.origin + base`, so the API is reached through the same prefix.
- **PWA:** service worker registered at `${base}sw.js` (so its scope is the base), `navigateFallback` and the denylist get the prefix, the manifest's `id`/`start_url`/`scope`/icons get it, and PWA route restore strips and adds it.
- **index.html:** the manifest link and `twitter:image` use `%BASE_URL%`, because Vite doesn't rewrite those.

The default build (no `VITE_BASE_URL`) produces the same `index.html`, `site.webmanifest` and service worker routes as before, apart from chunk hashes.

Not covered: the server's pairing redirect (`/auth/connect/…` → `/`) is still absolute, so pairing through a prefix needs the proxy to rewrite `Location`. That's a server-side follow-up.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Unit tests for the base path helpers, plus a `vite.icons` test that builds under `/opencode/`.
- Built with and without `VITE_BASE_URL` and diffed the output. Under `/opencode`, `index.html`, CSS font URLs, the manifest, the SW registration and the SW fallback/denylist all carry the prefix. The root build is unchanged.
- Served the `/opencode` build behind a proxy that strips the prefix, in front of a real `opencode serve`, and drove it in Chromium: home loads and calls `/opencode/api/*`, the SW registers with scope `/opencode/`, opening a new session goes to `/opencode/new-session?draftId=…` with the tab active, and back returns to `/opencode/`. No requests escape the prefix.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint:changed`. The only remaining findings are the existing `as any` and conditional spread in `vite.config.ts`.

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: fix(util): hand pacote a real npm so git plugins with a build step install
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #49704

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`opencode plugin add github:...` fails with `git dep preparation failed` for any Git dependency that builds itself in `prepare` / `build`.

pacote builds a Git dependency by running `npm install` inside the clone, and takes the binary from `npmBin`. When that name ends in `.js`, `pacote/lib/util/npm.js` spawns `process.execPath` with the script as its first argument. In the compiled binary `npm_execpath` is `/$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js`, so the child process is opencode itself: it runs its own CLI, never that script, and nothing gets installed.

`strace -f -e trace=execve` over the command shows 23 `git` execs, zero `npm` execs, and one re-exec of the opencode binary with the `npm-cli.js` argument. No npm debug log is written, which fits npm never running.

The change gives pacote a real npm: `resolveNpmBin()` ignores an `npm_execpath` that lives inside the bundle or does not exist, and returns `"npm"`, which pacote resolves through `PATH`. Arborist forwards the option. Machines without npm on `PATH` keep the current behaviour.

I did not build the compiled binary to test this end to end. The failure and the fix were reproduced at the pacote/arborist level, which is where the defect lives.

Related: #60201 skips the preparation instead. That removes the error but leaves packages that build in `prepare` installed without their built entry point — measured here: `dist/` absent with `ignoreScripts: true`, present with a real npm.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/npm.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 19 pass, including the new `Npm.resolveNpmBin` case.
- `bun run typecheck` from the repository root: 33 tasks, no type errors.
- Isolated with the pinned `pacote@21.5.1`: `npmBin: "/$bunfs/bin/npm-cli.js"` → `git dep preparation failed`; the same call with `npmBin: "npm"` gets past preparation.
- Same failure from a clean Debian container on 1.19.5 with four public plugins: `numman-ali/opencode-openai-codex-auth`, `griffinmartin/opencode-claude-auth`, `tickernelz/opencode-mem`, `slkiser/opencode-quota`.

prs.title: refactor(codemode): thread Rust runs by program complexity
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Stacks on #64437 (base branch `codemode-rust`).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

This changes how PsychoScript runs programs, not what they can do. There are no new APIs.

**Inline or thread is decided by nesting, not size.** Compiling is the only step whose native recursion follows syntax depth, and the oxc parser has no guard of its own.
- `nesting::bound` scans tokens once to get an upper bound on syntax depth. It is conservative by construction: a `/` that could be a regex or a division makes the rest of its line count raw, where every opening bracket counts and no closer does. Source that can't be tokenized, or that might span lines, counts raw to the end of the file. An undercount could overflow the stack and abort the process; an overcount only costs a thread.
- `bench/examples/stack_probe.rs` measured the stack per bound unit: 737 B in release and 9.3 KB in debug for the worst form. The budgets are 1 KiB and 12 KiB per unit.
- A program compiles on the caller's thread when that fits the 512 KB run budget, however long it is. Otherwise only the compile moves, to a thread sized to the bound. This now protects `Runtime::program`, `execute_async` and resume too, which used to compile inline unchecked.
- Runs always use the same 512 KB budget, so where a program runs never changes its outcome. As a result, `execute` no longer spawns a thread for the run.

**Long runs move off the executor.**
- A run's state is now `Send`: `Rc` became `Arc`, and runs own an `Arc<Setup>`. Instruction counts for the nine benchmark programs stay within ±2%.
- When a run driven as a future computes for more than 1 ms without stopping, it stops at its next safepoint and finishes that stretch on a worker thread.
- Host code (tool calls, extension calls, host accessors such as a streaming body's `cancel`, `search`'s hooks, the first poll of host futures, hooks) is handed back to the executor and runs there in the same order. A handed-back call costs about 5 µs. Blocking `run` and `execute` stay on the caller's thread.
- Dropping a run that is on its worker brings it back first, so its calls are cancelled on the executor.

**Call depth.** Native frames on `codemode-rust` mean built-in callbacks no longer use native stack: re-entrant callbacks cost 0 B per level in release and debug (`stack_probe run`, 500 and 4,500 levels deep). The single 512 KB runtime budget therefore no longer limits depth. Map, map in map, forEach, reduce, sort comparators, toString, replace callbacks, toJSON, `Array.from` and generators all stop where the reference does: 10,000 program frames, or 5,000 levels where each level costs two frames. One difference comes from the base, not this PR: both the base and this branch stop at 9,999 where the reference stops at 10,000.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, round-trip conformance and `bash test262/run.sh` all pass.
- Conformance now runs every case both blocking and as a future.
- New tests cover regex-versus-division and other unclear tokens hiding deep nesting (the previous scanner undercounted 10 of the 19 cases), deliberately deep and disguised programs on a 1 MiB caller stack ending with a diagnostic or outcome, a streaming `cancel` started while the run is on its worker, equal recursion limits on both routes, host code staying on the executor while a run is offloaded, and dropping or suspending a run that is on its worker.
- Plugin event for `reducer-padded.js` (2957 B): about 58–63 µs on the base, 44–48 µs here (`bench/RESULTS.md`: 47.7 µs). Instruction counts for the nine benchmark programs are within −0.6% and +2.4% of the base.

### Screenshots / recordings

n/a

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
