prs.title: feat(core): always run subagents in the background
prs.body:
**Subagents always run in the background now.** The subagent tool's `background` option is gone: every call returns a `sessionID` immediately, and the parent receives a `<subagent>` message each time the child goes idle.

Stacked on #63209 (report subagent results on every idle), which makes background reporting reliable across multi-turn and shell-woken work. Replaces the default flip from #62035, without its metadata-based foreground claim.

❌ **Before**
- Foreground by default: the parent blocks until the child finishes. Parallel work is opt-in with `background: true`.
- A foreground follow-up to a running background child returns "still running" anyway; #62035 worked around that by writing `subagent.notify = false` to the database, which leaves the child muted after a normal wait or a crash.

✅ **After**
- One mode: `subagents.start(recovery, { background: true })` and return the running handle. No `jobs.block`, no inline answers, no Ctrl+B handoff for subagents.
- A follow-up to a running child joins its current run; a follow-up to an idle child starts a new background job. Results always arrive as reports.
- Pressing Escape on the parent no longer cancels its running children; they keep going and report later. Per-child stop (`composer.subagent.interrupt`) stays.
- Ctrl+B / `Session.background` / `jobs.backgroundAll` stay for foreground shells.

```diff
- subagent({ background?: boolean })  // default: block and return the answer inline
+ subagent({ ... })                    // always: return sessionID now, <subagent> report on every idle
```

🖥️ **UI:** subagent "Background" badges, the `(background)` subtitle, and the subagent `ctrl+b background` hint/footer item are removed from the TUI, app, session-ui and mini footer; blocking work is shells only. Docs (`tools.mdx`, `agents.mdx`, GUI plugin docs) describe the idle-report model.

🧰 **`opencode run`:** already waits for running jobs, pending inbox items and owned executions. Now every run that uses a subagent prints "waiting for N background job(s)", and the report-triggered parent turn decides the exit code. New test covers it.

🚩 **Flag:** none. We're shipping this as the new behavior.

prs.title: fix(desktop): deliver the opencode:// link the app was started for
prs.body:
Clicking an `opencode://` link while the app is closed opens the app, and the link is lost. The main process routes links only from `second-instance` and from an `open-url` listener that registers after the first window. The link a launch itself carries never enters the deep-link machine.

- **Since:** the Electron port (#15663). The Tauri app read the launch link with `getCurrent()` (#10072).
- **Scope:** this PR makes the main process deliver the link to the first renderer. No renderer code acts on a link today (its handlers were removed in #43789), so a person still sees nothing after the app opens until a handler lands.
- **Overlap:** #64180 captures the launch link too, replaces the machine this PR keeps, and adds a handler. #59058 and #57246 also cover this gap. If #64180 merges first, close this one.

## Cause

| Launch for a link | Where the link is | Before |
|---|---|---|
| Windows, Linux | `process.argv` of the first instance | never read |
| macOS | `open-url`, before `ready` | no listener yet: it registers after `ready`, the first window and the main bundle's import, and Electron keeps nothing for a late listener |

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant OS
  participant E as entry module
  participant L as lifecycle layer
  participant M as deep-link machine
  participant R as first renderer
  OS->>E: start with link (argv, or open-url before ready)
  Note over E: before: nothing reads it
  E->>E: holdEarlyLinks() keeps open-url links
  E->>L: ready, first window, import("./desktop")
  L->>M: links.received [argv links, held links]
  Note over M: queued: no renderer is ready
  R->>M: window.ready
  M->>R: links.deliver, once
```

## Fix

- **Entry module:** `holdEarlyLinks()` listens for `open-url` from the first statement after the lock (`deep-links/launch.ts`).
- **Lifecycle layer:** it takes the held links and the links in its own arguments, and feeds them to the machine as `links.received`. The take and its own `open-url` listener are in one tick, so a link is neither lost between the two listeners nor seen by both.

  ```ts
  const launch = [...deepLinkArguments(process.argv), ...takeEarlyLinks()]

  if (launch.length) {
    runFork(Effect.logInfo("deep link received at launch", { urls: launch }))
    deepLinks.receive(launch)
  }
  ```

- **Machine:** unchanged. It already queues a link until a renderer reports ready and forgets it once acknowledged.
- **Once only:** only the process that holds the single-instance lock reads its arguments, one time. A relaunch started with the same arguments, so it would open the link again; it now drops them: `app.relaunch({ args: relaunchArguments(process.argv) })`.
- **Not links:** the executable, Chromium switches, a source build's app folder and file paths are ignored. `second-instance` uses the same filter.

## Tested

| | By test | Live |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | argument table; machine table (link before the first window, while it loads, two arrivals, first window closed while holding; delivered once) | Source build with its own test root, link on the command line, protocol registration off. Before: `window.__OPENCODE__.deepLinks` stays unset. After: `["opencode://cold-start/proof?run=after"]`, and the log has `deep link received at launch` |
| Linux | same tables | not run |
| macOS | machine table only | not run: the `open-url`-before-`ready` path rests on Electron's documentation |

Not tested anywhere: an installed build started by the OS for a real link, and a live relaunch.

No feature flag: a fix. #64556 adds the same argument filter in `deep-links/registration.ts`; whichever lands second imports this one.

prs.title: feat(app): support key chords in shortcuts
prs.body:
## Summary

Shortcuts can be key chords: a sequence of key presses separated by spaces, such as `mod+k mod+c` or `g i`. This is the second of three stacked PRs, based on the `@opentui/keymap` engine PR.

- **Keymap.** Each binding parses into strokes. A chord whose first key types a character only starts outside text fields, so typing is never taken. A chord that starts with a modifier works anywhere. Escape cancels a pending chord and Backspace removes its last key.
- **Next-key panel.** While a chord is pending, a panel near the bottom of the window lists the keys that continue it and the command each runs.
- **Labels.** Chords show one keycap per stroke, for example ⌥G ⌥S, in Settings, the palette and tooltips. `parseKeybind` and `matchKeybind` still only match single-stroke combos.
- **Recording in Settings > Shortcuts.** A key saves as soon as it is pressed, as before. The row just saved then shows **+**. Clicking it records one more key onto the shortcut, up to 4. Backspace while adding drops that key; with nothing before it, Backspace still unbinds the shortcut.
- **Conflicts** now include prefixes. A chord is rejected when it starts, or is started by, another shortcut. For example ⌘K ⌘J is rejected because ⌘K opens the palette.

prs.title: feat(app): dispatch command shortcuts through @opentui/keymap
prs.body:
## Summary

Desktop and web shortcuts now run through `@opentui/keymap`, the engine the TUI already uses. This is the first of three stacked PRs. The next two add key chords and a leader key on top.

- **One dispatcher.** A single keymap in `shell/commands/keymap.ts` replaces the keydown listener in `command.tsx`. Commands register exactly as before, and dispatch keeps its current rules:
  - The palette's keys win over other commands.
  - On shared keys, a command with a `when` comes first, then the user's own binding, then registration order.
  - A command can return `false` to pass the key on.
  - Keys that type a character don't fire in text fields unless the command is `editable`.
  - The ⌥ and bracket layout fallbacks still apply.
  - Shortcuts pause while a dialog is open or a shortcut is being recorded.
- **Keys during IME input.** Keys are ignored while an IME is composing, including Safari's keyCode 229 case.
- **Shortcuts scoped to an element.** A command can take a `target` element, and its keys then only fire while focus is inside it, ahead of global commands on the same keys. The first user is a new **Stop session** command (Escape, Ctrl+G) scoped to the prompt editor, which can now be rebound in Settings > Shortcuts.
- **The keymap is the only handler for attach and stop.** The composer no longer handles ⌘U or Escape/Ctrl+G itself. `file.attach` and `prompt.stop` own those keys, so rebinding either one takes effect in the prompt too.

Shortcuts are still single key combos in this PR. Settings > Shortcuts is unchanged apart from the new Stop session row.

## Feature flag

None. Shortcut behavior should be unchanged. The visible additions are the **Stop session** command in the palette and its row in Settings, which keep the Escape and Ctrl+G keys the prompt already used.

## Stack

1. **This PR**: the `@opentui/keymap` engine.
2. Key chords, based on this branch.
3. Leader key, based on the chords branch.

## Validation

- `bun typecheck` and lint pass in `packages/app`.
- `bun run test:unit` (2733) and `bun run test:browser` (357) pass.
- The new `keymap.test.ts` drives the real keymap with DOM key events. It covers dispatch order, declining commands, text fields, focus targets, IME composition, blocked shortcuts and keyboard layouts.
- Moved coverage:
  - `composer-ime.test.ts` drops its three Escape rows. The contract that Escape doesn't stop a session while an IME composes is now owned by `keymap.test.ts` ("keys are left to the IME while it composes"), since the keymap is what stops.
  - The composer component test that checks opening the file picker keeps history browsing now opens it from the Add menu instead of ⌘U, because stories run without the command keymap. It still fails when `attach()` ends browsing.
- The composer component tests pass. The shortcut-heavy e2e specs fail the same set of tests with and without this change on macOS, because those tests press Ctrl and assume Linux.

prs.title: feat(core): durable video jobs
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Prepares https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63666 (the agent's video tool).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Video jobs now survive a server restart. Until now, running and failed jobs lived only in memory: a restart lost them, and a running job's videos were never collected. Each job now has a record in the kv table, and the server resumes polling running jobs when it starts.

The video ID is still the only handle. The provider's job ID (`remote`) stays inside the video service.

Record, key `video:<videoID>`, decoded with a schema on read:

```ts
{ status: "submitting" | "running" | "completed" | "error",
  model, location, created,
  remote?,          // running
  blobs?,           // completed: blob IDs
  reason?, error?,  // error
  finished? }       // completed, error
```

Lifecycle:

```
start     write submitting -> provider accepts -> write running (remote) -> return { id, status: "running" }
          provider rejects -> remove the record, return the error
done      save each video as a new blob -> write completed (blobs, finished)
          any download fails -> remove the blobs saved so far -> write error
startup   running    -> poll again until 2 h after created (already past: error "unknown")
          submitting -> error "unknown": never resubmitted, it's paid and not idempotent
hourly    remove records 24 h after finished (or 26 h after created if they never finished)
```

`get` reads the record. For a completed job it reads each blob, drops the ones that no longer exist, and returns not found if none remain. Memory holds only the polling fibers.

`start` takes an optional `location`, stored on the record and used for every later provider call, including after a restart. The HTTP route still uses the server's base configuration; the agent tool will pass the session's location.

API differences (`/api/experimental/generate/video`):

- Blob IDs are generic again: `blob_` + 26 characters, instead of `<videoID>_<n>`.
- `GET /generate/video/:id` returns running, failed and completed jobs after a restart, and 404 from 24 hours after the job finished.
- Blobs are kept until removed: no more 7-day cleanup, and `Blob.Info` drops `expiresAt`. They're written straight to `blob_…` and flushed to disk (no `.part` file); a failed write deletes its file. The blob route's cache lifetime goes from 7 days to a year, since a blob ID never changes content.

**Servers sharing a database** (the background service plus `opencode serve`) never poll the same job. A job has a lease in kv (`video-lease:<id>` = `{ owner, until }`), taken with a conditional write the same way automation elects its scheduler:

```text
owner     renews every 30 s (until = now + 1 min); stops the job if the lease was taken
every server, at startup and every minute
          unfinished job whose lease expired → claim it → poll it (or fail an interrupted submission)
```

So when a server dies, another one that's still running picks up its jobs within about 1–2 minutes, instead of waiting for a restart.

Still behind the `video_generate` flag.

Known limits, accepted for now:

- After a hard crash, the restarted server waits for the old lease to expire (up to a minute) before it resumes a job.
- If the server crashes between saving a blob and updating the record, the next start downloads the videos again and the first blob stays on disk. A crash mid-download can also leave a partial file that no job references. Nothing removes blobs yet; a delete endpoint comes later.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/video-generation.test.ts` (one test): a job with two videos completes with two `blob_` IDs; a fresh layer on the same data dir and database still reads it; a job running when the first process stops completes in the next one; a `submitting` record becomes an error on startup; records are gone 25 hours later (TestClock). Passed with `--rerun-each 10`.
- `packages/server/test/video-generate.test.ts` updated for `blob_` IDs and reading the job back after a restart.
- `bun typecheck` in core, server, schema and protocol; `bun run check` at the root.
- Live, against xAI (`grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite`): two jobs started, server stopped mid-generation, restarted; both completed and their blobs stream as H.264 MP4. Then two servers on one data dir: started a job on A, killed A with SIGKILL; B claimed the expired lease and completed the job about two minutes later.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): fall back to the classical TLS handshake on networks that drop the post-quantum one
prs.body:
Refs #60399, #60661, #60533, #60422.

Bun 1.4.1+ sends a post-quantum key share in every TLS ClientHello. The ClientHello grows from about 500 B to about 1500 B and no longer fits one TCP segment. Networks that drop a two-segment ClientHello (Rostelecom and other Russian ISPs since Oct 29, a Turkish ISP, some Cloudflare ranges) leave every request hanging or failing with `ECONNRESET`, while `curl` on the same machine gets through. Nothing for this shipped before; #60399 went quiet because the filter stopped matching `opencode.ai`, and `models.dev` was still dropped afterwards.

- **What changes:** the shared fetch detects this per host and moves that host to the classical handshake (`ecdhCurve: "X25519:P-256:P-384"`, Bun's default groups without the post-quantum one).
- **No setting and no flag:** an affected user can't reach the docs or the model, so it has to work unattended.
- **Default is unchanged:** a host keeps the post-quantum handshake until a check shows that the network drops it and passes the classical one.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as OpenCode
  participant F as Filtering network
  participant H as Host
  O-xF: request, ClientHello 1502 B (X25519MLKEM768 + X25519)
  Note over O: no response after 2 s, or a connection reset
  par check on two fresh connections
    O-xF: HEAD /, ClientHello 1502 B
  and
    O->>F: HEAD /, ClientHello 280 B (X25519)
    F->>H: passes
    H-->>O: any response
  end
  Note over O: standard failed, classical completed: host uses classical
  O->>H: the same request, sent once, ClientHello 280 B
  H-->>O: response
  Note over O: later requests go classical at once, and the standard handshake is tried again hourly beside a request
```

### Behaviour

- **Trigger:** a request with no response after 2 s, or one that fails with `ECONNRESET`, `EPROTO`, `ETIMEDOUT` or `ConnectionClosed`.
- **Check:** two `HEAD /` requests on new connections, 3 s each, over the request's own route (proxy, CA, client certificate). Any response counts as a completed handshake.
- **Verdicts:**

| Standard | Classical | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| completes | any | Host left alone for 10 minutes. A slow model response costs two `HEAD` requests per host in that time. |
| fails | completes | Host uses the classical handshake. The stalled request is aborted and sent again. |
| fails | fails | No verdict (no network, host down). The request fails as it does today. |

- **One send:** a request is resent only when the check shows the standard handshake cannot complete, so the first attempt never left the machine. A streamed body is not resent; the next request takes the classical handshake.
- **Coverage:** everything on the shared fetch (model requests on both routes, the model catalog, Console, web fetch, remote MCP) and requests that present a client certificate. WebSocket connections, npm installs, the CLI updater and the desktop app's own downloads do not use this fetch and are unchanged.
- **Log:** `The network drops the post-quantum TLS handshake to this host; using the classical handshake origin=https://opencode.ai`

### Security

- **Lost on an affected host:** protection against a session recorded today being decrypted by a future quantum computer. The classical handshake is what `curl`, OpenCode 1.19.3 and Bun before 1.4.1 send.
- **Kept:** certificate verification, the cipher suites and TLS 1.3. A test covers a classical connection rejecting an untrusted certificate.
- **Who can force it:** anyone on the path who can drop packets, which is who is doing it on these networks. The alternatives users found in #60399 were disabling certificate verification and running an intercepting proxy.

### Evidence

**1. Real hosts behind the filtering rule.** A local CONNECT proxy tunnels to the real hosts and drops any ClientHello over 1200 B, as the capture in #60661 shows (first segment acknowledged, second never). Bun 1.4.4, Windows.

| Host | Bun fetch today | With this PR, first request | With this PR, next request |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opencode.ai` | no response, 10 s timeout | HTTP 200 in 5.6 s | HTTP 200 in 0.5 s |
| `models.dev` | no response, 10 s timeout | HTTP 200 in 5.3 s | HTTP 200 in 0.2 s |
| `registry.npmjs.org` | no response, 10 s timeout | HTTP 200 in 5.3 s | HTTP 200 in 0.2 s |
| `api.openai.com` | no response, 10 s timeout | HTTP 401 in 5.3 s | HTTP 401 in 0.2 s |
| `api.anthropic.com` | no response, 10 s timeout | HTTP 401 in 5.3 s | HTTP 401 in 0.3 s |

What the filter saw for `opencode.ai` (the 401s are unauthenticated requests reaching the provider):

```text
DROPPED 1502 B  opencode.ai  key shares: X25519MLKEM768(1216B) + X25519(32B)   request
DROPPED 1502 B  opencode.ai  key shares: X25519MLKEM768(1216B) + X25519(32B)   check, standard
passed   280 B  opencode.ai  key shares: X25519(32B)                           check, classical
passed   280 B  opencode.ai  key shares: X25519(32B)                           request, resent
```

**2. The CLI behind the same rule.** `opencode run --standalone --model opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` with an empty profile and `HTTPS_PROXY` set to that proxy.

| | `dev` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Result | No answer in 60 s | The gateway answered; the run ended in 19 s |
| Output | `retrying (attempt 3): ECONNRESET: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly…` and `Failed to fetch models.dev` | Fallback logged for `opencode.ai` and `models.opencode.ai` |

The answer in the PR run was `Free usage limit reached` for this source build. A control run with the filter off and the standard handshake got the same answer, so it is not caused by the classical handshake.

**3. The same ClientHello on affected lines.** Measurements from reporters in #60399, not from this PR:

| Line | Bun 1.4.4 default (1491 B) | `ecdhCurve: "X25519:P-256"` (267 B) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rostelecom, Perm | times out | HTTP 200, same minute |
| Rostelecom, Irkutsk | stalls | answers instantly |

This PR's ClientHello carries the same single X25519 key share and lists one more group, so it is 2 bytes longer.

**Not done:** a run on an affected line. I have no vantage point inside one of these networks. Several reporters in #60399 offered to test a patch; a preview build to them closes that gap.

### Test

`packages/util/test/tls-fallback.test.ts` runs real TLS handshakes through a relay that applies the same rule (`test/fixtures/tls-filter.ts`). The first test fails the day Bun's default ClientHello fits one segment again, which is when this can be removed.

```ts
test("sends the request once, on the classical handshake, when the standard one is dropped", async () => {
  const send = tlsFallbackFetch({ ...timing, onFallback: (host) => fallbacks.push(host) })
  const response = await send(`${filter.origin}/chat`, post(filter.ca, "hi"))

  expect(await response.text()).toBe("echo hi")
  expect(seen).toEqual(["POST /chat hi"])
  expect(Math.max(...passed.map((hello) => hello.bytes))).toBeLessThan(600)
  expect(passed.flatMap((hello) => hello.shares)).not.toContain("X25519MLKEM768")
})
```

`test/fixtures/tls/localhost.key.pem` is a throwaway key for a self-signed `localhost` certificate used only by this test.

prs.title: feat(core): choose tools and Code Mode placement from the session's model
prs.body:
**Chooses tools, and which of them go into Code Mode, from the session's model, in one hard-coded function.** It's decided in `SessionContext.select`, in the same pass that filters tools by permissions, using the model the user selected (session model → agent model → default). The `experimental.model.resolve` hook still runs in `load`, so Copilot "auto" routing is unaffected.

The three rules (`packages/core/src/tool/model-policy.ts`, `modelTools()`):
1. **GPT models use `patch`; other models use `edit` + `write`.** Same predicate as before; it moves here from `patch.ts`'s `context` hook.
2. **`websearch` is hidden** when web search is turned off or no provider is available (moved from `websearch.ts`'s `context` hook).
3. **GPT and Anthropic models** get `read`, `write`, `edit`, `patch` and `shell` inside Code Mode, with `glob`, `grep` and `webfetch` hidden (scripts use `shell` and `fetch`). Other models keep them as top-level tools. MCP, `opencode.*` and plugin tools stay in Code Mode as before.

How it works:
- `Tool.snapshot(permissions, { location, tools })` skips hidden tools and puts the listed tools into Code Mode in the same loop as the permission filter.
- Tools register once, without checking `full_codemode`. `shell` and `read` carry a Code Mode variant (`Tool.Info.codemode`: description, input, pinned) used when they land in Code Mode; shell's 10-minute default applies only to Code Mode calls.
- The Code Mode catalog cache keeps the 5 most recently used tool sets per location (was one slot), cleared on any registry change.
- MCP instructions no longer mention `execute` when Code Mode is off; the "Code Mode no longer available" message says tools are now direct; the worktree hint names whichever tool exists.

⚠️ **This applies to everyone, regardless of the `full_codemode` flag:** GPT and Claude users get file tools and shell inside Code Mode and lose `glob`, `grep` and `webfetch`. Draft for evaluation.

Known open items: the `explore` agent denies `execute`, so on GPT/Claude it loses `glob`/`grep`/`webfetch` without gaining Code Mode; `read`'s description still mentions grep.

📊 **Proof**
- New `tool-model-policy.test.ts` (rules per model family, websearch, and `SessionContext.select` end to end), cache and Code Mode variant tests in `tool-registry.test.ts`.
- 681 tests pass across the policy, tool, session and Code Mode suites; `typecheck:tsc` passes in schema, core, plugin, server, cli and sdk; `check:generated` passes.

prs.title: feat(app): add experimental tab groups to side tabs
prs.body:
Adds browser-style tab groups to the vertical side tabs, behind **Settings → Experimental → Tab groups** (`settings.general.tabGroups`: on in local dev builds, off in releases). With the setting off, the sidebar is unchanged from `dev`. Top (horizontal) tabs are never grouped.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d54d686d-758f-45b7-bd84-a7adab055379

- **Automatic grouping:** The sliders menu next to the filter groups tabs by `Server` (the default, which stays flat until a second server connects), `Project`, or `None`.
- **Manual groups:** With automatic grouping set to `None`, you make a group by holding a tab over another for 220ms, dropping a tab on a group header, choosing `New group` in the sliders menu, or right-clicking a tab and choosing `Add to group`. Dragging a tab below its group takes it out.
- **Group actions:** Click a header to collapse or expand the group; it expands again when you open one of its sessions. Drag a header to move the whole group. The header menu renames the group, sets one of 6 colours, ungroups manual groups, and closes the group.
- **Filter tabs:** A filter under **Search sessions** narrows the open tabs in place. The **Search sessions** button still opens the global search dialog. Dragging is off while a filter is active.
- **Drag engine:** Grouped side tabs use a pure state machine (`tab-group-drag-machine.ts`) instead of `@dnd-kit`. It measures rows once when a drag starts, moves the dragged row with the pointer, and slides neighbours out of the way. Colour stays a group's identity; while you hold a tab over another, the preview rail is neutral grey.
- **Persistence:** Group state is saved per window (`Persist.window("tabs.groups")`), so two desktop windows don't overwrite each other's groups. Default colours don't depend on group order, so recolouring or reordering one group never changes another.
- **Desktop dev:** `bun dev:desktop` can clone a running `OpenCode Dev` profile and reuse its server. Debug builds only (`OPENCODE_DESKTOP_USER_DATA`, `OPENCODE_DESKTOP_REUSE_SERVER`, `OPENCODE_DESKTOP_REUSE_SERVICE_FILE`).

**Flag:** `settings.general.tabGroups` (Settings → Experimental → Tab groups).

**Tests:** Unit tests cover the drag machine, colour stability and grouping (`tab-groups.test.ts`). The tabs e2e keeper adds a case for reordering, recolouring, collapsing, filtering and dwell-to-group. Locally, 4 other cases in `tabs.spec.ts` (mobile drawer attention dot, failed dot, Recent/Pinned dots) fail the same way on `origin/dev`.

prs.title: fix(app): stop the timeline crashing when a row leaves mid-update
prs.body:
Fixes #63944. Fixes #62800.

Two renderer crashes left the session view dead:

- `effect/match/Match/exhaustive: absurd` from `renderRow`, in the New timeline when a thought ends without any text. Some providers stream thinking with no readable text.
- `Expected a user-message timeline row`, in either timeline when a row leaves and another row takes its index.

## Root cause

Rows found their data in two lists that update at different points of one flush: TanStack's virtual items, and the projection's rows. Each row looked itself up by key, and fell back to `rows()[index]`.

```ts
// before
const initialRow = rowByKey().get(rowProps.rowKey)!
const row = createMemo(() => rowByKey().get(rowProps.rowKey) ?? rows()[item().index] ?? initialRow)
```

The New timeline also built rows from a visibility signal that lags the transcript by one computation, so a thought that ended empty was published once more as a row, then dropped in the same flush.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Transcript
  participant P as New timeline rows
  participant T as TanStack items
  participant R as VirtualRow
  S->>P: thought ends, still empty
  P->>P: built with the old visibility: 37 rows, thought included
  P->>T: setOptions(37 rows)
  P->>P: visibility flips: 36 rows
  Note over T: still lists the thought
  T->>R: mount the thought's key
  R->>R: rowByKey has no such key, rows()[36] is undefined
  R-->>R: TimelineRow.key(undefined) throws "absurd"
```

- **#63944:** the mounted row had no row at all.
- **#62800:** a row whose key had left read `rows()[index]`, another key's row, when its renderer's cleanup read the row.

## Fix

A row now mounts with its row and its place, so it has nothing to look up and nothing to fall back to (`packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx`):

```ts
type MountedRow = { key: string; row: TimelineRow.TimelineRow; item: VirtualItem }

// One row per key the projection still has.
const mountedRows = createMemo(() => [
  ...new Map(
    virtualizer.getVirtualItems().flatMap((item): [string, MountedRow][] => {
      const key = String(item.key)
      const row = rowByKey().get(key)

      return row ? [[key, { key, row, item }]] : []
    }),
  ).values(),
])
```

```tsx
<Key each={mountedRows()} by={(mounted) => mounted.key}>
  {(mounted) => <VirtualRow mounted={mounted} />}
</Key>
```

- `Key` only ever hands a row values with its own key, so a row cannot read another key's row.
- The `!` lookups, the index fallback and the `virtualItemByKey` and `virtualRowKeys` memos are gone.
- Two rows can share a key (a turn interrupted twice has two `turn-divider` rows). One mounts, as before one measurement existed.

The New timeline reads a part's visibility from the part, and uses the signal only to hear that it flipped (`packages/session-ui/src/timeline-next/projection.ts`), so it no longer publishes the row list that started #63944.

## Tests

| Test | On `dev` |
| --- | --- |
| `timeline-virtualizer.spec.ts`: a row dropped in the flush that added it | `Match/exhaustive: absurd` |
| `timeline-virtualizer.spec.ts`: a row that left while another took its index | `user-message:a read user-message:b` |
| `timeline-virtualizer.spec.ts`: two rows that share a key | guards the one-row-per-key step |
| `timeline-projection.test.ts`: the New timeline drops a thought that ends without text in one step | publishes the ended thought once more |

## Not measured

No strobe benchmark is attached. The mounted list does the same work per change as the two memos it replaces: one pass over the visible rows.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related: #61696, #43703

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds an optional `window` (in tokens) to compaction configuration so automatic compaction can plan for a smaller target context window without reducing the model's actual request limit:

- **Top-level:** `compaction.window` in `opencode.jsonc` sets a default automatic compaction window across models.
- **Per-provider / model / variant:** `settings.compaction.window` overrides the top-level setting for a provider, model, or variant (including setting a larger value to opt back into a large model's full context window when a lower global `compaction.window` is set).
- **Per-agent:** `agents.<id>.compaction.window` (or `compaction.window` in Markdown agent frontmatter) overrides the model and global window for that agent's sessions.

`autoLimit` caps the effective window at the model's actual limit so it never raises a model's window, and leaves the summary request's own budget at the model's limit so single-turn bursts past `window` still summarize cleanly.

Long lines in timeline code blocks are cut off, the scrollbar is hidden, and the hover buttons sat directly on the code.

- **Setting:** Settings › General › Timeline › **Wrap code blocks** (`general.wrapCodeBlocks`, off by default) wraps every code block.
- **Per-block override:** a **Wrap lines** button flips one block against the setting. Choosing the setting's value again clears the override.
- **Only when needed:** Wrap shows only when a line is wider than the block, so short blocks keep just Copy.
- **Fill behind the buttons:** the top-right buttons get the block's own background behind them, fading out toward the start and bottom, the same treatment as the shell output's Copy. Code no longer shows through the icons.
- **No flag:** the setting is opt-in, and the button only appears on blocks that are already cut off.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d91551b-3a16-4c4d-8e50-01809fb89f05

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Settings: wrapCodeBlocks] --> P[SessionUIProvider MarkdownProvider codeWrap] --> T[timeline cache view context] --> R["markdown root data-code-wrap"]
  B["Wrap button: data-wrap=true|false"] --> C{"pre-wrap?"}
  R --> C
  O[ResizeObserver + hover] --> M["measure unwrapped width"] --> V["data-code-overflow shows Wrap"]
```

- **Fill colour:** `--markdown-code-background` follows the block. A completed block's highlighter paints its background inline, so the shell colour applies only to blocks without one (`:has(> pre:not([style*="background"]))`).
- **Timeline cache:** each cached timeline view re-provides the Markdown context field by field (`session/timeline/cache.ts`), so it now passes `codeWrap` through. Covered by a case in `timeline-cache.spec.ts`.
- **Overflow check:** one shared `ResizeObserver` measures each block unwrapped (`data-code-measure` forces `white-space: pre`) and restores it in the same layout. Hovering re-checks, since a streamed line can grow without a resize.
- **Stories:** `current-session-code-blocks--long-lines` and `components-markdown--long-code-lines`.

prs.title: feat(core): add Bun.file, Bun.write and Bun.Glob to Code Mode behind full_codemode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds a subset of Bun's file APIs to Code Mode as a `Bun` global, behind the `full_codemode` flag. With the flag off nothing changes. The execute description is unchanged, so models aren't told about it yet.

```js
const text = await Bun.file("notes.md").text()
await Bun.write("out/copy.md", Bun.file("notes.md"))   // creates out/
for (const name of new Bun.Glob("src/**/*.ts").scan({ cwd: "packages/core" })) ...
import { file, write } from "bun"                        // same as the Bun global
```

**Surface**
- `Bun.file(path | URL, { type? })`: `text`, `json`, `bytes`, `arrayBuffer`, `exists`, `stat`, `slice`, `write`, `delete`/`unlink`, `writer`, plus `name`, `type`, `size`, `lastModified`.
- `Bun.write(dest, data, options)`: `dest` is a path, URL or BunFile; `data` is a string, bytes, a BunFile or slice, or a `fetch` response. Creates missing parent folders unless `createPath` is false (`mode` throws), writes exact bytes, returns the byte count. Numbers and booleans are written as text, as Bun does.
- `new Bun.Glob(pattern)`: `scan` / `scanSync` (both return an array) with `cwd`, `dot`, `absolute` and `onlyFiles`; any other option throws. `match(path)`.

**Behaves like the tools.** Every read asks `read` permission through `FileAccess`, every write asks `edit` through `FileWrite`, with the same diff the write tool shows, and a scan asks `glob` for its pattern as the glob tool does (which `full_codemode` turns off). Permission errors reach the program as core reports them; other failures are Node-shaped (`code`, `syscall`, `path`). All I/O goes through the session's `Environment.Files`, never the server's own filesystem.

**Locking.** A write, append or delete holds the file's `FileMutation` lock from reading the file to changing it, the same lock an edit or a patch holds, so a program's write and an edit can't interleave on one file. Whole-file writes go through `FileMutation.write` and appends through a new `FileMutation.append` (still exact bytes, no BOM handling or formatting), so the watcher, snapshot and LSP hooks planned there will cover them. A delete removes the file directly under that lock, as a patch's delete does.

**Cost**
- `Bun.file()` reads the file's size and date once (Bun's `size` is a plain value), asking `read` once; later reads through that file don't ask again.
- `slice()` reads only its range.
- `writer()` buffers chunks and appends each flush instead of rewriting the file.
- A scan lists only the folders its pattern can reach, and skips hidden folders unless the pattern names them or `dot` is set.

**Wiring.** The registry already gives runs `path` when `full_codemode` is on; the session now passes its file services along with its Location, and those runs get `fetch`, `path` and `Bun` from the one cached runtime. The extension names `bun` as its module, so `import { file } from "bun"` and `require("bun")` load the same global, only in runs that have it. `Glob.match` in `@opencode/util` gains an optional `{ dot }` (default unchanged) so scans can leave dot files to patterns that name them.

**Differences from Bun** (checked against Bun 1.4.4)
- `Bun.file()` throws when `read` is denied; Bun never throws there.
- `size` and `lastModified` are read once, at `Bun.file()`.
- `writer()`'s first flush replaces the file; Bun overwrites from the start without truncating.
- Scan results drop a leading `./`.

**Same as Bun, on purpose** (both checked against Bun 1.4.4)
- `match` takes dot files (`new Bun.Glob("*").match(".env")` is `true`), though a scan without `dot` leaves them out.
- A scan doesn't follow symlinks: with the default `onlyFiles` a symlink to a file isn't listed, `onlyFiles: false` lists symlinks, and a pattern that names a symlinked folder (`linked/*.ts`) lists inside it. `followSymlinks` is still an unsupported option and throws.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `packages/core/test/tool-execute.test.ts`: the flag and `import ... from "bun"`, reads and slices and a missing file, writes (including `createPath: false`, a rejected `mode`, and a writer), glob options, the permissions asked, and denied permissions changing nothing.
- `packages/core/test/tool-registry.test.ts`: `Bun` missing without `full_codemode` and present with it.
- `packages/core/test/file-mutation.test.ts`: `append` adds exact bytes and creates a missing file.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, the tests above, the environment conformance suite, `packages/util` and `packages/codemode` tests, and `bun run check` from the root pass.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(browser): hand off passkey sign-in to the system browser
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #60191 — the passkey/security-key hang this turns into an explicit, consented handoff. #63002 takes the wider signed-in-pane direction; how this fits alongside it is covered in the review reply.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Sign-in that needs a passkey, security key, or SSO hangs in the in-app browser (#60191): GitHub sudo mode's "Use passkey", Cloudflare → Google SSO. The pane has no platform authenticator — Electron services none until `configureWebAuthn()`, its Touch ID path makes app-scoped credentials in a per-attachment partition, and using existing iCloud Keychain passkeys needs associated domains or Apple's managed web-browser entitlement, which OpenCode can't hold. Evidence and rejected alternatives: `packages/plugin-browser/docs/passkeys.md`.

`browser.handoff({ tabID })` is the escape hatch. Nothing opens on the agent's word: the pane shows a banner with the page's URL and an **Open** button, and `shell.openExternal` fires only on that click. The banner then waits for **Done** or **Cancel** (10 minutes; the server's backstop is 12) and the tool resolves `{ state: "completed" | "cancelled" | "timedOut", host }`. The pane stays signed out on purpose — inheriting the session would mean copying its cookies. Work that needs the sign-in stays with the user in the system browser.

Manual checks (both need a real credential step):

1. `github.com/settings/tokens` → Generate new token (classic) → sudo mode → Use passkey: the handoff opens the page in the default browser after the user clicks **Open**; **Done** resolves `{ state: "completed", host: "github.com" }` and the pane stays signed out.
2. `dash.cloudflare.com` → Google SSO → passkey/security-key step: same flow.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/gui-plugins/src/browser/handoff.test.ts` — nothing opens before the user's **Open**; one launch even on a double click; Done/Cancel/timeout/abort/tab-close/binding-close each settle exactly once; non-web and credential-bearing URLs are refused; results are `{ state, host }` only; launch errors never echo the URL. `connection.test.ts` — the banner's answers reach main with `{ binding, id, action }`. `plugin-browser/test/rpc.test.ts` — the output schema and the search terms. A banner story in `packages/app/component-tests/browser-pane.spec.ts` walks pending → **Open** → opened → **Done** → completed through the real model. `bun run check` passes repo-wide. The two `tunnel.test.ts` failures on my machine also fail on pristine `dev` (local TCP/proxy environment).

### Screenshots / recordings

Before, asking (nothing has opened yet), opened, finished:

| Before | Asking |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://github.com/wra-sol/opencode/releases/download/handoff-screenshots/handoff-before.png) | ![pending](https://github.com/wra-sol/opencode/releases/download/handoff-screenshots/handoff-pending.png) |

| Opened | Finished |
| --- | --- |
| ![opened](https://github.com/wra-sol/opencode/releases/download/handoff-screenshots/handoff-opened.png) | ![completed](https://github.com/wra-sol/opencode/releases/download/handoff-screenshots/handoff-completed.png) |

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR


---

releases.body:
### Highlights

- **GPT-6.2 Prompt Caching**: GPT-6.2 models don't cache a system prompt sent in the Responses `instructions` field, so every step re-billed it as uncached input. OpenCode now sends it as a leading developer message on every Responses route, including OpenAI (API key and ChatGPT sign-in), GitHub Copilot, Zen, Azure and OpenRouter, so it is cached from the second step on. ([#64542](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64542), [#64544](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64544))

### Core

#### Bug fixes

- Fixed GPT-6.2 models re-billing the system prompt as uncached input on every step. On GitHub Copilot `gpt-6.2-sol`, uncached input per step dropped from about 14,000 tokens to 3. Compaction through `/responses/compact` now reads the same cached prefix. ([#64542](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64542), [#64544](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64544))
- `webfetch` structured output no longer repeats the `url` and `format` it was called with. ([#64534](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64534))

releases.name: v2.3.1
releases.body:
### Highlights

- **Timed-Out Shell Commands Keep Running**: A shell command still running when its timeout expires now moves to the background instead of being killed, so long builds and test runs finish and report back. A foreground `timeout: 0` now means the default 120 seconds. ([#63699](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63699))
- **Compaction Without the Wait**: As a session nears automatic compaction, the summary is now written in the background, so your next prompt doesn't pause for it. Set `compaction.background: false` to turn it off; a background summary that ends up unused still costs tokens. ([#64290](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64290))
- **GPT 6.2 with ChatGPT Sign-In**: GPT 6.2 Sol and GPT 6.2 Astra, plus their fast variants, now show up in the model picker when you sign in with ChatGPT. ([#64508](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64508))
- **Update Plugins from Settings**: Open **Settings › Extensions**, click **Check for updates**, then **Update** on any plugin with a new version. ([#64511](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64511))
- **Comment on Selected Code**: Selecting code in diff and file viewers now just selects it, so you can copy it, and an **Add comment** toolbar appears beside the selection. ([#64410](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64410))

### Core

#### Improvements

- Shell commands still running when their timeout expires now move to the background instead of being killed, in every build. The `shell_timeout_background` flag is gone; configs that still set it keep loading. A foreground `timeout: 0` now uses the default 120 second timeout instead of waiting until the command exits. ([#63699](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63699))
- Background compaction is now on by default: as a session nears automatic compaction, the summary is written in the background so the next prompt doesn't wait for it. Turn it off with `compaction.background: false`; a background summary that is never used still costs tokens. The `experimental.background_compaction` setting is removed. ([#64290](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64290))
- OpenCode again reads `CLAUDE.md` in any directory that has no `AGENTS.md`, and falls back to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when the global `AGENTS.md` is missing. This also applies to instructions found when the agent reads nested files. Set `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE` or `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT` to skip every `CLAUDE.md`. ([#64474](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64474), [#64533](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64533))
- Added GPT 6.2 Sol and GPT 6.2 Astra, plus their fast variants, to the ChatGPT model list. ([#64508](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64508))
- `websearch` now returns a flat list of results, each with its `url`, `title`, `content` and `published` date. ([#64471](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64471))
- Code Mode and plugins get a simpler structured result from `read`: `text` (with `offset`, `lineCount` and `next`), `directory` (entry names) or `media` (a URI instead of base64). What the model sees is unchanged. ([#64361](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64361))
- Code Mode programs can use Node's `Buffer` for encoding and decoding bytes. ([#64365](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64365))
- In Code Mode, `search("issues")` now works as shorthand for `search({ query: "issues" })`. ([#64347](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64347))
- Code Mode tool summaries in the catalog can now be up to 500 characters instead of 120, so the model sees more of each tool's description. ([#64341](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64341))
- The `glob` and `grep` tools now report a malformed filename glob (for example `[`) as an error that names the parameter to fix, instead of returning no results. ([#63960](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63960))
- Server requests that crash now return a 500 with a readable JSON `UnknownError` body instead of an empty one. Storage problems name the cause (for example "Storage is full" or "Storage is read-only"); other crashes include a `ref` you can find in the server log. ([#64022](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64022))
- The shell tool description now tells the model that its session ID is in the `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` environment variable. ([#63718](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63718))
- Experimental schedules are now automations, behind the `automations` flag (the old `schedules` flag still works). An automation runs on a time, an interval, a cron or a pushed MCP event, and either sends a prompt (to the creating session, another session or a new subagent) or runs a Code Mode program that decides whether to send one. Use `/automation` or the `automation_*` tools. Active or paused plain prompt schedules carry over; schedules with a condition or run limit, and finished ones, are dropped. ([#64160](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64160))

#### Bug fixes

- Fixed finished shell commands leaving zombie processes under `opencode-pty`. The process daemon now cleans each command up when it exits. Background processes started by a successful command (`cmd &`) keep running, and a failed command's leftovers are stopped. ([#64266](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64266), [#64251](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64251))
- Fixed ChatGPT and OpenAI subscription logins losing their sharing-limit safeguards and context caps when a token refresh failed. ([#64470](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64470))
- Fixed Claude Agent models falling back to a 200K context window when Claude Code adds or renames a model. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#64107](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64107))
- Fixed requests being rejected after switching models mid-session on OpenAI-compatible providers. Models that declare a different reasoning field (such as `reasoning_content`) no longer receive `reasoning_details` from earlier turns. ([#64243](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64243))
- Rejecting a permission request now rejects only the other pending requests from the same step, not every pending request in the session. ([#64343](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64343))
- Fixed a finished subagent being reported to its parent as still running when its answer quoted the "Background work still running" heading. ([#64026](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64026))
- Fixed ACP clients missing turns that a background shell woke after the original turn ended. ([#64262](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64262))
- Reading a small text file now applies the default line and byte limits, so a short file with very many lines is paged instead of returned whole. ([#63810](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63810))
- Paged reads that select a single blank line now return that line instead of an empty result. ([#63809](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63809))
- `read` now rejects `limit: 0` with "Limit must be a positive integer". ([#63808](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63808))
- Text files that start with `BM` are no longer mistaken for BMP images, and only real `GIF87a`/`GIF89a` headers count as GIFs, so these files read as text again. ([#63822](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63822), [#63811](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63811))
- Fixed shell output pages, grep previews, generated titles, read lines and shell output tails splitting emoji and other multi-byte characters, which showed up as `�`. ([#63984](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63984), [#63967](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63967))
- Shell commands using unknown ANSI-C escapes such as `$'\q'` are now read the same way Bash and Zsh read them, so permission rules can match them. ([#64263](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64263))
- Session title search is now case-insensitive for non-ASCII letters, such as Cyrillic and accented text. ([#64259](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64259))
- Fixed `grep` results being dropped when a matching line or path is not valid UTF-8. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62249](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62249))
- The `@` file picker now finds files in hidden folders such as `.github/` and dotfiles such as `.env.example` when file search uses ripgrep (the default on Windows and outside git repos). `.git` and gitignored files stay excluded. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62577](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62577))
- An unreachable well-known integration source is now skipped instead of dropping every well-known source. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62578](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62578))
- A corrupt cached project ID is now ignored instead of being used. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62576](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62576))
- Plugin tool renames from `tool.execute.before` now apply to calls inside Code Mode programs, and a renamed call returns the new tool's structured result. ([#63633](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63633), [#64333](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64333))
- In Code Mode, calling a tool that doesn't exist now returns a rejected promise, so `.catch` and `Promise.allSettled` can handle it instead of the whole script failing. ([#64510](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64510))
- A Code Mode program that only logs no longer shows a stray `null` line before its logs. ([#64344](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64344))

### TUI

#### Improvements

- Permission prompts from a subagent, and from that subagent's own subagents, now appear while you view the subagent's session. Prompts also show in front of an open composer. ([#64343](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64343))
- The export dialog under the new designs can save to the system temp directory as well as the project folder. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62490](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62490))
- Removed time to first token (ttft) from the assistant message footer. Tokens per second still shows when `session.tps` is on. ([#63759](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63759))

#### Bug fixes

- When another TUI sharing your tabs closes the session you're viewing, closing it here now moves to the neighbouring tab. ([#64261](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64261))
- Fixed broken characters at the edges of the shell output viewer and the inline shell display when output is long. ([#63967](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63967), [#63984](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63984))

### Desktop

#### Improvements

- You can check for and install plugin package updates from **Settings › Extensions**. Use **Check for updates** to look for new versions, then click **Update** on any plugin that has one. ([#64511](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64511), [#64525](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64525))
- Selecting code in diff and file viewers now just selects text, so you can copy it. An **Add comment** toolbar appears next to the selection to comment on those lines; line numbers and the gutter `+` still start a comment directly. ([#64410](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64410))
- Cmd+F (Ctrl+F) now finds text in Markdown, Mermaid, CSV and HTML previews in the side panel, using the same find bar as the code view. ([#63663](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63663))
- Disconnecting a provider or removing an account in **Settings → Providers** now asks for confirmation first. Disconnecting OpenCode Console says how many providers will stop working. ([#64212](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64212))
- The model picker's variant flyout now follows the keyboard: it opens beside the highlighted row, `→` enters it to pick a variant or toggle Favorite, and `←` or `Escape` goes back. A model's Console budget and reset time now show in the flyout. ([#64409](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64409), [#64423](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64423))
- When **New worktree** is selected for a new session, the composer shows the base branch (`from dev ▾`). Click it to pick another base; the choice applies immediately, and **Use main checkout** switches back. ([#64228](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64228))
- Redesigned the folder picker for remote servers, with a path bar, up to three recent-project pills plus a **More projects** menu, and a search box that shows the selected folder. ([#64241](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64241))
- ` ```latex ` and ` ```math ` code fences now render as display math once complete. ([#64380](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64380))
- The new icon set is now the default, and the **New icons** experiment has been removed. ([#64466](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64466), [#64451](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64451))
- The copy button under assistant messages is now always visible. Message metadata still appears on hover. ([#64478](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64478))
- Text files opened in side-panel tabs now have the same copy and download actions as other files. ([#64463](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64463))
- **Manage models** now shows every provider as a card with a `⋯` menu, whether or not you're signed in to OpenCode Console. ([#64235](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64235))
- The connect provider dialog has a cleaner layout for every sign-in step: breadcrumbs, method icons, full-width device codes, and a "Signing in from another device?" row for pasting a redirect URL. ([#63829](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63829))
- **Collapse long messages** is no longer experimental. It is now a setting under **Timeline** preferences. ([#64441](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64441))
- Settings now opens on your client preferences, which are listed first, pairing is grouped with Servers, and there's a **Help & feedback** link. ([#64440](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64440), [#64220](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64220))
- Automatic compactions now always show as a single quiet divider; manual and failed compactions still show the full record. ([#64290](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64290))
- Pairing QR codes can carry a server name, which becomes the paired server's default name. ([#64139](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64139))
- Image attachment thumbnails are larger, with a 3:2 crop, and a failed image no longer moves the message below it when retried. ([#64215](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64215))
- The Hex voice tip no longer appears when Hex is already installed, its copy now says what Hex is, and tips wait an hour after first launch before the first one shows. ([#64130](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64130), [#64131](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64131), [#63974](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63974), [#63760](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63760))

issues.title: External SIGTSTP stops pi without restoring the terminal, leaving mouse tracking armed at the shell prompt

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What happened?**

If pi is stopped by a `SIGTSTP` it did not send itself, it stops without restoring the terminal. Mouse tracking (SGR 1006/1002) and the kitty keyboard protocol stay enabled while the shell reads input, so a mouse movement over the terminal types an escape sequence like `ESC[<35;24;10M` into the shell's input line, and typed characters get escape codes appended. The shell runs each fragment as a command, so hundreds of `command not found` lines appear, and a typed command arrives shredded (`reset` becomes `5ureset`). The tab is unusable until the user closes it, or manages to send a terminal reset into a prompt that is being flooded.

Ctrl+Z inside pi is clean because `handleCtrlZ()` calls `ui.stop()` before `process.kill(0, "SIGTSTP")`. A stop from outside never reaches that code: nothing catches `SIGTSTP`, so the kernel stops the process with the modes armed.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In one terminal, run `pi -ne`. This reproduces with no extension loaded.
2. From another terminal, stop it externally: `kill -TSTP $(pgrep -n -x pi)`.
3. The shell prints `[1]+ Stopped pi` and takes the prompt back.
4. Move the mouse over the terminal, then type anything.

A mouse movement writes an escape sequence into the prompt line, and typed characters get escape codes appended. `kill -CONT` restores pi, but the shell line is already full of garbage.

**Expected behavior**

An external `SIGTSTP` restores the terminal exactly as Ctrl+Z does, and `SIGCONT` restarts the TUI.

**Version**

1.5.2, Linux. Present on 1.5.0 and on current `main`.

I want to fix this myself: catch `SIGTSTP` and restore the terminal the way `handleCtrlZ()` does before stopping. The stop needs `SIGSTOP`, because a caught `SIGTSTP` cannot stop the process afterwards. `SIGKILL` stays uncovered, since no JavaScript runs.

issues.title: [Windows] [sink-thread] How do you use Pi on windows? What issues are you seeing?
issues.body:
## Motivation

There are gazzilion developers on windows. Some use pi. Many could use pi. There are however too many ways pi can be run on windows and as such it is hard to know where to focus energy (fixing bugs, having best docs, having out of box) vs what ways can be delegated out of core to extensions. 

## Ways to run pi on WIndows:

- Pi runs on windows, uses git bash (default)
- Pi runs on windows, uses wsl bash (?semi-automatic fallback)
- Pi runs fully on windows with pwsh.exe/powershell.exe bash replacement (only plugins?)
- Pi runs fully in wsl2

## Issues seen:

All of these have some papercuts. Windows/wsl bash suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7064, Windows/*  suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7427, Windows/git-bash suffers from git bash being iffy and e.g. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6817 (among some closed). Full wsl2 has least amount of problems but might not be feasible due to compliance + still pi uses wrong keybidnings for copy/paste images with WT/allactitty. Running fully natively on windows/powershell isn't easy even with plugins as bash tool cannot be easily replaced (just shadowed; ie same name) and not all shell invocations can be hooked (RPC, ...).

## Call to action:
As such, I'd like to ask: how do you use pi on windows? Why this particular way and not any of other of the abovementioned ones? If you use some plugins, why and which ones? What's missing? What's challenging? What UX gaps are you seeing? 

Feel free to also link your other more specific issues.

issues.title: Resume drops all built-in tools when the session branch is truncated (orphan parentId after ENOSPC)
issues.body:
**Version:** `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0 (latest release at the time of writing), Windows. Anthropic provider, several extensions (pi-hashline-edit-pro, @ff-labs/pi-fff, @tintinweb/pi-subagents, pi-mcp-adapter). `defaultTools`: `read, bash, powershell, edit, write, grep, find, ls, codemode, tool_search`.

### What happened

1. In a long session the disk filled up. `appendFileSync` in the session persist path (`dist/core/session-manager.js:812`) threw ENOSPC for one entry. `_appendEntry` (`session-manager.js:815-819`) had already put that entry into `byId` and `leafId`, so the process kept running, and the next persisted entry references a parent id that is not in the file. In my file entry `49231a1f` has `parentId: "29d71f0c"`, which does not exist, and carries `errorMessage: "ENOSPC: no space left on device, write"`.
2. After later restarts, `getBranch()` (`session-manager.js:1062-1072`) walks from the leaf and stops at that orphan. The branch no longer contains the initial system message with the full tool loadout, only three later system patch messages.
3. `_restoreToolsFromTranscript` (`dist/core/agent-session.js:1389-1412`) rebuilds the loadout only from the system messages on the branch (`getCurrentTools(systemMessages)`), and excludes built-in tools from the "new tools" (`!this._baseToolDefinitions.has(name)`, line 1405). The comment on line 1404 says "Built-in tools follow `defaultTools` instead", but `defaultTools` is not applied on this path. The `compaction.systemMessage` checkpoints on the branch, which still declared `read`/`bash`, are not consulted (comment, lines 1391-1392).
4. Result: on the first prompt after the restart, Pi persisted a system message whose `toolsRemoved` lists `read, bash, powershell, write, grep, find, ls, codemode, tool_search`. Only extension tools stayed active. The next compaction checkpointed the reduced set. Because the removal is now recorded, a plain restart and `/reload` keep these tools inactive ("Removed tools stay inactive", line 1399). The model silently lost its shell and file reading in the middle of a long session.

### Expected

Any of:
- seed the restore from the latest `compaction.systemMessage` on the branch, which holds the full loadout;
- when the branch has no initial/full declaration, fall back to `defaultTools` for built-ins, as the comment on line 1404 says;
- surface and retry persist failures, or detect an orphaned `parentId` on load instead of silently truncating the branch.

### Workaround

From reading the code, not verified yet: `pi --session <id> --tools +read,+bash,+powershell,+write,+grep,+find,+ls,+codemode,+tool_search`. `applyToolModifiers` runs after the replay (`agent-session.js:1407`), and a list of only `+name` entries modifies the default selection (`docs/cli.md`, `--tools`).

### Related

#11376 (removing an initial tool mid-session), #10785 (tool restore on resume).
