issues.title: Crash on cancelling a read during file open

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

When a read tool call is cancelled while opening or statting a local file, Pi can exit with an uncaught AbortError.

I encountered this when a codemode script used Promise.all to run multiple tools. One read failed because its file didn’t exist,
so codemode cancelled the other pending reads. Pi then crashed:

```text
  pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
  AbortError: The operation was aborted
      at ReadStream.Readable (node:internal/streams/readable:352:7)
      at new ReadStream (node:internal/fs/streams:227:3)
      at FileHandle.createReadStream (node:internal/fs/promises:362:12)
      at Object.readLocalFileChunks
      at async selectLinesFromStream
```

readLocalFileChunks can pass an already-aborted signal to handle.createReadStream(), resulting in an unhandled stream error event.

PR #11906 describes the same failure

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Pi with codemode enabled.

2. Ask Pi to execute this codemode script, replacing existing-file-1 and existing-file-2 with readable text files:

   ```js
     const results = await Promise.all([
       tools.read({ path: "this-file-does-not-exist", offset: null, limit: null }),
       tools.read({ path: "existing-file-1", offset: null, limit: null }),
       tools.read({ path: "existing-file-2", offset: null, limit: null }),
     ]);
     results.forEach(text);
   ```

3. Repeat if necessary. The missing-file read rejects, causing codemode to cancel the other reads. If cancellation lands while one
   is opening or statting its file, Pi exits with an uncaught AbortError.


### Expected behavior

Cancellation should return a tool error without terminating Pi.

### Version

1.5.0

issues.title: openai: ChatGPT sign-in still uses 272K for GPT-6.1 Sol despite 500K account catalog
issues.body:
### What happened?

With `openai` authenticated through **Sign in with ChatGPT**, Pi 1.3.0 reports a 272K context window for `gpt-6.1-sol`, although the same account's live model catalog reports a 500K default. This gives Pi a smaller context/compaction budget than the server advertises.

An authenticated `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` using the stored `openai` OAuth access token returned HTTP 200 and:

```json
{"slug":"gpt-6.1-sol","context_window":500000,"max_context_window":872000}
```

This is an account-specific catalog check, not an inference test above 272K. [OpenAI's documentation](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference) directs this sign-in flow to use `/v1/models` for the account's current catalog.

Related: #10840 and commit 5712b134e corrected `openai-codex` to 500K, but left `openai` at 272K. The static short-context pricing cap also applies when `openai` uses subscription OAuth, not an API key.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to `openai` through Sign in with ChatGPT.
2. Run `pi -ne --no-mcp --list-models gpt-6.1-sol`:

```text
provider  model        context  max-out  thinking  images
openai    gpt-6.1-sol  272K     128K     yes       yes
```

3. With the same OAuth access token, query `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` and inspect the entry whose `slug` is `gpt-6.1-sol`. The tested account returns `context_window: 500000`.

### Expected behavior

For ChatGPT subscription authentication, use the account's advertised default context window (500K here), rather than inheriting the API-key pricing cap. This report does not request a blanket change to API-key defaults or use of the separate 872K maximum.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Session: an idle second Pi instance appends with a stale leaf, forking the session tree (resume then lands on the empty branch)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

Two Pi processes can open the same session file. Each keeps its own `leafId` from load time. When the idle one appends an entry later (e.g. an extension writing state on `session_shutdown`), the entry is parented to the *stale* leaf instead of the file's current end, so it becomes a sibling of the branch that actually continued the conversation.

Because Pi resumes at the **last entry of the JSONL file** (`SessionManager._buildIndex()` sets `leafId` to the last entry), that stray entry becomes the resume position: the session opens on a 1-entry branch and the conversation looks lost until the user navigates in `/tree`.

There is no locking and no leaf re-validation: `appendCustomEntry()` writes with `parentId: this.leafId` and there is no `flock`/`O_EXCL`/lockfile in `session-manager.js`, nor any doc note about running two instances on one session.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| pi (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`) | 1.5.2 |
| Node | v26.13.1 |
| OS | macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), Ghostty + tmux |

## Reproduction (deterministic, no third-party extension)

`/tmp/leafprobe/probe.ts`:

```ts
import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";

export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) {
  pi.on("session_start", async (_event, ctx) => {
    pi.appendEntry("probe-start", { leafAtStart: ctx.sessionManager.getLeafId() });
  });
  pi.on("session_shutdown", async (_event, ctx) => {
    pi.appendEntry("probe-shutdown", { leafAtShutdown: ctx.sessionManager.getLeafId() });
  });
}
```

All steps use `pi -ne -e /tmp/leafprobe/probe.ts --session-id repro1` so no other extension interferes:

1. `pi ... --session-id repro1 -p "erste nachricht"` — creates the session.
2. Start instance **A** interactively on the same session, then leave it idle (no prompts).
3. From another shell, run `pi ... --session-id repro1 -p "zweite nachricht"` (instance **B**) so the conversation advances.
4. Quit instance **A** with `/quit`.

## Resulting JSONL (13 entries, trimmed)

```
probe-start    73e3436b  parent 5d73b760  {leafAtStart: 5d73b760}
message        6e0af459  parent 73e3436b  system
message        ed9e8ea5  parent 6e0af459  user          <- first run
message        551f8299  parent ed9e8ea5  assistant
probe-shutdown c1329db3  parent 551f8299  {leafAtShutdown: 551f8299}
probe-start    277eaf83  parent c1329db3  {leafAtStart: c1329db3}   <- A loads here
probe-start    da9af869  parent 277eaf83  {leafAtStart: 277eaf83}   <- B loads here
message        9e09a77a  parent da9af869  user          <- B
message        ff459937  parent 9e09a77a  assistant
probe-shutdown 7e0e037f  parent ff459937  {leafAtShutdown: ff459937}  <- B quits: correct parent
probe-shutdown af0e234f  parent 277eaf83  {leafAtShutdown: 277eaf83}  <- A quits: STALE parent
```

* Branch point: `277eaf83` now has two children — the conversation (`da9af869`) and A's shutdown entry (`af0e234f`).
* A reports `leafAtShutdown: 277eaf83`, i.e. **A's load-time leaf**, not the file's current end (`ff459937`).
* `af0e234f` is the **last line of the file**, so the next resume (`_buildIndex()` → `leafId` = last entry) opens the session on that 1-entry orphan branch.

## Code pointers

- `appendCustomEntry()` — `parentId: this.leafId` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts`, around the `append*Entry` helpers).
- `_buildIndex()` — `this.leafId = entry.id` for every entry, so a resume starts at the last line.
- No lock acquisition around the session file anywhere in `session-manager.js` (verified: no `flock`, `O_EXCL`, or lockfile usage).

## Why it matters in practice

The writing extension does not have to be exotic. In my sessions, `@narumitw/pi-plan-mode` appends `plan-mode-state` on `session_shutdown`; an idle second instance therefore produced phantom branches in 4 of 41 session files (10 branch points, 2 of them leaving the file leaf on a 1-entry branch). That package now mitigates its own duplicates ([narumiruna/pi-extensions#1926](https://github.com/narumiruna/pi-extensions/issues/1926), PR [#1932](https://github.com/narumiruna/pi-extensions/pull/1932)), but the underlying behaviour affects **every** extension that appends custom entries — the reproduction above has no plan mode at all.

## Suggested fixes (any one prevents the corruption)

1. **Refresh before append:** in `appendCustomEntry()` (and the other `append*` helpers), if the session is persisted, read the last entry id from the file (or the file's size/mtime) and update `leafId` before writing. A stale cursor then self-heals instead of forking.
2. **Detect and warn:** compare the cached leaf against the file's last entry; on mismatch, log a diagnostic and skip the append rather than writing a sibling.
3. **Lock or refuse:** take an advisory lock (or `O_EXCL` marker) on the session file and warn the second instance that the session is already open elsewhere.

## Relation to #8525

Closed as not planned, and the same stale-cursor root cause — but that report was about an *abort interleaving inside one process*, which was hard to minimize. This one is deterministic, needs two `pi` invocations, and requires no abort. If running two instances on one session is intentionally unsupported, a startup check with a clear message would already help; today the second instance silently corrupts the tree.

Happy to test a patch against the reproduction above.

issues.title: Thinking scale has no `ultra`, and `:ultra` is parsed as part of the model id

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happens

Pi 1.5.2 has no `ultra` level in its thinking scale (`off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max`). An OpenAI-compatible gateway can advertise `ultra` in `capabilities.effort_tiers` (e.g. a Codex model whose tiers are `["low","medium","high","xhigh","max","ultra"]`), and Pi cannot select it.

Passing it is parsed as part of the model id:

```
$ pi -p --model "omniroute/codex/gpt-6.1-sol:ultra" "say ok"
Warning: Model "codex/gpt-6.1-sol:ultra" not found for provider "omniroute". Using custom model id.
omniroute API error (400): Model 'gpt-6.1-sol:ultra' is not available in the active live catalog for provider 'codex'.
```

So `ultra` is unreachable, and the error message points at the model name, which is misleading.

### Expected

Either add `ultra` to the scale (`max` is currently the top) or reject `:ultra` as an unknown thinking level instead of treating it as part of the model id.

### Why it matters

The gateway exposes `ultra` for at least one model we use daily, and because Pi's models.json cannot express it, the level silently disappears in the picker.

issues.title: compaction.modelOverrides are ignored for the routed model when a virtual model is selected

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

I have a router extension that registers a virtual model (`hybrid/auto`) and routes between Qwen3.8-27B (131K window) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (64K window). While setting up per-model compaction settings for it, I traced how Pi resolves them and found something that looked a bit off.

Compaction takes the context window from the routed model, but reads `reserveTokens` and `keepRecentTokens` from `this.model`, which is the virtual model. So an override keyed by the physical model never applies. Here's `_exceedsCompactionThreshold` on main (5f89cc0):

```ts
return shouldCompact(
	estimateProjectedContextTokens(projection, this.sessionManager.getBranch()).tokens,
	model.contextWindow,                                    // routed model
	this.settingsManager.getCompactionSettings(this.model), // virtual model
);
```

`prepareRequest` passes `route.model` in as `model`, so a single call ends up mixing the two. The same `this.model` lookup happens in `_checkCompaction` (line 3122), manual compaction (line 2946) and `_runAutoCompaction` (line 3268).

This looks related to #12035, which hits the same `_checkCompaction` path, but for the window instead of the settings.

### Steps to reproduce

I worked these out from the code and haven't run them as a standalone repro yet.

1. In `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, set `compaction.reserveTokens` to 16384 and `compaction.modelOverrides["<provider>/<physical-model>"]` to `{ "reserveTokens": 4096 }`.
2. Load an extension that registers a virtual model whose `route()` always returns that physical model, and select it.
3. Fill the context. Compaction triggers at `contextWindow - 16384`.

### Expected behavior

Compaction triggers at `contextWindow - 4096`, the override for the model that actually serves the request.

I think the fix is to read the settings from the `model` argument in `_exceedsCompactionThreshold`, and from `_limitsModel()` in the other three. `routedModel` is only set after the first response though, so `prepareRequest` would need to pass `route.model` through to `_runAutoCompaction`.

For now I'm keying the override by the virtual model name (`hybrid/auto`), which does work. Let me know your thoughts!

### Version

1.5.2

issues.title: pi-ai: wire stream timeoutMs on google-vertex and classify mid-stream ECONNRESET / timeout aborts as retryable
issues.body:
## Summary

While running multi-turn coding agent evaluations on `google-vertex` (`@earendil-works/pi-ai@1.5.2` + `@earendil-works/pi-durable@1.5.2`), we found three related issues in `pi-ai` that cause stalled or reset Vertex AI streams to either hang indefinitely or fail without triggering `retryAssistantCall` / Pi Durable's `GenerationTask` retry loop:

### 1. `google-vertex` (and `google-generative-ai`) ignores `options.timeoutMs`
- `StreamOptions` / `SimpleStreamOptions` (and `pi-durable`'s `HarnessSettings.stream.timeoutMs`) pass `timeoutMs` into `stream` / `streamSimple`.
- However, `packages/ai/src/api/google-vertex.ts` (`buildParams`) never reads `options.timeoutMs`, nor does the `for await (const chunk of googleStream)` loop enforce a per-chunk idle timeout.
- When Vertex AI stalls mid-SSE stream (especially after a transient connection drop under load), `for await (const chunk of googleStream)` hangs indefinitely until the caller's outer process/task timeout kills the entire run.

### 2. Timeout aborts via `config.abortSignal` are not classified as retryable
- If a caller attaches `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` to `config.abortSignal` (via `onPayload` / `beforeProviderRequest`), `@google/genai` catches the abort and throws `Error: This operation was aborted` (stripping `TimeoutError`).
- If `options.signal` itself is aborted by a timeout, `google-vertex.ts` sets `output.stopReason = options?.signal?.aborted ? "aborted" : "error"`, which is treated as a user cancellation and never retried.
- Even when `stopReason === "error"`, `"This operation was aborted"` does not match `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`, so `isRetryableAssistantError` returns `false`.

### 3. Bare `ECONNRESET` / `EPIPE` / `ETIMEDOUT` error strings in `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN`
- `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts` matches `"fetch failed"`, `"connection.?refused"`, and `"connection.?lost"`, but does not include `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `ETIMEDOUT`, or `ECONNABORTED`. When a mid-stream socket reset surfaces without the `fetch failed` prefix (e.g. `read ECONNRESET`), `isRetryableAssistantError` returns `false`.

## Proposed Fix
1. Enforce a per-chunk stream idle timeout from `options.timeoutMs` in `google-vertex` / `google-generative-ai` that aborts the underlying `@google/genai` request while recording `stopReason: "error"` and `errorMessage: "Request timed out after <N>ms"` (when the caller's own `options.signal` was not aborted).
2. Add `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `ETIMEDOUT`, and `ECONNABORTED` to `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`.

issues.title: OpenAI Decisions drops GA cache usage and uses zero cache rates

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

OpenAI Decisions GA cache usage is lost in `pi-ai`. [`parseClassifierUsage()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/5f89cc0a7df669813650bfdac498f8ff865e8233/packages/ai/src/api/classifier-shared.ts#L117-L130) sets both cache counters to zero. The bundled `gpt-6-luna` classifier also has zero cache prices, so cache telemetry and cost estimates are inaccurate. Choice classification itself succeeds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `Models.classify()` with `openai/gpt-6-luna` and an injected `options.fetch` returning a valid choice answer plus this usage:

```json
{
  "input_tokens": 2000, "output_tokens": 0,
  "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 1600, "cache_write_tokens": 100}
}
```

2. Inspect `result.usage`: it reports `input: 2000, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0` and cost `$0.0002`, treating everything as uncached input.

Reproduced directly through the SDK with synthetic auth/fetch, without the CLI, extensions or live API requests.

### Expected behavior

Preserve the cache-read/write counts without double-counting them in total input, and price them using the Decisions cache rates. [OpenAI's GA documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions#reuse-shared-input-with-prompt-caching) states that both counts are included in `input_tokens`; cache reads are discounted and writes are charged.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.5.2, Bun 1.4.4. The same usage parser is present on current `main` (`5f89cc0a`).

issues.title: Emit session_compact when boundary drafts (turn_end / agent_before_settle) commit a compaction

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What do you want to change?**

In `packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`, `_commitBoundaryDrafts()` appends compaction entries that come from extension boundary drafts (`turn_end` / `agent_before_settle`), but it only emits `entry_appended` — never `session_compact`, unlike `compact()` and `_runAutoCompaction()`.

Proposal: emit `session_compact` (`fromExtension: true`, `reason: "threshold"`, `willRetry: false`) for each committed compaction draft. The method becomes `async`, both call sites await it. Tests added in `test/suite/agent-session-boundaries.test.ts` (red before the fix, 32/32 green after, `tsc --noEmit` clean). Branch ready on my fork `SoulKyu:fix/emit-session-compact-on-boundary-drafts` (PR #12262 was auto-closed by the gate).

**Why?**

Extensions listening to `session_compact` to learn that the history was rewritten never hear about extension-driven compactions. Concrete case: `pi-claude-bridge` discards a parked provider query on `session_compact` (its fix for bridge issue #101, "one compaction per tool call, usage never dropping"). Without the event, the next tool result resumes the stale query, which answers from the pre-compaction conversation and reports pre-compaction usage (`cacheRead ≈ 886k` on a 1M window). The compaction threshold then re-triggers at every LLM step, each compaction summarizing only the delta since the previous one. Real session evidence: 60 compactions, all `fromHook: true`, `tokensBefore` stuck 886k→893k, only 2 message entries between consecutive compactions.

This is a core bug, not an extension bug — `pi-auto-compact` only exposes it through the boundary-draft path. Reproduced with pi's own compaction functions: with stale post-compaction usage the threshold re-triggers every step (~1.1k tokens summarized per compaction); with corrected usage one compaction suffices.

**How? (optional)**

Small diff in `agent-session.ts` (+21/−4): after `entry_appended`, if `entry.type === "compaction"` and handlers exist, `await this._extensionRunner.emit({ type: "session_compact", compactionEntry: entry, fromExtension: true, reason: "threshold", willRetry: false })`. Three new tests: `turn_end` draft, `agent_before_settle` draft, and a negative case (non-compaction drafts emit nothing).

I'd like to submit this as a PR once approved (lgtm). Version: pi 1.5.2.

issues.title: A tool call naming an unregistered tool never resolves, silently halting the agent's turn and leaking call framing to the TUI

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
> One caveat up front: the failure is confirmed by direct reproduction, twice, in two separate sessions, and the control case that isolates it to parse-or-not-parse is confirmed as well. What I could **not** do is name the exact function where the call-shaped text is discarded, because I did not instrument the provider parsing layer. The section "What I could not isolate" marks exactly where observation stops and inference begins.

## Summary

When a model emits a tool call whose name is present in the conversation but **absent from the session's tool schema**, the call is not recognized as a call at all. Three consequences follow, in this order:

1. **The agent's turn ends and the session goes idle.** No retry, no report, no continuation — the work simply stops at the point of the failed call and does not resume until a human notices and sends something. This is the part that costs real time, and it is what this report is primarily about.
2. The raw call framing is streamed as **assistant text**, so it appears on the user's screen.
3. Because nothing was dispatched, pi's correct and documented handling for unknown tools (`packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts:726-732`, which returns a clean `isError` result naming the tool) **never runs**. The same markup comes back to the model **as the tool result payload**, wrapped in an echo of the model's own preceding outgoing message — so the transcript feeds the agent its own text, labeled as tool output.

The net effect is a failure mode with no error in it, and therefore no continuation in it. A model that receives a readable "tool not found" corrects in one turn. A model that receives its own previous message back — with nothing stating that anything failed, and nothing indicating pending work — has nothing to act on, and stops.

This is worse than a confusing error, because it is **unbounded in wall-clock terms and invisible until someone looks**. The only reason the stall described below cost three minutes rather than the rest of an afternoon is that the operator runs an idle watcher that pages them after a fixed period of silence. Remove that watcher, or run the same agent headless overnight, and the failure mode becomes a silently abandoned task that looks exactly like a completed one.

Requested: two narrow guarantees, both about failure presentation rather than behavior.

- A tool call that fails to parse or resolve must produce a **model-readable error result** — the same shape `agent-loop.ts:726` already produces for a name that parses but does not resolve — **and the turn must continue**. Erroring is not only how the model learns to correct; it is what keeps the loop from terminating on a non-event.
- Call framing must **never render as assistant text**. If the harness could not parse it, the human should see a diagnostic, not the wire format.

I do not think the tool-resolution logic needs to change at all; as far as I can tell it is already correct.

## Environment

| Item         | Value                                                      |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| pi           | 1.5.2, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, npm global       |
| Source read  | `earendil-works/pi` @ `d78a75ecb` (`v1.5.2-95-gd78a75ecb`) |
| Host         | Pi coding agent, `tuiMode: "regular"`, Linux, node v24     |
| Session type | long-running agent session with extension-registered tools |
| Extensions   | third-party tool packages, via the extension mechanism     |

## Observed behavior

**Reproduction.** In a fresh session, invoke a tool whose name is not in the schema — any name will do, for example `some_registered_tool_typo`, with otherwise well-formed arguments. The result is not an error message. The result content returned to the model is its own previous assistant turn plus the literal serialized call:

```text
 <tool_call>
 <function=some_registered_tool_typo>
 <parameter=example_param>
 example value
 </parameter>
 </function>
 </tool_call>
```

The framing above is illustrative and lightly redacted; the structure is as observed. It appeared on the operator's screen, which is the only reason either of us knew the call had been attempted at all.

**Control.** Invoking a **registered** tool with deliberately invalid arguments produces a clean, readable error result and no markup anywhere. So argument validation, execution, and error conversion are all healthy — the divergence happens entirely before any of that, at the point where a call is or is not recognized.

That contrast is the whole finding: the defect tracks "was this parsed as a call," not "did the tool exist."

**The stall, described precisely.** After the call above, the agent's turn ended. The session sat idle with a task outstanding and nothing in the context to indicate otherwise. The operator, who had walked away expecting work to continue, learned of it only from an idle watcher that pages after roughly three minutes of silence, and had to send a message to get the agent moving again. On recovery the agent had no record of having failed: the last thing in its transcript was its own message echoed back, not an error.

Both incidents behind this report behaved this way. In the first, the same unresolvable call was attempted twice more before a workaround was found, and each attempt ended the turn again.

## Why the existing handling is not being reached

pi states the intended contract explicitly, and implements it. `agent-loop.ts:818`, on `runToolCall`:

```text
Never rejects for tool failures: unknown tools,
validation errors, blocked calls, and thrown errors
come back as `isError: true`.
```

and `prepareToolCall` at `:726-732` does exactly that for a name that misses the registry:

```ts
const tool = tools.find((t) => t.name === toolCall.name);
if (!tool) {
  return {
    kind: "immediate",
    result: createErrorToolResult(`Tool ${toolCall.name} not found`),
    isError: true,
  };
}
```

A call that reached this code would have produced a one-line, self-explanatory correction, the turn would have continued, and the incident would have cost nothing. The observed behavior — no error payload at all, and a turn that ends — is positive evidence that it did not get there. The `tools.find` never ran, because there was never a `toolCall` object.

One related path is worth naming so the next reader does not stop at the wrong file: `core/tools/index.ts:137` and `:160` throw `Unknown tool name: ${toolName}`, but those are inside `createTool` and `createToolDefinition`, a **startup factory keyed by core tool names**, not the runtime dispatch of a model-emitted call. Grepping for that string looks like the answer and is not it. Similarly, `packages/ai/src/utils/validation.ts:40` throws `Tool "…" not found`, which also presupposes a parsed call.

## Why it is worth fixing

- **The cost is unattended wall-clock time, and it has no upper bound.** A wrong result wastes a turn. A silently ended turn wastes every minute until a human happens to look. This is the only failure mode I encountered that costs *clock* rather than tokens, and it is the one that survives being noticed only by external monitoring.
- **It is hostile to exactly the use case pi is built for.** Headless, overnight, and long-running agent sessions are a primary reason this tool exists, and they are precisely the sessions where nobody is watching for a stall. An agent that stops without erroring is indistinguishable from an agent that finished.
- **It is the one failure mode in this layer that is invisible to the agent and alarming to the human.** Every other error path is designed to be instructive; this one is silent in one direction and noisy in the other. A user who sees internal wire format in their terminal loses trust in the tooling, not in the model.
- **The self-echo is worse than a display bug, and is the likely mechanism of the stall.** Returning the model's own outgoing text as tool output is a feedback path that contains no signal of failure or of remaining work.
- **Cost is asymmetric and unrecoverable from inside.** A clean `Tool X not found` is corrected in one turn. What was actually observed was repeated attempts with the same unresolvable name, a manual workaround, the operator interrupting to ask what the garbage was, and eventually an abandoned session.

## Proposed fixes

Any one of the first two closes the user-visible half; the third closes the agent-visible half; all three are subordinate to the first constraint below, which is the actual requirement.

| Option                           | Shape                                                                   |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A. Never render framing as text  | detect unresolved call-shaped output, suppress it, emit a one-line note |
| B. Route it through `:726`       | recognize the call, let the existing `Tool … not found` handle it       |
| C. Error result on parse failure | `isError: true` naming the tool, instead of echoing the transcript      |

Notes on the three, in the same order:

- **A** fixes the human-visible symptom on its own, independent of where in the parse layer the gap is.
- **B** reuses correct code that already exists and needs no new error copy. Preferred if the parse point is findable.
- **C** is the cheapest guaranteed floor, and it also implies suppressing the self-echo, which should never be a result payload.

Three constraints worth recording, whichever shape you pick:

- **A tool call that fails to parse or resolve must not end the turn silently.** Whatever the error text, the loop has to continue with an actionable signal in it. This is the requirement the report exists to make; the other two are secondary to it.
- **The result payload must not contain the model's own outgoing turn.** Even if nothing else changes, echoing the assistant message back as tool output is a distinct defect from the leak and worth fixing separately.
- **The error should name the tool and nothing else.** A model can recover from "`foo` is not an available tool" in one turn; it cannot recover from a paragraph, and long guidance text in a repeated failure gets truncated anyway.

## What I could not isolate

I did not find the code that discards the call, and I would rather report that than imply I did:

- I read `agent-loop.ts` and `core/tools/index.ts` and confirmed the runtime handling is correct and unreachable in this path, but I did **not** instrument the provider streaming/parsing layer to observe where the framing is treated as text.
- I did not test whether the behavior differs by provider or by transport (structured tool-call API versus a text-framed protocol). If it is specific to one adapter, that would narrow the fix considerably, and I would expect it to be the one where a name outside the advertised schema can appear at all.
- I did not test whether a correctly-parsed call to a name registered *after* session start behaves the same way. That is a related but separate question, and this report does not depend on its answer.

So: the **symptom, the control, and the fact that `:726` is bypassed** are observation. "The parse step is where it is lost" is a well-supported inference from the control case, not a located line of code. Likewise, the causal link between the echoed payload and the ended turn is inferred from the fact that the agent had no other reason to stop — the loop-exit decision itself was not observable from inside the session.

## Non-goals

I am not asking for changes to tool resolution, the registry, argument validation, or extension loading — all of which appear to work correctly. Not asking for retries, aliases, or fuzzy name matching, which would make a silent failure silent in a more expensive way. Not asking for automatic session revival or watchdog behavior from pi, which is a policy question for the operator's harness; the request here is only that a failed call be *reportable* rather than absent. Not asking for tool calls to become visible to the user by default; the request is that failures not leak their wire format, not that successes be displayed.

## Workaround in the meantime

Two, and neither is a fix.

**Against the stall:** monitor for silence, not for errors. There is nothing to alert on — the session exits cleanly and looks finished. An idle watcher that pages after a few minutes of inactivity is currently the only reliable detector, and any unattended run without one should be assumed capable of hanging indefinitely at this point.

**Against the trigger:** restart the session after any change to the installed tool set. A session resumed across a tool rename can hold a stale render of the profile and tool registry and keep advertising names that nothing on the machine registers — which is how the unresolvable name appeared in the first place. This sidesteps one cause; it does not address the failure mode, which will reproduce for any other reason a name and schema disagree.

issues.title: Concurrent pi processes race managed npm install on the shared project .pi/npm prefix (no install lock)
issues.body:
## Summary

When several pi processes run concurrently against the same project (e.g. a parent session that spawns parallel subagent child sessions), the managed-package reconciliation in `package-manager` can run `npm install --prefix <project>/.pi/npm` from multiple processes at once. The concurrent installs race on the shared install root; one process wins, the others die with a bare `failed with code N` spawn/install error.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (also reported on the same setup multiple times)
- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.0.4 (verified the same code path is unchanged in latest 1.1.0)
- Project-scoped npm package pinned to an exact version in `.pi/settings.json` `packages`

## What happened

Right after bumping the pinned version of a project package, two child pi processes were spawned concurrently in the same project. Each saw the installed copy not matching the pin (`resolvePackageSources` → `installedNpmMatchesConfiguredVersion` → false) and each executed:

```
npm install <pkg>@<version> --prefix <project>/.pi/npm --legacy-peer-deps
```

against the same install root. One finished normally; the other failed at spawn time with:

```
npm install <pkg>@<version> --prefix <project>/.pi/npm --legacy-peer-deps failed with code 190
```

Re-running the identical command manually right after reports `up to date` (exit 0) — the failure is a transient race, not a registry or pin problem.

Earlier occurrences of the same pattern on this setup: parallel subagent spawns dying with npm `ENOTEMPTY`/`EPERM` on the shared `node_modules` (Windows file locking), in one case leaving the install root corrupted.

## Root cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts` performs managed npm installs (`installNpm` / `installNpmBatch`, and the update path via `updateNpmBatch`) with no inter-process mutual exclusion on the install root. Any N concurrent pi processes sharing a project can race reconciliation whenever an install is genuinely needed — first session after a version bump, a missing package, or an unpinned-package update. Within one process the checks are sequential, but nothing serializes across processes.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Single-flight managed installs**: take an inter-process lock on the install root (e.g. a stale-pid-aware lockfile at `<installRoot>/.pi-install.lock`) around managed npm install/update. Waiters re-check `installedNpmMatchesConfiguredVersion` after acquiring the lock and skip the install if another process already satisfied it. This also makes the reconciliation idempotent under concurrency.
2. **Surface stderr in failures**: `runCommand` currently rejects with `... failed with code N` only. Including the tail of npm's stderr would let reporters distinguish network / lock / permission failures without manual reproduction.

## Impact / workaround

Multi-agent workflows that spawn several child sessions in parallel within one project (a common code-review setup) hit this probabilistically whenever a real install is pending. Current workarounds: spawn serially, or run one session first so reconciliation completes before spawning the rest.

issues.title: SDK embed: /login status line reports the global auth.json path when a custom agentDir is in use
issues.body:
### What happens

When pi is embedded through the SDK with a custom `agentDir` (and therefore a custom credential path), the status line after `/login` still reports the global one:

```
Saved API key for DeepSeek. Selected deepseek-v4-pro. Credentials saved to /home/<user>/.pi/agent/auth.json
```

The credential is actually written to the configured path. In my case it landed in `data/system/auth.json` (the custom `agentDir`) and `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` was left untouched, with an older mtime. So the write is right and only the message is wrong.

### Expected

The status line names the path the credentials were actually written to.

### Why

The message is built from `getAuthPath()`, which derives the path from the global agent dir and knows nothing about the session's runtime:

- `dist/config.js` `getAuthPath()` returns `join(getAgentDir(), "auth.json")`
- `dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js` prints `` `Credentials saved to ${getAuthPath()}` ``

A `ModelRuntime` can be created with its own `authPath`. `createAgentSessionServices` does exactly that for an embedded session, passing `join(agentDir, "auth.json")` when a custom `agentDir` is given.

### Repro

Embed the agent with a custom agent dir, open the TUI and run `/login`:

```ts
await createAgentSessionServices({
  cwd: process.cwd(),
  agentDir: join(ROOT, "data", "system"), // not ~/.pi/agent
});
```

The status line names `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`. The file that gains the entry is `data/system/auth.json`.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 0.85.1

### Impact

Cosmetic, no data loss. It does send people hunting in the wrong file when they debug credentials in an embedded setup, which is how I hit it.

issues.title: Google adapters reject Gemini 4 Hydrogen's advertised xhigh level

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

 Gemini 4 Hydrogen supports a fourth thinking level, xhigh (Google docs), and models.dev exposes it as low/medium/high/xhigh. A model whose
 thinkingLevelMap contains "xhigh": "xhigh" is therefore selectable via /thinking, but selecting it throws before any HTTP request is sent:

 **_Unsupported Google thinking level mapping for google/gemini-4-hydrogen: xhigh -> xhigh_**

 resolveGoogleThinkingLevel() in packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts only accepts minimal | low | medium | high, and ResolvedGoogleThinkingLevel excludes xhigh/max. Both google-generative-ai and google-vertex go through this resolver. This is reproducible directly in the adapter, with no extension loaded and no network access.

### Steps to reproduce

```
import { resolveGoogleThinkingLevel } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/google-shared";

const model = {
  provider: "google",
  id: "gemini-4-hydrogen",
  api: "google-generative-ai",
  reasoning: true,
  thinkingLevelMap: {
    low: "low",
    medium: "medium",
    high: "high",
    xhigh: "xhigh",
    max: null,
  },
  input: ["text"],
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
  contextWindow: 1048576,
  maxTokens: 65536,
};

resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, "xhigh");
// Error: Unsupported Google thinking level mapping for google/gemini-4-hydrogen: xhigh -> xhigh
```
 The same mapping is what a models.dev sync writes into a custom Google provider, and what models.json accepts for a model override.

### Expected behavior

 xhigh should resolve to XHIGH and be sent as thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel: "XHIGH" for both Google adapters. Models that do not declare
 thinkingLevelMap.xhigh should keep the current behavior. The existing google-thinking-level-map test, which only allows extended levels to map down to high, needs updating for Hydrogen.

### Version

1.5.2. The same resolver is still present on main, which pins @google/genai 2.32.0. @google/genai 3.3.0 added the native ThinkingLevel.XHIGH  enum.

issues.title: Stray OSC color-query reply injected as input; trailing BEL auto-triggers Ctrl+G external editor (pi freezes waiting for invisible notepad)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

 ## Environment
  - pi 1.5.2 (latest per npm), package @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
  - Node v24.14.1
  - Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC (10.0.19044)
  - Terminal: mintty (Git Bash / MINGW64, TERM=xterm)
  - No `externalEditor` setting, no `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` set

  ## What happened
  Without pressing anything, pi suddenly prints:

  ```
  Launching external editor: notepad
  Pi will resume when the editor exits.
  ```

  The TUI stops and pi appears frozen. No editor window is visible to the user
  (it opens behind the terminal / in the taskbar). Killing pi leaves an orphaned
  `%TEMP%\pi-editor-*` directory behind (the `finally` cleanup never runs).

  This happened 6 times over ~24h, always shortly after starting pi:
  2026-11-16 16:50, 2026-11-17 15:02, 15:46, 15:48, 15:49, 16:14 (UTC+8).
  The 15:46–15:49 cluster is three consecutive pi restarts hitting it again.

  ## Root cause (evidence)
  Every orphaned `%TEMP%\pi-editor-*/prompt.md` contains exactly the same 21 bytes:

  ```
  ;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000
  ```

  That is the literal tail of an **OSC 4 palette reply** `\x1b]4;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000\x07`
  with the `ESC]4` prefix consumed. pi sends this query burst at startup:

  ```
  TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY = \x1b]10;?\x07  \x1b]11;?\x07  (\x1b]4;{i};?\x07 × 16)  \x1b[c
  ```

  When one of the replies arrives **after pi has stopped reading replies**, the input
  parser apparently treats it as typed input:
  1. `ESC]4` is discarded as an unrecognized escape sequence,
  2. the remaining payload `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000` is inserted into the editor as text,
  3. the terminating **BEL (0x07)** is dispatched as **Ctrl+G** — the default binding of
     `app.editor.external` — which opens the external editor automatically with the
     junk text as the draft.

  `handleOpenExternalEditor()` then stops the UI, writes the draft to a temp file, and
  spawns `cmd /c notepad <file>`, awaiting its exit. Since the user never sees the
  notepad window, pi looks dead until it is killed.

  ## Expected behavior
  - Terminal replies that arrive outside the query-response window should be swallowed
    (complete OSC/CSI sequences dropped), not have their payload inserted as editor text.
  - A stray `0x07` should not dispatch a keybinding in that state.

  ## Possible fixes
  - After the reply-read window closes, keep draining/discarding terminal responses.
  - Don't map a single control byte to an action that launches a subprocess while a
    stray-sequence payload was just consumed.
  - Optionally show a persistent "waiting for <editor> to exit" hint so the state is
    discoverable.


### Steps to reproduce

issues.title: codemode: aborting in-flight tools.read() crashes the Pi process with unhandled ReadStream AbortError

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
On `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.5.2, if a `codemode` script runs concurrent `tools.read()` calls (`Promise.all(...)`) and exits or rejects while a sibling `tools.read()` is still opening or streaming (for example, one path fails with `ENOENT` while another is between `fsOpen()` and `yield* stream`), the entire Pi CLI process crashes with an uncaught `AbortError` (`ABORT_ERR` on `ReadStream`).

**Repro (inside `codemode`):**
```js
await Promise.all([
  tools.read({ path: "does-not-exist.txt", offset: 1, limit: 10 }),
  tools.read({ path: "existing-file.txt", offset: 1, limit: 100 }),
]);
```

**Root cause (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/read.ts` — `readLocalFileChunks`):**
When `Execution.finish()` aborts still-running tool calls in `codemode`:
1. If `signal` aborts while `fsOpen(path, "r")` or `handle.stat()` is resolving, `handle.createReadStream({ end, signal, autoClose: false })` is called with an already-aborted `AbortSignal`. Node's `ReadStream` immediately emits an `"error"` event (`AbortError`) on next tick before `yield* stream` attaches its async-iterator error listener, triggering `uncaughtException` and `process.exit(1)`.
2. Guarding `if (signal?.aborted) return;` before `fsOpen`, `handle.stat()`, and `handle.createReadStream()`, and attaching `stream.on("error", () => {})` before `yield* stream`, prevents the unhandled stream error while still letting `yield* stream` reject/terminate cleanly on abort.

(Also reported via `/bug` telemetry as `01a1e791-9842-7391-b468-69c9b03d50f1`.)

I have a minimal fix + regression test ready and would like to submit a PR if approved (`lgtm`).

issues.title: A prompt accepted during switchSession runs on the disposed session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

A prompt that arrives while pi is replacing a session is accepted and then runs on the old session after it has been disposed. The window is the time pi spends awaiting `session_shutdown` handlers inside `ctx.switchSession`. In RPC mode the prompt gets `{"disposition":"started"}`.

That run is live. It sends provider requests and executes tools. None of it is rendered or saved, and the prompt never reaches the replacement session.

The only sign is a "This extension ctx is stale" error from any `before_provider_request` handler that reads `ctx`. That is how I noticed it: the errors showed up after an extension command reopened a session with `ctx.switchSession`.

### Steps to reproduce

Two files, no API key needed: https://gist.github.com/nertzy/1728c161ae8dddc3db0b5205d9fe5116

Run `node repro.mjs`. It starts pi with `--no-extensions -e stale-run.ts` in RPC mode against a local fake Anthropic endpoint.

The extension has a 200 ms `session_shutdown` handler, a 500 ms `before_agent_start` handler, and a `/reopen` command that calls `ctx.switchSession`. The host sends one prompt when the shutdown handler starts. The fake endpoint asks for a tool call on every request, so the old session keeps looping until the script kills pi after 3 seconds.

```text
[ext] session_shutdown begin
[host] prompt sent during session_shutdown
[ext] session replaced
[host] prompt response: {"disposition":"started"}
[server] request AFTER the session was replaced
[ext] tool executed
...
provider requests from the replaced session: 11
tool executions from the replaced session:   10
stale-ctx extension errors:                  11
prompt saved in a session file:              false
```

### Expected behavior

The prompt is either rejected or carried into the replacement session.

A disposed session sends no provider requests and runs no tools.

### Version

1.5.2 (the same code is on main at d917b3e)

- **Unnecessary full-scrollback redraws:** In regular mode, when a long assistant response or tool result continues updating after its top rows scroll above the viewport (`firstChanged < prevViewportTop`), the renderer falls back to `fullRender(true)`[cite: 1]. Clearing both the screen and scrollback to replay the entire transcript on every streaming tick causes visible flashes, jumping output, and duplicated history[cite: 1].
- **Cursor misalignment on Windows:** Windows ConPTY eagerly wraps full-width rows, advancing the hardware cursor beyond the renderer's tracked coordinates and misaligning subsequent updates[cite: 1].

## Changes

- **Viewport-pinned scrollback layout:** Keep the mutable conversation tail inside the visible working area while archiving completed components in order, reusing their rendered rows until their revision changes[cite: 1].
- **Explicit mutability and revision tracking:** Track mutability and revision states on assistant and tool components so deferred edit previews and image transcoder initialization remain mutable until settled, while explicit result, expansion, or display updates advance the revision[cite: 1].
- **Stable archived task cards:** Keep archived task cards intact while displaying live status in the viewport task area[cite: 1].
- **Working-area padding preservation:** Retain working-area padding when a long preview collapses into a short result so shrink handling does not trigger a transcript clear[cite: 1].
- **Controlled line wrapping:** Disable automatic wrapping during main-screen writes and restore it afterward and on exit, keeping full-width rows aligned with the renderer's cursor accounting on Windows[cite: 1].

The full-redraw path remains intact for genuine layout changes, while routine streaming updates no longer trigger it repeatedly[cite: 1].

## Validation

- Manually verified on Windows 10 with long streaming output and tool updates: screen flicker and repeated transcript redraws were significantly reduced.
- `npm run check` passed

Related: [#9255](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9255), [#9583](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9583)

prs.title: fix(tui): avoid input cursor flicker during streaming
prs.body:
## Bug

During assistant streaming or footer updates, the input cursor turns into a high-speed strobe light—flickering far faster than the terminal's normal blink rate and slowly blinding anyone trying to type. Three rendering behaviors are behind this light show:

- **Spamming visibility sequences:** Every frame re-sends the cursor show/hide sequence (`DECTCEM`), resetting the hardware blink timer even when cursor visibility hasn't changed at all.
- **Collateral row erasure:** In regular mode, repainting the span between updated response and footer rows wipes out and redraws the completely unchanged input rows caught in the crossfire.
- **Exposed cursor teleportation:** Main-screen rendering restores the hardware cursor *after* ending synchronized output, exposing its intermediate jumps across the screen.

## Changes

- **Track cursor visibility state:** Maintain cursor visibility in `TuiBase` and emit `DECTCEM` sequences only when visibility actually changes (resetting on startup, forced redraws, and alternate-screen transitions).
- **Batch main-screen cursor updates:** Append main-screen cursor placement and visibility changes directly into the same synchronized output write as the content update.
- **Leave unchanged rows alone:** Skip unchanged visible rows during differential updates so response and footer refreshes leave the input area untouched.
- **Optimize hardware cursor tracking:** Track cursor coordinates across both screen modes, avoid redundant moves and empty alternate-screen writes, and clamp the cursor column to the terminal width.

Streaming can now update the response and footer smoothly without continually repainting the input or restarting the hardware cursor's blink cycle. My eyes finally get a break.

## Validation

- Manually verified on Windows 11 during active streaming (including typing while output updates): input and cursor flicker are dramatically reduced, and no sunglasses are required anymore.
- `npm run check` passed.

Related: [#8003](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8003)

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): defer sendMessage triggerTurn until compaction ends
prs.body:
Closes #10982.

`pi.sendMessage(msg, { triggerTurn: true })` started a run while a manual compaction was in progress. `sendCustomMessage` only checked `isStreaming`, while `prompt()` rejects during compaction and the interactive UI queues input. The run used the uncompacted branch, so its entries landed before the compaction entry, and in one report the compaction never landed.

While `isCompacting` (manual, automatic, or branch summarization), a `triggerTurn` send is now deferred and replayed from `_resolveIdleWaitIfIdle()`, the point all three paths reach when they finish. Replaying before idle waiters are released means `waitForIdle()` covers the deferred run, matching how actions deferred during `agent_settled` already work.

When deferred sends are dropped:

- Cancelling only the compaction (Esc calls `abortCompaction()`) or a failed compaction: still sent, so an extension's wake-up is not lost.
- `abort()` and `dispose()`: dropped. Session switch, `/new`, and runtime shutdown call `abort()` first; without this, the aborted compaction settles, the deferred run starts after `agent.abort()` already ran, and `abort()` waits for a full turn on the outgoing session. This includes sends that arrive while `abort()` waits for the aborted compaction to settle: compaction still counts as running then, so they would be deferred again. A counter of pending `abort()` calls drops them. Sends after `dispose()` already throw, because it invalidates the extension context.

Sends without `triggerTurn`, and sends while a run is active, are unchanged.

#11077 took the same approach and was auto-closed by the contributor gate before review.

Validation on main `682c7b93c`:

- `test/suite/regressions/10982-send-message-during-compaction.test.ts`: the run starts after `compaction_end` and its entries follow the compaction entry; a cancelled compaction still starts it; `abort()` and `dispose()` mid-compaction start no run; a send that arrives while `abort()` waits for compaction to settle starts no run. The first, third, and fourth fail without the fix; the last fails without `3187879a2a`.
- `test/suite/`, agent-session, compaction, extension, RPC, and print-mode tests pass.
- `npm run check` passes. `./test.sh` (rerun with `3187879a2a`) passes except tests unrelated to this change:
  - The `find` tool tests fail because `fd` is unavailable in my sandbox.
  - Two deep-chain durable stress tests timed out.
  - One timing test in chord's `workers.test.ts` failed, then passed twice on rerun.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): emit session_compact for boundary-draft compactions
prs.body:
## Problem

When an extension commits a compaction through a boundary draft (`turn_end` / `agent_before_settle` returning `entries: [{ type: "compaction", ... }]`), `_commitBoundaryDrafts()` appended the entry but only emitted `entry_appended` — never `session_compact`.

Extensions that rely on `session_compact` to learn that the history was rewritten never fired. Concrete impact with `pi-claude-bridge`: the bridge discards a parked provider query on `session_compact` (its fix for issue #101, "one compaction per tool call with usage never dropping"). Without the event, the next tool result resumed the stale query, which answered from the pre-compaction conversation and reported pre-compaction usage (`cacheRead ≈ 886k` on a 1M window). The compaction threshold then re-triggered at every LLM step, and each compaction only summarized the delta since the previous one.

Observed in a real session (60 compactions, all `fromHook: true`, 2 message entries between consecutive compactions, `tokensBefore` stuck at 886197 → 893312 while each summary was ~10k chars).

## Fix

`_commitBoundaryDrafts()` now emits `session_compact` (`fromExtension: true`, `reason: "threshold"`, `willRetry: false`) for each committed compaction draft, matching what `compact()` and `_runAutoCompaction()` already do. The method became `async`; both call sites await it.

## Tests

- New tests in `test/suite/agent-session-boundaries.test.ts`: `session_compact` is emitted for compaction drafts on both `turn_end` and `agent_before_settle`, and not emitted for non-compaction drafts.
- Reproduction before the fix: with a stale post-compaction usage (bridge behavior), the threshold re-triggers at every step and each compaction summarizes only ~1.1k tokens; with a corrected usage, one compaction suffices.
- `vitest` on the boundaries suite: 32/32 pass; compaction-related suites pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Closes the loop for extension-driven compaction (e.g. `pi-auto-compact`) with providers that mirror the session externally.

prs.title: Fix scoped skill collision diagnostics
prs.body:
## Simple Description

Skill precedence already determines which resource wins, but Pi currently warns for every same-name collision. This change suppresses diagnostics for intentional higher-precedence overrides while retaining warnings for genuinely ambiguous collisions at the same precedence.

## What Changed

- Filter skill-collision diagnostics using the existing resource-precedence metadata.
- Keep same-precedence collisions visible and preserve the winning skill selection.
- Document the distinction between intentional overrides and ambiguous collisions.
- Add coverage for project-over-user and top-level-over-package overrides, plus same-precedence warnings.

## Why This Change

Projects and packages can intentionally provide different versions of the same skill. Warning for those declared overrides produces persistent collision noise even though resource ordering has already selected the correct skill. Same-precedence conflicts still need operator attention and continue to warn.

## Testing Instructions

- `npm run build:offline`
- `cd packages/coding-agent && HOME=/tmp/pi-upstream-test-home npx vitest run test/resource-loader.test.ts` — 59 tests passed.
- `npx biome check packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts packages/coding-agent/test/resource-loader.test.ts packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md`

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In the OpenTUI renderer on Linux (X11 and Wayland), middle-click should paste the PRIMARY selection into the composer, matching the usual desktop behavior where selecting text anywhere and middle-clicking pastes it.

#16799 adds right-click paste from CLIPBOARD to OpenTUI. With `ui.mouseTracking` enabled, the terminal forwards mouse events to the app instead of handling them, so middle-click currently does nothing and the terminal's own PRIMARY paste is unavailable.

Scope:

- **Read:** middle-click with no dialog open reads PRIMARY and inserts it through the same path as right-click paste (or into a focused foreground shell).
- **Write:** a completed OpenTUI selection is also written to PRIMARY, in addition to CLIPBOARD. With mouse tracking the terminal never sees an in-app selection, so without this, selecting text in Qwen Code and middle-clicking pastes whatever was last highlighted in another application. It also lets text selected in Qwen Code be middle-click pasted elsewhere.
- Without `wl-clipboard` or `xclip`, both read and write are a silent no-op.
- Non-Linux platforms are unaffected.

### Why is this needed?

Middle-click PRIMARY paste is a standard X11/Wayland workflow, and Linux users expect it to keep working inside the TUI. Without it, the only mouse-based paste is right-click (CLIPBOARD), and getting the terminal's native middle-click back means disabling `ui.mouseTracking`.

### Additional context

- Raised in https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16799#issuecomment-6966860164 (Ubuntu GNOME on Wayland).
- The bundled native clipboard addon (`@teddyzhu/clipboard`) only exposes CLIPBOARD, so PRIMARY access depends on `wl-paste`/`wl-copy --primary` (Wayland) or `xclip -selection primary` (X11). Neither is installed by default on a fresh Ubuntu desktop; in that case middle-click does nothing and selections are copied to CLIPBOARD only.
- On GNOME/mutter, the addon's `isWaylandClipboardAvailable()` returns `false` even when the clipboard works, so it should not be used to decide availability.
- Related: #8672 (middle-button behavior in PuTTY over SSH, Ink renderer).
- Depends on #16799 (right-click paste plumbing in OpenTUI).
- The implementation will be submitted as a new PR after #16799 is merged.

---

## 简体中文

### 希望新增的功能

在 Linux（X11 与 Wayland）的 OpenTUI renderer 中，按鼠标中键应将 PRIMARY selection 粘贴到输入框。这与一般桌面环境的习惯一致：在任何地方选中文字，再按中键就能粘贴。

#16799 为 OpenTUI 加入了右键粘贴 CLIPBOARD 的功能。开启 `ui.mouseTracking` 时，终端会把鼠标事件转交给程序，自己不再处理。所以目前中键没有任何作用，终端原生的 PRIMARY 粘贴也无法使用。

范围：

- **读取：** 没有对话框打开时，按中键读取 PRIMARY，走与右键粘贴相同的路径插入输入框。若有获得焦点的前台 shell，则送入该 shell。
- **写入：** 完成 OpenTUI 选取时，除了 CLIPBOARD，也写入 PRIMARY。开启 mouse tracking 时终端看不到应用内的选取，若不写入，在 Qwen Code 里选中文字后按中键，会粘贴出其他应用最后选中的文字。写入后，在 Qwen Code 里选中的文字也能到其他地方用中键粘贴。
- 没有 `wl-clipboard` 或 `xclip` 时，读取与写入都静默不执行。
- 非 Linux 平台不受影响。

### 为什么需要

中键粘贴 PRIMARY 是 X11/Wayland 的标准操作，Linux 用户会预期在 TUI 里也能使用。目前鼠标唯一的粘贴方式是右键（CLIPBOARD）。想恢复终端原生的中键粘贴，就必须关闭 `ui.mouseTracking`。

### 补充信息

- 来源：https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16799#issuecomment-6966860164 （Ubuntu GNOME on Wayland）。
- 内置的 native clipboard addon（`@teddyzhu/clipboard`）只支持 CLIPBOARD，因此访问 PRIMARY 需依赖 `wl-paste`/`wl-copy --primary`（Wayland）或 `xclip -selection primary`（X11）。全新安装的 Ubuntu 桌面默认没有这些工具；此时中键不会有任何动作，选取只会复制到 CLIPBOARD。
- 在 GNOME/mutter 上，即使剪贴板工作正常，addon 的 `isWaylandClipboardAvailable()` 仍返回 `false`，因此不应以它判断剪贴板是否可用。
- 相关：#8672（PuTTY over SSH 的中键行为，Ink renderer）。
- 依赖：#16799（OpenTUI 的右键粘贴基础实现）。
- 实现将在 #16799 合并后以新 PR 提交。

issues.title: ci: argv/cwd reaper fixtures can collide with real ancestor PIDs
issues.body:
### What happened?

The required Lint & Static check on #17571 failed in the CI helper test `selects by argv and by cwd as well`. Both attempts in the helper battery reported expected `[101, 102, 103]`, actual `[102, 103]`; the final helper result was 1,010 passed / 1 failed. ESLint, formatting and the other preceding static checks passed. [Failing job](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44247846545/job/134611319028).

The helper and its test are unchanged by that SDK PR. At main `78f8bfb1dc40577ad99ba628dfc35519455bd6e1`, they still have the same blobs as the PR: script `891703f882542521b1c074bc4a34392ffd7655eb`, test `8feb7351286cede81bb5b4c1ac1b4683ec74fc57`.

The test fabricates PIDs 101/102/103. The script intentionally excludes its real ancestors from `/proc`, even when its scan root is a fabricated proc tree. A fixture that reuses a real ancestor PID is therefore omitted before the argv/cwd selection is evaluated.

I reproduced that mechanism using the unchanged helper: use the test process's actual PID for the first fabricated argv process, retaining the original expected-array assertion. The test fails with only the two cwd entries selected. With three noncolliding safe-integer fixture IDs, the same unmodified script selects all three. Every fabricated-process invocation used `REAP_DRY_RUN=1`; nothing was signalled or removed.

The original fixed-101 test passes on the local process layout. The remote log does not record its ancestor chain, so this report does **not** claim to have proved that PID 101 was a real ancestor in that particular runner. It establishes a deterministic fixture-collision mechanism consistent with the observed missing entry.

### What did you expect to happen?

The argv/cwd selection test should exercise all three matching inputs independently of the runner's process numbers, while the real-ancestor safety exclusion remains intact.

For a deterministic reproduction, in an isolated copy of the existing test and helper, change only the first fixture's `pid: 101` to `pid: process.pid` and the expected first array element to `process.pid`. Run only `selects by argv and by cwd as well`. The first PID is then an actual ancestor of the spawned Bash helper, so the existing assertion reliably fails. Changing the synthetic selection fixtures to noncolliding IDs makes the controlled case select all three again.

### Client information

CI helper test; no interactive client session is involved. Observed upstream check: Linux / Node 22.x. Local mechanism reproduction: Linux / Node.js 24.22.1, Bash, unchanged script bytes.

### Login information

Not applicable; no provider authentication is involved.

### Anything else we need to know?

#13169 already changed the separate environment-selection fixture from PID 100 to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. The argv/cwd fixture remains unchanged. This report concerns that remaining case; it does not propose weakening ancestor exclusion or adding unrelated CI changes to the SDK PR. Existing-issue searches found no matching open report at the recorded snapshot.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 问题

#17571 的必需静态检查在 CI 清理脚本的 argv/cwd 选择测试失败：两次尝试均期望 `[101,102,103]`，实际为 `[102,103]`，最后 1,010 通过、1 失败。此前 ESLint、格式等检查通过；该 PR 没有修改这两个 helper 文件，当前 main 的相应 blob 也未改变。

测试使用固定假 PID，但脚本会从真实 `/proc` 排除自身祖先。已用原脚本独立复现：把第一个假 PID 和对应期望值改成测试进程的真实 PID，原断言稳定失败，只选中两个 cwd 项；使用不可能与真实祖先冲突的安全整数 PID 后，三项均被选中。全部假进程验证都开启 dry-run，没有发送信号或删除 home。

原固定 101 的测试在本地正常通过。远端日志没有打印祖先链，因此这里只确认冲突机制，不断言已经证明该 runner 的祖先恰为 101。

选择测试应不受 runner 进程号影响，并保留真实祖先排除保护。本地为 Linux、Node.js 24.22.1、Bash；这是 CI helper 问题，不涉及交互客户端或登录。

issues.title: Follow-up hardening of the managed /loop guards deferred from #17594

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/development
labels.description: Development experience

labels.name: scope/testing
labels.description: Test frameworks and cases

issues.body:
## What would you like to be added?

Follow-up hardening for guard gaps that the review rounds of #17594 recorded as deferred under the convergence posture (explicitly "not requested in this round", no Critical open). Each is a case where a wrong edit still passes the suite, or where a legitimate edit reddens an unrelated package.

**Open items:**

1. **Execute the classifier decision instead of scanning for it.** In the managed-agent E2E runner the seam is drawn at `blockProperties`, so the schema lookup, the gate and the answer site stay inline in each fake and a hand-rolled AST scanner has to inventory them (`scripts/run-managed-agent-server-e2e.ts:2718` and the two fakes). Drawing the seam around the whole decision would let the meta-test execute one pure function per arm instead of asserting structure, and would retire the scanner's inventories. The scanner has since been extended twice (in-place writes, template-literal tool names, per-callback scoping, helper-call inventory); each extension was driven by a measured survivor, which is the argument for replacing it with an executed seam rather than growing it again.
2. **Derive the caveat's degeneration threshold.** "A step of 31 or more matches only the 1st of each month" is the one number in the caveat paragraph that no assertion derives (`packages/core/src/skills/bundled/loop/SKILL.md:82`). Derive it from the same Managed slot compiler that already yields the N ≤ 30 bound, so the threshold and the bound cannot disagree.
3. **Bind the caveat's oracle to the Java evaluator.** The shared `managed-automation-slots-v1` fixtures (30 cases) contain no day-of-month step case, so `CronSlots.java` is not bound to its TypeScript twin `compileCron` for `*/N` expansion. The caveat test now derives from `compileCron` and requires `parseCron` to agree, but both are JavaScript: a change to `CronSlots.values()` alone would leave the shipped Managed bodies teaching a cadence the Java scanner no longer honours. Add day-of-month step cases (for example `0 0 */2 * *`, `0 0 */30 * *`, `0 0 */31 * *`) to the shared fixtures consumed by both `managed-automation-slots.test.ts` and `CronSlotsTest.java`, and run the Java verification suite. This is a cross-language contract change, which is why it was kept out of #17594.

**Landed in #17594 (commit `f7d80e2cb4`), no longer open:**

- *Pair the boundary-gap examples with their month lengths* — each worked example is now asserted as one composed clause built from the derived day, ordinal and gap, so swapping the 30-day and 31-day gaps reddens (witnessed).
- *Compare the Java routing targets as a set of reachable keys* — the pin now parses each `forProfile` branch into profile→key pairs and asserts the mapping plus the reachable-key set, and strips Java comments before scraping, so a key swap reddens and a comment-only edit does not (both witnessed).

## Why is this needed?

#17594 closed six deferred review findings and then spent several rounds making its own guards load-bearing: token counts were replaced by AST inventories, prose pins by values derived from the Managed slot compiler, and a supply-map pin by supply plus routing plus the profile→key mapping. Every inventory and derivation has a mutation witness. The open items are the next layer of the same root cause — a guard that asserts a shape rather than the behaviour it claims to protect, or an oracle that is not the evaluator that actually runs — and were deferred to keep that PR from widening further, per the repository's convergence rule.

## Additional context

- Sources: the `qwen-review-deferred` lists in the round-5 and round-6 review bodies of #17594, and the round-2 independent verification report (four measured survivors, all closed in `f7d80e2cb4`).
- Acceptance for each item is a mutation witness in the established style: apply the wrong edit, watch the matching assertion redden, restore byte-equal and watch it return green. Item 3 additionally requires the Java verification suite to run.
- No production runtime behaviour is involved: the runner is E2E-only, the skill generator is test-only, and the Java file is read as text by the parity test. Item 3 changes shared contract fixtures, so both language suites must be run.
- Related merged work: #17272, #17433, #17470, #17506, #17594.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 希望增加什么？

对 #17594 各轮评审按收敛姿态延后的守卫缺口做跟进加固（评审明确「本轮不要求修改」，无未决 Critical）。每一处都是「错误改动仍能通过套件」或「合法改动红到无关包」的情形。

**未关闭项：**

1. **执行分类器判定，而非扫描它。** managed-agent E2E runner 的接缝画在 `blockProperties`，故 schema 查找、门与 answer 站点仍内联在每个 fake 里，只能靠手写 AST 扫描器做库存（`scripts/run-managed-agent-server-e2e.ts:2718` 与两个 fake）。把接缝画在整个判定之外，就能让元测试对每臂执行一个纯函数、而非断言结构，并可退役扫描器的各项库存。该扫描器此后已两次扩展（原地写入、模板字面量工具名、按回调域计数、helper 调用库存），每次都由一个实测存活缺口驱动——这正是「用可执行接缝取代它、而不是继续加库存」的论据。
2. **派生 caveat 的退化阈值。** 「步长 31 或更大只匹配每月 1 日」是该段中唯一无断言派生的数字（`packages/core/src/skills/bundled/loop/SKILL.md:82`）。应由已给出 N ≤ 30 上界的同一个 Managed 槽编译器派生，使阈值与上界不会互相矛盾。
3. **把 caveat 的 oracle 绑定到 Java 求值器。** 共享 `managed-automation-slots-v1` fixtures（30 案例）无月内日期步进案例，故 `CronSlots.java` 在 `*/N` 展开上未与其 TS 镜像 `compileCron` 绑定。caveat 测试现从 `compileCron` 派生并要求 `parseCron` 一致，但两者都是 JavaScript：只改 `CronSlots.values()` 会让发布的 Managed body 继续教一个 Java 扫描器已不再遵守的节奏。应向同时被 `managed-automation-slots.test.ts` 与 `CronSlotsTest.java` 消费的共享 fixtures 增加日步进案例（如 `0 0 */2 * *`、`0 0 */30 * *`、`0 0 */31 * *`），并跑 Java verification 套件。属跨语言契约改动，故留在 #17594 之外。

**已在 #17594 落地（提交 `f7d80e2cb4`），不再开放：**

- *月界间隔示例与月份配对* —— 每个示例现作为一条由派生日、序数后缀与间隔组合的子句断言，对调 30 天月与 31 天月的间隔即红（已见证）。
- *Java 路由目标按可达 key 集合比较* —— 钉子现把每个 `forProfile` 分支解析为 profile→key 对并断言映射与可达 key 集合，且刮取前剥离 Java 注释，故 key 对调红、仅改注释不红（均已见证）。

## 为什么需要？

#17594 关闭了六条延后评审发现，随后用数轮让自己的守卫承重：token 计数换成 AST 库存、散文钉换成由 Managed 槽编译器派生的值、提供 map 钉换成提供＋路由＋profile→key 映射。每项库存与派生都有变异见证。未关闭项是同一根因的下一层——守卫断言的是形态而非它声称保护的行为，或 oracle 不是真正运行的那个求值器——为遵守仓库收敛规则、避免该 PR 继续加宽而延后。

## 补充上下文

- 来源：#17594 第五、六轮评审正文的 `qwen-review-deferred` 清单，以及第二轮独立验证报告（四个实测存活缺口，均已在 `f7d80e2cb4` 关闭）。
- 每项验收沿用既有风格的变异见证：施加错误改动→对应断言红→字节级还原→复绿。第 3 项另需跑 Java verification 套件。
- 不涉及生产运行时行为：runner 仅 E2E、skill 生成器仅 test、Java 文件由 parity 测试按文本读取。第 3 项改共享契约 fixtures，故两侧语言套件都须跑。
- 相关已合入工作：#17272、#17433、#17470、#17506、#17594。

</details>
