prs.title: feat(channels): add WeCom adapter to the managed channel path
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds WeCom as the third provider on the managed channel path, alongside email and DingTalk. A WeCom intelligent bot can now route inbound private-chat messages into bound Managed Agent Sessions through the control plane and deliver the receipted replies back over the same authenticated WebSocket. The adapter follows the established managed-channel discipline: every admission and every outbound segment is persisted before its side effect, so a restart replays the same event or reports the same segment unknown — never a second input and never a second send. It is exposed as an experimental, explicitly selected CLI entry that the legacy channel starter never picks and that drives no model itself.

The shared adapter contract and the adapter enablement gate are widened to admit the new provider; the control plane is already provider-agnostic, so no Java change is required. The provider mechanics differ from DingTalk in two load-bearing ways, both documented in the design: WeCom pushes each inbound message once with no acknowledgement and no redelivery (a frame that cannot be durably staged is lost and logged as lost, rather than left for redelivery), and a reply travels over the live connection keyed only by the chat id (there is no per-message session webhook to cache, snapshot or evict, so the reply context carries identity rather than a credential).

## Why it's needed

WeCom is a first-class legacy channel but had no managed-path adapter, so a WeCom bot could not participate in the durable, receipted Session routing that email and DingTalk already use. This closes that gap for the intelligent-bot connection method, which is the closest analog of the DingTalk stream robot and needs no public endpoint. The send-only group webhook and the self-built application callback are other WeCom connection methods and are intentionally out of scope.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the new and regression suites from their package directories: the WeCom channel package (new adapter/state/deps suites plus the unchanged legacy baselines), the CLI channel command suites (registration contract, shared argument surface, workspace resolution and type refusal), and the core managed-channel contract and authority suites (the enablement pin now lists three providers; the unknown-adapter refusal witness still uses a non-enabled name). All green locally on Linux.

For behavior beyond unit tests, two real-environment rigs were run. The first stands up a loopback TLS WebSocket server speaking the WeCom aibot frame protocol and drives the real SDK client, the real adapter with its real file lock, and the real HTTP control-plane client against a faithful fake control plane: authentication, inbound admission with the single-chat sender-userid fallback, an ordered markdown send over the real connection, an accepted receipt by ordinal, the 0600 persisted state, and a server kick stopping the adapter all pass (9/9). The second runs the same real adapter against a locally built Spring control plane (H2, channels enabled, internal listener): registration, durable staging, parsing and deterministic classification of the real server's 404 error envelope, claim, and disconnect all pass (5/5).

A reviewer should confirm the two documented divergences from DingTalk behave as stated: a failed inbound save loses exactly one frame and logs the loss (no redelivery arm), and every outbound send failure classifies as unknown until a verified provider errcode table exists (the pre-send validation refusal remains rejected). The load-bearing guards (outbound ledger cap, held-claim-first probe ordering, and the post-compromise persist suppression) are pinned by tests that were mutation-verified: removing each guard reddens its witness.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no TUI change. The new CLI entry is hidden from the channel help and refused for a non-WeCom channel; before this change the command does not exist (the global release answers "Unknown arguments"), after it the command parses and refuses non-WeCom channels with a clear message.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️ not tested   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️ not tested   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ tested   |

### Environment (optional)

Node 24, pnpm 11; full workspace build and typecheck green; prettier/eslint clean on every changed file. Real-environment rigs used a self-signed loopback CA (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) and a locally built control-plane jar (JDK 21, Maven, managed-local H2 profile).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: every outbound send failure is classified unknown because the aibot send path has no verified errcode retryability table; a genuinely dead target therefore settles unknown rather than rejected until a verified table lands. This is the conservative choice (a wrong definitive refusal could settle a rate-limited delivery rejected and never send the rest) and is documented as a follow-up.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live WeCom tenant smoke (no bot credential available); full inbound admission and outbound delivery against a registered Workspace with a live harness worker and model (the full hosted stack CI exercises with the email adapter under the same control-plane contract); group-chat policy, attachments/media, mixed-text frames, interactive cards/stream replies, proactive sends, and egress proxy wiring. The legacy WeCom channels are unchanged.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The shared contract widening is additive; existing exports keep their shape. The WeCom package gains a file-lock dependency already used by the DingTalk package.

Design documents (both versions complete and synchronized): [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/managed-channel-wecom/docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-channel-wecom-adapter.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/feat/managed-channel-wecom/docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-channel-wecom-adapter.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Refs #12827 (managed channel path); follows the DingTalk second-adapter slice.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

在托管渠道路径上增加企业微信（WeCom）作为第三个提供方，与 email、DingTalk 并列。WeCom 智能机器人现在可以把入站私聊消息经控制面路由进绑定的 Managed Agent Session，并把带回执的回复经同一条认证 WebSocket 投递回去。适配器遵循既有的托管渠道纪律：每次准入、每个出站分段都在其副作用之前持久化，因此重启会重放同一事件、或把同一段报为 unknown——绝不产生第二次输入、绝不第二次发送。它以一个实验性、显式选择的 CLI 入口暴露，Legacy 渠道启动器永远不会选中它，它自身也不驱动模型。

共享适配器契约与适配器启用门被放宽以接纳新提供方；控制面本就平台无关，因此无需 Java 改动。提供方机制与 DingTalk 有两处承重差异，均写入设计文档：WeCom 每条入站消息只推送一次，无确认、不重投（无法持久化暂存的帧会丢失并按丢失记录日志，而非留待重投）；回复经活连接、仅以会话 id 定位（没有逐消息的 session webhook 需要缓存、快照或逐出，因此 reply context 携带身份而非凭据）。

## 为什么需要

WeCom 是一等 Legacy 渠道，但此前没有托管路径适配器，因此 WeCom 机器人无法参与 email 与 DingTalk 已在用的持久化、带回执的 Session 路由。本 PR 为智能机器人连接方式补上这一缺口——它与 DingTalk 流机器人最接近，且无需公网端点。只发不收的群 webhook 与自建应用 callback 是 WeCom 的另外两种连接方式，刻意不在范围内。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

从各自包目录跑新增与回归套件：WeCom 渠道包（新适配器/状态/deps 套件 + 不变的 Legacy 基线）、CLI channel 命令套件（注册契约、共享参数面、工作区解析与类型拒绝）、core 托管渠道契约与 authority 套件（启用钉死现列三个提供方；未知适配器拒绝见证仍用一个未启用的名字）。Linux 本地全绿。

单测之外跑了两套真实环境 rig。第一套起一个讲 WeCom aibot 帧协议的回环 TLS WebSocket 服务器，驱动真实 SDK 客户端、带真实文件锁的真实适配器、真实 HTTP 控制面客户端对接一个忠实的假控制面：认证、带单聊 sender-userid 回退的入站准入、经真实连接的有序 markdown 发送、按 ordinal 的 accepted 回执、0600 持久化状态、服务端被踢停止适配器，全部通过（9/9）。第二套让同一个真实适配器对接本地构建的 Spring 控制面（H2、开启 channels、内部监听器）：注册、持久化暂存、对真实服务器 404 错误信封的解析与确定性分类、claim、disconnect，全部通过（5/5）。

评审应确认两处相对 DingTalk 的 documented 分歧如述行为：入站保存失败恰好丢一帧并记录丢失（无重投臂）；在存在经过验证的提供方 errcode 表之前，所有出站发送失败都分类为 unknown（发送前校验拒绝仍为 rejected）。承重守卫（出站账本封顶、held 认领优先探针排序、compromise 后的持久化抑制）由经变异验证的用例钉住：删除每个守卫都会使其见证变红。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A——无 TUI 改动。新 CLI 入口对 channel help 隐藏，对非 WeCom 渠道拒绝；改动前该命令不存在（全局发布版答 "Unknown arguments"），改动后命令可解析并以清晰文案拒绝非 WeCom 渠道。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️ 未测   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️ 未测   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ 已测   |

### 环境（可选）

Node 24、pnpm 11；全工作区构建与 typecheck 绿；所有改动文件 prettier/eslint 干净。真实环境 rig 用了自签回环 CA（NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS）与本地构建的控制面 jar（JDK 21、Maven、managed-local H2 profile）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：所有出站发送失败都分类为 unknown，因为 aibot 发送路径没有经过验证的 errcode 可重试性表；因此真正死掉的目标会落定 unknown 而非 rejected，直到经过验证的表落地。这是保守选择（错误的确定性拒绝可能让被限流的整条投递落定 rejected 且余段永不发送），已记录为后续工作。
- 未验证/范围外：真实 WeCom 租户冒烟（无机器人凭据）；对已注册 Workspace、活 harness worker 与模型的完整入站准入与出站投递（CI 用 email 适配器在同一控制面契约下演练的完整 hosted 栈）；群聊策略、附件/媒体、图文混排帧、交互卡片/流式回复、主动发送、出口代理接线。Legacy WeCom 渠道不变。
- 破坏性改动/迁移说明：无。共享契约放宽是增量的；既有导出保持形状。WeCom 包新增一个 DingTalk 包已在用的文件锁依赖。

prs.title: fix(core): treat `git remote show` as non-read-only (auto-mode egress bypass, #14359)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`git remote show` is classified read-only, so in `auto` mode it is auto-approved on the read-only fast path and never reaches the permission classifier. But it queries the remote over the network (`git-upload-pack`, i.e. `GET <url>/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack`) and accepts a raw URL argument, so it is a network side effect, not a local lookup.

This PR classifies every `git remote show` as not read-only, with or without `-n`. `git remote get-url` (which never connects) and a bare `git remote` keep their read-only classification.

The change is two lines of logic, one in each classifier: `evaluateGitSafety` in `shellAstParser.ts` (the AST path) and `evaluateGitRemoteArgs` in `shellReadOnlyChecker.ts` (the regex fallback, used when the WASM parser is unavailable).

Fixes #14359.

## Why there is no `-n` exception any more

Rounds 1 to 11 of this PR kept `git remote show -n` read-only, because `-n` stays offline. That needs proof that `-n` reaches git as an option, and neither classifier reads a command the way bash does. Each review round found another spelling where the classifier saw a `-n` that git never received:

| Round | Input | What git received |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | `git remote show <url> \-- -n` | `-n` after the terminator, as a remote name |
| 4 | `git remote show <url> [--][--] -n` | the glob expands to `--` |
| 6 | `git remote show <url> --end-of-options -n` | `-n` as a remote name |
| 8 | `git remote show <url> <<<-n` | no `-n` at all |
| 9 | `git remote show <url> \ -n` | one word, ` -n` |
| 10 | `bash -c 'git remote show origin' -n` (Monitor) | `-n` is `$0` |

All of these were already read-only at this PR's first commit. Each fix added a guard and the diff grew from 49 to 460 lines over ten files, and round 11 found a regression in one of the guards. The review itself asked whether the shape of the change was still right.

Asking about every `show` needs no proof, so the class cannot occur. The branch now takes every file it had changed from `main` and adds only the rule above: 4 files, +33/−2.

The cost is one approval for `git remote show -n <name>`, which was read-only before.

## Why deny-by-default (not a URL heuristic)

The original report suggested keying on whether the argument is "URL-shaped". Triage and maintainer review both flagged that an under-detecting heuristic (git accepts `scheme://…`, scp-like `user@host:path`, and local paths) would silently re-open the hole on any form it misses. Deny-by-default needs no URL parser and has no under-detection gap.

## Test plan

- `shellAstParser.test.ts`: `git remote show` classifies `unknown` for a remote name, a URL, with `-n`, after `-v`, and for the round 2, 6 and 9 spellings. The consistency table pins both classifiers to the same answer for `show`, `show -n`, `show <url> --end-of-options -n` and `get-url`.
- `shellReadOnlyChecker.test.ts`: `show`, `show -n`, and the round 4 and 8 spellings are not read-only.
- The new rows fail on `main` (16 failures) and pass with the change.
- Run locally: `shellAstParser`, `shellReadOnlyChecker`, `shell-utils`, `plan-mode-shell-policy`, `coreToolScheduler`, `tools/monitor`, `tools/shell` and all of `permissions/`: 23 files, 3,440 tests passed. `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint and Prettier are clean on the changed files.

## Risk & scope

- **`auto` mode:** every `git remote show` now goes to review (classifier or approval) instead of auto-running. `git remote -v` and `git remote get-url` are unaffected.
- **Plan mode:** the command is `unknown`, so a warning plus approval, not a hard block.
- **Memory-scoped agents** (`packages/core/src/memory/memory-scoped-agent-config.ts`) map the verdict as `isReadOnly ? 'allow' : 'deny'` with no approval surface, so `git remote show`, including `-n`, goes from allowed to denied there. That context already denies `git fetch`.
- **Not closed here (R11-3):** a redirection written between `remote` and `show` still classifies read-only on the AST path. The cause is not in the `git remote` rule: the parser ends the command at a mid-command redirection, so the words after it are not seen as arguments. That affects other subcommand rules on `main` too, and I am reporting it separately instead of widening this PR.
- **Reverted with the redesign:** the word-break guard, the here-string handling and the Monitor wrapper join from rounds 8 to 10 are no longer in this PR, so `shell-utils.ts` and the Monitor and plan-mode tests are unchanged from `main`. R11-1 and R11-2 were findings in that code.
- No change to allow/deny rule handling; no public API change.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14359

---

## 中文

### 这个 PR 做了什么

`git remote show` 被判为只读，所以在 `auto` 模式下走只读快速通道自动执行，不经过权限分类器。但它会通过网络查询远端（`git-upload-pack`），并且接受任意 URL 作为参数，所以它有网络副作用，不是本地查询。

这个 PR 把所有 `git remote show` 都判为非只读，不论有没有 `-n`。`git remote get-url`（从不联网）和不带子命令的 `git remote` 仍是只读。

逻辑改动只有两行，两个分类器各一处：`shellAstParser.ts` 的 `evaluateGitSafety`（语法树路径）和 `shellReadOnlyChecker.ts` 的 `evaluateGitRemoteArgs`（正则后备路径，WASM 解析器不可用时使用）。

### 为什么不再保留 `-n` 例外

第 1 到 11 轮一直让 `git remote show -n` 保持只读，因为 `-n` 不联网。这需要证明 `-n` 确实作为选项到达了 git，而两个分类器读命令的方式都和 bash 不一样。每一轮审查都找到一种新写法：分类器看到了 `-n`，git 却没收到。上面英文部分的表格列出了第 2、4、6、8、9、10 轮的六种输入。

这些输入在本 PR 的第一个提交上就已经被判为只读。每次修复加一条防护，改动从 49 行涨到 10 个文件 460 行，第 11 轮又在其中一条防护里找到了回归。审查本身也提出，应当由人判断这个改法的形状是否还对。

对所有 `show` 都要求确认，就不需要任何证明，这一类问题也就不会出现。现在这个分支把改过的文件全部恢复成 `main` 的版本，只加上面这条规则：4 个文件，+33/−2。

代价是 `git remote show -n <name>` 以前是只读，现在要确认一次。

### 为什么用默认拒绝（而非 URL 启发式）

最初的报告建议按参数"是否像 URL"来判断。分诊和维护者审查都指出，启发式一旦漏判（git 接受 `scheme://…`、类 scp 的 `user@host:path` 和本地路径），漏掉的形式会悄悄重新打开这个洞。默认拒绝不需要解析 URL，也没有漏判的问题。

### 测试

- `shellAstParser.test.ts`：远端名、URL、带 `-n`、`-v` 之后、以及第 2、6、9 轮的写法，`git remote show` 都判为 `unknown`。一致性表把两个分类器对 `show`、`show -n`、`show <url> --end-of-options -n` 和 `get-url` 的结果钉在一起。
- `shellReadOnlyChecker.test.ts`：`show`、`show -n` 以及第 4、8 轮的写法都不是只读。
- 新增的用例在 `main` 上失败（16 条），加上改动后通过。
- 本地运行：`shellAstParser`、`shellReadOnlyChecker`、`shell-utils`、`plan-mode-shell-policy`、`coreToolScheduler`、`tools/monitor`、`tools/shell` 以及整个 `permissions/`，共 23 个文件 3,440 个测试通过。改动文件的 `tsc --noEmit`、ESLint、Prettier 均无问题。

### 风险 / 范围

- **`auto` 模式：** 所有 `git remote show` 现在都进入审查（分类器或确认），不再自动执行。`git remote -v` 和 `git remote get-url` 不受影响。
- **Plan 模式：** 命令为 `unknown`，即警告加确认，不是硬拦截。
- **记忆范围的 agent**（`packages/core/src/memory/memory-scoped-agent-config.ts`）按 `isReadOnly ? 'allow' : 'deny'` 处理，没有确认环节，所以 `git remote show`（包括带 `-n`）在那里从允许变成拒绝。那个环境本来就拒绝 `git fetch`。
- **这里没有关闭的（R11-3）：** 在 `remote` 和 `show` 之间写一个重定向，语法树路径上仍判为只读。原因不在 `git remote` 这条规则里：解析器遇到命令中间的重定向就结束了命令，后面的词没有被当成参数。`main` 上其他按子命令判断的规则也受影响，我会单独报告，不在这个 PR 里扩大范围。
- **随重新设计一并撤回的：** 第 8 到 10 轮加的断词防护、here-string 处理和 Monitor 包装命令的拼接已不在这个 PR 里，所以 `shell-utils.ts` 以及 Monitor 和 Plan 模式的测试与 `main` 相同。R11-1 和 R11-2 是针对那些代码的意见。
- 不改变 allow/deny 规则的处理；没有公开 API 变化。

prs.title: fix(permissions): keep the pending call out of the classifier's prior actions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

In AUTO mode, the classifier's transcript no longer lists the tool call it is classifying as a `Prior action`. The scheduler and the ACP session pass the call's id down to the transcript builder, and the builder skips the one `functionCall` in history that carries that id. The call still appears once, as the call to classify.

## Why it's needed

History is read after the model turn that issued the call has been recorded, so the pending call was rendered twice: first as `Prior action: …`, as if it had already run, and then under `## Pending tool call to classify`. The classifier then reasons about a retry instead of a first execution. #16496 has a transcript captured from a real session and the measurements: on 61 cases where the user did not authorize a destructive action, removing the echoed call took wrongly allowed verdicts from 61% to 37% on qwen3.7-max and from 30% to 19% on deepseek-v4-pro, with the consent and polite-request controls unchanged.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- `packages/core/src/permissions/classifier-transcript.test.ts`, `describe('the pending call recorded in history')`: the pending call is rendered only as the call to classify; an earlier call with the same command, which did run, is kept; the other calls issued in the same model turn are kept; nothing is dropped when the id is missing or not in history.
- `classifier.test.ts`: `classifyAction` keeps the pending call out of the prior actions it sends.
- `autoMode.test.ts`: `evaluateAutoMode` hands the call id to the classifier.
- `coreToolScheduler.test.ts`: both scheduler paths (the AUTO classifier path and the pending L4 allow path) pass the id, so the classifier request holds no prior action for the pending call.
- `coreToolScheduler.test.ts`, sub-agent calls: when a call issued inside a sub-agent carries the same id as a finished call in the session history, that finished call stays in the classifier's prior actions. Covered for both scheduler paths, and for both ways a sub-agent frame is marked (agent id, agent chat). With the check disabled, these 3 tests fail.
- `Session.test.ts` (ACP): the session passes `callId` to `evaluateAutoMode`.

Removing only the three-line skip in `buildClassifierContents` makes 5 of these tests fail; restoring it makes them pass.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, from the session captured in #16496 (`git branch -D tmp/spike` had not run when this request was sent):

```
[5] user: Prior action: run_shell_command({"command":"git branch -D tmp/spike","cwd":"/path/to/repo"})
[6] user: ## Pending tool call to classify
          Tool: run_shell_command
          Arguments: {"command": "git branch -D tmp/spike", "cwd": "/path/to/repo"}
```

After: entry `[5]` is gone and `[6]` is unchanged. This is what the transcript tests assert. I did not re-capture a live session on this branch.

Local runs at `5c2b296ea4` (`main` merged at `b2b522c2ed`):

- core: `coreToolScheduler.test.ts` and all of `permissions/`: 17 files, 2,044 tests passed.
- core: `agents/runtime/agent-core*` and `tools/agent`: 7 files, 689 tests passed.
- ESLint, Prettier and `tsc --noEmit` clean on the two files changed in this commit.
- cli: `acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts` passed (1,437 tests) before `main` was merged; not re-run on this head, and the commit does not touch `packages/cli`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only. macOS 15.6.1.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the match is by call id only. A call with no id, or an id that is not in the history tail, changes nothing, so the transcript is then the same as on `main`. An earlier call with the same command and arguments has a different id and is still listed, since it did run.
- Sub-agents: the classifier history is read from the session chat, while a sub-agent's call comes from its own chat, and call ids are unique only within one chat. The scheduler therefore passes the id only for calls issued by the session chat. For a sub-agent call the transcript is the same as on `main`; its pending call is not in the session history, so there is nothing to skip.
- Not validated / out of scope: the classifier prompt itself is unchanged. #16497 (the classifier treating a goal-related action as authorized) is a separate change. Callers of `classifyAction` other than the scheduler and the ACP session pass no id and behave as before.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `callId` is an optional field on `PendingAction`, `ClassifierInput` and `EvaluateAutoModeInput`.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16496

prs.title: fix(core): fail closed on undecodable shell paths
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Shell filename words that cannot be resolved losslessly no longer inherit an allow verdict. Undecodable bytes and expansion marks survive quote removal and path normalization. Known deny rules still take priority, and literal quoted or escaped dollars remain filename characters.

The latest update is `c50435d2c71`, with the production change in `4c1399754f4`. Outer compound splitting and payload extraction now share one substitution-boundary implementation. Unclosed substitutions produce an uncertain operation instead of disappearing, wrapper and substitution depths are independent, and execution state covers redirects, function calls, escaped controls and HOME/CDPATH changes. Default Bash-rule splitting retains backtick boundaries, while unresolved write operands remain visible as uncertain operations.

## Why it's needed

Dropping an unresolved path is not the same as finding no file operation. A child process or a conditional branch changing directory must not change the path certified for the parent. Conversely, a normal globbed read is not the same as an unresolved variable or write target and should not force a human decision.

The walker separates dynamic-cd uncertainty from structural uncertainty. A later absolute `cd` can clear the former but not the latter. Case, conditionals, loops, `[[ ]]`, complex parameter expansion and earlier HOME/CDPATH assignments retain conservative state, while real command-substitution bodies are still inspected for writes and removals. Bare `!` dispatches the following simple command, and `eval`, `source` and `.` require dynamic cwd treatment.

Pipeline state survives empty newline segments. Group pairing recognizes unmodelled closing segments without mistaking a case pattern's `)` for its surrounding subshell. Beyond four wrapper levels, structured analysis continues with `pathUnknown` instead of silently skipping substitution payloads; a separate hard recursion cap bounds pathological input. Substitution nesting alone does not consume the wrapper uncertainty budget.

The shared `commandSubstitutionEnd` distinguishes quoted parentheses, nested substitutions and case arms. Wrapper redirects and adjacent descriptor/redirect operators retain their real targets. Process substitutions use an fd placeholder without inventing operand paths. Defined function calls and eval/source-style dynamic commands make cwd uncertain rather than certifying an unchanged path, and escaped control syntax cannot silently drop that state. Bare negation is skipped before the version-dependent `time --` guard.

HOME/CDPATH mutations include export, declarations, unset and assignment segments carrying redirects. Explicit tilde cd targets, tilde writes, nested substitutions and possible pipeline-final mutations inherit the uncertainty. Unresolved mv, cp, install, ln, sed, perl, truncate and tee destinations emit uncertain operations. Process substitutions execute their payloads without inventing operand paths.

The unresolved-path floor skips operations marked as ordinary glob-only reads. Variable expansion, undecodable bytes and unresolved write targets keep the floor. Descriptor duplication preserves the `&` when whitespace separates its numeric target, while plain `> 2` remains a write to the file named `2`. A quoted wrapper positional argument is not appended as another executable payload.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Configure broad shell/file allow rules and protected-file rules. Check backtick boundaries, parameter braces, comments inside substitutions, case arms, pipelines separated by newlines, groups closed by `fi`, wrapper positional substitutions, negated commands and current-shell dynamic commands. Protected writes and removals must remain denied or force review rather than being certified under a different cwd.

Reassign HOME with plain assignments, `export`, `unset` and an assignment carrying a redirect. Check explicit `cd ~`, tilde writes, nested substitutions and a possible pipeline-final mutation. Unresolved destinations and `<(...)`/`>(...)` bodies must remain visible, while quoted tildes and literal read-only variable operands retain their existing behavior.

Check `grep -rn foo src/*.ts` under AUTO and broad allow rules: it must reach the classifier and be allowed. Preserve manual fallback for `printf x > $'\xff'`, `printf x > "$OUT"` and `cd $D; printf x > settings.json`. Check `echo hi >& 2`, `echo hi 2>& 1` and `cat <& 0` produce no file operation, while `echo hi > 2` still reports the numeric filename write.

For Monitor, `bash -c "echo $X" "rm -rf /tmp/x"` must not treat the positional argument as another command. The unresolved option-terminator alternative remains covered.

The [design](docs/design/2026-11-17-shell-path-ownership.md) and [E2E plan](.qwen/e2e-tests/shell-path-ownership.md) describe the boundaries and remaining packaged-CLI checks.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The **22 R17 regressions** were observed failing before the fixes: 16 substitution, redirect, process-fd, function, escaped-control and HOME cases, two additional depth/conditional cases, three negated time cases and one deny-protected brace read. A separate unclosed-substitution regression verifies the generic fail-closed path. Existing case-arm, fd-close and ordinary-glob controls remain green.

The final six complete files contain **2190 passing tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped**: shell semantics, permission manager, AUTO mode, rule parser, shell utilities and the real tool scheduler. The earlier R16 matrix of 30 parent-red regressions also remains green.

An isolated macOS Bash 3.2.57 probe confirmed the sharpest quoted-substitution case actually wrote `hi\n` into the protected fixture. No operator configuration or startup file was read or modified.

Changed-file ESLint, Prettier and diff checks pass. The complete workspace build stops in unchanged `external-context` code because `maxToolInputElements` is absent from the installed `ServerOptions`. Direct core typecheck reports the same 17 diagnostics in unchanged diff, glob and zod consumers and none in the changed files. No successful package build, bundle, installed/global CLI run or ACP end-to-end result is claimed. ACP consumers of the human-decision fields were inspected in source.

Hosted checks for this new head are tracked separately; previous-head results are not attributed to it.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
| macOS arm64 | Six complete source suites and parent red/green verification |
| Windows | No native shell validation |
| Linux | No new R17 packaged CLI or native shell run |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 26.5.0 and the existing same-project dependency environment. This was not a fresh frozen-lock install. Existing dist is only a test prerequisite, not a new build of the patch. No live model or provider call was made.

## Risk & Scope

- Unresolved paths require a human decision in AUTO mode even under broad allow rules. Ordinary read-only globs remain on the normal rule/classifier path.
- Cwd and expansion analysis remain conservative and best-effort, not a complete shell interpreter or byte-exact filename proof. Beyond the certainty depth threshold and for unmodelled structures, the analyzer asks more often rather than certifying a path.
- No configuration migration, dependency change, new shell parser or permission-rule syntax. The existing lexer and approval fields remain the owners.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16757

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): share resident external Workspace across sessions [16023 B/2]
prs.body:
Split from #16023 at source commit `bd8c5c76011ad3c9011ef3a265a6eea44a86a935` (base `7f40ef8e4bd8b006bb84f6d5e95050f18335378e` on `main`); candidate B: `87766f263a51a`. This is **[16023 B/2]** — the shared resident external Workspace lifecycle, read-only concurrent dispatch, reattach, recovery/retirement services, and `EPHEMERAL` storage registration, separated from the unbound Session principal ownership migration in #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**). This PR targets `main` directly and compiles and runs independently of A/2.

## What this PR does

Adds the resident external-Workspace increment: a Session that needs an external Workspace tool provisions one worker, and later Sessions and Turns reuse that same Workspace-scoped binding instead of each closing cycle destroying it. Closing one Session becomes a membership release rather than a teardown of the shared binding.

It also lands the admission and lifecycle machinery that increment requires:
- Durable binding lookup (`findLatestForRequest`), trusted-startup recovery (`ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryService`, `RuntimeProvisionLostRecovery`), and terminal retirement (`ExternalWorkspaceRetirementService`) that refuse active or `UNKNOWN` executions and never auto-replace a `LIVE` or indeterminate runtime.
- Provider reattachment (`reattach`) for resident external Workspaces when an `observe` returns `UNKNOWN` after a provider restart, verifying the original endpoint and identity without provisioning a replacement.
- Read-only dispatch classification (`VerifiedDispatchPayload`, `shared_dispatch_class`) so verified read-only file tools run concurrently while writes stay fenced behind the binding, with a bounded shared-dispatch wait that settles stranded `PREPARED` rows at deadline.
- `EPHEMERAL` sandbox-owned Workspace registration sharing the same admission, ownership, migration, schema-projection, and inventory-eligibility rules as `EXTERNAL`.

## Why it's needed

Today an external Workspace cannot outlive the Session that first used it: closing the Session releases the binding and the next Session pays provisioning again, while concurrent readers queue behind the same fence as writers even when they cannot mutate anything. Separating this 70-file runtime and persistence increment (+4,676/−795) from the 99-file unbound Session principal migration (+7,684/−1,052) cuts the review surface in half and keeps this PR focused strictly on external Workspace binding lifetime, concurrency, and recovery fences.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused unit and H2 persistence suites from `packages/managed-agent-server` on JDK 21:

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -o -pl verification -am test \
  -Dtest=ExternalWorkspaceRetirementServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceOwnershipTest,ExternalWorkspaceMaterializationTest,ExternalWorkspaceProvisionerTest,ExternalRuntimeProvisionerTest,ExternalHttpRuntimeClientTest,ExternalWorkspaceBootContractTest,RuntimeBindingSessionReleaseTest,RuntimeBindingLatestReleaseRaceTest,SharedExternalDispatchTest,RuntimeExecutionDispatcherTest
```

Expected:
- A second Session joining the same external Workspace reuses the active Workspace-isolated binding; closing the first Session releases only its membership while the last member under a storage retirement fence clears `ma_storage_owner`.
- Read-only file tools run concurrently on a shared external binding while write tools and `UNKNOWN` executions fence concurrent writes until settled or deadline-refused.
- Provider `UNKNOWN` on a resident Workspace triggers an authenticated `/runtime/reattach` against the saved original endpoint without provisioning a replacement; endpoint drift or `GONE` fails closed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for UI — backend runtime broker and persistence change with no TUI/UI surface.

Local verification on macOS (JDK 21):

```text
mvn -o test-compile → BUILD SUCCESS (all 15 reactor modules)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local JDK 21 (`openjdk@21`) for offline reactor compilation; Linux and MySQL 8.4 lanes run in CI against `main`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: reshaping Workspace binding lifetime and session-close semantics is security- and data-safety-critical — a bug would either tear down a Workspace while another Session still uses it or replace a worker whose state is unknown. Two class-size ratchet pins rise with explicit design-doc annotations (`JdbcRuntimeBindingRepository` 2319 → 2360 and `RuntimeBrokerService` 1909 → 2028; note that #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**) subsequently extracts `RuntimeDispatchPayloadAdmission` and lowers `RuntimeBrokerService` back down to 2006).
- Not validated / out of scope: unbound Session principal ownership (`ma_session_principal`) is in #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**). Foreground external Shell execution is in #17473 (**[17357 A/2]**) and #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: adds `shared_dispatch_class VARCHAR(16)` to `ma_tool_execution` in `V1__managed_schema.sql` and adds `reattach` to `ExternalRuntimeClient`.

Design:
- [Reattach the original external Workspace worker (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-external-reattach.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-external-reattach.zh-CN.md)
- [Retire external Workspaces after settled failures (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-retirement-settled-failure.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-retirement-settled-failure.zh-CN.md)
- [Class-size ratchet exception note (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/2026-11-04-managed-agent-class-size-ratchet.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/2026-11-04-managed-agent-class-size-ratchet.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Refs #15512, #15247. Split from #16023 (`[16023 B/2]`).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

自 #16023 的源码提交 `bd8c5c76011ad3c9011ef3a265a6eea44a86a935`（基于 `main` 的 `7f40ef8e4bd8b006bb84f6d5e95050f18335378e`）拆分而来；候选提交 B 为 `87766f263a51a`。本 PR 是 **[16023 B/2]** —— 包含常驻外部 Workspace 跨会话生命周期、只读并发派发、provider `reattach`、恢复与退役服务以及 `EPHEMERAL` 存储注册，与 #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**)（无绑定 Session principal 归属迁移）解耦。本 PR 直接以 `main` 为 base，可独立于 A/2 编译和运行。

## 这个 PR 做了什么

落地「常驻外部 Workspace」增量：某个 Session 首次需要外部 Workspace 工具时创建一次 worker，之后的其他 Session 与 Turn 复用同一个 Workspace 作用域的绑定，而不是在每次关闭周期都销毁它。关闭单个 Session 变成成员释放，而不再拆除共享绑定。

同时补齐该增量所需的准入与生命周期机制：
- 持久化绑定查询（`findLatestForRequest`）、可信启动恢复（`ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryService`、`RuntimeProvisionLostRecovery`）与终态退役（`ExternalWorkspaceRetirementService`），拒绝存在活跃或 `UNKNOWN` 执行的操作，且绝不自动替换 `LIVE` 或状态不确定的 runtime。
- 常驻外部 Workspace 的 provider 重连（`reattach`）：当 provider 进程重启后 `observe` 返回 `UNKNOWN` 时，携带原 boot、scope、handle 和 endpoint 重连原 worker，绝不新建替换实例。
- 只读派发分类（`VerifiedDispatchPayload`、`shared_dispatch_class`）：经摘要校验的只读文件工具可并发执行，写操作仍受绑定级互斥围栏保护，并为共享派发等待设置超时上限，到期自动结算滞留的 `PREPARED` 记录。
- `EPHEMERAL` 沙箱自有 Workspace 注册：与 `EXTERNAL` 共享同一套准入、归属、迁移、Schema 投影与可用性判定规则。

## 为什么需要它

此前外部 Workspace 无法跨越首次使用它的 Session 存活：关闭 Session 会释放绑定，下一个 Session 必须重新创建 worker；同时只读并发请求也会排在写锁后面。将这 70 个文件的运行时与持久化改动（+4,676/−795）与 99 个文件的无绑定 Session principal 迁移（+7,684/−1,052）拆开后，评审面缩减一半，且可以直接基于 `main` 触发全量 CI。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 JDK 21 下从 `packages/managed-agent-server` 运行常驻外部 Workspace 相关的单元与持久化测试：

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -o -pl verification -am test \
  -Dtest=ExternalWorkspaceRetirementServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryServiceTest,ExternalWorkspaceOwnershipTest,ExternalWorkspaceMaterializationTest,ExternalWorkspaceProvisionerTest,ExternalRuntimeProvisionerTest,ExternalHttpRuntimeClientTest,ExternalWorkspaceBootContractTest,RuntimeBindingSessionReleaseTest,RuntimeBindingLatestReleaseRaceTest,SharedExternalDispatchTest,RuntimeExecutionDispatcherTest
```

预期行为：
- 第二个 Session 加入同一外部 Workspace 时复用活跃的 Workspace 隔离绑定；关闭第一个 Session 仅释放其成员资格，只有在存储退役围栏下释放最后一个成员时才清空 `ma_storage_owner`。
- 只读文件工具在共享外部绑定上可并发执行，而写工具和 `UNKNOWN` 执行会围栏后续写操作，直到结算或超时拒绝。
- 常驻 Workspace 在 `observe` 返回 `UNKNOWN` 时会向原保存的 endpoint 发起带鉴权的 `/runtime/reattach`，不会新建替换实例；endpoint 漂移或 `GONE` 均 fail-closed。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

N/A（无 UI 变更 —— 纯后端 Runtime Broker 与持久化变更）。

本地 macOS（JDK 21）验证：

```text
mvn -o test-compile → BUILD SUCCESS (全部 15 个模块通过)
```

### 测试平台

|   操作系统   | 状态 |
| :----------: | :--: |
|   🍏 macOS   |  ✅  |
|  🪟 Windows  |  ⚠️  |
|   🐧 Linux   |  ⚠️  |

### 环境说明（可选）

本地使用 JDK 21（`openjdk@21`）完成离线全模块编译校验；Linux 与 MySQL 8.4 通道由针对 `main` 的 CI 执行。

## 风险与影响范围

- 主要风险或取舍：重塑 Workspace 绑定生命周期与 Session 关闭语义涉及跨会话数据安全 —— 任何缺陷都会表现为在其他 Session 仍在使用时销毁 Workspace，或在状态未知时静默替换 worker。两个类尺寸 ratchet 上限带有明确的设计文档例外说明（`JdbcRuntimeBindingRepository` 2319 → 2360，`RuntimeBrokerService` 1909 → 2028；其中 `RuntimeBrokerService` 在后续 #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**) 抽离 `RuntimeDispatchPayloadAdmission` 后进一步回落至 2006）。
- 未验证 / 范围外：无绑定 Session principal 归属（`ma_session_principal`）位于 #17471 (**[16023 A/2]**)；外部前台 Shell 执行位于 #17473 (**[17357 A/2]**) 与 #17474 (**[17357 B/2]**)。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：在 `V1__managed_schema.sql` 的 `ma_tool_execution` 表中新增 `shared_dispatch_class VARCHAR(16)`，并在 `ExternalRuntimeClient` SPI 中新增 `reattach`。

设计文档：
- [Reattach the original external Workspace worker (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-external-reattach.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-external-reattach.zh-CN.md)
- [Retire external Workspaces after settled failures (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-retirement-settled-failure.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/managed-retirement-settled-failure.zh-CN.md)
- [Class-size ratchet exception note (EN)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/2026-11-04-managed-agent-class-size-ratchet.md) · [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/split/16023-resident-workspace/docs/design/2026-11-04-managed-agent-class-size-ratchet.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

关联 #15512、#15247。拆自 #16023（`[16023 B/2]`）。

prs.title: fix(core): do not call a command read-only when a redirection hides part of it
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The read-only shell classifier no longer calls a command read-only when part of the command is hidden inside a redirection node.

- **A file redirection followed by more words.** `git branch < /dev/null -D main` and `find . 2>&1 -delete` now classify `unknown`. A redirection that carries more words than its operator takes is not read-only: one for every operator except `<&-` and `>&-`, which close a descriptor and take none, so `find . >&- -delete` is `unknown` too.
- **A heredoc followed by more on the same line.** Whatever shares the heredoc's first line is now judged: a redirection or a statement by the existing rule for its kind, a plain word as `unknown`. `cat <<EOF > out.txt` and `cat <<EOF && rm x` now classify `write`; `cat <<EOF | sh` classifies `unknown`.
- **A command in a heredoc body.** When the delimiter is unquoted, bash expands the body, and the parse tree does not show what it expands: a backtick substitution is plain text there, and so is `$(...)` behind leading whitespace. The body is therefore read from its own text. Every expansion bash performs in a heredoc body starts with `$` or a backtick, so an expandable body holding either is `unknown`. `detectCommandSubstitution` in `shell-utils.ts` already scans a heredoc body's text this way for `$(` and a backtick; this is the same test on the AST path, widened to any `$` because `$[x]` and `$((x))` run a command held in `x`. With a delimiter quoted as a whole (`'EOF'`, `"EOF"`, `\EOF`) the body stays read-only. A delimiter that is neither one plain word nor quoted as a whole, such as `${X:-'E'}` or `$X`, is `unknown` whatever the body holds.

A redirection with one word, a heredoc with nothing after it, and a heredoc piped into a read-only command stay read-only.

## Why it's needed

A read-only verdict is an allow with no prompt and no classifier call (`ShellToolInvocation.getDefaultPermission`, `if (isReadOnly) { return 'allow'; }`). tree-sitter-bash files the words after a redirection under the redirection node, so `getArgumentNodes` never returns them and no rule reads them. #16856 has the mechanism and the first set of cases.

**Behaviour change to accept on purpose:** `cat <<EOF > file` is how an agent often writes a file. On `main` it classifies read-only, so it takes the read-only fast path. With this PR it is a `write` like any other output redirection.

While fixing the issue I found two more shapes that are not in it:

- `2>&1` in the middle of a command hides the words after it the same way as `<`.
- A heredoc hides the rest of its first line. The redirection, the pipeline or the next command of a list is a child of the `heredoc_redirect` node, and `evaluateRedirectionSafety` only looked inside that node for command substitutions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`packages/core/src/utils/shellAstParser.test.ts`, `describe('words after a redirection in the middle of a command')`. The new cases fail on `main`'s source (39 failures) and pass with the change; the controls pass on both.

A sweep outside the test file: each of 27 redirection spellings and 7 heredoc spellings inserted at every word boundary of 7 write commands (`find . -delete`, `git branch -D main`, `sed -i …`, `git push …`, `git remote add …`, `sort -o …`, `tee out`), plus heredocs followed by those commands and heredoc bodies that run something. 1,291 commands: 357 classify read-only on `main`, none on this branch.

A second sweep for heredoc bodies, with real bash as the reference: 26 delimiter spellings × 4 operator forms × 9 bodies (backtick and `$(...)` commands at line start, behind a tab, behind a space and on an indented second line, `$[x]` and `$((x))` with `x` holding a command, and `${V:-$(...)}`), closed both by the delimiter as written and by its quote-removed form. Each body creates a marker file when bash runs it. Of 1,548 commands, 207 on `main` classify read-only while bash (3.2.57) runs the body's command; none do on this branch.

### Evidence (Before & After)

`classifyShellCommandSafety`, measured on `main`'s classifier and on this branch (heredoc rows show the first line; the body and the closing `EOF` follow):

| Command | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git branch < /dev/null -D main` | read-only | unknown |
| `git < /dev/null push origin main` | read-only | unknown |
| `git remote < /dev/null add origin <url>` | read-only | unknown |
| `find . < /dev/null -delete` | read-only | unknown |
| `sed < /dev/null -i 's/a/b/' f` | read-only | unknown |
| `git branch 2>&1 -D main` | read-only | unknown |
| `find . 2>&1 -delete` | read-only | unknown |
| `find . >&- -delete`, `find . <&- -delete`, `find . 2>&- -delete` | read-only | unknown |
| `git branch <<EOF -D main` | read-only | unknown |
| `cat <<EOF \| sh` | read-only | unknown |
| `cat <<EOF` with `` `id -u` `` in the body | read-only | unknown |
| `cat <<EOF > out.txt` | read-only | write |
| `cat <<EOF && rm x` | read-only | write |
| `cat <<EOF \| tee out.txt` | read-only | write |
| `cat <<EOF \| git push origin main` | read-only | write |

Unchanged (asserted by the new tests):

| Command | Both |
| --- | --- |
| `git status < /dev/null`, `git status 2>&1`, `git status 2>&1 \| head`, `git status >&-`, `git status <<< x` | read-only |
| `cat < a.txt < b.txt`, `cat < "my file.txt"` | read-only |
| `cat <<EOF`, `cat << EOF`, `cat 3<<EOF`, `cat <<EOF # note`, `cat <<EOF \| grep hi`, `cat <<EOF \| grep hi \| wc -l` | read-only |
| `cat <<'EOF'` with a backtick in the body | read-only |
| `git branch -D main < /dev/null`, `git branch > out.txt -D main`, `< /dev/null git push origin main`, `git branch <<< x -D main` | write |

Local run: `shellAstParser`, `shellReadOnlyChecker`, `shell-utils`, `plan-mode-shell-policy`, `coreToolScheduler`, `tools/monitor`, `tools/shell` and all of `permissions/`: 23 files, 3,753 tests passed at `ecf4814f4e` (`main` merged at `5916929761`). ESLint and Prettier are clean on the two changed files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only. The classifier was called directly from the source tree; I did not run an end-to-end AUTO session.

## Risk & Scope

- **Design choice for the words after a file redirection.** The issue offered two directions: collect those words back into the argument list, or refuse read-only when they are present. This PR takes the second. Collecting them would give exact verdicts (`git < /dev/null push` would be `write`, not `unknown`), but it means rebuilding the argument list bash hands the program, with ordering across several redirections to get right. Refusing needs no model of bash, so it cannot be wrong about one. If you prefer exact verdicts I can do the first as a follow-up.
- **Why the heredoc is handled differently.** Refusing everything after a heredoc would also stop `cat <<EOF | grep hi`, which is common and harmless. The pipeline, command or redirection inside the heredoc node is a complete node of a kind the classifier already judges, so it is passed to the existing rule. Only a bare word is refused, and so is any node the classifier has no rule for.
- **Main risk or tradeoff:** more prompts. A harmless command that puts words after a redirection, such as `cat < a.txt b.txt` or `grep foo < in.txt -r .`, now classifies `unknown`. And `cat <<EOF > file` goes from the read-only fast path to a `write`, as described above. A heredoc with an unusual delimiter (`"$X"`, `E"O"F`, `$'EOF'`) is `unknown` even where bash would leave its body alone; only the three whole-delimiter quotings are vouched for. A heredoc under a plain delimiter whose body holds any `$`, such as `$HOME`, is `unknown` too, although a bare variable runs nothing.
- **Not in this PR (review finding R1-3):** `extractCommandRules` builds the "always allow" rule from the same shortened argument list, so approving `git < /dev/null push origin main` offers the rule `git`. On `main` that dialog never appears because the command is read-only; with this PR it can. What rule should be offered for such a spelling, or whether none should be, is a separate decision in a different function, and I would rather a maintainer made it than widen this PR.
- **Not in this PR (review finding R3-1):** the dialog's rules are built per line, so a heredoc body line becomes a rule of its own. That is already the case on `main` for `cat > f <<EOF` and `tee f <<EOF`; it is written up on #17001, where the fix for that path is planned.
- **Not validated / out of scope:** the regex fallback (`isShellCommandReadOnly`) is unchanged; it already answers not-read-only for every row of the first table. The git-config risk check also reads `getArgumentNodes`; it derives a config warning from it, not a read-only verdict, and is unchanged.
- **Related:** this also covers the remaining finding on #14360 (R11-3, `git remote < /dev/null show <url>`), which the new tests include.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none in the API.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16856

prs.title: feat(serve): add daemon restart recovery inbox
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a daemon restart recovery inbox. After a daemon restart, `POST /sessions/recovery` lists workspace sessions whose newest prompt did not settle, and `POST /sessions/recovery/continue` resumes a selected batch without opening or switching conversations. The scan reads the bounded tail of the existing prompt terminal ledger; session enumeration reads only the transcript head for project membership. Session ids are validated against the persisted file shape before deriving a ledger path, and continuation cold-loads through the existing restore core and the live session-owner continuation path. The routes are advertised by a new `restart_recovery` capability, exposed as `DaemonClient.getRestartRecoveries` / `continueRestartRecoveries`, and surfaced in Web Shell as a sidebar panel above the session list.

## Why it's needed

After a restart, recovery was only reachable after opening each interrupted conversation: the recovery summary is produced after a cold load, and the Continue button lives inside the chat surface. With several workspaces and interrupted tasks, users had to find every conversation in the sidebar and click Continue one by one. This change gives one place to see the interrupted tasks and resume them, while keeping the existing per-conversation recovery behavior unchanged.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused daemon, SDK, and Web Shell suites from the repository root:

```bash
(cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/restart-recovery-scan.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-restart-recovery-continue.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry-catalog.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry.test.ts src/serve/rest-integration-docs-contract.test.ts src/serve/capabilities-docs-contract.test.ts src/serve/capability-parity.test.ts)
(cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx vitest run test/unit/daemon-public-surface.test.ts)
(cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx vitest run test/unit/DaemonClient.test.ts -t 'restart recovery')
(cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/RestartRecoveryPanel.test.tsx client/i18n.test.ts)
npm run build && npm run bundle
(cd integration-tests && QWEN_SANDBOX=false npx vitest run cli/qwen-serve-restart-recovery.test.ts)
```

Expected: the scanner classifies `in_flight`, interrupted terminals, and the normal-shutdown `error`/`daemon_shutdown` terminal, and skips settled ones; the query route enforces workspace trust, per-member errors, the 30-day clamp, and omits live active sessions; the continuation route cold-loads, requires `confirmToolTurn` for tool turns, and refuses degraded history; the sidebar panel lists interrupted sessions, continues one or all, stays hidden when the capability is absent, and routes cancellation confirmations to the conversation. The integration test starts a real daemon, SIGKILLs it mid-turn, restarts it, scans the persisted session, continues it, and checks the transcript and ledger.

To exercise the real flow manually: start a daemon, start a long turn, kill the daemon process, restart it, call `POST /sessions/recovery` with the workspace, then `POST /sessions/recovery/continue` and confirm a new turn appears in the persisted transcript. Two daemon-level runs passed in this worktree against the built daemon and a loopback fake model: the SIGKILL run reported `interruption: in_flight`; the SIGTERM run reported `interruption: daemon_shutdown`. In both cases `POST /sessions/recovery/continue` returned `accepted` with a `promptId`, the persisted transcript contained the new assistant output and its `turn_result`, the prompt ledger reached `completed`, and a second scan no longer listed the session.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for screenshots. Daemon-level evidence comes from the restarted session's persisted transcript: the continuation `promptId` appears in a new `turn_result` followed by assistant output, and the prompt ledger records the matching completed terminal.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Linux covers the focused unit, contract, component, and committed daemon restart integration suites, plus local SIGKILL and SIGTERM daemon runs. macOS and Windows were not run.

### Environment (optional)

Focused vitest suites and a built daemon in this worktree; no Docker or sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the scan reads a persisted sidecar ledger, so a missing or unreadable ledger fails closed and that session is not listed. The continuation route loads selected sessions into memory; the batch is capped at 10 and workspaces per scan at 20.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows, standalone conversation coverage, and automatic continuation. Tool-turn continuations require `confirmToolTurn: true`; `degraded_history` is never continued.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The new `restart_recovery` capability is additive; older daemons do not advertise it, and Web Shell hides the panel when it is absent.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-11-17-daemon-restart-recovery-inbox.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-17-daemon-restart-recovery-inbox.zh-CN.md)

prs.title: fix(channels): address Aone channel deferred review findings (#17517)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Follow-up to the merged Aone Code channel plugin (#17442), addressing the non-blocking review suggestions tracked in #17517 and the refinements from this PR's own review rounds. It is based on latest `main` and changes the Aone adapter's connect-time diagnostics, its aging diagnostic and error logging, and the bilingual design docs. It adds one backward-compatible optional field (`lastPoll`) to the persisted cursor, stamped only on fully-drained polls; dispatch, polling, dedup, budget, and outbound behavior are otherwise unchanged, and there is no core change.

- **R4-1 — aged-out cursor diagnostic.** The diagnostic fires when the pagination walk missed the cursor, there is something to resume to, AND the previous fully-drained poll predates the window start (`agedOut`). This distinguishes genuine loss (an outage, or a drain slower than arrival) from a quiet gap: a repo polled continuously within the window lost nothing even if its cursor event aged out, and a recent empty-window baseline (cursor 0) fills normally — neither is reported. The per-repo `cursor.lastPoll` instant is stamped only at the success exit of a fully-drained poll (`fresh <= slice`, including a dormant empty window); a failed poll never reaches it and a capped poll is not a complete observation, so a chronically backlogged repo keeps its last fully-drained instant until it precedes the window and the loss is diagnosed. Genuine loss records a durable `cursor_aged_out` journal event beside the stderr line (deduped per distinct stale instant), so the permanent loss is visible on the status page even though the poll itself resolves ok.
- **R4-2 — posture diagnostics.** The posture-by-posture warning enumeration is replaced with one per-repo posture-resolution pass that reproduces the base `groupConfigFor` key match (exact, then normalized) and the `senders`/`allowedUsers` repo→`*`→empty fallback chains. It adds two previously-missing diagnostics: **sender-dead** (a reachable repo whose effective senders is `allowlist` with an empty resolved `allowedUsers` list — every event dies `group_sender_denied` while the poll journals ok) and **pairing-open** (under `groupPolicy: pairing`, open senders are warned as a post-approval posture, not immediate reachability). The existing permissive / all-dead / mixed-dead warnings are preserved.
- **R4-3 — documentation accuracy.** The design docs (EN + zh-CN) now state that Aone is configured by hand in `settings.json`: it is not in the Web Shell's `SUPPORTED_CHANNEL_TYPES`, so the channel editor cannot create or edit it and the descriptor's `default: open` never seeds an editor draft; an absent `groupPolicy` resolves to `disabled` (connect warns). The previous "management UI seeds groupPolicy / editor-created channel" narrative described a path that does not exist for this plugin.
- **R4-4 — stderr sanitization.** The four raw a1-derived stderr sinks (per-repo poll failure, per-event dispatch failure, MR-view failure, and the unparseable-`createdAt` value) now pass through `sanitizeLogText`, so an error cause carrying newlines cannot forge a second `[Channel:…]` log line and a long cause stays bounded. The per-repo poll failure shares one sanitized message between the journal record and stderr.
- **verify-r4 M17/M21 coverage gaps.** The all-dead test now also asserts the mixed dead-repo wording is absent (the two diagnostics are exclusive), and a new mixed-allowlist test with two entry-less repos asserts every dead repo is named.
- **Review-round refinements (this PR's R1–R3).** R1 added the pairing-sender-dead diagnostic and made `lastPoll` stamp only at success exits (a failed poll is not an observation). R2 unified the staleness discriminator across both cursor arms (a quiet repo no longer writes a false `cursor_aged_out`). R3 made a capped poll not refresh `lastPoll` (so a drain slower than arrival is diagnosed), deduped the journal record per stale instant, and added a dormant empty-window witness for the success-exit stamp. Each refinement carries a bidirectional mutation witness.

## Why it's needed

These are genuine improvements deferred from #17442's round-4 review under its convergence posture (the PR was merge-ready with two approvals; a new commit there would have dismissed them). #17517 tracked them so they could land as a real fix based on `main` rather than being lost. Each is verified against the code: the aging over-fire, the sender-dead and pairing blind spots, the false editor narrative, and the unsanitized stderr were all reproducible.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit and meta tests (no credentials needed):

```
cd packages/channels/aone && npx vitest run
npx vitest run scripts/tests/package-scripts.test.js scripts/tests/unit-vitest-configs.test.ts
```

Expected: 109 passed / 1 skipped in the channel package (the skip is the `AONE_LIVE_SMOKE=1` live smoke); the workspace-mirror and vitest-config meta-tests stay green.

Behavioral checks, each pinned by a named test in `packages/channels/aone/src/AoneAdapter.test.ts`:

- R4-1: `an empty-window baseline (cursor 0) does not over-report aging`, `a continuously-polled quiet repo reports no aging loss`, `a stale cursor-0 repo (last poll before the window) reports genuine aging`, `a failed poll does not refresh lastPoll, so recovery reports aging`, `a drain slower than arrival reports aging, journaled once` (two capped polls over a stale `lastPoll` → aging fires both polls, exactly one journal record), and `a successful empty-window poll advances lastPoll`. Real mutation witnesses: deleting the `agedOut` clause, the `recordChannelEvent` call, the drain condition (`fresh <= slice`), the journal dedupe, or the trailing `lastPoll` stamp each turns the corresponding test red (the drain-condition mutation reds the backlog test while the quiet-repo and empty-baseline tests stay green).
- R4-2: `senders allowlist with no allowedUsers anywhere warns sender-dead`, `senders allowlist whose list lives on "*" is NOT sender-dead` (pins the repo→`*` fallback — reading only the repo entry would falsely warn), and `pairing with open senders warns the post-approval posture`.
- R4-4: `the poll-failure stderr is sanitized: no forged line, bounded`, `the per-event dispatch stderr is sanitized`, `the fetchView stderr is sanitized`, and `the unparseable-createdAt stderr is sanitized` each seed a newline-bearing forged cause and assert the captured stderr line has no forged column-0 `[Channel:…]` line and is bounded. These are adapter-only guards (the journal write path does not cover stderr); reverting any interpolation to raw turns its test red.
- M17/M21: `allowlist with no watched-repo groups entry warns dead channel` (asserts no mixed wording) and `mixed allowlist names EVERY dead repo, not just the first`.

The prior tests still pass (one pre-existing aging test was updated in place to seed a stale `lastPoll`, simulating an outage); the suite is 109 passed / 1 skipped. The posture-resolution refactor preserves the prior warning behavior.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI channel service). Before: a mixed allowlist with a sender-dead repo connected silently; an empty-window baseline printed a spurious aging warning; a newline-bearing a1 error forged a stderr log line. After: each posture is diagnosed, the aging diagnostic is gated and durable, and stderr is sanitized — as pinned by the tests above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

`npm run build && npm run bundle`, `node dist/cli.js channel start` (standalone ACP-backed runtime), real model via the host's configured provider, real `a1` reads against `middleware/tddl5` with the only write command intercepted. Windows/Linux rely on CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the change is confined to connect-time diagnostics, the aging diagnostic, and error logging. The posture-resolution pass reproduces the base gate order and fallback chains (verified against `ChannelBase.groupConfigFor`/`groupAllowedUsersFor`/`groupSendersFor`); an empty allowlist denies everyone (it does not fall through to open). The pairing-open warning deliberately does not claim immediate reachability (a pairing group needs one-time approval). The persisted cursor gains an optional `lastPoll` map (backward compatible — cursors without it still validate and are treated as stale, the safe base behavior); dispatch, dedup, budget, and outbound behavior are unchanged.
- Not validated / out of scope: the actual comment-create POST against the live platform (intercepted in verification — its argv contract is unchanged), Windows/Linux real machines (CI). Adding `aone` to the Web Shell `SUPPORTED_CHANNEL_TYPES` (the alternative R4-3 fix) is deliberately NOT done here — it would expand into the editor UI; this PR takes the documentation-accuracy branch instead.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — the optional `lastPoll` cursor field is backward compatible; existing configs behave identically (the prior tests pass, one aging test updated in place).

Design docs: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/aone-channel-r4-followup/docs/design/2026-11-16-aone-channel-plugin.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/aone-channel-r4-followup/docs/design/2026-11-16-aone-channel-plugin.zh-CN.md) (updated and synchronized).

## Linked Issues

Closes #17517 (the deferred-suggestion tracker). Follow-up to #17442 (merged).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

已合入的 Aone Code channel 插件（#17442）的后续，处置 #17517 跟踪的非阻塞评审建议及本 PR 自身评审轮次的细化。基于最新 main，改 Aone 适配器的 connect 期诊断、老化诊断与错误日志、双语设计文档。给持久化游标新增一个向后兼容的可选字段（`lastPoll`），仅在完整排空轮询写入；派发/轮询/去重/预算/出站行为其余不变，不改核心。

- **R4-1 老化游标诊断**：在翻页遍历未命中游标、有可续接事件、且**上次完整排空轮询**早于窗口起点（`agedOut`）时触发。区分真实丢失（停机或排水慢于到达）与安静间隙：窗口内持续被轮询的仓库即使游标事件老化也什么都没丢，近期空窗口基线（cursor 0）被正常填满——两者都不报。按仓库的 `cursor.lastPoll` 只在完整排空轮询（`fresh <= slice`，含休眠空窗口）的成功出口写入；失败轮询到不了那里，封顶轮询不算完整观测，故慢性积压仓库保留上次完整排空时刻直到早于窗口而丢失被诊断。真实丢失在 stderr 旁落持久 `cursor_aged_out` 台账事件（按不同陈旧时刻去重），永久丢失在状态页可见（轮询本身记 ok）。
- **R4-2 姿态诊断**：把逐姿态枚举改为对每个监听仓库做一次 posture 解析，复现基类 `groupConfigFor` 键匹配（精确→归一化）与 `senders`/`allowedUsers` 的 repo→`*`→空 回退链。新增两条此前缺失的诊断：**sender 层死**（可达仓库生效 senders 为 allowlist 但解析 allowedUsers 为空——每条事件死于 group_sender_denied 而轮询记 ok）与 **pairing-open**（pairing 下 open 发送者按批准后姿态告警，非当前可达）。既有宽松/全死/混合死告警保留。
- **R4-3 文档准确性**：双语文档更正为 Aone 由手写 settings.json 配置——不在 Web Shell `SUPPORTED_CHANNEL_TYPES` 里，编辑器无法新建/编辑，descriptor `default: open` 不播种编辑器草稿；缺省 groupPolicy 解析为 disabled（connect 告警）。此前「管理界面播种/编辑器创建」叙事描述了本插件不存在的路径。
- **R4-4 stderr 净化**：四处原样 a1 来源 stderr（逐仓库轮询失败、逐事件派发失败、MR view 失败、不可解析 createdAt 值）改经 `sanitizeLogText`，带换行的错误 cause 不再伪造第二条 `[Channel:…]` 日志行、长 cause 有界。逐仓库轮询失败共享同一净化消息给台账与 stderr。
- **verify-r4 M17/M21 覆盖缺口**：全死测试加断言不含混合措辞（两诊断互斥）；新增含两个无条目仓库的混合 allowlist 测试断言点名每个死仓库。
- **评审轮次细化（本 PR R1–R3）**：R1 增 pairing-sender-dead 诊断、lastPoll 只在成功出口写入（失败轮询不算观测）；R2 两游标臂统一陈旧判别（安静仓库不再写假 cursor_aged_out）；R3 封顶轮询不刷新 lastPoll（排水慢于到达被诊断）、台账按陈旧时刻去重、增休眠空窗口 stamp 见证。每条细化均带双向变异见证。

## 为什么需要

这些是 #17442 第 4 轮评审收敛姿态下延后的真实改进（当时 PR 已 merge-ready 且有两个人工批准，再提交会 dismiss）。#17517 跟踪以便基于 main 收成真修复而非丢失。每条均对照代码核实可复现。

## 评审验证计划

`cd packages/channels/aone && npx vitest run` 预期 109 过/1 跳过；元测试保持绿。每条修复由 `AoneAdapter.test.ts` 中具名测试钉住（R4-1 空窗口不误报/安静仓库不报/陈旧 cursor0 报/失败轮询不刷新/排水慢于到达报且台账去重/休眠 stamp、R4-2 sender-dead/`*`回退/pairing、R4-4 四处 stderr 反伪造有界、M17/M21）。真实变异见证：删 agedOut 子句、recordChannelEvent、排水条件（fresh<=slice）、台账去重、尾部 lastPoll stamp 各使对应测试变红（排水条件变异使 backlog 红而 quiet/empty-baseline 绿）。既有测试仍过（一条老化测试就地更新为种陈旧 lastPoll 模拟停机）。

## 风险与范围

仅限 connect 期诊断、老化诊断与错误日志；posture 解析复现基类门禁顺序与回退链（空 allowlist 谁都不放行，不回落到 open）；pairing-open 告警刻意不声称当前可达。持久化游标新增可选 `lastPoll` 映射（向后兼容——无此字段的游标仍校验通过并按陈旧处理，即安全的基类行为）；派发/去重/预算/出站不变。刻意**不**把 aone 加进 Web Shell SUPPORTED_CHANNEL_TYPES（R4-3 的另一选项，会扩进编辑器 UI）——本 PR 取文档准确性分支。无破坏性变更。

## 关联 Issue

关闭 #17517（延后建议跟踪）；#17442（已合入）的后续。

</details>

prs.body:
## What this PR does

Two prerequisites for phase 1 of the stateless Hosted Harness design, both useful before any suspension exists:

First, the daemon client now notifies its owner whenever it retires an attachment on its own — a heartbeat's definitive not-found answer or a proven generation change. The connector registers a handler at both points where it takes ownership of a client, and the handler removes exactly the retired reference from both attachment caches under the same per-key identity rule the eviction path uses, so a notice arriving after a newer publication leaves the newer reference and its recovery marker alone.

Second, the suspension wait codes get their control-plane classification and bounds. A full cold-open admission slot becomes a transient conflict on public routes and a budget-exempt wait for Turns, lifecycle operations, and the message/child relays. Pool waits (closing, cold-open busy, ownership handoff, drain cutoff) now age out at the same churn cap generation waits already use: after four budgets of failures without journaled progress, the Turn fails with its phase's unavailable code instead of retrying forever. A wedged teardown is a refusal, not a wait: Turns fail immediately under that code, lifecycle operations keep it through their blocked record, and it is never classified as transient.

## Why it's needed

The design (docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-stateless-harness.md) requires the control plane to recover from retired attachments and to bound every suspension-related wait before the Harness may suspend idle Sessions. Without the retirement notice, verbs outside the coded-not-found rule hold stale references indefinitely once the heartbeat retires them. Without the churn cap, any caller can fill an instance's cold-open slots with its own suspended Sessions and keep other callers' Turns retrying forever — the existing exemption only aged out generation waits. The wedged-teardown code must never enter a wait set, because only an operator or the lifecycle authority can reconcile it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

SDK: the new heartbeat tests prove a definitive not-found retirement and a generation-change retirement each notify the listener with the exact retired reference, and a reloaded replacement gets its own notice; the existing retirement and mid-flight-close tests pin unchanged semantics. Connector: the new pool test captures the registered handler and proves a notice evicts the published reference together with its recovery marker; the identity test proves a stale notice leaves a newer reference and marker intact in both caches. Control plane: the new parameterized churn-cap cases prove pool waits below the cap still retry exempt and at the cap fail with the phase's unavailable code (pre and post admission); the wedged-teardown cases prove immediate failure under its own code; the lifecycle, relay, automation, and conflict-code suites pin the classification. The two existing pool/drain wait tests were updated to the new semantics: they still prove the waits outlive the charged admission budgets, and now also prove they age out at the cap.

Local results: SDK focused 4/4; server suites 247/247 (full coordinator class 169, reproduction 21, SDK boundary 17, lifecycle budget 16, plus the focused connector/relay/automation/conflict cases); dual Checkstyle executions 0 violations across all modules; SDK Checkstyle 0 violations.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — control-plane and SDK behavior, no UI.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

JDK 21 + Maven 3.9.12, isolated local repository, sibling SDK installed from the same checkout. Full Hosted/MySQL tiers are CI-owned.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: pool waits that were previously exempt without bound now fail at the churn cap; this is the designed behavior change, and the updated tests pin both halves (outlive the charged budget, age out at the cap). The retirement handler scans the caches by reference identity because the notice carries only the reference while the caches are keyed by tenant, Session and placement epoch; retirements are rare and the scan mirrors the existing generation-adoption path.
- Not validated / out of scope: the Harness suspension mechanism itself (separate track); real dual-control-plane takeover under these classifications (CI Hosted tier); the relays' closing/open-busy waits are bounded indirectly by the Harness escalating a wedged teardown to the refusal code, which spends their attempt budget.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; no schema or protocol change.

## Linked Issues

References #17527 (phase-1 prerequisites of the merged design). Design: [English](docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-stateless-harness.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-stateless-harness.zh-CN.md).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

无状态 Hosted Harness 设计第一阶段的两个前置改动，两者在任何挂起功能存在之前就有用：

其一，daemon client 现在会在自行退休 attachment 时通知其持有者——心跳的确定性 not-found 回答或已证实的 generation 变更。connector 在取得 client 所有权的两个入口注册处理器，处理器按与驱逐路径相同的按 key 身份规则，从两张 attachment 缓存中恰好移除被退休的引用；因此晚于新发布到达的通知不会动新引用及其恢复标记。

其二，挂起等待码获得控制面分类与界限。冷打开准入名额满成为公共路由上的暂时性冲突，以及 Turn、lifecycle 操作、消息/子 relay 的免预算等待。池等待（closing、冷打开忙、ownership 交接、drain 截止）现在按 generation 等待已有的同一 churn 上限老化：在没有 journal 进展的情况下经过四倍预算的失败后，Turn 以其所处阶段的 unavailable 码失败，而不是永远重试。卡死的 teardown 是拒绝而非等待：Turn 立即以该码失败，lifecycle 操作在其 blocked 记录中保留该码，且它绝不被分类为暂时性。

## 为什么需要

设计（docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-stateless-harness.zh-CN.md）要求控制面能够从被退休的 attachment 恢复，并在 Harness 可以挂起空闲 Session 之前给每一种挂起相关等待设界。没有退休通知，coded-not-found 规则之外的动词会在心跳退休引用后无限期持有过期引用。没有 churn 上限，任何调用方都可以用自己挂起的 Session 占满某个实例的冷打开名额，让其他调用方的 Turn 永远重试——现有豁免只让 generation 等待老化。卡死 teardown 码绝不能进入等待集合，因为唯有运维或 lifecycle authority 能对账它。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

SDK：新心跳测试证明确定性 not-found 退休与 generation 变更退休各自以被退休的精确引用通知监听器，重加载的替代引用获得自己的通知；既有退休与在飞关闭测试固定不变的语义。Connector：新池测试捕获注册的处理器，证明通知将被发布的引用连同其恢复标记一起驱逐；身份测试证明过期通知在两张缓存中都不动新引用与标记。控制面：新参数化 churn 上限用例证明低于上限的池等待仍以免预算重试、到达上限以阶段 unavailable 码失败（准入前与准入后）；卡死 teardown 用例证明以自身码立即失败；lifecycle、relay、automation、冲突码套件固定分类。两个既有池/drain 等待测试已更新到新语义：仍证明等待免扣准入预算，并同时证明在 churn 上限处老化失败。

本地结果：SDK 聚焦 4/4；server 套件 247/247（完整 coordinator 类 169、复现 21、SDK 边界 17、lifecycle 预算 16，加聚焦的 connector/relay/automation/冲突码用例）；双 Checkstyle execution 全模块 0 violations；SDK Checkstyle 0 violations。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A — 控制面与 SDK 行为，无 UI。

### 测试平台

macOS ✅（JDK 21 + Maven 3.9.12，隔离本地仓库，sibling SDK 从同一 checkout 安装）；Windows/Linux ⚠️ 未本地测试。完整 Hosted/MySQL 层级归 CI。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：此前无界豁免的池等待现在在 churn 上限处失败；这是设计内的行为变更，更新后的测试固定了两半（免扣预算、到上限老化）。退休处理器按引用身份扫描缓存，因为通知只携带引用而缓存按租户、Session、placement epoch 键控；退休罕见，扫描镜像既有的 generation 采纳路径。
- 未验证/范围外：Harness 挂起机制本身（独立轨道）；这些分类下的真实双控制面接管（CI Hosted 层级）；relay 的 closing/open-busy 等待由 Harness 将卡死 teardown 升级为拒绝码间接设界，该码消耗其尝试预算。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无；无 schema 或协议变更。

## 关联

引用 #17527（已合并设计的第一阶段前置）。设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-stateless-harness.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-16-managed-stateless-harness.zh-CN.md)。

</details>
