prs.title: feat(cli): polish terminal layout and streaming interactions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keeps the composer at the bottom, centers bounded dialogs over the transcript, and places approval mode beside its cycling shortcut on the input's lower-right border in main and agent views. Virtual scrolling uses smaller paced updates; transcript, preview, and input share consistent drag selection and copying.

Shows completed safe tool/thought activity as muted summaries. Expanding reveals compact command/path rows and retains a clickable collapse header; Ctrl+O reaches original full details. Closing a process clears its expanded children, and independently virtualized members retain their own viewport visibility.

Uses fixed deadlines for streamed state updates and terminal drawing, reuses stable Markdown prefixes and unchanged code-line highlights, and keeps original stream-boundary ordering. Actual controls-height measurement and consistent virtual-message budgets keep advancing text and the final transcript line visible when the footer or auxiliary panels change height.

## Why it's needed

Short conversations left the input above unused space; large settings/session dialogs could overflow. Repeated process details competed with answers, and opening a tool summary could not be reversed. Selection could include popup borders or trigger expansion on release, while approval mode and its shortcut appeared in different places.

Regular small text chunks still appeared in uneven groups. A full new buffering window after each batch introduced avoidable waiting, and stable Markdown/code was processed repeatedly. Long pending paragraphs could hide their advancing tail in short virtual viewports. A stale controls-height budget could also clip the final checkpoint name from `/restore` until scrolling corrected it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start an empty session and open `/settings`, `/resume`, model, theme and permission dialogs. The composer should stay at the bottom; dialogs should remain centered and bounded, with the draft restored afterward. Check main and agent inputs: mode and cycling shortcut should share the lower-right border, without a duplicate footer hint. Resize narrow and restore.
2. Run reads, commands and thinking. Completed safe activity should use a muted summary, while live work, failures and approvals remain visible. Click to open compact details, click the retained header to close, and use Ctrl+O for original output. Repeat during and after generation; opening a child then closing its parent should leave the process closed.
3. Scroll slowly, rapidly and in reverse; use PageUp/Home/End and drag the scrollbar. One upward row should remain detached as content arrives. Drag ASCII, Chinese and multiline text in transcript, preview and main/agent input: copied text should match the highlight and exclude borders. Releasing a selection on a summary should not toggle it; an ordinary click should.
4. Stream prose, Chinese, open code and Markdown/list/table content. Updates should advance with less repeated work and retain the exact final suffix. Resize and change rendering context; completed prefixes, syntax colors, gutters and copy hints should remain correct. A long paragraph should keep advancing before completion in a short virtual viewport.
5. Cancel during buffered output and stream reasoning-to-answer, tool-to-answer and inline-image transitions. Preserve the received tail and ordering. Native scrollback and screen-reader modes should retain their existing layout and completion behavior. Do not infer a physical terminal frame rate from a timer setting.
6. Open and close completion, shortcuts and auxiliary panels after history overflows. The final transcript line should remain visible. List checkpoints with `/restore`, then hot-restore and cold-resume one; the name, files and retained conversation should agree without a scroll workaround.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Installed CLI layout | Bottom-composer layout |
| --- | --- |
| ![Installed CLI](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/b254b90397b50e768275c772449a21a27a936925/docs/design/images/tui-workspace/before-installed.png?raw=true) | ![Bottom composer](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/b254b90397b50e768275c772449a21a27a936925/docs/design/images/tui-workspace/after-startup.png?raw=true) |

These earlier layout captures use isolated fake providers and synthetic data. The installed CLI reports a 0.25.0 banner and is an environment comparison, not a rebuilt PR base. Separate E2E reports record the later pointer, expansion and approval-shortcut checks with their exact artifacts.

With identical synthetic payloads in real PTYs, Chinese visible-marker gap P95 changes from 67ms to 51ms; ASCII remains 51ms. Server-marker-to-visible lag P95 changes from 59/65/93ms to 52/50/88ms for ASCII/Chinese/mixed Markdown. Mixed Markdown visible-gap P95 rises from 117ms to 134ms, so this is not a uniform improvement across all intervals. All five final payloads, including bursts and an 80-line open code block, match exactly.

In a separate controlled 72-update renderer profile, body-write gap P95 changes from 34.73/37.61/38.58ms to 19.77/20.40/19.97ms for prose/labeled code/unlabeled code. Repeated highlighting of unchanged code lines drops from 1296 calls to zero. This profile excludes the application event buffer and native terminal presentation.

Full build, repository typecheck, bundle, focused unit tests, scoped lint/format checks and clean Ink patch application pass. The separate streaming E2E comment records the baseline, candidate and final measurements, exact-content checks, coverage and exclusions.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Real PTYs, Canary/xterm, main and Arena agent views |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not runtime tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not runtime tested |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 26.13.1; default Ink renderer; loopback fake providers; isolated settings, sessions, workspace and clipboard shim. Automated pointer checks use standard SGR through Canary/xterm. The user confirmed transcript dragging in Warp; this is not a native Warp/Grok frame-rate comparison.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: shared viewport geometry, pointer ownership, cache invalidation and the existing Ink patch affect terminal behavior. Frozen prefixes are conservative; unfinished text/code still requires work, and very large provider bursts can appear in one update.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows/Linux runtime interaction and full OpenTUI parity. Arena retains its committed-round display. No output worker or physical VSync acknowledgement is introduced, and no fixed visible 60/120 FPS is promised.
- Known follow-up: continuing one unfinished answer can shift a detached viewport toward older content. The same 16-row shift reproduces in archived pre-increment source with pinned Ink and a test-only JSX runtime shim; this auxiliary replay establishes behavior, not binary timing. The limitation is retained for a focused viewport fix and is not claimed resolved here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no configuration migration, provider/protocol change or permission-policy change. Input selection copies text; editable replacement ranges are not added. Native scrollback retains its height safety limits.

Designs: [visual hierarchy — English](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/b254b90397b50e768275c772449a21a27a936925/docs/design/tui-visual-hierarchy.md) / [中文](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/b254b90397b50e768275c772449a21a27a936925/docs/design/tui-visual-hierarchy.zh-CN.md); [workspace layout — English](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/53d4cbd95f513d4511fc666fb96258c6d58384d7/docs/design/tui-workspace-layout.md) / [中文](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/53d4cbd95f513d4511fc666fb96258c6d58384d7/docs/design/tui-workspace-layout.zh-CN.md); [scrolling and selection — English](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/43275f059d96d46a2f926ef1519e56bd83848adc/docs/design/tui-pointer-and-composer.md) / [中文](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/43275f059d96d46a2f926ef1519e56bd83848adc/docs/design/tui-pointer-and-composer.zh-CN.md); [streaming and controls — English](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/507e7dfc5410be0460279d503cb4ce3329e55b72/docs/design/tui-streaming-cadence.md) / [中文](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/507e7dfc5410be0460279d503cb4ce3329e55b72/docs/design/tui-streaming-cadence.zh-CN.md); [incremental streaming — English](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/116632670d512725dbeedfb8ae523c55a1bf88c7/docs/design/tui-incremental-streaming.md) / [中文](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/116632670d512725dbeedfb8ae523c55a1bf88c7/docs/design/tui-incremental-streaming.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

N/A — locally reported UI issues.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

将输入框固定在底部，让有尺寸约束的弹窗居中悬浮在聊天区上方，并在主视图和 agent 输入框右下边框，将权限模式与切换快捷键并排显示。虚拟滚动采用较小的按帧位移，聊天区、预览和输入文字采用一致的拖选、复制行为。

将已完成的安全工具和思考过程显示为淡色摘要。展开显示紧凑的命令、路径明细，并保留可点击的收起标题；Ctrl+O 可以查看原始完整详情。收起父过程时清理已展开子项，各个独立虚拟行仍保留自身的视口可见状态。

流式状态更新和终端绘制采用固定截止时间，复用稳定 Markdown 前缀和未变化代码行的高亮，并保留原有流事件边界顺序。跟踪控件的实际高度，并统一虚拟消息的内容预算，使文字持续推进，底部栏和辅助面板改变高度后聊天区最后一行仍可见。

## 为什么需要

短对话的输入框原本悬在空白上方，大型设置和会话弹窗可能溢出。重复过程详情会抢占回答的注意力，打开工具摘要后也无法收起。选择文字可能复制到弹窗边框或在松手时触发展开，权限模式与快捷键也出现在不同位置。

持续到达的小文字分片仍会不均匀地成批出现。每批结束后再等待一个完整缓冲窗口会引入额外等待，稳定 Markdown 和代码也被反复处理。长段落在较矮的虚拟视口里可能藏住正在增长的尾部，控件高度预算过时还会裁掉 `/restore` 的最后一个检查点名，直到滚动触发修正。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 启动空会话，打开 `/settings`、`/resume`、模型、主题和权限弹窗。输入框应保持底部，弹窗应居中且有尺寸约束，关闭后恢复草稿。主输入和 agent 输入的权限模式、切换提示应在右下边框同一组，页脚没有重复提示。缩窄窗口，再恢复。
2. 运行读取、命令和思考。完成的安全过程应采用淡色摘要，运行中活动、失败和审批保持可见。点击打开紧凑明细，再点保留的标题收起，Ctrl+O 查看原始输出。在生成中和完成后分别重复；打开子项再收起父过程，应保持关闭。
3. 缓慢、快速和反向滚动，使用 PageUp/Home/End，并拖动滚动条。向上一行后，新内容到来时保持脱离底部。在聊天、预览、主输入和 agent 输入拖选 ASCII、中文和多行文字，复制应与高亮一致、不含边框。拖选到摘要松手不应切换状态，普通点击可以。
4. 流式输出正文、中文、开放代码和 Markdown、列表、表格。更新应减少重复工作并保留准确最终尾部。缩放窗口并切换渲染上下文，稳定前缀、语法颜色、行号和复制提示仍正确。长段落在较矮虚拟视口里应在完成前持续推进。
5. 在存在缓冲文字时取消，并验证思考转回答、工具转回答和内联图片转换。保留已接收尾部和顺序。原生回滚、读屏模式保留既有布局及完成行为，不将定时器设置视为实际终端帧率。
6. 历史溢出后打开、关闭补全、快捷键和辅助面板，聊天区最后一行应保持可见。用 `/restore` 列出检查点，再执行热恢复和冷启动恢复，显示的名称、文件和保留对话应一致，无需滚动补救。

### 证据（改动前后）

| 已安装 CLI 布局 | 底部输入框布局 |
| --- | --- |
| ![已安装 CLI](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/b254b90397b50e768275c772449a21a27a936925/docs/design/images/tui-workspace/before-installed.png?raw=true) | ![底部输入框](https://github.com/DragonnZhang/qwen-code/blob/b254b90397b50e768275c772449a21a27a936925/docs/design/images/tui-workspace/after-startup.png?raw=true) |

这些较早的布局截图使用隔离模拟模型和合成数据。已安装 CLI 的启动标识为 0.25.0，属于环境对照，不是重建的 PR 基线。独立 E2E 报告记录后续指针、展开及权限快捷键验证和对应准确产物。

相同合成内容在真实 PTY 中回放，中文可见标记间隔 P95 从 67ms 变为 51ms，ASCII 仍为 51ms。ASCII、中文、混合 Markdown 的服务端标记到可见延迟 P95 从 59/65/93ms 变为 52/50/88ms。混合 Markdown 的可见间隔 P95 从 117ms 增至 134ms，因此并非所有间隔都一致改善。五个场景的最终内容均完整一致，包括突发分片和 80 行开放代码块。

独立的 72 次更新受控渲染器测量中，正文、有语言代码、无语言代码的写入间隔 P95 从 34.73/37.61/38.58ms 变为 19.77/20.40/19.97ms。未变化代码行的重复高亮从 1296 次降至零。此测量不包含应用事件缓冲和原生终端实际呈现。

完整构建、仓库类型检查、bundle、定点单测、范围内 lint 和格式检查及 Ink 补丁干净应用均通过。独立流式 E2E 评论记录基线、候选及最终测量、完整文字检查、覆盖和排除项。

### 测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 真实 PTY、Canary/xterm、主视图和 Arena agent 视图 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未做运行验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未做运行验证 |

### 环境（可选）

Node.js 26.13.1；默认 Ink 渲染器；本机回环模拟模型；隔离的设置、会话、工作区和剪贴板替身。自动化指针检查通过 Canary/xterm 的标准 SGR 完成。用户已确认 Warp 主聊天拖选正常，这不是原生 Warp/Grok 帧率对比。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：共享视口几何、指针归属、缓存失效和现有 Ink 补丁影响终端行为。前缀冻结采取保守边界，未完成文字和代码仍需计算，极大的模型分片也可能一次显示。
- 未验证或不在范围内：Windows/Linux 运行交互和完整 OpenTUI 对齐。Arena 保留按已完成轮次显示。没有新增输出线程或实际屏幕 VSync 反馈，也不承诺固定每秒 60/120 可见帧。
- 已知后续事项：同一条未完成回答继续输出时，脱离底部的视口可能向较早内容移动。改动前的归档源码、固定 Ink 和仅测试使用的 JSX 运行时替身可复现相同的 16 行位移；该辅助回放只用于确认行为，不用于二进制性能对比。此限制留待单独修复视口，不宣称已在这里解决。
- 破坏性变更与迁移说明：无需配置迁移，不改变模型、协议或权限策略。输入选区用于复制，不增加可替换的编辑选区。原生回滚保留高度安全限制。

prs.title: fix(core): deliver background async hook output to the model
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Fixes the capability ledger's L11 defect: background (async) hook output now reaches the model. Async hooks run between turns and their completed output (additional context and notification messages) accumulates in the async registry, but `HookSystem.getPendingAsyncOutput()` — the get-and-clear drain meant "for delivery to the next turn" — had no caller, so the output was collected and silently dropped. This drains it when the outgoing request is assembled and appends it as a reserved-tag context part, before the send and its in-chat auto-compaction. Adds a self-contained `hooks/async-hook-context.ts` helper, unit tests with mutation witnesses, and a bilingual design doc.

## Why it's needed

The ledger maps L11 ("Async hook output reaches the model") as `missing`: main collects async hook output but nothing reads it before a request, while the 1.0 loop drains the equivalent pending context in its request preparation and injects it before compression. #17284 carries L11 explicitly as a defect. A user whose background hook produces `additionalContext` or a `systemMessage` today gets nothing delivered to the model; this closes that gap.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/hooks/async-hook-context.test.ts src/core/prompt-context-order.test.ts` — 21 + 9 tests pass. The helper tests drive a real `AsyncHookRegistry` (delivery, get-and-clear drain-once, blank output yields no part, closing-tag forgery escaped, envelope matcher); the prompt-context-order tests pin the wire reorder hoisting the async block ahead of the user's instruction. `client.test.ts` adds eleven call-site tests under "async hook output delivery (L11)" driving the real `sendMessageStream`: delivery, drain-once, nothing-pending, a co-occurrence UserQuery turn (sync receipt stays the last part, async immediately before it), a ToolResult turn (block appended after the unchanged `functionResponse` parts), the in-memory-only boundary (the persisted user record carries no async block while the wire request does), the `/btw` ownership gate (a flagged side send and its unflagged ToolResult continuation leave the block for the owning turn, which receives it once), and two continue-interrupted ToolResult-first turns that must still deliver — one whose prompt id was never claimed and one where a prior turn left a stale claimed budget id — plus two late side continuations (arriving after a new main turn starts, or after a same-id retry of the main turn) that must still be refused while the new turn's own continuation receives the block. `sessionTitle.test.ts` adds two cases pinning that the fallback title input excludes the async envelope (trailing and co-occurrence). Mutation witnesses (mutate → run → restore byte-identical) each kill exactly their target: drain-delivers-nothing, escape-removal, blank-guard-removal, splice-collapse, call-site-delete, wire-matcher-drop, `syncReceiptTrailing=false`, ToolResult-drain-skip, title-filter-drop, drain-into-recorded-request, a flag-only ownership gate (dropping the recorded-side-query-id check kills the `/btw` test), reverting the gate to exploration-budget ownership refusal (kills the two continue-turn tests), clearing the record when a new main turn starts (kills the late-side-continuation test), and an unconditional clear (kills both late-continuation tests). The ownership gate records each flagged side query's prompt id and refuses only that id's unflagged ToolResult continuation, keeping the record for the client's lifetime so a still-pending side continuation stays refused even after a new main turn starts; it deliberately does not use the exploration-budget prompt id, which is claimed only on `startsInteraction` and would silently drop a continue-interrupted turn's ToolResult-first send. The wiring is a single call site at the `requestToSend` assembly in `LlmClient.sendMessageStream`, after the UserPromptSubmit receipt and before the IDE-context merge; the envelope is also registered with the wire-order classifier so the user's instruction stays last on the wire. A real-environment run (headless CLI against a mock OpenAI server with an `async: true` PostToolUse hook) confirmed the block reaches the outgoing provider request body.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (no UI change; the delivered context is model-facing).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only (vitest, real `AsyncHookRegistry`); CI covers all three platforms.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the drain runs at the request assembly of every send; it is get-and-clear (delivered once), placed immediately before the send to minimize the consume-but-not-sent window on a failed send, consistent with the existing `getPendingAsyncOutput` contract.
- Not validated / out of scope: (1) the ACP default legacy round, which sends through the session's own chat rather than `LlmClient` and so does not drain yet — the ledger row therefore moves to `differs`, not `have`, and that surface's delivery is carried in #17284; (2) display projection and resume provenance for the async tag (the synchronous UserPromptSubmit context hides itself from the transcript projection and re-stamps on resume; the async block is delivered as a tagged part but not yet wired into `projectUserTranscriptForDisplay`). These are separate concerns from "the output reaches the model" and are documented as follow-ups in the design doc.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; a previously-dropped output is now delivered.

Design doc: [English](docs/design/2026-11-16-async-hook-output-delivery.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-16-async-hook-output-delivery.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

References #17284 (carries L11 as a defect) and the [agent loop capability ledger](docs/design/2026-11-15-loop-capability-ledger.md) row L11.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

修复能力台账 L11 缺陷：后台（异步）hook 输出现在送达模型。异步 hook 在轮次之间运行，其完成输出（additional context 与通知消息）累积在异步 registry，但 `HookSystem.getPendingAsyncOutput()`——意为「交付给下一轮」的取走即清空 drain——没有任何调用方，输出被收集后静默丢弃。本 PR 在组装外出请求时 drain 它，并作为保留标签上下文 part 追加，位于 send 及其 chat 内自动压缩之前。新增自包含 `hooks/async-hook-context.ts` helper、带变异见证的单测、双语设计文档。

## 为什么需要

台账把 L11（「异步 hook 输出送达模型」）标为 `missing`：main 收集异步 hook 输出但请求前无人读取，而 1.0 loop 在请求准备中 drain 等价待交付上下文并在压缩前注入。#17284 明确把 L11 作为缺陷承载。今天后台 hook 产出 `additionalContext` 或 `systemMessage` 的用户得不到任何交付；本 PR 关闭该缺口。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

跑 `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/hooks/async-hook-context.test.ts src/core/prompt-context-order.test.ts`——21 + 9 条通过。helper 测试驱动真实 `AsyncHookRegistry`（交付、取走即清空只 drain 一次、空白输出不产生 part、闭合标签伪造被转义、信封 matcher）；prompt-context-order 测试钉住线上重排把异步块前移到用户指令之前。`client.test.ts` 在「async hook output delivery (L11)」下新增十一条调用点测试，驱动真实 `sendMessageStream`：交付、只 drain 一次、无待交付、共现 UserQuery 轮（同步回执仍是末位 part、异步紧随其前）、ToolResult 轮（块追加在原样的 `functionResponse` parts 之后）、仅进程内边界（持久化用户记录不含异步块而线上请求含之）、`/btw` 所有权门（带标志侧问首发与其不带标志的 ToolResult 续传都把块留给归属轮，归属轮恰收一次）、以及两条必须仍交付的中断续跑 ToolResult 首发轮——其 prompt id 从未被认领，与先前轮留下陈旧已认领预算 id——另加两条迟到侧问续传（新主轮开始之后、或主轮同 id 重试之后到达）必须仍被拒，而新主轮自身的续传收到该块。`sessionTitle.test.ts` 新增两条用例钉住回退标题输入排除异步信封（尾随与共现）。变异见证（改→跑→按字节还原）各恰杀其目标：drain 不交付、去转义、去空白守卫、splice 塌缩、删调用点、去 wire matcher、`syncReceiptTrailing=false`、ToolResult 跳过 drain、去标题过滤、drain 入被记录 request、仅标志所有权门（去掉已记录侧问 id 检查恰杀 `/btw` 用例）、把门回退为探索预算所有权拒绝（恰杀两条续跑用例）、新主轮开始时清空记录（恰杀迟到侧问续传用例）、无条件清空（恰杀两条迟到续传用例）。所有权门记录每个带标志侧问的 prompt id，仅拒绝该 id 的不带标志 ToolResult 续传，记录保留至 client 生命周期结束、使仍在等待的侧问续传即使在新主轮开始后仍被拒；刻意不用探索预算 prompt id——它只在 `startsInteraction` 时认领，会静默丢掉中断续跑轮的 ToolResult 首发 send。接线是 `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` 中 `requestToSend` 组装处的单一调用点，在 UserPromptSubmit 回执之后、IDE 上下文合并之前；信封也登记到线上顺序分类器，使用户指令在线上保持末位。一次真实环境运行（headless CLI 指向 mock OpenAI server、配置 `async: true` 的 PostToolUse hook）确认该块到达外出的 provider 请求体。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A（无 UI 改动；交付的上下文面向模型）。

### 测试平台

macOS ✅；Windows N/A；Linux N/A（CI 覆盖三平台）。

### 环境（可选）

仅单元测试（vitest，真实 `AsyncHookRegistry`）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：drain 在每次 send 的请求组装处运行；取走即清空（交付一次），紧贴 send 之前以最小化失败 send 下「已消费未送达」窗口，与既有 `getPendingAsyncOutput` 契约一致。

prs.title: feat(web-shell): worktree carry metadata + snapshot-then-delete cleanup (#17237, P6 partial)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR advances the Web Shell worktree Codex-parity follow-up (#17237) with the carry-metadata contract and the first half of the retention/snapshot phase (P6). It does three things. First, it records the dirty overlay that a managed session worktree carries in from its source checkout (`carriedPaths`) in the session sidecar, and teaches the orphan reaper's has-work gate to exempt exactly those paths, so a checkout whose only content is the carried copy is collected instead of preserved forever. Second, it adds a worktree snapshot service that captures a worktree to a self-contained `tar.gz` plus a JSON metadata header (excluding regenerable directories, the `.git` link, and the session marker), with atomic writes and a schema version a reader refuses if unknown. Third, it replaces the reaper's permanent preserve of a dirty managed session worktree with snapshot-then-delete: when the checkout has genuine work, the reaper snapshots it into the session chats directory and then removes the checkout, so the work survives cleanup and can be restored when the chat is reopened; a capture failure falls back to the conservative preserve. It also adds the `worktree.maxRetained` setting (default 15, `0` disables count-based auto-deletion) that the upcoming retention sweep will consume.

## Why it's needed

A managed session worktree whose only content was the carried overlay used to read as "has uncommitted work" and was preserved forever by the orphan reaper, because the carried paths never reached the sidecar and the has-work gate takes only a path (the R9-6 defect reproduced in #17228's verification). More broadly, any dirty managed session worktree was stranded on cleanup rather than archived. Codex keeps the most recent managed worktrees and never loses work on cleanup: it snapshots before deletion and offers restore on reopen. This PR lays the carry-metadata and snapshot foundations and lands the snapshot-then-delete behavior so cleanup preserves work in an archive instead of stranding the checkout. Tool/agent worktrees keep their existing refusal semantics throughout.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The carry-metadata exemption: create a session worktree from a dirty source so the overlay is carried, confirm the sidecar records `carriedPaths`, delete the session, and confirm a carried-only checkout is collected while a checkout with additional non-carried work is snapshotted then deleted. The snapshot service: capture a worktree with committed, dirty-tracked, and untracked content plus a `node_modules` directory and the session marker, restore over a fresh directory, and confirm the work round-trips while `node_modules`/`.git`/marker are excluded; confirm an unknown schema version is refused and a capture error rejects without leaving a final archive. The reaper behavior: a git-ignored-only checkout and a legacy carried-only checkout (no recorded overlay) are now snapshotted then deleted, a clean or carried-only-with-overlay checkout deletes as before, and a checkout whose git state cannot be read for the snapshot is preserved (fail-closed). Focused suites: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/worktree-snapshot-service.test.ts src/services/worktreeSessionService.test.ts src/services/gitWorktreeService.dirty-carry.integ.test.ts src/services/worktreeCleanup.test.ts` and `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/server/worktree-orphan-cleanup.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-worktree-handoff.test.ts`. Mutations dropping the reaper's `carriedPaths` argument, widening the exemption to a directory prefix, reverting snapshot-then-delete to a permanent preserve, dropping the snapshot exclusion filter, and dropping the schema-version check each kill a committed case.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI (core/cli service + daemon cleanup behavior). Real-daemon probes (isolated `dist/cli.js serve` + real git + loopback HTTP) confirm: R9-6 probe 5/5 (sidecar records `carriedPaths` including the untracked file; carried-only checkout collected; non-carried work snapshotted then deleted with the archive present); P6 U3 probe 5/5 (dirty session worktree deleted, snapshot archive + meta exist in the chats dir, archive contains the session work).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, Node 24, real git 2.43; isolated daemon probes on loopback ports with throwaway repositories; `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` after merging `origin/main`. core/cli `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; core worktree/snapshot suites 190 green, cli reaper/handoff/server suites 1541 green.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: snapshot-then-delete changes the delete-path behavior for dirty managed session worktrees (previously preserved forever). It is fail-closed — a capture failure preserves the checkout, and `removeUserWorktree` still protects unmerged commits — and the snapshot preserves the work for restore. The snapshot archive includes git-ignored files (user work) but excludes regenerable directories.
- Not validated / out of scope: the count-based retention sweep (P6 U4, spec documented in the design doc), the restore affordance on reopen (P6 U5, route + Web Shell UI), and the configurable worktree root (P7). macOS/Windows runtime not exercised locally. The `worktree.maxRetained` setting is added but not yet consumed by a sweep.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `carriedPaths` is an optional sidecar field; legacy sidecars without it behave exactly as before. The snapshot meta carries a schema version.

Design documents (both languages, complete and synchronized): [carry metadata (R9-6)](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-carry-metadata.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-carry-metadata.zh-CN.md); [retention + snapshots (P6)](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-retention-snapshots.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-retention-snapshots.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

References #17237 (P6 retention + snapshot/restore; R9-6 carry metadata). Builds on #17228 (P1–P5, merged). R9-6 originates from #17228 review comments 6900008905 / 4579730709.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

本 PR 推进 Web Shell worktree 对齐 Codex 的后续（#17237），落地搬运元数据契约与保留/快照阶段（P6）的前半部分。做三件事：其一，把托管会话 worktree 从源检出携带进来的 dirty 覆盖层（`carriedPaths`）记入会话 sidecar，并让孤儿回收器的 has-work 门精确豁免这些路径，使仅含搬运副本的 checkout 被回收而非永久保留。其二，新增 worktree 快照服务，把 worktree 捕获为自包含 `tar.gz` + JSON 元数据头（排除可再生目录、`.git` 链接与会话 marker），原子写入，schema 版本未知时读取方拒绝。其三，把回收器对 dirty 托管会话 worktree 的永久保留改为「先快照再删除」：checkout 含真实工作时，回收器先快照到会话 chats 目录再移除 checkout，使 work 在清理后存续、重开 chat 时可恢复；捕获失败回退到保守保留。并新增 `worktree.maxRetained` 设置（缺省 15，`0` 关闭按数量自动删除），供即将到来的保留清扫消费。

## 为什么需要

仅含搬运覆盖层的托管会话 worktree 过去被读作「有未提交工作」而被孤儿回收器永久保留，因为搬运路径从未进入 sidecar、has-work 门只接受路径（#17228 验证复现的 R9-6 缺陷）。更广泛地，任何 dirty 托管会话 worktree 在清理时被搁置而非归档。Codex 保留最近的托管 worktree 且清理时绝不丢失 work：删除前快照、重开提供恢复。本 PR 奠定搬运元数据与快照基础，并落地「先快照再删除」行为，使清理把 work 保存在归档中而非搁置 checkout。工具/agent worktree 全程保留现有拒绝语义。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

搬运元数据豁免：从 dirty 源创建会话 worktree 使覆盖层被携带，确认 sidecar 记录 `carriedPaths`，删除会话，确认仅含搬运的 checkout 被回收、含额外非搬运工作的 checkout 被先快照再删除。快照服务：捕获含 committed/dirty-tracked/untracked 内容加 `node_modules` 目录与会话 marker 的 worktree，在新目录恢复，确认 work 往返而 `node_modules`/`.git`/marker 被排除；确认未知 schema 版本被拒、捕获错误拒绝且不留最终归档。回收器行为：仅 git-ignored 的 checkout 与旧版仅搬运（无记录覆盖层）的 checkout 现被先快照再删除，干净或含记录覆盖层的仅搬运 checkout 照旧删除，git 状态无法读取以快照的 checkout 被保留（fail-closed）。聚焦套件：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/worktree-snapshot-service.test.ts src/services/worktreeSessionService.test.ts src/services/gitWorktreeService.dirty-carry.integ.test.ts src/services/worktreeCleanup.test.ts` 与 `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/server/worktree-orphan-cleanup.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-worktree-handoff.test.ts`。去掉回收器 `carriedPaths` 参数、把豁免放宽为目录前缀、把先快照再删除还原为永久保留、去掉快照排除过滤、去掉 schema 版本校验的变异各击杀一条 committed 用例。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A — 非 UI（core/cli 服务 + daemon 清理行为）。真实 daemon 探针（隔离 `dist/cli.js serve` + 真实 git + 回环 HTTP）确认：R9-6 探针 5/5（sidecar 记录 `carriedPaths` 含 untracked 文件；仅搬运 checkout 被回收；非搬运工作被先快照再删除且归档存在）；P6 U3 探针 5/5（dirty 会话 worktree 被删除、快照归档+meta 存在于 chats 目录、归档含会话 work）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

Linux、Node 24、真实 git 2.43；回环端口隔离 daemon 探针 + 一次性仓库；合并 `origin/main` 后 `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`。core/cli `tsc --noEmit` exit 0；core worktree/快照套件 190 绿，cli reaper/handoff/server 套件 1541 绿。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：先快照再删除改变了 dirty 托管会话 worktree 的删除路径行为（过去永久保留）。它 fail-closed——捕获失败保留 checkout，且 `removeUserWorktree` 仍保护未合并 commit——快照保存 work 以供恢复。快照归档包含 git-ignored 文件（用户 work）但排除可再生目录。
- 未验证/范围外：按数量保留清扫（P6 U4，规格已记入设计文档）、重开恢复入口（P6 U5，路由 + Web Shell UI）、可配置 worktree 根（P7）。macOS/Windows 运行时未本地执行。`worktree.maxRetained` 设置已加但尚未被清扫消费。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。`carriedPaths` 是可选 sidecar 字段；无该字段的旧 sidecar 行为完全如前。快照 meta 带 schema 版本。

设计文档（双语，完整同步）：[搬运元数据（R9-6）](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-carry-metadata.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-carry-metadata.zh-CN.md)；[保留 + 快照（P6）](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-retention-snapshots.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-17-worktree-retention-snapshots.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

引用 #17237（P6 保留 + 快照/恢复；R9-6 搬运元数据）。基于 #17228（P1–P5，已合入）。R9-6 源自 #17228 评审评论 6900008905 / 4579730709。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): report terminal model errors in headless JSON output
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keeps terminal failures inside reusable stream-json sessions: failed turns emit one error result without exiting the host process or running process-wide cleanup. This includes tool/time budgets, local and cumulative session turn limits, and non-recoverable turn cancellation. Recoverable SDK interrupts keep their existing continuation behavior. Provider control characters are neutralized when rendered to stderr, while the original error value is preserved.

Background task callbacks belong to the reusable session. Started/completion notifications stay paired during stream cancellation and EOF draining, and completed turns do not wait indefinitely for in-flight background agents. The documentation explains that EOF cancels unfinished background work, that wall-time/tool-call budgets reset for each user or notification turn, and that the core session turn cap remains cumulative.

## Why it is needed

At the current merge base, terminal provider errors already fail across output formats. The remaining problem is ownership: process-level handlers can terminate a reusable SDK host, and queued notification/result handling can lose terminal signals or emit duplicate results. After preserving the host, cumulative turn-limit events must also remain failures instead of becoming empty successful results.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- In a reusable stream-json session, trigger a tool/time budget or a cancelled turn and verify one terminal error result. Interrupt a turn through the SDK and verify a later normal message still receives a response.
- Exhaust the cumulative session turn cap. The host must remain alive; later messages must explicitly fail without another model request. Start a new session to continue.
- Verify one-shot turn-limit and cancellation exits remain 53 and 130. Supply a provider error containing terminal controls and verify stderr is neutralized while structured/raw error data remains intact.
- Close stdin while background agents are running. Each started task must receive its cancellation notification without starting a new model turn. Keep stdin open when waiting for a background agent’s output.

### Validation

Validation: 308 relevant unit tests passed (1 pre-existing skip); full build, typecheck, bundle, changed-file ESLint and Prettier passed. Independent verification passed 4 source probes and 7 CLI E2E scenarios on macOS with deterministic localhost providers, including cumulative-cap errors, interruption recovery, and one-shot exits 53/130.

Validation used macOS and deterministic localhost providers with dummy credentials. These results do not establish Windows/Linux runtime or real remote-provider behavior. The isolated bare-abort source probe supplements the CLI signal checks.

## Risk & Scope

- Reusable hosts receive per-turn error results and retain ownership of process shutdown. An exhausted cumulative session turn cap is not reset automatically.
- There is no shared wall-time/tool-call budget across user and notification turns, and no new typed budget discriminator in the public SDK envelope; the failure reason is in error.message.
- No configuration migration or public SDK schema change is introduced.

## Linked Issues

Related to #11217 and #8920. Rate-limit retry changes belong to #11216.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 改动与原因

让可复用 stream-json 会话中的失败回合输出一次错误结果，并由宿主保留进程退出和全局清理的控制权。覆盖时间和工具预算、单次调用及累计会话回合上限、普通取消；SDK 的可恢复中断继续支持后续回合。stderr 渲染会过滤服务商错误中的终端控制字符，同时保留原始错误值。

当前合并基已经让各输出格式正确处理模型终止错误。本 PR 处理剩余的宿主生命周期、重复结果和通知清理问题；进程不再被回合上限终止后，也确保核心层的累计上限事件不会变成空的成功结果。

后台任务回调由可复用会话持有，在取消和 EOF 清理时保持开始/结束通知成对。回合结果不无限等待后台任务；stdin EOF 会取消未完成任务，若需要其输出应保持 stdin 打开。时间与工具预算按用户/通知回合重置，核心会话回合上限仍然累计，耗尽后需新建会话继续。

## 验证与范围

独立复现并验证了宿主不退出、单一错误结果、累计上限后的明确失败、SDK 中断后继续应答、单次运行退出码 53/130，以及 stderr 控制字符过滤。相关单元测试、完整 build/typecheck/bundle 和改动文件检查已通过，英文验证段给出本轮具体结果。使用 macOS、localhost 确定性服务和假凭据，未据此宣称 Windows/Linux 或真实远端服务验证通过。

不新增跨回合共享的时间/工具预算，也不修改 SDK envelope schema；预算原因仍通过 error.message 表达。无需配置迁移。

</details>

issues.title: opencode-zen: free model rows are dead ends in Codewhale — the gateway checks an exact payload and TLS cipher list (429 FreeUsageLimitError)

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: os:linux
labels.description: Linux-specific behaviour

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
### Before you start
- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. Closest closed issue: #6705 (different problem — stale curated wire list).

### What happened?

`opencode-zen` lists Zen's free model ids in the model list — `codewhale model list --provider opencode-zen` returns 50 rows, 11 of them `*-free` (`hy4-flash-free`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `beam-free`, …) — and `docs/PROVIDERS.md:998` documents the free rows as supported `/chat/completions` models. Every request to one of them fails with the provider's client-scoped refusal:

```
Rate limit exceeded: Free usage limit reached. Free models work in OpenCode (https://opencode.ai);
subscribe to OpenCode Go to keep going: https://opencode.ai/go; … automatic retry stopped
```

The same key and the same model id work in the official OpenCode CLI at the same minute, so this is not a credential or account problem: the entitlement is scoped to the first-party client. Codewhale already recognises the message (`opencode_go_hint`, `crates/engine/src/llm_client/mod.rs:469`), but the catalog surface still offers the rows, so the user selects a model and hits a dead end after the turn has started.

Expected: the free rows work from Codewhale the way they work in the OpenCode CLI with the same key.

### Request

Please make the free OpenCode Zen models work from Codewhale on the `opencode-zen` route.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Zen route with a key via `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (documented fallback env var, `crates/config/assets/provider_descriptors.json` → `opencode-zen.env_vars`).
2. `codewhale exec --provider opencode-zen --model hy4-flash-free "hi"` (same in the TUI: `/provider` → OpenCode Zen, `/model` → a `*-free` row).
3. The turn ends with the quota-window error quoted above (classified `llm_quota_window`).

Plain curl, same key, outside Codewhale — the same refusal, so it is not a Codewhale request-shape bug:

```bash
curl -s https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"hy4-flash-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"max_tokens":8}'
# HTTP 429
# {"type":"error","error":{"type":"FreeUsageLimitError","message":"Free usage limit reached.
#  Free models work in OpenCode (https://opencode.ai); subscribe to OpenCode Go to keep going: https://opencode.ai/go"}}
```

Control — same key, same model id, same minute, official CLI:

```
opencode run -m opencode/hy4-flash-free "hi"    # normal answer; the session row records
                                               # {"id":"hy4-flash-free","providerID":"opencode"}
```

`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` with the same key returns 200 and lists the free ids, so the key is valid and the catalog is reachable.

### Verified 2026-11-18: what actually gates the free rows

#### How it was measured

The `opencode` provider's `baseURL` was pointed at a local HTTP capture server through `provider.opencode.options.baseURL`, and one `opencode run -m opencode/hy4-flash-free` was made through it. The captured request (all headers and the full body) was saved and then replayed byte-for-byte against the real endpoint with three clients, using the same key and no proxy:

| Client | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `bun` `fetch` | captured request, byte-for-byte | **HTTP 200**, streamed answer from `hy4-flash-free` |
| `curl` 8.23.0 with OpenSSL defaults | captured request, byte-for-byte | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |
| Node 26 `fetch` (OpenSSL) | captured request, byte-for-byte | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |
| `bun` `fetch` | same headers, simplified body (short system prompt) | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |

#### Correction to the first hypothesis

The first reading of that table was "a TLS fingerprint that only Bun can pass". That was wrong. A second round of measurements with a plain `curl` isolated three independent conditions, all reproducible with standard command-line flags:

1. **Payload.** The system prompt (61 901 characters) and the `tools` array (11 870 characters) must be the client's own, byte for byte. Only the user message (`messages[1].content`) and the model id may change. Truncating the system prompt, dropping `tools`, or keeping a single tool returns 429; changing only the user message returns 200.
2. **TLS cipher list.** The gateway checks both the order and the exact set of suites: TLS 1.3 in the order `AES128 → AES256 → CHACHA`, then this exact TLS 1.2 list:

   ```
   ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA:AES128-GCM-SHA256:AES256-GCM-SHA384:AES128-SHA:AES256-SHA
   ```

   With OpenSSL's default order the request returns 429 even with a valid payload; with the lists below it returns 200. The two curl flags are `--tls13-ciphers` and `--ciphers`. Set separately, either flag alone still returns 429 — both are required.
3. **Session id.** A real `x-opencode-session` id captured from the CLI (`ses_` + 24 characters) is required. A randomly generated id of the same shape returns 429.

Not required: the API key, an `Authorization` header, a proxy, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, `x-session-affinity`, `x-session-id`, or a particular header order. The free tier answers anonymous requests. `wget`, Python `ssl`, `openssl s_client` and 11 `curl-impersonate` profiles (Chrome 100-136, Safari, Firefox, Edge) all return 429 with an otherwise identical request, which is why the first hypothesis looked like a transport fingerprint; the cipher-list comparison shows the check is narrower than that.

#### Working example

The payload is captured once from a real CLI request via the `baseURL` override described above and saved as `free-payload.json` (about 104 KB on disk, about 32 KB gzipped). Replace the session id with a freshly captured one. Note that this route is `https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions`, different from the `/zen/v1` route used in the original reproduction above.

```bash
jq -c --arg q 'Say hi in one word' '.messages[1].content = $q' free-payload.json \
| curl -sN https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'User-Agent: opencode/latest/2.2.0/cli' \
    -H 'x-opencode-session: <real-session-id-from-cli>' \
    --tls13-ciphers 'TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256' \
    --ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA:AES128-GCM-SHA256:AES256-GCM-SHA384:AES128-SHA:AES256-SHA' \
    --data-binary @- \
| sed -n 's/^data: //p' | grep -v '^\[DONE\]$' \
| jq -r 'select(.choices[0].delta.content != null) | .choices[0].delta.content' | tr -d '\n'
```

Observed on 2026-11-18 with curl 8.23.0, no key and no proxy: `hy4-flash-free` answered with a single-word greeting, `glm-5.3-flash-free` answered `pong`. A control request with the same payload and the same session id, but with neither cipher flag, returned HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 78867` seconds. The 429 is the per-IP free-tier limit, so wait for that window instead of retrying in a loop; this is a rate limit, not a ban.

#### Caveats

The payload is tied to client version `2.2.0`: if the server-side prompt changes, a fresh capture is needed. The session id may expire and needs to be captured again. These measurements describe an intentional client gate; whether Codewhale should reproduce a first-party client is a maintainer decision.

#### Implication for the fix

Codewhale has to reproduce the exact payload, carry a valid session id, and present a matching cipher list. Changing the User-Agent or adding `x-opencode-*` headers alone is not enough.

### Codewhale version
`codewhale 0.10.3 (dev)` (built from a git checkout)

### Where did it happen?
TUI (terminal interface), CLI command (`codewhale exec`)

### Operating system
Linux

### How did you get Codewhale?
Built from a git checkout

### Provider and model
`opencode-zen` / `hy4-flash-free` (also `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `glm-5.3-flash-free`, `beam-free`, … — 11 free rows in total)

### Possible cause (not verified)
`client_user_agent()` (`crates/engine/src/client.rs:331`) sends `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; codewhale/<version>; +https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale)` on every route, so the provider can distinguish Codewhale from the OpenCode app. I did not test whether a different User-Agent changes the result: that would mean impersonating the first-party client, and whether this project should do that is the maintainers' decision, not mine.

Update 2026-11-18: verified above — sending the first-party User-Agent alone does not change the result. The exact request body, a real session id and the matching TLS cipher list are all required. Whether Codewhale should impersonate the first-party client remains the maintainers' decision.

issues.title: bug: the TUI freezes for the whole next turn when a save-snapshot is requested as a new turn starts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

When a turn ends and a new turn starts within milliseconds, the TUI freezes for the **entire duration of the new turn** — keystrokes are ignored, nothing renders, and the only way out is to close the terminal. In the session below the freeze lasted **209 seconds**, and the same session recorded it twice more at 541 s and 848 s.

The visible message afterwards is:

```
Session <id> could not be saved (resource busy). Recent work may not be saved.
```

That message is a symptom, not the cause: `resource busy` is the fallback error string the UI uses when its session snapshot does not arrive.

## Mechanism

1. A turn settles. The TUI's turn-complete handler requests a snapshot from the engine (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs`, `engine_handle.get_session_snapshot().await`). The await is **unbounded** — no `tokio::time::timeout`.
2. The engine serves `Op::GetSessionSnapshot` only from its run loop between turns. `handle_send_message` awaits the whole turn inline, and nothing inside the turn loop drains `rx_op`. So while a turn runs, the snapshot request sits in the 32-slot op channel.
3. If the next turn starts before the snapshot is served — which happens when the message is already queued — the UI blocks until that turn finishes.

The UI event loop is a single async loop: while it awaits the snapshot it does not poll the terminal, so input and rendering stop. That is the freeze.

The codebase already knows this hazard. `get_subagent_settlement` on the same handle carries the warning:

```rust
/// Query after the active turn settles, without competing with events.
/// The caller must keep draining events and bound this future: an active
/// turn can be awaiting provider/tool work or a full event channel.
```

`get_session_snapshot` has no such note, and the turn-complete call site does not bound it. The startup path uses the same method **with** a timeout (`LAUNCH_SESSION_SYNC_WAIT = 2s`, `await_engine_session_sync`), so the bound exists in the codebase — it is simply missing here.

## Natural control experiment

One session (`2a4365be`, workspace `~/`, 16 November) produced four identical `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` failures within 15 minutes. Only one froze:

| Failure | Next turn started | Warning | Freeze |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18:54:29 | **+0.02 s** | 18:57:59 | **209 s** |
| 18:57:59 | +375 s | same instant | 0 s |
| 19:06:33 | +8.3 s | none | 0 s |
| 19:09:12 | +31.9 s | none | 0 s |

The only difference is whether a new turn started before the snapshot could be served. Same error, same session, same binary — freeze only when the next turn starts immediately. The user reproduced this live: the third failure did not freeze.

## Timeline of the 209-second freeze

```
18:54:29.929  turn 4156686f  phase=idle
18:54:29.944  turn completion settled status=Failed   (stream closed before [DONE])
18:54:29.966  turn 6a12cd4b  started                  (+22 ms)
              … UI awaits get_session_snapshot(); engine is inside the new turn …
18:55:07.188  turn 6a12cd4b  phase=streaming the model response
              … nothing in the log for 172 s …
18:57:59.786  turn 6a12cd4b  settled status=Failed    (same stream error)
18:57:59.798  WARN terminal session source no longer matches; checkpoint retained
```

The warning fires the moment the snapshot is finally served — and it no longer matches, because the engine's source has moved on. The UI then reports `Session … could not be saved (resource busy)`.

So the sequence is: the stream error is what makes the new turn end; the snapshot request is what makes the UI wait; the mismatch is what produces the misleading "not saved" notice.

## Not caused by the old workspace-lock issue

The "resource busy" wording is the same string the workspace-lease refusal used, so it is worth ruling out: this session ran in `~/`, its log shows the delegated-store read-only warning at startup (the known legacy-store case), but the save failure here is not a flock — no `Resource temporarily unavailable`, no coordination-lock line at the time of the freeze. The text comes from `snapshot_error.unwrap_or_else(|| std::io::ErrorKind::ResourceBusy.to_string())` in the same turn-complete handler.

## Frequency in one month of logs

`terminal session source no longer matches` appears **15 times across 7 log files** (9–16 November). Four have a measurable freeze:

```
848 s   tui-2026-11-14-4002283.log   turn eebd894f
541 s   tui-2026-11-15-55504.log     turn 93494e2e
209 s   tui-2026-11-16-880180.log    turn 4156686f
 69 s   tui-2026-11-13-1149827.log   turn 1443f6d1
```

The 848 s case is confounded by the separate late-usage-ledger defect (#7356) in the same session; the other three are clean (zero ledger failures in their logs) and share the exact signature above.

Underlying stream errors: **9** `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` across 6 sessions since 10 October (10, 14, 18 ×2, 21 Oct; 16 Nov ×4). That error is separate — it is the trigger, not the freeze.

## Still present upstream

`upstream/main` at `b107c4996` (350 commits ahead of the reporting build) has the same unbounded call at `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:3906`; the turn loop still does not drain `rx_op`. No open issue covers this: #6184 is the engine going silent, #7328 is missing failure causes in the log, #7356 is the ledger blocking saves. This is the UI blocking itself on a busy engine.

## Suggested fix

Bound the await and keep the loop alive:

1. Wrap the turn-complete `get_session_snapshot()` in `tokio::time::timeout` — the same 2 s used by `await_engine_session_sync` is a reasonable start. On timeout, keep the checkpoint (already done today) and skip the completion commit instead of blocking.
2. Or serve `Op::GetSessionSnapshot` while a turn runs — it reads session state, but the engine is single-threaded, so this likely needs the snapshot to be published out-of-band rather than computed on demand.
3. While here, make the refusal say what it is: `resource busy` reads like a lock, and it sent at least one operator looking for a stale process. A sentence naming the pending Engine snapshot would have saved that search.

Option 1 is the smallest change and removes the freeze entirely; the snapshot will still mismatch sometimes, which is already handled.

## Reproduction

Not deterministic, but the conditions are simple: with a message already queued, let a turn fail with `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason` (or any fast failure), so that the failure's turn completion and the queued turn start land within the same few milliseconds. The UI then stops responding until the next turn ends.

## Related

- #7356 — late-usage ledger blocks session saves; the 848 s case overlaps with it.
- #7328 — provider failures leave no cause in the log.
- `CHANGELOG.md` 0.10.3 — "Turns no longer fail on a cost bookkeeping error"; the same principle applies to a UI that must not block on a busy engine.

prs.title: fix(tui): translate tool labels, /help, /diff, composer and /status catalog text
prs.body:
## What and why

The six remaining hard-coded English strings from #7304 now come from the locale packs. All 15 packs get the new keys, and English output is unchanged byte for byte. zh-Hans uses full-width punctuation as in #7299 / #7314. (The `/status` label column from the same issue already shipped in #7314.)

| # | Surface | zh-Hans before | zh-Hans after |
|---|---------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | Tool cell subtitle (`exploring_label`, `tool_routing.rs`) | `读取 完成 · Reading src/foo.rs` | `读取 完成 · 正在读取 src/foo.rs` |
| 2 | Collapsed activity row (`tool_run.rs`) | `浏览了2个文件, 1次搜索: read file, search` | `浏览了2个文件、1次搜索：read file、search` |
| 3 | `/help` count and aliases (`views/help.rs`) | `216 entries`, `  (aliases: /qingping)` | `216 个条目`, `  （别名：/qingping）` |
| 3 | Command palette (`command_palette.rs`, `traits.rs`) | `aliases: image, media, fujian`, `1 shown / 1 entries`, `3 / 9 matches` | `别名：image、media、fujian`, `显示 1 个 / 共 1 个条目`, `3 / 9 个匹配` |
| 4 | `/diff` pager and edit cards (`diff_render.rs`) | `summary: 2 files, +3 -1, 2 hunks`, per file `1 hunk` | `摘要：2个文件，+3 -1，2处改动`, per file `1处改动` |
| 5 | Composer context preview (`file_mention.rs`) | `[git] git status · resolved on send` | `[git] git status · 发送时解析` |
| 6 | `/status` window source row (`status.rs`) | `目录: models.dev live · 9070 offerings · fetched 2m ago · 云端事实: off` | `目录: models.dev 实时 · 9070 个可用模型 · 2 分钟前获取 · 云端事实: 关闭` |

Notes per item:

1. `exploring_label` takes the UI locale. The card picked the `find` verb by checking whether the label started with the English word `Searching`, which would break once the label is translated. `ExploringEntry` now carries a `search` flag set from the tool name (`grep_files`, the only tool that produced that label). I removed the comment sentence that this change made false.
2. List and clause separators and the `clause: families` join are pack strings (`ListSeparator`, `ActivityClauseSeparator`, `ActivityFamilies`). Tool family names stay as they are: they are tool identifiers, and the existing `a_collapsed_run_summary_names_what_actually_happened` test requires `read file` in every locale.
3. `/help` alias suffixes, the slash-menu alias hint (`widgets/mod.rs`, same string) and the palette count and alias text are pack strings. `shed_to_width` in `views/help.rs` also treats `（` / `）` as parentheses and ` （` as a field joint, so a narrow `/help` still drops the whole zh alias field and never cuts it in half.
4. `codewhale-tui-kit` does not depend on `codewhale-localization`, so `render_diff_bounded`, `render_diff_window`, `search_diff`, `search_diff_from_origin` and `diff_row_for_origin` take a `DiffSummaryLabels` (its `Default` is the current English text). The TUI builds it from the pack, and the diff pager rebuilds it in `set_locale`.
5. `pending_context_previews` takes the locale, and the git and file previews use one pack string.
6. The config group reads text through `StatusMessages`, so the new keys are added there and in `config_policy_messages.rs`. The age uses the existing `SessionsTime*` strings, whose English text matches `cloud_facts::age_label` (`just now`, `2m ago`, `3h ago`, `1d ago`). The group still builds as `codewhale-portable-config`.

Not changed: the row labels in `/status` still use an ASCII `: ` (`目录: `) like every other `/status` row. A cloud-facts state other than `off` still reads `cloud_facts::label()` in English. Other English nearby that the issue does not list is also unchanged: the git mention label `working-tree diff`, `use /attach for media bytes`, and the `1 file +3 -1` header from `diff_summary_label`.

## Where this came from

Closes #7304

## How I tested it

The machine locale is `zh_HK` (`LANG=zh_HK.UTF-8`), which makes the English-asserting `/status` tests run in zh-Hant. So I ran the TUI tests with `LANG=en_US.UTF-8 LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` through `scripts/with-hermetic-test-home.sh`.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo test -p codewhale-localization -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib --locked` (includes the pack completeness and placeholder tests):
  - `test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out` (localization)
  - `test result: ok. 216 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out` (tui-kit)
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked -- tui::history tui::command_palette tui::file_mention tui::active_cell tui::pager tui::views::help tui::widgets tui::ui::tests::exploring_label commands::groups::config commands::config_policy_status_tests commands::contract commands::traits commands::config_main_host commands::debug_diagnostics_baseline_tests`:
  - `test result: FAILED. 880 passed; 2 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 4962 filtered out`
  - The first failure was my new pager test, which expected two spaces in the per-file row where the rendered body has one. I fixed the assertion.
  - The second failure is `tui::widgets::tests::slash_completion_hints_model_deepseek_provider_uses_bare_ids`. It checks the `/model` model-candidate list from the provider inventory, which this change does not touch, so I think it depends on this machine's setup. CI will show whether it fails there too.
- After the fix, the new and changed regression tests:

  - `cargo test -p codewhale-portable-config --lib --all-features --locked` (with `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings`): `test result: ok. 38 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-localization -p codewhale-tui-kit -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-portable-config --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, with the three CI allowances: clean

I did not run the full `codewhale-tui` lib suite locally, because unrelated `commands::groups::plugins::tests` tests hang on this machine. CI covers it.

prs.body:
## What and why

Bound the terminal session snapshot requested at turn completion to the existing two-second Engine snapshot wait. If the Engine is busy with a newly started turn, the TUI returns to its event loop instead of freezing until that turn ends. A timeout skips the completed snapshot commit and retains the recovery checkpoint. Timeout and session-identity mismatch now show distinct reasons.

prs.title: fix(models): keep MCP tools with null-default optionals on the Moonshot route
prs.body:
## What and why

On a Moonshot (Kimi) model, an MCP tool from a Python server is dropped from the request whenever it has an optional parameter such as `limit: int | None = None` or `filters: Filters | None = None`, so the model never sees the tool.

FastMCP and Pydantic v2 write that parameter as `{"anyOf": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}`. The provider-neutral `sanitize` collapses it to `nullable: true`, and `normalize_kimi_compatibility` restores the `anyOf` but carries `default: null` into the integer branch, where `validate_mfjs_default` rejects it (`InvalidDefault`). For a `$ref | null` union the collapse is skipped and `default` stays beside `anyOf` (`InvalidKeywordValue`). Either way `project_tool_schema` returns `Omitted`.

This drops a `default: null` from a node that already admits null (`nullable: true`, or an `anyOf` with a `{"type": "null"}` branch) before the union is rebuilt. It removes the incompatible default annotation while preserving accepted values and optionality.

## Where this came from

Bug fix, no issue. Found while testing Pydantic-shaped MCP schemas against the Moonshot projection; the existing `kimi_parameters_restores_registry_collapsed_nullable_anyof` covers the same path with a hand-written `anyOf` that has no `default`.

## How I tested it

`kimi_parameters_accepts_pydantic_optional_with_null_default` runs the production two-stage path (`sanitize`, then `sanitize_for_kimi_parameters`) on both shapes and validates the result with `validate_mfjs_parameters`; it fails on `main` and passes with the change. `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/models/src/schema_sanitize.rs`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-models --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.title: fix(tui): recapture focus without erasing the viewport
prs.body:
## What and why

Ordinary window focus recovery currently erases the viewport before repainting it. On terminals that ignore DEC 2026, this exposes an intermediate blank screen. Separate focus recapture from explicit clear requests: restore terminal modes and margins/origin, then repaint the viewport, including blank cells, without `CSI 2J`.

Resize, suspend, theme changes and external terminal handoffs retain clear-and-redraw recovery. A queued clear takes precedence over focus recapture. The draw still runs once, preserving the per-frame hyperlink registry and cursor handling.

Full repaint recovery remains intentional. Ratatui's cell directives can cause one additional ordinary diff before settling; this change does not promise less repaint traffic.

## Where this came from

Refs #7343. Thanks to @scripting-drafts for the detailed report and control-stream diagnosis. This addresses the ordinary-focus erase path; it does not establish zero redraw or native GNOME Terminal visual behavior.

## How I tested it

Focused TUI tests, including the new recapture regression and existing focus, cursor, mode-recovery and resize coverage:

```sh
CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 bash scripts/dev-test.sh tui -- \
  focus_recapture_repaints_cells_without_erasing_the_viewport \
  focus_gained_forces_terminal_viewport_recapture \
  focus_loss_defers_frames_until_focus_or_input_returns \
  focus_loss_defers_frames_only_on_vte_terminals \
  focus_loss_keeps_painting_inside_tmux_even_under_a_vte_host \
  recover_terminal_modes_emits_expected_csi_sequences_with_gating \
  frame_cursor_is_hidden_during_diff_then_positioned_before_reveal \
  cjk_composer_cursor_and_mouse_geometry_agree_in_compact_and_wide_frames \
  g3_resize_clear_and_failure_are_inside_synchronized_output
```

`test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5830 filtered out`.

- `cargo fmt --all` and `bash scripts/preflight.sh --check`: passed.
- `bash scripts/dev-cargo.sh build -p codewhale-cli --locked`: succeeded for clean main and the fix.
- Real offline PTY comparison at 80×24 and 120×40, synchronized output off/on, three focus pairs per case: clean main emitted 12 whole-screen erases across 12 FocusIn events; the fix emitted 0. Mode recovery, synchronized-output gating and input liveness remained functional; all four fixed runs exited 0.

prs.title: fix(snapshot): roll back partial file-scoped restores
prs.body:
## What and why

When a file-scoped restore fails after earlier checkouts or removals, undo can report failure while leaving those changes in the workspace. This PR uses the existing safety snapshot to roll back attempted checkout batches and completed removals. Recovery stays within those paths and preserves newer contents it detects. The error identifies any incomplete recovery and includes the safety snapshot ID. Directory pruning, when requested, runs after a successful restore. A failed checkout can still leave empty parent directories it created.

## Where this came from

Refs #6559 (F02-10). Thanks to @7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for reporting partial restores, and to the maintainers for identifying the remaining file-scoped case.

## How I tested it

- `CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 bash scripts/dev-test.sh snapshot restore` — 20 passed, 0 failed, including a late removal failure and a Git checkout that failed after writing part of a batch.
- Ran the new regression on the unpatched base and confirmed it failed because a file remained overwritten after the restore returned an error.
- `bash scripts/preflight.sh --check` — passed.

prs.title: fix(engine): avoid rereading history for named-turn undo
prs.body:
## What and why

Named-turn undo loads every source turn and item to resolve a tail-relative depth, then delegates to depth-relative preparation, which loads the history again. Long sessions pay an extra whole-history read while undo preparation holds the admission guard.

Reuse the loaded records through the existing `prepare_fork_from_cutoff`. Resolve the anchor with the shared user-turn indexing rule and use the anchor itself as the cutoff and receipt, preserving removal of the selected turn and everything after it. Source capture, external-executor rejection, workspace/store ownership checks and the session lease remain in the existing preparation flow.

The shared fallback retains its existing retained-prefix item reads. This change removes the named path's redundant complete preparation pass; the evidence below measures turn-file reads rather than wall-clock speedup.

## Where this came from

Refs #7355. Thanks to @soarkit for tracing the duplicate reads and providing the file-open benchmark that made the extra pass visible.

## How I tested it

```sh
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CODEWHALE_DEV_NEXTEST=0 bash scripts/dev-test.sh engine -- \
  named_turn_undo_reads_turn_store_once_and_drops_anchor \
  fork_at_user_message_ fork_at_user_turn_ \
  saved_checkpoint_validation_and_forks_preserve_history \
  abandoned_backtrack_fork_leaves_no_session_document --test-threads=1
bash scripts/preflight.sh --check
git diff --check
```

- Negative control with original production code and the same regression: `test result: FAILED. 8 passed; 1 failed`. The regression failed exactly at turn-file reads: **10**, expected **5**.
- Fixed code: `test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed`. The fixture includes three user turns, an intervening compaction and an unrelated thread; it verifies one turn-store scan, the dropped range and receipt, the retained prefix, and source preservation.
- Final preflight: `preflight: OK`, including rustfmt. `git diff --check` passed.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] Formatting passes and tests cover the changed behavior
- [x] Existing undo behavior is preserved; no new user-facing feature requires a registry row

prs.title: fix(tui): bound completed-turn session snapshot waits
prs.body:
## Status

Closed as a duplicate of the earlier #7360, which already has maintainer review. Thank you @deosiree for carrying the fix and @7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the diagnosis; I missed the new PR while this branch was building. This branch and its test evidence remain available, including the full-mailbox and held-reply regression. This closure is about duplicate scope, not CI status.

## What and why

When a queued turn starts before the preceding completion handler receives its Engine snapshot, the TUI can wait for the entire new turn without polling terminal input or rendering.

Bound the completed-turn snapshot request, including mailbox capacity and reply waits, to the existing two-second session confirmation budget. A timeout reports a localized pending-snapshot reason and leaves the recovery checkpoint in place. The existing source, owner, session, workspace and message guards still gate the completed-session commit. Snapshot read failures no longer also log an unverified source mismatch.

This bounds the snapshot wait to two seconds; snapshots are still served between Engine turns. The provider stream failures described in the report remain separate.

## Where this came from

Refs #7357.

Thanks @7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the session timelines, control comparison and diagnosis of the unbounded snapshot wait.

## How I tested it

- Five focused TUI regressions passed on the final commit (**5 passed, 0 failed**): the new busy-Engine regression plus four existing startup and persistence regressions.
- The new test covers both a held snapshot reply and a full request mailbox, including rejection of a late reply. Existing tests cover Engine session installation, retaining the checkpoint after a failed save, clearing it only after a successful save, and a complete fresh-session persistence lifecycle.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `bash scripts/preflight.sh --check`, `python3 scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py` and `git diff --check`: passed. All 15 complete locale packs include the new reason.

The new regression uses the existing mock Engine handle to hold the reply or fill the mailbox. It exercises the completion snapshot helper rather than a live provider turn or a full PTY session.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior.
- [x] Bug fix; no new feature registry entry is needed.

prs.title: fix(subagent): inherit the session's reviewed memory in child prompts
prs.body:
## What and why

A sub-agent's system prompt now carries the session's reviewed native-memory packet and its `## Memory Hygiene` guidance, the same bytes the root session's prompt carries.

Today a child gets neither: `Engine::new_child_admitted` clears `memory_enabled`, and `host_owned_system_prompt()` returns the child's role prompt before the memory block is ever composed. So a rule the user pinned in Context Lens — "cloud deploys need your approval", "edit code in the dev directory, not the runtime directory" — binds the orchestrator and silently not the agent that actually edits files. The memory tools still work in a child, but `memory_search` is lexical and explicit pins only enter through the packet path, so pins never surface there either.

The fix is one seam: `build_subagent_system_prompt_with_skills` composes the packet from the inherited `ToolContext.memory_path` and appends it after the role contract, before the skill catalog. A shared helper `memory_prompt_section` (extracted from the root prompt's inline formatting, byte-identical output) guarantees parent and child never ship the packet without its guidance.

Design notes:
- The packet is re-composed, not copied out of the parent prompt: a memory edited mid-session reaches a later spawn, and an isolated worktree still resolves to the same workspace scope through its shared git remote.
- No `memory_enabled` flip: enabling it on the child would run session-start reconciliation under the root session id, duplicating a receipt and possibly reporting false interruptions.
- Memory keeps its existing standing — untrusted evidence, not an authority channel.
- Nothing is injected when memory is disabled, the store is empty, or every entry is reviewed off; a child records no context receipt of its own.

## Where this came from

Not tied to an issue. A behavior gap found while investigating why pinned rules did not reach sub-agents.

## How I tested it

- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine child_system_prompt` — 3 passed. Asserts one packet, pin ordering, guidance after the packet, role framing ahead of it, nested children inheriting through `runtime_for_nested_agent_tools`, and no envelope when memory is disabled / empty / reviewed off.
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine memory_guidance` — 5 passed (root prompt behavior unchanged).
- `scripts/dev-test.sh engine 'tools::subagent::tests::'` — 620 passed with one failure, `late_launch_permit_still_gets_the_full_work_budget`, a wall-clock/HTTP-fixture test whose context carries no `memory_path`; it passes 3/3 alone and the whole module passes 621/621 with `--test-threads=1`.
- `scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-engine --lib`, `clippy -p codewhale-engine --lib --tests -- -D warnings` (exit 0), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
- `scripts/preflight.sh --check` — OK.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] `docs/MEMORY.md` and `docs/SUBAGENTS.md` describe the inheritance; the `memory` row in `docs/features.toml` already points at `docs/MEMORY.md`
- [x] No `CHANGELOG.md` hunks (CONTRIBUTING.md asks for entries at merge time)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

Local setup keeps an existing `tools.profile` (or writes `full` when none is set) and never says which profile the agent ends up with or what it allows. A config that still has `tools.profile: "messaging"` finishes setup with chat working and no file, command or web tools, and nothing in the setup output points at the profile. Support reports traced exactly this: chat worked, tools did not, and changing the profile fixed it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start from a config with `{ "tools": { "profile": "messaging" } }` in an isolated state dir.
2. Run `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice skip --skip-health --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-search --workspace <dir>`.
3. Read the output, then the saved config.

### Expected behavior

Setup ends with one plain line that names the effective profile, where it is set, what it lets the agent do, and how to add a tool. For example: `Tool profile: messaging (tools.profile). The agent can chat, send messages and manage sessions; it cannot use files, commands or the web.` plus the `alsoAllow` path for one tool.

### Actual behavior

Real run on main `7ff0d902b94`, macOS arm64, Node 24, isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`:

```text
== seed config: { "tools": { "profile": "messaging" } }
== exit 0; full setup output (tmp path shortened):
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
Workspace OK: <tmp>/workspace
Sessions OK: <tmp>/state/agents/main/sessions
Updated config: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json
  Backup: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json.bak
Tip: run `openclaw configure --section web` to store your Brave API key for web_search. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web
== saved tools section: {"profile":"messaging"}
```

The profile is kept and not mentioned. A fresh install (no seed config) prints the same lines and saves `{"profile":"full"}`, also without mentioning it. An agent-level `agents.entries.<id>.tools.profile` outranks the `full` that setup writes, and is not mentioned either.

The guided setup summary (`applySystemAgentSetup` lines: `Workspace: ...`, `Gateway: ...`) and the interactive wizard finish have the same gap.

### OpenClaw version

main at 7ff0d902b94 (2026-11-18)

### Operating system

macOS

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

Not applicable (setup output, no model call)

### Impact and severity

Affected: users who rerun setup on a config with a restricted profile (`messaging`, `minimal`, `coding`), often left from older setup defaults. Severity: confusing; chat works, so the missing tools look like a bug elsewhere. Frequency: every setup run on such a config. Consequence: users widen unrelated permissions or ask for support before finding `tools.profile`.

### Additional information

Related: #200933 covers the other half (an agent that hits a missing tool cannot name the setting). #36868 proposed a profile picker in onboarding and was closed; this report does not ask for a picker or a default change, only for setup to say what it kept. Tool profile reference: docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md.

issues.body:
## Problem

`openclaw logs --limit` / `--max-bytes` produces **different results for the same input depending on which delivery path serves the request**, and the option help documents no cap at all:

- Gateway reachable → the `logs.tail` RPC rejects the request: `invalid logs.tail params: at /limit: must be <= 5000`
- Gateway unreachable → the journalctl/local-file fallback **silently clamps** the same values and succeeds

## User impact

An operator pulling a larger log window — a completely reasonable ask given the help text says only "Max lines to return" — gets a hard protocol error or a silent success depending on Gateway availability at that moment, with no way to learn the real cap from the CLI. The same command in a script behaves differently across environments.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1) With a local Gateway running:
$ openclaw logs --limit 6000 --max-bytes 2000000 --token x
invalid logs.tail params: at /limit: must be <= 5000          # exit non-zero

# 2) Same command, Gateway unreachable (fallback path):
$ openclaw logs --limit 6000 --max-bytes 2000000 --token x
Local Gateway RPC unavailable; reading configured file log instead.
Log file: …openclaw-2026-11-16.log                              # exit 0, silently clamped

# 3) Control (in-range value, either path):
$ openclaw logs --limit 200 --token x
…log lines…                                                     # works everywhere
```

The Gateway-side caps (5000 lines / 1,000,000 bytes) live in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/logs-chat.ts`; the CLI parses without an upper bound (`src/cli/logs-cli.ts`), while its own journalctl fallback already clamps to the same constants (`JOURNAL_MAX_LIMIT` / `JOURNAL_MAX_BYTES`) — so the inconsistency is purely at the CLI entry.

## Observed evidence (origin/main 940e76922e5)

Both transcripts above were captured against a real local Gateway and against a dead loopback port on the same build; outputs shown verbatim.

A closed PR (#199596) implemented the repair: clamp once at the CLI entry with the existing fallback constants and name the caps in the option help, so all three delivery paths agree for any input. Happy to rework/resubmit it against this issue if the approach is acceptable.
