### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.9 for macOS, local agent runs repeatedly fail with "Auth profile read owner was revoked" despite successful OAuth verification.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.10.9 on macOS with two configured agents: william and nails-customer.
2. Verify OpenAI OAuth using `openclaw models auth activate --agent nails-customer <saved-profile-id>`. The CLI reports that inference and sign-in were verified.
3. Run `openclaw agent --local --agent william --message 'Rispondi solo TEST OK'`.
4. Observe repeated `Auth profile read owner was revoked` errors instead of the expected reply.
5. Repeat with nails-customer and a new session ID. The same error occurs.
6. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` and retry the local agent. The error persists.
7. In a separate codex-test profile with the same Codex plugin version, a local agent successfully replies `Test riuscito.`

### Expected behavior

Previously, the configured OpenClaw agents could run successfully. On OpenClaw 2026.10.9 for macOS, local agent runs now fail repeatedly with "Auth profile read owner was revoked". OAuth sign-in and inference verification succeed, but local agent execution still fails.

### Actual behavior

Local agent runs for both william and nails-customer fail repeatedly with "Auth profile read owner was revoked". The agents do not return the expected test response. The main profile also reports "missing-openclaw-peer-link" for the Codex runtime. OAuth inference verification succeeds, and an isolated codex-test profile can respond successfully. Running doctor --fix did not resolve the local agent failure.

### OpenClaw version

macOS (MacBook Pro, Intel)

### Operating system

macOS (Intel MacBook Pro, exact version not yet confirmed)

### Install method

npm global + OpenClaw macOS app

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw local agent -> Codex plugin -> OpenAI OAuth -> OpenAI model

### Additional provider/model setup details

Default model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol. Authentication: OpenAI OAuth. The Codex plugin is installed and enabled. OAuth inference verification succeeds, but local agent runs fail with "Auth profile read owner was revoked". An isolated test profile can successfully run an agent. No proxy or external model router has been confirmed.

### Logs

```shell
OpenClaw 2026.10.9 on macOS.

Observed during local agent execution:
[agents/auth-profiles] auth usage committed but runtime snapshot publication failed: Auth profile read owner was revoked

Observed in model runtime status:
Agent harness "codex" owner plugin "codex" is unavailable (missing-openclaw-peer-link).

OAuth sign-in and inference verification succeeded.
The same local agent error persisted after `openclaw doctor --fix` and after selecting the valid OAuth profile explicitly.
An isolated `codex-test` profile successfully returned `Test riuscito.`
SQLite integrity and plugin compatibility checks reported no issues.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected systems: Two local OpenClaw agents, william (administration) and nails-customer (customer support).
Severity: Blocks normal local agent operation.
Frequency: Reproduced repeatedly during local testing.
Consequence: The agents cannot reliably return AI responses. The WhatsApp customer support workflow has not been re-enabled pending verification. No confirmed data loss.

### Additional information

The last known working OpenClaw version is not confirmed. The failure was observed on version 2026.10.9. The affected agents are william and nails-customer. A separate codex-test profile successfully completed a local inference test. The failure persisted after OAuth reauthentication, selecting the valid auth profile for william, and running doctor --fix. The root cause remains unknown.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.6** (fe06181), Node v26.12.1, Linux (Proxmox host, x64)
- Provider: `opencode-go` (OpenAI-compatible), primary model `glm-5.3-flash` with model fallbacks
- Prompt cache mode: `boundary-aware:openai-completions`
- Multi-agent setup: ~17 configured agents, cross-agent handoffs via `sessions_send` with inline wait; ordinary turns run 2-6 tool calls each
- Channels: Telegram forum topics + Home Assistant Assist through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.enabled: true`)

## Symptoms

Every model request logs `cache read dropped N -> 0`, so the full prompt (14k-27k tokens) is reprocessed from scratch on **every** call — including consecutive calls **within the same turn**. Each call costs 1-8 s of stream time (measured window: 41 calls, median 4.1 s, max 14 s), and a user message needing a 4-11 call chain takes 20-50+ s end-to-end. Synchronous clients (voice Assist) hit their timeout and disconnect mid-turn (`ClientDisconnectError`).

## Evidence (gateway journal, sanitized)

1. Within-turn drop with NO tracked change (request 3 of the same run, 5.5 s after request 2):

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] cache read dropped 14592 -> 0 runId=<redacted> request=3
for opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash via boundary-aware:openai-completions;
no tracked cache input change; requestGapMs=5544 promptTokens=18176 providerPrefix=prefix-match
```

2. historyRewrite because the user-message envelope is re-stamped on every request:

```
[agent/embedded] [prompt-cache] message 0 (user) differs from the previous request;
history must be append-only; changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw
```

```
cache read dropped 15104 -> 10240 ... historyRewrite(message 27 (user) differs ...;
changed fields: envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw, envelope.idempotencyKey);
requestGapMs=31690 promptTokens=17043 providerPrefix=message:2
```

3. Runtime-context carrier invalidating the provider history mid-turn (request 8 of the same run):

```
cache read dropped 13056 -> 0 ... request=8 ...
runtimeContextCarrier(runtimeContextCarrier changed provider history);
requestGapMs=2317 promptTokens=14866 providerPrefix=message:14
```

4. System-prompt digest change (expected after workspace file edits; listed for completeness):

```
cache read dropped 12160 -> 0 ... systemPrompt(system prompt digest changed (sections: Project Context)),
historyRewrite(message 27 ... envelope.timestamp, envelope.__openclaw, envelope.idempotencyKey);
requestGapMs=538656 promptTokens=17220 providerPrefix=message:0
```


### Steps to reproduce

Multi-agent gateway + any OpenAI-compatible provider with prompt caching. Send a message that makes an agent perform 2+ tool calls (or a `sessions_send` handoff with inline wait) and watch `[prompt-cache]` lines in the gateway journal. Drops appear on every request, including back-to-back requests in the same run.


### Expected behavior

Per `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`, consecutive request histories in the same session extend the previous request, and transient runtime-context carriers "remain outside the cached prefix" — a tool loop inside one turn should pay prefill once and reuse the cached prefix on follow-up calls.


### Actual behavior

The cache drops to zero on effectively every request, including same-turn follow-ups where the log reports `no tracked cache input change`.

2026.10.6

Proxmox

_No response_

Opencodego glm5.3 and all models wotch cache

-


_No response_

- Every multi-tool agent turn re-processes 14k-27k token prefixes: 20-50+ s per user message.

issues.body:
## Problem

When the Gateway is unreachable in a way that keeps TCP open but never completes its side of the exchange (a wedged process, a restart window behind a proxy, a half-open connection), `openclaw mcp serve` completes `initialize` and then leaves **every `tools/call` hanging forever with no error, no log line, and no deadline**. The MCP client's own timeout is the only thing that eventually surfaces anything.

## User impact

MCP clients (Claude Code and anything speaking MCP stdio through `openclaw mcp serve`) silently hang on all tool calls during exactly the moments an operator is most likely to be looking — a Gateway restart or a network hiccup. There is no actionable failure to react to; it looks like OpenClaw is frozen rather than waiting on a dead connection.

`ECONNREFUSED` already fails fast (`MCP server failed to start: connect ECONNREFUSED …`), so only the wedged-endpoint class regresses to silence.

## Reproduction

1. Start a blackhole endpoint that accepts TCP but never speaks (this reproduces the "Gateway up but wedged" class):

```bash
node -e 'require("net").createServer(s=>s.on("data",()=>{})).listen(18997,"127.0.0.1")'
```

2. Attach an MCP stdio client and call any tool:

```bash
openclaw mcp serve --url ws://127.0.0.1:18997 --token x
# client: initialize → responds
# client: tools/call messages_read → no response, no stderr error (observed 110s+, still nothing)
```

3. Control: point at a port with nothing listening — the server fails immediately with `MCP server failed to start: connect ECONNREFUSED`, proving the silent hang is specific to reachable-but-unresponsive endpoints.

## Observed evidence (origin/main 940e76922e5)

```
[base] initialize responded: true (16774ms)
[base] tools/call responded: false (after 110014ms)     ← no response, no error
[base] server: still-running (elapsed 141792ms)          ← hangs indefinitely; stderr only carries the token warning
```

Cause: the bridge absorbs retryable Gateway connect errors for reconnect resilience (`shouldRetryInitialMcpGatewayConnect` → `onConnectError` swallows them) and `start()` awaits the readiness promise with **no deadline** (`src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts`); every tool handler first awaits `waitUntilReady()`, so all calls inherit the unbounded wait. The stdio MCP client already models the fix (`mcp-stdio-client.ts` uses an explicit `startupDeadline`).

A closed PR (#199598) implemented the repair: readiness deadline derived from the configured handshake/challenge budgets (`resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` / `resolveConnectChallengeTimeoutMs`) plus a retry grace, with the same live capture now failing cleanly at 60s: `MCP server failed to start: gateway did not become ready within 60000ms`. Happy to rework/resubmit it against this issue if the approach is acceptable.

issues.body:
## Summary
When `channels.feishu.accounts.<id>.streaming.mode` is `partial`, the rendered streaming card repeats earlier assistant messages of the same turn. The number of repetitions grows with the number of assistant messages produced in the turn, so a turn that emits N assistant messages shows the earlier ones N times.

## Root cause (verified in source)
The Feishu channel plugin re-prepends text that Core already includes in the partial payload.

Core (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.reply-delivery.ts`, `advanceStream()`) accumulates partial text **across assistant messages within one turn**:

```ts
if (stream.blockIndex !== state.assistantMessageIndex) {
    stream.prefix = stream.text;          // previous message text becomes prefix
    stream.blockIndex = state.assistantMessageIndex;
}
const text = finalMessage
    ? data.text
    : stream.prefix && data.text ? `${stream.prefix}\n${data.text}` : stream.prefix || data.text;
```

So the partial payload delivered to `onPartialReply` already contains **all previous assistant messages of the turn**.

The Feishu plugin then prepends the same content a second time:

- `onAssistantMessageStart`: `snapshotBaseText = streamText ? `${streamText}\n\n` : ""`
- `queueStreamingUpdate()` (snapshot mode): `streamText = `${snapshotBaseText}${nextText}``
- final delivery: `mergeStreamingFinalText(streamText, `${snapshotBaseText}${reply.text}`, ...)`

`streamText` already holds the cumulative text, so `snapshotBaseText + nextText` duplicates the prefix on every message boundary.

The previous official plugin (`@larksuite/openclaw-lark`, `src/card/streaming-card-controller.js`) does **not** prepend any prefix to partial text — it only tracks `streamingPrefix`/`lastPartialText` to detect reply boundaries — and does not exhibit this duplication.

## Reproduction
1. Configure a Feishu account with `streaming.mode: "partial"`.
2. Send a prompt that makes the agent emit more than one assistant message in a single turn (e.g. a message followed by several tool calls, then a final answer).
3. Observe the streaming card: the earlier assistant messages appear more than once, and the repetition count increases with each additional assistant message.

## Suggested fix
Do not re-prepend accumulated text to a partial payload. Treat the partial payload as authoritative when it already contains the previously accumulated text, and only fall back to prepending when it does not. Something like:

```ts
const isCumulative = (candidate: string, previous: string) => {
    const prev = normalize(candidate, previous);
    if (!prev) return true;
    return normalize(candidate).startsWith(prev) || normalize(candidate).includes(prev.slice(0, 120));
};

streamText = isCumulative(nextText, streamText) ? nextText : `${snapshotBaseText}${nextText}`;
```

The same check should be applied on the final delivery path, where `${snapshotBaseText}${reply.text}` is used.

## Impact
Affected: Feishu channel with `streaming.mode: "partial"`. Users see visibly broken, repeated output. Reported on OpenClaw `2026.11.3 (847611d)` with `@openclaw/feishu@2026.11.3`.

## Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.11.3 (847611d)
- Plugin: @openclaw/feishu 2026.11.3
- Node: v26.13.1
- Channel: Feishu (open.feishu.cn)

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.11.5, Slack Socket Mode input processing became stuck with `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`; retry counters reached 59 and 60, a Gateway restart did not restore processing, and operator intervention using `operator-skipped` restored service.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

This is a production incident report, not a deterministic reproduction. The observed incident and recovery sequence was:

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.11.5 with Slack Socket Mode on macOS 27.2.1, with a local Strata model backend.
2. During the incident, Compaction timeouts and repeated pending-input idempotency conflicts were observed.
3. Slack ingress retry counters reached 59 and 60.
4. Restart the Gateway: the stuck input processing did not recover.
5. Apply operator intervention using `operator-skipped`: service recovered.

The precise initial trigger, ordering of the first timeout versus first input conflict, elapsed outage duration, and exact recovery command are not established in this report. The counters are reported values, not a claim that there is a configured 60-attempt limit.

### Expected behavior

PR #193602 documents recovery of the same channel message after a failed, unconsumed attempt. A recoverable first-attempt failure should allow subsequent redelivery to run rather than repeatedly reject the same input. This is a reference to the intended behavior in that PR, not a claim that its fix was shipped in our installed build.

### Actual behavior

- Repeated `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`.
- Slack input processing remained stuck through retry counts of 59 and 60.
- Compaction timeouts were also observed during the incident.
- Gateway restart did not restore service.
- Service resumed only after operator intervention using `operator-skipped`.

The relationship between the Compaction timeouts and the input conflict is unknown. We have not established a transcript sequence collision, an external CLI transcript writer, changed request hashes, or the pending-input row state for this incident.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (reported installed version; exact installed commit and local modifications not verified)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1; Apple M1 Max, 64 GB unified memory

### Install method

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Model

`strata/qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs` (configured primary model in the environment record; effective model for each failing attempt not independently verified)

### Provider / routing chain

Slack Socket Mode -> OpenClaw Gateway -> local Strata OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### Logs

Exact reported error text:

```text
Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input
```

Reported observations, not verbatim log lines: retry counters 59 and 60; Compaction timeout; recovery using `operator-skipped`.

Raw logs, database dumps, message contents, and configuration files are not attached. This report is based on operator observations and the environment record; no new live reproduction was performed for filing.

### Impact and severity

The affected Slack workflow stopped processing normally and required manual recovery. Gateway restart alone was insufficient. One incident is reported here; recurrence rate and the number of affected messages are not established. Recovery by skipping an input restores service but does not demonstrate that the skipped message was processed successfully.

### Additional information

Related upstream work, checked on November 18, 2026:

- #193602 is **closed/merged** (November 5, merge commit `cb719feef55c307d473129525a41ec3ebdf1d0d6`). It addresses cancelled, unconsumed channel inputs being rejected on redelivery with a new run ID. Its documented scope excludes interrupted rows and changed request bytes; it does not fix the underlying transcript sequence collision.
- #199155 remains **open**. It documents a separate established trigger involving an external CLI transcript write and a resident Gateway actor. We link it because the downstream error and restart-resistant retry behavior overlap; we do not claim the same initial cause here.
- #199155 also has a stable-2026.11.5 Slack Socket Mode report: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/199155#issuecomment-6962955004. That contributor reports the #193602 logic is absent from the published stable bundle. This is external evidence, not an inspection of our installed bundle.
- Comparing the #193602 merge commit with `v2026.11.5` returns diverged ancestry, so that merge commit is not an ancestor of the release tag. This alone does not rule out an equivalent backport.
- #199365, the candidate fix for #199155, remains **open/unmerged**. No confirmed release date for resolution of this incident was found in the reviewed threads.

This is a new follow-up to the merged #193602, recording this operator's Slack/local-model incident and recovery. Please link or consolidate it with #199155 if maintainers establish the same root cause. Please clarify which published version contains the channel-redelivery fix and whether the Compaction/restart recovery path needs separate handling.

Privacy: credentials, tokens, workspace/channel/user IDs, event/run/session IDs, message contents, private URLs, machine names, and user-specific filesystem paths are omitted.

issues.body:
## Problem
The team-mode Control UI sidebar has no manual agent section order. Operators cannot keep their frequently used agents near the top without changing unrelated agent configuration.

## Proposed behavior
Add drag-and-drop and keyboard-accessible Move up / Move down controls to team-sidebar agent headers, moving the entire agent section with its children. Reuse the existing sidebar header grip, interactive-control guards, header-midpoint before/after insertion feedback and array-move helper. Provide Reset agent order.

Persist ordered agent IDs in the existing Gateway-scoped, synced operator display preferences (`ui.prefs.sidebarAgentOrder`), including existing local cache and pending-intent behavior. Empty/unset order preserves current ordering; explicit order may put another agent before the default. Unlisted/new agents retain their existing relative order after listed agents. Normalize invalid/duplicate IDs but retain temporarily missing saved IDs. Activity updates and rendering must never write preferences.

## Boundaries
Sidebar only. Agents home activity ordering, identity/routing, membership, session categories/ownership and session-group configuration remain unchanged. Agent drag payloads must not trigger session reassignment/group persistence and other drag kinds must not reorder agents. No new preference or drag framework. Existing offline/read-only preference semantics apply; do not imply that a local-only edit is synced.

## Acceptance / verification
- Default ordering unchanged; explicit order overrides default-agent promotion.
- Drag and keyboard moves use the same operation, preserve focus, announce position, and reset restores default order.
- Reload and Gateway preference synchronization preserve order, with Gateway isolation and stale-intent safeguards.
- Duplicate/invalid/new/deleted/missing agent IDs handled deterministically without dropping temporarily absent saved IDs.
- Expanded sections use header geometry; collapse, navigation and menus remain functional.
- All drag-type crossings leave session groups/routing unchanged.
- Preference, interaction and regression tests; real before/after browser screenshots.

Related: #146383 (broader per-agent rank/sidebar + Agents home proposal). This is a narrower display-preference/sidebar-only alternative and does not close or fully implement that issue. #153686 concerns named groups in team mode, not agent order. Live issue/PR searches found no focused duplicate at intake.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let Discord `autoThread` open the thread with the bot's first message (progress row or reply), instead of before the run starts.

### Problem to solve

With `autoThread: true`, the thread appears under the person's message the moment it's admitted, and it sits empty until the agent's first progress row or reply. In a small founders' channel that reads as a dead thread for a few seconds every time, and quick answers that use no tools show nothing but a typing indicator in it.

The thread is created up front in `resolveDiscordAutoThreadReplyPlan` ([threading.auto-thread.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d13d1f09392def8826f5e6c6d807b7fb6012953/extensions/discord/src/monitor/threading.auto-thread.ts#L134)), I think because the thread id decides the session key.

### Proposed solution

An option such as `autoThread: "on-first-message"` that keeps the session keyed as it is today, but creates the Discord thread only when the first outbound message (the progress draft or the final reply) is about to be sent.

Discord's start-thread-from-message endpoint works at any time after the parent message exists, so the thread would open with content already in it.

### Alternatives considered

- Replying in the channel instead of threads avoids the empty card, but loses the fresh session per question that makes threads nice.
- The ack reaction helps people see the message was received, but the empty thread still shows.

### Impact

Affected: Discord channels using `autoThread`.
Severity: cosmetic, but it's the first thing people see on every question.
Frequency: every message.

### Evidence/examples

Slack's thread replies don't show an empty thread before the first reply, since a Slack thread only exists once something is posted in it.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

issues.body:
> Form note: this is a feature request (`feature_request.yml` fields). Summary: expose the auth profile that served a turn to the `/usage full` footer template, as `/status` already does.

## Problem

The `/usage full` footer template (`messages.usageTemplate`, schema `openclaw.usageBar.v1`) exposes `model.auth_mode` (`token`, `oauth`, `api-key`...) but not which auth profile served the turn. With two profiles of the same mode for one provider (for example `anthropic:personal` and `anthropic:work`, both `token`), the footer cannot tell them apart.

`/status` already shows it: `🔑 Auth: token (anthropic:personal)`, built by `resolveModelAuthLabel` from the session's `authProfileOverride` and the provider's auth order.

## Proposal

Add `model.auth_label` (and ideally a bare `model.auth_profile` id) to the usage-line context, resolved the same way `/status` does, so a template can render `{model.auth_label}`.

## Where

`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner*`: the state handed to the usage-line builder carries `authMode: runResult.meta?.requestShaping?.authMode` and the builder maps it to `model.auth_mode`. Nothing carries the profile.

## Local workaround (2026.9.8)

We patched the bundled dist: import `resolveModelAuthLabel`, set `authLabel` on the footer state from `{ provider: providerUsed, cfg, sessionEntry: activeSessionEntry, agentDir, workspaceDir }`, and emit `model.auth_label`. It resolves the same label `/status` prints. A cleaner fix would carry the profile actually selected for the run (`selectedAuthProfile.authProfileId`) through `runResult.meta`, so a mid-run profile rotation is reflected.

Docs to touch: `docs/concepts/usage-tracking.md` field table.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Status quo: run `/status` when it matters.** It works, but it shows the selection at the time of the command, never per turn in the footer.
2. **Our local dist patch (above): resolve the label with `resolveModelAuthLabel` at footer build time.** It prints the same label `/status` prints, but it reflects the session's current selection; after a mid-run profile rotation it can name a profile that did not serve the turn (the gap ClawSweeper also points out).
3. **Carry the profile actually selected for the run (`selectedAuthProfile.authProfileId`) through `runResult.meta` into the usage snapshot.** The shape we prefer: the field stays unavailable where a runtime cannot attribute the profile exactly, and the existing `/status` masking of personal-account identifiers is preserved.

## Impact

- Affected: operators with two or more auth profiles of the same mode for one provider who use `messages.usageTemplate`.
- Severity: annoying; the footer cannot say which profile served the turn, so profile-level usage needs a separate `/status`.
- Frequency: every turn on such an agent.
- Measured cost (time lost, wrong-profile incidents): **unknown**, not recorded.

## Implementation intent

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. We will not open a PR until a maintainer answers the open question (sanitized label vs profile id, supported runtimes, rotation semantics). Our dist patch stays local meanwhile.

### Summary

Expose the provider's plan usage windows (used percent and reset time for the 5-hour and weekly windows) as paths in the usage footer template.

### Problem to solve

We run an agent on a ChatGPT Pro plan through the Codex harness, in a Discord channel shared by two people. What we actually want under each reply is how much of the weekly allowance is used against how much of the week has passed, so we can see at a glance whether we're spending too fast.

The template can't show that today. The docs say so directly ([usage-tracking.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d13d1f09392def8826f5e6c6d807b7fb6012953/docs/concepts/usage-tracking.md?plain=1#L374)): "Provider rate-limit windows are **not** in this contract".

The figures already exist in OpenClaw, since `/status` and `openclaw status --usage` print them.

### Proposed solution

Add scalar paths for each window, something like `quota.weekly.used_pct`, `quota.weekly.elapsed_pct`, `quota.weekly.resets_at`, and the same under `quota.five_hour`. Elapsed percent is the useful one next to used percent, and it's easy to derive from the reset time and the window length.

An array path for an `each` piece would work too, but fixed names are simpler to write a template against.

### Alternatives considered

- A `reply_payload_sending` plugin can append the line, but any such hook turns off the Discord progress preview ([message-handler.draft-preview.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9d13d1f09392def8826f5e6c6d807b7fb6012953/extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.ts#L61-L67)), so we'd lose the live tool rows.
- Editing the reply after `message_sent` keeps the preview, but it means calling Discord directly from a plugin with the bot token, which felt too fragile to ship.

### Impact

Affected: anyone on a subscription plan (Codex, Claude) who shows the usage footer.
Severity: annoying, since the alternative is typing `/status`.
Frequency: every reply.

### Evidence/examples

Claude Code's status line shows the same pair as `7d: 12%/30%`, and it's the number we look at most.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

issues.body:
### Summary

Three Codex documentation pages name older bundled versions, while main pins `@openai/codex` to `0.169.0`. They also need clearer guidance for newer OpenAI models that require a newer Codex than an OpenClaw release bundles.

### Affected docs

- `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference/model-discovery.md`
- `docs/plugins/codex-harness-reference/app-server-transport.md`
- `docs/plugins/codex-native-plugins.md`

### Steps to verify

1. Check the Codex dependency in `extensions/codex/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` on main.
2. Compare it with the bundled-version statements in the three pages.
3. Compare model availability before and after installing a newer Codex and restarting the Gateway, with the Codex runtime explicitly selected.

### Actual content

The model-discovery and app-server-transport pages name `0.162.1`. The native-plugins page names `0.160.1`.

The transport page already describes installed-Codex selection, but does not clearly present the between-release upgrade workflow or the GPT-6.2 minimum. The guidance also needs to distinguish upgrading Codex from selecting the runtime that uses the ChatGPT/Codex login.

### Expected content

- Identify `0.169.0` as the current bundled version.
- Keep the October 18 model-list snapshot explicitly historical, rather than relabeling it as a test of `0.169.0`.
- Explain that newer OpenAI models can require a newer Codex. GPT-6.2 requires `0.166.0` or newer, so the current bundle already meets that minimum.
- Explain the supported between-release path: run `npm i -g @openai/codex` on the Gateway host, ensure the installed `codex` is on the Gateway's `PATH`, then restart the Gateway.
- For the ChatGPT/Codex login path, tell users to select the **Codex runtime**. Do not claim that installing Codex alone fixes automatic routing or authentication.
- Preserve the existing binary-selection checks and account-access caveats.

### Impact

Readers can mistake stale version numbers for a model-support limit or miss the supported upgrade path while waiting for an OpenClaw release. They can also install a suitable Codex version but still encounter an authentication error if automatic routing does not select the Codex runtime.

### Evidence

Reporter-supplied live check on **OpenClaw 2026.11.5**, using a **ChatGPT/Codex login in a disposable profile**, with model **`openai/gpt-6.2-sol`**:

1. **Bundled Codex `0.164.0`, with no `codex` on `PATH`:**  
   The turn failed with:
   > Unknown model: openai/gpt-6.2-sol

   `/codex models` listed no GPT-6.2.

2. **After `npm i -g @openai/codex` installed `0.169.1` and the Gateway restarted:**  
   The log reported:
   > using installed ... codex 0.169.1 (newer than bundled 0.164.0)

   A session with the **Codex runtime explicitly selected** completed the turn. `/status` showed `Runtime: OpenAI Codex`. `/codex models` listed `gpt-6.2-sol` as the default and also listed `gpt-6.2-astra`.

3. **After removing the installed Codex:**  
   The refusal returned:
   > Runtime "codex" is not available for openai/gpt-6.2-sol.

4. **Automatic-routing caveat:**  
   With no runtime explicitly selected, the same turn failed with:
   > No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai.

   The docs should therefore instruct users on this login path to select the Codex runtime, rather than claim that the npm installation alone fixes the problem.

### Scope

Documentation only. No runtime, dependency, or compatibility-policy changes.

### Summary

Extend the existing llama.cpp managed `local-media` setup to Apple Silicon Macs (macOS arm64), using Metal and the existing verified installation and activation flow.

### Problem to solve

`openclaw models auth login --provider llama-cpp --method local-media` explicitly rejects macOS arm64, although the managed llama.cpp installer already supplies a pinned macOS arm64 Metal runtime. Mac users must manually download matching OCR/vision models and projectors and configure image routes.

This extends @duyufansh2008's work in #148193 (original issue #148056), merged as `0ff0202128f1289fcdbcc466f3d1c0dc120911fc`. The feature shipped in stable **v2026.10.10** and remains Linux x64 CPU only in v2026.11.1. This request is a platform extension of that released feature.

### Proposed solution

- Keep implementation and hardware policy in the llama-cpp plugin.
- Detect the Apple chip, unified and available memory, model/runtime disk capacity, and actual Metal capability. Select compatible pinned OCR and vision recipes within the measured resource budget, loading one model at a time.
- Reuse consent, verified downloads, runtime installation, isolated native presets, model registration, and image routing.
- Require separate real OCR and spatial-vision image inference before returning an activation patch. Decline, cancellation, or failed verification must preserve prior configuration.
- Retain Linux x64 CPU behavior and clearly explain unsupported hosts or insufficient resources.

### Alternatives considered

Manual configuration remains possible but requires users to choose compatible model/projector pairs and manage runtime flags. Removing the platform guard alone would incorrectly retain CPU placement and would not establish Metal capability or resource fitness.

### Impact

Affected: Apple Silicon Mac users of the llama-cpp plugin. The current guard always blocks managed local OCR/vision setup. This would remove manual provisioning work while retaining explicit consent and inference-based activation.

### Evidence/examples

- Original implementation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148193
- First stable release: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.10
- Released platform guard: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/extensions/llama-cpp/src/media-setup.ts#L101
- Planned physical test host: Mac mini, Apple M4, 16 GiB unified memory, macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Metal 4. Real inference and rollback evidence will accompany the implementation PR; it has not yet been completed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

No new core manager, public configuration schema, or dependency is intended. Tests will cover Apple capability/resource selection, setup activation/rollback, and Linux compatibility. Evidence will distinguish automated tests from physical-device inference.

issues.body:
## Summary

When an `approvals.plugin.slack` reviewer list applies to a plugin approval, Slack delivers it to those reviewers whatever session raised it: the agent and session filters are read only when no list is set. Add optional `agentFilter` and `sessionFilter` to `approvals.plugin.slack`, with the same matching as everywhere else, applied to reviewer delivery and to reviewer decisions. They only narrow; a request they exclude is not sent to Slack at all, never through generic forwarding.

## Problem to solve

A gateway serving several people: A and B each talk to the same agent from their own Slack DM, so both are on `channels.slack.allowFrom` (the DM allowlist). A's plugin approvals should reach a reviewer's Slack DM (A, or someone who reviews for A). B's should not reach that reviewer; B decides hers in her own Gateway client.

No config gives this today:

- **No reviewer list:** plugin approvers are the account's `allowFrom` plus `defaultTo` (`extensions/slack/src/approval-auth.ts`, `resolveSlackApprovalInputs` and `getSlackApprovalApproversForTeam`). Under `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` that is everyone who may chat, so B receives A's cards as DMs and may decide them. `channels.slack.execApprovals.sessionFilter` can keep B's sessions off Slack, but not B off A's cards.
- **A reviewer list:** in `isSlackNativeApprovalAccountEligible` (`extensions/slack/src/approval-native-gates.ts`) a selected list makes eligibility `approverCount > 0`; `execApprovals.agentFilter` / `sessionFilter` are read only in the other branch. Generic forwarding is blocked once a list applies (`shouldBlockForwardingFallback` in `approval-native.ts`), so `approvals.plugin.sessionFilter` does not narrow it either. The list is keyed by plugin and tool, and A and B call the same tools, so the reviewer receives B's cards too.

So a list picks *who* reviews and the filters pick *which sessions*, but the two cannot be combined. The docs read both ways: `plugins/plugin-permission-requests.md` says a selected list delivers "independently of native exec approvals and plugin forwarding", while `channels/slack/rich-messages.md` says the native-client path handles plugin approvals "when Slack plugin approvers resolve and the request matches its filters".

## Proposed solution

Two optional keys on `approvals.plugin.slack`, beside `approvers` and `plugins`:

```json5
{
  approvals: {
    plugin: {
      slack: {
        approvers: ["team:T12345678:user:U12345678"],
        agentFilter: ["main"],                 // optional, agent ids
        sessionFilter: ["slack:direct:<A's user id>"], // optional, substring or regex, as elsewhere
      },
    },
  },
}
```

In `isSlackNativeApprovalAccountEligible`, the selected-list branch becomes:

```ts
(selectedPolicy !== undefined
  ? approverCount > 0 &&
    matchesApprovalRequestFilters({
      request: params.request.request,
      agentFilter: params.cfg.approvals?.plugin?.slack?.agentFilter,
      sessionFilter: params.cfg.approvals?.plugin?.slack?.sessionFilter,
    })
  : /* unchanged */)
```

What follows from that one condition, with no further change:

1. **Delivery:** `shouldHandleSlackNativeApprovalRequest` and `resolveSlackApproverDmTargets` go through it, so an excluded request gets no reviewer DM, on any account (`listSlackNativeApprovalEligibleAccountIds` uses it too).
2. **Decisions:** custody (`isPluginAuthorizedSender` in `approval-native.ts`) re-runs `shouldHandleSlackNativeApprovalRequest` for a selected list, so a button or `/approve` from a reviewer on an excluded request is refused, as a reviewer removed from the list is today.
3. **No leak through forwarding:** `shouldBlockForwardingFallback` still keys on the list being selected, so an excluded request is not handed to generic `approvals.plugin.targets` Slack forwarding. It goes to whatever other approval surfaces exist (Gateway clients, other channels), or takes "No approval route" if none.
4. **Existing configs unchanged:** both keys are absent unless set, and an absent filter matches everything, so every current reviewer list behaves as now.

Docs: a sentence each in `plugins/plugin-permission-requests.md` (reviewer lists) and `channels/slack/rich-messages.md` saying the two keys narrow reviewer delivery and decisions, and that excluded requests are not sent to Slack.

## How it fails closed

- **Request without the field the filter needs:** `matchesApprovalRequestFilters` already returns false for a set `sessionFilter` with no `sessionKey`, or a set `agentFilter` with no agent id, so such a request is excluded, not delivered.
- **Excluded request:** never falls back to the account's `allowFrom` approvers or to generic Slack forwarding; it leaves Slack entirely.
- **Older gateway:** `PluginSlackApproversSchema` is a closed object, so a gateway without this change refuses the config instead of ignoring the filter and sending every card to the reviewers.
- **Unsafe or invalid regex:** handled as today's filters do (literal substring first, then a bounded safe regex; a pattern that is neither matches nothing, so it excludes).

## Alternatives considered

- **Apply `channels.slack.execApprovals.agentFilter` / `sessionFilter` to selected lists.** One line and no schema change, and it matches the rich-messages sentence, but it changes what existing configs do (an operator who scoped exec cards would silently scope plugin reviewers too), against the reviewer-list design in #159525. Fine by us if maintainers prefer it.
- **Reuse `approvals.plugin.agentFilter` / `sessionFilter`.** Same objection: those are forwarding filters, and the docs say reviewer lists are independent of forwarding.
- **Per-level or per-reviewer scope** (filters inside `plugins.<id>` and `tools.<key>` beside `approvers`, inheriting like `approvers`; or reviewer entries as `{ id, sessionFilter }`). More precise (reviewer X only for A's sessions, reviewer Y only for C's), but a larger schema and a second inheritance rule. The top-level keys cover one reviewer group per gateway; per-level keys could follow the same matching later.
- **A per-request audience set by the plugin** that raises the approval: needed when two people share one session, which no session filter can split. This issue does not depend on it.

## Additional information

Read in `extensions/slack/src` at `v2026.10.10`, `v2026.11.1`, `v2026.11.5-beta.1` and main at `87c57b41c590`; the cited code is identical in all four. Related: #159525 (reviewer lists), #166160 (reviewer lists beyond Slack), #159516 (requester context in reviewer DMs). I can open a PR (the condition, the two schema keys, docs and tests for delivery, custody and the no-forwarding fallback) if the shape is acceptable.

issues.body:
**Summary.** On Anthropic models with extended thinking, the API binds each replayed thinking block to the exact request prefix it was generated under. OpenClaw builds a different prefix depending on how a run starts. When the prefix differs, the API drops every earlier thinking block (`thinking_dropped`, reason `prefix_binding_mismatch`). The blocks written in the odd run are then dropped again when the session returns to its normal prefix. #155868 reports the prompt-cache cost of the roster difference. This issue is about the correctness cost: the model loses its earlier reasoning exactly on the runs that resume work.

**Environment.** OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Node 26.12.1, Linux; `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, thinking high; Slack channel sessions; `contextPruning` cache-ttl 5m.

**Observed** (gateway log, `anthropic` subsystem: "replayed thinking dropped: N block(s) (prefix_binding_mismatch at messages.X.content.0, ...)"). The cause in each case comes from OpenClaw's own `[prompt-cache]` attribution for the same request:

| Run | Attribution | Thinking blocks dropped |
|---|---|---|
| Run started by a `sessions_send` message into a long channel session | `tools(7 -> 5 tools; removed: "computer", "openclaw"; description: "message"; schema: "message")` | 366 (all) |
| Second `sessions_send`-started run | same | 367 |
| `settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer — running isolated finalization` | `systemPrompt(digest changed: Project Context, Runtime Context, Other), systemPromptSuffix(digest changed: Skills, Tooling, Memory Recall, Runtime, Conversation Context, Other), tools(7 -> 0 tools)` | 218 (all) |
| Every later normal (human-message) run in that session | none | 1: the block generated by the finalization request, dropped on every run since |

A second session shows the same pattern. A run started by an inter-session reply dropped all 24 earlier blocks. Each later human-message run then drops the 2 blocks that run generated.

**Source.** `resolveGatewayOwnerOnlyToolDenylist(senderIsOwner)` (dist `dangerous-tools-*.mjs`) removes `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS` (control-plane tools, `sessions`, `screen`, `terminal`, `portal`, `conversations_*`, `nodes`, `computer`, `mobile_ui`, `openclaw`, `intent`) from the request when `senderIsOwner === false`. Inter-session deliveries are non-owner. The `message` tool description and schema also depend on the run source. The isolated finalization request uses its own system prompt and no tools.

**No workaround for automation.** An agent-initiated `openclaw agent --session-key <key> -m ...` is refused with "Gateway agent from agent exec would lose inter-session attribution". That is intended, but it means a watchdog or pacemaker can resume a stalled session only through `sessions_send`, which is exactly what drops the reasoning.

**Expected.** Within one session, the tool definitions and system prompt sent to the provider stay byte-stable across run types, so replayed thinking (and the prompt cache) survive. Possible approaches:
- Keep owner-only tool definitions in the request and refuse them at execution time for non-owner turns, or state the per-turn restriction in the turn's context, instead of removing the definitions.
- Make the `message` tool definition independent of the run source; put source-specific defaults in per-turn context.
- Run isolated finalization with the session's normal prefix, or do not persist its thinking into the transcript.

**Repro.**
1. Use a long-lived channel session on an Anthropic thinking model, built from human-message runs.
2. Deliver a `sessions_send` message into it.
3. Observe on the first request: the `[prompt-cache]` attribution `tools(7 -> 5 ...)` and "replayed thinking dropped: N" with N equal to the number of earlier blocks.
4. Send a normal human message. The blocks generated in step 2's run are now dropped.

Related: #155868 (roster difference and cache cost), #166271 (history rewrite also dropping thinking).

issues.body:
### Summary

On macOS (Intel x64), `openclaw gateway stop` and `openclaw gateway stop --force` both fail with:

```
Gateway stop failed: ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected.
Use the Gateway update action for a managed handoff, or retry from an independent terminal
without inherited service markers.
```

The command is run from a **standalone Terminal.app login shell** (not spawned by the Gateway, no inherited service markers), so the suggested remedy cannot be followed. `--force` — documented as "Allow stop from a non-interactive shell" — does not bypass the check either.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.10.10 (7dc3350) |
| Install | npm global, launchd LaunchAgent (macOS) |
| OS | macOS 15.8.1, x86_64 (Intel) |
| Node | v26.12.1 |
| Shell | zsh login shell in Terminal.app (ttys000) |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch the macOS Terminal app from Spotlight (independent shell, no gateway ancestry).
2. Run `openclaw gateway stop` → fails with `ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected`.
3. Run `openclaw gateway stop --force` → fails with the identical error.

### Expected

`gateway stop` either succeeds, or at minimum `--force` overrides the ancestry heuristic as documented.

### Actual

Both variants refuse to act. The only working path is bypassing the CLI and driving launchd directly:

```
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<gateway-label>
# run offline maintenance (e.g. openclaw doctor --fix)
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<gateway-label>.plist
```

### Related symptom (possibly same root cause)

`openclaw doctor --fix` also reports process-inspection failures and therefore retains temporary updater runtimes:

```
[infra:temp-artifacts] Runtime retained at <path>: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes:
ProcSafeError: layout-mismatch: invalid Darwin argument alignment
```

Three retained runtime directories (~1.8 GiB total) had to be cleaned manually.

### Analysis

Both failures point at the native process inspection layer (`proc-safe`) rather than the service itself: the ancestry check cannot complete, and the same layer reports a sysctl/kernel-struct layout mismatch on Darwin x86_64. This suggests the process inspection helper mis-parses Darwin process arguments on this platform/build.

### Impact

- Cannot stop the Gateway through the documented CLI path.
- Cannot reach an offline state to run `mcp probe`, `memory status`, or DB path repairs (they require exclusive offline state ownership).
- Workaround requires knowing the launchd label and plist path.

### Environment notes

- No inherited `OPENCLAW_*` service markers in the shell environment.
- `openclaw gateway status --deep` itself works and reports the service correctly.

issues.body:
With legacy Codex login, OpenClaw’s own harness gets a model list filtered by the Codex binary version. In the live probe, GPT-6.2 Sol completed with OpenClaw’s `version: 2026.11.5`. Changing only that header to `0.164.0` returned `400 model_not_found`. The same legacy token got `403` from `/v1/models` because it lacked `api.model.read`.

**Proposal.** When users opt in through **Sign in with ChatGPT**, use the documented `https://api.openai.com/v1/models` endpoint from OpenCode’s implementation and send turns to `/v1/responses` with the same token. OpenClaw already has this path. Existing users keep their current login and routing. [OpenCode request](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/54b4698a72b73b200501ebcb5eae8e2be3800f2a/packages/core/src/plugin/provider/chatgpt.ts#L419-L431) · [OpenAI docs](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference)

**Josh’s concerns**

1. **A version override can break deployments.** The opt-in route sends no Codex version override. The `99.0.0` change was [reverted at 00:10 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200870).
2. **A harness can’t run unsupported models.** A listing alone proves neither account access nor harness compatibility. Verify a completed OpenClaw turn.
3. **A fallback isn’t enough.** It can recover a failed fetch, but it can miss an incomplete successful response. [OpenCode paused live refresh for that reason](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/53466).
4. **Ship a hotfix and tell users.** Do that when the executing harness needs an update. Installing Codex helps only when Codex runs the turn.
5. **We still bundle Codex.** Its version still governs Codex-run sessions. The [merged `0.169.0` pin](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200784) addresses the GPT-6.2 catalog gap there.
6. **OpenClaw may become the default.** That makes its picker more important. Changing the default harness should not automatically switch anyone’s login.

**Verified.** With a Sign in with ChatGPT token-sharing grant on a test account, `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` returned 200 and listed `gpt-6.2-sol` and `gpt-6.2-astra`. One `/v1/responses` turn on each completed with `response.completed`.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug. A follow-up message in the same Telegram topic, sent about a minute after the previous turn finished, reuses a `claude-cli` session whose runtime has not finished closing. The first tool call is then refused as if the user declined it, and model fallbacks in that same turn die because the plugin invocation scope is already closed. The user sees the generic "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request."

## Version

OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (`d843d6a`), Linux arm64, channel `telegram`, agent `main`, model `claude-cli` / `claude-opus-5-5`.

## What happened

Two occurrences, same chat (a Telegram forum topic), same shape:

1. **2026-11-16 20:40 and 20:43 Europe/Vilnius.** A turn completed and delivered. The next user message arrived about three minutes later. The reused Claude Code session refused the first `exec` with: `The user doesn't want to take this action right now. STOP what you are doing and wait for the user to tell you how to proceed.` The user had not declined anything. The turn then failed with `source execution authority is no longer active | Plugin invocation scope is closed`. Telegram delivered the generic failure notice.
2. **2026-11-17 07:24 and 07:25 Europe/Vilnius.** Same topic, follow-up about one minute after the previous reply. Same refusal text on the first tool call, then the same closed-scope failure. Gateway log at 07:25: `CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended.`

A later message in a different chat, on a fresh model turn, ran the same command successfully. So this is not a standing exec denial and not the user's config.

## Expected

A follow-up should wait until the previous `claude-cli` runtime has actually closed, or start a clean session. A cut tool connection must not be reported as a user refusal, and fallback models in that turn should not inherit a scope that is already closed.

## Actual log sequence (2026-11-17 ~07:25)

- inbound Telegram message queued
- `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown` (also seen on the healthy turns; may be unrelated)
- `cli exec: provider=claude-cli ... useResume=true session=present`
- lane error: `CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended`
- `model-fallback/decision`
- lane error: `source execution authority is no longer active | Plugin invocation scope is closed`
- dispatch outcome `error`; the generic failure text is sent to the user

The assistant transcript for the failed turn shows the tool result text above, then a `run-failed-before-reply` record with the closed-scope summary.

## Notes

- Related but not the same: #170868 (false user refusal when claude-cli children outlive a killed Gateway) is closed and was about a Gateway restart. This happens with the Gateway staying up.
- #198423 is the closed plugin scope on `subagent_ended`, not on an ordinary user follow-up.
- Repro hint: two user messages in the same Telegram topic, roughly 60–180 seconds apart, while the first turn's Claude Code process is still shutting down. The second message's first tool call is the one that comes back as a decline.

Bug type: Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)
Beta release blocker: No

## Summary

When the gateway's own model provider fails, the reply in a group or channel tells every sender to fix provider setup, including senders who do not own the gateway.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Drive a reply turn (`executeAgentTurn`) for a Discord channel message from a sender with `senderIsOwner: false`, on a config with `commands.ownerAllowFrom` set.
2. Have the model run fail with a missing OpenAI key (`ProviderAuthError` `missing-provider-auth`).
3. Read the reply payload.

This was observed through the turn error path in a test, not in a live Discord run.

## Expected behavior

On a gateway with an owner list (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`), a sender who is not on it, in a group or channel, gets a reply saying the assistant is temporarily unavailable, with no provider name, command or sign-in prompt. The owner and direct chats keep the current setup guidance.

## Actual behavior

The reply is:

> ⚠️ Couldn't connect to OpenAI. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then try again. If it still fails, open Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`.

Billing, expired login and outage failures get the same treatment ("Check your account's credit balance", "Send `/login openai`", provider and model names). The only audience check today hides saved login labels in groups.

## OpenClaw version

main at c05f52233d2 (2026-11-17)

## Operating system

macOS 27.2

## Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout)

## Model

openai/gpt-5.5

## Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai

## Logs

```shell
Reply for a non-owner in a Discord channel, missing OpenAI key, from the turn error path test:
"⚠️ Couldn't connect to OpenAI. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then try again. If it still fails, open Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`."
```

## Impact and severity

Affected: anyone in a shared Discord, Slack, Telegram or WhatsApp chat with a gateway whose provider is failing, most visibly public support bots.
Severity: annoying to misleading. Readers take the text as a problem with their own install.
Frequency: every message while the provider is failing.
Consequence: people try to fix their own setup, or ask whether they need their own API key to get help.

## Additional information

`followupRun.run.senderIsOwner` is already available where the failure reply is built (`handleAgentExecutionError` and `buildKnownAgentRunFailureReplyPayload`). Related: #167341 asks for operator-configurable failure copy for the same kind of deployment.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a `heygen` speech provider so OpenClaw can speak through HeyGen Voice.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw users with a HeyGen account cannot use HeyGen voices for TTS. This includes the public voice library and the instant and professional voice clones in their own workspace. They must use another voice, so agent replies and calls cannot use a voice they cloned in HeyGen.

### Proposed solution

Add an external plugin, `@openclaw/heygen-speech`, in `extensions/heygen-speech`. It registers the speech provider `heygen`, and it follows the same shape as the other hosted speech providers.

- Models: `heygen-voice-1`, `heygen-voice-1-turbo` (default), and `heygen-voice-1-turbo-free`.
- Transport: HTTP streaming to `POST /v3/models/audio/tts/stream`, for buffered and streamed audio.
- Output: MP3 for audio files and streamed playback, Opus voice notes through `ffmpeg`, and 24 kHz PCM for telephony.
- Voices: `tts voices` lists workspace voices, then a page of public voices.
- Config: `HEYGEN_API_KEY` or `tts.providers.heygen.apiKey`, plus `baseUrl`, `model`, `speakerVoiceId`, and `language`.
- Overrides: voice and model directives, personas, Talk mode, and `infer tts convert --voice --model`.

The plugin does not create voices. Its README shows how to create an instant clone with the HeyGen API and use the returned `voice_id`.

### Alternatives considered

- Call the HeyGen API from a custom skill or script. This does not reach `tts.provider`, auto-TTS, voice notes, Talk mode, or telephony.
- Publish a third-party plugin outside this repository. This works, but users do not get the provider docs or the plugin inventory entry, and the provider does not run in this repository's plugin contract checks.

### Impact

Affected: OpenClaw users with a HeyGen account who want HeyGen or cloned voices in replies, voice channels, or calls.
Severity: Medium. It blocks HeyGen voices. Other TTS providers continue to work.
Frequency: Always, for these users.
Consequence: These users cannot use their HeyGen voices in OpenClaw.

### Evidence/examples

- API docs: https://developers.heygen.com/docs/voices/heygen-voice-speech
- Fork branch with tests and live results: https://github.com/spro-heygen/openclaw/pull/1

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

The change adds no core code. It adds one extension, its docs, and the generated inventory and config baseline entries that repo checks require. The `@openclaw/heygen-speech` package needs a maintainer to publish it, because the `@openclaw` scope and ClawHub release belong to the project. No OpenClaw maintainer has reviewed or agreed to this proposal yet.

issues.body:
**Ask.** Re-export `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` (and its `SessionKeyChatType` type) from a plugin-sdk subpath, e.g. `openclaw/plugin-sdk/routing`. That subpath already exports `parseAgentSessionKey` (`src/plugin-sdk/routing.ts:27`). The change is additive, one export line.

**Why.** A plugin tool factory gets `ctx.sessionKey` but no chat type. A tool that should only be offered in a direct chat (for example, one that shows the owner something a group or channel shouldn't see, since a group or channel reply is read by everyone in it) has to classify the key itself.

**What a plugin has to do today.** It re-implements the session-key rule by hand: drop an `agent:<id>:` prefix, split on `:`, and look for `direct`/`dm` versus `group`/`channel` tokens. That copy drifts from the host's canonical parsing (`src/sessions/session-chat-type-shared.ts:41`, `:92-117`), which uses peer-shape parsing with legacy and plugin-supplied fallbacks. With the export, a plugin calls the host's function and drops its copy.

issues.body:
## Summary

On the same host, two maintenance commands (`doctor --fix` on **2026.10.6**, `update repair` on **2026.11.3**) entered an unbounded loop in the **update-run admission** machinery. Both times the Gateway service was **stopped** at entry (the doctor flow stops it itself; `update repair` was run manually with the service down).

Signature (Incident A): the admission reader (`createUpdateRunAdmissionReader`) re-evaluates admission on every call — "no grant is cached" — and each evaluation spawns `sqlite-source-revision.worker.js --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child content-version <state/openclaw.sqlite>` workers that re-hash the **same, unchanged** state database. Observed rate: ~33 workers/min, ~310 MB/s sustained reads, **~1.26 TB cumulative reads**, ~2 % CPU spread over workers, **zero writes** for ~52 minutes. The process never reaches a terminal state; SIGTERM exits cleanly.

Incident B shows the same storm via a second entry point (`update repair` → `update finalize:doctor`), plus a second hang mode: after the per-agent database pass the process idles in `ep_poll` (0 % CPU, flat I/O) for minutes before the storm starts.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: **2026.10.6 (fe06181)** (Incident A) / **2026.11.3** (Incident B)
- Node.js v24.22.1 (patched line), npm global install at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.1/lib/node_modules/openclaw`
- Ubuntu 22.04, ZFS root, systemd user service `openclaw-gateway.service` (port 28789)
- State DB `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` ≈ 166 MB; agent DBs up to ≈ 888 MB (large-state checks are in scope per the 11.1 notes)

## Reproduction

### Incident A — `openclaw doctor --fix`, 2026.10.6 (2026-11-13)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:59 | `openclaw doctor --fix` started (interactive) |
| 14:02:45 | doctor stops the managed Gateway (expected) |
| 14:10:43 | pre-repair recovery capture completes (2.2 GB, SHA-256) — `~/.openclaw.update-captures/doctor-d21f43d4-8219-40a1-8b3c-929a1ae53879/manifest.json` |
| 14:15:44 | **last doctor output** |
| 14:16:44 | **last DB write**; afterwards: update-activation recovery loop |
| 14:16→15:09 | livelock: `sqlite-source-revision.worker.js` respawned ~33×/min, re-hashing `content-version` of the unchanged state DB; ~1.26 TB reads at ~310 MB/s; no writes, no further output |
| 15:09 | SIGTERM (clean exit) |
| 15:10:02 | Gateway restarted manually → symptoms stop |

### Incident B — `openclaw update repair --yes`, 2026.11.3 (2026-11-13)

Context: fresh `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.3` completed; Gateway intentionally stopped; `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive < /dev/null` had **also** hung minutes earlier (see "Hang modes" below) and was killed.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 18:04:55 | `openclaw update repair --yes` reaches `[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"in_progress"}`; log shows `operation=update.run elapsedMs=1337` on the state DB |
| 18:06:13–18:06:18 | per-agent DB inspection completes (`mr-review elapsedMs=14494`, then `mr-summary`, `tutor-package`) |
| 18:06:18→18:09 | idle: process in `ep_poll`, 0 % CPU, zero I/O growth (no workers) |
| 18:09:48 | log: `core/doctor/native-status - fs-safe: loaded`, `proc-safe: loaded` |
| 18:09:48→ | storm: child worker 100.7 % CPU (one core, 17 threads), **5.95 GB read per 10 s (~595 MB/s)**, cumulative `rchar` **226 GB**, no progress logs. Killed. |

## Observed hang modes

1. **Re-hash storm** (both incidents): unbounded `sqlite-source-revision` work over the same unchanged state DB, driven by repeated admission evaluation. IO-bound, sustained hundreds of MB/s.
2. **Idle deadlock** (Incident B, also `doctor --fix` on 2026.11.3 at `state.admission.fast-path`): event loop parked in `ep_poll`, 0 % CPU, flat I/O, no output — appears to wait on something that never resolves (both times while the Gateway service was stopped).

## Evidence

- Log excerpts (host log `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-11-13.log`): timestamps above; `operation=update.run`, `state.admission.fast-path`, `core/doctor/native-status` lines quoted verbatim in the timeline.
- `/proc/<storm-pid>/io` samples: rchar 220,519,096,461 → 226,467,236,978 in 10 s (Incident B); cumulative ~1.26 TB (Incident A).
- Worker cmdline: `sqlite-source-revision.worker.js --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child content-version <state/openclaw.sqlite>` (Incident A, ~33/min).
- Module pointers from dist inspection: `createUpdateRunAdmissionReader` (`update-run-reader-26jSfn0A.mjs`), `package-update-activation-recovery.mjs`, `doctor-maintenance-admission-D7tIXhlB.mjs`, `sqlite-snapshot-source-Dd_uWirj.mjs`.

## Relation to previous fixes

Several changelog entries look like they target this family — but the loop still reproduces in 2026.11.3 through `update repair`:

- 2026.10.7: "post-activation Doctor waits are bounded", "stale receipts cannot veto a valid repair" (#181166, #181307, #173862, #167459, #172768, #172769, #181389)
- 2026.10.8: "an orphaned maintenance worker no longer blocks every CLI command and Gateway start" (#180668, #181695)
- 2026.10.10: "bound Doctor inspection"
- 2026.11.1: "resolve pending package steps **without repair loops**", "avoids repeated full-database copying during large-state checks" (#177932, #186787, #189647, #182632, #187921)
- 2026.11.2: "avoid update self-fencing", "Keep unavailable environments out of admission budgets" (#189321, #174735)

Hypothesis: the bounded paths cover `doctor --fix`'s update-activation loop, but the same admission reader is reachable from `update repair`'s `finalize:doctor` step and is still unbounded there (or the bounding only applies when the Gateway is up).

## Related issues

- #176112 — same command (`doctor --fix`) livelock on Windows, different mechanism (state-owner lock renewal); ours is the admission / `sqlite-source-revision` re-hash storm and reproduces cross-version and via `update repair`.
- #184516 — `update repair` misbehaving under maintenance contention (2026.10.7); may share the `finalize:doctor` path described here.

## Impact

- Gateway (and thus bots/cron integrations) down for ~1 h in Incident A; maintenance commands unusable in Incident B.
- ~1.4 TB of aggregate useless reads in two days (I/O wear, ARC/page-cache pressure) plus burned CPU.
- Operator risk: these are the *repair* commands users run when something is already wrong.

## Workarounds

- SIGTERM exits cleanly; restart the Gateway to clear symptoms.
- Avoid `doctor --fix` / `update repair` **while the Gateway service is stopped**; on this host, plain `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` (no `--fix`) completed fine (exit 0, ~13 min) with the Gateway running.
- Targeted `openclaw plugins install <name>` replaced `update repair` for provider restoration without side effects.

## Suggested fix direction

- Cache the admission grant for the lifetime of a maintenance run instead of re-evaluating per call (the reader comment admits "no grant is cached").
- Put an overall bound/wall-clock budget on `finalize:doctor` database work, and make it fail loudly instead of spinning.
- In both hang modes, emit periodic progress with the current admission decision and DB revision so a stalled loop is diagnosable from logs.

## Additional context

- Reproduced twice in one day on one host after a storage cleanup that shrank DBs (state DB 166 MB, largest agent DB 888 MB); DB sizes don't appear to be the trigger.
- Host logs and the update capture manifest are retained and can be attached on request.

issues.body:
## Summary

Memory indexing/persistence appears to key off **normal turn completion**. When a session run ends abnormally (crash, model/backend failure, timeout) — but assistant content was already **emitted and delivered** during that run — that content is never written to the agent's memory index. The agent permanently loses the ability to recall its own delivered output. Nothing errors; the loss is silent.

## Incident (2026-11-17, OpenClaw 2026.11.3 / 847611d)

Agent-to-agent flow: Agent A `sessions_send`s a consult request to Agent B's main session. B's model lane is degraded; the run crashes once, is retried, and B answers via a `sessions_yield` acknowledgment (a documented inter-session reply path for subagent-style runs).

Observed state afterward:

- The acknowledgment text **was delivered** to Agent A (A relayed it onward, so delivery is certain).
- The event **exists in B's `transcript_events`** and is even matched by the session transcript FTS index.
- B's memory index (`memory_index_chunks`) has **zero hits** for any distinctive term of the reply — no memory write ever happened.
- B's own workspace memory files likewise have no record.

Hours later the owner asked B about the consult. B searched its available recall surfaces (memory files, notes), found nothing, and honestly reported it could not recall giving feedback. Recovery required another agent to do direct sqlite forensics on the transcript store — a layer the agent itself has no tool-level access to (`sqlite3` refuses databases under the live state dir, by design).

So the data was recoverable but **not recallable**: transcript ≠ memory, and agents only get recall.

## Root cause

Memory indexing is coupled to the happy path of run completion. Any abnormal end skips it, even for content that already crossed a delivery boundary.

## Proposal

Make persistence of assistant content **at-least-once on delivery**, independent of run outcome. Two candidate mechanisms (not mutually exclusive):

1. **On-delivery write**: when assistant final text or an inter-session delivery (e.g. `sessions_yield` acknowledgment, `sessions_send` reply) is actually emitted/delivered, enqueue the memory-index write at that moment rather than at turn end.
2. **Crash-recovery backfill**: on next session start (or Gateway boot), scan the transcript for assistant content that completed delivery but was never memory-indexed, and backfill the index.

For long-lived agents whose continuity *is* the memory layer, this is the worst failure class available: no error, no log, just a self that no longer remembers what it said.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)
- Linux x64, agent-to-agent `sessions_send` / `sessions_yield` flow
- Local llama.cpp model lane behind an LB with failover (degraded lane is what triggered the abnormal run ends)

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw gateway restart` reports a hard failure on restarts that actually succeed, and **exits 0 while doing so**. The readiness budget it enforces is hardcoded to 60 s, which is shorter than a real cold start of this gateway, so the CLI times out on a service that comes up healthy a minute later.

There is no flag to raise the budget: `--wait` controls the delay *before* restarting, not the post-restart readiness timeout.

## Version / platform

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac, npm latest)
- macOS 26 / arm64, Node 26.8.1
- LaunchAgent-managed gateway (`gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`), `--max-old-space-size=6144`
- Config `/Users/jiang/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, bind loopback, port 18789

## The budget

`gateway-shutdown-budget.mjs`:

```js
// Shared stop policy; v2026.9.5 restart-health.constants.ts fixes the replacement window.
export const GATEWAY_RESTART_REPLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;
export const GATEWAY_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 315_000;
```

and `dist/restart-health.constants-*.mjs` derives the probe budget directly from it:

```js
const DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS = GATEWAY_RESTART_REPLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS;   // 60_000
const DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_ATTEMPTS = Math.ceil(DEFAULT_RESTART_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS / 500);
```

So the health budget is the shutdown budget constant, reused verbatim. 60 s is not configurable from the CLI — `gateway restart --help` exposes only `--force`, `--json`, `--preserve-definition`, `--safe`, `--skip-deferral`, `--wait`, and none of them adjust the readiness timeout.

## Reproduction

Observed cold starts of this gateway (measured by polling `/healthz` + `/readyz` every 5 s from a separate shell):

| Run | Elapsed to `healthz=200` **and** `readyz=200` |
|---|---|
| 1 | 70 s |
| 2 | 75 s |
| 3 | 75 s |
| 4 | 200 s |

Every one of these is a successful start. The 200 s run is presumably a slow catalog/plugin warm-up, but the point is that the spread is wide and unbounded from below the user's perspective — a fixed 60 s budget will miss part of the distribution.

Actual `openclaw gateway restart` output from the run above:

```
Restarted LaunchAgent: gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway
Timed out after 98s waiting for gateway port 18789 to become healthy.
Readiness budget exhausted after 98s. Last observed startup phase: waiting for Gateway health and identity.
Service runtime: status=running, state=active, pid=65913
Port 18789 is already in use.
- pid 65913 jiang: /opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node --max-old-space-size=6144 ... (127.0.0.1:18789)
Gateway probe failed: gateway timeout after 3000ms
Gateway target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
Gateway restart timed out after 98s waiting for health checks.
Tip: openclaw gateway status --deep
Tip: openclaw doctor
```

Total wall time: 121 s. The service came up and served requests normally immediately afterwards (`healthz=200`, `readyz=200`, and the log shows successful `ws` traffic on the same pid 65913).

Two separate problems are visible in that output:

**1. The false failure.** The service was `status=running, state=active, pid=65913` and the port was bound by *the new process*, yet the CLI still concluded "timed out". The health probe that failed was a 3 s `ws` connect attempt, which is a much stricter criterion than the service being up.

**2. `exit 0` on failure.** The command printed a timeout error and a stack of "Tip:" lines, then **exited 0**. Any wrapper script or automation that checks the exit status will treat a failed restart as a success. This is the more dangerous half of the bug — it is what let a nightly restart silently do nothing for 8 hours on my host before I noticed.

## Suggested fixes

- Exit non-zero when the readiness budget is exhausted, regardless of the underlying service state
- Either raise `GATEWAY_RESTART_REPLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS`, or derive it from `GATEWAY_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (315 s) the way the drain budget already is, or expose a `--health-timeout <ms>` flag
- Distinguish "service is not running" from "service is running but slow to become ready" — the latter should not be reported as a restart failure, and the `Port 18789 is already in use` line is misleading here, since the process holding the port *is* the replacement

## Workaround

Drive `launchd` directly (`launchctl bootout gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway` + `launchctl bootstrap gui/501 <plist>`) and poll readiness yourself with a larger budget. Note that `bootout` is asynchronous — bootstrapping immediately afterwards fails with `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error`, so the replacement needs a wait-and-retry loop. That part works reliably and is what I use for a scheduled daily restart.

issues.body:
# Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

# Beta release blocker

No

# Title

[Bug]: Codex OAuth profile rotation stops tool-using turns instead of continuing safely

# Summary

When a Codex turn reaches an OAuth usage limit after tool actions have completed, OpenClaw marks the attempt as non-replay-safe and stops the turn instead of continuing from the next safe boundary with another eligible OAuth profile.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two eligible OpenAI OAuth profiles for the Codex provider.
2. Start a turn that performs one or more tool actions.
3. During the same turn, exhaust the active profile's Codex usage limit.
4. Observe that OpenClaw surfaces the usage-limit message and stops the turn.
5. Send a new user message and observe that the second OAuth profile is selected successfully.

# Expected behavior

When another eligible OAuth profile exists, OpenClaw should preserve completed tool calls and their results, switch profiles, and continue from the next safe boundary without replaying previously completed tool actions. This should use continuation semantics rather than replaying the whole turn. PR #108966 demonstrates the same safe-continuation principle for Codex tool-terminal turns.

# Actual behavior

The in-progress turn stops after the usage-limit error because the attempt is marked `replaySafe=no`. Auth-profile rotation occurs only on the next separately triggered user turn, so the original workflow does not continue.

# OpenClaw version

2026.10.1 (e178c39)

# Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04

# Install method

npm global

# Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol

# Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> Codex app server -> OpenAI OAuth

# Additional provider/model setup details

Two eligible OAuth profiles were configured. The first profile reached its usage limit during the tool-using turn. A subsequent new turn selected the second profile successfully, confirming that the alternate profile was available. Profile identifiers and account details are intentionally omitted.

# Logs

```text
User-visible error: You've reached your Codex subscription usage limit.
Completed tool actions before the error: 8
Replay classification: replaySafe=no
Observed recovery: the next separately triggered turn selected the other eligible OAuth profile
```

# Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Related safe-continuation implementation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108966

# Impact and severity

- Affected: installations using multiple OAuth profiles with long, tool-using Codex turns.
- Severity: high for state-changing workflows because manual replay can duplicate external actions.
- Frequency: 1/1 observed attempts matching this condition.
- Consequence: the workflow stops and requires a new user turn; blindly retrying risks repeating completed tool actions.

# Additional information

This report does not request replaying the failed turn. It requests a continuation path that carries forward the existing transcript and completed tool results, rotates the OAuth profile, and resumes only unfinished work. For tools with an unknown external outcome, continuation should reconcile or stop at an explicit recovery boundary rather than invoke the tool again automatically.
