### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With the Discord progress draft in verbose tool-log mode (`channels.discord.streaming.mode: "progress"` + `streaming.progress.toolProgress: true`), every tool call is rendered as two identical rows in the same live draft message, even though the session transcript shows each tool call executed exactly once.

### Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.11.1 with the Discord plugin 2026.11.1, config set to verbose progress:
   ```json
   {
     "channels": {
       "discord": {
         "streaming": {
           "mode": "progress",
           "progress": {
             "toolProgress": true,
             "commandText": "raw",
             "commentary": true,
             "maxLines": 12,
             "maxLineChars": 160
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Use a session/agent configuration where the model invokes deferred tools through the `dispatch_action` wrapper (observed with the model below; all web_search/web_fetch calls in the captured turn were `dispatch_action` calls).
3. Send a message that triggers a few web tool calls (e.g. one `web_search` and one `web_fetch`).
4. Watch the live progress draft message while the turn runs.

### Expected behavior

The docs describe `progress` mode with `toolProgress: true` as "the rolling tool log … rows such as `🛠️ Exec: running` or `📖 Read from notes.txt`" (docs/channels/discord/messaging.md, "Live stream preview"). Expected: exactly one row per tool call.

### Actual behavior

Each tool call appears twice with identical text, e.g. `🔍 Web Search for "…" (top 8)` twice and `🌐 Web Fetch from https://www.reddit.com/r/manhwa/comments/1titmy5/…: running` twice in the same draft message. Both rows for a given call show the same `: running` status at the same time.

The session transcript for the same turn (`runId 79856c52-9412-4ac8-8562-ab9b2689cbb1`) contains exactly one `toolCall` id `chatcmpl-tool-994abc162b70c16c` (dispatch_action → `web_search`) and one `toolCall` id `chatcmpl-tool-94690b4a8ec25181` (dispatch_action → `web_fetch`), so each call ran once; the doubling is purely in the progress-draft rendering.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), Discord plugin @openclaw/discord 2026.11.1

### Operating system

CachyOS Linux x86_64, kernel 7.2.9-1-cachyos

### Install method

npm global (node v24.21.0 via nvm)

### Model

9router/Blablador/alias-qwen3.8-flash-next (display: "02 - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, general purpose large model")

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> 9router (local OpenAI-compatible model router) -> Qwen3.8-Flash-Next backend

### Additional provider/model setup details

The effective model uses deferred tool discovery, so third-party/deferred tools (web_search, web_fetch) are invoked as `dispatch_action` wrapper calls in the transcript rather than as direct tool calls. The model/provider itself should be irrelevant to the rendering layer; the wrapper correlation is the part that may matter (see Additional information).

### Logs

N/A — display-layer artifact; no gateway error occurs. The relevant config is quoted in the reproduction section and was live-applied without restart.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Attached screenshot of the live draft (mobile Discord): every row duplicated; message marked "(edited)" confirming a single draft message with duplicated lines.

Transcript excerpt of the same turn shows one toolCall per action:

```text
seq 52  assistant toolCall  id=chatcmpl-tool-994abc162b70c16c  name=dispatch_action
        args.id=openclaw:core:web_search  query="Mia is back manhwa who does Tae-su end up with ending theory" count=8
seq 55  assistant toolCall  id=chatcmpl-tool-94690b4a8ec25181  name=dispatch_action
        args.id=openclaw:core:web_fetch   url="https://www.reddit.com/r/manhwa/comments/1titmy5/…"
```

The draft rendered the web_search call twice and the web_fetch call twice for these two single calls.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Discord users who opt into verbose progress drafts (`streaming.progress.toolProgress: true`), at least when tool calls go through `dispatch_action` wrappers (deferred tools).
Severity: Low/cosmetic — no duplicate execution, no duplicate API spend, the final answer is delivered correctly. But it doubles every row, which makes the rolling tool log noisy and undermines trust in the live status surface.
Frequency: 100% of observed tool rows in the captured turn (all calls were wrapper-mediated).
Consequence: Verbose progress mode is visually broken/noisy for this configuration; quiet mode (default) hides the problem because it only renders a single rolling "Last activity:" status row.

### Additional information

Correlation observed (not a confirmed root cause): every duplicated row in the screenshot belongs to a call the model made through the `dispatch_action` wrapper. Reading the shipped 2026.11.1 code as a starting point:

- `unwrapToolCallForDisplay()` (`src/agents/tool-display-call.ts`) projects the wrapper call to the inner tool's display name/args, so the wrapper's own progress row renders as "Web Search for … (top 8)".
- The Discord compositor receives both a tool-stream event (`onToolStart`, row id `tool:<toolCallId>`, `src/channels/progress-draft-events.ts` / `streaming` `buildChannelProgressDraftLine`) and an item-stream event (`onItemEvent`, row id = the activity item's `itemId`), merged only when ids/correlation keys match (`mergeProgressDraftLine` in `src/channels/progress-draft-lines.ts`).
- Plausible (unverified) mechanism: for wrapper-mediated calls, the wrapper-projected row and the nested inner call's activity row carry different ids but identical display text, so they never merge and paint as two rows. Plain non-wrapped calls were not captured in the screenshot, so they may or may not be affected; quiet-mode's single rolling status row masks the issue entirely.

Search of open issues for "progress draft duplicate" / "duplicate tool progress line" did not surface an existing report of this specific duplication (closest matches concern different surfaces: #192864 Slack literal chars, #179867 Telegram checklist carryover, #151345 Telegram hook suppression).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The iOS app sends `chat.send` with `thinking: "off"` to sessions whose model doesn't advertise `off` (here `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, levels `low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra`). The Gateway treats that as an explicit per-message override and rejects the turn with a gateway-injected reply: `Thinking level "off" is not supported for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5. Use one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra.` The user never chose `off`. The same session works from the macOS app.

### Root cause (from source, main at 8dd41fc95291)

Three pieces combine:

1. `OpenClawChatViewModel.init` seeds `preferredThinkingLevel` with `"off"` when no initial level is passed (`ChatViewModel.swift:561`, `normalizedThinkingLevel ?? "off"`). iOS never passes one (`apps/ios/Sources/Chat/IOSChatViewModelOwner.swift`, `OpenClawChatViewModel(...)` has no `initialThinkingLevel`).
2. `preferredThinkingLevel` is only corrected when live `chat.history` applies `payload.thinkingLevel`, when a `sessions.patch` result comes back, or when the user picks a level. `syncThinkingLevelOptions()` updates the displayed `thinkingLevel` ("Inherited medium") but not `preferredThinkingLevel`, and the send path reads `preferredThinkingLevel` (`ChatViewModel+Outbox.swift:410`). With the offline transcript cache and outbox, iOS accepts a send on cold launch or resume before live history arrives, so the seed `"off"` goes out.
3. `effectiveThinkingLevelForSend` (`ChatViewModel+Thinking.swift:186`) clamps against the model's advertised levels only for `ultra`. `normalizedThinkingLevel(_:options:fallback:)` (`:366`) returns any non-`ultra` level unchanged, so an unadvertised `off` passes through even after the profile has loaded. Queued outbox commands replay their captured `thinking` through the same function (`ChatViewModel+Outbox.swift:931`), so a message queued with `off` keeps failing after metadata loads.

The Gateway then rejects: `chat.send` maps `p.thinking` to `thinkingLevelOverride`, and `get-reply` returns the "not supported" reply whenever an explicit override is unsupported, instead of falling back the way it does for inherited or stored levels.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway with a session on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` (or any model whose thinking profile omits `off`), no thinking override stored on the session.
2. On iOS, force-quit the app, reopen it into that chat, and send a message right away, before the chat finishes its live reload.

### Expected behavior

The app sends no `thinking` field unless the user picked a level (inheritance stays on the Gateway). If it does send one, it clamps any level the model doesn't advertise to the session's or profile's default, not just `ultra`.

### Actual behavior

The turn is rejected with the gateway-injected "Thinking level "off" is not supported" reply. Telling the agent in plain text to use medium doesn't help, because the rejection happens before the run.

Evidence from our Gateway log, one iOS connection: both rejected sends (`agent.wait` at 07:54:56 and 07:55:21 local) came before that connection's `sessions.list` (07:55:25), `chat.history` (07:55:31) and `models.list` (07:55:31). `sessions.list` for the session reports `thinkingLevel: null`, `thinkingDefault: "medium"`, `thinkingLevels` without `off`; `chat.history` reports `thinkingLevel: "medium"`. So the Gateway metadata was right, and the app sent its seed value.

### Suggested fix

- Don't seed `"off"`. Send `thinking` as nil/omitted until the user explicitly picks a level, and let the Gateway resolve inheritance.
- In `effectiveThinkingLevelForSend`, clamp any level not in the advertised options (fall back to session `thinkingLevel`, then profile `defaultLevel`, then nearest supported non-off), not only `ultra`.
- Optionally, server-side: when a client-supplied `thinking` is unsupported and the client didn't mark it user-explicit, fall back like stored levels do rather than rejecting the turn.

Related, but not the same bug: #190301 (write-scoped iOS operators can't change Thinking), #111485 (iOS Talk hard-codes `low`), #109351 (Watch forces `adaptive`).

### OpenClaw version

Gateway 2026.9.7 (c074824). iOS app version not captured. The code paths above are unchanged on main at 8dd41fc95291.

### Operating system

macOS 15.7 (Gateway host); iOS 26.6.2 on iPhone. The paired operator token has `operator.admin`, so #190301 is not involved.

### Install method

npm global (Gateway)

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 via the claude-cli runtime

### Provider / routing chain

iOS app -> Gateway (`chat.send`) -> rejected before run

### Workaround

Wait for the chat to finish loading (the Thinking chip shows the level) before sending. If a send fails, resend after the load finishes. Picking a level explicitly in Chat actions → Thinking level fixes it for the rest of that app session. From source, a message already queued in the outbox with `off` would keep failing on replay; sending it fresh after load should work (not live-tested).

> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/executor · model: claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: agent-initiated

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A claude-cli turn fails with `CLI history changed before preparation` when the previous run of the same session settles its own transcript rows after the lane released the session. Nothing re-plans: the turn ends failed; a queued delivery is dead-lettered, a fallback chain moves the turn to another provider.

- `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.ts` `prepareCliHistoryBoundary`: plans with the transcript watermark (rewrite generation + max seq), then commits writer adoption via `patchSessionEntryCore`.
- `src/config/sessions/session-entry-patch-guard.ts` `assertSessionEntryPatchCliHistory` re-reads the watermark inside the write transaction → differs → throws. The throw happens before anything commits; a fresh plan would succeed.
- Late writers seen: post-delivery assistant display rewrite (`openclawDelivery.mediaUrls` + display content → `rewriteSqliteTranscriptEventRowsInTransaction` → generation rotation) of a reply carrying an image; aborted-run partial persistence before a resubmit.

Related, not duplicate: #159661 (stale `activeWriterRunId`, "owner changed" refusal — fixed), #165954 (boundary never stored / decays to unknown).

### Steps to reproduce

1. claude-cli agent session; turn A replies with a generated image (any outbound media).
2. While turn A runs, a second input is queued for the same session (e.g. a media-generation completion wake).
3. Turn A finishes; its lane releases; queued turn B starts (~30 ms later) and plans the CLI history boundary.
4. Turn A's delivery rewrites its reply row with display content (~330 ms after the reply insert) → transcript generation rotates while B is between plan and commit.
5. B's commit guard throws `CLI history changed before preparation`.

Deterministic repro on `main` (f986a7aaf1) in `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.test.ts`: wrap `patchSessionEntryCore` once, append or rewrite a transcript row after the planner returned and before the guarded commit → `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` rejects (existing test "refuses an intervening append|rewrite …" asserts exactly this).

### Expected behavior

The turn plans the boundary again against the settled transcript and runs — the same result as a turn that started a few hundred ms later. A boundary is still never committed for a plan whose watermark moved; a live foreign writer ("owner changed") still refuses.

### Actual behavior

Turn fails in ~350 ms with `CLI history changed before preparation`:
- queued session delivery: `session delivery: retry failed for entry <id>: CLI history changed before preparation` → `queued session delivery requires durable dead-letter settlement`; the queued input never reaches the session (no user/assistant row).
- direct turn with fallbacks: `model fallback decision: candidate_failed … detail=CLI history changed before preparation` → turn rerouted to another provider family.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.8 (ab2e926); same code on main f986a7aaf1

### Operating system

Linux (Debian 13), x64

### Install method

npm global install, gateways run as systemd units

### Model

claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

claude-cli backend (Claude Code CLI, subscription login) → fallback openai/gpt-6-sol

### Additional provider/model setup details

Several gateways on one host, each with dashboard and executor sessions on claude-cli. `cliBackends` default for claude-cli; no custom history config.

### Logs

```text
12:57:01.392 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=45696
12:57:01.687 [diagnostic] lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:main:dashboard:<id> waitedMs=259600 queueAhead=1 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=0
12:57:02.037 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:dashboard:<id> durationMs=349 error="CLI history changed before preparation"
12:57:02.060 [gateway] Transcript update dispatch failed sessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:<id> error="This operation was aborted"
12:57:02.105 [session-delivery-recovery] session delivery: retry failed for entry <id>: CLI history changed before preparation
12:57:07.114 [restart-sentinel] queued session delivery requires durable dead-letter settlement queueId=<id>
```

Second instance (abort → resubmit):

```text
20:01:17.404 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:executor:<id> error="agent run aborted"
20:01:18.446 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:executor:<id> durationMs=363 error="CLI history changed before preparation"
20:01:18.451 model fallback decision: candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 next=openai/gpt-6-sol detail=CLI history changed before preparation
```

`openclaw doctor` / `openclaw status --all` omitted: the defect is fully evidenced from stored state (transcript rows + `transcript_rewrite_watermarks`) and source; gateway health is unaffected.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Stored state of the session at the failure:
- reply row of turn A (seq 469) carries `openclawDelivery.mediaUrls` + display content with a managed image artifact.
- `transcript_rewrite_watermarks.updated_at` = 12:57:02.020 — 17 ms before the lane task error, after B started (12:57:01.688).
- next row (seq 470) = custom message `Your request couldn't be completed: CLI history changed before preparation`; no row of B's input.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: claude-cli sessions that receive a queued input right after a reply with media, or a resubmit right after an abort.
- Severity: lost work — a queued input (media completion wake to an owner-facing dashboard) dead-lettered with no reply; a direct turn silently moved to another provider family.
- Frequency: intermittent; 3 failures across 5 gateways in 7 days.

### Additional information

Fix proposal (PR follows): `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` re-runs plan + guarded commit up to 3 times while the commit fails with exactly this message and the run is not aborted. Safe because the guard throws inside the write transaction before writer adoption, ALS binding or caller-entry mutation; each attempt recaptures read fence, assertions and watermark. "CLI history owner changed before preparation" and every other error stay terminal.

## Summary

On **2026.10.6 (fe06181)**, every agent turn on the **native Codex harness** appears to load the Codex plugin's module graph from `state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/...` again, in the **main isolate**. The old copies are never released. In a controlled test, 3 one-word turns left **+152 MB of retained heap**, roughly **50 MB per turn**. That alone matches the slow main-heap growth reported in #159783 / #184843.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181), bundled Node runtime, Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 26.04), `systemd --user`, 8 GB RAM
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048 --max-semi-space-size=8 --heapsnapshot-signal=SIGWINCH`
- 8 agents; 6 use `openai/gpt-6-sol` through the native Codex app-server harness (ChatGPT OAuth). Plus 7 Telegram accounts and WhatsApp.

## Controlled reproduction

1. Gateway started at 15:35. A heap snapshot (`kill -WINCH`, which forces a full GC first) was taken at 15:38:50: **A**.
2. Exactly 3 sequential turns ran on three different Codex-backed agents, each in a fresh session key: `openclaw agent --agent <id> --session-key agent:<id>:test:leakexp --message "answer with one word"`. Each finished in 7–10 s. No other agent runs were started in that window, and the Codex rollout directories show exactly 3 new threads.
3. A second snapshot was taken at 15:46:13: **B**.

Retained self size by node type (streaming aggregation of both snapshots):

```
total self size: 633.0 MB -> 785.3 MB (+152.3 MB); nodes 6,844,191 -> 8,674,890
  +57.6 MB  string                      244.3 -> 301.8
  +10.5 MB  array                        35.4 ->  45.9
   +9.7 MB  array (object properties)    36.2 ->  45.9
   +8.7 MB  concatenated string          22.7 ->  31.4
   +8.5 MB  object Object                29.5 ->  38.0
   +3.1 MB  object system / Context      10.3 ->  13.4
```

Strings grouped by prefix show **whole module sources duplicated, two copies per turn**:

| string (module source / path prefix) | copies in A | copies in B | per turn |
|---|---|---|---|
| `import { registerCodexCliMetadata } from "./cli-metadata.js"; ...` (Codex plugin entry) | 11 | 17 | +2 |
| `import { i as isJsonObject } from "./protocol-CANUwXJ3.mjs"; import { _ as resolveCodexPolicyMo...` | 128 | 220 | ~+31 |
| zod `core/util.js` locale modules (`const Sizable = ...`) | 684 | 1026 | +114 |
| zod `core.js` / `errors.js` / `$ZodCyclicError` modules | 12 | 18 | +2 |
| `/…/state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/…` path strings | 64,062 | 93,005 | ~+9,600 |
| `file:///…/state/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/…` URL strings | 47,903 | 71,864 | ~+8,000 |

The same pattern shows over a longer window of the previous process: 8 → 17 copies of the Codex plugin entry, and 513 → 1,026 copies of the zod locale module, in 17 minutes with ~5 Codex turns.

## Expected

The Codex plugin modules are imported once per plugin generation and reused across turns. Or, if a fresh evaluation is intentional, it should run in a disposable worker or vm context that can be collected. ESM modules loaded into the main isolate can never be unloaded.

## Impact

About 50 MB of permanent main-heap growth per Codex turn. An active multi-agent gateway with a few hundred turns a day hits the V8 heap limit or the systemd memory cap within hours, and needs scheduled restarts. A tighter heap cap only shortens the time to OOM.

## Notes

- Snapshots were aggregated by node type/constructor and by normalized string prefix with a streaming parser. Happy to run more targeted checks, for example a retainer path for one duplicated module record, if a maintainer suggests what to look for.
- Possibly related: #181687 (catalog worker retention), #156191 (plugin capture memory pressure, closed for 9.5).

issues.body:
**Version:** openclaw 2026.10.10 (npm), Node 26.13.0, macOS 27.x (Apple silicon). `agents.entries.main.heartbeat = {every: "30m", session: "heartbeat"}` (isolated heartbeat session), specialists spawned with `sessions_spawn(runtime: "subagent")`, execution-identity admission active (the "bounded contract" check).

## Summary

Four consecutive scheduled heartbeats were skipped `requests-in-flight` (17:39, 18:09, 18:39, 19:09) while no run existed on `agent:main:main` or on the heartbeat session key in any persisted state, the admin lane view showed the main lane `active 0 queued 0`, and a user's direct Telegram turn on `agent:main:main` was admitted and completed normally in the middle of the window (18:28:48 → 18:32:06). The block appeared between the 17:09:53 heartbeat completion and the 17:39:32 skip and coincides with a failed requester-settle wake sequence for a coding batch (admission refusal at 17:22:54, then `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` at 17:23:24 and 17:31:55). `sessions.abort` on the requester key returned `{status: "aborted", abortedRunId: null}`, cascaded into a verifier grandchild, and the next scheduled heartbeat (20:09:33) ran. Which entry blocked the gate cannot be identified from outside the process: the skip reason names no session key or run, and the heartbeat path has no expiry for a stale active-run entry (visible turns do).

## Timeline (one day, local time)

1. 16:52:49 → 16:53:46 — a coding sub-orchestrator (`agent:coding:subagent:48629c78-…`) finished a batch of five children. Its batched requester-settle announces were refused: `lane task error … error="execution identity admission token violates its bounded contract" taskKind=spawn sessionKey=agent:coding:subagent:48629c78-…` (16:52:49, 16:53:19) and the same error on the turn path for the requester, `taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=announce:v1:agent:coding:subagent:48629c78-…:announce:requester-settle:…` (16:53:28, 355-char runId). **This occurrence did not block anything:** the 17:09:30 heartbeat completed (`ok`, 22 s).
2. 17:22:54.036 — `[warn] Subagent announce give up (expiry) run=announce:requester-settle:coding:agent:coding:subagent:48629c78-…:<5 child run ids>:yield-1 … retries=6 endedAgo=1804s deliveryError="delivery path none did not complete"` (the coding-requester announce).
3. 17:22:54.297 — `[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=24 error="execution identity admission token violates its bounded contract" errorName=Error taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=announce:requester-settle:main:agent:main:main:announce:requester-settle:coding:agent:coding:subagent:48629c78-…:<5 child run ids>:yield-1` (331 chars; the admission bound is 256). The trigger is #183416, closed 2026-10-26 by #183454; that fix merged to `main` on 2026-10-26 and is not present in the published 2026.10.10 dist (no digest builder; a 2026-10-30 comment on #183416 reports the same for the 10.7 / 10.9 / 10.10-beta tarballs). Single-child announces (136 chars) and a 5-child batch under a `main` requester (231 chars) succeeded the same day; a coding requester with 5 pending children (284 chars, nested wrappers 331 / 355) failed every time.
4. 17:22:54.342 — `[agents/subagent-announce] requester settle wake attempt failed; retry scheduled … requesterSessionKey=agent:main:main … attemptCount=1 retryDelayMs=30000 disposition=retryable`. 17:23:24.862 — `Session "agent:main:main" changed while starting work. Retry. | SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` with `attemptCount=2 retryDelayMs=120000`. 17:31:55.747 — the same `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` failure as a bare `Subagent completion direct announce failed` line, with no `retry scheduled` and no give-up line after it. Two rows stayed `interrupted` in `session_pending_inputs` for `agent:main:main` (similar shape to #144594).
5. Heartbeat receipts (`cron_run_receipts`, the declared heartbeat job): 17:09:30 `ok`; 17:39:32, 18:09:32, 18:39:33, 19:09:33 `skipped — heartbeat skipped: requests-in-flight` (each finishing in the same second); 19:39:33 `cron-in-progress` (that gate is evaluated before the active-run check).
6. 18:28:48 → 18:32:06 — a direct Telegram turn on `agent:main:main` (`agent turn milestone runId=dd38e18b-… sessionKey=agent:main:main`) was admitted, ran tools and replied. Other `agent:main:cron:*` and group sessions also ran during the window. So the main session was not blocked; the heartbeat gate was.
7. What was NOT there during 17:40 → 19:45 (MEASURED): no `session_windows` row in status `running` for `agent:main:main` or the heartbeat key in any store (the heartbeat sessions of the skipped fires were never created); the stored `agent:main:main` entry `done`, `abortedLastRun=false`; admin `diagnostics.lanes`: main lane `active 0 queued 0`; no `lane task error` lines; no stuck-session recovery lines.
8. 19:45:56 — `sessions.abort {key: "agent:main:heartbeat:heartbeat"}` → `no-active-run`. 19:45:59 — `sessions.abort {key: "agent:main:main", agentId: "main"}` → `{ok: true, status: "aborted", abortedRunId: null}`. 19:46:01 — the cascade (`cascadeDescendants` → `abortControlledSubagents`) killed a verifier subagent 13.8 min into its work: `lane task error: lane=session:agent:verifier:subagent:315910c7-… error="agent run aborted" errorName=AbortError taskKind=spawn`, whose requester was the coding sub-orchestrator 48629c78 (a grandchild of the aborted key).
9. 19:46:57 — a manual heartbeat run (`cron run`, intent manual, which bypasses the active-run check) completed (`ok` 19:49:31); the next **scheduled** fire at 20:09:33 completed `ok`, so the block was gone after the abort.

## Reading the 2026.10.10 dist

- `heartbeat-runner-run-*.mjs` (~1160–1190): the busy stage returns `requests-in-flight` on any of: main lane queue size > 0; `hasActiveRunForAgent(agentId, listActiveReplyRunSessionKeys) || hasActiveRunForAgent(agentId, listActiveEmbeddedRunSessionKeys)` (skipped for intent `immediate` / `manual`); main-session restart-recovery state or a restart-recovery delivery on the heartbeat session entry; a `pendingFinalDelivery` younger than 30 s; an active reply/embedded run on the heartbeat key; heartbeat session lane size > 0. `listActiveReplyRunSessionKeys()` is `[...replyRunState.activeRunsByKey.keys()]` (`reply-run-registry.registry-*.mjs`), so any key of the agent counts. From outside the process I could rule out the lane sizes, the stored windows and the heartbeat key; I cannot see the reply-run registry, the embedded-run projection or the recovery fields — and neither can the skip event, which carries only the reason string.
- Release paths exist and none fired for this entry over two hours: `expireVisibleStaleOperation` (`reply-run-registry.state-*.mjs`, visible turns only — the user turn at 18:28 ran, yet the gate stayed blocked, so either the entry sits on another `agent:main:*` key or the heartbeat path simply never calls that expiry); `forceClearReplyRunBySessionId` in `dispatch-from-config-*.mjs` (only for a stored status of failed/timeout/killed; this entry was `done`); stuck-session recovery (`recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`, driven from a session's own diagnostic state; no recovery lines in the window); finalization settle timers (arm only when a lease is `finalizing`); `agent-runner-run-*.mjs` `operation.complete()` on an admission failure and `fail("run_failed")` — the 16:53:28 refusal on the same key left nothing behind, so the admission refusal itself is probably not the leak; the `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` retry path (items 4 above) is the other candidate. `evictPriorLifecycleReplyRuns` runs only on an in-process restart rotation (`prepareGatewayRestartIteration`).
- `sessions.abort` with no `runId` sets `cascadeDescendants: true` (`sessions-abort-*.mjs`) and aborts the control tree under the key (`chat-abort-handler-*.mjs` → `abortControlledSubagents`); `aborted: true` with `abortedRunId: null` can come from the descendant cancellation alone, so the abort result does not say what, if anything, was cleared on the key itself. Cascading on a real run is by design (#169700).

## Expected

1. The `requests-in-flight` skip (event and log line) names the blocking session key, run id, its age and which of the busy conditions matched, so an operator can tell a real run from a stale entry.
2. The heartbeat gate applies the same stale-entry expiry that visible turns get (`expireVisibleStaleOperation`), or a bounded age for active-run entries with no backing run (no session window, no lane task, no run id), as #105819 did for `active_reply_work` with no activity evidence.
3. `sessions.abort` on a key with no run of its own reports `no-active-run` (or says what it cascaded into) instead of `aborted / abortedRunId: null` while killing live descendants.

## Actual

Heartbeats (and anything else gated on `requests-in-flight` for that agent) stay skipped indefinitely; the only visible symptom is a growing run of `skipped: requests-in-flight` receipts; nothing names the blocker; recovery needs an abort that can kill live subagents, or a gateway restart.

## Repro

Not deterministic. The sequence here: execution-identity admission on, 2026.10.10, a coding sub-orchestrator with 5 pending children (batched requester-settle runId > 256 chars, #183416), the requester-settle wake for `agent:main:main` refused and then failing twice with `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`; the scheduled heartbeats then skip `requests-in-flight` with nothing running until the requester key is aborted or the gateway restarts. The same admission refusal 30 minutes earlier did not leave the block, so the retry path after the refusal looks like the more likely place the entry is left behind.

## Related

#183416 (closed 2026-10-26) / #183454 (merged to `main` 2026-10-26): the trigger, fix not in the 2026.10.10 dist. #116488 (closed; a superseded reply operation never released from `replyRunState.activeRunsByKey`, fixed by #102160 / #106792 — same registry, different producer). #105712 / #105819 (closed; reclaim of phantom `active_reply_work` with no activity evidence). #167005, #187099 (open; stale reply ownership not reclaimed by recovery). #190427, #170562, #158154 (open; refused or expired requester-settle wakes and their leftover state). #159691 (closed; same `requests-in-flight` gate, opposite symptom: a completed isolated heartbeat retained and re-run). #166952, #92523 (closed; other `requests-in-flight` starvation causes), #167844 (closed; the cron-in-progress gate). #144594 (open; interrupted pendingInputs never replayed). #127195 (open; `changed while starting work` has no reason code). #169700 (merged; stop cancels descendants by design).

_Redacted logs or a test of a patch are available on request._

issues.title: Claude CLI resume fails with "Native tool authority capture is no longer active", then every retry fails with "Plugin invocation scope is closed"

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:message-loss
labels.description: Channel message delivery can be lost, duplicated, or misrouted.

issues.body:
Version: OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), macOS 27.2.1 arm64, Bun. Agent main on the claude-cli runtime (claude-sonnet-5-5, liveSession claude-stdio), Telegram + webchat.

## Symptom
Replies fail with "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request". 103 occurrences in one day; continues after a Gateway restart.

## Log sequence (every failure)
1. `cli exec: provider=claude-cli ... useResume=true session=present resumeSession=<id> reuse=reusable`
2. ~1s later: `cli terminal failure ... error=Native tool authority capture is no longer active.` (FailoverError)
3. Retry/fallback candidates (including non-claude-cli ones) each fail in ~15 ms with `source execution authority is no longer active | Plugin invocation scope is closed`. The cause is cached in the sticky `sourceFailure` in prepareAgentRunAdmission (admitted-run-context), so the already-closed scope is reused and no fallback can succeed.

## Pattern
Resumed runs of the same stored Claude session alternate: one resume works, the next resume fails at step 2. A turn started without resume succeeds. Also logged just before: `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown`.

## Expected
A failed resume or stale native tool capture should discard the live session and start a fresh capture/scope, rather than reusing the closed scope for fallback candidates.

## Workaround
Resend the message; avoid reusing the warm session.

issues.body:
> **Reporter status update — 2026-11-18: both symptoms now resolved on this installation.** The reporter confirms that Settings entry is no longer sluggish after updating the Gateway to 2026.11.5 overnight (November 17–18, Asia/Shanghai). The installed CLI/package is independently verified as 2026.11.5 (e13cf15); this check does not independently verify the live Gateway process version. Dark-theme input visibility had already recovered following the macOS 27.3 beta 3 upgrade reported on November 17. These are reporter observations, not a controlled attribution to a particular commit or proof of resolution on every affected installation. Original report and historical evidence follow unchanged.

# [Bug]: macOS app Settings sluggish after opening a conversation; input fields not visible in dark theme

## Summary

On OpenClaw.app 2026.10.10, Settings is responsive immediately after restarting the app, before opening the affected conversation. After opening that conversation, Settings becomes sluggish through both the Dock context menu and the lower-left account/avatar menu. The browser Control UI remains responsive against the same Gateway.

This was noticed after a macOS upgrade, but an OS regression has not been established. A dark-theme input visibility problem was also observed: selecting a light theme restores input visibility but does not resolve Settings slowness.

## Environment

- OpenClaw macOS app: 2026.10.10, build 2610001090
- Gateway: 2026.10.10, local, reachable
- macOS: 27.3, build 26C5035r
- Architecture: Apple Silicon / arm64
- WebKit WebContent version reported by sample: 22626 (22626.1.12.11.4)
- Node: v26.12.1
- App location: /Applications/OpenClaw.app

## Steps to reproduce (observed on one installation)

1. Fully quit and restart OpenClaw.app.
2. Before opening the affected existing conversation, right-click the app's Dock icon and open Settings. Settings is responsive.
3. Open the affected existing conversation in the app.
4. Open Settings again via the Dock context menu. Settings is now sluggish.
5. Open Settings via the lower-left account/avatar menu. The same slowness occurs.
6. Compare with the browser Control UI connected to the same Gateway: the browser is responsive.
7. Select a light theme: input visibility is restored, but Settings remains sluggish in the app.

The observed trigger is loading the conversation, not which Settings entry point is used. The exact conversation content is private and has not been minimized into a shareable reproduction. A fresh/empty-conversation control has not yet been tested. No precise latency measurements are available.

## Dark-theme input visibility (additional observed symptom)

In the macOS app with a dark/black theme, input fields are not visually discernible. The user switched to a light theme through the browser Control UI, after which the input fields became visible again in the app. The browser was reported normal while the app was affected.

This is a user-observed visibility defect; no screenshot or computed-style capture is available. It has not been established whether the field background/border, entered text, or multiple visual elements are affected. Do not interpret this as a confirmed loss of input functionality. The relationship between this visibility defect and the Settings slowness is unknown: light theme fixes visibility but Settings remains sluggish after opening the conversation.

## Expected behavior

Opening a conversation should not make subsequent Settings navigation sluggish. Settings should remain responsive through either entry point. Input fields should remain visually discernible and usable in both light and dark themes.

## Actual behavior

Settings becomes sluggish after opening the affected conversation. WebKit reports the embedded page becoming unresponsive. Restarting the app permits the responsive pre-conversation control case again.

## Sanitized diagnostic evidence

App unified logs on 2026-11-04, local time UTC+8:

```text
16:33:04.833 WebProcessProxy::didBecomeUnresponsive
16:33:04.833 WebPageProxy::processDidBecomeUnresponsive
16:41:46.966 WebProcessProxy::didBecomeUnresponsive
16:41:46.966 WebPageProxy::processDidBecomeUnresponsive
16:43:54.115 WebProcessProxy::didBecomeUnresponsive
16:43:54.115 WebPageProxy::processDidBecomeUnresponsive
```

Repeated font warnings were also present (association only, causality unknown):

```text
Serialized font InstrumentSans-Regular reconstructed to Helvetica.
Subbing system-ui; may result in garbled text.

Serialized font Geist-Regular reconstructed to Helvetica.
Subbing system-ui; may result in garbled text.
```

A short WebContent sample included this call path:

```text
ScriptedAnimationController::serviceRequestAnimationFrameCallbacks
JSRequestAnimationFrameCallback::invoke
JS callback (minified/unsymbolicated)
jsElement_scrollHeight
Element::scrollHeight
Document::updateLayoutIfDimensionsOutOfDate
Document::resolveStyle
RenderLayerCompositor::computeCompositingRequirements
```

Important limits: the samples were not synchronized to a sustained freeze. Most main-thread samples were in the run-loop wait state. These frames are investigation leads, not proof of an infinite layout loop, a specific JavaScript function, or a WebKit regression. A separate sample after app restart also included layout/style/compositing work but did not establish the blocking cause. No sustained RegExp hot stack was identified in these captures.

## Related but not established duplicates

- #143713: macOS Control UI hangs in JavaScriptCore RegExp while handling WebSocket messages. Similar WebContent hang symptom, but no matching regex stack established here.
- #149361: umbrella for WebUI performance and stability.
- #156789: native SwiftUI chat hangs while searching inline-math transcript; different observed trigger and sampled stack.

## Scope and uncertainty

- Confirmed user observation: browser normal; app affected after opening an existing conversation; both Settings entry points affected.
- Confirmed user observation: light theme restores input visibility but not responsiveness.
- Not established: macOS upgrade is the cause; dark-theme visibility and slowness share one root cause; every conversation triggers it; exact content trigger; frontend lifecycle/retained view versus WebKit defect.
- No conversation text, credentials, raw logs, personal paths, or raw process samples are attached.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output without a crash)

### Summary
On Windows, the read tool silently replaces non-ASCII characters in ANSI text files when PATH omits the Windows PowerShell directory. The same file reads correctly with the normal PATH.

### Environment
Fresh upstream main ee00ba6be092965acb14c82268348e4403c6e26d; native Windows 11 x64; Node 24.22.1; Windows system ANSI code page 1252. Source checkout with a separate locked dependency installation.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a temporary directory and an `ansi.txt` file containing bytes `63 61 66 e9 0a` (Windows-1252 `café\n`).
2. In a fresh Node process, set only its PATH to that directory (no PowerShell directory); preserve SystemRoot.
3. Invoke the actual local `createReadTool(tempDirectory).execute("proof", { path: file })`. No custom read operations or module mocks.
4. Compare with the same fresh process using the normal PATH, or resolve the stock Windows PowerShell executable by its absolute SystemRoot path.

### Expected behavior
The read result contains `café\n`, using the system ANSI code page.

### Actual behavior
The read result contains `caf�\n`. An absolute stock Windows PowerShell query under the identical restricted PATH confirms `[Text.Encoding]::Default.CodePage` is 1252.

### Root cause and scope
`src/infra/windows-encoding.ts` probes the system text encoding with bare `powershell.exe`, caches the failed lookup as null, and falls back to UTF-8 replacement decoding. The console probe and other Windows native utilities already resolve their executable through the canonical Windows install-root helper.

### Real behavior proof
Native reproduction through the actual read tool on unmodified main returned `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"caf�\n"}]}` (details repeat the same text). Reusing `getWindowsPowerShellExePath` in the system-encoding probe returns `café\n` through that same tool and real on-disk file. No Gateway, real user files, or live state were touched. A focused regression fails on the original code and passes after the repair; UTF-8/UTF-16 behavior and diagnostic environment tests remain passing.

### Impact
Windows callers with a deliberately reduced PATH can receive corrupted legacy text from read rather than a visible setup error. This report is about the system ANSI file decoder, not OEM console decoding or launcher-script encoding.

issues.body:
## Summary

A WhatsApp group's description is fetched on every inbound group message and then
discarded before anything can read it, and no plugin can recover it. Inbound group
context exposes the subject and the participants but not the description.

## Problem to solve

We run an agent in WhatsApp groups shared with customers, one group per customer, and
need each group to tell the agent which customer account it belongs to so the agent
stays scoped to that account's data. The group description is the natural place for
that: it is set once when the group is created, it is visible to everyone in the group,
and WhatsApp can already restrict editing it to admins ("Who can edit group settings →
Only admins"). The alternative is a config entry per group, which does not scale and
drifts the moment someone creates a group without touching the deployment.

`extractGroupMetadata` already returns `desc`, and the extension already asks for it —
both `sock.groupMetadata(jid)` and the connect-time `groupFetchAllParticipating()` query
include a `<description>` node. `summarize()` in
`extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/group-metadata-cache.ts` then keeps `subject`,
`participants` and `mentionParticipants` and drops the rest, so `desc` is gone before
the cache, the hooks, or the prompt see it.

Nothing downstream can get it back:

- No typed hook payload carries group metadata. `before_channel_ingress` can transform
  an inbound event and `before_prompt_build` / `agent_turn_prepare` can add context, but
  none of them is ever given the description.
- The plugin SDK does not hand one plugin another plugin's channel client, so a
  third-party plugin has no way to reach the Baileys socket and ask for it itself.

So a plugin can solve the injection half and has nothing to read. The only remaining
workaround is to put machine-readable data in the group *name*, which is delivered — at
the cost of showing it to every customer in the chat header.

## Proposed solution

Keep `desc` wherever `subject` already travels, and surface it through
`channelStructuredContext`, which the extension already uses for media, contacts and
external ad replies. Core needs no change: it renders structured context generically,
whereas the prompt metadata fields beside `group_subject` are a fixed allowlist in
`inbound-meta`.

Arriving as structured context is also the correct framing — whoever can edit the group
writes the description, so it is untrusted input, and that is exactly how core labels
this block in the prompt.

## Alternatives considered

- **A new `group_description` prompt metadata field** beside `group_subject`. Rejected:
  it changes core for something one channel produces, and it would present a
  customer-editable string with the same weight as host-provided metadata.
- **Patching `node_modules` locally.** What we run today. It works, but it is reverted by
  every extension upgrade and helps nobody else.
- **Encoding the data in the group subject.** Works with no code at all, but the subject
  is the chat title every participant sees.

## Impact

Any operator running an agent in WhatsApp groups can scope it from the group itself
instead of from per-group deployment config. No behaviour changes for groups without a
description: the entry is omitted when `desc` is empty.

## Evidence/examples

`extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/group-metadata-cache.ts`, `summarize()` — `desc` is
present on the `GroupMetadata` argument and absent from the returned entry.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes

## Additional information

Related, not duplicates: #95142 asked for the *outbound* side (setting a description via
the message tool) and was closed as not planned; this is read-only inbound context.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

During one Android gateway-relay Talk turn, the gateway failed a `talk.event` broadcast with `write ECONNRESET`, terminated that websocket, and the Talk session closed while the accepted agent-consult run was still active.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

One observed occurrence on 2026-11-05. The session owner then reported, in the same chat, "we just had a voice conversation bug". No client toast, screenshot, or close code was captured. Gateway file and journal logs show:

- 20:37:58.828Z talk `turn.started` (`sessionId=de4c34d8-a493-425b-b892-f9647e9e7556`, `talkMode=realtime`, `talkTransport=gateway-relay`, `talkBrain=agent-consult`, `talkProvider=xai`)
- 20:38:00.356Z `session.ready`
- 20:38:06.406Z–20:38:06.412Z `transcript.done`, `output.text.done`, `tool.call`, `turn.ended` (`talkFinal=true`)
- 20:38:06.470Z another `turn.started` on the same Talk session
- 20:38:18.327Z main-thread stall `elapsedMs=1303` task `plugins.metadata.scan`
- 20:38:18.333Z several plugins force-retired after 5000ms with a still-running call (concurrent gateway condition; not claimed as the cause)
- 20:38:20.572Z–20:38:20.608Z fifteen `talk.session.appendAudio` responses on `conn=d7c8fd74-3971-4b4b-b149-608b19666f57`, each `res ✓`, `bytes=90`, handler time 2234–2263ms
- 20:38:20.608Z ERROR `broadcast send failed conn=d7c8fd74-3971-4b4b-b149-608b19666f57: write ECONNRESET` event `talk.event`
- 20:38:20.628Z `session.closed` for `de4c34d8-a493-425b-b892-f9647e9e7556` (payload has no close reason)
- 20:38:25.937Z `slow chat send 18531ms` with `preparation=18428ms` and `detail.plugins.metadata.scan=1308ms`
- 20:38:29.113Z the consult run `talk-b1636416384383f300f4a89de379d0a627ac01d296159684a5431d0724be7747` was still active (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol` via `openclaw-native-codex-responses`, session `f961ad3a-cae2-4781-8c78-f3ffbfa8e885`)
- The consult's text answer was persisted in the chat. The voice session had already closed.

In this build, the broadcast send error callback logs that message and then calls `socket.terminate()` (`dist/gateway-prewarm.js`, `broadcast send failed conn=`).

The same chat's next Talk session (`321af1b8-3b6a-4058-a3a3-4f32bfc3efc2`) reached `session.ready` at 20:39:43.906Z and `session.closed` at 20:40:11.684Z with no `ECONNRESET` in this window.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.5 (7e15622)

### Operating system

Gateway: Linux 6.12.111+deb13-amd64 (Debian 13). Client: Android OpenClaw (`openclaw-android`); device label on the same chat was a Samsung S24 FE. The reset websocket was not logged with a user-agent.

### Install method

npm global under nvm (Node v24.22.1)

### Model

Realtime provider `xai` (`gateway-relay`, `agent-consult`). Consult run model `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`.

### Provider / routing chain

Android node chat -> gateway Talk relay -> xai realtime, with agent-consult continued on `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` via `openclaw-native-codex-responses`.

### Additional provider/model setup details

No credentials included. Gateway heap was already at the critical threshold in the same process (20:34:30 local: heap 3.83 GiB / threshold 3.77 GiB; 20:39:30 local: heap 3.85 GiB, rss 5.58 GiB).

### Logs

```
2026-11-05T20:38:20.608Z ERROR gateway/broadcast broadcast send failed conn=d7c8fd74-3971-4b4b-b149-608b19666f57: write ECONNRESET event=talk.event
2026-11-05T20:38:20.628Z INFO talk session.closed sessionId=de4c34d8-a493-425b-b892-f9647e9e7556 talkMode=realtime talkTransport=gateway-relay talkBrain=agent-consult talkProvider=xai
2026-11-05T20:38:44.350Z WARN steering rejected; applying follow-up policy reason=reply_expectation_mismatch disposition=followup-policy channel=webchat sessionId=f961ad3a-cae2-4781-8c78-f3ffbfa8e885 runId=9b5d865a-cfe2-4919-9e1d-18d86c9375c5 activeRunId=talk-b1636416384383f300f4a89de379d0a627ac01d296159684a5431d0724be7747
```

The 20:38:44Z line is the owner's bug report arriving while that talk run was still the active reply. Follow-up policy ran; the report was not dropped. That steering line is timing context, not a second defect.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

No client toast, screenshot, or recording. Server evidence is the gateway journal and `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-11-05.log` lines cited above.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: one Android Talk / webchat session on gateway 2026.10.10-beta.5
- Severity: the live Talk session closed during consult. The text answer was still stored.
- Frequency: 1 observed `ECONNRESET` in this window. Not reproduced on a second attempt.
- Consequence: owner immediately reported a voice-conversation bug. Exact on-screen symptom was not captured.

### Additional information

Searched open `openclaw/openclaw` issues. Not filing onto these because the logged signature differs:

- #131768 and #138272 describe the live response owner being dropped / `session.error` "no live response owner". This window has no such log.
- #172275 describes Talk failure aborting the accepted consult. This consult was not aborted; its text answer was persisted.
- #138972 describes `talk.session.submitToolResult` → `Unknown Talk session`. This window has no `submitToolResult` error.

Unknown: whether the peer, a network path, or the client app reset the TCP connection. `appendAudio` had already returned success acks (`bytes=90`, same size as other small acks on that conn). No repeatable repro was run.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a call-language setting to voice-call so classic (non-realtime) calls can understand and speak languages other than English.

### Problem to solve

The classic call flow always uses English speech recognition and English `<Say>` output.

- Twilio: `<Gather input="speech" … language="${input.language || "en-US"}">` and `<Say voice="${pollyVoice}" language="${input.locale || "en-US"}">` (`extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts`).
- Telnyx: `language: input.locale || "en-US"` for speak and `input.language || "en"` for gather (`providers/telnyx.ts`).
- Plivo: `<GetInput … language="…">` and `<Speak language="…">` default to `en-US` (`providers/plivo.ts`).

Nothing ever sets `language` or `locale`. In `manager/outbound.ts`, `playTts` passes `{callId, providerCallId, text, voice}` and `startListening` passes `{callId, providerCallId[, turnToken]}`. The voice-call config schema has no language or locale field.

A German or Spanish caller on a classic call therefore goes through English speech recognition, so the transcript the agent receives is wrong. Realtime calls don't have this problem, but realtime isn't available on every carrier (Plivo is classic-only) or every model setup.

### Proposed solution

- Add a `language` (BCP-47) setting at the voice-call level, overridable per `numbers.<E.164>` route.
- Pass it as `startListening({ language })` and `playTts({ locale })`. The three providers already accept these fields; nothing populates them today.
- Optionally let a call override it (for example on `initiate_call`), for outbound calls in a different language.

### Alternatives considered

- **Realtime voice:** multilingual, but needs a realtime-capable provider and carrier (not Plivo), and changes the whole call mode.
- **Twilio media `streaming` with a multilingual transcription provider:** Twilio-only, and only covers recognition.
- **Choosing a non-English Polly voice through `tts`/voice mapping:** the `<Gather>`/`<Say>` `language` attribute stays `en-US`.

### Impact

- **Affected:** any non-English deployment on classic voice calls (Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo).
- **Severity:** blocks classic calls for non-English callers.
- **Frequency:** every classic call.
- **Consequence:** wrong transcripts, so wrong answers, for every non-English caller.

### Evidence/examples

Read at v2026.9.8 and main `f4870f5`:

- `providers/twilio.ts`: the `<Gather>` and `<Say>` `language` attributes.
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: the speak and gather `language` fields.
- `providers/plivo.ts`: `xmlSpeak` and `xmlGetInputSpeech` default to `en-US`.
- `types.ts`: the optional `locale`/`language` on the play and listen inputs.
- `manager/outbound.ts`: the `playTts`/`startListening` call sites, which pass no language.
- `config.ts`: no language field.

Re-checked 2026-10-26 at v2026.10.7 and main `71eacdfe9b`: the classic path is unchanged. The per-call brief added in 2026.10.5 has a `language` field, but it reaches only realtime speech and the voicemail text. Details and current line numbers are in the comment below.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

_No response_

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), gateway on macOS 26.5.1 arm64 (Apple Silicon Mac mini)
- Config: `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode` = `"propose"`, `skills.workshop.approvalPolicy` = `"auto"`
- Heavy multi-agent, multi-channel usage; the model ladder is frequently rate-limited, so detached reviews often land on the bottom fallback rung (`zai/glm-5.3-flash`)

**Symptom**

The background experience review from self-learning (docs.openclaw.ai/tools/self-learning) has never completed on this install. From 2026-09-27 through 2026-10-03, `gateway.err.log` shows **50 consecutive `skill experience review failed` entries with zero completions**. Foreground immediate repair/staging works fine (hundreds of proposals; 7 created on 2026-10-02 alone); the last background-review-shaped proposals date from Sep 13/20, i.e. background learning has produced nothing since the streak began.

Per the docs each review gets exactly one attempt and failures are recorded rather than retried, so all 50 opportunities were permanently lost.

**Failure reasons (all 50 attempts, verbatim)**

```
 17  Error: Skill Workshop failed.
 14  Error: Exec failed.
  5  Error: Yield failed.
  4  SessionTranscriptReadFenceError: Completed-turn transcript anchor changed
  2  GatewayDrainingError: gateway is draining for restart
  2  FailoverError: API rate limit reached
  1  FailoverError: Usage limit reached for 5 hour
  1  Error: Tool Call failed.
  1  Error: Provider completed tool call with malformed JSON
  4  429 rate-limit / weekly-monthly cap errors
```

Per day: 2026-09-27: 3 · 2026-09-28: 13 · 2026-09-29: 3 · 2026-09-30: 10 · 2026-10-01: 10 · 2026-10-02: 9 · 2026-10-03: 2

**Additional signal — session-writer race on the review session**

> settled-turn finalization failed: runId=skill-workshop-review:… provider=zai/glm-5.3-flash error=session writer claim changed before transcript persistence — preserving original failure

and nearby:

> assertInputsCurrent … "inputs changed before commit" (dist/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-UCl9kr-O.mjs:253:12)

**Reading**

- ~10/50 clearly environmental (gateway restarts mid-review, provider 429s).
- 4/50 are the documented transcript-anchor fence: the saved turn was rewritten between turn end and the 30s-quiet async read (plausible with compaction/retries in busy concurrent sessions).
- The dominant ~37/50 cluster (Skill Workshop failed / Exec failed / Yield failed / Tool Call failed / malformed-JSON tool call) looks like the detached review agent's own run dying — consistent with the session-writer/transcript races above under heavy concurrency, and aggravated when the review lands on a weak fallback model that can return malformed tool calls.

**Questions**

1. Is 0% completion of experience reviews under concurrent load a known issue?
2. Any planned resilience change (retry/backoff, model floor for reviews, fence handling)?

Happy to share fuller log excerpts if useful.

issues.body:
When using OpenClaw with a screen reader, navigating back to the latest user or assistant message can require moving backward through multiple elements from the message input.

For longer responses, this can make reviewing recent conversation turns unnecessarily cumbersome.

It would be helpful if each conversational message were exposed as a semantic heading so screen reader users could navigate directly between messages using standard heading navigation.

For example:

- Heading: You
- User message content
- Heading: OpenClaw
- Assistant response

The exact heading level could be chosen based on the existing page hierarchy, with user and assistant messages using the same heading level.

This would make it much easier to move between conversation turns and quickly reach the most recent response.

issues.body:
## Summary

On a long-lived (13-day, ~310k token) WeChat-bridge session, the agent repeatedly received **user prompts that the user never sent**. Those prompts exist in `trajectory_runtime_events.data.prompt` but have **no corresponding `transcript_events` user row** — so the user (looking at Control UI) and the agent (looking at its own context) disagree about what was said. This is not the same as #143632 (no serialized context envelope in the body) nor #148338 (prompts are not empty).

The same session also shows **system-internal strings being submitted as user prompts** and one **runtime event persisted as a `role: "user"` transcript row**, which points at prompt assembly / inbound dispatch rather than at the model.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.1** (gitSha `ad6fe23`), npm install, gateway local (`gateway --port 18789`)
- Windows 10.0.19045 (x64), Node **v24.15.0**
- Channel: `openclaw-weixin` (community WeChat bridge), single DM conversation, single account
- Model: `deepseek/deepseek-flash` (1M ctx), `thinking: high`
- Session: created 2026-09-05 during a `session-sqlite` migration (jsonl → sqlite), still running today (~2,930 transcript events)
- Config relevant bits: `contextPruning: {mode: "cache-ttl", ttl: "5m"}`, `compaction: {mode: "safeguard", keepRecentTokens: 50000}`, `heartbeat: {every: "60m", isolatedSession: true, lightContext: true}`
- Heavy use of **background exec** during the affected window (long downloads, benchmarks) → many `async command completion` events

## Observed behaviour

1. **Phantom user messages.** Three prompts were submitted to the model that the user confirms he never sent. For each of them:
   - `transcript_events`: **no** `role:"user"` row
   - `trajectory_runtime_events.prompt` (the input actually submitted): present
   - `trajectory_runtime_events.messages` (the history array shipped with the run): **absent** → rules out "history replay"
   - Later they appear in `assistantTexts` (the agent quoting them) and then again in later prompts after the user copy-pastes the agent's reply back (the bridge has no quote/reply feature, so the user must paste).

2. **System-internal strings submitted as user prompts.** In the same window, `prompt.submitted` events include prompts that are clearly not user text:

```
[Queued user message from a previous active turn; preserved as context only. Continue with the active prompt below.]
[OpenClaw heartbeat poll] An async command completion event was triggered, but user delivery is disabled ...
```

```
The previous assistant turn recorded reasoning but did not produce a user-visible answer.
Continue from that partial turn and produce the visible answer now. Do not restate the reasoning or restart from scratch.
```
(observed 6×)

```
[System] Your previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart while OpenClaw was waiting on tool/model work. ...
```

```
[Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]
```

3. **A runtime event persisted as a user message.** The event text below was written into `transcript_events` with `role: "user"`:

```
Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.
```

4. **Message splitting.** One inbound user message of **245 characters** was submitted as **two separate prompts** (first half, then second half as its own prompt).

5. **Duplicate submission.** The same 245-character message was submitted twice, verbatim, ~4 minutes apart (two distinct runIds).

6. **Timeline skew.** The same content appears as a `prompt.submitted` at `15:22:43Z` and as a `transcript_events` user row at `15:36:24Z` (~14 min apart).

## Impact

- The agent answers questions nobody asked, and quotes "user statements" that do not exist → it makes decisions on non-existent instructions.
- User and agent end up with **two different versions of the conversation**; the user reasonably concludes the agent is hallucinating, and the agent reasonably concludes the user forgot what he said.
- It is self-reinforcing: the agent quotes the phantom text → the quote appears in `assistantTexts` → it re-enters later prompts.

## Hypothesis

Prompt assembly appears to **merge** three things into one prompt when they coincide:

- a **queued user message** ("preserved as context only")
- a **heartbeat poll** event
- an **async command completion** event

If the "preserved as context only" queued item (or the internal string itself) is promoted to the *active* prompt, the agent will answer old/internal content as if it were a fresh user request. The three coincide exactly in the window where the phantom messages appear — and in this session they coincided because of heavy background-command usage.

## Notes / limits

- `trace.metadata` for the affected runs is redacted (`config: {redacted, runtime}`, `metadata: "[Truncated]"`), so the run's trigger source could not be inspected further from the client side.
- `standing_intents`, `session_pending_inputs` and `context_engine_turn_outbox` were all **empty** at inspection time.
- Persistence gap is separate: even the legitimately-injected prompts were **not** written to `transcript_events`, so a DB-only audit cannot see them.

## Related issues

- #143632 — inbound messages re-delivered with serialized internal context envelope (iMessage)
- #148338 — empty inbound envelopes trigger phantom turn scheduling (closed)
- #100368 — withheld finals stay in agent context, desynchronizing memory
- #143334 — queued user messages starved / settle-yield interaction

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Every inbound iMessage in a direct conversation includes a `reply_to_id` field pointing at the immediately preceding message — even when the user did not use iMessage's native reply/swipe gesture and simply typed and sent a normal message. This makes `reply_to_id` indistinguishable from "previous message in the conversation," rather than reflecting a genuine user-initiated reply relationship.

A related effect: because the agent's own internal reasoning/tool-use narration is sometimes delivered as a separate message from its actual final answer, the "reply target" resolved for the user's next message can end up being that internal-dialog message — not the message that actually contains the content the user is responding to. The two are sometimes bundled together and sometimes not, so the reply target is inconsistent even from the same conversation flow, reproduces on 2026.7.1-2 and 2026.9.4.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In an active iMessage DM with the agent, send a normal message (no swipe-to-reply, no tapback-reply — just type and hit send)
2. Inspect the internal context passed to the model
3. Observe `reply_to_id` is populated, pointing at the prior message, along with a fully resolved "Reply target of current user message" block
4. Note that the resolved reply target is often a long internal-narration message (agent reasoning/tool commentary) rather than the specific content the user meant to respond to

### Expected behavior

`reply_to_id` should only be populated when the user actually performs a native reply action (e.g., swipe-to-reply in Messages.app), and should be absent/null for ordinary sequential messages. When it is populated, it should point at a coherent, user-facing message — not an arbitrary internal-narration fragment that happened to be the most recent bubble.

### Actual behavior

`reply_to_id` is populated on effectively every message regardless of any reply gesture, and resolves to whatever the most recent message happens to be — including agent internal-dialog/narration content that isn't the actual reply target the user intended.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4

### Operating system

macOS 15.7

### Install method

npm global

### Model

anthropic/claud-sonnet-5

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> opencode zen -> anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

iMessage channel connected to agent dedicated apple id conversing with another apple id.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Example payload from a message that was just typed normally, not replied to anything:

{"chat_id":"chat_id:2","message_id":"2137","reply_to_id":"4D503960-ADED-410C-A9D8-5D34E4DF2C50","was_mentioned":true}
A later example in the same conversation resolved `reply_to_id` to an entire prior multi-paragraph agent message (reasoning + a full draft bug report embedded in it) — again with no reply gesture performed by the user.


### Impact and severity

Affected: iMessage channels from 2026.7.1-2 and 2026.9.4; signal channel on same installs seems to not be affected.
Severity: Low-to-moderate- any consumer relying on `reply_to_id` to detect genuine reply intent (vs. plain sequential chat) will get false positives on every message, and the resolved "reply target" content can be misleading (internal narration rather than the intended answer).

### Additional information

Seems to be new behavior since upgrading in 2026.7.x; remains in 2026.9.x

 Channel: iMessage (direct message)
• Reproduced across 2 independent sessions, multiple consecutive normal (non-reply) messages, consistent every time

issues.body:
### Summary
Let any plugin register counters, gauges and histograms that `diagnostics-prometheus` serves from its existing scrape route.

### Problem to solve
A plugin that wants operator metrics has to register its own HTTP route and its own scrape job. Operators then run two exporters for one Gateway, with separate auth and separate retention rules, and the plugin cannot reuse the exporter's label and cardinality limits (`prometheus-family-budget.ts`).

Minimal example, a plugin today:

```ts
api.registerHttpRoute({
  path: "/my-plugin/metrics",
  auth: "gateway",
  handler: (req, res) => res.end(renderMyOwnPrometheusText()),
});
```

Prometheus now needs a second `scrape_configs` entry for `/my-plugin/metrics` next to the one for the Gateway exporter.

### Proposed solution
A small registration call on the plugin API that the exporter consumes when it is enabled, and ignores when it is not:

```ts
const m = api.metrics?.register({
  namespace: "my_plugin",            // prefixed as openclaw_plugin_my_plugin_*
  families: [
    { name: "retain_total", type: "counter", help: "Retains by outcome", labels: ["outcome"] },
    { name: "recall_seconds", type: "histogram", help: "Recall latency", buckets: [0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5] },
  ],
});
m?.counter("retain_total").inc({ outcome: "ok" });
m?.histogram("recall_seconds").observe({}, 0.12);
```

- `api.metrics` is undefined when `diagnostics-prometheus` is not running, so plugins stay optional-safe.
- Namespace is enforced by the host, and families count against the existing family and label budget.
- Labels must be declared up front; values are bounded by the existing budget code.

### Alternatives considered
- Plugin-owned route (today): works, but doubles scrape config and bypasses the budget.
- Emit diagnostic events and let the exporter map them: needs a core change for every new metric.
- OTel only: `diagnostics-otel` users are served, Prometheus users are not.

### Impact
Affected: operators who run a plugin with its own metrics next to `diagnostics-prometheus`. Severity: low, quality of life. Frequency: every deployment that uses such a plugin. Consequence: extra scrape config, inconsistent labels, no shared cardinality protection.

### Evidence/examples
See the code references above. Comparable pattern: a shared registry that extensions write into.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information
The same API could also feed `diagnostics-otel` later. This request is only about the Prometheus exporter.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a session's run is interrupted (gateway restart, cooldown, provider error killing the run), inbound inter-session messages that were already **accepted** (sender received `status: accepted`, `targetDisposition: queued`) can remain in the receiver's `pendingInputs` in `state: interrupted`. Observed behavior:

1. **No automatic replay** — interrupted items are not re-delivered to the model on subsequent activity by themselves; they require external intervention (a new inbound delivery/wake, or manual handling). In some cases a later session run consumes the item ("consume-on-activity"), but this is not guaranteed and no completion/presentation acknowledgment is emitted either way.
2. **No bilateral warning** — the sender's transcript shows `accepted`; the receiver's model context shows nothing. Neither side receives an error, retry notice, or queue-depth signal. The failure is observable only by out-of-band inspection of `pendingInputs`.
3. **Content-level impact** — because the message text is on disk (transcript/queue), content is not lost, but *processing* is deferred indefinitely. In one observed case an accepted directive sat unprocessed for ~10.5 hours and the receiver's dependent downstream discipline slipped accordingly; recovery happened only via a manual sweep triggered by unrelated work.

A related, distinct channel: when a run **fails before producing a reply** (e.g., provider rate-limit or context-length error), inputs consumed by that failed run are *not* lost — they remain in the transcript and are visible to the next successful run — but there is **no immediate processing, no receipt, and no automatic re-trigger**. If no further inbound message arrives, the session shows no activity ("processing-delay" type, to be distinguished from the `interrupted` retention above, which may never replay without manual recovery).

## Minimal reproduction (observed path)

1. Session A sends to Session B via `sessions_send`; A observes `status: accepted`.
2. While B has an active/queued run, trigger an interruption of B's run (gateway restart, cooldown window, or a provider-side error that kills the run).
3. Inspect B's `pendingInputs` (e.g., via session-history tooling): the item is present with `state: interrupted`.
4. Let B process later inbound messages normally. The interrupted item is not replayed to the model by the platform; no warning is surfaced to A or B. (In some sessions a subsequent run consumes the item; behavior is inconsistent across sessions/windows.)

## Observed signatures

- `pendingInputs.items[].state == "interrupted"` with `acceptedAt` far in the past while the session is otherwise active.
- Sender side: `accepted` / `queued`, later `no_reply`; no error propagated back.
- Gateway log: run kill events (auth/rate-limit/network) temporally correlated with the retention window; batched retentions cluster in cooldown/restart windows.
- Stale header timestamps on replayed/retained items (hours off from the `date`-anchored wall clock), complicating forensic ordering.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected**: accepted inter-session inputs are eventually delivered to the receiver's model context, or a delivery failure is surfaced to both sides; interrupted items are retried/replayed automatically with backoff.
- **Actual**: silent retention; delivery guarantee ends at `accepted`; end-to-end confirmation requires manual transcript forensics.

## Suggested mitigations (platform side)

1. Auto-replay of `interrupted` pending inputs on the next session run (or bounded retry with backoff), with a dedupe key.
2. Bilateral surfacing: warn the sender when an accepted item enters `interrupted`/unprocessed state beyond a threshold; expose queue/pending state in `sessions_send` follow-up or session status.
3. An empty-wrapper/announce suppression: a run that produces no final text should not emit an announce wrapper to the sender (see secondary item S1 — empty final-text announces caused queue congestion feedback loops: each empty envelope triggered a full model turn on the receiving side).

## Secondary observations (same delivery/presentation layer)

- **S1 — Empty final-text announce noise**: with `delivery.mode: announce`, tool-only or empty closing turns emit empty announcement envelopes to the sender; batches of dozens were observed, each consuming a receiver-side model turn (self-inflicted lane congestion). Suggest gateway-level suppression of empty announces.
- **S2 — Fallback-chain length exhaustion is signature-indistinguishable**: when the primary model (large context) is unavailable and the fallback model has a smaller window, oversized sessions fail with `stopReason: length` / empty content, surfaced only as a generic "couldn't generate response". Rate-limit, context-window, and reasoning-budget failures are indistinguishable to the operator. Suggest distinct error surfacing per root cause, and a compact/degrade strategy that considers the fallback model's window.
- **S3 — Paragraph/section truncation**: occasional truncated presentation of long structured messages observed at the presentation layer (transcript contains the full text; model-visible rendering may drop trailing sections). Low confidence, reported for correlation.

## Environment (sanitized)

- OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23), multi-agent setup (15+ agent sessions, same host), `sessions_send` inter-session routing with `delivery.mode: announce`.
- Observed across a multi-day incident window involving provider rate-limit/auth errors, a gateway restart, a cooldown window, and an intermittent host DNS failure (all inbound/outbound provider calls affected simultaneously).

---

*Business specifics intentionally omitted per submission scope; internal audit trail on file.*

issues.body:
## Summary

`web_search` calls routed to the native Perplexity provider reject requests that include both `freshness` and `date_after`/`date_before`:

```text
conflicting_time_filters: freshness and date_after/date_before cannot be used together.
Use either freshness (day/week/month/year) or a date range (date_after/date_before), not both.
```

The generic docs list all three parameters, but do not clearly state this mutual exclusion for native Perplexity. A scheduled digest interpreted the resulting all-lane provider errors as a "quiet week," producing a false zero-result report.

## Reproduction

1. Configure `web_search` to use Perplexity.
2. Call with `freshness: "week"` and `date_after: "2026-09-03"` (optionally date_before).
3. Observe the provider error above.
4. Omit the explicit dates and retain `freshness: "week"`; the same query returns normal results.

## Requested improvements

- Document the mutual exclusion in `docs/tools/web.md`, ideally in the parameter caveat section and/or a provider capability table.
- Validate/reject the incompatible combination locally before issuing the provider call, with an actionable error that explicitly advises the caller to select one mode.
- Consider exposing this constraint in the generic tool schema/provider capabilities so agents can avoid the invalid call.

## Why it matters

Search automations can otherwise receive zero candidates without a tool-level failure. For scheduled editorial workflows, that creates the risk of silently reporting content scarcity when the actual problem is request validation.
