issues.body:
## Recurrence check (update 2026-10-15)

Re: the review's next step ("trace fresh-session provider exhaustion at the execution owner"). That trace runs in source on `main`; from a release install I can only report whether the failure still reaches us, and it does not. Gateway journal 2026-09-28 → 2026-10-15 13:40 UTC (859,987 lines, `openclaw@2026.9.6`–`2026.9.8`): **0** `trajectory-flush error=FOREIGN KEY` lines and **0** `agent cleanup failed` lines, against **316** lines matching `status=429` in the same window. The one `FOREIGN KEY` hit in the window is our own grep command echoed by the exec log (2026-09-28 11:59 UTC), excluded. Control: the same grep over 2026-09-01..09-08 returns 5. So 17 days with the trigger (429 on a fresh run) present and the failure absent. I am not claiming a fix and I have no commit to point at; if a maintainer can name the change between 2026.8.1 and 2026.9.6 that commits session identity before the first provider call, this issue can close against it. Until then there is nothing further a reporter on a release build can supply.

## Recurrence check (2026-10-12)

No new evidence of the original failure. Gateway journal from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-12 18:00 UTC (185,560 lines, `openclaw@2026.9.8`): **0** `FOREIGN KEY` lines and **0** `agent cleanup failed` lines, with 84 lines matching HTTP 429 in the same window. Control: the same grep over 2026-09-01..09-08 returns 5 `FOREIGN KEY` lines. Together with the 2026-10-08 update below, that is 14 days with no FK failure on 2026.9.6–2026.9.8. I cannot separate cleanup failure, terminal-event suppression and audit-persistence loss from this install while the failure does not occur; I am not claiming a fix.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash): the run registry keeps a leaked `agent.run.started`; the gateway process does not exit.

### Beta release blocker

No — not a plugin-compatibility blocker for the current beta window.

## Summary

A run whose session was never committed dies during teardown, and the run registry keeps its
`agent.run.started` open forever because no `agent.run.finished` is ever recorded.

Session identity is created **lazily**: `ensureSessionEntrySync`
(`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-initial-entry.ts`, doc comment *"Lazy session
identity creation, including the original admission's first writer claim"*) is reached from
`SessionManager` persistence (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence.ts:205-215`), i.e.
on the **first transcript persistence of the turn**. A run that fails before that point — ours
died on a provider `429` on its first assistant call, then exhausted auth-profile rotation — has
no `session_nodes` row and no `session_windows` row.

Teardown then assumes both exist, and fails twice for the same reason:

1. **Trajectory flush.** `trajectory_runtime_events` is keyed to the session window:

   ```sql
   -- src/state/openclaw-agent-schema.sql:436-444
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS trajectory_runtime_events (
     session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
     ...
     FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES "session_windows"(session_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
   ) STRICT;
   ```

   With no window row the insert fails, and the cleanup wrapper logs and swallows it:
   `agent cleanup failed: ... step=openclaw-trajectory-flush error=FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.

2. **Transcript persistence.** `appendTranscriptEventSync`
   (`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:321-353`) reads the entry row,
   `resolveTranscriptAppendRefusal` finds none, and because the scope carries a writer fence the
   refusal is escalated to a throw:

   ```ts
   // session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:334-351
   const fresh = readSessionEntryRow(database, resolved.sessionKey);
   const refusal = resolveTranscriptAppendRefusal(fresh?.entry, resolved, fencedScope);
   ...
   if (fencedScope.expectedWriterRunId !== undefined && !result.ok) {
     throw new SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError(result.error);
   }
   ```

   ```ts
   // session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-guard.ts:29-36
   const identity = {
     agentIdHash: redactIdentifier(resolved.agentId),
     expectedSessionIdHash: redactIdentifier(resolved.sessionId),
     sessionKeyHash: redactIdentifier(resolved.sessionKey),
   };
   if (!entry) {
     return { ...identity, code: "session-entry-missing" };
   }
   ```

   That is byte-for-byte the payload we observe in production, so the failing path on `main` is
   the one we are running.

The throw escapes to the command-queue lane (`src/process/command-queue.ts:413`,
`lane task error: ...`) and the message is recorded `outcome=error`. **What never happens is the
terminal run event.** `agent.run.finished` is projected exclusively from a lifecycle event with
`phase: "end" | "error"` (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts:139-168`), every emitter of it is
guarded by `state.lifecycleEnded` (`src/agents/command/lifecycle.ts:123-200`), and there is no
reconciliation anywhere else: the lane's error boundary only logs. The `agent.run.started` row
stays as the newest event for that session forever.

**Second, smaller defect on the same line:** `agent cleanup failed ... error=FOREIGN KEY
constraint failed` names neither the table nor the session, so the operator-visible message
cannot be attributed without reading the schema. SQLite's bare FK message is the whole diagnosis
we get.

I could not pin **which** of the three terminal emitters was reached before the throw replaced the
run's outcome — the ordering in the logs (cleanup failure at `.100`, lane error at `.104`) is
consistent with `post-run.ts:640-645` (`catch { emitPostTurnError; throw }` / `finally { await
deferredLifecycle.complete() }`) but I did not prove it. The **absence of the terminal audit row
is not an inference**; it is queried below.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a turn on a session key with no committed session yet (a fresh cron/isolated run is the
   natural case — the session row does not exist until the first transcript write).
2. Make the run fail before its first transcript persistence. Ours: provider returns HTTP 429 on
   the first assistant call, auth-profile rotation runs, all candidates fail.
3. Watch teardown: `openclaw-trajectory-flush` fails the FK, transcript persistence throws
   `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` with `code=session-entry-missing`.
4. `openclaw audit --run <runId> --kind agent_run --json` — only `agent.run.started`.

## Expected behavior

Every `agent.run.started` gets a terminal counterpart. A run that dies on the session-persistence
path is still a run that ended, and the registry is the documented way to ask whether a session is
busy — a leaked `started` is indistinguishable from a live turn.

Secondarily: teardown of a run that never committed a session should be a no-op, not two failures.
Nothing is being flushed for a session that does not exist.

## Actual behavior

Two runs, 2026-09-06, gateway journal (verbatim, `America/Sao_Paulo`):

```
19:52:46.916 [discord] embedded run agent end: runId=443ca53f-2767-4245-b187-18e06dae00ec isError=true
             model=claude-opus-5 provider=anthropic error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.
             rawError=HTTP 429: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error", ...}}
19:52:46.953 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=443ca53f-... stage=assistant
             decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit from=anthropic/claude-opus-5
19:55:36.100 [agent/embedded] agent cleanup failed: runId=443ca53f-... sessionId=443ca53f-...
             step=openclaw-trajectory-flush error=FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
19:55:36.104 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=170082
             error="session writer claim changed before transcript persistence |
             {"agentIdHash":"sha256:befa156f0283","expectedSessionIdHash":"sha256:b86d508bc19f",
              "sessionKeyHash":"sha256:cdffe4490bef","code":"session-entry-missing"}"
19:55:36.107 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron sessionId=443ca53f-...
             sessionKey=agent:arthur:heartbeat outcome=error duration=170111ms error="session writer
             claim changed before transcript persistence | {... "code":"session-entry-missing"}"
```

The second run (`0aeb6ffc-3768-498f-8997-e5b832bc7bbc`, 20:27:18 → 20:34:37, `durationMs=440619`)
is identical line for line.

State that proves the leak — the run registry itself, not the log:

```console
$ openclaw audit --run 443ca53f-2767-4245-b187-18e06dae00ec --kind agent_run --limit 100 --json \
  | jq -r '.events[]? | "\(.occurredAt/1000|todate) \(.action) \(.status) \(.sessionKey)"'
2026-09-06T22:52:46Z agent.run.started started agent:arthur:heartbeat

$ openclaw audit --run 0aeb6ffc-3768-498f-8997-e5b832bc7bbc --kind agent_run --limit 100 --json | ...
2026-09-06T23:27:17Z agent.run.started started agent:arthur:heartbeat
```

No terminal row, ever — queried 24h later. For contrast, the healthy runs on the same session key
in the same hour pair correctly:

```
2026-09-06T22:39:16Z agent.run.started  started  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:44:53Z agent.run.finished blocked  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:45:25Z agent.run.started  started  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:45:35Z agent.run.finished blocked  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:46:36Z agent.run.started  started  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:47:45Z agent.run.finished blocked  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:52:46Z agent.run.started  started  run=443ca53f   <-- never finishes
2026-09-06T23:27:17Z agent.run.started  started  run=0aeb6ffc   <-- never finishes
```

There was no concurrent run on that session key between 22:52:46Z and 23:27:17Z, so the session
was not rebound by a sibling turn — the row was simply never created.

## Environment

- openclaw **2026.8.1 (ea80657)**, global npm install (`~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)
- Failing code re-verified against `main` @ `0015b20995` — `resolveTranscriptAppendRefusal`,
  `appendTranscriptEventSync`, the `trajectory_runtime_events` FK and the audit projection are
  unchanged, and the error payload our production emits is produced verbatim by current `main`.
- Node v22.23.2, Debian in a Proxmox LXC, Linux 6.17.2-1-pve x64
- Model `anthropic/claude-opus-5`, embedded runtime

## Provider / routing chain

Cron job (`channel=cron`, lane `cron-nested`) → embedded agent runner → anthropic provider with
several auth profiles. First assistant call HTTP 429 → `decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit`
→ profile cooldown → candidates exhausted → teardown on the path above. The 429 is only the
trigger; any failure before the first transcript commit reaches the same teardown.

## Additional setup details

Multi-agent fleet (7 agents, one gateway), local plugins (a context-engine plugin and MCP servers),
Discord + WhatsApp channels, cron-driven heartbeat sessions. We carry local `dist` patches for
other, unrelated defects — none touches sessions, transcripts, trajectory or audit, and the
`session-entry-missing` payload above is produced by stock `main` code.

## Impact and severity

- **Frequency:** 3 occurrences in 7 days on this gateway (2026-08-31 → 2026-09-07), all with both
  signatures, against 1,623 `agent.run.started` events in the same window.
- **Cost:** any consumer of the run registry reads a leaked `started` as a live turn. Ours is a
  pre-restart guard: both corpses blocked every gateway restart until an age backstop expired, one
  of them while an operator restart was pending — the operator waited on a session that had been
  dead for minutes. Time-to-notice was a day: nothing surfaces a leaked run, the session simply
  looks busy.
- The turn's own outcome is also lost: no transcript, no trajectory, and the only trace is a
  `[diagnostic]` line.

Happy to test a patch against this gateway; the failure reproduces on its own roughly twice a week
under provider rate limiting.

issues.body:
**Version:** `2026.8.1-beta.1` (ff8a3fe)
**Runtime:** `claude-cli` backend, `anthropic/claude-opus-5`
**Surfaces affected:** Control UI (webchat) and the Android app. Telegram is **not** affected.

## Summary

With the `claude-cli` backend, every assistant turn is persisted twice through two independent writers, and clients that render the transcript show both. The user sees the full turn, then immediately a second copy of the same turn as one plain block.

The two copies are not byte-identical, so the Control UI's "consecutive duplicate text-only messages collapse into one bubble with a count badge" rule (documented in `web/control-ui.md`) never fires.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** one assistant turn appears once.

**Actual:** the turn appears twice:

1. **Live/canonical view** — each assistant text block as its own bubble, interleaved with tool-call cards, imported from the Claude Code transcript (`importedFrom: "claude-cli"`, `api: "anthropic-messages"`, `stopReason: "end_turn"`).
2. **Aggregate record** — a single message whose `content` holds **one text block** with every intermediate narration line *and* the final answer concatenated (`api: "cli"`, `stopReason: "stop"`, `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:<runId>"`), written ~650 ms later.

The more intermediate text a turn emits, the larger the visible duplicate.

## Evidence

Session store: `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`, table `transcript_events`.

```sql
select seq, event_json, created_at
from transcript_events
where session_id like '<session>%'
order by seq;
```

A turn that emitted two narration lines plus a final answer produced this aggregate:

```
seq 44  api=cli  len=1835  text blocks in content: 1
"Son 18 (16 "New chat", una sin etiqueta y la del móvil). Voy con la del móvil primero…
 \n\nLa herramienta está limitada a mi propio árbol de sesiones. Voy por la CLI.
 \n\nHecho. Las 18 archivadas, verificado contra la base de datos. …"
```

That single record reproduces, verbatim and in order, the three separate bubbles the client had already rendered for the same turn.

Across the whole store: **84 duplicated turns out of 307 assistant messages carrying text.** The pattern is constant — a `cli` record paired with a twin whose `api` differs (`anthropic-messages`, `openclaw-transcript` or `openai-responses`) and whose byte length is identical.

## Where it comes from

`persistCliAssistantTranscript()` in `dist/cli-runner-*.js` writes the aggregate via `appendExactAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript` with `idempotencyKey: cli-assistant:${runParams.runId}`.

It is gated by `runParams.persistAssistantTranscript`, computed in `dist/agent-runner.runtime-*.js` as:

```js
persistAssistantTranscript:
  turn.followupRun.currentInboundEventKind !== "room_event" &&
  turn.followupRun.run.suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence !== true
```

and `suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence` is only set for room events (`get-reply-*.js`: `suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence: isRoomEvent`). So for ordinary DM turns the aggregate is always written, in addition to the per-block import from the CLI transcript. There is no user-facing setting to disable it.

## Possibly related condition

`openclaw doctor` reports on the same install:

```
- Main session transcript missing (~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/sessions/<sessionId>.jsonl).
```

That directory holds **138 `*.trajectory-path.json` pointers and zero `.jsonl` transcripts**. With no native transcript to reconcile against, the two writers never converge.

## Why Telegram is unaffected

Channel delivery sends the final text once — the gateway log shows a single `outbound send ok` per message. Telegram renders what was delivered, not the transcript, so the aggregate is never shown there.

## Related

PR #98117 (`fix(ios): avoid transient duplicate final replies`) addresses a neighbouring symptom in the shared chat view model, where a live `chat.final` row is adopted by the canonical `session.message` instead of being appended twice. This report is one layer lower: two rows are genuinely persisted, so adopting at render time would hide the duplicate rather than prevent it.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With the codex plugin enabled (sessionCatalog on, OpenAI via ChatGPT OAuth), `codex app-server` processes accumulated to 54 (~3.8 GiB) over ~6 h without being reaped, pushing the container to 998/1024 PIDs, after which thread creation failed (EAGAIN) and the gateway stopped serving chats, Telegram replies, and config changes until the plugin was disabled and the gateway restarted.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.10.5 in Docker with a container pids limit of 1024 and memory limit of 8 GiB.
2. Configure the OpenAI provider with ChatGPT browser sign-in (OAuth), no explicit `agentRuntime` on the provider or models.
3. Have the `codex` plugin enabled with `plugins.entries.codex.config.sessionCatalog.enabled: true` (in our case it was re-enabled automatically after saving settings in the Control UI).
4. Use several agents normally (Telegram + Control UI chats) for a few hours.
5. Watch `docker stats` (PIDs, memory) and the process list inside the container.

### Expected behavior

Codex app-server processes are reused or shut down when no longer needed; their number stays bounded and the gateway stays responsive. Disabling the codex plugin should stay in effect and not be reverted by OpenAI route selection.

### Actual behavior

- `codex app-server` processes (node wrapper + codex-linux-x64 binary, ~100–115 MB RSS each pair) accumulate and are never reaped: 54 processes after ~6 h, ~3.8 GiB RSS total, started at different times (minutes to hours apart) and all still alive.
- Container reached 998/1024 PIDs and 7.0/8 GiB memory.
- Then new threads could not be created and Codex crashed:
  `Codex resident catalog background update failed error="codex app-server exited: code=101 ... thread 'codex-main' panicked at .../tokio-1.52.3/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/worker.rs:503:13: OS can't spawn worker thread: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)"`
  `codex app-server exited: code=1 ... node[58473]: pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable Error: spawn <path> EAGAIN`
- After that the whole gateway degraded:
  - `openclaw models list` aborted (`Aborted (core dumped)`, exit 134)
  - Control UI chat: `res ✗ openclaw.chat errorCode=UNAVAILABLE ... Cause: prepared model runtime owner was not committed after replacement for <agent dir>`
  - Telegram: `dispatch failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main` (updates spooled for retry)
  - `config.patch persisted but was not applied to the active Gateway (failed)`
  - On restart: `shutdown step failed (gateway close): Plugin runtime still owns resources` (stability bundle written: `gateway.stop_close_failed`)
- Disabling the plugin + restart fixed it (memory back to ~2.7 GiB, ~140 PIDs, 0 codex processes).
- The plugin had been disabled earlier the same day but came back enabled. Per the docs/config schema, OpenAI on the official endpoint "defaults to the Codex harness when omitted" and an implicitly Codex-compatible route "can enable the Codex plugin". Setting `models.providers.openai.agentRuntime.id: "openclaw"` was needed to stop this.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (host), OpenClaw running in Docker 29.8.2

### Install method

docker

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol (utility model) and openai/gpt-6-sol (fallback); primary agents on deepseek

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai (ChatGPT browser sign-in / OAuth, official endpoint) -> implicit Codex harness (codex plugin app-server)

### Additional provider/model setup details

10 agents, Telegram channel (2 bots) + Control UI. Container limits: pids_limit 1024, memory 8 GiB. `plugins.entries.codex.config.sessionCatalog.enabled: true` while the issue occurred. Same accumulation pattern was observed earlier the same day (memory reaching 7+ GiB) before the plugin was first disabled. Suggestions: bound/reap idle app-server processes, respect a disabled plugin instead of auto-enabling it from route selection, and surface a clear warning when the runtime is chosen implicitly.


issues.body:
## Summary

Sixteen production call sites across eleven files throw or return the **byte-identical** string
`Session "<key>" changed while starting work. Retry.` No discriminator — no reason code, no call-site
tag, no cause field — reaches the log or the thrown error. When this fires in production, **which of
the sixteen branches ran is not knowable from the output.**

This is the diagnosability half of the family that #118873 / #117096 / #116694 / #121269 covered
behaviourally. Those are all closed and the stuck-session behaviour is fixed. The string is not.

## Verified against `main`

`587c7524e58`. `rg 'changed while starting work' src --type ts`, excluding tests and comments:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts` | 573 |
| `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts` | 333 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts` | 259 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` | 166 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-prepare.ts` | 185 |
| `src/sessions/session-diff-baseline.ts` | 41 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-entry-persistence.ts` | 98 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts` | 241, 284, 292 |
| `src/agents/agent-command-recovery-owner.ts` | 110, 132 |
| `src/agents/agent-command.ts` | 213, 220 |
| `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.ts` | 73 |
| `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` | 57 (the shared helper) |

Three of these are in one function's three branches (`reply-turn-admission.ts:241/284/292`), so even
narrowing to a single file does not narrow to a single cause.

## Why it costs an operator a diagnosis

Production, `2026.8.1-beta.2`, one Discord channel session: **27 rejected runs across 4 inbound user
messages** between `09:58:05` and `10:24:09` (-03:00), each aborting in 4–8 ms with exactly this
string. Worst case, 9 attempts over 6 min 11 s before one user message ran. Every cluster started
within ~90 s of a gateway restart.

```text
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord outcome=error duration=4ms
  error="Error: Session \"agent:<redacted>\" changed while starting work. Retry."
```

The three plausible causes on that path — an `expectedSessionId` mismatch, a recovery-owner claim
returning `invalidated`, and the abort check — call for three different operator responses. The log
distinguishes none of them, so triage is guesswork or a source read per occurrence. Filing this
separately because a fix here is useful whether or not any specific admission bug is open: the next
one in this family will produce the same undiagnosable line.

## The seam already exists

`src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` already owns the discriminating helper:

- `resolveSessionWorkStartError()` already distinguishes *deleted* / *changed* / *still initializing*
  / *archived*, and
- `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED_ERROR_CODE = "SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED"` (line 24) is already
  the shared code.

Roughly fourteen sites route through that helper. The sixteen above bypass it with a hardcoded
template literal, which is what makes them indistinguishable.

## Suggested shape

Not a behaviour change and not a message rewording — the retryable contract and the operator-facing
sentence can stay exactly as they are.

1. Give the helper a `reason` discriminator alongside the message (e.g.
   `session-id-mismatch` | `recovery-owner-invalidated` | `aborted` | `entry-deleted` |
   `initializing` | `archived`).
2. Route the sixteen hardcoded literals through the helper so the reason travels with the error.
3. Log the reason on the rejection path.

Happy to send the PR if the shape is agreeable — I would rather have the reason names settled by a
maintainer first than guess at the taxonomy.

## Version

`2026.8.1-beta.2` for the production data; source claims verified against `main` at `587c7524e58`.

> **Form note (edited 2026-10-08):** this is a feature request that was filed in bug shape. The sections below add what `feature_request.yml` asks for (alternatives, implementation intent) without changing the evidence above.

## Environment (form fields)

- Production data: `2026.8.1-beta.2`, npm global install, Linux (Debian in a Proxmox LXC).
- Model / provider routing chain of the 27 rejected runs: **unknown** — not recorded with the 2026-08 occurrences. The string is emitted before any model call, so the defect is model-independent.
- Steps to reproduce / actual: this is a diagnosability gap, verified by source inspection (table above) and confirmed by ClawSweeper on current `main`; no runtime repro on current `main` was run.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Status quo — read the source per occurrence.** What we do today; it costs a source read per incident and still cannot separate the three branches inside `reply-turn-admission.ts`.
2. **Reword the sixteen messages.** Rejected: it changes an operator-facing sentence and the retryable contract, and the next caller that copies the template literal is undiagnosable again.
3. **A stable public `reason` field on the shared error.** Possible, but it creates a compatibility obligation. ClawSweeper's recommendation — bounded **diagnostic-only** labels in operational logs, retry codes and public messages unchanged — is the shape we prefer.

## Implementation intent

We will open the PR once a maintainer settles the open question (diagnostic-only labels vs public field, and the label names). Not before: we would rather not pick the taxonomy unilaterally.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw: 2026.11.5-beta.2 (c0f42f6)
- Node: v24.22.1, linux/x64 (WSL2)
- Gateway host: WSL2 Ubuntu; all 25 agent workspaces live on /mnt/d (Windows drive via drvfs)
- dreaming config: plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming = { enabled: true, model: "zai/glm-5.3-flash", frequency: "0 5 * * *", timezone: "Asia/Shanghai" } (defaults otherwise)

## Symptom
Every nightly sweep logs, for 13 of 25 workspaces:

```
memory-core: light dreaming failed: ENOENT: no such file or directory, fstat
memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=25, candidates=0, applied=0, failed=13, degraded=0, narrativesPending=0).
```

The error carries no path, so the missing file cannot be identified from logs.

## Impact pattern (progressive, per-workspace death)
- Affected workspaces stop producing memory/dreaming/rem/* and deep/* phase files and DREAMS.md diary entries, while light/* files continue to be written daily (light phase partially executes, then errors mid-phase).
- Onset differs per workspace: one workspace stopped 2026-09-04, another 2026-11-06 - suggests a state-file loss/creation failure that accumulates per workspace rather than a single global event.

## Ruled out
- Not DREAMS.md absence: restoring a valid DREAMS.md to an affected workspace did not heal the sweep.
- Not filesystem-wide: all 25 workspaces are on the same drvfs mount; a plain fs.fstatSync on workspace files works fine.
- Not migration leftovers: ~/.openclaw/agents/*/agent/*.pre-startup-migration-*.bak files exist for ~all agents (26), not just the 13 failing ones.
- Not visible to doctor: openclaw doctor (read-only) has no dreaming checks and reports nothing about it.

## Requests
1. Include the failing path in the light dreaming failed error message (currently swallowed).
2. Handle/repair the ENOENT condition - e.g. recreate the expected state file, or skip gracefully instead of killing the phase pipeline for the workspace.
3. Consider a doctor check for dreaming artifact/state health.

## Extra context
- Happy to provide full sweep logs or run a debug build if you tell me which subsystem flag would surface the path.

issues.body:
### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.7** (npm `latest`), Node **v26.12.1**, Linux x64, 14.8 GB RAM
- systemd service, no `--max-old-space-size`, so the runtime V8 ceiling is the default ~2144 MB
- ~50 sessions across 3 agents, several high-traffic group chats
- `agents.defaults.compaction`: `mode=safeguard`, `maxActiveTranscriptBytes=12mb`
- `session.reset`: `{mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 4320}`

### Symptom

The gateway aborts with:

```
FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

after roughly 20h of uptime. Four aborts in 14 days (Oct 18, 19, 24, 27). No kernel OOM kill in that period - it is always the V8 abort.

At the last abort: RSS 4.05 GiB, `heapUsed` 1.93 GiB, worker isolates ~0.5 GiB, pinned around the 2144 MB old-space cap for hours before dying.

### This is not steady-state workload: the floor only moves up

`diagnostics.stability` emits `diagnostic.memory.sample` every ~30s. Over the last 13 hours before the abort, min/max `heapUsed` per 4-hour block:

| window | min heap | max heap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Oct 26 18-20 | 1,716 MiB | 1,727 MiB |
| Oct 26 20-22 | 1,717 MiB | 1,811 MiB |
| Oct 26 22-24 | 1,738 MiB | 1,856 MiB |
| Oct 27 00-02 | 1,800 MiB | 1,905 MiB |
| Oct 27 02-04 | 1,819 MiB | 1,935 MiB |
| Oct 27 04-06 | 1,881 MiB | 1,946 MiB |
| Oct 27 06-08 | 1,916 MiB | 1,966 MiB |

Within a run the heap does come back down: the largest single-step change observed was **+123.7 MiB in 5 minutes, then -121.2 MiB five minutes later**. Transient allocations are reclaimed. What does not come back is the floor - it rises ~15 MiB/h and never recedes.

### Heap snapshot diff: the growth is prompt strings

Two native snapshots from the same process, 1h49m apart (480.0 MiB -> 527.7 MiB total `self_size`):

| node type | growth |
|---|---:|
| string | **+22.8 MiB** |
| object | +10.3 MiB |
| array | +5.7 MiB |
| code | +2.8 MiB |
| native | +0.2 MiB |

In the later snapshot, the duplicated text looks like this:

| content | copies | total |
|---|---:|---:|
| skills instructions block (`The following skills provide specialized instructions...`) | 215 | 6.2 MiB |
| full system prompt (`You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw...`) | 23 | 2.5 MiB |
| `<!-- openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->` block | 23 | 2.2 MiB |
| heartbeat scratch line (`Follow the heartbeat monitor...`) | 917 | 2.4 MiB |
| memory `## Goal` block | 65 | 1.8 MiB |
| memory `## Decisions` block | 65 | 1.8 MiB |
| base64 JPEG data URL | 11 | 2.0 MiB |

### Retainer path (BFS from GC roots)

```
(GC roots)
  -> global
  -> WeakMap
  -> Array (128 KiB)
  -> Object ... Object
  -> closure observeToolOutcome
  -> Context
  -> closure shouldEmitToolResult
  -> Context
  -> ... -> string (29.3 KiB, the skills block)
```

Of the 215 copies of the skills block, **208** are held on this path, **6** are internalized strings (reachable from `(Internalized strings)` under GC roots, therefore permanently live for the process), 1 via a separate array.

Code side:

- `observeToolOutcome` is the per-run closure created in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-loop.ts:196`. It captures `terminalToolPresentation`, `turnTaintState` and `postCompactionGuard`.
- The strings are produced per attempt by `buildAttemptSystemPrompt()` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.ts`, which rebuilds `baseSystemPrompt` and `skillsPrompt` for every model attempt.
- `sessionPromptStates` (`openclaw.embeddedSessionPromptStates`, `MAX_SESSION_PROMPT_STATES = 64`) bounds session-level prompt state with an LRU prune. It does not bound the per-run object graph.

### Hypothesis

After a run completes, the observer closure (or whatever retains it - here a module-global `WeakMap` whose keys are still alive) keeps the run `Context`, and therefore the attempt prompt strings, reachable. GC keeps them; old space ratchets up ~15-25 MiB/h until the 2144 MB cap aborts the process.

### Expected

After `agent_end`, the completed run tool-outcome observer, prepared attempt and prompt strings should become unreachable, and old space should return to the process baseline (~0.5 GiB) instead of climbing monotonically.

### Question about the in-flight fixes

#184990 (`fix(agents): release completed run state from retained async contexts`), #184898 (`perf(agents): release settled replies and redundant run indexes`) and #185255 (`perf(agents): release settled context engine execution state`) merged Oct 26-27 and are contained in `2026.10.10-beta.4`.

Do they cover the `observeToolOutcome` path described above? If yes, this can be closed as covered and I will wait for the stable cut. If not, this looks like an additional retention site with the same shape.

### How this was measured

- `openclaw gateway stability` and `openclaw gateway call diagnostics.stability` for the 30s memory samples
- `openclaw gateway call diagnostics.heapSnapshot --params '{"reason":"..."}'` for the two snapshots
- `openclaw gateway call diagnostics.heapProfile` (60s, 16 KiB sampling) - not useful here; only ~2 MiB of new allocations land in a 60s window at this growth rate
- streaming parse of the snapshot `nodes` / `edges` arrays with BFS from GC roots for the retainer path

Happy to attach the raw snapshots, but each is ~400 MB; say the word and I will upload trimmed per-type aggregates instead.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

When a tool is outside the agent's tool profile, `session_status` with `capabilities: true` lists it under `messaging profile` and stops there. It does not say which config key sets the profile or which `alsoAllow` list adds the tool back. The agent then guesses, and users widen permissions or switch the whole profile to fix one tool.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile` to `"messaging"`.
2. In a session of that agent, call `session_status` with `capabilities: true`.
3. Read the "Not available in this session" section.

### Expected behavior

The profile line names where the profile is set and the narrowest grant, for example `messaging profile (agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile); to allow one, add it to agents.entries.assistant.tools.alsoAllow: exec, read, ...`. The Gateway's `tools.effective` result already carries both values (`reasons[].source` and `alsoAllowPath`).

### Actual behavior

From a real Gateway on main (`POST /tools/invoke`, `session_status` with `capabilities: true`):

```text
- messaging profile: agents_list, agents_wait, apply_patch, automations, browser, ..., exec, ..., read, ..., write, x_search
```

Deny and allowlist lines already include their path (`Denied by tools.deny`, `Not included in agents.entries.<agent>.tools.allow`). Only the profile line drops it.

### OpenClaw version

main at f3638439b92 (2026-11-17)

### Operating system

macOS and Linux

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

Not applicable (tool output, no model call)

### Impact and severity

Affected: agents on a restricted tool profile (messaging, minimal, coding) and their users. Severity: confusing, and leads to over-broad permission changes. Frequency: every time a needed tool is outside the profile. Consequence: the agent cannot give the one-line fix, so users open all permissions or give up.

### Additional information

Related: #158384 (an agent answered "My available tools are limited to messaging" with no path or fix). #176073 added the capability summary. Control UI Agents > Tools already shows the source path.

### Summary

The official `@openclaw/atlassian` plugin (v1.0.1, the only Atlassian entry on ClawHub) points at `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2` in `openclaw.plugin.json`, `.mcp.json` and `clawhub-mcp.json`. Atlassian's server now marks that endpoint as deprecated: every tool description it returns starts with a notice that the endpoint "will be removed on 2027-03-01", and that manually configured connections should move to `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`. Without an update, the plugin stops working for every install after that date.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install and connect `@openclaw/atlassian` 1.0.1.
2. In an agent session, list the Atlassian MCP tools.
3. Every tool description begins with the deprecation notice.

### Expected behavior

The official plugin targets Atlassian's supported endpoint.

### Notes for the fix

- `https://mcp.atlassian.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v2/mcp` is live and uses the same authorization server, but different scopes (`*:agent-interface` instead of `read:jira-work`, `read:page:confluence` and so on). Because the operator OAuth store is keyed by server name plus URL, existing users will need to sign in again after the switch, which may deserve a release note.
- The notice also tells the model to relay it to the user after the first tool call. Agents therefore surface it in chat, along with advice about ChatGPT's plugin directory, which is confusing for OpenClaw users.

### Version

OpenClaw 2026.11.4, @openclaw/atlassian 1.0.1

### Related

#197763 (a separate bug: plugin OAuth credentials are not passed to native Codex sessions)

## Summary
When a local model with an 8,192-token context window is chosen in setup, setup's inference check (onboarding Test & use, or creating an agent with onboarding) passes, so setup reports the model as working. The first real message then fails with "Context overflow: the system prompt, injected context, or tool definitions exceed the model's context window before chat history."

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start a local OpenAI-compatible server with an 8,192 context, for example `llama-server -m <chat model>.gguf -c 8192 --jinja --port 18299`.
2. Configure it as a model: provider `local`, `baseUrl` `http://127.0.0.1:18299/v1`, `api` `openai-completions`, model `nemo-8k` with `contextWindow: 8192`.
3. Choose it in setup, for example create an agent with onboarding: `openclaw gateway call agents.create --params '{"name":"Ctx Proof","onboarding":true,"model":"local/nemo-8k"}' --json`. It returns `"ok": true` with onboarding `completed`. The onboarding Test & use check passes the same way.
4. Send a first message, for example `openclaw agent exec --model local/nemo-8k "Reply with exactly the word OK."`.

## Expected behavior
When a model is chosen in setup, setup does not accept it if its context window cannot hold a first turn. The error names the effective window and the minimum.

## Actual behavior
Setup passes. The setup check sends a 51 to 54 token prompt with tools disabled. The first real turn needs about 11,800 to 18,500 tokens of system prompt and tool definitions and fails:
`Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (precheck).` (main) / `Context window exceeded: estimated input 18485 leaves only 0 output tokens within the 8192-token context.` (2026.11.5)

## OpenClaw version
2026.11.5 and main 0c19bcdf293

## Operating system
macOS 27.2 (arm64)

## Install method
npm global / source checkout

## Model
local llama.cpp GGUF (12B, 8,192 context)

## Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> local openai-completions (llama-server)

## Logs
```
[context-pressure-diagnostic] admitted provider attempt for local/nemo-8k route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=14129 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=6144
[context-overflow-midturn-precheck] provider=local/nemo-8k pressure=overflow estimatedPromptTokens=11800 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=8192 overflowTokens=3608
```

## Impact and severity
New local-model users: setup succeeds, then every message fails. Older releases (before 2026-04-30) failed with "Model context window too small (8192 tokens). Minimum is 16000."; that guard was removed in #72958 and the setup check never covered the gap.

## Additional information
Guided Ollama and LM Studio auto-selection already skip models under 16,384 (#112028). Manually configured and custom local models do not.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add opt-in OpenTelemetry trace attributes for message origin, starting with the native Slack channel ID, and allow useful identity correlation without enabling prompt or tool-content capture.

### Problem to solve

We operate 5–10 OpenClaw gateways across a variable number of Slack channels. We want a consistent way to observe where our agents operate and how their usage changes over time across those gateways. We use several OpenTelemetry consumers, including Datadog, and would prefer a portable solution based on OpenTelemetry rather than a backend-specific integration. We hope a general pattern would help other teams operating agents across channels, too.

On current `main`, OpenClaw can export the channel integration (for example, `slack`) and agent metadata on relevant spans, but the integration name alone does not identify the originating Slack channel. Current documentation also says that the OpenClaw session UUID is exported as `gen_ai.conversation.id` and `openclaw.session.id` only when `diagnostics.otel.captureContent` is enabled. That same setting enables message and tool-content capture. We need operational correlation without sending prompts, responses, or tool content to our observability backends.

Our deployed version is **2026.9.5**; we are preparing to upgrade to **2026.11.5 or later**. The current behavior and code references below are based on our review of `main`, not a claim that every capability exists in our deployed version.

### Proposed solution

Provide explicit, content-independent opt-ins for origin metadata and session identity on traces. One possible configuration is:

```json5
{
  diagnostics: {
    otel: {
      captureContent: false,
      // Name and interaction with existing behavior are open for maintainer input:
      captureMessageOrigin: true,
    },
  },
}
```

`captureMessageOrigin` is a concrete proposal, not an existing setting. It would enable selected origin identifiers, initially the native Slack channel or conversation ID, without enabling content capture. A separate session identity control would allow the existing session UUID attributes to be exported without content; [PR #171119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171119) is relevant prior work on that control. Names and final configuration shape are open to maintainer guidance.

For example, an opted-in run span might contain these **synthetic** attributes:

```text
span:                       openclaw.run
openclaw.channel:           slack
openclaw.origin.channel.id: C012EXAMPLE
openclaw.agent:             support-agent
gen_ai.conversation.id:     00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
```

The custom attribute name is illustrative. The origin ID should describe the source of the **current turn**, not an immutable property of an OpenClaw session: a shared session can receive turns from different sources. It is distinct from the OpenClaw session UUID in `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

#### Desired behavior

- Origin identifiers are off by default and only exported when explicitly enabled. A channel ID is still identifying metadata and should have a documented privacy policy.
- Operators can enable origin and session identity correlation without enabling content capture. Neither opt-in should itself export raw session keys, prompts, responses, tool inputs, or tool outputs.
- Preserve the documented behavior of existing `captureContent: true` configurations for session IDs, or agree on and document a migration. Enabling existing content capture alone should not silently add the new origin ID.
- Export origin on relevant message-processing and agent-run spans, and document exactly which spans receive it. Child spans do not automatically inherit parent attributes; we would welcome guidance on whether model and tool spans also need explicit attribution.
- Keep session and channel IDs off metric dimensions by default to avoid increasing metric cardinality.
- Attribute Slack channels and DMs correctly, including threaded and queued turns and sessions shared across origins. When origin is unavailable, omit it rather than guessing or reusing an earlier turn's origin.
- Ensure non-Slack and missing-origin paths continue to work without fabricated identifiers.

Slack already supplies `message.channel` as `nativeChannelId` in [inbound message preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/91614b5c377897783779a55ad82f3e6cb594cb2a/extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts#L1239-L1253). Where possible, propagate the correct current-turn source metadata through the diagnostics boundary rather than parsing the session key. We recognize that propagating this data to each span family and protecting it from unintended diagnostic listeners needs design review.

### Alternatives considered

1. **Enable `captureContent`:** this exports session identity on current `main`, but also enables content capture and does not provide the native Slack channel ID.
2. **Parse the session key:** keys can represent shared sessions, DMs, threads, bindings, or enterprise-scoped routes, and may not contain the current origin. The native ID is already available at Slack ingress.
3. **Join traces with another session or Slack metadata store:** this requires another operational data source and a reliable join. It can be a workaround but is less portable than documented OTel span attributes.
4. **Add channel IDs to metrics:** this increases metric cardinality. Trace attributes are a more appropriate default for the requested correlation.

### Impact

**Affected:** Operators using OpenClaw across Slack channels and collecting OTel telemetry, including our deployment of 5–10 gateways across a variable number of channels.

**Frequency:** Whenever we need to attribute agent activity to an originating channel or track usage over time without collecting content.

**Consequence:** The current metadata does not provide a consistent trace-based way to answer where our agents operate. This blocks the usage-observation workflow we want and requires manual correlation or a separate data source.

This feature would support operational visibility, not serve as a complete audit trail: trace sampling, export failures, and retention can make trace data incomplete.

### Evidence/examples

- [OpenClaw session identity documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/91614b5c377897783779a55ad82f3e6cb594cb2a/docs/gateway/opentelemetry/privacy-and-trace-context.md#L63-L85) describes the current `captureContent` coupling and exclusion of session IDs from metrics.
- [PR #193700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193700) was merged and added session UUIDs to run-scoped spans behind content capture.
- [PR #171119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171119) is open and proposes a separate session identity control; its proposed identity semantics differ from the merged behavior. This request also asks for native origin attribution.
- [Issue #179822](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/179822) requests channel and other context on model-call spans; it does not specifically request the native Slack channel ID.
- The [OpenTelemetry GenAI agent span conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md) distinguish available conversation identifiers from opt-in content attributes. The conventions are marked Development; this request does not assume identifier export must be enabled by default.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes. We are willing to contribute a prototype and tests and help manage the discussion. We would appreciate maintainer guidance on the privacy policy, configuration, propagation scope, and where the capability should live before treating a prototype as the final design.

### Additional information

Questions for maintainers:

1. Would an explicit `captureMessageOrigin` opt-in, separate from content capture, be welcome? Should session identity be controlled separately or grouped under a broader identity setting?
2. Should origin IDs initially cover message and run spans only, or also be propagated explicitly to model and tool spans?
3. Is a generic OpenClaw-namespaced attribute preferable to a Slack-specific attribute, and what should its precise semantics be?
4. Would this fit the bundled `diagnostics-otel` plugin and existing diagnostic event contracts, or should it use another plugin or SDK extension point?

issues.body:
### Summary

On gateway start, the SQLite index repair rebuilds `memory_index_chunks_fts` ("Rebuilt stale SQLite FTS indexes"). Afterwards stock SQLite's `PRAGMA quick_check` reports `malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.memory_index_chunks_fts`, although queries return the same rows as before. Each repair also leaves a full copy of the agent database in an `openclaw-index-recovery-*` directory that nothing removes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent with a few hundred MB of transcripts so the memory index is populated.
2. Start the gateway when it decides the index is stale (seen on 2026.11.5-beta.1 repeatedly over three weeks; the log line is "Rebuilt stale SQLite FTS indexes").
3. Stop the gateway and run `sqlite3 <agent>/openclaw-agent.sqlite "PRAGMA quick_check"` with stock SQLite 3.53 or 3.54.
4. List the agent directory for `openclaw-index-recovery-*`.

### Expected behavior

- The rebuilt index passes `quick_check` (or the integrity-check command for the FTS table), or the docs say that the CLI check cannot be used on these files.
- The recovery copy is removed once the rebuild verifies, or a setting limits how many are kept.
- The log says why the index was judged stale.

### Actual behavior

- `quick_check` fails with `malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.memory_index_chunks_fts`. Row counts and a sample of MATCH queries return identical results before and after, so the damage looks structural rather than data loss. Any backup or integrity job that runs `quick_check` on the file fails on it.
- A manual repair does not hold: the next startup rebuilds the index again and the check fails again.
- Each repair leaves an `openclaw-index-recovery-<random>` directory next to the database holding a full copy (300-400 MB here, including transcripts). `backupDoctorSqliteRepair` creates it and there is no cleanup or retention setting that I could find, so they accumulate (two present at once here; the directories are created with private permissions, so nothing else cleans them).

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5-beta.1

### Operating system

macOS (Darwin 27), SQLite 3.53/3.54 CLI

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A client that is not paired yet, for example a CLI or TUI on another machine, gets "device pairing required". The TUI then says to run `openclaw devices approve --latest` and to pass the same `--url` and `--token/--password` flags. Run from that client, the command fails with the same "device pairing required" error. Approval only works from the Gateway host or its Control UI, and the hint does not say so.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Gateway with `gateway.bind: "lan"` and token auth, fresh state.
2. On a second state dir (or another machine), set `gateway.mode: "remote"`, `gateway.remote.url: ws://<gateway-lan-ip>:<port>` and the same token.
3. From the client, run `openclaw tui`. It shows "device approval needed" and the hint above.
4. From the same client, run `openclaw devices approve --latest`.

### Expected behavior

The hint names an approval path that works before this client is paired: the Gateway host CLI or the Gateway's Control UI (Settings -> Devices).

### Actual behavior

Step 4 fails: `device pairing required (requestId: ...)`, exit 1. Running `openclaw devices approve <requestId>` on the Gateway host works, and the client then connects.

### OpenClaw version

main at f3638439b92 (2026.11.4 dev)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (arm64); also reported on a fresh Ubuntu install

### Install method

source checkout

### Model

n/a (connect fails before any model call)

### Provider / routing chain

n/a

### Logs

```
[client] $ openclaw tui
 gateway disconnected: device pairing required (requestId: <id>) | device approval needed: preview latest request
 Run `openclaw devices approve --latest` to preview the pending request, then rerun the printed
 `openclaw devices approve <requestId>` command and reconnect (pass the same --url and
 --token/--password flags if you connected with explicit credentials).

[client] $ openclaw devices approve --latest
gateway connect failed: GatewayClientRequestError: device pairing required (requestId: <id>)
[openclaw] Reason: device pairing required (requestId: <id>)
(exit 1)

[gateway host] $ openclaw devices approve <id>
Approved <deviceId> (<id>)
(exit 0)
```

### Impact and severity

New users on a fresh install, or right after TUI onboarding against a remote Gateway, follow the printed hint and hit the same error, with no pointer to the path that works.

issues.body:
**Summary**

The autonomous skill-workshop background review (`skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: auto`) forks the conversation and reuses the *foreground* session's tool schemas — which include `skills_search`. But the background run executes under a restricted tool allowlist that excludes `skills_search` (only `skill_workshop`, `read`, `ls`, `view_image`, `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_search`, `memory_search`, `memory_get` are allowed). When the review model calls `skills_search`, it is rejected with:

```
skills_search is not available in this background run. Use skill_workshop, read, ls, ... instead; do not retry skills_search.
```

This produces repeated `Code Mode execution failed` log entries for the review (19 observed in a single day on one install), alongside related rejections of the same class (`code mode module access is disabled`, `Invalid arguments for tool`, ENOENT on a missing SKILL.md). The review self-recovers by retrying with the allowed tools, so learning still works — but the failures are noisy, spin wasted model turns, and obscure real errors in the log.

**Expected behavior**

The set of tool schemas the review is *shown* should match the set it is *allowed to execute*. Either exclude `skills_search` (and other foreground-only tools) from the schemas the review reuses, or add them to the background execution allowlist. Ideally the review should be guided to `skill_workshop`/read/ls up front rather than discovering the restriction through a rejected call.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run OpenClaw with `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: auto` (the default).
2. Do substantial work in a session (>= 10 iterations) so a background review queues.
3. Watch `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway` for `Code Mode execution failed … skill-workshop-review` and the `skills_search is not available in this background run` rejection.

**Environment**

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (npm install)
- Node 26.8.2
- Model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
- Linux (Ubuntu 7.0.0-43-generic, x64)

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Plugin-provided MCP servers using OpenClaw-managed OAuth are projected into native Codex thread configuration without a bearer credential: Atlassian reports authorized in Settings, but Codex cannot initialize it or expose its tools. The same saved token successfully initializes the server and reads Jira issues in a direct MCP diagnostic.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On OpenClaw 2026.11.3 with @openclaw/codex 2026.11.3, install/enable @openclaw/atlassian 1.0.1.
2. Connect Atlassian through the OpenClaw UI. Plugin inspection reports `mcpAuth: [{ serverName: "atlassian", state: "authorized" }]`.
3. Leave the connection supplied by the plugin; do not add a separate `cfg.mcp.servers.atlassian` entry.
4. In a Codex-backed chat, ask to discover Jira tools or read an issue. Observe missing tools and native MCP initialize authentication failures.
5. As a diagnostic, inspect the output of `loadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfigCore` for this bundle server, printing only auth-field presence, not credential values. It contains the Atlassian URL but no authentication header or token environment reference.
6. Independently initialize the same MCP endpoint using the existing OpenClaw-saved access token in memory: initialize, tools/list, and read-only Jira calls succeed.

Plugin declaration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "atlassian": {
      "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2",
      "auth": "oauth",
      "type": "http"
    }
  }
}
```

### Expected behavior

The plugin's authorized connection should use OpenClaw's saved OAuth credentials for native Codex tool discovery, just as the existing user-configured MCP bearer projection path does. Direct MCP discovery/read calls demonstrate that the credential and service are usable.

### Actual behavior

- UI/plugin inspection: authorized.
- Saved access token: present, not expired during tests; refresh token present; stored/discovered issuer binding matches; no pending interactive authorization requirement.
- Native Codex: initialize fails with `invalid_token` / `Missing or invalid access token`; server omitted from the callable tool catalog.
- Direct MCP check using that same saved token: initialize HTTP 200; tools/list returns 41 tools; accessible-resource lookup, bounded Jira search, and getJiraIssue all succeed.
- Actual bundle thread config projection: URL present; `http_headers` absent, `bearer_token_env_var` absent, no environment-header token reference.
- Isolated diagnostic applying the existing `resolveMcpBearerBundleConfig` with literal projection before normalization correctly produces an Authorization header. No production config or package edits were made.

A refresh exchange was not forced or tested because the saved access token was valid. No tokens or private Jira content are included in this report.


### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3; @openclaw/codex 2026.11.3; @openclaw/atlassian 1.0.1

### Operating system

Amazon Linux 2023, Linux aarch64; Node.js v24.18.0

### Install method

npm global OpenClaw; managed Codex and Atlassian plugins

### Model

gpt-6.1-sol, native Codex harness

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> @openclaw/codex native app-server -> plugin-provided Atlassian remote MCP

### Additional provider/model setup details

Operator-owned OAuth connection supplied by the plugin. No explicit `cfg.mcp.servers.atlassian` override and no `oauth.authProfileId` on the plugin declaration.

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized native runtime observations during the same diagnostic window:


MCP server startup failed server_name="atlassian"
handshaking with MCP server failed ... Auth required, when send initialize request
error="invalid_token", error_description="Missing or invalid access token"
omitting MCP server without an exact ready client server_name=atlassian


Secret-free projection output:


{
  "actualBundleThreadProjection": {
    "present": true,
    "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2",
    "httpHeaderNames": [],
    "bearerTokenEnvConfigured": false
  },
  "diagnostics": []
}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Observed in installed distribution code:

- `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.ts` / `loadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfigCore`: prepares bundle data directories, then directly calls `buildCodexMcpServersConfig(preparedDataDirs.config, configuredGrants)` without resolving OpenClaw-managed OAuth bearer credentials.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.ts` / `buildCodexUserMcpServersThreadConfigPatchForRuntime`: does call `resolveMcpBearerBundleConfig`, but selects explicit user-configured servers. The plugin-only Atlassian server is not in that input.
- The Codex run-attempt and thread-lifecycle code load the bundle configuration and user-server projection through these separate paths.

This local code inspection plus the actual projection output supports a missing bearer-resolution step on the bundle path. Current upstream main was not executed or independently reproduced.


### Impact and severity

Blocks Jira tool discovery and use through the native Codex plugin integration in the tested setup despite successful UI authorization. Direct authenticated MCP reads work. No tickets, settings, installed packages, credentials, or services were modified during diagnosis.

### Additional information

Related issues checked before filing:

- #98447 was closed as fixed by #96120, which added plain MCP-native OAuth bearer resolution to the **user-configured** server path. In the installed version, that resolver exists and works in isolation; this report concerns the separate **plugin/bundle** projection path that does not call it.
- #142333 concerns an issuer mismatch discarding credentials on another runtime path. Here the issuer binding matches and the same saved token succeeds directly.
- #194825 concerns merging same-name bundle and explicit configured servers; this reproduction has no explicit same-name user server.

Suggested repair area: reuse the existing OAuth bearer resolver for native plugin/bundle projection with appropriate local/remote transport restrictions, redaction, unavailable-server handling, and token-rotation lifecycle. Verify with plugin-only OAuth discovery plus a native Codex read-only tool call, not only a direct HTTP probe. No last-known-good version has been established.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw's injected configuration-routing instruction leaves a working, owner-authorized native Codex agent unable to repair local configuration when the mandatory `openclaw` setup helper fails on its separate inference provider.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed in a real Discord/Codex session on November 17, 2026:

1. Run the caller on native Codex with working OpenAI subscription authentication, `tools.exec.mode: "full"`, and native `danger-full-access` / approval policy `never`. Expose the `openclaw` helper. These native permissions are not a claim of an explicit OpenClaw session Full Access grant.
2. Request a specific local configuration repair. In this incident, the operator requested `tools.openclaw.autoApproveChanges = true` after unexpected per-change setup approvals. That setting and the per-agent override were unset; ordinary execution remained full.
3. Invoke the setup helper. Its effective route reports xAI/Grok billing exhaustion, then an unavailable auth profile, while the parent Codex conversation and local diagnostic commands continue working.
4. The operator explicitly asks the working agent to perform the repair with exec or a file patch instead.
5. Observe repeated refusal based on the injected instruction to route this Gateway's configuration writes through `openclaw`; the setting remains unset.

This is an observed production sequence, not a clean-install fixture. We did not induce the billing failure. Why setup could not select another usable inference route is not established by this report. No direct fallback write was attempted.

### Expected behavior

An owner-authorized configuration repair should have a supported recovery path that does not require the unavailable helper's LLM to work first.

The existing [configuration CLI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5fb231527f4f14d83bc27067879370debe4d2b7a/docs/cli/config.md#L10-L26) already documents non-interactive validated writes routed through the running Gateway's configuration owner. The [control prompt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5fb231527f4f14d83bc27067879370debe4d2b7a/src/agents/system-prompt-control.ts#L53-L54) also permits explicitly authorized non-disruptive repairs under normal execution policy. The missing contract is how the agent can use a supported repair path when the configuration-specific helper is unavailable.

Requested acceptance criterion: distinguish helper/provider failure from an actual authorization denial, and let the operator authorize the exact repair through a working, validated local path. Keep required approvals enforceable without requiring the failed helper's inference just to reach them. This is a requested recovery contract, not a claim that such an agent fallback is already documented or previously tested.

### Actual behavior

The helper failed; the healthy caller then treated its configuration-routing instruction as prohibiting exec/patch fallback, even after repeated explicit operator requests. It could inspect the file and explain the exact repair but would only give the operator a CLI command to run manually. Readback still showed the target setting unset.

The local configuration was syntactically valid. This was an inability to make the requested operational repair, not a parser failure, Linux filesystem denial, or total loss of all administrative access.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.4, installed Git HEAD `5fb231527f4f14d83bc27067879370debe4d2b7a`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux x86_64; Node v26.13.1.

### Install method

Git source checkout; Gateway managed by a systemd user service.

### Model

Working caller: `openai/gpt-6-astra`, native Codex 0.164.0. Failing helper route reported: `xai/grok-4.7`.

### Provider / routing chain

Discord -> OpenClaw -> native Codex / OpenAI subscription for the caller. Its `openclaw` tool delegates to the separate setup/system-agent flow; the failing tool results identify xAI/Grok. Intermediate helper candidate selection was not captured.

### Additional provider/model setup details

OpenAI and xAI use separate authentication profiles. No keys, account identifiers, full private configuration, or unrelated conversation content are included. No billing change, model switch, restart, or direct configuration edit was performed to investigate this recovery failure.

### Logs

Selected real tool-result excerpts; account identifier redacted:

```text
The inference request failed or returned no usable reply. Try again; if it persists, check the model runtime logs. Cause: 402 "Grok Build usage balance exhausted"

OpenClaw requires working inference: Auth profile "<redacted>" is temporarily unavailable for xai/grok-4.7.
```

The parent then answered that configuration writes must use the setup helper and that it could not apply an exec/patch fallback. A final read-only check established:

```text
tools.exec.mode: full
tools.openclaw.autoApproveChanges: unset
per-agent tools.openclaw.autoApproveChanges: unset
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- [Injected control guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5fb231527f4f14d83bc27067879370debe4d2b7a/src/agents/system-prompt-control.ts#L24-L35): `For the Gateway hosting this session, config writes, channels, plugins, agents, models/providers: ask` the `openclaw` tool. This is the prompt source of the caller's routing refusal, not a native Codex file-access failure.
- [Helper admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5fb231527f4f14d83bc27067879370debe4d2b7a/src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent.ts#L450-L469) returns `UNAVAILABLE` when helper inference verification fails, before constructing the chat engine.
- The prompt source is byte-identical in inspected upstream main `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110`. The live incident was on the installed build above, not a main-branch runtime replay.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed Discord/native-Codex administration workflow. Severity: blocks the requested agent-performed configuration repair. Multiple helper calls failed in the same incident while the parent continued operating. The only recovery offered was for the operator to perform the change manually or restore helper inference; neither recovery was completed in the observed exchange. No data loss was observed; prevalence outside this installation is unknown.

### Additional information

This report targets the configuration-recovery dead end, not removal of authorization checks or a general entitlement to ignore tool denials.

- #196984 explains why native Default runs now need an independent delegation grant or exact approval. It explains the initial approval prompts, but is not established as the origin of the helper-only prompt rule.
- #151605 / #151648 track configured-model fallback during bound helper admission; #162077 was closed into that work. #136592 was closed based on an earlier fallback implementation. This report does not assert that no fallback code exists or that a particular configured fallback was skipped here. Its requested outcome is a supported authorized repair path when helper inference remains unavailable.
- #198290 concerns helper runtime/context-engine incompatibility, another helper failure trigger, not this billing-triggered incident.

No known-good agent fallback baseline was tested, so this is not labeled a proven regression. No implementation or upstream PR is included.

issues.body:
## Summary

On a host with no supported service manager (Home Assistant OS SSH add-on, Alpine, no systemd), `openclaw uninstall --all --yes --non-interactive` exits rc=1 and **blocks state/workspace cleanup** because it tries to tear down a systemd user service first.

This makes the documented uninstall path unusable on HAOS/similar containers. A missing service manager should be treated as "no service to remove," not as a failed teardown that preserves state.

## Environment

- Home Assistant OS 18.5, SSH add-on container Alpine Linux 3.24.3, aarch64
- OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (`e13cf15`), Node 24.22.3, npm 11.12.1
- No `systemctl`; service manager unavailable
- SSH user `<user>`, home on Docker overlay
- Installer SHA-256 `7e126cc3497b5e3bae2ecb915c0acd3689061c56a8e6f4062124ae5b2fd36b16`

## Steps

1. Install and onboard (with `--no-install-daemon`, since HAOS has no systemd).
2. Run:

   ```bash
   openclaw uninstall --all --yes --non-interactive
   ```

## Expected

- Service teardown is a no-op when no service manager exists.
- State/workspace/config cleanup proceeds, or the command reports exactly which scope is blocked and offers a supported override.

## Actual

```text
Recommended first: openclaw backup create
Gateway service disabled.
Gateway uninstall failed: busctl --user machine Manager.Version: error; Command failed during launch or output capture (ENOENT)
No supported service manager detected. Manage the Gateway through the supervisor or terminal that started it.. Run openclaw gateway status --deep for the service state.
State and workspace cleanup blocked because gateway service teardown failed.
macOS app cleanup is not applicable on this platform.
```

- rc=1.
- `~/.openclaw` and the CLI remain.
- `openclaw gateway status --json` correctly reports `service-manager-unavailable`, so the CLI knows there is no manager, but uninstall still gates state cleanup on teardown.

## Impact

- Users on HAOS, minimal containers, or systemd-less environments cannot use the normal uninstall path.
- Manual `rm -rf ~/.openclaw` + `npm rm -g openclaw` is required.
- The state clean-up gate is reasonable for a running service, but should not apply when no service manager exists.

## Related

- #134000 — closed issue: `uninstall --all` blocks cleanup when the unit is missing
- #190061 — open: CLI refuses commands on Linux hosts without a systemd user bus
- #200692 — HAOS install/platform feature request
- #200693 — HAOS setgid onboarding bug

## Workaround used

```bash
rm -rf ~/.openclaw
npm rm -g openclaw
# remove installer-added PATH lines, then remove ~/.npm-global and temp files
```

issues.body:
### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.11.1 with `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.1, one native child completion that had entered the abandon/retire path could not be retired. The Gateway has logged the same pair of warnings every 15 seconds for more than 36 hours (about 240 pairs per hour, one child thread, more than 8,000 pairs so far):

```text
Native assignment durability could not be updated  {error: "Native submission session lifecycle is no longer current."}
Native completion retirement remains pending       {childThreadId: <id>, error: "Native submission session lifecycle is no longer current."}
```

No `Native subagent completion retries exhausted`, `Failed to deliver Codex native subagent completion` or `Holding native completion with unresolved history owner` lines accompany it. Other children on the same Gateway retire normally. No user-visible effect was observed; the impact is unbounded log growth and a retirement that never settles until the Gateway process restarts.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (a5eb9ec), `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.1
- macOS, global npm install, Codex app-server harness
- Long-running Gateway (no restart during the incident)

### What the installed source shows (2026.11.1)

1. `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-completion-delivery.ts`, `abandon()`: when `dependencies.abandon` throws, it logs "Native completion retirement remains pending" and calls `scheduleRetry(state, child, message, false)`.
2. `scheduleRetry()`: the retry cap is checked only when `chargeAttempt` is true, and an uncharged retry does not advance `completionDeliveryAttempt`. The delay therefore stays at the current index (15 s here) with no cap, backoff or expiry.
3. `run-attempt-resources.ts`: the assignment store writes under an authority captured from the parent session entry at monitor registration (`errorMessage: "Native submission session lifecycle is no longer current."`). Once that check refuses (session id or lifecycle revision changed, or the capture was released), every `consume-native-subagent-assignment` write through that store fails.
4. `native-subagent-parent-registration.ts`: `state.assignmentStore ??= params.assignmentStore` keeps the first store for the parent state, so later registrations do not replace the stale authority.
5. `claim()` validates only the synchronous binding check, which still passes, so the child is neither unregistered nor retired.

The same `abandon()` → `scheduleRetry(..., false)` path is present in v2026.11.5 and on main.

In the logs, 8,126 of 8,137 consecutive intervals are exactly 15 s, which matches an uncharged retry pinned at delay index 1 of `[5s, 15s, 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s]`.

### Expected

Retirement of an undeliverable completion terminates. If the captured parent authority is permanently not current, the monitor should stop retrying (drop the in-memory child and leave the persisted assignment for `codex-native-assignment-repair`, or retire under fresh authority), or at least back off and cap.

### Actual

An infinite 15-second retry that only a Gateway restart ends. The persisted assignment then remains until `openclaw doctor --fix` (or update-time Doctor) runs `codex-native-assignment-repair`.

### Reproduction status

Observed on a long-running Gateway; no controlled reproduction yet. Suggested regression: register a parent, let a native child complete and reach `abandon()`, then change the parent session's lifecycle revision (or release the captured session check) before the retirement write, and assert that the retry terminates.

### Related

- #195436 (same two warnings on 2026.11.1, but transient and with a different error)
- #188422, #166022
- #172837 / #173018 (introduced the retirement path)

issues.body:
## Observed behavior

OpenClaw 2026.9.6 on macOS with Node 24.19.0 logged a successful agent database opening that took 128.846 seconds. Its synchronous integrity and foreign-key checks accounted for 128.816 seconds. The outcome was healthy, canonical index validation took 14 milliseconds, and no indexes were repaired. An earlier measurement put the database file at approximately 2.96 GB.

The delay nearly filled the interval before model transport began, but the database row lacked a request trace. We cannot prove that it caused the whole subsequent request timeout, or identify the worker entrypoint and receipt/proof state at that opening.

## Relevant upstream change

[The merged peer-worker integrity reuse fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155785) addresses repeated checks with peer leases and an absent persisted verification receipt. The relevant receipt-dependent conditions remain in the published version's [reuse predicate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/state/openclaw-quarantine-store.ts#L116), [schema admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/state/openclaw-agent-db-schema.ts#L150), and [receipt publication](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/state/openclaw-agent-db-lease.ts#L311), matching our installed code.

This is a plausible candidate, not a confirmed reproduction of that bug. We have not run the upstream synthetic regression on this host. The package channel lookup on September 29 still returned 2026.9.6 for latest and beta.

Could you identify a supported release or backport containing this change, or the minimum additional diagnostics needed to distinguish this case? We want to preserve the existing integrity and migration safeguards.

## Investigation boundary

A temporary logging-only patch was installed for one passive 15-minute observation. No diagnostic marker appeared. All five original module files were restored and verified; already-loaded logging code could remain until the corresponding worker naturally exits. No additional database check, forced worker start, restart, or repair was performed during that observation.

This report contains no database contents, credentials, local filesystem paths, account identifiers, or case research. No attachments are proposed.
