prs.title: fix: reduce completion churn and preserve first-chat authorization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each isolated title, summary, or side question copied the whole prepared model catalog even though it selected one model. A 500-model catalog meant 100,000 copied model rows for 200 short completions.

## User Impact

Simple completions use less CPU and allocate less memory. Model selection, provider routing, host authorization, credentials, and prompt-cache identity retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

ModelRegistry can now materialize only the normalized selected row from its captured generation while keeping fresh request-local AuthStorage. A different-model lookup, inventory access, or model registration promotes that local registry to its full captured catalog, preserving the already-exposed row. Agent runs, provider-stream preparation, and custom SDK resolvers retain their full mutable stores by default. No registry instances or mutable rows are shared between requests.

The production change adds 62 lines to carry selection through existing owners and preserve mutable SDK contracts. Existing runtime row materialization moves to its sibling module to respect the registry module's line cap. No new cache or configuration is introduced.

## Evidence

The single-row regression fails against the base registry and passes with this change. Focused tests cover alias normalization through agent, worker, and actual isolated completion paths; two overlapping HTTP completions with distinct credentials; mutable registry isolation; and captured catalog generation replacement. All 133 focused consumer tests pass, including isolated authorization/fallback and prompt-prefix stability. `pnpm check:changed` passes on head `9670e9d37e73598560f566ec28066836ff3a8c31`. Another 26 selection/generation/prefix tests pass after integration. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings, including the materializer extraction; separate Codex passes also cleared the mechanical lint corrections and the CI measurement repair.

The committed synthetic workload makes 200 actual isolated completions to a loopback SSE provider with 500 catalog rows, after five warmup requests. A1/A2 load the base registry owner into the same completion pipeline; B uses the candidate owner. Five serial, counterbalanced rounds per arm; timing and GC-inclusive V8 main-isolate allocation sampling use separate processes. Acceptance: identical selections/replies, 200 copied rows, lower allocation/CPU, and no measured latency regression.

Median / p95 per 200 completions (p95 is the maximum of five samples):

| Metric | A1 | A2 | B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Copied model rows, count run | 100,000 | — | 200 |
| Registry CPU ms | 190.57 / 204.21 | 190.07 / 207.56 | 8.55 / 9.09 |
| Registry wall ms | 193.02 / 206.68 | 192.23 / 210.34 | 10.21 / 10.77 |
| Whole loop CPU ms | 2219.61 / 2382.76 | 2138.02 / 2218.33 | 1776.33 / 1972.11 |
| Whole loop wall ms | 1039.81 / 1163.63 | 1015.57 / 1023.30 | 814.60 / 894.31 |
| Sampled allocation MB | 585.35 / 610.06 | 588.64 / 612.80 | 512.70 / 543.52 |
| First five requests wall ms, separate | 2778.58 / 3401.22 | 2779.99 / 3595.40 | 2655.95 / 2922.68 |

Against mean A medians: registry CPU -95.5%, whole-loop CPU -18.5%, allocation -12.7% (~74.3 MB), wall time -20.7%. A/A allocation medians differ 0.6%; process CPU 3.7%. Allocation ranges: A1 584.4–610.1 MB, A2 585.0–612.8 MB, B 499.7–543.5 MB. Host load rose during allocation runs; all samples are retained and profiler-run timings are excluded from the timing results. Independent CPU profiles show inclusive fork time falling from 199.8 to 10.2 ms.

This is a synthetic catalog/isolated-request benchmark, not a full large-state Gateway benchmark. The first-five metric excludes explicit catalog refresh. No production data is used. Responses fingerprint representation is untouched; the prior incremental work is already present in #189796, #193553, and #200715.

Reproduce with Node 26 and the repository dependencies:

```sh
git show 0ca4e7d3db4b83fd82bd74f43844e25605b52b85:src/agents/sessions/model-registry.core.ts > /tmp/model-registry-base.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/isolated-completion-registry-measure.ts --owner /tmp/model-registry-base.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/isolated-completion-registry-measure.ts
```

Repeat serial A1/A2/B five times; run `--allocation` and `--counts` separately. Timing was repeated with the final receiver-bound instrumentation. Allocation/count arms do not enable that instrumentation; their measured runtime inputs are unchanged and their existing proof is reused. The final materializer extraction is outside the measured warm fork path; final-source count proof confirms one copied row per completion.

The first local check exposed two main-parent dead-export regressions, reproduced unchanged on exact parent `0ca4e7d3db4b83fd82bd74f43844e25605b52b85`: `describeSpawnAuth` introduced by #191324, and `ADVANCED_FIELDS` introduced by #200808. They were already fixed on main by #200943 (`abdff0b25697f`) and #200935 (`e592d76967f3e`). This branch incorporates main through the latter commit for that named failing gate. Patch-caused line-cap and lint errors were corrected. No inherited-failure waiver is requested.

PR CI on `9670e9d37e735` exposed one patch-caused test failure: the measurement script introduced a lint suppression not on the production allowlist. The script now binds the actual registry instance and instruments its factory result, removing the suppression entirely. The receiver-independent `fromCapturedSources` factory declares `this: void`, matching the existing static factories. The exact failed guard, core/scripts typechecks, targeted core/scripts lint, and formatting pass locally on `84046ad961f2cb474e55ebc35d36fae0fedacb5f`; the timing rerun asserts all 200 owner calls are observed. No test baseline or suppression allowlist was changed.

## Main CI repairs included in this PR

CI run [44237078089](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44237078089) exposed two main regressions on its exact main parent, `97b03f7428d3711fb4b5653beeac5f0a62ab8afe`. Both are repaired here in separate commits rather than waived as inherited failures.

The participant-custody expectations were stale after #200952 (`e235b2b983b63c4365895fd87cb8fac72cb9658d`). Alice requests these spawns; choosing Bob's execution authority does not transfer ownership away from Alice. The test now expects Alice in both cases. The production ownership rule is unchanged, and autonomous agent ownership remains covered. All 174 spawn-boundary, child-custody, and provenance tests pass.

The runtime reload test intermittently rejected its first chat when background catalog persistence created the initially absent agent database. The native registry publication invalidated retained missing-session facts even though no session row had changed. The session-facts acquisition now accepts the selected absent database's first registration, with matching agent and schema; actual session creation, row/lifecycle changes, unknown publications, and physical replacement keep their existing invalidation. Catalog persistence remains intact, preserving #197784's restart behavior. The small registration setup moves into the existing fact-acquisition owner to keep the preparation module within its line cap.

A local `git bisect run` of the focused real-runtime test, followed by direct qualification of the earlier observed boundary, identifies `2c4413a6abbfeb4ac23cd07b775a105586548af1` (#197510) as the first failing commit for first-chat authorization. Its parent `636454ee16af5d125bfe3c680e66bbcf371efe75` admitted the warmup in three trials; those historical full tests then failed a separate later capability assertion, which is not claimed as a passing suite. The introducing commit fails during first-chat fact acquisition; the current main failure occurs when the retained facts are consumed. #199565 had already repaired other cold-registration orderings. The new deterministic owner regression fails before this repair and proves both empty-store continuity and invalidation on actual session creation.

Repairs are separate commits: custody `b9e54e551ddb5`, first-chat authorization `617f4d97ce36eb18dc099238a365722acc824bad`. On the final source, all 66 session-facts/creation-settlement tests and three complete real Gateway reload trials pass. Codex autoreview with the complete authorization/publication owners is scoped-clean through P0–P2. The repair adds 26 production lines; total production delta is 88 lines, preserving the narrow registry and authorization contracts. No configuration, schema, cache representation, or prompt-prefix identity changes.

`pnpm check:changed --base 97b03f7428d3711fb4b5653beeac5f0a62ab8afe` completed: all typechecks, lint, format, line caps, database guards, import-cycle checks, and remaining guards pass. Its only failure is the unused-export scan: 6 production and 7 full-tree entries, 9 distinct symbols. Running the same export owner on untouched exact parent `97b03f7428d3711fb4b5653beeac5f0a62ab8afe` reproduces both lists identically. These are main regressions, not a passing-check claim:

- #200533 (`703c82d20c5cbff62ba3c53eb35045006c9b1d02`) made `prepareSessionEventDelivery` module-private in use while retaining its export, and introduced unused `DurablePilotCustody`/`DurablePilotInput` exports.
- #198455 (`bd1c54cfde534824d31a4cc3c01ce3a116234549`) introduced the unused `PluginMetricFamily`, `PluginMetricFamilyDeclaration`, `PluginMetricLabels`, and `PluginMetrics` exports.
- #200817 (`14b9fc3c8d9454b89b9ff402ce31e39b75e41dfb`) introduced `formatDays` and made `selectSegmented` module-private in use while retaining its export. Peer #201019 already owns the private cron/session-test helper cleanup; this PR does not duplicate it.

Exact-head CI run [44249719486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44249719486) tests head `617f4d97ce36eb18dc099238a365722acc824bad` in merge `49cc7ff2a26d94630dc5230d2f0d04722c363609`, with main parent `75a31ed2854cd7c3448cb35d4b6b4b9a547ef1cb`. Its build, extension-boundary, and typecheck jobs encounter a newly introduced main regression from #201017 (`62a9ca09124d408b1db45a9148f7048b04338c31`): six plugin types became private while `src/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry.ts` still re-exports them. The same six TS2724/TS2459 errors reproduce on that exact untouched main parent with `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --noEmit -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.templates.json`. The three source files are identical between parent and tested merge. This is a main regression requiring owner repair, not a passing check or a defect introduced by this PR. Final CI accounting and final-head ClawSweeper review remain pending.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native sessions during worker recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retained Codex sessions can lose native conversation continuity when reconnecting or replacing a confirmed lost worker. Worker exits also need useful diagnostics without exporting native stderr, which can contain prompts or credentials.

## User Impact

Retained reconnects require their recorded native state. A confirmed lost-worker replacement can seed a fresh thread from bounded retained conversation history, while preserving the original binding if recovery fails. Worker logs expose bounded exit facts and classifications. A home directory left by interrupted startup does not prevent the session's first native thread from starting.

Depends on #201026 and targets its branch, `galiniliev/main7-codex-worker-credentials`. Both ultimately depend on the unpublished schema/auth prerequisite snapshot at `1f67db94064`; land those prerequisites and the parent before retargeting this PR to `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep placement lineage, native thread binding, history bootstrap, and replacement under their existing owners. The binding's existing-thread requirement decides whether a fresh thread is forbidden; directory existence only checks required retained storage. An uncertain start cannot create another thread on the same duplex. Bounded diagnostics reconstruct only enum/numeric metadata at the remote boundary.

Simplification keeps credential lifetime changes in the parent and excludes the unused resource-readiness type from the source commit. Existing supervision preparation moves with the owning lifecycle code rather than introducing a second recovery owner.

## Evidence

- Worker diagnostics, native-state decoding, thread lifecycle binding/recovery, and attempt diagnostics suites: **127 tests passed**.
- Pinned native app-server integration: **1 test passed**, proving startup with a preexisting home and no thread, exact reconnect, fresh-thread refusal for required retained state, resource readiness, and cleanup custody. The new startup assertion failed on the original code and passes with the fix. Inference uses a local synthetic HTTP response fixture, not a live model account.
- Touched-file formatting, scoped Oxlint, `git diff --check`, and test-line budget passed. The dedicated 55-line allocation covers distinct native startup, continuity, binding recovery, and diagnostic boundaries above the default allowance. Local wrapper times were 106 seconds for the four-suite batch and 35 seconds for native integration, including compiled worker setup; CI timing is not available.
- Independent local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, reviewed the complete staged candidate against parent `e233ef1c1de` with unchanged lifecycle context. It identified the startup retry issue; the fix received a subsequent review with no actionable findings. Review was static and limited to supplied context.
- **Draft:** production writers for the new native-placement/retained-session facts are absent from the two extracted source commits. Their owning integration must supply those facts before this becomes a complete live recovery feature. Full build, supported declaration/typecheck, SDK/owner review, and live Gateway/model/upgrade proof also remain pending. The local declaration guard refuses dependencies symlinked from another checkout; it was not bypassed. No live operator Gateway was changed.

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200990
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200991

## What Problem This Solves

The PostgreSQL qualification covered prepared completion acquisition and auth-profile bookkeeping, but did not exercise the plugin completion entry point or prove that cancellation keeps asynchronous plugin cleanup attached to its parent operation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. No SQLite schema version, DDL, migration, persisted-format, configuration, or production code changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the existing stored-profile failover and pinning cases through `runtime.llm.complete`. Keep the configured-key acquisition/disposal cases. Add one PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL cancellation case using a real loopback provider request and a gated plugin lifecycle disposer; verify that parent drainage waits for cleanup. The eight cases reuse the existing three database-pair fixtures and still reject host-thread PostgreSQL access.

This is the next bounded qualification slice from the maintainer-requested PostgreSQL audit. It does not qualify whole-Gateway shutdown or database-connection closure.

## Evidence

- Independent owner and fixture reviews; corrected the drain assertion to keep disposal gated for one event-loop turn.
- Full local autoreview against base `5e677bad858c331ec7db0a547bebf0b15e4786d4`, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2: scoped-clean. Runtime success was not inferred from review.
- [Initial exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44245784760) executed all eight cases: seven passed; cancellation failed during auth setup before HTTP. The correction declares explicit direct-key auth and omits stored-profile order for configured-key/cancellation fixtures. This also excludes cooldown profiles retained by preceding cases. The corrected head passed all eight completion cases in [PostgreSQL shard 3/4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44247904779/job/134611849357), including cancellation and parent-owned disposal.
- The final auth-fixture correction passed independent review and a second scoped-clean P0–P2 autoreview with the auth planner, selection owner, and shared fixture lifecycle included.
- Initial CI typecheck, lint, changed checks, security, source contracts, and baseline ratchets passed. The broad dependency audit failed on unchanged, unrelated unused exports and a test file; it is not counted as passing.
- Matching pinned formatter and `git diff --check`: passed. Production LOC delta: 0.
- No local test execution: this managed checkout has no qualified dependencies. A queued Blacksmith Testbox allocation was stopped and its cleanup reconciled. Exact-head CI owns runtime proof. The eight-case focused file and shard 3/4 passed; remaining PostgreSQL shards and final ready-PR CI are tracked before landing.

<details>
<summary>Dependency-audit attribution</summary>

[The corrected-head dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44247904779/job/134611849518) repeats the original head's `deadcode production report failed` and `deadcode full-tree report failed` diagnostics. It reports unused exports in gbrain release helpers, message-tool discovery, session-event delivery, subagent wake scope, hook/metric types, cron UI helpers, and existing agent/session test-support modules; the unused file is `test/scripts/pr-cache-deferral.node.mjs`.

The reported files, `config/knip.config.ts`, `config/knip-dynamic-consumers.mjs`, and `scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` are unchanged from frozen main `5e677bad858c331ec7db0a547bebf0b15e4786d4`. The complete PR changes only `src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.postgres.test.ts`, which is absent from both reports. These existing dead-code findings remain a separate repository-maintenance follow-up; no failed audit is described as green.

</details>

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve worker GitHub execution credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker-hosted Codex commands need the original session's admitted GitHub execution identity, including rotating credentials. Worker Goal continuations must retain that dispatch authority when the originating turn ends.

## User Impact

GitHub commands on the dedicated worker receive the selected identity and current credential. Private profiles follow the worker connection's lifetime; renewal requires worker acknowledgment, and teardown revokes the grant. Git's credential helper is scoped to the admitted HTTPS host.

This is the first Codex PR in a two-PR stack, extracted from `5eea78634ab` with the related Goal continuation changes from `23dcc5f19b1`. Its base is `galiniliev/main7-worker-prerequisites` at `1f67db94064`, containing the preceding schema/auth changes. Those prerequisites must land before the stack is retargeted to `main`. Native-session recovery and worker diagnostics belong to the dependent PR.

Next in this stack: #201032.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Gateway execution-grant owner and a private worker gh profile. The app-server transport owns installation acknowledgment, renewal, and revocation; each native command receives the current credential environment. The helper is registered for the exact admitted host instead of every HTTPS remote.

Simplification keeps native-session recovery, history seeding, and lifecycle diagnostics out of this PR. No new durable credential store is introduced.

## Evidence

- Credential/native-command environment suite: **5 tests passed**, covering public GitHub, enterprise hosts, token rotation, and connected execution.
- Git URL credential-helper regressions failed for all three host cases on the original code and pass with exact-host registration.
- Goal continuation and follow-up runner suites: **112 tests passed**.
- Touched-file formatting, scoped Oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, reviewed the complete staged candidate against `1f67db94064` with unchanged credential-owner context. It identified the helper host-scope issue; the fix received a subsequent review with no actionable findings. Review was static and limited to supplied context.
- **Draft:** full build, supported declaration/typecheck, end-to-end Gateway/model proof, and live GitHub execution remain pending. The declaration guard refuses dependencies symlinked from another checkout; it was not bypassed. No live operator Gateway or account settings were changed.

prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid rescanning history when conversations alternate (#183848)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bounded model-context reads rescan session history whenever two conversations alternate on the same SQLite connection.

### Summary

Keep a bounded two-session working set instead of making each conversation displace the other.

## User Impact

User impact: alternating conversations can reuse their prepared navigation without changing the messages, context limits, or stored transcripts. A third session still causes least-recently-used eviction. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root Cause

`session-model-context-pages.ts:readModelContextNavigationPages` previously retained one `NavigationSnapshot` per connection. Reading B replaced A, so returning to A fell through to the canonical `readRows(-1, through)` traversal despite unchanged transcript facts.

The production path is `readSessionTranscriptModelContext -> readModelContextNavigationPages -> readRows`. Each session now retains its own existing generation, anchor, window, pairing, and page-receipt state in the same connection-owned cache.

### Changes

- Retain at most two session snapshots, refresh recency after successful reads, and clear both on native disposal.
- Extend the existing SessionManager retention regression to interleave a second real session.
- Extend the existing native-SQLite measurement command with exact navigation-owner substitution and a source hash.

No receipt cells are pinned, no persistent retention or schema changes, and no new production API or setting is introduced. The production change is 14 added / 7 removed lines; the regression reuses existing helpers without increasing total test lines.

## Evidence

### Current-main integration (November 18, 2026)

Head `d9d4e458440` merges current `main` (`af50b8e6ee1`). The only conflict was with #200793 on the append path in `src/config/sessions/session-model-context-pages.ts`: main's page discovery is kept, and this PR's two LRU refresh lines are re-applied there. On this head, the committed owner measurement against current `main`'s navigation owner (2 sessions × 2,000 turns, 20 alternating reads, identical event bytes and SHA-256 on both sides) measured 138,061 µs → 999 µs CPU per read, and the 36 SessionManager and 18 transcript-context worker tests pass. The sections below keep their original head (`927b7829d8e`).

### Shipped Gateway/model-flow proof

Ran the built Gateway from head `927b7829d8ec6f15cc386831c623ef6ecf0a3331` with isolated state, a temporary plugin, and the repository's loopback OpenAI Responses fixture. Two distinct conversations were created through the Gateway `agent` RPC and awaited to completion. The plugin then invoked the shipped `api.runtime.subagent.runForkedTurn` adapter on anchors returned by `chat.history`, in A/B/A order.

The executed path was Gateway plugin runtime -> `runPluginForkedTurn` -> `readSessionForkTurn` -> `runSessionFork` -> local model HTTP/SSE request. A pass-through observer counted native `StatementSync` navigation-query execution in the history worker; it did not substitute owner code, change query results, mutate the source conversations, or bypass admission, generation, anchor, transaction, or receipt checks.

```text
Fork                              A1    B1    A2
Source conversation                A     B     A
Navigation SQL executions          1     1     0
Expected source in model input   yes   yes   yes
Other source in model input       no    no    no
Model response returned           yes   yes   yes
Response tag suffix                 A     B     A
```

All assertions passed and the proof process exited 0. The fixture's existing response-control contract returned distinct A/B tags, and the Gateway results were checked against them. Both cold navigation queries ran on the same history-worker thread; the returning A fork made no navigation query. The Gateway shut down cleanly afterward. This demonstrates eligible bounded, anchored source reuse through a shipped Gateway/model flow, not reuse across arbitrary new user turns. The provider is an explicit local protocol fixture, not a live commercial model or an end-to-end latency benchmark.

The local-only driver, observer, sanitized JSON, and raw execution logs are retained for this task. No transcript bodies, keys, endpoints, or operator state are included in the trace above.

### Native SQLite owner proof

Independently reproduced on current `main` at `141890196ac`, using macOS arm64, Node 24.20.0, and real SQLite data. Before coding, the expanded real SessionManager regression failed because returning to A decoded 596 discarded-prefix bytes; after the repair it passes.

A separate native-SQLite probe with 30,000 physical rows per session produced:

```text
Read sequence       A    A    A    B    A    B    A
Before rows     30000    0    0 30000 30000 30000 30000
After rows      30000    0    0 30000     0     0     0
```

The after probe also admits C, reuses A without a query, and then rereads the evicted B, confirming bounded LRU behavior rather than unbounded retention.

The committed measurement command exercises the real model-context owner, actual agent database importer, native navigation SQL, and bounded output. Each process uses two sessions, 7,500 four-message turns per session, and 40 measured reads. Timing and sampled allocation were separate, with five baseline/candidate pairs per mode, run in alternating baseline/candidate order.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 40 warm alternating reads, median | 21,732.31 ms | 39.12 ms |
| Same batch, p95 across five samples | 24,212.33 ms | 67.81 ms |
| Thread CPU, median per batch | 21,269.11 ms | 39.15 ms |
| Sampled allocated bytes/read, median | 138,933,462 | 906,141 |
| Event count per measured batch | 5,160 | 5,160 |
| First-session event bytes | 81,036 | 81,036 |

Every run produced the same first-session event SHA-256:
`11e07e696148970f1ee6e9d592bea36e321050f53cb428c96c706cfe7a286f04`.
The baseline owner copy's Git blob matches the original source exactly.

Reproduce either side with a fresh output directory:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-model-context-measure.ts \
  --output .local/context-candidate --mode timing --iterations 40 --sessions 2 --turns 7500
```

For the baseline, extract `src/config/sessions/session-model-context-pages.ts` from `141890196ac` and add `--navigation-owner-file <extracted-file>`. Repeat with `--mode allocation` for sampled allocation. One-minute host load was recorded for every run and ranged from 16.68 to 36.38; these are synthetic owner-boundary measurements, not production latency attribution or a whole-Gateway/live-provider load claim.

### Test

- Three related SessionManager suites: **38 passed**, covering rewrites/appends, prefix accounting, compaction/reset, historical reads, and interleaved-session reuse.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- Core, all core-test shards, and scripts `tsgo`: passed.
- Changed-file typed lint, formatting, dead exports, SQLite ratchets, and the other changed checks: passed.
- Independent Codex reviews through P2 and P3: no actionable findings; native `codex review --uncommitted` also completed without findings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The first hosted run rejected test-line growth. The same regression now uses the existing `readModel` helper and shares its smaller-window options, preserving all assertions without adding an allocation or changing a ceiling. The test-line ratchet passes locally with six lines of slack. Production and measurement code are unchanged by this repair.

Hosted CI run [42499544161](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42499544161) passed on the repaired head `927b7829d8ec6f15cc386831c623ef6ecf0a3331`, including the baseline ratchets, changed tests, production and test types, lint, build artifacts, and all three PostgreSQL conformance lanes.

`check:changed` is **not fully green**: its only failure is the existing changelog-attribution guard, which rejects bot credits in unchanged historical `CHANGELOG/**` files. For example, `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md:27` contains `Thanks @steipete-oai`. Those release-owned files and the checker are unchanged from the base; this PR does not suppress the guard or change credits.

## Risk

Feature-owner acceptance of two-session memory residency is still required and is not claimed here. The first hosted review's shipped Gateway/model trace request is addressed above; the separate native-owner measurements are not presented as whole-Gateway latency measurements.

- **Session state:** output hashes and event counts are unchanged; native generation, transaction, anchor, rewrite, and receipt checks remain in their original path.
- **Memory:** two snapshots intentionally retain more than one. A separate matched full-GC probe measured retained JS heap at 95,067,784 -> 96,742,880 bytes (+1,675,096; +1.76%). Uncollected timing RSS medians were 873,250,816 -> 994,590,720 bytes; allocation-mode RSS medians instead fell from 1,246,380,032 -> 990,216,192 bytes, so RSS is not claimed as a stable retained-cache metric. No lifetime pins are added; existing receipt pruning still invalidates stale tokens. Workloads rotating through more than two sessions can still miss.
- **Availability:** the cache remains connection-local and is cleared on native disposal. No Gateway lifecycle or recovery policy changes.

The two-slot limit is per native connection, not a fixed-byte or process-wide memory cap. Each snapshot retains the existing page metadata and request/pairing state; aggregate residency depends on history shape, read limits, and the number of retained connections. The measured heap delta qualifies the stated fixture only.

## Changelog

Release-note context: avoid repeated full transcript navigation when two sessions alternate on one SQLite reader. No release-owned changelog files were edited, per current contributor policy.

## Notes

AI-assisted: yes. Testing degree: focused runtime, native-store performance, full build, type/lint/format, and independent review. No code was copied from the previously closed proposals.

Closes #183848

prs.title: fix(feishu): let isolated topics process messages concurrently
prs.body:
Related: #72972, #89687, #96315

## What Problem This Solves

Configured Feishu topic sessions currently share a group-wide ordinary-message execution queue. A long run in topic A therefore delays unrelated topic B, even when their conversation contexts are isolated.

This change uses the existing canonical session identity for execution scheduling. Different topics can run concurrently within the configured agent concurrency limit. Messages within one topic remain FIFO. `group_topic_sender` additionally separates senders. Default group/direct-message scheduling and out-of-band control commands retain their existing behavior.

## Design

Durable receipt identity remains the shipped `chat:<chatId>` format. The durable-ingress production module is unchanged against the original PR base. No topic-scoped durable format, new schema, migration, dependency, or configuration option is introduced.

Before debounce buffering, the receiver registers an ordering reservation. It then releases durable intake while retaining the message claim until adoption or abandonment. Execution awaits the existing keyed sequential queue and the complete message handler. Receiving later messages therefore does not start a second ordinary run in the same execution queue.

A message without reliable native `thread_id` creates a group barrier: it waits for earlier reservations and blocks later topic work. Registering every reservation before intake handoff includes the complete durable backlog. Such fallback messages bypass batching. Same-topic debounce batches preserve sender identity.

The existing five-minute execution-queue timeout remains unchanged: a timed-out handler can continue running while later same-key work proceeds. This PR does not promise unlimited-duration mutual exclusion.

## Maintainer decision requested

Please confirm that existing `group_topic` and `group_topic_sender` settings should enable topic-scoped inbound execution scheduling. Prior merged work intentionally retained group-wide ordinary-message FIFO. This proposal changes that boundary only for configured topic isolation, while preserving per-queue FIFO and unidentified-topic barriers. No extra opt-in setting is proposed. Maintainer acceptance remains pending.

## Evidence

### Built-Gateway runtime proof (scheduling repair)

Tested/build-info commit: `0dd05196b1022bd8dcc3c46a91d226514cf3ad50`.

An isolated built Gateway received eight authenticated, encrypted, locally signed Feishu webhook event replays. The run used real Feishu message/thread references, real message metadata lookup, real model calls, and actual Feishu replies. Exact output message IDs from this Gateway's streaming logs were independently fetched; all eight expected reply markers were present.

This is a signed-envelope replay, not naturally delivered WebSocket traffic. The replay uses native `topic_group` envelopes referring to existing ordinary-group threads. It does not claim a newly provisioned native topic group was tested. The model was `magpie/group/gpt-6.1-sol`; `maxConcurrent: 4`; debounce disabled for the distinct backlog messages. Nonzero debounce is covered by integration tests.

The first phase admitted A1, waited for its model start, then admitted same-topic A2 followed by different-topic B. A1 requested a bounded 35-second command. B completed before A1, while A2 started only after A1 completed.

The second phase admitted A1, waited for its model start, then admitted A2, A3, F, B in that order. F's signed envelope omitted native `thread_id`; the real Feishu API hydrated its native session. The observed execution order was A1,A2,A3,F,B.

Sanitized runtime observations, November 8, 2026, America/Los_Angeles:

| Phase / message | Model start | Dispatch complete |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency / A1 | 19:14:24.218 | 19:15:07.719 |
| Concurrency / B | 19:14:24.499 | 19:14:29.237 |
| Concurrency / A2 | 19:15:07.910 | 19:15:11.291 |
| Barrier / A1 | 19:15:11.463 | 19:15:55.783 |
| Barrier / A2 | 19:15:55.938 | 19:16:00.358 |
| Barrier / A3 | 19:16:00.504 | 19:16:04.678 |
| Barrier / F | 19:16:05.373 | 19:16:09.411 |
| Barrier / B | 19:16:09.579 | 19:16:14.559 |

All eight Gateway-created replies matched `PR194688_V6_<phase>_<message>_DONE` on independent readback. The isolated Gateway was stopped and temporary bot/provider credentials were removed afterward. Production receiver configuration and service were not changed for this run.

## Current-head long-backlog runtime proof

Tested build-info head: `426e9db4ead55b4f53653c83173e4c72fabadf13`. This focused run uses the built Gateway, the default five-minute adoption watchdog (300,000ms), real model execution, and real Feishu replies. No watchdog interval was shortened for this observation.

Three same-topic messages A1,A2,A3 and a different-topic B entered an isolated authenticated/encrypted webhook endpoint through locally signed replay. Real existing Feishu message/thread references were checked before replay. No new user input messages were sent for this run. This is signed-envelope replay, not naturally delivered WebSocket traffic.

A1 and A2 each invoked the real exec tool with `sleep 180`, a 240-second command timeout, and waited for the process. B completed while A1 was active. A2 started after A1 completed; A3 started after A2 completed. Debounce was disabled to keep all three messages distinct; global concurrency was four.

Runtime observations, November 8, 2026, America/Los_Angeles:

| Message | Model start | Dispatch complete |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | 21:49:08.904 | 21:52:19.032 |
| B | 21:49:09.716 | 21:49:13.693 |
| A2 | 21:52:19.741 | 21:55:27.586 |
| A3 | 21:55:27.975 | 21:55:32.018 |

A3 waited **379.038 seconds** from authenticated acceptance to model start, exceeding the default 300-second watchdog. A direct read through the candidate queue owner at 2026-11-09T05:54:24.470Z still found A3's durable claim, with **zero retry attempts** and no failed rows.

Exactly four model starts and four completed message dispatches were recorded. Each Gateway-created reply was independently read back by its exact output message ID and matched `PR194688_V8_<message>_DONE`. Final queue: pending 0, claimed 0, failed 0. No claim-to-adoption stall or retry-policy event occurred.

The isolated Gateway was stopped and its temporary credentials removed after verification. Production service/configuration were unchanged. This current-head observation supplements the earlier fallback scheduling proof; it does not claim a newly provisioned native topic group was tested.

## Latest-stable retained-data upgrade

Official npm `openclaw@2026.11.2` was installed as an isolated consumer with its own dependencies. Repository metadata points to the canonical OpenClaw repository. Package integrity:

`sha512-SgBml4WLp8V1DdAYkrTPLzVdA/iYo3iuHCtm4788GjaG83QZdd1VeOTlue0HBJGdn3SbFE06b6uPs+AM5ShMgg==`

The published stable queue owner acknowledged three Feishu writes before stopping with pending rows and retained WAL. The complete stopped state was copied before migration; no raw SQL seeded the queue.

Commit `0dd05196b`'s built `doctor --fix --non-interactive` performed backed-up schema migration from 22 to 39 using isolated state and home paths. The candidate queue and Feishu ingress then recovered IDs `stable-one, stable-two, stable-three` and bodies `one, two, three`, once each in order. Pending: 0; failed: 0.

Every original configuration field retained its value, including global and per-group topic isolation. Doctor added normal `agents/meta/wizard/skills` metadata; configuration byte identity is not claimed. This upgrade check ran on `0dd05196b`; the subsequent heartbeat repair does not change the durable-ingress module or migration code. It exercises durable delivery, not a model turn.

## Deferred-custody repair

Current head: `426e9db4ead55b4f53653c83173e4c72fabadf13`.

The latest review found that early-deferred backlog messages could expire the five-minute adoption watchdog while waiting behind healthy runs. The receiver now sends the existing lifecycle heartbeat at the interval supplied by durable ingress while it owns debounce/barrier/queue waiting.

At the actual sequential execution start, the receiver stops heartbeats for every constituent in a batch. Abort, abandonment, and queue rejection also stop them. The normal execution/adoption watchdog therefore remains effective once the execution slot starts.

A regression uses the actual durable queue with a 300ms adoption watchdog and holds the active run for 900ms. Both topic-only and fallback-barrier cases lost queued claims before this repair. Both now retain the claims and execute the backlog in order. The affected two suites pass 32 tests. The heartbeat repair also passes its full build, source/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks. Build-info records the current head. The earlier scheduling observations remain attributed to 0dd05196b. The separate current-head long-backlog observation above now covers the heartbeat repair through the real five-minute watchdog interval.

## Validation and review repairs

- 53 tests pass across durable ingress, receive-handler ingress, and topic durable integration. The unchanged canonical-key suite adds 13 passing tests. Coverage includes topic concurrency, same-topic FIFO, missing-thread/root fallback, nonzero debounce, different senders, defaults/overrides, controls, abandonment, rejection, and timeout behavior.
- The backlog regression failed on the prior implementation with A1,A2,F,B,A3. It now passes with A1,A2,A3,F,B. Without F, B starts while A1 is held.
- Package/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The scheduling candidate `0dd05196b` passed a full build in 2m 8.6s. Runtime: macOS, Node 26.3.0, repository-pinned wrappers; no Python. Existing dependency/asset warnings remain.
- Independent native review (`group/codex-auto-review`, `xhigh`) found no actionable correctness finding in the simplification. The latest heartbeat repair review also ran both affected suites: 32 tests passed. Typecheck and lint were checked separately by the lead.
- Removed all recovery adapters and branch-format tests for unreleased topic durable lanes, as requested by the latest review. Stable chat-lane recovery coverage remains. The durable-ingress production file now matches the original base exactly.
- Tests add 607 net lines against the original PR base, with an exact dedicated allocation. The previous candidate's hosted baseline job failed only the test-line ratchet: +627 lines matched its +627 allocation, but the tested base already exceeded the ceiling by 59. The local original base has a 14-line excess. Neither failure is represented as green. Current-head CI is reported by GitHub checks.

## Limits

Maintainer approval of the scheduling boundary remains outstanding. Real current-head proof uses signed webhook replay, not a current-head WebSocket run or a newly created native topic group. Existing timeout behavior remains unchanged. No permanent deployment or merge was performed.

prs.title: fix: harden remote Codex hook callbacks against planted links, replays and slow hook starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs Codex in a dedicated app-server, Codex's native hooks call back to the Gateway over HTTPS with a per-turn relay credential. Three gaps weakened that path:

- The credential file keeps the same name for the whole chat session and is absent between turns. The Codex app-server's `fs/writeFile` follows links, so a link planted at that name between turns made the next turn's credential (URL and token) land in a file of the planter's choosing.
- A holder of a live relay credential who also knew the current Codex thread and turn ids could post `pre_tool_use`, `post_tool_use` and `before_agent_finalize` callbacks that the Gateway accepted, could replay identical bodies, and left no log line.
- Codex starts a hook's timeout before it spawns the hook process and treats a hook it kills as non-blocking, so the tool call runs. The hook CLI started its own (shorter) deadline only after its modules loaded, so a slow process start could still run into Codex's timeout instead of returning the relay's refusal.

## User Impact

Operators of dedicated Codex app-servers get a credential delivery that cannot be redirected by a link left in the credential directory, remote tool hook callbacks that are accepted once per tool use, a Gateway log record for every remote callback (refusals as warnings), and a hook that refuses the call when the Gateway does not answer in time even if the hook process was slow to start. Local (loopback) relays are unchanged apart from the deadline.

A hook process that cannot start and reach OpenClaw's code before the Codex timeout still lets the call run; the docs now say so.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Credential delivery:** the app-server filesystem API offers neither no-follow nor exclusive create, and the name must stay stable because warm threads keep their hook commands. Delivery now removes whatever is at that name (`fs/remove` removes a link, never its target) and then writes. A process running as the same user while the turn starts can still race the two requests, but such a process can read the credential directly anyway; the docs already say the directory is not a boundary against same-user code.
- **Remote callbacks:** Codex runs each tool hook once per tool use and the remote hook client never retries, so the remote bridge now requires `tool_use_id` on `pre_tool_use` and `post_tool_use` and accepts each event once per tool use id for the life of the relay registration; a repeat gets 409, which the hook CLI turns into its normal unavailable answer (deny for `PreToolUse`, no-op for `PostToolUse`). `permission_request` and `before_agent_finalize` can legitimately recur and have no per-call id, so they keep the existing checks. Every remote callback writes one log record with relay id, event, tool use id and status: accepted ones to the file log only, refusals as warnings.
- **Hook deadline:** the relay CLI now counts its deadline from process start (`performance.now()` origin). The deadline was already a little under the Codex hook `timeout` it is installed with, and a timed-out `PreToolUse` already returned a deny.

## Evidence

Each new test was run against `main` sources (red) and against this branch (green) on a Linux test VM with Node 24, `--maxWorkers=1`:

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-hook-relay-remote.test.ts`, "replaces a link planted at the stable name instead of writing through it": a fake app-server that writes through links like Codex does. On `main` the credential lands in the linked workspace file; with the fix the workspace file is untouched and the credential is a regular file.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.remote-http.test.ts`, "accepts each remote tool callback once and logs every outcome": on `main` a replayed `pre_tool_use` gets 200 and nothing is logged; with the fix the repeat gets 409 and each callback, including the unknown-relay 403, writes one record.
- `src/cli/native-hook-relay-cli.test.ts`, "counts the deadline from process start and refuses before Codex's hook timeout": on `main` the transport is still open 5 ms after the deadline measured from process start; with the fix it is aborted then and the hook answers deny.

With the fix, the relay suites that consume the changed code also pass (`pnpm test` over 18 files: the core relay, bridge, remote HTTP callback, remote client, hook CLI and CLI process tests, and the Codex extension's relay, remote credential and remote-hook thread lifecycle tests). `pnpm check:changed` typecheck and guards, the formatter on touched files and the docs format check pass on the same VM; the SQLite worker ratchet (`--staged`, no T1 call growth) and type-aware oxlint on the touched files (0 warnings, 0 errors) pass too. A full `pnpm lint` of the branch fails on existing `max-lines` errors in files this PR does not touch.

Two existing cold-process tests now pass a longer `--timeout`, because the relay deadline includes their TypeScript process start.

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-hook-relay-retention.test.ts` treated any `fs/remove` as early disposal of the credential; it now counts only removals after the last write (none while the yielded parent waits, one after the retained child finishes). Its remote case fails with the old assertion and passes with the new one. The relay CLI keeps no test-only parameter: its test helper moves the `performance.now()` origin to the call, or to a simulated process age.

Not verified: a live run against a real Codex app-server; the fix was reproduced against a fake app-server with Codex 0.164's filesystem semantics (writes follow links, removal does not).

prs.title: fix: keep the final answer after a progress message in claude-cli chats
prs.body:
Root cause: src/agents/cli-runner/terminal-reply.ts:66 (on main) clears a non-final source-reply mirror only for result-required turns, so in message-tool-only or optional-completion turns a `final: false` progress send stays the "delivered" source reply and replaces the CLI's later visible final answer.

Related: #187827 (release-line report of the same symptom; this PR fixes current main, it is not the backport)

## What Problem This Solves

In a WebChat (Control UI) chat with a `claude-cli` agent that must reply through the `message` tool (`messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`), the agent can send a progress update with `final: false`, keep working, and then end with a plain-text answer. That answer was dropped: the progress send counted as the turn's reply, so the answer was never saved to the conversation and never went through the normal undelivered-reply recovery. The user was left with the progress line as the answer; the final text only showed through the Claude Code session import.

## User Impact

A turn that sends progress and then answers in plain text now behaves exactly like a turn that answers in plain text without progress: the answer is saved to the conversation, and in `message_tool_only` the existing undelivered-reply recovery runs once so the agent can deliver it. Turns that end in `NO_REPLY`, or that already delivered their answer with a `final: true` send, are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareCliRunTerminalReply` is the one place that decides whether a message-tool send replaces the CLI's terminal text. It now classifies the raw terminal reply first and drops a mirror made only of progress sends (`final: false`) when the run also ended with a visible answer. A progress send still completes a turn that ends empty or silent, and a turn with a `final: true` send still counts as delivered, so nothing is saved twice. This matches how the embedded runner already treats progress sends. No config, schema or delivery policy changes.

Thanks @chaeyn for the fix and the original live proof, and @jorge-monalee for the detailed report in #187827.

## Evidence

- Isolated Gateway from built `dist/`, real Claude Code 2.1.322 as the `claude-cli` runtime against a local Anthropic fixture (no real provider), `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, one WebChat-route `chat.send`. Base `5e677bad858c` (main), candidate `8928c93f55a8` (production tree identical to head `e0015fbec3d9`; later commits are test-only).
  - Progress then plain final, base: canonical transcript has only `PROGRESS-...`; no recovery run; the final exists only in the Claude session import.
  - Progress then plain final, candidate: canonical transcript has `PROGRESS-...`, `FINAL-...`, then the recovery run delivers `FINAL-...` once through `message`.
  - Plain final with no progress (parity), base and candidate: `FINAL-...` saved, then recovery delivers it once. Same as the candidate progress turn.
  - Control, one `final: true` send that is the whole reply: one `CONTROL-...` row on both base and candidate, no recovery, no duplicate.
- Regression: `cli-runner.reliability` case "keeps the final answer after WebChat progress in message_tool_only" fails on main (`expected [ 'Build started.' ] to deeply equal [ Array(2) ]`) and passes with the fix; the full file passes (64 tests).
- Consumer test updated: the #177417 progress-mirror accounting case in `agent-command.restart-recovery.test-harness.ts` now ends with `NO_REPLY`, the progress-only path it protects; with a visible final the progress mirror no longer stands in for the answer. `agent-command.live-model-switch` passes (93 tests).
- Diff vs merge base: production +9/-4 in `terminal-reply.ts`, test +47/-2.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert fully undoes it; no state, config or contract changes. Blast radius: claude-cli (and other CLI-backend) turns that send `final: false` progress through the message tool and then end with visible text; if wrong, such turns could show the final answer twice or miss the progress-only completion.

Live proof capture: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200470#issuecomment-6970550032

prs.title: fix: keep shell snapshot capture from freezing the gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Capturing a shell snapshot before a host command could freeze the entire Gateway for several seconds while btrfs committed a transaction. Exec preparation and a detached upload-cleanup timer also lacked task names in main-thread stall reports.

## User Impact

Shell snapshot capture now creates its temporary directory and output file asynchronously, so those filesystem operations no longer block the Gateway event loop. Remaining preparation or upload-cleanup stalls have structural task names. No configuration, protocol, dependency, or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Production kernel samples showed 6.3-second and 7.9-second main-thread freezes in `D / wait_current_trans / syscall 437` (`openat2`); one overlapped a 13.5-second btrfs commit and had no CPU profile. Subsequent tracing identified `.` followed by `openclaw-shell-snapshot-<uuid>-<rand>` as the main-thread opens. The async fs-safe temp-workspace API synchronously creates its native root and exclusive file, identifying shell snapshot capture as the owner.

Use async `node:fs/promises` at that owner: `mkdtemp` creates a fresh private directory, directory permissions are 0700, and the output opens with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` and 0600 permissions. Capture reads the retained descriptor and closes it before recursive cleanup in `finally`, including failure exits. The existing capture subprocess still writes its output inside that private directory. This removes the fs-safe temp-workspace path without adding a worker or changing fs-safe; the existing trusted temp-root resolver remains responsible for root admission.

Exec preparation runs under `exec:spawn-prepare`; detached upload expiration runs under `terminal-upload:cleanup`, both using the existing stall-attribution owner. No path contents or user data enter either label.

## Evidence

The owner regression failed on the base for both successful capture and shell failure: no async output open was observed (`expected [] to have a length of 1`). It now passes through real shell capture with private-directory permissions, exclusive/no-follow creation, cleanup on failure, and an injected symlink collision that leaves its target untouched. Existing shell behavior, cache, subprocess and broker-deadline suites pass. The Node-specific exec-entrypoint test records a simulated 1,200 ms resumed preparation stall as `exec:spawn-prepare`; the existing upload-expiry test checks its detached callback's task name.

Focused validation passed:

- Shell snapshot, cache, spawn, broker, exec-host-spawn and terminal-upload run: 33 passed, one Bun-only skip; that skipped V8 continuation test subsequently passed on Node. The snapshot environment-worker and exec-host-gateway suites also passed in the initial run.
- Node stall-attribution, stall flight-recorder, exec-host-spawn and fs-safe wrapper run: 163 passed, six platform skips. Remaining fs-safe environment and stall-observer run: 15 passed, one platform skip.
- Core typecheck (`run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`), changed test graphs (`agents-root`, `agents-tools`, `infra`), targeted oxlint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated Codex autoreview of the complete local change against base `42731417524048fccefad9be332dc134173bd6b7`, through P2: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. `pr-simplify` retained the direct owner fix and existing task mechanism; no new machinery.

The first terminal-test attempt exposed an extra timer created by its new monitor fixture; removing unnecessary heartbeat sampling restored the existing one-timer invariant. The initial test typecheck caught an optional `fs.open` argument type in the observation record; it now uses the actual API parameter types. Both checks pass after those test-only corrections. Tests remain bounded: the three new real-filesystem capture cases took 51/9/10 ms in the focused run; the existing broker deadline proof retains its existing six-second wait. No production access or btrfs contention reproduction was performed; Linux-native contention remains production evidence, with broad cross-platform proof delegated to PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Remaining filesystem candidates and follow-ups</summary>

The confirmed snapshot caller runs on a cache miss or refresh (five-minute freshness per shell/cwd/environment key), rather than every command. The detached upload timer runs at the earliest retained expiry, with hourly error retries; it is now attributed, while its shared cleanup lock remains unchanged.

The audit found these other create/mutate paths. Absolute event rates are unavailable, so workload-dependent candidates cannot be ranked by measured frequency:

- `src/infra/terminal-file-upload.ts:114` timer and `:138` cleanup-lock acquisition: confirmed detached main-thread route; task attribution fixed here. Moving the shared lock requires preserving its cross-process recovery semantics.
- `src/plugin-sdk/file-lock.ts:166`: generic fs-safe sidecar acquisition, per lock acquisition; the promise-returning API reaches synchronous native exclusive create when no lock root is supplied.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-profile-lock.ts:16`: per OAuth profile mutation/refresh, via the shared lock owner. No separate detached recurring entry was established in this audit.
- `src/plugins/provider-auth-persistence.ts:255`: one lock per persistence target, via the same owner; entry context depends on the auth flow.
- `src/config/write-lock.ts:197`, `:301`, `:341`: config/source lock acquisition and contention, per config mutation. Reentrancy, stale recovery, borrowed-resource guards, and multiple source locks make this a separate owner-level change.
- `src/media/store.ts:275`, `:549`; `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.ts:164`; `src/storage/filesystem.ts:80`, `:105`: per artifact/media write; native parent creation/admission can be synchronous inside these async methods. An untracked entry was not established.
- `src/infra/package-lifecycle.ts:169`: per lifecycle operation; rooted and unrooted lock paths differ. No recurring untracked entry was established.
- `src/config/source-file-stability.ts:24`, `:38` via `src/infra/fs-observation-snapshot.ts:16`: 50 ms metadata polling while a config file settles, a read-stall candidate rather than a confirmed exclusive-create route. The primary watcher already carries a task scope.

These are follow-ups, not additional identified incident owners. Shared lock behavior was not replaced speculatively.
</details>

prs.title: fix: setup says which tool profile the agent has and what it allows
prs.body:
Closes #201042

## What Problem This Solves

Setup keeps an existing tool profile, or picks `full` when none is set, and never says which one the agent ends up with. A config that still has `tools.profile: "messaging"` finishes setup with chat working and no file, command or web tools, and nothing in the output points at the profile.

## User Impact

User impact: at the end of setup, people see which tool profile the agent has, where it is set, what it allows in plain words, which other kept tool settings change it, and how to add one tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

Setup already decides the profile in `applyLocalSetupWorkspaceConfig`. One helper next to it reads the effective profile from the existing tool policy owner (`resolveEffectiveToolPolicy`, which also gives the config path and the narrowest `alsoAllow` path) and builds one line. The three setup flows that end with output print it: guided and app setup (the `Workspace:` / `Gateway:` summary), the wizard (a note before the finish), and non-interactive setup (before the web search tip, not in `--json`).

An agent-level profile (`agents.entries.<id>.tools.profile`) outranks the `full` that setup writes, so the line names that path. Kept `allow`, `alsoAllow`, `deny` and `byProvider` settings are named, not modeled: "These settings also change which tools the agent gets: tools.deny." Which profile setup writes is unchanged. No new config and no profile picker (#36868 was closed).

Related: #200936 (an agent that hits a missing tool names the setting and the fix). It changes `session_status` output only; no file overlap.

## Evidence

- Real `openclaw onboard --non-interactive` runs on main and on this branch, below.
- New tests: two cases in `setup-apply.test.ts` (guided setup summary for a written `full` and a kept `messaging`) fail on main, pass on this branch, and fail again with the production change reverted (`git apply -R`). Three cases in `onboard-config.test.ts` cover an agent-level profile, a kept `alsoAllow`, and kept `deny`/`byProvider`/agent `allow` settings.
- Touched and consumer suites on the head: setup-apply, onboard-config, wizard setup, non-interactive onboarding (gateway, migration, default agent, legacy fleet), system-agent setup operations, guided onboarding, tool catalog, Gateway tools catalog and templates schema. All passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 4a44f2031e8` (current main): typecheck, lint, format, import cycles and the guards pass. The dead export scan fails on two exports this change does not touch (`describeSpawnAuth` in `subagent-spawn-billing-route.ts`, `ADVANCED_FIELDS` in `ui/src/pages/cron/view-delivery.tsx`).
- Local ClawSweeper review (local range, Claude runner, 4 rounds): the last round on this head is complete, patch correct, no findings, security cleared. Earlier rounds found that the line ignored kept `allow`/`deny`/`byProvider`, that provider entries can widen tools, and that `alsoAllow` was not named. All are fixed here.

### Runtime output

Setup: `pnpm build`, then `node openclaw.mjs onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice skip --skip-health --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-search --workspace <tmp>/workspace` with isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under `/tmp`. No Gateway, no model call. macOS arm64. Temp paths shortened to `<tmp>`.

**Before, on main `7ff0d902b94`**

```text
######## case kept-messaging
== seed config: { "tools": { "profile": "messaging" } }
== exit 0; full setup output (tmp path shortened):
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
Workspace OK: <tmp>/workspace
Sessions OK: <tmp>/state/agents/main/sessions
Updated config: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json
  Backup: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json.bak
Tip: run `openclaw configure --section web` to store your Brave API key for web_search. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web
== saved tools section: {"profile":"messaging"}

######## case fresh
== seed config: none (fresh install)
== exit 0; full setup output (tmp path shortened):
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
Workspace OK: <tmp>/workspace
Sessions OK: <tmp>/state/agents/main/sessions
Updated config: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json
  Backup: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json.bak
Tip: run `openclaw configure --section web` to store your Brave API key for web_search. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web
== saved tools section: {"profile":"full"}
```

Setup keeps `messaging` (and writes `full` on a fresh install) and says nothing about either.

**After, on this branch `38adb441f39`**

```text
######## case kept-messaging
== seed config: { "tools": { "profile": "messaging" } }
== exit 0; full setup output (tmp path shortened):
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
Workspace OK: <tmp>/workspace
Sessions OK: <tmp>/state/agents/main/sessions
Updated config: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json
  Backup: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json.bak
Tool profile: messaging (tools.profile). This profile allows chat, messages and sessions, but not files, commands or the web. To add one tool, list it in agents.entries.main.tools.alsoAllow, or set tools.profile to "full".
Tip: run `openclaw configure --section web` to store your Brave API key for web_search. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web
== saved tools section: {"profile":"messaging"}

######## case fresh
== seed config: none (fresh install)
== exit 0; full setup output (tmp path shortened):
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
Workspace OK: <tmp>/workspace
Sessions OK: <tmp>/state/agents/main/sessions
Updated config: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json
  Backup: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json.bak
Tool profile: full (tools.profile). This profile allows every tool, including files, commands, the web and plugins.
Tip: run `openclaw configure --section web` to store your Brave API key for web_search. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web
== saved tools section: {"profile":"full"}

######## case kept-deny

== exit 0; full setup output (tmp path shortened):
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main

Updated config: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json
  Backup: <tmp>/state/openclaw.json.bak
Tool profile: full (tools.profile). This profile allows every tool, including files, commands, the web and plugins. These settings also change which tools the agent gets: tools.deny.
Tip: run `openclaw configure --section web` to store your Brave API key for web_search. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web

```

The same runs now end with a `Tool profile:` line. The saved config is unchanged. The kept-deny case names `tools.deny` next to `full`.

Not shown: the interactive wizard and a guided setup run (they need a TTY and a verified model). Both print the same helper's line; the guided summary is covered by the `setup-apply.test.ts` cases above.

Maintainer decision: the profile wording is new user-facing copy, English only like the surrounding setup summary lines.

prs.title: fix(browser): report crashed tabs as tab-scoped failures
prs.body:
Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the browser tool reports a crashed tab as a generic 20 s timeout and tells the agent the whole browser is unavailable, even though the browser and its other tabs keep working. `navigate` on a crashed target waits the full request budget, and the tab list gives no hint that the target is dead.

## User Impact

User impact: a crashed tab now fails fast with tab-scoped guidance to open the page in a new tab (or retry once a busy page settles), instead of steering the agent into browser-wide troubleshooting. `snapshot`, `screenshot`, and `navigate` all take that path; `tabs` marks targets observed as crashed in both the JSON payload and the CLI text output, and implicit tab selection prefers a healthy tab. Existing-session and extension-relay drivers keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A crashed renderer leaves its Chrome target listed while every page-level CDP command stalls. Snapshots waited out the full action budget and then attached the browser-wide unavailability hint, and `navigate` timed out the same way. The fix adds one bounded `Page.getFrameTree` liveness probe before snapshot and navigate work, maps Playwright `Target crashed` errors to a 409 with tab-scoped recovery text, and keeps the observed crash on the tab record for listing, the CLI handle list, and implicit selection. A dead renderer and a long-blocked main thread look the same to that probe, so the wording names both and suggests a retry once the page settles. Snapshot media helpers moved to a sibling module to stay under the file line cap.

## Evidence

- Targeted suite: `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/target-crash.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.local-managed.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.selection.crash.test.ts` — 6 files, 93 tests passed.
- Real renderer crash (gated Chromium test, system Chrome): `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_CRASH_E2E=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=... pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.chromium.test.ts` — `Page.crash` then probe rejects with `BrowserTargetCrashedError` inside the bounded probe window.
- Real crash-frame shape on `79e875aabfa`: the same gated test crashes a renderer and asserts the message Playwright itself produces for a screenshot on the dead tab. Measured locally, the first line is `page.screenshot: Target crashed ` (trailing space) followed by a `Call log:` block; the matcher accepts the headline, the typed error is returned, and reverting only `target-crash.ts` makes 2/7 `target-crash.test.ts` cases and 1/23 `client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts` cases fail.
- Shipped Gateway + CLI proof on `4b9f8291e0d` (isolated state dir, local loopback only, no real credentials; headless system Chrome 157; local HTTP fixture; the target was crashed with CDP `Page.crash`, then observed through the normal CLI entry point):
  - `openclaw browser navigate http://127.0.0.1:18080/crashme.html --target-id crashme` — fails fast (~2 s) with `The tab crashed or stopped responding. The browser and other tabs are still available: open the page again in a new tab, or retry this target once the page settles.` instead of waiting out the request budget.
  - `openclaw browser tabs` — `2. crashme [crashed use: crashme tab: t1 label:crashme]`; the healthy tab stays listed unchanged (`1. healthy [use: healthy tab: t2 label:healthy]`).
  - `openclaw browser screenshot crashme` — same tab-scoped crash error before Playwright reports its own `Target crashed` frame; `openclaw browser screenshot healthy` still writes `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/media/browser/<uuid>.png`.
  - Recovery: `openclaw browser open http://127.0.0.1:18080/crashme.html --label recovered` then `openclaw browser snapshot --target-id recovered` returns the page's AX tree (`RootWebArea "crashme"` / `heading "crash target"`).
- Independent live check by @wr-web (`Page.crash` + CLI on Windows) confirmed snapshot/screenshot on `906d205`; their navigate and tab-list findings are wired in `76b7e18520f` and `905b07cae7b`.
- Base behavior reproduced locally: after `Page.crash`, the listed page's WebSocket accepts connections but `Page.getFrameTree`, `Runtime.evaluate`, and `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` never answer; a healthy page answers in milliseconds.
- Ratchet and suite on the merged tree: merged `origin/main` (`e7bbd05236e`) to clear inherited base ratchet drift; `check-test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main --no-merge-base` reports `Test lines OK: 6620445; ceiling: 6620470; slack: 25`; the full browser suite passes under the repo runner (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`), and the single `--expose-gc` artifact seen under a bare `vitest` invocation passes 7/7 through that runner.
- Gap: the live check drives the shipped CLI routes but not a full agent model turn; request-boundary behavior stays covered by the route tests.

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse admitted prepared project snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A worker dispatch repeats repository admission and prepared-content validation that its own preparation already completed. Snapshot capture also needs to verify the selected workspace, toolchain, and runtime cache before that content is reused.

## User Impact

Prepared projects can carry verified initial-snapshot facts through the original admitted dispatch. Fresh eligible starts can reuse that work, while ordinary starts, replay, and code-capable activity return to normal verification. Setup commands can receive approved worker-local initializer values without returning them to the Gateway.

Depends on #201025 and targets its branch, `galiniliev/main7-worker-runtime-startup`. Both ultimately depend on the unpublished schema/auth prerequisite snapshot at `1f67db94064`; land those prerequisites and the parent before retargeting this PR to `main`.

Related older proposals: #193776, #193872, #194279. They remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing project preparation, intent admission, bundle installer, and workspace owners. Initial-snapshot custody travels once through the complete producer/consumer path. Snapshot inspection verifies machine caches as well as workspace manifests, and setup diagnostics export bounded classifications around credential-bearing initialization.

Simplification removes repeated remote admission within an already admitted operation and keeps the snapshot shortcut with its invalidation. The provider provisioning extraction keeps allocation and readiness handoff under the existing lifecycle owner. Unrelated provider configuration documentation, inference-model code moves, and operation-tracking changes from the source commit are excluded.

## Evidence

- Bundle reuse, prepared-workspace ownership, machine-cache, setup-environment, and snapshot-verification suites: **113 tests passed** across three configurations (209 seconds including compiled worker setup).
- Repository admission, provider intent, and lease-validation suites: **66 tests passed**. Repository-access suite: **4 tests passed** after replacing the obsolete post-binding remote-revalidation expectation with one-admission/no-duplicate-check assertions. Source unavailable, caller revoked, and identity replaced cases remain covered.
- Touched-file formatting, scoped Oxlint, `git diff --check`, and test-line budget passed. The dedicated 498-line allocation covers distinct setup credential, snapshot inventory, custody, and reuse boundaries beyond the default allowance. CI timing is not available.
- Independent local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, reviewed the complete staged production change against parent `2433aa99c24`: no actionable findings in supplied context. Subsequent changes were the test-contract correction and allocation records; parent advancement adds only its allocation record. Provider-specific implementation was outside this review.
- **Draft:** provider-specific snapshot/initializer producers, supported build/declaration/typecheck, and real-provider/model/upgrade integration proof remain pending. The local declaration guard refuses dependencies symlinked from another checkout; it was not bypassed. No paid provider resources or live Gateway state were changed.

prs.title: fix: show what keeps sandboxes paused during publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Some local managed sandboxes remain frozen for ten seconds or longer during GitHub publication, while the unpause log attributes nearly all elapsed time to one `operation` bucket. Operators cannot tell which part of publication held the guest frozen.

The supplied incident evidence contains 68 publication pauses, with 18 (26%) lasting at least ten seconds. Six operation durations clustered around ten seconds (9,872–10,299 ms), and others reached 16,867 ms. This is coordinator-provided evidence; no production systems were accessed for this investigation.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish reconciliation, source admission, Git policy preparation, snapshot safety checks, index preparation, staging, admission pruning, verification, and cleanup in pause diagnostics. Filesystem consistency and pause/resume behavior are preserved. This change does not claim to reduce pause duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local publication callback runs under the projection owner's pause. Publication intentionally omits the adapter that allows ordinary reconciliation to resume early; that adapter also carried the only reconciliation phase observer. Pass timing independently of lifecycle control, and expose structural snapshot phases through the same quiescence and diagnostics-timeline observers. Names contain no paths or workspace content.

No fixed ten-second wait was found in this paused path. The feedback-scan deadlines and node-worker availability deadline are outside local snapshot publication. SQLite queue admission can wait up to ten seconds, but wakes when capacity is available and rejects on expiry. The snapshot's Git staging bounds are ten minutes overall and three minutes without output. Per the investigation scope, this PR adds diagnostics only.

The existing Git metadata checks move unchanged into a focused module to keep the transport within its file-size limit; no guards or validation are removed. The regression lives in a focused support file reused by the existing projection suite. No new state, protocol, configuration, dependency, or public compatibility path is introduced.

## Evidence

A regression through the real publication snapshot entry point, with synthetic engine I/O and an injected clock, is red on the base: all 12,500 ms appears as `phaseDurationsMs={"operation":12500}`. With this change, it reports `{"staging":2500,"operation.snapshotStage":10000}` in the unpause log and the same exclusive durations in the diagnostics timeline. It also verifies that the guest stays frozen through both stages, the Git snapshot contains the guest edit, and the guest resumes afterward.

Focused validation: quiescence, projection operation/recovery, Git index, and native publication suites passed (167 tests passed, 2 skipped; 470.01 s runner wall time). The new regression took 744 ms. An initial run was invalidated by the source-integrity guard because source moved while compiled worker artifacts were active; the final source was held unchanged and every previously failing native-publication case passed.

Production core typecheck and targeted Gateway test typecheck passed, along with targeted oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check`. After pr-simplify moved recovery attribution behind the existing recovery guard, the publication regression plus nine recovery/conflict tests passed again (10 passed; 52.32 s runner wall time), and targeted typecheck/lint/format passed. Broad proof is reused for unaffected behavior; CI seconds are pending.

## What Problem This Solves

Inline widgets have no native title or precise feedback action, so users must describe a target in prose or create a separate marked screenshot. Agent-authored preview controls also have to be rebuilt inside each widget.

Related: #136712. This PR targets inline widget cards; #136715 targets Dashboard side-panel comments.

## User Impact

Users can switch local preview states, select or mark rendered widget content, and add an annotation to the existing chat composer without sending it. The widget keeps its live state and the composer keeps typed feedback and attachments.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native header shows the agent-supplied title, one annotation pen, and the existing pin/menu actions. Optional segmented controls use a bounded local-only bridge. Browser and widget capture share their toolbar, tooltip, drawing, compositing, and composer-admission owners; the old floating-action placement is removed. No config, permission, protocol-version, or database change is introduced.

171 checks passed: 142 UI unit cases, 27 wrapper/tool-prefix cases, the Chromium user-flow regression, and the isolated real-Gateway recording flow.
