prs.title: fix(meetings): one slow browser audio pull ends a talk-back call
prs.body:
Fixes #177633

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one slow browser audio pull ends a meeting talk-back call. The browser audio transport closes the realtime bridge on the first failed pull, so a single browser request that misses its 5 s deadline drops the call, even though the page capture is still alive.

## User Impact

User impact: a talk-back (`bidi`) meeting call now survives one stalled audio pull. The participant loses at most a few seconds of audio: the batch the stalled pull was carrying, if the page had already handed it over, and what the page dropped while the pull was stuck. Two failed pulls in a row still end the call, and a capture the page reports as closed still ends it at once. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createBrowserMeetingRealtimeAudioTransport` pulls captured audio from the page about three times a second. Any pull error called `fail()`, which stops capture and closes the bridge.

A failed pull does not mean the capture is gone. The node audio transport (`realtime-node-audio-transport.ts`) already tolerates transient input errors, counting `consecutiveInputErrors` up to 5. The browser transport now uses the same counter and warning, with a limit of 2. Two is a cautious limit, not one the page forces. The page keeps only the newest audio (47 chunks) and closes a capture after 10 s without a pull reaching it. A pull that reaches the page resets that clock even if it then stalls, as in the clearest run below, so the page could survive more than two such failures in a row. Ending the call on the second keeps a capture that is truly gone from leaving the participant talking to silence for long. The count resets after the pull and any audio processing complete without an error, so unusable audio or a failed hand-off to the realtime engine still counts as a failure. Every browser safety and authority check still runs on every pull; nothing is skipped or cached.

## Evidence

### Live run

Live Slack huddle in a lab container: Linux, Chrome 155, OpenClaw built from #177357 (`83d04fa`) with #173898 applied, OpenAI realtime voice. Lab-only stage timing was added inside the browser plugin's `/act` route. IDs are placeholders.

Four talk-back runs failed 5–15 s after the join with `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out`. In each run, successful pulls finished their page work in about 3 ms. The failing pull in the clearest run finished its page work, then waited in the response's URL check until the request was cancelled:

```text
02:07:12.426 guard assert-done
02:07:12.426 fffvt evaluate-start
02:07:12.428 fffvt evaluate-end
02:07:12.681 fffvt guard-exit
02:07:12.682 post json-ok-start      <- resolveTabUrl -> navigation URL check (hostname lookup)
02:07:17.411 post released           <- request cancelled; 4.7 s with no further stage
02:07:17.413 Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out
```

With the SSRF policy active, that check resolves the page hostname on every call. In the same container, 2 of 200 lookups of the Slack hostname took about 5006 ms, exceeding the audio pull's 5 s budget. In another run, the failing pull stalled before its page work started, at a step that run did not split further.

With the hostname pinned in the container's hosts file, a two-way conversation ran for 2 minutes: 371 audio pulls, no failures, and the participant heard the agent answer.

With this change (and #173898) and normal DNS, the same lab ran a two-way conversation for over 12 minutes. Four pulls stalled in the first 30 s; each was retried, participant audio resumed, and the agent kept answering the participant coherently for the rest of the call:

```text
03:07:16.375 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:24.193 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:33.775 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:41.694 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
```

Twelve minutes after the join, `slackhuddles status` still reported `inCall: true`, `audioInputRouted: true`, `providerConnected: true`, `bridgeClosed: false`, and the log had no `capture failed` or session-close entry. Before this change, every normal-DNS run ended at the first such stall. The live run used `8cc7ccc`; later commits only move the counter reset after audio processing and reword its comment; a stalled pull never reaches that point. The participant heard some agent replies cut short. The log shows four `audio output backpressured` warnings, which may explain them; that output path is not touched here and the cut-offs were not matched to log times.

Proof artifice: the live runs were built on #177357's branch and applied #173898's production files by hand (talk-back stops before this point without them) and one diagnostic run pinned the Slack hostname in the container's hosts file; the 12-minute run used normal DNS, a real Slack workspace, a real participant and a real voice model.

### Tests

`realtime-browser-audio-transport.test.ts` adds "keeps the call through one stalled pull and ends it on a second in a row". It fails on `main` (the first rejected pull ends the call) and passes here. "ends the call when pulled audio keeps failing to reach the model" covers unusable audio and a failed hand-off twice in a row. All 35 `src/meeting-bot` test files pass, and `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean.

After merging current `main`, the two tests were rewritten to the test file's new layout; on `main` they fail and with this change all 4 tests in the file pass (5 repeat runs).

After merging current `main` again on 4 Nov (`baaa01091c5`; only the test-line record conflicted), the targeted checks were rerun on an isolated Linux test machine (Node 26): the four realtime meeting test files (browser, node audio transports, engine, shutdown) 51 passed; core test typecheck shards and core typecheck clean; oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files clean.

After merging current `main` on 18 Nov (`3460f617860`, which includes #191059's background audio pulls; only the transport test file conflicted, both sides' tests kept), the transport test file and its neighbours (`chrome-transport`, `realtime-node-audio-transport`) were rerun on an isolated Linux test machine: all 5 transport tests and the 26 neighbour tests pass; `pnpm check:changed` passes except the dead-export scan, which also fails on that `main`. The pull-limit code comment was also reworded and the now unneeded test-line allocation record removed (no code change).

Test lines are net +47 against `main`, within the per-PR allowance (the earlier allocation record is removed): one regression that fails on `main` and one consecutive-failure case, both in the existing transport test file and reusing its harness; no smaller set covers the single retry and the end on a second failure.

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- **Why not change the URL check.** Skipping it for audio pulls, or remembering a tab's approval, could miss a tab that moved to another page or a hostname that started resolving to a private address. Reducing the repeated lookups while keeping those checks is for the browser owners; the timing above is the evidence.
- **Related:** #173896 (audio stopped when the join's requester disconnected) is fixed on `main` by #191059, so talk-back now runs long enough to reach the pull timeouts this change tolerates.

</details>

prs.title: docs(plugins): say where before_model_request messages differ from the payload
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

The `before_model_request` docs say `messages` is the model-facing history with sender metadata, and tell scanners to decide sender trust from that metadata. Two request kinds do not work that way: a compaction summary request packs the older history into one text message, so `messages` has no per-message metadata at all, and a CLI `/btw` side question puts the history into `payload.prompt` as text. A scanner that follows the docs screens nothing on compaction and nothing in a CLI side question. This PR documents both shapes so plugin authors know where the history is and what metadata they get.

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin author writing a `before_model_request` content scanner follows the docs and keys sender trust on `messages` metadata. On a compaction summary request that metadata does not exist, and on a CLI side question the history the model reads is text in `payload.prompt`, so the scanner silently lets outside content through on those two request kinds.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can see, in the hook docs and the type comment, which request kinds carry history as text and what metadata `messages` holds for them. No runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root Cause

`createModelRequestTransformer` passes `structuredClone(context.messages)` as `messages`. For a compaction summary, the context is built by `createSummarizationContext` in `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/summarization-completion.ts` from one string: `<conversation>\n${conversation.text}\n</conversation>...`, where `serializeConversation` turns every user, assistant and tool result entry into text. So `messages` is that single synthetic user message, and nothing in it says which parts came from an outside sender or a tool. For a CLI side question, `btw-runtime.ts` builds the prompt with `buildBtwCliPrompt`, which writes the history as `User:` / `Assistant:` text inside `<conversation_history>`, while `messages` holds the history plus the side question. The docs added with the hook (#193550) describe neither.

Behavior before: a sender-trust scanner that keys on `messages` metadata (as the docs instruct) found zero outside messages in a compaction summary request, so content it had withheld from every earlier turn request reached the summarizer unscreened.

### Exact change

- `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`: one bullet under the event contract saying `messages` does not always map onto `payload`, describing the compaction summary and CLI side question shapes, and what a metadata-based handler can and cannot do with them.
- `src/plugins/hook-model.types.ts`: the same two facts in the type comment.

Docs and comment only. No runtime change.

### Scope boundary

This does not add per-message provenance to compaction requests; that is a separate host change. Embedded side questions and session forks send real provider messages and are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 Gateway on Linux, a local trusted plugin with `allowModelRequest: true` that logs one metadata row per `before_model_request` call (runtime, requestKind, message count, count of messages carrying `provenance` or `__openclaw`). Test sessions only; an embedded session on a hosted model and a `claude-cli` session.

Steps: one embedded turn whose tool output held a test canary, then `sessions.compact` on that session; one CLI turn, then `/btw` through `chat.send`.

Observed rows (trimmed):

```
embedded turn          messages=4 tagged=3   (tool result present, screened and withheld)
embedded compaction    messages=1 tagged=0   (twice; nothing for a scanner to key on)
cli side_question      messages=7 tagged=6   (history with metadata; history text sits in payload.prompt)
```

The compaction summary written to the session then described the canary tool output as visible, although every turn request had withheld it. That is the outcome the new bullet warns about.

### What was not tested

- No docs site build; only the MDX check and formatter on the two files.
- Server-side compaction (`isResponsesCompactRequest`) was not exercised; the new text names only the summary request.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`: passed.
- `oxfmt --check` with the repo config on both files: correct format.
- Pre-commit hooks passed on the commit.
- Each claim in the new text was re-checked against current `main`: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model-request-hook.ts` (`messages: structuredClone(context.messages)`), `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-session-agent.ts` (summary stream wrapped with requestKind `compaction`), `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/summarization-prompts.ts` (`createSummarizationContext` returns one user message), `src/agents/btw-runtime.ts` and `src/agents/btw-prompts.ts` (CLI side question prompt carries the history as text; gate `messages` is the history plus the question).

prs.title: fix: honor Azure Sandbox memory limits and worker sizes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Azure Sandbox worker commands inherit the Gateway's host memory reserve and can be stopped below the Sandbox's own limit. Worker sizing also exposes generic machine classes instead of Azure's native CPU, memory, and disk tiers.

## User Impact

Dedicated Azure Sandbox workers use the provider's outer memory boundary. Operators can select native tiers from XS through 3XL in the machine picker or configure `settings.type`; generic classes keep their existing 2 CPU / 4 GiB mapping. Gateway commands and workers on shared hosts retain host memory protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports `feaa5332d4b` to current main, including the prerequisite launch-descriptor and exec plumbing that the original branch already contained. The provider attests the boundary through authenticated launch authority, and only the deployed worker consumes it; tool arguments and environment variables cannot grant it.

The simplification pass omits the retired reconciliation test-budget record and an unreachable check for a snapshot setting that current main does not support. It also inlines a temporary set at its only use to keep the launch module within its existing line limit. The remaining growth supplies the native-size adapter and authority propagation: production +161/−15 lines, tests/support +200/−4, docs +3/−0.

## Evidence

- Focused worker/provider, supervisor, exec cleanup, and launch-descriptor tests: **157 passed**, with **4 Linux-only tests skipped on macOS**. Both the supervisor memory regression and native-sizing regression failed under their pre-fix behavior and passed with the change.
- Core and plugin production typechecks, targeted lint/format checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- CI artifact build passed, including deployed worker bundles and Plugin SDK declarations/exports.
- Native sizes and generic-class behavior verified against Crabbox v0.83.2's published Azure Sandbox contract. No live Azure allocation was performed; real Linux exec enforcement and live provisioning remain proof gaps.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) covered base `5e677bad858` and the complete local candidate. It reported one staging-only P1: prerequisite plumbing was still unstaged. All reviewed working-tree changes are now staged together; the reviewer found no other P0–P2 defects in the combined candidate. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review is requested after publication.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands and timing</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-sizing.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-profile.test.ts extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts src/process/supervisor/supervisor.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-group-cleanup.real.test.ts src/worker/launch-descriptor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts ciArtifacts
```

The focused test command completed in 94.33 seconds. The existing real-process cleanup suite took 44.76 seconds because it exercises surviving services, cleanup, and a ten-second post-turn response check. Launch-descriptor tests took 3.22 seconds; supervisor tests 0.62 seconds; the two provider/sizing files 9.97 seconds combined; profile tests 3.72 seconds. CI timing is pending.

An initial run was invalidated by the source-artifact guard when an install-generated lockfile change was restored during execution; the passing run used stable source inputs.

prs.title: feat(templates): install local projects through live Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #196193

## What Problem This Solves

Template authors cannot install unpublished local projects while their Gateway is running without downtime or premature ClawHub publication.

## User Impact

Install with `openclaw templates add ./my-template`, or click **+ Import** in the Templates page header to choose a `.tgz` from your computer. Selection opens a review modal with the filename, disclosures, and a **Choose another file** action; installation still requires explicit confirmation. No Gateway restart is needed.

Templates remain Labs-gated. Local paths refer to the **Gateway host**; browser uploads transfer the selected archive. Neither source is published to or scanned by ClawHub. Online `--workspace` overrides are rejected; offline behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both entry points reuse the existing Gateway Add owner, consent, integrity checks, leases, rollback, and runtime activation—rather than bypassing its state lock. Preview/apply are bound to canonical artifact integrity; local/upload sources require current operator-admin authority. No new state store or configuration option.

- Upload limits: **1 MiB compressed / 8 MiB extracted / 4,096 entries**, with unsafe-path/link rejection and temporary cleanup.
- Diagnostics contain correlation ID, source kind, stage, outcome, and duration—not archive bytes, template contents, request data, or caught errors.
- Invalid-project responses include corrective validation guidance.
- Latest repair preserves explicitly empty `--agent-id ""` for validator rejection, uses the canonical source type in handler tests, and fixes real-Gateway CI routing and inventory ordering.

## Evidence

### Main-conflict resolution — `f8842fe40b3c32205fec8cc7945d41be3f5c170e`

Integrated main through `b21829a4c85f` without rewriting the existing PR commits. Three content conflicts were resolved:

- `test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts`: retain both browser-pair-code and Template upload in serial-Gateway expectations.
- `test/vitest/vitest.ui-paths.mjs`: retain both real-Gateway test registrations.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js`: regenerate with `gateway:validators:gen` from the combined schemas, preserving main's catalog-detail contract and this PR's local/upload source validation. A second generation produced no changes.

Main's auto-merged catalog detail, automations naming, and config-activation changes were also checked. Fresh independent review of the conflict resolution and those integration contracts found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

**Post-integration proof:** all **54 affected tests passed** (15 UI E2E inventory/ownership, 30 Gateway Add handlers, 6 Template schema validators, 3 CLI ownership), core typecheck, focused lint/format, and staged diff checks passed. The Chromium real-built-Gateway upload scenario also passed (**1 test**, test body **12.73s**), exercising header picker → modal review → explicit Add → persisted agent config/workspace. Production Gateway/configuration untouched.

The WebKit and upgrade evidence below remains **prior-head evidence**; it was not rerun after this main integration. New-head broad CI remains separate. The existing hosted ClawSweeper review is in progress against `dfcd6f485d74`, not this integration head; no duplicate active request was posted. No PR merge is authorized/requested.

### Header Import UX — `dfcd6f485d748e7b396826e4cfb47be1674198ed`

**WebKit verification passed on 2026-11-10.** Playwright WebKit **27.2** ran the existing `ui/src/e2e/template-upload.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` scenario against an isolated built Gateway and production Control UI assets: **1 test passed**, test body **16.52s**, Vitest duration **42.12s** (excludes build/setup). Runtime logging confirmed `engine=webkit version=27.2`.

The test clicks the header Import button, receives a native filechooser event, selects a real `.tgz`, checks the review dialog and selected filename, explicitly confirms Add, checks the installed-agent message, and verifies persisted agent config/workspace. It also compares the served entry asset hash with the built asset. Screenshots of the header, review controls, and installed state were retained locally and inspected. The review screenshot is scrolled to the manifest/footer, not the full disclosure panel.

**Harness scope:** the shared E2E launcher currently hardcodes Chromium. For this run only, its browser factory was temporarily replaced with `webkit.launch({ headless: true })`, omitting Chromium-only connection/executable/arguments; assertions, fixtures, application code, and Gateway behavior were unchanged. The launcher was restored after the run and the checkout is clean. The wrapper still initializes/logs its unused Chromium pool; the actual scenario browser was independently identified as WebKit above. This is Playwright WebKit proof, not a manual Safari/native-macOS file-dialog test or a permanently added WebKit CI lane.

Focused invocation (with that temporary launcher adaptation):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/template-upload.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
```

Earlier verification of this same header-import change passed the Chromium real-Gateway scenario (1 test), Template review tests (2 tests), UI typecheck, scoped lint/format, and i18n baseline. prs.title: fix(cli): clamp logs --limit/--max-bytes to the Gateway caps on every path
prs.body:
Fixes #201036

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw logs --limit/--max-bytes` behaved differently per delivery path: the Gateway RPC rejects values over 5000 lines / 1,000,000 bytes with `INVALID_REQUEST`, while the journalctl and local-file fallbacks clamp the same values silently. One command could fail hard or succeed quietly depending on which path served it, and the option help named no cap at all.

## User Impact

The same `--limit 6000` invocation either errors (`invalid logs.tail params: at /limit: must be <= 5000`) or silently reads 5000 lines, depending on Gateway availability. Operators cannot tell what cap applies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Clamp once at the CLI entry using the same constants the fallback paths already apply (`JOURNAL_MAX_LIMIT`/`JOURNAL_MAX_BYTES`, equal to the Gateway schema caps), and name the caps in the option help. All three paths now agree for any input.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `21f57343876` (branch `fix/logs-limit-consistent-caps`; squashed single commit, tree identical to the reviewed head).

Before (base, live CLI against a local Gateway): `logs --limit 6000 --token x` → `invalid logs.tail params: at /limit: must be <= 5000` (exit non-zero), while the same value against the local-file fallback clamped silently and exited 0.

After (head tree, built `dist`, `node openclaw.mjs`):

```
== Gateway path (live local Gateway built from this PR's tree) ==
$ openclaw logs --limit 6000 --max-bytes 2000000 --token x --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999
Log file: …\tmp\openclaw\openclaw-2026-11-16.log
2026-11-16T02:39:34.349+08:00 info gateway loading configuration…
2026-11-16T02:39:34.419+08:00 info gateway resolving authentication…
2026-11-16T02:39:34.439+08:00 info gateway starting...
…
                                                    ← oversized values now succeed through the Gateway: the RPC
                                                      accepted the clamped 5000/1000000 and returned log lines

== fallback path (dead loopback port, local-file reader) ==
$ openclaw logs --limit 6000 --max-bytes 2000000
Local Gateway RPC unavailable; reading configured file log instead.
Log file: …\state\tmp\openclaw\openclaw-2026-11-16.log
exit=0                                              ← same input, same outcome as the Gateway path

$ openclaw logs --limit 200 --token x
Local Gateway RPC unavailable; reading configured file log instead.
exit=0                                              ← control value unchanged
```

The same oversized input now yields the same successful result on both delivery paths instead of failing on one and silently clamping on the other. Focused test: `pnpm test src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 18 passed, including `clamps oversized --limit/--max-bytes to the Gateway caps before the RPC` (fails on base: the RPC receives `limit: 6000`).

prs.title: fix(mcp): bound the channel bridge's initial Gateway readiness wait
prs.body:
Fixes #201035

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp serve`'s channel bridge absorbs retryable Gateway connect errors so a briefly unavailable Gateway can still come up, but nothing bounded that wait: with a Gateway that completes the WebSocket upgrade but never answers the challenge, `bridge.start()` stayed pending forever and every MCP `tools/call` blocked with no error until the client's own timeout.

## User Impact

An MCP client pointed at `openclaw mcp serve` while the Gateway is wedged sees `initialize` succeed but every tool call hang indefinitely with no failure message. `close()` still resolves readiness, so shutdown was never blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

Race the readiness wait against a deadline derived from the production timeout owners — the **max** of `resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` and `resolveConnectChallengeTimeoutMs` (honoring `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` and `OPENCLAW_CONNECT_CHALLENGE_TIMEOUT_MS`; the bootstrap's optional preauth field is never populated in production, so the resolvers are called directly) — plus a 30s retry grace, mirroring the stdio MCP client's `startupDeadline`. A late hello after the deadline still resolves the shared readiness promise harmlessly; a slow-but-succeeding connection under an extended budget is never cut short.

## Evidence

Base `940e76922e5`; head `789446ac6d` (branch `fix/mcp-channel-bridge-readiness-deadline`; live captures ran on local commit `0b52faa7d8075` — the deadline semantics are unchanged by the final max() widening, which only raises the budget under extended env overrides).

**Live red/green through the changed path.** Fake Gateway on `ws://127.0.0.1:18995` that completes the real WebSocket 101 upgrade and then never replies to the challenge (the retryable "gateway request timeout for connect" class the WS handshake timeout cannot reach). Same stdio JSON-RPC probe against both trees, each built from its own `dist`:

```
[base 940e769] initialize responded: true (16774ms)
[base 940e769] tools/call responded: false (after 110014ms)     ← 110s, no response, no error
[base 940e769] server: still-running (elapsed 141792ms)          ← hangs forever; stderr shows nothing but warnings

[fixed 0b52faa] initialize responded: true (17244ms)
[fixed 0b52faa] tools/call responded: false (after 110039ms)
[fixed 0b52faa] deadline error on stderr: did not become ready within 60000ms
[fixed 0b52faa] stderr tail: MCP server failed to start: gateway did not become ready within 60000ms.
                Run openclaw gateway status --deep --require-rpc to inspect Gateway health.
```

**Budget-aware behavior through the production resolvers (fake timers over the real bridge startup):**

```
$ pnpm test src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1   → 14 passed
  - retryable error never recovering → rejects at 60s (default budgets + grace)
  - OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 → pending at 90s, rejects at 150s
  - OPENCLAW_CONNECT_CHALLENGE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 → pending at 90s, rejects at 150s
$ pnpm test src/mcp/channel-server.test.ts --maxWorkers=1  → 10 passed
```

Control: against a live local Gateway, `tools/call messages_read` answers with real data (~13s) on the base and is unchanged by this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled job created by a Telegram owner can report that its account is unavailable even when the bot is healthy. A later repair turn can also lose the identity of the owner who authorized the job.

## User Impact

Newly authorized jobs retain their Telegram account context and authenticated requester. An owner can reauthorize an existing job in its original Telegram conversation while keeping its current tool list.

## How It Works

Capture the Telegram principal from authenticated channel ingress and bind it to the current owner authority. Scheduled execution and repair use that captured identity. A missing, mismatched, or revoked grant cannot establish ownership.

## Evidence

The original three-commit fix passed independent source review. [The first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44243492687) found grant and fixture failures and an unused export. Corrective commits kept the internal helper private, passed verified channel/account values through the fixture, preserved native non-owner Discord requester behavior, and added a scoped creation regression.

prs.title: fix: let the next update finish a killed update after the machine restarted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If `openclaw update` is killed and the machine then restarts, the next `openclaw update` refuses and tells you to run `openclaw update repair`. That happens even though the restart ended every process the killed update had started. The refusal exists because the proof the update relied on, a lease row in a temporary file, is gone after a restart.

## User Impact

On Linux and macOS hosts, an update killed by a crash or power loss before a reboot no longer needs a manual repair. The next `openclaw update` settles what the killed update left and continues. Windows, containers, and updates that were killed while running an older version keep today's refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

When an update adopts its run, it now also records the boot it runs in: platform, kernel boot ID, Linux PID namespace, and a digest of the machine identity. That is the existing `captureNamespacedStateLeaseProcessOwner().namespace` value. It is stored as an optional `namespace` key on `origin.driver` and on each `origin.previousDrivers` entry. When the next update finds the lease row gone, it settles the killed run only if all of the following hold:

- the run has no `driver:identity-unavailable` step and no managed handoff;
- every recorded driver has a namespace from this same host, with the same non-null machine identity, on the same platform, from a different boot;
- the platform is Linux or macOS, and on Linux both the recorded driver and this process are in the host's initial PID namespace;
- the run's last write predates the current boot. A cloned machine that shares the host name, machine identity and state directory has its own boot, and its live updater keeps writing.

The installation is still claimed the normal way, the claim must land in the same lease store path, and the drivers are checked again under the claim. Every other #200680/#200866 condition is unchanged, including the recorded-exit check and the store identity comparison on the lease path.

Storage: this is additive JSON in `update_runs.origin_json`. There is no table, column, schema version, or migration change. The maintainer approved this field before implementation, as `docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md` (review checkpoint) asks; it follows the additive driver-metadata precedent in `docs/reference/database-schemas/layout.md` (the `origin.driver` paragraph, now extended).

- The origin and driver schemas are non-strict, so older readers drop the key: `src/infra/update-run-driver-schema.ts:3` (`z.object`) and `src/infra/update-run-schema.ts:225`/`:234` at `v2026.11.5`, and the same on `main`.
- Lease payload schemas are strict (`src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-schema.ts:11` `processIdentitySchema` and `:137` `currentPayloadSchema`, same at `v2026.11.5`). The namespace never reaches them: `recordedUpdateRunDrivers` now returns plain process identities for every lease, recovery, interruption and backup caller, and the managed-handoff helper entry stays plain.
- The public run record uses a closed `driver` (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/update-runs.ts:27`), so `toPublicUpdateRun` strips the key.
- Origin byte budget: with eight maximally escaped drivers, the namespaces would push admission identities and routing out of the 16 KiB origin. The codec now drops namespaces first in that case, so a run without them simply keeps today's repair path.

Update behavior: the installed updater runs first and cannot be patched. On the first update from a published version, the killed run was recorded by old code without a namespace, so nothing changes: it still refuses after a restart until a run recorded by this code is killed. A downgraded or older reader drops the key when parsing, and if it rewrites the run the namespaces are lost, so that run falls back to the refusal. A downgrade never reads the namespace as authority.

Not covered: a reboot in the middle of package publication still refuses through package settlement's own lease-store rule, which this PR does not change. Git-checkout behavior is untouched.

## Evidence

The killed-run process test now starts each restart case from a real child updater killed with SIGKILL. It removes the lease store the way a restart clears the temporary directory, then rewrites the run's recorded driver boot to an earlier one. The current process's namespace and uptime are injected at their readers. The decision code is not mocked. The test also asserts that the killed child recorded its own real boot namespace.

- Red on base `d4195774b99`: both new positive cases (Linux and macOS) refused with "The update lease store no longer holds that update's lease" (`3 failed | 40 passed`; the third failure was a control whose expected refusal I then corrected).
- Green on the fix: both positive cases settle the recovery, roll back the dead run's config change, and proceed.
- Controls that still refuse, each asserting the refusal text, that the update did not proceed, and that the reserved recovery, run status and config bytes are unchanged:
  - the same boot with the lease gone;
  - a run from an older version without a namespace, or with a `null` namespace;
  - a null machine identity, or a different machine identity;
  - a non-initial Linux PID namespace for this process, and for the recorded driver;
  - a managed handoff;
  - a `driver:identity-unavailable` step;
  - one of several drivers without a namespace, or recorded in the current boot;
  - another platform;
  - run activity after this boot began.
- `update-run-abandonment.test.ts`: adoption records the namespace, keeps earlier drivers' namespaces, keeps them out of `recordedUpdateRunDrivers`, and strips them from the public record (checked against the wire schema).
- `update-run-ledger.test.ts`: with eight maximal drivers carrying maximal namespaces, admission identities and routing are kept and the namespaces are dropped.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-killed-run.process.test.ts` on `e4b80179501`: 47 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-run-abandonment.test.ts src/infra/update-run-ledger.test.ts src/infra/update-run-capture-receipts.test.ts src/infra/update-run-ledger.compaction.test.ts`: 73 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`: 24 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:all`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base d4195774b99 --no-merge-base` (all ok, including session-identity and test-lines), `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`
- 17 sibling update, Doctor-maintenance and Gateway update suites (`update-command-migrated`, `update-repair-command`, `update-finalization-lifecycle`, `doctor-update-schema-guard`, `update-status` and others), plus `update-command-install-layout.test.ts`: 437 passed, 1 skipped
- CI on `512cdd5d11e`: all checks pass
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: all lanes ok except the dead-export scan, which reports exports in `src/plugins/plugin-metrics.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-delivery.ts` and `src/sessions/session-controller-model.test-support.ts` that this PR does not touch

</details>

Review: one independent reviewer read the diff without my conclusions. It found no critical or high defects. I applied its findings: the cloned-machine case is now refused by the last-activity check, the claim on the restart path must use the same store path, an unrecognized captured namespace records as unknown instead of failing adoption, the codec comment was corrected, and controls were added. CI then caught that the plain-identity helper pulled zod into Control UI boot bundles; it now lives in the zod-free run record module. CI also showed that `update-command-install-layout.test.ts` built its expected printed run from the stored origin; it now expects the driver without its namespace and asserts that the printed JSON carries none. The `autoreview` helper does not run on this machine, so it was not used.

prs.title: fix: stop expected automation skips from posting did-not-start notices
prs.body:
Root cause: src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts:581 treats every skipped run as "did not start", because src/cron/service/timer-outcome-finalization.ts:153 never forwards the executor's existing `admissionDeferredReason` ("active-hours" or "busy") in the transient CronEventContext, so expected deferrals are written into the owner conversation as failures.

Fixes #194261. Thanks @slatem for the detailed report and @wr-web for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Since 2026.11.5-beta.1, every skipped automation run writes this notice into the job's owner conversation:

> Automation "<name>" did not start: <reason> Check automation history, resolve the cause, then run it again.

That includes scheduled deferrals that need no fixing: a tick outside the job's active hours, or an idle-only run deferred while the agent is busy. For heartbeat-style jobs whose session target is the agent's own main session, the notice lands in the session the next run executes in. The next announced reply repeats it, and the copies multiply every cycle. The reporter saw 163 Slack messages in about 25 minutes, each with up to 26 copies.

## User Impact

Active-hours and busy deferrals no longer post a "did not start" notice, so they no longer feed the next run. Run history still records them as skipped with the same summary, and completion webhooks are unchanged. Other unstarted outcomes keep the notice: preparation or admission errors, and skips without a deferral reason.

## Why This Change Was Made

The executor already classifies these outcomes with `admissionDeferredReason` (timer-execution.ts). Finalization now forwards that fact in the transient CronEventContext, next to `runNotStarted` and `quietTrigger`; it is not projected into the public CronEvent. The notifier skips the conversation notice when the reason is present. No new classifier, wording, setting or stored state.

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`), isolated state, deterministic local Responses provider that records every model request. A heartbeat job (every 1h, session target `session:agent:main:main`, active hours excluding now) is run three times, then its active hours are cleared and it runs once more (the next in-hours run). Control: a second job in the same session with `skipIfScratchEmpty` and an explicitly empty scratch, which skips without a deferral reason.

| | main 5e677bad858c | this PR a0b0a959d097 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 active-hours runs | skipped, "Outside this automation's active hours" | same |
| "did not start" notices in the session | 3 | 0 |
| copies of the notice in the next run's model input | 3 | 0 |
| control: scratch-empty skip notice | written (3 -> 4) | written (0 -> 1) |

Raw output from both runs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194276#issuecomment-6970544767

- `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts`: the existing conversation-outcome table gains active-hours and busy rows that expect no conversation commit while the completion webhook is still sent. Both rows fail on main and pass here (29/29). Test lines net 0.
- Production change: +12 lines across three files, no deletions.
- The contributor's earlier Windows proof (isolated source Gateway, CLI `cron run --wait`) showed the same result: the notice in the main session's transcript tables on main, none with this change.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the old notices; nothing is stored or migrated. Blast radius: owner-conversation notices for skipped cron runs only.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep private test helpers out of export reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The full-repository unused-code check reports private cron helpers and session-test types as exported API. It also reports a cache regression script as unused even though the existing suite launches it directly with Node.

This is a maintainer-requested repair for [main CI run 44244251610](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44244251610/job/134599902609).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The cache regression remains executable, and the cron formatter retains its edge-case coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep module-private helpers and model types private. Exercise day-list formatting through the public cron-sentence formatter, preserving the same empty, disjoint, and ranged-day cases. Register the cache subprocess as an exact full-repository Knip entry beside the existing standalone Node test entry; do not ignore or delete it.

## Evidence

- Normal commit hooks and targeted formatting passed for all five files.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete committed range `5e677bad858c..3508f9b60d30`: no actionable correctness or security findings (confidence 0.96). This was source review, not execution proof.
- Exact-head private native checkout: all four owner suites passed (57 tests): cron sentence/view (31), session controller model (11), and cache lifetime collection (15), including the real Node subprocess entry. macOS / Node 26.13.0; hosted Linux / Node 24 remains separate evidence.
- The canonical UI-pages and core-other test type graphs passed. Targeted type-aware source lint, config lint, and five-file formatting passed. The initial lint selector rejected the config path before execution; checking config separately resolved that setup limitation.
- Required `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` passed: production and full-tree scans both report zero unused files.
- Exact-base production/full export scans failed on the known inventory. Candidate production/full export scans still exit 1, but `formatDays`, `selectSegmented`, `DurablePilotInput`, and `DurablePilotCustody` are absent. Remaining reports concern unchanged GBrain, lifecycle-wake, message-discovery, session-event delivery, plugin types, and agent test-support exports, owned by separate work. This is not a full-Knip-success claim.
- The full-repository baseline failure also contains separately owned findings; this repair is limited to its named helpers and subprocess entry.

prs.body:
Related: #189600, #187952, #177713

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin hook can't tell which paired device sent a turn. The gateway already knows: every `chat.send` from a paired operator device runs with `ApprovalReviewerDeviceId` set from the connection's verified device (`client.connect.device.id`), and exec approvals are bound to it. But neither the agent hook context nor the tool requester context exposes it. What hooks do see, `senderId`, names the kind of client (for example `openclaw-ios`), not the device, so two phones running the same app look identical to a plugin. A plugin that wants to allow or refuse a turn based on which paired device sent it has no field to read.

## User Impact

Plugins get the verified device id for turns a paired device sends:

- agent hooks (`before_agent_run`, `before_prompt_build`, `agent_end`, …): `ctx.requesterDeviceId`
- tool hooks (`before_tool_call`, …): `ctx.requester.deviceId`

Both are optional and read-only. Both are set only from the authenticated connection, never from request params (`chat.send` still rejects unknown properties), and only for user-triggered turns. A device-less client (shared token, no device identity) gets neither field. Nothing changes for plugins that don't read them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The id already exists on the run (`approvalReviewerDeviceId`, threaded into the embedded attempt for approval binding). This change copies it onto the two hook contexts at the points where they're built. It doesn't add a new source or a new trust decision:

- `src/plugins/hook-agent-context.types.ts` / `hook-agent-context.ts`: `requesterDeviceId?` on `PluginHookAgentContext`, set by `buildAgentHookContextIdentityFields` from `approvalReviewerDeviceId` under the same `trigger === "user"` (or unset) rule that already governs `senderId` and `chatId`.
- `src/agents/harness/hook-context.ts`: passes the attempt's `requesterDeviceId` through.
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-context.ts`: the Codex app-server runtime builds its own agent hook context, so it sets `requesterDeviceId` from the attempt's `approvalReviewerDeviceId` too. The shared builder still applies the user-trigger rule.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare-hook-context.ts`: CLI backend turns build their `before_prompt_build` context separately, so it takes `requesterDeviceId` from the shared identity projection (same user-trigger rule). The CLI's other hooks already used that projection.
- `src/plugins/hook-tool-context.types.ts` / `src/agents/harness/host-requester.ts`: `readonly deviceId?` on the tool requester, set from `attempt.approvalReviewerDeviceId`.
- Docs: `docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md` and `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`.
- Tests: `src/plugins/hook-agent-context.test.ts`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.auth-context.test.ts` (the Codex prompt and compaction hooks carry the id on a user turn and drop it on cron), a case in `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` (the CLI prompt-build hook receives it), and new `src/agents/harness/host-requester.test.ts`. `prepare-mcp.test-support.ts`'s grant-transfer case now expects `deviceId` on the tool requester.

**How this relates to #189600.** That PR gives tool factories `toolContext.requesterProfile`, the verified Gateway *profile* (the person) behind an admitted Control UI turn, with a liveness check. This one gives hooks the verified *device* behind any paired device's turn, phones and native apps included, which have no profile and no Control UI session. They answer different questions (which person, which device) at different layers (tool factory, hooks), they touch none of the same files, and either can land first. If maintainers would rather have one requester-identity object, `deviceId` fits next to `requesterProfile` without changing this PR's meaning.

Accepted edge cases:
- Only user-triggered turns carry the id, the same as `senderId`. Cron, heartbeat and other system-triggered runs don't.
- A run a plugin starts with `api.runtime.subagent.run` carries the id only when it's started inside the paired device's gateway-method request. That's when the in-process `agent` dispatch uses the device's connection. A run started from the plugin's own detached context runs as the plugin and carries none, which is correct: no device asked for it.
- The id is the device that sent the turn. It isn't a person; for that, see #189600.

## Evidence

**Real gateway with a real model.** Source build of this PR's head (80af2eefc62). The model was `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, which runs on the Codex app-server runtime. Clients were OpenClaw's own `GatewayClient`, and a probe plugin logged every hook's context. Device ids are cut to 8 characters:

| Case | `before_prompt_build` / `agent_end` | `before_tool_call` (every tool the model called) |
|---|---|---|
| a: paired device `openclaw-ios`/ui sends `chat.send` | `requesterDeviceId c74f633c…`, `senderId openclaw-ios` | `requester.deviceId c74f633c…` |
| c: second paired device, same client id and display name | `requesterDeviceId 03d163ad…` (its own) | `requester.deviceId 03d163ad…` |
| d: device-less `cli` (shared token) | no `requesterDeviceId`, `senderId cli` | no `requester.deviceId`, including on `device_probe_tool` |

This run found a gap in this PR's first head (9449852c725). On the Codex runtime, tool hooks had the id but `before_prompt_build` and `agent_end` didn't, because that runtime builds its own agent hook context. The second commit fixes it. With the first commit's tree restored, the extended Codex test fails (`expected … to match object … requesterDeviceId: 'device-a'`).

The stub-model runs below use the embedded runtime (`openai-completions` provider) and cover the request-param and pairing cases.

Real gateway, source build of this change (6e198d5d6a9, before the rebase) against its parent on main (5fb231527f4), with a probe plugin that logs both hook contexts, OpenClaw's own `GatewayClient` and a local OpenAI-compatible stub model. No provider keys were set, and device ids are cut to 8 characters:

| Case | This head | Base (5fb231527f4) |
|---|---|---|
| Paired device (`openclaw-ios`/ui) sends `chat.send` | `before_agent_run`: `requesterDeviceId bc313985…`; `before_tool_call` (`dispatch_action` and the inner plugin tool): `requester.deviceId bc313985…` | `senderId openclaw-ios` only; no device id anywhere |
| Same device adds `requesterDeviceId` or `approvalReviewerDeviceId` to `chat.send` | `INVALID_REQUEST … unexpected property` (closed schema), no run | same |
| Second device with the same client id and display name | sees its own id (`cc3b699f…`), never the first's | n/a |
| Device-less client (`cli`, shared token) | no `requesterDeviceId`, no `requester.deviceId` | same |

`grep -rl requesterDeviceId dist` finds nothing in the base build.

The same change, backported onto 2026.11.4, was also run with a plugin whose gateway method starts `subagent.run` inside the device's request. The id was on every hook of the run, including hooks that fired after the device's socket had closed, and the run finished normally.

Checks on this PR's head (abe48fb77f8, on main bb45ba99390):
- Tests: 19 test files that touch the requester device or hook contexts (hook-agent-context, host-requester, Codex run-attempt.auth-context, native-hook-relay and dynamic-tools, CLI prepare, tool-authority and reliability, embedded attempt tool context, before-tool-call approval policy, plugin tool context, reply authority and others) pass, except one Codex `dynamic-tools` case ("bounds high-cardinality validation errors") that fails the same way on main bb45ba99390. The new hook-agent-context, Codex and CLI assertions each fail with main's production line.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass.
- oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files, `git diff --check` is clean, and `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes (+49 net test lines, within the 400 allowance).
- The local Codex autoreview (`--mode branch --engine codex --max-priority P2`) found nothing on the first commit.
- On the change before the rebase (6e198d5d6a9), every `lint:tmp:*` script, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety`, `check:test-timeout-race-ratchet` and `config:docs:check`/`config:schema:check` also passed.
- Plugin SDK API diff: additive optional fields only (`PluginHookAgentContext.requesterDeviceId`, `PluginHookToolRequesterContext.deviceId`).

Not run: the full test suite locally (CI covers it), the CLI runner path with a real model, and a real phone app.

prs.title: fix(models): relist provider model lists older than 15 minutes on picker reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A model that a provider launches does not appear in the Gateway model picker until the Gateway restarts, its config or credentials change, the next 6-hourly hosted catalog revision is adopted, or the user presses **Refresh**. Example: OpenAI launched `gpt-6.2-astra` and `gpt-6.2-sol` on 2026-11-17. Typed `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` turns worked on every release, but the picker kept the OpenAI listing saved before the launch.

Cause: #167008 stopped ordinary `models.list` reads from renewing an expired provider listing, because that expiry was the provider's 60-second HTTP response-cache TTL and almost every picker open rebuilt the catalog. Nothing replaced it, so a saved live listing never ages on its own.

## Why This Change Was Made

- A successful live listing now expires at the later of its response-cache deadline and 15 minutes after acquisition (`discoveryDeadline`). The floor keeps short TTLs from renewing on almost every read (#167008). A longer TTL still wins (#168050, ClawRouter's one hour), so the expiry relist, which honors each feed's cache, always reaches the provider instead of re-stamping a cached response as fresh.
- `models.list` calls the catalog owner's existing `refreshExpiredModelCatalog`, which relists only expired providers in the background. The read still returns the published rows at once; open pickers update through the existing catalog publication push.
- The listing still decides which models a signed-in provider shows (#114356). This change only keeps that listing fresh.

Accepted cost: at most one background relist per live-listed provider per 15 minutes (or per its cache TTL, when longer), and only while someone opens a picker. Providers whose listing is not retained in the live response cache (`ttlMs: 0`, self-hosted discovery) keep the previous behavior.

## User Impact

A newly launched provider model appears in the picker within about 15 minutes of the provider listing it, on the first picker open, with no restart, no **Refresh** and no OpenClaw release.

## Evidence

- **Regression (vitest-source):** `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list.freshness.integration.test.ts` keeps the real live response cache (500 ms TTL, no cache clearing). It asserts that the listing ages out on the 15-minute floor rather than the short TTL, and that an ordinary `models.list` read on an aged listing serves saved rows, relists once in the background, then publishes the new model. Fails on merge base `e235b2b983b6` (3/3, deadline equals the cache TTL), passes on this branch (3/3).
- **E2E (fix: `ocx src` source tier; base: `e235b2b983b6` dist-nodts):** two isolated Gateways, each with a fake LiteLLM proxy as its live listing and hosted catalog refresh disabled. At 04:03:46Z each proxy starts listing `fake-2`; an ordinary `gateway call models.list` (no refresh) runs once a minute.

  | Time (UTC) | Fix Gateway picker | Base Gateway picker |
  |---|---|---|
  | 04:03:41 (before) | `fake-1` | `fake-1` |
  | 04:04 to 04:17 | `fake-1` | `fake-1` |
  | 04:18:58 | `fake-1`, `fake-2` | `fake-1` |
  | 04:23:58 | `fake-1`, `fake-2` | `fake-1` |

  Proxy request logs: the fix Gateway listed at 04:02:48 (startup) and once more at 04:17:58, the first read after the listing aged; no other requests. The base Gateway listed once at startup and never again.
- **Affected suites (vitest-source):** freshness, worker recovery, chat-metadata catalog renewal, prepared-runtime sources, native picker failures and configured catalog index: 46 tests across 4 shards pass.
- **Build:** `ocx build --dts` (full) passes on this head. Packaging is left to CI.
- **Local ClawSweeper review** (`gpt-6.1-sol`) on this head: patch is correct, no findings. An earlier revision used a flat 15-minute age; the review found that the expiry relist would reuse a warm response for TTLs longer than 15 minutes, which this head fixes.

People using the Codex harness see stale bundled-version numbers and lack a clear path to use models that need a newer Codex between OpenClaw releases. Installing Codex alone also does not ensure that a session uses the ChatGPT/Codex login.

## User Impact

Users get accurate bundled-version information and a supported upgrade path: install a newer compatible Codex on the Gateway host, expose it on the Gateway's PATH, restart the Gateway, and explicitly select the Codex runtime when using a ChatGPT/Codex login. Existing compatibility checks and account-access requirements still apply.

prs.title: improve(memory): upgrade managed local embeddings to EmbeddingGemma 2
prs.body:
Closes #194634

## What Problem This Solves

Managed local memory needs a supported EmbeddingGemma 2 option without making a routine update invalidate existing users’ working embedding indexes.

## User Impact

- Fresh native managed setup selects text-only EmbeddingGemma 2 Q8_0 and saves its model selection explicitly.
- For existing managed preset/router services, Doctor and setup preserve implicit legacy local-memory selections by recording EmbeddingGemma 300M explicitly. Explicit models, per-agent selections, local fallbacks, disabled selections, and keyword-only configurations keep their intended behavior.
- Existing users opt in by selecting the new model URI, rerunning managed setup, and rebuilding each affected agent using the documented offline maintenance procedure. Model mismatch withholds **all memory search, including keyword results**, until rebuilding; source notes remain intact.
- Doctor upgrades only the exact shipped b10809 runtime path to verified b12110 (llama.cpp v0.9.0). Custom executable paths and service settings remain operator-owned. Model preservation does not depend on that exact runtime path.
- Direct `--model` services must explicitly identify the model they actually load. A newly hand-written preset service is indistinguishable from an existing implicit one, so manual configurations should explicitly select the EG2 URI; native fresh setup records it automatically.

This revision adopts ClawSweeper’s recommendation: **no automatic embedding-space switch for established implicit-model users**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing llama.cpp provider, verified installer, Doctor config writer, and memory index-identity owners remain authoritative. Setup and Doctor share a small plugin-local model-selection helper; no new service, config option, migration ledger, or runtime compatibility reader is introduced.

The model artifact remains revision-, size-, and SHA256-pinned. Legacy model aliases/cache identities remain separate from EG2 despite their identical 768 dimensions. Existing router-section names and authored tuning are retained; operating context remains 2,048 tokens. No multimodal projector or image/audio/video memory capability is added.

## Evidence

- Revised native behavior proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194637#issuecomment-6766507897
- Focused llama.cpp lane: **327 tests / 26 files passed**, 18.74s Vitest, 20.67s command wall time. Initial regression run demonstrated five expected failures for legacy preservation and fresh explicit-model persistence before the fix.
- Doctor declarations/import-closure checks: **10 tests / 2 files passed**, 36.09s Vitest, 38.22s command wall time.
- Focused production and test-closure typechecks, touched-file type-aware lint/format, docs pre-commit lint, whitespace checks, and test-line ratchet passed. Native repository wrappers used their documented Node/oxlint/oxfmt fallbacks when the pinned Bun artifact could not be staged.
- Full build on commit `74d3a26ab1bd77fed16e852b4bdbfd65fc68e6d5` exited 0 in 1m44.6s; existing Control UI size advisories were printed, not treated as a clean UI-budget audit.
- Fresh independent production-code review covered the change against `ae0739da8acc9d2f2d8630533f19688da7e00a15`; actionable findings were corrected, followed by final diff/privacy review. This was independent agent review, not local autoreview or ClawSweeper. Hosted ClawSweeper review is separate from this local review.

The prior [native operational and artifact evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194637#issuecomment-6721711041) remains historical evidence for unchanged runtime/model artifacts, not proof of this revised migration policy. Revised proof uses a genuine private filesystem/PID/network sandbox, rather than environment overrides alone.

## Scope and limitations

Native execution covers Linux x64 CPU with six synthetic notes and verified cached model/runtime artifacts; it is not a general retrieval-quality benchmark, a fresh-download installer test, or all-platform execution proof. Doctor’s synthetic-environment advisories and any unsuccessful fixture setup attempts are disclosed with the proof. Production configuration, installed OpenClaw, and Gateway were not changed for this PR work.

Simplification keeps one model-pinning policy shared by both config writers and moves the existing pure preset-path resolver into the light configuration module. Whole-PR net growth is source +198, tests +200, docs +57, manifest/allocation +4 across 19 files; the exact 200-line test allocation covers independent migration, identity, setup and preserved-media regressions.

## What Problem This Solves

A user with `operator.write` could resume a dashboard chat that an agent had started, ask for a recurring job, and repeatedly get “this turn was not started by the owner.” The scheduler never received the request.

## User Impact

After the parent agent releases the chat, fresh authenticated Control UI requests can use the caller’s existing permission to schedule their own work. No administrator role or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat still records which session spawned it. That record describes how the chat began, not who sent the current message. For cron creation, distinguish a dashboard chat with no live parent controller from an actively supervised child. Keep the direct-input checks and the caller’s tool restrictions. Even an administrator using this exception receives no global cron management or local-operator grant.

## Evidence

Reproduced the denial through `chat.send` with a persisted spawned dashboard session, for both a write-scoped user and an administrator. Both cases failed on unchanged `main` and passed with the fix. The focused WebChat suite passed (17 cases), as did the operator admission and cron transport suites, production and test type checks, and formatting and lint. prs.title: fix: separate agent run time from slow chat-send preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A steer send acknowledged in 51 ms later logged `slow chat send 476459ms stage=steer ... preparation=476386ms`, even though most of that interval was a full agent turn. This sent operators looking for a roughly 476-second preparation stall that had not occurred.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish prepared-reply execution from preparation in slow chat-send logs and diagnostic events. This changes diagnostics only; acknowledgement, admission, dispatch, steering, and behavior-controlling timings remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing dispatch timing scope remains in `preparation` while `reply.run_prepared_reply` runs. The diagnostics owner now switches that scope to `run` for the existing span and back to `dispatch` afterward. Detail spans retain their inclusive durations, and startup/queued diagnostics still stop at their existing boundaries. The logging guide documents the boundary and `chat.send.run` event.

The simplification pass retained the existing owners and removed no execution machinery. The necessary growth is 18 production lines and 66 test lines, covering the reported attribution bug, structured event, and startup/queued cutoff contracts.

## Evidence

The clock-controlled diagnostics regression failed on base `af50b8e6ee1d8`: a 476382 ms prepared reply yielded `preparation=476416ms` and no `run`. With this fix it reports `preparation=14ms`, `run=476382ms`, `dispatch=20ms`, and emits `chat.send.run` with the same duration. Detail-span durations remain intact.

All 49 tests across chat-send diagnostics, startup timing, prestart steering, direct followup, auto-reply dispatch, and dispatcher settlement passed (6 files; 237.00 s command wall time, including cold compiler/setup work). The changed diagnostics file independently passed all 15 tests (63.63 s command wall time, 49.63 s Vitest duration; test bodies 1–29 ms). Exact-head CI run 44244110068 attempt 1 completed with two participant-custody assertion failures; all other jobs passed or were skipped. The failed file reproduced locally (142 passed, 2 failed; 460.73 s). Both failing cases also reproduce with the original production diagnostics restored from base (42.56 s); their owner/authority inputs are unchanged in the CI merge. The native inherited-failure route retains CI as failed and verifies security and review gates independently.

Targeted Gateway-methods typecheck passed in 3.7 s. Targeted Oxlint, formatting for all three files, and `git diff --check` passed. Isolated Codex autoreview of the complete local change against `af50b8e6ee1d8`, through P2, was scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The subsequent pr-simplify pass required no changes.

The supplied production observation was the only production evidence used; no live-server access was needed.

prs.title: fix: warn on small-context manual picks and skip them in automatic setup
prs.body:
Closes #200920 ## What Problem This Solves When you set up a local model with an 8,192-token context window, setup's AI check passes and treats the model as ready. The first real message then fails with "Context overflow: the system prompt, injected context, or tool definitions exceed the model's context window before chat history." The setup check sends a one-line prompt with tools off, so it fits. A real first turn also carries the system prompt and tool definitions, measured at 11.8K to 18.5K tokens. ## User Impact Setup now tells you when the model's effective context window is below 16,384 tokens: - Automatic setup skips such a model and moves to its next candidate. - A model you choose yourself is still accepted, with a warning that names the model, its window, the usual first-turn need and what to raise. The warning shows in onboarding Test & use, in Control UI Model Setup and CLI onboarding (as a note before the model is switched on), in Control UI Add provider (under the success message), and in `openclaw models auth activate` output. Nothing else changes: chat, existing routes, update repair and agent creation keep today's behavior, and utility models (for example Apple's on-device model, minimum 8,192) are not checked. ## Why This Change Was Made The setup check already runs one turn through the real runtime, and the runtime reports the effective context window it used. Setup compares that value with one floor, 16,384, the floor guided Ollama and LM Studio discovery already apply (#112028). That change kept smaller models available through manual selection, so a manual pick warns instead of refusing. A manual pick could instead be checked against the selected route's real first-turn size (system prompt plus tool schemas). That needs the full agent prompt and tool set assembled outside a turn, a much larger change than a warning, and the runtime already reports the exact overflow if a turn does not fit. The warning is the smaller correct change. ## Evidence Control UI, Models > Available models > Test & use on a local llama-server running with an 8,192-token context (real Gateway, real server). Before (base 0c19bcdf293): the model is verified and switched on with no warning. After (54cec6d075c): a `Context window` note appears before the model is switched on. - Real runs on a Mac Studio against a local llama-server (12B GGUF), isolated state and Gateway, same config at base and head: - Control UI Model Setup (`openclaw.setup.activate.start` + `wizard.next`) with the 8,192-window model: the head shows a `Context window` note after the connection test and before the model is switched on; the base goes straight to done. - Direct activation (`openclaw.setup.activate`, the path Add provider and `models auth activate` use): both succeed, and only the head adds the warning line. At 32,768 the head adds no warning. - Automatic setup (`openclaw.setup.auto`) on a fresh install with one llama-server discovered by the llama.cpp provider: at 8,192 the head records the floor message as the candidate's failed attempt and does not activate it; at 32,768 the head activates it; the base activates the 8,192 server. - Agent creation is unchanged. - Not shown live: (1) automatic setup skipping a small model and then activating a viable successor in the same run. Local discovery candidates rank last (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) and the llama.cpp provider discovers one server, so two llama-servers cannot form that ladder, and no other local server type is installed on the test host; the ladder's move to the next candidate is covered by tests. (2) A screenshot of Add provider: its activation runs only for an agent with no usable model, and a provider with a declared small window already counts as one, while a discovered window is unknown and treated as large, so a real small local server never reaches that message; the notice is covered by a UI test and by the direct activation run below, which returns the same warning line. - First real turn with that 8,192 config on the base: `Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (precheck)`, `estimatedPromptTokens=11800 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=8192`. 2026.11.5 fails the same way (`estimated input 18485 ... 8192-token context`). - Tests: automatic activation refuses an 8,192 primary and succeeds at 32,768; a manual 8,192 pick succeeds and warns once (a prompter note when there is a prompter, else an activation line); utility models are not checked; onboarding Test & use shows the warning; Add provider shows the notice under its success message. With the production change reverted (`git apply -R`), the new tests fail. - `pnpm check:changed --base 0c19bcdf293` (merge base with fresh `origin/main`): exit 0. - Local review: native ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner). Two findings after the first hosted review were fixed: the warning reached only the CLI (now also Model Setup and Add provider), and a note after the config commit could report an activated model as failed (the note now comes before the commit). Last round at 54cec6d075c: patch is correct, no findings.
Runtime output Studio, own llama-server (12B GGUF, `-c 8192` or `-c 32768`), saved model `{"id":"nemo","contextWindow":}`, isolated state, own Gateway on loopback. Production code is identical at 5e09b68bdcf and 54cec6d075c (patch vs base sha256 prefix `fec0b0c263b6c111`); the last commit changed one test line. Model Setup: `node openclaw.mjs gateway call openclaw.setup.activate.start --params '{"sessionId":"ctx-proof","kind":"existing-model","modelRef":"local/nemo"}' --json`, then `wizard.next`. ``` ## HEAD, ctx=8192 {"done":false,"status":"running","step":{"type":"progress","message":"Testing your AI connection…"}} {"done":false,"status":"running","step":{"type":"note","title":"Context window","message":"local/nemo has an effective context window of 8192 tokens. A first OpenClaw turn usually needs at least 16384 for the system prompt and tool definitions, so messages may fail with a context overflow. Raise the model's context limit (the server's context size, and contextWindow or contextTokens in its model settings), or choose a larger model."}} {"done":false,"status":"running","step":{"type":"progress","message":"Turning on your AI connection…"}} ## BASE 0c19bcdf293, ctx=8192 {"done":true,"status":"done","step":null,"modelActivation":{"modelRef":"local/nemo"}} ``` Direct activation: `node openclaw.mjs gateway call openclaw.setup.activate --params '{"kind":"existing-model","modelRef":"local/nemo"}' --json` ``` ## HEAD, ctx=8192 {"ok":true,"modelRef":"local/nemo","lines":["Inference verified: local/nemo","local/nemo has an effective context window of 8192 tokens. A first OpenClaw turn usually needs at least 16384 for the system prompt and tool definitions, so messages may fail with a context overflow. Raise the model's context limit (the server's context size, and contextWindow or contextTokens in its model settings), or choose a larger model."]} llama-server: prompt eval time = 117.08 ms / 51 tokens (the setup check turn) ## HEAD, ctx=32768 {"ok":true,"modelRef":"local/nemo","lines":["Inference verified: local/nemo"]} ## BASE 0c19bcdf293, ctx=8192 {"ok":true,"modelRef":"local/nemo","lines":["Inference verified: local/nemo"]} ``` Automatic setup: `node openclaw.mjs gateway call openclaw.setup.auto --params '{}' --json` (no model chosen; llama.cpp provider at the server; no CLI sign-ins on the host path) ``` ## HEAD, -c 8192 {"status":"needs-sign-in","selected":null,"attempts":[{"kind":"provider-auto:llama-cpp-existing-server","label":"Existing llama-server","error":"llama-cpp/nemo has an effective context window of 8192 tokens. A first OpenClaw turn usually needs at least 16384 for the system prompt and tool definitions, so messages may fail with a context overflow. Raise the model's context limit (the server's context size, and contextWindow or contextTokens in its model settings), or choose a larger model."}]} ## HEAD, -c 32768 {"status":"activated","selected":{"kind":"provider-auto:llama-cpp-existing-server","modelRef":"llama-cpp/nemo"},"attempts":[]} ## BASE 0c19bcdf293, -c 8192 {"status":"activated","selected":{"kind":"provider-auto:llama-cpp-existing-server","modelRef":"llama-cpp/nemo"},"attempts":[]} ``` First real turn with that 8,192 config on the base: ``` [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-midturn-precheck] provider=local/nemo-8k pressure=overflow route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=11800 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=8192 overflowTokens=3608 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=local/nemo-8k candidate=local/nemo-8k reason=context_overflow next=none Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (precheck). ```
