prs.title: fix: remove updater-only restrictions from agent maintenance guidance
prs.body:
Related: #200779, #200809, #198396, #136588

## What Problem This Solves

An operator can explicitly request a Git-based source update and forbid the updater, yet the agent's prompt requires the updater and forbids exec for its own installation. The agent then refuses a valid maintenance method or substitutes a different update path. The config-recovery change in #200809 left this separate restriction intact.

## User Impact

User impact: a source-checkout maintenance request no longer conflicts with an updater-only prompt rule. This removes that rule, rather than adding a new exception or permission setting.

Existing execution permissions, owner admission, approval decisions and live-output build protection are unchanged. This does not make rebuilding files used by a running Gateway safe or deploy an update.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Delete the no-exec maintenance mandate, forced updater/helper routes, duplicate tool-description directives and the redundant component-build exception.
- Keep capability descriptions and existing restart/cleanup safeguards; reconcile the corresponding docs and regenerate the canonical prompt artifacts.
- Remove the Gateway-specific cross-tool description rewrite. Production delta: **7 added / 20 removed lines**. Existing test delta: **13 added / 26 removed lines**; no new test suite, configuration, runtime policy or fallback.

## Evidence

- Canonical `pnpm build:runtime` passed at exact head `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb` in 287.7 s, including core, bundled plugins, Codex and Control UI. Independent verification matched current source signatures and every recorded Codex output hash; this is runtime-build proof, not a full SDK declaration build.

- The original prompt fails the four tool-availability regression cases. The changed ordinary and native-harness prompts remove the exclusive routing while retaining restart-custody and authorization-denial guidance.
- Canonical snapshot generation/check passes all six outputs. After the main refresh, the Telegram Codex fixture, including dynamic tools, shrinks from 118,516 to 117,822 characters: **694 fewer characters, 173 fewer rough tokens** (the repository's text estimate, not provider token accounting).
- Focused coverage passes: 174 prompt/harness/catalog cases, 14 Gateway-tool cases, 17 owner-admission cases and 7 snapshot cases. Unaffected successful cases were reused; corrected assertions were rerun. The snapshot/catalog/Gateway-tool follow-up took 112.76 s, and the two affected owner-prompt cases took 149.06 s (cold compilation dominates). Upstream CI timing is pending.
- Targeted TypeScript graphs pass: agents-root (44.0 s), agents-tools (29.4 s), gateway-methods (36.4 s). Scoped lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. The automatic typecheck selector expanded to all graphs and was stopped; these explicit affected graphs are the claimed typecheck scope.
- A bounded independent native source audit found no remaining direct updater-only/no-exec maintenance mandate in the inspected surfaces. Local Codex autoreview against base `bd1c54cfde534824d31a4cc3c01ce3a116234549`, through P2, returned `reviewer_unavailable` without a report. The subsequent [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200978#issuecomment-6968967010) covered head `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb`, identified no actionable code findings, and required real-behavior proof and an area-owner decision. The unavailable local review is not represented as clean.

### Real-model source maintenance (November 18)

An isolated Gateway ran the exact reviewed runtime with OpenAI Codex `gpt-6-astra`, reasoning `xhigh`. One user request asked it to inspect its deployment and update a designated Git revision without an updater. Deployment/ref/service facts and the canonical build entry point were supplied, not a step-by-step recipe. The model chose a local `git fetch` plus `merge --ff-only`, authored an independently supervised systemd worker and recovery command, built with `pnpm build:runtime`, restarted the Gateway, and verified the result.

The first worker failed because its PATH lacked `corepack` (exit 127). Its recovery command restored the previous source/runtime and a healthy Gateway. Native restart recovery resumed the model without another user message; it diagnosed the PATH error, launched a corrected worker, and completed the update. The final model response accurately reported both completion and the recovered failure.

Independent observations establish:
- Both actual Gateway shutdowns had a running worker in a separate systemd cgroup, with no `PartOf`/`BindsTo` dependency on the Gateway. Native monotonic worker-start/stop pairs were `258159467141 < 258168804254` and `258239308076 < 258247297301` microseconds.
- The final worker exited 0; the original failed worker remains recorded as exit 127. The new Gateway invocation started at `258450560472` microseconds, after the final stop.
- Git HEAD and build identity match `6fe8e4ac013e5b36b24fd8007e011bac9a77203b`, a local marker-only child of reviewed head `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb`. The checkout is clean. Independent source/build/runtime signatures and every recorded Codex output hash match.
- `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/startupz` returned HTTP 200; readiness reported `ready=true`, `coreReady=true`. A read-only Gateway history query found exactly one user request and the final OpenAI/Astra response with positive usage (499 input, 47,232 cached input, 112 output tokens).

Redacted actual worker log excerpt (UTC):
```text
05:12:20 ERROR line=109 exit=127
05:12:42 Original revision and service health restored; requested update FAILED
05:13:38 building
05:16:57 starting
05:17:35 SUCCESS: exact target built, restarted and healthy
```

**Instrumentation failures are not green tests.** Earlier attempts exposed a unit-file quoting error, ambiguous fixture paths, contradictory worker scope, and incomplete Luna/low follow-through. An Astra attempt reached the target but the harness incorrectly read a discarded stop timestamp; cleanup triggered a verified rollback. The final run completed in reality, but its harness incorrectly required the *first* worker to finish successfully even after the model recovered and used a second worker. A separate read-only recorder captured the completed result before cleanup; an independent validator checked both shutdown boundaries, the successful final custodian, health, build provenance and final model response. No claim is made that the original Vitest harness passed; the failures and exact inputs remain retained.

**Limits:** This proves the exercised Linux/systemd source-maintenance and recovery flow, not universal model behavior or automatic method selection for an unspecified update request. The synthetic target changes no product/dependency files; dependency installation, a release/schema migration, and Discord delivery were not exercised. No production deployment was performed. Full CI remains unverified; the published CI run requires maintainer action.

## Owner decision

Merge-conflict follow-up: merged main `5e677bad858c331ec7db0a547bebf0b15e4786d4` in `2e69e54bf57f0b97309927378e55fadae3776140` without rewriting history. Only two generated prompt snapshots conflicted; canonical regeneration resolved them and all six outputs pass `prompt:snapshots:check`. `git diff --check` passes. The non-generated PR patch is identical (stable patch ID `e30b142e7757c4bcb49218a177b0cbace0071168`), and all three maintenance-guidance/tool owners are byte-identical to reviewed/live-tested `f6bf7dc8c7cf981766ae7b762c852c7ec93529eb`. The prior review and runtime proof are reused for that unchanged patch, not claimed as a new full live run on the merge commit. No additional hosted review was requested for this mechanical refresh, consistent with the repository's review-reuse policy.

This intentionally changes the updater-only routing policy retained by #198396 following the self-stop incidents described in #136588; it is not restoration of an established product contract. Requested decision: accept owner-selected source-maintenance methods under existing execution authority and mandatory restart custody. This PR does not claim that tests or a bot review supply that product approval.

prs.title: fix(macos): show full icon captions in the DMG installer
prs.body:
Fixes #200365

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the default macOS DMG in Finder clips the OpenClaw and Applications captions. Native testing also found that Finder can add a vertical scroll bar over the artwork, while the captions need a clearer backing in light and dark appearance.

## User Impact

Both captions have frosted plates behind them, and the taller installer window gives Finder enough room to display the artwork without the vertical scroll bar. Icon sizes, icon positions, the window-bounds override, and drag-to-Applications behavior are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set the default outer window to 680×478 (bounds `400 100 1080 578`), leaving 680×446 below Finder's 32-point title bar. The icons centered at y=305 need about 436 points of content height including their labels. Extend both background images downward by 16 points and bake in the selected frosted caption plates, with a wider plate for localized Applications names.

## Evidence

- Daniel reports that the selected plates were checked in a macOS VM in light and dark appearance; that run identified the scroll bar and the required height adjustment. Native verification was supplied by Daniel, not rerun by this Linux editing session.
- Regenerated both PNGs from `524f1e7` with the supplied script and Pillow 13.0.0. Dimensions are 1360×892 and 680×446. Daniel confirmed that both decoded RGBA pixel hashes exactly match the approved images and authorized these PNGs despite different compression bytes. The generator and temporary Python dependencies were removed and are not committed.
- Re-ran `pnpm test test/scripts/create-dmg.test.ts test/scripts/package-mac-dist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **17 passed, 26 macOS-only tests skipped** on Linux; both test files passed.
- `/bin/bash -n scripts/create-dmg.sh` and `git diff --check` passed. Both generated artwork assets were visually inspected.
- Completed `pr-simplify`: the existing packaging script remains the sole layout owner; only its default and explanatory comments change alongside the two baked PNGs. No new runtime machinery, dependencies, or tests. Whole-PR text delta against the prepared base: +6/−2 lines; this follow-up against `524f1e7`: +6/−3 lines.
- [Original native before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200836#issuecomment-6963514366) document the initial caption-clipping fix at 680×462. They do not show this follow-up's plates or 680×478 window. The prior local Auto Review attempt timed out; no new independent review verdict is claimed here.

Reported and verified on macOS by @daniel-lxs.

prs.title: fix: let macOS dashboard updates switch to the release launcher
prs.body:
Closes #200833.

## What Problem This Solves

The first dashboard update of a checkout-backed macOS Gateway could select a new release without ever starting it. The old process still answered `/readyz`, even though live RPC reported its old build and the target trial had zero starts. This also happened when the two builds had different package versions.

## User Impact

A dashboard update can switch the LaunchAgent to the stable release launcher without asking the serving job to replace itself. If the installer confirms the rebind was refused before activation, OpenClaw keeps the old service and restores the previous release selection. An uncertain install result is not treated as proof that rollback is safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

The serving Gateway hands this first conversion to a temporary sibling LaunchAgent. It verifies that the helper is outside the serving job before transferring update ownership; the installer's self-install guard stays in force. A healthy old endpoint is not a successful update: the verifier must observe the target build.

**Overlap:** #200876 addresses rollback after refusal, not successful conversion. This combined fix includes that recovery, tightens the evidence required to restore a never-started trial, and adds the activation path. It does not require #200876 to be applied separately.

## Evidence

- **Linux: 379 passed / 15 skipped across 15 focused files.** In the process fixture, the old PID still served with zero trial attempts after selection. After rebind, a different PID on the same port served the full target build ID, answered health RPC and `/readyz`, and settled its trial after one start. The handoff helper exited successfully.
- Refusal coverage checks that the previous selection and serving-process record survive, the matching unstarted trial is cleared, and the installer issues no mutating `launchctl` command. Incomplete inspection does not authorize rollback.
- **Native macOS launchd was not tested.** Linux used real scratch processes and modeled launchd; this was not an end-to-end dashboard run on a Mac. The native case in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-launchd.process.test.ts` still needs a disposable macOS GUI account to verify sibling placement and survival through incumbent bootout.
- Core and focused-test typechecks, lint, formatting, the line-cap check, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent local autoreview of the complete combined tree `f14c4358f9f2e0395bd6aef89409daa3f9c6404b` against `e93a426be3297ed947f54b4e15c87827225b6c90` found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The park function was extracted for the line-cap check; expanding it reproduces the previously reviewed helper byte-for-byte.

@hannesrudolph reported the two affected profiles and verified the original patch hash. The included rollback work from #200876 credits @steipete.

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

<!-- openclaw-publication:119e1b05-bf63-4145-8ad7-127d02e1e3e2 -->

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: chore(release): update appcast for 2026.11.5
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mac users need the stable Sparkle feeds to advertise the signed v2026.11.5 assets. This publishes the prepared universal, arm64, and x86_64 appcasts instead of leaving in-app update discovery on the previous feed revision.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native publisher reuses the signed preflight artifacts; this promotion does not rebuild, sign, or notarize them. Only the three generated appcast XML files change. Release source: 76cbb32ecd4f41954d211c5af404dafd4b31e7c1.

## User Impact

Compatible Mac clients can discover v2026.11.5 through their existing architecture-specific feed. Compatibility requirements and signatures come from the prepared feeds without modification; no updater code, configuration, or release-source changes are made here.

## Evidence

- [Signed macOS preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/actions/runs/44152110008): successful; prepared all three architectures.
- [Swift validation](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/actions/runs/44165660649): successful; validation tag and source match the prepared artifacts.
- [Native promotion](https://github.com/openclaw/releases/actions/runs/44230711236/attempts/1): artifact provenance and appcast-to-ZIP identity checks passed; all nine asset names verified on the [release](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.5). This run may still be in progress when the PR opens.
- Appcast checks cover packaged version/build, variant feed URL, release download URL, ZIP length, and Ed25519 signature presence, not independent cryptographic verification.
- Public main feed readback remains pending until this PR lands. No installed Sparkle-client upgrade is claimed.

### Prepared artifact identities (SHA-256)

prs.title: chore: add build heap refusal diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hourly Telegram validation can refuse its prerequisite runtime build before any test runs. The existing failure record shows the remaining budget but not the controller limits, reclaimable file pages, or immediate parent memory needed to explain the shortfall.

## User Impact

No user-facing behavior changes. This adds diagnostics for build admission failures; it does not fix the capacity shortfall or change the heap minimum, reserve, runner size, or test concurrency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing failure-only record now includes nullable numeric controller limits, inactive file bytes, and immediate-parent RSS. Detailed controller reads are opt-in at that failure path; normal Vitest resource snapshots keep their existing read set. Output remains bounded to eight controller depths and excludes paths, PIDs, environment, and raw process status.

## Evidence

- Actual hourly main run [44238824446](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44238824446/job/134582267784) refused at 4293 MiB against the existing 4352 MiB minimum. No Vitest case ran. The prior hourly run also refused at 4309 MiB.
- Existing refusal coverage now checks numeric-only output, the eight-row bound, deterministic parent RSS and unreadable-parent null, while retaining the no-cleanup/no-compiler assertions. Existing snapshot coverage checks that detailed reads stay opt-in.
- The complete `tsdown-build.test.ts` file passed: 94 tests on the exact candidate with Node 24.22.1 in a private native macOS checkout. The scripts-test type graph, targeted source/test type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Local macOS correctly reports null for Linux-only parent RSS.
- Hosted Linux/Bun [job134601356486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44244684696/job/134601356486) passed the full target file (94 tests), including the parent-RSS success/unreadable refusal case and opt-in snapshot case.
- Local committed-range ClawSweeper review completed against base `0ee50d7b` and final head `ee0626b5`: no actionable findings (correctness confidence 0.91).

The sample remains explicitly after-refusal. It can identify a candidate source of memory pressure; it cannot establish that releasing a parent or changing allocation is safe.

prs.title: fix(ios): group iPad conversations like Mac
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iPad conversations can show repeated avatar-only rows for nested tool activity, fragmented working/waiting status, and an embedded conversation palette that does not match the native sidebar.

## User Impact

Supported online iPad conversations reuse Mac-style grouped transcript/activity, spinner and plain working/waiting status, with output tokens before elapsed time. The conversation follows the native iPad light/dark palette without rewriting saved web/profile theme preferences. iPhone retains its native conversation.

The native shell remains. Pending native work, offline operation, and native voice/attachment controls retain the native path. This changes online composer ownership on iPad, not just styling. Existing components still own pairing, credentials, gateway/session selection and draft/send exclusion. Gateway-keyed web storage survives access retirement and is removed by Forget Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing authenticated web conversation and platform-neutral native route contract rather than duplicating grouping policy in Swift. Recognize existing nested-tool audit records rather than hiding them. The existing theme owner consumes the iPad-conversation-only host palette before mount; ordinary web, unsupported hosts and malformed metadata retain their existing behavior. Separate raw catalog and native presentation snapshots preserve selected-read and revision semantics; replacing them with one overlaid snapshot would change that contract.

## Evidence

### Current frozen qualification candidate — draft, not ready

- The reviewed local source is commit `90a22249a040e34e3e997c7e080c938292c8310e`, tree `3462018cb90b2b9981aa185dec64458bc1502442`, a child of published `221c5539df3c0931f5879fb1c0f974ef5487b16f`. Normal staged-content, formatting and freshness hooks passed without changing the reviewed tree. The commit is +1928/-213 across 26 files. Publication and hosted CI must be verified separately against the actual remote head; this source checkpoint is not a successful CI receipt.
- Fresh independent source/static/test-quality reviews found no actionable P0-P2 findings in the cleanup and final lint repair. All 18 outbox cases and all 18 native adapter test identities remain. Both production outbox TypeScript owners are unchanged from the prior published head. Independent review is not native/runtime/compiler/performance qualification or a substitute for the selected whole-range ClawSweeper/AutoReview route and enforced/security checks.
- Behavioral carry proof: **341 passed across 13 files, 0 skipped**. The subsequent five-finding lint-only repair refreshed the affected outbox owner: **18 passed, 0 skipped**, with normal `tsconfig.ui.json` lint and formatting passing. The entire touched test owner was audited; real duplicate-key request error and real transaction-abort settlement remain exercised. The 341-test run was not repeated after the lint-only delta.
- **Canonical paired performance is FAIL, not waived.** Against the same maintained baseline, largest JS gzip is **575195 > 574809 bytes (+386)** and chat boot JS gzip is **1328296 > 1327951 bytes (+345)**. New-session JS **818740 <= 819003** passes. Baseline also has the same inherited largest CSS **59233 > 58315** and chat boot request count **21 > 20**. The current raw result remains failed. Source/static review found no remaining transient diagnostics to remove; the remaining measured cost belongs to the retained iOS appearance integration, not a justification for changing caps, offsetting metrics or weakening semantics.
- **Local UI compiler qualification is blocked by the maintained physical-checkout input boundary:** installed compiler/declaration dependencies resolve into the canonical global pnpm store. Neither compiler switching nor normal lint constitutes compiler proof. No guard bypass, private install, dependency relinking or repeated refused compiler invocation was used. The maintained draft route is `scripts/pr ci-dispatch 200521` after verifying the actual published head. Hosted qualification must verify actual checkout SHA, completed selected production/test compiler graphs and successful `build-artifacts` inner steps. Node **24.22.1**, pinned pnpm **12.15.0**, Vite **8.3.5** and Pako **3.0.3** are source pins, not a claim that the next run has executed.
- `build:ci-artifacts` intentionally omits global/full declaration emission while retaining package declaration checks and SDK-only declaration preparation. Any required full declaration/package proof remains pending. A dispatch receipt, workflow-ref SHA, skipped job, Vite build or prior-head success is not current compiler/build proof. Earlier draft run [44168169952](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44168169952) targets prior head `221c5539df3c0931f5879fb1c0f974ef5487b16f`, not this repaired candidate.
- **Native acceptance remains unqualified for this candidate:** exact accessibility hints/default actions, production behavior, and original genuine send/steering witnesses are still required. Swift formatting/lint/parser passes are not compilation or runtime proof. Earlier native passes, failed attempts and simulator artifacts remain historical. Historical broad UI execution reported **379 passed/4 failed**, with three phone-landscape cases and one small-phone composer-height case; those baseline-attributed failures are retained, not deleted, skipped or relabeled as current success.
- The existing **1003-line test allocation** remains necessary for native-conversation theme/admission regressions and affected workflow coverage; `config/test-lines-allocations/ipad-conversation-theme.txt` is retained unchanged. The latest counted test delta is **1157 <= 400 + 1003**. No valid failing test or assertion was removed to make checks pass.
- **PR stays draft. No ready or merge request.** Exact-head hosted compiler/CI, performance disposition, native/visual proof, remaining whole-range selected-tool provenance and enforced/security gates remain open. Publication changes proof timing only. It performs no native installation, live app, Gateway/configuration or deployment operation.

### Historical failures and carry limits

History-preserving integration retains the prior publication, reviewed source `65ce65bb5683562ad8a00d5950c4737be675cb3b`, integrated source `81ab70e93926a25056622817a420f5992effce2d`, and upstream main `e5b1ad9f320d5d8c52308501335fa67a8b60d211`. Historical production-browser parity covered orientation, helper working/waiting, continuation and final results. None is a new-head rerun.

The first selected local AutoReview was incomplete. Its trust/release-wait findings were repaired. A later 4/4 assessment found a hello-derived mount P2, subsequently repaired; historical delta review at `c40e39e585cef31ee886941cb25cf133117b6f96` completed 1/1 scoped-clean and affected native coverage reported 19 passed/1 skipped. ### Clean renderer comparison

prs.title: fix: let the next update finish a killed source checkout update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw update` on a source (Git) checkout is killed partway through, every later `openclaw update` refuses until you run `openclaw update repair`. Package installs stopped needing that step in #200680 and #200866. Checkouts kept it, because the version number of a checkout does not show whether the killed update had already swapped in its new build.

## User Impact

User impact: after a killed source-checkout update, the next `openclaw update` settles the leftover recovery itself and continues, as it already does for package installs. When the checkout was changed by hand afterwards, it still stops and names `openclaw update repair`.

## Why This Change Was Made

An in-place checkout update now records the commit and build it activated, as `origin.gitActivation` on its run, just before it reserves its plugin recovery. The next update reads that record and checks the checkout on disk. It must still be at that commit, have no local changes, and hold that exact build, complete and made from that commit. Then the checkout runs the killed update's build, and the update uses the same settlement as the package path:

- Killed after the Gateway was verified on the new build: the plugin and config changes are kept.
- Killed before verification: the plugin changes are rolled back and the installed build is finished the way `openclaw update repair` finishes it (Doctor, plugin convergence, Gateway restore), using the stage from #200866.

Anything else keeps the refusal, now with the specific reason. That covers runs recorded by older updaters (no record), a pulled, edited, or rebuilt checkout, and a missing or incomplete build.

What I checked in source:

- The Git runner reserves the cohort only after the runtime swap (`src/infra/update-runner-git.ts`, `activate()` then `onTransaction`). The command-level rollback settles the cohort before it restores the old runtime (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-rollback.ts`, `settleUpdatePluginCohortInCandidate` before `packageTransaction.rollback`). So whenever a cohort exists, `dist` is the candidate build.
- Runtime promotion copies `dist/build-info.json` byte for byte. `relocateRuntimeTree` rewrites only `.modules.yaml` and `.bin` launchers (`src/infra/update-runtime-relocation.ts`). A runner test now asserts the live file equals the validated candidate's file.
- Package-to-Git conversion hands `onTransaction` to the package exposure swap (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-git.ts`), so it never records the fact and keeps refusing. The Git release layout never calls `onTransaction` and never reserves a cohort, so its behavior is unchanged.
- `openclaw update repair` already runs the same settlement and finalization on a checkout, with none of these gates. A new test compares the update's recorded run with repair's for the same killed state and finds them identical.

**Update behavior.** The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched. On the first update from a published version, nothing changes: published updaters do not record `gitActivation`, so a run they leave behind still gets today's refusal. The new path applies only once a run recorded by this code is killed. A downgraded updater's origin schema is a non-strict `z.object` (`src/infra/update-run-schema.ts:234` at `v2026.11.5`), so it drops the key and refuses as today. If an older writer rewrites the row, the record is lost, which is the safe direction.

**Storage.** One additive, optional key in the existing `update_runs.origin_json` column. No column, table, schema version, or migration. It is kept as an exact receipt beside `origin.driver` and `origin.packageRelease`, and public history projections omit it. Documented in `docs/reference/database-schemas/layout.md` beside the `origin.driver` precedent.

## Evidence

Each killed-run case starts from a real child process that checks out the candidate commit in a real temporary Git repository the test owns, installs its build, records the run and cohort, and is then killed with SIGKILL. The next `openclaw update` runs from its command entry.

- Red on base `14b9fc3c8d9`: the 10 new checkout cases failed, all with the old "left by an update of a source checkout" refusal (10 failed, 31 passed).
- The branch was then rebased onto `af50b8e6ee1`. None of the 28 intervening commits touch the update, cohort, or run-ledger code. The killed-run file passes 44/44 on the rebased head.
- Green on the head: the verified case keeps the changes. The unverified case rolls back, finishes as repair does, and proceeds. The comparison with repair matches.
- Controls that keep refusing, each asserting the message, that the update did not proceed, that Doctor did not run, and that the cohort, run status, config bytes, HEAD, tree, and build are unchanged: no record, recorded build or previous build that differs from the cohort, HEAD moved, untracked file, edited tracked file, missing build, incomplete build (no entry point), build from another commit, and a hand rebuild.
- The independent review found that the first version checked only `build-info.json`. The "incomplete build" control failed on that commit (the update went ahead), and passes now that the gate uses the updater's own runtime check.
- Writer: the run row carries the record, the record is absent for package-style transactions, and the public projection omits it (`update-command-execution.test.ts`). The Git runner's transaction names the validated commit and a distinct build ID (`update-runner-git-transactions.test-support.ts`).

Not covered by a dedicated test: a killed checkout update that left the Gateway stopped (it uses the shared stage the package tests cover), and the checkout changing between inspection and the claim (inspection reruns under the claim). Leftover `*.openclaw-update-*.tmp` runtime backups are not retired by this path, which matches repair. The `autoreview` helper does not run on this machine, so review came from an independent reviewer agent.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-killed-run.process.test.ts` (base and head)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over the Git runner, execution, database rollback and retention, cohort settlement, run ledger and record suites, `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`, and `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:all`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 14b9fc3c8d9 --no-merge-base`, `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`

</details>

CI note: the first `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` run hit its 25-minute limit after about 15 minutes of slow Ubuntu package downloads during browser setup. This PR changes no UI code. That one job was rerun once.

prs.title: fix: let Gateway owners continue child tasks
prs.body:
Related: #168406

## What Problem This Solves

An agent driven by an authenticated Gateway owner can fail to send a follow-up to its child with `Followup has no retained original caller policy`, even though the Gateway has successfully retained that owner's authority. This interrupts otherwise authorized multi-turn child work.

## User Impact

Preserves the validated caller identity when preparing an owner-driven follow-up. No configuration or migration is required. This is a candidate fix with an isolated live-model round trip qualified; it is not deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The continuation producer creates its synthetic client before capturing the original operator source. For an owner without an explicit role actor, capture succeeds but the synthetic client still has no actor; the follow-up custody guard then refuses it.

After successful capture and current-authority assertions, project a missing actor from the captured authority's profile ID. Preserve an existing actor. The follow-up guard, scope ceiling, role/session checks, and retained-source revocation remain unchanged. Owner attribution alone does not acquire an actor: without successful authority capture this code does not run.

This deliberately addresses the validated owner-capture path rather than broadly admitting actorless device/control-plane clients. Jaxon Parrott's #168406 identifies the overlapping admission error and informed the comparison; no patch or tests were copied from it. This PR does not claim to replace its broader profileless-device fix.

## Evidence

- Source investigation identified the mismatch between authenticated owner capture and the actor-required follow-up guard. A prior isolated propagation reproduction rejected the owner-shaped synthetic client and accepted a named-user client. That reproduction stubbed authority capture; it was not full Gateway acceptance proof.
- Added three regression cases in the existing Gateway continuation suite: real owner authority capture through follow-up custody preparation, native device revocation blocking custody re-entry without running the supplied effect, and owner attribution without authenticated authority remaining refused. Capture and follow-up admission are not mocked; the existing suite's agent-turn service fixture remains mocked.
- Fresh independent source review found and corrected a revocation-fixture issue; no concrete production defect was found in the final five-line fix. This is source review, not executed security qualification.
- `git diff --check` passed. Simplification review retained one producer change and reused the existing test suite; no new helper, manager, state, configuration, or permission policy.

## Executed validation and remaining gate

The upstream patch remains pinned at `d05371a50a75d96ec8b9cab0e3c83538a08451c6`; fork-only proof does not change this PR's code.

- [Initial fork run](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/44187949041): 18 continuation tests and 5 custody-consumer tests passed. The same owner regression against the original authority module failed with `Followup has no retained original caller policy`, while attribution-only refusal remained intact.
- [Corrected scenario run](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/44192798788) at `b61d65330a40b900457fcab481b5df89cdfabca7`: authenticated token-WebSocket ingress, child spawn/initial completion, follow-up admission, and follow-up child completion passed. Requester callback assertion failed (`completionCalls` was zero). This did not qualify requester delivery or establish a production defect. E2E test time: 14.84 seconds; Vitest duration: 97.51 seconds, excluding prerequisite builds.
- The first fixture omitted its provider's required prompt marker. Further inspection found that the provider extractor strips internal task-completion events before the scripted model can respond. Fork proof commit `be4744d7ca4701c0850f508358b21af7c4096039` preserves model-visible completion carriers and waits for the produced sink-delivery outcome. It does not synthesize results, bypass custody, or edit production code.
- [Successful scripted qualification run](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/44200935990) at `be4744d7ca4701c0850f508358b21af7c4096039`: PASSED all workflow steps, including the full authenticated owner → child spawn → follow-up → child completion → exact-once requester sink delivery. E2E test time 15.184 seconds; Vitest duration 94.53 seconds, excluding builds. This uses a real isolated Gateway and agent execution with scripted provider/channel I/O, not a live external model or Telegram acceptance.

**Live-model round trip now qualified:** see the OAuth run below. **Still unqualified:** full exact-head upstream CI/build/typecheck and real Telegram delivery. Reviewer readiness remains pending; no cleared merge gate or new rating is claimed.

## Review and boundaries

The latest completed ClawSweeper review recognized successful scripted delivery: patch quality 4/6, proof confidence 3/6, overall readiness 3/6, with no actionable findings. That review predates the successful live OAuth run below. A fresh review is being requested against this evidence.

Scripted tests ran on GitHub. The explicitly authorized live-model proof used a task-owned checkout, synthetic isolated state, free ports, a local channel sink, and an environment-only provider credential. Runtime prerequisite build passed. The live proof source is pinned at `f28ad77b210f077dae1948fc8d31a9eb7e8fe335`.

Three live attempts failed before exercising child follow-up behavior:
- First attempt: setup rejected a group-writable disposable state ancestor; no model call occurred. The rerun used process-scoped private permissions without weakening the safety check.
- Second attempt: the ordinary test environment stripped the provider credential; secret resolution failed before model execution.
- Third attempt: supported live mode with an empty task-owned source home passed startup and secret resolution, but the first model request returned `invalid_api_key` (78.73-second suite duration). A separate minimal response-endpoint check also returned HTTP 401, while model listing returned HTTP 200. Credential validity for listing does not establish response-endpoint access; the precise authentication cause remains unresolved.

These are setup/authentication failures, not evidence of success or failure of the follow-up implementation. The subsequent OAuth run below closes the isolated live-model round-trip gap; hosted reassessment is pending. No credential was stored in the checkout or published. No installed Gateway/configuration change, restart/reload, credential migration, Iris retry, deployment, or history repair occurred.

The reported historical Talk failure is established, but its internal caller identity was not captured; the reproduced owner path is not proven to be that incident's exact cause.

## Successful subscription OAuth live proof

Fork-only proof revision [`653fe12409df20ca51ed88ce1558993baaca8f8a`](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/commit/653fe12409df20ca51ed88ce1558993baaca8f8a) corrects the harness, not production code:

- Uses the existing ChatGPT/Codex subscription access token, `auth: oauth`, the supported `openai-chatgpt-responses` adapter, and the ChatGPT subscription endpoint. The token is passed only through an environment SecretRef; no refresh token is copied, no credential is migrated, and no production login is changed.
- Explicitly uses the OpenClaw runtime to exercise the same `sessions_spawn` / `sessions_send` continuation boundary as this patch, rather than substituting native Codex child-management tools.
- The first OAuth run authenticated and completed child spawn and follow-up, but the requester sink stayed empty. Inspection found the live fixture used a target ID outside the synthetic channel's recognized `provenance-` namespace. The corrected test uses that namespace and a complete message-send instruction; the exact-result and one-delivery assertions are unchanged. Failure-only diagnostics read synthetic requester history through the public Gateway API.

**Executed locally on November 18 UTC: PASS — 1 test, 1 file.** Real model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, real authenticated owner WebSocket ingress, isolated Gateway and synthetic session state:

`owner → sessions_spawn → initial child completion → sessions_send(mode=followup) → follow-up child completion → requester completion handling → exact-once local sink delivery`

- Both owner turns and both child runs returned `status: ok`.
- The real registry contained one initial child and one follow-up run.
- The local outbound sink received exactly one message with the expected recipient, account, and exact nonce-bearing child-result text; the Gateway then drained idle without provider errors.
- Test: **30.561 s**; Vitest: **92.70 s**; wrapper wall time: **97.44 s**.

prs.title: feat(update): capture PostgreSQL stores while the Gateway serves
prs.body:
Related: #196154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update of an install with PostgreSQL stores keeps the Gateway down for the whole run, because the PostgreSQL rollback capture needs exclusive state ownership and a Gateway the updater does not manage has to be stopped before the update starts.

## User Impact

User impact: PostgreSQL stores are captured while the Gateway still serves, and after the stop only the stores written since their capture are captured again. With the new opt-in `--wait-for-gateway-stop <seconds>`, an update on a Gateway the updater does not manage (custom service, foreground process) prepares while it serves and asks the operator to stop it only for the swap, migrations and restart. On the real install below the Gateway was down about 287 s instead of 941 s. SQLite stores are captured after the stop as before.

## Data-model compatibility

This change adds no store schema and no migration. The only persisted shape change is an optional `sourceDigests` field in the update backup record; records written without it still parse.

Existing data keeps loading and working after the upgrade, shown end to end on real Git installs:

- From the latest stable `v2026.11.5`: config, agents, an automation and 2,500,000 rows written on stable are read back on this head `0ed342608473` (with the #200381 build cherry-pick, see Upgrade from the latest stable release), then ported to PostgreSQL and kept through one update and one forced-failure rollback by this change's updater.
- From this branch's base, all on PostgreSQL: data written on the base `2516bca9fdb8` is read back on this change after the base updater moves the install, and kept through a forced-failure rollback (below). That run used the head before two merges of `origin/main` (`7da4339c06f7`); the change's own diff differs from the current head only by the merge conflict resolution.

Existing data, end to end, on a real Git install with every store family on PostgreSQL 17.11 (macOS, private cluster, foreground Gateway). Data is written on the base `2516bca9fdb8`, the base updater moves the install to the earlier head `7da4339c06f7`, that head reads it back, and then the head's updater runs again into a target whose Doctor throws after the stop, so the database rollback has to restore it.

Data written on the base, with the Gateway serving:

```text
$ openclaw automations create "0 0 1 1 *" "proof acknowledged write" --name occ-proof-written-on-base --agent main --json
{
  "id": "32f86522-2a99-45f6-8a3f-7aca56342499",
  "agentId": "main",
  "name": "occ-proof-written-on-base",
  "enabled": true,
  "schedule": { "kind": "cron", "expr": "0 0 1 1 *" },
  [... cut ...]
}
$ psql -qAt -d openclaw -c "INSERT INTO \"$AGENT_NS\".cache_entries (scope, key, value_json, updated_at) SELECT 'occ-proof', 'k' || g, json_build_object('n', g, 'text', repeat(md5(g::text), 12))::text, 1 FROM generate_series(1, 2500000) g"
```

`$AGENT_NS` is the idle agent's PostgreSQL schema (1.5 GB after the insert). Each check below reads the automation back through the Gateway with `openclaw automations list --json` (count of entries named `occ-proof-written-on-base`) and counts the rows with `psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM \"$AGENT_NS\".cache_entries WHERE scope = 'occ-proof'"`.

Hop 1, base updater with the Gateway stopped (`openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart`, dev target pinned to `7da4339c06f7`):

```text
23:48:31 base data: seeded rows 2500000, automation written on base present 1
23:48:32 hop 1: gateway stopped; base 2516bca9fdb8 updates itself to 7da4339c06f7
Update mode: git
Update target: 2026.11.4 (7da4339c)
00:05:04 hop 1: update exit 0
00:05:18 hop 1: gateway ready on 7da4339c06f7; down 1006.1 s
00:05:19 hop 1: read back on the head: seeded rows 2500000, automation written on base present 1
```

Hop 2, this head's updater (`openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart --wait-for-gateway-stop 600`) into `28745954995a`, which is `7da4339c06f7` plus a Doctor that throws once the harness creates a flag file:

```text
00:05:20 hop 2: 7da4339c06f7 to 28745954995a (Doctor fails after the stop)
16:13:55.288   ✓ database snapshot (Gateway serving) (91.16s)
00:13:56 update asked for the stop after 516.1 s of preparation while serving
00:13:57 acknowledged write: automation occ-proof-between-capture-and-stop created through the Gateway
00:13:57 armed forced Doctor failure
00:13:57 gateway stopped
16:14:30.024   ✓ database snapshot (17.63s)
16:15:03.268   ✗ openclaw doctor (30.09s)
16:15:03.268     Failing check openclaw doctor (command-failed): proof: forced Doctor failure after the Gateway stopped
16:17:31.123   ✓ database rollback (147.3s)
16:18:18.445 Warning: Kept the capture taken while the Gateway served: <state>/agents/probe/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
00:18:32 update exit 1
00:18:42 gateway ready on 7da4339c06f7; down 284.7 s
00:18:43 acknowledged write present after the update: 1
00:18:44 after rollback: seeded rows 2500000, automation written on base present 1
```

Result: the automation and all 2,500,000 rows written on the base are read back on this head through the Gateway and in PostgreSQL. After the forced failure, the rollback restores them, and the idle store that holds the rows is restored from the capture kept from while the Gateway served. The write made between that capture and the stop is also present. `HH:MM:SS` lines are the harness in UTC; `HH:MM:SS.mmm` lines are the update output in local time.

## Upgrade from the latest stable release

From `v2026.11.5` (`e13cf15ece9b`, latest stable) to this head `0ed342608473`, with one proof-only commit on top: a cherry-pick of #200381's commit `133cfd5d3f76`. The candidate is `b283d867a8f5`. It was never pushed. The cherry-pick only touches the declaration build (`scripts/lib/native-declaration-emitter.mts`, `scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts` and its test); nothing in it touches update, Doctor or storage. It is needed because of #200357 (open, fixed by #200381): the updater builds the candidate in a worktree inside the install, and without the cherry-pick the `v2026.11.5` updater refuses this exact head at `preflight-build` (`Error: Declaration input escapes checkout`), before the checkout, on the same install:

```text
04:39:19 stable data: settings {"port":19431,"bind":"loopback","auth":"token","channel":"dev","agents":[]}, agents main,probe, SQLite rows 2500000, automation present 1
04:39:20 hop 1: gateway stopped; e13cf15ece9b (v2026.11.5) updates itself to candidate 0ed342608473
04:43:09 hop 1: update exit 1
  ✗ preflight-build (18.55s)
```

`v2026.11.5` keeps shared state and agent stores on SQLite, so the run starts from a SQLite install, moves to the candidate with the stable updater, then ports every store to PostgreSQL on the candidate and updates twice more with this change's updater. Same macOS host, private PostgreSQL 17.11 cluster, foreground Gateway, synthetic data written through the product.

Data written on `v2026.11.5`, with the Gateway serving: an automation created through the Gateway (`openclaw automations create ... --name occ-proof-written-on-stable --json`) and 2,500,000 rows in the idle `probe` agent's SQLite `cache_entries`. Each check reads gateway and update fields from the config file, `openclaw agents list --json`, the automation through `openclaw automations list --json`, and the row count (SQLite before the port, `psql` after). The config file has no `agents.list` entries on this install (`"agents":[]`), so agents are checked through the CLI. Blocks below are excerpts in order; lines between them are cut. `HH:MM:SS` lines are the harness in UTC; `HH:MM:SS.mmm` lines are the update output in local time.

Hop 1, the `v2026.11.5` updater with the Gateway stopped (`openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart`, dev target pinned to the candidate):

```text
04:46:43 stable data: settings {"port":19431,"bind":"loopback","auth":"token","channel":"dev","agents":[]}, agents main,probe, SQLite rows 2500000, automation present 1
04:46:44 hop 1: gateway stopped; e13cf15ece9b (v2026.11.5) updates itself to candidate b283d867a8f5
[... update output cut ...]
  ✓ preflight-build (259.31s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor (19.68s)
  ✓ candidate-gateway-startup (8.77s)
  ✓ git-checkout (11.51s)
  ✓ database snapshot (8.51s)
05:00:14 hop 1: update exit 0
05:00:22 hop 1: gateway ready on b283d867a8f5; down 818.6 s
05:00:27 hop 1: on the candidate: settings {"port":19431,"bind":"loopback","auth":"token","channel":"dev","agents":[]}, agents main,probe, SQLite rows 2500000, automation present 1
```

Port on the candidate, Gateway stopped, after adding `database.postgres.connection` (`openclaw doctor --fix`, `openclaw database port --to postgres --dry-run`, then `openclaw database port --to postgres`):

```text
05:04:17 port: openclaw database port --to postgres exit 0
Database port: complete (postgres); 3 database stores.
2 other stores remain on SQLite.
Memory index (main): rebuilt in 3.2s.
Memory index (probe): rebuilt in 3.0s.
openclaw_agent_686ab2c0f4944e4a|51|1379 MB
openclaw_agent_f9e07ca3446c40aa|51|1656 kB
openclaw_state_f27ef1a1665345c3|104|3560 kB
05:04:29 port: probe agent store now openclaw_agent_686ab2c0f4944e4a; settings {"port":19431,"bind":"loopback","auth":"token","channel":"dev","agents":[]}, agents main,probe, PostgreSQL rows 2500000, automation written on stable present 1
05:04:30 acknowledged write: automation occ-proof-written-on-postgres created through the Gateway
05:04:32 postgres data: rows 2600000, automations present: stable 1, postgres 1
```

The two stores left on SQLite are the local credential and service stores, as in the runs below. After the port, 100,000 more rows and a second automation are written on PostgreSQL.

Hop 2, this change's updater (`--wait-for-gateway-stop 600`) to the candidate plus one docs line (`a51b715bf269`):

```text
05:04:32 hop 2: b283d867a8f5 to a51b715bf269 with --wait-for-gateway-stop
21:13:03.544   ✓ database snapshot (Gateway serving) (72.37s)
05:13:04 update asked for the stop after 512.1 s of preparation while serving
05:13:06 acknowledged write: automation occ-proof-between-capture-and-stop-hop2 created through the Gateway
05:13:06 gateway stopped
21:13:30.242   ✓ database snapshot (12.97s)
21:17:55.797 UPDATE_EXIT=0
05:18:04 gateway ready on a51b715bf269; down 297.6 s
05:18:05 acknowledged write present after the update: 1
05:18:08 hop 2: on a51b715bf269: settings {"port":19431,"bind":"loopback","auth":"token","channel":"dev","agents":[]}, agents main,probe, rows 2600000, automations present: stable 1, postgres 1
```

Hop 3, same updater into `c5a501c958b5` (`a51b715bf269` plus a Doctor that throws once the harness creates a flag file after the stop):

```text
05:18:08 hop 3: a51b715bf269 to c5a501c958b5 (Doctor fails after the stop)
21:25:05.990   ✓ database snapshot (Gateway serving) (63.43s)
05:25:06 update asked for the stop after 417.9 s of preparation while serving
05:25:07 acknowledged write: automation occ-proof-between-capture-and-stop-hop3 created through the Gateway
05:25:07 armed forced Doctor failure
05:25:08 gateway stopped
21:25:27.270   ✓ database snapshot (9.32s)
21:25:51.941   ✗ openclaw doctor (22.62s)
21:25:51.941     Failing check openclaw doctor (command-failed): proof: forced Doctor failure after the Gateway stopped
21:27:59.300   ✓ database rollback (127.04s)
21:28:37.039 Warning: Kept the capture taken while the Gateway served: <state>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
21:28:37.039 Warning: Kept the capture taken while the Gateway served: <state>/agents/probe/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
21:28:49.032 UPDATE_EXIT=1
05:28:56 gateway ready on a51b715bf269; down 228.7 s
05:28:57 acknowledged write present after the update: 1
05:29:01 hop 3: after rollback on a51b715bf269: settings {"port":19431,"bind":"loopback","auth":"token","channel":"dev","agents":[]}, agents main,probe, rows 2600000, automations present: stable 1, postgres 1
```

Result: a `v2026.11.5` SQLite install reaches this head (with the #200381 cherry-pick) through the stable updater with its config, agents, automation and all 2,500,000 rows intact. After the port to PostgreSQL, this change's updater completes one update and rolls back one forced failure, and every write survives both, including the writes made between the capture and the stop. Once #200381 merges, its commit is on main and this head needs no cherry-pick.

## Why This Change Was Made

This answers the three open questions on #196154:

- **Capture generation.** Each PostgreSQL store is captured from its own `REPEATABLE READ` snapshot. Inside that same snapshot the capture records the store's existing generation fingerprint and a reuse digest: catalog facts, sequence allocations, and per table `count(*)` plus `sum(hashtextextended(row_to_json(t)::text, 0))`, computed on the server. After the stop, under exclusive ownership, the update reads the digest again. Equal: the capture is kept with its recorded generation. Different or unreadable: that store's capture is dropped and it is captured again exactly as today. A write acknowledged after the capture therefore always lands in the rollback point.
- **Shutdown handoff.** Managed services keep today's drain and stop. For a Gateway the updater does not manage, `--wait-for-gateway-stop` prints one line asking the operator to stop it, then polls for state ownership until the bound. The updater never stops, signals or starts that Gateway. On timeout it drops the captures it took, changes nothing, and refuses with `database-engine-preflight` as today.
- **No acknowledged write lost, including the updater's own writes.** The update writes its run record and plugin cohort reservation to the shared state store before the capture under ownership, so that store is normally captured again; idle stores keep their capture. A capture that fails while serving falls back to the capture after the stop.

The digest is not a new generation format. Restore checks keep using the existing fingerprint, recorded from the capture snapshot itself. Accepted edge case: two different row multisets with an equal row count and an equal 64-bit hash sum read as unchanged (about 2^-64 per changed store). Cost on one 1.27 GB table on PostgreSQL 17.11: digest 1.36 s, in-database copy 6.13 s.

Signals considered and rejected: `pg_stat` counters (asynchronous, resettable, miss `TRUNCATE`), `xmin` plus row count (PostgreSQL 16+ opportunistic freezing hides updates), WAL position (cluster wide), logical decoding (needs `wal_level=logical`), and change-marker triggers in every store (a schema change and a cost on every write).

Online captures live where raw update captures already live: the update-capture root for package installs and the checkout's `.artifacts` directory for Git installs. A run that ends before the capture under ownership adopts it drops it. A failed online capture drops the finished stores' server schemas one by one and keeps the directory if any schema cannot be dropped. When automatic restoration is unavailable and a package install keeps its online capture, `openclaw doctor` lists it with the other retained update snapshots.

Two files were split to stay under the 700-line cap: the online capture lives in `src/infra/update-database-backup-online.ts`, and `migrateDatabasePortSource` moved unchanged to `src/infra/database-engine/port-source-migration.ts`.

Maintainer decisions:

- `--wait-for-gateway-stop <seconds>` is a new public `openclaw update` option.
- PostgreSQL stores are now captured while serving on every update, including updates of a managed service. That adds one full capture while the Gateway serves (65 to 70 s for the 1.5 GB store below) and takes it out of the stop window (85 s to 11 s).
- Alternative: capture while serving only with `--wait-for-gateway-stop`, so managed-service updates keep the single capture after the stop.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, red on base and green with the change: `update-database-backup-engine.test.ts` "captures each PostgreSQL store while the Gateway serves, from its own capture snapshot" and "keeps an unchanged online capture and captures a written store again under ownership". Both fail on base with `PostgreSQL update capture requires exclusive ownership`, pass on the head, and fail again with the production change reversed (`git apply -R`).
- `doctor-update-snapshots.test.ts`: a retained online capture under the update-capture root is listed by Doctor, and an unreadable update-capture root warns even without an npm install ("warns about an unreadable update-capture root without an npm install"); each red without its fix.
- A capture under ownership that throws no longer orphans the online capture: the cohort hands it over only after that capture succeeds, so the run's cleanup drops it. No dedicated test for this one.
- Cleanup regressions in `update-command-database-backup.online-abort.test.ts`, each red without its fix: a run cancelled as the online capture finishes drops it; a failed online capture drops its finished stores one by one, skips the unfinished one, and lives under the update-capture root on package installs.
- PostgreSQL conformance (`node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres`, PostgreSQL 17.11): `src/snapshot/postgres-generation.postgres.test.ts` 3/3, including the new digest case (stable, changes on a committed update, a sequence allocation and a `TRUNCATE`, unchanged after a rolled-back delete).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean. `pnpm check:changed` against `origin/main` at `9a6a00e3e2bb`: every check passes except the dead export scan, which reports only exports outside this change; the scan also fails on `origin/main` itself. The assertion safety ratchet, which flagged one cast in the Doctor listing, passes after the follow-up commit.

### Runtime output

Real Git install on macOS with every store family on PostgreSQL 17.11 (private cluster): state store 3.5 MB, main agent store 1.4 MB, and an idle agent store with 1.5 GB of rows. The local credential and service stores stay SQLite. The Gateway runs in the foreground (`openclaw gateway run`), so the updater does not manage it. Each run updates between two real commits, the start commit and the same commit plus one docs line, pinned with the updater's detached dev target. Downtime runs from the Gateway stop to `/readyz` on the new build. Timestamped `HH:MM:SS` lines are the harness in UTC; `HH:MM:SS.mmm` lines are the update output in local time.

Base, stopped native update (`2516bca9fdb8` to `63d1c9a8e2da`):

```text
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart        # Gateway stopped first
18:10:45 gateway stopped; running the native update with the Gateway stopped
[... update output cut ...]
  ✓ database snapshot (84.79s)
[... update output cut ...]
18:26:18 update exit 0
18:26:26 gateway ready on 63d1c9a8e2da; down 941.0 s
```

Head, same install shape (`8a7da6d4b6ee` to `5beb516a80cf`; the later head only adds Doctor's snapshot listing, which update-time Doctor skips):

```text
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart --wait-for-gateway-stop 600
13:09:37.023   ✓ preflight-build (116.18s)
13:12:05.909   ✓ database snapshot (Gateway serving) (69.62s)
13:12:06.282 Update prepared while the Gateway served. Stop the Gateway through its owner now; waiting up to 600s for it to release state ownership (<redacted: holder detail>)
21:12:06 update asked for the stop after 506.2 s of preparation while serving
21:12:07 acknowledged write: automation occ-proof-between-capture-and-stop created through the Gateway
21:12:08 gateway stopped
13:12:32.810   ✓ git-checkout (5.27s)
13:12:44.453   ✓ database snapshot (11.29s)
[... Doctor output cut ...]
13:16:47.427 Warning: Kept the capture taken while the Gateway served: <state>/agents/probe/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
13:16:47.492 UPDATE_EXIT=0
== gateway ready on 5beb516a80cf after 7.9 s start
== acknowledged write present: 1
```

The write lands after the online capture and before the stop. After the stop, the store it changed is captured again while the idle 1.5 GB store keeps its capture (`database snapshot (11.29s)` and the `Kept the capture` warning), and the write is present on the new build. The stop to update exit is 279.5 s; with the 7.9 s start, the Gateway was down about 287 s. The harness lost the exit code to a locale error after this run, so the last two lines come from a restart of the same install and state right after the update. Two earlier head runs on the same shape, before the cleanup fixes, were down 341.4 s and 303.0 s.

Head, forced Doctor failure after the stop (`8a7da6d4b6ee` to a target whose Doctor throws once the harness creates a flag file after the online capture):

```text
13:29:19.310   ✓ database snapshot (Gateway serving) (65.35s)
13:29:19.712 Update prepared while the Gateway served. Stop the Gateway through its owner now; waiting up to 600s (<redacted: holder detail>)
21:29:21 acknowledged write: automation occ-proof-between-capture-and-stop created through the Gateway
21:29:21 armed forced Doctor failure
21:29:21 gateway stopped
13:29:40.197   ✓ git-checkout (5.48s)
13:29:52.208   ✓ database snapshot (11.7s)
13:30:16.210   ✗ openclaw doctor (21.98s)
13:30:16.210     Failing check openclaw doctor (command-failed): proof: forced Doctor failure after the Gateway stopped
13:32:11.291   ✓ database rollback (114.75s)
[... update output cut ...]
13:32:46.252 Warning: Kept the capture taken while the Gateway served: <state>/agents/probe/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
13:32:59.628 UPDATE_EXIT=1
21:33:07 gateway ready on 8a7da6d4b6ee; down 225.9 s
21:33:08 acknowledged write present after the update: 1
```

Doctor fails after the stop. The database rollback then restores every store, including the capture kept from before the stop; restore refuses a store whose live generation differs from the recorded one, so this also shows that the generation recorded inside the capture snapshot matches. The previous build `8a7da6d4b6ee` serves again, and the write acknowledged between the capture and the stop survives the rollback.

What remains in the stop window is mostly Doctor (three passes, about 3.5 minutes here), which this change does not touch. Both base and head successful runs also report `Automatic database restoration unavailable: databases changed after snapshot capture; the writer is unknown` after Doctor on this fresh install; it predates this change.

Upgrade from the latest stable release: see the section above. Without the #200381 cherry-pick, the `v2026.11.5` updater refuses this head at `preflight-build` (`Declaration input escapes checkout`, #200357), before the checkout.

Not run: Linux and systemd, a managed service, a package install, a Gateway-initiated update.

### Local review

Local ClawSweeper, `--local-range` against a fresh `origin/main`, four rounds:

| Round | Head | Correctness | Ratings (overall / proof / patch) | Findings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `70df3ac2a12c` | patch is incorrect | F / F / C | P2: online capture leaked when the run is cancelled as it finishes. Fixed. |
| 2 | `37d4b3e9e123` | patch is incorrect | C / D / C | P1: package-install capture outside the update-capture root. P2: failed-capture cleanup refused the whole batch. Both fixed. |
| 3 | `ec3111b6baa9` | patch is correct | D / D / B | P3: retained online snapshots on package installs were not listed by Doctor's update-snapshot check. Fixed. |
| 4 | `37a356b966e9` | patch is correct | F / F / B | P3: an online capture was orphaned when the capture under ownership threw. P3: the incomplete-inspection warning needed an npm install. Both fixed in `7da4339c06f7`. |

The proof rating reflects that a local range review has no PR body or attached output. After round 3 the head makes one helper private for the dead export scan and adds the Doctor listing for the P3, without a type assertion. Security: cleared in all four rounds. The round 4 fixes at `7da4339c06f7` have not had a local round of their own.

prs.title: improve(ci): prepare Watch companion during build
prs.body:
## Summary
- Prepare the selected Watch simulator's actual paired phone alongside existing foreground Xcode build/settings work; join before Watch boot, installation or tests.
- Preserve the selected pair, all five test selections, product resolution, independent failure statuses and early-exit cleanup. No new jobs, caches, setup steps, planner or concurrency-cap changes.

## Why and expected effect
In [CI43995805967, iOS job133747919619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43995805967/job/133747919619), iOS took80m53s with ~2s queue. The Watch step took ~940s; paired-phone boot occupied **75.803s**, following ~106s build/settings work. Hiding this independent boot offers an ideal **~76s native-branch reduction**, not940s. CPU/I/O contention can reduce or erase it. Actual overlap is observed; a controlled end-to-end speedup is **not established**.

This is **not a measured whole-FRV speedup**. [Parent43995308737](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43995308737) finished a failed93m34 diagnostic envelope: CI ended02:50:43, candidate checks' final receipt02:56:29. That downstream barrier means **zero parent benefit** from this native saving alone. The change targets native-dominated cycles, with no additional runner queue/setup. Do not land if native qualification shows regression.

## Historical constraint
[56c643947272575869cb051d020a7fc419eb8ac0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/56c643947272575869cb051d020a7fc419eb8ac0) deliberately prepared the actual paired phone to fix Watch XCTest startup timeouts. It may differ from IOS_SIMULATOR_ID. Successful preparation remains mandatory before Watch operations; existing build-product reuse remains intact.

## Proof and limits
- Actual workflow-shell regression: base fails the overlap handshake; candidate passes. No timing-threshold assertion or production test hook.
- **78 iOS workflow tests pass** (5.68s suite /6.42s wrapper), covering unpaired destinations, actual companion selection, exact boot-failure status, product-resolution failure and foreground-build cleanup. Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, pinned actionlint, zizmor and workflow scanner pass.
- Removed redundant status bookkeeping to keep workflow size479,980 bytes under unchanged480,000-byte limit. Upstream #200402 repaired inherited UI ownership failure, retaining author credit and assertions.
- Head `a04c57876347c1873523150fb61f0b051859a28c` removes one stray `app.tap()` from the bootstrap UI test, preserving every assertion. Native logs show the tap opens QR scanning and camera permission intercepts Connect Manually. Siblings use explicit navigation. This follows [#196284](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196284), commit `3fa0f3a75c697c9b973e15822481ac6a72408f64`.
- **Exact-head ordinary [CI44230439548](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44230439548) succeeded.** It does not run release-only native Watch proof. Hosted review completed without code findings; comparable native timing remains an open proof item. **Not RFR.**

## Simplification
Move existing pair discovery; background one command; join and clean up its PID. No new helper or alternate path. Against merge base: workflow+22/-12, tests+32/-1. Against first revision: workflow+7/-10,315 fewer bytes; tests unchanged. Best-effort termination covers the owned bootstatus client; runner cleanup owns the simulator process tree. No claim that terminating the client rolls back a partially booted simulator.

## Native evidence — November18,2026 UTC

| Frozen source / run | Outcome | Measured phases / limitations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline `6ba51132e323cff0239e1d91279836202c060e00`, [44049787925 attempt1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44049787925/attempts/1) | Job133925089592 exceeded150-minute limit; no terminal Watch result | API: build succeeded09:51:20, Watch began10:29:03, cancelled11:24:18. Build succeeded05:12:43.739; phone boot05:13:03.011–05:14:29.447 (~86.4s). Watch bootstatus finished05:24:05.062. Complete job04:03:22–05:32:40 =89m18s. [Artifact14400779226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44049787925/artifacts/14400779226) contains full logs/results. |

Not green whole-job proof. |
