prs.title: feat(agents): hide picker-hidden agents from user-facing pickers
prs.body:
Related: #166678

## What Problem This Solves

Internal worker agents must be configured as full `agents.entries` entries to stay spawnable as `sessions_spawn` targets, so every user-facing agent picker (sidebar roster, agent switcher, New Session target picker) lists agents that are never meant to be chatted with directly. The only way to remove one from the picker today is to delete its entry, which breaks spawning.

## User Impact

Operators can set `agents.entries.<id>.picker.hidden: true` to keep those agents out of chat-facing agent pickers and switchers. Hidden agents remain valid `sessions_spawn` targets and stay listed by `openclaw agents list`, marked `(hidden)`. Administrative and automation surfaces keep them selectable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the config flag proposed in #166678. The UI distinguishes the two roster predicates: `listSelectableAgents` and `findSelectableAgent` remain the administrative/automation projection (system rows only), while chat-facing surfaces use the new `listChatAgents`/`chatAgentsList` helpers (`kind === "system"` and `hidden` excluded). That fixes the first review's Settings finding: `SettingsAgentSelector` still offers picker-hidden agents for management. Docs state the scope as the Control UI and the TUI `/agents` picker; native apps (macOS, iOS) do not yet consume this flag. The follow-up round (head `e736f2bda`) added TUI picker filtering, dock-Home resolution for hidden selections, and the roster-mode/default-agent doc notes.

## Evidence

**Visual proof** (agent switcher, `scout` with `picker.hidden: true`):

Mocked dev UI (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`, Chromium). Before — switcher rows `[Show all, Molty, Forge, Scout, Bloom]`:

![Control UI switcher before (mock)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce6ed333-9be2-485b-ad02-68a594270dd9)

After — `[Show all, Molty, Forge, Bloom]`: Scout gone, no other change:

![Control UI switcher after (mock)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48f7da5f-e042-4b39-9ec1-eb2b98d2e732)

Real Gateway (same head, `node ./dist/index.js gateway --port 19900`, loopback, isolated state — full evidence in the [real-Gateway proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194575#issuecomment-6707068779)):

Switcher without `picker.hidden` (Scout listed):

![Real Gateway switcher before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2222fc31-fb3f-41f8-8b08-f5a8368c5842)

Switcher with `picker.hidden: true` (Scout hidden):

![Real Gateway switcher after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f881e6e9-2780-49af-ad1d-eb987d55812c)

**Real-Gateway New Session and Settings proof** (loopback gateway on this head, isolated state, `scout.picker.hidden: true`; a second visible agent was added so the New Session selector renders):

New Session target picker — the AGENTS list shows Main Agent and Bloom Helper; Scout Worker is absent:

![Real Gateway New Session picker with Main Agent and Bloom Helper, Scout Worker absent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5fcde6f-cd84-470a-88a0-80562b23d08a)

Redacted live output from the same run (token omitted):

```text
NS_MENU_LINES=["Main Agent","Main Agent","AGENTS","Main Agent","Bloom Helper"]
NS_SCOUT_ABSENT=true
```

Settings agent selector (administrative) — on the same real Gateway the hidden Scout Worker remains listed and selectable:

![Real Gateway Settings selector with Main Agent, Bloom Helper, and Scout Worker present](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd5ccb45-92c3-46e0-8f19-78667367882b)

```text
SETTINGS_MENU_LINES=["Main Agent","Main Agent","Bloom Helper","Scout Worker","AGENTS & TOOLS"]
SETTINGS_SCOUT_PRESENT=true
```

**Follow-up round surfaces (head `e736f2bda`):**

TUI `/agents` picker — real gateway (`ws://127.0.0.1:19900`, `agents.entries.scout.picker.hidden: true`); only `main (Main Agent)` is listed, Scout Worker absent:

![TUI agent picker listing only main; picker-hidden Scout Worker absent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52171270-2aa5-4331-b7c6-667e231a1096)

Control UI dock Home with a picker-hidden selection — Scout's non-main session open while the dock Home resolves to the hidden agent (dock composer reads "Message Scout"); the switcher excludes Scout:

![Control UI dock Home targeting the hidden Scout agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/389698b0-ea57-4910-bd6a-82a8a53fd069)

These surfaces are additionally covered by the red-on-base test proofs listed above.

**Focused tests**, all green on this head:

- `src/config/zod-schema.agents.test.ts` — accepts `picker.hidden`, rejects unknown picker keys / non-boolean values, and asserts the default stays visible when omitted
- `src/gateway/session-utils.picker-hidden.test.ts` — projection carries `hidden: true` for hidden agents, omits it for visible agents, and legacy rosters without `picker` still project
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-models-skills.test.ts` — `AgentSummarySchema` accepts `hidden`, rejects a non-boolean flag
- `src/commands/agents.commands.list.test.ts` — text output marks `- worker (hidden)` while JSON keeps the row
- `ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts` — `listSelectableAgents` keeps picker-hidden rows for administration; `listChatAgents` excludes them; `findSelectableAgent` still resolves hidden agents so existing sessions stay reachable
- `ui/src/components/settings-sidebar.test.tsx` — Settings switcher still offers a picker-hidden agent and selects it
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-navigation-logic.test.ts` — the sidebar switcher excludes picker-hidden agents while a hidden agent's existing session stays resolvable by id

Follow-up round (head `e736f2bda`), each red on base and green with the fix:

- `src/tui/tui-agent-selector.test.ts` (new focused file) — the TUI `/agents` picker excludes a picker-hidden worker from its items
- `src/tui/tui-session-actions.test.ts` — `hidden` survives roster normalization in `applyAgentsResult`
- `ui/src/components/assistant-panel.test.ts` — dock Home resolves a hidden selected agent instead of falling back (`expected 'main' to be 'worker'` without the fix)

**Targeted gates** (`pnpm check:changed` on the follow-up head): typecheck (core, core tests, UI), lint, format, config docs baseline, dead export scan, and all ratchets pass; only `changelog attributions` fails, pre-existing on clean `main` (historical `CHANGELOG/*` bot thanks, untouched here). Line-cap ratchet OK against canonical `main` (no over-cap growth in the three pre-existing over-cap TUI files — the new test lives in a sibling file for that reason). `pnpm build` exits 0 locally.

The config surface deliberately grew by 2 (the new key), so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.{counts.json,sha256}` are regenerated in this PR per the config-surface bar. Test-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/194280-picker-hidden.txt` records exactly this change's net test growth (186 after the follow-up round); the shared scalar is unchanged.

**CI triage (head `2d580895a`, merge of current `main`):**

- `android-access-native (4096, google_apis)` (infra-killed on the prior head) **passes** on this head.
- `checks-node-changed` fails on `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.clone-identity.e2e.test.ts` ("sessions.create fences clone Git effects when its identity is allowed"). Reproduced with the identical assertion on merged `main` alone (`6091f622f`) in an isolated worktree — pre-existing/inherited, named here per the landing policy. No change in this PR touches git-identity fencing.
- `control-ui-performance`: `/new` boot JS gzip main `803,216 B` → head `803,504 B` (+288 B, CI Node 24) against committed cap `803,364 B` — `main` itself sat only 148 B under the cap. Module attribution puts this PR's source delta at ~20 B standalone; the remainder is shared-chunk compression shift. `newBootJsGzipBytes` updated to `803_568` with the repo-standard measured comment (same treatment as #195865 +623 B and #196181 +386 B).
- `changelog attributions` continues to fail pre-existing on clean `main` (historical `CHANGELOG/*` bot thanks, untouched here).
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (`test-lines`): on CI's synthetic merge the ratchet requires the PR allocation to equal `total - base ceiling` exactly. At the measured run that value was 479 = +186 own test growth + **293 of `main`'s own un-pruned test-line debt** (main's tree is over its ceiling without this PR; the debt grew from 71 to 293 within ~35 minutes). The allocation tracks this figure; the underlying debt is main-side and clears on the next baseline prune.
- The `Security High` / `Critical Quality` / `Scan changed paths` failures in the07:2x UTC window were `API rate limit exceeded for installation` during SARIF upload — all scans completed their analysis; the failures are GitHub App rate-limit infra, unrelated to the diff (a `.txt` allocation change was the only delta between the green and red scan runs).

No failure points at the changed contract.

### Data-model compatibility proof (latest stable → this head)

Isolated run: `npm` latest stable = **OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf)**, fresh state dir, old-shape config with no `picker` key (entries `main` + `scout`; `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` isolated, loopback token auth; token redacted from outputs):

1. Stable created `agent:main:main` on that state — `openclaw sessions list --all-agents` printed `Sessions listed: 1`.
2. This head's build against the same config and state:
   - `agents list`: agent rows byte-identical to the stable output (diff clean once CLI banners are stripped).
   - `sessions list` first refused with the sanctioned migration instruction — `agent database ... uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 41` — touching no data.
   - `openclaw doctor --fix` on this head: `Doctor complete`, exit 0. Config preserved — entries, names, descriptions, model, and gateway auth unchanged; only standard bookkeeping added (`wizard.lastRun*`, `meta.lastTouchedVersion` + `meta.migrations`, plugin enablement flags).
   - `openclaw sessions list --all-agents` after migration: `Sessions listed: 1` with `agent:main:main` unchanged (model `gpt-5.4`, same flags).
   - Gateway restarted on the migrated state: HTTP 200 within ~15 s; a follow-up `openclaw doctor` exits 0 with zero error lines.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): attribute provisioning reflink fallbacks
prs.body:
Related: #200845.

## What Problem This Solves

When included worktree files fall back from reflinks to byte copying, the preparation log counts the copies but cannot identify the source category or error. Older GNU coreutils reports the same `unsupported` text for cross-device and incompatible btrfs-policy failures.

## User Impact

Operators can correlate the first fallback with its actual source checkout and top-level directory using bounded hashes, and distinguish common errno classes. Provisioning selection, symlink rejection, contents, timestamps, and preserve-existing behavior stay the same. This change diagnoses fallback; it does not claim reduced copying or fix an unconfirmed filesystem cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

The copier receives one resolved source checkout, which need not be the canonical Git repository. It admits regular files with `O_NOFOLLOW`; `cp -L` follows only the pinned procfs descriptors. Unanchored includes can select dependencies below nested artifact directories, and nested mounts are allowed. Changing symlink handling or discarding caches would change provisioning correctness without evidence.

The first fallback now records 16-character SHA-256 hashes of the source checkout and relative top-level component. Explicit reports classify `EOPNOTSUPP`, `EINVAL`, or `EXDEV`; missing errno remains `unknown`. For the older `unsupported` report only, the existing small helper makes one clone-only attempt into private staging using the same pinned source. A separate probe errno avoids claiming a retry proves the original failure. No second byte copy, new configuration, cache, schema, source walk, or per-file probe is introduced.

## Evidence

Acceptance: existing 65,880-file / 1.647 GB synthetic dependency fixture on scratch btrfs, with four dependency groups bind-mounted from tmpfs and file/directory symlinks pointing off-filesystem. A/A controls and five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs; identical counts, bytes, modes, nanosecond timestamps, independent writes, and symlink skips; no >20% wall/CPU/allocation regression. Timings cover the copy owner, not Gateway/session preparation.

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy owner wall (s) | 3.967 / 4.031 | 3.722 / 4.732 |
| CPU, parent + children (s) | 3.850 / 3.969 | 3.657 / 4.394 |
| V8 sampled allocation (MB) | 303.184 / 311.597 | 296.510 / 306.430 |

Five interleaved pairs, warm source and fresh destination; p95 is nearest-rank (the maximum with n=5). Each sample starts after a btrfs transaction sync outside the timed region and after our local compiler/review scans finished. A/A wall controls: 3.489/4.222 s. Each run confirms 47,244 cloned files / 1,181,100,000 logical bytes and 18,636 copied files / 465,900,000 bytes, with all 65,880 files verified and both off-filesystem symlinks skipped. All candidates report the expected first-fallback root/prefix hashes and separate `EXDEV` probe. Destination extents remain 534,331,392 exclusive / 1,354,579,968 shared bytes (block-rounded).

The wall p95 rose 17.4%, while median wall/CPU/allocation fell; this meets the predeclared <20% regression threshold and is not a speedup claim. An earlier series overlapped compiler/reviewer source scans and failed median acceptance (wall 6.222→8.542 s; maxima 14.086→11.486 s). It was retained as a rejected, contended measurement; the separate series controls those known confounders. CPU profiles identify filesystem calls/child waits as the remaining cost. Focused local tests passed (15 tests, 8 Linux skips; 66.33 s wrapper wall, test bodies under one second). Real Linux owner smoke and the full fixture cover the native copy path. Two independent Codex reviews found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

`pnpm check:changed`: all gates passed except dead-export scanning. The same 11 distinct findings reproduce on the untouched parent `819d09be7ce7ed230fd41a02cc307853fe2c9243`. These are main regressions, not ignored failures: #200533 (`703c82d20c5cb`) left `prepareSessionEventDelivery` exported after moving its caller into the same module and added internal `DurablePilotInput`/`DurablePilotCustody` exports; #193550 (`2b7950cae3c39`) added unused model-request hook exports; #198455 (`bd1c54cfde534`) added four unused metric-type exports; #200817 (`14b9fc3c8d945`) added `formatDays` and left `selectSegmented` exported after moving external calls behind its new helper. No failing owner is changed here.

Production delta: +41 lines. The growth supplies bounded attribution and a single clone-only diagnostic because the existing report cannot recover a discarded errno. No copying reduction is claimed.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/worktree-provisioning-copy-measure.ts --dependencies --symlink-target /absolute/synthetic/file`, bundled baseline/candidate owners, and separate destinations. After seeding, bind-mount synthetic `next`, `lucide-react`, `es-toolkit`, and `@babel` groups from tmpfs below `source/node_modules`; use `--profile` for CPU and sampled allocation profiles. No production data is needed.

The updated parser regression fails against the original owner (3 failures for missing attribution, 2 legacy/incomplete-report passes). Local Linux smoke distinguishes same-policy btrfs cloning, tmpfs→btrfs `EXDEV`, and NOCOW→COW btrfs `EINVAL`. Both fallback cases report `unsupported` with coreutils 9.7 before the diagnostic probe. Focused platform tests retain skip/authority/metadata/independent-copy coverage.

prs.title: fix: shorten sandbox pauses when retrying PR refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retrying a PR workspace refresh with many partially staged files keeps the sandbox paused while checking each file with a separate Git subprocess. The repeated checks also run the publication and workspace authority guards for every command.

## User Impact

Refresh recovery can verify existing staged work while the guest keeps running. Exact staged paths, modes and object IDs remain checked, and first-time PR imports retain their pristine-workspace check.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing bounded Git pathspec batches instead of one subprocess per entry. Resume after settlement for refresh/recovery; the synchronization owner still captures and fences projection writes. Keep composed prepared-effect authority and the existing reconciliation/recovery owners. No new cache, configuration, protocol or schema.

The focused run also found an inherited test-observer defect from #200828: speculative prehash scans were counted as captures in three sandbox-layout cases. It reproduces on the exact parent; #200896 independently landed the same correction. This branch now uses that exact observer condition, allowing the pristine-content assertions to execute.

## Evidence

The registered-action regression fails on the parent because ORIG_HEAD verification sees a paused guest. It passes after the fix and preserves a guest write made during verification, including exact staged entries with spaces, brackets, tabs, newlines and colons where supported.

79 focused cases pass across preparation, refresh, acquisition and base-refresh action coverage (76 in the full run, then the three corrected inherited cases). `pnpm check:changed` passed; final changed-file lint passed. Independent Codex autoreview through P2 is clean. No Control UI runtime imports changed.

Performance acceptance, fixed before the comparison: native Git and the registered action, synthetic GitHub/container I/O, 62,000 baseline files (~1.1 GB), a ~35 GB synthetic agent database and 4,000 partially staged recovery entries. Two baseline controls, then five interleaved A/B pairs; separate CPU/allocation profiles. Measure owner wall, total/longest requested guest pause, longest synchronous callback, main CPU, allocation and Git command counts. Require fewer per-entry commands and shorter paused Git-state work, with no 20% regression in wall/CPU/allocation/longest callback; control spread is context, not a waiver. Verify host tree, guest contents and final index every sample. APFS owner measurements do not establish native btrfs or live Gateway transport latency.

All twelve unprofiled runs passed full preservation checks. The two unchanged controls paused for 95.6–109.3 s and took 115.3–130.7 s overall. Five interleaved samples per arm on Node 26.12.1 give:

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 [range] | Candidate median / p95 [range] | Median change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Owner wall (s) | 83.007 / 191.715 [56.879–191.715] | 16.533 / 19.522 [13.780–19.522] | -80.1% |
| Total pause (s) | 72.015 / 171.880 [49.355–171.880] | 7.566 / 9.065 [6.486–9.065] | -89.5% |
| Longest pause (s) | 71.967 / 171.486 [49.320–171.486] | 7.512 / 8.984 [6.446–8.984] | -89.6% |
| Longest callback (ms) | 62.364 / 332.357 [47.262–332.357] | 10.587 / 37.393 [3.444–37.393] | -83.0% |
| Main CPU (s) | 28.823 / 33.631 [21.328–33.631] | 0.806 / 1.028 [0.646–1.028] | -97.2% |
| Process CPU (s) | 52.713 / 75.153 [34.106–75.153] | 16.961 / 19.174 [14.022–19.174] | -67.8% |
| Main allocated (MB) | 7767.519 / 7810.890 [7754.565–7810.890] | 202.773 / 206.535 [199.913–206.535] | -97.4% |

No measured median or p95 regressed by 20%; with five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum. Median paused Git state falls 62.81 s → 46.5 ms. Native ls-tree commands fall 4,000 → 32 (all candidate calls unpaused); lease-current checks fall 16,085 → 212. Main/process CPU excludes native Git child CPU on macOS.

prs.title: fix(sessions): title sessions opened with slash-prefixed task text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveSessionTitleSource` discarded every first message starting with `/`, so sessions opened with a pasted path (`/tmp/notes.md summarise this file`) or a free-form command (`/explain how DNS resolution works`) never received a title.

The selector now distinguishes, in order:

- **Registered skill command** — unchanged: its arguments title the session; a bare command stays titleless.
- **Canonical control command** — full-runtime callers pass `isControlCommandMessage` (the chat-command registry contract from `src/auto-reply/command-detection.ts`) via a new optional predicate, so `/new`, `/reset`, `/status`, `/model …`, `/steer …`, abort triggers, and config-disabled commands all stay titleless.
- **Unregistered slash text** (pasted paths, free-form commands) — the de-slashed text titles the session, only when both a skill registry and the control predicate are supplied. Metadata-free consumers (`deriveGoalSessionTitle`, Doctor's persisted missing-title repair) and extracted wrapper contexts keep the legacy titleless contract, so a registered bare `/code-review` stored in an old transcript cannot turn into a `code-review` title there.

The predicate injection (rather than importing command-detection into the selector) keeps the trusted-anchor wrapper closure unchanged — that module's runtime closure is ~1.5k files and cannot join `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`; ownership of control detection stays with `command-detection.ts`.

`prepareDashboardSessionTitle` routes slash-prefixed messages through the registry first via `needsSkillCommandsForSessionTitle` (mirroring the selector's metadata stripping), preserving lazy skill loading for plain text — including date-prefixed `/skill <name> <args>` invocations.

Closes #192031

## Evidence

**Regression suites** (red first: the slash-text cases below failed against main, reproducing the issue's examples exactly):

- `src/sessions/session-title-source.test.ts`: skill-aware matrix (paths, free-form, `/status` `/model` `/steer` controls, bare slash, registered skill with/without args) plus the metadata-free legacy contract.
- `src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts`: a leading-slash path message reaches the title-generator boundary with source `tmp/notes.md summarise this file`; all existing cases pass, including lazy skill-loading counts, date-prefixed `/skill` invocations, persisted display-name preservation, and the transport suite's `/status` non-titling expectation that failed on the first revision of this PR.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/sessions/session-title-source.test.ts src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts` — 53/53 green.

**Real Gateway + real provider proof** (2026-11-15, PR head `3688e5d3bc`):

- Built the PR head and ran it as an isolated Gateway with synthetic state. The completion path used real DeepSeek models (`deepseek-v4-flash` utility and `deepseek-v4-pro` primary), not a stub or mocked completion. Credentials were read from the local provider config and are not included in this evidence.
- The installed 2026.11.3 Gateway was run with the same provider configuration as the base control. Ordinary text produced `DNS troubleshooting task summary`; the two slash-task inputs below produced `null`.
- PR `sessions.title.prepare` over the real Gateway WebSocket:

```text
Summarize a DNS troubleshooting task       -> "DNS troubleshooting task summary"
/tmp/notes.md summarise this file          -> "Summarize notes.md file"
/explain how DNS resolution works          -> "How DNS resolution works"

```

```text
  -> displayName="How DNS resolution works", hasActiveRun=false

```

- The real persistence proof passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/pr194557-real-title-proof.test.ts` (1/1 test, real provider completion).
- Worktree allocation is unchanged and is not claimed as fixed here: titleSource-only creation without an initial turn retained the existing short-name allocation for both plain and slash input in a control run. This PR's proof covers draft preparation and ordinary persisted Dashboard naming.

**Data-model compatibility**: the selector only runs at title-generation time; stored `displayName` values are read verbatim and never re-derived (existing "skips a persisted display name" suite). No schema or stored-shape change; existing sessions keep their names after upgrade.

prs.title: fix: stop telling group members to fix the gateway's model setup
prs.body:
Closes #201001
Related: #167341

## What Problem This Solves

When a gateway's own model provider fails (missing API key, expired login, billing, rate limit, outage), the reply in a group or channel tells the reader to fix provider setup: "Run `openclaw doctor --fix`", "open Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`", "Check your account's credit balance", or "Send `/login openai`". Everyone in the room gets that text, including people who do not run the gateway and cannot act on it. A public support bot running a stock gateway shows this to people asking for help, and they read it as a problem with their own install.

## User Impact

When a channel has a configured owner (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`), a group or channel member there who is not an owner now gets "⚠️ This assistant is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later." when the gateway's provider fails. When the provider gives a rate-limit reset time, the reply says "Please try again after <time>." instead. Owners, direct chats, senders whose ownership is unknown, channels without a configured owner, CLI timeouts and stops, and failures that are not about the provider keep today's text. The gateway log still records the cause.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each turn already knows whether the sender is an owner (`senderIsOwner`). Both reply paths for a failed run (the turn error handler and the outer run error path) now check it before any provider-specific copy. The neutral reply needs all of: `senderIsOwner === false`, an owner configured for the sender's channel (resolved the same way command auth does, so wildcards and other channels' entries do not count), and a group or channel chat. Without such an owner every sender reads as a non-owner, the operator included, so those channels keep today's text.

A provider failure here means a failover reason of `auth`, `auth_permanent`, `billing`, `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `server_error`, `route_unavailable`, `tls_certificate` or `model_not_found` on the error, an earlier fallback attempt that failed on billing or credentials, or a missing-key, OAuth refresh, removed CLI credential or auth-profile failure in the error's cause chain. Timeouts are not in the list, so a non-owner gets the same timeout message as the owner, including its "some work may have completed" warning. CLI timeouts and CLI terminal stops are also excluded when an earlier fallback attempt failed on billing or credentials, for the same reason. The reset time comes only from a provider rate-limit reset more than a minute away, formatted with the operator's saved locale and time zone like the existing rate-limit copy.

The turn error handler logs `Embedded agent failed before reply: <error>` before it returns the neutral reply, so the operator still sees why.

Maintainer decision: group chats show provider failure copy to every sender today. This changes it for known non-owners on gateways with an owner list.

## Evidence

Real Gateway run (QA Lab: isolated Gateway, qa-channel, mock provider returning HTTP 503 after a tool call, sender `alice` in a channel):

- Non-owner, base: `⚠️ The model provider returned a temporary internal error before replying. Try again in a moment, or switch to another model if it keeps happening.`
- Non-owner, head: `⚠️ This assistant is temporarily unavailable. Please try again after Nov 18, 2026, 3:47 AM UTC.` (the time comes from the mock provider's Retry-After)
- Owner (`provider-http-503-visible-failure` with `alice` as owner), head: passes with the provider copy, one reply, no tool replay.

Turn-level checks, with a Discord channel context and an owner configured: a non-owner gets the neutral reply for a missing API key, an expired login, a billing failure (also with a saved-login cooldown, which is not a retry time), a provider outage, and a billing failure followed by a fallback timeout. The gateway log gets the cause. A non-owner gets the reset time for a rate limit with a known reset. The owner in the same channel, a non-owner in a direct chat, unknown ownership, no owner, a wildcard-only owner list, an owner only on another channel, a provider request timeout (the non-owner gets exactly the owner's text), a run timeout, a fallback CLI timeout after an outage, an overload followed by a context overflow, and a non-provider failure keep today's text.

- Before the fix (fix reverted, tests present): 6 failed, 28 passed. The 6 failures are the behavior cases; the controls pass.
- With the fix: 34 of 34 pass, plus 85 tests in the direct consumers (`agent-runner-failure-reply`, `agent-runner-core`, `agent-runner-execution-terminal-failures`, `user-copy`, `command-auth.owner-default`).
- With only the ownership, owner and chat type check removed: 13 fail, so the tests guard that check.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format, line caps and import cycles pass for the changed files. The dead export scan fails on `SubagentRequesterWakeProgressChangedError` in a file this PR does not touch; it fails the same way on the base commit.
- Local ClawSweeper review (`--local-range` against the base) on the final head: patch is correct, no P0 to P2. Earlier rounds' findings are fixed, each with a regression test. Open P3, left on purpose: the reset time is formatted inline instead of reusing the rate-limit formatter in `src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts`. That file is at its 700-line cap (the line-cap ratchet rejected the shared helper), so sharing it means a new sibling module and touching the owner rate-limit copy, which is out of scope for this fix. The inline block uses the same date options, threshold and locale and time zone settings.
- The `provider-http-503-visible-failure` QA scenario now lists its sender as an owner, so it keeps checking the provider copy.

Gap: no live Discord account run; the Gateway run uses the QA channel and a mock provider.

<details>
<summary>Runtime output</summary>

QA Lab, `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario provider-http-503-visible-failure`, non-owner sender (owner line removed for this run only):

```text
base c05f52233d2: saw ⚠️ The model provider returned a temporary internal error before replying. Try again in a moment, or switch to another model if it keeps happening.
head 9793128c854: saw ⚠️ This assistant is temporarily unavailable. Please try again after Nov 18, 2026, 3:47 AM UTC.
```

Same scenario as committed (sender is an owner), head 9793128c854 (the last commit, c325c1dcb62, only adds a test; production code is the same):

```text

```

Before the fix, base c05f52233d2, `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-provider-failures.test.ts`:

```text

-   "text": "⚠️ This assistant is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.",
+   "text": "⚠️ Couldn't connect to OpenAI. Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then try again. If it still fails, open Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`.",

+   "text": "⚠️ Your model provider needs a new login. Send `/login openai` from a private chat or the OpenClaw app. Where shown, you can also select **Sign in**. You can also re-auth with `openclaw models auth login --provider openai` on the gateway.",

× provider failures seen by non-owners in shared chats > says the assistant is unavailable for a billing failure followed by a fallback timeout
+   "text": "⚠️ The AI service reported a billing problem. Check your account's credit balance and usage limits before trying again.",

+   "text": "⚠️ The model provider returned a temporary internal error before replying. Try again in a moment, or switch to another model if it keeps happening.",
× provider failures seen by non-owners in shared chats > names the provider's reset time without naming the provider
"⚠️ openai/gpt-5.5 is rate-limited. The provider says to retry in 26,343 days (Jan 1, 2099 at 3:00 PM UTC). Choose another model in the model picker, or configure Model fallbacks in Settings (`agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`)."
      Tests  6 failed | 28 passed (34)
```

With the fix, head c325c1dcb62, same command (34 of 34 pass; the non-owner cases):

```text

✓ provider failures seen by non-owners in shared chats > keeps the completed-work warning when a run times out
✓ provider failures seen by non-owners in shared chats > gives a non-owner the owner's copy when the provider request times out
✓ provider failures seen by non-owners in shared chats > keeps the completed-work warning when a fallback times out after a provider outage
✓ provider failures seen by non-owners in shared chats > keeps the final failure's copy after an earlier transient provider failure
✓ provider failures seen by non-owners in shared chats > keeps failures that are not about the provider

```

prs.title: fix: avoid repeated state hashing during Doctor admission
prs.body:
Related: #198218

Thanks to @gregb100 for tracing the admission-reader cost path, and to the earlier reporters on #198218 for the timelines.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor repair and update activation can repeatedly inspect the same unchanged state database, spending minutes without a progress line on large installations. Hash reuse currently stops working outside a maintenance scope or when Doctor changes scope.

## User Impact

Repeated Doctor and update admission checks reuse an unchanged database hash. Each check still enforces ownership, quarantine, schema and update-run admission; writes, WAL changes and database replacement still invalidate reuse. No schema, protocol or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Content hashes describe the physical database, not the ambient maintenance-scope object. The existing owner now retains one current observation per canonical path, guarded by the existing DB/WAL/journal device, inode, size and nanosecond timestamp fingerprint. Admission assertions and before/after metadata observations are unchanged.

Cold reads still make an artifact-preserving copy. Removing it could change SQLite sidecars before capture, so that optimization is deferred.

## Evidence

Two real Doctor-admission regressions count actual hashing workers against isolated synthetic state. Both fail on base `ff216927e47`: 10 hashes without a scope and 7 across Doctor's real owner/repair scopes, versus one hash each with this change. These are work-count results, not large-database timing measurements.

All 35 focused tests pass, including existing write/replacement/quarantine/schema/capture/continuation and artifact-preservation cases. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Independent local review found no P0–P2 findings.

Not yet run: installed `doctor --fix` on a large database and a latest-stable upgrade. The separate idle `ep_poll` stall in #198218 is not reproduced or claimed fixed; the issue remains open.

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep claude-cli replies after a session reset or an interrupted run
prs.body: Closes #195856 Related: #164293, #166511 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: with the `claude-cli` backend, replies sent before the final message vanish after a CLI session rotation, or after a run is killed or fails. ## User Impact User impact: completed user-addressed replies remain in the conversation after a session reset. Text from an interrupted run remains visible, marked "Interrupted". Yielded progress remains progress; scheduled execution prose retains its audit-only policy. ## Why This Change Was Made Previously, only the final reply was durable; earlier replies depended on the currently bound Claude log. This change buffers the latest revision per native UUID and persists it when the next assistant record arrives or the process ends. Writes retain normal preparation hooks and ownership checks. Final settlement deduplicates by native identity and awaits queued writes, including on failure. The change works with commentary streaming enabled or disabled. #164293 covers commentary-enabled persistence; #166511 covers a watchdog interruption slice. Settlement uses a closed assistant-metadata operation: content, identity, timestamps, topology and replay inputs cannot change. It preserves the account-bound history generation and returns the current anchor without relaxing generic rewrite invalidation. Current native login is attested before a snapshot append; foreign or unattested credentials still cannot authorize history coverage. ## Evidence ### November 18 conflict-repair update — `51bc1056a612` Updated against main `b609d22c129f2944c1abaec1d2895eb659493a36`, preserving the newer transcript-lease and stopped-first-session recovery behavior. - Held replies arriving without snapshot callbacks now use the same native-keyed settlement writer as streamed snapshots. Both paths retain each answer once, including transformed output and a final interim result. The separate recursive interim writer and its identity helper were removed. - Three held-history cases failed after a mechanical merge (one saved answer instead of two), then passed after reconciliation. The existing history matrix now also exercises streamed snapshot deduplication. - Independent review identified three P2 cases: saved commentary trimming an unrelated answer, an unterminated final revision losing to an earlier snapshot, and delivered-failure recovery skipping settlement. Seven regression cases failed before their repairs, including confirmed progress (`final: false`) delivery; matching mirrors are hidden without promoting progress into completed-answer evidence. - Repaired runner/parser/chat-consumer checks: **217 passed, 3 skipped** across 10 files (86.64 s). Final parser/framing/budget/reasoning/persistence checks: **229 passed, 3 skipped** across 8 files (54.67 s). The final progress/final delivery correction passed 90 tests (3 skipped) across history, transcript, and settlement suites (66.49 s). These selections overlap and are not additive totals. - Core and UI typechecks, targeted format/lint, `git diff --check`, and exact-base max-lines/test-lines ratchets passed. The test allocation is 860 lines beyond the ordinary 400-line allowance, covering native identity/settlement and the held-reply/commentary/terminal-revision/delivered-failure regressions. Whole-change net delta against this base: +831 production lines and +1,260 test lines. Stream framing and budget accounting now live together in the existing stream-limits owner, with unchanged limits, keeping the parser within its file-size cap. - **Independent review:** User-authorized, separate read-only source review covered the candidate against the stated base and the subsequent repair deltas. Three P2 findings were reproduced and corrected; the same reviewer confirmed all findings resolved. This was source inspection, not an independent test rerun. Native autoreview was unavailable: its bounded attempt timed out after 180 seconds without a report; no clean autoreview result is claimed. - **Proof limits:** the live Claude/Control UI and stable-upgrade evidence below is retained evidence from the stated earlier revisions, not a new live run of this update. Current-head hosted CI must be read separately; no prior-head result is represented as a current-head pass. ### Earlier implementation evidence - Native Claude CLI steering: three accepted steers (A/B/C), with one `DONE: STEER-A, STEER-B, STEER-C` live and after reload. Narration stays between the steers. - Stable upgrade from v2026.11.3: Doctor migrated schema 27 → 42. Old history loaded before the next turn; Claude recalled the seed and produced one settled reply, preserved once after reload. The durable reply has `stopReason: "stop"` and nonzero usage. - Hook visibility: two snapshot-persistence/stranding regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward, covering explicit `display: false` and `display: true`. - Steering and history/stream consumers: 79 tests passed. Saved-prefix replay, whitespace, foreign-run isolation, and idempotent reconciliation are covered. - Chat-entry gzip diagnostic: 132,226 B before and after the state-owner projection change (+0 B). - Pruned redundant saved-stream adapters and unused cached prefix state without changing reconciliation behavior; exact-head [control-ui-performance passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43852886496/job/133250595655). Final live settlement and after reload: ### Prior live-proof head `9bc5ccf5489`: Stop retention, native replacement, single narration Throwaway proof Gateway built at the exact head (buildstamp `9bc5ccf5489`, clean inputs), driven through the real Control UI with the `claude-cli` backend: - **Stop before flush:** a ~120-word story was streamed as visible text, then Stop was pressed while a `sleep 60` tool was pending. The story remains visible exactly once, marked "Interrupted", both live and after a full page reload; no tool card or error banner is left behind. - **Native replacement:** the next turn (`REPLACEMENT-OK-196092`) settles as a new assistant message; the interrupted story is retained exactly once, live and after reload. - **Single narration:** a 6-step narrate-then-tool run showed each `Narration N` line exactly once while streaming; the final accumulated assistant message contains each of the six lines exactly once (192 chars), with no duplicated narration live or after reload. - **Budget:** paired chat boot +222 B vs the merge base, 187 B under the CI cap; `control-ui-performance` and the max-lines ratchet are green at this head. - **CI:** the only red check is `checks-node-changed-compact-large-11-1` — 7 tests in `run.prepared-harness-source-delivery.integration.test.ts` failing with the `run-loop.ts:501 .providerOutcomes` TypeError introduced by main #200073. The identical 7 failures reproduce on the pure merge base `30e9d3ee295` (local attribution run); this PR touches no `embedded-agent-runner` files. Inherited from main, not caused by this change. Stop retention (live, then after reload): Native replacement (live, then after reload): AI-assisted: implementation and validation with Claude and GPT agents. Original PR author: @Marvinthebored. The work-session link below records the November 18 PR update. ## Work sessions Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public. - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/67a23b12-5823-42b8-9aff-a9c829b2b8d8) ### Round 5 (head `267a360d9d7`): source-reply delivery no longer hides distinct snapshots Addresses the 16 Nov ClawSweeper P2 (`cli-assistant-settlement.ts:146`). When a message tool delivers the source reply, settlement now marks `display:false` only on saved snapshots whose text matches a delivered source-reply body (the dispatch-owned mirror). Distinct earlier snapshots such as `Findings: BLUE-HERON-42` followed by a tool-delivered `Done` keep their prepared visibility. - New regression `keeps distinct snapshots visible when the message tool delivers a different reply`, plus the settlement matrix now asserts per-row visibility (mirrored `Answer` hidden, distinct `Progress` visible). Both fail on `9bc5ccf5489` (2 failed) and pass after the fix. - Acceptance: `cli-run-transcript.test.ts`, `cli-runner.history-ownership.test.ts`, `cli-session-history.segments.test.ts` pass; `tsgo:core`, oxlint/oxfmt, max-lines and test-lines ratchets clean. - Stop, native-replacement and narration paths are unchanged by this commit; the live proof above (exact-head `9bc5ccf5489`) still covers them.

prs.title: improve: reduce CPU and allocation during GitHub PR preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing an existing GitHub pull request repeatedly allocates the same session-target routing descriptor while revalidating publication authority before Git commands. Deeply delegated sessions amplify that avoidable work.

## User Impact

PR preparation does less main-thread work and allocates less memory. Authority revocation, lifecycle changes, cancellation and effect custody are still checked at every existing boundary. There is no configuration or storage migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the immutable routing descriptor inside its admitted-sharing owner, creating it on first use so absent-to-created sessions still work. This retains no authorization result and changes no Git step order. Production delta is +1 line; the retained descriptor replaces repeated normalization, alias-set construction and freezing.

The full O(1) authority path depends on the policy-revision contract in #182383 and its security-owner review. This PR does not introduce that API or skip live policy callbacks.

## Evidence

Ten interleaved A/B pairs and five A/A control pairs completed, excluding warm-ups. Workload: 4,000 changed entries, depth-16 delegated authority, a synthetic 35 GiB database, 10,000 sessions/runs, 2,000 role assignments and a 62,000-file workspace. All 34 preparations, including warm-ups, passed.

| Median per preparation | A/A arm 1 (n=5) | A/A arm 2 (n=5) | Paired A (n=10) | B (n=10) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU, ms | 6,887.177 | 6,387.107 | 6,107.378 | 5,992.966 |
| Peak 1 ms timer gap, ms | 149.599 | 133.965 | 135.668 | 128.046 |
| Timer-gap histogram p95, ms | 1.442815 | 1.361919 | 1.329663 | 1.352703 |
| Wall time, ms | 101,311.635 | 106,645.565 | 74,766.788 | 80,100.949 |

The predeclared acceptance rule requires B's median CPU to beat both A/A arms and paired A, median peak delay to lie within A's spread, and delay p95 not to regress. CPU improves 1.87% against paired A and beats both controls; nine of ten pairs use less CPU. Median peak delay improves 5.62%, within A's spread, with six improving pairs and four increasing pairs. There is no consistent peak regression.

**Owner-accepted tradeoff:** median delay p95 increases 23.04 microseconds (+1.73%), missing the literal acceptance criterion. Six of ten p95 observations increase; the median paired p95 delta is +10.752 microseconds. Median wall time is 7.13% higher. The first five pairs had +9.216 microseconds p95; five additional pairs were predeclared and all original observations remain in this combined analysis. No unfavorable pair was discarded. These results supersede the original one-pair timing conclusion. The owner explicitly accepted this tradeoff and directed landing after reviewing all ten pairs.

The timer gaps are an event-loop delay proxy, not exact synchronous task durations. Histogram p95 is summarized as the median of the per-action p95 values. Host load was recorded before and after every action but was not controlled: controls ranged 9.97–38.25, paired A 8.21–34.91 and B 8.32–31.78. Follow-up warm-up load reached 55.23; this was not a quiet or load-controlled campaign. No task-owned tests or checks ran alongside timed observations.

Separate full-shape allocation evidence for the same production patch shows cumulative sampled allocation 3,954,669,104 → 3,603,923,904 bytes (−8.87%), including roughly 354 MB removed from repeated target capture. This is a separate one-pair allocation campaign, not ten-pair allocation evidence or RSS. A separate small owner census records target captures 347,168 → 0 with every other measured predicate and Git-attempt count unchanged. This exercises the registered action with real authority owners, SQLite and local Git, with synthetic GitHub I/O on APFS; it is not a live Gateway or btrfs measurement. Exact per-owner CPU and longest synchronous-task duration were not attributed.

Existing source, sharing, operator, placement and admission proof passes. The preparation test now covers inherited sharing revocation after fetch and observes that no later host Git or sandbox command runs. Lifecycle rotation, replacement, archive, abort, role and linked-identity cases retain that assertion. The placement reservation owner separately proves rejection after placement retirement and stale claims after awaited verification; the non-adopting preparation fixture does not model a delegated placement handoff.

The nine requester/revocation cases pass with the corrected request-scoped fixture client. Codex reviews through P2 found no actionable issue. Initial CI caught a fixture type error, corrected in `1a025cd5e838124ee5ea8d6cda218b63e2201e7f`. Full `pnpm check:changed` passes, and [CI run 44238223662](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44238223662) is green at that exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. [ClawSweeper’s final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200965#issuecomment-6968275199) has zero findings and zero open checklist items. The owner has accepted the recorded performance tradeoff and directed landing.

Owner decision (verbatim):

delay p95 +23 µs (+1.73%) is within run-to-run noise at this sample count. Wall time +7.13% was measured under uncontrolled host load and contradicts the first pair (−22%), so it isn't attributed to the change. Accepted against: median CPU −1.87% beating both A/A controls, peak delay −5.62%, allocation −8.87% (~354 MB of captureSessionTarget churn per 4k-entry preparation removed). +1 production line; all live authority/lifecycle/effect checks retained; the full O(1) path is deferred to #182383.

prs.title: fix(macos): defer Local Network permission until discovery starts
prs.body:
Fixes #200364

## What Problem This Solves

Launching the macOS app can show the Local Network permission dialog before the Welcome screen, before users have chosen to start discovery.

## User Impact

Users can see Welcome without an early Local Network prompt. The permission request still appears when discovery starts. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Defer both hostname lookup and the caller's display-name expression until the existing discovery task runs. Direct remote-discovery refreshes use that same task, and repeated entry points do not duplicate it. Existing local-gateway filtering and cancellation stay in place.

The regression test checks that an inactive model neither evaluates its display-name expression nor remains retained after release.

## Evidence

- @daniel-lxs reports that a separate macOS VM built and tested this exact patch on `b60b11474606`: the macOS build passed, all **15/15 GatewayDiscoveryModelTests** passed, Welcome showed no Local Network prompt, and the prompt appeared only once discovery started.
- This publication session applied the supplied patch cleanly to `main` at `3460f61786013ff711efbcb6ce9a91fa003a178a`. Both resulting file hashes match the supplied patch. `git diff --check` passes.
- Completed `pr-simplify`; no further changes were needed. Hostname resolution now has one lifecycle owner instead of an eager initialization path plus discovery-time lookup. The complete change is +17/-7 production lines and +9/-2 test lines.
- **Auto Review could not complete.** The first attempt was stopped after stalling; the bounded retry failed without producing a report. @daniel-lxs explicitly authorized publication without independent review.
- **Not independently rerun here:** the macOS build, native tests, or VM flow. This Linux publication environment has no Swift toolchain; the local test launch failed with `swift: not found`. The VM evidence above is attributed to @daniel-lxs, not a claimed local rerun. Test wall time and CI duration are not available here.

## Contributor credit

Patch and macOS VM verification provided by @daniel-lxs.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's curated recommendations still list GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Qwen3.8 Max without their newly released successors.

## User Impact

After the next hosted catalog publication, providers serving GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.2 Astra, or Qwen4 Max can recommend them in the existing family positions. Providers serving only the predecessors keep their recommendations. All unrelated ordering remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the approved, eligibility-only successor additions: `gpt-6.2-sol` before `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.2-astra` before `gpt-6-astra`, and `qwen4-max` before `qwen3.8-max`. Retain every predecessor and all other entries.

[OpenAI's launch announcement](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-2-astra-sol/) confirms both GPT-6.2 API IDs. [Alibaba's announcement](https://www.alibabacloud.com/en/press-room/alibaba-unveils-qwen4-max?_p_lc=1) confirms Qwen4 Max availability and its Qwen3.8 Max predecessor. This is not a cross-family reranking or a claim of setting-matched benchmark superiority. Provider discovery, defaults, runtime implementation, and pricing are unchanged.

## Evidence

- All 32 focused tests pass across catalog publication, recommendation suggestions, and canonical model identity.
- Actual catalog projection selects each successor when both versions are served, retains predecessor-only support, ignores disabled or replaced successors, and preserves provider IDs.
- The list contains 36 unique canonical IDs, below the 200-entry limit. Removing only the three new IDs exactly reproduces the prior 33-entry list and ordering. JSON formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: fix(codex): plugin tool denies disable unrelated native apps
prs.body:
Related: https://community.openclaw.ai/t/denying-intent-disables-the-native-codex-github-plugin/423

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native Codex hosted apps disappearing when an agent denies OpenClaw-owned memory plugin tools such as Memory Core `intent`.

## User Impact

Users can deny the audited Memory Core, LanceDB, and Memory Wiki tools without losing unrelated native apps such as GitHub. The named tools remain denied. Unknown or unaudited tools, restrictive allowlists, wildcards, and mixed unsafe policies still isolate the native surface. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared harness policy now recognizes explicitly audited plugin tool identities from the existing configuration- and workspace-scoped manifest metadata, rather than requiring every safe deny to be a core tool. One owner resolves the known audited set for both restriction classification and native-enforcement projection. Manifest ownership alone never grants an exemption or tool execution.

The Codex audit covers the adjacent OpenClaw memory-store and wiki tool families, not just `intent`. An unrelated synthetic plugin regression proves that the mechanism is generic; undeclared and unaudited controls remain restricted. These stores and vaults are separate from Codex native memory and goals. No new state store, cache, permission setting, or plugin manifest field is introduced.

## Evidence

- Before the repair, the exact and normalized `intent` regressions fail because the native surface is restricted. The original seven sibling cases pass.
- Focused policy, environment, harness-selection, and prompt-prefix suites: 145 tests pass. After the final internal helper rename, the changed policy and prefix suites pass again: 31 tests. The expanded policy file uses under one second of test execution; the complete four-file command takes 108.66 seconds including compiler preparation. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Production core typecheck and the selected `agents-tools` test typecheck pass. Targeted core/Codex lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. The Codex lint route also prepares the SDK boundary declarations.
- Independent local Auto Review through P2 reports no actionable findings; this was a static review, not another test execution.
- The 93 net regression-test lines have an exact dedicated allocation. The aggregate test-line ratchet retains seven lines of inherited overage; it is not reported green. The contribution-guide source-wide extension inventory command refers to a file absent in this checkout; no new direct bundled-extension import is introduced.
- Native source inspected at Codex `rust-v0.164.0`, commit `6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`: `core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`, the dynamic-tool handler, `ext/goal/src/spec.rs`, and `ext/memories/src/tools/mod.rs`.
- Real macOS Gateway/Codex validation is now reported in [@jjjhenriksen’s completed retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6803150138), superseding the [fixture-blocked first attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6788842023). The results and limits are summarized below.

### Real Gateway/Codex behavior evidence

The local validator reports testing exact head `29503a892663d3be00392a59d08a9c0363a9e943` and separately built parent `086d2574a92e5d705b76615716d392e9de7e3ad1` on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node 24.22.1, and the explicitly selected Codex 0.164.0 executable. The fixture used a real disposable Gateway and existing owner-authorized hosted GitHub connection, not an API-key fallback or mock provider.

- **Allowed operations:** an actual Gateway-originated native `codex_apps.github.get_repo` call returned public `openclaw/openclaw` metadata. A real `intent.create` positive control succeeded through the native dynamic dispatcher and persisted an `armed` SQLite record. The positive control used `scope:"anywhere"` with sender scoping because that client entry point did not supply a separate conversation ID.
- **Base/head reproduction:** with only `intent` denied, the Gateway-created base thread returned `unknown MCP server 'codex_apps'` for the real read-only native GitHub RPC. On the fixed head, both a model-originated hosted GitHub call and the identical native RPC succeeded. A forwarding test-only stdio wrapper collected the unmodified Codex server’s RPC replies; it did not fabricate model/tool results or alter production policy/hooks.
- **Denied effects:** actual Gateway `tools.invoke` create/cancel attempts returned `Tool not available: intent`. Relevant full-row snapshots remained equal and no denied-marker intent records were created. The positive-control intent had automatically fired before the frozen comparison; its earlier transition is not credited to denied cancellation.
- **Tightening and resume:** the existing OpenClaw conversation continued under the deny on a safe successor native thread with working GitHub. Explicit reattachment of the old intent-capable thread was refused before inference by the existing Codex-home ownership/adoption guard, including with only `intent` denied; relevant records stayed unchanged.
- **Conservative control:** `deny:["intent","exec"]` again produced `unknown MCP server 'codex_apps'`; removing the `exec` deny restored the real hosted GitHub result.

**Coverage limits:** the retained-thread evidence is a restart/safe-successor plus explicit ownership-refusal case. The old app-server processes had terminated; it does **not** demonstrate revocation of a still-live captured callback after hot policy tightening. End-to-end coverage is for the Memory Core intent scenario and native-isolation control, not every LanceDB/Memory Wiki operation. This summary reviews the validator’s published observations; raw sanitized artifacts remain local to the validator and were not independently replayed here. The validator reports all task-owned Gateway/app-server processes stopped and disposable credentials/state removed, with the normal Gateway unchanged.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen requested the repair; Saul_Burgos supplied the original community report.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f6c2a127-d753-4253-88fe-554a758a194e)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

## What Problem This Solves

The shared PDF test fixture accepts an agent-directory argument that it never reads, obscuring where runtime directory facts come from.

## User Impact

No production behavior or public API changes. Existing authorization, requester, cancellation, resource-disposal and Windows file-URL assertions remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only the unused first parameter and its seven identifier arguments. The options object becomes first; async/await, tool-construction directories and the captured acquisition directory/config/workspace remain unchanged. No new fixture API, case or assertion.

## Evidence
