prs.title: fix(feishu): keep CardKit streaming alive past the ten-minute window
prs.body:
Related: #161350 (dispatcher-side settlement/deduplication; intentionally separate from this change)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Feishu streaming card freezes at its last snapshot and a second static card is posted when an agent turn runs longer than ten minutes.

Feishu CardKit closes a card's `streaming_mode` ten minutes after it was switched on. The next element write fails with `code=200850 card streaming timeout` and every later one with `code=300309 streaming mode is closed`. `FeishuStreamingSession` does not handle this, so the final text can never be written into the card, `closeWithResult` throws, and the reply dispatcher recovers with a second delivery.

## User Impact

User impact: long-running Feishu turns now finish in the same card they started in — no frozen preview, no duplicate card. Short turns (< 8 minutes) are unchanged apart from one `Date.now()` comparison per push. No configuration change and no new options.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Renew before expiry** — when a push happens 8 minutes or more after `streaming_mode` was switched on, toggle it `false → true` via `PATCH /cardkit/v1/cards/:id/settings`. This restarts the server-side timer and also re-opens a window the server already closed (same mechanism as larksuite/channel-sdk-node#21).
- **On 200850/300309** — renew once and retry the write; if renewal fails, mark the window closed and stop element writes instead of spamming (one production gateway logged 19,597 × `300309` in September).
- **Finalize without streaming** — at close, when the window is closed, land the final text and note with a full-card update `PUT /cardkit/v1/cards/:id` (`streaming_mode:false`, same header) and skip the streaming close. The returned `content` then equals the final text, so the dispatcher sends no recovery card. If the full-card update also fails, the existing `FeishuStreamingFinalizationError` path with the accepted preview content is unchanged.

Window helpers live in `streaming-card-window.ts` to keep `streaming-card.ts` under the `max-lines` limit.

## Evidence

**Live observation** (production gateway running `@openclaw/feishu@2026.9.3` with the same logic applied to the bundle; a controlled 11m20s turn — four `sleep 170` steps — crossed the server window):

```
16:04:26 [feishu] Started streaming: cardId=7691236156303166665, messageId=om_x100b64f8666…
16:19:04 [feishu] Renewed streaming window (age): cardId=7691236156303166665
16:19:30 [feishu] Closed streaming: cardId=7691236156303166665
16:19:30 [feishu] dispatch complete (queuedFinal=true, replies=1)
```

Zero `200850`/`300309` in the run; the chat shows one card with the four step lines, the final line and the footer. Before the change, the same gateway's journal shows every `200850` landing exactly 10:00 after `Started streaming` in 11 of 60 streaming turns, each followed by a frozen card plus a recovery card.

**Full-card fallback path, real Feishu API probe** (standalone script against CardKit, no gateway; same request shapes as the patch): create streaming card → two element writes OK → `PATCH settings streaming_mode=false` (simulates the server closing the window) → element write rejected with `code=300309` → `PUT /cardkit/v1/cards/:id` full card accepted with `code=0` → the chat shows the card with the final text and note (visual readback by the operator).

**Focused tests** (this branch):

- 4 new cases in `streaming-card.test.ts`: age-based renewal on the same card (two settings PATCHes then the write, sequence strictly increasing); re-opening a server-closed window and retrying the rejected write once; stopping element writes and finalizing via full-card update with header and note preserved and no streaming close afterwards; partial-visibility finalization error when both renewal and the full-card update are rejected.
- `streaming-card.test.ts` 34/34, `streaming-card.error-release.test.ts` 3/3, `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` 79/79.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on the three touched files.

Not changed here: the Feishu per-chat 300-second sequential-queue cap (#70133). It evicts a timed-out task from the queue without aborting it and is unrelated to the card window.

prs.title: fix: reduce sandbox pauses during workspace refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing a large sandbox workspace writes the same rollback journal for both the host checkout and guest projection, even though refresh recovery never consumes either copy. Preparation can also capture the whole workspace immediately after finishing a pending projection apply.

## User Impact

Large workspace refreshes do less SQLite work and keep guests running during materialization and patch preparation. Preparation skips the redundant capture when the existing unchanged probe confirms both trees still match the accepted result. Independent guest edits and real conflicts remain protected.

Final application still runs under the existing guest pause. This change does not introduce a whole-root swap: a native btrfs/Podman experiment shows that renaming the host root leaves the guest bind mount on the old tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

Base refresh already resumes from its durable pending Git receipt; that recovery contract predates this change. It now omits the unused persistent rollback journal and its publication copy. Ordinary checkpoints retain their durable journals, and live apply still keeps its rollback snapshot. Fresh refreshes can prepare immutable bytes while the guest runs; recovery of a partially applied refresh retains its pause.

The existing unchanged probe is shared by initial reuse and post-settlement preparation. Confirmed preflight also makes a second directory check unnecessary for ordinary modified files; new paths and directory replacements still get derived-child cleanup. No schema, configuration, or cache is added.

## Evidence

Three regressions fail against base `5cb4520c7e1d2d4ef519508c2c5dd091e446d789`: redundant journal serialization, redundant post-settlement capture, and redundant directory cleanup. Their candidate runs pass; the independent guest-edit case passes on both. Interrupted refresh recovery, rollback/conflict handling, and caller-stop behavior remain covered.

The affected suites passed 144 tests; two local scratch-capacity failures subsequently passed on adequate isolated storage. Two platform-specific cases were skipped on macOS. A native Podman guest pause/resume and btrfs rename/bind-mount proof also passed. All changed-file lint, format, typechecks and structural checks pass. `pnpm check:changed` remains red only for the two exact-parent export regressions named below. Full `pnpm build` passes, including declarations and UI assets. After retaining probe admission at its original boundary, all 93 projection tests pass (two expected macOS skips), as do the identity ratchet and targeted type/lint/format checks. Both native A/A/B comparisons are complete below. Final-head CI [44239787831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44239787831) passes at `c1c6e403e981521dd532be7828834cef7aece26d`.

Codex autoreview of the complete local change against the base above, including recovery and quiescence owners, is scoped-clean for P0–P2. No actionable findings remain.

Measurement acceptance: serial A/A/B on the same synthetic 62,000-file workspace, 22,795 incompressible changes, 10,001 sessions and 40.6 GiB of SQLite history. Expect two rollback-journal mutations on A and zero on B, unchanged accepted bytes, and no regression in owner wall time, CPU, allocation, or guest freeze. Native results are reported below.

Production LOC is +82, primarily to share the existing unchanged probe at the owner and preserve the distinction between fresh and partially applied refreshes. Recovery code moves to the existing checkpoint owner to stay within the file-size limit. No new production module or persisted state is introduced.

Related: #200917, #200828.

Main-parent check regressions: the production dead-export scan also fails on exact base `5cb4520c7e1d2d4ef519508c2c5dd091e446d789` for `describeSpawnAuth` (introduced by `0ca4e7d3db4b8`, #191324) and `ADVANCED_FIELDS` (introduced by `dce9dd13b53e5`, #200808). These are newly observed main regressions, recorded for their owners; neither file is changed here.

The earlier CI run [44236046486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44236046486) found the moved session-identity comparisons; those now remain at the original projection admission boundary, and the ratchet passes locally. It also found `cron-human-owner.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` waiting for `#cron-name` at line 342. That failure reproduces on exact parent `5cb4520c7e1d`: #200808 changes the default job view from settings to history, but this test still assumes the editor. The separate roster browser timeout did not reproduce locally and remains unattributed; it is not declared inherited.

The native harness now preserves its rootless engine home, explicitly uses `keep-id`, and asserts that reconciliation pauses its registered guest. Earlier samples with mismatched engine homes are excluded from pause comparisons. OpenClaw configuration and state remain isolated synthetic fixtures. Codex review of the admission repair and full measurement driver is scoped-clean for P0–P2.

## Native refresh A/A/B

Same synthetic fixture, serial fresh processes: 62,000 files, 22,795 changed files, 10,001 sessions, 43,563,536,384-byte agent database; Linux 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM, rootless Podman, btrfs loop filesystem over ext4. Candidate reopens the same database and projection written by the base. Every changed canonical/projection byte and subsequent guest read passes.

| Measurement | A1 | A2 | B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Durable refresh journals | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| Journal pack + JSON bytes | 315,252,714 | 315,252,714 | 0 |
| Guest paused | 107.954 s | 90.812 s | 18.383 s |
| Owner wall | 109.800 s | 92.717 s | 90.131 s |
| Owner process CPU | 65.008 s | 60.046 s | 57.801 s |
| Owner main-isolate allocation | 874.7 MB | 869.3 MB | 756.4 MB |

Guest heartbeat independently observed the baseline 107.9/90.8-second gaps; B's maximum gap was 10.5 seconds. Both B patch preparations ran unpaused. Its remaining pauses were initial refresh staging (10.5 s) and final confirmation/apply (7.8 s, including 3.3 s apply). Subsequent unchanged preparation paused zero times and wrote no journals in all arms.

The 80–83% pause reduction and journal elimination exceed the A/A spread. Wall time is noisy; this is not a precise production-latency forecast. Bytes are logical journal fields, not physical device writes. CPU excludes child processes; whole-VM counters are retained separately. Allocation is main-isolate V8 allocation, excluding worker heaps and native buffers. Warmup, correctness reads, and fixture reset are excluded from owner timing. The fixture projection is an ordinary directory on btrfs; the separate EXDEV experiment covers a subvolume root. Final-swap-only publication is not implemented here.

## Native pending-preparation A/A/B

The real preparation owner resumes a staged ordinary checkpoint interrupted before projection patch. Every arm applies exactly one 157,626,357-byte pack+JSON journal and verifies accepted bytes.

| Measurement | A1 | A2 | B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Guest paused | 11.071 s | 9.781 s | 8.516 s |
| Owner wall | 44.051 s | 40.622 s | 41.051 s |
| Owner process CPU | 30.911 s | 25.758 s | 26.103 s |
| Owner main-isolate allocation | 304.5 MB | 290.2 MB | 262.2 MB |
| Post-settlement paused capture | 1.353 s | 1.274 s | none |

The capture disappears while the ordinary checkpoint journal remains intact. Total pause falls 13–23%; candidate wall and CPU are within the A/A spread, so no wall-time speedup is claimed for this case. All six source manifests match their intended owner commits and the identical measurement harness.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep replies going when a native model catalog lookup times out (#198970)
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.ts:497,523` (`loadProviderScopedThinkingCatalog`) rethrew every selected native capability-read failure, so a Codex catalog scope timeout (`codex app-server request timed out`, from `account/read` + `model/list` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/model-catalog.ts`) ended reply preparation before the selected model or its configured fallbacks ran.

Fixes #198970
Related #192725 (same `account/read` timeout ending the turn before a reply; this PR lets that turn continue, while the report's requests for clearer failure copy and execution-state diagnostics stay open there)

## What Problem This Solves

Reply preparation reads the prepared runtime's native model catalog for thinking and input capabilities. When the Codex app-server is slow to answer that lookup (its `account/read` waits on ChatGPT workspace routing for up to 15 s; OpenClaw's discovery budget is 10 s), the lookup times out and the whole reply fails with "The request took too long", with no model run and no fallback attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadProviderScopedThinkingCatalog` is the one owner every reply, agent-command and cron path uses for these capability reads. Capability metadata is advisory at that point: the run itself still resolves and validates the model, and model setup already records native catalog failures and routes them into the normal fallback chain. Both branches now keep the owner's retained catalog when the native read times out (the admitted owner keeps this turn's captured facts; the published owner keeps its latest accepted catalog). Cancellations and every other lookup error still propagate. Timeouts are recognized with the existing failover classifier `isTimeoutError`.

Codex contract (openai/codex `7fb4014d52`): `account/read` is serialized on `global("account-auth")` and its workspace routing waits up to 15 s on `accounts/check` (`app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor/workspace_routing.rs`); `model/list` refreshes `OnlineIfUncached` (`catalog_processor.rs`). Neither has a server-side deadline shorter than OpenClaw's, so the OpenClaw scope deadline is the one that fires.

## Evidence

Full capture: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199039#issuecomment-6942776932

Real Gateway plus the real bundled Codex app-server (user-scope `CODEX_HOME` in a temp dir, ChatGPT auth fixture), with `openai_base_url`/`chatgpt_base_url` pointed at a local HTTPS fixture whose `accounts/check` stalls for the first 60 s and then recovers. Agent `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` on runtime `codex`, fallback `fixture/fallback-model`. One webchat `chat.send`.

- `main` `ff9b38134a5f`: `codex app-server scope timed out phase=client-request timeoutMs=10000`, then `message dispatch completed ... source=replyResolver outcome=error error="Error: codex app-server request timed out"`. The user sees "The request took too long". Neither the Codex responses endpoint nor the fallback provider receives a request.
- This PR: the same lookup timeout is logged, the turn continues (`model_resolution` -> `attempt_dispatch` -> `turn_accepted`), Codex posts to `/codex/responses` once the backend recovers, and the assistant reply `FIXTURE-CODEX-REPLY` (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, stop) lands after 80 s.
- `prepared-model-catalog.scoped-thinking.test.ts`: the existing admitted native-observation table gains `timeout` (fails on `main`) and `cancelled` (an AbortError that reads like a timeout still propagates) outcomes, plus one published-owner case that keeps the owner's latest accepted catalog on a timeout (fails on `main`); 22/22 pass.

Thanks @sangwf for the report and the parallel fix in #199359, @kqtxmaster-boop for the account/read report in #192725, and @MoerAI for this fix.

#170457 shares the error string but not the root: a disabled Codex plugin still being probed and spawning unreaped app-server children belongs to plugin enablement and app-server process lifecycle, not this capability read.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no state, config or published contract changes; a revert fully restores the old behavior. Blast radius: turns on native runtimes (Codex) whose capability lookup times out now continue with the retained catalog instead of failing; model resolution, policy checks and fallback rules are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ci): finish the WebKit end-to-end shard when a hosted runner's apt mirror is slow
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI end-to-end shard that runs the WebKit suites (`checks-ui-e2e (1/2)`) keeps getting cancelled at its 25-minute limit when it lands on an AWS-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runner. It never reaches the tests: the "Install selected Control UI E2E WebKit" step is still downloading WebKit's system packages when the job is killed. Another open PR, #200835, hit this on three heads in a row.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Contributors whose CI lands on a slow hosted runner get the WebKit shard through in a few minutes instead of a cancelled required check; on healthy runners the step behaves as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hosted image configures apt with a ranked mirror list (`mirror+file:/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt`). On the AWS-hosted image (region us-west-2) the first entry is `us-east-2.ec2.archive.ubuntu.com`, and its package pool trickles. apt only moves to the next mirror on errors, never on slow transfers, so `playwright install --with-deps webkit` waits on it indefinitely.

Both WebKit install steps in `ci.yml` now share one inline script (a YAML anchor):

1. With an `APT::Get::Download-Only` drop-in, `playwright install-deps webkit` only downloads, under a 120 s deadline. Stopping it there is safe because dpkg never runs. The deadline runs as root: Playwright elevates through its own `sudo`, which does not pass a signal sent from outside on to `apt-get`. A deadline outside `sudo` leaves the download running with the archives lock held.
2. If the deadline fires and the image has more than one mirror, it drops the first entry for the retry, so apt uses the image's next mirrors (`archive.ubuntu.com` / `security.ubuntu.com`). The retry has a 300 s deadline, and the step fails with an explicit error if that runs out too. On an image without a mirror list, the step keeps waiting without a deadline, as before.
3. It removes the drop-in and runs `playwright install-deps webkit` again without a deadline. That run installs from the downloaded archives. The mirror list is then restored, and `playwright install webkit` fetches the browser.

The CLI path is resolved once as the runner user (`pnpm --dir ui exec which playwright`), so pnpm, a Corepack shim configured through the runner user's environment, never runs as root. Root runs only that Playwright binary. The healthy path costs one extra `apt-get update` (1 to 9 s in the logs below). No native APT retries, no new actions, no runner placement or timeout changes.

Alternatives not taken: restoring the `.deb` files from a cache (like the Chromium action does) has more moving parts and only helps once a warmer has run. Raising the timeout or moving the job to another pool hides the problem.

## Evidence

Before (step "Install selected Control UI E2E WebKit", recent `ci.yml` runs):

| Runner | Step time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 (4 runs) | 18 to 23 s | success |
| ubuntu-24.04, Azure centralus (`azure.archive.ubuntu.com`) | 43 s (125 MB fetched in 9 s, 13.6 MB/s) | success |
| ubuntu-24.04, AWS us-west-2 (`us-east-2.ec2.archive.ubuntu.com`) | 880 s, 1398 s | job cancelled |

From a cancelled AWS-hosted job: the indexes arrived fine (`Fetched 13.2 MB in 9s`), and in the same job `security.ubuntu.com` served its indexes at full speed. Then `Need to get 125 MB of archives`, `fonts-freefont-ttf [5641 kB]` alone took 99 s, and 186 packages were still downloading 23 minutes later. The Chromium browser download on the same runner took 8 s, so the runner's network was fine. Only that mirror's package pool was slow. (`archive.ubuntu.com` and `security.ubuntu.com` resolve to the same Canonical servers.)

After: a reproduction in fresh `ubuntu:24.04` containers on a remote test VM, running the step body from `ci.yml` with the real chain: the Node 24.22.1 tarball, pnpm 12.15.0 through a Corepack shim from the repo's `packageManager` pin, real `playwright@1.64.1` in a `ui/` workspace package, and a non-root user with passwordless sudo. apt uses the hosted image's layout: a `mirror+file:` list whose first entry is a local stand-in mirror that serves indexes at full speed and package files at 30 KB/s.

| Case | After |
|---|---|
| Slow first mirror | 120 s deadline, then `::warning::WebKit system packages did not download in 120s from http://127.0.0.1:8080/ubuntu/; retrying with the image's other archive mirrors.`, `Fetched 216 MB in 9s`, install from the downloaded archives (`Need to get 0 B/219 MB`), WebKit browser downloaded. Whole step: **176 s**. Before, it would trickle at 30 KB/s |
| Healthy first mirror | `Fetched 219 MB in 16s`, install from cache, browser download. Whole step: 70 s, no warning |

In both cases the mirror list was restored, the drop-in removed, no `apt-get` was left running, the runner user's home had no root-owned files, root's cache stayed empty, and every WebKit system package was installed. An earlier iteration that put the deadline outside `sudo` failed this test with `E: Could not get lock /var/cache/apt/archives/lock. It is held by process … (apt-get)`, which is why the deadline runs as root. On real runners the package set is smaller (125 MB) because the image already has many of these packages.

Checks run locally: `actionlint`, `shellcheck` on the step body, `zizmor` 1.31.1 with the repo config, `scripts/generate-ci-git-owner.mts --check`, the composite-input interpolation check, and `test/scripts/ci-ui-browser-dependencies.test.ts` (plus `ci-workflow-complete` and `ci-browser-and-grep-setup`). The first test runs the step with stubbed `pnpm`, `id` and `sudo`, and now expects download, install, then browser.

Not proven here: the slow path on a real AWS-hosted runner. Both WebKit steps are skipped on this PR's own run: preflight enables the Control UI WebKit step only for UI WebKit-owner paths, and the end-to-end shard installs WebKit only when its selection includes a WebKit suite. Which runner pool a run lands on is also not under the PR's control. The first PR or main run that selects the WebKit suites on an AWS-hosted runner will show it.

prs.title: test(agents): qualify PostgreSQL completion auth health
prs.body:
Closes #200990

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL qualification previously covered simple completion with a configured API key, but did not verify stored-credential failover or durable auth health. A successful backup response could hide a failed bookkeeping write.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. This is test-only qualification; SQLite and PostgreSQL schema versions, DDL, migrations, persisted formats, public configuration and APIs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing real-transport fixture with a shared primary credential that returns HTTP 429 and an agent-owned backup that succeeds. Fresh worker reads check both stores, and a PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL case verifies that explicitly pinning a profile prevents rotation.

All seven cases retain Gateway main-thread admission enforcement, cold-plugin acquisition and lease disposal. The three engine pairs cover PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL, PostgreSQL/SQLite and SQLite/PostgreSQL. This tests the same acquisition/completion/failover owners composed by the plugin runtime, not the entire plugin API entry point.

## Evidence

- Independent source reviews found no actionable issue in fixture isolation, transport timing, owner selection or persistence assertions. The [exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200991#issuecomment-6969285688) has no findings or before-merge items. Both optional rank-up moves are addressed: seven executed cases are linked below, and the dependency failure is attributed below. No head change followed that review.
- Pinned oxfmt 0.74.0 and `git diff --check` passed.
- All seven completion cases passed on the exact head in [merge-context PostgreSQL shard 3/4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44239899842/job/134585491045): configured-key acquisition on all three engine pairs, stored-profile failover with fresh cross-owner health reads on all three, and explicit pinning on PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL. Each case took 2–4 seconds; none skipped. The earlier branch-head run also passed all seven cases.
- The completed [merge-context CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44239899842) is green: all selected checks, four PostgreSQL shards, and PostgreSQL 16 smoke passed. Its checkout was `d5a900a8ec9c7854109aad118eddbe49bcc9a565`, with parents `13a9deb0a57da3e4fc19442379b560652f493e69` and the reviewed PR head `aa03e9c008e86b43c2b5e7b49fe27dd9f4fa5c23`. [PG16 smoke](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44239899842/job/134585491067) executed and passed all 12 tests. Local dependency qualification rejected a broken shared workspace link; the Testbox allocation queued and was stopped and its cleanup reconciled. Exact-head CI supplied the runtime proof.
- Production delta: 0 lines. Test delta: +150 net lines.

Related qualification: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200956

### CI failure attribution

[The dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44237564864/job/134577870603) reports unused exports in session delivery, plugin metrics, cron helpers and session test support. Those files, their consumers and Knip configuration are unchanged by this test-only PR. Independent source review traced the findings to earlier changes: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200533, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198455 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200817.

This is source-backed attribution, not a claim that the baseline was rerun. The CI classifier reports unknown because the newest scheduled main run has no matching dependency job. That historical failure remains visible and separate from PostgreSQL qualification; declaration cleanup belongs to those owners. The later normal pull-request run is green and does not select that broader dependency check.

prs.title: fix(build): Git install updates fail with "Declaration input escapes checkout" since #198661
prs.body:
Closes #200357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` on a Git install fails at `preflight-build` with `Declaration input escapes checkout`, and the install stays on its old commit. This affects updates started by v2026.11.5 and earlier, which do not have #189463, when the target contains #198661 and the install's dependency versions differ from the target's for a package the SDK declarations reach. Today's trigger is the `undici` 8.12.3 to 8.12.4 bump in #200006. The CLI and `update.run` fail the same way, because `update.run` hands off to `openclaw update --yes`.

## User Impact

User impact: Git installs can update to main again. Normal builds keep the fast command-line declaration pass. A dependency that exists only outside the checkout still fails the build and names the escaped file.

## Why This Change Was Made

On POSIX the updater builds each candidate in a worktree inside the install it replaces (`<install>/.artifacts/.openclaw-update-preflight-*/worktree`). The Anthropic and OpenAI SDK declarations type `RequestInit` with relative `node_modules/undici` imports up to 10 parent directories up, so the compiler also reads the install's own `node_modules/undici`. The command-line pass from #198661 cannot deny that read, so it fails the build. When both sides have the same `undici` version the compiler does not read the parent copy separately, so updates between matching versions pass; any dependency bump between the installed release and the target brings the failure back. Updaters built from main set `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1` (#189463) and skip this step, but no release tag contains that change yet.

This keeps #198661's intent: declarations still depend only on files inside the checkout, and normal checkouts keep the fast pass. #198661 accepted "parent-install shadowing now fails loudly" because the command line cannot hide those reads. The updater's own preflight worktree is such a parent install, and already shipped updaters choose that path, so moving the worktree cannot fix updates from them.

When the command-line pass lists a file that is outside the checkout by path and by real path, the build discards that pass and emits through the bounded API filesystem from before #198661, which treats outside candidates as absent (the contract from #158674). Links that leave the checkout still fail as before. If the bounded compile fails, the error shows the compiler's diagnostic first, then the escaped read.

Maintainer decision: this undoes #198661 behavior change 1 for parent installs (fall back to the bounded compile instead of failing).

## Evidence

### Runtime output

Fresh Git install at `v2026.11.4` (d843d6af39a4), built with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && pnpm ui:build`, macOS arm64, home directory not a symlink, internal disk. Gateway stopped, isolated state and config. Command:

```
OPENCLAW_UPDATE_DEV_TARGET_REF=<target sha> node <install>/openclaw.mjs update --channel dev --yes --no-restart
```

Base, target f947bdc94981:

```
install at d843d6af39a4 (2026.11.4), target f947bdc94981
update exit 1
install now at d843d6af39a4
[... 8 lines cut ...]
  ✓ preflight-checkout (229ms)
  ✓ preflight-deps-install (15.85s)
  ✗ preflight-build (23.11s)
    Failing check preflight-build (command-failed): Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: [redacted-path]
  ✓ preflight-cleanup (13.21s)
Failed: validating
[... 1 line cut ...]
```

`preflight-build` fails on the escape and the install stays at d843d6af39a4. The updater redacts the path. Building f947bdc94981 by hand in the same nested layout shows it:

```
Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: <install>/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts -> <install>/node_modules/.pnpm/undici@8.12.2/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts.
```

Head, target 133cfd5d3f76 (this PR), same built install:

```
install at d843d6af39a4 (2026.11.4), target 133cfd5d3f76
update exit 0
install now at 133cfd5d3f76
[... 8 lines cut ...]
  ✓ preflight-checkout (366ms)
  ✓ preflight-deps-install (27.42s)
  ✓ preflight-build (330.54s)
  ✓ candidate-state-snapshot (2.04s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor (14.96s)
  [... 18 lines cut ...]
  ✓ git-checkout (18.96s)
  ✓ git-runtime-activation (111ms)
  ✓ database snapshot (3.65s)
  ✓ database migration writes (0ms)
  ✓ git-verify-head (14ms)
  ✓ preflight-cleanup (15.4s)
```

`preflight-build` passes, the candidate checks run, and the install moves to 133cfd5d3f76.

Bisect from the same install: target 1c1814a0bf78 (parent of #198661) exit 0, target 5a7d1718aa5 (#198661) exit 1 with the same escape.

Scope check against main 54d85be92e92 (undici 8.12.4 since #200006), same harness:

| From | Entry point | Target | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| v2026.11.5 (e13cf15ece9b, undici 8.12.3) | CLI | 54d85be92e92 | exit 1, `preflight-build` escape, install unchanged |
| v2026.11.4 (d843d6af39a4) | `gateway call update.run` | 54d85be92e92 | handoff `openclaw update --yes` fails at `preflight-build` with the escape, install unchanged |
| v2026.11.5 | CLI | b9d1882fab51 (main-based, undici 8.12.3) | exit 0, install moved |
| install at b9d1882fab51 (has #189463) | CLI | 54d85be92e92 | exit 0, install moved |

Nested build of 54d85be92e92 inside the v2026.11.5 install:

```
Declaration input escapes checkout: <install>/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts -> <install>/node_modules/.pnpm/undici@8.12.3/node_modules/undici/types/utility.d.ts.
```

### Tests

- `test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`, `bounds optional SDK relative imports to a checkout nested in a parent install`: on base f947bdc94981 it fails with `Declaration input escapes checkout`. On head it passes. With the fix reverted by `git apply -R` it fails again. It also checks that changing the parent install changes neither the declarations nor the inputs.
- Declaration consumers on head: `native-declaration-boundary`, `tsdown-declaration-resolution` (the escaped ancestor module, ambient types, package symlink, source symlink and source reference cases still refuse), `native-declaration-subprocess`, `write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts`, `run-tsgo-worktree`, `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.native`: 6 files, 77 passed, 7 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed --base f947bdc94981` on head: passed. The dead export scan was skipped: on this base it reports unused exports only in files this change does not touch.

### Local review

Local ClawSweeper (`review --local-range`, Claude runner) on base f947bdc94981, head 133cfd5d3f76, complete review: patch is correct, security cleared, no maintainer decision required, patch rating B. Remaining: one P3 suggesting the escape note be added only when the bounded compile fails on module resolution. The compiler's diagnostic now comes first; matching diagnostic codes was left out to keep the error path simple.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep hourly test plans within existing capacity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hourly main CI fails before running its tests: [run 44237410638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44237410638) planned 78 compact Node rows against its 77-row allowance. Main push CI selects fewer tests and therefore stays green. Inventory growth in #200967 exposed the packing failure; #200980's installed-probe change was not the cause.

## User Impact

Hourly CI can run its full selected inventory within the existing capacity policy. There is no product behavior change or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing hosted file-count bounds while balancing weighted stripes, extending the storage owner's existing behavior to the other bounded groups. Splitting those stripes afterward fragmented placement when agent-support grew from 485 to 486 files. The fix removes the storage-only exception (net −2 production lines).

No runner, concurrency, worker, file-count, time, or matrix limit changes. The manifest still reserves two standalone worker rows from its 77-row nondist budget; the compact planner accounts separately for two dist rows. Simply enabling final whole-row packing for GitHub was insufficient because no complete pair fit the existing limits.

## Evidence

The real scheduled manifest failed identically twice on main `819d09be7ce7ed230fd41a02cc307853fe2c9243` and succeeds with this change, emitting exactly 77 nondist rows. The largest predicted compact row stays 407s; summed compact predictions decrease from 17,757s to 17,597s. Bisection found the first failing commit `bb28b72b14429557b4f87ab02453d76e2ec753bf` (#200967); its parent fits.

The expanded scheduled-capacity test fails before the fix for both GitHub cases, including synthetic inventory growth, and passes afterward alongside hybrid. All 174 focused planner/hosted-bound tests pass (136.30s Vitest, 138.97s wrapper), including exact-once inventory and existing file/worker limits. The tooling-test typecheck passes.

Codex autoreview of the final local diff against `819d09be7ce7ed230fd41a02cc307853fe2c9243`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. Its review covered the supplied diff; local execution supplies the surrounding behavior proof.

Same-head full-inventory A/A and B/B owner measurements: sampled allocations 9.27/9.20 GB before versus 8.01/8.05 GB after. CPU 10.25/5.54s versus 5.38/5.26s; wall 18.37/8.39s versus 8.22/9.28s. The first baseline sample has substantial filesystem variation, so no wall-time speedup is claimed. No Team data was used.

`pnpm check:changed` passed all checks except unrelated main unused exports. Replaying the dead-export owner on untouched exact parent `819d09be7ce7ed230fd41a02cc307853fe2c9243` reproduced the identical 8 production and 8 full-tree entries (11 distinct symbols). Introducing changes: #200533 (`prepareSessionEventDelivery`, `DurablePilotCustody`, `DurablePilotInput`); #193550 (`PluginHookBeforeModelRequestEvent`, `PluginHookBeforeModelRequestResult`); #198455 (`PluginMetricFamily`, `PluginMetricFamilyDeclaration`, `PluginMetricLabels`, `PluginMetrics`); #200817 (`formatDays`, `selectSegmented`). These are main regressions requiring separate repair; no ignore, baseline adjustment, or passing-check claim is made for that scan.

prs.title: fix: let users steer a chat while a Code Mode shell command runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A correction sent while Code Mode is waiting for a shell command can sit in the chat queue until the command exits. Stopping the turn just to deliver it also stops the work.

## User Impact

An ordinary steer can now reach the next model decision in the same turn while the shell keeps running. No Stop, second click, configuration change, or restart of the command is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Code Mode already keeps a paused program and its outstanding calls together. When the only outstanding work is a core shell call, it can return that program’s wait handle to the model instead of blocking the chat. Collecting the handle resumes the same program with its remaining execution budget. Other required operations keep waiting; so does the shell if all continuation slots are occupied. The change does not make aggregate tools cancellable or change who may steer.

Related: #193665, #194953, #199878.

## Evidence

On the unchanged base, the next model request received the correction only after the real shell exited. With this patch the next request receives the correction before releasing the process, then collects its original output; the command ran once. A separate test verifies that steering cannot detach a required non-shell action. These are local embedded-session tests with scripted inference, not live provider measurements.

All 89 focused tests passed across four suites. Independent tests with both the cell and the shell set to `awaitResults: true` reproduced the delay on main and verified the fix on Node and QuickJS. Both engines delivered the correction before shell exit and the command’s result exactly once. Targeted types, lint, and formatting passed. Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(subagents): deliver finished results instead of refusing on store path or operator authority
prs.body:
## Problem

Finished subagent results were dropped by identity checks that run after the work is done:

- **Store-path veto.** Each result recorded the requester's session store path at spawn. If the path resolved differently later (for example after a config reload republished the resolver), the result was suspended as "store replaced" and never delivered. Delivery never used that path: it finds the requester by agent and session key.
- **Operator-authority refusals.** A settle turn refused to run when a child's retained operator custody was missing or revoked. The parent then saw "authority is no longer active" and the result was lost.

Previous fixes exempted one case at a time.

## Fix

Delete both refusal classes. A finished result is delivered to the requester chat by `(requesterAgentId, requesterSessionKey)`.

- Removed the store-path comparison as a delivery veto: settle-wake `isStoreCurrent` / `retireReplacedStore`, the store branch in `isSubagentCompletionDeliveryAllowed`, `suspendReplacedStoreNotifications` and its store-owner registration, the post-announce store block, and the `storeReplaced` plumbing through the completion mutation kernel and receipt admission.
- Removed `requiredCompletionEntries` and the authority throws. #200873 already splits settle batches by retained operator turn; within a batch, `runWithSubagentCompletionBatchAuthority` now runs under retained custody only when every member has the same live source and permission ceiling, and otherwise at the System write-only baseline, which settle turns already use after every Gateway restart. It never borrows a sibling's permissions.
- Kept: explicit stop/cancel, requester deletion, cancellation-notice callers, and the temporary access-policy outage retry.

## User impact

Subagent results no longer disappear after config edits or Gateway restarts. A continuation turn that lost its original operator custody runs at the baseline permission instead of being dropped; this already happens after every restart.

## Accepted tradeoffs (maintainer decision)

- **Revoked requester.** If the operator who spawned a child loses access before the child finishes, the result still wakes the requester session, at the System write-only baseline. It is no longer dropped. Gateway admission still checks the requester session.
- **Different physical store, same session key.** If `session.store` is changed to a different database that has its own session with the same key, a pending result from the old store is delivered to that session. This reverses the automatic suspension from #152828. Delivery has no stored identity that separates a moved store from an unrelated one; adding one is a schema change and is out of scope here.

## Evidence

- Regression in `subagent-registry.requester-delivery.test.ts`, red on the merge base (zero settle turns) and green with the fix: a finished child with a mismatched recorded `requesterStorePath` and a live requester is delivered through the real in-process dispatcher.
- `subagent-control.publication.test.ts` now asserts that a revoked owner's result is delivered at the baseline.
- Affected registry, announce, completion, sweep-settle and restart-custody suites pass after rebasing on #200873 (189 tests across 8 files).
- `test/gateway-subagent-completion-restart.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway restart): 8 of 9 cases pass. `announcing-crash` fails identically on the merge base when run alone; #200873 documents the same pre-existing failure.
- Full build and packed install smoke pass.
- Production: 46 lines added, 271 removed; tests: net -439 lines.

Known follow-ups, not changed here: a deleted requester can leave an owed wake retrying (pre-existing); `ensureSubagentControllerOwnsRun` still compares the recorded store path for kill/steer control.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): keep mid-turn directive acks out of the active turn's context
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #194451. A directive-only command such as `/think medium`, sent while an ordinary turn is running on the same session, kills that turn. The directive is applied and acknowledged. But its acknowledgement is recorded as a **context-bearing** command exchange while the running turn owns the transcript's model-context fence. When the turn commits its first model answer, the prepared append fails with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` ("SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite"). The completed answer is discarded, the user sees "Your request couldn't be completed", and the original request is lost. #192585 fixed this for `/status` by marking its reply `contextFreeCommand`. Directive acknowledgements (`/think`, `/reasoning`, `/verbose`, `/fast`, `/elevated`, `/model`, `/queue`, …) still took the context-bearing path. ## User Impact Changing the thinking level (or any other directive) in the middle of a running request no longer throws that request away. The answer is delivered, and the directive still applies to the session. ## Why This Change Was Made The review asks to coordinate directive recording with active-turn transcript ownership while keeping the documented "exchanges enter later model context" behavior. This PR does that at the single place where directive-only replies are produced (`applyInlineDirectiveOverrides` in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-directives-apply.ts`): - **While a turn is running** (`isSessionRunActive(sessionEntry.sessionId)`), the directive-only acknowledgement gets the existing `contextFreeCommand` reply metadata, the same treatment `/status` has. The exchange stays in session history, but it does not move the running turn's context fence, so the turn's answer commits. - **When the session is idle**, nothing changes. The command and acknowledgement still enter later model context, as documented. - Both recording paths already honor `contextFreeCommand`: the channel `dispatch-from-config` mirror and Gateway `chat.send` finalization. So no recorder or transcript-fence change is needed, and stale-write protection stays as strict as before. - `docs/tools/slash-commands.md` now documents the mid-turn case. Mixed messages (a directive plus text) are untouched, because they are ordinary turns that queue normally. ## Evidence **Live run on Windows.** Source Gateway on loopback with isolated state, and a stub OpenAI-compatible model that holds its response for 20 s. Steps: 1. `chat.send` "original request". 2. About 6 s into the in-flight model request, `chat.send` `/think medium` to the same session. 3. After the run, an idle `chat.send` `/think low`. Only `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-directives-apply.ts` differs between the two columns. | | `main` | this PR (77fa3ee) | | --- | --- | --- | | original turn | ❌ `Embedded agent failed before reply: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite …` | ✅ answer committed, no conflict | | `chat.history` | `original request` · `/think medium` · `Thinking level set to medium.` · `custom: Your request couldn't be completed.` · `/think low` · `Thinking level set to low.` | `original request` · `/think medium` · `Thinking level set to medium.` · `answer to the original request (req 1)` · `/think low` · `Thinking level set to low.` | | mid-turn `/think medium` rows | `excludeFromContext=false` | `excludeFromContext=true` (history kept) | | idle `/think low` rows | `excludeFromContext=false` | `excludeFromContext=false` (documented behavior kept) | The issue comment has the current-main reproduction together with a `/status` control (no conflict): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/194451#issuecomment-6702496521 **Regression test.** In `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-directives-apply.test.ts`, `keeps directive acks out of an active turn's context: false/true` checks that a `/think medium` directive-only reply carries `contextFreeCommand` only when `isSessionRunActive` reports a running turn for that session id. Against unmodified `main`, both cases fail (the active case gets `undefined` instead of `true`). With this PR, all 16 tests in the file pass. **Gates:** - `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on the changed files: clean. - `pnpm lint:docs`: 0 issues. - `check:line-cap-ratchet`: OK. `check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK with `config/test-lines-allocations/194451-mid-turn-directive-context.txt` (24 lines, the net test-line delta of the new table). - `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json`: clean.

prs.title: feat: add HeyGen Voice speech provider
prs.body:
Closes #194470

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw users cannot speak with HeyGen voices, including the instant and professional voice clones in their own HeyGen workspace.

## User Impact

User impact: after installing the plugin and setting `HEYGEN_API_KEY`, users can set `tts.provider: "heygen"` and get MP3 audio, streamed playback, Opus voice notes, 24 kHz PCM telephony output, and voice listing. Nothing changes for users who do not install it.

Required action: a maintainer must publish `@openclaw/heygen-speech` to npm and ClawHub. The install path does not work until then.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an external plugin in `extensions/heygen-speech`, in the same shape as the other hosted speech providers, with no core code change. All synthesis uses HTTP streaming to `POST /v3/models/audio/tts/stream`.

The guarded fetch timeout covers the whole response body, and playback can read a long reply for minutes, so the provider restarts that timeout on each audio chunk. The plugin does not create voices. Its README shows the instant-clone API call.

The config baseline plugin count rises by 21, from 5018 to 5039, for the new plugin entry. The other files outside the extension are repo-required registration, generated inventory, and docs.

## Evidence

Since the ClawSweeper review of `9d9fa3be322`:

- `speakerVoice`, the canonical voice key, was ignored, so a config or persona that set it got the default voice. The provider now reads `speakerVoice`, then `speakerVoiceId`, then `voiceId`.
- The missing-key errors for synthesis and voice listing now name `HEYGEN_API_KEY` and `tts.providers.heygen.apiKey`.
- The mocked timeout-refresh test is removed. The live streaming run below covers that behavior.

Checks at this head (`d1ec0f66f77`) on a Linux devbox with Node 24:

- `extensions/heygen-speech`: 27 unit tests passed.
- `src/plugins/contracts`: 1085 tests passed.
- oxlint, oxfmt, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and the test-line ratchet against upstream `main` (slack 75) passed. The assertion ratchet, config docs, plugin inventory, docs MDX and links, and dead-export checks passed at `9d9fa3be322`. This head changes only the plugin source, its test, and its test-line allocation.

Installed-plugin proof at this head, against the production HeyGen API:

- The package was packed with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack extensions/heygen-speech` and installed with `openclaw plugins install npm-pack:` into an empty `OPENCLAW_HOME`. `plugins list` shows it loaded from the installed package's `dist/index.js`.
- `openclaw infer tts convert`, with `tts.providers.heygen.speakerVoice` set to a public voice, returned 26.4 s of 44.1 kHz MP3.
- Streaming through `textToSpeechStream` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tts-runtime`, with `timeoutMs: 3000`: first audio at 586 ms and the last of 863 chunks at 3613 ms, so the stream ran past its original deadline. A control at `timeoutMs: 200` timed out before first audio. `infer tts convert` passes its own 120 s timeout, so only the streaming run exercises the refresh.
- With no key, `infer tts voices` names `HEYGEN_API_KEY` and `tts.providers.heygen.apiKey`.

- `voiceId`, `speakerVoice`, and invalid `model` directives, persona `modelId`, Talk with the key only in the TTS config, and `infer tts convert --voice --model`.
- Refusals for a bad key, a bad voice, a regional language code, a rejected tag, and a professional clone on Turbo. HeyGen's `code` and `request_id` stayed in the errors, and the next turn worked.
- Fallback to the next provider, three turns in a row, release mid-stream, and a dropped connection mid-stream.

The failed case used a 5 s `timeoutMs` on a 16 s professional clone take. The timeout also covers time to first audio, which varies on this path. In 3 retries, 1 passed and ran 7.4 s while audio arrived, and 2 timed out before first audio. With the chunk refresh removed at an earlier commit, the same case failed mid-stream at the timeout.

At earlier commits, two live 429 responses kept `code` and `request_id`. One arrived after a 30 s wait.

Not tested:

- Real Discord voice playback, a real phone call, and Telegram delivery. These runs covered output formats only.
- Talk through a connected client. The runs called the gateway config and synthesis functions directly.
- Long replies at the default timeout. Live text stayed short.
- Installing from npm or ClawHub, because the package is not published. The proof above installs the packed tarball.

The test-line ratchet and `checks-node-core-tooling-3` fail only because the fork's `main` is behind upstream. The rest are timeouts, browser and gateway tests, native locale parity, a tooling fixture, and iOS screenshots, all outside this PR's files. Fork CI did not select the `extensions/heygen-speech` tests, so they ran on the devbox.

Local review: local autoreview was not run. Instead, an adversarial agent review and two over-engineering agent reviews ran, and the verified findings are fixed.

prs.title: test: cover stale quarantine hashing and Doctor cleanup
prs.body:
Companion for #190683, building on **goutamadwant's** fix in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190712. Their exact commit `7ad976471df1468672fa55ebfd6919f1a198585f` is preserved unchanged as the immediate parent, with original authorship. Later commits on this branch, including the Doctor extraction and this head, are authored and committed by Jerome <jeromequeck@jeromegroup.org>.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the slowdown reported in #190683. When a repaired memory database still has an obsolete quarantine record for an older generation (a different file size), every database admission hashes the whole database before noticing the size mismatch, so memory searches and agent preparation repeatedly rescan large databases. Doctor could also leave that stale record behind indefinitely. This companion keeps goutamadwant's fix and adds regression coverage proving definite size mismatches skip generation hashing, possible matches still hash, and Doctor clears the stale record only after a successful integrity check.

## What changed on this head

Current head is `82d40ac226ff5a4930b24d77f7b5bbf0f7792acd`. This is not a tests-only range. After the original fix, `bb72dee6a42c` / `82d40ac` extract Doctor quarantine admission into `src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence-quarantine.ts` so the production-file line cap is respected. That extraction is production code.

PR range `3259404694bc9e54ba39a2b9587376e90f8eda53...82d40ac226ff5a4930b24d77f7b5bbf0f7792acd` (8 files, +357/-22):

- Production source: 4 files, +141/-22, net +119. New file `src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence-quarantine.ts` (+61). Also `src/infra/sqlite-file-generation.ts` (+50), `src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.ts` (+12/-22), `src/state/openclaw-quarantine-store.ts` (+18).
- Tests: +175 across `src/state/openclaw-database-verify.test.ts` and `src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.test.ts`.
- Docs: +39 in `docs/root-cause/194440.md`. Allocation file +2.

## Evidence

All of the following was run on exact head `82d40ac226ff5a4930b24d77f7b5bbf0f7792acd`, with no merge of `main` and a clean worktree. Built CLI: `node openclaw.mjs` after `pnpm build:runtime` (exit 0). It prints `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (82d40ac)` — the tree's version stamp plus the abbreviated head. `dist/entry.js` SHA256 `89772fb931af631b705cc9d89b5bb6968ac95d0d96394109d612909099350d5c`. Node v24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0. Isolated `HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Memory search uses provider `none` (keyword / fts-only). No remote embedding service and no credentials.

Hash counts use a scratch-only `crypto.createHash` / `fs.readSync` preload that attributes SHA-256 updates whose buffer is the `readSync` result for the agent database path. That is generation-content hashing, not every SHA in the process. A live positive control on this preload hashed a 720896-byte file and counted exactly one target digest of 720896 bytes (exit 0). On the CLI searches below, the same counter still recorded hundreds of unrelated `createHash("sha256")` calls while target generation-content digests stayed 0.

Focused unit tests on this head (10 Nov 2026, 19:52:45–19:53:47 SGT, exit 0): 2 files, 42 passed, 0 skipped.

### Latest stable is still v2026.11.2

`npm view openclaw dist-tags` at 20:16:52 SGT (Asia/Singapore) still has `"latest": "2026.11.2"` (beta is `2026.11.5-beta.1`; this proof does not use the beta). Published tarball `openclaw-2026.11.2.tgz`, npm shasum `4185b164092d40a2b49d5630808031a0b28632de`, SHA256 `7881887b88d81e5fdff361b7aac59b6a736308e1815a175b9ccd9cdca1bb5e48`. Installed in scratch (`npm install --omit=dev --legacy-peer-deps`, exit 0). The published launcher prints `OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf)`.

The upgrade + data-model + stale-recovery run started 20:22:43 SGT in `/tmp/oc-194440-proof-r2-x8C6Ir` (proof script exit 0 at 20:25:22 SGT).

### Data written by v2026.11.2, retained after upgrade on this head

Stable `memory index` / two searches (exit 0) created an agent database at `user_version` 27 and a state database at `user_version` 22. Workspace files `MEMORY.md` (needle `alpha-harbor-quarantine-needle`) and `COMPAT.md` were present. The v2026.11.2 memory source set is `MEMORY.md` + `memory/*.md`, so only `MEMORY.md` was indexed (1 memory chunk). `COMPAT.md` is a workspace file retained on disk, not an indexed memory row.

A whole-state copy pointed at this head first refused search (exit 1). That refusal is not hash-skip proof:

```
# node openclaw.mjs memory search 'alpha-harbor-quarantine-needle' --agent main --json
# exit=1
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "memory search failed (main): Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix."
  },
  "agentId": "main"
}
```

`doctor --fix --non-interactive` on that copied state exited 0 and printed `Doctor complete.` It saved pre-migration SQLite backups and upgraded the agent database `v27 -> v39`. The state database moved 22 → 39.

```
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-3fb272b7-ab12-8f2d-8cf7-e1af6f8325fd.bak
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-3fb272b7-ab12-8f2d-8cf7-e1af6f8325fd.bak
- Upgraded agent database schema in .../openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v39.
```

Before/after data-model checks on the same copied tree:

- Settings retained: `gateway.mode=local`, `gateway.bind=loopback`, `memory.search.provider=none`, vector store disabled. The workspace path only changed because the state tree was copied (`.../stable/state/workspace` → `.../fixed/state/workspace`).
- Workspace files retained with identical SHA-256: `MEMORY.md` `652bc24e12b760310b7fd24e4055bd661ce2db452da148deea789df132d6f835` (63 bytes) and `COMPAT.md` `cdf60d47ce6bc24cd7c7a0083408255302348359b9a9f1b58a8a71259719a5a0` (72 bytes).
- Indexed memory rows unchanged: `memory_index_chunks` 1→1, `memory_index_sources` 1→1, and every other nonempty agent-DB table counted had delta 0. The indexed needle was still present:

```
# memory_index_chunks before and after (identical)
{ "path": "MEMORY.md", "text": "The quarantine proof needle is alpha-harbor-quarantine-needle.\n" }
```

- Post-migration CLI search for that needle exited 0 and returned the same `MEMORY.md` snippet.
- Existing state rows retained: `agent_databases` 1→1, `plugin_state_entries` 3→3, `schema_meta` 1→1. Doctor wrote additional upgrade records, as expected: `migration_runs` 0→1, `migration_sources` 0→2, `config_health_entries` 1→2, plus `config_machine_state` and `diagnostic_events`.
- Media: this fixture did not write media blobs. State table `outbound_media_provenance` stayed 0→0. There were no nonempty agent-DB media tables before or after.

### Stale-size admission, Doctor cleanup, and Gateway search on the upgraded tree

A stale-size quarantine row was then inserted against the migrated 720896-byte database (recorded size 724992). Two shipped-CLI searches on this head exited 0; the needle search returned `MEMORY.md` and recorded **0** generation-content hashes (`target_sha256_digests=0`, `sha256CreateHashCalls=662`).

`doctor --fix --non-interactive` on that fixture exited 0, printed `Doctor complete.`, and left the quarantine store at 0 rows (`quarantineRow: null`). The indexed needle was still present at schema 39. Follow-up CLI search exited 0, returned the needle, and again recorded 0 generation-content hashes (`sha256CreateHashCalls=659`).

The stale-size row was re-seeded and a shipped Gateway on the same upgraded state became ready. Two `gateway call memory.search` requests for the needle both exited 0, `searchMode` `fts-only`, and returned `MEMORY.md`. Combined gateway processes: **0** generation-content hashes (`target_sha256_digests=0`, `target_update_bytes=0`).

### Earlier exact-head receipt on a fresh tree (still this head)

A prior isolated run on the same `82d40ac` binary (10 Nov 2026, 19:58:12 SGT) already showed the same CLI / Gateway zero-hash admission, Doctor cleanup, and a published-v2026.11.1 upgrade (schema 27→39, pre-migration custody refusal shown separately). The review asked for the same scenario from current latest stable, which is the v2026.11.2 run above.

## Commands

```sh
git rev-parse HEAD
# 82d40ac226ff5a4930b24d77f7b5bbf0f7792acd
node openclaw.mjs --version
# OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (82d40ac)
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-database-verify.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.test.ts
```

No whole-repository gate is claimed. This proof is for exact head `82d40ac226ff5a4930b24d77f7b5bbf0f7792acd`.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation custody store** in the per-agent database persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts, and hands each delegate off to the subagent run registry before spawn (RFC `docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md` §5.4). The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **Durable custody**: delegates and their replay state live in the continuation custody store, with one transactional authority for replacement and a pre-spawn handoff to `subagent_runs` (upstream has removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime, #159179) - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → custody record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from the custody store (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` (tree `53363f7964f31a47109cf0575aa23f31eefa0338`), the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. It was reached by fast-forward on 2026-11-05. Running live rows here needs a deployment whose runtime has this SHA as an ancestor. That is a migrating cut (an agent-schema step), gated on its own timed restore rehearsal. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` does not point at this packet, and nothing here is a terminal rollup claim. ### Earlier evidence: provenance, not exact-target proof The live behavior observed on earlier heads, and the earlier corpora, are ancestry and materiality evidence for this head. The behaviors those corpora observed are the ones this feature exists for: - stale ambient backlog suppression; - typed and bracket `continue_work` wakes with granted provenance and Tempo model-call spans; - cost-cap rejection; - max-chain, scheduler, durable recovery and delegate surfaces. They are re-fired against this head's runtime once one is deployed. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. - [Exact-head packet for `a22bd9c05c`: README, status and limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md: identities and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [Gate 4 receipt: Mode-B and the local cut shards](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/gates/GATE-4-MODE-B-AND-LOCAL-SHARDS.md) - Historical corpora (provenance only): [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567), [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) -
