Each packet's `METHOD.md` carries the exact reproducer commands. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers, because OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access. Structural completeness is not proof: a row counts only with an authoritative receipt at the exact SHA. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially host Cron plus / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A tool adapter over durable flow records is also not a lifecycle host, and upstream has since removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime (#159179) that such an adapter would have called. Marking a stored record as running neither reacquires a session lane nor invokes the model; continuation needs the turn machinery itself to own which session runs next, how child results return, and what survives finalization. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix: keep sandbox preparation from losing exec turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long, silent sandbox preparation can lose an otherwise bounded exec turn at the 900-second quiet window because exec only published its deadline after spawning. In the supplied incident evidence, one roboclaw task session lost three consecutive runs this evening (19:38, 19:54, and a retry that re-ran the same command); the outer and nested exec records were cut at 900 seconds with a null bridge deadline. Cold preparations of 168 seconds and container starts of 49 seconds were also observed under filesystem/container contention. The production evidence alone does not establish which phase each aborted run reached.

Related: #200670.

## User Impact

Sandbox preparation can now finish and a silent command can deliver its own timeout result without losing the parent turn at the quiet window. Stall diagnostics distinguish preparation from a running command and identify commands without a timeout, without logging tool arguments or results.

A truly hung preparation is now retained for the effective timeout plus the unchanged 900-second quiet window (45 minutes with the ordinary 1800-second default), rather than 15 minutes. This change does not add an aggregate preparation timer. Explicitly unbounded commands and services without a configured timeout retain the existing quiet-window behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec producer publishes `dispatchTime + timeoutMs` before asynchronous process preparation, then replaces it with the supervisor's enforced deadline after spawn. The liveness carrier already accepts updates while the invocation is active and ignores retained callbacks after close, so no carrier guard or watchdog policy changes are needed. Keeping the spawn update is necessary when preparation is long enough that the initial allowance would expire before the supervisor can return its timeout.

Every pending tool gains `explicitDeadline`. Local and sandbox exec expose `preparing`/`running` and `default`/`explicit`/`none` through the existing structural `awaiting` view. No new store, diagnostics channel, protocol field, or configuration is introduced.

## Evidence

The real Code Mode/exec/supervisor reproduction is red on base `4a44f2031e866`: a fake sandbox preparation exceeding 900 seconds aborts with no published deadline. With the producer fix, preparation takes 1000 seconds and the command still receives its own timeout after a further 1800 seconds; the turn remains alive beyond the initial dispatch allowance. The parameterized regression also proves explicit timeout attribution and unchanged quiet-window aborts for disabled timeouts before/after spawn and service preparation. It replaces the overlapping synthetic deadline regression.

- Focused Code Mode, exec liveness, watchdog, cron watchdog-cause, and liveness-carrier suites: 116 tests passed across five files. Final typed-fixture lifecycle rerun: 31 tests passed.
- Production typecheck (`tsconfig.core.json`) and agent-tools test typecheck passed. The latter initially caught a fake-adapter contract mismatch, which was corrected before the final run.
- Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local Codex autoreview at P0–P2 against base `4a44f2031e866`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. Author pr-simplify pass retained the small producer change and removed the superseded synthetic regression; no further simplification was needed.
- Changed test-file test times: lifecycle 11.7 seconds (the five new cases total 0.526 seconds), watchdog 0.115 seconds, cron watchdog-cause 5.859 seconds. Combined wrapper wall time: 132.57 seconds; final lifecycle-only wall time: 54.67 seconds. Existing lifecycle cases include the real executor and cancellation/settlement boundaries. CI seconds pending.

No production access was used. The fake sandbox and process adapter isolate external I/O; the exec tool, supervisor timers, Code Mode bridge, and watchdog are real.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The installed-terminal observer test rejects Node 26's native error for an invalid `maxBuffer` array even when the observer preserves the exact native result. Node 24 reports `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`; Node 26 reports `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The test can validate observer transparency on both supported Node versions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the redundant assertion for one Node-specific error code. The test still compares the complete observed output with the uninstrumented process, exercises the malformed array, and requires failed observation without claiming native completion.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200980

## Evidence

- Existing baseline: the exact case fails on Node 26.13.0 at the error-code assertion; the complete output-parity assertion passes. Node 24.22.1 passes the original file.
- Candidate on repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`: Node 26.13.0 full observer file passes (23 tests, 7 platform skips); Node 24.22.1 passes the exact malformed-input parity case.
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint, and the root-scripts test TypeScript project pass. This is a test-only change; production observer code is unchanged.
- Local ClawSweeper review completed against frozen base `88387ae8` and head `1db7adb5`: no actionable correctness or security findings (confidence 0.98).

prs.title: fix(agents): omit message when no supported route exists
prs.body:
Related: #169091

## What Problem This Solves

Agents are offered the message tool even when their session has no supported reply route and no configured outbound sender. That advertises an action they cannot use.

## User Impact

Route-less agents stop receiving an unusable messaging tool. Supported source replies and prompt reactions, configured offline/outbound-only channels, and unbound configured senders remain available. Existing target/action restrictions still apply at execution. Discovery omission does not deny a later child or automation that has a route.

No new public configuration, permission rule, or database schema is introduced. Existing WebChat sessions record prompt support on their next operator declaration. Cold SDK constructors remain usable before configuration preparation; invocation still requires canonical preparation and authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery consumes existing session-metadata and channel-configuration owners, not transport health or default schema actions. Existing policy and schema gates enforce permission ceilings before route-only presentation filtering, including coding, Gateway/CLI MCP, and skill dispatch. Omitted-config discovery and session binding use only the published runtime snapshot without cold-loading configuration or freezing invocation-time settings.

## Evidence

**Published head:** 3db3474c3ba4eb40a08e916063014df66dd654c3; tree ebfb7fb0bf9c47c2ab16bdcb0c9c0241bf56d73c exactly matches qualified source 3e38b66b9e369267fc02217265ae9b5c404d47d5. Original published ancestry and integrated main 3460f61786013ff711efbcb6ce9a91fa003a178a are retained.

- **434 focused tests across 14 distinct files pass**, including constructor/config preparation, five late-bound Codex source cases, Gateway room delivery, source-only effects, prefix stability, offline/unbound senders, child/cron capture, MCP grants/schema admission, and skill dispatch.

The five Codex assertions and awaited SDK source declarations remain unchanged; the positive Telegram fixture now registers a supported outbound test adapter and restores the previous registry. No availability or authority mock.
- Core types, scoped typed lint/format, six canonical prompt snapshots, and diff checks pass. Line-cap ratchet passes across **41 changed source files**. Net test growth **+696 LF** passes unchanged allowance 400 plus existing allocation credit 523. No assertion, timeout, skip, baseline, or cap weakening.

First requests retain flat/direct/nondeferred message; static instructions/tools, native session/cache identity, history, and source-delivery policy assertions pass. Each turn produces exactly one actual synthetic channel-bus outbound receipt. All three normal private-QA build stamps match the commit.
- The actual Codex package-build-and-pack entry passes under official Node 24.22.1 with CI settings: 203 entries, bundled acorn, and clean restored source. Loopback deterministic inference/synthetic delivery is not paid-provider runtime inference, real external delivery, real-model compliance, or a cache-efficiency measurement.

**Review:** fresh independent P0–P3 clean review and structured scoped-clean/exit-0 autoreview cover the four-file repair, tree ebfb7fb0 relative to source 5057b540. Earlier functional/integration reviews remain scoped to their unchanged inputs, not a fresh full-PR autoreview claim. The completed [earlier hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197553#issuecomment-6815833811) covers an earlier revision; no duplicate request.

### Current CI and inherited-failure qualification

[CI 44232922509](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44232922509), attempt 1 on exact head 3db3474c, is **terminal and failed: 118 jobs—90 successful, 25 skipped, 3 failed**. Actual tested checkout **8e4af7f9fef10ab22ca925dba289fc14eaa5b527**, tree **3c35d96bee86bcd1c7abd675cf130d002608461b**, has ordered parents **main 14b9fc3c8d9454b89b9ff402ce31e39b75e41dfb** and this PR head. Its retained Git tree independently matches merge-tree reconstruction.

Private frozen install, fresh normal E2E build, official Node 24.22.1, pinned Bun 1.4.4, and the same maintained six-file selector/order/default profiles: one 526-second run, **120 other cases passed, three E2E cases failed plus Discord teardown**. prs.title: fix: keep approved releases on trusted validation tooling
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An approved release can stop before core npm publication because the core workflow validates its parent using code from the product tag, rather than the trusted publisher. This occurred during 2026.10.33 when the tagged validator rejected the parent's versioned workflow display name.

## User Impact

Release operators can publish a qualified product tag using the current trusted approval policy without rebuilding or moving that tag. This changes release tooling only; package contents and approval requirements are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing workflow-SHA checkout before parent validation and run its validator from that checkout. Keep the live parent identity, exact SHA, receipt, attestation, and environment gates intact.

## Evidence

- Original failed core run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44222387834 (failure before any core npm publish).
- The new regression executes the actual workflow shell in step order with a rejecting candidate validator and the real trusted validator. Before the fix it fails by executing candidate code; after the fix it accepts the versioned parent name and rejects a wrong parent SHA.
- Focused approval suite: 12/12 pass; package-acceptance sibling suite: 586/586 pass. Targeted tooling typecheck, oxlint, workflow lint/security checks, formatting, and diff checks pass. The workflow checker initially rejected an inherited empty GITHUB_TOKEN; removing only that empty environment variable allowed the unchanged check to pass.
- Independent read-only review covered the two-file delta from base 13a9deb0a57da3e4fc19442379b560652f493e69 to the final source snapshot (committed as 5de1da8231caac28243f0d3992299d05791b4836). It found no correctness or authority issues. Its fixture-cleanup suggestion was applied and the focused checks rerun. The local autoreview CLI could not run because its codex executable is unavailable; this is not recorded as a passing review.
- The already published 2026.10.33 tag and artifacts are untouched. That publication was completed through the documented separately approved recovery route, not by weakening the failed parent check.

prs.title: fix: show the whole token conflict hint in openclaw status
prs.body:
Related: #200937

## What Problem This Solves

When `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` is set and `gateway.auth.token` uses a different value, `openclaw status` warns about the conflict, but the hint is hard to use. The first word of the fix, "Remove", shows as `***`, and the line stops at 160 characters, in the middle of the instruction. `openclaw doctor` shows the same hint in full.

## User Impact

`openclaw status` now shows the whole conflict hint, readable, the same as doctor. Real secret values in status diagnostics are still masked.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hint was built as `... conflicts with gateway.auth.token: Remove ...`. Both the status redactor and the console output redactor read `token: Remove` as a key and a value, so they masked "Remove". The hint now joins the title and the fix with a period, so no redactor sees an assignment. The redaction rules are unchanged.

Status also cut every command-local secret diagnostic at 160 UTF-16 units (added in #126786). The conflict hint is about 290 units, so it was cut mid-sentence. Command-local diagnostics now use a 400-unit limit instead. That fits the whole hint, and the list stays bounded for readability as #126786 and the status docs intend, so long Gateway-returned diagnostics and wrapped error messages are still cut. This follows the review's recommendation: keep the period separator and use a finite limit of about 400 instead of no limit. Both redaction passes still run before the cut, `openclaw status` still prints at most 10 lines, and owner ids and config paths from runtime secret degradation keep the 160 limit.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `src/commands/status-all/report-data.test.ts`: the real conflict hint passes the console redactor unchanged and appears whole in the status report. Secret masking still holds: the console redactor turns `gateway.auth.token: <real-looking ghp_ value>` into `gateway.auth.token: ghp_R3…8sW1`, and the status report shows a value after `gateway.remote.token:` as `***`. A local diagnostic longer than 400 units is still cut at exactly 400. The test fails on main and passes here.
- Mutation check: reverting with `git apply -R` makes the test fail again in each of 4 cases: the whole fix, the period alone, the limit change alone (back to 160), and the 400 bound alone (back to no limit).
- Touched and consumer suites pass: status report, status command, status overview rows, status format, doctor security, security audit gateway (98 tests).
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` passes (main at `2301af4923c`, which has no changes to the touched files or the redaction code; 0 lint warnings, 0 errors).
- Local review: ClawSweeper (local, `--local-range`), base `f3638439b92`, head `f094ac3eb97`: review complete, patch correct, security cleared, no findings. The proof rating there is low only because a local range review reads commit messages, not this body.

### Runtime output

Setup: built dist, `node openclaw.mjs status` with its own state dir and config, no Gateway running. All token values are synthetic `ghp_` strings, and each full output was checked for them before printing.

- Scenario A: local mode, `gateway.auth.token` set in config, and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` set in the shell to a different value.
- Scenario B: remote mode, with a fake token in the `gateway.remote.url` query string, to show that status output still masks secrets.

**Before, on main `f3638439b92`**

Command:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs status
```

Output (the matching status lines):

```text
-- scenario A
Secret diagnostics:
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN conflicts with gateway.auth.token: *** OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN from the shell, ~/.openclaw/.env, or launchctl env if gateway.auth.token is
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
-- scenario B
│ Gateway                 │ remote · ws://127.0.0.1:28799/?token=*** (config gateway.remote.url) · unreachable         │
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
```

"Remove" is masked as `***`, and the line ends at 160 characters.

**After, on this branch `f094ac3eb97`**

Command:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs status
```

Output (the matching status lines):

```text
-- scenario A
Secret diagnostics:
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN conflicts with gateway.auth.token. Remove OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN from the shell, ~/.openclaw/.env, or launchctl env if gateway.auth.token is intended, or point gateway.auth.token at ${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN} if the environment variable should supply the token.
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
-- scenario B
│ Gateway                 │ remote · ws://127.0.0.1:28799/?token=*** (config gateway.remote.url) · unreachable         │
leak check: no synthetic token value in the full output
```

The whole hint is shown with "Remove" readable, and the fake token in the URL is still `***`. No synthetic token value appears in either output.

Not shown: `openclaw status --all` output. It uses the same diagnostics helper, which the regression test covers through the `status --all` report.

Known limit: other diagnostics shaped `<path>.token: <words>` can still lose their first word to the console output redactor. This change does not touch the shared redaction rules.

prs.title: improve(ci): avoid duplicate release source guard scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release qualification's combined source check runs the full database-first legacy-store scan twice: once during fail-fast preflight and again at the end of architecture checks.

## User Impact

Developers and release qualification retain the same checks, but a combined architecture run performs one full legacy-store scan instead of two. Standalone architecture and policy-only invocations still enforce the guard. The accompanying CI repairs preserve ambiguous announcement custody, wait for Crabbox heartbeat cleanup, and correct QA request classification. No migration or action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the early preflight guard and share the remaining architecture chain through a package script. The existing orchestrator selects that chain only when its ordered preflight stage succeeds. Failed preflight still stops before typechecking; no cache, environment flag, parallel runner, or new planner is added.

Historical intent is preserved: commit `50c82b3020064d553ff0110c668b465325cff569` wired the guard into both preflight and standalone architecture. This removes only their duplicate composition, not either independent entry point.

## Optimization evidence and limits

- Production orchestrator regression: the base records **two** actual package-script guard leaves and fails the assertion; the change records **one**. Full, non-lint, preflight-only, policy-only and standalone architecture retain one guard; injected preflight exit 7 prevents typechecking.
- **84 focused tests passed**, plus targeted TypeScript, script/test lint, formatting and diff checks.
- [Existing npm qualification job 133761031368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43995795589/job/133761031368) ran the guard at 02:03:53–02:08:28 UTC, then again at **02:31:00.701–02:31:51.175 UTC (50.474 s)** on November 17. The first overlaps other preflight work; only the trailing copy is removed.
- **No measured patched-host or whole-FRV speedup claim.** About 50 s is a log-based per-job opportunity. Another qualification job or independent CI can dominate the parent barrier, yielding zero parent improvement. Setup, job count, runner allocation and dependency barriers are unchanged: there is no new queue/setup cost in exchange for less aggregate work.
- Optimization-only simplification: production +9/-3; tests +39/-1 against merge base. Necessary growth protects standalone/fail-fast coverage at the real orchestration boundary, without test-only production hooks.

## CI repairs and provenance

The owner requires repair of inherited failures, not attribution-only waivers. Historical [CI 44007899705](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44007899705) failed seven substantive jobs and its aggregate gate on synthetic merge `093beb6f6ae1e4a8df5c209d79708fd8cb32f48f`. Historical ClawSweeper success is not current-head approval.

Original-author cherry-picks retain their upstream references: #200402 UI test ownership (`a62e4e1`), Docker copied-fixture dependency manifest (`84262afe`), #200419 FaceTime mock (`36549cb`), #200428 browser exit/error contracts (`d0daf88`), #200450 Codex auth/recorder fixtures (`8f0d03f`), and #200466 Crabbox physical process cleanup (`6247dc4`). The nine affected browser/Codex/FaceTime/Crabbox focused files pass; the Docker copied-harness reproduction and UI inventory guard pass. No tests are skipped, expected-failed or weakened.

### Discord completion custody

An automatic send without a message identity correctly produced an ambiguous receipt but omitted the completed-answer fact. Settlement then mistook it for failure before answering and credited consumed child input as successful delivery. The fix records the empty visible-answer fact already used by the adjacent failed-delivery branch; it adds no schema, retry policy or settlement owner.

The original isolated-Gateway E2E passes **9.255 s** with its assertions unchanged; **122 announcement/requester-settlement tests pass**. The compact classifier regression fails on the unpatched producer (one failed, four passed). Earlier proxy-induced ECONNRESET runs were setup failures, not product proof. Scoped types, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. [Runtime evidence follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200379#issuecomment-6968363903) distinguishes synthetic transport proof from a live Discord send.

Simplification: two production lines and a strengthened existing assertion with zero test-line growth. Before the Telegram repair below, upstream/Discord repairs added production +27/-13 and tests/config fixtures +134/-95 against the previous revision; whole-PR deltas at that point were production +36/-16 and tests/config fixtures +173/-96.

### Telegram QA request classification — `be4c9288b492`

[CI job 134554652358](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44230434402/job/134554652358) failed the recovered-artifact E2E. The original test reproduced on its actual merge `d17eebcfc4cc2cc0133a543072e0f1f99befc30e` (PR `bac8d1b03098` into main `a2c1b0e86ff9`). prs.title: fix(feishu): streaming cards repeat the reply so far when preview and block streaming are both on
prs.body:
Related: #192446, #192482

## What Problem This Solves

With `channels.feishu.streaming` set to `{ mode: "partial", block: { enabled: true } }`, every card after an idle close restarts the reply and repeats earlier paragraphs. Replays on main `06e3bb94b2d1` confirmed this after #192482, which documented but did not fix it.

## User Impact

Ordinary continuation cards start after accepted text. The fix stays Feishu-only with no configuration or public API change.

Recovery credit belongs to its first covering preview occurrence. Block-only recovery grants no credit. Partial receipts must cover the frozen earlier base before crediting the current message. A start during a held close freezes earlier text without provisional credit.

An old block uses its source's accepted remainder only with unused current-preview coverage. A frozen open-card copy survives previews and text-free starts. A matching old block advances that copy. Suppression needs a known cursor and current preview coverage. Without a cursor, the first matching block appends. Suppression grants no recovery credit.

When no earlier message has shown preview or block text, a covered lower index prompts the dispatcher to re-learn its source offset. The same callbacks can describe a restarted subscription or a previewless earlier message's late block. That trade matches main.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core idles before delivery finalization. Feishu closes the card and corrects provisional coverage at settlement. Recovery cannot cross a failed gap. Rewritten prefixes keep the whole snapshot. Final text prevents rebuilding. Late settlement keeps appended blocks, but later snapshots can replace them.

Continuation cards reopen unfinished fences. A cut after the marker or inside the info string completes the opening line from the extending snapshot and keeps the code. With no code yet, the completed opener stands alone. A cut after the complete opening line reuses the original opener. A matching closing-fence remainder and following blank lines drop. A completed non-opener stays literal. The scanner uses CR, LF and CRLF endings and treats Unicode line separators as data. The old card gets no synthetic closer. Continuations drop leading separator whitespace and keep indentation.

Accepted limits remain.

- The unlearned index gap can lose text with rejected closes. No built-in route was established.
- Measured text-free restarts now match main's count except `u4-block-first-next`, `u11-nomatch` and the selective-prefix case. Restarts after the failed attempt or any earlier message showed preview or block text still repeat. A first block arriving before its preview or not covered by it can leave later blocks repeating too. The selective-prefix replay closes `[P] C.[P] C.` where main closes `[P] C.`. This PR introduced those above-main repeats.
- A fresh subscription creates the index gap only after an earlier counted assistant start. Pre-start failures add no epoch. Retry evidence combines source traces and synthetic core-subscriber replays. No complete provider retry loop was run. The configured-prefix replay uses the core dispatcher, so that case reaches a built-in formatting route.
- Rejected CardKit writes recover the whole block, including already shown text. Main sends the same static. Gaps, non-prefix receipts, recovered tails and preview catch-up can repeat accepted text. A lagging preview can add a copy. A successful held close after a new message starts repeats its frozen earlier preview, as on main. Eleven recorded core pipelines kept preview delivery before blocks.
- Eight direct plain-index orders still exceed main and round 17. They are `f22-1512`, `f22-0767`, `f22-1889`, `f21-1582`, `f21-0555`, `f22-0378`, `f21-2129` and `f21-2032`. They combine accepted-rest consumption, starts, held closes or partial receipts. No safer Feishu-only replacement was established.
- An unmatched old block appends after current text. A later snapshot can replace it and an accepted close suppresses recovery, as on main. In `f22-2327`, the final behavior and main show no `Y.`. In `f61-1644`, the final behavior shows two `X.` copies against three at round 18 and main. Main replaces the same old occurrence, then masks its loss with another repeat.
- A held close rejected before any later preview can lose its unaccepted text, as on main. A later rejected close can lose an earlier frozen base, as on main. A restarted twin can coalesce with an in-flight close. These complete routes remain unproven.
- Core collapses identical consecutive paragraphs in previews but not blocks. A removed preview copy can arrive later as a block or share recovery with a separately authored copy. The latter gets credit once. Normal response prefixes decorate blocks but not previews, so unmatched text appends on main too.
- Block chunks, including reopened fences, glue to the preview without a separator, as on main. Covered blocks can open empty cards. Finals during an earlier close show the whole message. Mid-word cuts remain.
- Only fenced code reopens. Tables, lists, block quotes, HTML and fences inside quotes or four-space indentation do not. Cuts inside markers, content lines including inner fences, continuation indentation or inline backticks can render wrong. Separator-only U+2028 or U+2029 extensions can lose that info-line separator, as before this change.
- An unfinished closer-looking line extended into code can lose one `~` after an empty-answer reasoning update. A final then preview before late settlement can lose `X.`. These and close-before-card-start lack an established complete core route.

A full fix needs core to pass the new message's index to `onAssistantMessageStart`, which this PR does not change.

Candidate b and the empty-preview relaxation pass all committed rows. Candidate b removes the `u4` and `u11` repeats, while the relaxation removes only `u4`. Both add `f22-2350` above main with four `X.` copies against three. A prefix-metadata repair also introduced other repeats and losses in probes. Older open-copy and recovery-credit variants lack final-file reruns. Removing the nonblank-opener-tail guard passes the fence rows but changes the separator-only Unicode probes.

Tests remove 88 blank separators and join mock calls, a comment and an assertion with a local rename to keep net test lines at 0. Existing assertions remain. The support file equals main. Removing blanks does not reduce those counts.

The Gateway proof comment reports runs on `5f153378`, before rounds 20 to 22.

Hash-restored swaps select 79 of 156 tests and skip 77.

| previous head `5f153378` | 7 failed, 72 passed |

The corpus ran on `40430f95`. Round 22 changes only comments and tests. Of 1,197 saved cases, 1,189 are identical and eight change. Of 119 final controls, 117 are identical and two change. All 119 matched-main controls are identical. Of 1,470 recordings, 1,460 are identical and ten change. Those changes are the split-fence repairs. All 117 source-order and 87 accepted-receipt comparisons stay unchanged from rounds 19 and 20.

prs.title: feat: install GBrain without Bun on Apple Silicon Macs and x86-64 Linux
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GBrain plugin (#200625) needs Bun to install GBrain. On a clean Mac or Linux machine that meant a terminal step after the one-click install: run Bun's installer, and on Linux install `unzip` first.

## User Impact

User impact: on Apple Silicon macOS and x86-64 Linux without Bun, installing the GBrain plugin is now the only step. The plugin installs GBrain's own release binary and connects; on a clean macOS VM it was connected 14 seconds after the install request. Existing Bun users keep the same Bun install. Intel macOS and ARM Linux, where GBrain publishes no binary, still show the Bun command.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `gbrain` is missing and Bun is not installed, the plugin:

1. Reads GBrain's stable version from its documented `stable/VERSION` file.
2. Downloads that release's asset (`gbrain-darwin-arm64` or `gbrain-linux-x64`) to `~/.gbrain/bin/gbrain`.
3. Accepts it only when GitHub's build-provenance attestation for its SHA-256 names that asset and GBrain's release workflow on `master`. This is the same check GBrain's own binary self-update uses (`src/core/binary-self-update.ts`). Nothing is made executable or moved into place before the check passes.

GBrain then owns the binary as it does any install: `gbrain mcp expose` supervises the service, and `gbrain upgrade` self-updates the binary in place. When Bun is present the plugin keeps using Bun, so existing installs and the GitHub API limit (see below) cannot block a host that can already install.

The release download uses GitHub's fixed download URL; only the attestation lookup uses GitHub's API (one unauthenticated request per install). The plugin logs where it installed GBrain and that `~/.gbrain/bin` must be on `PATH` to run `gbrain` in a terminal. It does not edit shell files.

## Evidence

**Clean hosts, packed candidate, live model:**

| | macOS 15 VM, Apple Silicon (binary path) | Ubuntu VM, ARM (Bun fallback) |
|---|---|---|
| Bun on host before install | none | none |
| User steps | install only | install + `apt install unzip` + Bun command |
| Connected after install | 14 s | 64 s after Bun |
| `~/.gbrain/bin/gbrain --version` | 0.60.734.0 | (Bun install) |
| Recall after Gateway restart | ✅ | ✅ |
| One `brain.pglite` holder, 2 concurrent sessions | ✅ | ✅ |
| Stop / kill / key rotation → recall | ✅ ✅ ✅ | ✅ ✅ ✅ |
| `gbrain upgrade` (from 0.60.733.0) → recall | ✅ | ✅ |
| Uninstall keeps service and brain | ✅ | ✅ |

- Earlier runs of the same flow each failed one step: macOS run 2 and ARM Linux run 1. The failing steps were the service-restart recall, where the Gateway's MCP client tried GBrain moments before its restarted service answered, and one of two concurrent recall turns. Both were green on the next run. This is the known MCP retry gap from #200625.
- One macOS run hit GitHub's unauthenticated API limit (HTTP 403, 60 requests an hour per network). That led to dropping the releases API call and to a clear "limit used up, resets within an hour" status. The plugin retries within 10 minutes.
- x86-64 Linux (privileged Ubuntu container under Rosetta): the binary runs, `gbrain init` and `gbrain serve` work with health `ok`, with no Bun, git or unzip on the host.
- Unit tests cover the binary install, a failed download, Bun-first ordering, and the attestation check rejecting a fork, another workflow, another branch, the wrong asset or the wrong digest.

- Local ClawSweeper review (local range `origin/main...90ad0c3793`): complete, "patch is correct", 0 findings. Earlier rounds found that an existing Bun install could be skipped, that a GitHub API limit could block a Bun host, and that the Bun-free e2e assertion could pass with Bun present; all fixed.

**Known gaps:**
- No full x86-64 Linux e2e. GBrain installs no service inside containers, and no x86 Linux VM was available.
- GBrain upstream: after an upgrade, `gbrain upgrade` checks the new version through `PATH`, not the binary it replaced. Without `~/.gbrain/bin` on `PATH` it swaps the binary, fails, and skips the service restart.
- GBrain upstream: `gbrain upgrade` reads the stable channel with `git ls-remote`, so a binary install on Linux needs `git` to upgrade (Bun installs had the same need).
- GBrain upstream: no binary for Intel macOS or ARM Linux.

prs.title: fix: keep Discord capture teardown safe after broker startup failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Discord transcript capture E2E can fail during teardown when background model catalog preparation opens the local spawn-broker socket. Its network fence mistakes IPC for an unexpected `null:NaN` network destination, and failed capture creation then leaves cleanup unable to finish. This signature appeared on five unrelated PR heads within three hours.

## User Impact

Developers retain the test's unexpected-network protection without rejecting local IPC. Catalog resource construction failures can settle cleanly; genuine cleanup failures remain owned and visible at shutdown. No configuration or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow nonempty IPC `path` options through the test fence while retaining its TCP host/port checks. Exercise a real IPC connection and negative TCP controls inside the existing E2E.

At the production owner, record whether an attachment attempted to dispatch its factory. A connection rejected before dispatch can abandon its uncreated broker claim through the existing `abandonUnattached` contract. After dispatch, native cleanup receipts remain mandatory. If construction cleanup itself fails, retain that obligation with the native source. The catalog pool stores only an acquired capture owner, so later close does not replay a settled creation failure.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and lifecycle producer inventory</summary>

The fence's host/port extraction was the immediate defect (`test/e2e/gateway-transcripts-discord-capture.e2e.test.ts:126`). Node normalizes `net.connect(path)` to an options object with `path`, without host or port. The broker client uses that exact call (`src/process/spawn-broker/resource-client.ts:121`).

Background catalog work is intentional: publication invokes `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs` without awaiting discovery (`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts:590`, `prepared-model-runtime.refresh-scope.ts:53`). Timing decides when the cold pool needs IPC. Pool preparation is joined by `WorkerTaskPoolCore.close` and `joinWorkerTaskPreparationCleanups`; there is no evidence that this signature requires an unjoined pool-startup defect.

Task producers traced through this lifecycle:

| Producer | Lifetime / settlement owner |
| --- | --- |
| Config/static publication and auth-change publication; degraded-startup continuation when enabled | Publication queue, agent build completions, standalone activation tails; `closeModelRuntime` joins them |
| Post-publication catalog refresh; explicit full/native catalog and scoped auth demand | Catalog access `pending`, `nativePending`, `pendingAuth`; generation custody spans acquisitions |
| Expiry refresh, native-login rechecks and failed-discovery retry timer | Catalog/auth owners; retirement cancels the retry timer and rejects further work |
| Synthetic-auth and Codex-version probes | Worker request `captures`, abort controllers and watchdog; `stop` aborts and joins probes |
| Catalog/auth task dispatch, notifications and host exchanges | Worker request `tasks`, pool task custody; request `finally` stops the watchdog and releases credential batches |
| Shared pool rotation, recovery and retirement callbacks | `gatewayCatalog.rotating` / recovery, registered process-close callback; retirement stops borrowers and closes the pool |
| Pool root preparation, plugin capture owner, source-root creation and worker launch | `preparingRoot`, core preparation cleanup, `releaseRoot`, capture-owner close |
| Broker process startup, socket-connect callback/retry/deadline, initialization microtask and resource-message delivery | Broker lease plus attachment; undispatched claims can be abandoned, dispatched resources require close receipts; failed constructor cleanup now remains source-owned |
| Capture native-load notifications and source/native root operations | Plugin capture owner/client; source/native roots release before independent-owner close |
| Test provider handlers, Discord capture/STT scheduler work, agent turns, Gateway startup and skill watchers | Existing response/error accounting, fixture close + scheduler stop, `agent.wait`, `startupSettled`, Gateway close and `closeSkillsWatchers`; test fence stays installed through cleanup |

Previously, the rejected connect made `attachment.close()` throw before `lease.close()` / `release()`, producing `Native resource creation cleanup failed`. The pool also cached the rejected capture promise, so its own close rethrew creation failure. Process runtime close correctly aggregates failed cleanup and keeps shutdown retained; this patch fixes the resource producers rather than suppressing that safeguard.

Smallest-fix pass completed. Delta: production +22/-9 lines; tests +41/-7 lines. No shared test helper, retries, timeout increases, assertion weakening, skips, baseline or changelog edits.

</details>

## Evidence

- A dependency-free probe executed the actual fence callback through real Node sockets: base `net.connect(path)` reproduced `unexpected socket destination null:NaN`; the fix accepted string/options IPC and allowed loopback TCP, while rejecting a foreign host, foreign port, empty-path TCP and numeric-string TCP.
- `git diff --check` passed. The pool regression now requires successful close after failed factory creation and adds a synchronous connect-refusal case, retaining the broker-retirement assertion.
- Requested local E2E attempt: `timeout 180s env OPENCLAW_TEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/e2e/gateway-transcripts-discord-capture.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. It exited 2 before collection: this worktree has no `node_modules`. The pool suite has not run locally; test wall time and CI seconds are unavailable.
- Touched-file lint commands for core files and this root E2E stopped before linting because dependencies are absent. The typecheck runner bootstrap also cannot resolve its compiler (`tsrs/package.json`); typechecking remains unverified.
- Repeated 20x / three-shard / load proof is blocked: `timeout 50s crabbox run --timing-json -- CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/e2e/gateway-transcripts-discord-capture.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed before allocation because the resolved `ascii-box` provider requires `ASCII_BOX_API_KEY`. No box or run URL was created. No stress, broad suite, install, container or browser work ran on the production host. PR CI supplies broad proof; the repeat campaign remains uncovered.
- Shared autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) reviewed the complete local candidate against `4a44f2031e866e7ee430d01ece41340cefddac5e`, identical to committed head `54b6e220fcad67cde9b9f5844a897261c544721b`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Review included unchanged broker claims, pool preparation/close, catalog request and generation lifetime owners; it did not execute tests or builds.

prs.title: fix(codex): continue unchanged protected turns without a relay
prs.body:
## Problem

`368809d32848` added `assertCodexProtectedContextCarrier`, which fails a Codex turn before dispatch when all of these are true:

- the turn carries producer-annotated conversation context
- the thread is protected by active native work
- the connection has no parent-local inference relay

It fires even when the context hasn't changed and no compaction has happened. The error, "requires a current parent-local inference relay; the native thread is claimed by active work", gives the user no next step. The guard shipped in `v2026.10.10`, `v2026.11.1` and `v2026.11.2`, but `main` never had it, so release-line behavior differs from `main`.

## Solution

Back out `368809d32848` on `release/2026.11.3`, removing all three call sites and `protected-context-carrier.ts`. This matches `main`, where the helper doesn't exist.

`git revert` conflicted in the tests, so this isn't a pure revert:

- The relay-after-compaction assertions in `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts` stay. They cover the relay itself, not the refusal.
- The no-relay test now asserts that an unchanged continuation reaches `turn/start`, with no `thread/start`, `turn/interrupt` or `thread/unsubscribe`.
- The relay-loss-at-dispatch test is removed along with the guard. The `client-runtime` mock keeps its `importOriginal` spread and `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` is unchanged; the first revision restored a closed mock and failed the mock-exports ratchet, which `1114170451fc` fixes.

## Impact

- Unchanged-context turns on protected no-relay threads now run instead of failing.
- Changed context on a protected thread is still refused, now with the actionable "still has background work after waiting for cleanup; stop its running work and retry." The old test matched `/claimed by active work/` only because the guard's own message contained those words.
- Accepted gap, same as `main`: without a relay, native compaction can drop conversation context, so a continuation can run without it. Codex rebuilds compacted history from user messages, the summary and canonical initial context (`codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs`). `dynamic-tools.md` keeps the existing limitation text; the paragraph describing the refusal is removed.
- Relay-backed connections are unaffected.

This branch keeps its existing doc wording rather than `main`'s "full handoff" text: `main`'s docs describe a handoff, but `thread-policy.ts` is identical on both branches and this PR changes no handoff code.

## Evidence

Rerun on the 11.3 rebase: `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts`, `run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts` and `thread-lifecycle.test.ts`, 92 passed. Original runs on the 11.2 branch:

- `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts` and `run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts`: 18 passed
- `thread-lifecycle.test.ts`, `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts` and `run-attempt.test.ts`: 297 passed
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `check:test-mock-exports --base origin/release/2026.11.3`: pass
- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: fail, with no errors in `extensions/codex` or other files this PR touches. Errors are in `feishu`, `browser`, `discord` and `telegram`; I didn't rerun these on the base commit.

Not proven: a live Codex app-server run, and how often real connections have no relay.

## Release note

This targets `release/2026.11.3`. It was first opened against `release/2026.11.2`, but that line shipped with the guard on 2026-11-08 before this landed, so the PR was rebased onto the 11.3 tip `40223c5cc262` (clean cherry-pick). Merging it changes product code on the 11.3 candidate. It's an operator-requested addition, not a confirmed release blocker.

prs.title: feat(plugins): tell agent hooks when the turn read network content
prs.body:
Related: #197881 (agent hooks only; tool hooks stay open there), #107069, #196857

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that stores turn content (memory, logging) cannot tell whether the turn read network-sourced tool results, so it stores text from a fetched web page with the same trust as text the user typed. Core already tracks this per turn and records its own memory writes as `untrusted` when it is set.

## User impact and contract

Seven existing hooks expose read-only `ctx.turnTainted`: `before_prompt_build`, `llm_input`, `llm_output`, `before_agent_finalize`, `agent_end`, `before_compaction`, and `after_compaction`. No new config or enforcement. Tool hooks remain out of scope.

- `true`: the tracker observed a network-marked tool result or inherited taint (for example, on a memory flush).
- `false`: the tracker observed none so far. This is not a trust attestation.
- `"unknown"`: no measurement is available, including on a runtime without a reporter. Treat a missing field on an older host the same way. Compare explicitly; the string `"unknown"` is truthy.

The change reuses core's tracker and does not record URLs or sources. It does not change what sets the flag, input provenance, or when hooks run.

## Evidence

At `65e5cef860f3`, the follow-up only documents the existing projection cast and braces two test loops; no runtime behavior changed. Four handler cases passed again. The accepted scope is the seven existing agent hooks only, under their existing permissions. Tool hooks remain out of scope.

Runtime proof of the unmeasured path: built the private QA runtime from `de0a27c40cfb` (the only later file change at `268be89fbdf5` is the handler regression test). A synthetic QA-channel message went through a real isolated Gateway and the production CLI runner to a deterministic local CLI backend, which received the prompt and returned the expected reply. No hosted inference or real credentials were used. A fixture plugin with the existing conversation-hook grant recorded:

```text
cli turn: provider=proof-cli model=sample
llm_input   turnTainted="unknown"
llm_output  turnTainted="unknown"
agent_end   turnTainted="unknown" success=true
```

The channel delivered the reply and the Gateway shut down with status 0. In a separate ungranted instance, the same turn completed but all three hook registrations were refused. Four handler regression cases also passed (absent, false, true, explicit unknown), covering all seven included hooks and two excluded hooks. Independent review of the test correction found no actionable issue.

At `de0a27c40cfb64f11355f875b4fe1fb825ac69c1`: independent full-delta review found no actionable findings. The projection has 10 isolated passing cases: seven intended hook names and three unrelated hooks. These cases exercise the projection, not a full runtime. GitHub checks and hosted review are recorded against the pushed head.

## Earlier contributor evidence (historical boolean-only revision)

Real Gateway on each side: built from the tree, isolated state, loopback, a local OpenAI-compatible model, and a small fixture plugin that logs whether `turnTainted` is present on each hook. Two turns through the Gateway's `/v1/chat/completions`: one asks for `web_fetch` of `https://example.com/`, one asks for `read` of a workspace file. The `after_tool_call` rows show which tools ran (tool hooks are not changed, so they never carry the field).

origin/main (7602443):

```
turn=network  hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=web_fetch
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=dispatch_action
turn=network  hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=network  hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=read
turn=local    hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=agent_end            has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolResults=read
turn=local    hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
```

Incoming contributor revision (8f0bbfa):

```
turn=network  hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=web_fetch
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=dispatch_action
turn=network  hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=true
turn=network  hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=true
turn=local    hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=local    hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=read
turn=local    hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=local    hook=agent_end            has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false toolResults=read
turn=local    hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
```

Known limitation, tracked in #197940: in our runs (2/2), after an embedded turn that called Tool Search `dispatch_action`, plugin `agent_end` handlers failed with `Plugin invocation scope is closed` before running. That is why the `web_fetch` turn above has no `agent_end` row: the model also called `dispatch_action`. With Tool Search off, `web_fetch`, `read` and `session_status` alone each ran `agent_end` normally.

This blocks the issue's main use case, retaining at `agent_end` after a network turn, whenever the turn used `dispatch_action`, until that bug is fixed. Tool Search is on by default, so that is common. The new field itself is correct on `before_agent_finalize` and `llm_output`, which run after the tools and are not affected, and a plugin can use those meanwhile. The `lifecycle-hook-helpers` test below covers `agent_end` handlers getting the field through the shared builder, and the `read` turn above shows it live on `agent_end`.

Tests (red on origin/main, green here):
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/agent-hook-context.test.ts`: the hook context reports the real `createAgentTurnTaintState` flag (false, false after a local result, true after a network result), and omits the field when the runtime gives no getter.
- `src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.test.ts`: `agent_end` and `before_agent_finalize` handlers receive `turnTainted` as `true` or `false` from the harness context, and no field when the harness does not report it.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts`: run-loop compaction hooks read the flag when they fire (false before, true after).

The `lifecycle-hook-helpers` test fails with the harness forwarding line removed (`expected [ undefined, undefined, undefined ] to deeply equal [ true, false, undefined ]`).

Gates on the earlier incoming head (rebased on 126e63bf05b):
- `pnpm test` on the three files above plus `hook-context`, `turn-taint-state` and `agent-end-side-effects` tests: 6 files, 36 tests passed.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`: 23 passed. This is the test that failed CI on the previous head; it was broken on main by #197697 and fixed by #197976 (fails on 2035b0730f8^, passes on 2035b0730f8), so the rebase picks up the fix.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: every step passed except the dead export scan, which reports the same unused exports in `scripts/lib/` and `extensions/` on unmodified origin/main 126e63bf05b; this PR touches neither.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm check:docs`: passed.

On 6417045 (same source; later revisions change only docs, a type comment and tests):
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base 7602443 --head 6417045`: exit 0. The only declaration change is the added `readonly turnTainted?: boolean;` on `PluginHookAgentContext` (2 reachable declarations, 183 exports that reach the type). Additive, no removals.

prs.title: fix: announce run_stopped for exact Stops of reserved and exec-only runs
prs.body:
Related: #190906 (merged: added `run_stopped` for confirmed user Stops, including the registered-run notice this PR moves)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `run_stopped`, the plugin hook for a confirmed explicit Stop, misreports a `chat.abort` naming an exact `runId`: silent when that run is reserved (queued with a session target, not yet registered) or exec-only (only commands it started remain), yet fired for a registered run whose Stop the Gateway refuses.

## User Impact

Plugins now receive `run_stopped` for exact Stops of reserved runs with session targets and of exec-only runs, and no longer for a registered run whose Stop the Gateway refuses. Events keep `source: "client"`, the session and the exact run id; authorization rules and the response shape are unchanged. Worker-inference Stops behave as on main (Not covered).

## Why This Change Was Made

An explicit Stop is a `/stop` message or a Gateway client Stop such as `chat.abort` ("Explicit Stop" in `docs/plugins/hooks/reference.md`); this PR changes only exact Stops, a `chat.abort` naming a `runId` (a `/stop` message stops by session key, a channel one through `abortSessionRunTargetWithOutcome` in `src/auto-reply/reply/abort-operation.ts` and a `chat.send` one through `abortChatRunsForSessionKeyWithPartials` in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts`; it touches neither). That page says `run_stopped` fires after the Stop's authority is confirmed and before the runs commit cancellation, so a rejected Stop fires nothing. Each exact-Stop path now announces at that point:

- **Reserved and registered runs:** at a new `beforeCommit` callback in `abortSessionControllerInput`, after its abortability and authority checks and before any abort.
- **Exec-only runs:** at a new `onStopAccepted` callback in `abortControlledSubagents`, past the final authority check that follows the awaited `command:stop` hooks, before the commands cancel.
- **Registered runs, removed:** the old notice in `onAbortPrepared`, which fired before the abortability check.

<details><summary>Design notes for reviewers</summary>

- `applySessionControllerStop` (`session-controller.stop.ts`) passes `beforeCommit` through as a new `onInputCancelPrepared` option; the reserved path and the live exact-run path (`stopExactClientRun`) both announce there. Reserved-run Stop handling is extracted into `stopReservedClientRun` in `chat-abort-exact-run.ts`, beside `stopExactClientRun`.
- The registered-run change fixes behavior already on main. The notice came from `abortChatRunById`'s `onAbortPrepared` (added in #190906), before `abortSessionControllerInput` checked whether the turn could still be cancelled. When a queued run started while the Stop was still preparing, the Gateway replied `aborted: false` and the run went on to its model, but `run_stopped` had already fired. A deterministic test reproduces it, and the live race below measures it.
- `onStopAccepted` sits after the descendants' own `assertCurrent` catch, which is the exec-only path's authority verdict, so a Stop refused during an awaited `command:stop` hook fires nothing.
- A mixed Stop (exec-only commands plus worker inference) keeps main's order: worker inference is cancelled first, as on main, then the notice fires once, then the commands cancel. So its notice comes after the worker cancel rather than before it; this PR does not change worker ordering.
- Known synchronous-handler reentrancy edge: the owner checks once, `run_stopped` fires, then `operation.abort()` checks abortability again. If a `run_stopped` handler synchronously froze or completed the operation in between, the notice would be out for a Stop that then does not commit. The event exposes only `source`, `sessions` and `runIds`, with no operation handle, and `freezeAbort()` is called only from the turn's own execution paths, so the operation is unchanged. A follow-up doc line could make `run_stopped` handlers observe-only.
- This PR and #194216 both edit `chat-abort-exact-run.ts` and conflict in one hunk; whichever merges second needs a rebase. #194216 is a separate fix (after a user's Stop, the session's next turn is told the user stopped it); neither depends on the other.

</details>

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, before and after.** Base [`3caa4235398`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3caa42353988bd9f30b1f5784a940dc640fffd19) and this branch were each built and run as `node openclaw.mjs gateway` with isolated state, against a stub provider and an observer plugin that logs every hook. The branch build was a local commit with exactly the tree of head [`c0f77ea3827`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c0f77ea38272a79152a9c87e2d29b35c4f0cc6ab); only its commit message differed. That local commit, `2fa8c8c31be`, was never pushed, so it has no page; the captured outputs below print its hash. Scripts and how to rerun each case (the scenario letters below, D, F and J, and `f-tally.py` are that gist's): https://gist.github.com/TheDoshus/b0cc18fcbfd65b0331e32a8bef111a33

| Case | Base `3caa4235398` | This branch `c0f77ea3827` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exec-only Stop (control) | `run_stopped`: 0 | `run_stopped`: 1 |
| Exec-only Stop; requesting paired device removed during the awaited `command:stop` hook | `run_stopped`: 0 (Stop not delivered) | `run_stopped`: 0 (Stop not delivered) |
| Exact Stop of a queued (reserved) run raced against its release (delays 0..400 ms in 2 ms steps, 201 attempts per side) | 17/201 fired `run_stopped` for a Stop the Gateway refused (`aborted: false`: the run had been released and registered first, so this is the registered-run notice that fired before the abortability check); Stop won: 129, run first with no notice: 55 | 0/201; Stop won: 129, run first with no notice: 72 |
| Paired device with operator scopes (no admin), exact Stop of a foreign reserved run | rejected `INVALID_REQUEST: unauthorized`, 0 `run_stopped` | rejected `INVALID_REQUEST: unauthorized`, 0 `run_stopped` |
| Same device, exact Stop of its own reserved run | accepted `aborted: true`, exactly 1 `run_stopped` | accepted `aborted: true`, exactly 1 `run_stopped` |

Not exercised on a real gateway: a mixed exec-only and worker Stop (needs an enrolled external worker over `/worker`). Its worker side is main's code, unchanged.

**Tests and checks** on `c0f77ea3827`: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` (0 cycles) and type-aware `oxlint` on the changed files pass; the 2 changed test files pass 57 of 58 (`chat.abort-authorization.test.ts`, `chat.abort-cascade.test.ts`); the one failure, "does not stop descendants after the original caller is revoked during parent cancellation", fails identically on base here ("Linux child ownership requires a process owner without source-loader hooks", a local environment limit) and is not touched by this PR. Red on base first: with only this branch's test files applied to `3caa4235398`, 5 of its tests fail there and pass here (plus the environment failure above). The test-line allocation (`config/test-lines-allocations/run-stopped-exact-stops.txt`, this branch's entry in the repo's test-line ratchet budget) credits the branch's measured net, 196 lines.

<details><summary>Captured outputs (excerpts)</summary>

Scenario F race tally (`f-tally.py`):
```
before 3caa4235398: 201 raced attempts; control aborted=True run_stopped=1
  129  stop won (aborted:true)
   55  consumed first (aborted:false), no run_stopped
   17  consumed first (aborted:false) WITH run_stopped  <- the bug
after 2fa8c8c31be: 201 raced attempts; control aborted=True run_stopped=1
  129  stop won (aborted:true)
   72  consumed first (aborted:false), no run_stopped
    0  consumed first (aborted:false) WITH run_stopped  <- the bug
```

Scenario D exec-only Stop, base (`before-D-control-plugin-events.jsonl`, whole file: the `command:stop` hook runs, no `run_stopped`):
```json
{"t": 1794311236264, "hook": "command:stop", "phase": "enter", "sessionKey": "agent:main:proof-exec-control"}
{"t": 1794311238272, "hook": "command:stop", "phase": "exit", "waitedMs": 2008}
```

The same on this branch (`after-D-control-plugin-events.jsonl`, whole file: one `run_stopped`, after the hook):
```json
{"t": 1794311276838, "hook": "command:stop", "phase": "enter", "sessionKey": "agent:main:proof-exec-control"}
{"t": 1794311278846, "hook": "command:stop", "phase": "exit", "waitedMs": 2008}
{"t": 1794311278847, "hook": "run_stopped", "event": {"source": "client", "sessions": [{"agentId": "main", "sessionKey": "agent:main:proof-exec-control"}], "runIds": ["exec-control-1794311266713155847"]}, "ctx": {"agentId": "main", "sessionKey": "agent:main:proof-exec-control"}}
```

</details>

## Not covered

- Worker-inference Stops (an admin stopping model inference that runs on a worker environment, a separate machine enrolled with the Gateway over its `/worker` endpoint: worker-only, mixed, and the worker fallback when a reserved or registered parent cannot cancel) behave exactly as on main. Earlier revisions of this PR also covered them (see `619ef9dff4a`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/619ef9dff4a6653e9f907929e97cbe06517246b2); they move to a separate PR, not yet opened, once they can be proven against an enrolled worker. That PR also fixes a main behavior this one keeps: in a mixed Stop, worker inference is cancelled before the `command:stop` hooks and the final authority check, so a Stop refused during those hooks has already cancelled it.
- The session-wide Stop (`chat-abort-session-plan.ts`) still announces before its per-run checks. That is the session-level contract, left as it is.
- A reserved input with no session target yet: there is no session to name, so it fires nothing, as today.
- An exact Stop that finds nothing to cancel fires nothing.

prs.title: improve: reduce host CPU during shared-state reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bursts of shared-state reads repeatedly walk the same database-engine selection while charging worker admission. That selection is already a readonly captured fact, so each request spends host CPU and allocation measuring it again.

## User Impact

Shared-state reads use less host CPU for admission accounting. Responses, exact byte charges, queue limits, configuration, schemas, and worker authority are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain only frozen selections’ measured sizes in the existing request-accounting module, keyed weakly by selection identity. Scoped frozen selections get independent entries and are collectible when their owner releases them. Boot and resolved selections freeze their nested data. Offline database porting intentionally updates an unfrozen holder in place, so those holders remain uncached and get fresh charges.

A context-wide cache would miss every request: the transport captures a fresh context and environment. Read contexts already project the process environment down to the state directory and optional supervisor mode (#158655); #191907 already removed serialization and entry-array allocations. This change preserves both improvements and continues to measure fresh environments, paths, and commands. A context-only cache was rejected after it increased CPU in the production-shaped burst.

There is no existing serialized command length to reuse. Raw JSON length would also undercharge the current contract (48 serialized bytes versus a 58-byte command charge for a small machine-state read). The command walk stays unchanged.

The production delta is +12 lines: one weak map and its miss handling avoid expanding the context or transport contracts. Tests add 60 lines; the standalone benchmark adds 125 lines. No retired compatibility path or new configuration is introduced.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the parent because the same selection is traversed three times instead of once. It passes with the fix, including interleaved selections, a replaced context, replacement of an existing context's environment, and in-place offline-holder updates. All 25 focused request/transport tests pass, including exact UTF-16 charging and queued-selector capture. The new test takes 2 ms; the request test file takes approximately 78 ms (the two-file wrapper took 59.94 s, mostly compilation).

Acceptance rule: byte-exact charges for every request; one selection traversal per identity; CPU and allocation improvements beyond the A/A spread for captured contexts; no >20% regression for the unconfigured-engine or artificial full-environment siblings. Five serial A1/A2/B triplets per shape, each with 100,000 fresh contexts and 100,000 equality checks before the timed burst. All **4.5 million comparisons** match.

| 100,000-request burst | A1 CPU median / p95 | A2 CPU median / p95 | B CPU median / p95 | A2 → B allocated bytes/request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Actual two-key capture, configured SQLite | 100.84 / 102.17 ms | 100.43 / 104.66 ms | 47.19 / 47.89 ms | 1,221.82 → 828.13 |
| Counterfactual 150-key request environment | 1,539.52 / 1,576.96 ms | 1,569.18 / 1,587.69 ms | 1,499.93 / 1,521.55 ms | 8,347.01 → 8,059.46 |
| Actual capture, engine not installed yet | 46.80 / 47.00 ms | 46.61 / 53.87 ms | 46.79 / 49.82 ms | 870.66 → 869.60 |

Configured-capture CPU improves **53.0%** and allocation **32.2%**. A/A CPU differences are below 2.5% per configured-capture pair. Median wall time improves from 100.18 to 46.93 ms; the unconfigured sibling stays within control variation. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. The 150-key case is a stress control, not the current read-context shape.

The fixture has 150 synthetic environment inputs, projected to the reader's two facts, an eight-family SQLite selection, and four small read-command shapes. The timed loop includes fresh request/context/environment envelope construction. Measurement uses Node 26.12.1, main-thread CPU, and cumulative V8 allocated bytes. Shared-host load averages ranged from 19.1 to 24.0; exploratory CPU profiles are diagnostic only. This isolates request accounting and does not claim whole-Gateway latency, large-database I/O, or filesystem performance.

Reproduce using the committed benchmark, saving the parent module outside the checkout:

```sh
git show fdf0c95ad6fb62c312c613ae0b0f00ee3e60096b:src/state/openclaw-state-read-request.ts > /path/to/baseline.ts
# A1 and A2 (same source), then B; repeat five times serially:
node scripts/perf/state-read-request-bytes.ts --baseline /path/to/baseline.ts --module /path/to/baseline.ts
node scripts/perf/state-read-request-bytes.ts --baseline /path/to/baseline.ts --module /path/to/baseline.ts
node scripts/perf/state-read-request-bytes.ts --baseline /path/to/baseline.ts
# Repeat with --environment full150 and separately --engine unconfigured.
```

Validation: all 25 focused tests and final core/script/test types, scoped lint, format, and diff checks pass. `pnpm check:changed --staged` completed with a benchmark literal-type error (repaired; script typecheck rerun passes) and three unused exports outside this patch. The same dead-export scans reproduce all three on exact parent `fdf0c95ad6fb62c312c613ae0b0f00ee3e60096b`, with valid dependency resolution: `prepareSessionEventDelivery`, `DurablePilotInput`, and `DurablePilotCustody`. All were made unused by `703c82d20c5cbff62ba3c53eb35045006c9b1d02` (#200533), which moved the delivery helper’s caller into its own module and added the two unconsumed exported types. These are main regressions requiring follow-up, not a claim that the aggregate check is green. All other aggregate checks passed. Final Codex autoreview of the complete staged change against `fdf0c95ad6fb62c312c613ae0b0f00ee3e60096b` is scoped-clean through P2, including the mutable offline-holder contract. No Control UI import reaches the changed module.
