prs.title: improve(backup): avoid a repeated SQLite capture read
prs.body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

SQLite backup capture performs a second full hash read before the archive writer reads the same image again.

## User Impact

Backups avoid that redundant capture read while checking the digest and length of the bytes actually archived. Changed or incomplete deferred images fail before archive publication. No configuration or archive-format migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only backup capture opts into deferral, and only hard-link-only publication qualifies. The archive reader compares exactly what it emits; unread or filtered images receive a full comparison before publication. Retries clear previous verification, and deferred alias copies retain their own checks so pre-copy verification cannot hide mutation during copying.

Copied publication, replacement, after-publication callbacks, and callers that do not opt in retain their existing comparison. The legacy-audit retry and publication preconditions move to sibling modules to meet the line budget. Simplification retained one verification obligation per image; production changes are +105 net lines, tests +343.

## Evidence

- **Current focused proof:** eight files / 87 tests passed, covering archive-time mutation, digest and emitted length, filtering, interrupted-attempt cleanup, alias copying, transfer/replacement, legacy audit, and CoW. Targeted `core`, `core-test-infra`, and `core-test-state-logging` typechecks, lint on 11 files, format, whitespace, and the line/assertion/mock ratchets passed.
- **Regression proof:** on exact base `5dbf569b4b8552253c37fac93b32bdaf87a872dc`, five mutation cases incorrectly publish archives; all five pass with this patch. The reconstructed candidate matches the worker patch byte-for-byte (SHA-256 `f916cd8d1eebc39019cf90a654cb6f7133ed9fe855f92dc81e9ea34c9f17aa1e`).
- **Build and real CLI:** `qaRuntime` build passed with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2` after the default thread pool exhausted sandbox resources. A supported Node-runtime CLI `backup create --verify` and restore passed on isolated synthetic SQLite state; restored `quick_check` was `ok` and its one 1 MiB row matched.
- **Independent review:** native Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, GPT-6.1 Sol), complete local candidate against the exact base above, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings. Reviewed tree: `5eecc275c025eaeb881c329bdb4c2ff71f78b524`.
- **Non-benchmark diagnostic:** five interleaved default/deferred captures of a 1,056,768-byte image measured 2,113,536 versus 1,056,768 capture-hasher bytes; both archived 1,056,768 bytes, and all deferred archive comparisons passed. This demonstrates the removed capture read, not an end-to-end speed claim. Archived CPU/wall benchmark numbers were not rerun and are not claimed here.

- **Author-side CI repair (`e31bec0ff5002ec5a5c30f747a9bdddc80c8f27b`):** added `sqlite-snapshot-preconditions.ts` to the native PR wrapper extraction inventory. The original small-2 closure assertion reproduced locally on `7451525f84de859321521008df0b56f77549bd5b`; after the repair, both wrapper-closure and eager-import-closure suites pass (24 tests), including actual extracted dependency/lease consumers. Incremental independent Auto Review, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings. The capture implementation is unchanged, so its existing build, CLI, behavioral and type/lint proof remains applicable. Current candidate tree: `f3dc04266a3a81e6d552c1dbe79b4f4589006e23`.

The initial large-10 private-provisioner injection failure remains under causal investigation; no baseline classification is claimed.

**Gaps:** the default Bun CLI smoke stopped at SQLite header-probe discovery before capture; the supported Node CLI completed on the same fixture. That Bun CLI boundary remains unqualified by this run. CoW tests pass 6/6 on both exact base and candidate on Linux, but this host cannot reproduce or clear the three archived APFS clone-ID failures. Broader platform proof remains with CI.

prs.title: fix(signal): unblock approvals while the requesting turn is waiting
prs.body:
Closes #194029

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Signal approval responses wait behind the turn they need to release. Once dispatched, UUID approvers can be rejected after command normalization, and a typed approval confirmation can cancel the waiting turn with a transcript conflict.

## User Impact

An authorized owner can approve a waiting command from Signal using `/approve` or a supported reaction. Ordinary messages and session-mutating commands retain their conversation ordering. Existing access, exact-target approval checks, and durable audit records remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Route the existing narrow set of Signal controls and canonical approval-reaction candidates through a conversation-scoped control lane. Previously stored controls can move only from their exact original conversation lane to that conversation's control lane.
- Supply text-command facts for core active-run admission.
- Preserve UUIDs through Signal command/allowlist normalization instead of stripping their letters into phone-number-like values.
- Keep fast `/approve` exchanges visible in history but outside model context, using the existing context-free recorder contract. Their confirmations must not invalidate the transcript snapshot of the turn waiting for approval; the decision still reaches the model through the tool result.

The lifecycle type lives in the existing leaf types module, removing the review's import cycle. The existing routing helper moves unchanged into the context sibling to respect the oversized handler's growth guard. No schema, dependency, public SDK surface, or configuration option is added.

Related reviews: #175345 does not change Signal ingress; #191787 concerns native-approval capability metadata; merged #153829 supplies the Telegram control-lane precedent. The final recorder fix follows the existing context-free status mechanism from #192585.

## Conflict refresh — 2026-11-17

Merged upstream `edbc5bcea9b605a826cc722d298c784c6a8fef78` into the existing branch, preserving its four original commits. Updated head: `8ce7760f3ebe8ea065b5f00099fbc6c0448fafab`.

The only textual conflict was in Signal's inbound context helper: this branch relocates the existing routing helper, while upstream #200058 renders native mentions in quoted messages. The resolution retains both. Automatically merged changes preserve upstream response-prefix handling and restart tests alongside the approval fixes. The introduced PR diff remains 15 files, +269/-70.

- **176 focused cases pass in 10 files** on the resolved tree: 81 Signal cases (including upstream quoted-mention and group-mention tests), and 95 shared command/transcript cases. Signal wrapper wall time: 120.55 seconds; shared wrapper wall time: 98.78 seconds, including compilation.
- Production core and Signal package type checks, focused regression-test types, targeted lint, formatting, diff checks, pre-commit guard, and import-cycle check pass (0 runtime value cycles). The current test-line budget passes: +138 test lines, 400 allowance, 138 existing allocation credit; no baseline or allocation changes.
- Fresh independent read-only review of the public conflict-resolution bundle found no actionable merge regression. The initial agy review timed out without a result; the completed fallback review covered the manual resolution and overlapping automatic merges.
- The first sandboxed test attempt was stopped after process-identity/loopback restrictions caused fixture failures. The completed run used the required local process and loopback permissions. One type-check attempt overlapped lint's artifact ownership; it was rerun successfully after lint completed.
- Live Signal/model, stable-upgrade, and final-effect authorization receipts below remain evidence for the explicitly pinned earlier head `d24bc8ab8ccbd869accc368c9b6a595016e65055`; those external/live checks were not repeated for this conflict refresh. New-head GitHub CI is separate from the earlier passing runs. [CI run 43902495410](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43902495410) currently reports `action_required` with zero jobs; no new-head CI pass is claimed. GitHub reports the updated PR mergeable; maintainer review and the workflow action remain pending.

## Evidence from the earlier tested head

- Base used for local proof: `8b023da72a1a595450b3071782ec1d4940bd459f`. Previously live-tested candidate: `d24bc8ab8ccbd869accc368c9b6a595016e65055`.
- Red before repair: DM/group queue controls do not dispatch; command context is `normal` rather than `text-slash`; three UUID formats fail approval authorization after command formatting; the fast-approval recording boundary omits `contextFreeCommand`. Corresponding regressions pass after repair.
- **206 relevant cases pass across 11 test files**: 113 Signal cases and 93 shared command/transcript cases. The final consolidated fixture was also verified by rerunning its 74-case lifecycle suite. Signal validation took 63.80 seconds; shared validation took 103.85 seconds, including compilation. Existing authorization, wrong-target, ordinary FIFO, replay, and routing controls remain covered.
- Official production-core and extension type checks, focused changed-test type checks, type-aware lint, formatting, diff and pre-commit checks pass. Temporary test configurations extend the repository configuration; no compiler settings were committed.
- Final clean Linux CLI-startup build passed in **2m 10.7s**. This is the startup profile, not a full release/package/declaration build. Local architecture check reports **0 cycles**.
- Independent reviews of the cycle repair, UUID repair, and final recorder diff returned scoped-clean. The test fixture stays in its existing suite and shrinks by consolidating repeated values.

### Live Signal and model proof

Verified the exact clean candidate with a real agent, configured OpenAI model, and the registered Signal account through Signal Desktop. Approval mode remained gated; only allow-once decisions were used.

```text
candidate: d24bc8ab8ccbd869accc368c9b6a595016e65055
whoami request: pending
/status during the wait: replied; displayed d24bc8a
/approve <redacted> allow-once: allowed via channel policy
whoami final reply: stdout openclaw
separate printf signal-final-ok request: pending
thumbs-up on its native prompt: allowed via channel policy
final reply: signal-final-ok
ingress after both cases: completed=20, pending=0, claimed=0, failed=0
```

These checks exposed and reproduced both the UUID normalization refusal and the typed-confirmation transcript conflict before their repairs. The final run completed without those failures. Only sanitized decision metadata and receipts are included here; no private transcript, account identifier, credential, or screenshot is published.

### Actual stable upgrade

The installed stable core and official Signal plugin, both 2026.11.1, accepted real Signal events into a separate state directory. The stable journal contained an ordinary completion, a claimed typed approval, and a pending reaction in the original direct-conversation lane. After stopping stable, applying the supported offline Doctor migration to the test copy, and starting the candidate, all three records were completed, with the pending reaction reconciled to the control lane; no pending or failed ingress remained.

Account, account UUID, owner allowlist, agent/session filters, default model, and exec/elevated/filesystem policies were checked against the verified native backup and retained. The fixture uses a separate workspace and disables scheduled jobs. Native reaction tests explicitly use forwarding mode `session` with the existing private-session filter; `targets` alone does not start Signal's native approval handler. This demonstrates real packaged-state transport replay, not continuation of an already terminated process's exec call.

### Final-effect authorization proof

The follow-up security review requested rejection at the actual decision owner, beyond the identity helper. On the same exact built head, a separate credential-free Gateway loaded the real Signal plugin and approval capability. Its real exec tool requested a harmless file-marker command; no approval or execution callback was mocked.

For each public resolver used by Signal—legacy `exec.approval.resolve` for typed commands and canonical `approval.resolve` for reactions—both checks passed:

| Resolver | Refused actor | Approval after refusal | Decision waiter released | Command ran before current approval | Same command ran after current approval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exec.approval.resolve` | Unlisted UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |
| `exec.approval.resolve` | Queued, then revoked UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |
| `approval.resolve` | Unlisted UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |
| `approval.resolve` | Queued, then revoked UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |

The unlisted UUID differs from the listed UUID only in letters, retaining the same numeric projection. In each revocation case, the old actor's control was first persisted with the real SQLite channel-ingress queue, and its pending row was checked. The Gateway's runtime configuration publisher then replaced the Signal approver policy while the original exec request remained alive. Only after publication was the unchanged queued control claimed and submitted to the real resolver. It was refused with `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`; `approval.get` still showed pending without a decision, the real decision waiter remained blocked, and the command's marker did not exist. A current listed actor then approved that exact request; the waiter returned allow-once and the real command created its marker. This positive control was repeated for all four cases.

This is an owner-boundary integration proof with synthetic identities and a test-controlled dispatch barrier, not another live Signal-network/model run. It deliberately submits to the final resolver rather than relying on earlier channel rejection. Runtime policy publication isolates the custody guard from file-reload scheduling; no authorization checks or process guards were bypassed. Separately, an attempted public `config.patch` policy reload was observed deferring Signal reload until active Gateway requests finish, so that timed-out attempt is **not** counted as revocation proof. The earlier exact-head live Signal/model proof remains the transport/user-flow evidence. The final isolated Gateway closed cleanly. No production source change was needed for this additional proof.

### Check boundaries

The local test-line guard against the historical base remains **25 lines over due to inherited debt**: base 6,533,876/6,533,851; candidate 6,534,014/6,533,989. The patch adds 138 counted regression lines and exactly 138 allocation credit. The shared baseline and unrelated tests were not changed.

The SQLite and HTTP fixtures were run on a qualified host with process-owner and loopback access. The exact candidate's [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42223925652/job/127915523030) and [architecture guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42223925652/job/127913150828) pass.

The candidate was used for bounded tests, and the normal stable service was restored. No permanent deployment or merge has been performed. Maintainer/security review remains required.

prs.title: fix(memory): resume watching when the remote memory subscription retires
prs.body:
Related: #177686

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: remote memory-file edits stop refreshing the index after the workspace subscription completes unexpectedly while the Gateway keeps running.

## User Impact

The manager warns and opens one replacement subscription. If that subscription also ends unexpectedly, it stops retrying and warns the operator to restart the Gateway. Existing indexed content remains searchable. No configuration or API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery stays with the existing watcher owner: clear the retired subscription's latches and retry once. Transport cancellation and retirement remain owned and joined by the existing shutdown path. A lifetime retry limit prevents a transport that repeatedly completes from spinning.

The previous description overstated search-time recovery: resident searches do not automatically refresh files on every query. Restarting the Gateway restores observation after the retry is exhausted.

#177754 adds diagnostics for the same completion path; this PR also implements bounded recovery. It does not claim to diagnose or fix the separate local macOS incident in #177686.

## Evidence

The count-only regression file and fixed 250 ms sleep are replaced by coverage in `manager-workspace-files.test.ts`:

- A later file edit after replacement must appear in SQLite before any search can refresh it.
- Repeated completion stops after two subscriptions, emits restart guidance, and preserves access to existing index rows.
- Normal cancellation remains quiet and manager close joins transport retirement.

Red-before proof: the terminal-warning regression failed on the previous PR head because the last warning was still “re-subscribing”.

Isolated post-replacement indexing/shutdown regression passed (67.425 s test time; 129.35 s total on Windows/Node 24.18.0). The terminal-warning/searchability regression passed separately (65.861 s test time; 130.10 s total). The normal shutdown case also passed. A combined run encountered a 180 s test-hook timeout; isolated replay does not establish the cause or fix that timeout.

Targeted lint, memory-core package typecheck, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. The test-line ratchet passed against the explicit PR base: the allocation is reduced from 89 to 66 net regression lines, leaving the shared baseline unchanged. The allocation covers indexing recovery and terminal/shutdown behavior in the existing suite.

An additional isolated proof launched the production native memory worker in real Worker threads, with actual file observation and the real index manager. It passed (70.471 s test time; 135.21 s total):

```text
native watcher started 1
native worker exited 0 aborted false
native watcher started 2
native post-replacement edit published in SQLite without search
native worker exited 0 aborted false
bounded retirement warning verified; both native workers joined
```

The earlier proof adapter did not boot a Gateway or exercise the remote Node duplex transport. The shipped-entrypoint proof below now covers that gap. Local autoreview could not isolate Codex authentication and produced no review verdict; isolation was not bypassed. CI results on the previous head do not validate these new changes.

The adjacent workspace-memory-client suite returned 6 passed and 1 Windows path assertion failure (expected POSIX /gateway/memory/note.md, received a Windows drive path). Its implementation and test file are byte-identical to the PR base and do not import the changed manager. This suite is not reported as passing.

## Shipped Gateway / Node proof (2026-11-09)

The earlier Worker-thread proof is now supplemented by the actual shipped transport on head `c9112c045571dcac661dd81b2eb95bb76553fd96`: separate Gateway and paired Node processes, the registered file-transfer workspace service, real `workspace.memory` duplex requests over WebSocket, native watch subprocesses, and the Gateway's SQLite index. This used a secretless Linux Docker container with Node 24.22.2, separate state directories, synthetic notes, and `memory.search.provider="none"`. It does not claim a two-machine/network-failure test or reproduce the separate local macOS incident.

Both processes were launched through `corepack pnpm openclaw` (`gateway run` and `node run`). A test-only Node preload observes the real `child_process.spawn`; on SIGWINCH it calls `stdin.end()` on the sole live `--watch-files` child. The shipped worker handles EOF and exits normally. No watch implementation, duplex channel, completion result, or indexing callback was replaced. No production source changes were needed.

Changed-head trace (UTC; synthetic process IDs):
```text
05:50:55.405 native watch PID 64083 started
initial SQLite row: alpha initial host note.
05:51:23.299 inject EOF into PID 64083
05:51:23.311 PID 64083 joined, exit 0
05:51:23.315 Gateway: workspace watcher ended unexpectedly; re-subscribing
05:51:23.333 replacement native watch PID 64212 started
05:51:34.379 edit remote memory/notes.md to beta changed host note.
05:51:48.927 read-only SQLite: memory_index_chunks and FTS contain beta
05:52:02.969 inject EOF into PID 64212
05:52:02.987 PID 64212 joined, exit 0
05:52:02.992 Gateway: workspace watcher ended unexpectedly again;
             restart the Gateway to restore remote memory watching
before shutdown: exactly two watch starts, no third; beta rows retained
```

The initial search only bootstrapped the manager. **No search or manual sync occurred between the first injected EOF and the beta SQLite observation.** The production configuration defaults periodic sync to zero.

A separate fresh Gateway lifecycle proved normal cancellation: watch PID 64818 started at 05:53:06.235; Gateway received SIGTERM at 05:53:21.712; the remote watch process joined at 05:53:21.769; Gateway reported clean shutdown at 05:53:21.863 (144 ms). No watcher-unavailable or unexpected-completion warning was emitted during this cancellation interval.

Original-base comparison used `5bd69e0a3365a3095df1d34576a6885de6fdf5d3` (the first PR commit's parent), rebuilt through the same CLI with the same paired Node/configuration. Initial alpha content was confirmed in SQLite. The native watch exited 0 at 05:57:16.182 after the same EOF injection. No replacement started. The remote file changed to beta at 05:57:28.968; at 05:58:13.410 (44.442 seconds later), SQLite still contained alpha, with exactly one watch start. No search/manual sync occurred in that interval. Thus the complete recovery behavior reproduces as failing on the original base and passing on the changed head.

Limitations retained: earlier combined-test timeout and Windows path assertion failure are not claimed fixed; this is not full-suite or fresh-CI proof. Setup/configuration failures were resolved before the traced scenarios. A nonfatal state page-cache warm `/proc/self/io` ENOENT appeared before the successful head run and is not claimed fixed by this patch.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor system agent for CLI defaults
prs.body:
Fixes #188953

## What Problem This Solves

On an explicit-ownership multi-agent install with `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set, `openclaw wiki status` without `--agent` fails with "No default memory-wiki agent is configured" even though an owner is configured.

- Problem: the CLI preAction resolves its default through the deprecated `resolveDefaultAgentId` (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts:528`), which only accepts legacy raw markers or a sole agent, so the configured system agent is ignored. The gateway request context and the active-memory query fallback have the same gap.
- Solution: use the core owner-aware resolver `resolveAgentOperationAgentId` at all three sites, reached through the existing private-local-only `memory-core-host-runtime-core` facade instead of expanding the public plugin SDK surface.
- What changed: three extension files (one import plus one call site each), one re-export line in `src/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-runtime-core.ts`, and regression assertions folded into the existing cli/query tests.
- What did NOT change: `--agent` precedence, legacy single-agent resolution, the no-owner error text, exit codes, and every non-wiki CLI surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveAgentOperationAgentId` is the existing core resolver for CLI operation owners; the memory plugin simply could not reach it, so the fix exposes it through the facade the plugin already imports.

Precedent: #197917 (agent-less cron job owners), #126504 (ambient owner resolution), #126234 (infer command owners) — same owner-aware resolver, merged.

- Best fix: swap the resolver in place at the three sites that decide an operation owner.
- Alternative: keep `resolveDefaultAgentId` and add a systemAgent fallback inside the plugin. Rejected: it re-implements ownership resolution in the plugin and drifts from the core rule.
- Risk: the only delta is which agent the wiki CLI picks when `--agent` is absent.

## User Impact

`openclaw wiki status`, `search`, `get` and `doctor` now work without `--agent` when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is set, matching other CLI operation surfaces. `--agent` stays authoritative, and installs with no configured owner still get the same actionable error.

## Compatibility

- Preserved: explicit `--agent` selection, legacy single-agent resolution, and the no-owner error string (byte-identical in the control rows below).
- Not claimed: no Windows or macOS run; gateway coverage is a local gateway only.

## Evidence

Base arm fails with the reported error; head arm resolves the configured `main` owner.

| Case (real CLI, isolated local gateway) | Before (base arm) | After (head arm) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wiki status`, no `--agent`, systemAgent=`main` | exit 1; stderr `No default memory-wiki agent is configured...` (107 B); no vault | exit 0; `Vault scope: agent (main)` (394 B) |
| `wiki status --agent ops` (control: explicit wins) | exit 0; `agent (ops)` (392 B) | byte-identical (`cmp` reports no difference) |
| `wiki status`, legacy single-agent config (control) | exit 0; `agent (main)` (394 B) | byte-identical (`cmp` reports no difference) |
| `wiki status`, 2 agents, no systemAgent (control) | exit 1; same 107 B error | byte-identical (`cmp` reports no difference) |

Controls: row 2 proves `--agent` still wins; row 3 proves the legacy path is untouched; row 4 proves the change cannot invent an owner when none is configured.

Both arms are the same checkout `4e94df6` built with the shipped pipeline (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts pluginSdkStrictSmoke`); the base arm restores only the three production files to merge-base `2995860`, and the control rows are byte-compared after normalizing the disposable run directory.

Latest-stable upgrade on the same state (release `2026.10.9` → this build): `wiki init --agent main` plus one ingest, then `doctor --fix`, then `wiki status` with no `--agent` reports `Vault scope: agent (main)` and `Pages: 1 sources ... 9 reports`, exit 0.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and a two-arm shipped build to analyze issue #188953, locate the root cause in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts`, and implement the fix. The implementer understands the code: agent-less wiki commands must resolve their owner through the core owner-aware resolver, which already honors `agents.defaults.systemAgent`. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix: keep rate-limited models visible in the model picker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a provider rate limit, a model can disappear from the chat model picker even though the account still has access to it. Users cannot see that the model is temporarily unavailable.

## User Impact

Models in a temporary cooldown remain listed as unavailable. The existing cooldown and retry time still apply, and models without credentials or excluded by model policy remain hidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared catalog visibility rule treated temporary unavailability as missing authentication. Keep credential-backed catalog membership during a cooldown, and let the Gateway and chat-command callers use that shared rule.

## Evidence

Same live Gateway before and after applying the patch. Private model names and the search term are redacted. The original cooldown deadline was preserved.

| Before: cooling model missing | After: cooling model visible and disabled |
| --- | --- |
| ![Model picker before the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af3a8dd0-8061-4f05-9dfa-6df577f0d21a) | ![Model picker after the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73fe328f-a24c-4a34-85c8-c725430a1b00) |

- Reproduced on a live Gateway: the default model list omitted a cooling model that the full catalog returned with `unavailableReason: "cooldown"`.
- Added one Gateway regression using the real auth-store projection. It fails on the base and passes with the fix; it also checks an available sibling, missing credentials, and a policy-excluded provider.
- All 33 focused tests passed, along with the production build, core typecheck, targeted lint, and whitespace checks.
- Independent review with the unchanged authentication and filtering context completed with no P0–P2 findings.
- Verified the fix on the same live Gateway while its original cooldown was still active: the row remained visible, `aria-disabled` was `true`, and the existing countdown was shown.

<details>
<summary>Change size</summary>

Production: 7 lines added, 3 removed. One 47-line regression extends the existing Gateway suite; one sentence documents the behavior. No new state or components.

</details>

prs.title: fix(postgres): preserve the first Gateway operation after host suspension
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the first Gateway operation failing after a suspended host resumes with dead PostgreSQL sockets retained by shared-state or update-bookkeeping workers.

## User Impact

The first resumed operation can use a new idle connection without restarting the Gateway. Transactions and uncertain writes still fail closed; dispatched SQL is never replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport already reconnects and validates idle connections on pool checkout. Retained connections never take that path. Reuse that same owner when the last completed server response was idle, and measure the existing one-second validation threshold with wall time so host suspension counts. No caller retry, new recovery service, schema change, or configuration switch.

The simplification pass retained 14 net production lines, 54 net test lines, six documentation lines and the required allocation. Existing transaction status supplies the safety boundary.

## Evidence

- Behavior qualification range: `938a72d4c1e4136d07f32156ed633f2f86a524a1..af098d8271d85899991b20b3b2b15423a8ed39e6`.
- The committed shared-state/update-bookkeeping regression expectations were run before changing production at `7e0ec3e59fad329618c43314d796529cf3ed59cc`: both failed (2 failed, 11 filtered/skipped; 12.07s), reporting `Shared-state worker retained a closed PostgreSQL connection` and `Existing-state writer retained a closed PostgreSQL connection`. These same regression cases pass with the fix. This base-red control is separate from the compiled Gateway comparison below.
- All 55 focused tests pass on that behavior-qualification head with real disposable PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector 0.8.7 (135.50s Vitest / 176.86s wrapper). Includes retained/pooled reconnect, suspension with only wall time advancing, lost-transaction refusal and shared-state historical migrations.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped typed lint and formatting pass. Independent agent review of the complete range found no actionable issues. This was not a local ClawSweeper/autoreview run.
- Real compiled Gateway comparison on the deployed integration source plus exactly this patch: baseline `7e0ec3e59fad329618c43314d796529cf3ed59cc` versus candidate `636cff64f7b83879d597c0936452745a3d900c34`. Relevant transport owners are byte-identical between baseline and this PR's upstream base. This is integration-build evidence, not a claim that upstream main was fully built.

<details>
<summary>Real Gateway reproduction and observed output</summary>

Use an isolated Gateway home, unique PostgreSQL schema/application name, and synthetic data. Create a coach through `agents.create` and a conversation with transcript messages. Freeze only that Gateway with `SIGSTOP`, wait 1.2 seconds, terminate its 17 application-scoped idle backends using `pg_terminate_backend`, then `SIGCONT`. Make `agents.create` the first post-resume RPC; do not retry it.

Baseline: first RPC returned `UNAVAILABLE` / `session_actor_reconciliation`; log contained `Shared-state worker retained a closed PostgreSQL connection`. Roster remained bootstrap + coach.

Candidate: first RPC returned `ok: true` in 2.726 seconds. New agent appeared; original bootstrap/coach entries, session ID and exact returned transcript messages were preserved. Transcript SHA-256: `825f9a4b6008b986200e7c2c89fefad402b8423d52a82b35254fe153f2915006`. Candidate run took 27.61 seconds, then shut down cleanly.

This is macOS process-freeze/socket-loss proof with real PostgreSQL, not a GCE suspend test or model-inference test. An ancillary cron-maintenance `Agent database resources are closing` warning occurred during new-agent provisioning; creation and transcript checks passed with no PostgreSQL reconnect error. Existing blackhole timeout and sub-second validation window are unchanged.
</details>

The integration source's full package build passes (4m54.3s), with its existing nonfatal UI gzip advisory. Its state test-type leaf has an unrelated unchanged `sqlite-file-copy.test.ts:142` callback/options mismatch; no aggregate `pnpm check` pass is claimed. Hosted CI remains separate.

The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193875#issuecomment-6674773643) covers the behavior-qualification head, finds no actionable correctness issues, and rates the real Gateway proof sufficient. Its requested base-red detail is supplied above. The small wall-clock unit contract is retained deliberately: a real terminated-backend test can recover through an already-observed socket error even if long-idle validation uses the wrong clock. The unit test advances only wall time and verifies validation before BEGIN and its absence inside an active transaction; the real PostgreSQL tests separately prove recovery and no write replay. No new review request is needed for this evidence clarification.

Current head `c9c8a257b9e8bb876b4b693e6ad525ec38d33a86` braces the pooled reconnect test's existing conditional and accounts for the two added test lines. Scoped `eslint/curly`, formatting, the test-line ratchet and whitespace checks pass. Production and test behavior are unchanged. OpenClaw main at `8ae6b3852f97` has pooled checkout validation; it still needs validation of retained idle transports. Hosted CI on the lint-fix head is pending.

prs.body:
Closes #200955

## What Problem This Solves

The PostgreSQL audit lacked real-database coverage of the first simple completion after Gateway plugin metadata is published. Existing plugin-scope tests did not exercise the PostgreSQL and mixed-store combinations.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. This adds qualification coverage only; production code, SQLite schemas and schema versions, migrations, persisted formats, and public configuration remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exercise the real acquisition and prepared-model owners with PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL, PostgreSQL/SQLite, and SQLite/PostgreSQL stores. The test discovers two plugins, loads only the selected provider, completes through a loopback HTTP fixture, rejects reuse after disposal, and checks for denied or executed host-thread PostgreSQL access. The file joins the existing database-worker test lane.

## Evidence

- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44231825547) passed at `66b29fee36eebc9530c2bdd54141bf32e95e638c`, including all four PostgreSQL 17 shards and PostgreSQL 16 Gateway cron smoke.
- All three added cases executed without skips on that head: PostgreSQL/PostgreSQL 6.970 s, PostgreSQL/SQLite 3.502 s, SQLite/PostgreSQL 2.702 s. See [the case-level log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44231825547/job/134559192607). These are individual case times; isolated-file wall time was not measured.
- Independent full-context autoreview, conflict-resolution review, and final guard-spy review found no actionable P0-P2 issues. [ClawSweeper reviewed the final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200956#issuecomment-6967984177) with no findings or remaining pre-merge moves. Formatting and diff checks passed. Production delta: 0 lines; tests and routing: +186 lines.
- The test observes synchronous admission throws through the pass-through spy's recorded results. The explicit negative control remains outside that observation window. Direct inspection of Vitest's implementation confirms caught synchronous throws remain recorded.
- Earlier CI caught and helped repair the guard binding lint errors. The branch also incorporates the already-landed unused-export fixes [#200935](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200935) and [#200943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200943).
- The initial broad run also reported two separate UI timeouts: [sidebar row after browser Back](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44227795099/job/134545885650), already recorded on main in [#200832](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200832) and still unresolved after [#200893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200893); and [automation editor field visibility](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44227795099/job/134545886213). These UI/Gateway paths and fixtures are unchanged by this PR; neither timeout is claimed fixed. Final scoped PR CI did not select those real-Gateway UI jobs.

Coverage is the configured-key auth branch and published Gateway metadata, not route-specific synchronous auth preparation, a full Gateway boot, or a live external provider. Next qualification candidates are persisted profile failover/health, plugin-owned credential revocation, and cancellation during preparation.

prs.title: improve(ios): fold live tool calls into one line per stretch during a turn
prs.body:
Related: #197429

## What Problem This Solves

While an agent works, iOS chat shows every tool call as its own row, so a busy turn pushes the conversation off screen until the reply finishes.

## User Impact

User impact: during a turn, each stretch of tool calls takes one line that shows the latest call, and tapping it lists the calls. Assistant narration, answers and media stay visible, and a finished turn looks exactly as it does today.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared chat presentation already folds finished tool work into **Worked** disclosures (#147540, #148002, #181339, #183557). This change applies the same grouping while the turn runs:

- **Live fold:** each contiguous stretch of tool calls, including pending ones, renders as one disclosure line labeled with the latest call. Visible assistant text freezes the stretch before it, and a new stretch starts after it. The line expands in place, and expansion survives updates, history prepends and the recorded history replacing the live rows.
- **Deliberate change, intended by design:** main keeps active work expanded (the iOS docs said "Active or unanswered work stays expanded", from #147540 and #148002). This PR folds active tool stretches by default on iOS and macOS. That is the purpose of the change: it brings native chat in line with the web Control UI, which now shows compact, chronological tool activity with independent disclosures (#198133). Three existing tests that asserted active work stays expanded now assert the folded line, and the docs sentence is updated.
- **Unchanged:** all assistant text and media stay inline in every state, whether or not the provider tags them `commentary` (the #181339 contract). Finished turns use main's disclosures, headings (operation kinds and non-success outcomes) and counts. Stored history, message identity, styling and scroll behavior are unchanged. Folding commentary is left for later, after #197429.

Fixed along the way, each with a regression test:

- Hidden tool activity stays hidden when search is open or folding is disabled.
- Tool and narration events that arrive in the same millisecond keep their arrival order.
- When recorded history replaces live narration, the narration is not drawn twice.

## Evidence

- 47 Kit tests in 7 suites and three real-app simulator UI tests pass on main `7bda9076ff9` with this change (`2f60e1c4464`, plus `b0fce8f535a`, which limits the 44 pt row height to iOS and passes the macOS Kit build and 47 tests; iPhone simulator, Xcode 27.2).
- Red/green: equal-millisecond ordering, live-anchor stability across history replacement, and duplicate narration on replacement each fail with only their fix reverted and pass with it.
- UI tests drive the real app through a deterministic fixture:
  - `testLiveToolFoldSegments` (provider-tagged commentary) and `testLiveToolFoldUnphasedSegments` (untagged text) tap the live and finished disclosures through five states. They assert all assistant text stays visible and answers stay in order.
  - `testLiveToolFoldPendingEvents` replays live agent events: a pending call before its result, a commentary stream update, the result, then recorded history replacing the live rows. It asserts exactly one call row and one copy of the narration after replacement, with the expanded line still open.
- On finish, the first answer moves 0 pt (tagged fixture) and 23 pt (untagged); on main it moves 36 pt. Geometry files are in the evidence branch.
- Strict SwiftLint parity with main on the configured iOS scope (58 = 58 findings, identical multiset). Changed files pass the pinned formatter, and the native localization inventory verifies.
- Codex and cross-family reviews of the earlier revision, plus ClawSweeper's review: all findings addressed.

### Clean comparison

Same fixture and simulator, mid-turn after the first answer while the last call runs. Before: main `7bda9076ff9` with the fixture and a capture-only UI test. After: `2f60e1c4464`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: five separate tool rows around the narration and answer](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/raw/4f3da94fbdee3c27657f3d45ca1865d17c2adebd/clean-before-live.png) | ![After: one line per stretch of calls, narration and answer visible](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/raw/4f3da94fbdee3c27657f3d45ca1865d17c2adebd/clean-after-live.png) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Separate live tool rows marked](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/raw/4f3da94fbdee3c27657f3d45ca1865d17c2adebd/annotated-before-live.png) | ![Folded stretch lines marked](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/raw/4f3da94fbdee3c27657f3d45ca1865d17c2adebd/annotated-after-live.png) |

Finished turn, before and after (unchanged layout):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: finished turn with Worked disclosures](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/raw/4f3da94fbdee3c27657f3d45ca1865d17c2adebd/clean-before-finished.png) | ![After: same finished layout](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/raw/4f3da94fbdee3c27657f3d45ca1865d17c2adebd/clean-after-finished.png) |

prs.title: test(ui): park the pointer outside the rail between titlebar trial clicks
prs.body:
## Problem

`ui/src/e2e/native-desktop-titlebar.e2e.test.ts` › "keeps linux window controls clear at 1280 pixels" times out intermittently in `checks-ui-e2e`. With the sidebar collapsed, `assertChromeClear` trial-clicks every visible rail and header button in turn. Since #199826, resting on a closed rail item for 300 ms opens that section's sidebar as a floating peek, which closes only when the pointer leaves the sidebar. On a slow runner the trial click on a rail item exceeds that delay. The peek opens, and the next header control sits beneath the floating panel. Playwright's pointer lands on the panel, never leaves the sidebar, and every retry reports `<div class="sidebar-panel-header"> from <div class="shell-nav"> subtree intercepts pointer events` until the 30 s timeout.

The peek behaviour is intended; the test's pointer path is what triggers it.

## Change

Move the pointer to the bottom-right corner, outside the sidebar, before each trial click. Leaving the sidebar cancels a pending peek and closes an open one. The assertions are unchanged. No product change.

## Proof

- Failure log: run 44217295448 (attempt 3), job `checks-ui-e2e (7/10)`, showing the interception above on PR #200655.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck and lint pass; the dead-export scan lists only three pre-existing exports in files this PR does not touch.
- Limitation: Chromium cannot launch on the authoring host, and the failure depends on timing, so a green CI run shows the case still passes but does not prove the race is gone.

Follow-up to the side-rail series (#199824, #199825, #199826) by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix: keep the Gateway responsive while extracting web pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fetching a large HTML page can stall unrelated Gateway work while Readability parses and renders it. The existing async extractor still performed that CPU work on the Gateway thread.

## User Impact

Readability extraction runs in a worker while preserving text, Markdown, titles, and the existing sanitized HTML size/depth limits. Cancellation and the existing HTTP request deadline stop the caller's wait; late extraction results cannot trigger fallback or enter the fetch cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin uses the existing SDK worker transport, compute sizing, shared admission, and pending task/byte limits. The extraction request contract is unchanged. Sanitization, cap checks, DOM parsing, Readability, and rendering move together; there was no redundant DOM parse or defensive clone to delete.

Accepted cancellation tradeoff: extraction already admitted to a worker continues to completion after a rare caller abort or timeout, and its result is discarded. Work retains the existing HTML limits. Core owns the race against the HTTP guard's existing composed signal; the plugin does not receive cancellation or create another timeout.

The production delta is +67 lines: +62 source lines for the offload and lifetime boundary, plus five lines declaring the package-owned worker entry. There are no new dependencies, configuration options, caches, or schemas.

## Evidence

Acceptance requires identical output and lower warm main-thread CPU/longest-callback p95. Any total-cost or first-use regression requires explicit owner acceptance.

The synthetic corpus has 20 pages across five article/document shapes and four sizes (50 KB, 250 KB, 900 KB, 2 MB), tested in text and Markdown modes. Five interleaved A1/A2/B rounds yielded 600 exact serialized-output matches in each of the source and packaged runs (1,200 comparisons total); all hashes also match the original checkout. The 2 MB cases preserve the existing null result after sanitization and the size cap.

| Warm packaged metric per extraction | Inline A1 | Inline A2 | Worker B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU median | 24.03 ms | 23.85 ms | 0.30 ms |
| Main-thread CPU p95 | 220.21 ms | 226.68 ms | 0.42 ms |
| Longest main callback median | 23.17 ms | 23.43 ms | 0.11 ms |
| Longest main callback p95 | 208.29 ms | 214.68 ms | 0.20 ms |
| Total process CPU median | 27.31 ms | 25.99 ms | 38.00 ms |
| Total process CPU p95 | 248.87 ms | 255.87 ms | 307.12 ms |
| Extraction wall time median | 24.11 ms | 23.93 ms | 27.80 ms |
| Extraction wall time p95 | 223.30 ms | 227.37 ms | 235.64 ms |

Node 26.12.1, 32 logical CPUs, 200 warmed samples per phase. Packaged-run host load fell from 32 to 24. Main-thread CPU uses `threadCpuUsage`; longest callbacks use async hooks without a spinning probe. Separate V8 sampling passes include collected objects: main allocation per 40 extractions was 2143.06/2131.89/9.81 MiB; total allocation was 2143.06/2131.89/2214.54 MiB. Retained RSS was not measured in isolated processes. This is extractor-owner proof, not a whole-Gateway surge benchmark.

The packaged first-use samples were 33 ms inline and 442 ms via the worker, including a 332 ms main callback in B. These are single first-use samples; A2 reused loaded dependencies and is not another cold control. The earlier source run measured 41/2,100 ms, with higher host load. **The performance owner explicitly accepted the packaged total-CPU p95 increase of 20–23% and one-time first-use cost on November 17, 2026, in exchange for the measured warm main-thread responsiveness improvement.** The measured median CPU increase remains 39–46%. The owner decision is posted verbatim in a PR comment.

Reproduce source: `nice -n 10 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs extensions/web-readability/test/web-content-extractor.bench.ts <output.json>`. For packaged proof, run `pnpm build`, copy the identical committed benchmark to `dist/extensions/web-readability/test/web-content-extractor.bench.ts`, and run that file with plain Node and an output JSON path. Remove the copied proof file afterward.

Focused proof covers the real worker's extraction output and real guarded HTTP abort/timeout flows, including discarded late results and no fallback/cache publication. The final candidate passed 51 focused tests across the extraction bridge, real HTTP abort/timeout and cache behavior, real worker extraction, and runtime process packaging. Both new cancellation regressions fail on the original bridge. `pnpm check:changed` completed: every gate passed except the moved assertion allowance and benchmark lint; both were corrected and passed focused reruns. The assertion baseline only shrinks, and benchmark cleanup adds braces, uses a nonmutating sort and removes a synchronous await. Core/UI/plugin/script/test typechecks, formatting, boundary checks, runtime import cycles and dead-export scans passed. Final `git diff --check` is clean.

The full local `pnpm build` passed in 6m 19s and the packaged-worker benchmark passed. [Initial-head CI 44222426669](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44222426669) skipped `build-artifacts`; no build success is inferred from that skip. It caught the missing package `workerEntries` declaration, now fixed at its metadata owner: production/full-tree unused-file scans and 19 build-entry tests pass. 

The remaining initial-run UI failure is proven inherited: `ui/src/e2e/chat-heartbeat-activity-rollup.e2e.test.ts:61` expects “Heartbeat Respond” but renders “Used tools”. The same focused browser test fails on both the candidate and exact main parent `fd2949d747c11a671676a1697232d67a6614772d`, using a clean detached checkout and its own frozen dependency installation. [Commit 18136c960eaf7 / PR #198133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/18136c960eaf70cac7ee083959c55d13d159afc2) introduced that assertion. This was a main regression, now repaired on newer main by [375daf6d3c3de / #200897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/375daf6d3c3dea98241357e355206243e61c5dc2). prs.title: fix: assign requested sessions and automations to the person who asked
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone asks an agent in a shared conversation to start work, a new child session can be assigned to the agent instead. A scheduled job can also record the person who opened the conversation rather than the person who asked for the schedule. The requester then cannot rely on the ownership shown for their work.

## User Impact

New work uses the verified requester captured by the host, without requiring the model to name an owner. The change is in shared Gateway and scheduler code, not a Discord adapter. It does not transfer existing sessions or jobs, grant administrator access, or enable a paused schedule.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the initiating profile when assigning a new child and when saving a new automation, rather than substituting the parent’s owner or displayed name. Keep the parent’s ownership, execution restrictions, and creation history separate. Autonomous work retains its existing fallback.

## Evidence

73 focused tests passed across six files, including child creation under a different owner, autonomous and sandboxed child creation, delegated cron persistence, authenticated creator transports, and owner-transfer recovery. Touched-file lint and format checks passed. Local autoreview of the change against `1619ecb28838` reported no actionable P0/P1 findings. No live per-channel replay or stable-version upgrade was run; this does not establish deployment or change the current watch.

prs.title: perf(update): reuse verified database digests within one update run
prs.body:
Related: #182616

## What Problem This Solves

On large SQLite installs, `openclaw update` keeps the Gateway stopped while Doctor hashes the same unchanged database files again and again. On a 10.8 GB test state, 92.7 s of SHA-256 CPU in a 302 s stopped window went to files nothing was writing.

## User Impact

Shorter Gateway downtime during updates on installs with large SQLite state. On a 10.8 GB test state the Gateway was down for a median of 233 s instead of 293 s (3 runs per side). Updating from the latest stable release (v2026.11.5) on a 10.7 GB state, it was down for 415 s instead of 481 s (one run per side). Nothing changes for small installs, and there is no new setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Doctor generation read starts a fresh worker, so no digest survived to the next read. A database without a journal or WAL was hashed twice per read (provisional and final), and Doctor plus the post-core Doctor read every database many times while the Gateway is stopped.

Following the maintainer answer on #182616 (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182616#issuecomment-6930916800, "don't redo verified work within a run"):

- The Doctor database write capture owns a digest map for its run, in memory only. Its generation reads, and the migration attribution reads inside it, pass the map to the existing generation worker and take back the digests the worker verified. Nothing is written to disk and nothing outlives the capture.
- A digest is reused only while the file matches the recorded fingerprint exactly (`dev`, `ino`, `size`, nanosecond birth, m and c times) and passes the existing `canRetainDigest` age rule. A new, recent or imprecise-timestamp file hashes fresh. Every family with a journal or WAL hashes fresh.
- Only a worker from the same runtime exchanges digests. Seeds leave the map before the worker runs; only a successful worker writes digests back.
- The activation snapshot, restore verification and refusal paths are unchanged.

Maintainer decision: this extends reuse to the final check of a read, not only the provisional read. Before this change a read of a database without a journal or WAL always proved fresh bytes at its final check, and `readUnchangedUpdateDatabaseGeneration` said "Never carry a digest reader across observations". That comment now states the new rule. A first read in a run still hashes fresh bytes twice; a later read of an unchanged file hashes none. If the final check must keep reading fresh bytes, the change reduces to provisional-read reuse only. An earlier version of this branch did exactly that: hashing CPU in the stopped window fell from 92.7 s to 64.2 s, and the stopped window did not change beyond run-to-run noise.

Accepted edge case: a write that leaves size and all nanosecond timestamps identical to a digest older than 2 s (for example a clock stepped back and a same-size write in the same timestamp quantum) would be read as unchanged for the rest of that update run. Per the boundary in the maintainer answer, no code is added for it.

## Evidence

Before and after on one machine, state and driver (macOS arm64, 32 cores, NVMe; Git install updated by driver 2516bca9fdb through `update.run`; synthetic state built through Doctor's legacy import, all SQLite). Base is 53278c30303; the fix is b9d1882fab5 (this branch). Runs alternate base and fix.

| activating (Gateway stopped) | 283.2 s (278.9 to 287.9) | 224.3 s (217.5 to 249.9) |
| . database snapshot | 56.7 s (55.3 to 56.7) | 57.7 s (56.3 to 59.6) |
| . openclaw doctor | 109.3 s (107.0 to 110.3) | 84.0 s (79.9 to 101.7) |
| . post-update verification | 96.1 s (95.0 to 98.8) | 61.3 s (59.1 to 65.8) |
| Gateway down (`/readyz`, 250 ms poll) | 292.6 s (288.1 to 296.4) | 233.3 s (226.5 to 259.2) |

Runs in order (activating / Gateway down): base 278.9 / 288.1, fix 217.5 / 226.5, base 287.9 / 296.4, fix 224.3 / 233.3, base 283.2 / 292.6, fix 249.9 / 259.2. Other jobs shared the host during these runs.

SHA-256 CPU inside the stopped window, from `--cpu-prof` on every process (one profiled run per side; profiling adds time):

| | base | fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| processes that hashed | 23 | 4 |
| database snapshot (activation snapshot, unchanged) | 11.7 s | 12.1 s |
| openclaw doctor | 42.3 s | 15.9 s |

- Update: `openclaw gateway call update.run` on the running v2026.11.5 Gateway, so the v2026.11.5 updater runs preflight, candidate Doctor, activation, Doctor and post-update verification. prs.title: improve(models): avoid duplicate catalog validation at startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cold Gateway validates a downloaded model catalog, then reads and validates the same bytes again before activation. The native baseline performs two full catalog parses during one fresh web turn.

## User Impact

This removes duplicate startup work while preserving the selected model rows and prices. The fixed latency comparison failed, so this experiment is closed unmerged. No configuration or storage-format change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The download owner passes its validated bundle through the immediate activation call. Activation still reads the current stored row and uses the bundle only if both source URL and exact JSON bytes match. A changed row takes the existing parser path. Version/source eligibility, cancellation, and publication ownership checks remain in place. There is no retained cache.

## Evidence

- The new matching-row regression fails on the original code; changed-byte and changed-source controls pass. The download-handoff regression also fails on the original code.
- All 49 focused tests pass, including refresh, rollback, source changes, Gateway startup, and HTTP/SQLite/prepared-model integration.
- Production and changed-test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and seven repository ratchets pass.
- The native runtime build passed. Fresh autoreview and committed-range local ClawSweeper reported no actionable findings.

### Performance acceptance — fixed before candidate measurement

Use a pinned catalog snapshot (SHA-256 `be77c49b711fb3f1c8e85f3b4693fc43b22fe607217c5333be35ba7c97cf6ccb`), mock OpenAI SSE `gpt-4.1`, default tools, and a fresh Gateway/state/workspace for each web trial. Compare the committed candidate with baseline `9122a49bd8a12baf734ec7bb78337bd556fcbef8` using the same committed controller.

1. Confirm native catalog parses fall from two to one.
2. Run 10 alternating A/B latency pairs: median at least 1% lower, at least 7/10 pair wins, and observed nearest-rank p95 no higher.
3. Only after latency passes, run six pairs each for lifetime CPU, external process-tree RSS, and complete main-plus-direct-worker heap. Both each resource median and its paired median delta must not increase.
4. Keep invalid trials and stop; never replace them. Run all four surface smoke checks before landing.

### Result — rejected

Native full-flow counts confirmed full catalog parses **2 → 1** and pricing-table parses **4 → 2**. All 20 fixed latency trials completed without replacement, but the candidate was slower:

| Web TTFT | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 1,160.16 ms | 1,225.32 ms |
| Observed p95 (10 samples) | 1,192.64 ms | 1,244.16 ms |

The paired median delta was **+59.06 ms**, with **0/10 winning pairs**. This fails the predeclared latency gate. CPU/RSS/heap and final surface smoke were therefore not run. Closing unmerged; no runtime performance improvement is claimed.

prs.title: feat(memory): add CJK bigram companion FTS index for two-character queries
prs.body:
Resolves #170997

## What Problem This Solves
When using `store.fts.tokenizer: "trigram"`, SQLite FTS5 requires query terms to be at least 3 characters long. As a result, two-character Han queries (ubiquitous in Chinese and Japanese, e.g. "設定", "記憶", "台北") cannot be matched by FTS5 trigram tokenization and currently fall back to an unranked substring scan. This causes:
1. **Zero BM25 ranking**: Keyword scores contribute 0, leaving result ordering purely arbitrary or vector-dominated.
2. **Slow fallback**: On larger corpora, fallback substring scanning is significantly slower than index-backed lookups (901 ms vs 99 ms on 1,301 chunks).

Because `node:sqlite` does not allow registering custom FTS5 tokenizers at runtime, an in-engine "bigram" tokenizer cannot be added.

This PR adds an opt-in companion Han bigram FTS index (`memory.search.store.fts.cjk: "bigram"`).

### Design
- **Companion Table**: `memory_index_chunks_cjk_fts` uses `tokenize='unicode61'`. Han runs in chunk text are encoded as overlapping character bigrams separated by spaces (e.g. `系統記憶體設定` -> `系統 統記 記憶 憶體 體設 設定`).
- **Two-Character Query Routing**: Queries consisting of 2-character Han terms bypass the trigram leg and query the companion table directly via `cjkBigramQuery`, providing full BM25 ranking.
- **Unicode NFC Normalization**: `isHanTerm` and `encodeHanBigrams` strictly normalize text using `normalize("NFC")` prior to matching and token generation, ensuring canonical equivalence between composite Unicode variants and standard forms (e.g. CJK compatibility ideograph `神社` U+FA19 properly normalizes and retrieves under `神社` U+795E with positive BM25 rank).
- **Typed Query Owners**: Companion row deletions in `MemorySourceIndexKernel` use typed Kysely query builders (`deleteFrom("memory_index_chunks_cjk_fts")`) rather than raw SQL `DELETE` strings.
- **Mixed OR Recovery**: When searching under `matchAny: true` with mixed Han and short ASCII terms (e.g. `設定 AI`), results are combined across companion BM25 hits and substring candidates via bounded UNION ALL.
- **Non-Regression & Strict Provenance**:
  - ASCII terms, single-character terms, and queries with 3 or more characters continue using their existing trigram/unicode61 execution paths.
  - Monotonic clock: Inherited probe cooldown strictly uses `performance.now()` in `manager.ts`.
  - Wrapper inventory: Runtime import closure in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` remains intact with only `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/cjk-bigram.ts` added.
  - Glob documentation: Documented hidden-path glob behavior in `docs/reference/memory-config.md` is strictly preserved.
- **Derived State & Lifecycle**:
  - Enabling or disabling `store.fts.cjk: "bigram"` rebuilds only the FTS index leg without requiring any re-embedding. When disabled, `dropDisabledMemoryFts` drops the companion table.
  - Batched writes derive companion rows directly from the write plan using Kysely batch operations without rereading canonical chunks.
  - Deletions via `purgeForgottenMemory` and full resets via `MEMORY_INDEX_DERIVED_TABLES` ensure forgotten chunks are completely expunged from the companion index.
  - Reused schema admissions skip redundant schema scans or DROP queries.
- **Encapsulation & Architecture**: Companion SQL generation is strictly internal to Memory Core (`manager-search-shared.ts`). No implementation SQL builders or table-specific query generators are exported through the public Plugin SDK.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve trusted daily quota assertions through failover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preserve trusted producer assertions for model-scoped daily quota exhaustion across streamed error projection, retry classification, and fallback normalization.

### Motivating scenario: Provider Cedar

“Provider Cedar” is an anonymized label for the motivating provider scenario, not a new public provider identifier. A producer can distinguish an explicit model-scoped daily limit from transient throttling, but core can lose that distinction while projecting streamed errors or normalizing nested failures. Treating the resulting error as transient can retry the same exhausted model without a useful recovery path.

The regression fixtures model this boundary with synthetic provider/model identities: a trusted producer emits numeric HTTP 429, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and a typed daily-model assertion. The assertion must survive unrelated or truncated diagnostics; conflicting enclosing status/code aliases or request identities must reject it. This is synthetic regression evidence, not a claim of a live upstream daily-limit reproduction.

- Require coherent numeric 429 and RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED facts on the asserting record; reject contradictory transport aliases and provider/model identities across wrappers.
- Capture the accepted assertion before diagnostic clipping or redaction. Diagnostic JSON cannot establish, erase, or resurrect the typed assertion.
- Suppress same-model transient retries only for the coherent typed daily-model assertion. Generic throttling remains unchanged.
- Preserve configured fallback precedence, explicit disablement, and selection locks. Unused switch-recovery policy and metadata are removed.

## Scope

Quota-assertion propagation and retry suppression only. Existing configured fallback progression is retained. No UI switch, resume action, prompt replay, dispatch journal, or storage migration is added.

### Resolved review items

- Session retry owner in `src/llm/utils/retry.ts` carries `quotaScope` and honors `sameModelRetry === false`.
- `assistant-failure.ts` preserves validated `quotaScope` when constructing `FailoverError`, with regression through outer fallback normalization.
- Removed unused switch-recovery policy, `quotaRecovery` metadata, `model-fallback-failure.ts`, and the leftover doc paragraph in `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/runtime-hooks.md`.
- Consolidated the diagnostic-body rejection table in `src/agents/daily-model-quota.test.ts` and added registered stream-transport boundary proof in `src/agents/daily-model-quota.stream-boundary.test.ts`.
- Merged current `origin/main` cleanly to resolve merge conflicts while preserving both quota retry vetoes and upstream `route_unavailable` vetoes.

## Evidence

Head: `e9dc2372526dd74347bec073803b7c055cbd4d75`.

- **Committed registered stream boundary test:** supporting projection/classification proof only. It uses a fabricated stream and a handwritten retry loop; it does **not** create an AgentSession or execute the embedded runner. The fault-sequence suite mocks the embedded attempt. The real session/HTTP proof below supersedes the prior overstatement.
- **219 focused tests** across 7 files and **102 sibling retry/classification/fallback-transcript tests** across 3 files passed. All 17 embedded-runner fault-sequence E2E tests passed.
- **Data-model & existing-transcript compatibility (`session-manager-failure-context.test.ts`):** legacy stored assistant/transcript records without `quotaScope` load with settings and data intact, and serialized `daily-model` scope survives a SQLite transcript round trip without schema migration.
- Core typecheck, `tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json` test-types check, scoped type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and diff checks passed.
- **Test-line ratchet:** `Test lines OK: 6564553; ceiling: 6564710; slack: 157` (exact allocation matches the consolidated test delta).
- **Canonical branch autoreview (pre-push on `e9dc23725` against `origin/main`, P0–P3):** `scoped-clean`, zero findings (`overall: patch is correct (0.85)`).
- Security budgets unchanged: 16 distinct quota objects × 11 own-data fields = 176 maximum descriptor reads, with accessors not invoked; diagnostic graph caps unchanged.
- Privacy audit passed.

### Real HTTP transport + shipped AgentSession behavior (red on base, green on head)

This additional runtime proof uses a real local HTTP fixture, the production `streamSimpleOpenAICompletions` adapter and HTTP client, `createAgentSession`, `AgentSession.prompt`, and production `runWithModelFallback`. It does not fabricate StreamFunction events, mock `runEmbeddedAttempt`, mock fetch, replace sleep, or implement a retry loop. Each fallback callback creates one real session and calls `prompt` once; the session owns all same-model retries. Resource discovery, authentication and session state are isolated; the credential is a synthetic fixture value. This is a real-transport/session-boundary proof, not a CLI/Gateway or full embedded-runner launch, nor a live upstream daily-limit claim.

The HTTP fixture observes POST request model IDs and returns:
```text
daily primary: HTTP 429
{"error":{"status":429,"code":"RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED","message":"429 request rejected","quotaScope":"daily-model"}}
ordinary primary, request 1: HTTP 429
{"error":{"status":429,"code":"RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED","message":"429 request rejected"}}
backup, or ordinary primary request 2: HTTP 200 text/event-stream
assistant content: "Cedar proof completed."
finish_reason: "stop"; terminal [DONE]
```

Configuration uses `provider-cedar/primary`, backup `provider-cedar/backup`, session retry `{enabled:true,maxRetries:2,baseDelayMs:1}`, and disabled automatic compaction. Scenario B has explicit configured `fallbacks: []` and `fallbacksOverride: []`. Retry counts below count actual `auto_retry_start` session events emitted at the real sleep boundary, with native timers left intact. Request counts independently verify those retries.

The identical temporary harness was executed with:

prs.title: fix(cli): recheck a saved account before each paired-node Claude invoke
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A paired-node Claude turn checks that the saved account still exists, then waits for skill setup, history authorization, and an approval retry. Removing the account during one of those waits could still submit the turn.

A later change also forwarded two thinking environment keys on every Claude node invoke. A released node decoder rejects those keys, so the Gateway now sends them only when the node advertises support.

## Evidence

Head `22a8f8ea755` on macOS. The Gateway behavior is `4ea1a89e172`; the later commits only allocate test lines. Claude Code 2.1.309 is `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude`, which resolves to `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code@latest/2.1.309/claude`. A loopback Gateway pairs a node. The session is created with the Claude CLI runtime and saved account `anthropic:pasted`, then placed on that node. Exec approval is required. The node runs the product Claude invoke handler with that resolved binary. The saved credential is a synthetic bearer token. Its value is not shown.

Retained account. The first node frame asks for approval. After one allow, the second frame launches the real binary. Claude Code exits 1. The Gateway log is:

```console
Embedded agent failed before reply: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 Invalid bearer token
TRACE retained status=error frames=2 launches=1
```

The invoke carried `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. It did not carry `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING` or `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`. This node did not advertise `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1`.

Removal while that Gateway approval is pending, then allow once. The real binary is not launched:

```console
Embedded agent failed before reply: Saved account "anthropic:pasted" was removed. Select a connected account or sign in again under Models, then retry. OpenClaw did not submit this turn.
TRACE removed status=error frames=1 launches=0
```

A node that does not advertise `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1` keeps `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` and drops the two thinking keys from both env and clearEnv. A node that advertises the capability receives both keys, and the current node decoder accepts them.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A retained saved account on a node-placed Claude chat turn reaches the real Claude Code binary after one approval. Removing that account while the Gateway approval is pending sends no second invoke and does not launch the binary. Thinking environment keys are sent only to a node that advertises `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, worktree `/tmp/oc-193712`, runtime commit `4ea1a89e172` (current head `22a8f8ea755` adds only the test-line allocation). Claude Code 2.1.309 at the Homebrew cask path above. The Gateway listens on loopback. The node is paired and runs `handleClaudeCliNodeInvoke`. The chat turn uses `sessions.create`, `sessions.patch`, `chat.send`, and `agent.wait`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Start the loopback Gateway with the saved synthetic account and exec ask set to always. Pair the node and point its Claude path at the resolved 2.1.309 binary. Create a Claude CLI session on that node. Send a short reply request. Allow the exec approval once. Send again, remove the saved account when the approval is requested, then allow once.
- **Evidence after fix:** Gateway and node terminal output from that chat turn:

  ```console
  Embedded agent failed before reply: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 Invalid bearer token
  TRACE retained status=error frames=2 launches=1
  Embedded agent failed before reply: Saved account "anthropic:pasted" was removed. Select a connected account or sign in again under Models, then retry. OpenClaw did not submit this turn.
  TRACE removed status=error frames=1 launches=0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The retained account produces two node frames and one launch of Claude Code 2.1.309. The binary rejects the synthetic bearer token with API 401 and exit code 1. Removing the account while approval is pending produces one node frame, zero launches, and the message that OpenClaw did not submit the turn. The thinking keys are absent from that invoke.
- **What was not tested:** A second physical computer, a released v2026.11.1 node build, and a completed model reply from a real Anthropic account. The synthetic token is rejected by Claude's API.

## Summary

Recheck the saved account before a paired-node Claude frame is sent, including after history authorization and on the approval retry. A detached chat turn reads the live Gateway. Thinking environment keys are forwarded only when the node advertises `claude-cli-thinking-env-v1`. An omitted working directory matches the directory stored on the approval plan.

prs.title: fix: replace superseded model recommendations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The recommended-model list kept older releases merely because some providers still served them, and the daily suggestion generator proposed both generations. That makes a curated shortlist behave like release history.

## User Impact

After the next hosted catalog publication, recommendations use the approved successors rather than five superseded versions. The full availability catalog, manual model selection, existing defaults, and provider-owned featured lists are unchanged. A provider serving only an old version may have no global recommendation for that family.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace rather than append. Remove `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra`, `qwen3.8-max`, `claude-sonnet-5`, and `deepseek-v4-flash`; keep their already-listed successors and every other entry's relative order. Fable 5.1 was already removed in #198632.

The generator now omits superseded explicit versions, replaces an unranked predecessor even without usage data, and explains each replacement. It preserves an older generation's Arena signal when an intermediate generation has only usage. The policy guide requires specific independent recommendation merit to retain an older model; provider availability alone does not qualify.

The audit preserves distinct canonical classes rather than guessing cross-tier succession. The two Muse Wonder IDs denote the same release ([existing alias decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/feeafd6b1e79ff4b8791ed6aa3096df4c47a6dae)), not two generations. HY4-preview retains independent open-weight, Apache-2.0 deployment/fine-tuning merit ([official model card](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-preview)). Kimi K3 and K3.1 Pro remain separate canonical tiers; this patch does not invent a cross-tier mapping or claim predecessor-only availability is a retention reason. Other Pro/Flash/Mini/size classes remain unchanged. No benchmark reranking is applied to the curated list.

## Evidence

- 33 focused tests passed across the suggestion generator, catalog v2 publication, and canonical identity. After the review repair, the two changed generator tests passed again (12 ms test time; 1.25 s command wall time). The initial combined command took 42.69 s including fresh compilation; hosted CI duration is pending.
- Both replacement boundary regressions failed before the change. Independent review identified a three-generation mixed-signal ranking loss; that scenario was reproduced red and fixed green. Final independent native source review found no P0–P2 findings. This is not helper-validated local ClawSweeper/autoreview.
- Live suggestion CLI completed against current Arena, hosted catalog, OpenRouter, Vercel, and NVIDIA feeds with authenticated usage deliberately disabled. Its proposed reranking/new entries were inspected, not applied.
- Actual publication projection checked all five pairs: successor-only recommendations when both are available; no stale recommendation for predecessor-only or disabled-successor inventories; input availability rows unchanged.
- The list now has 31 unique canonical IDs; only the five specified entries were removed. Scripts and tooling-test typechecks, targeted lint, code formatting, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.

Requested and approved by @obviyus in the [Model Catalog correction](https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1557525023957323817/1572451112793935983).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @obviyus](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4d305774-0281-49e1-9d70-1294e20ed5b3)

Co-authored-by: obviyus <22031114+obviyus@users.noreply.github.com>
