prs.title: fix(ui): enable heading navigation between chat turns
prs.body:
Related to #154524. Keep the issue open until the remaining review and acceptance work is complete.

## What Problem This Solves

Screen-reader users cannot quickly return from the chat input to a user or assistant turn using heading navigation.

## User Impact

Users can navigate between rendered conversation turns through level-two sender headings, including assistant replies while they stream. The visible chat layout is unchanged. Long histories remain virtualized: only mounted turns are available to heading navigation until more history is scrolled into view.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing sender name as a screen-reader-only heading before each user or assistant message group. Keep a single heading for a grouped assistant turn and preserve it as a reply streams and settles. Headings inside Markdown message content remain independent navigable headings.

## Evidence

### Bundle reduction investigation — November 10, 2026

Four scoped alternatives were measured with the installed UI toolchain and the comparison build identity. The native-hidden candidate was compared with pinned main `f60bf92ea585f9ef06a8f6c443467bdc6dc5aa1d` through `pnpm ui:check-performance:base`; the remaining alternatives used candidate builds with those same identity variables and the canonical `ui:check-performance --report-only --json` measurement.

| Candidate | Chat boot normalized gzip | Over the 1,301,131-byte cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Reviewed implementation | 1,301,525 B | 394 B |
| Native hidden headings, removing conditional components | 1,301,506 B | 375 B |
| Native hidden plus one-pass stream timestamps and connector guard deduplication | 1,301,505 B | 374 B |
| Shared heading component | 1,301,541 B | 410 B |
| Native hidden with inline localized stream labels | 1,301,515 B | 384 B |
| Official boot-manifest regeneration, unchanged renderers | 1,301,525 B | 394 B |

A further official `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` capture using the supported Chromium executable override refreshed nine manifest entries, but `pnpm ui:check-performance:base f60bf92ea585f9ef06a8f6c443467bdc6dc5aa1d` measured exactly the same chat-boot size. The generated change was reverted. Source inspection also considered optional handoff controls; deferring their UI would require additional loading/layout behavior, so no such refactor is included.

The native-hidden candidate passed all 51 existing heading, transcript-invalidation, and message-group tests unchanged. The additional stream cleanups passed 45 stream/sibling tests. Independent headless Chrome Dev 159 component-boundary proof with the real renderers and production CSS confirmed that hidden working/commentary/tool/continuation headings were excluded from the accessibility tree, sender headings preceded message bodies, streaming/settlement retained heading identity, and Markdown headings remained independent. This is synthetic renderer-boundary proof, not a Gateway/provider round trip or new Safari/VoiceOver recording.

None of these alternatives meets the enforced cap. All experiments were reverted; no new commit, budget increase, weakened assertion, or new review request was published. The reviewed head remains `51dcddd7cc3db591e5528c26556ef9461c419b47`.

**Maintainer decision requested:** explicitly accept or decline the reviewed implementation's +457-byte chat-boot gzip increase (394 bytes above the current cap), alongside the existing default-heading semantics decision. The seven inherited test-budget lines remain separately documented below. A broader performance change has not been attempted in this accessibility PR.

### CI follow-up — November 10, 2026

Current head: `51dcddd7cc3db591e5528c26556ef9461c419b47`. This follow-up only adds `config/test-lines-allocations/chat-message-headings.txt`; production and test code remain identical to `bb9987da5a9584c478ecf9da03f997091e30ac32`.

The [completed CI run for bb9987da5a9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42939378592) passed all three UI shards, the scheduled UI E2E shard, test typechecks (including the previously failing core-3 job), lint, localization, and security checks. The UI shard jobs took 313, 316, and 322 seconds including setup; these are shared-job times, not isolated heading-test costs. The real-Gateway browser lane was skipped.

Two checks remain unresolved; CI is **not green**:

- **Test-line budget:** added an allocation for exactly this PR's 191 net regression lines (187 in the heading renderer tests and four native transcript assertions). These protect heading order, streaming/settlement identity, continuation suppression, Markdown headings, and virtual-window navigation, which existing coverage did not assert. The staged ratchet against pinned main reports 6,643,656 test lines against a 6,643,649-line ceiling: **seven inherited lines remain over budget**. The shared scalar was not raised and inherited debt was not absorbed.
- **Control UI bundle:** CI and the same-machine local comparison against `f60bf92ea585f9ef06a8f6c443467bdc6dc5aa1d` both report chat boot gzip **1,301,068 → 1,301,525 bytes (+457)**, exceeding the **1,301,131-byte cap by 394 bytes**. Startup JS, CSS, and route request counts are unchanged. CI source-map attribution shows +253 compiled raw bytes in the group renderer and +109 in the stream renderer; standalone module gzip changes are +63 and +27 bytes, respectively (not additive whole-bundle costs). The shared largest-JS chunk also has a 32-byte baseline overage, which the comparison treats as inherited. No budget was raised or assertion removed.

Maintainer/owner disposition of the bundle cost and inherited test-line debt is pending. The [completed CI run for the current allocation-only head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42940820461) again passed the UI shards, scheduled UI E2E, typechecks, lint, localization, and security checks. The bundle and baseline-ratchet jobs remain failed, along with the aggregate gate. Its test-line total is 6,643,777 against a 6,643,770 ceiling, still seven inherited lines over. The real-Gateway browser lane was skipped. [ClawSweeper's completed review of this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154962#issuecomment-5763803957) accepts the submitted media evidence and requests a bundle reduction or explicit owner-approved exception; default-heading product acceptance also remains pending.

### Main conflict and CI repair — November 10, 2026

Merged upstream `f60bf92ea585f9ef06a8f6c443467bdc6dc5aa1d` into the existing branch in `bb9987da5a9584c478ecf9da03f997091e30ac32`, preserving its history. GitHub reports the updated head as mergeable.

- Retained main's framed-message rendering and localized assistant fallback while preserving sender headings. Continuation fragments now honor `frameHeader: false`, so a split assistant turn does not repeat its heading.
- Reproduced the prior CI failure from [check-test-types-core-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41251432566/job/124686083942): the virtual-window fixture supplied a JSX callback where `TranscriptContent` was required. The fixture now uses the existing native `GuardedTranscriptItem` descriptor, preserving lazy row ownership and all navigation assertions. The exact UI-chat test typecheck passes.
- Independent canonical Codex autoreview through P2 identified the continuation-fragment heading issue. The added regression failed before the repair and passes afterward; that finding is resolved.
- Final focused heading, transcript-invalidation, and message-group run: **51 tests passed**, 4.83 seconds runner wall time with one worker. The heading file has nine cases; its focused run took 1.49 seconds. The final assertion-only line-limit cleanup also passed its targeted transcript test (1.77 seconds). New-head hosted CI timings are pending.

prs.title: feat: let agents participate selectively in group conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents in groups need to recognize invitations and useful opportunities without replying to every message when mention gating is disabled.

## User Impact

With Decision assistance enabled and an effective Decision Model, eligible unmentioned group messages receive a pre-generation participation assessment. An invitation or useful opportunity takes the ordinary agent reply path, including its normal permissions, tools, streaming, and delivery. A negative assessment records the message without starting a primary agent run. Explicit mentions, commands, ambient room events, and generic CLI backends retain their existing paths. Unavailable assessments and unassessable media fall back to ordinary replies.

The existing default-off Labs flag opts into current and future Decision Model consumers, including on upgrades with an already-saved enabled preference. No separate participation setting is added. Hosted evaluations receive bounded conversation evidence and may incur provider charges. Opt-out invalidates pending participation judgments; ordinary cancellation and current-turn authority continue to govern execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deciding before generation avoids unnecessary agent runs and keeps sent-message history accurate. There is no private draft generation, post-generation review, revision loop, or special publication queue. Accepted-input and configuration changes invalidate stale preflight decisions before generation.

## Evidence

Updated November 1, 2026. Evidence is scoped to the tested inputs; this is not a merge-ready claim.

- **Earlier published tree:** head `60becc8feacd3aa5d4d7eb149470e25d8cce97b6` has tree `214f54dc7f68c057f47bd66bee5a6a26a6db541c`. Isolated validation of that tree passed **149 tests across nine files**, full `pnpm build`, configuration-doc generation, and generated-file drift checking. The overall run failed `check:changed` on a stale max-lines baseline entry; it was not an all-green run.
- **Saved configuration:** the built CLI accepted fixtures with Decision assistance absent, false, and true, with no warnings and identical before/after configuration SHA-256 values. This proves parsing and byte preservation, **not** runtime rollout, fresh installation, or version-upgrade behavior.
- **Actual-provider rubric smoke:** four bounded TypeSafe calls using synthetic conversations returned the expected invitation, opportunity, chatter, and resolved-conversation categories (`jev-1.13.0`). These used the installed evaluation tool, not the candidate's exact provider adapter or Telegram path; they are a small semantic smoke set, not a reliability guarantee.
- **Telegram prerequisite:** the canonical Test Server doctor now exits 0 with Convex credentials, isolated TDLib state, authorized Test Server user, and verified SUT bot. This was a DM authentication/readiness check, **not** selective group-participation proof. Actual candidate group scenarios remain pending.
- **October 23 rebase:** head `73edfa2d43da3f86d5f27621b2497843c4a31d29` integrates main `c6facd08e4b5aa14c4424a716f097388537f52ae` using Git’s merge-preserving rebase. All 15 original logical PR commits are retained. The preceding 14 commit IDs are unchanged; only the final integration commit was recreated, preserving its original author, author date, and message. Its complete tree is `d4fe891304f55ec637b23d1bf573c406add897d9`, identical to the previously validated candidate. That unchanged tree passed the full build, core/extension typechecks, affected messaging/plugin test typechecks, focused participation/Decision/transcript/queued-turn suites, all 230 reply entry-point tests, and all 8 prompt-prefix stability tests. Targeted lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/mock-export ratchets, configuration-doc generation checks, and documentation links passed. The prior static review reported no actionable P0–P2 finding; it did not execute project code. Validation and review are reused based on exact complete-tree equality. Exact-head GitHub CI remains pending.

- **November 1 rebase (published):** head `38c5e6ff1261f22b2938bcb976e97b8369e84131` integrates main `d43ab9c516e6dd1effeee8cb50ea479be550232e`, with complete tree `af053b6ad4df37c0d560ac1a9f98095915a9ffe5`. The preceding 14 PR commits are unchanged; the recreated integration commit preserves its author, author date, and message. Conflicts now use current-main reply input admission and Decision type owners. On supported Node 24.16.0, core and affected messaging/plugin-test typechecks, targeted lint/formatting, and documentation links passed. Focused participation, Decision consent/admission/V2, plugin-hook, followup execution/admission/delivery, transcript guard, and prompt-prefix tests passed. Local autoreview of the complete candidate against the pinned main at P0–P2 found one mixed-queue participation defect; it was fixed with a regression test that failed on the reviewed candidate and passes with the fix. All 87 existing collected-queue tests also passed. GitHub reports the pushed head as mergeable. Exact-head CI has not been validated; earlier full-build and live evidence remains scoped to its recorded trees.

Still required: full changed-file CI checks; runtime saved-config and persisted-session upgrade proof; actual candidate real-Decision-provider Telegram group send/silence cases; exact-head CI verification. The isolated real-provider tests still need a task-scoped TypeSafe credential or ready local Kev endpoint. No gate is waived and no merge is authorized.

The ClawSweeper review of the preceding published head `60becc8feacd` reported no actionable introduced code/security finding, but retained rollout, real-provider, integration, and compatibility verification work.

auto_merge.commit_title: fix: let the next update finish a killed update that had already installed the new version (#200866)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix: let the next update finish a killed update that had already installed the new version

When a killed openclaw update had replaced the installed version without
confirming it, had begun rolling its plugin changes back on it, or had left
the Gateway stopped, the next openclaw update refused and named
openclaw update repair. It now settles the plugin recovery as before and then
runs repair's own finalization (Doctor, plugin convergence, Gateway
restoration) as a stage that records its own repair run, prints no result and
never exits, then continues. A stopped Gateway is finished only when the update
would restart it anyway; --no-restart, other unfinished update history, or a
failed finish still refuse and name openclaw update repair. Repair and
standalone finalize are unchanged.

* test(e2e): kill an installed update and let the next update finish it

Each installed-recovery cut now kills an updater in its post-activation Doctor, after it installed its candidate, and checks that the next plain openclaw update finishes that run as repair does before updating.

prs.title: feat(diagnostics-prometheus): let plugins add metric families to the scrape route
prs.body:
Closes #197880

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that wants operator metrics has to serve its own HTTP route, so operators add a second Prometheus scrape job for one Gateway, and that plugin's series skip the exporter's label and series budget.

## User Impact

Prometheus still scrapes one authenticated Gateway URL. Core metrics work as before. Plugin metrics are **off by default per plugin**, even if both Prometheus and the producer plugin are enabled. To publish one plugin’s metrics, explicitly set `plugins.entries.<producer-id>.allowMetrics: true`. This setting does not enable the plugin or the exporter, and does not change other plugins. Omitting the setting or setting it to `false` keeps that plugin’s `api.metrics` undefined.

```json5
{ plugins: { entries: {
  "diagnostics-prometheus": { enabled: true },
  "my-plugin": { enabled: true, allowMetrics: true },
} } }
```

Risks:

- The type change is additive and optional. Plugins built against this host that use `api.metrics?.` run unchanged on older hosts, where the field is absent.
- Samples recorded during `register()` are dropped, because the exporter service starts after registration. Plugins record from their runtime paths (routes, services, hooks).
- Reloading a plugin resets its counters in the scrape: the Gateway disposes the previous instance before it registers the replacement, so the old series are dropped and new ones start at zero. Prometheus treats this like any counter reset.
- Plugin label values are checked only against the character policy, not redacted. A plugin could still put an identifier in a label; the 128 series cap per family bounds the cardinality cost of that mistake.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197880 is marked as needing a product decision; this PR is a concrete proposal for that contract, with working code.

`api.metrics` is a small optional field on the plugin API:

```ts
const metrics = api.metrics?.register({
  families: [
    { name: "retain_total", type: "counter", help: "Retains by outcome", labels: ["outcome"] },
    { name: "recall_seconds", type: "histogram", help: "Recall latency", buckets: [0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5] },
  ],
});
metrics?.counter("retain_total").inc({ outcome: "ok" });
metrics?.histogram("recall_seconds").observe({}, 0.12);
```

- Namespace: the host sets it. Every family becomes `openclaw_plugin_<plugin id>_<name>`, so a plugin cannot claim another plugin's names. The issue proposed a plugin-chosen `namespace`; this is the main point for owners to decide.
- Budget: plugin families get no reserve. They draw from the existing shared pool, keep at most 128 label sets per family, and drops appear in `openclaw_prometheus_family_series_dropped_total{family="openclaw_plugin_..."}`. Core reserves do not change.
- Lifecycle: declarations are admitted under the existing plugin lifecycle authority (`capturePluginLifecycleAuthority`, captured when `register()` runs), and samples are delivered only while the recording instance is the published one (`isPluginRecordActive`, the same check the session attachment path uses). There is no separate fence for metrics. A replacement instance can register the same families during a reload, but what it records before the reload commits (from `register()` or a service started in the preparation scope) is dropped and cannot reset the live instance's series. A previous instance that a failed reload resumes keeps its series and recorders without registering again. A family leaves the scrape only when no remaining registration of the plugin declares it: when the same instance registers again without it, or when its owning instance is disposed. When the exporter stops, plugin series reset with the core series.
- Exporter availability: the operator grants the producing plugin a recorder; delivery requires a live exporter. No listener means samples are discarded, not buffered. Starting or stopping Prometheus does not require a producer reload.
- Consumer: [`@etzelm/openclaw-memory-hindsight`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@etzelm/openclaw-memory-hindsight), a memory slot plugin, serves its own Prometheus route (`/plugins/hindsight-native/metrics`) today, so operators add a second scrape job. With this API it would register `recall_total`, `retain_total`, `recall_skipped_total`, `retain_queue_replays_total`, `retain_queue_drops_total` (counters), `retain_queue_depth` (gauge), and `recall_duration_seconds`, `retain_duration_seconds`, `recall_injected_memories`, `recall_injected_chars` (histograms), labelled by agent, bank and fixed outcome or reason enums, and drop the route.

Owners can accept this shape or redirect it; the registration, namespace and allocation choices are theirs to make.

<details><summary>Admission, delivery and SDK surface details</summary>

- `api.metrics` is defined only for the live full registration, and only if the operator opts this producer in. Otherwise it is `undefined`; optional chaining keeps plugin code compatible. Samples recorded while no exporter listens are dropped.
- The plugin id is lowercased and other characters become `_`, so two ids can still map to one exported name (`a-b` and `a_b`, or plugin `foo` family `bar_baz` and plugin `foo_bar` family `baz`). The second registration of such a name throws at load, so the clash is loud but depends on load order. A histogram also reserves its `_bucket`, `_sum` and `_count` names, so histogram `lat` and gauge `lat_count` cannot both register, in one plugin or across plugins (plugin `a` histogram `x` blocks plugin `a_x` gauge `count`).
- `register()` checks names, counter `_total` suffixes, declared label names and histogram buckets, and throws during plugin load on bad input. A sample whose labels differ from the declaration is dropped with one warning per family on the plugin logger. Label values outside the low-cardinality policy (`[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, at most 120 characters) are exported as `other`.
- Each `register()` result is one registration owned by its plugin instance. The first call binds teardown to the instance (`lifecycle.onDispose`) and captures the instance's lifecycle authority; `register()` throws when that authority cannot be minted (a disposed, retired or not-yet-published instance outside its own registration). Recorders publish only while their registration is held, the authority still holds and the record is published, so an instance paused by a reload drops samples until it resumes, and an uncommitted replacement's samples (including ones recorded inside the reload preparation scope, where the authority itself still allows calls) are dropped until publication.
- Re-registration by the same instance replaces only that instance's families and retires the ones no other instance of the plugin declares; recorders from the earlier call go quiet. Disposing an instance retires only names no remaining instance declares, so neither a disposed nor an older instance can evict the live instance's families. If a family's type, help, labels or buckets differ between instances, the exporter drops the old series once the new shape is published: when the previous instance is disposed after the reload commits, or at the first published sample of the new shape, whichever comes first. The scrape keeps one `TYPE` block per name, and a failed replacement never reaches this step.
- Delivery follows the existing exporter listeners (`onGatewayWsMetrics`, `onWorkerRequestMetrics`): a new trusted `internalDiagnostics.onPluginMetrics` listener, offered only to the trusted diagnostics exporters and bound to the service capability lease. Core keeps no metric values.
- No new SDK export names. The types are reachable as `NonNullable<OpenClawPluginApi["metrics"]>`. The SDK surface changes only by the new optional `metrics` field on `OpenClawPluginApi` and the optional `onPluginMetrics` on the service context's `internalDiagnostics`.
- Docs: a "Plugin metric families" section in `docs/gateway/prometheus.md` and one row in the SDK overview field table.

</details>

## Evidence

- The per-plugin regression failed on `27e80d369930` (an unapproved plugin still received the recorder), then passed after the fix. The same operator config covers allowed, denied, and unlisted plugins, including mixed-case plugin IDs.
- An isolated AWS run passed the updated producer registration/lifecycle and Prometheus rendering suites, including stopping and restarting the exporter listener with the same opted-in producer. The config documentation baseline was regenerated and checked against the integrated main branch.
- The earlier review found that exporter-only reload could leave a producer without its recorder. `7e78ce7546ca` removed that coupling. CI subsequently flagged unsafe reserve-table indexing, mock isolation, test allocation, and two unnecessary conversions. The repair uses an own-key type guard and string diagnostics, and documents the mock’s isolated request scope. The three ratchets passed against the integrated base. The 217-line test allocation covers the 617 net test lines minus the standard 400; it retains distinct regressions for producer opt-in/denial, overlapping registration and retirement, exporter reload, and shared-series limits.

### Live Gateway upgrade and scrape, `339c12b0edfb5e20efeed381e13aafc01f5650ee`

On isolated Linux, the published **2026.11.5** package (`e13cf15`, npm integrity verified) ran two fixture plugins. Its own CLI saved one plugin setting, and authenticated requests to that plugin wrote two SQLite rows. Both plugins were enabled, neither had an `allowMetrics` setting, and the exporter was off. Stopped stable, ran the candidate’s normal `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migration, and started the Gateway built from this exact PR head against the **same config, state and plugin databases**. The original producer entries, load paths, setting and both rows survived. Nothing opted itself in.

| Operator action on the upgraded Gateway | Authenticated scrape | Producer result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No config change | 404 | Both recorders absent, as on stable |
| Enable only Prometheus | 200, core build info | Neither producer exported |
| Set `allowMetrics: true` only on `allowed-producer`; hit both producers | 200, `openclaw_plugin_allowed_producer_hits_total 1` | Ordinary producer absent |
| Stop then start only the exporter | 404 → 200 | Both registration UUIDs unchanged; approved counter reads `1` after a new hit, not a replay of samples while off |
| Set that producer’s `allowMetrics` to `false` | 200, core build info | Neither producer exported; both stored rows still present |

`pnpm build`, targeted type-aware lint and the 11 registration/lifecycle tests passed on this head. The 5 exporter tests passed on its parent; the final commit only touched the producer declaration error wording. The fixture used the real Gateway, real HTTP requests and two deterministic local producers, not a production Hindsight deployment. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44225064169). No owner sign-off is implied by the proof.

**Review and CI on this head:** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198455#issuecomment-6864872853) accepted the live and upgrade proof, reported no findings or pre-merge checklist items, and recommends accepting the SDK contract; a maintainer still owns that decision. The lint and baseline-ratchet jobs that failed on the previous head now pass. [CI remains blocked](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44225064169/job/134539641439): the Discord transcript capture test rejects a native broker socket during setup/cleanup (`unexpected socket destination null:NaN`). [An unrelated PR hit the identical assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44224297723/job/134534544344), and [a clean-main reproduction is documented here](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200564). The test, broker client and catalog-worker files are byte-identical between that reproduced main parent and this run’s main parent. Our own clean-base run stopped earlier on a temp-directory permission check, so it is not counted as a reproduction. No test guard or CI status was overridden.

### Original contributor proof (before per-plugin opt-in)

Isolated Gateway (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`, token auth, `diagnostics-prometheus` enabled) with a small standalone fixture plugin that calls `api.metrics?.register(...)` and records one counter, gauge and histogram sample per request to its route. Two requests, then one scrape:

| Build | `api.metrics` | Scrape | `openclaw_plugin_` lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| origin/main | undefined | 200 | 0 |
| this branch | defined | 200 | 13 |
| this branch, exporter disabled | undefined | 404 | 0 |

Reload through the same Gateway: a manifest fixture whose gauge records which registration served the request. A config edit replaces the plugin; a second edit sets `fail: true`, so the replacement's `register()` throws right after `api.metrics.register()`, and the Gateway restores the previous registration (it registers the previous code and config again, "registration 4" in the log). Sample lines per scrape (7 = counter, gauge and 5 histogram lines):

| Step | Previous revision of this branch | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. start, 2 requests | 7 lines, `jobs_total` 2, instance 1 | 7 lines, `jobs_total` 2, instance 1 |
| 2. reload applied, 1 request | 7 lines, `jobs_total` 1, instance 2 | 7 lines, `jobs_total` 1, instance 2 |
| 3. failed reload, previous restored, 2 requests | 7 lines, `jobs_total` 2, instance 4 | 7 lines, `jobs_total` 2, instance 4 |

The Gateway disposes the previous instance before registering a replacement, so this path re-registers and both revisions keep the families. The other recovery path, a reload that fails early and resumes the paused previous instance without registering it again, is not reachable from a config edit; the "keeps the live instance's families when a reload fails and the instance resumes" test drives it through the real registry, lifecycle authority and `PluginInstance` pause/resume, and fails on the previous revision.

<details><summary>Scrape lines on this branch</summary>

```text
# HELP openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_jobs_total Fixture jobs by outcome
# TYPE openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_jobs_total counter
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_jobs_total{outcome="ok"} 2
# HELP openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_queue_depth Fixture queue depth
# TYPE openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_queue_depth gauge
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_queue_depth 3
# HELP openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds Fixture job latency
# TYPE openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds histogram
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_bucket{le="0.1"} 0
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_bucket{le="1"} 2
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_bucket{le="+Inf"} 2
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_sum 0.5
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_count 2
```

After the failed reload (step 3):

```text
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_jobs_total{outcome="ok"} 2
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_recording_instance 4
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_bucket{le="0.1"} 0
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_bucket{le="1"} 2
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_bucket{le="+Inf"} 2
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_sum 0.5
openclaw_plugin_metrics_fixture_job_seconds_count 2
```

</details>

Tests:

- New `src/plugins/plugin-metrics.test.ts` (10 tests): `api.metrics` undefined with no exporter, an explicitly disabled exporter, a scoped registry or discovery mode, and defined with only `diagnostics-otel` on; prefixed samples reach the trusted exporter listener and stop after the lease is revoked; label mismatch drops with one warning and unsafe values become `other`; invalid and colliding families are rejected; histogram `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count` names are reserved in one call, in either order, and across plugins in both directions; the same instance registering again retires only its stale family and silences old recorders, and disposal releases the names; a replacement registering during a reload leaves the live instance's family alone, the paused instance drops samples, the failed replacement's disposal retires only its own new family, and the resumed instance records again without a second `register()`; a committed reload hands shared families to the replacement, restarts a relabelled family at its first new sample, and retires only the family the replacement dropped; for a `generationOverlap` plugin, a replacement that relabels a family and records from inside its real `register()` call and from the real reload preparation scope (`withPluginRegistryPreparationScope`, where candidate services start) delivers nothing and retires nothing while the live instance keeps recording; a failed replacement leaves the live series intact, and a committed one switches the relabelled family over when the previous instance is disposed; a disposed or older instance cannot register or evict the live family. Registration runs inside the loader's real `register()` call with the registry's lifecycle authority. Red on origin/main (`Cannot find module './plugin-metrics.js'`); on the previous revision of this branch the preparation-scope test fails (`expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 2 times`: the replacement's uncommitted samples retired the live series) and the other 9 pass.
- New `extensions/diagnostics-prometheus/src/service.plugin-metrics.test.ts` (5 tests): rendered counter, gauge and histogram text; 133 label sets admit 128 and count 5 in the family drop counter; retired families leave the scrape and a re-registered name renders one `TYPE` block; retiring a full family releases its series budget; exporter stop clears plugin series. Red on origin/main (`expected Plugin metrics listener to be defined`, the exporter never subscribes), green here.
- `pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-metrics.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-prometheus`: 8 files, 77 tests pass.
- `pnpm test` on the 29 `src/plugins` files for `registry*`, `api-facades*` and `service-diagnostics*`: 324 tests pass.
- `pnpm test` on the 6 `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload*` files other than the one listed below: 146 tests pass.
- `pnpm test` on 926 more files across `src/plugins` and `src/plugin-sdk`: pass, except the failures listed below. `update.work-deadline.test.ts` and `plugin-metadata-state-worker.test.ts` failed once on a heavily loaded host and pass when rerun alone.
- Not run locally: `src/plugins/loader.test.ts`, `plugin-module-generation.sdk.test.ts`, `setup-registry.migrations.test.ts`, `source-checkout-runtime.test.ts` and `src/plugin-sdk/channel-entry-contract.lifecycle.test.ts`. The test runner refuses to prepare their built runtime on the test host (it cannot verify separation from a managed Gateway install), so PR CI is their first run. `loader.test.ts` is the most direct consumer of the registry change.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm check:docs`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports`, and format check on the touched files: pass.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base <origin/main> --head <this branch>`: passes with no export added or removed; 11 reachable declarations changed (the optional `metrics` field, the optional `onPluginMetrics` listener and the new metric types they reference). Acknowledgement digest `fa187f0a` (against origin/main `f3957e8653e`).

Not caused by this change, same result on origin/main:

- `pnpm lint`: fails on findings in unrelated files (13 `max-lines` errors among them); the finding list is identical on origin/main.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: fails with the same four budget counts on origin/main (entrypoints 163 > 162, exports 3888 > 3867, callable exports 2243 > 2236, wildcard re-exports 1 > 0). This branch adds no SDK export names.
- `src/plugins/plugin-preparation-exec-argv.test.ts` fails on origin/main too, with a Darwin descriptor ACL error from the test host.
- `src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.installed-package.test.ts` ("loads installed package roots and retains a sibling with empty runtime conf...") fails the same way on origin/main `f3957e8653e`.
- `bundled-plugin-icons.test.ts` (no `extensions/celeris/assets/icon.png` on origin/main), `bundled-plugin-categories.test.ts` (`perplexity` category) and `plugin-sdk-deprecated-imports.test.ts` fail the same way on origin/main; this branch touches none of their inputs.

prs.title: fix(ios): show oversized video warnings in chat drafts
prs.body:
Related to #195267

## What Problem This Solves

When a video selected from the iOS photo library exceeds the attachment limit, the composer drops it and shows a generic error. Send stays enabled, so a caption can go out by itself when the sender expects the video to be attached.

## User Impact

The composer now shows the rejected video's filename, its size, and the available attachment limit. The caption stays in the draft, and Send becomes available once the rejected selections are removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warning belongs to the draft, so it stays with the same conversation when switching agents or resolving the default conversation during the current app run. If several videos are rejected, the composer shows how many remain and presents one warning at a time. The existing upload limits still apply.

## Evidence

On unmodified main, the simulator sent the caption alone after rejecting a 25.8 MB clip against a 19.5 MB limit. With the fix, the warning blocked Send. Removing the rejected selections preserved the caption and left a small accepted clip staged. After removing the small clip, I sent the preserved caption and confirmed that the isolated Gateway received it once and returned a reply. The warning and caption also survived switching to a second agent and back.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic error with Send enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0aceb2e3-6124-4554-8dcf-2b8278ecc379) | ![Video filename, size and limit in the composer with Send disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d53b5136-0301-4214-9aea-ea9307eb9192) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic attachment error and enabled Send button highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15ee9c74-1fd6-4be9-af75-30b20a94fb2b) | ![The in-composer rejection warning highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e507af9-1bbd-4847-b60b-42330cea5ddd) |

Captured in the native app on an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator running iOS 27.0 with synthetic clips and messages. The before capture used main at `e93a426be3`. The after capture shows the updated composer before the final routing-only changes. Those changes passed the automated validation below.

<details>
<summary>Automated validation</summary>

- Seven attachment tests passed, including per-file and remaining-draft limits, draft ownership, and routing resolution. Both Send regression cases failed when the new guards were removed.
- All 264 iOS app model tests passed, including four combinations of standard or custom default conversations and same-account or account-change routing.
- The iOS build and native localization verification passed. The final focused local review reported no actionable findings in the custom default-route correction.
- Submitted head `c9cc19d824d1905f9c1c262fe88744dd66806ab1`.

</details>

Reported by Holger Gruenhagen in #195267.

prs.title: fix(ui): scroll Activity from the side margins
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scrolling the Activity Sessions page did nothing when the pointer was over the blank space beside the centered session list. The scrollable element stopped at the reading column rather than including the page margins.

## User Impact

Users can scroll the session list from either side margin or the content itself. The centered reading width, fixed desktop filters, and existing mobile page scrolling are preserved. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native feed scroller now spans the available desktop page width, with the reading-column spacing inside it as padding. This is a CSS-only fix, without wheel interception or additional scrolling state. Current work and Run inspector retain their existing column insets.

## Evidence

- Real mouse-wheel regression fails on the original layout and passes with the fix. Both margins and the center are checked at 1600, 820, and 390 CSS pixels; desktop filters remain fixed and no horizontal overflow is introduced.
- All three Activity geometry tests pass against the bundled Control UI with synthetic Gateway data (6.1 seconds of test time, 18.5 seconds including the UI build). Both additional Activity loading/feedback tests pass. Production deployment and live Gateway data are not part of this proof.
- Scoped test typecheck, CSS lint, test lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent local autoreview using Codex GPT-6.1 Sol covered the complete final change against `59cea6c2b3e46cedc9ea6dbe48c6c87c10a1e8ba` at P0–P2 and found no actionable defects.
- The initial CI performance failure exposed CSS growth on an already-over-budget base. The repair replaces the superseded narrow-wrapper and clipping rules instead of layering overrides. `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 59cea6c2b3e46cedc9ea6dbe48c6c87c10a1e8ba` now passes locally; total CSS is only 25 raw bytes above the base, within the existing build-variance allowance. No budgets, thresholds, or baselines changed. Exact-head CI verifies the pushed repair.

The captures below use the real UI with synthetic sessions at 1600 × 900. Both show the result of the same 300 px wheel gesture over the left page margin. Before is base `59cea6c2b3e46cedc9ea6dbe48c6c87c10a1e8ba`; after uses the production CSS in this PR.

prs.title: fix(release): compare changelogs with the previous shipped release
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release notes can omit unreleased work when the previous shipped release lives on a divergent branch. The stable workflow rejected that release as a baseline and recommended a reachable main-closeout commit instead; work already on main before closeout could disappear from the next release notes.

## User Impact

Release operators can compare against the actual previous published release without losing pre-closeout beta development or counting proven backports twice. Missing legacy evidence produces warnings and conservatively retains uncertain work; malformed selected or canonical historical provenance, duplicate rows, and unsupported exclusions remain integrity errors. No existing release, tag, asset, or live release notes are changed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Stable generation captures public npm `latest` before publication; beta preserves its public npm `beta` selector semantics. Both freeze the resolved tag for replay. Extended-stable uses its own line. Local tag ordering is not publication evidence.
- Keep the shipped tag as the semantic base and traverse `base..target`, including side branches. A merge base is informational, never a substitute for the shipped boundary.
- One shared owner loads cumulative shipped records and canonicalizes evidenced release carriers before subtraction. Exact cherry-pick/forward-port origins and unique author/path-supported matches deduplicate backports; contextual references and title-only similarity do not. Stable inventory ignores unshipped beta drafts.
- Generation freezes canonical main history for deterministic alias replay. Candidate validation, checklist, full-release validation, and existing render/publication consumers use the same inventory/provenance contract. Removed duplicate shipped inventory loaders, redundant candidate provenance parsing, and superseded inventory exports.

### Regression provenance

Raw-parent inspection confirms:

- `f684527085ebeeeff0de13e62decb0c5b1bd4457` (June 17, 2026) introduced merge-base traversal.
- `336e43c31482a6ace6764b018293ce68930bef6c` (July 10, 2026, release pipeline convergence) added the strict ancestor requirement and reachable main-closeout guidance.
- `a94074f6a4987ee27796e572be33b8cd1367fdc3` / #166881 (October 8, 2026 UTC) added a divergent-tag exception only for beta, replacing its base with the merge base while subtracting the shipped record. This is a beta-only contributor, not the direct cause of stable closeout substitution. The legitimate renderer, beta-delta, and attribution improvements are preserved.
- `6dd12ab0eeeea8f7462dd990fbc1bd18961a94c1` added the initial 11.5 record on November 16, 2026 with the incorrect main-closeout base; subsequent refreshes preserved it. GitHub returned no associated PR for this commit or the two older introducing commits above.

The observed 11.5 baseline `90a5029e427822745c59e4f1268db08ade257d5b` is the **10.9 main closeout**, not the 11.4/11.5 merge base. The previous tag `v2026.11.4` peels to `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`; its merge base with code cut `e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff` is `459cad76530457e5c0a32bc21d4982920e9991e7`.

## Evidence

- Before editing, the real verifier rejected `--base v2026.11.4 --target e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff --version 2026.11.5 --source-ref e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff` at its ancestor guard.
- Six real-Git divergent-history regressions fail on the original verifier at that same guard and pass with the repair. They cover pre-closeout beta work, shipped backports, side ancestry, reversals, missing records, and normal merge carriers. Generation-to-candidate replay rejects missing/forged subtraction provenance.
- End-to-end canonical credit tests cover backports and differently titled release-first forward-ports. These address two findings from independent review.
- Final affected core coverage passes: 209 verifier tests, 127 candidate checklist tests, 10 candidate changelog tests, 15 renderer tests, and 17 ledger tests. The verifier was rerun after fixing an old fixture that paired canonical provenance with a nonexact `HEAD` target; integrity validation was not weakened.
- Broader affected pipeline run: 430 tests across seven files passed, including candidate-owned full-release dispatch and publish-closeout preflight. Later historical-record changes are additionally covered by the final core suites and real baseline read.
- Script and tooling-test typechecks, targeted script/test lint, formatting of all ten changed files, docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The final shared owner successfully loaded real `v2026.11.4` against code cut `e13cf15...`. It reported the existing stale legacy total in the 2026.6.9 historical section as a warning, preserving explicit rows instead of introducing a blanket failure.
- Final canonical autoreview (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2) of `0ca4e7d3db4b83fd82bd74f43844e25605b52b85..43bf2dd91c1c3d8ad206922047d46b6fa231cafc`, with renderer/parser context, completed **scoped-clean: no actionable findings**. This was static review, separate from executed tests. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; the maintainer fallback uses autoreview plus hosted review on the ready PR.

### Limitations

Explicit ancestral SHA baselines remain accepted for historical replay with a generation diagnostic, not as the default or recommended new-release boundary. Missing legacy evidence can retain duplicates rather than silently lose contributions. Old historical `merged PRs` totals can be stale: these warn and use explicit rows, never the declared total. Ambiguous canonical aliases remain unsuppressed.

The full historical 11.4-to-11.5 live inventory was bounded and stopped after partial GitHub discovery, with a reusable snapshot retained locally. The Git range contains 11,811 commits; that is **not a verified unique-PR count**. No corrected PR count or live-note repair is claimed.

prs.title: fix(sessions): record queued input end causes and recover them across crashes
prs.body:
## Problem

An accepted (acknowledged) queued chat message could disappear without a trace:

- It could be cancelled with no stored reason. History showed nothing, and retrying the same message ID could return a cached success although the message never ran.
- A Gateway crash (SIGKILL) lost it. Recovery depended on a graceful-shutdown marker, so a crash before the acknowledgment, or between claiming the message and the turn taking it over, left neither a queued row nor a running turn. On restart nothing answered and nothing explained why.

This changes #185730's accepted SIGKILL loss for acknowledged queued input.

## Fix

**Recorded end causes**
- Store a closed `end_cause` (`user-stop`, `delete`, `reset`, `revoked`, `restart-unrecoverable`, `overflow`, `policy-refused`, `failed`) through the existing pending-input owner. One settlement owner classifies causes (an explicit Stop, delete, reset or revocation wins over a temporary outage), releases consumed custody and records terminal endings.
- Temporary authority or dispatch outages: before the input is accepted (no acknowledgment sent; the caller gets the error), the row ends `failed`, as main cancels it today. After acceptance, the row stays queued and the failed attempt gives up its live ownership, so the existing owner (follow-up drain, mailbox, or startup replay) runs it once.
- Read durable cancellation before cached success/abort responses; a queued retry reports in flight.
- Chat shows one translated sentence per cause (for example "The Gateway restarted before this message ran. Send it again."). A message the user stopped shows no notice, as before (#186073).
- Channel redelivery under a fresh run ID still reclaims an attempt that ended `failed`, `restart-unrecoverable`, or with no recorded cause (#193602). Explicit caller retries may reopen a cancelled row unless a final completion receipt exists or the user stopped it. One function (`isRetryableSessionPendingInputEndCause`) defines retryable endings for redelivery and Doctor repair; when Doctor merges two copies of one input, a deliberate ending in either copy wins.

**Crash recovery**
- Store the already captured, authenticated sender source on the pending row (`origin_source_json`). Startup replays queued, unconsumed rows in FIFO order after running-root resume admission and revalidates current authority when work starts. A missing source ends as `restart-unrecoverable`. The column is cleared when custody ends. It is not the retired, untrusted `recovery_intent_json` envelope; historical v24 interruption is unchanged.
- The transaction that appends the user message and consumes the pending row also writes the turn's existing lifecycle start fields, so restart recovery always finds the input as either a queued row or a running turn. No new table, scheduler or reconstruction machinery.
- If replay defers because authority or dispatch is temporarily unavailable, the session keeps its older rows ahead of new input: the shared admission point (`waitForAgentInputAdmission`) runs that session's deferred replay once before admitting fresh input, and refuses fresh input with the same retryable error while it still defers. Other sessions are unaffected. No timer or retry loop.
- Legacy `queuedInputSources` move from shutdown markers to their pending rows through the startup/Doctor rewrite owner. #200394's `resumeAfterRestart.operatorSource` (the interrupted root requester) is kept; a crash writes no marker, so source-less root recovery keeps the existing session-principal policy.

## Agent schema 43 (one bump)

The agent database schema advances from 42 to 43 on SQLite and PostgreSQL through the existing versioned migration owners. It adds nullable `end_cause` and `origin_source_json` to `session_pending_inputs` and, in the same transaction, sets `end_cause = 'user-stop'` for older cancelled rows whose message carries `__openclaw.pendingInputCancelledByUser: true` or `display: false` (message bytes unchanged; dismissed rows stay hidden). Runtime readers use only `end_cause`.

Every pre-43 historical schema, including the schema-14 preflight, is derived without the two columns; PostgreSQL v42 predecessor DDL is unchanged. Older builds refuse schema 43; rollback needs the pre-upgrade backup and the matching binary. No schema-version bypass.

Pre-migration backup: `session_pending_inputs` is the agent schema's only `AUTOINCREMENT` table, and the scoped migration snapshot does not cover `AUTOINCREMENT` tables (shared `sqlite_sequence`), so Doctor takes its existing full-database backup for 42 → 43 wherever that table exists. Upgrades from stable 2026.11.4 already take a full backup (schema 30 has no scoped entry). For stores already on 42 this is a one-time copy about the size of the agent database (3.0 GB on one measured long-lived store). The migration inserts no rows, and no backup code changes.

## User impact

- A queued message survives a crash: it is answered once, or ends with a visible reason. Same-ID retries never start a second answer.
- Cancelled messages explain why, in plain words, instead of looking successful.
- During a startup access outage, new messages in an affected session get a "try again" error until its older messages have run; nothing runs out of order.

Accepted edges:
- Explicit `sessions.delete` removes input rows and message bodies; the delete confirmation is the visible result.
- Stop on 2026.11.4 and earlier wrote no marker; such rows stay generically cancelled and reclaimable by a same-content channel redelivery, as on main.
- An accepted input whose path has no in-process retrier (direct agent execution after acknowledgment) and that hits a temporary outage stays visibly queued until the next Gateway start replays it.
- The upgrade from 42 to 43 takes a full-database backup where `session_pending_inputs` exists (see Agent schema 43).
- No exactly-once guarantee for external tool effects or provider billing.

## Evidence

- Head `ed2c3b46d558`, rebased on current main: format, lint and line caps pass; `pnpm tsgo:core`, all `pnpm tsgo:core:test` configurations and the script typecheck pass; all baseline ratchets and the import-cycle guard pass. Regression tests (each red on an earlier head) cover deferred replay ordering, the shared-store graceful-restart agent, pre-acceptance outages, an accepted follow-up that waits out an outage and then runs exactly once, a same-key attempt with a different run ID (refused), startup replay racing the follow-up drain (one run), a user Stop during an outage, and the original abort signal on cleanup. An internal stop is not recorded as `user-stop`; only a user-initiated Stop is. Only the recorder that confirmed a relinquish may re-attach its queued row; a fresh send, a redelivery or a row whose settlement failed cannot (the revoked-parent-after-stop test stays refused). Startup replay re-attaches only its exact durable row by input ID after a deferred outage.
- Schema: reopening a main v42 PostgreSQL store failed before the migration (`PostgreSQL schema drift detected against generated DDL`) and now migrates to 43; 10 real PostgreSQL tests pass. The v14-to-v15 migration test failed with `column definitions differ for session_pending_inputs` before the historical-schema fix and passes now. Each review fix carries a regression test that failed before it.
- Crash proof on head `ed2c3b46d558`: isolated source Gateway, Node inspector, real model, external SIGKILL at the exact breakpoint; `plugins.allow=["openai"]`, `plugins.slots.memory="none"`, `cron.enabled=false`. Baseline is main at `6747b1ec5ae3`.

  | Fault | Main answers / queued model calls | This PR answers / queued model calls | Stored outcome |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Message row written, before acknowledgment | 0 / 0 | 1 / 1 | Answered; no pending row; session done |
  | Message claimed, before the turn took it over | 0 / 0 | 1 / 0 (one running-turn recovery call) | Answered; the message was already in the transcript and the row gone at the pause; session done |

  Each produced exactly one answer and no extra model calls after a same-ID retry. Earlier runs on pre-43 head `975900737b4f` covered a crash just after takeover (one answer, no duplicate) and mid-turn (one answer).
- Upgrade from 2026.11.4 (schema 27), clean shutdown and SIGKILL: both reach schema 43 with both columns; a message still queued after the SIGKILL ends `cancelled / restart-unrecoverable`, shown in history and on same-ID retry, with zero model calls. Both this branch and pinned main fail their first start after that SIGKILL with a secrets/SQLite disk-I/O error and succeed on the second start; filed separately as #200617. Doctor's Control UI build during that upgrade is #200618.
- Chat notice before/after screenshots are in the PR comments.

No full release declaration proof or real PostgreSQL conformance suite is claimed beyond the tests above.

prs.body:
## Current correction and proof status

**READY FOR REVIEW — M3/M4 evidence resolved; native preparation completed.** Current signed head: `bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051` (tree `c8a203d47cc697a578ec478d79bdfcf2b80d340d`). Native publication verified; independent exact-candidate source review found no actionable P0–P3 issue. This is readiness qualification, not merge approval.

- Earlier owner-recorded `sentBeforeError` stays `delivery_unconfirmed`, even with later nested rejection. A typed Matrix HTTP 403 proves permanent rejection only for a fresh SDK event with exactly one matching wire request; repeats, redirects and existing events remain uncertain. Queue-reconciliation wording requires held custody.
- **M4 resolved in source and current CI:** unique per-client mock transaction IDs preserve the production duplicate-dispatch guard; all 97 SDK tests, including concurrent room ordering, passed.
- Added real Matrix SDK → guarded loopback HTTP regressions for first-403 versus 307→403, with wire count/path and client cleanup. These do not exercise SDK-event reconstruction/resend.
- Native baseline refresh incorporates canonical `976a4fb8784a326579108e03d0df4356dad501a3`, including scripts typecheck fix `5e302bddf1cbf56acc94bc84061bff1eede74031`; no duplicate repair.
- Signature, ancestry, product-diff identity, `git diff --check`, and trusted formatting passed. Product diff SHA256: `a21a1ad7197749e6513cfb8a3bb99c5e5cb3d8fc2aa86bcdf9e6ffc5d2095971`.
- **M3 causal/timing portion collected:** the independent original-module-red/candidate-green pairs and isolated Matrix test-file wrapper wall times are now available below. The original-module differential is not a full historical-baseline checkout; the separate authenticated live proof is recorded below.
### Current-head CI — passed

CI [43618778733](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43618778733), attempt 2, completed successfully on November 14, 2026 at 17:13:43 UTC: 47 jobs passed, 28 skipped, no failures; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. Workflow Sanity, OpenGrep, CodeQL and Critical Quality also passed. Periphery reporting passed with platform scans skipped.

This run binds head `bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051`; tests checked out GitHub merge commit `15e89eb3ced433a73cb7c6c8bdfb3ac40cbb3ed8` against canonical main `89c5b179fc3d82eb37dba517b789475d4314e0e3`, not a literal head-only checkout.

- Matrix SDK: 97 tests; transport: 16; transport authority integration: 14. Actual SDK→HTTP direct-403 and redirect→403 regressions passed (56ms and 37ms). Matrix times are per-case sums (26.850s / 0.658s / 0.048s), **not isolated file wall times**.
- Message-tool execution: 74 tests / 22.71s Vitest duration; scheduled lifetime: 18 / 18.28s; accepted results: 35 / 13.37s. Total across these six requested files: 254 passing tests.
- Production types, extension/scripts test types, all five core test-type stripes, general lint and all five core-lint stripes passed. Neither the prior duplicate transaction-ID error nor scripts TS18048 recurred.
- This establishes candidate-green, not independently replayed baseline-red/fix-green. No live homeserver delivery or encrypted recipient event was tested.

## Matrix — causal original-module qualification

PR #197000 candidate `bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051`; original module source `937f77cb20ded2e041f5ea876200d01b449d0329`. Product code is unchanged by this proof. Execution tooling `08e028a6bba5f6e1dcdc09739cdb26730ea55dd8`; final admission-only tooling `f00d850619271dbd39cf713dc43322d2fd622925`.

- Run 43790032640 (tooling `a95800834f9353eb801eebff4a8b274ecb9f1d99`): all **97 SDK cases passed**, isolated wrapper wall time **71.404 s**. Its job was red only because the old evidence gate incorrectly rejected a legitimate repeated parameterized title; the retained report was re-admitted, not rerun.
- Run 43790694571 (tooling `a4dec2e6e0c3f006aeaf24a195bfc514da4de2eb`): candidate **transport 16/16** (**51.330 s**), **authority integration 14/14** (**3.005 s**), and selected message-owner cases **2/2** (**65.565 s**) passed. These are isolated, serial wrapper wall times including setup, not per-case sums or full-file timing for the filtered owner suite.
- The same run replaced only `sdk/client-core.ts`, `sdk/message-wire-dispatch.ts`, and `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.ts` with original bytes, keeping candidate dependencies and tests. In the real SDK → guarded loopback HTTP pair, the **direct 403 failed** the intended permanent-rejection assertion at `transport.test.ts:154:35`, while **307 → 403 passed** its uncertainty assertion. Original-wire wrapper wall time **50.774 s**, launcher exit 1.
- The driver initially rejected that genuine causal failure because Vitest abbreviated `Cannot send to room` to `Cannot se…`. The repair admits only the exact observed M_FORBIDDEN/403 prefix, expected `retryable: false` object, pinned assertion path/line/column, required two case identities/statuses, and launcher exit 1; it still rejects missing/extra/duplicate cases, setup/timeout/connection failures, wrong error, wrong assertion, wrong expectation, and unrelated truncation. The original structured JSON is preserved and replayed; no product rerun was spent on the admission repair.

This is an **original-module differential in the candidate environment**, not a full historical-baseline checkout/build, live homeserver test, or proof of encrypted recipient delivery. The tests and all three changed-module hash pairs are checked against the retained report before the continuation executes.

Validation: 26/26 synthetic admission checks pass; the exact retained report is rejected by the old gate and admitted by the repaired gate. Targeted lint, format, Node syntax, whitespace checks and repository workflow validation pass. Workflow validation initially encountered empty token variables; rerunning with only those empty variables removed passed. Fresh independent native review found no P0–P2 findings in the continuation three-file delta (SHA-256 `3df2a28366a1d16d76015b792192b26d20235b4b64c8a2223c929b574fd3a70f`). This is the established explicitly labeled native fallback, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper result; the configured service's 402 credit failure was not retried or bypassed.

[Continuation run 43791792505 / job 133051654842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791792505/job/133051654842) downloaded only the two fixed retained artifacts using read-only Actions access and executed only the previously missing **original-owner** pair. Original `sentBeforeError=false` passed; original `sentBeforeError=true` failed with `OutboundDeliveryError: message failed: MatrixError: [403] M_FORBIDDEN`, created at the pinned test's line 457, rather than returning `delivery_unconfirmed`. Candidate versions of both cases passed in the prior run. Original-owner isolated wrapper wall time: **66.949 s**, launcher exit 1; per-case times 30.257 ms / 12.829 ms.

The continuation job remains **red**: its evidence gate mistook Vitest's ordinary `runWithTimeout` stack-frame name for a timeout diagnostic. The final admission-only correction filters stack frames out of infrastructure diagnostics, preserves real timeout/setup/connection rejection, and requires the exact original-owner error prefix and source location. All six retained JSON reports replay successfully through that corrected gate, with no further product execution. The final workflow disables the completed Matrix job; no completed SDK, candidate, wire, history, audio, permission, or billing stage was rerun.

[Retained artifact 14193046368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791792505/artifacts/14193046368), `goal24-matrix-43791792505`, contains the six source reports, original-owner log, and the original red summary. The corrected admission result is a local replay, **not a new green hosted run**. Fresh independent native review of the final admission/disable delta also found no P0–P2 findings (SHA-256 `f2eeb134d198b733cdd40f441837d580cc4f7c0ddfd4321dc2606e188889a13e`). Final 26/26 admission tests, exact six-report replay, targeted lint/format/syntax, workflow validation, and whitespace checks passed.

### Real Matrix homeserver proof — November 17, 2026

[Hosted run 43990720491 / job 133730280334](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43990720491/job/133730280334) **passed all three required live contracts** against unchanged candidate bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051, using execution tooling b25f1009d0b0dfafc2e1ffe624751f28fa94ee0f. The earlier causal/timing jobs were not rerun.

Disposable Ubuntu 24.04 / Node 24.22.1 ran real Synapse 1.165.0, pinned to ghcr.io/element-hq/synapse@sha256:b7f105b3c5f6d8bdb0a1aaff51ec4264dd109d8ed5532009d176bcb28a57ca0a. Temporary local Alice/Bob accounts exercised the production SDK, transport, SQLite-backed durable plan, and crypto.

- Authenticated send: Bob independently read exactly one event matching the returned event ID and sender (0.969 s).
- Accepted-then-429: the proxy received upstream HTTP 200 before returning 429; retry reused the identical transaction path and event ID, with one delivery callback and one recipient event (2.700 s).
- E2EE: an independent recipient SDK decrypted the plaintext; server history independently showed one m.room.encrypted / m.megolm.v1.aes-sha2 event containing ciphertext and no plaintext body (1.810 s).

[Artifact 14286724744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43990720491/artifacts/14286724744), goal24-matrix-live-43990720491, is 3,677 bytes; archive SHA-256 0c2c15a77af0ac2cd7d06e32681af4ea4a496d686ad7acc9caaf367191193b48. Downloaded report/observations passed exact identity and three-case admission. Fixture SHA-256 d5337fc5ce60f4741ed87bab770c1dd40e35ae9ef3c3366b01aee277c30d23dc. Inspection found no token/password fields or bearer credentials; raw SDK/server-state/install logs were not uploaded. Container cleanup exited 0.

Initial run 43990033248 at c408675efbcce1a96ca983a4478aa7d8df66664e passed authenticated delivery but could not open SQLite for the remaining cases. The driver correction selected the canonical isolated database-worker configuration, narrowing only its include list; the unchanged fixture then passed. This is a harness correction, not a product-code fix. Six admission tests plus targeted lint, format, syntax, and whitespace checks passed. Prior independent findings were addressed; @RomneyDa explicitly waived further independent/formal review for this proof-only patch on November 17, 2026. No new formal review is claimed.

**Limits:** retry is within one sendMessageMatrix invocation, not Gateway queue restart/replay or persisted-plan reload. Cross-signing/device trust is not verified. No real-user device, real-model flow, merge, main write, deployment, backport, or release is claimed. Final retention head 4f4d4c3baa37a1c41ed9e60f222e4b499ea44b9f disables the live job; all five prior jobs remain disabled.


### Native readiness qualification — November 17, 2026

Reused the unchanged exact-head independent source review; no new review or signature is claimed. Native `review-init`, `review-checkout-pr`, and `review-validate-artifacts` completed with `READY FOR /prepare-pr`, zero findings. Native `prepare-run` completed at the same head and verified that the remote already matched; no product commit or push was needed. The native gate receipt is `github_pending` (not a fabricated successful-test stamp); separately observed exact-head CI run 43618778733 attempt 2 and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. PR remains open, non-draft and mergeable; no merge was requested.

### Historical failures and environmental limits

- Historical head `4aa0faa30907ba9ce07cfaccdaa7dd21c4bbf1b9`: CI run 43606138401 attempt 2 failed on M4 fixture collision and inherited scripts TS18048. It passed message-tool execution (74 tests), scheduled lifetime (18), accepted results (35), production types and lint. None of this is current-head runtime proof.
- Secretless AWS allocation failed before any lease because credentials were unavailable. No AWS tests or credentialed fallback ran; no contributor runtime executed on the trusted local host.
- The earlier absence of live Matrix credentials was resolved by the disposable, secretless Synapse fixture above; no production credentials were used.

The results below belong to the contributor's earlier head and are retained for attribution/history, not current-head proof.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor description and earlier-head evidence (superseded where noted above)</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

A `message` tool send can pass the point where the channel may already have accepted it and still come back as a failure — #196802 has Matrix answering `/send/m.room.encrypted/<txn>` with `429 Server is unavailable` after it accepted the event. The tool then reported a plain failure (`message failed: MatrixError: [429] ...`), the model did what "failed" implies, and the room got the same text twice. The delivery queue already knew better: it recorded `unknown_after_send` and reconciled the entry as already sent minutes later, but that knowledge never reached the tool result.

The queue's terminal failure already carries it. `OutboundDeliveryError.sentBeforeError` is set when an earlier attempt of the same intent started or its outcome is unknown, which is exactly the "may have landed" state. This projects that one case as a `delivery_unconfirmed` tool result so the model waits instead of minting a second send.

Two facts decide what the model may be told, and both already exist on the error:

- **Who owns reconciliation.** `owner.project(...)` stamps `queueCustody = "held"` while the durable queue still owns the attempt and `"released"` once it is retired; a `skipQueue` send (`message-tool-execution.ts:575`, scheduled direct sends) has no owner at all. Only `"held"` keeps the Gateway-reconciliation wording. Undefined or `"released"` reports `No queued retry owns it, so the send may already have reached the recipient; check it before resending.` — because there is no row to reconcile and promising one would be false.
- **What the provider already proved.** A permanent pre-dispatch rejection can carry `sentBeforeError` evidence from another payload in the same batch. When the error graph holds a `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError{retryable:false}`, the projection returns nothing and the rejection keeps its actionable error and cause.

Everything else keeps its current behavior: a failure that provably never left still throws, and a failure with confirmed platform sends keeps its existing partial-delivery path (`projectScheduledMessageActionPartialResult`), because the projection requires an empty `results` list.

Open question for the Matrix owner: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/transport.ts:269-283` wraps `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` only when the fetch never started, so a post-dispatch 403 is still reported as `sentBeforeError` and is indistinguishable here from an accepted-then-429 send. Classifying those as `retryable: false` in the adapter would route them through `isProvenDeliveryNotSentError` and out of this projection; that policy is not decided inside a tool-result projection.

Closes #196802

## Evidence

Red — both new behaviours fail against the previous projection, test kept (`node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts`):

```
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is undefined
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is released
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > keeps a provider-proven rejection actionable
   Tests  3 failed | 70 passed (73)
```

Green — same command on `937f77cb2`:

```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  73 passed (73)
```

Other checks, on `origin/main` at `584084d77`:

- `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` — passed.
- `src/agents/tools/message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts` — 17 passed, 1 failed (`settles provider revocation during send via direct as accepted`). That failure reproduces identically with this change reverted, so it is a pre-existing Windows baseline, not a regression.
- `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` on the touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json` — no diagnostics for the touched files (the repo's pre-existing `@openclaw/fs-safe` drift in unrelated files is unchanged).
- `run-format.mts --check` — all files formatted.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/196802-message-tool-unconfirmed-delivery.txt` = 67, matching the +67 test lines.

Diff against `584084d77` is +96/-3 across `message-tool-execution.ts` (rename), `message-action-execution.ts` (projection), the test file, and the ratchet allocation.

Why the proof is not here: this machine cannot build the dist (`@openclaw/fs-safe` in `node_modules` predates `preserve`, so `build-all.mts runtime` dies in `plugins:assets:build`), and the remaining item needs a live homeserver that accepts a message and then answers 429 without an event id. A maintainer proof run only has to assert `status: "delivery_unconfirmed"` with `delivered: false` on the tool result plus one recipient event.

</details>

prs.title: fix(workboard): omit retained path from scratch worker prompts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Workboard scratch worker prompt can include the retained host path from a previous worktree after the card switches to scratch.

## User Impact

User impact: scratch workers receive context that matches their current workspace, while a later switch to `dir` can still reuse the stored path and branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing worker-context formatter omits the path only for scratch workspaces. Stored workspace metadata remains intact for later directory reuse.

## Evidence

- **2026-11-18 conflict repair (current head `640c9500c82afcaec36a94772f5d2e0368444f74`):** Normal merge of main `b15c658270ddab1a3942a6560f6520301f6aed6c`, preserving the upstream dispatcher-test retirement and moving the prompt regression to the current SQLite dispatcher harness. The identical regression fails on that main baseline. The repaired source passes 103 tests (dispatcher regression 1, store 87, provider-prefix stability 15), formatting, changed-file lint, extension production/test type checks, the test-line ratchet, and whitespace checks in a secretless isolated Linux/Node 24.22.1 container. Canonical local AutoReview (Codex, P0–P3, complete static assessment) found no actionable issues; the reviewer did not rerun tests. The reviewed and tested Git tree is `013172324369cdf50c6cf97d5072ea36433265f5`, matching this merge commit. [Exact-head CI run 44228971680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44228971680) is currently `action_required` with no jobs executed, so broad CI proof is pending repository workflow approval.

The unchanged regression failed on base `b0fdadd6b3448af5e23c45794465d48d97944fbe` (1 expected failure, 40 passed).
