prs.title: fix(codex): reduce CPU and allocation while streaming long answers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long Codex answers repeatedly copied and broadcast their entire growing candidate text alongside the existing assistant stream. A synthetic 40 KB answer split into 2,000 deltas produced 40 MB of redundant candidate text.

## User Impact

Answer streaming and final selection stay unchanged, with substantially less CPU and allocation while Codex answers. No configuration, migrations, or protocol fields change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The assistant stream owns growing answer text. Candidate telemetry now publishes only the first visible candidate, authoritative completed text when changed, and exact superseded/selected transitions. The existing candidate status provides the early exit before trimming or comparing accumulated text; no timer, cache, or deferred lifecycle work is introduced.

Consumer audit: the current UI, TUI, and progress replay validators reject the candidate-specific status values. Visible answer text is already delivered by the assistant stream. This change preserves those consumers and candidate boundary payloads; it does not introduce new Activity UI behavior. The existing schema mismatch is a separate follow-up.

Runtime production LOC: net zero. The candidate owner remains within its file cap by inlining a trivial final-phase helper and simplifying its supersede branch.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule established before measurement: 2,000 × 20-byte deltas, preserve all assistant bytes and candidate boundaries, at most three candidate snapshots for an ordinary item and bounded candidate payload bytes proportional to final answer size. Separate warmup; ten timing samples per arm; allocation sampled separately including collected objects at 4 KiB intervals. Two identical baseline controls precede the candidate. One synthetic subscriber serializes candidate events; these are owner-level measurements, not full Gateway fanout measurements. No database or workspace I/O enters this path.

| Per 40 KB answer | Baseline A1 | Baseline A2 | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Candidate events | 2,001 | 2,001 | 3 |
| Candidate text bytes | 40,053,997 | 40,053,997 | 80,011 |
| Sampled allocation, MiB | 79.445 | 79.426 | 3.274 |
| CPU median, ms | 66.325 | 66.118 | 4.142 |
| Elapsed median, ms | 42.197 | 42.342 | 2.054 |

At 4,000 deltas / 80 KB, the fixed owner still emits three candidate events, with 160,011 candidate text bytes and 6.149 MiB sampled allocation. Candidate payload growth is linear even without tick coalescing.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/codex-answer-candidate.ts`; optional positional arguments are delta count and measured rounds. A separate CPU profile was also captured.

The regression fails on the original producer because it emits thousands of candidate snapshots. Focused assistant, commentary, async-delivery, and source-finish suites pass (58 distinct tests). The final assistant suite passes all 33 tests, including interleaved-item whitespace reopening. They cover streaming equality, candidate → superseded → selected, authoritative replacement, silence, and terminal suppression. Four test files took 67 seconds including compiler preparation; actual tests took about two seconds. Final assistant rerun took 27.24 seconds including preparation (0.3 seconds in tests).

The whitespace check exposed that the directive accumulator buffers trailing spaces; candidate transitions therefore inspect the prepared delta or original delta, including when prepared text has not grown. The growing-status early return still happens before touching accumulated text.

`pnpm check:changed` ran; its initial file-cap and benchmark fixture type errors were corrected and their focused gates rerun successfully. The changed-file run completed; all its other checks passed. Its dead-export scans report two unrelated main regressions: `describeSpawnAuth` introduced by #191324 (`0ca4e7d3db4b8`) and `ADVANCED_FIELDS` introduced by #200808 (`dce9dd13b53e5`). Production and full-tree dead-export scans reproduce the same findings on the exact unchanged parent `0ca4e7d3db4b83fd82bd74f43844e25605b52b85` in a separate worktree. These are main regressions for their owners to fix, not suppressed checks; this PR changes neither owner. Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local change against `0ca4e7d3db4b83fd82bd74f43844e25605b52b85` completed scoped-clean through P2 with no accepted/actionable findings. Final focused lint passed. Extensions, extension tests, and scripts typechecks passed. No UI-imported runtime module changed, so the UI browser-import gate does not apply.

Timing spread (min–max): baseline A1 elapsed 41.78–42.83 ms / CPU 65.44–68.09 ms; A2 elapsed 41.69–42.82 ms / CPU 64.61–70.64 ms. Final fixed elapsed 1.30–2.44 ms / CPU 1.70–8.07 ms. With ten samples, observed maximum is the nearest-rank p95. Shared-host load was recorded; this is not a claim about full Gateway or browser latency.

prs.title: fix: keep background completion attempts out of Activity recency
prs.body:
Related: #200918

## What Problem This Solves

An old conversation can appear newly active when OpenClaw tries to deliver a background completion, even if delivery fails before any useful work happens. The attempt incorrectly replaces the last human-interaction timestamp used by Activity.

## User Impact

Internal completion attempts no longer advance the session's last human-interaction time. Ordinary user messages still advance it. Existing inaccurate timestamps are not rewritten; no configuration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry-stop fix landed in #200918 while this PR was being prepared. This branch incorporates that change unchanged and removes the duplicate retry patch and tests.

The remaining fix carries the already-computed completion-state preservation decision into the initial session update. This prevents a failed background attempt from changing its activity clock. It adds no scheduler, timer, cache, or persisted state.

## Evidence

The Activity regression failed before the production change and passed afterward:

- A real isolated Gateway creates a managed worktree, removes it, and receives both individual and batch completion requests through RPC. The requests fail without changing the saved activity clocks.
- An ordinary `chat.send` still advances the interaction clock and reports the removed-worktree recovery guidance.
- After integrating current main, **41 focused tests passed**: the product regression plus 40 existing requester-settlement cases, including the upstream permanent-versus-transient worktree refusal tests.
- Targeted TypeScript checking, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed on the integrated candidate. Line-cap checks also passed before integration; the final authored patch is smaller.
- [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44228542405) for `3c36da45a84d093b91f81568128b90b42cd14764`; the native exact-head watcher finished with `GREEN`.

<details>
<summary>Commands, scope, and review limits</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-dispatch.test.ts src/gateway/server.chat-removed-worktree.product.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-turn-service.ts src/gateway/server.chat-removed-worktree.product.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check docs/web/control-ui/settings.md src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-turn-service.ts src/gateway/server.chat-removed-worktree.product.test.ts
git diff --check
```

The targeted typecheck included the two changed TypeScript entry points and their imports, extending the repository's `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.shard.json` without changing compiler rules.

The passing local test command took 58.35 seconds including worker compilation. The product test's execution took 10.23 seconds. Broad proof ran in the linked hosted CI rather than a full local suite; aggregate CI runner-seconds were not measured. This change does not alter package boundaries or build output.

Author simplification and self-review completed. No separate local automated review was run and no additional agents were delegated. The automatic hosted ClawSweeper review is advisory. No live Gateway deployment is part of this PR.

Final authored delta against integrated main: production +3/-1 lines; tests +26/-1; documentation +1/-1. The existing admission and state-preservation owners remain responsible.

</details>

Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski for the report and direction.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix: reduce sandbox preparation and resume delays
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat preparation and checkpoint resume can wait on redundant Podman commands when the container engine is busy. Each extra process joins the engine's lock queue, so even a small inspect can delay the user's send.

## User Impact

Sandbox creation, reuse, and pause/resume each issue one fewer engine command on the successful path. Existing image freshness, container replacement, engine selection, and failed-resume recovery behavior remain covered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Creation now lets `create --pull=never` establish whether the image exists, consulting the image diagnostic only on failure. One structured container inspection carries state, labels, and mount facts through allocation and mount preparation; replacement containers obtain their own facts. Successful `unpause` of the recorded immutable container ID is authoritative. A failed resume still inspects that exact ID to distinguish an already-running or removed container from an unresolved paused container.

Runtime discovery is already process-stable. Dependency identity still resolves mutable image tags: documented image builds happen outside the Gateway, so there is no in-process pull/build owner that can safely invalidate a new cache. Browser-only environment inspections and cross-engine recovery checks are outside these hot paths and remain intact. No config, schema, target-selection, base-refresh, journal, or pause-scope changes.

Production code grows by 29 lines for structured inspection parsing, carrying facts for the current container generation, and failure-only resume recovery. There is no new cache or state owner.

## Evidence

The recorded subprocess harness exercises the actual sandbox backend and quiescence owners. Baseline is `e93a426be3297ed947f54b4e15c87827225b6c90`; measured production candidate is `e7b2288a3bccf10697531dc0bbc6003338be0c57`. Final head `95f34852fa066ea2b492c3ed3802407e8de95991` adds only the retirement test correction described below.

| Flow | Engine calls before → after | Wall time median before → after | Main-thread CPU before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold container creation | 6 → 5 | 12.211 → 10.123 s | 23.889 → 19.462 ms |
| Warm reuse | 3 → 2 | 6.063 → 4.038 s | 10.682 → 8.500 ms |
| Pause/resume | 4 → 3 | 8.081 → 6.055 s | 12.303 → 9.265 ms |

These are synthetic results with an injected 2-second latency per command, ten warmups, A/A controls, and five interleaved A/B pairs per flow. A/A wall times were 12.139/12.199 s, 6.068/6.050 s, and 8.077/8.068 s. Before/after p95 (maximum of five) was 12.326/10.571 s, 6.080/4.054 s, and 8.123/6.078 s. The one-time runtime probe is outside the warm-process measurement. The separate dependency-identity image lookup remains one call; these numbers do not claim to measure all cold preparation.

Separate allocation A/A/B runs used 100 iterations per arm, no injected latency, heap sampling and CPU profiles. Mean baseline-control allocation versus candidate: cold 3.484 → 3.089 MB/action (-11.3%), warm 1.975 → 1.516 MB (-23.2%), pause 2.203 → 1.750 MB (-20.6%). Allocation controls differ by under 1.2%; profiled timing is diagnostic only. CPU is the Node main thread, excluding subprocesses and workers.

The synthetic workspace contains 62,000 files totaling 1.1 GB and 40 resource mounts. These owners do not scan workspace content or read session transcripts, so no large session database was synthesized. No production data was accessed. Local Podman has no running machine: native lock queueing and real container execution were not measured. Actual Docker 29.8.2 and Podman 6.1.4 CLIs did validate the JSON template against a synthetic Unix-socket API, with absent and populated tmpfs fields.

Focused regression assertions fail on the exact baseline for the redundant image lookup, warm mount inspection, and resume inspection. Candidate coverage includes image/tag changes, engine changes, container replacement, failed and already-completed resume, mount boundaries, and existing lifecycle behavior. The final broader run passed 144 support tests (one opt-in skip) plus six agent-configuration E2E tests; the recreate command suite passed six tests. The final quiescence rerun passed all 22 tests. Targeted lint and scripts typecheck pass; Codex review is clean through P2.

`pnpm check:changed` exposed an inherited unused export: `ADVANCED_FIELDS` in `ui/src/pages/cron/view-delivery.tsx`. The same export check fails on the exact baseline above; `git log -S` traces its introduction to `dce9dd13b53e5` / #200808. This is a main regression, not noise. All other check stages passed after correcting scoped lint findings and rerunning the affected lint/type checks. The PR does not modify UI-imported modules.

Reproduction tools are committed: `scripts/perf/sandbox-start-measure.ts` accepts `--call-latency-ms`, `--workspace-fixture`, and `--pause-cycle`; `scripts/perf/sandbox-inspect-smoke.ts` validates native CLI formatting without a container daemon.

CI run 44225253488 found one PR-caused stale test expectation in retirement recovery after physical removal. Reproduced locally, corrected the fake engine to fail unpause of a missing ID and updated the expected exact-ID attempt; all 19 retirement tests and targeted lint now pass. The follow-up Codex review is clean. Production code and benchmark inputs are unchanged. Final-head CI run 44226660787 passed. ClawSweeper reviewed `95f34852fa066ea2b492c3ed3802407e8de95991` with zero findings and no open checklist items (issuecomment-6967705570). Merged as `044391093eb61fc196b6e1428046148d4c99528d`. The final UI E2E shard had a slow WebKit installation, then passed without a rerun or override.

prs.title: fix: dismiss old questions after sending a new prompt
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Control UI, sending a new instruction can leave an older blocking agent question docked in the conversation. This makes an obsolete manual-step prompt look as though it still needs an answer, even after the user has redirected the work.

## User Impact

Sending an ordinary composer prompt successfully dismisses the Gateway questions that were already docked in that conversation, including child-session questions displayed there. Cancellation is not an answer, approval, verification request, or completion of a required manual step. Failed or blank sends, explicitly queued messages, slash commands, newly arriving questions, and optional Codex ASYNC questions retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required; this PR does not deploy or restart a live service.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the existing pane send operation and cancel its pre-send question snapshot only after the send is accepted and the pane/session/connection/question-client still owns it. Reuse the existing cancellation lifecycle, which settles once and retains a visible question error on cancellation failure without failing or replaying the accepted prompt. No new state store or cancellation framework is introduced.

## Evidence

- The real Control UI browser regression failed before the fix because the accepted prompt never cancelled the old question. After the fix, all **19 question-flow browser tests passed**. The added scenarios use visible composer controls and assert cancellation requests, own/child question dismissal, blank/rejected-send preservation, unrelated-session exclusion, and retention of questions arriving during the send.
- Related owner/unit suites: **143 tests passed across 6 files**. Both touched test files were audited in full; distinct regression coverage and fixture teardown are preserved, with no valid tests removed or skipped.
- Focused lint on all 4 changed TypeScript files, formatting on all 5 changed files, the Control UI controller guard, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent parent source QA found no blocking findings on candidate tree `74027c05c5c5055764f237f19c3e3a2e30b6f905`.
- Canonical local AutoReview through ClawRouter (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, high reasoning, regular Fast), base `29ce933e9e0fb59b47650f14c70bdeae7fa8791a`, same candidate tree: **scoped-clean for P0–P2**, exit 0, validated report with no findings. Reviewer assessment covered the supplied patch/context and did not execute project code. An earlier native OpenClaw review attempt was unavailable and produced no report; it is not counted as a passing review.
- Initial exact-head CI caught a PR-caused `catalogReason` reference error and a redundant default type argument. Both are repaired. Re-running the complete browser file exposed its existing explicit-queue preservation regression; cancellation now excludes the queue override, with an added focused regression. The repaired candidate passed all **19 browser tests** and **143 owner tests**. No existing assertion was weakened. Canonical AutoReview of the repair delta against `b66c8338f75788d8b4d9fcafb6f1e3943fe15580` was **scoped-clean P0–P2**, exit 0, no findings. Repaired tree: `c852ffcb57ec8767368bb05b07993655f888ca0f`; published head: `946aa692816b60383944437ca184d88bf971284e`. Prior-head CI remains a failed result, not passing evidence.
- **Typecheck gap:** UI typechecking was attempted but the existing physical-path guard rejects the canonical global pnpm graph because its compiler/declaration dependency resolves outside the checkout. The guard was not bypassed and no private dependency graph was created. This is not a successful source typecheck; exact-head PR CI remains required.

<details>
<summary>Exact focused commands and change size</summary>

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-question-actions.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-state.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-child-questions.test.ts ui/src/app/question-prompt*.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/question-flow.e2e.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config ui/src/pages/chat/chat-question-actions.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-question-actions.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-render.ts ui/src/e2e/question-flow.e2e.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check ui/src/pages/chat/chat-question-actions.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-question-actions.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-render.ts ui/src/e2e/question-flow.e2e.test.ts docs/tools/ask-user.md
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-controllers.mts
git diff --check
```

5 files, +283/−13: production +48/−11, tests +226/−2, docs +9. The necessary growth protects accepted-send ordering and lifecycle ownership while preserving existing optional-question handling. The old separate send-action spread is removed in favor of the single wrapped owner. The catalog reason object remains shared by its text and recovery action; redundant text aliases are inlined to stay within the render-file line limit.

prs.title: improve(ci): avoid recompressing candidate registry artifacts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared FRV candidate producer recompresses the prerelease plugin registry, which already consists almost entirely of gzip-compressed npm tarballs. Its neighboring package/image uploads and the other registry uploaders already disable this redundant compression.

## User Impact

No validation or published package changes. Set the existing upload action’s compression level to zero; retain every registry file, manifest/digest check, artifact identity, missing-file error and consumer. This is a small runner-efficiency improvement, not a claim of minutes saved from FRV.

## Evidence and Wall-Time Assessment

- Real input: [candidate run 43998194486, artifact 14291137296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43998194486/artifacts/14291137296), 54 files / 130,006,985 bytes.
- Five interleaved Python ZIP proxy pairs over those exact files: median level-6 wall **1.800 s**, stored wall **0.098 s**. Archive sizes **129,960,111 → 130,015,299 bytes**: +55,188 bytes, approximately 0.042%. Every member’s bytes were verified after every archive round trip. This measures local ZIP work, **not** the hosted action or whole FRV.
- The transfer tradeoff is explicit: the extra ~54 KiB would erase the measured ~1.70 s saving only below roughly 32 KiB/s incremental throughput. No extra job, queue delay, setup, dependency barrier or concurrent memory load is added. Parent wall improvement can be zero while another qualification branch dominates.
- The pinned [upload action](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9/action.yml) supports level zero for incompressible data. Registry upload began in a0deb8edae1a (#120107); this does not undo a documented compression requirement.
- Compact workflow regression fails on the base’s missing compression setting. The complete package-acceptance workflow suite passes: **587 tests, 147.56 s** on the pinned Bun runner. Scoped canonical typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and pinned actionlint/zizmor/workflow guards pass.
- These are configuration/coverage and archive-byte proofs; no end-to-end hosted upload speedup is claimed.

## Simplification

Production **+1/-0**, tests **+6/-0**, two files. No new helper, policy owner, benchmark framework or committed bulky fixture. The regression extends the existing registry-consumer contract and retains missing-file failure behavior.

## Historical review evidence (superseded readiness assessment)

Verified November 17, 2026, 03:36 UTC at **a6f06b529aa2c37dffd2706183831440680095f6**: conflict-free; ClawSweeper completed with no findings or before-merge items. Exact-head CI completed with no related failing checks. CI is **not all green**: its sole substantive failure is the unchanged private-UI ownership inventory assertion (91 versus 90), reproduced locally and independently on #200380; the aggregate gate reflects it. prs.title: improve(ci): avoid repeated SDK declaration fallback walks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release SDK qualification repeatedly walks the same complete declaration fallback for different exports. On the full current-root workload this dominated rendering time, delaying release validation.

## User Impact

No SDK API or runtime behavior changes. Release operators get faster SDK baseline rendering with identical declaration text, sections, hashes, and diagnostics. This is not a measured end-to-end FRV speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep complete fallback roots once within the existing immutable declaration renderer. Recursive partial walks remain uncached because cycles omit visited ancestors. No global cache, new planner, skipped declarations, or relaxed guard. The map is bounded by source roots in one renderer and discarded with it.

Simplification: +12/-4 production lines and one 37-line regression, using existing owners. The regression checks repeated work and complete cyclic A/B roots together; existing cycle/diagnostic tests remain.

## Evidence

Baseline: 6ba51132e323cff0239e1d91279836202c060e00. Candidate production SHA256: 83d4eda87517643e9bbef178a57d21f2e4b1a5a4f7f0351992cf5f0456c3bfbc.

Full production render of 163 modules, 3,888 exports, 13,497 pooled sections; all ten outputs byte-identical (26,225,966 bytes; SHA256 ad65d211bf49f5c46976ba8ad26ef708cebb175f6568d519795436bb3b61c2a4). Five serial interleaved cold-process/warm-filesystem pairs on a shared 32-CPU Linux host, Node 26.12.1, native compiler singleThreaded unchanged, 6GiB JS heap limit. No parallel heavy work from this batch; lightweight source/ref work occurred during A1. Ambient contention remains a limitation.

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Whole-process wall seconds | 529.126 / 676.878 | 88.901 / 110.855 |
| Aggregate process-tree RSS KiB | 10,231,824 / 10,430,812 | 10,303,348 / 10,600,236 |
| Node max RSS KiB | 4,052,080 / 4,125,184 | 3,625,344 / 3,779,072 |
| Observed heap bytes | 2,955,018,592 / 3,067,822,760 | 2,059,847,352 / 2,190,881,968 |

Wall ranges: baseline 485.182–676.878s; candidate 83.776–110.855s. Median saving 440.225s (83.2%). p95 is nearest rank (observed maximum for n=5), not a population-tail guarantee. Aggregate RSS maximum +1.62%, within the predeclared 20% ceiling.

Predeclared rule: at least 5% median wall improvement; no >20% regression in p95 wall, aggregate RSS, Node RSS, or combined observed heap, including a per-pair stop. All passed. Combined observed heap is the maximum of timer samples, main-isolate GC-boundary object sizes and endpoint heap; it is not a continuously observed exact peak. An earlier four-pair series stopped on noisy timer-only heap (+99.35% in pair four) and remains separately retained, not pooled. A diagnostic established that timers miss synchronous baseline peaks; the corrected instrumentation was approved and predeclared before this fresh series. Raw timer-only median increased; no claim that it improved.

Harness calls the complete production renderer and production inventory with frozen six-owner copies. It does not time historical revision preparation or the outer multi-revision command. Tracked/generated inputs, dependency metadata and compiler/runtime fingerprints were checked. Commands/evidence retained in task scratch: sdk-gc-qualification/{acceptance.md,qualify.py,run.mts,series.json,summary.json}; original stopped evidence retained separately. No new benchmark command is committed.

Regression: base required 3 checker traversals where 1 expected; candidate 22 focused tests passed. Scoped type-aware lint, typecheck, formatting and diff checks passed. Local independent review waived by task owner; hosted ClawSweeper and exact-head CI remain required before RFR.

Critical-path limit: rendering savings apply only where this SDK work is on the release path. Historical roots, queues, setup and downstream barriers were not benchmarked; other FRV branches can erase the end-to-end gain.


### Current readiness — November 18, 2026

Repaired exact-head CI is fully green, hosted ClawSweeper is complete with no findings or before-merge items, and GitHub reports MERGEABLE. Ready for review; no merge performed. [Exact-head receipts and qualification evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200954#issuecomment-6967999751). This supersedes historical pending/red-CI status above.

prs.body:
## Integration update (2026-11-18)

Current candidate: `b3db8b351ac3910858693a4f0a444d226177e81d`. [Full current-head Node/Bun validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104) completed with 127 successful, 22 failed, 13 skipped and 2 cancelled jobs. Workflow and checkout both used this SHA, with base `42b907f`, `validation_tier=main`, `test_runtime_policy=dual-all`, no release gate and no PR-selection input. This exercised the previously omitted cases. The PR remains draft; the pin is not qualified.

- [Doctor continuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904495388): Node 24.22.1 passed both cached-writer cases. Bun timed out in the cached-writer case, including teardown; the following uncached case failed while seeding its fixture with closed read admission, before Doctor started. Both runtimes passed the warm IPC regression and activation siblings. The original stall remains unlocated; the subsequent setup failure does not independently establish a second Doctor bug.
- [Invitation retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904501591): Node passed commit and rollback. Bun retained the commit callback sentinel while its control collected. The test and relevant callback owners match the original diagnostic candidate, but matching symptoms do not establish an identical root cause.
- [Control UI shard 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904491089): Bun failed `preserves newer model controls when accepting an older draft (identity=false)` while waiting for the model-picker option to appear, before selecting the newer controls or accepting the older submission. The cause of the missing option is unresolved. UI performance passed. This failure is separate from callback retention.
- [Spawn proxy retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904495351) failed in the default Node shard with one retained proxy; the corresponding Bun group passed. It is not evidence of a common Bun retainer.
- [Dependency analysis](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904492764) reported unused production exports `resolveSessionTranscriptPath` and `resolveSessionTranscriptPathInDir`. Their source, analysis inputs and dependency lock match main at `42b907f`. Other failed jobs remain unresolved; this summary does not waive them.

This signed merge preserves the original pin commit and both signed fixture integrations, and incorporates main at `42b907fdd6764ad34177c7fbec56a4f052881f6f`. Relative to that main revision, only the canonical Bun pin and two documentation references differ (+19/-19). All three landed fixture files match main byte-for-byte. Independent source review, signature verification, formatting and diff checks passed. The Bun pin is unchanged from the original candidate.

- [PR #200074](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200074) prevents the anchor preload from consuming startup IPC.
- [PR #200310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200310) limits Doctor fixture request observation to its canonical readonly child while preserving every child's database guard.
- The [superseded scoped PR gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44040670671) ended with 48 successful, 1 failed, 20 skipped and 7 cancelled jobs. It omitted the Doctor continuation, invitation retention and warm regression cases; it does not qualify this pin. Older pre-merge runs are likewise not current-head proof.

The [closed-admission root-cut comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44041176672) used original candidate `4ea5bab`, with the original timer, collection and assertions. Old Bun passed all 8 cases; new Bun passed 7 and failed commit callback retention. Both pins collected all 4 closed admissions and the control in each case. This rules out the removed closed-admission roots in that projection, without identifying the surviving reference. Both cells settled and restored cleanly.

The [callback-identity comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44227751894) used the same original candidate and eight case identities. Old Bun passed all eight; new Bun passed seven and reproduced commit retention. Immediately after the original timer and GC, the new-pin commit case retained both `prepareMentionInvitation` and its returned `assertCurrent` guard, while the outer persistence Promise and control had collected. Rollback and both old-pin cases collected all observed objects. Both cells settled and restored the test and pin cleanly. This narrows the surviving identities without identifying their strong retainer; weak-reference instrumentation changes allocation/layout and does not qualify the current pin. The [signed diagnostic controller](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/commit/fbba4f90be4d9486e68565826ae2e0258a830a43) received independent source review, parser tests, syntax checks and source-projection validation before execution.

A [follow-on operation-spy probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44229002630) invalidated its old-pin control: old Bun changed from eight passes to seven passes and commit retention. Its observed operation parameters and run callback collected, while acknowledgement/completion callbacks survived, but the added observer changed the previously passing behavior. No runtime attribution or production repair is justified from this probe. The old cell settled and restored cleanly; the new cell was cancelled before a verdict, and the run is fully stopped. The uninstrumented current-head failures remain the qualification blockers.

The [transformed-code capture](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44039352845), also on the original candidate, recorded 7 passes and the commit retention failure. Its sole variant uses lowered disposal with both disposal calls present; helper identity remains unresolved. It establishes neither cause nor qualification.

Historical evidence below belongs to its stated source or projection. It does not supersede the current-head failures above.

## What Problem This Solves

CI and app-managed runtimes still select the October OpenClaw Bun build.

## User Impact

Updates the shared Bun pin to [the signed November prerelease](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.4-20261115-9debcc4b9d-webkit-3357f9d63e) across all six supported targets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Regenerates the shared pin from the published manifest, including archive and executable checksums, and updates the two current documentation references.

## Evidence

**Validation remains blocked by Doctor, invitation retention and other unresolved findings. The separate POSIX fixture repair has landed with passing projected proof and its own successful CI; this unchanged pin candidate is not ready to land.**

- Candidate: `4ea5babab09c338812ae50dbcdaed990f48cd0fc`.
- [Bun publication run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43794773536) passed six-target build/signing/smoke and its frozen OpenClaw/Birdclaw consumer gates; published checksums and cryptographic provenance were verified. Those consumer gates tested their frozen sources, not this PR head.
- Static checks passed: canonical manifest projection, signed Windows flags, JSON parsing, exact scope, and diff hygiene. Independent source/diff review found no P0–P2 issues. Full local ClawSweeper review covered the complete three-file, one-commit range with no actionable findings. After the shared repository history repair, the retained native review-artifact validator passed with the candidate and workflow unchanged. This is structural validation only: the review remains NEEDS WORK with failing tests and behavioral gaps.
- [Exact-candidate Linux Bun-only qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43808664006) passed all ten canonical package and smoke stages.

Old-pin execution covered Darwin ARM64; the new pin also passed the Darwin x64 Rosetta probe. Linux asset checks in that run were format/hash checks, not Linux runtime qualification.
- [Actual-head dual-runtime CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43805983669) finished with failure: all 270 jobs completed, with 218 passed, 38 failed, six cancelled, and eight skipped. The macOS test job was cancelled and skipped bundled app recovery. The dual-runtime UI2 failure still needs runtime attribution.
- Focused ARM packaged-recovery proof is now accepted from the [corrected app-host run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43825007091): seven preparation steps and all three expected native phases passed; six ARM receipts covered both native-first settings and sharing omitted/true/false at the exact candidate, new pin and build. Cleanup exited zero and source remained clean. The outer workflow failed only after native proof, when its parser selected a different-schema fs-safe receipt and raised `KeyError: 'revision'`. This closes the focused ARM recovery gap, not full Swift, x64 or overall repin qualification. The [initial broader-build run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43818225493) timed out before cases.
- Doctor remains a qualification blocker. The [matched Linux old/new comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006) had identical 1,052 case identities and five skips: 1,047 old-pin passes versus 1,045 new-pin passes and two failures, including SQLite snapshot allocation/cleanup errors and timeout with uncertain settlement. - The Doctor readonly-child observer candidate still fails in the original 116-file group. The [uninstrumented helper-only run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43942906159) timed out cached-writer=true at 120,025 ms while false passed in 6,006 ms. The [same candidate with case/cycle phase writes](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43948269897), controller `59bc44ff`, reversed those outcomes: true passed in 5,432 ms; false failed in 300,006 ms across the 120-second test and 180-second hook budgets. Both runs recorded 114 files passed, one failed and one skipped; 1,046 tests passed, one failed and five skipped. Each completed with native exit 1, no controller failure or settlement uncertainty, five passing preparation steps, and restored source/pin with tracked source clean. Native arguments, environment, full preset, reporters and budgets stayed unchanged. The phase run recorded 62 contiguous case-attributed frames: true had no unmatched entry; false entered maintenance acquisition and finally-isolation without returned markers, with afterEach preceding the finally frames. Framing completeness means only untruncated attributed records; a missing returned marker may reflect a throw, not a stall. Marker writes can affect timing and scheduling. Neither failure is waived, and no internal cause, timeout fix or unchanged-C qualification is established. The [earlier cause diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43869768145) remains distinct: snapshot-staging readiness-deadline and channel-closed cleanup errors, native 143, uncertain settlement and no restoration.
- The same controlled comparison found a candidate-only invitation failure in `session-mention-invitation.test.ts:285`: identical 3,308 case identities and 34 skips, with 3,274 old-pin passes versus 3,273 new-pin passes and one failure. The callback sentinel remained retained while its control collected; both runs settled and restored cleanly. See the [old evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006/artifacts/14204168676) and [new evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006/artifacts/14203779105). prs.title: fix(plugins): read JSON5 plugin manifests in doctor and recovery paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` (and the install-record recovery path) silently skips any managed npm plugin whose `openclaw.plugin.json` uses JSON5 — comments, trailing commas, or unquoted keys — because the stale-managed-npm-shadow check (`doctor-plugin-registry.ts`) and the recovery reader (`installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts`) parse the manifest with a strict JSON reader that returns `null` on such syntax. The plugin is documented as JSON5-capable (`docs/plugins/manifest.md`: "Native manifests are parsed with JSON5"), the main loader accepts it (`manifest.ts:218` `parsePluginCacheJson(file, { json5: true })`), and `openclaw plugins install` installs it. But Doctor's shadow check reads the same file strictly, so a stale managed npm package shadowing a bundled plugin is never reported and never repaired — the user's plugin silently keeps the old version with no hint from `openclaw doctor`.

Precedent: #198808 (same shape: a JSON5-capable manifest reread with strict `JSON.parse`; the CLI browser builder was switched to the JSON5-capable reader). This PR applies the shape to the two remaining strict readers of installed-plugin manifests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two remaining strict readers are the only places that parse a user-installed `openclaw.plugin.json` with plain strict JSON. `package.json` reads stay strict (npm `package.json` is never JSON5). The fix adds one shared reader, `tryReadJson5ObjectSync` in `src/infra/json-files.ts`, that keeps the strict-JSON fast path, falls back to JSON5, and preserves the `null`-on-failure contract of the existing `tryReadJsonObjectSync` — so a malformed manifest degrades exactly as before. Both call sites route their `openclaw.plugin.json` read through it.

Production LOC is `+72/-10` (net +62), two call sites change, one shared helper added in the JSON-reader owner, plus a recovery rekey. No new validator / option / config / persistence.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (a stale shadow that was silently skipped is now reported and repaired, matching the loader's documented JSON5 acceptance).

## User Impact

A user who installed an npm plugin with a JSON5 manifest (comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys) now gets the stale-managed-npm shadow warning and `--fix` repair from `openclaw doctor`, instead of the shadow being silently skipped and the bundled plugin staying shadowed by an old managed copy. Strict JSON manifests and all other doctor behaviors are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Discriminating test (producer-chain, real repair path)

The regression adds a JSON5 variant of the existing `warns about stale managed npm packages that shadow bundled plugins` case in `src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts`: it builds the same bundled-vs-managed fixture but writes the managed package's `openclaw.plugin.json` as JSON5 (`{ id: 'bundled-demo', ..., }` with a leading comment), then runs `maybeRepairPluginRegistryState` and asserts the shadow warning and the `@openclaw/bundled-demo@2026.5.2` note are emitted.

- RED on base (`121b720292e1`): the JSON5 case fails at `expect(notes).toContain("Managed npm plugin packages shadow bundled plugins")` — the strict reader returns `null`, `pluginId` is undefined, and the stale package is skipped.
- GREEN on head (`23deadb73807`): the same case passes; the full file stays green (33/33).

Remote proof run (sandboxed runner, docker Node 24.22.1, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`), tree-local md5-pinned base vs head:

```text
RED  (base, strict read):   1 failed | 32 passed  ->  expected '' to contain "Managed npm plugin packages shadow bundled plugins"
GREEN (head, JSON5 read):   Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 33 passed (33)
```

### Fixup: retain the atomic-writer import

A first revision of the shared reader accidentally replaced the `@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic` import in `json-files.ts`, leaving `writeTextAtomic` with an undefined `writeFsSafeTextAtomic` (ClawSweeper P1). The current head restores the atomic import alongside the new read import; the atomic-writer tests stay green (`src/infra/json-files.test.ts`: 22/22 on head).

### Fixup: rekey persisted package-name recovery records

A released strict reader could already have persisted an install record keyed by the npm package name for a package whose JSON5 manifest declares a different `id`. Reading the JSON5 id then yields the same install path under the manifest id (ClawSweeper P1). `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmInstallRecords` now rekeys the persisted record to the recovered manifest id **before** building recovery candidates — deleting the old key first would discard persisted metadata (`integrity`, `installedAt`, …) and lose the active-path authority. A regression in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts` covers the previously persisted package-name case and asserts the persisted metadata is retained:

```text
RED  (JSON5 id read, no rekey):   expected { source: 'npm', …(6) } to match object { source: 'npm', …(8) }  (metadata lost / duplicate key)
GREEN (JSON5 id read + rekey):    Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 11 passed (11)
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 33/33 on head (RED on base for the discriminating assertion).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/json-files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 22/22 on head (atomic writer tests intact).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.managed-npm.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 15/15 on head (reconcile regression included).
- `git diff --check` — clean.

### Shipped proof: real `openclaw doctor` on a JSON5 manifest

Built both trees to a real `dist` and drove the actual CLI binary (`node dist/entry.js doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json`), not the test harness. The fixture is a genuine managed npm plugin install under an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: `npm/projects/openclaw-a2a-d83b9340a9/` with a `package.json` declaring `@openclaw/a2a`, the installed package's strict `package.json`, and an `openclaw.plugin.json` written as JSON5 (leading comment, unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing comma):

```json5
// Native manifests are parsed with JSON5 (docs/plugins/manifest.md).
{
  id: 'a2a',
  name: 'A2A',
  configSchema: { type: 'object' },
}
```

`@openclaw/a2a` is a real bundled plugin, so the managed copy is a genuine shadow. Four-cell matrix, same fixture, two real builds:

| `openclaw.plugin.json` | base `121b720` (strict reader) | head `23deadb` (JSON5 reader) |
|---|---|---|
| strict JSON | `Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.` | same — no regression |
| JSON5 | **no finding** (`ok: true`) | **`Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.`** |

The strict-JSON row proves the diagnosis path itself is unchanged; only the JSON5 row changes. Raw head output:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/ev2-head/.openclaw node dist/entry.js \
    doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":0,"findings":[
  {"checkId":"core/doctor/plugin-registry","severity":"warning",
   "message":"Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.",
   "path":"/tmp/ev2-head/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-a2a-d83b9340a9/node_modules/@openclaw/a2a",
   "target":"a2a",
   "fixHint":"Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove stale managed npm packages and rebuild the plugin registry."}]}
```

Repair path, end to end on the same state:

```text
$ node dist/entry.js doctor --fix --non-interactive
before --fix: package exists = yes
after  --fix: package exists = no
$ node dist/entry.js doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json
ok: true   findings: <none>
```

### Shipped proof: v2026.11.3 → head upgrade keeps legacy keys and metadata

The compatibility question is whether an install record persisted by the **released** strict reader (keyed by the npm package name) survives the upgrade. Both sides here are the real thing: the released tag `v2026.11.3` resolves to `847611dcaa3b` (not the PR's merge base `121b720`), and that commit was built to its own `dist` and run as a CLI.

The fixture is a non-shadow managed npm plugin — `@vendor/demo@1.2.3`, not in the bundled set — so the upgrade path exercises the record rekey rather than the shadow repair:

```json5
// JSON5 manifest
{
  id: 'demo',
  name: 'Demo',
  configSchema: { type: 'object' },
}
```

Steps, all against the real SQLite state (`state/openclaw.sqlite`, `config_machine_state.value_json` under `plugins.installedIndex`):

1. **v2026.11.3 (`847611dcaa3b`) reads the manifest strictly**, so it identifies the package by its npm name: `v2026.11.3 key: "@vendor/demo"`. Head identifies the same package as `head key: "demo"`.
2. **v2026.11.3 persists that record** through the production write path (`withPluginLifecycleLease` + `writePersistedInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsWithLease`, the same pair the plugin-install commit uses), recording `integrity: "sha512-legacy-v2026.11.3"`, `installedAt: "2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z"`.
3. **On disk before upgrade** — `keys: ['@vendor/demo']`, metadata and `installPath` intact.
4. **Upgrade to head `23deadb` — read** — `loadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecords` returns `keys: ['demo']` with `metadata retained: {"integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.3","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z"}` and the same `installPath`.
5. **Upgrade to head — write** — the rekeyed records go back through the same production write path; on disk afterwards: `keys: ['demo']`, `integrity: "sha512-legacy-v2026.11.3"`, `installedAt: "2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z"`, `installPath` unchanged.
6. **Reload in a fresh process** — `keys: ['demo'] | integrity: sha512-legacy-v2026.11.3 | installedAt: 2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z`.

Note on where the write comes from: `loadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecords` itself only reads and caches, as the review observed. The rekeyed map reaches disk when a caller that owns registry persistence writes it — the plugin-install commit path, or `openclaw doctor --fix` when its preflight selects `migrate`/`initialize` (with a readable index already present, preflight selects `skip-existing` and doctor intentionally writes nothing). Step 5 above uses that same production write pair rather than inventing a new one.

Result: the identity migrates, the persisted metadata and install path survive, and the state is stable across persistence and a fresh-process reload.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+72/-10` net +62 (one shared helper in `json-files.ts`; two call sites; atomic import retained; recovery rekey)
- Test LOC: `+61`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback` (the JSON5-capable parser already used by the main loader and `state-migrations.fs.ts`) and the existing `tryReadJsonObjectSync` null-on-failure contract; the reconciliation reuses the existing `recordsShareInstallPath` owner predicate — no new abstraction beyond the shared helper the two call sites need.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. `package.json` reads remain strict; the JSON5 reader is used only for `openclaw.plugin.json`.

### Cleanup

The shipped-CLI proof runs used isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` directories under `/tmp` created for this run and removed afterwards. Three separate builds were used: the released tag `v2026.11.3` (`847611dcaa3b`), the PR merge base (`121b720`), and the PR head (`23deadb`), each in its own worktree. No running Gateway, session, token, or production config was touched.

prs.title: fix: stop newer-schema refusals sending you to doctor --fix after a source build wrote your data
prs.body:
Closes #200886

## What Problem This Solves

If a source build of `main` upgrades your database and an installed release then refuses to open it, the refusal tells you to run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor then refuses too, and tells you to run "a build at least as new as the writer", which can be the build you are already running. Following the advice goes nowhere and can make a database that is simply newer look damaged.

## User Impact

User impact: when OpenClaw refuses a database with a newer schema, it no longer suggests `doctor --fix` or points back at the running build. It says the data was written by a different build with a newer schema and points to a build that supports that schema, or to a backup. The refusal itself, its exit code and the database files are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both refusal messages chose their advice by comparing release labels (`isNewerSqliteWriterVersion`). A source build of `main` carries the label of the last release closeout, so its label can sort equal to, below, or outside the release order (for example `2026.11.6-dev.1` compares as unknown) while its schema is higher. Those cases fell into the "older writer" wording.

These messages are only built when the stored schema is already newer than this build supports, so the writer is newer whatever its label says. This keeps the label comparison for the case where it adds something (a writer whose label really is newer still gets "Use the newer install ... or run openclaw update"), and otherwise:

- `createNewerSqliteSchemaVersionError` (status, Gateway, Doctor maintenance): drops "run openclaw doctor --fix to inspect this database" and says the writer was "a different build with a newer schema (such as a source or development build)".
- `formatIncompatibleDatabaseSchemas` (Doctor and Gateway preflight): replaces "Run a build at least as new as the writer that supports these schemas" with "Use a build that supports these schemas with this state directory".
- `docs/cli/gateway/restart-and-supervision.md`: same sentence fix.

#186971 deliberately kept the `doctor --fix` hint for same-version and unknown writers, because a schema number alone does not prove the writer *release* is newer. The new wording keeps that caution: it does not claim a newer release, only a newer schema, which the schema number does establish. The hint itself has to go because, as the [integrity and recovery guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas/integrity-and-recovery#the-gateway-refuses-to-start-with-a-newer-schema-version-error) says, `doctor --fix` cannot repair a newer schema, and Doctor refuses on this path. That is why the existing expectation in `src/infra/sqlite-user-version.test.ts` (the same-version runtime case expecting `doctor --fix`) changes.

Message-only change; no schema, admission, exit-code or downgrade-policy change.

## Evidence

**Regression (red on base, green with the fix).** `src/infra/sqlite-user-version.test.ts` now covers newer, equal, lower (`2000.1.1`), unrecognized (`2026.11.6-dev.1`) and absent writer labels for both the runtime and Doctor-maintenance formatters and the preflight formatter. On unmodified `main` both cases fail (`expected ... not to contain 'doctor --fix'`); with the fix all 5 tests pass. The two checkonce tests that asserted `OpenClaw 2026.10.8; ... doctor --fix` at the state and agent admission boundaries now assert the new wording.

**Live CLI, isolated state.** A source build of this branch with throwaway `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, home/app-data directories and a non-default Gateway port. Seeded state with `doctor --fix`, then marked the state database as written by a future build (`user_version` 40 → 41, writer label `2026.11.4` or `2026.11.5`), then ran `status` and `doctor --fix --non-interactive`. Paths replaced with placeholders.

Before (unmodified `main`, writer label `2026.11.4`), `status`, exit 1:

```text
It was written by OpenClaw 2026.11.4; run openclaw doctor --fix to inspect this database.
```

Before, `doctor --fix --non-interactive` preflight, exit 1:

```text
... writer build 2026.11.4. Refused by OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (4dbd70f) installed at <source checkout>. Run a build at least as new as the writer that supports these schemas, or stop the service and restore your pre-upgrade backup created with openclaw backup create. ...
```

After (this branch, writer label `2026.11.4`), `status`, exit 1:

```text
This OpenClaw build cannot open your existing data.
OpenClaw state database <state dir>\state\openclaw.sqlite uses newer schema version 41; this build supports 40.
It was written by OpenClaw 2026.11.4, a different build with a newer schema (such as a source or development build).
Refused by OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (4dbd70f) installed at <source checkout>.
Use a build that supports schema 41 or newer with this state directory. To use an older build, restore your pre-update backup created with openclaw backup create.
See https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas.
```

After, `doctor --fix --non-interactive` preflight, exit 1:

```text
Doctor refused to continue because 1 OpenClaw database schema(s) are newer than this build. state database <state dir>\state\openclaw.sqlite uses schema 41; this build supports 40; writer build 2026.11.4. Refused by OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (4dbd70f) installed at <source checkout>. Use a build that supports these schemas with this state directory, or stop the service and restore your pre-upgrade backup created with openclaw backup create. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas.
```

The equal-label run (`2026.11.5` against `2026.11.5`) gives the same guidance. In every run, before and after, the SHA-256 of every `*.sqlite*` file in the state directory was identical before and after `status` and `doctor`, and no new sidecar files appeared.

**Other checks.**

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-maintenance.finish-revalidation.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts src/cli/run-main.gateway-startup.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run.option-collisions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: no new failures. These files have Windows-only failures on this machine (POSIX `/tmp` path expectations, POSIX directory-permission checks, sidecar path casing); the failure list is identical with and without this change.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, dead-export scan, schema and boundary guards pass. The format step flagged line wrapping in the three test files; fixed with the repo formatter and rechecked clean.

**Gaps.**

- The two checkonce tests (`src/state/openclaw-state-db-checkonce.test.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.checkonce.test.ts`) fail on Windows at fixture setup (`EPERM` renaming a replacement file over an open SQLite file) both on `main` and on this branch, so their new assertions are proven by Linux CI, not locally. The live `status` run above goes through the same state admission path.
- Test cost: `src/infra/sqlite-user-version.test.ts` adds two writer labels to an existing loop; the 5 tests run in tens of milliseconds (local wall time is dominated by cold transform).

prs.title: fix: stop the recurring cold-storage failure when an agent has no database
prs.body:
Closes #200830

## What Problem This Solves

Gateways that set `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` and have any configured agent without a database logged `transcript cold storage failed: … SQLite archive pruning requires its existing file owner` every minute, indefinitely. A store with no database now simply has nothing to prune.

- Problem: cold-storage maintenance asks the archive owner to prune retention for **every** configured agent id, including ids with no database yet (a fresh agent, or an `acp.allowedAgents` id that never ran). The page-reclamation guard rejects that path-only identity, so the whole pass fails.
- Solution: return no removals when the store's captured identity is not an existing file.
- What changed: `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-store.ts` (guard in `prunePublishedSessionArchivesByRetention`) and a regression case in `session-cold-storage.inventory.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: stores that have a database prune exactly as before, and the page-reclamation guard still rejects identities it cannot explain, so a replaced or inaccessible database is not silently skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The read side of the same retention query already returns "nothing" for a store with no database, and the archive step beside this call returns early for the same case; only the prune call treated it as an error.

- Best fix: keep the guard in the archive owner (`prunePublishedSessionArchivesByRetention`) so every caller of the retention query behaves like its read counterpart. `path:` is produced only when the database path does not exist, so this cannot hide a permission or replacement problem — those fail identity resolution and still throw elsewhere.
- Alternative: skip absent stores in the maintenance loop in `session-cold-storage.ts`. Smaller diff, but leaves the same trap for the next caller of the prune entry point.
- Risk / non-goals: a store created between inventory and prune is skipped for that one pass and pruned on the next; retention is age-based, so no archive is lost.

## User Impact

A Gateway with an unused ACP allowlist id, or with a freshly configured agent, stops logging `transcript cold storage failed` every 60 s, and `sessions.storage.status` stops reporting `lastError` for a normal state.

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway run on a source build of this PR head (`5a31f7f`, Debian 13, Node 24.22.1). Config: one agent (`main`) plus one `acp.allowedAgents` id (`codex`) that never ran; `session.maintenance.mode=enforce`, `resetArchiveRetention=365d`, cold storage enabled. `sessions.create` gave `main` a database, then two maintenance passes ran:

```text
== populated sibling databaseBytes(main) = 700416

== retention pass 1
maintenance: {"lastError": null, "lastCompletedAt": 1794970950128}
agents: main databaseBytes=700416 hotTranscripts=1 | codex databaseBytes=0

== retention pass 2
maintenance: {"lastError": null, "lastCompletedAt": 1794970974544}

== sessions.storage.status
agents: {'main': 700416, 'codex': 0}
maintenance: {'lastError': None, 'archivedTranscripts': 0,
              'externalizedTranscripts': 0, 'lastCompletedAt': 1794971010035}
running: false

== gateway log: 'transcript cold storage failed' occurrences: 0
```

This is the reported scenario: the absent `codex` store no longer fails the pass, the populated `main` store stays in the inventory of every pass, and repeated passes complete with `lastError: null` instead of one error per minute. Neither store had eligible archives to remove, so both counters are legitimately 0; removal itself is covered by the existing retention suite below.

Regression test — before/after on the same checkout:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.inventory.test.ts -t "no database"
 # before: × keeps the maintenance pass healthy when a configured agent has no database
 #         Caused by: Error: SQLite archive pruning requires its existing file owner
 # after:  ✓ keeps the maintenance pass healthy when a configured agent has no database
```

Pruning for stores that do have a database is unchanged — the same store set still prunes:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-cold-storage.inventory.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-history-archive-retention.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

What was not tested: no pre-fix Gateway run was repeated for this revision (the pre-fix failure is covered by the regression test above and by the `lastError` in the linked report); no archives were eligible for removal in the Gateway run, so end-to-end removal is covered by the retention suite rather than that run.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `gh`/`git`/`grep` to trace issue #200830 from `runSessionColdStorageMaintenance` down to the page-reclamation guard, plus a source Gateway run and `vitest` for the before/after. The implementer understands the code: the inventory reports `path:` for a database that does not exist yet, the read side of the same retention query already treats that as "nothing to prune", and the guard belongs at the archive owner so every caller agrees. All evidence above comes from real local runtime execution.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a failed chat on an explicitly selected alternate model, switching back to an available same-provider configured default requires finding it in the model picker.

## User Impact

Control UI offers **Switch to configured default** for eligible failed chats. The action changes the model for the next message; it does not retry the failed message, resend the original prompt, or alter completed tool work. Existing confirmation preferences still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action uses the existing selection and session-patch owners, preserves pinned runtime/auth choices, and rejects stale selections, sessions, failures, connections, agent inventories, locks, permissions, or unavailable targets. It only offers catalog-confirmed available models on the exact same provider.

Configured fallback chains remain authoritative. This does not supplement an existing or exhausted chain, implement automatic fallback/continuation, or infer daily quota exhaustion from a generic rate limit.

## Evidence

### Current reviewed follow-up

Head `e4bdadeb0cb3932527bc49ca32f3b53475c081c5` is an ordinary merge of the previous PR head and public main `16eb36d69a95d4d2f88e76454955c2aab096b954`; final tree `3d75ec22956f690f1c9444135c125f1522b2a36a`. It resolves the CSS conflict while retaining main's audio-player styling, and repairs the reviewed cascade defect: neutral eye/archive icons keep the muted color; the eye stays14px rather than inheriting18px warning styling.

The production-composer Chromium regression reproduced both eye/archive failures before the repair, with warning as a passing control. After repair, all3 variants plus7 existing recovery-layout cases pass. Original before/after captures were visually inspected. Focused UI40/40 and core fallback4/4 pass; UI build, production UI types, format, stylesheet lint and changed-test lint pass. Native differential performance against the pinned main passes with unchanged thresholds: raw CSS−530 bytes, gzip+33 bytes. Both revisions still exceed existing absolute CSS ceilings; this is not absolute-budget compliance.

The final complete candidate received independent P0–P3 review (`scoped-clean`), independent TestAudit and native named NoComments. The final delta from the tested production tree removes only one fixture narration comment; no executable line changed. No live-provider or current-head full Gateway recovery journey is claimed by this CSS follow-up. The maintainer decision on the explicit recovery shortcut remains open. Earlier evidence below retains its own tested commit and limitations; it is not relabelled as current-head execution.

- 93 tests passed across the recovery action, composer notices, native-runtime restriction recovery, and composer/session-controls suites (11.96 seconds wall time for the final run).
- 47 focused core model-selection tests passed for the retained strict-selection correction.
- Production UI typecheck and changed-file lint passed.
- Stylesheet lint, formatting, UI ownership guard, English-copy baseline, and `git diff --check` passed.

- Corrected an existing test's stale “Offline” expectation to the unchanged canonical “Disconnected” copy.
- The 343-line test allocation covers 56 retained strict-selection test lines, 224 explicit-switch regression lines, 26 readiness regression lines, and 37 browser geometry regression lines. The shared test-line ceiling is unchanged.

### Layout and upstream merge follow-up

- At `4eee8c3ca781b991bb6d9a76325655bb46c12e58`: 66 UI tests, 4 fallback tests, and 51 model-selection tests passed. Production and UI-chat test types, targeted lint, architecture/Madge guards, test-line ratchet, i18n verification, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Mandatory canonical autoreview ran **before push**, against `origin/main`, at P0–P3: `scoped-clean`, zero findings, exit 0. Privacy inspection passed. Hosted CI is tracked separately; these are local validation results.

### Real Gateway + shipped Control UI behavioral proof

Verified at `3e7966a5c6d6805f3891729c9d4281ecea90bc29` in an isolated installation and state directory. Frozen-lockfile dependency preparation and the full supported production build passed. The browser scenario passed twice against a real Gateway and shipped UI, with synthetic provider/model entries (no mocked Gateway responses).

Redacted chronological observation and WebSocket RPC excerpt (session identifier normalized; setup/concurrent-writer RPCs distinguished from browser actions):

```text
1. Browser chat.send {message: "Synthetic failure proof"}
   Failed reply -> "Switch to configured default" visible.

   Runtime selection before/after unchanged.
```

The trace is intentionally limited to relevant allowlisted fields; credentials, addresses, endpoint URLs, private filesystem paths, and raw diagnostics are not published. Captures below identify their exact source heads; the earlier behavioral trace remains attributed to its original head.

**Proof limits:** the strict-confirmation fixture uses a synthetic nonlocal-classified endpoint resolving locally; the existing SSRF guard rejects transport without any bypass. This proves recovery from a real transport failure, not a live upstream model response. A separate local fixture reached a rejecting synthetic provider and exercised the real patch, but correctly skipped confirmation under local-runtime policy. No live model or continuation was exercised. Recovery remains switch-only. The updated behavioral harness passed (1 test): confirmation, stale-selection rejection, preserved auth/runtime overrides, and no prompt replay. These replace the earlier synthetic previews.

prs.title: fix(config): retain intentional offline reductions across startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An operator cannot acknowledge an intentional large reduction through `config patch`. Direct file replacement can then be undone by normal recovery. Exercising the real CLI also exposed two native startup defects: the first accepted write did not establish a missing health baseline, and early recovery could miss a retained PostgreSQL baseline before database selection.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly authorize an offline reduction and retain that accepted configuration across cold startup. The larger backup remains available. Default size-drop refusal, explicit agent deletion, validation, source/lease checks and live Gateway ownership remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI forwards the existing writer's narrow `allowConfigSizeDrop` option through `config patch --allow-size-drop`; it refuses the option while a Gateway owns state. The existing health owner establishes a first accepted baseline while preserving inherited-anomaly refusal, newer-writer precedence and rollback to a truly absent baseline. Existing early core-only recovery scopes selection to the STATE family. PostgreSQL STATE still requires its configured credential; SQLite STATE can recover a damaged config before full-engine admission checks unrelated auxiliary credentials. No new recovery policy, process-global engine installation, schema or storage format is added.

The new public offline-only option still needs a maintainer's product decision; this PR does not claim that approval.

## Evidence

Current head: `210024f410cbfcadf895d80614050e0efabb9419`, integrating OpenClaw main `8ae6b3852f97`. The PostgreSQL conformance registration follows the new shard inventory owner.

- The reported first-file regression is fixed. With a readable state store and a genuinely absent config file, the existing writer establishes a healthy baseline. An existing unreadable or inherited-truncated source still cannot be promoted. The new test failed on the previous code with an inherited anomaly marker. All 16 promotion tests and eight conformance-inventory tests pass with the repair.
- Exact-head disposable proof used the real built CLI. After seeding an isolated SQLite state store and stopping that Gateway, `config set gateway.mode local` created a 570-byte file at a previously absent path. Read-only state inspection confirmed a matching SHA-256 and no anomaly. A cold Gateway boot kept the accepted config and healthy baseline.
- A broader local roster test run had two fixture validation failures, for shorthand subagent primary and escaped references. These have not been classified against a current-main control. Hosted CI on this head remains separate.

The original stable-upgrade, size-reduction and mixed-engine evidence below ran on the previously qualified head `2229fc8b3ae5a0a6328d14976553c13f1fec07cc`.

- [Executed exact-head stable-upgrade and real CLI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193636#issuecomment-6666855199): clean frozen install/runtime build; official stable session/history/preferences preserved after native migration; unflagged 13,728→1,701-byte reduction refused; flagged reduction accepted with byte-identical original backup; two cold boots retain the smaller config and original RPC data. A real live-owner request refuses with stop guidance and unchanged config.
- [Executed downstream PostgreSQL-state lifecycle proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193636#issuecomment-6665890210): fresh and retained homes each cold-boot twice with only bootstrap, preserve the larger original backups, refuse a live-owner write, retain session/history across coach detach/reattach, and still recover genuine corruption. This includes the separate #193596 repairs and existing overlay; it is explicitly distinct from exact-head proof.
- The reported mixed SQLite STATE/PostgreSQL Workboard regression is fixed: actual startup recovers the config.env-only DSN and exact healthy backup; a credential-only negative control still fails at final admission without rewriting config. The new process regression began red and is now green.
- Downstream byte-identical production fixes pass 157 affected CLI tests, 15 health/promotion cases, 166 affected observation/recovery/writer cases, 22 early-bootstrap process cases and eight PostgreSQL inventory tests. New controls began red. They cover missing-baseline first writes, inherited truncation, rollback to absence, retained PostgreSQL health with external and config.env-only DSNs, and no global engine installation.
- Production types, scoped typed lint, formatting and exact test-line allocation pass. Independent review found no actionable issues.

The stable proof uses SQLite. Doctor completed with disclosed plugin/Skill Workshop inspection and provider-context gaps in the runtime-build fixture; those checks are not claimed clean. Live inference/channel behavior and broad exact-head hosted CI remain unqualified. The PR remains a draft pending the maintainer decision on the public offline CLI option.

Separate PostgreSQL recovery admission repairs remain in #193596.

prs.body:
Related: #193579

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex post-tool turns can fall back to “no final summary was produced” when the host already persisted the input and suppresses native prompt persistence.

## User Impact

Turns that require a result retain the completed tool evidence needed to produce their final summary. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing admission owner to annotate an admitted initial input, then carry the complete resolved source snapshot separately from verified persisted messages. Preserve the original prompt identity on continuations and avoid inserting the current prompt twice. Internal retry instructions, removed or edited admissions, and revoked authority remain excluded.

Current upstream already filters silent replies before finalization eligibility, so this PR omits that redundant part of the installed backport. No queue, polling, or new delivery path is introduced.

## Evidence

- On base `56753f7762a`, the new native-attempt regression returns `source: "unavailable"` instead of the complete user/call/result context. The pre-persisted annotation and mirror regressions also fail at their intended assertions.
- Fixed source: 93 harness-selection, 24 annotation, 7 mirror-admission, and 4 selected native-attempt cases pass. After moving eligibility to the admission owner, the 24 annotation cases and native regression pass again.
- Core and full extensions typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and the test-line ratchet pass. `pnpm build:runtime` passes (4m 29.4s). Independent local autoreview of the final source found no P0–P2 defects.
- A corresponding 2026.10.10 backport was verified with a real Gateway/model: one tool execution and one recovered final reply; peer/subtask/yield delivery also completed once. This is backport operational proof, not an upstream package-build claim.
- Net +96 test lines are allocated specifically for the native composition, admission authority, and removed-input controls; the shared baseline is unchanged.

Local file wall times, including setup/worker compilation: selection 144.91s; annotation final rerun 184.78s; mirror 49.14s; native four-case run 62.78s, with the final extracted-owner regression rerun in 134.31s. These cases exercise the real SQLite/worker/admission composition; cold worker compilation dominates the longer runs. CI timing is not yet available.

Build note: the successful runtime build reports a non-fatal Control UI chat boot JS gzip budget warning (1264.5 KiB versus 1264.0 KiB). No base size comparison was run.

Upstream CI passed for head `15e8a00111c2f6b226be5fbb91885774c99d0d1f`: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42073766837). CodeQL and CodeQL Critical Quality also passed.

## Current-head runtime proof (November 8)

[Redacted real Gateway/Codex trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193616#issuecomment-6726433599) from a fresh, unmodified build of the exact published head `15e8a00111c2f6b226be5fbb91885774c99d0d1f` (`pnpm build:runtime`: 5m 30.4s).

The Gateway committed the admitted user input before the native turn started. The real model ran one shell command with one independently counted `completed-once` effect, then produced an actual empty final (`last_agent_message: null`). The existing tool-free settled finalizer recovered one visible final answer. The Gateway receipt names `codex-settled-finalizer:…`, matching the single persisted recovered-final row. Readbacks confirm one user row, one shell call, one effect-file line, and one final row. No production source, model responses, transport, or persistence owner was replaced or mocked.

The isolated test Gateway was stopped and its copied login, configuration, state, and home removed. This proves Gateway RPC/transcript recovery; external-channel delivery and restart durability are outside this trace. The existing base-red regression remains the patch-only comparison.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway can fail to start when recovering a valid backup after its active configuration unexpectedly shrinks.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared recovery now uses the existing asynchronous backup validator. The final durable lease-ownership read uses existing engine-store admission while remaining synchronous immediately before filesystem effects. Expired or revoked ownership still refuses recovery.

## Evidence

Exact PR head: `f4f3b0cf1fcfbba16b8d19038300844f8b3cee05`.

Regressions cover the failing cold metadata path, expired/revoked leases refusing filesystem changes, and ordinary main-thread PostgreSQL reads remaining forbidden. Production types, scoped typed lint and the worker-boundary ratchet pass.
- [Latest exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193596#issuecomment-6663467986): sufficient real proof, no actionable findings, ready for maintainer review.
