prs.title: improve(backup): faster PostgreSQL export hashing for blob-heavy stores
prs.body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL backups and database ports of blob-heavy stores spend much of their export time turning every BLOB into hex inside JSON just to hash the row.

## User Impact

`openclaw backup create`, update rollback captures and `openclaw database port` export PostgreSQL stores faster when they hold large BLOB rows. On a state store with 1 GiB of BLOB rows, the PostgreSQL export phase drops from about 24 s to about 18 s.

Existing backups and exact captures verify and restore with this build, including ones written by the published 2026.11.3 release. Port receipts in the old format still verify.

Downgrade limit: export manifests written by this build record `verification.digest: "typed-v1"`. Published releases with PostgreSQL support (2026.11.1 through 2026.11.3, Workboard only) read that object strictly, so their reader refuses these manifests with `Unrecognized key: "digest"`. The refusal happens before any PostgreSQL namespace or anchor is written. In practice this applies to exact captures and port captures. In 2026.11.3, `backup restore` of an archive from this build extracts the PostgreSQL capsule as files without importing it, `backup git restore` has only `--global` and `--agent` scopes, and an upgraded state directory is refused anyway (state schema 39, while 2026.11.3 supports 22). This downgrade limit is accepted: before upgrading, keep a verified PostgreSQL backup made with the release you might roll back to, and restore that backup with its matching release. No database migration or staged writer rollout is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every table digest used to hash `JSON.stringify` of each row with BLOB cells hex-encoded. The digest now hashes typed raw bytes: one tag byte and 8 bytes per value (integer, real, or byte length), then the TEXT or BLOB bytes as they are. Values cannot run into each other, and null, empty text, empty BLOB, integer, real, text and BLOB stay distinct. Integral numbers still hash as integers, as before, because PostgreSQL returns `integer` and `boolean` columns as JavaScript numbers while SQLite returns bigints; the SQLite and PostgreSQL sides of a port therefore still produce the same digest.

New digests are recorded with `verification.digest: "typed-v1"`. A stored proof without that id (an exact export, Git or archive capture, or a port receipt from an older build) is checked with the old JSON digest, so update rollback and port recovery across an upgrade keep working. The id only matters where a stored digest is compared: exact restores, and the database port staging and `verify` steps.

Across an update, the in-process updater retains the running package and binds every worker it starts, including the database backup worker, to that retained copy before replacing the package. Its update captures and rollback restores therefore read and write one manifest format. If retention fails, workers load the new package, which reads both formats.

## Evidence

### Cross-release restore (2026-11-18)

Tested the portable exact Workboard capture twice on disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 clusters, using the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` package and PR head `c3934f6e218f`. Both exports used Workboard schema 3 and had byte-identical SQLite images, isolating the verification-format change.

- **Old export → new reader:** the candidate verified and restored the unmodified release export. An independent dump matched the source after normalizing only the generated namespace name: all 18 tables, including six populated tables and a 70,003-byte binary attachment.
- **New export → old reader:** 2026.11.3 rejected `verification.digest` before connecting to PostgreSQL or writing an anchor. The full destination dump, three namespaces, 51 catalog objects, existing anchor and sentinel were unchanged. The release restored its own export on the same destination as a positive control.

This tests exact captures, not whole-archive restore or updater behavior. Independent P0–P3 source review of the candidate plus the rollback documentation found no actionable issues; it does not replace hosted CI or ClawSweeper clearance.

### Regression refresh (2026-11-15)

The branch history is preserved. [Commit c3934f6e218f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c3934f6e218ff739f8894af1805a29a73e286b10) adds only the INTEGER/REAL same-payload collision case; production code is unchanged. The downgrade limit described above has since been accepted.

Fresh checks on the published source tree:

- Repository-planned focused run: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/infra/database-engine/port-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 14 tests passed; Vitest duration 0.965 s, wrapper shard time 1.91 s. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available for this head.
- Negative control: changing the REAL tag to the INTEGER tag passes the prior test cases, but fails with the new variant (14 distinct hashes where 15 are required). Restoring the encoder makes all 14 tests pass. No mutation remains in the published source.
- Owning infra-test typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The lint wrapper emitted its required SDK declarations. Initial manually selected infra/boundary configs collected no tests; the repository planner correctly selected `unit-fast`.
- Fresh independent Native Auto Review (OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol), local mode against `ca2bf94f193b583f1efa810e648d5fbf628e7231`, covered all 12 PR files and supplied full owner contracts at **P0–P2** severity and returned `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings. The reviewed tree `9c8edb9afc99610fafec86eb1a51d9fdb3609585` matches published head `c3934f6e218ff739f8894af1805a29a73e286b10`. This was source review, not an independent test rerun or approval of the documented downgrade limit.

Full hosted CI has not run for this head: [CI run 43732643393](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43732643393) reports **“This workflow is awaiting approval from a maintainer in #197777”** (Action required). The security/dependency review jobs passed; that does not establish a passing CI gate. The local checks above are not an aggregate CI pass.

The supplied archive additionally records 17 PostgreSQL conformance files / 116 tests passing and 12 paired BLOB-heavy backup runs, with export median 73.25 s → 56.8 s, the branch faster in 11/12 pairs and verification passing 24/24. Those are historical measurements of archived candidate `816e8256fbf6290c991dfb2fe834dfbd2b5eab24` against `8f3d2597a2dd33b021602849d4e87213e2189ab8`; they were inspected, not rerun here. The original upgrade and performance evidence below is retained as historical author-reported proof.

Upgrade from published 2026.11.3, run locally on macOS arm64 with PostgreSQL 17.11:

- Installed `openclaw@2026.11.3` from npm (build `847611d`) into an isolated prefix and state directory. Through a running 2026.11.3 Gateway, created a board with settings (name, description with non-ASCII text, icon, color), five cards with labels, priorities, comments, a status change and a 16418-byte binary attachment. Moved Workboard to PostgreSQL with the 2026.11.3 `openclaw database port --to postgres`, then added a second board and five more cards on PostgreSQL. `openclaw backup create --verify` succeeded. Its Workboard manifest has profile `user-backup`, schema 3 and no `digest` field.
- Switched the same state directory and database to this build (`899504c`). `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` passed and kept the 2026.11.1 Workboard-only PostgreSQL setting. The Gateway served both boards and all ten cards with their comments and attachments. A per-table fingerprint (row count and MD5 of every row) of all 17 Workboard tables matched the pre-upgrade fingerprint. The same build then wrote a third board with cards and an attachment.
- Pre-upgrade backup restored with this build: `openclaw backup verify` and `openclaw backup restore` accept the 2026.11.3 archive. A 2026.11.3 archive has no PostgreSQL capsule inventory, so archive restore extracts the capsule as files and says so (behavior this PR does not touch). Restoring that extracted 2026.11.3 capsule by calling this build's matched-export restore functions directly produced a namespace whose 17 table fingerprints, board settings and attachment SHA-256 values are identical to the pre-upgrade store. A fresh installation of this build pointed at the restored anchor served the restored boards, cards, labels and the 16418-byte attachment.
- Exact capture written by 2026.11.3: on a second 2026.11.3 installation, interrupted `openclaw database port --to sqlite` after it had written its exact PostgreSQL capture (profile `exact`, no `digest`). This build's matched-export restore functions, called directly, verified and restored that capture, so exact verification on the legacy JSON digest passed. (This build's `database port --resume` and `--rollback` cannot take over that interrupted port for an unrelated reason: under the 2026.11.1 Workboard-only setting they ask for `--family`, which they also reject.) The restored rows match that installation's fingerprint. The same capture relabelled `typed-v1` is refused with `Exact PostgreSQL export verification differs from its manifest.` No anchor is written and no namespace is left behind.
- New backup with this build: `openclaw backup create --verify` writes `digest: "typed-v1"` and Workboard schema 4. `openclaw backup restore` of that archive imported a namespace identical to the live store, table by table.
- 2026.11.3 against a manifest from this build: its packaged reader refuses the Workboard capsule with `unrecognized_keys: digest`, writes no anchor and creates no namespace. 2026.11.3 `backup verify` of the whole archive passes, and its `backup restore` extracts files only. Pointed at the upgraded state directory, it refuses to start the restore because of the state schema.

Unit and integration tests:

- SQLite digest tests through `inspectDatabasePort`: 15 single-row variants hash differently (`["a","b"]` vs `["ab",""]` vs `["ab",null]`, null vs empty text vs empty BLOB, `1` as integer, text and BLOB vs `1.5`, an integer with the same eight payload bytes as REAL `1.5`, one changed byte in a 70 KB BLOB, swapped values, one vs two rows), and reordered schema columns change the digest. The legacy digest of a fixed table matches the value the unpatched build computes. The typed digest matches an independent implementation of the format.
- The typed encoder matches an independent unbuffered reference encoder for values of 65527 to 65545 bytes (around the 64 KiB scratch buffer), 20,000 small rows spanning many buffer flushes, multibyte UTF-8, and empty text vs empty BLOB. Integers outside 64 bits are refused.
- Port `verify` accepts a receipt in the old format and refuses both old and new receipts after a row changes. Port staging against a source proof in the old format succeeds, records an old-format receipt that then verifies, resumes, and still refuses changed rows (this staging test fails on the previous revision).
- PostgreSQL round trip: an exact export rewritten to the old format restores; new digests without the id are refused.
- PostgreSQL conformance on PostgreSQL 17.11 (CI extensions), 17 files and 103 tests: port provider, state, agent and logbook ports, archive restore, Git backup with and without secret exclusion, port command (integration, mixed, recovery, refusals), backup, backup schema capture, update candidate state and update preflight. Changed-file typecheck, lint and format pass.
- Same-server captures (#196236): a capture kept in a PostgreSQL schema is copied on the server and then hashed from the source in the same snapshot, now with the typed digest. Its manifest records `digest: "typed-v1"` (the schema capture test now compares the whole verification, digest included), and restore checks a schema capture without the id on the old JSON digest, like any other exact capture.

Performance, state store ported to PostgreSQL 17 with 1024 rows of 1 MiB BLOBs, `openclaw backup create`, PostgreSQL export phase (`capturePostgresBackup`):

| build | run 1 | run 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 24.9 s | 23.6 s |
| after | 18.2 s | 17.9 s |

Row copy and verification inside it (`materializeDatabasePort`): 21.1 s / 20.2 s before, 14.7 s / 14.5 s after. The exact capture used by update rollback took 22.6 s before and 16.8 s after (measured before the rebase, as a file capture). Small rows are not slower: one million rows of text, integer, null and real hash in 5.1 to 5.8 s, against 5.8 to 9.6 s before, on a loaded machine.

## Contributor credit

Original implementation and supplied regression case: @etzelm.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ac30b821-5414-4259-953b-dc9fccc11b0b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/ee7a435f-b987-48e5-a41d-2bde664f2793)

prs.title: fix: stop native completion retirement from retrying forever
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #200892.

When a completed native Codex child can no longer retire its persisted assignment, the monitor currently retries the retirement write every 15 seconds forever. This bounds the retirement phase with the existing retry budget, then stops the in-memory monitor while preserving the unresolved assignment for Doctor repair.

## User impact

- persistent retirement-write failures stop producing an unbounded retry/log loop
- the completion result is still delivered at most once
- unresolved persisted assignment state remains available for diagnosis and repair
- transient retirement failures continue to retry and can still complete cleanup

## Implementation

- reset the existing completion-delivery attempt counter when entering the retirement phase, giving that mutually exclusive phase its own bounded budget
- charge every retirement retry against that budget
- unregister the in-memory child after persistent retirement exhaustion; the assignment-settlement guard retains the unresolved persisted locator
- add a regression that rejects every retirement write and proves finite termination, single result delivery, retained assignment state, and no transcript/system-note delivery

## Evidence

Candidate head: `17a80c2183d20765634d94b33eda7782ac1fc090`

- Regression first failed on base `8f321bcc7e14569939ee9648a9663f3927816f2c` because a retry timer remained after the bounded window.
- 63 focused assertions passed across `native-subagent-inventory.test.ts`, `native-subagent-completion-delivery.contention.test.ts`, and `native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts`.
- Extension source and extension-test typechecks passed.
- Focused oxlint passed for both changed files.
- Plugin boundary report, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent local P0-P2 autoreview reported no actionable findings (confidence 0.9).

The broader changed-lane wrapper completed its selected guards and Doctor tests, then exceeded the local 10-minute wrapper budget at the plugin-boundary phase; that boundary command passed separately. No live Gateway or live Slack configuration was changed for this proof.

## Codex contract check

I inspected `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs`. They expose thread/turn completion receipts and collaboration state, but no host assignment-retirement acknowledgement. The bounded retirement lifecycle therefore remains owned by the OpenClaw monitor.

## Scope

This does not delete unresolved assignment state, change delivery routing, resend completion output, or alter live authentication/channel configuration.

prs.title: fix: finish replies to subagent results after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart can interrupt a requester after it has read a subagent result but before it answers. Crash recovery could leave that requester parked indefinitely, so the result was present in its conversation but the user never received the final reply.

## User Impact

The Gateway resumes that interrupted requester turn from its saved conversation. Completion inputs are delivered once, and intentional Stop and current authority checks still apply. No protocol, schema, or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup classified any retained requester-settle cohort as yield-waiting, including an interrupted execution whose exact settle input was already committed ([`session-restart-resume.ts:511` on base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8f16d1323f8fac4dec49d97267f5c11edf30ef8c/src/gateway/session-restart-resume.ts#L511)). The registry's consumed-input check ran only after dispatch ([`subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts:648` on base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8f16d1323f8fac4dec49d97267f5c11edf30ef8c/src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts#L648)), allowing an unnecessary resubmission to conflict with the committed input.

Gateway restart-resume now recognizes the committed input for the interrupted settle run and uses the existing restart admission and continuation path. The registry settles consumed receipts before dispatch. This preserves delivered-on-commit semantics: the registry owns unconsumed results, while the Gateway owns completing a requester turn that already consumed its input. No new state, continuation owner, replay path, or authority fallback is added; queued-input ordering and store/cancellation guards remain intact.

The existing graceful-shutdown checkpoint now permits `delivered`, as required by #200249. The final assertions still require `HUB_RECEIVED_RESTART_COMPLETION`, exactly one completion input, exactly one final reply, and no duplicate after a second restart. Self-simplification retained the existing owners and receipts. The test budget is raised from zero to exactly **+15 net lines** to extend an existing parked-requester case with a real committed settle input; no additional Gateway boot or test case is added. An ended execution without a terminal status remains deliberately yielded, preserving registry ownership of its wait.

## Evidence

On base `8f16d1323f8fac4dec49d97267f5c11edf30ef8c`, after correcting that checkpoint, the focused command reports **1 failed, 1 passed, 8 skipped**: `(announcing-crash)` misses `HUB_RECEIVED_RESTART_COMPLETION`; graceful `(announcing)` passes. The earlier uncorrected cases both failed on the base and head of #200873, as recorded there.

```sh
pnpm test test/gateway-subagent-completion-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'restart \(announcing(-crash)?\)'
# Base: Tests 1 failed | 1 passed | 8 skipped (10)

pnpm test test/gateway-subagent-completion-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Fix: Tests 10 passed (10), 335.63s Vitest
```

This proof runs isolated real Gateway processes, a synthetic local model endpoint, and native SQLite custody across graceful shutdown, process crashes, and subsequent restarts. It includes public/private announcing, nested, captured, busy, retrying, unmarked, and stale-settle cases.

All **89 focused tests** pass across restart, requester dispatch, and custody suites, including real Stop, authority refusal, queued inputs, and deliberate yield. The extended committed-input yield case first failed against the initial candidate (**1 failed, 9 skipped**) and then passed with the lifecycle distinction. Core and affected Gateway/root-test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, line-cap and identity ratchets, and the final `pnpm build` pass. Fresh independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.

The local broad sibling command completed four shards with **842 passed** before its remaining agents-support shard was stopped under shared-host contention; that incomplete shard is not claimed as passing. Exact-head PR CI supplies the remaining broad proof.

Related: #200873, #200823, #200249.

## Inherited CI failures

[CI run 44221908417](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44221908417) fails only `checks-node-changed-3` and its aggregate gate. Its two Workshop learning cases reproduce on both this PR and the exact CI main baseline `e93a426be3297ed947f54b4e15c87827225b6c90` (**2 failed** on each): the review request exceeds the old 64 KiB expectation, and the learned-skill notice is absent. The first expectation predates #200545, which intentionally removed that clamp; the notice failure is also inherited. The failing tests and inspected Workshop/fork source inputs are unchanged in the tested merge. Security and all other jobs pass. These failures remain recorded as failures and use the native inherited-failure landing exception.

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/gateway-workshop-learning.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'patches a learned skill|sends one bounded review request'
# PR: Tests 2 failed (2); baseline: Tests 2 failed (2)
```

prs.title: chore(ui): upgrade Control UI to stable Solid 2
prs.body:
Maintainer request: [@vincent_koc on the Solid 2.0 announcement](https://x.com/vincent_koc/status/2122877487961293120).

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's Control UI and bundled plugin views still pin Solid 2's rc.18 toolchain after the stable release. This moves the existing Solid 2 integration to the stable runtime and compiler together, rather than introducing another UI framework or mixing incompatible versions.

## User Impact

The Control UI and its eight Solid-dependent bundled plugins use Solid 2.0.0. No intentional interface or application-state behavior changes, configuration migration, or user action are required. This upgrades an existing release-candidate integration; it does not introduce server functions or replace Gateway-owned state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Checked the [official release announcement](https://www.solidjs.com/blog/solid-2-0-the-long-hold/), [migration guidance](https://docs.solidjs.com/migration/from-solid-1/), published package contracts, and direct/transitive consumers. Runtime, renderer, signals and compiler move to 2.0.0; the Vite plugin moves to 3.0.1. Testing Library stays at the compatible 1.0.0-rc.2: its latest tag still targets Solid 1.

Both local Solid retention fixes are present upstream and pass the original browser probes without patches, so their files, registrations and documentation are removed. The heap census follows stable's production owner slots. Seroval resolves to 1.8.0 under the existing release-age gate; obsolete 1.7.0 exceptions are removed. No new patch, override, compatibility layer or budget exception is added.

## Evidence

- **47 focused tests passed:** 12 real Chromium retention cases across production/development/observe, 25 bridge/projection/mount integration tests, and 10 package-guard/heap-analyzer tests.
- The updated heap fixture fails against the old analyzer with “Solid owner fingerprint matched no nodes,” then passes with the fix. A real Chromium production heap independently reports two owners: one live, one disposed, zero unknown states.
- Production UI build, UI typecheck, tooling-test typecheck, targeted lint/format, package patch guard, frozen-lockfile install and diff checks passed. No new Solid peer conflicts.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local candidate against base 3460f61786013ff711efbcb6ce9a91fa003a178a; scoped-clean, no actionable findings. It reviewed supplied source/diff context and relied on the reported runtime proof.
- Simplification removes both dependency patches (191 patch lines) and their duplicate registration/documentation; no application production code is added. The only TypeScript logic adjustment updates the existing heap fingerprint.

**Limitations:** full cross-browser/product E2E and hosted CI have not run locally. The successful build's report-only performance check reports CSS and chat/new boot-budget overruns; no ceilings or baselines were relaxed, and this PR does not claim those warnings are pre-existing.

<details>
<summary>Commands and test cost</summary>

- `pnpm ui:build`
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config scripts/control-ui-retention/vitest.config.ts --configLoader runner scripts/control-ui-retention/dependency-retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 12 passed, 4.13 s Vitest duration.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/solid-bridge.test.tsx ui/src/lib/reactive/projection.test.ts ui/src/test-helpers/mount-solid.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` — 25 passed, 6.38 s runner wall time.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/control-ui-retention.test.ts test/scripts/check-package-patches.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 10 passed, 4.42 s runner wall time. Changed-file durations: 0.155 s and 0.983 s; hosted CI seconds pending.
- Targeted oxlint on the three affected script modules and two changed tests; oxfmt check; `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-package-patches.mts`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; `git diff --check`.

</details>

prs.title: improve(ios): rebuild the chat transcript around the web reading model
prs.body:
## Problem

On long, tool-heavy sessions the iOS chat fell well short of the web Control UI:

- Scrolling back stopped after the first history page. `olderCursor` was never decoded, so older pages were never requested.
- Every tool call between messages was its own card. Completed turns had no "Worked for <duration>".
- Subagent spawns showed only the wrapper card: no "Launched <name>" row and no way to open the child.
- `sessions_yield` acknowledgments were hidden under "Tool details". Failed commands showed no exit code.
- Raw paths and plain `#123` appeared instead of file and PR chips.
- The header had no session title. The composer read "Message main…" (the agent id) and cut the model name.
- Assistant replies sat in cards capped at 560 pt, and iPad width depended on size classes.

## Solution

One transcript model, with the web UI as the guide:

- **Layout:** assistant replies span one reading column, and user messages keep a tinted bubble. One width rule uses the measured pane width `w`:
  - margin 16 pt, or 24 pt from 700 pt;
  - column `min(768, w − 2·margin)`;
  - user bubble 82% of the column, or 68% above 600 pt.

  This deletes `openClawAssistantBubblesInCleanChrome`, `openClawAssistantUsesReadingColumn`, the assistant card style with its seam drawing, and `readingColumnWidth` / `usesExpandedLayout` / `expandedHorizontalMargin`.
- **Container:** iOS keeps `List` (#192232).
  - Older pages load after an upward scroll within ~1200 pt of the top, and the reading position is restored after the prepend.
  - Rows are deduped by `__openclaw.id`, then `seq`.
  - "Show earlier" appears only after a failed load.
- **Tool activity:**
  - A completed turn folds into one "Worked for <d>" row (web `chat-turn-presentation.ts`).
  - Adjacent tool rows in unfolded turns become one "Ran commands, read files" disclosure.
  - Subagent launches always stay visible as "Launched <name>" rows that open the child.
  - A confirmed `sessions_yield` shows its acknowledgment.
  - Commands read "Ran <cmd>", with "Exit code N" on failure.
  - Continuation rows keep a multi-run turn together.
- **Chips:** file references and GitHub items in message bodies get chips, following the web markdown rules. PR merge state is not fetched; chips use the web's unknown-state look.
- **Chrome:**
  - the session title shows in the navigation bar;
  - the composer placeholder uses the agent identity name from `agent.identity.get`;
  - the model label is readable.
- **Reply footer:** relative time. Exact time, duration, tokens, cost, context and model sit behind a tap, like the web tooltip.

Newly decoded fields, all already sent by the Gateway, so there is no schema change: `olderCursor`, `hasMore`, `__openclaw.seq`, `recordTimestampMs`, `customType`, `continuation`, tool `exitCode`.

**References and what we didn't adopt:**
- T3 Code mobile: per-turn fold.
- opencode-mobile/opencode-mobile: prepend restore.
- Ice Cubes: `List` with re-anchoring by id.
- Not adopted: a UIKit collection-view host, a manual-only "Load earlier" button, lazy tool loading (needs a new Gateway API), and multiple timeline styles.

## Evidence (draft: more to come)

- **Real session, iPad 13" simulator:** 35 history pages, 4,414 messages, 2,199 tool calls.
  - Scrolling back reaches the first turn in about 30 swipes.
  - All 161 user messages render; the web DOM also has 161.
  - Every subagent launch is visible: 55 rows for 57 spawns.
  - The other row kinds are within a few rows of the web.
- **Replay:** feeding all 35 pages through the view model keeps every one of the 4,414 messages.
- **Scroll workload** (iPad simulator, behavior probe, 120 slow swipes each way):

  | | main (1 page) | this PR (35 pages) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Bubble body evaluations | 10.1/s | 1.6/s |
  | Long frame gaps per 1,000 frames | 58.2 | 48.8 |
  | Viewport jumps | 0 | 1 |

  These numbers predate the scroll-owner change below; prepend behavior is now measured by `prepend-no-jump`.
- **OpenClawKit (macOS `swift test`):** 2,700 of 2,705 pass. The 5 failures are timing tests under full-suite load: 2 audio-player tests that also fail on `main`, plus TLS cancellation and canonical-history tests that pass when run alone.
- **iOS unit tests (iPhone 17 simulator):** 1,117 pass. The one failure, the audio case of `managed assistant media starts its artifact load with the playback route`, also fails on `main`: since #196787 audio loads only after Play is tapped, and the test still expects an automatic load.
- **macOS:** the package and test targets build.

Still pending:
- before/after screenshots from synthetic fixtures (iPhone and iPad);
- the AdaptiveLayoutUITests matrix, including accessibility text sizes;
- device Animation Hitches and before/after phone traces (`ChatScrollPerformanceUITests`, dedicated iPhone);
- a macOS test run.

## Scroll, gesture and redraw ownership

On a phone the transcript bounced on expand/collapse, could scroll while the sidebar opened, and redrew every row on unrelated state changes. Five writers set the scroll offset independently (reader run anchor, synchronous follow, paging restore, bottom-pin `follow`, scroll commands), and two gestures (the shell's SwiftUI drag and the transcript's pan) ran at once.

- **One scroll owner:** `ChatReadingPosition` (pure policy `ChatReadingPolicy` + a UIKit adapter on the transcript's collection view) is the only code that writes the transcript offset on iOS. `ChatReaderRunAnchor.swift`, `ChatSynchronousFollow.swift`, the paging restore and the bottom-pin writer are deleted. Rules:
  - following: stay at the bottom as rows stream in;
  - reading: hold the top visible row, no write unless rows above it changed;
  - expand/collapse: the tapped header keeps its screen position;
  - older-page prepend: hold the distance from the end of the content, so `List`'s own compensation is never counted twice;
  - the transcript scroller has a directional lock, so a sideways swipe never scrolls it.
- **One drawer gesture owner:** `SidebarDrawerPanRecognizer` opens the sidebar only from a 44 pt leading-edge zone below the nav-bar row; the transcript's pan waits for it to fail. The shell's SwiftUI `DragGesture` is gone.
- **Rows redraw only on their own content:** Gateway health, link previews, the agent name and the drawer flag no longer reach every row's inputs.

**Accepted edge:** when an older page lands mid-fling, the reader's scroll in the ~2 frames where `List` changes the content is not kept (8.4–8.8 pt measured). There `List`'s compensation cannot be told apart from the reader's scroll (it can land before the content height changes); an attempt to observe the offset during that window adopted `List`'s write and jumped ~1,500 pt, so it was reverted. `prepend-no-jump` stays a `bad` case for this.

**Measurement tooling** (DEBUG, only with `--openclaw-behavior-probe`): offset-writer attribution and signposts (`ChatScrollInstrumentation`), drawer-pan marks, and four `pnpm ios:behavior` cases with gates; plus `ChatScrollPerformanceUITests` (XCTHitchMetric) for device hitch runs.

**Behavior cases** (iPhone 17 simulator, 3 samples each, same seeded 40-turn chat):

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sidebar-open-still` (edge swipe and button) | passes | passes 3/3 |
| `swipe-right-still` (40 pt drift down and up) | passes | passes 3/3 |
| `disclosure-header-still` | header and drawn rows move up to 71 pt (bottom-pin writer) | header 0 pt, rows 0.2 pt, no offset writes; now a `guard` |
| `prepend-no-jump` | no restore owner | one `ReadingPosition.prepend` write per landing; −8.4 to −8.8 pt on the first prepend, 0 on the second (gate ≤ 4 pt, stays `bad`) |
| `stream-turn` (8 samples) | passes | passes 8/8, 0 pt drawn movement |

The simulator's synthetic drags never start the transcript's own pan, so the sidebar and swipe cases pass on `main` too: they guard the fix but don't reproduce the device bug. Device hitch numbers are pending on a dedicated iPhone.

Offset writers during the prepend case, all samples: `user` (reader), `system:…UpdateCoalescingCollectionView…` (`List`), and `ReadingPosition.prepend`. No other writer.

**Streamed list items stopped re-fading.** `ChatStreamingAssistantTextBody` swapped a plain render for a `TimelineView` whenever a word reveal started or caught up between chunks. That rebuilt the subtree, and every list item in the streaming reply (each holds its own reveal state) faded in again from zero. On this branch the finished bullets blinked in 2 of 8 `stream-turn` runs (read by the screen check as a 55 pt move); `main` has the same code but didn't trigger it in 5 runs. One `TimelineView`, paused while idle, keeps the identity; 8/8 runs clean after. `stream-turn`'s early drawn window now spans three 40 pt strips, so the setup gate stops failing when the reply draws sooner.

## Impact

macOS shares `OpenClawChatUI`:
- the reply footer becomes a tap popover, matching the web;
- the QuickChat user bubble uses the tinted surface;
- the desktop column is 768.

prs.title: fix: explain failed local workspace reconciliation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When local workspace reconciliation fails and preparation retries it, the finish log says only `outcome=aborted`. Operators cannot tell a caller stop from lease loss, worker failure, or unconfirmed publication, making expensive retries difficult to diagnose.

## User Impact

Operators get a closed failure reason and the last entered apply phase on the existing finish line. Successful reconciliation and recovery behavior are unchanged; no migration or configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint owner already retains workspace authority independently of the execution caller's signal. Keep that boundary, including real ownership revocation and conflict recovery. Classify the original failure at the reconcile owner, without logging exception prose or paths, then rethrow the same exception. Unknown failures are explicitly `operation-failed`.

The production diff is +54 lines: new reason classification and phase attribution. No duplicate reconciliation path, cache, persisted field, or cancellation guard was added. Related: #200077.

## Evidence

The new integration proof leaves a real pending projection receipt, stops the checkpoint caller after real patch preparation, completes checkpoint settlement, and prepares the workspace again. Both baseline and candidate write one journal, with no second journal during preparation. The two new tests fail on main parent `4dbd70ff5fd3edf197dafdd2f4b407627ffdcc64` specifically because the abort reason is absent, and pass with this fix. Five focused tests pass, including concurrent-edit fencing, conflict preservation, and interrupted base-refresh recovery.

Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2. `pnpm check:changed` completed all stages; its only failures were three test lint findings, now fixed with the exact core lint rerun passing. Four affected tests also pass after that cleanup. Scale A/A/B completed with all content and freshness assertions passing. A1/A2 use the exact main parent above; B uses final head `eda07776b73b22b351c6c578bcd042f193d27177`. Exact-head CI [run 44220507292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44220507292) passed. ClawSweeper reviewed that head with zero findings and zero open items.

| Sample | Checkpoint wall / CPU (s) | Owner pause (s) | Allocation (MB) | Next prep wall / CPU (s) | Prep allocation (MB) | Journal bytes | Checkpoint / prep journals | Prep pause |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A1 | 231.604 / 95.435 | 231.526 | 306.495 | 6.998 / 6.678 | 8.209 | 157,626,443 | 1 / 0 | 0 |
| A2 | 125.572 / 65.119 | 125.506 | 292.765 | 5.462 / 5.122 | 10.126 | 157,626,444 | 1 / 0 | 0 |
| B | 249.629 / 177.358 | 249.552 | 295.098 | 6.838 / 6.720 | 11.284 | 157,626,444 | 1 / 0 | 0 |

The measured pair writes one journal on every arm, then zero on preparation. The pack is 151,311,089 bytes and journal JSON 6,315,268 bytes in every arm. The one-byte serialized-envelope difference is not a second mutation. Warmup, deliberate staging failure and later freshness work are outside this pair.

The candidate runtime owner emits `outcome=aborted durationMs=7729.4 abortReason=operation-failed phase=patch` for the deliberate staging failure; the retained checkpoint then finishes `outcome=applied durationMs=214899.3` after its execution caller was stopped. Main has no reason or phase on the equivalent failed finish. These are synthetic runtime owner logs, not a native CLI/VM end-to-end trace.

Fixture: Node 26.12.1, 62,000 initial files (~1.1 GiB), 22,795 incompressible 6,600-byte changes, 10,001 sessions. APFS, synthetic engine I/O, and an 8,056,832-byte agent database: this does not qualify 35 GiB database storage or native Linux/btrfs guest pauses. Both proof arms use the same private external-disk-backed APFS scratch image and identical synthetic-only temp-root routing; no temp-root change is in the PR. Logical journal bytes are not physical host writes. Allocation is main-isolate V8 cumulative allocation; CPU includes process workers but excludes external Git processes. Shared-host pressure was substantial; B CPU was higher and A/A wall times varied widely. No speedup or performance-equivalence claim is made. The change makes a retry's cause observable.

prs.title: fix: tell agents which setting hides a tool and how to add it back
prs.body:
Closes #200933

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent is on the `messaging` tool profile and needs a tool outside it, its capability check says only `messaging profile: exec, read, ...`. It does not say where that profile is set or how to add one tool back. The agent guesses, and users widen permissions or switch the whole profile to get one tool.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent that is missing a tool because of its profile can name the exact setting and the one-line fix, for example `add it to agents.entries.<agent>.tools.alsoAllow`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway's tool inventory already knows the profile's config path and the narrowest `alsoAllow` list for each excluded tool, and the Control UI shows the path. The `session_status` capability summary dropped both. It now prints them on the profile line. Deny and allowlist lines are unchanged, since their text already names the path. Tools the session never loaded keep the path but get no fix line, because a grant cannot show they would load.

Open #192971 also edits `session-status-capabilities.ts`, but only the branch where the inventory check is refused. This change only touches the reason lines of a successful check. The two do not overlap in behavior and merge cleanly (`git merge-tree`, no conflicts).

## Evidence

- New regression test in `session-status-capabilities.test.ts`: fails on main, passes on the committed head `04f7ee0c9f3`, and fails again with the fix reverted.
- The existing `tools-effective-inventory.policy.test.ts` suite (18 tests) still passes on the committed head.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 7f395779d12` (current main) on `04f7ee0c9f3`: passed.
- Real Gateway run on Linux, before and after, below.
- Local ClawSweeper review (local range, base `f3638439b92`, head `04f7ee0c9f3`, full diff): complete, patch correct, no findings, security cleared. Rating: patch A, proof D, overall D. That run saw only the commit, not the Gateway output below.

### Runtime output

Setup: a real Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`, built from source) with one agent, `agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile = "messaging"`, isolated state and a loopback port. A session is created with `openclaw gateway call sessions.create`, then `session_status` with `capabilities: true` is called through `POST /tools/invoke`. No model call and no channel. Linux arm64, Node 24.22.1.

**Before, on main `f3638439b92`**

```text
Not available in this session:
- messaging profile: agents_list, agents_wait, apply_patch, automations, browser, canvas, code_execution, computer, create_goal, dashboard, dismiss_task, edit, exec, get_goal, github_identity_status, github_publish, image_generate, ls, memory_get, memory_search, mobile_ui, music_generate, nodes, openclaw, pdf, plugins, portal, process, progress_card, read, screen, show_widget, skill_library, skill_workshop, skills_read, skills_search, suggest_task, terminal, transcripts, tts, update_goal, video_generate, view_image, web_fetch, web_search, write, x_search
```

The profile line names no setting and no fix.

**After, on this branch `04f7ee0c9f3`**

```text
Not available in this session:
- messaging profile (agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile): browser, canvas, code_execution, dismiss_task, image_generate, memory_get, memory_search, music_generate, pdf, progress_card, screen, show_widget, skill_library, skill_workshop, skills_read, skills_search, suggest_task, video_generate, view_image, web_search, x_search
- messaging profile (agents.entries.assistant.tools.profile); to allow one, add it to agents.entries.assistant.tools.alsoAllow: agents_list, agents_wait, apply_patch, automations, computer, create_goal, dashboard, edit, exec, get_goal, github_identity_status, github_publish, ls, mobile_ui, nodes, openclaw, plugins, portal, process, read, terminal, transcripts, tts, update_goal, web_fetch, write
```

**After, with the printed fix applied (`alsoAllow: ["exec"]`)**

```text
Available tools: ask_user, conversations_list, conversations_send, conversations_turn, exec, gateway, message, presence, secrets, session_status, sessions, sessions_create, sessions_history, sessions_list, sessions_search, sessions_send, sessions_spawn, sessions_yield, subagents, theme
```

The Gateway log for the same request shows the cause: `tool policy removed 26 tool(s) via tools.profile (messaging): agents_list, ..., exec, ..., write`. Those are the tools that get the `alsoAllow` line. Tools the session never built (the first line) keep only the path.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

Gateway proof, one run per state: start `openclaw gateway run --port 18789 --allow-unconfigured` with the config above, then `openclaw gateway call sessions.create --json --params '{"agentId":"assistant","key":"agent:assistant:main"}'`, then `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18789/tools/invoke` with `{"tool":"session_status","agentId":"assistant","sessionKey":"agent:assistant:main","args":{"capabilities":true}}` and a synthetic bearer token. The base run reverts the source change before the build. `dist` is rebuilt for each run.

Tests on the committed head: `pnpm test src/agents/tools/session-status-capabilities.test.ts src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.policy.test.ts`, 2/2 and 18/18 passed.

</details>

prs.title: fix: stop completion retries into removed worktrees
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed sub-agent results can retry forever when their requester session is bound to a removed managed worktree. Each settle wake encounters the same admission refusal and schedules another attempt.

## User Impact

A removed-worktree refusal now ends the completion batch as `permanent_failure`; the result remains readable in the child session. Removal that is still in progress continues to retry and can recover when the claim clears. Restoring a removed worktree remains an explicit user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/agents/worktrees/run-lease-store.kernel.ts:75` and `:80` previously emitted the same message for a removed/missing record and an active removal claim. An active claim can abort automatically or self-heal after remover death, so the producer split is necessary to avoid treating that transient state as permanent. The active-claim branch now says `managed worktree removal is in progress: <path>`.

`src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:61` adds an anchored match for the exact removed/missing-record message. The real `GatewayClientRequestError` preserves this message without a prefix. Previously this refusal fell through to retryable delivery, so `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts:665` kept the batch owed indefinitely. Existing permanent settlement at `:659` now handles it.

The complete production change is two lines; no new owner, helper, state, schema, protocol, config, or SDK surface is introduced. Sweep cadence, GC, restore, startup recovery, and other retry decisions are unchanged. The docs describe the distinction.

## Evidence

The new integration table exercises real direct announcement, Gateway error wrapping, classification, and settle-wake handling with synthetic requester-dispatch failures. Removed worktrees complete once without rearming or another dispatch. An in-progress removal remains pending with `nextAttemptAt`, then succeeds on retry. The lease regression also proves admission after the current removal claim aborts; the existing dead-remover self-heal case remains green.

- Red on base `08df47114b984cc47afd874e18964c21e2ff7350`: the removed settle case expected `permanent_failure` but received `retryable` (1 failed, 1 passed); the active-claim lease assertion expected the transient text but received the old removed text (1 failed).
- Green: all 228 tests across seven focused files passed using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1`: delivery-retry, delivery, direct-delivery, requester-settle-dispatch, requester-settle-wake, run-lease, and agent.worktree-race.
- The complete focused command took 328.18 seconds including cold compilation. The two new settle cases took 4 ms each; the changed active-claim test took 1.83 seconds. The existing lease suite uses real Git and worker admission, accounting for its longer runtime. PR CI completed successfully.
- Production typecheck and the selected `agents-tools`/`agents-sessions` test graphs pass. Targeted lint, format, `git diff --check`, source/max-line ratchets, and the test-line gate pass. Net test growth is 46 lines, within the 400-line allowance; no budget increase is needed.
- Proof is local and synthetic. No production server was contacted.
- Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against base `08df47114b984cc47afd874e18964c21e2ff7350` completed `scoped-clean` through P2, with no actionable findings. The committed candidate is `fe70b290f0d4b8b22a482c0c08be848ea61eb605`. Hosted Codex review of that exact head also completed without findings; ClawSweeper intake acknowledged the PR.

CI run [44221468360](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44221468360) completed successfully on the exact PR head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. The independent dependency and security review statuses also passed. The native maintainer workflow landed this exact head as `1619ecb28838309a2bf8691d98deb6145bddcc7e`. No CI rerun, head rewrite, or guard bypass was needed.

prs.title: fix: stop logging restricted skill calls as Code Mode failures
prs.body:
Related: #200907

## What Problem This Solves

Background skill reviews reuse the conversation's foreground tool definitions. When a review tries to list, search, or read installed skills, Code Mode can record a normal policy refusal as an execution failure. This makes expected restrictions look like broken reviews in Gateway logs.

## User Impact

Code Mode returns a normal result explaining which operation is unavailable and what the review can use instead. Real execution failures still report as failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Code Mode bridge checks the existing execution allowlist before looking up the installed-skill binding. A background review can legitimately have no such binding. The review's permissions, foreground schemas, and cached conversation prefix are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The embedded runner regression invokes `skills.list()`, `skills.search()`, and `skills.read()` through the real Code Mode worker with only `skill_workshop` allowed. The baseline returned `status: failed`; the revised cell completes with all three refusal messages pointing to `skill_workshop`.
- Four test files (39 tests) passed, covering the restricted runner, permitted skill access and genuine errors, tool refusal behavior, and prompt prefix stability.
- Core typecheck, changed-file lint, and formatting passed. The reproduction uses the embedded runner and Code Mode worker with a scripted tool call.

Closes #190536

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin notices can say an API “keeps working until” a date that has already passed, even though the plugin is still loaded. A [November 17 report on 2026.11.5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190536#issuecomment-6952934071) confirms the outdated notice appears on stable.

## User Impact

Dated notices show the migration date and recommend checking for a plugin update. The date remains visible without implying that OpenClaw automatically disables the plugin or removes the API on that day.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same wording in the CLI and the Control UI. The date, details link, undated notices, and plugin behavior stay the same.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Node 24, `openclaw plugins inspect sdk-compat-proof --runtime` loaded the same local fixture importing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/cli-runtime` on both builds. The baseline said “retire on Oct 1, 2026. It keeps working until then”; the fix printed “Migration date: Oct 1, 2026. Check for a plugin update.”
- The Control UI browser test used the built app in Chromium with a fixture Gateway. It verified the text comes from the structured date, the Details link remains available, and no enable/disable request is sent. The two focused test files passed all 18 tests; the browser test and i18n verification also passed.

The screenshots use the same installed-plugin row on November 18, 2026, comparing `e93a426be32` with this change.

### Clean comparison

Before

![Before: enabled plugin notice says the APIs keep working until the elapsed migration date](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91882376-4719-446a-957c-41ab30543f9e)

After

![After: enabled plugin notice displays the migration date and update advice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b66e1409-c2ef-4111-91f0-0536bb710618)

### Annotated comparison

Before

![Before: past-date availability wording highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55ad5bd4-8de8-4a0f-bc13-a9e62a9d0aef)

After

![After: date and update advice highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/909b8eb1-12e6-4f60-bee6-39a560597dcd)

Core and Control UI typechecks, changed-file lint, and formatting passed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid automatic profiler hang risk on macOS
prs.body:
Related: #181120

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic continuous CPU profiling exposes macOS Gateways to a native lock-stall risk implicated in #181120.

## User Impact

macOS users no longer need a local patch to keep the automatic CPU flight recorder off. Callback attribution, stall warnings, event-loop delay/utilization, and CPU health metrics stay enabled. The tradeoff is losing automatic trailing CPU profiles on macOS. No configuration change is required; Linux and Windows recording and explicitly requested on-demand profiling are unchanged.

This removes the automatic profiler exposure; it does not fix Apple's lock implementation or claim every Gateway hang is resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the recorder at its existing owner, before the first native profile starts. Eligible macOS processes emit one explanatory warning per monitor. There is no new configuration, dependency, timer, or fallback profiler. Recording can be reconsidered once the native interaction is demonstrated safe.

Maintainer decision requested: @vincentkoc, could you review this macOS-only safety tradeoff promptly? The reported failure leaves the Gateway unresponsive; this change removes automatic CPU profiles while preserving non-profiling diagnostics, without claiming the native OS/Node bug is fixed.

## Evidence

### November 18 local refresh — not pushed

The published head remains `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35` and currently conflicts with main. A six-file resolution is prepared against exact main `08df47114b984cc47afd874e18964c21e2ff7350`; it has **not been committed or pushed**. Prior CI/review and macOS results below do not cover this candidate.

- The recorder excludes Darwin from native profiling but retains current main's interrupted-stack path. Its selected mode is passed through the kernel worker payload, removing the observer's independent Node-version assumption. Short-stall captures, late-dispatch rejection, bounded stack credits, ongoing-stall reporting, heartbeat recovery, callback attribution and event-loop/CPU health are preserved. Linux/Windows native recording and manual profiling remain unchanged. The [main-based proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6854072945) informed the refresh; mode propagation is additionally needed on this newer base.
- Current main's Gateway test file is unchanged; the old budget-driven cleanup is not carried forward. Delta: production +15/-8, tests +91/-40, docs +11/-2. No new configuration, dependency, timer, native patch or parallel profiler.
- **Exact candidate: 49 focused tests passed, 1 Node-version skip on Linux x64 / Node 24.20.0**, using the repository wrapper (19.93 seconds). This includes real interrupted-stack and Linux futex subprocess evidence; the skipped ongoing-spin case requires Node 26. Removing only the Darwin guard makes the macOS26 regression fail at the automatic-profile result. The macOS/Windows table cases mock native APIs, not their host platforms.
- State/logging typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, six-file formatting, health-doc MDX and diff whitespace checks passed. A repeated run exposed kernel messages sharing the observer fixture's stack-count assertion; the fixture now counts stack payloads separately, with real kernel coverage retained. All focused Node suites passed after that correction.
- A pinned macOS test kit is retained in the [refresh work session](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/151bd4f2-a142-4b32-a2da-b9318e3d8637): exact-base patch, per-file manifest, SHA256SUMS, detached-worktree preparation, focused tests, and isolated Gateway instructions/harness. Patch SHA-256: `ce1f0bc01caace3c8f6baee4376a5cc8b93e25a5df5da31451cdc1372d6b7751`. Delivered ZIP bundle SHA-256: `035c49e8d318488b14848a84b868aa53a1b470c5829ab550dedddf174d9d0ff5`.
- The kit uses fresh HOME/state/config and a loopback token-protected Gateway, no channels/providers/model requests, native samples before/after one named 1.5-second block, live health, and Gateway-PID-only SIGTERM. Script syntax, current config-schema validity, actual exact-base patch application and all resulting source hashes passed. Its preload produced real named-stall and interrupted-stack evidence on Linux. **The full macOS Gateway run is assigned to the human and has not yet run.** No deployment or long-term deadlock-resolution claim is made.
- **Code-publication blocker:** independent Auto Review returned no validated report (missing response artifact, then same-route timeout). The required fresh independent-review checkpoint remains incomplete. No clean review, fresh PR CI, pushed refresh or merge is claimed.

### October 27 refresh and CI repair

- Refreshed against `main` at `7bce7a61639ae959406736876f2f0cf8cee991ce`; current PR head is `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`. Resolved the recorder-test conflict while preserving main's interval-object sampling API, 25 ms interval, and timing-attribution tests. The production macOS exclusion is unchanged.
- The newly upstream real-native-profiler test excludes actual Darwin hosts, so its Linux platform mock cannot accidentally enable the unsafe native sampler there. Mocked macOS no-start and Linux/Windows rotation coverage remain active. This is an intentional platform eligibility limit, not a suppressed failure.
- The first refreshed head `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7` failed the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40512027532/job/122216871729) with a net addition of 27 test lines. This repair removes duplicate mock layers, a forwarding fixture, and repeated lifecycle/redaction setup without dropping scenarios or assertions. All six redaction cases remain; additional cases now also check later-sample recovery and shutdown. The complete PR now has **zero net additional test lines** against the refresh base (75 added / 75 removed); production remains +7/-1. The unchanged ratchet passes locally; no ceiling, baseline, or exemption was changed.
- **Linux / Node 26.12.1: 35 focused tests passed**, including the real native-profiler block test (19 Gateway + 16 recorder; wrapper 21.54 s). The preceding test-consolidation revision passed pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 34 passed / 1 skipped because its native V8 profiling API is unavailable (wrapper 12.05 s); the only subsequent source change restores the erased TypeScript cleanup contract. Removing only the macOS guard makes the consolidated macOS no-start regression fail; restoring it passes.
- CI confirmed the [test-line ratchet passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122229495293) on `f6ac5a2bd09679ccd07b1e35a9a570feab6a8e33`, then exposed an [await-thenable lint error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122230905307). The final one-line repair restores the test table's `void | Promise<void>` cleanup contract: skill tracking drains asynchronous work, so removing `await` would be wrong. The exact CI type-aware lint configuration reproduced the error before this repair and passes afterward on all three changed TypeScript files. The gateway typecheck and all 35 Node tests were rerun successfully, and the local test-line delta remains zero.
- Both affected typecheck graphs (`state-logging`, `gateway-server`), targeted lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed on this candidate. Earlier MDX validation remains applicable to the unchanged documentation. **Current-head CI passed**: [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122254287794) succeeded for `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`, including all selected aggregate lanes, with no known-main-red waiver. The previously failing [type-aware lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122244976210) and [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122243448980) both passed. GitHub reported the PR cleanly mergeable at that October checkpoint; current conflicts are recorded above.
- Fresh independent Auto Review of the complete final local candidate against the pinned refresh base returned `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings. Its final patch pass covered all four files and explicitly checked the consolidated assertions and fixture semantics; earlier passes contained only the staged base-refresh inventory. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6362662214) reported no findings or before-merge items for `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7`; that is prior-head review evidence, not a claim it reviewed this test-only repair.
- **Proof boundary:** the macOS Gateway A/B below remains evidence for the original head, not a new macOS execution of this refreshed revision. The guard is unchanged; updated sampling and Gateway consumers were checked by the current focused suites.

### Original revision validation

- **Actual macOS Gateway A/B supplied by @Marvinthebored:** [run report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6367004169) and [pinned artifacts](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/aaf4683affe31fde5d83512918ef64610dd31133/PROOF.md) compare original head `00d27c442c5d8b8886f6e40c22b41b241f366c96` with `ded4d430df859f35599fbb4d0ef32d8dec31e3b5` on macOS 26.6.1 ARM64 / Node 26.12.1. Both isolated source-CLI Gateways reached readiness, retained named callback-stall and live event-loop health reporting after the same 1.5-second block, returned final readiness/liveness HTTP 200, and shut down cleanly with exit 0. Native samples before/after the block contain the V8 profiler thread in stock and none in patched; the patched recorder warning appears exactly once. The corrected comparison uses Gateway-PID-only SIGTERM. I inspected the harness, logs, health snapshots and complete native-sample thread inventories and verified all 40 artifact hashes against the pinned manifest; this is a review of the reporter's run, not a separate execution.
- **macOS-host red/green:** the same two suites pass 33/33 on that original head; restoring only stock recorder source gives 32 passed / 1 failed, specifically the new macOS exclusion test. These recorder tests mock native APIs; the separate Gateway A/B above supplies native-runtime evidence.
- CI: [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39935940769/job/120358914893) passed for head `00d27c442c5d8b8886f6e40c22b41b241f366c96`, with no failed or timed-out selected jobs. Native macOS runtime jobs were not selected.
- The reporter's macOS ARM64 reduction stalled with pthread read/write locks plus SIGPROF at both tested signal intervals. The no-signal rwlock control and signaled ordinary-mutex control completed. Repeated native samples showed the same blocked lock waiters.
- The new macOS regression failed before the guard and passes with it: startup, sampling, and shutdown never call the native profiler. Existing rotation/cleanup coverage now runs for both Linux and Windows runtime facts.
- **33 focused tests passed** across the recorder and Gateway event-loop health suites on Linux with Node 26.12.1. The Gateway tests preserve callback reports, health metrics, telemetry, idle sampling, and cleanup.
- Production TypeScript checking, the affected state/logging and Gateway-server test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, documentation MDX parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- **Limits:** the new successful macOS Gateway A/B supersedes the earlier readiness-timeout evidence gap. Both stock and patched complete this short scenario: it proves removal of automatic profiler exposure with working startup, health sampling and shutdown, not reproduction or repair of the original deadlock or long-term stability. Source execution with tsx does not cover a release distribution, channel/model traffic or manual profiling. Short Node port-churn controls also did not reproduce the native hang; manually requested profiling is not made safe by this change.

<details>
<summary>Original revision validation commands, cost, and broader-check gaps</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic-stall-flight-recorder.test.ts src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 33 passed; wrapper 39.19 s, including a 33.35 s cold worker build. Regression lives in existing fixtures; no new worker, server, or sleep is added.

prs.title: fix(cron): add remedy hints to scheduled read and message target errors
prs.body:
Closes #193196
Related: #154801, #126634, #150166

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: legacy cron jobs that predate scheduled tool policy fail every delegated channel read with an error that names no remedy, when their stored job has no `toolsAllow`.

## User Impact

Operators hit by this now see the recovery command in the error itself (`openclaw automations edit <jobId> --tools message`), and the automation troubleshooting page gains an entry for the exact failure signature alongside the existing inference-account ladders. The message tool's target error now names a concrete target shape (`channel:<id>` / `user:<id>`) instead of restating the requirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery is already documented in prose (`payloads.md`) and a same-style embedded-command precedent exists in `resolveCronToolsAllowExecTargetRecoveryError`; the errors were the only place the remedy was missing. Hints follow the existing `Hint:` convention in `target-errors.ts`. No gate behavior, policy, or authority decision is changed — fail-closed stays fail-closed.

## Evidence

- Both touched error strings keep their asserted prefixes; existing assertions were extended to pin the new hint text (`message-action-dispatch.registry.test.ts`, `message-tool.test.ts`).
- Targeted Vitest runs on the touched files pass locally (registry gate suite + message-tool suite); full gate CI runs on the branch.
- Production verification of the remedy (not this diff): two jobs on v2026.10.10 failed with the exact signature, recovered after `automations edit --tools message`, verified `ok` by forced runs — recorded in #193196.


## Behavior proof (patched shipped entry point, head `eef09c1e846`)

Gateway built from this branch ran as the live gateway on an Ubuntu 24.04 host with the official Discord plugin loaded; a test cron job in the legacy shape (no stored `toolsAllow`) ran isolated scheduled turns through it. Raw gateway log captures (verbatim, channel id redacted):

```
2026-11-08T18:08:18.276+00:00 [tools] message failed: GatewayClientRequestError: Error: Delegated discord:read requires current provider and account context. Hint: if this read runs from a scheduled job, reauthorize its complete tool cap, including message, from a trusted operator shell: "openclaw automations edit <jobId> --tools <tool,...>". | UNAVAILABLE
2026-11-08T18:24:44.888+00:00 [tools] message failed: BeforeToolCallFailureError: Explicit message target required for this run. Provide target/targets (and channel when needed). Hint: use a target such as "channel:<id>" or "user:<id>".
```

Both turns reported the patched hints verbatim and the first acted on them (citing the `automations edit` remedy in its run summary). Details in the proof comment (2026-11-08). Paired base-fail: the old unactionable strings on v2026.10.10 recorded in #193196 (2026-11-05).

prs.title: fix: exec refuses every command once lost launches fill the spawn broker
prs.body:
Related: #177656

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every exec fails with `Spawn broker child capacity exceeded (512); close running processes before retrying` until the Gateway restarts, once 512 commands have been lost between their launch grant and the broker's ownership receipt. On 2026.10.8 the same leak showed up as `Spawn broker request capacity exceeded` ([#177656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6629331547)): that release's `worker.ts` refused once `owned.size + starting.size + (resources?.size ?? 0)` reached 256. #166488 replaced that with the 512 owned-child cap and a separate 256 limit on pending spawns.

## User Impact

User impact: a command the Gateway loses after granting its launch no longer leaves a slot behind in the spawn broker, so a long-running Gateway keeps running exec instead of refusing every command after 512 such losses.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the service-child relay fails a command after the host has granted its launch, but before the broker's `owned` receipt arrives, the host retires the request at `owned`. The broker then transfers that command's pipes. The host's branch for requests it no longer tracks answered each transfer with `pipe-received` only. The broker forgets an owned command only once every transferred fd is drained (`forget()` in `worker.ts`). Until then the entry stays in the worker's `childAdmissions`, which `childCapacityError()` counts against `MAX_OWNED_CHILDREN = 512` (`protocol.ts`, since #166488). Nothing else drains a retired request's pipes before the broker shuts down, so the slot was gone for the life of the Gateway.

The untracked-pipe branch now also sends `output-drained` with an error for that fd. That is the same acknowledgement `BrokerChild.attachPipe` already sends for tracked requests. The helper is in `pipe.ts` because `host.ts` counts 690 lines against its 700-line `max-lines` cap (oxlint 1.89.0, blank lines and comments skipped), and the helper would take it over.

This is the leak in [KarolAdamiec's heap readings on #177656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6629331547): one `owned` entry with `openPipes=1` left per post-launch identity loss, until the broker hit its cap and exec was dead for about 9 h. The host-side `nativeInitiated` path from [an earlier comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6546377246) does not leak on main: the worker answers `launch allowed:false` with an `error` frame, which clears it (re-measured below).

## Evidence

Measured on head `eae91e923b9` and main `3855c896edd` (2026-11-09), macOS arm64. `src/process/spawn-broker/` is identical in this PR's merge base `d44c9ad927d` and in `3855c896edd`. Runtimes are stated per result. The real-broker runs are Node 26.12.1, as in a shipped Gateway. Vitest results are given under Node (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`) and under the pinned Bun 1.4.4 fork. Bun is the local default, and it is what this PR's CI node shards run (`OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY: bun-all`).

**Real broker with an injected post-grant loss.** A standalone script drives the real `SpawnBrokerHost`. The worker is a real Node process (`node --import tsx src/process/spawn-broker/worker.ts`), with real V8 IPC, really transferred stdio sockets and real `/bin/sleep 300` commands. Both the script and the worker run on Node 26.12.1, recorded from inside each process (`process.versions.bun` unset). The loss is the only injected fault. The launch callback writes the grant and then fails the host's child on the same turn, so `owned` cannot have arrived yet:

```ts
child = host.spawn("/bin/sleep", ["300"], { stdio: "pipe" }, (launch) => {
  const written = launch(); // `launch allowed:true` is written to the worker here
  child.fail(new Error("injected relay loss after launch grant"));
  return written;
});
```

Read-only taps record both ends of the IPC: a pass-through wrapper on the host's `ChildProcess.send` plus message listeners, and a `NODE_OPTIONS=--import` preload in the worker that logs what it receives and what it spawns. No broker code is patched.

| | main `3855c896edd` | this PR `eae91e923b9` |
|---|---|---|
| losses injected | 512, then loss #513 refused | 1100, none refused |
| late pipes (host no longer tracked the request) | 1536, each answered `pipe-received` only | 3300, each answered `pipe-received` + `output-drained` |
| `output-drained` received by the worker | 0 of 1536 | 3300 of 3300 |
| native exit of the lost commands | 512 of 512 exited on `SIGTERM`, 0 alive | 1100 of 1100 exited on `SIGTERM`, 0 alive |
| `/bin/sh -c 'printf exec-ok'` after the losses, and 2 s later | `Spawn broker child capacity exceeded (512); close running processes before retrying`, both times | `exit=0 stdout="exec-ok"`, both times |
| free slots (admit `sleep 300` until refused) | 0 | 512, then #513 refused at the cap |
| broker restarted | no: same pid, host generation 1 | no: same pid, host generation 1 |

The taps record each command's exit signal, not who sent it. That the SIGTERM comes from the cleanup the host retains at `owned` (`terminateLostBrokerChild`) is from reading the code; nothing else in this flow signals those commands. On both trees the host's own `requests` and `childAdmissions` are empty at every checkpoint (loss #1 and every 128th loss), so the slot that leaks on main is the worker's. When main refuses, the worker has no live command children, only tsx's esbuild service. The same script on this PR merged locally into `3855c896edd` gives the same numbers as the `eae91e923b9` column.

<details><summary>Loss #1 and the outcome on each tree (redacted terminal output; tree paths replaced with <tree>)</summary>

Excerpt: lines are verbatim except that the local Node install path is shown as `<node-v26.12.1>`; some lines are omitted. `broker live children=1` is tsx's esbuild service.

```text
== main-3855c896-r2: tree HEAD 3855c896edd83827405dfe21df89f85b1130246d
   harness runtime: execPath=<node-v26.12.1>/bin/node node=v26.12.1 bun=none
   broker worker runtime (from inside the worker): pid=32814 execPath=<node-v26.12.1>/bin/node node=v26.12.1 bun=none execArgv=["--import","file://<tree>/node_modules/.pnpm/tsx@4.23.15/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs"]
    741.4ms loss #1 timeline, request 1 (injected loss at 646.1ms):
       645.3ms host->worker prepare-spawn
       646.1ms worker->host prepared
       646.1ms host->worker launch allowed=true
       735.9ms worker->host owned pid=32828
       736.1ms worker->host pipe fd=0 (host still tracks request: false)
       736.1ms host->worker pipe-received fd=0
       736.6ms worker->host pipe fd=1 (host still tracks request: false)
       736.6ms host->worker pipe-received fd=1
       736.9ms worker->host pipe fd=2 (host still tracks request: false)
       736.9ms host->worker pipe-received fd=2
       737.0ms worker->host spawned pid=32828
       737.1ms worker->host exit code=null signal=SIGTERM
       737.1ms worker->host closed
   worker tap: {"event":"worker-received","type":"pipe-received","id":1,"fd":0}
   worker tap: {"event":"worker-received","type":"pipe-received","id":1,"fd":1}
   worker tap: {"event":"worker-received","type":"pipe-received","id":1,"fd":2}
   4331.8ms loss #512: native pid 33485 gone (kill -0 -> ESRCH); host.waitForCleanup() resolved; broker live children=1; host requests=0 host childAdmissions=0
   4373.9ms loss #513: request 513 REFUSED by the broker: "Spawn broker child capacity exceeded (512); close running processes before retrying"
   4403.8ms census over 512 injected losses:
   late pipes (arrived after the host retired the request): 1536; arrived while still tracked: 0
   host answered pipe-received + output-drained: 0; pipe-received only: 1536
```

prs.title: fix: stop stalled GitHub requests from hanging Code Mode turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Code Mode `exec` awaiting `github_publish` can remain in its `callValue` bridge until the reply watchdog stops the turn when a Gateway request never settles.

## User Impact

Stalled direct GitHub requests now return a catchable timeout after ten minutes. Publication receipts and yielding handoffs keep their existing contracts. A response timeout does not undo accepted work: inspect the existing publication before retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

On base `08df47114b98`, `src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.ts:611` awaits a direct publication without a timeout. `src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.ts:491` converts an omitted timeout to `null`, leaving the in-process wait unbounded. The same gap affects the other direct actions without an explicit limit.

Bound the whole direct request promise at the GitHub tool owner with the existing non-cancelling `waitForGatewayDispatch` helper, including preparation before handler dispatch. Reuse the existing 600,000 ms preparation budget and preserve explicit action timeouts. Yielding preparation and local-checkout publication are already direct-only; their receipts and later session resumption remain unchanged. The incident's exact action remains unknown; this fixes the reproduced missing-deadline path.

## Evidence

The regression uses real Node and QuickJS workers, the Code Mode bridge, and the subscribed tool runtime, with a Gateway request held pending. On base, both cases fail after 600,001 simulated milliseconds because `exec` still has no result. With the fix, both return the catchable Gateway timeout without another request.

- Red on `08df47114b984cc47afd874e18964c21e2ff7350`: **2 failed**, `expected undefined to match object { status: 'completed' }`.
- Green: **42 passed** across the new bridge regression, existing GitHub tool tests, and all nine handoff lifecycle cases.
- Production and agent-tool test typechecks, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm build` passes, including Code Mode workers.
- Codex autoreview, P0–P2, against the local candidate based on `08df47114b98`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewed source is committed unchanged.

New regression timing: 2.013 s test time, 25.66 s wall in the final focused run; all three focused suites took 199.79 s including worker compilation. CI timing is pending. The change adds 7 net production lines and 83 test lines, reusing the existing deadline owner without new state or a bridge-specific policy.
