prs.title: fix(state-migrations): allow OAuth dirs reached through a state-dir alias
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` is spelled through a symlink alias of the copied state directory, the legacy state migration plan refuses it as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` even though its real path is inside the snapshot. The containment check compares two lexical spellings, so a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through an alias fails closed.

Precedent: #195061 (path containment through a canonical spelling owner). That PR audited 53 files combining path resolution with containment comparison and explicitly deferred this exact wrong deny: "**`infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` OAuth-dir check.** It compares two lexical spellings, so `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` spelled through a state-dir alias is refused as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`. This is a minor wrong deny that fails closed."

Related: #195061

## Why This Change Was Made

The plan's `oauthDirOutsideSnapshot` predicate compares `callerOAuthDir` against `requestedSnapshot.stateDir` with `isPathInside`, which is purely lexical (`@openclaw/fs-safe/path`). `resolveOAuthDir` expands `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` with `resolveUserPath` (tilde + absolute, no realpath), so an alias that resolves inside the snapshot is judged outside.

The fix resolves both sides through `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` (the same helper the sibling endpoint check at `listMigrationEndpointsOutsideRoot` uses) before the containment comparison. The admission lives in `resolveSnapshotOAuthDirAdmission` in `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts`, next to the plan-env owner (`createLegacyStateMigrationPlanEnv`); `planLegacyStateMigrationsReadOnly` consumes the admission. This re-spells the OAuth dir to its real location, so an alias inside the snapshot is admitted while a genuinely external directory stays refused.

No new validator, option, config, or persistence policy. The refusal path is otherwise unchanged.

The assignment that feeds later discovery also changes: it now stores the already-resolved canonical identity rather than the raw alias spelling. Admitting a path and then handing the unverified spelling to later directory I/O would leave a window where retargeting the alias redirects reads outside the admitted snapshot. Resolving once and reusing the checked result closes that window without adding a second resolution site.

Production LOC vs base: `state-migrations.plan.ts` `+32` (new admission owner), `state-migrations.doctor.ts` `+22/-3` (net +3 physical lines; counted lines stay under the base 2805 — the file is grandfathered over its line cap and the ratchet rejects any growth, which is why the admission lives in `plan.ts`).

Classification: `behavior-completing` (completes the path-containment canonicalization that #195061 landed).

## User Impact

Operators who keep their OAuth credentials inside a symlinked state-dir alias no longer get a spurious `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` refusal from the migration plan; the read-only doctor/startup plan now recognizes the directory as snapshot-bound. Truly external OAuth directories are still refused, and the security boundary that rejects symlinked state snapshots (`captureLegacyStateSnapshotIdentity`) is untouched.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI proof (source entry, same argv as the packaged CLI)

Proven through the shipped CLI entry `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-home <h> --snapshot-config <c> --snapshot-state <s> --json` (argv tree is identical to the packaged `openclaw` binary), with a real filesystem fixture: `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials` where `alias` is a symlink to the copied state dir, and `operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json` inside it. No credentials involved.

```text
# BASE (production without the fix): the shipped CLI refuses the alias-spelled OAuth dir
$ OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{
  "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": {
    "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot",
    "message": "Configured OAuth migration directory is outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials"
  }
}

# HEAD (this fix): the shipped CLI no longer refuses it (planner proceeds to its normal
# staged-candidate identity refusal; no oauth-dir-outside-snapshot anywhere)
$ OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{
  "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": { "code": "candidate-artifact-digest-required", ... }   // planner's fixed artifact guard, unrelated to OAuth
}
```

No wrong allow — the same shipped CLI still refuses both a genuinely external OAuth dir and a **reassigned** alias (alias retargeted to an outside dir). Re-verified on the current head after the refactor:

```text
# HEAD, OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof-external/operator-credentials (outside the snapshot)
{ "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot", "message": "...outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof-external/operator-credentials" } }

# HEAD, alias reassigned to point outside (/ws/proof/alias -> /ws/proof-external)
{ "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot", "message": "...outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials" } }
```

### Directory I/O confinement after admission (alias retargeted)

The admitted plan must not leave later discovery reading through the alias spelling: retargeting the alias afterwards would redirect directory I/O outside the snapshot. The plan records the OAuth source in the `channel-pairing` step, so that step is the readback boundary.

Same fixture (alias `.../alias` -> `.../state`, `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=.../alias/operator-credentials`), same shipped CLI, only the assignment under test differs:

```text
# BASE (assignment keeps the raw alias spelling)
channel-pairing source: /ws/proof2/alias/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json

# HEAD (assignment stores the resolved canonical identity)
channel-pairing source: /ws/proof2/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json
```

Re-verified on the current head: `channel-pairing` source is the canonical `/ws/proof2/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json`. BASE resolves through the alias for the containment check but then re-spells the env var with the alias, so a retarget after admission moves the recorded source outside the snapshot. HEAD records the checked canonical location, so the same retarget cannot change where the admitted plan reads.

### Retarget between admission and directory I/O (same run)

The two runs above retarget the alias between invocations. The stricter case retargets *inside one plan run*, after the containment check admits the directory and before `detectLegacyChannelPairingState` enumerates it.

Instrumentation is a `--import` preload on the shipped entry, hooking `fs.readdirSync`: when the OAuth directory is first enumerated, it repoints the alias to an outside directory and then performs the read, tracing the actual path. The outside directory holds `discord-pairing.json`, which the snapshot copy does not, so any external read shows up in the plan itself.

```text
# BASE trace
RETARGET before readdir of /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials
RETARGETED /ws/rt/alias -> /ws/rt/outside
READDIR /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials          <- reads outside the snapshot
plan refs: /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials/{telegram,discord}-pairing.json

# HEAD trace
READDIR /ws/rt/state/operator-credentials          <- reads the admitted snapshot dir
plan refs: /ws/rt/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json
external-only "discord-pairing" occurrences in plan: 0
```

On BASE the retarget lands, the plan enumerates through the alias and picks up the external-only `discord-pairing.json`. On HEAD the alias spelling never reaches the directory read: the admitted plan reads the canonical snapshot directory and the external-only file never appears.

Reproduce: `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --import <preload> src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-home <h> --snapshot-config <c> --snapshot-state <s> --json`, with `alias` a symlink to the copied state dir and the preload retargeting it on the first `readdirSync` of the OAuth directory.

The regression test `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias` asserts exactly this: on the base it fails on the canonical path mismatch (it previously asserted the alias spelling), on this head it passes.

Red (base) / green (head) / external-rejection (head) all captured on the same fixture and CLI. Current head: `37dec884e1cb` — `state-migrations.plan.ts` sha256 `b99eae1f52f0e978fe42fc5cab12fe0ef4fc357523547d701dc7d2ba9979a697`, `state-migrations.doctor.ts` sha256 `3c5c11494159520e8b3cd04c083c0e433a20d265324aa4ea530d5b34a571cac1`.

### RED -> GREEN

The alias case is covered by a new regression test `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias` in `src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.refusal.test.ts`. On the base with production WITHOUT the fix and the test WITH the alias case, the test fails with `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`; on this head it passes.

- Baseline (RED) SHA: `cdcef6c25f75fd7e2e2ddea93636a0ff629ce45a` (the branch's original base) + alias regression test → test FAILs. `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` and `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts` are unchanged between that base and current `main` (`3e9d22d51026`), so the RED verdict still holds on current main.
- Head (GREEN) SHA: `37dec884e1cb` (this branch) + alias regression test → test PASSes
- Production entry: `planLegacyStateMigrationsReadOnly` in `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts`; admission owner: `resolveSnapshotOAuthDirAdmission` in `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts`
- Decision surface: `oauthDirOutsideSnapshot` / `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR`
- Recorder/readback boundary: plan `refusal.code` and `channel-pairing` step `source`

```text
# RED (base cdcef6c25f + alias test): plan refuses the alias-spelled OAuth dir
FAIL: preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias
  AssertionError: oauth-dir-outside-snapshot refusal present

# GREEN (head 37dec884e1cb + alias test): plan admits the alias-spelled OAuth dir
PASS: preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias
```

### Legal control (no over-broadening)

- `refuses an OAuth migration directory outside the copied state without inspecting it` — still PASSes (external dir kept refused)
- Retargeted-alias control: after the alias is repointed outside, the shipped CLI still refuses with `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` (see above)
- `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory in the read-only plan` — still PASSes (direct inside path unchanged)
- Security boundary `rejects a symlinked state snapshot before migration detection` — unchanged, untouched code

### Latest-stable upgrade run (published-driver × candidate)

The upgrade cell uses the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` npm package (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)`, dist-tag `latest`) installed in an isolated prefix against a **real state it produced itself** (`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` in a clean `HOME`): config `openclaw.json`, state `openclaw.sqlite` (+wal/shm/seal), plus a synthetic `operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json` (stub `{"version":1,"requests":[]}` — no real credentials anywhere). The state is copied to a snapshot (`--snapshot-home/--snapshot-config/--snapshot-state`), `alias -> snap/state`, and `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials`. Same snapshot for both cells.

```text
# PUBLISHED DRIVER (openclaw@2026.11.3, the real latest-stable CLI) — reproduces the bug
$ HOME=<snap-home> OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials openclaw update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{ "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot",
               "message": "Configured OAuth migration directory is outside the copied state snapshot: /tmp/oc-upgrade/alias/operator-credentials" } }

# CANDIDATE (head 37dec884e1cb, source entry, identical argv) — OAuth admission passes
$ HOME=<snap-home> OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{ "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": { "code": "candidate-artifact-digest-required",
               "message": "Candidate artifact content identity must be supplied by the staged-candidate owner." } }
  oauth-dir-outside occurrences: 0
  channel-pairing source: /tmp/oc-upgrade/snap/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json   <- canonical, not the alias
  snapshot digests: configDigest sha256:df51e382…, stateDigest sha256:06817eca…
```

`candidate-artifact-digest-required` is this diagnostic command's by-design terminal refusal (see `update-command-migration-plan.ts`: "This diagnostic command cannot bind candidate bytes, so the planner returns a closed artifact-identity refusal"); it fires **after** the OAuth admission, so the cell shows exactly the boundary under change: the published driver refuses at `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`, the candidate passes it and records the canonical discovery path.

Equivalence check — the same snapshot run with a directly spelled `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<snap>/state/operator-credentials` produces a **byte-identical plan JSON** to the alias-spelled run (steps, digests, refusal, warnings all equal), so the alias spelling is admitted on equal footing with the direct spelling.

**Settings and data remain intact:**

- 6-file sha256 manifest of the snapshot is identical before and after all four runs (1 published-driver + 3 candidate) — the plan never writes.
- Original config bytes unchanged: `sha256 a91d2ac9b4b6…` for both the original `HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json` and the snapshot copy taken before any plan run.
- Published stable re-opens the original state after the runs: `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite validate --json` → exit 0, `issues: 0`; `openclaw doctor --lint --json` findings are only environmental fixture facts (gateway never started in this fixture: auth off, `gateway.mode` unset; host `proc-safe` native check), no config/state corruption.
- Sensitive values: the fixture is fully synthetic; evidence carries only paths and digests, no credentials.

**Gap named:** this cell runs the upgrade's copied-state planning stage (the surface ClawSweeper's item cites: `update-command-migration-plan.ts:29`) from source entries; a full `openclaw update` install-switch was not run because the candidate is an unpublished branch (no published artifact to switch to), and the fixture gateway was never started (integrity proven by manifest + stable validation instead).

### Verification

Current head `37dec884e1cb` (rebased onto current `main` `3e9d22d51026`), all re-run after the line-cap refactor:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.refusal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 23/23 pass.

- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Not tested locally: `tsgo:core` (the pinned `tsrs` native binary needs GLIBC 2.34; this host's libc is older — environment limitation, not a code verdict) and the full repository suite. PR CI covers both.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC vs base: `state-migrations.plan.ts` `+32`; `state-migrations.doctor.ts` `+22/-3`; Test LOC: `+28`.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` (same helper as the sibling endpoint check) and `isPathInside`; no new validator or resolution primitive.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none beyond admitting alias-spelled snapshot-bound OAuth dirs (the intended fix); external dirs and symlinked-snapshot defenses unchanged.

`src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` is grandfathered over its line cap (2805 counted lines, cap 700), and the checks-fast-baseline-ratchets line-cap job rejects **any** growth on such files (`allowed = max(cap, base count)`). prs.title: improve(agents): name the child's runtime and credential on spawn receipts
prs.body:
Related: #191323

## Decision needed

**Question:** should accepted native and local visible spawn receipts expose `resolvedRuntime`, `resolvedAuth` and `resolvedAuthProfile` for the primary model?

| Option | What ships | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| A. Approve (recommended) | all three optional fields | none beyond the known limits below |
| B. Approve narrower | `resolvedRuntime` and `resolvedAuth` only | no field names a profile; two API-key profiles cannot be told apart |
| C. Decline | nothing | orchestrators keep calling `session_status` on each child after it starts, which is after the first billed turn |

**Recommended answer: A.** The fields are descriptive only: they never change admission, routing or billing, an evaluation failure reports `unknown` and the spawn proceeds, and they come from the same credential owner that `session_status` and `models.list` already show, with personal account ids masked the same way.

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_spawn` receipts do not say whether a child bills through an API key or a subscription login, so an orchestrating agent cannot notice when a config change moves its subagents to API billing.

## User Impact

User impact: accepted native-subagent and local visible-session spawn receipts now say which runtime and credential the child uses, so an agent can see an API-key route before it fans out. The new fields are `resolvedRuntime`, `resolvedAuth` (`api-key`, `oauth`, `token`, `native`, `unavailable`, or `unknown`), and `resolvedAuthProfile` (`personal account` for personal profiles). They describe the primary model at spawn time; the run re-resolves credentials and may use a configured fallback. Cloud-placed visible sessions, ACP spawns, and the `subagent_spawned` hook are unchanged. Existing fields are unchanged.

Result contract (additive, optional, no behavior change):

| Field | Values | When present |
|---|---|---|
| `resolvedRuntime` | runtime id, for example `openclaw`, `claude-cli`, `codex` | accepted native-subagent and local visible-session spawns |
| `resolvedAuth` | `api-key`, `oauth`, `token`, `native` (a CLI runtime's own login, such as the Claude CLI's), `unavailable`, `unknown` | with `resolvedRuntime` |
| `resolvedAuthProfile` | auth profile id, or `personal account` | when a profile supplies the credential |

Clients that ignore unknown fields need no change.

Known limits if approved, all documented in `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md`: the snapshot covers the primary model only, not a fallback the run later takes; a credential that changes between spawn and run is not reflected; before the Gateway publishes its prepared model facts (for example right after startup), a CLI or harness child whose credential cannot be seen reads `unknown`; `native` does not tell a Claude CLI signed in with an API key, an `apiKeyHelper`, or a third-party provider login apart from a claude.ai subscription login, because the Claude CLI discovery reports one mode for every login method (`session_status` shows `native (claude-cli)` for all of them).

## Why This Change Was Made

The receipt already echoes model facts from the spawn plan. The plan now also asks the existing owners for the runtime and the credential:

- Runtime: CLI backend first, then harness selection with the model's transport (`api` and `baseUrl` from the published catalog, then authored config), in execution mode, the same order and fallback the run uses.
- Credential: when the Gateway has published its prepared model facts, the same prepared decision owner that `session_status` and `models.list` use, so native logins, synthetic auth refs, native-command and plugin-owned auth count exactly as they do there. The kind is read in `session_status` order. A harness login that names its kind reports it: the Codex plugin reads `codex login status`, so a Codex child on an OpenAI API key reads `api-key` and one on a ChatGPT login reads `oauth`. A CLI backend's own login reads `native`, which is how `session_status` labels it; the Claude CLI discovery reports one fixed mode for every login method, so that mode says nothing about the kind.
- Without published facts, the runtime-aware evaluator over configured profiles and environment credentials. A runtime's own login is invisible there, so a non-`openclaw` child it cannot find a credential for reads `unknown`, not `unavailable`.

It never starts discovery and adds no policy or config. Like `session_status`, it masks personal account ids and ignores externally synced CLI profiles. The fields are display-only: an evaluation failure logs a warning, reports `unknown`, and never fails the spawn.

## Evidence

Re-checked on this head merged into `main` 2e13c52c97bb (clean merge, same 9 files): the 102 tests in 7 files below, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:architecture` (0 import cycles), `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` (test lines OK), `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass. The traces and cost numbers below were taken on the same code merged into `main` 4c4c87301111; since then the branch only merged `main` and changed docs and a code comment.

- Real seam for the Codex finding, isolated Gateway, `POST /tools/invoke sessions_spawn`, one sitting:
  - Setup: Codex CLI 0.167.0, isolated OpenClaw state and OS home, fixture Gateway token, Codex plugin with `appServer.homeScope: "user"`, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` pinned to `agentRuntime: codex`, no `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment, no auth profile. Two fixture Codex logins in the isolated home: a fake API key (`codex login status`: `API key configured - sk-fixtu***00000`) and a fake ChatGPT login (`Logged in using ChatGPT`). The Codex app-server talks to a loopback HTTPS stand-in for the ChatGPT backend that answers only workspace routing; all other outbound traffic goes to a dead proxy, so no provider is reached. `gpt-5.4` is not in the catalog the Codex app-server lists, so admission rejects it; `gpt-6.1-sol` takes the same provider, harness and credential path.

    ```text
    login     before (0527409)   this head   child session_status
    API key   (not run)          api-key     Auth: api-key (codex)
    ChatGPT   unavailable        oauth       Auth: oauth (codex)
    resolvedRuntime is "codex" in every run; Runtime: OpenAI Codex
    ```
    Before, the evaluator lacked the synthetic auth facts. Supplying them alone would report `native` for every Codex login and hide the API-key login, so this head also reads the kind first, like `session_status`.
- API-key and Claude CLI receipts, isolated Gateway with a fixture API-key model (config key, closed loopback baseUrl) and no Anthropic API key in the environment. BEFORE is current `main`, AFTER is this head merged into it:
  - Fixture API-key model: BEFORE `resolvedModel`, `resolvedProvider`, `modelApplied` only. AFTER adds `"resolvedRuntime": "openclaw", "resolvedAuth": "api-key"`.
  - Local visible session spawned from a `sessions.create` parent, same fixture model (redacted excerpt):

    ```text
    BEFORE  {"status": "accepted", "mode": "run", "cleanup": "keep", "publicRead": false, "owner": {"type": "agent", "id": "main"}}
    AFTER   {"status": "accepted", "mode": "run", "cleanup": "keep", "publicRead": false,
             "resolvedRuntime": "openclaw", "resolvedAuth": "api-key", "owner": {"type": "agent", "id": "main"}}
    child session_status (both): Auth: api-key (models.json) | Runtime: OpenClaw Default
    ```
  - `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` pinned to `claude-cli` with the host's real claude.ai login and no auth profile (one tiny subscription turn, this head): receipt `"resolvedRuntime": "claude-cli", "resolvedAuth": "native"`; the child's `session_status` says `Auth: native (claude-cli)`, `Runtime: Claude CLI`; no `provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages` transport line.
- Regression tests:
  - Through the real prepared decision owner and evaluator: a registered Codex harness signed in with an API key reports `api-key`, with a ChatGPT login `oauth`, and with no login `unavailable`; a prepared Claude CLI login reports `native`, and none `unavailable`. With no published owner, a Claude CLI child reads `unknown`. The mapping table adds a Codex `api_key` runtime login (`api-key`) and a CLI-backend login with a fixed mode (`native`). On the previous head 4 of 19 fail: both Codex signed-in cases and the table row (`native`), and the no-owner case (`unavailable`).
  - A harness selected only by a catalog-supplied transport (`api: "openai-responses"`, no api in config) is reported as the receipt runtime.
  - The child-plan receipt for an API-key route, a direct CLI-backend model, and an OpenAI model whose Codex harness is not registered (falls back to `openclaw` like the turn does). The visible-session receipt with an API-key credential. These assert fields that `main` does not return.
  - A table test for the credential mapping, and a credential-owner failure that reports `unknown` while the spawn proceeds.
- Green: billing-route resolver (19), child-plan sandbox-CLI (5), visible receipts (9), `subagent-spawn` (33), `sessions_spawn` plan (13), cloud spawn (15), spawn hooks (8): 102 tests in 7 files.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:architecture` (0 import cycles), `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`, oxlint and oxfmt on touched files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Test lines: current `main` enforces the test-line ratchet, and this PR adds 370 net test lines, so it carries its own record, `config/test-lines-allocations/191324-spawn-receipt-billing-route.txt` (370). The lines are the real-evaluator cases above, which the review asked for, plus the native and visible receipt assertions.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local): billing-route resolver 18.0 s (51% transform: the real decision owner loads the agent model graph; the tests themselves take about 7 s), child-plan sandbox-CLI 32.5 s, visible receipts 29.2 s (the last two are existing files with a few added assertions). CI seconds will be available after the run.
- Runtime cost: `resolveSpawnBillingRoute` with a published prepared owner and a registered Codex harness, 200 warm calls: mean 0.365 ms, p95 0.480 ms per spawn (0527409: 0.276 ms mean). Measured before the credential-kind mapping change, which adds no evaluation work.
- Gaps:
  - The Codex trace uses a fixture login and a stand-in backend, so it proves the receipt and admission path, not a real Codex turn.
  - Native-command auth reads the same synthetic auth refs that the Codex case lacked and now gets them from the same owner; the mapping table covers `native-command`, but there is no real-evaluator case for it.
  - Without published prepared facts (for example right after startup), a CLI or harness child reads `unknown` rather than its credential kind.
  - A Claude CLI child reads `native` whether it signs in with claude.ai, an API key, an `apiKeyHelper`, or a third-party provider login: the Claude CLI probe reads the login method, but the discovery descriptor reports one mode for every method. `session_status` has the same gap. A follow-up can map the probe's login method onto the discovery mode, which fixes both.
  - The receipt does not re-check that the prepared decisions are still current after preparing them, as `session_status` does; a superseded owner could yield the previous kind. No input that produces this was found, because the lookup does not return retired owners.
  - Prepared auth routes that execution resolves per credential attempt are not projected; the receipt uses the model's catalog or configured transport.

prs.title: fix: show app update guidance instead of a failing Update button on app-managed Macs
prs.body:
Closes #198506

Prior work: #198562 tried this and was closed without merging because the update handlers it edited have since moved. This PR is written against current main.

## What Problem This Solves

On a Mac where OpenClaw.app owns the Gateway, Settings > Updates still shows an enabled "Update Gateway..." button and an "Update status unavailable" row. Clicking the button gets a refusal from the Gateway ("Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."). The page then keeps that refusal as an update error with a "Retry update" button, and the error stays until the page is reloaded. A healthy install looks like it failed an update, and Retry cannot succeed because the Gateway marks the refusal as not retryable.

## User Impact

User impact: on an app-managed install, Settings > Updates now says "Managed by OpenClaw.app" in the status row and shows the app's own guidance ("Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.") where the update button used to be. There is no button to click, so no error appears and nothing is left to retry. Other installs (package, Git checkout, separately managed Gateways) look and behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already knew the install was app-owned, but `update.status` dropped that fact, so the page had no way to tell this install from any other and offered the normal action. The Gateway now sends the owner under `schedule.install.host`, and the Settings page uses it. Ownership comes from the same install marker the Gateway's refusal already uses, so a Mac connected to a separately managed Gateway still gets the normal update flow.

The protocol schema gains an optional `install.host` object and a `host` install kind, and the generated validators were regenerated from it. The Control UI adds four English strings. The updating doc notes where the owner is reported.

## Evidence

Before the change, the new Settings test fails the way the issue describes: the status row reads "Update status unavailable" and there is no ownership guidance. After the change it passes.

Tests run locally (Node 26, macOS arm64):

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/config.test.ts`: 12 passed, including a new case that accepts the host owner and rejects unknown owners or an empty hint.
- `src/infra/update-install-status.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-startup-host-owned.test.ts`: 10 passed, with expectations updated to include the owner.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts`, `update-status.test.ts`: 49 passed, with the app-owned case now expecting `install.host`.
- `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts` plus the neighboring updates, overlay and i18n suites: 241 passed. The new Settings test takes about 5 ms.
- `generate-gateway-validators` and `generate-control-ui-validators` in `--check` mode report no drift, and `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean.

Not verified:

- No native macOS run and no screenshots. I could not launch Chromium in my environment, and I did not run the app against a real app-managed Gateway. The issue's reporter offered to check a fix on their Mac.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/update-host-owned.test.ts` had one failure ("refuses an immutable surface discovered after initial admission"), a SQLite state lock error in the test's temp directory. It runs code this change does not touch, and I did not check it against main.
- The full `pnpm check:changed` and `pnpm install` were not run. Dependencies were installed with npm in a scratch folder and the checks above were run against those.

prs.title: fix(goals): block on the first authorization limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`update_goal` told the model to wait for the same blocker on three consecutive goal turns before marking a goal blocked. An authorization limit this session cannot change does not get better on turn two or three. The hidden "Advance the active goal" nudge keeps firing while the goal is still active, so the model repeats the same limit.

On 2026-10-31 a team-server Roboclaw session (nerfed payload `a7be6336-5cd4-48d7-86df-cda538eae143`, client report `449c85a5-d5b9-46ea-a2ea-c670ecbe2669`, OpenClaw 2026.10.9 at `731030eb512e`) held only `operator.sessions.write`. It could not dispatch Actions or merge. Several "Advance the active goal" turns restated that limit before the goal was marked blocked. Ordinary difficulty still waits for three turns. A missing scope, or another authorization limit this session cannot change, is a blocker on the first turn.

The same exception now appears in the per-turn active-goal context, which ordinary turns and admitted goal continuations both receive. Once the goal is blocked, continuation eligibility stops. An empty resume staying blocked is [openclaw/openclaw#192883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192883). This pull does not change that resume rule and does not change the grant.

## Evidence

Head `f56fa56c733` on macOS. An isolated loopback Gateway used `xai/grok-4.7`. The main agent allow list was only `update_goal`, so the session had no mail tool and no shell. `chat.send` delivered `/goal set Read the newest subject line from the operator Gmail inbox.` and then `Do the goal now.`

The model searched the grant, found no Gmail tool, and called `update_goal` on that same turn. The tool result stored the goal as blocked with `continuationTurns` 0. The visible reply named the limit. The Gateway log has no `session_goal_continue` event during the run or in the following 8 seconds.

```console
dispatch_action update_goal result: {"status":"updated","goal":{"status":"blocked","continuationTurns":0}}
assistant: I couldn't read the newest Gmail subject line. This session has no Gmail or mail tool, so the inbox is unreachable from here. That is a capability limit this session cannot change.
session_goal_continue count: 0
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** On the first turn, a missing mail grant makes the model mark the active goal blocked and send the visible limit. No automatic goal nudge follows. Other blockers still use the three-turn rule in the tool text.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-192975`, head `f56fa56c733`. Loopback Gateway, model `xai/grok-4.7`, agent tool allow list `update_goal` only.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Start that Gateway. Create a session. Send the Gmail goal text, then `Do the goal now.` Read `chat.history` for the `update_goal` result and the assistant text. Confirm the Gateway log never records `session_goal_continue`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Gateway chat history and log counts:

  ```console
  dispatch_action update_goal result: {"status":"updated","goal":{"status":"blocked","continuationTurns":0}}
  assistant: I couldn't read the newest Gmail subject line. This session has no Gmail or mail tool, so the inbox is unreachable from here. That is a capability limit this session cannot change.
  session_goal_continue count: 0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The same turn records `blocked` and `continuationTurns` 0, then shows the authorization limit. No later automatic nudge is queued.
- **What was not tested:** A provider auth error from a tool the grant does include, and a second machine. Ordinary three-turn blockers were not run through the model.

## Summary

`update_goal`, `docs/tools/goal.md`, and `ACTIVE_GOAL_CONTEXT_SUFFIX` now say a missing scope or other authorization limit this session cannot change blocks on the first turn. Difficulty and missing polish still do not. A rejected complete-to-blocked transition still requires the stored goal to stay unchanged.

prs.title: fix(session-status): name scopes held when capabilities cannot be read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`session_status` with capabilities enabled asks the Gateway for `tools.effective`. When that call is refused, the model only sees the refusal plus a line that this is not proof a tool is missing. It does not see the scopes the session already holds, so it goes looking.

On 2026-10-31 a team-server Roboclaw session held only `operator.sessions.write`. `session_status` returned `missing scope: operator.read`. The model then spent turns on catalog search. The grant was already known. This pull repeats the held scopes in the capability failure. It does not add `operator.read`, `operator.write`, or a dispatch action.

## Evidence

Head `1a4b1d591fc`. Isolated Gateway on loopback port 19032, token auth, channels skipped. The client connected with only `operator.sessions.write` and called the shipped `tools.effective` method. The same connection was the `callGateway` used by `createSessionStatusTool` with `capabilities: true`.

```console
{
  "rawToolsEffective": "Session-scoped access requires a verified user profile.",
  "checked": "unavailable",
  "error": "Session-scoped access requires a verified user profile.",
  "grantedScopes": ["operator.sessions.write"],
  "textHasHeldScope": true,
  "textHasNotEvidence": true
}
```

The running Gateway refused `tools.effective`. The tool text includes `This session holds operator.sessions.write.` and `This is not evidence that OpenClaw lacks a capability.`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A refused capability check names the scopes the session already holds.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, Gateway from `/tmp/oc-192971` at `1a4b1d591fc`, loopback port 19032.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run` on that worktree, then `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/proof-oc-192971.mts`, which calls `callGateway({ method: "tools.effective", scopes: ["operator.sessions.write"] })` and `session_status` execute with `capabilities: true`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The console block in Evidence. `checked` is `unavailable`, `grantedScopes` is `operator.sessions.write`, and the visible text names that scope.
- **Observed result after fix:** The refusal came from the running Gateway, and the status text repeated the held scope.
- **What was not tested:** A verified user profile whose only missing grant is `operator.read`. This client was refused one step earlier, because session-scoped access required a verified profile.

## Summary

`resolveSessionCapabilities` keeps the status usable when `tools.effective` fails and adds the caller scopes already on the admitted run. Blank scopes are still dropped.

prs.title: docs: guide small-host setup from saved keys to verified chat
prs.body:
Related: #200110, #200111, #200112

## What Problem This Solves

Someone setting up one Linux agent has to connect installation, a saved API key or existing local model, service startup, and their first working chat across several reference pages. The existing secure credential-import transport does not by itself make that journey discoverable for a beginner.

## User Impact

User impact: a guide linked from Getting Started and onboarding connects saved credentials or an existing Ollama server to first chat, with reusable non-secret configuration and precise resume actions. It now also supplies an assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios aligned with the native macOS and model-management implementations below. Loading the dashboard is no longer described as proof that everything works.

This is a documentation-first contribution, not a new credential importer, profile format, installer, automatic receipt, or completed first-run UI. It should not close the broader workflow requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guides compose the existing onboarding, credential, config, service, Template, and plugin owners. They distinguish configured from exercised capabilities, explain that config dry-run is validation rather than a before/after diff, preserve separate plugin consent, and avoid replaying completed setup mutations.

Maintainer follow-up requested for #200110: its supported stdin/SecretRef transport is acknowledged. Please keep the basic-user access gap owned under #200112: a person with one API key in 1Password or a similar manager should be able to discover the supported connection path, authorize only the intended field, and reach verified chat without source inspection or assembling several internal workflows. A CLI pipeline is an optional route for people already using that CLI, not proof that password-manager selection is integrated into onboarding. No duplicate credential store/flag or reopening solely for the existing transport is requested.

## Coordination with implementation work

This PR supplies a shared assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios for the work below; it is not a replacement implementation. States below were checked on 2026-11-18; the linked PR is authoritative. Cross-references are coordination context, not a claim that the authors have agreed to a dependency or handoff.

| Implementation work | Relationship to this documentation |
| --- | --- |
| #181011 (open) and #182075 (open, stacked on #181011) — custom endpoint editor and unified provider connection | Reuse Settings → Models, configuration/auth/discovery owners, and their preserved local-admin endpoint-definition boundary. Adding an endpoint or credential does not select or verify the primary model. Broader tracking: #177163 and #193323. |
| #200272 (experimental draft) — native macOS account/local-model onboarding | Apply the same detected → chosen → verified distinctions and first-chat acceptance, without treating the proposed picker as shipped or requiring a parallel CLI setup. |
| #200425 (merged) — native Gateway terminal-command installation | Preserve app/profile ownership and existing terminal defaults. For an app-managed Mac, use the bundled runtime and native setup; do not add a global runtime just because a CLI is not found. |
| #194841 (draft) — macOS existing-Gateway choice | The remote/attach acceptance scenario must not create or retain unwanted local hosting while approval is pending. Its native proof remains separate. |
| #200840 (draft) — compatible installed-browser dashboard handoff | Treat dashboard admission and an actual chat reply as separate evidence. The PR reports macOS dashboard validation but only partial onboarding proof. |
| #200329 (open) — Chat routes an unconfigured user to model setup | Preserve the unsent draft and use the existing setup entry point rather than making the user research model configuration. |
| #200858 and #200859 (open) — onboarding completion and diagnostic output | Keep phase completion and actionable diagnostics accurate; neither message formatting nor a success outro establishes working inference. |
| #200836 (open) — native macOS DMG captions; #200910 (open) — app-owned update guidance | Keep installation/maintenance instructions aligned with the native surfaces and installation owner. Installer presentation and update guidance are not first-chat acceptance. |

### Next implementation slice: let the setup agent use the framework

The documentation now defines **inspect → choose → propose through the existing owner → verify → resume → hand off** and four acceptance scenarios: a saved password-manager key, existing Ollama, native/remote macOS hosting, and interrupted setup. The assistant should do the routine inspection and present one next action, not assign these pages to the user.

**Current integration gap, verified in source:** the initial OpenClaw system agent receives docs/source locations, but its primary loop is restricted to the typed `openclaw` tool and its fallback planner explicitly has no file/network lookup. A pointer is not loaded documentation. Ordinary agents have separate docs-first guidance and may read/search only through their available tools. This PR does not claim to wire automatic documentation consumption into the initial bot.

Implementation should start at the existing `src/system-agent/assistant-prompts.ts` prompt builder and `src/system-agent/overview.ts` reference-discovery boundary, with the tool restriction in `src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts`. Reuse the release-matched canonical guide through bounded, deterministic setup context; do not create another installer, config owner, unrestricted reader, public receipt format, or growing copy of the whole docs tree in the prompt. A runtime implementation must preserve the normal/native app action owners, prompt-prefix stability, capability limits, consent, and source-of-truth rules.

Keep #200112 open for that integration and real entry-point acceptance. Validate through the actual initial setup agent and native/CLI entry points: no human documentation hunt, no raw key in model context, no duplicate installation on resume, and an observed chat result or one precise blocker. A documentation-only check or a prompt-string test cannot establish that outcome.

## Evidence

### Bot-consumption and adversarial review

Three sequential rounds used fresh `openai/gpt-6-astra` instruction-following consumers and independent `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` adversarial reviewers: six child runs and 16 synthetic scenario responses across successive drafts. No unsafe next action was observed in those responses; this is not a 16-case live regression suite or a separate verified “Astra-scale” mode.

The review-driven changes stop failed/partial secret reads before import, preserve the actual agent ID, scope the shortcut to OpenAI keys, separate terminal selection from native automatic trials, require an actual intended-agent Gateway chat result, avoid creating an agent or broadening permissions for an optional tool check, reconcile failed rescue work before retry, and gate service start on successful install. A contradictory incidental planning-tool claim in the existing reference was removed rather than treated as a new capability.

### Executed Bash failure/control tests

Actual documented snippets ran in real Bash with synthetic `op`/`openclaw` functions only. **All six final fixtures passed:** failed read; partial read then failure; importer failure; successful import under inherited tracing/autoexport; failed service installation; successful installation control. The captured key was not traced or exported to the importer environment. No real credential, password manager, or OpenClaw service operation ran.

The original snippets wrongly continued to onboarding after read/import failure and started a service after installation failure. The intermediate pipefail-only revision still started the importer after a partial failed read. The final snippet starts neither importer nor onboarding on a failed read, and starts no service after a failed installation. Success controls still proceed.

### Documentation checks and limits

- MDX syntax and targeted formatting pass for all seven changed/new pages; six Bash-fence syntax/continuation checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- The full configuration-example audit validates 1,408 examples with no findings; both new JSON5 examples are included. Internal route checks report no broken routes.
- The anchor audit still reports three unrelated findings in untouched pages/targets: ACP setup duplicate heading, release 2026.10.1 OpenAI runtime anchor, and Code Mode troubleshooting loop-detection anchor. No changed-link anchor finding was reported. ClawHub fragments remain unverified without their separate source checkout.
- Original source/draft review and this follow-up simplification keep the change documentation-only: no production code, state, new public command, receipt format, or competing config/installer owner.
- **Not verified:** a clean-host install, real password-manager import, actual initial setup-agent documentation loading, real model/provider/tool execution, native first-chat handoff, logout/reboot persistence, or outage failover. The synthetic reviews and shell stubs do not replace those implementation acceptance checks.

Requested by Richard O’Shaughnessy through the linked issues and discussion.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d1f8b252-c950-4999-b9ef-66e08f64c9a6)

## Worked on by

- @oshaughnessy-junior

prs.title: improve: avoid scanning unrelated agent files during updates
prs.body:
Related: #182616

## What Problem This Solves

Update database discovery walks default-agent files to inventory temporary directories even when those trees cannot contain a selected plugin database. Installations with large agent trees pay for this unrelated traversal during update preparation.

## User Impact

Updates avoid scanning agent subtrees outside retained plugin resource roots while keeping the same database selection and backup coverage. Full backup archives retain their complete temporary-directory inventory. No user configuration or migration is required. An older installed updater retains its own shipped discovery behavior on the first hop.

This is a draft implementation PR: the real installed released-driver upgrade and readiness checks pass, but full package-rollback/recovery proof and the structured local-review checkpoint remain incomplete. No total-update or Gateway-downtime improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resource-inventory owner can limit temporary-root discovery to the plugin paths that database discovery already selects, including their ancestors. Explicit nested includes and custom agent roots keep their existing policy; ordinary archive callers keep the complete default inventory. This removes unrelated traversal rather than introducing a cache or another database-discovery owner.

Simplification: 18 net production lines, 74 net test lines, plus a rerunnable discovery phase in the existing update I/O workload. The remaining test/workload growth protects scoped exclusions and records counts independently of wall-clock noise.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against `b255cc584c9b5b31de7f89df56357bdfe4b317f9`: the real discovery owner selected the correct core database but issued three unrelated agent-directory reads; the fixed regression issues zero.
- 20 focused tests pass across database resources, resource inventory, and backup ownership. Coverage includes every retained account/token database beneath a disabled plugin resource, snapshot payload rows, custom roots, protected children under temporary exclusions, privacy markers, aliases, restore, and refusal paths. The targeted command took 70.39 s including a 37 s compiler-cache preparation; actual test bodies were about 26 s. CI seconds are not yet available.
- A complete candidate package build and package-tarball integrity check pass. The build reports UI asset-budget warnings; no UI source is changed.
- The actual installed `2026.11.2` CLI successfully updates to the built `2026.11.4` candidate through ordinary `update --yes --json --tag <tarball> --no-restart`. Real foreground Gateways pass HTTP readiness before and after; WebSocket probes confirm their actual serving version/build IDs. Probe connection succeeds, but privileged diagnostic RPCs remain scope-limited (`operator.read` was not granted); no grants were widened. Seeded Unicode rows in two core and three disabled-plugin databases, full integrity checks, and 2,000 ordinary files survive the update.
- This single functional CLI invocation takes 174.99 s including launch/cleanup. It is not a before/after full-update benchmark. Gateway downtime is unmeasured: this fixture externally stops/restarts foreground processes with `--no-restart`, so no managed-downtime value or zero-downtime claim is inferred.
- Scoped TypeScript validation and workload lint pass; changed-file format and `git diff --check` pass. Core lint reports one inherited `max-lines` violation in `backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts`: baseline 720 counted lines, candidate 721, existing limit 700. No limit or baseline was weakened.

Acceptance declared before measurement: exact selected database set, zero unrelated agent-tree reads, and no discovery median/p95 regression. Five warm interleaved baseline/candidate samples use 200 nested directories, 2,000 ordinary files and one existing core SQLite database. Both changed baseline production modules are frozen from the base; other dependencies and fixture state are shared. Linux, Node 24.20.0; starting load averages 8.44/12.70/11.92.

| Discovery-owner measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unrelated directory reads, every sample | 201 | 0 |
| Median | 94.48 ms | 90.13 ms |
| p95 (maximum of 5) | 94.83 ms | 92.44 ms |
| Range | 92.57–94.83 ms | 85.35–92.44 ms |

Rerun: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts --baseline b255cc584 --phase discovery --samples 5`. A separate CPU-profile run is attribution evidence, not part of the timing table. These are owner-only observations, not installed CLI-update or downtime measurements.

Outstanding proof: the controlled post-activation Doctor-failure fixture returns the expected failure and reports all seven pre-migration database snapshots restored, but does not restore the previous package. The run remains pending on the intentionally failing fixture version. Supported `update repair --yes --no-restart --json` refuses with `Plugin cohort recovery belongs to a different installation.` Full package rollback and recovered-Gateway readiness are therefore **not proven**. The fixture is stopped; recovery materials are preserved. No owner checks or journals were changed to force a pass. The maintained Docker runner is separately unavailable (no Docker executable); the successful package/process route above is not a synthetic driver substitute.

Two bound Auto Review attempts were interrupted around Gateway restarts and produced no validated report; no clean Auto Review result is claimed. A fresh independent OpenClaw subagent (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, separate context) performed a P0–P2 static review of the complete five-file frozen delta and requested dependency/caller context against `b255cc584c9b5b31de7f89df56357bdfe4b317f9` (diff SHA-256 `a701791945d56673e2e0791f3f90da11981776781150f6a1c7c2e7413e1b73db`); no P0–P2 regression or remaining material source-context gap was found. It is a source-snapshot review, not checkout-based execution or helper-validated Auto Review. Directory counts are asserted by the workload; timing acceptance is checked against the printed sample table rather than enforced by a timing assertion. Full-update baseline/candidate timing, managed downtime comparison, and current-head CI remain outstanding.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen.

prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid repeated session-list invalidation scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent streaming sessions repeatedly scan every row in every retained session list and update every list's selection accounting. This consumes Gateway CPU even when most lists do not contain the changed session.

## User Impact

Session-list publication does less work during streaming bursts while preserving list contents, conditional baselines, selection freshness, and prompt release of obsolete entries. No protocol, configuration, schema, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cache prepares row-key membership once during its existing admission loop. Fact invalidation checks membership instead of scanning rows. It also tracks only views with populated selections: publication releases those selections immediately, and later events do no selection accounting until a reader populates another selection. Eviction and reset remove their membership. Retired row vectors remain identity-only comparison witnesses; directly filling those vectors avoids TypedArray.from temporary allocation.

## Evidence

Acceptance recorded before formal measurements: five serial A1/B/A2 rounds at 50 and 200 lists of 200 rows, 5,000 synthetic sessions, and 40 hot keys. Each arm performs 10,000 fact and selection changes after 10,000 warmup changes, reading lists every 200 changes. Candidate must beat both baseline arms in warm main-thread CPU and cumulative V8 allocation, including full replay with admission/read work. Cold admission is reported separately. This is synthetic publication-owner proof, not database, filesystem, model, transport, or production latency proof.

Final candidate passed all five serial rounds at each size (Node 26.12.1). Medians:

| Lists | Metric per 10,000 changes | A1 | Candidate | A2 |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | Invalidation CPU, ms | 1200.81 | 17.17 | 1195.90 |
| 50 | Invalidation allocation, MB | 55.49 | 22.43 | 54.19 |
| 50 | Full replay CPU, ms | 1258.10 | 63.19 | 1253.96 |
| 50 | Full replay wall, ms | 1261.73 | 63.29 | 1255.55 |
| 50 | Full replay allocation, MB | 85.40 | 63.58 | 84.78 |
| 200 | Invalidation CPU, ms | 4793.48 | 72.24 | 4806.25 |
| 200 | Invalidation allocation, MB | 186.20 | 55.65 | 185.98 |
| 200 | Full replay CPU, ms | 4902.13 | 194.24 | 4913.00 |
| 200 | Full replay wall, ms | 4913.91 | 196.45 | 4933.30 |
| 200 | Full replay allocation, MB | 257.59 | 178.40 | 258.13 |

Every candidate warm CPU and allocation sample beat the entire range of both controls. Serialized final row hashes matched across all arms. At 200 lists, full-replay p95 (maximum of five) was 197.44 ms CPU / 179.15 MB versus controls 5223.49 / 261.62 and 4928.96 / 259.11. At 50 lists it was 76.92 ms / 64.44 MB versus 1285.57 / 86.22 and 1353.76 / 85.29. Host load is recorded in every sample.

Tradeoff: membership adds about 0.30–0.33 MB retained heap for 50 lists and 1.07 MB for 200, accounted within the existing 32 MiB budget. Cold first-admission CPU medians A1/B/A2 were 5.54/5.73/5.37 ms and 10.47/11.72/10.20 ms respectively. Cold allocations include JIT and varied: 8.34/8.90/6.98 MB and 12.81/13.88/12.56 MB. Runtime production delta is +24 lines (39 added, 15 removed): membership preparation/accounting and populated-selection lifecycle replace repeated scans without another cache owner. Facts still cost O(lists) membership checks plus affected-vector retirement; selection work is proportional to populated selections, once between reads.

The new publication regression fails the base with 100 unrelated row reads and passes with zero. It covers targeted/reset retirement, duplicate-key replacement, unaffected baselines, display-only reuse, immediate selection release, and zero update calls on 100 further selection changes without reads. Existing focused delta, history, viewer, and retention tests passed (30 tests before the CI repair).

First-head CI exposed a genuine lifetime regression in lazy selection invalidation: the existing projection-retention test reproduced locally with eight obsolete objects still alive when no reader returned. The final implementation removes revision stamping and releases populated selections immediately. All 12 publication/cache/projection-lifetime tests now pass, including that exact failure. No inherited-failure exception is claimed.

Independent Codex autoreview of the staged complete final diff against `457486d4adee2cd28ea1a5989bbcd298c0f0c63f` is scoped-clean through P2. The simplification pass retained only cache-owned membership, populated-selection retirement, and direct identity-vector fill. No UI-imported module changed. Final repair scale-retention proof passed eight tests, including 60,000 sessions and 25 readers with ten queries. Final repair `pnpm check:changed --base b5518c21e327889f4c19dc585e63c5d060396846` passed completely, including production/test types, lint, dead-code scans and repository guards. Earlier broad checks against the original base passed except mechanical test/driver lint that was corrected and rechecked.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-publication-invalidation-measure.mjs --lists 200`. For baseline arms, add `--baseline-dir <directory>` containing the original three owner modules from the base. Run both sizes five times in serial A1/B/A2 order. Separate traces use `--cpu-profile <path>`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: new Venice setups default to `zai-org-glm-4.7`, which is no longer Venice's default model, and the Venice docs still describe it as the "live default trait".

## User Impact

User impact: onboarding Venice now selects `venice/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-uncensored`, which Venice's `GET /models/traits?type=text` currently returns for both `default` and `function_calling_default`. Existing configs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Points the manifest `defaultModel` and onboarding alias at the current Venice default, and adds that model to the offline catalog. Its specs come from Venice's public `/models` API: private, 1M context, 131k max output, text and image input, and $0.33 / $1.32 / $0.00825 per 1M tokens for input, output and cache read. The provider docs examples, default row and catalog table are updated to match.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension venice`: 4 files, 27 tests passed
- `oxfmt --check` on changed files and `pnpm format:docs:check`: clean
- `curl 'https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/models/traits?type=text'` returns `"default":"deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-uncensored"`


### Real behavior proof (exact head `01a4042`)

These runs used a live Venice key from env and isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_HOME` directories. The key does not appear in any config or captured log.

**Fresh onboarding selects the new model**

```
$ openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health --auth-choice venice-api-key
onboard exit: 0
agents.defaults.model: {"primary":"venice/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-uncensored"}
agents.defaults.models: {"venice/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-uncensored":{"alias":"DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Uncensored"}}
```

```
$ openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-id history-proof \
    --message "Use the read tool to open proof.txt in the workspace and tell me the code word. Do nothing else."
```

prs.title: docs(plugins): align prompt and session hook contracts with runtime behavior
prs.body:
Related: #192753

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` misstates or omits several runtime hook contracts when plugin authors target multiple OpenClaw runtimes, input gates, finalization relays, or active-run steering.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors get accurate runtime-specific contracts—including that the Agents API harness ignores `toolsAllow` while ACPX rejects any returned value, that `before_agent_run` fails closed on errors and timeouts, and which SDK types and return shapes `before_agent_finalize` and `steerActiveRun` actually expose.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligned `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` directly against the current `main` hook runner, harness adapters, and session steering implementations, and updated the remaining `prompt injection` permission prose on the page to match the `allowPromptModification` rename (#192634).

<details>
<summary>Verified contract updates against source owners</summary>

- `before_model_resolve`: note that `attachments` is currently populated for prompt images (`{ kind: "image", mimeType }`) and omitted otherwise (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/setup.ts`), and that a canceled/superseded source run aborts preflight (`AgentHarnessPreflightError`) rather than continuing model preparation.
- `before_prompt_build` (`toolsAllow`): document worker-turn application (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-prompt.ts`), CLI filtering plus rejection only when native tools cannot be limited exactly (`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/cli-backends.ts`), ACPX rejection of any returned value including `["*"]` (`extensions/acpx/src/harness-attempt.ts`), Codex rejection of values without `"*"`, and that Agents API ignores the field (`extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.ts`).
- `heartbeat_prompt_contribution`: document `{ sessionKey?, agentId?, heartbeatName? }` input and that contributions from all handlers are joined before each combined field is truncated to a 1,000-character CJK-weighted budget (`src/infra/heartbeat-compat.ts`, `src/plugins/hooks.ts`).
- `requiresToolAuthority: true`: include worker turns (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-prompt.ts`) and Agents API (`extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.ts`) among runtimes supplying `toolAuthority`, and clarify that ACPX skips the post-policy phase.
- `before_agent_run`: separate Gateway worker-turn admission from the embedded/CLI timing (`/plugins/hooks#choose-a-hook`), describe `prompt` as the model-bound prompt including prompt-hook context (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.ts`), list optional event/decision fields (`void`, `category`, `metadata`, `accountId`, `channelId`, `senderId`, `senderIsOwner`), document the 15s default timeout and fail-closed blocking on error/timeout/invalid decision (`src/plugins/hooks.ts`, `src/agents/harness/before-agent-run.ts`), and clarify the formatted `Your message could not be sent: ...` block notice stored in `message.content`.
- `ctx.inputProvenance` & `ctx.memoryAudience`: add Agents API and remaining optional `InputProvenance` fields (`sourceRole`, `sourcePromptPrefix`, `jobId`, `runId`), plus `ctx.memoryAudience` as the kind-tagged `MemoryAudience` object (branch on `.kind`, linked to the memory SDK contract) and `ctx.assertMemoryAudienceCurrent()` revalidation guidance (`src/plugins/hook-agent-context.types.ts`, `src/plugins/memory-provider-types.ts`).
- `ctx.chatId` vs `ctx.channelContext.chat.id`: clarify where `ctx.chatId` carries the native ID (user-triggered embedded hooks and CLI hooks other than `agent_turn_prepare` and `before_prompt_build`) and that those CLI preparation hooks and the harnesses can mirror `ctx.channelId`; `ctx.channelContext.chat.id` takes the same value whenever the host sets a transport-native `ctx.chatId`, and CLI `agent_turn_prepare`/`before_prompt_build` contexts omit `ctx.channelContext` (`src/plugins/hook-agent-context.ts`, `src/agents/harness/hook-context.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/plugin-turn-context.ts`).
- `before_agent_finalize`: document `{ action: "continue" }` (and empty-`revise` normalization), describe `retry` as a field shape typed through `api.on("before_agent_finalize", ...)` rather than an importable SDK type (neither `PluginHookBeforeAgentFinalizeResult` nor `BeforeAgentFinalizeRetry` is exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`), and clarify bidirectional Codex native `Stop` hook relay translation (`src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-events.ts`).
- `steerActiveRun`: clarify `{ steered: true, runId }` when a stored duplicate key's receipt is available (`src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts`), describe Copilot accurately as exposing V1 `messageInjection` handles rather than a legacy V1 harness (`extensions/copilot/harness.ts`), distinguish the rejected promise when the plugin is already unloaded or unloads while the host prepares the steer (`src/plugins/registry.ts`, `src/plugins/contracts/active-run-steering.contract.test.ts`) from the `steered: false` result when the guarded runtime detects the unload during dispatch (`src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts`), and clarify the Control UI **`<plugin>` guidance** display-name label.

</details>

## Evidence

- Verified every changed statement line-by-line against current `main` runtime owners (`src/plugins/*`, `src/agents/*`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/*`, `src/infra/heartbeat-compat.ts`, `extensions/{acpx,agentsapi,copilot}/*`).
- Ran OpenClaw documentation gates on the rebased head commit:
  - `OPENCLAW_FORMAT_TOOL=oxfmt node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` → clean
  - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` → passed (0 MDX issues)
  - `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` & `--anchors` → 0 broken links/fragments in `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`
  - `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts --base upstream/main` → clean
  - `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs`, `bash scripts/docs-spellcheck.sh docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`, `git diff --check` → clean
- Follow-up `1fb9ac94d00` (Codex/ClawSweeper P2 on unload-time steering): rechecked against `src/plugins/registry.ts` (`assertCurrent()` after `await loadSteering()`), `src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts` (dispatch-stage `sourceRefusal` → `runtime_rejected`), and the `rechecks the plugin lifetime after loading the dispatch module` contract test; `check-docs-mdx`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` clean on the new head.
- Follow-up `8bc3a748e37` (Codex P2 on `ctx.memoryAudience`): documented the `{ kind, agentId, ... }` object shape from `src/plugins/memory-provider-types.ts` and linked `/plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context#memory-audience` (heading present, route in `docs/docs.json`); `check-docs-mdx`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` clean.
- Follow-up `c9057da91f9`: independent claim-by-claim source audit of every changed statement against `upstream/main` `37d5c24faec`; corrected `toolsAllow` per runtime, heartbeat budget semantics, `before_agent_run` worker timing and `prompt` content, `ctx.chatId`/`channelContext.chat.id`, and the finalize `retry` type reference. `check-docs-mdx`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` clean.
- Follow-up `3c18652dbba` (ClawSweeper P2 on CLI chat identity): rechecked that `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` builds the prompt-build hook context from `buildAgentHookContextChannelFields` only (`chatId: channelId`, no `channelContext`) and that `resolvePromptBuildHookResult` forwards the same context to `agent_turn_prepare` through `resolvePluginTurnContext` (`src/agents/plugin-turn-context.ts`); added `agent_turn_prepare` to the CLI exception and qualified the `channelContext.chat.id` mirroring statement. `format-docs --check` (oxfmt), `check-docs-mdx`, and `git diff --check` clean; `docs-spellcheck.sh` reports no hits in this file.
- Review: completed `pr-simplify` self-audit on `upstream/main..HEAD` (1 file changed: `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`, +97/-65 lines, docs-only; shared `~/.agents/skills/autoreview` helper is not installed in this environment).

prs.title: fix: open the dashboard in a compatible installed browser
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Onboarding and `openclaw dashboard` can open a browser that cannot run the Control UI even when a compatible browser is already installed. Switching browsers using only the clean dashboard URL loses the one-time pairing handoff and creates avoidable recovery work; this is not a failure of normal pairing.

## User Impact

When the default browser is known to lack required features, OpenClaw can open an identified compatible alternative on macOS, native Windows, or Linux for this session only. Supported and unknown defaults keep their existing opening path. No browser is installed, no OS default is changed, and no automation browser profile is selected.

**Draft: native macOS dashboard fallback was validated on earlier head `29dae7868b21`. The inherited-SSH repair below has focused regression proof but still needs native macOS confirmation. Onboarding remains only partially verified; native Windows/Linux desktop verification and before/after media remain pending.** Windows Hub is independently released and is not changed here. WSL keeps its existing Windows desktop opener rather than selecting a Linux browser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing browser opener now accepts an installed-browser target, while the existing private-file handoff still carries each newly issued one-time pairing URL. Browser-version estimates and actual browser feature probes share the same requirements; browser-side verification remains authoritative.

- macOS reads application registrations and bundle metadata, including `~/Applications`.
- Native Windows reads HTTPS registration and installed executable versions without running browsers to identify their versions.
- Linux reads the XDG HTTPS association and normal Chrome/Chromium, Firefox, and Edge executables on `PATH`. Custom wrappers, Flatpak-only installations, and `BROWSER` overrides remain conservative unknown cases.
- Selection order is deterministic. Unknown metadata retains the existing fallback, while missing compatible alternatives retain a terminal/recovery path.
- Explicit remote sessions do not launch on the wrong desktop. Cold GUI processes acknowledge startup without waiting for their lifetime; onboarding separately waits for a newly connected Control UI client.

There is no new pairing mechanism, stored browser preference, configuration option, token handling, or installation step. Changes target main only; no backport or older-Gateway compatibility is proposed. Necessary growth is the three platform discovery adapters and their common selection contract; no registry/cache/manager is introduced.

## Evidence

### ClawSweeper repair: inherited SSH variables on macOS

Commit [`cee9b3506c21`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cee9b3506c218358154da01c7de7bb7ac8afaf75) restores the local-shell behavior protected by [#67088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67088) and [#85340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85340). SSH environment variables alone no longer reject a local Mac GUI terminal. After verifying the console owner, SSH-marked Mac sessions must identify as the current launchd `Aqua` GUI bootstrap; background, unknown, or failed context checks remain blocked, as do Remote Containers/Codespaces. Linux/Windows SSH and WSL handling are unchanged.

Four inherited-SSH regressions failed on the previous PR head and pass with this repair. **70 focused tests across four affected/consumer files pass** (15.44 seconds wall time), along with strict affected typechecking, targeted lint/format, and diff checks. Independent source review found no concrete P0/P1/P2 issue in this narrow repair. This is fixture/source proof, not a new native macOS run: the earlier report's simulated-SSH result applies to `29dae7868b21`, not the new GUI-context distinction.

### Native macOS dashboard validation — passed

[@jjjhenriksen’s native test report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200840#issuecomment-6966181964) validates head `29dae7868b2139b5829806475c52b1f9076d2138` against comparison build `e9561fb93e23aca2a797ed0cf28593cac45edc17` in a disposable Apple Silicon Tart VM running macOS Sequoia 15.7.7, using a foreground loopback Gateway and disposable state.

- **Before:** the dashboard opened the HTTPS default, Safari 18.6, which displayed the unsupported-browser screen; the Gateway recorded no admitted Control UI connection.
- **After:** with Safari still the HTTPS default, the dashboard selected Chrome 158.0.8127.37 installed only in `~/Applications`. Both a cold launch and a repeat launch into the running Chrome process produced fresh, authenticated Control UI connections at the Gateway. The HTTPS default remained Safari.
- **Additional checks:** removing the compatible alternative produced the recovery notice; `--no-open` suppressed launch; `--json` returned the handoff and expiry fields; a simulated SSH session suppressed GUI launch.
- **Onboarding is partial, not passed:** the browser-handoff helper selected Chrome and the Gateway recorded a separate fresh Control UI connection, but the helper did not return before the test cutoff. This was not a full interactive onboarding run or confirmed handoff completion.

The report includes sanitized terminal/Gateway excerpts, not before/after screenshots. It does **not** establish supported-default behavior, unknown/custom metadata, failed browser startup, a forced expired handoff, or a successful chat reply.

### Automated and source validation

- **Prior-head validation:** 89 targeted tests across 8 files passed on `29dae7868b21` (16.96 seconds wall time). The repair reruns the four affected/consumer suites above; unchanged feature-floor, private-handoff, Linux subprocess, and browser feature-admission proof is retained from that run. Focused tests cover browser feature floors, supported/unknown defaults, user-installed macOS alternatives, deterministic selection, native Windows metadata fixtures, Linux XDG subprocess fixtures, headless/SSH/WSL behavior, selected-launch failure, cold long-lived GUI process startup, private-file delivery, and fresh handoffs on repeated dashboard runs. Existing dashboard/onboarding handoff suites and browser feature admission remain green.
- Selected-launch regressions were red on base `e9561fb93e23aca2a797ed0cf28593cac45edc17` (three intended failures) and green with the target-aware opener.
- Strict typechecking of affected production/tests with repository ambient declarations, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm ui:build` succeeds. Existing advisory size budgets also fail on the pinned base: CSS 57.8 KiB vs 56.9 KiB; chat boot requests 21 vs 20; chat JS 1297.2 KiB vs 1296.8 KiB. The candidate reports 1297.3 KiB chat JS; no CSS/request-budget exception is added.
- Independent read-only source review identified cold-GUI lifetime and kernel-only WSL classification defects; both were repaired with regressions. The follow-up review confirms both repairs with no remaining concrete P0/P1/P2 findings in those repairs. Native platform execution is not established by that review. The structured Auto Review attempts were interrupted by Gateway restarts and did not produce a completed receipt.

Linux-specific proof uses real Linux subprocesses for XDG discovery fixtures and a real long-lived process for cold-launch lifetime; those pass locally. This runner has no installed desktop browser or display, so real Linux desktop opening/pairing and screenshots remain unverified, not claimed as passing.

### Remaining native verification

Use disposable state/profile and a foreground Gateway on an unused port, never normal Gateway credentials.

- Finish a full interactive onboarding run and establish why the helper did not confirm completion in the reported test.
- Verify the new macOS distinction between a local GUI shell carrying inherited SSH variables and an actual SSH/background session belonging to the same console user. Also cover the supported-default and unknown/custom browser paths, failed browser startup, forced expired-handoff recovery, and a separately observed chat reply.
- Exercise native Windows and Linux desktop selection, private-file pairing, cold/warm launches, and remote/headless behavior. Linux subprocess fixtures and process-lifetime tests do not establish desktop browser behavior.
- Capture sanitized unsupported-default before/after media with actual OS/browser versions. Do not publish pairing URLs, credentials, or private desktop content.

Reported and scoped with @jjjhenriksen. Native test-box verification is still pending.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfef40a9-b1b9-4014-a803-f5a73399e554)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen
