prs.title: fix: give schema-compatible recovery advice when a database is newer
prs.body:
Closes #200886. Reported by @woodmanlegion.

### Work sessions

[Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

## What Problem This Solves

After a source or development build advances a database schema, an installed release can correctly refuse it but suggest `doctor --fix`, which refuses too. The stored writer label can be equal, lower, or unrecognized, so advice to use a release “at least as new as the writer” can point back to the build already refusing the data.

## User Impact

Refusals now direct users to a build supporting the required schema (every listed schema for a fleet), or a verified pre-update backup with its matching build. They preserve useful writer-label provenance without promising that Doctor or an unconditional update can make arbitrary development schemas readable. Strict refusals and stored data remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Schema compatibility determines the recovery target; release labels are supplementary provenance. The two existing diagnostic owners retain the schema numbers, refusing installation identity, paths, agent facts, and error classes. No schema, migration, admission, backup, permission, configuration, or dependency contract changes.

## Evidence

The lower-label regression failed on unchanged production for both state and agent databases, then passed through real runtime openers, CLI error rendering, Doctor preflight, and explicit state preflight. Database bytes, metadata, sidecar entries, and modes were preserved. **33 distinct focused tests passed**, including label/context and replacement/readmission coverage; touched-file lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh independent review of the complete change found no actionable P0/P1/P2 issues.

**Draft; not ready to land.** The production Team host is unqualified for builds and broad checks; remote proof capacity is unavailable to this task. Required build proof is deferred to exact-head CI under the draft/CI policy. Build, separate targeted TypeScript compilation, CLI/Gateway startup consumer tests, latest-stable installed-package upgrade/preservation, Windows qualified flows, and live Gateway/model proof remain unrun. Linux owner-boundary tests do not establish Windows or native-service behavior. CI artifact builds also do not cover full declaration emission; remaining platform/live gates are still owed.

<details>
<summary>Exact candidate and focused commands</summary>

Candidate: `29e9d60686092798b6085b2c730abc6ca4649095` (prepared base `9618c4116960556e5519dd4c3eee404423a93318`). Production delta: +7/-14 lines.

The repository's supported source-mode launcher avoids unrelated global compiled-worker preparation. No schema decisions were mocked or test semantics disabled.

```sh
# Red on unchanged production: two diagnostic failures; green after repair.
node scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor-database-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'reports schema-based recovery'

# Full Doctor preflight file: 6 passed, 15.61s wall.
node scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor-database-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Message/context and replacement/readmission consumers: 27 passed, 9.31s wall.
node scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/sqlite-user-version.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db-checkonce.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.checkonce.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Each invocation used a 180-second timeout. Final assertion reruns passed (integration: two cases, 10.70s; message table: five tests, 1.46s); these overlap the 33 tests above. CI seconds are not yet available. The reviewed and committed tree is unchanged from this proof.

</details>

prs.title: fix(macOS): stop the Dashboard and docked Web Inspector from flickering
prs.body:
Closes #200614

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS Dashboard and Web Inspector can both flicker when the Inspector is docked. The flashing makes it difficult to inspect the Dashboard without moving the Inspector to its own window.

## User Impact

The Dashboard and the bottom-docked Inspector now keep their respective areas in the same window. Resizing the window keeps the split, and undocking restores the Dashboard to its full size.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebKit adjusts the inspected view's frame when the Inspector docks. The Dashboard's edge constraints were restoring the full frame during AppKit layout, so the Dashboard covered the Inspector. The Dashboard now uses AppKit's width and height autoresizing within the existing pane. The browser import banner keeps its own constraints.

### Compatibility with WebKit

WebKit's `324654@main` inserts a docking container only for eligible views positioned by Auto Layout constraints. With this patch, the Dashboard has a frame-based layout, so WebKit continues to resize the Dashboard and Inspector directly. WebKit's upstream change includes a regression test for docking and detaching a frame-based view. [WebKit docking condition](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/590746c297667e9a2cffff7e359ae8c67a3b72eb/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/Inspector/mac/WebInspectorUIProxyMac.mm#L1259-L1263) · [WebKit regression test](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/590746c297667e9a2cffff7e359ae8c67a3b72eb/Tools/TestWebKitAPI/Tests/WebKit/WKWebView/mac/WKInspectorAttachment.mm#L559-L576)

## Evidence

- Built both versions of the full macOS app from 2026.11.4 (`d843d6af`) and ran them in an arm64 Lima guest on macOS 27.2.1 (26B131). Each used an isolated test profile and its own loopback Gateway.
- Docked the real Web Inspector at the bottom three times in each build. The unpatched app failed the split-frame check in 120 of 120 samples and changed the Dashboard frame during 98 layout passes. The patched app passed in all 120 samples with zero frame changes during layout. Resizing preserved the split, and both undock cycles restored the full Dashboard frame.
- The reduced WebKit reproduction using the Dashboard pane from `main` (`f1d40db4`) measured overlapping frames in 15 of 15 docked samples on the baseline and 0 of 15 with the fix.
- The new regression test checks that another layout pass preserves the docked frame and that the Dashboard still autoresizes with its parent. Its frame assertions failed before the change and passed after it in the VM. The full native Swift test target compiled on `main`.
- The Lima tests used system WebKit `22625.2.8.11.9`. Compatibility with `324654@main` is based on source review and awaits a run on macOS with that WebKit change.
- The automation that opened and docked Web Inspector was local to the VM verification build. The change is AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover guest tasks after concurrent managed-workspace edits (#187911)
prs.body:
Closes #187911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a managed sandbox conversation stays stuck when an administrator and the guest edit the same file at once. Both versions are preserved, but Files and every later turn of the original task keep returning "Local sandbox edits conflict with the managed workspace" instead of letting the authorized user merge the contributions and continue.

## User Impact

The affected conversation can recover without discarding either side. A normal authorized Files save is the acknowledgement: when the operator's expected hash matches the guest copy they read, the save is recorded against that guest version, the resolved file is copied into the private sandbox checkout, and the original task can continue. Files that are still conflicted stay pending. A guest version written after the capture is still rejected, and a save on a worktree without a pending conflict no longer writes a synthetic checkpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Conflict acknowledgement goes through the projection state's own update operation, so the next synchronization sees the current binding rather than a changed one.
- A Files save binds the selected candidate path through the actual write, so nested `fileRoot` sessions cannot resolve the same relative path twice.
- Acknowledgement is only recorded for a retained conflict or a pending receipt, so ordinary saves leave the checkpoint empty.
- A save whose own file is accepted while other conflicts remain is reported as an accepted save, while real write and authority failures still propagate.
- Reconciliation commits resolved canonical files onto the complete accepted baseline, preserving unconflicted guest additions, edits, and deletions.
- Canonical imports hold the existing guest pause through acceptance for either direction, so a background guest process cannot race verified bytes.
- A guest directory that may contain unreviewed descendants is refused, never recursively deleted; a legacy checkpoint without the new fields still settles.
- Resolved copies keep the existing authority revalidation, realpath/symlink containment, recursive replacement of a conflicting type, and a recorded guest version so a later guest edit of the same path conflicts again instead of being overwritten.

## Evidence

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm tsgo:core` — clean, no diagnostics.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.worktree.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.conflict.test.ts --maxWorkers=4` — 2 files, 32/32 tests passed. Key cases:
  - `acknowledges and saves a reconciled version via sessions.files.set during conflict` (then prepares the next guest workspace successfully)
  - `resolves conflict hash correctly when session has a nested fileRoot`
  - `preserves compare-and-swap protection for unseen canonical edits outside retained conflicts`
  - `accepts a newer guest version that the operator actually reviewed in projection`
  - `treats a resolved path as a new conflict after the guest edits it again`
  - `does not synthesize a checkpoint for an ordinary managed save`
  - `resolves canonical workspace-relative path when saving absolute path candidates`
  - `overlays resolved paths onto complete accepted baseline preserving unmutated baseline entries`
  - `preserves newer guest divergence in projection if edited while conflict is pending`
  - `rejects unreviewed newer guest version written after administrator review`
  - `refuses to replace a guest directory that gained unreviewed descendants`
  - `settles a legacy checkpoint that predates the conflict fields`
- Broader focused batch (projection, manifest scan, store, checkout, CAS, fingerprints, diagnostics, reconcile/publication, workspace-local reconciliation): 205 passed, 1 skipped.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 pnpm test:unit:fast --maxWorkers=4` — 13,740 passed, 49 skipped; failures only in untouched suites: `completion-fish` spawnSync result shape, `bench-session-history` node spawnSync ETIMEDOUT under load, and one provider-header test that passes alone and only failed in the full shard.
- The suite runs the production `sessions.files.*` handlers against prepared git worktrees, the projection custody owner, and the SQLite worker boundary; it is not a mocked handler harness.
- Live Docker-backed product proof: `pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-workspace-conflict-recovery.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 1/1 passed (28 s). It starts a real Gateway child with a Docker sandbox, creates a managed worktree session, provisions the private projection, preserves a real conflict, recovers it through `sessions.files.set`, and completes the next guest turn with both trees holding the merged bytes.
- The branch is merged with current `main` (`910f6b9427d`).
- Latest-stable upgrade proof (`openclaw@2026.11.5`): created a real managed-worktree conflict with a pending canonical result through the stable release, then opened the same state with this branch. Before upgrade the checkpoint contained only `baseManifestRaw`, `baseManifestRef`, `currentManifestRaw`, `currentManifestRef`, `fingerprints`, `records`, `removed`, roots, tree roots, and `version` — none of the new fields. The upgraded run migrated the state database, preserved an unrelated settings file byte-for-byte, kept the pending ref and both file contributions, and after acknowledgement settled to `pending_ref: null` with canonical and projection both holding `merged after stable upgrade`. All paths and identifiers are redacted here.
- Accepted limits: guest-version probing is bounded at 8 MiB, so a larger guest file records no reviewed version and the retained conflict capture stays authoritative; automatic file-to-directory conflict resolution is refused instead of partially applied.

prs.title: improve: clear mention notifications once you see their messages
prs.body:
Related: #194147 (complementary in-app mention alerts; not a dependency).

## What Problem This Solves

A mention stays in your Inbox even after you have seen its message in the conversation. Clearing the notification requires a second, manual dismissal.

## User Impact

User impact: a mention clears automatically when its source message becomes visible in a foreground chat pane, including either desktop split pane. Off-screen messages, hidden mobile panes, background tabs, and prepared transcript rows stay unread. Manual dismissal still works.

A visible portion of the source message counts as seen. This does not remove messages or alter browser/OS notification history. No setting, migration, permission, retention, or protocol change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message bubble reports viewport visibility only after its transcript row is presented and initial positioning has settled. Exact message, session, and agent identity select the existing authenticated Inbox entries, which clear through the existing durable dismissal owner and synchronize across browsers. Shared projections and the pooled intersection observer avoid a separate Inbox or read-state store.

The change is deliberately separate from #194147, which draws attention to mentions in other sessions but leaves Inbox entries untouched.

## Evidence

The regression fails on base `c53f0575b`: a source message is on-screen, but no dismissal is sent. It passes with this change: only that mention clears; the older, off-screen entry clears after scrolling to its source.

- Built Control UI browser checks: **4 passed** (2 new mention-read scenarios plus 2 existing mobile Inbox scenarios). New scenarios took **2.21 s** and cover off-screen sources, identical message IDs in different sessions, hidden mobile panes, desktop splits, and late Inbox arrivals while document visibility changes. Document visibility is driven through the browser fixture's platform boundary, not a physical-device test.
- UI owner and affected consumer tests: **109 passed**, 6 files, **6.42 s**.
- Existing Gateway named-recipient/cross-browser dismissal regression: **1 passed**, **17.88 s**; the other 31 tests in that file were not selected.
- UI typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, Control UI controller guard, and `git diff --check`: passed. PR CI supplies broader coverage; CI timing is not yet available.
- Fresh independent source review of the final candidate against `c53f0575b`, P0–P2: **no actionable findings**. Source-only review; the reviewer did not execute tests. Local Auto Review was interrupted and produced no completed report. Delayed native-observer delivery and dismissal rejection were inspected rather than covered by new dedicated tests.

**Before**

![Before: both mention entries remain while the source message is visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f775311c-9f22-465f-9a9f-6419200cb651)

prs.title: fix: stop background exec completion wakes from landing mid-line
prs.body:
A background exec's completion wake lands mid-line when the output is long. The wake embeds a fixed 2,000-char slice of the command output, and on a long run that slice starts where the bytes happened to be, so the woken turn cannot tell whether the last line is the command's result or just where the cut landed. This PR makes the wake carry the last non-empty line of the output instead, but only when the retained tail was actually truncated. Output that fit in the tail keeps the full tail exactly as before.

How it works: when the session's total output exceeded the retained 2,000-char tail, the wake producer selects the last non-empty line of the tail, strips a leading `OK: ` or `ERR: ` marker when one is present, trims it through the same 2,000-char cap when it is longer, and falls back to the previous slice when there is no usable last line (empty output, structured tails). When the output fits, the content is the trimmed tail, byte-identical to the pre-change behavior. Header, duration, output-file pointer, routing and delivery are unchanged.

Evidence:

- 10 unit cases in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`: last line, trailing blank lines, `OK: ` / `ERR: ` markers, empty marker line, empty and whitespace fallback, JSON object/array tails.
- 2 wake-owner cases in the same file drive the real path (`appendOutput` + `maybeNotifyOnExit` → `prepareExecExitWake`): a truncated oversized tail surfaces the stripped `OK: ` summary with the truncation header, and output that fits keeps every line of the tail.
- The existing wake tests in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` pin the header, the `with no output.` case, the bounded tail and the file pointer. Their fixtures end in a single line, so the selected line equals the old tail and those assertions hold unchanged.

Behavior proof (review host): `pnpm install`/build/test are not available on this host, so the proof runs the patched sources directly under Node 26 type-stripping through an ESM hooks loader (`node --import ./loader.mjs proof.ts`). The loader resolves the repo's `.js` specifiers to `.ts` sources and maps workspace packages to their `src`; the only shims are delivery plumbing the wake path does not exercise (logger, system-event queue, terminal-core pass-throughs, published `@openclaw/fs-safe`/`@openclaw/proc-safe` bindings, `chalk`/`tslog`/`semver`/`string-width`, and the parameter-property-only leaves `retry`, `runtime`, `env-substitution`, `plugin-instance-error`). Wakes are rendered through the real entry point (`maybeNotifyOnExit` → `prepareExecExitWake`) with three synthetic fixtures:

```
=== (a) short multi-line output that fits the retained window (input 27 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-0, code 0, 0s):
line one
line two
last line

=== (b) oversized multi-line output truncated mid-line, last line is an OK: marker (input 2009 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-1, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2009 output chars (process log has the rest):
done

=== (c) structured multi-line JSON tail (input 2008 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-2, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2008 output chars (process log has the rest):
yyyy...yyy            (1,994 y's, abbreviated)
{
  "a": 1
}
```

(a) fits, so the full tail is kept, the pre-change content, unchanged. (b) is truncated mid-line and ends in an `OK: ` marker, so the wake carries just `done`. (c) is a structured tail whose last line is a JSON closing bracket, so the whole tail is kept.

Cut from upstream main `375daf6d3` (rebased after review). Verified against the main tip that no open PR or recent commit covers this.

One ask: the fork CI run needs a maintainer to approve it before hosted CI executes. Could a maintainer approve https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44219905140 ?

prs.title: fix: recycle MCP sessions rejected as invalid
prs.body:
Closes #200106

## What Problem This Solves

A streamable HTTP MCP server can reject an existing session with `invalid session`. OpenClaw kept sending later tool calls through that stale session, so GitHub-hosted MCP tools stayed unusable until the Gateway restarted.

## User Impact

When a stateful streamable HTTP server returns a 4xx response containing `invalid session`, the next explicit tool call now uses a fresh MCP session instead of remaining stuck on the rejected one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared MCP session-expiry classifier now recognizes the reported invalid-session response alongside the existing stateful HTTP 404 signal. The failed call is still returned to the user and is never replayed; retirement and replacement use the existing lifecycle path.

## Evidence

The following is a redacted, inspectable trace from the production `createSessionMcpRuntime` against an isolated local streamable HTTP server. It records the MCP method, `mcp-session-id`, HTTP status, and response body.

### Base `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110`

```text
HTTP request method=POST mcp=initialize session=<none>
HTTP response status=200 session=s1 body={"...":"initialize"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=notifications/initialized session=s1
HTTP response status=202 session=s1 body=
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/list session=s1
HTTP response status=200 session=s1 body={"...":"probe"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s1 attempt=one
HTTP response status=400 session=s1 body=invalid session
error one SdkHttpError: Error POSTing to endpoint: invalid session
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s1 attempt=two
HTTP response status=400 session=s1 body=invalid session
error two SdkHttpError: Error POSTing to endpoint: invalid session
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s1 attempt=three
HTTP response status=400 session=s1 body=invalid session
error three SdkHttpError: Error POSTing to endpoint: invalid session
error four Error: bundle-mcp server "proof" is paused after repeated tool failures
{"initializeCount":1,"calls":[{"attempt":"one","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"two","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"three","session":"s1"}],"activeSession":"s1"}
```

Base keeps the rejected `s1` and eventually pauses; no replacement initialize occurs.

### Fixed `8f38a4530223a4e11c34b7747e53e3ec26e9de25`

```text
HTTP request method=POST mcp=initialize session=<none>
HTTP response status=200 session=s1 body={"...":"initialize"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s1 attempt=before
HTTP response status=200 session=s1 body={"...":"ok:s1"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s1 attempt=expired
HTTP response status=400 session=s1 body=invalid session
[bundle-mcp] recycling server "proof" after expired HTTP session
expired SdkHttpError: Error POSTing to endpoint: invalid session
HTTP request method=POST mcp=initialize session=<none>
HTTP response status=200 session=s2 body={"...":"initialize"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=notifications/initialized session=s2
HTTP response status=202 session=s2 body=
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/list session=s2
HTTP response status=200 session=s2 body={"...":"probe"}
HTTP request method=POST mcp=tools/call session=s2 attempt=after
HTTP response status=200 session=s2 body={"...":"ok:s2"}
after { content: [ { type: 'text', text: 'ok:s2' } ] }
{"initializeCount":2,"calls":[{"attempt":"before","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"expired","session":"s1"},{"attempt":"after","session":"s2"}],"activeSession":"s2"}
```

Fixed retires `s1` after the 400 rejection, initializes `s2` only for the next explicit call, and does not replay `expired`.

## Verification

- The focused Docker proof passed with non-root, no network, read-only source, 256 MiB memory, 0.5 CPU, 64 PIDs, and 32 MiB tmpfs.
- The trace harnesses above exited 0 and exercised the production runtime over real local HTTP.
- `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and esbuild syntax checks passed for both changed files.
- The focused Vitest worker was SIGKILLed by the mandated 256 MiB limit before tests started; repository CI should run the committed regression. The local oxlint config could not load its Solid plugin from the offline dependency copy, so lint remains for CI.
- Independent read-only review of the complete `origin/main..HEAD` diff found no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings.

prs.title: improve: resume cold-history navigation after update readiness
prs.body:
Related: #182616

This is one narrow update-window change; it does not claim to resolve the issue’s separate historical copy/hash and repeated-Doctor costs.

## What Problem This Solves

Updates can keep the Gateway stopped while Doctor builds navigation for old cold-history archives. That projection is reconstructible, and the archives remain restorable before it finishes.

## User Impact

Update Doctor leaves SQLite cold navigation pending for the Gateway's existing post-readiness background worker. Required migrations and integrity checks remain before activation; standalone Doctor and PostgreSQL retain their existing repair behavior. No schema, configuration, retention or permission changes.

This remains a draft until the five-pair update/downtime comparison and foreground-latency acceptance are complete. Installed-updater correctness and controlled rollback proof passed on 2026.11.2; latest-stable qualification remains limited by the release-age policy. One complete archive remains an atomic writer transaction and can exceed the active-facts row/time budget; a large-archive test observed approximately 676 ms admitted execution for one 4,096-event archive. No foreground latency regression has been accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing SQL pending predicate and existing transcript-facts scheduler, background writer admission, cancellation and database lifetime. Discover pending cold archives without reading their payloads; prepare archive decoding lazily only for a cold command. Recheck pending state in the writer so concurrent restoration or retirement cannot resurrect an archive. No second scheduler, progress sidecar or schema is introduced.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on the original production source and green with the fix for both package-swap and post-core convergence Doctor phases.
- Five focused owner/consumer files initially passed 49 tests across four shards. After the independent-review repair, three relevant suites passed 39 tests, including the new missing/corrupt archive progress regressions. Exact restores, unchanged archive payloads, cancellation/recreated pass, no duplicate work, and a real foreground actor transcript append preceding cold backfill are covered.
- Core and scripts typechecks, touched test type graphs (state-logging and agents-sessions), targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Canonical package build and tarball integrity passed; the repaired runtime was rebuilt and the final tarball was packed and integrity-checked again. Packaging reported UI size-budget warnings; this backend-only change has not attributed those warnings against baseline.
- Actual released CLI 2026.11.2 (b556fdf) produced baseline schema 27 and reached readiness. Its correctly bound package entrypoint then ran a real npm update to the final candidate: status ok, schema 42, 0 cold archives migrated and all 3 pending. Two separate installed-candidate Gateway processes reached HTTP readiness with pending counts 3 and 2; the first stopped after one archive, the second completed the remaining two. Independent SHA-256 checks matched all archive bytes to the pre-update fixture; foreign-key checks were empty.
- The installed-update fixture contains 3 archives × 4,096 events (12,288 events; roughly 150.9 MB raw envelope bytes). This complete installed run supersedes an earlier source-runtime attempt whose aggregate timed out amid startup/filesystem stalls. The earlier failure is retained and is not treated as a latency pass.
- The maintained state-scoped failing-Doctor package fixture produced a real post-activation failure. The updater reported rollbackOutcome=succeeded and restored 2026.11.4. Exact config, finalize-worker, six agent table snapshots, archive payload hashes, and schema matched the pre-failure oracle; the restored installed Gateway reached readiness with no foreign-key failures. This proves an injected failure/rollback path, not a failure in the normal candidate.
- Required gaps: latest stable 2026.11.5 and 2026.11.4 installations were refused by the release-age cutoff; date-qualified 2026.11.2 was used without policy overrides. Five interleaved A/B samples, TOTAL UPDATE/GATEWAY DOWNTIME distributions and foreground latency comparison remain unproven. One successful older-driver update is not the complete performance acceptance rule.
- Independent narrative frozen-source review found a real P2 starvation defect, reproduced and repaired: one unreadable archive must not stop healthy archives later in the pass. Only typed archive-read errors are isolated after confirmed rollback; authority/cancellation/SQL/lifecycle failures remain terminal. Follow-up independent narrative review of patch 839d30cc3584aa17bbcefeeb3738162553104dc30231a5ef7307793cb3bedb56 confirmed the P2 resolved and identified no new actionable P0–P2 findings; it retained the unproven foreground-latency/shutdown-duration caveat and frozen-input/live-checkout limitations. Bound Auto Review failed before launch because its installed helper script is absent; no helper-validated review is claimed.

Requested by Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with Jacqueline Henriksen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0883b476-2af0-4f4f-9bc7-593c230557af)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/f43cbe3d)

prs.title: fix: send native clients their requested startup model catalog
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native clients can negotiate an initial model catalog successfully but never receive the requested model list, even when they have the same operator permissions as the browser Control UI. The Gateway silently skips publication unless the connecting client uses the browser's product ID.

## User Impact

Native macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android client identities can receive the initial model catalog they requested, using the same operator scopes and session-access checks as browser clients. No configuration changes, migrations, or additional permissions are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Honor the existing model-catalog capability negotiation instead of filtering by browser ID. Catalog reads continue through the ordinary authenticated request dispatcher, so pairing, model policy, session authorization, and delivery checks remain unchanged. Clients that do not request a snapshot keep using ordinary catalog reads.

This is a focused fix for model-catalog startup, not a claim to remove every native/browser UI difference. It removes one redundant product-ID gate without adding helpers, state, or compatibility paths (production delta: +1/-2; tests: +46/-1).

## Evidence

- Reproduced through a real isolated Gateway and signed WebSocket clients: the regression fails against the original code with `openclaw-macos did not receive its negotiated model catalog`.
- With the fix, the same suite passes for paired macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android client identities, alongside the existing browser, saved-session, and non-opt-in cases. Test body: 6.43 seconds; command wall time including compilation: 49.04 seconds. CI timing is not yet available.
- Targeted Gateway-methods typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review did not produce a validated report because its response-handoff integration failed after interrupted attempts. The requester explicitly approved publishing this focused fix for human review with that limitation disclosed. No clean independent review is claimed.
- This is Gateway protocol proof with synthetic credentials and model fixtures, not physical-device or native-rendering proof. No UI layout or rendering code changes.

prs.title: fix: tell a client waiting for pairing to approve it on the Gateway host
prs.body:
Related: #200904

## What Problem This Solves

A new client that is not paired yet, such as a CLI or TUI connecting to a Gateway on another machine, gets "device pairing required". The hint then says to run `openclaw devices approve --latest` and to pass the same `--url` and `--token/--password` flags. Run from that client, the command fails with the same "device pairing required" error, so a new user following the hint gets stuck.

## User Impact

The hint now says to approve the request from the Gateway host, or in the Gateway's Control UI (Settings -> Devices). Both work before the client is paired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approve command reaches the Gateway as the same unpaired device, so the Gateway rejects it the same way. Only the Gateway host CLI or an already trusted Control UI session can approve it. The shared remediation text, shown by the TUI and the session commands, now names those paths. It keeps the note about `--url` and `--token/--password` for a host CLI that needs them. The wording matches the hint the TUI already prints for stored device auth.

## Evidence

Real CLI and TUI run against a fresh Gateway (bind lan, token auth, default pairing policy) and a second fresh state dir acting as a remote client (`gateway.mode: remote`, LAN URL plus the token). On the base, the TUI prints the old hint, and following it on the client fails with "device pairing required". On the head, the TUI names the Gateway host and the Control UI. On both, approving on the Gateway host works and the client connects.

- Regression test: the pairing-required rows in `connect-error-details.test.ts` assert the new wording. 2 failed with the source change reverted (`git apply -R`), 27 passed with it.
- Consumer tests: TUI, gateway chat, session target, session ref, daemon probe, restart health probe, gateway probe all pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed (lanes core, coreTests).
- Local ClawSweeper review of the committed range: complete, no defects found, patch rated A.

### Runtime output

Base `f3638439b92`, head `58a69057562`. Same script on both: Gateway in one fresh state dir, client in another, macOS arm64. Request IDs, the LAN address and the token are redacted.

The TUI runs under a pseudo-terminal for 25 seconds. The script keeps only screen lines that match pairing, approve, devices or gateway, so wrapped lines outside that filter show as `[...]`. Line order is restored; no line is reworded.

Base, client:

```
[cl] $ openclaw tui --session main
 gateway disconnected: device pairing required (requestId:
 <id>) | device approval needed: preview latest
 Run `openclaw devices approve --latest` to preview the pending request, then
 rerun the printed `openclaw devices approve <requestId>` command and reconnect
 [...]

[cl] $ openclaw devices approve --latest
gateway connect failed: GatewayClientRequestError: device pairing required (requestId: <id>)
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: device pairing required (requestId: <id>)
(exit 1)
```

Head, client:

```
[cl] $ openclaw tui --session main
 gateway disconnected: device pairing required (requestId:
 <id>) | device approval needed: preview latest
 Approve this request from the Gateway host: run `openclaw devices approve
 [...]
 devices approve <requestId>` command (add --url and --token/--password if that
 CLI needs them to reach the Gateway), or approve it in the Gateway's Control
 UI (Settings -> Devices). Then reconnect.
```

Head, following the hint on the Gateway host, then the client:

```
[gw] $ openclaw devices approve <id>
Approved <deviceId> (<id>)
(exit 0)

[cl] $ openclaw health
Gateway event loop: ok max=1ms p99=0ms util=0.006 cpu=0.009
Gateway check duration: 1ms
Agents: main (default)
Heartbeat interval: disabled (main)
```

prs.title: feat(ios): filter sessions by attention and work
prs.body:
Related: #162814

## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, finding conversations waiting for an answer or approval requires checking individual session rows.

## User Impact

Sessions gains All, Needs you, and Working filters with conversation counts for the selected Gateway, agent, and existing status scope. One conversation counts once even when it has multiple requests. Working includes active or queued runs and active child work; it can overlap Needs you. Request badges reuse the existing native preview and approval flow.

All preserves offline browsing. Live activity filters are disabled while disconnected, and incomplete rosters retain a + count qualifier.

This is a draft for the initial iOS design review. Physical Duo and VoiceOver checks remain before readiness. Android parity is a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Sessions screen consumes the existing live roster instead of keeping a second nonarchived snapshot. The existing owners retain question/approval matching, expiry, navigation, grouping, mutations, and Gateway policy. No server, protocol, schema, permission, or persistent setting is added.

Android's native SessionsScreen already has the needed roster and attention/run-state contracts. This PR does not modify or claim validation of Android.

## Native Sessions proof with a real Gateway

Captured on the Mac Studio with an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator running iOS 27.0. The comparison uses upstream `ed3230dd29d1` and published draft head `5c8b666d53e5`. Both apps used the same three fictional conversations from an isolated OpenClaw `2026.11.4` Gateway. The agent ran Qwen3 4B locally through llama.cpp. A test operator created and answered the ordinary question through the Gateway API, and the model generated the separate work turn.

### Clean comparison

| Upstream Sessions | Draft Sessions |
| --- | --- |
| ![Upstream Sessions shows three rows with no activity filter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e28e8bf-83a1-4663-b9a6-20923b75021e) | ![Draft Sessions shows the same three rows, with All 3, Needs you 1, and Working 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee20cc17-e197-439d-a1c0-984f26e77384) |

### Annotated comparison

| Upstream | Draft |
| --- | --- |
| ![The rows start immediately below the status scopes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2e07899-2d29-4309-b46e-9541c2e72b3c) | ![Activity controls and counts appear between the status scopes and the rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad6e8492-764d-4e94-866c-2401e19d519e) |

### Live updates

| Needs you selected | Working selected | After both settle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Needs you shows only Color review with a pending question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9f2873e-da2d-4a86-8442-6b27f3315369) | ![Working shows only Launch checklist during a real model run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd7b47fe-cea3-49e2-9fe2-3a98893e1d4e) | ![After the question and run settle, All stays at 3 and both activity counts are 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad309f62-7f9f-45ce-af63-cf17e4183e86) |

The native Sessions screen stayed open during the transition. This trace records the visible filter values and the corresponding Gateway state.

```text
Pending question in Color review     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 0
Needs you selected                  Color review is the only row
Qwen starts on Launch checklist     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 1
Separate capture with Working open  Launch checklist is the only row while the model runs
Gateway accepts Fern                Question status: answered
Model finishes                      All 3   Needs you 0   Working 0
Gateway final state                 Launch checklist: done, no active run
```

The captured proof covers this simulator and the published Sessions screen. The broader design previews below are from separate work.

## November 17 draft update

Merged upstream `ed3230dd29d1` into the existing activity-filter branch. Resolved the four conflicts while retaining upstream session grouping, collapsed sections, and the partial-load retry. The Sessions clock now refreshes when the roster changes and continues to refresh when request or snooze deadlines expire.

Verified on the iOS 27.0 iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator at `5c8b666d53e5`:

- 19 focused Swift tests passed (3 activity logic and 16 typography).
- Both native Sessions flows passed against an isolated synthetic Gateway. The activity flow verified filter counts and live request/run updates. The recency regression verified that a planning row aged past “just now” when a different row changed, with no pending requests or snoozes.
- Native localization verification, SwiftFormat, app-target SwiftLint, and diff checks passed.

The layout images below are from the earlier design prototype. This draft is still asking for an iOS design decision on the focused activity filters.

## Layout prototype for design feedback

The latest local prototype puts a compact filter dropdown beside **Sessions** in the sidebar, with compact icon-and-count cards on the full Sessions screen. Both locations offer **All**, **Needs you**, and **Working**.

On the full Sessions screen, attention rows have one tappable hand or shield on the left. The hand means **Waiting for answer**; the shield means **Waiting for approval**. Both use amber status text and a subtle warning tint because both need a user response. Working rows and the Working card use informational blue. Text and distinct symbols convey the state as well as color. Status labels consistently use sentence case, including Recent, Working, Waiting for answer, and Waiting for approval. The existing native request previews remain available. The sidebar keeps its native attention badges and work indicators.

These images show eight fictional conversations: two waiting for an answer or approval, three working, and three idle. Each image compares **All / Needs you / Working**, with no before/after panels. They are native standard-iPhone simulator captures with synthetic Gateway state. No personal conversations, private Gateway addresses, or real agent tasks appear.

Feedback requested: does keeping the sidebar control beside Sessions make its scope clear? Do the compact cards and the attention-row styling feel clear without adding clutter? Feedback on wording, spacing, colors, and selection styling is welcome. Android parity remains a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

**Sessions screen: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local Sessions prototype with amber question and approval rows, blue Working states, and compact filter cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04f3b1a7-059a-4c8e-80d0-7aa24a343e14)

**Sidebar: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local sidebar prototype with filtering beside the Sessions heading and fictional conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49b52069-9ba1-41c3-b259-5b3b8bf28392)

These are design previews from uncommitted local refinements atop local prototype `4650e6cf067c249871fa7ee7871c466a450b6d01`. The sidebar placement, card styling, status-row cleanup, and adaptive scope control shown here have not been pushed to this draft's published head, `cbb83f9eff100aa5437f15c19c9c3383ee4657d4`. They are not exact-head merge proof. The PR remains a draft for design feedback.

Local refinement checks: 24 typography tests and four activity-owner logic tests pass, as do the native filter flows at standard and largest accessibility text sizes. The sole leading hand and shield were each tapped to verify that the correct native preview opens without leaving Sessions. Light and dark appearances were inspected. The latest local prototype, including sentence-case status labels, was installed and launched on the physical Duo as the separate OpenClaw Sessions build 10. The installed version was read back from the device. A fresh physical visual/interaction check of this revision and a full VoiceOver audit are still pending. The Evidence section below describes the earlier published implementation separately.

## Evidence

- Base: 42aab1ce38cdde59eaa3f2babc3eef488ea9db2c. The native baseline reaches All Sessions and fails because the activity filter is absent.
- Three focused native logic tests pass: distinct conversation counts, overlapping work/attention, terminal and explicit run-state precedence, resolution/expiry/agent matching, and offline/partial data. Test execution: 0.016 seconds; runner setup/execution: 20.805 seconds.
- Native iPhone UI flow passes with synthesized screen taps at rendered targets, selected-state and membership assertions, 44-point targets, and live count changes after run completion and question/approval resolution. Standard-size run: 53.400 seconds; largest system accessibility text: 47.326 seconds. The filters stack vertically at the largest size. Existing session-row text still elides at that size; this is not a full accessibility audit.
- XCTest AX hit-point lookup reports no hit point for the activity filters and existing status picker on this simulator. The test explicitly synthesizes screen touches rather than relying on AX activation, then checks the resulting state. VoiceOver is not covered by this result.
- 23 focused typography tests pass. Targeted SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, Node syntax, native i18n verification, docs formatting/MDX, link audit, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Fresh independent source review has no actionable P0-P2 findings. It caught an offline-cache cold-open regression and incomplete archive counts, both repaired before the final run.
- Full-app local qualification: unchanged base strict SwiftLint fails in the Apple review demo fixture, also tracked by #191296. Both UI comparison builds use an independently written, local-only extraction of two unchanged fixture branches, preserving guards, payloads, and timestamps. The synthetic Gateway path never enters those branches. No guard or lint configuration is weakened. That qualification and unrelated generated Info.plist changes are excluded from this PR. These results are not exact-tree full-app CI.
- Evidence uses the native app and an isolated synthetic Gateway. No live agent, provider, command, or account is used. Physical Duo, VoiceOver, exact-head CI, ClawSweeper, and maintainer approval are not claimed.

prs.title: fix(agents): move active node presence to current-turn context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #192364. `active_node` and `active_node_identity` are on the Runtime line, and `openai-completions` routes relocate that line into the first user message. When a Mac app quits or comes back, the value changes, message 1 is rewritten, and everything after the system prompt falls out of an exact-prefix cache. The report measured 67-85 s replies instead of about 1 s on a ~90k-token session.

## User Impact

A node going away or returning no longer rewrites earlier messages, so the conversation stays cached. The model still sees the current active computer every turn, now in the newest message's runtime context.

Two visible changes:

- CLI backends now always get the fact in the turn context. It used to be skipped when the system prompt was sent, because the Runtime line carried it.
- **Known gap:** `settled-tool-finalization` and raw model runs carry no runtime facts by design, so those runs no longer see `active_node`. They previously saw it through the system prompt. The report also flags this. I kept their exact-prompt rule rather than adding text; a maintainer may want to weigh in if finalization needs it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direction comes from @dertbv's diagnosis and local test in the issue. The CLI and harness paths already deliver this as a per-turn fact, so this moves the embedded path onto the same model:

- Removes the two fields from `buildRuntimeLine`, the runtime info types, `buildSystemPromptParams` and the prompt-cache field labels.
- `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` runs `prepareActiveNodeContext` for the admitted run's operator profile and then adds `buildActiveNodeContextText` as a `conversation-data` fragment. The hint is read synchronously, so the keyed refresh has to come first or a revoked pairing could still show the retired node.
- `buildCliTurnAppendContext` appends it unconditionally, before media progress, which stays last.

## Evidence

![Prefix A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/192364/proof-192364.png)

Real Gateway on Windows with real agent turns in one session. A stub `openai-completions` provider diffs each request's messages against the previous request. Presence is on for requests 1-2, gone for 3-4, and back for 5.

| Request | Presence | Before: earlier messages | After: earlier messages |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `mac-node-1` | identical | identical |
| 3 | gone | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |
| 4 | gone | identical | identical |
| 5 | back | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |

Before, the value lives in `msg[1]` and changes there. After, each turn's value is in that turn's own message (`msg[2]`, `msg[5]`, `msg[8]`, ...) and later requests leave those bytes alone. In the before run, the rewritten requests kept 54162 of 56011 and 54162 of 57600 characters as an unchanged prefix; the small size is the stub session's, not a real session's.

**CLI backend.** I registered a stub executable with `api.registerCliBackend` (`systemPromptArg`, `systemPromptWhen: "first"`, `resumeArgs`), so the real CLI runner builds the arguments. The stub logs what it received:

| Turn | Before: value in system prompt / prompt | After: value in system prompt / prompt |
|---|---|---|
| First (new session) | `mac-node-1` / none | none / `mac-node-1` |
| Resumed, node gone | not passed / `unknown` | not passed / `unknown` |
| Resumed, node back | not passed / `mac-node-1` | not passed / `mac-node-1` |

Tests, with regressions in `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` that fail without the embedded fact and without the refresh before reading it:

| File | Result |
|---|---|
| `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` | 21 passed |
| `system-prompt-params.test.ts` | 23 passed |
| `runtime-facts-prompt.test.ts` | 10 passed |
| `runtime-prompt.test.ts` | 8 passed |
| `gateway/node-registry-pairing.test.ts` | 12 passed |
| `worker-turn-launcher-remote-handoff.test.ts` | 2 passed on `42b8f41` |
| `tool-result-truncation.test.ts` | 1 failed, 55 passed: a Windows path error (ENOENT on a drive-letter path joined under the temp dir) in a spill-pointer test this PR does not touch; I did not rerun it on base |
| `attempt-prompt-build.*`, `attempt-prompt-submit`, `attempt-context-advancement`, phase and media-hint tests | passed |
| `cli-runner/prepare.durable-context.test.ts` | 13 failed, 7 passed, same as base |
| `cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 13 failed, 100 passed, same as base |

Those two CLI files already fail on this Windows machine (for example `/bin/echo` not resolvable and `EBUSY`). I compared failing test names with and without the change and none are new, but this means CLI path coverage is weak locally, so please check them in CI.

Passed locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (net 0 test lines), `agents-root` and `agents-other` test types (the project CI failed on before).

## What was not tested

- Presence was changed with a preload calling `setActiveNodeContexts`, because this box has no paired Mac. The node connect and disconnect path was not exercised; the report did exercise it on a similar patch.
- The stub compares bytes. I did not measure real cache hits or latency on a caching server; the report's numbers are from its own patched build.
- The CLI proof uses a stub executable through the real runner, not Claude Code or another real CLI.
- Requester-scoped refresh is covered by unit tests and the default-profile live path; I did not run a non-owner profile with a revoked pairing end to end.


## Related defect deliberately left out of this PR

The remote macOS skills note has the same effect on the cached prefix: `getRemoteSkillEligibility` builds `Remote macOS node available (…). Run macOS-only skills via exec host=node on that node.` in `src/skills/runtime/remote.ts`, `prepareSkillsForPrompt` appends it to the skills text, and that text becomes the `## Skills` section of the frozen system prompt. A Mac node going online or away therefore rewrites the same bytes this PR just moved out of the Runtime line.

@ensignwesley reproduced that on main with serialized-request evidence (two identical online requests, first differing byte at offset 6444; [run](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/actions/runs/43812563271)) and is preparing a separate embedded-only change that sends the note through the current-turn carrier introduced here, leaving CLI and Codex output byte-identical. It is not folded in because the note lives in the snapshot/projection path shared by the CLI and Codex skill-prompt builders, so including it would widen this PR's proof scope from presence placement to skills-snapshot behavior. It will be linked here once opened.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin service `ctx.getCron().add()` creates agent-turn automations without recording their inference account. Stored-account execution then refuses both isolated and custom-session tasks before model execution.

Closes #192327.

## User Impact

New service-created automations retain the selected account and runtime. Existing bound jobs retain ownership; existing unbound jobs still require explicit adoption.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the Gateway's existing target/session capture composition and account authorization owner. The service pins the effective agent across asynchronous capture, retains authorization through store acceptance, and releases it after settlement. Service stop, scheduler replacement, credential replacement and personal-account authorization remain admission boundaries. Gateway creator attribution and optional session-lookup ownership are preserved.

## Evidence

### Final-effect service authorization proof

Additional formal `ocpr prove 192327 --phase post` executed unchanged head `0122a28d0203d01901346d58bb59530ef80700d1` in response to the current-head authority-chain request. A private source-entry driver ran the actual `createPluginServiceCronGetter`, shared capture, canonical account writers, `CronService` and SQLite mutation owners. ### Checks

- After the export-preserving fixture repair, the affected **9 tests**, official mock-export gate, targeted lint and core test types passed. Production-source checks and broader local coverage were retained because production code did not change.

prs.title: fix(subagents): private child results no longer show as delivered in the parent's context
prs.body:
Related: #173650

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the parent agent's runtime context and the `subagents` tool report `delivery=delivered` for a `completionTarget: "parent"` child when the result was only processed in a private turn and nothing was sent to the user.

## User Impact

User impact: after a private subagent completion, the parent's own facts no longer claim the result was delivered. It sees `delivery=consumed_privately`, so it has no runtime fact telling it the user already has the result. When the turn that processed the result did reach the user (a private turn that sent its final with `message`, or a yielded parent's resumed answer), the label stays `delivered`. Settlement outcomes, retries and channel delivery are unchanged, and nothing new is sent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main settles a private completion as `delivered` once the private requester turn processes it (`resolvePrivateCompletionDeliveryResult`: "no external receipt is owed"), and `docs/tools/subagents/announce.md` says later parent turns own any outstanding answer (#185388). This PR keeps that contract. The problem is the projection: `buildSubagentList` copied `delivery.status` into the list view and `buildActiveSubagentRuntimeContext` printed it as `delivery=delivered` under "Recently Completed Subagents" for 30 minutes, the same label an announced child gets. The `subagents` wait view copied it too. In #173650 (2026.10.3, `1ecf113bef64`, same rendering code) the registry recorded `delivered` with 0 messaging-tool outcomes and no channel send, and 13 minutes later, inside that block's 30-minute window, the parent told the user the result was already "in the thread above". That turn's request was not captured, so the label is the likely source of the claim, not a proven one.

- Settlement records the fact. Both settlement writers, `recordAnnounceDeliveryResult` (direct private turn) and the requester batch in `subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts` (settle wakes, including a yielded parent's resumed turn), call `recordPrivateConsumption`. It sets `delivery.consumedPrivately` for a `completionTarget: "parent"` result only when the host did not confirm a visible final (`requesterVisibleFinalDelivered`).
- `resolveSubagentDeliveryStatus` in `subagent-list.ts` reads that fact. The list view (runtime context and `subagents` list) and the `subagents` wait view both call it.
- My first revision inferred private-only consumption from a missing `requesterVisibleFinal`. That was wrong: it is a per-requester-turn dedupe receipt that the requester release deletes, that is bound only while `requesterTurnRunId` is set, and that the batch settlement never writes, so a yielded parent's answer that reached the user was labeled `consumed_privately`. The projection no longer reads it.
- Rows settled before this change have no `consumedPrivately` and keep reporting `delivered`. No migration: it is an optional field in `subagent_runs.payload_json`.
- Docs: the private parent completion section and the `subagents` tool reference.

Not changed:
- Settlement outcomes. The existing case "preserves private parent consumption and final evidence: private text" still pins `delivered: true` with no visible final and no send, and the QA scenario still waits for `delivery.status=delivered` on both private runs.
- No tracking of an update the model promised in prose. That is the open product question in #173650.
- "Child results awaiting delivery" keeps the raw status: rows there are outstanding, and the one way a `delivered` row lands there (a retained settle marker) is what #166270 removes.
- The private final text stays in the parent's model transcript as hidden assistant text. That can also feed an "already sent" claim; this PR does not touch it.

pr-simplify: one helper decides private consumption and both settlement writers call it; one helper projects it for both readers. No schema version and no change to settlement outcomes. Removed in the review round: the projection's reads of `requesterVisibleFinal` and `completionTarget`, and the seeded-receipt test. Deltas vs main: production +28/-2 in 6 files, tests +58 (allocation 58), QA scenario +50/-1, docs +9/-2.

## Evidence

**Merged with main** (head `dcd997f6f2f`, main `5767fe7aae6`, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). The branch was 2,873 commits behind. Main's #199695 reworked requester settlement: the requester batch now marks delivery through `markDelivered`, the registry records the requester's consumption as `requesterDelivery`, and a blocked completion whose input the requester already consumed (a private continuation cancelled by a restart, for one) is now also marked `delivered`. That last path is a third writer of the label this PR fixes. Conflicts:

- `subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts`: main's version, with `recordPrivateConsumption` after both `markDelivered` calls. The requester batch passes the outcome's `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered` as before. The blocked path passes `false`, because its outcome delivered nothing to the user.
- `subagent-registry-lifecycle-delivery.ts`: both imports.
- `subagents-tool.ts`: `deliveryStatus` keeps `resolveSubagentDeliveryStatus`, next to main's new `requesterDelivery` field.
- `subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts`: both sides' new cases.

Main's cancelled-continuation test (`subagent-requester-delivery.test.ts`) now also checks the reported status: `consumed_privately` without a visible final and `failed` with one, through both the requester batch and the blocked path. Re-run on the merge:

- QA Lab `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` (mock-openai, qa-channel): passes 1/1, follow-up labels `consumed_privately`, `consumed_privately`, `delivered`. With main's 6 production files it fails at `[private-follow-up] later parent turn mislabeled private or announced child delivery`, labels `delivered`, `delivered`, `delivered`.
- With main's two writers (`subagent-completion-mutation.kernel.ts`, `subagent-registry-lifecycle-delivery.ts`), 4 cases fail with `expected 'delivered' to be 'consumed_privately'`: requester-wake `visible=false`, lifecycle `completionTarget=parent visibleFinal=undefined`, and the two `visibleFinal: false` rows of the cancelled-continuation test. With all 6 production files from main, `subagent-active-context.test.ts` fails `expected '## Recently Completed Subagents\nChil…' to contain 'delivery=consumed_privately;'` and the `subagents` tool case "reports private parent consumption without claiming user delivery" fails. All pass on the merge.
- Dropping only the blocked-path call fails only the `{"kind":"block","visibleFinal":false}` row.
- 18 test files, 405 tests, 0 failed: the 10 completion files, registry lifecycle (222 tests), lifecycle wake retry and settle-yielded, delivery state, list, active context, SQLite store, requester delivery and the `subagents` tool.
- `tsgo`, all 7 lanes, 0 errors. oxlint and oxfmt clean. Test-lines (+58, allocation 58), line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets pass.
- Test cost of the changed `subagent-requester-delivery.test.ts` (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local default runtime): 35.8 s cold and 7.5 s wall, 4 tests.

Everything below is from the pre-merge heads.

Base `f5f27c3ef6e`, head `519a4826f87`, macOS arm64. Correction: the QA lab run and the test suites in this section used the local default runtime, which since #172625 is OpenClaw's pinned Bun, not Node 26.12.1 as this line said. The real-model run, the upgrade runs and the Node re-run below are on Node 26.12.1.

**QA lab** `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` (mock-openai, qa-channel, real Gateway child). After both private children settle, the scenario sends one more DM in the private conversation, reads that turn's model request from the mock, and checks the `delivery=` label for the two private runs and the announced `visible` run.

| Source | Result | Labels (private-first, private-second, visible) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | pass, 1/1 | `consumed_privately`, `consumed_privately`, `delivered` |
| main's 6 production files | fail at `[private-follow-up]` | `delivered`, `delivered`, `delivered` |

On this branch the same labels appear on the session's turns after `gateway.restart`, so the recorded fact survives the SQLite round trip. Both private runs still settle `delivery.status=delivered`. In the private conversation qa-channel saw only "Worker started." and the follow-up reply; 0 of 20 captured outbound events carried private child text or media.

**Real model, real Gateway** (head `cb4d3469f05`, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). An isolated Gateway from this build ran the bundled Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API, with a real model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700`; an earlier run with `qwen3.8-27b` gave the same labels for P, V and A). Every model request was recorded. One DM session. The model was told the exact `sessions_spawn` arguments and made the calls itself:

| Child | Spawn and parent's handling | Registry after settlement | Sent to the chat |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lp-private` | `completionTarget: "parent"`; the private turn ended `NO_REPLY` | `delivered`, `consumedPrivately: true` | only "Worker P started."; the child text 0 times |
| `lp-visible` | `completionTarget: "parent"`; the private turn sent the result with `message` (`final: true`) | `delivered` | "Worker V started.", then "Child V says LP191857-CHILD-V-..." |
| `lp-announced` | default target | `delivered` | "Worker A started." |
| `lp-yield-visible` | `completionTarget: "parent"`, then `sessions_yield`; the resumed parent's final was "Child Y says ..." | `delivered` | "Child Y says LP191857-CHILD-Y-..." |
| `lp-yield-private` | the same, but the resumed parent ended `NO_REPLY` | `delivered`, `consumedPrivately: true` | nothing |

The yielded parents were resumed by the requester-settle run (`announce:requester-settle:...:yield-1` in the Gateway log), the batch settlement path the Codex P2 was about.

On the next DM turn, the parent's own request listed all five under "Recently Completed Subagents": `consumed_privately` for `lp-private` and `lp-yield-private`, `delivered` for the other three. The model then called `subagents` `list` and `wait` (`timeoutSeconds: 0`); both returned the same five `deliveryStatus` values, and the model's reply listed them. After a Gateway restart on the same state, the same turn read the same five values in all three places. In the whole run the Bot API got 7 `sendMessage` calls: the five texts in the table and the two check replies.

Before the change, on released 2026.11.1 with the same private spawn (registry `completionTarget: "parent"`), the parent's context, `list` and `wait` all said `lp-private=delivered`. Without this PR, same five children with the same model: this PR's base `d44c9ad927d` and current main `3855c896edd` both label all five `delivered` in the parent's context, `list` and `wait`, before and after a restart, including the two silent ones.

**Upgrade from the latest releases**, 2026.11.1 (asked for) and 2026.11.2 (npm `latest`). Installed from npm into a scratch prefix, isolated state, the same real Gateway setup. The released CLI wrote `agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent: 4`, `archiveAfterMinutes: 240` and `runTimeoutSeconds: 600`. The released Gateway ran a private child, an announced child and a check turn, then stopped.

This build on the same state:
- `config validate` is clean before and after main's own `doctor --fix --non-interactive` (exit 0: schema migrations 22 to 39 and 27 to 41, with pre-migration backups). Plain main `d44c9ad927d`, upgraded in a separate 2026.11.1 run (model `qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700`; there the release's own private row had already ended `suspended`, the release failure below), gives the same `validate`, `doctor --fix` and settings results, and a new private child on it reads `delivered`.
- The three subagent settings read back unchanged. Doctor's only config edits are `meta.migrations.skillLibraryToolSplit`, `agents.entries.main {}`, `channels.telegram.groupAllowFrom`, three `skills.entries.*.enabled: false` and `wizard.lastRun*` (and, from 2026.11.2, `meta.lastTouchedVersion` to 2026.11.1, this build's package version).
- The session continued with the released build's turns in its history.
- The released build's rows load as they were stored: its private row has no `consumedPrivately` and still reads `delivered`, as described above for rows settled before this change. Its announced row reads `delivered`.
- A new private child on this build reads `consumed_privately` in context, `list` and `wait`, before and after a restart.

On 2026.11.2, the released build's own private completion failed in that run: `Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`, row `suspended`, `permanent_failure`. This build loaded that row as `suspended`. The failure is the release's, not this change's: in my runs it hit 4 of 6 private spawns on 2026.11.2 and 2 of 5 on 2026.11.1, against 0 of 11 on this head's build across five runs. Released 11.1 and 11.2 still treat a private completion turn as owing an answer, so a `NO_REPLY` there is retried as an empty response; main settles it quietly since #185388.

**Settlement**, through the real writers instead of a seeded receipt:
- Lifecycle receipt cases (`recordAnnounceDeliveryResult` via announce cleanup): parent without a visible final -> `consumed_privately`; parent with `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered` -> `delivered`; non-private -> `delivered`.
- Persisted requester batch (`mutateRequesterBatch` on SQLite): private batch with a confirmed visible final -> `delivered`; without -> `consumed_privately`.
- On the first revision `2a25638df1e` the visible-final case fails in both: `expected 'consumed_privately' to be 'delivered'`.
- Removing the visible-final check, the `completionTarget` check, the kernel call or the lifecycle call each fails exactly one of these cases.

**Projection**: `subagent-active-context.test.ts` and `subagents-tool.test.ts` render a settled `consumedPrivately` row as `delivery=consumed_privately` and `deliveryStatus: "consumed_privately"`.

**Focused suites**: 33 files, 668 tests passed (completion admission and kernel, registry lifecycle, delivery state, list, active context, requester yield, maintenance, SQLite store, catch-up integration, announce delivery and requester-settle cases, `subagents` tool, runtime facts, prefix stability, gateway prompt cache, recent-subagents prompt, silent-completion and announce-owner product tests).

**Focused suites on Node** (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, Node 26.12.1, head `cb4d3469f05`): 6 files, 303 tests passed, 0 failed, including the requester-wake cases `keeps a private batch delivered only with a confirmed visible final`.

**Checks**: `pnpm tsgo:all` exit 0; oxlint and oxfmt clean; line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets OK. Test-lines: +54 with a matching allocation; at `f5f27c3ef6e` main itself is 10 lines over its ceiling (6421662 vs 6421652), so the ratchet reports "over by: 10" until main is back under.
