prs.title: feat: customize agent welcome prompts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents offer generic welcome prompts instead of the tasks their authors recommend.

## User Impact

On an agent’s main/new-chat page:
- With recent chats, show the recent-chat list only.
- Without recent chats, use the agent’s configured `recommendedPrompts` instead of the defaults.
- An unset or empty list keeps the existing defaults, including “What can you do?”.
- An authored description replaces generic welcome guidance; required placement/terminal hints still take priority. Incognito help remains available without shifting the agent identity.

Existing permission, model-setup, incognito, and phone visibility rules remain unchanged. Opening the page sends nothing; clicking a starter submits its text normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse ordinary agent metadata and the existing recents-or-suggestions layout. Optional description and starter metadata travel through `agents.list`; starters share the existing three-prompt/128-code-point validation and whitespace normalization.

Template pages, install-time task selection, bootstrap, and Retry are restored to their pre-PR behavior. Templates may supply welcome metadata in `CLAW.md`, but it is used only by the installed agent’s welcome page. There is no selected-task setup state or additional workflow.

## Evidence

- [Follow-up: agent-description hint and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197402#issuecomment-6964619050).

- **Scope:** 34 changed files, down from the original 60; no general test-allowance or UI-size-budget increase. Current net test delta is +434 lines. CI still mechanically requires a record despite the documented required-regression exemption, so the exact 34-line excess is allocated specifically to the reproduced description-bearing Incognito geometry/popover regressions; no assertions were removed. Recommendations retain the existing recents guard and click/send owners.
- **Prior feature checks:** 181 focused tests, five built-UI browser cases, core/UI types, targeted lint/format, generated validators and docs checks passed. The docs-only follow-up passes MDX, format and whitespace checks; Add/Retry documentation is byte-identical to the retained comparison base.
- **Prior picker measurement:** 37 WebKit and 37 Chromium picker cases passed after making the geometry fixture wait for the existing opening animation. The original 0.5 px centering and 6 px spacing assertions remain unchanged; no production layout/CSS changed. The exact cause of the preceding CI-only offset is not established.
- **Real Gateway + real model:** the built UI loaded all three configured starters from an unmocked Gateway via `agents.list`. Opening created no session. Clicking the first starter created one session and persisted exactly one matching user message in `chat.history`. Actual local Qwen3 4B Instruct inference replied: “Cedar Notes search works offline and will ship on Friday.” Gateway, browser and model cleanup completed.
- **Latest-stable upgrade:** official npm OpenClaw 2026.11.4 produced the agent configuration, SQLite session and transcript through its CLI/Gateway. The candidate opened that same state, then cold-restarted again with a third distinct process ID. Original agent settings, session identity/label and exact transcript roles/content remained intact; newly configured prompts also survived restart and reached `agents.list`. Only main’s existing Doctor normalization retired the legacy heartbeat enrollment; this PR adds no migration.
- **Prior-head CI:** revision `ed34c0676132` passed [the required gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44063689752/job/133984514711): 152 check runs plus three successful commit-status contexts, with complete pagination recorded. That run predates the conflict integration and is not current-head CI for the candidate.
- **Conflict-repair validation:** published signed candidate `0b56450e3b22` integrates captured main `0c19bcdf2939`. The only conflict was the generated configuration-baseline checksum manifest, recreated with its owning generator. All original feature added/deleted lines are preserved apart from that manifest. **167 focused tests passed** (schema/config, Template install, agent-list projection, welcome behavior, wrapper import inventory and 37 Chromium picker cases), as did UI typechecking, generated-baseline verification and whitespace checks. Fresh independent static review of the exact candidate tree found no actionable issues. Existing real-Gateway, real-model, latest-stable and visual proof is retained for unchanged feature behavior; it was not repeated for checksum-only conflict repair. That candidate was later superseded by the description-first revision and correction below.
- **Description-first follow-up:** @vyctorbrzezowski removed redundant generic guidance when an agent has a description. Fresh review exposed a real 11px Incognito identity shift on phones. Signed correction `42a5f0601c7e` floats only status-without-text, preserving textual hints and the existing popover lifecycle. All **11 focused Chromium welcome/Incognito cases** passed, plus UI typecheck, targeted TSX/CSS lint and format. Fresh independent review of the exact corrected tree found no actionable issues. [Inspected clean and annotated regression comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197402#issuecomment-6965701058); [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44214240324) completed with the two unrelated failures qualified below.
- **CI-only correction:** signed `80e0e68f4494` adds that exact 34-line record and fixes the observed picker-test `no-shadow` error by renaming one local; no production code or visual inputs change. The owning ratchet, targeted lint/format and all 37 Chromium picker cases pass. Independent review found no actionable issues. Prior-revision CI also exposed three source-independent browser failures: a heartbeat assertion stale after main’s action-summary change (`457486d`), a WebKit sheet-dismissal stall, and final Inbox Escape cleanup. The latter timing causes remain unproven; focused local heartbeat/Inbox replays passed but do not prove a repair, and local WebKit could not connect (zero tests). These are not represented as passing CI or waived security.
- **Final CI qualification:** exact `80e0e68f4494`, run `44214240324`, attempt 1: **66 successful, 23 skipped, two failed root jobs and their failed aggregate; no cancelled or running jobs**. `security-fast` passed. UI E2E shard 6 fails only because main `457486d` intentionally changed the heartbeat summary to “Used tools” while its unchanged E2E still expects “Heartbeat Respond”. Android 4K-page native validation stopped during dependency resolution when Maven returned **HTTP 429** for the Kotlin Compose plugin; this was not an application/native assertion failure. The actual tested merge (`5c8778e36df8`, baseline `4dbd70ff5fd3`) has identical heartbeat owners/test and Android/toolchain/workflow inputs to baseline. The automatic table reports UI “unknown” and Android “new”; the independent source/error qualification—not those labels—establishes their unrelated cause. Landing selects the explicit native inherited-failure exception under the scoped maintainer request. CI remains red; no security or enforced-review waiver and no rerun is claimed. The other Android matrix case, prior sidebar/Inbox failures, ratchet and lint checks passed in this attempt.
- **Review:** the original hosted review’s P3 documentation finding was fixed and its Gateway/latest-stable evidence supplied. This landing subsequently received fresh independent static review of the mechanical integration, description-first revision, Incognito correction and CI-only repair. The identified layout finding was reproduced and fixed; final correction reviews have no remaining actionable findings. Hosted review remains advisory; enforced checks/reviews are not waived.

### Clean comparison

Retained original comparison: main `8b2831e1daae` before; `98e4e7028263` after. This is the original feature comparison; the later description-first adjustment and Incognito stability correction are shown in the linked follow-up evidence. Actual built Control UI, same synthetic Gateway fixture with no recent chats, 1280×900, light theme and reduced motion. Main ignores the optional welcome metadata; the candidate shows the agent description and replaces the default starters with the configured list. Gateway responses are mocked.

**Before**

![Before: default welcome starters on original comparison main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3904744-0a69-42d8-99b2-29695e8b6493)

**After**

![After: agent description and three authored welcome starters](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce17c76f-e38c-4350-a93d-7a1b22565df4)

### Annotated comparison

Measured callouts on copies of the same clean frames.

**Before**

![Before: default starters highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e13f1b5d-64f8-4d53-b748-1c8d2ca54d8c)

**After**

![After: authored agent starters highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87458e97-a0ea-436b-b7f9-44c5037c29f6)

Two CI-only fixture repairs remain because their failures were observed in this PR's CI: typed-exit/JSON error assertions and first lazy-import readiness in the model-picker test. No production lifecycle behavior is changed; the Windows fixture and OAuth import are now already covered by main.

Contributor credit: Miguel Branco. Description-first welcome refinement: Vyctor H. Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski). Landing integration and regression correction requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4254b8dd-73d4-4bdb-845c-bf58e2ae476c)
- [Landing discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8ba547ec-36a6-4aee-964a-fe55b52c4c67)
- [Landing integration, correction and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e01621bd-dd1b-420c-a947-30076d096da7)

prs.title: docs(cloudflare): include the startup completion check in deployment verification

## What Problem This Solves

The Cloudflare deployment guide describes `/startupz` as the startup-completion check, but its verification commands never call it.

## User Impact

Operators can check startup completion separately from channel readiness when verifying a deployment. An unhealthy channel can make `/readyz` return 503 after startup has finished.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the missing authenticated `/startupz` command beside `/healthz`, and explain the separate `/readyz` command with a link to the HTTP health-check reference. This is a documentation-only correction to the verification flow introduced in #122963.

## Evidence

- Verified the distinction against `docs/gateway/health.md` and the existing startup/readiness cases in `src/gateway/server-http.probe.test.ts` at base `da5ff0fa303695e8268a69ec6c84bf907142c33a`; these tests were inspected, not executed.
- Focused oxfmt 0.74.0 check (`npm exec --yes --package=oxfmt@0.74.0 -- oxfmt --check docs/install/cloudflare.md`) and the repository MDX checker both passed for `docs/install/cloudflare.md`. The commit hook could not use the tooling owner's older oxfmt 0.73.0; committed with `--no-verify` after the separately pinned formatting proof, as documented by the hook.
- Verified the new `/gateway/health#http-checks` destination against the target page's heading with markdown-it and markdown-it-anchor.

prs.title: fix: let new sessions send their first message reliably
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first message in a new session can fail with “session changed” even though the user did not change anything. A background model-catalog save can create the database after the message has already captured its authorization facts; cold session creation also failed to retain its newly published entry through a logical store alias.

## User Impact

Users can create a session and send its first message without these database-creation races. Configured writable model owners now prepare their local canonical database before publishing request-visible facts, including owners added after startup. This may create an empty database even when discovery finds no models; network discovery still does not block readiness. Read-only and admission-refused owners keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing database-preparation owner before runtime publication, resolve the physical catalog owner, and adopt cold-created session facts only from the acknowledged creation publication. Keep authorization invalidation, cancellation, recovery, and existing deadlines intact. The synthetic caption fixture also bypasses ambient proxies only for its loopback server, preserving and restoring existing environment values.

## Evidence

- Both new startup/new-owner regressions fail on the base and pass with the repair.
- Original implementation head `624b0f6eb0fffa5dd5c77f5c0f2fecc6c6f93b87` on base `4dbd70ff5fd3edf197dafdd2f4b407627ffdcc64`, Node 24.22.1, supported isolated runner: **58 tests passed** across six files.
- Includes 17 cold-creation/settlement tests, 10 unchanged authorization and stop tests, 8 startup/static tests, 21 owner/supersession tests, the original caption test (29.159s), and public create → read → turn → history (17.800s). Original assertions and deadlines unchanged.
- Type-aware lint of all eight changed TypeScript files, formatting of all nine files, docs MDX, and diff-check passed. Required QA runtime build passed. Temporary public-flow proof substitution restored byte-for-byte; test containers removed.
- Source snapshot SHA256: `073a47ac699917d58000a1d6b17f69f83f3706edc4840bcba3b59b990db9b4ae`.

Independent review was explicitly waived for this repair task; validation and security gates remain. Other beta qualification failures remain under investigation and are not cleared by this focused proof.


## CI Fixture Follow-up

CI run 44214721325 exposed an auth-replay fixture whose 100ms real-time build deadline expired during newly required native database readiness, before testing replay ordering. The fixture now controls its timer clock, advances the same 100ms after publication, and restores real timers in `finally`. Native readiness, every assertion, and production deadlines remain unchanged. The startup fixture preserves inherited module exports; exactly two retired mock-baseline entries were removed.

- Final head: `b0803a982324f54ad5fe1b8650039078e4a821f6`.
- Exact failing owner-selection case reproduced locally on Node 24.22.1 (26 passed / 1 failed). Final supported isolated owner-selection run: **27/27 passed**, including following siblings. The unchanged startup fixture retains its prior **8/8** passing proof.
- Final type-aware lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet (6210 retained factories), and diff-check passed. No production code changed in this follow-up; original six-file product proof is retained, not represented as a fresh run.
- Repair patch SHA256: `858f357a1b3316e068167b7b18c30a34e407098ddbea693a75f22cdcfb0237ba`. Final source snapshot SHA256: `ee2a9df551d6095b2347bd30e2c615ef69747420d8e5e7c38fda1e910febf17f`.
- Simplification: test-local clock ownership and existing import-original support, no new helper or production state. Follow-up delta: 3 files, +23/-17.

Hosted CI must qualify the replacement head; the failed original-head run remains failure evidence.

prs.title: fix: keep expanded sidebar sessions from overlapping
prs.body:
Related: #199541

## What Problem This Solves

Expanding or reopening a session’s children can make the next sidebar session overlap them, especially with enlarged text. This was reported in the macOS desktop app and reproduced with the real sidebar renderer in WebKit.

## User Impact

Expanded child sessions keep enough space for their rows when a child refresh finishes. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A child refresh changed the cached geometry signature even when existing children stayed visible and no loading placeholder was rendered. That discarded the correct measured height without a size change to trigger another measurement. Use the existing loading-placeholder predicate for both the estimate and its signature; retain the mounted-measurement protection from #199541.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry-point qualification

**Passed:** the production-built Control UI was served over HTTP/WebSocket by a real isolated Gateway, using synthetic sessions created through its real `sessions.create` RPC. No Gateway mock or renderer-only fixture was used for this qualification.

- Selected **125%** text through the shipped Appearance settings, then opened Sessions through the real in-app rail.
- Repeated parent collapse/reopen **10 times**, observing **10 matching successful child-list responses** from the real Gateway before checking each completed refresh.
- All four children were present; each row was **37px** high. In every cycle the last child ended at **235px** and the following root started at **235px**: no overlap.
- The focused real-Gateway E2E finished successfully: **1/1 passed**, **15.58s wall time**. The owned Gateway shut down cleanly; the temporary qualification probe was removed from test discovery afterward.
- Source binding: the three changed files were byte-checked against PR head `f614e7149c73ba0336a3d78cd25fd6c44c6e2d2f`; its parent is the local base `7c1c497a0fe3b4ad0cfad1db02ae6cfa7ffbacd6`. The production HTML SHA-256 was `caeedc017d1a174720bb72cd17f8d82dd2ca081c3d799d56f718d29741cf3bf5`.

This closes the requested built-UI/isolated-Gateway proof gap for the sidebar scenario, not native macOS app qualification. Separate full-document chat navigation attempts hit a native Chromium renderer crash (errorCode 11); that case remains unqualified and is not claimed fixed by this PR. The passing scenario used normal in-app navigation and disclosure controls.

### Remaining CI failure

The [failed checks-ui (1/3) job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44200657650/job/134454690042) reports `keeps Pages flat and rail pins independently ordered`: its fixture loads `sidebar-reorder.css` and `sidebar-rail.css` but omits `sidebar-pages.css`, where its expected flex styles now live. Source comparison traces that extraction to [#200013](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200013), before this PR’s base; the affected fixture/styles are unchanged by this patch. This is source-attributed inherited failure evidence, not an executed exact-base replay. CI remains red; this PR does not silently repair that separate fixture.

### Focused regression evidence

- The maintained browser regression fails on base `7c1c497a0`: the following root starts at 219px while the last child ends at 244px. It passes with this fix, including collapse/reopen.
- Focused sidebar suite: 2/2 passing in Chromium and 2/2 in Linux WebKit. The earlier synthetic diagnostic also passed 100 collapse/reopen cycles in each engine. The existing two-line-row regression remains covered, and this suite is added to WebKit’s test list.
- UI production and UI-component-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Lint retains two pre-existing Solid reactivity warnings.
- Broader Chromium sibling-suite attempts ended with a browser connection closing; those runs are not counted as passing. Actual macOS WKWebView was not run; the production-built UI/real-Gateway sidebar scenario above has now passed. Native AutoReview returned no usable report; fresh independent source review (separate native reviewer) found no P0–P2 issues in the complete three-file patch against base `7c1c497a0`. This narrative review did not execute tests and does not replace the missing AutoReview report.
- Test cost: maintained Chromium file 2.4s wall / 1.4s test time; WebKit approximately 4.1s wall / 1.8s test time. CI seconds pending.
- Simplification: one existing geometry owner, no new state or compatibility path; production +1 line, one focused browser regression, one WebKit test-list entry.

### Visual evidence

#### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the following session overlaps the expanded children](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6045c15-505b-434f-9b6a-248e6cd6c6ef) | ![After: the following session stays below every child](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dd7b4b8-d3ca-4b24-ac40-5fe467b058b5) |

#### Annotated comparison

prs.title: fix: show multi-question reply format
prs.body:
Closes #173760

AI-assisted. Substantially follows the shared-guidance and regression shape from #173845 by @D41910; the commit credits Winoren as co-author.

## Summary

- Show one bounded, copyable multiline example in the initial multi-question prompt and invalid-answer recovery notice.
- Document the same accepted reply format.
- Derive the regression's successful reply from the displayed example so guidance and parser behavior cannot drift.

## Issue

Closes #173760.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: messaging-channel users can be told to answer every `ask_user` question by number or id without being shown that each answer needs its own keyed line.

## User Impact

User impact: after an incomplete grouped answer is rejected, the user sees a concrete two-line reply template and can fill it in while the same question remains open.

## Root cause

The multi-question parser already accepts one keyed answer per line, but the shared prompt owner and rejection notice exposed only abstract wording. A normal one-line prose reply fills question 1 and leaves later required questions empty, so the recovery path repeated guidance that did not demonstrate the required shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared prompt guidance is the canonical owner for this format. Reusing one bounded constant in the initial prompt and rejection notice fixes both user-visible paths without changing parsing, validation, authorization, custody, or question lifecycle. #190513 remains complementary parser/numbering work; #193400 remains complementary correction-delivery work.

## Verification

- Exact upstream base: `c61a7c0cf6b72f9c35ad8acdc432e132f4d86a50`; the five touched files were unchanged from the reproduced `95363ce54afd893d89cc6bd6645578dba52888d0` snapshot.
- Before source oracle: exit 1. A one-line two-question answer populated `where`, left `game` empty, and found no copyable example in prompt, rejection, or docs.
- After the same oracle: exit 0. It extracted `1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>`, filled it as `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000`, and mapped both keyed answers while confirming the rejection notice and docs use the same format.
- `node --experimental-strip-types --check` passed for all four touched TypeScript files.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head GitHub Actions at `b53ab9bf4816e1b41767192072e59dbf914d5750` passed `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review. Job `128927468471` ran `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.question-custody.test.ts`: 17/17 tests passed, including `reports an incomplete multi-question answer and keeps the question open` in 24 ms.
- Production delta: `+6/-2` (net +4); tests `+13/-6`; docs `+10/-3`.

## Before/after

Before:

```json
{"answers":{"where":"either is fine, and lets do X","game":""},"hasExample":false,"docsExplain":false,"reproduced":true}
```

After:

```json
{"example":"1: <answer for question 1>\n2: <answer for question 2>","completeAnswer":"1: Lisbon\n2: 2000","answers":{"destination":"Lisbon","budget":"2000"},"correctionUsesShared":true,"docsExplain":true,"fixed":true}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Multi-question text prompts and invalid-answer recovery now show the keyed multiline reply shape the existing parser accepts.
- **Real environment tested:** Exact current OpenClaw source snapshot on macOS with Node 22.22.3; source-level behavior oracle plus syntax/docs/diff checks; exact-head GitHub Actions on Linux.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Node source oracle reading the production prompt, rejection, parser contract, and docs; `node --experimental-strip-types --check` on the four TypeScript files; `node scripts/docs-list.js`; `git diff --check`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The oracle derived `1: Lisbon\n2: 2000` from the displayed example, resolved both keyed answers, confirmed both runtime messages share the guidance, and exited 0. Exact-head CI also ran the owning custody regression file: 17/17 tests passed, including the changed incomplete-answer case in 24 ms.
- **Observed result after fix:** The user-visible recovery text now contains a copyable answer that satisfies both questions without changing parser or lifecycle semantics.
- **What was not tested:** No live Telegram account, deployed Gateway, or external model/API. Focused Vitest was not run locally; the exact-head GitHub Actions job ran the owning regression file successfully.

## Risk and scope

Low. This changes shared bounded guidance, one recovery string, one documentation paragraph, and assertions around the existing custody flow. No config, schema, protocol, persistence, parser, validation, authorization, or delivery lifecycle changes.

## Not tested

No live Telegram account, deployed Gateway, or external model/API was tested. Local focused Vitest and autoreview were unavailable in the original publication environment. The exact current head is now covered by GitHub Actions run `42544696697`: `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review passed, and job `128927468471` ran `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.question-custody.test.ts` with 17/17 tests passing; the changed incomplete-answer regression passed in 24 ms.

prs.title: fix: let agents repair config when the setup helper cannot run
prs.body:
Closes #200779

## What Problem This Solves

An agent can have working inference and permission to repair configuration while the separate setup helper's model is unavailable. Requiring that model before even presenting an exact change for approval leaves recovery stuck. The helper-only routing instruction also leaves explicitly requested ordinary local-file repair ambiguous when configuration or setup tooling is broken.

## User Impact

User impact: exact config commands can reach the existing approval and configuration writer without helper inference. Explicitly requested ordinary local repairs have documented file/exec recovery guidance when the normal route is operationally unavailable.

Existing runtime approval checks still govern exact tool operations. The file-recovery guidance prohibits overriding denials or changing access, approval or ownership policies; it does **not** add a filesystem authorization boundary to broadly permitted file/exec tools. Existing readonly, containment and tool restrictions remain in force. No migration or new setting is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing command grammar and executor already provide deterministic operations. Verified inference is now prepared only when conversational work needs it; exact-command provenance stays with the existing approval owner. Model-generated proposals retain their inference checks. A helper outage does not grant authority.

The prompt explicitly describes ordinary local recovery: inspect, preserve a rollback copy, make the narrow repair, validate and read back. One model finding a way through ambiguous wording does not excuse another refusing the same authorized repair.

This is a concrete proposal for the recovery contract requested in the [issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200779#issuecomment-6959713599), not a claim that the product/security decision is already approved.

## Evidence

**Live before/after:** an isolated built Gateway and a real native Codex parent, with only the configured helper provider fault-injected to return HTTP 503. The natural-language helper control actually reached that endpoint and failed.

```text
Baseline ea94eb3bd38e:
  exact logging command -> helper HTTP503, no approval, saved value unchanged

Candidate 8a13db0c9c37:
  exact logging command -> unchanged before allow-once, then saved debug
  ordinary file repair  -> exact backup, only requested repair, validation exit 0
  exact policy request  -> real deny, config bytes unchanged
  requested file fallback after denial -> config bytes still unchanged
  NEW exact policy request -> distinct approval ID; unchanged until allow-once;
                              autoApproveChanges=true, valid saved config

Candidate helper requests during all five parent phases: 0
Native parent input/output tokens per phase:
  8868/56, 1768/748, 499/52, 1513/103, 609/73
Live test: 1 passed; runner exit 0; disposable Gateway and runner homes removed
```

Each parent phase had native thread/model lifecycle, matching provider/model transcript metadata and positive usage. Approval decisions used the real operator `approval.resolve` path, not mocked decisions. This was an isolated Gateway test, not a Discord UI replay. The denied file-fallback observation proves that interaction, not universal filesystem enforcement.

**Counterevidence retained:** ordinary direct-file repair already succeeded on the baseline, including an exact backup and valid result. Its original harness failed on an incorrect expectation of universal blockage; that run was not relabeled passed. The prompt change clarifies the recovery contract rather than claiming direct repair never worked before.

**Snapshot follow-up `7e83c107e368`:** regenerated the Telegram base prompt and Discord delta with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` reproduced both stale outputs before the fix and now passes for all six generated files. Independent diff checks confirm only the existing recovery paragraph and derived counters, hashes and offsets changed. Runtime and generator source are unchanged from live-tested `8a13db0c9c37`, so its live/build evidence is reused, not claimed as a new run.

Additional verification:
- 280 focused tests passed: engine 87, Gateway/session 62, approval 32, prompt/tool 74, stable-prefix 15, TUI 10.
- Delegated-authority Gateway E2E passed: 1 test, 95.21 seconds total, including exact commands with helper HTTP 503. This used standalone source execution on the repository-pinned Bun runtime with verified prebuilt Gateway artifacts.
- Core typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Canonical runtime build passed at `8a13db0c9c37`. Clean source, current build/runtime input signatures, Codex compiler inputs and all 188 recorded Codex output hashes were verified. Native Codex version: 0.164.0; Node: 26.13.1.
- Fresh independent native source review found no actionable production findings; the subsequent TUI type-only correction and evidence claims were also reviewed. The standalone review CLI was unavailable; no machine-clean review status is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Failed attempts and remaining verification limits</summary>

Failed live setup attempts are retained: an unsupported baseline preload; a candidate client missing the approval-event capability; and an incorrect fixture capability import. The latter two were corrected only in the private harness, with actual import validation before the successful run. The five candidate assertions were not weakened and the reviewed candidate source stayed unchanged.

Extra E2E preparation failed in declaration generation without recoverable compiler diagnostics. The normal test wrapper's subprocess compiler then exited 137 before collection; standalone Node execution hit the Linux source-loader ownership restriction before Gateway startup. These are not passing runs or proven inherited defects. The subsequently executed pinned-Bun standalone E2E passed.

CI success, stable-version upgrade proof and exhaustive file/exec enforcement are not claimed. See the current PR checks for CI status. Production configuration and the deployed Gateway were not modified.

</details>

prs.title: fix: allow uninstall on Linux hosts without a service manager
prs.body:
Closes #200695

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux hosts without a service manager, uninstall can fail on a nonexistent Gateway service before removing the data the user selected. A separate workspace-only path could remove files while an unmanaged Gateway was still using them.

## User Impact

When OpenClaw confirms that the Gateway service is absent, uninstall warns and continues without a new flag or prompt. An installed but unloaded service still goes through teardown. If inspection or teardown fails, or a live Gateway owns the selected workspace’s state, uninstall does not proceed with destructive workspace cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service adapter already knows how to establish absence. The workspace cleanup path now acquires the existing state-ownership lock when the state directory is retained, including with `--service --workspace` and no `--state`.

Reported and reproduced on HAOS by @DonnieFi in #200695.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c652a86c-e891-476f-ae2b-e2eceafb85c7)
- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3274099c-a65a-499c-a642-ca578a6cb0af)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/bdfc0811-5256-45e6-89ed-db109e36468d)

## Evidence

The regression test failed before the ownership fix: the workspace marker was missing after uninstall returned an error. The built CLI was then exercised in an isolated Linux x64 environment, using only temporary state and workspace directories. Both cases ran `openclaw uninstall --service --workspace --yes --non-interactive`.

```text
No Gateway service to remove. Continuing uninstall.
absent: exit 0, workspace removed, unselected config retained

No Gateway service to remove. Continuing uninstall.
Workspace cleanup failed: Cannot remove OpenClaw state while the Gateway or another state maintenance command owns this state directory.
live: exit 1, marker preserved, independent Gateway healthy
```

The running Gateway returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before and after uninstall. All 71 focused tests passed. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and the mock-export check passed. Independent P0–P3 Auto Review found no actionable defects. The CLI build passed; the broader local declaration build was blocked by inputs resolving outside the worktree. The original HAOS/Alpine aarch64 device was not retested.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: explain when policy skips an advisor review
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Advisor reviews can be skipped when a Codex session restricts native tools, uses OpenClaw sandboxing, or assigns execution to a paired node. Previously these expected refusals were reported only as `fork_failed`, so operators could not tell that policy prevented the review.

## User Impact

Gateway warning logs now record `advisor: review skipped` with `tool_policy`, `sandbox`, or `exec_host_node`. No review ran in these cases. Unexpected fork failures remain `fork_failed`; cancellation handling stays intact. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catch in `extensions/advisor/index.ts:103` collapsed every non-timeout exception into `fork_failed`. The existing fork dispatcher in `src/gateway/server-plugin-subagent-runtime.ts:344` delegates Codex sessions to their harness; `extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.ts:325` correctly refuses unsupported native execution and restricted native tools. Those guards stay untouched.

This takes option (b), through Advisor's existing warning-log outcome contract. Step 0 found no advisor-specific per-agent/session exclusion: the plugin has global enablement and trigger settings, plus its existing hook permissions. Its documented contract uses the session's model, context, and credentials. The non-native fork in `src/agents/session-fork-run.ts:583` explicitly selects the OpenClaw runtime; it cannot preserve a Codex-owned model/auth connection automatically. `docs/concepts/agent-runtimes.md` also forbids replaying an executing harness's failures through another runtime. A fallback would require a separately authorized runtime/auth contract.

The SDK currently carries these refusals as plain `Error` values, without an exported policy classifier. The adapter matches only the three pinned Codex `/btw` refusal sentences, including the terminal period, and logs fixed reason codes. This avoids a private cross-plugin import or new SDK export. If those sentences change, classification must be updated with the owning guard tests; an unrecognized error remains an unexpected failure. No tools, authority, runtime, or credentials are widened.

## Evidence

The advisor fork-boundary regression uses fixed refusal fixtures from the Codex side-question contract and checks the actual scheduled review's warning outcome. On unchanged production code, the three policy cases failed because they logged `fork_failed`; with the fix, all three log distinct skips. The unexpected-error control passes in both versions. This is boundary-fixture proof, not a live Codex/provider call or production validation.

- Red: `pnpm test extensions/advisor/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — `Tests 3 failed | 11 passed (14)`; expected `review skipped`, received `review failed ... fork_failed`. Cold run wall time: 104.38s.
- Green: advisor suite `Tests 14 passed (14)`, 7.18s file wall time; all six requested files passed, 89 tests, 174.89s total wall time. Exact-head [CI run 44215122212](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44215122212) succeeded without retries. Shared CI job wall times: extension config checks 136s; compact-small-1 231s (shared job timings, not isolated advisor test time).
- Green command: `pnpm test extensions/advisor/index.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.fork.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.model-selection.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.app-consent.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Targeted Oxlint, formatting, plugin reference regeneration, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Targeted typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/advisor/tsconfig.json --incremental`) and `pnpm build` passed. The initial typecheck lacked unbuilt SDK declarations; it passed after generation. Build completed in 3m 27.3s and exited 0, with advisory UI asset-budget violations (largest CSS gzip 58,957/58,315 B; chat boot JS 21/20 requests and 1,331,328/1,331,081 B gzip); this patch changes no UI source.
- Codex autoreview against base `4dbd70ff`: scoped-clean at P0–P2, no actionable findings; full local candidate and fork/runtime owners supplied as context.

The author simplification pass kept the fix inside the existing advisor catch: +20 production lines, +20 test lines, +6 documentation lines, no helper, state, or new fork owner. The lane's test allowance is raised to exactly 20 lines in `config/test-lines-allocations/advisor-policy-skip.txt` to retain the three policy cases and unexpected-error control without deleting unrelated coverage.

prs.title: fix(active-memory): Italian recall questions skip deep recall
prs.body:
Closes #188550

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Italian questions about the past never trigger Active Memory deep recall in `escalate` mode.

## User Impact

User impact: Italian users get deep recall for questions like "che motto usavo?".

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an Italian entry to the localized recall patterns, with future cues and "ti ricordi di + verb" kept quiet.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof: isolated Gateway (scratch state dir, loopback port), Active Memory in `escalate` mode, local stand-in model, each message sent with `chat.send` to `agent:main:main`. "recall" means Active Memory logs `start`; "skipped" means the main model receives the "intentionally skipped deep recall" note.

```text
                                                  main (ee75d02)   PR (d6e1b3f)
che motto usavo?                                  skipped          recall
cosa avevamo deciso sul motto, nei mesi scorsi?   skipped          recall
ricordami di comprare il latte domani             skipped          skipped
ti ricordi di chiamare Marco domani?              skipped          skipped
ciao, come stai?                                  skipped          skipped

PR gateway log, "che motto usavo?":
[plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=mock activeModel=stub thinking=off fast=inherit start timeoutMs=15000 queryChars=103 searchQueryChars=16
[plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=mock activeModel=stub thinking=off fast=inherit done status=no_relevant_memory elapsedMs=1731
main gateway log, same message: no active-memory start line
```

`resolveRecallEscalationDecision`, `escalate` mode:

```text
main: "che motto usavo?" no-recall-intent
PR:   "che motto usavo?" recall
```

Escalation tests: 7 fail on main, 148 pass here. `tsgo:extensions`, oxlint and oxfmt pass.

### Real behavior proof (real model)

Same scenarios with a real model instead of the stand-in: isolated Gateway (scratch state dir, loopback, throwaway token) built from this head (`d6e1b3f`), `qwen3.5-0.8b` (Unsloth GGUF) served by a local llmman/llama.cpp process, used as both the main model and the Active Memory recall model, `escalate` mode, each message sent with `chat.send` to `agent:main:main` and the previous run finished before the next. Base is the same tree with only `extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts` reverted to the merge base (`ee75d02`). Gateway log lines, trimmed (`recall skipped reason=session-ineligible` lines from the recall sub-run itself are omitted):

```text
                                                  base (ee75d02)            this PR (d6e1b3f)
che motto usavo?                                  skipped no-recall-intent  start ... done status=no_relevant_memory
cosa avevamo deciso sul motto, nei mesi scorsi?   skipped no-recall-intent  start ... done status=failed
ricordami di comprare il latte domani             (not run)                 skipped no-recall-intent
ti ricordi di chiamare Marco domani?              (not run)                 skipped no-recall-intent
ciao, come stai?                                  (not run)                 skipped no-recall-intent

PR, "che motto usavo?":
active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=llmman activeModel=unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF thinking=off fast=inherit start timeoutMs=60000 queryChars=16 searchQueryChars=16
active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:main activeProvider=llmman activeModel=unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF thinking=off fast=inherit done status=no_relevant_memory elapsedMs=34775 summaryChars=0
base, same message:
active-memory: recall skipped reason=no-recall-intent
```

The recall model is tiny, so what it returns (`no_relevant_memory`, `failed`) says nothing about recall quality; this only shows the gate: the two Italian past-recall questions start a real-model recall on this head and are skipped on base, while the reminder and greeting messages stay quiet. The main turn of the fourth message ended with an error from the tiny model after its skip decision, which does not affect the gate. Not run: a populated memory with a hit, other model sizes, the upgrade path from a stable release.

prs.title: fix(subagents): fail children interrupted by a Gateway crash
prs.body:
## Problem

When the Gateway process dies without a graceful shutdown (crash, `SIGKILL`, stall-watchdog kill), a sub-agent that was still running is restored from SQLite as an unended row. Restore retires its completion authority and nothing reconstructs its execution, so the row never reaches a terminal state. Its requester never receives a completion and can wait indefinitely. Restart resume skips the child itself (sub-agent keys are not resumed independently), so nothing else settles it.

Graceful shutdown already ends live children through `terminateLiveSubagentsForShutdown`; only the crash path leaves them hanging.

## Change

The registry sweeper now settles such a row as failed with an interruption error through the existing recovery completion path, so the requester is woken through normal completion delivery. The settle applies only when the row:

- has not ended, is not yielded, and is neither live nor queued,
- has retired completion authority, and
- was created before the current process started (only an earlier process could have owned it).

Yielded rows keep their existing unreachable-yield handling. Docs: `docs/tools/subagents/operations.md` restart section.

## Proof

- New unit tests (`subagent-registry-sweep-settle.restart.test.ts`): settles the restored running child and leaves ended, yielded, live, queued and current-process rows alone.
- Integration (`subagent-registry.store-replaced.test.ts`): a running child persisted by an earlier Gateway is restored, swept and stored as a terminal error. Fails on base with the sweeper hook reverted; passes with it.
- Focused registry suites green: sweep-settle restart (38), store-replaced + sweeper lifecycle/recovery (35).
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint and guards pass; the dead-export scan reports only five pre-existing exports in files this PR does not touch.

## Limitations

The crash path is exercised by restore + sweep tests, not by killing a live Gateway. Queued rows restored from an earlier process are deliberately left to their existing handling.

prs.title: fix(telegram): stop Plugin SDK deprecation warnings blamed on the bundled Telegram plugin
prs.body:
Closes #191786
Closes #191785
Related: #174937, #190243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway logs `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warnings blamed on "Plugin telegram", and the Plugins catalog marks Telegram as using APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026, when the bundled Telegram plugin loads, or when a Telegram group message from another member steers an active run under collaborative steering.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram operators no longer see the startup deprecation warning, the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warning on steering, or the retiring-API notice those two cause. A Telegram group message that steers another member's run under collaborative steering still logs `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`, and those still show as a catalog notice; that read is out of scope here (see "Not in this PR"). Discord, Slack, Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp sessions now list `nativeApprovals` in the agent Runtime capabilities, and Telegram keeps it. Approval authorization, routing and delivery are unchanged. For those 8 channels the Runtime line gains one token, so their system prompt changes once after upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Telegram was the last bundled caller of the sync `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`. It now uses `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapabilityAsync`, as #174937 did for Discord; `isNativeDeliveryEnabled` wraps the same check.
- `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` read only `native` and `nativeRuntime`. The async factories expose `nativeAsync` and `nativeRuntimeAsync`, so moving Telegram alone would have dropped `nativeApprovals` for Telegram, as it already had for 8 channels. The check now reads all four.
- `prepareFollowupRunToolAuthorityFingerprint` re-read its prepared fingerprint through the deprecated plugin-facing `fingerprint()`. Steering runs in the channel plugin's frame, so the warning and the deprecated-API record landed on Telegram. Core now uses a module-private reader with the same checks; plugin callers of `fingerprint()` still warn.
- Not in this PR: core's sync placement `getMany` (10 call sites, several inside synchronous commit guards; its warning has no fixed removal date), and the collaborative steering read that still calls `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Both need their own core reader and proof.

pr-simplify: no production code removed. One test assertion on a statically defined factory output was removed. No new state, exports or test-only hooks. Production +30 -11 in 3 files; tests +117 -4; three test-line records totaling exactly the 113 net added test lines.

## Evidence

### Gateway run (2026-11-09)

A real Gateway from a built `dist` (`node --trace-deprecation dist/index.js gateway run`, Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64; Vitest also on Node), a local fake Telegram Bot API that grammY talks to as its transport, and a scripted Responses provider that records the `Runtime:` line of every request. Base: main `3855c896edd`. Head: this PR merged onto that main (`git merge-tree --write-tree 3855c896edd d096fe01a3c` = `8f366fba0b5`, no conflicts, same patch-id as this PR's diff). `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`. `channels.discord` and `channels.slack` are `{ enabled: true }` with no tokens, so the Gateway loads both plugins (`5 plugins: discord, memory-core, qa-lab, slack, telegram`) and `channels.status` shows both accounts `configured: false, running: false`. Two runs per scenario per build.

Steering. A run is held open at the provider and a second Telegram message arrives while it is active. In every run the second message is injected into that run (session controller `injection-outcome: consumed`, no "steering rejected" record), the provider gets it in the same session, and Telegram receives both answers.

| scenario | build | DEP_PLUGIN_SDK warnings, all "Plugin telegram" | `plugins.list` notices (of 268 plugins) |
|---|---|---|---|
| group, a second member steers, `allowCollaborativeSteering: true` | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup); at the steer `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 4 APIs |
| same | this PR | at the steer `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 2 APIs |
| DM, the sender steers their own run | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup) | telegram, that 1 API |
| same | this PR | none | none |

Stacks from `--trace-deprecation` on main:
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`: `fingerprint <- read <- prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority <- prepareReplyMessageJoin <- runActiveReplySteer`. Gone here.
- `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`: `<- read <- prepareCurrent <- prepareCurrent <- beginPreparedReplyMessageInjectionTarget`. Same stack here.
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`: called from inside that `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Same here.
- Startup: `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability <- channel-*.mjs` module load. Gone here.

Two things this shows that the description had wrong or left out:
- On main, a message from the run's own sender does not reach `fingerprint()` at all. A plain message is a `continue-existing` steer, which goes through `prepareReplyMessageContinuation` (since #177698) and never calls the deprecated reader. The fingerprint warning needs the legacy steering path, which a second member's message reaches under collaborative steering.
- On that collaborative path this PR leaves two warnings in place, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` (the second comes from inside the first), and both still put a retiring-API notice on Telegram in the catalog. The first is the collaborative read already listed under "Not in this PR".

Runtime capabilities. The provider's view of `channel=<id> | channel_capabilities=...`, the same in every run of a build. Discord and Slack turns come from the Gateway `agent` RPC with `channel` set and `deliver: false`, on fresh sessions:

| channel | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| telegram (DM and group turns) | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` |
| discord | `threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` | `nativeapprovals,threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` |
| slack | `none` | `nativeapprovals` |

Telegram keeps `nativeApprovals` after moving to the async factory, and Discord and Slack gain it.


- At this head the three changed test files pass 37 of 37 (26 + 7 + 4). With the three source files from `19aff5bfd42`, they fail 1 of 26, 5 of 7 and 1 of 4.
- Red on base, green here, each with only that commit's source file reverted:
  - `extensions/telegram/src/approval-native.test.ts`: 5 failed / 2 passed vs 7 passed; the new test receives the deprecation message.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.test.ts` (follow-up read): fails with the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` usage record vs passes.
  - `src/channels/plugins/approvals.test.ts`: `expected false to be true` vs 4 passed. Dropping either async field alone fails its own assertion.
- `--trace-deprecation` over the message-join and fallback-steering suites (101 tests): `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warnings 3 -> 0.
- All 9 bundled approval capabilities: `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` true for 1 of 9 on base, 9 of 9 here.
- Prompt consumers 16 files / 174 tests, Telegram and Discord approval suites 9 files / 218 tests, core steering and authority suites 19 files / 371 tests: all pass. `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap, assertion-safety and test-lines ratchets pass against `19aff5bfd42`. If CI's test-lines job is red, that is main's own overage (main has been over its ceiling since `2a32ab046f2`, #191638); this branch adds 113 test lines and 113 lines of allocation.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `approval-native.test.ts` 26.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 6.6 s wall, 413 ms and 376 ms of tests; `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 8.8 s and 7.8 s wall, 1.3 s and 1.2 s of tests; `approvals.test.ts` 10.0 s and 6.2 s wall, 11 ms and 9 ms of tests. CI run 41606285186, Bun: `approval-native.test.ts` 744 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`); `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 9.0 s Vitest duration, 1.6 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-7`); `approvals.test.ts` 50.1 s Vitest duration, 17 ms of tests (`checks-node-changed-channels`).
- Not covered end to end: real Telegram, Discord or Slack. The Discord and Slack sessions above came from the Gateway `agent` RPC with their plugins loaded and no accounts running, not from those services. Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp were not run.

prs.title: improve: reduce allocation when preparing long conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing an agent session from a long conversation clones mutable model-context data, then validates all of those newly created containers again before freezing them. That repeated inspection allocates unnecessary keys and descriptors during attempt preparation and compaction.

## User Impact

Long conversations require less allocation and CPU during initial-context preparation. Prompt bytes, writable SDK views, stored snapshot sharing, and opaque SDK values retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript copier already knows which containers it creates. It now optionally freezes its output, using trusted freezing only when its existing traversal established the plain-data guarantee. Maps, Sets, symbol members, and native structured-clone fallbacks retain inspected freezing. A blanket trusted-freezer substitution would be unsafe for those SDK inputs.

Existing frozen-payload sharing and revision-bound prepared-context reuse remain the owners of those optimizations. Runtime delta is +21 lines to preserve the opaque-value contract; there is no new cache or session-row projection change.

## Evidence

Five counterbalanced A1/A2/B process groups on Node 26.12.1/macOS arm64, each with 20 warmups and 100 measured operations. A1 and A2 use the same parent copier/codec. Synthetic workload: 4,000 entries, 1,000 user/tool-call/tool-result/answer turns, 2 KiB tool output, 3,171,895 serialized input bytes. Acceptance was fixed before measurement: B must beat both controls on allocation and CPU, preserve context bytes, and avoid a material latency regression.

| Per operation, median across processes | A1 | A2 | B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Construction + initial context allocation, MB | 38.2274 | 38.2322 | 23.7080 |
| Construction + initial context CPU, ms | 30.2312 | 31.1711 | 28.4604 |
| Mutable owner allocation, MB | 30.4333 | 30.4234 | 15.9188 |
| Mutable owner CPU, ms | 22.4081 | 22.5343 | 19.5968 |
| Frozen owner allocation, MB | 5.6160 | 5.6169 | 4.1845 |
| Frozen owner CPU, ms | 3.7429 | 3.6921 | 3.4247 |

Construction wall median/p95: A1 29.719/36.586 ms, A2 30.327/37.498 ms, B 28.073/35.405 ms. Mutable owner median/p95: 21.351/29.054, 21.924/28.027, 19.256/27.374 ms. Frozen owner median/p95: 3.569/4.361, 3.569/4.504, 3.316/4.325 ms. Host one-minute load ranged 4.61–6.66. Allocation uses exact cumulative V8 counters, including later-collected objects; CPU uses thread CPU counters. CPU profiles confirm the removed validating traversal at this call site. Profiled timings are excluded from the table.

Every measured model-context hash matches across all arms. The 20 MB mutable-owner regression budget fails on the parent at 30.19 MB/operation and passes with this change. The SDK construction measurement includes `fromEntries` import cloning; owner measurements separately cover mutable and deeply frozen branches. These are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway throughput or production deployment claims.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-manager-context-freeze-measure.ts --output <json>`. For A, save the parent's `session-manager-codec.ts` and `transcript-snapshot.ts`, then pass `--codec-file <file> --snapshot-file <file>`. Add `--max-owner-bytes 20000000` for the allocation regression check.

Validation: 94 focused tests passed across codec, transcript snapshot, stored-context isolation, retained data, and prompt-prefix stability. New SDK coverage exercises mutable nested arguments, Maps/Sets, typed arrays, symbol members, and frozen payload identity. Codec test file: 30 tests; initial full invocation 43.73 s including compilation and the snapshot shard. Consumer invocation: 62 tests, 135.46 s including compilation. CI timing pending.

Independent local Codex autoreview of the parent-to-working-tree change and full ownership sources is scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. Production and full-tree unused-file scans pass. Browser output-fidelity E2E: 4 passed; Chromium tool-card tests: 3 passed. The first component run could not launch because the pinned headless shell was absent; installing that exact Playwright shell resolved setup, and all component tests then passed. All selected `pnpm check:changed` stages now have passing proof: the full invocation found one benchmark-only unique-symbol typing error; the module-namespace fix passed the exact failed scripts typecheck and reran the allocation budget successfully. Every other stage passed in that invocation, including all core/test typechecks, lint, format, export scans and runtime guards. No inherited-main failure is being claimed.

prs.title: fix: observer fallback models get time after a primary timeout
prs.body:
Closes #191600

## What Problem This Solves

Session assessments can stop even when a configured recovery model is usable. The observer's shared timer includes preparation, every fallback candidate, and the JSON validation retry. Increasing that timer by the configured candidate count does not fix a slow invalid first reply followed by a valid retry: 25 seconds plus 10 seconds still exceeds the default 30-second deadline.

## User Impact

Each completion keeps its existing bounded execution budget, including configured fallback candidates and the second JSON-output attempt. Caller cancellation and physical settlement retain their existing ownership. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing bounded preparation phase, then clear its timer when preparation finishes. Isolated completion already owns candidate deadlines, cancellation, and cleanup. #191199 owns the richer utility-fallback diagnostics; this PR does not duplicate them.

Current main's regression still expected the retired shared signal to abort after 60 seconds. It is now reconciled with the actual utility fallback owner: parameterized recovery and exhaustion cases verify both candidates receive 30 seconds, the request does not finish before the fallback's turn, and the observer releases its active controller. The existing JSON retry and physical-settlement regressions remain covered.

## Evidence

- Current head: `b06239dbe55c7bd98967341364e25861569f1302`; integrated base: `84a72ed32320a44ac161e1e0be4f858d44861b3c`.
- The original merged consumer was reproduced locally with its `expected true, received false` failure before updating it. Removing the production repair from the current integrated tree also makes the candidate-exhaustion and JSON-retry regressions fail: **2 failed, 1 passed, 11 skipped**. Restoring the repair returns the two complete gateway files to **22 passed**. The utility completion runtime file separately produces **17 passed**.
- The gateway run took **29.31 seconds wall time**, mostly compiler preparation and imports; the prior run took 35.58 seconds. Individual completion cases took at most 214 ms with fake timers. No wall-clock sleeps were added.
- Focused oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Full-index test-line accounting reports `6653545` lines against a `6653549` ceiling, with **4 lines of slack**. The separate `session-observer-candidate-deadlines.txt` allocation is exactly **91** lines, matching net regression growth across the two files. The shared scalar baseline is unchanged.
- The current narrow typecheck did **not** run to completion: the repository's declaration-input guard rejects the existing dependency installation outside this checkout. No guard was bypassed and no dependencies were reinstalled. The repaired head's hosted production and test typechecks now pass; earlier-head local typecheck results are not claimed for this head.
- Local self-review covered the complete four-file change against the integrated base, timer ownership, both fallback outcomes, JSON retry, cancellation, settlement, and the allocation. This is not a claim that local autoreview or local ClawSweeper ran.

The current fallback regressions execute the real utility fallback runner with controlled candidate I/O. They are not live-provider or production-Gateway validation. Earlier loopback HTTP evidence at `621fc9b34240818185a75e692f3204e3c7572c07` exercised default preparation/completion, utility fallback, isolated completion, and real local HTTP transport: the primary timed out after 29,771 ms, the fallback returned a valid digest, and the active controller was cleared. That is prior-head transport evidence, not a fresh transport run on this head. The current production change still clears the same preparation timer; no provider adapter or isolated-completion implementation is changed by this PR.

Fresh hosted checks are green: 51 passed, none failed or pending, and run `42974000216` completed successfully at this exact head. This includes the repaired changed-test lane, baseline ratchet, and production/test typechecks. Maintainer review remains pending. The full local suite, live model service, production Gateway, and native addon execution are not claimed as passing.

prs.title: fix(agents): cache drop warnings blame max_completion_tokens when only the output cap changed
prs.body:
Closes #191648

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `[prompt-cache] cache read dropped` warnings blame `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens` when the prompt prefix is unchanged and only the per-request output cap moved.

## User Impact

User impact: on Chat Completions routes, a cache drop with an unchanged prompt prefix now reads `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix` with `providerPrefix=prefix-match`, so the warning points at the provider instead of an OpenClaw request change that did not happen. Prompt, tool, message and other parameter changes are still attributed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Chat Completions transport clamps `max_completion_tokens` (or `max_tokens`) to the remaining context budget on most requests (`openai-completions-params.ts:511`). `describeProviderPrefix()` compared every tracked request parameter, so the cap alone turned `prefix-match` into `parameters:max_completion_tokens`. An output cap bounds the completion; it does not change the prompt tokens a prefix cache keys on.

The parameter comparison now leaves out `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens`:
- A cap-only change keeps `prefix-match`.
- When something else changed as well, the warning names only that: `parameters:temperature`, or `system`.

`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md` and `docs/logging.md` say so.

The provider-prefix description, with this filter, now lives in `prompt-cache-provider-prefix.ts`. With current main, `prompt-cache-observability.ts` would otherwise pass its 700-line cap; the functions moved unchanged.

Accepted edge case: if the cap changed and the only other difference is the JSON key order of the remaining parameters, the `order` signal is not reported.

## Evidence

- Production (details in #191648): on two hosts running a 2026.10.10-beta.5 based build, all 66 and all 83 drops labeled `parameters:max_completion_tokens` had equal `prefixHash` and `routeHash`. 35 and 17 of them went to 0 cached tokens.
- Unit: one new table in `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` with 5 cases:
  - `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` alone -> unchanged prefix.
  - Cap plus `temperature` -> `parameters:temperature`.
  - Cap plus changed instructions -> `system`.
  - On base `19aff5bfd42` all 5 fail. The received values are `provider-input-change:parameters:max_tokens`, `...:max_completion_tokens`, `...:max_output_tokens`, `parameters:temperature+max_completion_tokens` and `system,parameters:max_completion_tokens`. With the fix the file passes 22/22.
- Consumers: 14 test files that use the observer pass (276 tests).
- End to end: an isolated `openclaw agent --local` turn against a scripted local Chat Completions server. Request 1 makes a tool call with 22560 cached tokens; request 2 reports 0. The bodies differ only by the two appended messages and `max_completion_tokens` (44468 -> 41385).
  - Base build: `provider-input-change:parameters:max_completion_tokens ... providerPrefix=parameters:max_completion_tokens`
  - This branch: `provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix ... providerPrefix=prefix-match`
- Checks:
  - `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files pass.
  - Against current main `3855c896edd`, with this branch merged locally:
    - CI's baseline ratchets (`ci-baseline-ratchets.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base`) pass 9 of 9, and the line-cap ratchet passes with `RATCHET_PR_HEAD_SHA` set. Before `a18dac5b480` it failed: `prompt-cache-observability.ts: 700 -> 712 counted lines (cap 700)`, because #192944 left that file at exactly its cap.
    - Test lines: main's test-line ratchet is now at its ceiling (slack 0; this branch measured 410 against its base), so `b094f0248d4` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/191649-cache-drop-output-cap.txt` with 30 lines, the net growth of the new table in `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts`, which is the regression test for this fix. The ratchet reads `Test lines OK: 6592398; ceiling: 6592398; slack: 0.`, and 31 is refused.
    - `check:changed --base 3855c896edd`: 35 of 36 lanes pass. The other, `changelog attributions`, reports the same 20 lines on unmodified main, in changelog files this PR does not touch.
    - The 12 test files that import the changed modules pass 191 of 191, under Node 26.12.1 and under Bun.
  - Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` 32.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 12.8 s wall, 7.2 s and 7.4 s of tests. CI run 41574334778, Bun: `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts` 36.0 s Vitest duration, 7.5 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-40`).
  - The new cases run in 1-2 ms each.
- Not covered: a live provider run. The qa-lab mock serves only Responses and Messages and reports no cached tokens, so it cannot produce a cache drop.

prs.title: chore(ui): reproduce sessions disappearing under All owners
prs.body:
Related: #199621

## What Problem This Solves

Publishes a real-Gateway reproduction of conversations disappearing when the sidebar owner filter changes from My sessions to All owners.

## User Impact

**Evidence-only draft: no product behavior changes and no fix claimed. Do not merge as a membership-policy decision.** Maintainers can reproduce the current transition and inspect the real requests before choosing whether to clarify the agent scope or change filtering semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reporter requested publication of the diagnostic evidence, with a draft PR as the alternative to an issue comment. This adds one focused case to the existing real-Gateway browser suite, reusing its isolated Gateway, synthetic owners, and cleanup. It clicks My sessions → All owners → My sessions, asserting both emitted query scope and rendered membership while keeping the chat URL and selected agent unchanged.

No new test server, production helper, schema, configuration option, or provider call is introduced. The assertions deliberately describe today's behavior; they should be revised with the eventual agreed fix. Related #198985 has a different, navigation-triggered transition.

## Evidence

- Real disposable Gateway + built UI + Chromium 156.0.8078.4; synthetic users/sessions. The diagnostic sends no model requests; the preceding rate test uses its synthetic loopback provider. No live service touched.
- Full-file red/green: published head 5b21bded reproduced the review finding (rate test passed; diagnostic failed on retained rate-proof rows). After scoping the locator to the diagnostic’s three keys: **2 passed together**, 46.62 s wall time, diagnostic 1.961 s. No test-name filter; CI timing unavailable.
- Owning UI E2E typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Review: initial Auto Review was P0-only. ClawSweeper’s P2 shared-fixture finding was independently reproduced and corrected; full-file proof is now green. No fresh hosted re-review is claimed.

prs.title: fix(ollama): refuse metadata and link-local base URLs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama used to allow a metadata or link-local base URL through the private-network SSRF policy, including the bearer token. Those base URLs now get no allow policy. Loopback and private LAN hosts stay allowed.

A supported local endpoint, `http://0.0.0.0:11434`, still opts into that private-network allow. The guard then treated `0.0.0.0` and `::` as blocked special-use addresses and threw before HTTP, so discovery reported the local server as unreachable. Exact-host trust, with no private-network allow, still rejects those addresses. Metadata and non-exempt link-local answers stay blocked.

Whether those metadata and link-local exclusions should override every explicit private-network opt-in, or only Ollama's automatic trust, is still a maintainer decision. This change does not narrow that scope.

## Evidence

Head `bd89f8052bf` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, Ollama 0.40.11 listening on `127.0.0.1:11434`. Production `fetchOllamaModels` ran from `/tmp/oc-191588`.

Before this commit, `http://0.0.0.0:11434` threw and opened no socket:

```console
[security] blocked URL fetch (ollama-provider-models.tags) targetOrigin=http://0.0.0.0:11434 reason=Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address
RESULT: unspecified discovery SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
```

`curl` to that same URL returned HTTP 200 from the daemon. After this commit the production discovery call reached it.

```console
OK: loopback discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: unspecified discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: authenticated loopback header=bearer models=1
OK: literal metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: dns metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: unrelated redirect denied stolen=0
OK: lan address admitted 192.168.1.20
OK: podman exact-origin embed length=2 requests=1
OK: podman origin metadata newRequests=0 connects=
```

The unrelated redirect target was `proof-unrelated.test`. The guard stopped on the hostname allowlist. The second server received 0 requests. The Podman case used production `createOllamaEmbeddingProvider` against `http://host.containers.internal:11434`, resolved to `169.254.1.2`, where a listener accepted one embed POST. A metadata answer for that same origin opened no further request. The hosts entry and the /32 alias were removed after the trace. Default route stayed on `en0` via `10.0.0.1`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Authenticated Ollama discovery reaches loopback and `0.0.0.0`. Literal and DNS metadata are rejected before a socket opens. An unrelated redirect is denied. The exact-origin Podman link-local exception still delivers the embed, and a metadata answer on that origin does not.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, Ollama 0.40.11 bound to `127.0.0.1:11434`, head `bd89f8052bf` in `/tmp/oc-191588`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Called production `fetchOllamaModels` for `http://127.0.0.1:11434` and `http://0.0.0.0:11434` with a bearer token. Called `resolvePinnedHostnameWithPolicy` for literal `169.254.169.254` and for `ollama.example` resolved to that address. Posted through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` to a loopback server that redirected to `proof-unrelated.test`. Embedded through `createOllamaEmbeddingProvider` at `http://host.containers.internal:11434` while that name resolved to a listener on `169.254.1.2`, then repeated the origin with a metadata DNS answer.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched tree:

```console
OK: loopback discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: unspecified discovery reachable=true models=3
OK: authenticated loopback header=bearer models=1
OK: literal metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: dns metadata SsrFBlockedError: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address connects=
OK: unrelated redirect denied stolen=0
OK: podman exact-origin embed length=2 requests=1
OK: podman origin metadata newRequests=0 connects=
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Loopback and `0.0.0.0` discovery both returned 3 models from the local daemon. The bearer was present on the loopback recorder. Metadata rejects opened no socket. The unrelated redirect delivered 0 requests to the second server. The Podman listener received exactly one embed and no metadata follow-up.
- **What was not tested:** A LAN Ollama on another machine. This daemon listens only on `127.0.0.1`, so the admitted `192.168.1.20` address had no server. The Podman hop was a listener on this Mac, not a Podman VM.

## Summary

The release note stays in this body. This branch does not edit CHANGELOG, which release tooling owns.

Metadata and link-local Ollama base URLs still get no private-network allow. `0.0.0.0` and `::` stay reachable when private networks are allowed, which is how Ollama names the local server. Exact-host trust still rejects them. A maintainer still needs to decide whether the metadata and link-local exclusions should override every private-network opt-in or only Ollama's automatic trust.
