prs.title: fix(models): honor disabled fallbacks when the primary is excluded
prs.body:
Closes #198189

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can run an unrelated provider despite having no model fallbacks when a wildcard model policy excludes its configured primary.

## User Impact

Requests with an empty effective fallback chain now fail before model invocation, with an actionable error naming the model and policy to repair. This includes explicit `fallbacks: []` and native agent primaries without their own fallbacks. Operators must correct the primary or the applicable allow policy rather than unexpectedly consume another provider’s quota.

Existing exact-only automatic-default exemptions and non-empty-chain catalog substitution remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared selector previously substituted a catalog model before ordinary failover could honor the empty chain. It now checks the already-resolved fallback chain and uses the existing authorization error so HTTP clients receive `permission_error`, not a generic internal error. The native PR-wrapper inventory includes the added dependency.

Simplification: one shared decision, no new routing owner, configuration, or state. Production +7/-0 lines; tests +202/-4 lines, including a real-Gateway regression using existing fixture helpers.

## Evidence

- **November 18 refresh:** integrated [current main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b609d22c129f2944c1abaec1d2895eb659493a36) and resolved the wrapper inventory conflict by retaining both dependency entries. The original ten-file PR scope and seven-line production change are unchanged. The rebuilt real Gateway still rejects streaming and non-streaming requests with zero inference calls, and the allowed-primary control succeeds. The focused runner reports **171 passing tests**; the additional HTTP regression, production and five test typecheck graphs, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh CI is attached to [the refreshed head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c2ad8f07bb07da4e1557db18adb090c6fdbcc5dd).

- **Real streaming reproduction, red then green:** on base `08103c5df8b87969bdb69ce0a8977ed402a3d09a`, `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: "openclaw/fastbot"` invoked the recording alternate provider despite `fallbacks: []`. The regression failed on the unexpected inference request.
- **Original real-Gateway verification:** streaming and non-streaming requests make **zero inference requests** and return the model/policy guidance (`permission_error`; HTTP 403 for non-streaming). An allowed-primary control successfully invokes the same recording provider and completes. Local e2e wall time: 19.60 seconds; test time: 17.26 seconds. Synthetic local provider only; no paid-provider or quota-consumption claim.
- **Initial production candidate: 164 tests passed across nine files / seven shards**, covering shared selection, command/reply consumers, installed provider identity, plugin tool execution, wrapper dependency closure, and the real HTTP regression. The three strict-selection owner cases also failed on the base before the fix.
- Production typecheck and all five changed-test typecheck graphs passed. Scoped lint, formatting, docs-list sanity, and `git diff --check` passed. The runtime was rebuilt from the candidate through the repository e2e preparation workflow. CI timings are pending.
- **Independent Auto Review:** initial production candidate against the base above, OpenClaw engine, P0–P2 coverage: scoped-clean, no findings. Review covered the supplied source/diff snapshot; it did not independently rerun the reported checks.

- **CI follow-up ([f1320f232d62](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1320f232d62974db4a44d514d320606c5e47696)):** reproduced the `get-reply.auto-fallback` failure from `checks-node-changed-2`, then explicitly configured the fallback required by that substitution fixture. All existing assertions remain intact; production code is unchanged. The corrected file and neighboring selection suites pass **45 tests**, with scoped lint, messaging-test typecheck, formatting, and whitespace checks passing. The earlier real-Gateway proof remains applicable to the unchanged production code.
- **Proof scope clarification:** the HTTP regression starts a separate built Gateway process and a local recording provider, not a mocked/in-process Gateway. No paid-provider quota or release-upgrade proof is claimed; this change introduces no schema, migration, or persisted-setting rewrite.

<details>
<summary>Refresh validation notes</summary>

The real-Gateway test completed in 22.50 seconds (62.37 seconds including test preparation), with exit 0. The focused test runner completed all six shards successfully; the execution host then reported a database lock while recording its final exit, so that run is supported by the runner’s pass summary rather than a clean outer exit receipt. Subsequent static checks and the HTTP proof exited cleanly.

A supplemental refresh review did not produce a report, so no new review result is claimed. The previously completed review remains evidence for the unchanged production patch; this update only integrates main and resolves the dependency-list conflict.

</details>

prs.title: improve: reduce allocation while streaming model replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming model replies repeatedly enter and restore the same transport context for every chunk. On Node 24, that creates new async-context frames and copies their Maps thousands of times per reply.

## User Impact

Lower CPU and allocation while streaming, with the same transport request identity, events, usage, and cleanup behavior. No protocol, configuration, or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture one async-context runner when the diagnostic iterator is acquired and reuse it for `next`, `return`, and `throw`. The existing transport owner still creates the context; this removes repeated entry/restoration work without changing one-shot lifecycle calls. Production grows by two lines for the import and captured runner. The runner retains the iterator's acquisition context, including other async stores; plugin stream admission and cleanup owners remain responsible for their existing live checks.

## Evidence

Interleaved streams preserve their own transport identity before and after awaits, through return/throw, and restore each caller's transport context. Diagnostic throws retain their existing policy of leaving provider cleanup to the provider. Focused diagnostic tests and prefix-stability tests passed on Node 24 (69 tests); focused diagnostic tests also passed on the pinned Bun runtime (54 tests). These are preservation tests; the performance regression is demonstrated by the A/A/B allocation profile rather than a brittle heap-allocation unit assertion.

Five serial A1/A2/B rounds on Node 24.22.1 using the committed `scripts/perf/model-stream-observation-measure.ts`: real diagnostic wrapper and plugin bindings, two requests × 2,000 chunks per turn, metrics listeners, 1,000 warm timing turns and a separate 100-turn sampled-allocation pass per arm/round. Both A arms use the exact baseline owner from `7ceb716273277ec6d493c62bc52e2c24cfdf941a`. Acceptance was B beating both A medians in CPU and allocation with identical stream events/results, request identity, response bytes, usage, and completion counts, and no median latency regression.

| Median per turn | A1 | A2 | B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled allocation MB | 9.310 | 9.304 | 7.064 |
| CPU ms | 3.774 | 3.799 | 3.367 |
| Mean turn latency ms | 3.581 | 3.599 | 3.187 |
| p95 turn latency ms | 4.027 | 4.100 | 3.742 |
| GC ms | 0.070 | 0.073 | 0.064 |

Allocation fell 24.1%; CPU fell 10.8–11.4%. Allocation ranges were A1 9.277–9.327 MB, A2 9.282–9.340, B 7.059–7.107; CPU ranges were A1 3.673–3.840 ms, A2 3.622–4.512, B 3.172–3.680. Shared-host contention affected the final timing round (p95 maxima 4.143/10.966/9.244 ms); this is owner-path evidence, not a whole-Gateway tail-latency claim. First-round sampled Map allocation fell from 1.723 MB/turn to 0.006 MB/turn.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/model-stream-observation-measure.ts --plugin-bound --listeners metrics --turns 1000 --chunks 2000 --mode timing --output <file>`. For allocation, use `--turns 100 --mode allocation`; for A, add `--owner <adjacent exact baseline source copy>`.

Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local change against the baseline, with lifecycle/transport/shared-context/plugin-iterator/cleanup source supplied, completed scoped-clean through P2. Simplification retained only the per-iterator runner and context preservation tests. No Control UI imports of the modified module were found.

The final dedicated context test file passes both Node 24 and pinned Bun (2 cases each). Cold commands took 45.76 s and 33.91 s respectively, dominated by compilation; hosted CI duration is pending.

`pnpm check:changed -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-events.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-events.transport-context.test.ts` passed, including TypeScript, changed-file lint/format, database/static guards and dead-export scans. An initial test placement exceeded the existing lifecycle suite's line cap; the dedicated file fixes that local validation failure. No inherited main red is being waived.

prs.title: fix: show inbound Twilio MMS photos to the agent instead of "attachment unavailable"
prs.body:
Closes #200804

Earlier attempts at the same fix, #156126 and #144098, were closed without merging. Nothing from them is on main, so this PR makes the change again, with a test that runs the real downloader.

## What Problem This Solves

When someone sends a photo by MMS to an OpenClaw SMS number, the agent receives "[1 Twilio MMS attachment unavailable]" instead of the image. Twilio redirects the media URL on `api.twilio.com` to `mms.twiliocdn.com`, and the SMS plugin only allows `api.twilio.com`, so the download is blocked at the redirect.

## User Impact

User impact: inbound MMS attachments reach the agent again. Messages with attachments that were already failing start working with no configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin adds `mms.twiliocdn.com` to the hosts the media download may reach. Nothing else about the download is loosened:

- The first URL must still be the media URL of the signed message on `api.twilio.com`, for the same account and message.
- The downloader still checks every redirect hop and still drops the Twilio `Authorization` header when the redirect leaves `api.twilio.com`. The CDN gets no credentials.
- A redirect to any other host is still refused.

The SMS channel doc now names the CDN host next to the existing host restriction.

## Evidence

The new tests in `extensions/sms/src/media.test.ts` run the real `saveRemoteMedia` downloader with a stubbed transport that answers the first request with a 307 to `mms.twiliocdn.com`. They check three things:

- the attachment is saved and the message body is unchanged,
- the first request carries the Twilio `Authorization` header and the CDN request carries none,
- a redirect to `evil.example.com` is refused and the notice is shown.

On main, the first test's redirect hits the same "Blocked hostname (not in allowlist)" check quoted in the issue, so it is written to fail there. That failure was read from the code and not observed by running it. Two existing assertions that spelled out the allowlist, in `media.test.ts` and `ingress-spool.test.ts`, now list the new host.

<details>
<summary>Validation and what was not run</summary>

- Not run in the environment that wrote this change: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/sms/src/media.test.ts extensions/sms/src/ingress-spool.test.ts`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxfmt and oxlint on the touched files. Dependencies could not be installed there, so these are left to CI. The regression was checked against the guard's redirect code by reading it, not by execution.
- Checked: `git diff --check` is clean.
- Not tested: a live Twilio account. The redirect target comes from the reporter's logs and `curl -L` on a real inbound MMS in the issue.
- Test cost: two small tests with one temporary state directory each, no timers or servers. Wall time not measured.

</details>

prs.title: fix: preserve subagent results under each requester turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Successful subagent results could disappear when children from separate requester turns finished together. A sandbox preparation failure or a restart-interrupted child's terminal notice could also retire an owed result without telling the requester.

## User Impact

Each requester receives its results under the authority of the turn that spawned them. Uncommitted preparation failures remain retryable, and children stopped by a Gateway restart deliver their interruption notice after fresh requester admission. No configuration, schema, or protocol changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry remains the single custody owner. Settle-wave selection now partitions both frozen and unfrozen cohorts by the retained source, invocation, and scopes before dispatch (`subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts:164–180`). The original authority comparisons are unchanged and moved into the registry's sibling policy module to keep the existing 700-line module limit. The retained-custody check remains in the registry owner and is invoked at the same point; the identity allowlist is unchanged. Each group preserves FIFO order and cannot borrow a sibling's authority.

The delivery classifier previously treated sandbox provisioning and non-retryable-tagged `UNAVAILABLE` errors as permanent failures (`subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:165–178`). Typed sandbox failures are retryable for requester settlement; generic `UNAVAILABLE` retries require the existing pre-execution replay-safe fact. Failures after tool effects or sends retain their original no-replay outcome. Send evidence, permanent authorization failures, real Stop handling, and committed-input no-replay remain intact.

Restart settlement previously required retired completion custody, then attempted the terminal notice through the guard that correctly rejects that custody. It now waits for the existing startup custody owner to admit the requester afresh before settling an old, non-live, non-queued execution (`subagent-registry-sweep-settle.ts:149–174`). The retired-store guard is unchanged.

## Evidence

On base `c97a173b040bce3a3553911a1be0f971e853e724`, the authority/preparation regressions report **4 failed**: both frozen/unfrozen batches throw `Subagent completion batch has incompatible operator authority`, and both typed preparation errors return `permanent_failure`. The native SQLite startup/sweep regression separately reports **1 failed** because the requester receives no interrupted-child notice. With the fix, all five regressions pass; the complete focused authority/dispatch/restart suites report **116 passed**.

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-dispatch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'delivers overlapping|failure=(sandbox|unavailable)'
pnpm test src/gateway/session-restart-resume-custody.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'restored interrupted'
```

Core typecheck, all 29 affected test-type shards, the final owning typecheck leaves, production/test lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `pnpm build` passed. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. The full subagent sibling run reported **2,209 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped**; its sole stale expectation required immediate terminal settlement under retired custody. That expectation is corrected to require the child and notice to remain owed before fresh admission; the complete affected store-replacement suite then reports **23 passed**. CI caught an overly broad `UNAVAILABLE` condition after tool effects or sends. Narrowing it to pre-execution failures preserves the existing real-Gateway side-effect boundary; the complete transcript-conflict suite and requester-dispatch suite pass together. CI also caught the relocated authority refusal in the identity ratchet. Keeping its custody check in the registry owner passes that ratchet without an allowlist change; the affected authority/dispatch suites report **106 passed**, and a fresh independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2. The plugin-reload continuation case also reported a CI startup timeout; all three continuations passed locally through the original product entry. CI on the updated head supplies broad proof.

The test budget for this repair is raised from zero to exactly **+134 net test lines**: real retained-invocation dispatch in frozen/unfrozen cohorts, two preparation-error representations in the existing retry table, and the native SQLite custody/sweep receiver proof. The old metadata-only queued-collector fixture is consolidated into the existing scheduler-owner integration test, which now proves a stale queued collector survives a sweep before its real reservation is withdrawn. No extra Gateway boot is added. Production growth is bounded to authority selection and the unchanged admission-policy extraction.

The existing `(announcing)` and `(announcing-crash)` restart e2e cases are intentionally out of scope here. Both reproduce red on the base above: **2 failed, 8 skipped**, using `pnpm test test/gateway-subagent-completion-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'restart \(announcing(-crash)?\)'`. The graceful case expects `pending` where delivered-on-commit semantics record `delivered`; the crash case encounters `Input completion retry conflicts with the committed input` and misses `HUB_RECEIVED_RESTART_COMPLETION`. They need Gateway-owned continuation from committed input, a separate follow-up; this PR preserves delivered-on-commit semantics and does not replay consumed completion input. The same two failures reproduce on this PR head `4aabf5c9a1439e97e5bc7501ad31e7bef2185083`: **2 failed, 8 skipped** (80.85s Vitest; 190.76s including runtime preparation). Related: #200823, #200807, #200249.

prs.title: fix: restricted HTTP conversations fail on their second turn
prs.body:
Closes #198678

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a restricted member's second HTTP chat request is rejected when it reuses the same conversation `user` and the role has `sessions.others: "none"`.

## User Impact

Members can continue their own newly created HTTP conversations while other profiles remain unable to access them. Existing unattributed sessions are not assigned to the next caller; this does not recover their historical ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing create-on-run owner now carries the admitted profile on genuinely new rows independently of sandbox requirements. Persistence continues to stamp only new rows, while existing sharing authorization, required sandboxing, and source cancellation/replacement checks remain intact. Both compatible HTTP endpoints share this owner.

No new schema, configuration, authority mechanism, or test-only production seam is introduced. Production is +9/-5 (net +4); those lines express creator attribution independently of optional sandboxing. Tests are +51/-2, extending the existing HTTP/authentication/persistence fixture.

## Evidence

### Current head after resolving the merge conflict

Merged main at `5dea6be4819a4ea7119e113fcc1a91eb6413dcc2` into the existing PR branch. The complete patch against that base still touches only `src/gateway/operator-session-run.ts`, `src/gateway/server-http.openai-sandbox.test.ts`.

The regressions on the earlier named main `2c47052dd994066da28f882fa0d97dc45d52f70d` failed as expected, with both creator second turns returning 403 without the fix.
- Core and affected test typechecks, targeted format/lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent P0–P2 review of the identical two-file patch was scoped clean.
- `corepack pnpm build` passed at the current head.

The standalone Gateway / SSE / local-model proof and fork CI below were executed at the original head `3993aff1b32aeb966150e04065ae1759af491325`. Fresh standalone Gateway proof is pending for the refreshed head.

### Upstream checks and review for the current head

prs.title: fix(update): skip unreadable foreign directories during update capture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Original-state capture and full backups abort when a workspace contains an unreadable foreign entry, such as the root-owned `.fseventsd` directory on a mounted APFS volume. Reported by @BorClaw.

Fixes #191855.

## User Impact

Capture and backup can finish around unreadable foreign entries, with one warning per omitted path and explicit manifest omissions. Unreadable owned files, explicitly selected resources, canonical databases, and present private-capture markers still refuse. The running updater needs this repair for original-state capture; installing a corrected candidate cannot change the older updater's capture code.

## Why This Change Was Made

At base `8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004`, [`update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts:312`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004/src/infra/update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts#L312) calls the privacy classifier before enumerating a directory. [`update-capture-paths.ts:18–23`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004/src/infra/update-capture-paths.ts#L18) probes the marker inside that directory and refuses on EACCES. The original-capture caller catches this as a continuation warning; it is not itself the stopping validation exception.

The other walks are agent scratch discovery, backup SQLite inventory, and payload tar traversal. The installed v2026.10.10 updater's broad [`backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts:183`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts#L183) reaches the same privacy check through `isTraversable`; its directory failures also propagate at line 192. Supplemental candidate-state discovery calls that owner during validation, inside the broad package-update catch. This is a source-supported validating-phase failure path, not identification of the report's discarded exception. Main already narrows supplemental discovery to declared plugin resources (`4a393be419f3`), so an unrelated workspace subtree need not be visited there. Capture and full-backup omission handling were still missing on main. Classification and exception-retention work belongs to #194160.

One shared permission/UID policy now serves the walkers. The backup inventory retains skipped paths across discovery and archiving, and checks deferred scratch-scan failures after all explicit includes are known. SQLite readability probes use descriptor-free access checks to preserve existing POSIX database locks. Capture records omissions in its existing `excludedRoots`; backup records `unreadable-foreign` entries in its existing `skipped` manifest. Mount traversal policy is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix owner-boundary reproduction: both `captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline` and `createBackupArchive` failed with the reported marker `lstat` EACCES. The focused reproduction took 44.53 seconds including subprocess fixture preparation.
- GREEN narrow proof: `CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-tar-walk.test.ts src/commands/backup-resource-inventory.test.ts src/infra/update-capture-paths.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **21 passed**, 4.78 seconds wall time. Covers permission-denied readdir/open, owned-file refusal, late explicit-resource protection, and privacy/symlink safeguards.
- Committed capture and archive/manifest regressions are in the existing Doctor capture and backup ownership suites. They use real chmod-000 denial and synthetic foreign UID metadata, skip root/Windows, and include foreign SQLite plus owned-file refusal. prs.title: fix: keep owner device approval working when the Gateway connection drops
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Approving a new browser from an owner browser ("Approve from another device") breaks if the owner browser's Gateway connection drops even briefly. The Control UI throws away the in-progress approval on every reconnect. The owner-side mailbox read then stops until someone clicks Retry, and the Gateway hides the real error. The new browser shows "Could not finish approval", even when the claw already added it as an owner.

This change keeps an in-progress approval across a reconnect to the same Gateway. The approval is held while reconnecting and continues only after the new connection is admitted again. The change also finishes a handoff whose admission already landed, gives the mailbox long poll enough timeout headroom, retries transient mailbox failures on its own, and logs the real relay error.

## What Problem This Solves

An owner approving a new device can lose that approval to a short network blip, a laptop waking from sleep, or a proxy that drops idle connections. The new device then fails, and the claw may already list it as an owner without it ever receiving its certificate.

## User Impact

User impact: owner approvals survive Gateway reconnects. A dropped connection during the number comparison or right after approval no longer forces the owner to start over or revoke a half-admitted device. Mailbox hiccups recover without a manual Retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **Keep approval attempts across a reconnect to the same Gateway** (`owner-approval-lifetime.ts`, `owner-approval.ts`, `device-mail.ts`).
   - The reader is kept when the reconnect targets the same Gateway URL. This includes when the store replaces the `GatewayBrowserClient`: `gateway-page-activation.ts` calls `gateway.connect()` when reachability returns, and that builds a new client.
   - While disconnected, the reader is suspended: no mail reads, handoff recovery, or decisions.
   - It resumes on the new client only after the same admission check used at start: local operator, owner, linked, this browser holds the owner key, same claw.
   - An account change, owner-key change, a different Gateway URL, or a `stopped` / `reload-required` phase still tears every attempt down and zeroes its secrets, as before.
2. **Finish an admission that already landed.** The sealed handoff is now sealed before the membership submit. If the submit's response or the handoff send is lost, the reader re-sends the same sealed handoff only when the Gateway already lists the new device. Before sending, it rechecks that the attempt is not expired, cancelled, or suspended. The membership change is never resubmitted.
3. **Mailbox long-poll headroom and retry** (`packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/discovery/device-mail.ts`, `device-mail-relay.ts`).
   - Discovery holds a read for 20 s. The relay deadline goes from 25 s to 35 s, and the browser RPC deadline from 30 s to 45 s. These are now derived from one constant.
   - The reader retries request timeouts, retryable `UNAVAILABLE`, and transport loss with bounded backoff (1 s up to 15 s), and clears the error after a successful read.
   - Refusals such as `INVALID_REQUEST` still stop and wait for an explicit Retry.
4. **Log the real relay error** (`openclaw-id-device-mail.ts`). The Gateway logs `openclaw-id: device mail <operation> failed: <name>: <message> (<cause code>)`. It never logs the ID token, signature, or body. The client error is now marked `retryable`.

Safety argument for keeping attempts: each attempt already expires on its own timer, at the start message's `received_at + 300 s` (member requests at their capped TTL). The new device enforces its own deadline too. Keeping an attempt across a reconnect cannot extend any approval window. The Gateway also still checks owner authority on every `device_mail` call.

## Root Cause

Observed on a Gateway behind a TCP proxy that drops connections. The owner browser reached the Gateway through that proxy, and the new browser went through the normal remote path.

- **Before behavior:** two approvals from a real browser failed with "Could not finish approval". In both, the Gateway logged `openclawId.authority … errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Owner-device mail could not be delivered` after 9025 ms and 13519 ms, from the same owner page on two different connections. The claw's owner count still went up.
- **The swallowed error, made visible:** with a diagnostic build that logs it, dropping the owner's connection during a mailbox read gives:
  ```
  device mail relay failed op=receive: AbortError: This operation was aborted
  ⇄ res ✗ openclawId.authority 11015ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Owner-device mail could not be delivered
  ```
  The relay's fetch is tied to the owner connection's `connectionSignal`, so a dropped connection aborts the in-flight long poll. Healthy reads return at about 20.7 s, which is Discovery's 20 s hold.
- **Separate timeout:** one read failed with `TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout` at exactly 25006 ms. The 25 s relay deadline left 5 s of slack over the 20 s hold.
- **Why a drop kills the approval:** the reader was bound to one live connection.
  - `bindOwnerApproval` stopped the reader whenever the snapshot left `connected`, which dropped every attempt and zeroed its SAS secret.
  - Reachability recovery also creates a brand-new client, so even a client-keyed fix would not survive it. I confirmed this with a logpoint trace in a real browser: during the reconnect, `snapshot.client` changed to a new object.
  - With the attempt gone, a submit that had already landed never got its sealed handoff, so the new device failed while the claw counted it as an owner.
  - Any mailbox read failure also stopped the read loop until Retry, and the Gateway's `catch {}` hid the cause.
- **Control:** with a stable owner connection, 6 of 6 approvals succeeded, including the order where the new device confirms first and the owner approves 45 s later. A drop landing after the handoff had already been sent did not break approval either.

## Real behavior proof

Environment: a real Gateway runtime behind a TCP proxy that drops connections. The owner is a Chromium browser on the local operator path, and the new device is a fresh Chromium profile on the remote path. Both are driven by a script. The proxy was killed and restarted to drop the owner's WebSocket.

**Before, on the unfixed build: drop while the numbers are shown, then approve.** The owner dialog lost the request ("No new devices are waiting for approval"). The approve button never appeared, and the new device stayed at "Waiting for your other device to approve…".

**After, on a runtime built from this PR's final head: same steps.** The trace comes from DevTools logpoints on the deployed approval-lifetime chunk.
```
T kill-proxy 00:25:11
[lt] suspend reconnecting                                   (reader held, attempts kept)
[lt] suspend connected
[lt] resume on admitted client ws://127.0.0.1:<port>        (re-admitted: local operator, owner, same claw, owner key)
Owner dialog after reconnect: "Approve a new device … 663 591 … The numbers match"   (same request kept)
T approve 00:25:22   → submit, sealed handoff sent
New device: navigated to the claw's chat page (approved)
```
The same scenario on the earlier iteration of this change, without the guards below, showed the same reader continuing with no new mailbox bind. The runtime used for the live run is this head's source, backported to that runtime's older OpenClaw base. That base predates member approval, so the member branch of the handoff recovery was left out there. All other code is identical.

## What was not tested

- These guards are not exercised live, only unit-tested; each test fails when its guard is removed:
  - Teardown on `stopped` / `reload-required` after a reconnect. `reload-required` needs a mismatched build redeployed under an open page.
  - Teardown when a reconnect targets another Gateway URL. The URL can't be switched mid-session through this harness.
  - The expiry recheck before a recovered handoff. It needs a lost sealed send held past the 5-minute attempt expiry.
- A live drop landing exactly between the membership submit and the sealed-handoff send. The proxy-kill timing couldn't hit that window reliably. Unit-tested: the handoff is finished once the Gateway lists the device, it is never resubmitted, and it is withheld if the attempt expires during the check.
- Member-device approvals across a reconnect. Unit-tested only.
- The longer relay and browser timeouts under a slow Discovery response. Reasoned and unit-checked, not reproduced live after the change.
- No before/after performance benchmark. The change adds no hot-path work: the long-poll cadence is unchanged, and retries only happen after failures, with 1 to 15 s backoff.

## Verification

- New regression tests. Before the fix, `owner-approval-lifetime.test.ts` (reconnect), `owner-approval.test.ts` (sealed handoff lost to a dropped connection; relay `UNAVAILABLE` retried without Retry), and `openclaw-id-device-mail.test.ts` (logged cause) all failed. The expiry recheck and the first-admission guard were each checked against a mutant.
  - Reconnect: same client; replacement client for the same Gateway; replacement that is no longer an owner; another Gateway, including mid-reconnect; account change; owner-key change; `stopped` / `reload-required`, also after `reconnecting`; first admission across unrelated snapshot updates.
  - Reader: the sealed handoff finishes after a lost send, including through a rebound client. There is no handoff for a submit the claw did not apply, and none when the attempt expires during the admission check. Decisions and mail are held while suspended. Transient `UNAVAILABLE` retries without Retry, and refusals still stop.
  - Gateway log line: includes the operation and the real cause, never the token or signature.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/ src/gateway/server-methods/openclaw-id-device-mail.test.ts src/gateway/openclaw-id/device-mail-relay.test.ts`: all passed (UI: 14 files, 117 tests; Gateway: 2 files, 5 tests).
- Test-lines ratchet: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` → net +390 of the 400 allowance. The reconnect cases are table-driven, with a shared dropped-handoff fixture. After consolidation, every regression test above still fails on the pre-fix code, and each guard (expiry recheck, first admission, Gateway check while reconnecting, teardown after reconnecting) still has a test that fails when the guard is removed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed (format, lint, assertion-safety, UI controller guard, typecheck core/UI/tests, dead-export scan, import cycles).
- Live: the drop-and-approve run above, on a runtime built from this head (scanned before deploy).

prs.title: fix: message from a scheduled run to a busy Claude CLI session fails once the run ends
prs.body:
<!-- Template source: .github/pull_request_template.md at origin/main 8aa2434748a. -->

Fixes #199278

## What Problem This Solves

A message that a scheduled run sends with `sessions_send` to a busy Claude CLI session fails with "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active" once the sender's run has ended. The receiver never sees the message and the sender only gets a failure notice.

## User Impact

User impact: a scheduled job can hand work to a busy Claude CLI session again. The queued turn can prepare after the sender finishes, without treating normal sender retirement as revocation.

Device removal, role or access-grant revocation, and explicit Stop remain authoritative. This change adds no configuration, grants, prompts, or broader permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

#194798 gave accepted turns a retained continuation, and the Claude CLI receiver already holds it. CLI preparation projects the run's MCP tools through `captureSessionControlAuthority`, which also asserts the ambient request client's `operatorRunAuthority`. A queued CLI turn prepares inside the sender's request scope, before the CLI run installs its admitted caller identity. The sender's run-bound authority is therefore asserted after its occurrence ended.

#181363 established that an admitted caller, not the ambient client, owns continuation authority. This fix applies that rule when the admitted run's own distinct authority is supplied. Passing the ambient authority itself as `prepared` still keeps its live-client check. The retained continuation continues checking role, device, and access grant.

The corrected candidate also migrates the scheduled-handoff regression to the current `captureGatewayOperatorContinuation` owner, replacing the removed `independentContinuation` option after integration with the selected main baseline. The original production fix and its ancestry are preserved.

## Evidence

**Current candidate: `675303067ee181ebeb9378368839c7196820cc19`; tree `a2de9e0720c6f2dc3644a0d60f5bba8667920bd3`.**

[Exact-candidate isolated proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7b8fb04e4daf66abb1439f924c216983) completed successfully with exit 0 on secretless AWS:

- **187 tests across seven files passed:** scheduled handoff, session-control authority, operator recovery, configured MCP authority, CLI preparation consumers, MCP requester lifecycle, and session creation.
- **29/29 canonical changed-scope type graphs passed**, along with scoped type-aware lint, formatting/Bun parity, final file hashes, and diff checks.
- **Causal red/green:** reverting only the production retained-authority selection made normal sender retirement fail with `Recovery claim retired`. Device removal, role change, and explicit Stop still rejected correctly. Restoring exact candidate bytes returned all four scenarios to passing.
- The parent independently checked source/tree bindings, all three changed-file hashes, the red-only diff, execution logs, and the terminal receipt. No source, policy, configuration, or type baseline was changed to obtain a passing result.
- Fresh independent local review covered all three complete changed-file bodies and fourteen owner/caller contexts at the current head, with no actionable P0–P2 source findings.

**Current-head live proof (November 18, UTC):** An isolated built Gateway used a deterministic QA cron sender and a real subscription-backed Claude CLI receiver. At 00:49:13.666 the foreground command had started, had not ended and was nonterminal. The Gateway admitted the cron job at 00:49:13.690. The handoff was queued at 00:49:14.118; that sender occurrence retired successfully at 00:49:14.243. At 00:49:14.769 the receiver was independently observed still executing the foreground command. After that command finished at 00:51:53.152, the intended receiver persisted the exact requested answer at 00:51:58.136, matching the accepted run ID and the native model probe. The sender transcript was read via its stable key, matched to the exact job and session incarnation; the short-lived alias had correctly retired. No product change was needed. Live revocation was not tested. [Isolated runner workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44209741822); evidence archive SHA-256: `4fc7adad93d7f5e9c9e5a3ee69a96851f803c5f91f59db2b2d63e579da03a541`.

**Landing gates:** The [security guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199343#issuecomment-6886871678) was approved. [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44173508511/job/134361029650) lost its hosted runner; all 11 baseline ratchets passed on an isolated replay of the exact tested merge (`8a8b52aa2f53`). This is not a CI waiver or a diagnosis of the disconnect. [Official attempt 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44173508511/attempts/3) passed on the current head. The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199343#issuecomment-6887059107) accepted the live proof and reported no actionable findings.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor evidence on original head 0ad321660b7 — retained with its limits</summary>

The contributor used a QA lab Gateway with a mock-provider sender and a real `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5` receiver on a Claude subscription login. The receiver ran `sleep 150`. A scheduled job created by an owner turn was force-run, sent with `sessions_send` while the receiver was busy, and ended before the receiver became idle.

| Revision | Receiver after its busy turn | Sender |
|---|---|---|
| base `8aa2434748a` | never answered the handoff | `Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active` delivery failure |
| original head `0ad321660b7` | answered `QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK` | received the reply without a failure notice |

Both runs used `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build` followed by `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario cron-authority-mix-repro`, one run per SHA. Selected recorded output, UTC on 2026-11-15; session identities are placeholders:

```text
BASE 8aa2434748a
01:40:21.654 sender    sessions_send(sessionKey=<receiver>, message="CRONAUTH handoff reply: answer with QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK")
01:40:51.731 sender    toolResult {"status":"accepted","sessionKey":<receiver>,"targetDisposition":"queued","delivery":{"status":"pending"}}
01:40:51.844 cron      run finished status=ok completionStatus=succeeded
01:42:34.580 receiver  assistant "BUSY-DONE" (no handoff in receiver history)
01:42:34.942 sender    assistant "sessions_send delivery to <receiver> failed: Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active."

ORIGINAL HEAD 0ad321660b7
01:34:22.064 sender    sessions_send(sessionKey=<receiver>, message="CRONAUTH handoff reply: answer with QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK")
01:34:22.129 receiver  queued handoff recorded while sleep 150 was still running
01:34:52.153 sender    toolResult {"status":"accepted","sessionKey":<receiver>,"targetDisposition":"queued","delivery":{"status":"pending"}}
01:34:52.262 cron      run finished status=ok completionStatus=succeeded
01:36:35.141 receiver  assistant "BUSY-DONE"
01:36:38.404 receiver  assistant "QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK"
01:36:38.536 sender    assistant "QA-CRONAUTH-HANDOFF-OK"
```

A temporary stack capture identified `captureSessionControlAuthority` through `captureMcpLoopbackScope` and `prepareCliMcpToolProjection`. The original regression covered real MCP projection with a retired recovery-fixture occurrence, plus device removal, role change, explicit Stop, and same-ambient-authority checks. The contributor reported twelve passing consumer files, clean scoped typing/lint/format, and a pre-existing dead-export failure. Their two-round local review ended without findings after the same-ambient-authority case was corrected.

These historical checks apply to the original head only; they do not waive current CI or replace the current-candidate proof above. The real run exercised handoff, not live revocation, and its sender model was scripted. The temporary live scenario was not committed.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Original fix and historical live evidence: @etzelm (Mitchell Etzel). Follow-up review, current-owner compatibility repair, and landing requested by @VACInc. Original ancestry is preserved, and the repair/materialized candidate retains VACInc co-author credit.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram progress streaming now retains a detached preview cleanup target when `deleteMessage` fails. A later `stream.clear()` retries that exact message once, while scheduled/in-flight guards prevent duplicate deletes and successful cleanup releases the retained reply target. prs.title: feat(sessions): choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automatic idle or daily reset always carries the last six user/assistant messages into the new session, and there is no way to change that number. Some deployments want more continuity after a reset, others want a clean start.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set `session.reset.tailMessages` (also in `resetByType` and `resetByChannel` entries) to choose how many recent messages an automatic reset keeps. The default stays 6, so nothing changes unless the key is set. `0` starts the new session empty. `/new` and `/reset` still always clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tail size was a constant inside the transcript selection. It is now resolved with the rest of the reset policy, so the per-type and per-channel overrides work the same way as `mode`, `atHour` and `idleMinutes`. The four places that write an automatic preserve-tail boundary pass the resolved value: the channel reply path, `openclaw agent`, the gateway agent turn and cron's stale-session rollover.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `src/config/zod-schema.session-config.ts`: `tailMessages` (integer, at least 0) on the reset policy object, with label and help text.
- `src/config/sessions/reset-policy.ts`: `SessionResetPolicy.tailMessages`, type override first, then base, then `DEFAULT_RESET_TAIL_MESSAGES = 6`.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript-replay.ts` and `session-reset-boundary-event.ts`: the preserve-tail request takes an optional `tailMessages`; omitted means the default. The default constant stays in `transcript-replay.ts`, and `reset-policy.ts` imports it, so the extracted PR wrapper module keeps no new dependency.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `session-hooks.ts`, `src/agents/command/session.ts`, `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-patch.ts`, `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-session-persist.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/session.ts`, `run-session-state.ts`: pass the resolved value. In `session-hooks.ts` the redundant `explicitReason` parameter is dropped: for explicit resets it always equalled `previousReason`, so `session.ts` does not grow.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/session.md`, `docs/gateway/config-agents/sessions.md`, regenerated config baseline.

</details>

## Evidence

- Focused tests:
  - `src/config/sessions/session-reset-boundary-event.test.ts`: with 4 turns, the boundary keeps from turn 2 by default, from turn 4 with `2`, from turn 1 with `10`, and nothing with `0`.
  - `src/config/sessions/reset-policy.test.ts`: default 6, base value, chat-type override, channel override, and the schema rejects `-1`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `config:docs:check`: clean. `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` passes.
- Test-line budget: +33 net test lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/session-reset-tail-messages.txt`. The tests cover two separate contracts that no existing test covers: the boundary tail for each size, and the policy resolution order (default, base, chat type, channel, negative rejected). The policy cases are one table. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes.
- Head `bd7c2b6a778` only moves the default constant and consolidates tests after the live runs below; runtime behavior is unchanged from the proven `891d01a7db3`.
- After merging current `main` (`891d01a7db3`): tsgo checks, `config:docs:check` and the 9 focused session, reply, gateway and cron test files (148 tests) pass again.
- 44 test files that import the changed modules (sessions, reply session, agent command, gateway agent turn, cron isolated agent): 574 passed. One test, `src/cron/isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts` "runs a linked current job as a child of its conversation", fails on this macOS machine identically on `main` without this change. `src/config/io.observe-recovery.test.ts` (2 tests) does the same.

Live run against a real Gateway:

- Clean Multipass Ubuntu 24.04 VM, Node 24.22.1. Candidate: this branch (`e8c6e67a793`), packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts` and installed with `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz>` (`openclaw --version`: `2026.10.9 (e8c6e67)`, tgz sha256 `ecf411c1…da63`). The model is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`, which logs every request body, so no provider key is used.

prs.title: fix: show device-code sign-in steps on separate lines when the Gateway runs the login
prs.body:
Closes #200749

Related: #198327 closed without merging; this is a new, separate change for the same symptom.

## What Problem This Solves

When the local Gateway is running, `openclaw models auth login` shows multi-line sign-in steps with the text `\n` instead of line breaks. The device-code box becomes one run-on paragraph: the instructions, URL, code, expiry and the warning not to continue if someone else gave you the code all run together. The login still works, but it garbles the step that carries the phishing warning, for every provider that signs in through this path (xAI and OpenAI Codex device codes, and any other multi-line note or progress step).

## User Impact

User impact: people signing in to a provider through the CLI while the Gateway is running see the instructions, URL, code, expiry and warning on separate lines, as they do in the offline sign-in path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway builds these messages with real newlines on purpose. The CLI then ran the whole message through the terminal sanitizer, which is written for single-line text and turns each newline into a visible `\n`. The CLI now sanitizes each line of a step message separately and joins them back with real newlines. Control characters are still stripped on every line, and a stray carriage return is still escaped. The shared single-line sanitizer is left alone, because other callers rely on it.

The fix applies to the step message the CLI forwards to note, progress and prompt rendering. It stays in the login command, since this is the only caller that needs line-preserving output. I did not add a shared multi-line helper, which would be better introduced once a second caller needs it.

## Evidence

Behavior before and after, run against the real sanitizer with the message shape from the issue (`Code: ABCD-1234` followed by a blank line and a completion note, with color codes and a bell character mixed in):

- Before: `Enter this one-time code.\r\nCode: ABCD-1234\n\nxAI OAuth complete` (the backslash sequences are literal text)
- After: the same text split across three lines, with the color codes and bell removed

A regression test in `src/commands/models/auth-login-gateway.test.ts` covers a progress note and a select prompt with CRLF and LF breaks, color codes, a bell, and a lone carriage return. It asserts the line breaks are kept, the controls are removed, and the carriage return is still escaped.

Not verified: I could not install the repository's dependencies in my environment, so I did not run `pnpm test`, oxfmt, oxlint or `pnpm tsgo:core` locally; the new test's cost is not measured. I also did not run a live Gateway login against a provider. CI runs the test suite.

prs.body:
## Head update — sixth mechanical integration (2026-11-12 23:17Z)

`main` regenerated the Gateway predicate again at `4ab02e3c0879aa5efb51e664b5e57c092144c9ed` (+6247/−6222 in `predicates.js`), which returned this PR to `CONFLICTING` on that one generated path — the same single-file recurrence documented below. Resolved the same mechanical way: integrated `main`, took main's clean `predicates.js`, re-ran `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, and committed the generator output. The approvable head is now **`14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699`** — a fast-forward of `06a288a4b05` (one merge commit, zero semantic change; every hand-written file and both proof e2e files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head, only the generated table moved). Both `session_authority` and `route_unavailable` are verified present in the regenerated table (one occurrence each), the generator exited 0, an ESM import smoke passed, and `mergeable` is back to `MERGEABLE` (`blocked` on the two maintainer actions only). Every `/allow-security-sensitive-change` reference below keys to this new SHA; any push re-keys it.

The CI and mergeability tallies in the historical sections below are snapshots of earlier heads, not claims about this one. On the previous head one lane stayed red for a PR-owned TypeScript error at `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-local-refusal-profile-health.e2e.test.ts:143` (`.map(readRunFailureNotice)` callback signature, TS2345); that file is byte-identical on this head, and the finding is recorded in the integration comment rather than silently folded into a mechanical integration.

**Update (2026-11-13 07:05Z):** the sixth mechanical integration
(`14a2d9eb509`, automation-run) exposed a latent type error that Revision 12
missed: `.map(readRunFailureNotice)` forwards the numeric array index into the
newly option-typed second parameter (`{ audience: "desktop" }`) and fails
TS2345 on `check-test-types-core-4`. Fixed at `8aadf02c7a4` — one
line, a one-argument callback — resolving the P2 finding from Revision 13.
The approvable head is now `8aadf02c7a44b41976c3cf00d113c07d716d3189`.
---

Closes #191473

## Needs from a maintainer (nothing is waiting on the author)

Two one-line actions, neither of which CODEOWNERS routes to anybody — which is the mechanical reason they have been waiting since Nov 3:

1. **`/allow-security-sensitive-change`** for head `8aadf02c7a44b41976c3cf00d113c07d716d3189` — this is the conflict-resolved head the re-derived review now names; `e960518954b` is one merge behind it, and approving a stale SHA does not clear the gate. This is maintainer-tier, not SecOps: matched against the repo's own security policy, the gate covers **one** non-test production file (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`) and **3 lines** in it. The gate is live and correctly keyed, verified from the shipped logic: `scripts/github/security-review-rollout.mjs` returns mode `enforced` for this PR (rollout pull 152415 merged 2026-09-19, this PR created 2026-11-03), and `.github/workflows/security-review.yml` triggers on `issue_comment` created/edited plus a ten-minute reconcile schedule — so posting the command is picked up on its own, with no push or re-run needed from anyone. The exact acceptance predicate is `scripts/github/guard-review.mjs:525-552`, with the command grammar at `scripts/github/guard-shared.mjs:128-138`, and four of its clauses fail silently - worth quoting before anyone posts, so the first attempt sticks: (i) the comment must be created **after** the guard's current approval request, because any push re-keys it; (ii) **every** non-empty trimmed line must be one bare command from the closed set (`/allow-security-sensitive-change` or `/allow-dependencies-change`) - `lines.every(...)` means prose wrapped around the command makes the parser return nothing at all; (iii) the comment must **never have been edited**, since `updated_at !== created_at` disqualifies it, so tacking a clarifying note onto an already-posted command silently revokes that approval; (iv) the author's own comment is ignored and the poster must hold `maintain` or `admin`. Two intuitive choices that do **not** work: a GitHub Review - Approve satisfies nothing here (no review state is read anywhere in these files), and re-editing the command comment is equivalent to deleting it. The same function also closes the loop on the #193250 comparison quoted above: when the PR author's own repository role is `maintain` or `admin`, `findMaintainerApproval` returns an author-kind approval immediately and no command is required at all.
2. **A yes/no on the `Decision needed`**: whether `session_authority` joins the closed failover vocabulary. The review's own recommendation is to approve it; the measured alternative is that a refused scheduled run's cause is dropped to `undefined` by the run-history reader's own enum (`z.enum(FAILOVER_REASONS)`), because the writer already emits the value. Who can answer: the repo requires explicit approval for protocol changes (`AGENTS.md` — “Protocol/version bumps … need explicit approval; fix/ship authority ≠ release authority”) but names no owner for them — `CODEOWNERS` is 23 lines covering only `openclaw-secops` and `openclaw-release-managers`, has no catch-all, and lists nothing for `packages/gateway-protocol/**`; searching `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` for a protocol/vocabulary owner returns nothing. So this is waiting for any maintainer, not for a specific team that has been silent. Measured so the decision is framed correctly: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` has **exactly two commits in its entire history** — created whole by #121334 (2026-08-10, `3d5f916523d`) after duplicated reason lists had drifted and worker live events were rejecting `tls_certificate` payloads, and touched once since by #158222 (2026-09-26, `3c449bd35be`), a refactor that preserves the contract. **That framing was accurate when written and is now obsolete — and the correction is the most useful paragraph in this body.** `6f69195cd6b` (#193250, landed 07:24:45Z the same day) added `route_unavailable` to this very list, so `main` is at 17 members and this PR would make 18. That commit is the precedent the reviewer said did not exist, and it is nearly line-for-line the same change: it touched `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` with a **one-line addition to the same no-cooldown-write list** (`main` now reads `params.failoverReason === "route_unavailable" ||` at line 35, immediately beside this PR's line 41), updated the same formatter files (`user-copy.ts`, `assistant-request-failure-copy.ts`, `probe-status.ts`, `failover-error.ts`), regenerated the same predicate (`+3187/−3185` — the ordinal shift described above), added its own `config/test-lines-allocations/clawrouter-credit-immediate-fallback.txt`, and merged. Its final state: **`rating: 🦐 gold shrimp` (3/6)** — the same rung this PR sits on — with **`status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`**, carrying `security-sensitive-changed`, and **zero** `/allow-security-sensitive-change` comments anywhere in its comments or timeline. Two consequences stated plainly: the vocabulary is extendable by exactly the mechanism used here, so a yes points at an in-repo template rather than setting a precedent; and a 3/6 rating has never been this repo's merge bar. (Verified 15:14:10Z against `main`; the gate asymmetry recorded here as unexplained **is now explained, from source**. #193250's guard comment states verbatim: "No secops approval is required. This comment is informational because the PR author has Maintain or Admin access.", names `Repository role: admin` for its author, and matches **the same file** this PR does (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`). The shipped predicate is `scripts/github/security-review-event.mjs:309`, which drops a PR from the review queue when the author's repository role is `maintain` or `admin` — so the exemption keys on the author's permission on the repository, not on the scope of the change. Both PRs do report `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR` in REST, which is exactly the field that misled the earlier version of this paragraph: the workflow does not read it. Two consequences, stated separately so neither overreaches: this PR cannot borrow that zero-approval path, because the command is genuinely required for a contributor-author change; and the rating argument is unaffected, because #193250 still merged at 🦐 3/6, which is why 3/6 is not this repo's merge bar. The `status:` difference is explained by the same mechanism plus the review's own definition - it labels `👀 ready for maintainer look` when it has no contributor-facing blocker left, and `⏳ waiting on maintainer` when an explicit approval or decision is outstanding, which is precisely the state the enforced gate plus the recorded vocabulary decision create here.) The two options, and their costs, both quotable from shipped code. **Option A** is this PR: name the state (`session_authority`) so every consumer that already keys on the vocabulary says the same thing - the 403 mapping (`src/agents/failover-error.ts:191`), the cron run-history cause (`src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`), and the four exhaustive copy maps. **Option B** is the narrower alternative the question implies: keep classifying the refusal as `auth` and only suppress the profile-health write, so no public member is added. Its cost is user-visible and specific: under `auth`, the shipped copy at `src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts:621-622` reads "Couldn't sign in to ${provider}. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works.", and `auth` additionally carries cooldown copy (`:652` → `AUTH_PROFILE_COOLDOWN_COPY.auth`) - so a local relay that never spoke to the credential would still tell the user their saved login is broken, which is the false statement these reports are about (#162119's own diagnostics log `reason=auth` for exactly these 403s). Option A's copy instead reads "refused this request before sending it. Start a fresh request with /new." (`:625-626`), true whether or not the credential works. `VISION.md:99` states the repo's preference for this shape of change - "Once several independent PRs or requests wire in the same kind of capability, the right response is a contract, not a queue of merges" - and three independent P1 reports (#162119, #165739, #191473) wire this one. VISION does not decide enum membership, so this remains a human ask rather than a citation that answers itself.

Head moved twice since the last review: `main` regenerated the one colliding generated path, first in 513c12703ad and again in d0e78b07144, each time flipping this PR to CONFLICTING and stopping CI, so the branch was re-integrated and the predicate regenerated — `e960518954b` (main `9cb29007ed1`, 56 commits) was the head to approve at that point (superseded twice since; item 1 names today's); `a58d99c1fbc` is one merge behind it, the durable review quotes `83e1c7e1d1b`, two merges behind, and the historical notes below still name `23ba4def295`. Re-verified on the newest merge: all five validator checks; the protocol registry, generation, native `--check` and since guards; the core test typecheck; the seven touched suites (45, 25, 13 and 72 passed across four shards); and the test-line ratchet with 15 lines of slack. On the previous merge the same set passed with the touched suites at 72, 13, 42 and 25. One environment caveat carried forward: `codex-app-server:protocol:check` cannot run here because it wants a sibling `openai/codex` checkout at `rust-v0.164.0`, and no workflow references it, so it is a dev-time sync check rather than a gate. One measured caveat: on that earlier merge `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` reported the tree 7 lines over the ceiling, and the identical 7 is `main`’s own overage (same checker, same throwaway-index method: `Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`), while this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292. Nothing was trimmed to hide it; the shared scalar is untouched.

Current state (03:08:18Z, head `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699`): **mergeable, and CI is red-free** — the run is **complete and red-free** (re-read 12:07Z): 111 succeeded / 72 skipped / 1 neutral (`CodeQL`), zero failures, zero cancellations, nothing in progress, and 3 checks that never report. `mergeable` is **MERGEABLE**, with `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` only on the two approvals above. Drift is measured as one full sweep plus hourly increments: the full head-to-`main` sweep at 07:07Z (66 `main` commits, 680 distinct changed paths) and every hourly window since (this round: 8 commits, 95 paths against `main` @ `9f5e8175577`) intersect this PR's 21 files in **0** paths, and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js` is still blob `c5df64e150ac` on that tip, identical to this branch's merge base - so no regeneration is pending and `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699` is a head that can be approved and merged as-is today. Concretely: `check-lint-core-1..5` all green, `checks-ui-e2e (1/4)`, `(2/4)` and `(3/4)` green, both `android-access-native` matrix cells green, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` green, the `openclaw/ci-gate` mirror green, and all 20 `checks-node-changed-*` shards — the family that runs the Gateway product proof — green. That clause is now a citation rather than an inference: in job `127671424815` (`checks-node-changed`, log fetched 21:20Z) the shard log shows `[shard:bun:test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-local-refusal-profile-health.e2e.test.ts] begin` at 02:30:35Z, then `[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 77.48s` and `end (exit 0)` at 02:31:53Z, and the neighbouring `gateway-codex-refusal-product-proof.e2e.test.ts` reports `Test Files 1 passed (1)` at 02:33:21Z. So both refusal-proof e2e files execute in CI on this head - the first is this PR's own, and the second predates it (same blob `50f493f86ad9` on `main`, first added by #136194 on 2026-09-04), which also means this PR does not disturb the lane that already covers the sibling refusal shape. Proof confidence 🦞 5/6 ("Sufficient (terminal)"), patch quality 🦞 5/6, zero open findings, no remaining rank-up moves, and the reviewer's `Before merge` has collapsed from two items to one. The two lanes that *were* red on earlier heads cleared exactly as attributed below (upstream repaired both), so what follows is kept as a measurement trail, not as open work:

- `checks-ui-e2e (1/4)`, `(2/4)`, `(3/4)` — Control UI copy assertions broken by upstream `f1a317d4674` ("chore(ui): refresh control ui locales", landed 17:50Z, i.e. after this branch's previous integration). All seven failing spec files (`cron-search`, `cron-filters`, `cron-run-completion`, `cron-run-suppression`, `boot-module-boundaries`, `settings-layout`, `new-session-page.workspace-memory`) are byte-identical to `main` here — `git diff 77c263b9fa1 HEAD -- <file>` is empty for each — and none is in this change's surface.
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` — the tree is 7 lines over the test-line ceiling, and `main`'s own tree is over by the same 7 under the same checker and method (`Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`); this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292.

Head `a58d99c1fbc` then merged main past `9938e65a609`, the upstream commit that realigned those e2e expectations with the refreshed locales, and past the test-line reconciliation: on this merge the ratchet measures 25 lines of slack rather than 7 over, and the seven UI spec files are byte-identical to a `main` that contains its own repair. Measured on this merge: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `checks-ui-e2e (3/4)` turned green, exactly as those two upstream reconciliations predict. Two lanes stayed red there for a **different** copy drift that the e2e-alignment commit did not cover: `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.device-dispatch.e2e.test.ts` still expects `No worker slots are available` while the UI renders `No session slots are available. Wait for a slot or pick another device.`, and `boot-module-boundaries` / `cron-filters` still expect `to the selected runner` where the UI now renders `to the selected device`. Concretely, on this tree `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-new-session-setup.ts:243` renders `deviceNoSlots: "No session slots are available…"` and `:96` renders `placementSyncsFolder: "Syncs {folder} to the selected device"`, while `ui/src/e2e` still holds 3 expectations for the retired `No worker slots are available` and 1 for `… selected runner`. The paired unit tests already assert the new wording (`ui/src/pages/new-session/device-placement.test.ts:43`, `checkout-chip.test.ts:245`), so the rename was deliberate and only the browser layer lags — a one-line alignment in those specs, not a product change. 
All three spec files are byte-identical to `main` on this branch (`git diff a58d99c1fbc^2 -- <file>` is empty for each), none is in this change's surface, and the alignment belongs to whoever owns that rename — not patched quietly inside a credential-health PR. Superseded — by 05:04:27Z `main` had completed that alignment; the commit-level closure is recorded once in the CI section below rather than three times here. Those strings still appear on this head only because the branch cannot be re-integrated from the contributor's machine right now: `git fetch` of this repository negotiates (the server announces the object count) but no pack data ever arrives, and it has stalled that way across every round since, while a small repository on the same SSH connection round-trips in 4 seconds — so it is specific to this repository's transfer, not a general network outage. Nothing in this list needs a decision anymore; it needs a merge.

Mergeability, stated plainly so nobody re-derives it: `main` regenerated that same generated predicate **again** at 00:44:29Z (`730b60991ee`, #186073), which is twenty minutes after the head above, so this PR went back to `CONFLICTING`. **That is now closed**: a fourth integration, `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699`, resolved it — preserving **both** `session_authority` and main's `route_unavailable` in the canonical tuple (18 members) and regenerating the Gateway predicate against the integrated schema, which is exactly what the reviewer's `Before merge` had begun to ask the contributor for — and the PR now reports `MERGEABLE`. The collision is one generated file and the resolution is mechanical — corrected at 15:14:10Z, because the earlier version of this sentence was wrong: it claimed *one* intersecting file, read from the `compare` API, whose `files` array silently caps at 300 entries — and `main` had changed exactly 300 files in the window, so the list was truncated rather than complete. Counting per file instead (`commits?path=<file>&since=<base date>` for each of this PR's 21 files) gives **12** overlapping paths: the generated predicate plus 11 source and test files — and **all 12 come from that single #193250 commit** (26 files in total), each as a one-line list addition at a different offset. Most are one-line additions at different offsets in the same lists, so the merge is expected to auto-resolve with only the predicate conflicting as it always does, but I cannot prove that from this machine (the fetch needed to test it fails — see below), so what is claimed here is a measured overlap count with an unverified merge outcome, which is strictly better than the false precision it replaces — take main's version of `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js`, run `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, commit the generator output (then re-`git add` it, because a merge commit records the index) — and it recurs on roughly every protocol-touching merge. One thing worth knowing before you merge, measured 13:07Z: two **open** PRs edit the same lists this change touches - #193752 edits `src/agents/failover/classify-core.ts` and `failover-error.ts` (this PR's priority-classifier slot and its 403 status mapping), and #148275 edits `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` (this PR's refusal matcher). Neither one is a competing repair of this bug; the point is only that whichever of them lands first will make this branch need one more mechanical integration, so the approval should key to the head you actually merge rather than to a SHA read earlier. `main` as of `b4c2c8f9e43` still has `session_authority` at 0 occurrences in `failover-reasons.ts` (344 B), `message-patterns.ts` (18,768 B) and `auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` (3,543 B), so nothing has landed ahead of this.

 every push re-keys `/allow-security-sensitive-change` to a fresh SHA and re-runs ~30 minutes of shared CI while changing no verdict. The order of operations that actually ends this is *final integration first, then the approval on whatever head lands*. Two artifacts can mislead whoever picks this up, so both are named rather than left to be rediscovered:

- *Resolved at 02:31:07Z.* The hosted review's `Before merge` checkbox had been asking for `/allow-security-sensitive-change` for `83e1c7e1d1b`, two merges dead — approving a stale SHA does not clear the gate. Re-requesting the review **with new dated facts attached** is what fixed it: the re-derived review is pinned to `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699` and its `Before merge` collapsed from two items to one. The artifact that tracks the live head automatically remains the pinned `openclaw:security-sensitive-guard` comment (it re-keyed to `e960518954b` at 00:37:32Z and re-listed the same single sensitive file, which is the entire scope of what is being approved).
- The inherited reds are tracked to commits, not described vaguely — and **both are now closed upstream**. `8168f831574` (01:39:19Z, #193097) gave the promise executors block bodies, and `9edb1d3e633` (05:04:27Z, #193160, sub-commit `test(ui): align placement expectations with device copy`) aligned `ui/src/e2e/session-placement-module-boundaries.test-support.ts:250` (`:262` had already been using the new wording, which is how the miss was visible). Re-reading both files on `main` returns **0** occurrences of the retired strings. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local Codex owner refusal (HTTP 403 produced by the in-process inference relay, before any provider request) was classified as a provider authentication failure, which cooled down the shared OpenAI OAuth profile and interrupted every other agent using that credential.

## User Impact

User impact: one refused run no longer logs an entire profile out. Sibling agents on the same credential keep working, the model fallback chain is not consumed for a refusal that says nothing about the model, API clients receive a permission rejection instead of a retryable server error, and the message no longer tells operators to sign in again — it tells them to start a fresh request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal is generated locally, so the credential answered nothing; the 401/403 rule in `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts` could not tell the two apart. The fix preserves the local refusal's identity instead of exempting HTTP 403 or the `model_permission_denied` code globally, so genuine provider permission errors keep their exact current handling.

- The local relay's own refusal copy is the identity carrier. Codex's transport drops the relay's JSON body and renders only `error.message` as `unexpected status {status}: {message}, url: {url}` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs`, `UnexpectedResponseError::display_body` / `Display`), so the copy is the part that survives to the runner.
- A new run-scoped `session_authority` failover reason carries it: `src/agents/auth-profiles` and `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` record profile health only for `auth`, `auth_permanent`, and `billing`, so the shared credential is never cooled.
- The reason resolves to `coordination` in `resolveModelFallbackError`, the owner that already stops the chain when "changing models cannot repair" the failure. Another model cannot re-establish the refused run's owner, so the chain surfaces the refusal instead of blaming a candidate, which is what the issue's "should not consume the model fallback chain" requirement asks for.
- `FAILOVER_STATUS` projects the reason as `403` with `permission_error`, so OpenAI-compatible clients stop seeing an unmapped reason fall through to a retryable `500`.
- Operator-facing copy for the reason avoids sign-in advice on both the assistant and auth-profile surfaces.

### Blast radius of the new member, measured rather than asserted

The concern worth answering for the vocabulary decision is whether a new canonical reason could change credential behavior somewhere unintended. The repo already encodes that boundary in types, and every number below is checkable in-tree:

- **There are two closed lists, and the canonical one is deliberately wider.** `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` holds 17 members on this head; `AuthProfileFailureReason` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/types.ts:85` — whose own doc comment says it is the set of "Closed reasons that drive cooldown, disable, and failure counters" — holds 13 and **already excludes three canonical reasons** (`server_error`, `tls_certificate`, `context_overflow`). So "a reason exists in the vocabulary" has never implied "a reason can cool a profile"; `session_authority` becomes the fourth member in that existing class rather than a new kind of thing.
- **One producer, zero casts.** `resolveAuthProfileFailureReason` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts:17`) is the only function that converts a canonical reason into a cooldown reason, and it returns `null` for `session_authority` at line 41. All four profile-health writers route through it and bail on `null` before calling `markAuthProfileFailure`, whose parameter is the narrow union (`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts:555`): `run/auth-controller.ts:318`, `run/failover-retry-controller.ts:134`, `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.ts:148`, `src/agents/simple-completion-profile-failover.ts:44`. Grepping production code for `as AuthProfileFailureReason` returns **no hits**, so there is no path — including no escape hatch — by which the new member can reach cooldown bookkeeping.
- **Stored history stays total.** `src/agents/auth-profiles/profile-usage-stats.ts:33` normalizes persisted reasons against `AUTH_PROFILE_FAILURE_REASONS`, so an unrecognized value in old data degrades to "not a cooldown reason" instead of throwing or cooling.
- **Wire and rollback tolerance, measured — and why it holds is the part worth reading.** The live telemetry schema *is* strict: `WorkerLiveFallbackAttemptSchema.reason` (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.ts:421`) and `fallbackStepFromFailureReason` (`:458`) are a union of one literal per member (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/failover-reason.ts:10-12`), so an older peer's schema literally cannot name `session_authority`. But nothing enforces them on ingress: the worker live-event receiver (`src/gateway/worker-environments/live-events.ts`) validates credential ownership, sequence and window state rather than payload shape, and the only production files that import the generated predicates at all are `src/chat/sender-identity.ts` and `src/config/sessions/session-participant-identity.ts`. So a newer worker reporting this reason to an older Gateway is not rejected, and stored values written by a newer build degrade tolerantly (`src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`). Flagging the caveat explicitly: that tolerance is **incidental to the absence of inbound validation, not designed in** — if these payloads ever gain boundary schema enforcement, widening this enum becomes a downgrade hazard that would need negotiation or a tolerant reader first.
