In the other direction, the three allow-lists that *grant* user-visible side effects all omit the new member deliberately, which is what makes "no re-login prompt" a measured property rather than an intent: re-login recovery (`src/auto-reply/provider-login-recovery.ts:58`, whose members are `auth`, `auth_permanent`, `session_expired`), session model auto-revert (`src/agents/session-model-auto-revert.ts:30`) and profile-recovery affordances (`src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts:656`). Sets like these are invisible to the build, so a maintainer reviewing the vocabulary question can read the three line numbers above as the whole behavioural surface.

- **Every other branch on the reason takes the safe default, and the reason for that is checkable: the new member is simply absent from them.** Grepping these files for `session_authority` returns nothing, so it falls through each predicate rather than being special-cased: `src/agents/failover-policy.ts:12` (the transient cooldown-probe-slot predicate) does not list it, so a refused local run can neither consume a probe slot nor be treated as transient; the provider-runtime diagnostic gates its auth/401 chat copy on `failoverReason === "auth"` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/provider-runtime-failure.ts:160`), so the new reason cannot be labelled an authentication problem on that path either; and the realtime relay's switch (`src/gateway/talk/relay/issues.ts:54`) reaches its `default` at line 68, producing a generic provider error rather than a credentials instruction — the same no-re-login rule the four maps this change *does* update follow.

None of this answers the *policy* question — the reason a human still has to decide is persistence: the value is written into cron run history and read back through `z.enum(FAILOVER_REASONS)` (`src/cron/run-error-reason.ts:6`, `src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`), so the vocabulary and the stored cause must agree. It does, however, bound what a yes costs on the credential side: the cooldown surface cannot receive the new reason.

**The user-facing blast radius is also not one issue, and it predates this PR.** A repo-wide search for the refusal string returns three open P1 reports: #162119 (2026-09-30) records what the classifier did, verbatim from the reporter's own diagnostics — "For each 403, OpenClaw classified the result as `reason=auth`, `attempt=1`, `retry=0`, `rotations=0`, `next=none`" — which is precisely the write path this PR stops; #165739 (2026-10-05) names the producer, `CodexInferenceAuthorizationError("owner")` surfacing as a 403 `model_permission_denied`; and #191473, the issue this PR closes. #176311 merged on 2026-10-23 against the *startup* variant of the native-child path and #165739 is still open, so the classification half was never taken by it. Neither reporter claimed a profile cooldown — that inference is mine, and it is the mechanism the fix exists for — but the `reason=auth` attribution they do record is what routes into `markAuthProfileFailure`, and it has been recorded against this message for five weeks.



**Two completeness questions a reviewer would reasonably ask about this member, each answered from source rather than from intent.** (1) *Does an added reason have to appear in every copy site?* Only in the maps written as `satisfies Record<FailoverReason, …>`, and those are the four the compiler already forces this PR to fill. `src/cron/failure-notification-text.ts` is deliberately **not** one of them: `cronFailureDetailLines` (`:18`) special-cases four members - `billing`/`server_error` at `:22`, `route_unavailable` at `:31`, `model_not_found` at `:37` - and the remaining 14 of the 18 render as the bare `Cause: <token>` at `:43`. A refused scheduled run therefore notifies `Cause: session_authority`, the same shape as today's `Cause: rate_limit` or `Cause: timeout`; giving this reason its own cron guidance is a product choice of the kind #193250 made for `route_unavailable`, not a completeness requirement this PR is missing. (2) *Does an added member require a protocol-version bump?* The repo's own history says no. The negotiated surface is `packages/gateway-protocol/src/version.ts:2-8` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4`, `MIN_CLIENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4`, `MIN_NODE_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3`, `MIN_PROBE_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3`), read today from `main` @ `8dd41fc9529`; `#193250` added `route_unavailable` without touching that file and neither does this PR. The four strict wire positions consuming the enum (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts:460` and `:740`, `schema/worker-admission.ts:421` and `:457`) are unions over the same generated list, and the published SDK declaration bundles are gitignored (`packages/*/dist/`, `.gitignore:45`), so there is no second in-repo artifact that can go stale with the vocabulary.

## PR surface

The `size: XL` label on this PR is generated code, not review surface. Of `+3499/-3153` across 21 files, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js` accounts for `+3155/-3153` by itself: the generator renumbers its internal check identifiers when the vocabulary grows, so adding one enum member rewrites the whole file. It was produced by `pnpm gateway:validators:gen` and verified by `pnpm validators:check`, never hand-edited. The reviewable part is `+41` production lines across 11 files and `+299` test lines across 8 files — which includes the 188-line Gateway-turn product proof — plus a 4-line `config/test-lines-allocations` record.

Regeneration is also the whole merge resolution, and the merge is now done. `main` @ `be881a7f8b1` (2796 commits) is merged into this branch, and the generated predicate was the only colliding path: the six hand-written files both sides touch (`message-patterns.ts`, `failover-error.ts`, `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`, `classify.test.ts`, `model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts`, `scripts/lib/vitest-build-prerequisites.mts`) auto-merged, and `3cee3643e13` publishes the regenerated output on top of main's numbering.

Because `build-artifacts` and the ratchets run on `refs/pull/191562/merge` — this head merged with whatever `main` is at that moment — the generated predicate can merge cleanly as text and still be stale as output. That was the first `build-artifacts` failure on this PR: `main` had advanced 25 commits, none of them under `packages/gateway-protocol/src`, and the merged tree no longer equalled the generator's bytes. Reproduced locally on that merge, fixed by regenerating against it (`23ba4def295`), and re-verified with `validators:check` + `protocol:check`. So regeneration is the last step before pushing, not a step that finishes once.


Integration also caught one stale assertion, which is the point of landing on a current base: `main` added a `model_fallback_chain_stopped` record for local coordination stops (`src/agents/model-fallback-runner.ts:597`), so the chain-stop case now pins that stop event and its `local_runtime_coordination` reason instead of asserting an empty record list. The behavior the case proves is unchanged and was re-verified on the merged base: the refusal rejects with the original error, `run` is called once, no fallback step fires, and no candidate is consumed. Re-ran green on the merge: `validators:check`, `protocol:check`, `tsgo:core:test`, the touched agent/gateway suites, and the Gateway refusal proof above (real build, `Tests 1 passed (1)` in 31s).

Two contributor-side items from the review are now also closed: the redundant helper-level refusal case in `src/agents/failover-error.test.ts` was removed as suggested (its classification, chain-stop and HTTP-status assertions are each pinned at their own owner boundary, and `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` is only a wrapper over the chain resolution), and the cooldown assertion reads the store's own predicate.

## Remaining Gates

For a quick pass, in order of cost:

1. **Approve** — post `/allow-security-sensitive-change` for head `8aadf02c7a44b41976c3cf00d113c07d716d3189` (the conflict-resolved head; the review's `Before merge` names this same SHA). Every push resets this approval, so it has to be keyed to whatever head you land.

   What the gate actually covers, so the approval is scoped: matching this PR's real file list against the repo's own `.github/security-review-policy.yml` (using the repo's `minimatch`, with the policy's own exclusions applied) yields **exactly one** security-sensitive non-test file — `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`, reached through the `credentials` glob `src/agents/**/*auth*.ts`. The production diff there is 3 lines that add `session_authority` to the condition returning `null`, i.e. "write no credential-health state for this run". That policy file's own header declares it the *maintainer-review tier* and says SecOps-only paths remain in CODEOWNERS — and `src/agents/**` has **no** CODEOWNERS entry, so clearing this needs a maintainer's command, not a security team member. The same gap explains why this has been sitting: `packages/gateway-protocol/**` is also unlisted in CODEOWNERS, so the vocabulary decision has no routed owner at all and is picked up only by whoever reads this.

2. **Decide** — the recorded `Decision needed`: whether `session_authority` joins the public failover vocabulary. The reviewer now recommends approving it **and has retracted its own earlier premise** — "the merged route_unavailable precedent establishes that the vocabulary can expand, correcting the earlier immutable-vocabulary premise, but no maintainer has approved this particular addition" — so what is missing is a written maintainer decision, and the readiness cap is now stated as that decision "independently of the enforced security approval".
3. **CI** — complete on `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699`: re-read 12:07Z, 111 succeeded / 72 skipped / 1 neutral, **zero red at all**, both `android-access-native` matrix cells included. (The disk-exhaustion note below is from head `23ba4def295`, kept because it records how that lane was ruled out rather than fixed.) `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` exhausted the disk while unzipping the 16 KB page-size system image (`You are running out of disk space … Free space left: 0 MB`, then `No space left on device`) before any instrumentation ran, and its `(4096, google_apis)` sibling passed on the same head; `openclaw/ci-gate` mirrors that single job. The two lanes that were genuinely red on the previous head — `build-artifacts` (generated predicate stale against a `main` that had moved again) and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` — are both green here.

Checked whether that red can block you: it cannot. The `16384/ps16k` variant is **skipped** on other recently landed PRs and never reports on `main` push commits, and `openclaw/ci-gate` is not a required status check either — PR #192499 landed with `openclaw/ci-gate` red on its merge commit. So this lane needs a re-run by someone with write access to be green, not a code change from me; nothing about it reflects the tree.

The latest review marks this explanation as contributor-supplied because its own log download was redirected to a blocked host, so here are the two lines verbatim from `gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/actions/jobs/126253990114/logs` (re-fetched just now, both still present): `##[warning]You are running out of disk space. The runner will stop working when the machine runs out of disk space. Free space left: 0 MB` at `22:42:12`, then `Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package 16 KB Page Size Google APIs Intel x86_64 Atom System Image: No space left on device.` at `22:42:20`. The job died inside SDK/emulator provisioning — the only earlier steps were Java setup and that `sdkmanager` download, and no Gradle build or instrumentation task had run yet — so the lane cannot be reporting anything about this diff. GitHub’s own record corroborates it without the log CDN: the annotations endpoint for that check run reports `No files were found with the provided path: apps/android/app/build/outputs/androidTest-results/connected/**`, i.e. the job produced no Android test results at all, which is only possible if it stopped before instrumentation.
4. **Optional** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` to cover the packaged update lifecycle, which the host-side checks deliberately do not claim.

As of the latest recorded review (re-keyed to `23ba4def295`), evidence is not the constraint and neither is code: proof confidence is graded 🦞 diamond lobster ("Sufficient (terminal)"), patch quality 🦞 diamond lobster with **no actionable findings and no remaining rank-up moves**, and overall readiness is held at 🦐 only by owner direction on the public vocabulary — the review states that in two places, so the sub-scores cannot lift it on their own. The two items that remain are maintainer-only: the security-sensitive approval for `23ba4def295` (any push resets it) and the recorded `Decision needed` on adding a member to the closed failover vocabulary, for which the review's own recommendation is to approve the additive reason. This section is kept as a record of what was produced locally and what a container would still add, not as a claim that more evidence is required.

Currency check, re-run at 10:04:12Z against today's `main` @ `43654d5fcea` (09:56:52Z) — still no competing repair. `session_authority` occurs **0** times, on that tip, in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` (344 B), `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` (18,768 B), `src/agents/failover/classify-core.ts` (16,997 B) and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` (3,543 B); the byte counts are quoted because a truncated or empty read would print the same zero. `auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` on `main` already carries the `route_unavailable` exclusion (1 occurrence) and not this one, and a repo-wide code search for `owner of this model request` on `main` returns **exactly one path** — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts`, the relay that emits the refusal — so nothing on the classification side mentions it. Earlier reads (at `be881a7f8b1`, then `8209e020b8c`) said the same; today's is the one that matters. So the misclassification is live on `main` as of now, and this PR remains the only fix.

Hook integrity was checked pre-merge against `df9d3240e52` because CI could not run while the branch was unmerged; the merge makes that reasoning moot and the live code is now the evidence. Between the old base and `be881a7f8b1` exactly one commit touched the classifier files this repair hangs off (`7e4bdf2f607`, provider deadline timeouts reported as auth failures), and after the merge the classification still resolves the refusal prose to `session_authority` (`classify.test.ts`), the profile policy still skips the health write (`run.harness-auth-failover.test.ts`), and the Gateway proof still shows the shared profile serving the next turn.

The one stronger form not reproducible on this host:

- **Latest-stable upgrade with existing state** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_BASELINE_SPECS="openclaw@2026.10.10 openclaw@2026.9.36"` (current `latest` and `extended-stable` from the registry) against this PR's candidate package; Package Acceptance resolves the same lane from `source=ref`, and the QA Lab scenario id is `docker-upgrade-survivor` (`qa/scenarios/runtime/docker-upgrade-survivor.yaml`, script `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`). Checked before writing this: every existing-state upgrade scenario the repo ships (`docker-upgrade-survivor`, `docker-release-upgrade-user-journey`, `docker-update-channel-switch`, `docker-update-migration`, `docker-update-restart-auth`) routes through `docker-e2e-lane.ts`, so there is no host-runner equivalent to substitute — this is the one gate that genuinely needs a container or a runner rather than more local evidence. That is the check that a pre-existing install still loads its stored cron, auth-profile and session state after moving onto this build. The additive-vocabulary probe above shows existing reason values still validate, but it is not the upgrade run the review asked for.

Correction worth recording: the Gateway-turn gate did **not** need a container. It runs on the host through the shipped QA product harness (`test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`, `--runner host` semantics), and the earlier claim that this sandbox could not exercise a Gateway turn was wrong. The survivor lane genuinely is container-only (`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` hands off to `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/run.sh` inside the harness image) and this machine has no running Docker daemon; starting one, or using a credentialed remote runner, is a host-level action that needs the operator's go-ahead, and remote execution is maintainer-authorized. I still tried the host route today, and it stops on a guard that should not be bypassed: published `openclaw@2026.10.10`, run in an isolated `HOME` on its own port, created real durable state (a seeded cron row, canonical `state/openclaw.sqlite`, per-agent SQLite, config journal), and this branch's CLI then refuses to load it with `UpdatePreMutationError: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified`, because the machine has a LaunchAgent-managed Gateway. That refusal is correct behavior on a live install, so the existing-state upgrade check needs a container or a runner without a live service rather than a workaround. One ordering detail matters for whoever runs it: until `main` is integrated, this branch's own version reads `2026.10.9`, which predates the `2026.10.10` stable baseline, so a meaningful upgrade run has to follow the merge rather than precede it. Integration is complete, and the blocker was local configuration rather than the link: this machine's global `http.lowSpeedLimit=1` aborted the fetch during the v0 full-ref advertisement ("expected flush after ref listing"), which is what the earlier failures looked like. `git -c protocol.version=2 -c http.lowSpeedLimit=0 fetch` pulled the whole pack at 9-11 MB/s. The merge itself was one generated file plus `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, and the branch version now reads `2026.10.10`, so a survivor run pairs a published `openclaw@2026.9.36` baseline against this build rather than treating `2026.10.10` as the newer side.

prs.title: fix(ios): open chat from a session dashboard
prs.body:
Fixes #199364.

## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone and iPad, tapping a session with a dashboard opens the Dashboard. Its toolbar offers no way to enter that session's chat, and **Done** returns to the previous chat.

## User Impact

Tap **Chat** in the Dashboard toolbar to open the transcript for the session you selected. **Done** still dismisses the Dashboard, and the Desktop shortcut still opens Desktop when that shortcut is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native toolbar already knows which session the Dashboard represents. **Chat** sends that session key through the app's existing chat navigation, so the sidebar selection can continue opening the Dashboard first.

## Evidence

- **Paired Gateway walkthrough.** On an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator with iOS 27.0 and an isolated OpenClaw 2026.11.4 Gateway, Home and Planning Notes had different transcripts generated by a local model. On main, opening Planning Notes showed its Dashboard, and **Done** returned to Home. On the fix, **Chat** opened the Planning Notes transcript.
- **Native regression.** Failed on main at the missing Dashboard **Chat** action. Passed in the iPhone drawer and iPad Pro 13-inch landscape split view using a synthetic Gateway fixture. These runs also checked **Done**, the Desktop shortcut and back navigation, **Home**, and **All Sessions**.
- **Focused checks.** All 83 tests in `SessionDashboardScreenTests`, `RootTabsPresentationTests`, and `OpenClawTypographyTests` passed. SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, native localization verification, fixture lint and formatting, and the diff check passed.
- **Independent review.** Read-only Codex review of the patch against `b1ec28178e0e` found no actionable regressions.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Dashboard on main offers Done without a Chat action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e87979c-87e5-4d4b-9189-05cd4b14852f) | ![Dashboard on the fix offers Chat beside the existing controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11a59187-67e2-425d-87f0-86952f690e33) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The space where a Chat action is needed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f72a0ec-c394-4640-b229-4f6cc48876d3) | ![Chat opens the selected dashboard's conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af52c653-e429-4349-a0ba-b5ebc9435ff2) |

Same synthetic Planning Notes session and iOS 27.0 iPhone simulator configuration. Before `b1ec28178e0e`, after `b82e5d3648a9`. These captures cover the native navigation flow on a simulator.

### Transcript after leaving the Dashboard

| Main after Done | Fix after Chat |
| --- | --- |
| ![Done returns to the Home transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48b6690e-3d76-4aed-8736-cdbe7d3bc6ae) | ![Chat opens Planning Notes with its own reply visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65c522f4-afdf-409b-a693-00c21f585260) |

<details>
<summary>Regression and review details</summary>

The baseline simulator regression ran at `2c47052dd994` and failed with `The dashboard must offer its own native Chat action`. The same test passed with the patch on both form factors. The affected iOS source, shared Swift code, test fixture, and pinned dependencies were identical on `b1ec28178e0e`. The paired Gateway walkthrough used that newer base and the submitted change. The temporary live-proof harness ran against the production iOS app and its real embedded Dashboard.

To rerun the committed regression, start `node scripts/test-ios-sidebar-attention-gateway.mjs` and use the fixture server's documented test-runner environment variables. Run `pnpm ios:test OpenClawUITests/SessionDashboardNavigationUITests/testDashboardOpensItsOwnChat` with `IOS_SIM` set to a disposable iPhone or iPad simulator.

</details>

prs.title: fix: reflect failed access checks in provider status
prs.body:
Fixes #200263

## What Problem This Solves

The Models page can show a green **Ready** badge even after an API-key access check fails. Successful model discovery does not mean the key can run an inference request, so the badge contradicts the failure shown inside the provider row.

## User Impact

User impact: failed or partly successful access checks now appear in the provider summary, including when the row is collapsed. A later successful check restores the normal status. Existing account and model-catalog problems keep their priority. No configuration, default, migration, or user action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the provider badge and expanded check result now use the same status decision. Saved-key checks update the existing scoped result; a request failure replaces a stale successful result rather than leaving Ready behind.

This covers the missing Ready-status portion of #200263. It does not duplicate quota wording in #192165 or change retry attribution in #187720. The fallback-model metadata warning remains outside this proven repair. Earlier proposal #200295 was closed unmerged.

## Evidence

Reproduced through the actual Control UI, isolated Gateway, and built-in OpenAI provider: model discovery succeeds while an inference request returns HTTP 429 with `insufficient_quota`. On the base, saving the failing key, testing access, and collapsing the row all leave Ready. With this patch, the status reflects the failure and a working replacement key restores Ready. Only the external HTTP provider was replaced by a loopback fixture with synthetic keys.

- Both real-Gateway browser tests pass; the new status assertions fail on the base.
- All 263 provider-page tests and 112 sidebar tests pass (375 total), including the previously failing Pages/rail ordering case. Provider regressions cover saved-check propagation, failed-request replacement, status precedence, and recovery.
- Production UI and UI-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent review unavailable: the bound autoreview attempt against `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90` (P0–P3, local candidate) failed because its response JSON was missing. No validated report or findings were returned. @daniel-lxs explicitly authorized opening the PR on the completed test, typecheck, lint, and simplification evidence without a completed local review. ClawSweeper subsequently [reviewed the original published head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200857#issuecomment-6964602484) and reported no actionable code findings.

**Base refresh:** merged main at `2d52a33ef7ac7debf890eb63e5388899be4851f0`, including #200847 (`32aeb4244cf277ad1760e47319e2e07f8f7254b6`), without rewriting PR history. Refreshed head: `e9933002346374a4d5bec3abf6dc6034c6ec079f`. Repeated pr-simplify found no further removal warranted; the eight-file provider patch remains byte-identical. All 375 tests, both real-Gateway browser tests, UI production/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks passed again. New-head CI has started; completion is not claimed.

**Limits:** no live paid API account or macOS run. Refreshed runtime and UI builds complete successfully. The refreshed asset report warns: CSS gzip 57.6 KiB > 56.9 KiB; chat boot requests 21 > 20; chat boot gzip 1300.1 KiB > 1299.9 KiB. No budgets were changed.

### Visual comparison

Real Models page, synthetic provider data, matching light theme and viewport. Before: `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`; after: `015e236110a1d169f9cb81364e82982f60296e28`. The existing quota fixture is labeled Rate limited; changing that classification or wording belongs to #192165.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: Ready contradicts the failed access check](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/813dbd0c-60f6-4fc8-b077-c135f414542a)

**After**

![After: the provider summary reflects the failed access check](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22aac797-f73b-4d1b-8ae6-73b141e58bfa)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before: contradictory Ready status highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55dabe8d-e0ac-4b7b-bd12-c4fba7d4779f)

**After**

![After: corrected provider status highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c61fb7fe-910d-4116-8800-d8613925bf96)

<details>
<summary>Commands and simplification</summary>

- `node scripts/ui.js test --run src/pages/model-providers src/components/app-sidebar.sessions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/model-key-save-check.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- Targeted `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.ui.json` and `scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the eight changed files.

The separate error path that retained a stale successful result is removed. Existing scoped check state remains the single owner; no new stored state is introduced. Production delta: +50/-22; test delta: +164/-4. Remaining growth connects saved-check outcomes and proves the affected user flow.

</details>

Reported by @daniel-lxs in #200263. Thanks to @LiuwqGit for the earlier Ready-status proposal in #200295.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_e96no7)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix(templates): allow re-adding a deleted template agent (#198475)
prs.body:
Closes #198475

## What Problem This Solves

When a Template agent is deleted (`agents.delete` with `deleteFiles: true`), its `agent_deletion_journal` row finishes cleanup (`cleanup_completed = 1`, `phase = "retiring"`). Re-adding the Template under that same agent ID through the running Gateway (`templates.add.apply` via Control UI or CLI) fails immediately during session admission with:

```text
templates.add.apply failed: Agent <id> deletion is in progress; new work is unavailable.
```

## User Impact

Users can delete a Template agent and re-add it with the same ID without restarting the Gateway. Deletions still in progress and requests without the matching creation claim remain blocked. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `applyTemplateAddForGateway`, `createAgentConfigEntry` runs `prepareConfigCommit` inside `withCreationClaim` before publishing `openclaw.json` and before `claimCompletedAgentDeletion` removes the completed tombstone. During `prepareConfigCommit`, `prepareAgentChat` stages the canonical `agent:<id>:main` chat through `beginSessionEffect` and the session transcript worker:

1. `beginSessionEffect` (`src/sessions/session-controller.lifecycle.ts` / `src/sessions/session-controller.lifecycle-agent.ts`) previously rejected every `agent_deletion_journal` status other than `"absent"`, including `"complete"`. It now admits `"complete"` only when the caller holds the matching active creation claim (`resolveAgentCreationClaimAgentId(agent.agentId, agent.statePath) === agent.agentId`), while keeping `"pending"` deletions and unclaimed requests fenced.
2. When an agent is deleted and recreated in the same Gateway process before config publication revives its database, `openOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly` (`src/state/openclaw-agent-db-readonly-open.ts` and `src/infra/agent-database-readers.ts`) checks whether the deleted path is owned by the matching creation claim beneath a `"complete"` tombstone.
3. `retainSessionHistoryWorkerDatabase` (`src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-runtime.ts`, `session-transcript-worker-scopes.ts`, `session-transcript.worker.ts`, `session-transcript-worker.types.ts`) captures the active creation claim on the host, reserves creation-claim admission so the worker reader is retired when the claim ends or revokes, and forwards the creation-claim witness to the worker scope.

## Evidence

### 1. Real Gateway End-to-End Proof (`templates.add.plan` → `templates.add.apply` → `agents.delete` → same-ID `templates.add.plan` → `templates.add.apply`)

#### Before (`113d6243f360`, live Gateway with completed `hopper` tombstone `cleanup_completed=1, delete_files=1, phase=retiring`)

```bash
openclaw templates add @donniefi/hopper --accept-capabilities --json
```

CLI output:
```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Gateway owning ~/.openclaw on local port 18789 could not complete templates.add.apply for Template configuration and provenance: Could not add this Template. Review Gateway logs before retrying.. The outcome may be partial; inspect the operation's status and the target before retrying. No local fallback was attempted."
  }
}
```

Gateway log:
```text
2026-11-17T09:30:56.595-04:00 [gateway/ws] ⇄ res ✓ templates.add.plan 10472ms bytes=9716
2026-11-17T09:30:56.754-04:00 [gateway/templates-add] templates.add.apply failed: Agent hopper deletion is in progress; new work is unavailable.
2026-11-17T09:30:56.755-04:00 [gateway/ws] ⇄ res ✗ templates.add.apply 134ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Could not add this Template. Review Gateway logs before retrying. bytes=180
```

#### After (`9c90bd8121a`, real Gateway on local port `28791` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`)

Full public Gateway lifecycle executed against the running Gateway:

1. **Initial Add (`id = "hopper"`)**:
   ```json
   {
     "agentId": "hopper",
     "workspace": "<state>/workspace-hopper",
     "status": "complete",
     "agentRetained": true,
     "sessionKey": "agent:hopper:main",
     "readiness": { "ready": true, "requirements": [] }
   }
   ```
   Initial `session_nodes` row: `('agent:hopper:main', '862905df-bdc7-480f-b184-6e7455e48f96')`

2. **Delete `hopper` (`agents.delete` with `deleteFiles: true`)**:
   ```json
   {
     "ok": true,
     "agentId": "hopper",
     "removedBindings": 0,
     "failed": []
   }
   ```
   `agent_deletion_journal` after delete:
   ```text
   [('hopper', 'b4767722-487c-4aef-823f-d1cbe5bf5179', 'retiring', 1, 1)]
   ```

3. **Same-ID Plan & Apply (`id = "hopper"`)**:
   - `templates add @donniefi/hopper --dry-run --json`:
     `{"agent": "hopper", "blockedActions": 0, "blockers": [], "ready": true}`
   - `templates add @donniefi/hopper --accept-capabilities --json`:
     ```json
     {
       "agentId": "hopper",
       "workspace": "<state>/workspace-hopper",
       "status": "complete",
       "agentRetained": true,
       "sessionKey": "agent:hopper:main",
       "readiness": { "ready": true, "requirements": [] }
     }
     ```
   - `agent_deletion_journal` after re-add: `[]` (tombstone claimed and removed)
   - Recreated `session_nodes` row: `('agent:hopper:main', 'ed2cffaa-7424-4cd3-b471-91a26d903feb')` (fresh canonical session)

Gateway WebSocket RPC log across the full cycle:
```text
2026-11-17T10:05:11.639-04:00 [gateway] http server listening (0 plugins, 3.8s)
2026-11-17T10:05:27.991-04:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ templates.add.plan 10704ms bytes=9724 conn=01db905f…c603 id=2:e73936cc-c…8d44
2026-11-17T10:06:25.514-04:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ templates.add.apply 57514ms bytes=575 conn=956639a0…2ad8 id=2:f3dbb900-2…165d
2026-11-17T10:06:28.814-04:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ agents.delete 2183ms bytes=835 conn=aef7119e…2167 id=2:d9f0cc67-0…a251
2026-11-17T10:06:52.066-04:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ templates.add.plan 8323ms bytes=9718 conn=005efd81…b5ae id=2:bd5973f2-8…2c2e
2026-11-17T10:07:22.588-04:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ templates.add.apply 30507ms bytes=568 conn=b50a094e…ea55 id=2:f30bc3a8-0…b9b9
```

### 2. Automated Tests, Typecheck, and Lint

```bash
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.templates.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/sessions/session-agent-work-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/templates/gateway-add-pending.test.ts src/infra/agent-database-readers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t 'admitted-recreated$|admitted-reviewed-chat-retry$|admitted-applied$|: revoked$|abort-before-commit$|runs every registered closer and keeps deleted databases closed until revived'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/sessions/session-store-reader-preparation.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-lanes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t 'reuses a live prepared source and rejects revoked custody|rejects a locator retargeted after qualification|revokes readers and joins cleanup.*pending=true, capable=true|retains reads dispatched after cleanup.*capable=true'
npx oxfmt --check <9 changed files>
npx oxlint --type-aware <9 changed files>
```

- `src/sessions/session-agent-work-admission.test.ts`: 8 passed (8)
- `src/templates/gateway-add-pending.test.ts` + `src/infra/agent-database-readers.test.ts`: 6 passed (including `admitted-recreated`, verifying same-ID recreation after `deleteGatewayAgent(..., true)`, creator warm-read success, outside-claim refusal, and tombstone removal)
- `src/config/sessions/session-store-reader-preparation.test.ts` + `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-lanes.test.ts`: 6 passed
- `tsgo`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint --type-aware`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

### 3. CI fixture follow-up

Revision `6e0d69dbc303` copies the already-landed [fresh empty-child accounting test repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1f75f9cec0eedbd58d8a358b97bdeaebebc31871) by @vincentkoc. CI on the prior revision correctly returned zero tokens for an empty child while its stale assertion expected the field to be absent. The correction changes only that test: it now positively checks zero tokens, freshness and the current accounting version on both the returned and stored child. The Template recreation production code is unchanged.

Fresh independent review found no actionable issues in the exact canonical test repair. Both affected table cases passed on trusted main with that identical repaired test; this is not a claim of executing contributor-fork source locally. The real-Gateway and focused production proof above remains prior-revision evidence for unchanged production inputs.

The prior CI attempt also cancelled a UI E2E shard at its 25-minute deadline; that is not passing coverage and its cause is not established. [New-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44205829460) must complete normally before landing. No failed-CI or security waiver is claimed.

Some Telegram chats need transcript echoes hidden while voice transcription remains available to the assistant. This adds per-chat and per-topic controls for group chats and direct chats. A topic setting overrides its parent chat; disabling the echo suppresses only the echo, not transcription or the assistant response. The existing global echo setting remains the top-level control.

## Evidence

Canonical config generators passed; focused run incomplete: 11 tests passed before the run was stopped. Local canonical typecheck unavailable due dependency layout. Exact-head CI passed ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43151112438)). Live voice screenshots supplied by the author show the before/after behavior for one Telegram chat (chat-level echo override disabled). Before: both Syncopia Bot and OpenClaw post transcripts. After: only Syncopia Bot posts a transcript; OpenClaw no longer posts its transcript echo. These screenshots document the visible behavior, not exact-head build provenance or every override case.

prs.title: fix(ui): summarize chat activity by action instead of tool name
prs.body:
Related: #198133, #200683

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent uses several skills or plugins, the collapsed chat activity summary becomes a long list of internal tool names. Repeated ways of reading or updating the same content compete with the conversation instead of giving a useful overview.

## User Impact

Chat activity is summarized by the work performed. Opening the group still shows every operation and its result. This changes Web UI presentation only, including apps using that UI; tool execution and other messaging channels are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The summary builder no longer enumerates unknown tool names. Equivalent operations share a category: skill reads join file reads, related searches share a label, and supported memory and message operations describe their actual work. Unrecognized tools share one fallback, so adding a new plugin cannot add another technical name to the title. Failed calls do not establish a successful result.

The change removes the per-tool title enumeration and obsolete labels. Production code grows by six net lines; the existing test suites gain two regression cases and updated expectations (47 net test lines). No protocol or generated schema changes.

## Evidence

The two reported tool mixtures now produce compact summaries. Expanding the second group retains all seven operation rows. Two regressions fail on the base and pass with the fix; all 79 focused tests pass. UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, and i18n verification pass.

The screenshots use the actual Web UI with synthetic mock-Gateway data, at the same viewport and state. Before: `dbf626f3ddb`; after: `6513bb26bd3`. This is renderer proof, not a live-model run.

CI follow-up at `73484d5642e`: updated the deduplication expectation and used distinct semantic actions in the long-summary fixture. Both affected suites pass (25 tests, including all four Chromium width cases). These are test-only changes; the captures below still represent the same rendered code.

### Before

![Before: internal tool names accumulate in both activity summaries](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e70d6707-a107-4c4a-badb-8155fa31b8b7)

### After

![After: related actions share compact labels and unknown tools share one fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/939d0a1c-2223-49c9-a80a-5daa4be81d2d)

### Annotated comparison

![Before: highlighted activity summaries list internal tool names](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5cea7f5-3cd2-47f0-8dca-f3488596009c)

![After: highlighted summaries describe grouped actions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c81b0fe-b2a8-45d7-b1bf-a9995d621456)

Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete five-file candidate against `dbf626f3ddb` and returned no findings. The committed code is the reviewed candidate. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; hosted review was requested on the ready PR. Broad CI is pending.

prs.title: fix(path): read and edit Markdown with carriage-return line endings
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/parse.ts:48` splits Markdown only on LF and CRLF, and the editor's offsets and line counts (`source.ts:4`, `emit.ts:13`) count only LF, so in a file that uses a lone CR as its line break, frontmatter is never found, items cannot be addressed, and edits land on the wrong line.

Fixes #200757

Thanks @LinzeShi for the report, the fix and the regression matrix.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path resolve` and `openclaw path set` fail on Markdown files whose lines end in a lone carriage return (CR). Frontmatter reads return `resolved: false`, bullet edits return `unresolved`, and inserts write LF lines into a CR file. The same file works with LF or CRLF endings.

## User Impact

Users can read and edit CR-delimited Markdown with `openclaw path`. Line endings and untouched bytes stay as they were, including in files that mix CR, LF and CRLF.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Markdown reader, source offsets, line-ending choice and edit splicing now all treat CR, LF and CRLF as line breaks. JSONL keeps LF record boundaries.

When an edit puts a CR directly before an existing LF (or an LF directly after an existing CR), the two bytes would read as one CRLF break. The edit owner (`replaceMdSource`) now keeps the edited text's edge breaks apart from neighboring source breaks on both sides. Before, only the left side was handled, and only for section inserts. Adding frontmatter to a CR file that starts with a blank LF line dropped that blank line, and a follow-up edit on the returned document wrote into the next section.

## Evidence

Bytes are shown with `<CR>` and `<LF>` for the line-break characters.

Built CLI (`node openclaw.mjs path ... --json --file <f>`, isolated home, state and config, `oc-path` enabled), run twice on each side with identical results. Bytes are JSON-escaped.

Base `1d82bed0a7fe` (merge base):
- `cr.md` `"---<CR>name: old<CR>---<CR>## Settings<CR>- name: before<CR>## Other<CR>- keep: untouched<CR>"`: resolve exits 1 `{"resolved":false}`; set exits 1 `{"ok":false,"reason":"unresolved"}`; file unchanged. LF and CRLF controls pass.
- `"<LF>## Intro<CR>- name: first<CR>## End<CR>- name: second<CR>"`: adding `[frontmatter]/+added` writes LF lines into the CR file (`"---<LF>added: x<LF>---<LF><LF>## Intro<CR>..."`); then `intro/name/name` exits 1 `unresolved`.

Previous PR head `c47277d99632`, same file: adding frontmatter gives `"---<CR>added: x<CR>---<CR><LF>## Intro<CR>..."`. The leading blank line is lost.

This head: the `cr.md` resolve returns `old`, and the set writes `"---<CR>name: old<CR>---<CR>## Settings<CR>- name: after<CR>## Other<CR>- keep: untouched<CR>"`. The second file becomes `"---<CR>added: x<CR>---<CR><LF><LF>## Intro<CR>- name: changed<CR>## End<CR>- name: second<CR>"`. LF and CRLF controls are byte-identical to base.

Tests: on the merge base, 8 of the new edit cases fail (two runs). On this head, `extensions/oc-path` passes 33 files and 510 tests (two runs). The new case `keeps an inserted trailing CR apart from a following LF` fails on `c47277d99632`: the follow-up edit changes `End`'s `second` instead of `Intro`'s `first`.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert fully undoes it; nothing is stored or migrated. Blast radius: `openclaw path` edits to Markdown files with the optional `oc-path` plugin.

prs.title: fix: restore Git release selection after a macOS self-install refusal
prs.body:
Reported by @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

## What Problem This Solves

A dashboard update that first converts a macOS Git installation to the release launcher can select its target before launchd refuses the service rebind. The old Gateway stays healthy, but the selected target has never started and cannot recover through the launcher. This PR repairs that refused-update settlement; **Gateway-initiated conversion itself still needs an external native service context**.

Related: #200833.

## User Impact

The refused conversion fails explicitly, preserves the serving Gateway, records the external-shell service action as owed, and restores the captured previous release selection when its exact trial is still unstarted. Started trials, newer publications, replaced links, and changed fallback builds retain their recovery facts. The LaunchAgent self-install guard remains intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release publication owner now returns the selected link identity, previous release identity, and exact initial trial identity/content. Its compensation uses the existing release-link compare-and-switch operation under the original update executor. The service-recovery owner invokes it only for the native pre-write self-install refusal during conversion, then returns failure instead of proceeding with target activation or plugin convergence.

This rollback is safe for this refusal because the native guard precedes definition publication and service stop, and the unchanged initial trial proves the launcher has not imported the target. Git-release startup migrations and post-activation plugin convergence have not run. This restores selection only; it performs no service restart or data rollback. The installed updater must contain the repair.

The handoff currently starts a detached child on macOS; its separate service launcher is systemd-only. `detached: true` changes the process session, without proving escape from launchd ancestry or resource-coalition membership. The existing macOS restart/park handoff also spawns a detached shell, accepts only lifecycle modes, and cannot execute a service-definition rebind. The `root-spawner-v1` capability check binds the command/executor/root; it does not grant native same-service installation. Service-command root verification and live Gateway build-ID verification remain separate activation requirements. Both observed builds reported `2026.11.4`, so version equality is insufficient.

## Evidence

- The combined owner-boundary regression was red on base `9618c4116960556e5519dd4c3eee404423a93318`: the real native guard refused installation, only launchctl reads occurred, and the target remained selected. It is green with the repair, retaining the incumbent PID/build/readiness facts and owed action without verifying the target.
- Started-trial, newer-publication, replaced-link, and changed-fallback refusals pass. Existing external conversion fixtures, already-converted activation, same-version build-ID checks, and startup recovery pass.
- Retained implementation proof at `883e996ccb263ef650f5a537fed03170aa481024`: all 94 distinct focused tests across five named files passed, including the combined refusal regression and service caller suite (39 tests, 9.02 seconds). Node sibling proof: 93 tests, 28.63 seconds.
- Current test-only repair at `5fa21d8475b66bb2d22af95a45abc11c1f7f9c70`: the named conversion regression passes (1 test, 7.68 seconds including setup; test body 162 ms). Touched-file CI-core typed oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Production code is unchanged.
- [Prior CI run 44205334762, job 134470592691](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44205334762/job/134470592691) failed `mock-exports` on `883e996ccb263ef650f5a537fed03170aa481024`: the runtime mock replaced the real exports. It now forwards the real module and preserves unaffected `defaultRuntime` methods, overriding only `log` and `error`. No isolation annotation, baseline, or script was changed. The old run is not green proof for this head; current-head CI is pending.
- CI-core typed oxlint of all eight touched TypeScript files, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. No broad local build/test/type/lint run was used.
- pr-simplify: selection stays with the existing release owner; service compensation stays with the existing recovery owner. No executor, config, persistent store, protocol bump, service-guard exception, or parallel pointer manager was added. Against the task base: production +118 lines, tests +247 lines, docs +9 lines. The growth carries exact publication evidence and refusal settlement; no existing owner was duplicated.
- Independent autoreview: Shared autoreview (Codex), medium reasoning, P0–P2, complete local snapshot against `9618c4116960556e5519dd4c3eee404423a93318`, committed unchanged as `883e996ccb263ef650f5a537fed03170aa481024`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Native observations and CLI child transport remain fixture boundaries. prs.title: fix: finish A2A tasks for messages sent while the agent is still answering
prs.body:
Root cause: `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.ts:165` completes an A2A task only when dispatch returns `deferredToActiveRun` unset, and #183803 settles only `"followup"` later through `onQueuedFollowupReplyBatch`; a `"steer"` result has no reply delivery or queued batch of its own, so nothing ever settles that task.

Fixes #200646

## What Problem This Solves

With the default `steer` queue mode, an A2A peer that sends a second message while the first is still being answered gets a new task for it. The agent answers that message inside the running turn, but the new task stays `TASK_STATE_WORKING` forever, so a peer polling `GetTask` waits indefinitely and never sees the answer.

## User Impact

A2A peers now get a terminal state for every message steered into an active turn: `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` with the replies the turn delivered after the message joined it, `TASK_STATE_FAILED` (`Agent run failed`) if that turn fails, or `TASK_STATE_FAILED` (`Agent run aborted`) if an operator stops it. These are the same states a queued followup gets. Tasks that start their own turn or queue as a followup are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The A2A dispatch whose run is executing in a session records the final replies it delivers. That is either its own run, or its queued followup's run once that starts: queued followups call the source dispatch's run-start observer. A dispatch that comes back as steered registers with that owner, and when the owner's run ends the steered task settles through the same settlement #183803 added for queued followups (same reply filtering, same `Agent run <kind>` failure). A followup run ends with its terminal batch. Core reports a run's end as completed or failed and reports nothing for a cancelled run, so a run that reported neither settles its steered tasks as aborted. A followup that never starts never becomes the owner, so a dropped followup leaves nothing behind. No core, SDK, schema or config change.

## Evidence

Real Gateway from source (`ocx src`, bundled `a2a` channel, `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`) with a local OpenAI-compatible provider fixture. An A2A peer sends m1 ("answer ONE", reply delayed 8 s), then m2 ("answer TWO") 2 s later in the same `contextId`, both with `returnImmediately`, and polls `GetTask` on both.

- Base `f3638439b9` (twice): m1 `COMPLETED ["ONE"]`, m2 `WORKING []` 45 s after the turn ended. The fixture log shows m2 was answered (`TWO`) inside m1's run.
- Candidate (twice): m1 `COMPLETED ["ONE"]`, m2 `COMPLETED` with an artifact holding the replies `ONE` and `TWO`, about 10 s after sending.
- Failure control (provider returns 500 on every request): base m1 `FAILED`, m2 still `WORKING` 65 s later; candidate m1 and m2 both `FAILED` (`Agent run failed`).
- Operator stop (`openclaw gateway call chat.abort`) after the run consumed the steer: base m2 still `WORKING` 60 s later (twice); previous head 4968ee20a3 m2 `COMPLETED` without text (the review finding); candidate m2 `FAILED` `Agent run aborted` (twice). Normal flow on the same build: m2 `COMPLETED` with `ONE` and `TWO`.
- Built artifact (`ocx build --dts`, `node dist/entry.js`) at this head for the stop and normal runs.
- Steered into a queued followup's run (start in `followup` mode so m2 queues, operator runs `openclaw config set messages.queue.mode steer` while m2's run executes, m3 then steers into it): base 8c09105a m3 still `WORKING` 60 s later (twice, plus once with an operator stop); candidate m3 `COMPLETED` with `TWO` and `THREE` (twice), or `FAILED` `Agent run aborted` when the operator stops the run (twice).
- Full captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200846#issuecomment-6963955920, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200846#issuecomment-6964428507 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200846#issuecomment-6965151308
- Regression tests: `settles a message steered into the active run when that run completes|fails|is cancelled` (red on base for all three; cancelled case red on 4968ee20a3) and `settles a message steered into a queued followup's run with that run's batch` (red on 8c09105a). `inbound.test.ts` + `http.test.ts` pass at this head (41/41).

Thanks @alexph-dev for the precise report and probe.

Merge danger: two-way door. The change is local to the A2A plugin's inbound dispatch and writes no new state; a revert restores the old behavior exactly. Blast radius: A2A peers only; other channels and the core queue are untouched.

prs.title: fix: tell the agent to answer in plain text when Telegram refuses a widget
prs.body:
Closes #200761

## What Problem This Solves

With Telegram widgets turned on, the agent builds an interactive card and calls `show_widget`. The production Telegram Bot API can refuse that send with `INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_NOT_ALLOWED`, even in a private chat. OpenClaw passed the raw error back as a generic `presentation_error`, the same code it uses for card problems the agent can fix. The agent then had to guess whether editing the card or retrying would help, and the user got no card and no answer.

## User Impact

User impact: when Telegram refuses a widget, the agent is told that retrying or editing the card will not help and to answer the current request in plain text, so the user gets a reply instead of a dead end. The `widgets` setting is not changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram widget presenter now recognizes `INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_NOT_ALLOWED` in the delivery error. It keeps the Telegram error text in the tool result and adds one sentence with the plain-text instruction. Every other delivery failure returns the same message as before. The Telegram rich messages doc has a new "Refused delivery" note.

## Evidence

I added two tests in `extensions/telegram/src/widgets/widget-presenter.test.ts`. One checks that a refused send keeps `INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_NOT_ALLOWED` and tells the agent to answer in plain text. The other checks that an unrelated delivery error gets no plain-text advice.

Not run here: the tests, typecheck and lint. The sandbox this change was written in could not install dependencies, so CI is the first run of them. I also did not exercise the refusal against the live Telegram Bot API.

<details>
<summary>Commands for the reviewer</summary>

```
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/widgets/widget-presenter.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/widgets/widget-send.test.ts src/canvas/widget-tool.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:extensions
pnpm lint:extensions
```

</details>

Related: #200766

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw leaves prompt images out of requests to GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra through ClawRouter when the router catalog omits input types for both the model and its selected endpoint. The fallback already recognizes image input for `gpt-6.1-sol`.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw can include prompt images in requests to GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra through ClawRouter when the catalog leaves input types unspecified. Input declarations on the model row or selected endpoint still take precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

#200766 added both GPT-6.2 models to the OpenAI catalog. ClawRouter's exact-ID fallback already included `gpt-6.1-sol` and was missing both new IDs. This change adds them and extends the existing fallback test. The ClawRouter test in #200766 supplies `input` in its mock row and bypasses the fallback.

## Evidence

Checked on macOS 15.7.9 (arm64), Node 24.22.2.

- With only the test change applied to the branch's base commit, the fallback test (`retains known native image inputs without granting unknown OpenAI models`) fails because both GPT-6.2 rows come back as `["text"]`.
- With the fix, that test passes, and `extensions/clawrouter/provider-catalog.test.ts` plus `extensions/clawrouter/gpt-62-compat.test.ts` pass together (10 tests, 47 seconds locally).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passes, and `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the two touched files. The extension test typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`) did not finish locally.
- No live turn was tested through ClawRouter. The fallback test verifies catalog classification, and the compatibility tests check request construction with mocked network calls. The image-loading guard in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/images.ts` skips prompt images when the model lacks image input.

prs.title: fix: keep setup diagnostics separate from progress output
prs.body:
Fixes #200825

## What Problem This Solves

During Quick start > One agent > Skip for now, a database diagnostic can appear directly inside the setup progress line. The two messages run together even though setup succeeds.

## User Impact

Setup diagnostics remain readable without hiding them. Normal stderr forwarding, JSON stdout, and persisted logs are preserved. No configuration change, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node forwards worker stderr without passing through the host logger's progress cleanup. The database-worker lifecycle now invokes the existing terminal line-clear owner before that forwarding. It does not replace the stream or add another logging path.

## Evidence

### Isolated real CLI before/after evidence (2026-11-18)

Real command: `pnpm openclaw onboard`. Interactive selections: Quick start > One agent > Skip for now.

Debian 12, Node.js 24.20.0, xterm-256color PTY, 110 columns by 50 rows. Each run used a fresh isolated HOME/state, excluding inherited credentials/config. `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` selected Node through the supported source launcher. No mocked diagnostics, manually seeded config, or background service installation. This was a source-built CLI run, not a new installer run.

Before: pristine production source at `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`. After: that base plus only this PR's four-file patch, matching published head `5d5fa6044aceb88788b39d0a95ba9639d3d9d6b4`. No sibling completion-message fix or additional production patch.

#### Before

Exact diagnostic boundary, with terminal line endings shown literally:

~~~text
Setting up your workspace, gateway, and sessions…[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main\r\n
~~~

The diagnostic follows the progress text on the same line.

#### After

Exact diagnostic boundary, with control bytes shown literally:

~~~text
Setting up your workspace, gateway, and sessions…\r\x1b[2K[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main\r\n
~~~

The added `\r\x1b[2K` returns to column 1 and clears the active line before the diagnostic. The visible diagnostic line is:

~~~text
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main
~~~

#### Successful completion, both runs

Actual output lines, omitting terminal formatting and intervening output:

~~~text
Workspace OK: ~/.openclaw/workspace
Sessions OK: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions
~~~

Both reached Next steps, including:

~~~text
Add AI later: re-run `openclaw onboard`
After AI connects, add a channel: `openclaw channels add`
Open the dashboard: `openclaw dashboard`
~~~

Both ended:

~~~text
└  Everything's in place.
~~~

Both processes exited 0. The separate duplicate-completion bug remains in this isolated patch, as expected. Fresh five-file focused test run after the capture: 76 passed in 56.14 seconds. Author simplification found no further changes justified; source was restored byte-identically after the baseline capture and `git diff --check` passed. No new commit or push was made for these captures. The captures are evidence for the explicitly named head above, not later base-refresh commits.

### Earlier verification

The real-worker regression failed on the unchanged production base because the stderr write immediately before the diagnostic was `Setting up workspace`, not the line-clear sequence. With this fix, the preceding write is `\r\x1b[2K` (escapes shown literally), the diagnostic remains present, JSON stdout still parses, and all expected log records persist through close.

- All five focused test files passed: 76 tests in 57.44 seconds of wrapper wall time. The changed logging test took 0.256 seconds; lifecycle tests totaled 0.037 seconds. CI timing is not yet available.
- State-logging typecheck, four-file lint, four-file format check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Author simplification reused `withProgress` instead of manual cleanup and a mutable result, removing 7 lines from the supplied candidate without removing assertions. Final delta: runtime +3/-0; tests and fixtures +16/-2.
- Independent review tooling did not return a completed report. The requester explicitly instructed publication using the passing tests and author simplification; no clean independent-review result is claimed.

The original interactive reproduction used the official 2026.11.5 installer on Debian 12 / Node 24.20.0, with installation and onboarding run separately. Source reproduction used base `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`; an earlier combined local fix passed the wizard replay. This isolated PR was verified by the focused real-worker and CLI tests above. No macOS/Windows, live-provider, background-daemon, or full-suite validation is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Exact local checks</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts src/cli/progress.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json src/cli/test-runtime-capture.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/cli/test-runtime-capture.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts
git diff --check
```

</details>

Contributor credit: @daniel-lxs.

prs.title: fix: show onboarding completion only once
prs.body:
Fixes #200826

## What Problem This Solves

After Quick start > One agent > Skip for now, onboarding prints "Everything's in place." twice, with the first message appearing before the next-step instructions. The repeated success message makes the end of setup unclear.

## User Impact

Onboarding now shows one final completion message after the setup summary and next steps. No configuration changes, migrations, or user action are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stop the setup spinner silently before displaying the Local setup summary. The final outro remains the owner of completion messaging, and setup failure handling remains in place.

## Evidence

### Isolated real CLI before/after evidence

Command: `pnpm openclaw onboard`. Interactive selections: Quick start > One agent > Skip for now.

Environment: Debian 12 container, Node.js 24.20.0, xterm-256color PTY, 110 columns by 50 rows. Each run used a separate initially empty HOME, XDG directories, and OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR. The PTY helper only supplied the real wizard keystrokes and captured output. No mocked setup, manual configuration, provider credentials, or background service installation.

Before: production source at `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`. After: that base plus only the patch published as PR #200858 head `a5fad898e67c017fa9eb794e90f85358584a2064`. prs.title: fix: let cron jobs bound to a Telegram chat post there when reply threading is on
prs.body:
Related: #196962, #196963, #177297, #165137

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a cron job that targets an existing Telegram conversation (`sessionTarget: "session:<key>"`) cannot post there with the `message` tool when the account's `replyToMode` is `first`, `all` or `batched`. The tool fails with `ToolInputError: replyTo must be a positive integer.` although the model passed no `replyTo`. Other session events (exec and task completion, hook wakes) take the same path.

## User Impact

User impact: with `replyToMode` `first`, `all` or `batched`, a cron job or background event bound to a Telegram chat can now post there with the `message` tool. Before, the user saw "⚠️ Message failed" instead of the content while the cron run recorded `ok`. Replies to real Telegram messages keep their reply target, an explicit `replyTo` is still validated, and no configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A session event's message id is its occurrence id (a UUID), not a channel message. The Telegram plugin's tool context set no current message id of its own, so the `message` tool inherited the UUID as its implicit reply target and the plugin's positive-integer check rejected the send. #177297 fixed the same defect for Feishu and #196963 for Discord. This applies the same rule to Telegram, in the plugin: the tool context's current message id is set only when it is a positive integer, the same parse the plugin already uses for history reads.

#165137 fixed this error for chat handoffs by dropping ids that arrive on an internal channel. A session event keeps its delivery channel, so that check does not apply to it.

Behavior to know:

- Only an implicit reply target that is not a positive integer is dropped. Native message ids, topic routing and `replyToMode` handling are unchanged.
- An explicit `replyTo` from the model is still validated.
- Button (callback-query) and widget turns use the query id as their message id. A query id that is not a positive integer is no longer used as an implicit reply target either.
- Block replies, compaction notices and final payloads are not changed, and no `resolveReplyTransport` is added: Telegram's outbound path already parses the reply id (`parseTelegramReplyToMessageId`) and drops a non-numeric anchor instead of failing.

Docs: `docs/channels/telegram/messaging.md` gains two sentences saying only native Telegram message ids are used as implicit reply targets.

<details>
<summary>Where the UUID comes from</summary>

- `buildSessionEventContext` sets `MessageSid` to the occurrence id, keeps the delivery channel as `Provider`, and sets `InputProvenance.kind: "internal_system"`.
- `buildThreadingToolContext` passes `MessageSidFull ?? MessageSid` to the channel's `buildToolContext` as `CurrentMessageId`, and keeps it as `currentMessageId` unless the channel's tool context sets the `currentMessageId` key (an explicit `undefined` counts).
- `resolveAndApplyOutboundReplyToId` turns `currentMessageId` into `replyTo` when the send targets the current conversation and `replyToMode` is not `off`.
- `buildTelegramThreadingToolContext` returned no `currentMessageId`, so the UUID reached the plugin's positive-integer check.
- The event keeps its `MessageSid` for admission, dedupe and recovery; core is not changed.

</details>

## Evidence

Tested at `89caa89ca2ee` (baseline `05243ef831d3`).

**Gateway, QA Lab:** an isolated Gateway, the real Telegram plugin against Crabline's local Telegram Bot API server, mock-openai, and the real cron scheduler. The new scenario `cron-session-telegram-reply-target` sets `replyToMode: first`, opens a Telegram DM, adds a cron job that targets that DM's session, and forces one run. The scripted model sends a marker to the conversation with the `message` tool and passes no `replyTo`.

| | `message` tool result | Telegram received | cron run |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline + the new scenario only | `ToolInputError: replyTo must be a positive integer.` | `⚠️ Message failed`, no marker | `ok` |
| this PR | sent | the marker, with no `reply_parameters` | `ok` |

In the same run, the reply to the user's own DM still carries `reply_parameters.message_id`.

<details>
<summary>Command and Bot API calls</summary>

    pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --channel-driver crabline \
      --channel telegram --scenario cron-session-telegram-reply-target

baseline:
    POST sendMessage {"chat_id":"<dm>","text":"QA-SESSION-REPLY-TARGET-READY","reply_parameters":{"message_id":1,...}}
    POST sendMessage {"chat_id":"<dm>","text":"⚠️ Message failed"}
this PR:
    POST sendMessage {"chat_id":"<dm>","text":"QA-SESSION-REPLY-TARGET-READY","reply_parameters":{"message_id":1,...}}
    POST sendMessage {"chat_id":"<dm>","text":"QA-SESSION-EVENT-REPLY-TARGET-SENT"}

</details>

**Regression test:** a new two-row case in `extensions/telegram/src/session-route.test.ts` builds the Telegram tool context with a native message id and a session-event UUID. On the baseline both rows fail: the plugin returns no `currentMessageId`, so core keeps the turn's id. At the head both pass.

Checks at the head:

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/session-route.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 53 passed, 13 s wall locally (10.8 s Vitest duration).
- `pnpm test extensions/telegram --maxWorkers=3`: 177 files, 2296 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: 34 lanes pass, including format, typecheck, the dead-export scan and the boundary guards. `lint` is red on one file this PR does not touch (`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-result-owed.expiry-discard.test.ts:53`, `no-underscore-dangle`); that file is unchanged from the baseline.

Local review: autoreview is not set up here and was not run.

Simplification pass: the fix reuses the plugin's existing positive-integer parse at the one place the id enters the tool context. Against the merge base, production code is +6, test code +13, docs +2. The QA Lab scenario is a separate commit.

Not covered:

- Only a cron job bound to a Telegram DM with `replyToMode: first` was run end to end. `all`, `batched`, groups and topics, and the other session-event sources (exec and task completion, hook wakes) take the same path but were not run.
- No live Telegram bot was used; Crabline stands in for the Bot API. The failing check runs in the plugin before any API call.
- Other channel adapters are not changed.

prs.title: fix(lmstudio): guard model discovery with the embedding SSRF policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LM Studio catalog refresh and dynamic model preparation fetched the configured base URL with platform fetch. That path follows redirects and sends the provider API key. Embeddings in the same plugin already build a guarded policy from the base URL and `allowPrivateNetwork`. Discovery now uses that policy. An omitted setting still allows a private local LM Studio. An explicit denial sends no request.

## Evidence

Head `35ec16b1f7e` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1. The shipped catalog owner is `extensions/lmstudio/provider-discovery.ts`, which calls `discoverLmstudioProvider` in strict mode. Dynamic preparation is `prepareLmstudioDynamicModel`. Both ran against a loopback HTTP server that speaks the LM Studio models JSON shape. The bearer value is a synthetic local marker and is not shown.

```console
OK: catalog allow=omit models=1 requests=1 auth=bearer custom=present
[security] blocked URL fetch (lmstudio-model-discovery) reason=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
OK: catalog allow=false models=0 requests=0 auth=none custom=none
OK: catalog allow=true models=1 requests=1 auth=bearer custom=present
OK: dynamic allow=omit model=proof-local requests=1 auth=bearer custom=present
OK: dynamic allow=false model=missing requests=0
OK: dynamic allow=true model=proof-local requests=1 auth=bearer custom=present
OK: redirect first=1 auth=bearer custom=present second=1 secondAuth=absent secondCustom=absent
```

The redirect was from the configured origin to another port on the same loopback host. The first hop carried the bearer and the custom `X-Proof-Client` header. The followed hop received the models request with both absent.

Upgrade from published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`) on Windows 11 10.0.26300, Node v24.19.0, same head `35ec16b1f7e`. Published `onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health --auth-choice lmstudio` wrote the provider, model id `proof-local`, apiKey field `LM_API_TOKEN`, profile `lmstudio:default`, and the synthetic marker in `authProfiles.store`. The listener was loopback HTTP, not the LM Studio app. The marker value is not shown.

Published `config set models.providers.lmstudio.request.allowPrivateNetwork false --strict-json`, then published `models list --refresh --provider lmstudio`. The server recorded the saved marker. The process then exited 1 with a clone error after that request.

```console
Gateway is not running. Refreshing the local model catalog.
{"method":"GET","url":"/api/v1/models","auth":"marker"}
```

This head loaded that same state with `loadAuthProfileStoreForRuntimeAsync` and ran the plugin catalog `run` plus `prepareLmstudioDynamicModel`. Denial opened no new socket. Allowing the saved setting returned `proof-local` and sent the marker.

```console
saved-profile credential=marker
[security] blocked URL fetch (lmstudio-model-discovery) reason=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
OK: head catalog allow=false models=none hits 2->2
OK: head dynamic allow=false model=missing hits 4->4
OK: head catalog allow=true models=proof-local hits 2->3
OK: head dynamic allow=true model=proof-local hits 3->4
{"method":"GET","url":"/api/v1/models","auth":"marker"}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Saved LM Studio settings and credentials from published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 still discover a loopback model on this head. An explicit private-network denial sends no request on this head. The same saved denial still sends the credential on 2026.11.2. Omitted and allowed discovery, and a cross-origin redirect that drops the bearer, stay as already shown on macOS.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 11 10.0.26300, Node v24.19.0, published OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf`) for the saved config, head `35ec16b1f7e` for the patched catalog and dynamic preparation. Earlier macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, same head. The listener was a local HTTP server, not the LM Studio app.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Published onboard wrote the LM Studio provider and credential against loopback. Published config set `models.providers.lmstudio.request.allowPrivateNetwork` to false, then published `models list --refresh --provider lmstudio`. This head loaded `authProfiles.store` and ran the plugin catalog `run` and `prepareLmstudioDynamicModel`. The published CLI then set the same path to true and the head calls were repeated.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied below.

```console
{"method":"GET","url":"/api/v1/models","auth":"marker"}
[security] blocked URL fetch (lmstudio-model-discovery) reason=Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
OK: head catalog allow=false models=none hits 2->2
OK: head dynamic allow=false model=missing hits 4->4
OK: head catalog allow=true models=proof-local hits 2->3
OK: head dynamic allow=true model=proof-local hits 3->4
OK: redirect first=1 auth=bearer custom=present second=1 secondAuth=absent secondCustom=absent
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Published 2026.11.2 still requested `/api/v1/models` with the saved marker when `allowPrivateNetwork` was false. This head blocked that denial before HTTP for both catalog refresh and dynamic preparation. With the saved setting true, both returned `proof-local` and sent the marker. The macOS redirect hop still received neither the bearer nor the custom header.
- **What was not tested:** The LM Studio desktop app. A server on another machine. The published `models list --refresh` process did not exit 0. It recorded the request, then exited 1 with a clone error.

## Summary

Catalog refresh and dynamic preparation use the embedding SSRF policy. The local default still allows a private LM Studio. An explicit denial is blocked before HTTP. A cross-origin redirect does not carry the bearer or the custom header.

The test-line ratchet on this branch is still red. The base tree is already over its ceiling, this branch adds lines, and `check-test-lines-ratchet` refuses to forgive that inherited debt. Raising the allocation above the lines this branch adds is rejected. The restored discovery regressions stay.
