prs.title: fix: avoid reinstalling unchanged ClawHub plugins
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
A second update of an unchanged ClawHub-backed plugin reinstalls the same artifact and reports a change. The unchanged shortcut covered npm installs only. This breaks the release upgrade survivor's no-op update check.

## User Impact
Updating an unchanged, verified ClawHub plugin no longer needlessly reinstalls it or reports a change. Changed or damaged installations still take the normal repair path. No configuration migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made
Keep ClawHub resolution, trust, compatibility, and download verification authoritative. Retain an installed plugin only when its recorded package/version/artifact kind and attested digest match the selected artifact, and existing installed-package validation and host-link auditing pass. Otherwise use the existing installer. Preserve unchanged install metadata and report the retained outcome through the updater.

File-list-only releases continue through extraction/install. The unchanged check still downloads and verifies the selected artifact; it is not network-free.

## Evidence
- Red on the original code: identical-artifact update incorrectly reported changed; changed-digest control passed.
- 71 tests passed across ClawHub resolver/trust/cleanup and the initial regression.
- Before the mechanical extraction, the regression and updater suite passed 95 tests in 148.54 seconds. Covers identical digest, changed digest, missing installed entry, blocked release, and incompatible release; exercises the real updater/archive installer with mocked network.
- After extraction, all 65 affected ClawHub resolver and unchanged-update tests passed in 56.16 seconds. Targeted typecheck, scoped type-aware lint (six TypeScript files), formatting, git diff --check, and line-cap ratchet passed after extraction of retained-install validation into its focused owner. Reused the existing ClawHub artifact normalization and removed the duplicate digest resolver; no line-limit waiver.
- The combined validation command initially exhausted its outer five-minute budget during test preparation after types/lint passed. Only the pending tests were run separately to the successful result above; no test timeout or assertion was changed.

- PR CI found a type-only circular dependency between the retained-install helper and its caller. The correction uses the existing leaf package-install parameter contract. Targeted types, lint, formatting, diff check, and Madge (0 cycles) pass on the corrected head; runtime logic and prior behavioral proof are unchanged.

## Limits
The original Docker upgrade survivor has not been rerun locally (no Docker daemon). The regression uses a synthetic ZIP; existing ClawHub tests cover npm-pack resolution/digest verification. Release qualification must prove the actual candidate upgrade. Independent review was explicitly waived by the operator; author source inspection was performed.

prs.title: feat(msteams): send private and shared channel files to the channel's own SharePoint site
prs.body:
Closes #185926

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bots cannot send files in Microsoft Teams private or shared channels unless an operator configures a single central `sharePointSiteId`, which exposes every private channel's files to that site's members and still shows "request access" to channel members.

## User Impact

User impact: in private and shared channels, file sends now land on that channel's own SharePoint site, where exactly the channel's members already have access, and the file card opens without extra permissions. No organization-wide sharing link is created for those files. Standard channels, group chats and explicit `sharePointSiteId` keep their current behavior. No new Graph permissions and no config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #189339. Teams keeps a private/shared channel's site membership in sync with the channel, so the channel's own site is the only upload target that preserves the channel audience. For a non-standard `membershipType`, the resolver reads `GET /teams/{groupId}/channels/{channelId}/filesFolder`, then `GET /drives/{driveId}?$select=sharePointIds` (drive resources spell it `sharePointIds`; driveItems use `sharepointIds`), and builds the site ID `{hostname},{siteId},{webId}`. Results are cached per account, tenant, bot, team and channel, like the team-site cache.

`resolveMSTeamsSharePointSiteId` now returns `{ siteId, memberScoped }`. Member-scoped uploads skip `createLink`: the organization link that channel sends create would let anyone in the tenant holding its URL read a private-channel file, and channel membership already grants access through the file card's `webDavUrl`. An incomplete drive response fails closed before upload.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** `vitest` msteams config, 92 files / 943 tests pass. New cases run the real send paths (proactive and reply) against stubbed Graph `fetch`: private and shared channels upload to the channel site, never call `/groups/.../sites/root` or `createLink`, and cache the channel site (one `filesFolder` call across two sends); member-scoped uploads create no link; incomplete `sharePointIds` fails closed.
- **Static:** `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: typecheck (extensions and extension tests), lint, plugin boundaries and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan fails only on `src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts` (`retireControlUiSessionPrState`), unrelated to this change.

### Real behavior proof (production)

Multi-team production deployment, private channel, `sharePointSiteId` absent.

**Before** (#189339's behavior; private channels rejected). Gateway file log, redacted:

```
14:00:01Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 3 rows of test data"
          conversation: 19:<private-channel-id>@thread.tacv2;messageid=<id>
14:00:01Z [msteams] dispatching to agent
14:02:57Z [tools] tool_call failed: msteams file send failed: Automatic SharePoint site discovery
          supports standard channels only. Set channels.msteams.sharePointSiteId to upload to a specific site.
14:03:02Z [msteams] dispatch complete — counts: { tool: 0, block: 0, final: 1 }
```

The user received a text-only reply. No file reached the channel.

**After** (this change, backported onto the deployed release). Same private channel, first file send after a gateway restart (empty cache):

```
11:24:17Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 4 rows of test data"
11:24:17Z [msteams] dispatching to agent — sessionKey: agent:main:msteams:channel:19:<private-channel-id>…
11:24:36Z [msteams:send] sent native file card — fileName: <report> 1.csv
```

Graph check after the send (bot application credentials):

- `<folder>/<report> 1.csv` (created 11:24:35Z) sits on the private channel's own site (`/sites/<team>-<private-channel>`).
- Item permissions are only the channel site's Owners / Members / Visitors groups. No `organization` link.
- The parent team site has no entry for this send.
- The requester opened the file card from the channel.

During rollout, the first build read `sharepointIds` from the drive and failed closed ("incomplete SharePoint IDs") without uploading anything; Graph returns `sharePointIds` on drive resources. A later build still created the organization link; Graph showed it on the item, which is why member-scoped uploads now skip `createLink`.

### Access check (member, non-member, removal)

Same private channel. Each person opened the file's direct document URL in a browser, signed in with their own work account. Times are UTC.

| Step | Who | File | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Channel member | `<report-1>.csv`, sent by the bot | Opens (09:14) |
| 2 | Owner of the parent team, not a channel member. Also tried with their admin account | `<report-1>.csv` | Access denied (09:16) |
| 3 | The step 1 member, removed from the channel about 6 minutes earlier | `<report-1>.csv` | "You need access" (09:24) |
| 4 | Bot sends a new file in the same channel. No gateway restart, so the channel site comes from the cache | `<report-2>.csv` | Lands on the channel site (09:23). Inherits the library permissions; no sharing link |
| 5 | The removed member | `<report-2>.csv` | "You need access" (09:26) |
| 6 | A channel owner | `<report-2>.csv` | Opens (09:25) |

The removed user left the channel site's Members group without any bot action (checked 09:18). Access follows Teams channel membership.

Before step 1, an organization link on `<report-1>.csv` was deleted. A manual "Copy link" in the Teams client had created it, not the bot. After that, both files grant access only to the channel site's Owners, Members and Visitors groups (checked through SharePoint REST as a channel owner).

prs.title: fix: keep chat backgrounds visible when switching sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switching chats could briefly replace an already-loaded background photo with a blank canvas. If the second download failed, the photo stayed blank.

## User Impact

Once your custom photo is loaded, opening another chat or switching back keeps it visible without another download. No settings changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The photo belongs to the signed-in profile, not to a conversation. Chat panes now reuse a finished image only when the connection, profile, and asset still match. In-flight reads remain private to their pane, and the image is released when its last owner leaves.

## Evidence

In Chromium with a mock Gateway, the test loads a photo, rejects any further request for it, and clicks from one session to another and back. Before, the second session requested the photo again and went blank. After, the same photo stayed visible on every sampled animation frame, with one image request in total.

All 21 background unit tests passed, including logout and client replacement. The Control UI typecheck and focused lint passed. Local autoreview of the complete change against `7338e1c1e4c1bd` (commit `5d1505084be9e7`) found no actionable P0–P2 issues. No live account or Gateway was used for the reproduction.

### Before and after

The same sidebar switch in the production UI at 1280 × 900 with synthetic sessions. The initial image succeeds; a repeated image request is deliberately unavailable so the blank frame is visible.

**Before**

![Before: the destination session has a blank background](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dcb950d-a859-4def-a98c-914ed6109f40)

**After**

![After: the loaded photo remains visible in the destination session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f39e98f-2f5f-4c6e-a33e-6ae212985994)

![After: the same region with the retained photo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58dcf399-e6a6-4755-990e-7a2611e9e3f5)

prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user ignores the question number in replies like "1. Deny"
prs.body: Closes #190485 Related: #173760, #173845, #146646 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a multi-question `ask_user` answer is saved as `1. Deny`, lands on the wrong question, or is rejected when the user numbers each reply line the way the prompt numbers the questions. ## User Impact User impact: replying `1. Deny` and `2. Approved` on separate lines answers question 1 with `Deny` and question 2 with `Approved`, in any line order. A reply that answers only some questions is still rejected and the question stays open. Multi-question prompts now label questions `Question 1: Deploy` and number each question's options from 1. On Telegram and Signal, the old `1. Deploy` header ran together with the option lines into one list (`4. Checks`), so answering by the displayed number picked the wrong question. Single-question cards rendered as Telegram messages or Teams cards now number their options to match "Reply with the number". Compatibility: in a multi-question reply, a line starting with digits, a dot and whitespace (`2. Approved`) is read as an answer to that question number. `1.5`, `Node.js: 22` and `U.S. region: East` parse as before. A line matched to a question by number or id no longer also fills another question by position. On main, `2: Approved` alone completed question 1 with the text `2: Approved`; it is now rejected as incomplete. ## Why This Change Was Made The reply parser only treated `:`, `=` and `-` as key separators. `1. Deny` stayed positional, so the agent received `1. Deny` as the answer, reordered lines landed on the wrong question, and questions with fixed options rejected the reply. Numbered lines are now a separate rule that requires whitespace after the dot, checked before the unchanged keyed syntax. The single-question card text now uses the same `1. Label - description` lines as the text prompt. Multi-question prompts numbered each question (`1. Deploy`) directly above options that also start at `1.`. Telegram and Signal render markdown lists with their own numbering, so the header and the options became one list: `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`. Questions are now labeled `Question 1: Deploy`. That is not a list marker, so each question's options render from 1, and the question number is the one the `1. answer` rule binds. The first revision of this PR also copied a single-line reply into every question. That was wrong: it invented answers the user never gave and broke the incomplete-answer contract from #146646. It is removed. The multi-question guidance wording is left to #173845, so this PR no longer touches that string. The live replies in #190485 were each a single line for a two-question card, so they were incomplete and their rejection was correct. That issue is corrected. ## Evidence - Real model, real Gateway, Telegram through a local Bot API. Two Gateways ran the bundled Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API, with `qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700` behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: one built from main `3855c896edd`, and one built from this branch merged onto it. The Gateway and Vitest ran on macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1. The model was told the exact `ask_user` arguments and made the call itself: two questions, Ruling and Authorize, each with options Approve and Deny. Every reply reached the Gateway as a Telegram update. Two runs per build gave the same results: | | main `3855c896edd` | this branch | |---|---|---| | numbered lines in the card the bot sent | `1. Ruling`, `2. Approve`, `3. Deny`, `4. Authorize`, `5. Approve`, `6. Deny` | `Question 1: Ruling`, `1. Approve`, `2. Deny`, `Question 2: Authorize`, `1. Approve`, `2. Deny` | | reply `1. Deny` / `2. Approve` | Ruling `1. Deny`, Authorize `2. Approve` | Ruling `Deny`, Authorize `Approve` | | reply `2. Approve` / `1. Deny` | Ruling `2. Approve`, Authorize `1. Deny` | Ruling `Deny`, Authorize `Approve` | | tool result in the resumed model request, reversed reply | `Ruling: 2. Approve` / `Authorize: 1. Deny` | `Ruling: Deny` / `Authorize: Approve` | | the agent's reply, reversed | `RESULT B \| ruling=2. Approve \| authorize=1. Deny` | `RESULT B \| ruling=Deny \| authorize=Approve` | | reply `1. Deny` alone | rejected (`question 'authorize' requires an answer`), question still pending, no model request in 40 s | the same | In the in-order reply, the model got the same `Ruling: Deny` / `Authorize: Approve` on this branch, and `Ruling: 1. Deny` / `Authorize: 2. Approve` on main. After the incomplete reply, both builds sent nothing to Telegram and retried the rejected message with backoff, 6 rejections in 40 s. That is #193159, which this PR does not change. - Regression table in `src/agents/harness/user-input-bridge.test.ts` (5 rows): 5/5 pass. With `user-input-bridge.ts` from main (`1b15b48e2f3`), 2 rows fail: `1. Deny\n2. Approved` is saved as `"1. Deny"`, and a lone `2. Approved` fills question 1 with `"2. Approved"`. With the previous head (`303c244630d`), 4 rows fail: lone `2` answers both questions, `1.5\n2.5` becomes `5`/`5`, and `Node.js: 22` / `U.S. region: East` split at the dot. - Consumers: 18 test files, 354 tests pass locally, including the 3 suites that failed in [run 41326074085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41326074085): `dispatch-from-config.question-custody` 17/17, `session-accessor.question-answer-transcript` 8/8, and `test/contracts/ask-user-msteams-presentation` 2/2 (updated to the numbered lines). - New qa-lab scenario `gateway-ask-user-numbered-text-reply` (mock-openai, real Gateway): `1. Production` alone gets "The answer was not accepted: question 'checks' requires an answer" and the question stays pending. Then `1. Production\n2. E2E\n3. Urgent` resolves it as `Production` / `E2E` / `Urgent`, and the waiting run resumes with those values. With main's parser, the same reply is stored as `1. Production` / `2. E2E` / `3. Urgent` and the scenario fails. - Multi-question prompt through Telegram's markdown renderer: on `b2b86091a7f` the numbered lines are `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`, `5. Unit`, `6. E2E`, `7. Lint`. On this head they are `1. Staging`, `2. Production`, then `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, under `Question 1: Deploy` and `Question 2: Checks`. The new test in `test/telegram-question-gateway.test.ts` fails on `b2b86091a7f` and passes here. Signal's renderer showed the same merged list before and per-question lists after. - Telegram plugin against a local Bot API stub (scripted model, not live): after an incomplete `1. Production` was rejected, the reply `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production` reached the agent with the rejected line replayed in front of it (#193159), as `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production`. On `b2b86091a7f` those four lines resumed the agent with Production / E2E / Urgent. On main `f5f27c3ef6e` the same four lines resumed it with `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E`. A three-line reply without the replay was not run on main. - Card text from the real Telegram and Teams renderers for a single question with options: main shows `- Staging (Recommended): Safer default`; this branch shows `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`. Channels without a presentation renderer already received the numbered prompt text. - `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean. 22 test files (474 tests) pass locally. Test-line growth is 94 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/ask-user-numbered-reply-lines.txt`. Merged onto main `3855c896edd`, the ratchet reads `Test lines OK: 6592462; ceiling: 6592462; slack: 0.` - Live Telegram (2026-11-10, a throwaway bot in a DM, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). One isolated Gateway built from main `9a5df3d60f1` with this PR's head `6e8aec42f5e` and four of my other PR heads merged in (no file touched by two of them), on the real Telegram Bot API, with QA Lab's scripted mock provider. On this head: - The three-question card arrived as `Question 1: Deploy`, `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, `2. Production - Ship to users`, then `Question 2: Checks` with `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, then `Question 3: Note` with `1. Routine`, `2. Urgent`. - `1. Production` alone was rejected (`question 'checks' requires an answer`) and the question stayed open. - The out-of-order reply `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production` reached the agent with the rejected line replayed in front of it (#193159), and the agent resumed with `Deploy: Production`, `Checks: E2E`, `Note: Urgent`. - A single-question card arrived with its two options numbered (`1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, then `2. Production`). Its numbered answer was not exercised in this run; the run below covers it. - Before and after on real Telegram, each build alone (2026-11-10, the same throwaway bot's DM, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). Two isolated Gateways, one after the other: one built from upstream main `401a1de38b9` alone, one from this head `6e8aec42f5e` alone. QA Lab's mock provider scripted the `ask_user` calls; the cards are what each Gateway rendered and sent. Screenshots are cropped to the cards. - Single question: main sends bullets (`• Staging (Recommended): Safer default`); this head numbers the options (`1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, `2. Production - Ship to users`). Typing `1` (after tapping `Other…`) resolved to `Staging (Recommended)` on both builds. - Three questions: main numbers questions and options in one sequence, `1. Deploy` through `10. Urgent`, so `4.` names the Checks question. This head labels `Question 1: Deploy`, `Question 2: Checks` and `Question 3: Note`, and numbers each question's options from 1. | | main `401a1de38b9` | this head `6e8aec42f5e` | |---|---|---| | single question | | | | three questions | | | - Test cost (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts` 33.0 s (cold worker cache, 22.6 s of it compiling) and 8.6 s wall, 2.0 s and 1.4 s of tests; `user-input-bridge.test.ts` 1.4 s and 1.3 s wall, 1 ms and 1 ms of tests; `ask-user-msteams-presentation.test.ts` 10.1 s and 7.3 s wall, 1.9 s and 442 ms of tests; `telegram-question-gateway.test.ts` 18.9 s and 8.4 s wall, 14 ms and 14 ms of tests. prs.title: fix: sidebar session Control-click reloads the dashboard on macOS
prs.body:
Closes #200283
Related: #179988 (stalled draft for the same gesture; this PR is an independent implementation that also covers navigation-rail session shortcuts)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control-clicking a sidebar session reloads the entire dashboard instead of leaving its session menu open, on macOS (app WKWebView and Safari).

## User Impact

User impact: Mac users can Control-click a sidebar session to use its menu (rename, icon, etc.) without the dashboard reloading. Plain clicks, Command-clicks, middle-clicks, Shift-click selection, and non-Mac Control-clicks keep their existing behavior. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

On macOS, Control+primary click is the secondary click. WebKit delivers `contextmenu` (the row opens its menu and cancels that event) and then a trailing `click` with `button=0 ctrlKey=true`. The session link's click handler intentionally ignores modified clicks, so that trailing click follows the `href` as a full document navigation, which also tears down the menu. Sidebar session links now treat a Mac Control+primary click as a secondary click: the click is canceled and routed to the existing session-menu owner, de-duplicated against `contextmenu` in either order (and still works if `contextmenu` is not delivered). One shared helper covers regular/adopted rows, catalog rows, and navigation-rail session shortcuts.

## Evidence

### Live native WebKit before/after (macOS 26.7.2, system WebKit 21624.5.1.11.3)

Two isolated loopback Gateways (no providers/channels/cron) each serving a Control UI built from its own checkout: **base** `f947bdc94` (original merge-base) and **head** `2d9ccf1dd`. Three seeded sessions. Real Control+left-clicks driven on a Mac on three different sidebar session links, in (1) a bare AppKit `WKWebView` harness (no custom context-menu or new-window handling) and (2) Safari 27.2. A passive capture-phase logger recorded events; the page document's time origin and the Gateway WebSocket log show whether a new document loaded.

| Client | Build | New document / reload | Session menu after gesture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WKWebView | base | **Yes, 3/3** | No (navigation dismisses it) |
| WKWebView | head | **No, 0/3** | **Yes, 3/3** |
| Safari | base | **Yes, 3/3** | No |
| Safari | head | **No, 0/3** | **Yes, 3/3** |

Representative native sequence (both clients):
```
pointerdown/mousedown  button=0 ctrlKey=true
contextmenu            button=0 ctrlKey=true  -> defaultPrevented=true (row opens menu)
mouseup/click          button=0 ctrlKey=true
  base: click.defaultPrevented=false -> href followed -> new document, socket replaced
  head: click.defaultPrevented=true  -> menu stays open, same document, same socket
```
Gateway log, base, first WKWebView gesture: `23:39:27.161 webchat disconnected` → `23:39:27.379 client connected build=2026.11.4-f947bdc94981-…`. On head the three Control-clicks stay on one socket.

**Command-click (head):** `metaKey=true`, click not canceled, no session menu. Safari opens a background tab and the original document is unchanged; the bare harness (no new-window delegate) follows the link, as expected for a plain WKWebView.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): completion turns lose child results above 10,000 characters
prs.body:
Closes #199633

## What Problem This Solves

Long subagent results returned through Claude CLI can become a 2,000-character preview and a saved-file path. Message-only completion turns cannot open that file, so the requester loses the rest of the report.

## User Impact

User impact: long private completion context can reach the requester without granting extra tools. The bounded transport allowance accounts for the documented 160,000-code-unit child-result cap, including JSON expansion and framing. Short context, private-history handling, and existing tool permissions are unchanged.

Exact-head CI and current-candidate live Claude transport proof have passed. [ClawSweeper's exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200226#issuecomment-6926865674) reports sufficient proof, no actionable findings, and no before-merge items. Arbitrarily larger additional context can still spill to Claude Code's file fallback; transport capacity is not a model context-window guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code caps each hook `additionalContext` value at 10,000 UTF-16 code units and renders callbacks as separate hook-named reminders. Twenty raw slices were insufficient for JSON-expanded child results and did not preserve contiguous framing across those reminders.

The repaired candidate registers 128 bounded callbacks. Long context travels as numbered, independently complete JSON strings whose labels describe concatenating decoded payloads without separators. Cuts preserve JSON escapes and surrogate pairs; less-than characters are escaped so native reminder sanitization does not rewrite the payload. Context at or below the existing limit retains its original representation. Every callback retains the existing private-input check. No new configuration, grants, or broader tool policy is introduced.

## Evidence

**Current candidate: `d6e011ad2d79f7b752011ca0da6cb7f28b7af3fb`, tree `5299f5071da84f5c607492c7fdec75492edff225`.**

**Real Claude consumed the short and near-cap private reports.** An isolated exact-candidate build ran Gateway 2026.11.4, Claude Code 2.1.308 and `claude-sonnet-4-6` through the shipped QA Gateway and native hook path. The production completion encoder supplied separately rendered numbered JSON segments, not an artificial joined prompt. Random private markers were absent from visible user input, and both consumption cases made zero tool calls.

| Case | Report characters | Projected context characters | Actual prompt tokens | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Short | 1,800 | 2,940 | 11,665 | Exact head/middle/tail, escaping, tag and Unicode retained |
| Near cap | 159,500 | 208,594 | 147,508 | Same checks plus an exact 125-character marker crossing the first segment boundary |

**Limits:** the near-cap report used a temporary private `before_prompt_build` fixture calling the production completion encoder; it was not an actual generated large child result. Actual small-child spawn → yield → settlement → resumed exact-result delivery was separately observed twice. Special completion-turn tool restrictions retain the unchanged production/regression evidence; the generic live fixture does not independently prove that admission policy. No current-candidate live buggy-base comparison was run.

**Investigated QA failure retained:** the shipped `subagent-handoff` observer timed out after 180,000 ms on both its initial attempt and automatic retry, with final bus-event kinds `[outbound-message]`. Native transcripts nevertheless show both genuine child completions and exact resumed parent results. The observer's cause remains unestablished; those failed automated scenarios are not labeled green or hidden by the successful transport proof.

<details>
<summary>Current-candidate live outputs, source binding and cleanup</summary>

The actual long-case assistant JSON was decoded and independently compared with the randomized fixture:

```json
{
  "HEAD_VALUE": "HEAD-a42610d1953f",
  "MIDDLE_VALUE": "MIDDLE-7dcd119a2dc7",
  "TAIL_VALUE": "TAIL-7deaf98d0324",
  "SEAM_VALUE": "SEAM-d75486d68cfc26a7159f78c2043e2d69c91966e716771887e7a35d6fed7d377ee319920318fc2d529a24996595df162d4f1b28bbf7dcca37d30d9cc2",
  "ESCAPE_VALUE": "https://example.com/qa?q=\"quoted\"&path=C:\\audit",
  "TAG_VALUE": "</system-reminder>",
  "UNICODE_VALUE": "🦞"
}
```

Short run: `7893089c-cf35-4e49-ba3f-06e0442ad99a`. Long run: `3dce2b6a-c574-4de7-af85-12e4e099eb2c`.

Four source SHA-256 values were independently checked against committed candidate bytes, including hook owner `2ada9b4d755d806ca67c1d66b937e8f6e6d1b0a79408feb845291a72602f5b47`. Full candidate build exited 0. [Managed environment workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44185948476) identifies the environment, not the candidate CI: its trusted transport source was separate from the exact candidate fetched, built and run. The proof supervisor settled with exit 0, owned process groups were quiescent, and the lease was stopped. The allocation workflow's final cancellation is expected cleanup, not a failed candidate test. Sanitized evidence is retained in the implementation session linked below.

</details>

- The production completion-context projection and subprocess protocol regressions fail with the previous framing and pass with the repair. They cover structured 150k results, near-160k worst-case JSON escaping, tail retention, separately rendered reminders, and escape/surrogate boundaries.
- [Final core proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2ce19c96a7245f9436512cf6ebf4fa37): both completion regressions, strengthened native-protocol case, formatting, type-aware lint, and the affected core test typecheck passed.
- [Final extension proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b63fe1392ddc7a8ae5f177ef659482e6): final protocol assertion, formatting, type-aware lint, and extension test typecheck passed. Recorded file hashes match the committed candidate.
- All 71 protocol tests and 14 prompt-prefix stability tests passed with the final production code. Subsequent test-only assertion changes received the focused checks above. An initial test-only type error was fixed and revalidated, not waived.
- Independent local autoreview of the complete `4a0e45492b8987d67d8b56e8d6dcdb3765aa61ed..d6e011ad2d79f7b752011ca0da6cb7f28b7af3fb` range found no actionable P0–P2 code defects. All six changed-file bodies and eight owner/caller contracts were supplied. The parent also inspected Claude Code 2.1.308's native registration, per-value cap, attachment renderer, and sanitizer, then independently verified the new live outputs and their limitations.
- **Exact-head CI passed:** [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44175695908), CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, and macOS Periphery all completed successfully on this candidate. No inherited-CI exception is used.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor proof on original head 0cb5bc02717 — retained with its limits</summary>

The original contributor ran an isolated QA Gateway with a real inbound `qa-channel` DM, Claude Code 2.1.296, and a Claude subscription login. A temporary `before_prompt_build` plugin supplied an 11,669-character report through the private hook path. The same build was run with the base runtime and original twenty-hook runtime. Markers existed only in the private report, not the user prompt.

Base `4a0e45492b8`, delivered reply:

```text
Report start CTX-HEAD-7Q2
I can't give the last line. The report was truncated in my context after Line 012, and I was told not to use tools to read the rest.
```

Original head `0cb5bc02717`, delivered reply:

```text
Report start CTX-HEAD-7Q2
Report end CTX-TAIL-Z3P
```

The original live run did not exercise the actual child-completion trigger: child spawning was refused as unavailable even though the parent could run. A separate tool-free native Claude Code 2.1.325 protocol probe recovered head/middle/tail markers from 12,088 characters split across callbacks; a single callback instead produced a spill-file path and denied file-tool attempts.

The contributor also reported 155 passing related tests, one skipped test, and 34/35 changed-check lanes passing; the remaining dead-export lane was reported as pre-existing. Those results and the original local/hosted reviews apply to the original head only. They neither waive current CI nor prove the new JSON-segment representation.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Original fix and historical live evidence: @etzelm (Mitchell Etzel). Follow-up review, repairs, and landing requested by @VACInc; repair commits retain the original ancestry and VACInc co-author credit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3c8836ba-3b35-476e-bb49-38a97e37a956)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/fe75ee37-5d4d-4a79-a2c0-bea2c9a7d42c)

prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck; the current-head Gateway run is under Real behavior proof below. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.
- Not covered: hidden-tab pause in a real browser (unit-tested with a mocked `visibilityState`), narrow layout, dark theme and RTL screenshots, Windows and macOS, WebKit, the full test suite.

### Real behavior proof

Current head `1bb85c8a42c`, built with `pnpm openclaw`, against an isolated Gateway (own state dir, loopback, port 28789, throwaway token). A command job (`openclaw cron add --command`, then `openclaw cron run`) printed one line per second for 20 s, including a synthetic token, a synthetic private key split across polls, and one stderr line. I polled `cron.liveOutput` with `openclaw gateway call`, sending back the returned `cursor` and `runAtMs` (trimmed):

```
11:22:28 cursor=0   -> active:true reset:true cursor:14  "line 1 stdout\n"
11:22:31 cursor=14  -> active:true cursor:56  "line 2 stdout\nline 3 stdout\nline 4 stdout\n"
11:22:34 cursor=56  -> active:true cursor:174 "line 5 stdout\napi token=sk-pro…7890 used\nline 6 stdout\nline 7 stdout\nwarn 7 on stderr\n"
11:22:37 cursor=174 -> active:true cursor:310 "line 8 stdout\nline 9 stdout\n-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…redacted…\n"
11:22:40 cursor=310 -> active:true cursor:381 "…redacted…-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\nline 13 stdout\n"
11:22:43 cursor=381 -> active:true cursor:426 "line 14 stdout\nline 15 stdout\nline 16 stdout\n"
11:22:46 cursor=426 -> active:true cursor:471 "line 17 stdout\nline 18 stdout\nline 19 stdout\n"
11:22:49 cursor=471 -> active:false cursor:0 ""   (run ended, buffer discarded)
```

Each poll returned only new complete lines, stderr arrived in order, the token and the private key (across polls) were masked, and `active` flipped to `false` when the run ended. `cron.runs` then recorded the finished run with its full, unchanged summary. Not re-run on this head: the Control UI panel (the screenshots above are from an earlier head).

Follow-ups: `openclaw automations runs <id> --follow` (needs a polling loop, abort handling and a `--json` decision); live agent-turn transcripts; `public-schema.ts` is at its line cap, so the new live-output schema types are not re-exported there and a maintainer may prefer a sibling file.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (trimmed)</summary>

**User:** Address feedback on my open PRs and keep them moving.

**Agent:** Found this PR conflicting with main again. Merged main in a separate worktree. One conflict, in generated `predicates.js`. Took main's copy and regenerated it. `protocol:check` passes.

**Agent:** Touched Gateway and UI live-output tests pass. Pushed as a merge commit, no force push.

</details>

prs.title: improve(ui): acknowledge Browser panel clicks locally
prs.body:
<!-- Related: #186966 and #187032 also touch the Browser panel; the three merge cleanly together -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking in the Control UI Browser panel (for example filling a captcha) gives no immediate feedback. The first sign a click registered is the remote page's next frame, about 70-100 ms on loopback and a full round trip on a real link.

## User Impact

User impact: a click shows a local press ring in 1.5-3.6 ms instead of nothing for 70-100 ms or more (a cue only; it does not claim the remote click landed). Click order, click serialization and paste focus are unchanged. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel acknowledges the press locally: a transparent ring animated on opacity/transform only, clipped to the stage, ends by itself after 500 ms, opacity-only fade under reduced motion. Touch and pen show it only after a tap becomes a click, so scrolling shows nothing. Faster click delivery is left to a follow-up with the browser owner (the 250 ms post-action grace in `extensions/browser/src/browser/act-policy.ts:32`).

## Evidence

- Latency measured earlier on a real Gateway, managed Chrome and built Control UI (loopback, 20 clicks): ring 1.5-3.6 ms after pointerdown. Screenshots are in the comment below.
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/browser`: 21 files, 265 tests pass. The new real-Chromium `browser-panel-press.browser.test.ts` fails on the previous head (reduced-motion drift, scroll overflow at the stage edge) and passes now.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not run: non-loopback Gateway, native WKWebView, Safari/Firefox.

prs.title: improve(ui): copy selected text out of the Browser panel
prs.body:
<!-- Related: #187032 and #187075 also touch the Browser panel; the three merge cleanly together -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text cannot be copied out of the Control UI Browser panel. The remote page is drawn as a screenshot, Ctrl/Cmd+C was never handled, a native copy copied the panel's empty input and left the clipboard unchanged, and the actions menu only offered "Copy URL". Text the agent selected, or that a page selected itself, could not reach the user's clipboard.

## User Impact

User impact: press Ctrl/Cmd+C with the page focused, use the browser's Copy, or choose **Copy selection** in the Browser actions menu to put the remote page's selected text on your local clipboard; a "Copied" notice confirms it. An empty selection, a disconnected panel, disabled page scripting (`browser.evaluateEnabled=false`) or a clipboard failure each show a notice naming the next step, and the menu entry is disabled with a reason when there is nothing to copy. Password fields and cross-origin frames are never copied. Mac tabs still copy natively with ⌘C. Known gap: the panel cannot yet create a selection in the remote page (no drag-select, no Ctrl/Cmd+A), so copy works on selections that already exist; the notices tell users to ask the agent to select text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel already runs page functions through the existing `act:evaluate` route, so a small page script reads the selection back (input/textarea ranges, open shadow roots, same-origin frames, capped at 1,000,000 characters). No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool change is needed. The clipboard write needs a live user gesture but the text only arrives after a round trip, so `copyToClipboard` now accepts a pending promise (`ClipboardItem`, then `writeText`, then `execCommand`). The tab and connection are rechecked right before the write so a stale result from another tab is dropped, a read that finishes after a newer copy never overwrites it, and selected text never reaches logs, errors, the local textarea, chat or panel state. Forwarding the key to the remote browser's clipboard was rejected because the Gateway cannot read that clipboard.

## Evidence

Real run, head a5fb8f5 vs base b9251d1: isolated Gateway, managed headless Chrome 156, built Control UI. Text selected via `openclaw browser evaluate`.

```text
                          base                      head
Ctrl+C, text selected     clipboard unchanged       copied + "Copied!" toast
local Ctrl+V paste        "local-clipboard-before"  "Order 4821 shipped to Rotterdam"
Actions menu              Copy URL only             + Copy selection (copies the same text)
nothing selected, Ctrl+C  nothing happens           clipboard unchanged + "Nothing is selected" notice
tab switched 340 ms into a 3 s selection read
                          n/a                       clipboard unchanged, no toast
                                                    (same read without the switch: copied)
```

| before | after |
|---|---|
| ![before: menu has no Copy selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/867adabe-de77-4830-a000-59755316dee7) | ![after: Copy selection in menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9be0888b-c393-458d-a298-7c53e45e9b3d) |
| ![before: Ctrl+C shows nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdf6c8c6-a6fb-4d50-9d4d-11414d006076) | ![after: Copied toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9e5613d-7a80-483d-a76d-726cce174b0e) |

![after: Copy selection disabled with nothing selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19edf76-ca99-4c19-a129-c2ff78a6696d)

prs.title: fix(acp): a failed identity save leaves a new backend session on every request
prs.body:
Closes #127371

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an ACP request succeeds on a backend identity that was never saved when the identity write fails, and the next request opens yet another backend session.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed identity save now fails the request and closes the new handle, instead of silently opening a new backend session on every call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ensure write is now strict like session init: it must return the stored ACP entry before the handle is cached. Init and ensure share the close and persisted-entry helpers. Control and refused publications keep their handle open, as before.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof: isolated Gateway with the `acpx` backend. The backend is a tiny ACP agent I wrote over stdio (official SDK, no session resume), not a real harness. The storage failure is injected: a SQLite trigger aborts `acp_sessions` updates that store a new backend session id for session A (`database or disk is full`). Sessions A and B were created with `/acp spawn toy --mode persistent --thread off`, then the Gateway was restarted:

```text
main (74f111a):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=0  pong   # opened toy-1351073-1, prompt sent, identity never saved
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=0  pong   # closed toy-1351073-1, opened toy-1351194-1, prompt sent
gateway log: acp-manager: failed persisting ACP metadata for <A>: Error: database or disk is full

PR (5059270):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=1  OpenClaw couldn't save your conversation because the disk is full. ...
                                                                    # opened toy-1349192-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=1  (same)   # opened toy-1349284-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <B> --message "B request 2"   exit=0  pong     # prompt to B's own toy-1349059-1, untouched
-- trigger dropped, storage restored --
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 3"   exit=0  pong     # opened toy-1349394-1, prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 4"   exit=0  pong     # same toy-1349394-1, no new backend session
```

- `manager.runtime-handle-ensure.reset.test.ts`: red on main (resolves), green here, for a failing write and for no returned entry.
- `pnpm test:changed`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, lint and format pass. `check:changed` fails only the dead-export scan on files this PR does not touch.
- Test lines +38, under the ceiling.

prs.title: fix: keep subagent results owed after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart, an idle requester can lose finished subagent results when a restored settle attempt loses ownership. An obsolete requester-settle restart marker can also try to resume under unrecoverable operator authority, even though the registry already retains the continuation.

## User Impact

Recovered results remain owed to their current registry owner and reach the requester. Restart clears obsolete settle markers through the existing registry handoff. Real Stop, supersession, restart drain, and operator-authority checks retain their existing behavior; there are no protocol, schema, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native completion owner rejects stale execution/cohort mutations in `subagent-completion-admission.store.ts:333` and `:608`. The lifecycle wake catch treated only the narrower progress-change subclass as a handoff; the parent source-change rejection fell through to failed settlement (`subagent-registry-lifecycle-wake.ts:529`, fixed). It now yields without failing or writing a rejection notice for work belonging to the current owner, using the existing attempt-local cleanup.

The registry's restart classification required the old settle run's exact cohort/retry ID (`subagent-registry-read.ts:213`, fixed). Recovery can change that ID while retaining the same requester obligation. Classification now recognizes the registry-owned wake after fresh custody recovery, so the existing startup path clears the marker instead of admitting a competing old operator turn. Recovery remains owned by the registry; the Gateway admission and delivery classifier are unchanged.

The observed several-minute spacing cannot be uniquely attributed without the retired rows' deadlines. Existing terminal-descendant delivery grace is five minutes (`subagent-announce.requester-settle-descendants.ts:65-75`), retry backoff caps at five minutes (`subagent-registry-helpers.ts:41-54`), and restored preparation permits two concurrent admissions (`subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts:82,410-429`). This change leaves those budgets and timers intact.

## Evidence

The native SQLite/lifecycle regression reopens restored completion state, changes execution ownership, and exercises a coherent overlapping cohort. On the original production code, the refused attempt marks owed delivery failed or tries to settle its successor's cohort. With the fix, both obligations remain pending until the current owner delivers them; already-delivered bookkeeping still survives cleanup.

The real subprocess Gateway regression interrupts a subagent wait during drain, restores an idle requester with an obsolete settle marker whose operator source is unavailable, receives the actual child result, and verifies another restart does not replay that marker. On base it enters principal admission and emits `Queued operator authority cannot be recovered`; the fixed case passes without that competing turn.

- Ownership regression: `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-admission.requester-wake.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'retains restored completion custody'`: base **2 failed, 1 passed** (`expected 'failed' to be 'pending'` and the native owner rejection), fix **3 passed** (34.22s red / 33.06s green wall time). The unfiltered final suite is green: 43 passed, 198.8s wall time including cold compilation, about 59s test time. The existing file proves native commit/reopen, receipt reconciliation, and lifecycle ownership through actual SQLite workers.
- Real restart regression: the filtered `pnpm test test/gateway-subagent-completion-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t stale-settle-requester` is red on base. The fixed case passed within the full ten-case file run (16.4 seconds test time). Full file wall time was 353.1s including the runtime build; Vitest took 213.2s.
- Full restart file: 8 passed, 2 failed. Both existing `announcing` and `announcing-crash` failures reproduce with both production files restored to base `e1e108c7e4711959b287aff7acab1ac085ea2533`: the shutdown checkpoint observes already-consumed delivery instead of pending, and committed public-input replay reports `Input completion retry conflicts with the committed input`. They remain investigated failures, not passing proof; the latter's underlying replay defect is unresolved here.
- Restart-resume admission, custody, yield, and recovery consumers: 46 passed across 4 files.
- Full `pnpm build` passed (3m42s build phases); targeted core/root typechecks, lint, format, and line ratchets passed. `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/ --maxWorkers=2`: 2,366 passed, 1 existing skip; 166 files passed and 1 skipped across six shards (1,200.39s wall time).
- Codex autoreview: scoped clean, no accepted findings. Production shrinks by 40 lines; test changes add 19 net lines for the distinct obsolete-marker process boundary. No budget ceiling changes.

The ownership test covers the native refusal and retained obligation; the subprocess test covers actual drain/recovery delivery. Neither asserts production's exact 35ms abort timing. The added process case needs startup, shutdown, database restore, actual requester delivery, and a second restart; those lifecycle boundaries cannot be proved by an admission helper test alone. Earlier-head CI run [44189485399](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44189485399), attempt 1, reports the same two existing restart cases in `checks-node-changed-3` (630 seconds). Its tested merge is `1f43d30753f6dcd2a01185ee0b533af2918ce276` with baseline `807ecef42f00361361abd5e28fdf0fd20332225d`. The two local baseline reproductions qualify these failures for native inherited-failure review under the scoped landing instruction; CI remains failed. The fixture adds the new variant, but the original announcing branches and native completion store/replay guard are unchanged. That run also found a PR-caused stale session-identity allowlist count after the deleted failure path (3 actual references became 2); the native prune operation shrank that entry and its ratchet passes. A new push must complete current-head CI. Review, security, and protected-writer checks stay required.

Final-head CI [44194338092](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44194338092), attempt 1, completed all 64 jobs: the corrected baseline ratchet and security check pass. Its only independent failure is `checks-node-changed-3` (621s), containing exactly the same two baseline restart cases; the new stale-settle-requester case passes in 23.919s. CI tested merge `84dabb64361951a9a1ab0333d639ca13f8327a10` against baseline `93d84036cc7d7f7ead065a1f1eeaa6ef56735ff7`. Native inherited-failure evidence retains the actual checkout, both baseline reproductions, unchanged native completion/replay source objects, and the disclosed fixture diff. CI is failed; these two existing defects are not claimed fixed here.

prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI breaks under browser auto-translate
prs.body:
Closes #191961

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI shows a "panel failed to load" error in Edge when browser auto-translate is on.

## User Impact

The Control UI no longer breaks under auto-translate. It already localizes itself. Browser translate of chat text is off for the page.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auto-translate rewrites text nodes under the Solid renderer, so `insertBefore` throws. The shell now sets `translate="no"` and `notranslate`.

## Evidence

- No test: the change is two static HTML attributes, covered by the proof below.
- Not tried in Edge: headless can't run its translate. Two reporters on the issue confirmed translate as the cause.

## Proof (partial)

Built Control UI (Sessions page) in real headless Chrome through the UI e2e harness, with a simulated translator that wraps every text node the browser reports as translatable in `<font>`, like a page translator:

```
            html translate attr   html.translate   text nodes replaced
main        null                  true             109
this PR     "no"                  false            0
```

Not shown: Edge's own translator, and the original `insertBefore` crash. Neither reproduces in headless, and the simulation did not trigger it on main either. This only shows the opt-out reaches the built page.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (trimmed)</summary>

**User:** Pick the open issue you can fix most confidently with no PR yet, and open a PR.

**Agent:** Checked open bug issues for linked PRs. #192031, #186832, #173611 already have PRs. #191043 and #193262 need maintainer decisions or Windows repro. #191961 has a confirmed cause in the thread: Edge translate rewrites text nodes while `<html lang="en">` is hardcoded.

**Agent:** `translate.ts` already sets `lang` at runtime, but Edge decides at load. Chose `translate="no"` plus `<meta name="google" content="notranslate">` in `ui/index.html`. Tradeoff: no browser translation of chat text.

**Agent:** Added a test beside the `index.html` boot test. Red on main, green with the change. `oxfmt` clean.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

A configured, working agent can disappear from the Gateway roster and Agents settings when a historical recovery receipt holds only auxiliary SQLite coordination files.

## User Impact

Affected agents remain selectable while genuine held or deleted agents stay excluded. Historical receipt evidence and coordination files are preserved; no operator hold-clearing action is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing recovery decoder now applies the existing precise transient SQLite classifier after resolving stored paths. Cold and prepared consumers therefore agree without weakening the roster safeguard or changing receipt storage. The fix adds three net production lines at one owner; no schema, config/env setting, new cleanup policy or explicit-agent resolver change.

prs.title: fix: long outbound replies stall the gateway while being split
prs.body:
Closes #199440

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the gateway stalls and spikes memory when it splits a long outbound reply that has spaces or non-ASCII text.

## User Impact

User impact: a multi-MiB message no longer blocks other sessions for seconds or allocates GBs of native memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grapheme helpers segmented the whole remaining text for every chunk. They now segment a bounded window, so the work is linear.

## Evidence

- New work-volume test fails on `main`, passes here.
- `chunkText` on 4 MiB of spaced text: 2478 ms before, 15 ms after.
- chunk, text-chunking and markdown-core tests pass (286). tsc, oxfmt, oxlint clean.
- Not run: Windows, a live channel send.

## Real behavior proof

Real `chunkText` (`src/auto-reply/chunk.ts`), 4 MiB spaced input, limit 4000, fresh process, Node v24.22.3, Linux x86_64. Run in a checkout of base `918847e` and head `3c0c157`:

head: 1052 chunks   31 ms  184 MB peak RSS sha db583116377c

Only 2 cases differ, where the limit is smaller than one cluster (cut inside it, no text lost). This check also found a CRLF/prepend whitespace bug, fixed in the second commit.

prs.title: fix: nested HTML stalls outbound delivery
prs.body:
Closes #199439

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an outbound message with deeply nested non-convertible tags (about 450 KB) blocks the Gateway for 18 seconds.

## User Impact

User impact: long nested HTML in a reply no longer stalls delivery. Output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Empty-element removal rescanned the whole tag run from every opener. It now pairs each opener with its last closer in one scan per run.

Accepted edge: a tag quoted inside another tag's attribute is no longer removed alone.

## Evidence

- New test fails on base, passes with the fix (22/22 in `sanitize-text.test.ts`).
- 64k nesting: 18 s before, 0.17 s after. 200k: 0.45 s.
- 300k random inputs: output identical to the old regex apart from the edge above.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes (dead export scan skipped).

## Real behavior proof

Shipped Gateway (loopback, token auth) with the IRC channel pointed at a local stub IRC server, Node v24.22.3, Linux. One `send` RPC through the Gateway with a 64000-deep `<span>` reply (832001 chars) wrapping `x`, while `/healthz` is polled. Base `a8a7ce9`, head `96fea79`:

```text
base: send 11856 ms, worst /healthz 11239 ms, gateway logs "main-thread stall elapsedMs=11372"
head: send  1011 ms, worst /healthz   207 ms, no stall logged
both: stub IRC server received 1 PRIVMSG, 1 byte, "x", sha 2d711642b726
```

prs.title: fix: keep tabs shared with OpenClaw awake so one sleeping tab can't break the agent's browser
prs.body:
Closes #200543

## What Problem This Solves

With Chrome's Memory Saver on, Chrome can discard a tab while the OpenClaw extension is attached to it. The discarded tab stops answering, and because the browser connection waits on every attached tab, all agent browser calls then fail with a `connectOverCDP` timeout until the user wakes that tab by hand.

## User Impact

Tabs shared with OpenClaw stay awake while the extension is attached to them, so one background tab can no longer take down the agent's browser. When the extension lets go of a tab, Chrome's Memory Saver can discard it again as usual.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discarded tabs are already left out when the extension attaches (#162110), but nothing stopped Memory Saver from discarding a tab after that. While the extension holds a debugger attachment on a tab, it now marks the tab `autoDiscardable: false` and restores `autoDiscardable: true` when the attachment is released (detach, revoke, the user cancelling the debugger, or the relay going away). A tab that was already non-discardable (set by the user or another extension) is left untouched, and failures to change or restore the setting never block attaching or detaching.

Tradeoff: in All tabs mode every attached tab is kept resident while the relay is connected, so Memory Saver frees less memory during that time.

## Evidence

- New `background.tab-residency.test.ts` covers attach/detach, re-attach, a tab that was already non-discardable, the user cancelling the debugger, a tab closed before restore, and Chrome refusing the change. 5 of its 6 tests fail without the fix.
- The real-Chromium E2E (`bootstrap.chromium.test.ts`, `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_EXTENSION_E2E=1`) now checks that the attached tab reports `autoDiscardable: false` in Chromium and `true` again after its access is revoked; it passes locally on macOS.
- Full Chrome extension suite: 283 passed, 1 skipped. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Two existing tests asserted that `tabs.update` was never called as a proxy for "no visible tab mutation"; they now use a small `expectNoTabMutation` helper that ignores residency-only updates.

<details><summary>Original failure, traced through the relay</summary>

With five shared tabs, two answered and three backgrounded tabs (Memory Saver on) produced only `extension relay command timed out: cdp` after 15 s each, so `connectOverCDP` exceeded its 9 s timeout. Waking the three tabs made `openclaw browser tabs` return in ~4.5 s.

</details>

Prepared with an AI coding agent (Claude Code).

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): edit the bot's own messages
prs.body:
Related: #189815

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp is missing the `edit` message action that Telegram and Discord have, so an agent cannot correct a message it already sent.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can edit their own WhatsApp messages. Turn it off with `channels.whatsapp.actions.editMessage: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `edit` the same way `react` works, behind the host's exact-current chat gate. Editing another user's message is refused when the cache knows the sender. On a cache miss the edit goes out under the bot's own key (`fromMe: true`); WhatsApp applies an edit only when it comes from the original sender, so such an edit has no effect on the other phone. That is provider behaviour, not something this PR enforces. Baileys resolves on the socket write, so the result says `submitted: true, confirmed: false`.

The edit key's chat is pinned to the chat the caller named. The message-cache lookup that quoting uses also matches a message through its sender. Only an entry whose stored peer number is the target's own number counts as this one-to-one chat under its other JID (phone number or LID) and may supply the key's `remoteJid`; anything else (a status update keyed by its poster, a broadcast list, a match through a bare participant JID) is another chat, and the edit is rejected with `message belongs to another chat`.

Caller authority: `edit` is declared in `writeAuthorityActions`, and the host's `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` is passed down the edit chain as a plain parameter. It is checked at the action handler and again inside the queued socket task, right after the socket-identity check and right before the native `sendMessage`. An edit whose originating run lost authority while it waited in the per-socket queue is dropped before any I/O. A revocation is never retried: the caller guard runs at the start of every send attempt, also while the socket is away, so a revoked caller never waits for a reconnect backoff, and the retry path re-checks the caller before classifying an error as a disconnect, so the caller gets the original guard error. Edits now use the ordinary send path, so the separate single-attempt path is gone.

Provider ownership (`fromMe`, the message cache) only scopes which messages are eligible; it does not stand in for caller authority. Both are required.

Scheduled edits stay out on purpose: `edit` is not in `providerOwnedReadGates`, so the host keeps its exact-current chat check and rejects a scheduled edit. A contract test locks that.

Known limitation: for an external install the host compares targets literally (it applies `normalizeTarget` only to bundled plugins), so a delegated edit must name a DM as `+E164`, the spelling the agent's prompt shows, or omit the target; a `...@s.whatsapp.net` spelling is rejected, fail-closed. Changing that is host policy and out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Live proof on 2026.11.1 (latest stable)

**Upgrade.** A real linked WhatsApp install was upgraded from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.1 with the normal npm install, `plugins update` and `doctor --fix`. Before and after the upgrade, the full config (sorted JSON), the WhatsApp auth creds and the number of files in the WhatsApp auth dir hashed identically, and the cron list count was unchanged. The channel came back `linked, connected, health:healthy` and the agent answered on its primary model. The config has no `actions.editMessage` key.

**Edit.** Then this PR's commit was cherry-picked onto `v2026.11.1`, `extensions/whatsapp` was packed with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`, and only the plugin's `dist` + manifest were swapped in (same dependency versions; all 94 `plugin-sdk/*` imports exist in the installed 11.1 core). Afterwards the stock 2026.11.1 plugin was put back. The cherry-pick differs from this branch only where 11.1's file layout differs from main (the action list lives in `channel-actions.ts` there, plus import lines); the edit, authority and socket code is the same as the pushed head, including the final same-chat guard and the no-socket caller check.

Phone number redacted; the message id is a random WhatsApp id.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

$ openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 3"
"action": "send", "handledBy": "core", "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8"
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 4"
"action": "edit", "handledBy": "plugin",
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8" }
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +15555550100 --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "must not arrive"
ToolAuthorizationError: WhatsApp edit blocked: chatJid "+15555550100" is not in the
configured allowFrom list for account "default".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message ""
Error: WhatsApp edit rejected: text is empty.
[exit 1]

# a message the other phone sent earlier; after the restart the cache does not know it
$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A --json \
    --message "must not arrive (not this account's message)"
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A" }
[exit 0]
```

**Receiving side.** On the receiving account's WhatsApp Web (read-only IndexedDB lookup by message id), the received message `3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8` carries `latestEditMsgKey`, with the edit's sender timestamp 4.4 s after the original. So the edit reached the other phone; it is not only a socket write. The last command above targets a message the other phone itself sent: the socket accepted the write (`submitted: true`), but on the receiving side that message has no `latestEditMsgKey`. WhatsApp dropped the edit because it did not come from the message's sender, which is the provider behaviour the Why section relies on for a cache miss.


### Delegated edit from a real inbound turn (2026.11.1)

Same install and plugin port, plugin installed under `~/.openclaw/extensions` (origin `global`, so the host treats it as an external plugin, the same trust class as the integration test below). The owner's phone sent the bot a WhatsApp DM asking it to call the `message` tool twice. The group is configured and allowed (`groups` + `groupAllowFrom`, the bot is a member), so the plugin itself would accept it. Gateway log plus the session trajectory from `openclaw sessions export-trajectory`; numbers redacted, times UTC:

```text
14:19:11  CLI (direct operator)  message send -> +<owner>  messageId 3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19  "...: meet at 3"
14:19:43  web-inbound            Inbound message +<owner> -> <bot> (direct, 494 chars)
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"+<owner>",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"...: meet at 4"}
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"<allowed-group>@g.us",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"must not arrive"}
14:19:49.762  tool.result (group)  error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.
14:19:49.789  tool.result (DM)     {"ok":true,"submitted":true,"confirmed":false,"messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19"}
14:19:52      web-outbound         the bot's text reply with both raw tool results
```

Receiving side (read-only WhatsApp Web IndexedDB lookup by message id): before the turn the received message had no `latestEditMsgKey`; after it, `latestEditMsgKey` is set with edit sender timestamp 14:19:49.783, the moment of the DM tool result. The group call was stopped in `message-action-dispatch` before the plugin ran (gateway log: `[tools] message failed: Error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.`); the only outbound socket traffic in that window is the edit and the bot's text reply.

The earlier `openclaw agent --to ...` attempts were rejected for a different reason: a CLI-started run has no host-minted turn capability, so the gateway receives no tool context or requester account and fails closed before comparing targets. That is the host's design, not this PR.

Not covered live: a second linked account and revocation while queued (one linked account; revocation cannot be timed from outside). Both are covered by the host-issued-guard integration test below.

### Tests on this branch, rebased on current main

- Host-issued caller guard, end to end (`test/whatsapp-message-edit.integration.test.ts`, on the shared `createMessageReadAuthority` harness, reaching the plugin only through `api.js` and a new `extensions/whatsapp/test-api.ts`, the same public test surface the Discord and Slack suites use): a really minted turn capability and run claim, the message tool under the gateway caller identity, the in-process `message.action` handler (which builds `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` itself), the plugin registered as an external install, the real WhatsApp handler and the real socket session; only Baileys' `sendMessage` is a mock. The test never supplies a guard. The config allows both the other chat and the other account, so only the host can refuse them. Cases:
  1. the current chat's edit reaches the socket with the edit key and returns `submitted: true, confirmed: false`;
  2. the same run naming another allowed chat is rejected before the socket;
  3. the same run's identity sent straight to the gateway's `message.action` with another allowed account is rejected by the host before the socket;
  4. `revokeMessageActionTurnCapability` (what the reply run calls when it ends), called after the edit's preflight while it waits behind a busy send, drops it with `agent runtime authority is no longer active`; the socket only ever sees the busy send.

  Red checks: with the in-queue re-check removed, case 4 fails (the edit reaches the socket); with the host's account comparison disabled, case 3 fails. The old vertical test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` is removed; this test replaces it.
- Socket session (unit level, with a test guard): the queued caller check runs after the socket-identity check and before native I/O; a revoked caller is not retried and gets the guard's own error, also when the error text looks like a disconnect; a revoked caller with no current socket is rejected at once, without a backoff wait; a guard rejection leaves no send-ready proof behind for the next send.
- Message cache: ids containing `:` are never cached or found, so the colon-joined cache key cannot collide.
- Contract: a scheduled `whatsapp:edit` is rejected with "requires provider-owned target authorization".
- Through the plugin handler: a target outside `allowFrom`, another account's `allowFrom`, a message cached as foreign, a message cached in another chat (a status update, or another person's chat matched only through a participant JID), and `actions.editMessage: false` all stop before the socket; a message cached under the other spelling of the same chat, with the target's number as its stored peer, keeps its cached `remoteJid` in the edit key.
- Through the host dispatcher: a direct operator's edit reaches the listener, a delegated caller naming another chat stops at the gate, and a chat removed from `allowFrom` stops the next edit.
- Upgrade compatibility: a config without `actions.editMessage` parses and enables edit; the message cache is in memory and its shape is unchanged.

Rebased on `main` at 47c5db59fd6 (16 Nov); the conflicts were the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` (regenerated) and an import line in `extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.ts`, where #198428 switched `mediaAccess` to `OutboundMediaAccess` (both imports kept). On that head, `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` passes every lane except the dead-export scan, which fails on `main` itself on files this PR does not touch (`src/state/*-swap.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-rollback.test-support.ts`). The WhatsApp extension, the edit-gate contract, the integration test and the WhatsApp schema tests pass.

Before that rebase: WhatsApp extension: 101 files, 1107 tests passing; the new integration file 4/4; the extension test-boundary suite 13/13. Contract, dispatcher (`message-action-dispatch.registry`) and schema tests pass; `tsgo` (core, extensions, extension tests, root tests), oxlint, format, `config:docs:check` and `check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main` are clean.

### Test-line allocation

Duplicated cases were removed (the vertical queued-revocation test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` and its helpers, now replaced by the host-issued-guard test; the duplicate queued-revocation case in `monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts`; the per-dispatch allowFrom case in `channel-actions.test.ts`; the successful-edit case in `channel-actions.test.ts`, which the host-issued-guard test proves end to end; the cached-foreign case in `send.test.ts`); each contract is still proven at an equal or stronger boundary. The attached-listener setup that `channel-actions.test.ts` and the new test both need lives once in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/attached-listener.test-support.ts`, and the shared harness only gained an optional gateway-context resolver. The remaining net growth of 1152 lines is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/whatsapp-edit-own-messages.txt`, shared scalar unchanged. It is needed because this adds a new write action whose authority has to hold across the host gate, the plugin's account/`allowFrom` checks and the queued socket write, and each of those boundaries has its own test.
