prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stable 2026.11.5 is published, but main does not yet describe the shipped release or retain several fixes present in its release history. This closes that gap without moving the immutable release tag or republishing packages.

## User Impact

Main retains completed CLI answers and cron history across ownership changes, fences message delivery during restart, reserves the correct reply session, preserves managed reload context and recovered dashboard authoring, and preserves model-owned installed-app relevance matching (including renamed app bundles such as Slack2). Older supported pnpm installations keep their first-hop update path. No user action or configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Synchronize version, exact shipped changelog and contribution record, generated SDK surface, measured CI costs, and integrity-verified updater inventory. Forward-port missing behavior through current owners rather than copying obsolete release implementations. Manifest-only CLI help no longer imports the runtime loader. The compatibility bridge preserves the older immutable updater’s explicit denial rather than granting newer lease authority.

The release remains pinned to `e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff`; this PR does not change its artifacts. Native app publication and final website verification are tracked separately.

## Evidence and Review

- Original behavior regressions failed with the original production owners and pass with the repairs. Explicit Node run: **150 tests across 15 files passed**; memory boundary proof: **27 tests across 3 files passed**.
- Build passed; compatibility validation passed for **31 releases**, preserving 29 existing inventory entries. Generated output, npm locks, docs, targeted typechecks, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Packaged artifact validation and isolated installed CLI cold help passed. An isolated Gateway with a real model completed response, read, exec/read, image recognition and follow-up scenarios.
- Fresh independent source review covered all 19 tracked production-source deltas plus the new pnpm helper, with no actionable findings. Lead review completed. The initial hosted review identified renamed-app candidate regression; the repair restores loose retrieval/model-owned matching.
- The 12-file repair committed as `7252dc277796e44166f7dfbdb90339e61de3fefc` passed canonical OpenClaw-engine autoreview at P0–P2 and separate independent owner review. The canonical review’s unchanged-context limitation remains. Hosted review of exact `7252dc2` subsequently completed with zero actionable code findings. These are prior-head review results.
- That repair preserves 2026.9.37 historical updater handoff denial, aligns generated chunks/dead-code consumers/loadability expectations, removes unsafe schema assertions, centralizes byte-identical interim transcript keys, and preserves service-mock exports. Its three repaired ratchets passed; 202 targeted tests passed; final service mocks passed 2/2; lead app-matching/history replay passed 17/17; core/tooling types, lint and format passed.
- Latest commit `38ed0145f0f91d28db0c2c521c4f4306b09c6a3b` removes 16 duplicated fixture lines without removing any of seven cases or assertions. Original test-line comparison reproduced +643 against allowance400+credit229; repaired comparison passes +627. All seven history tests, targeted commands-test typecheck, lint, format and diff checks pass. Independent read-only delta review found no P0–P2 issues. This used the documented subagent review fallback, not autoreview-helper isolation. No exemptions or baseline expansion.

## Remaining CI Attribution and Accepted Proof Gaps

- CI `44078981871/1` tested merge `7958cb84393f98ec552b5f1e3efb1ab529580a77` on base `2a7ca163a57d77e8220965855329795791d7d5ec`. Stale session-fork inventory and Node24 registry-fixture socket failures were reproduced on that actual base.
- CI `44092127959` tested `7252dc2` through merge `1d5ecc48c102d82f41be47833b6832829b387d6a`, actual base `ae0d37b3c442c1ff4c06ea9a30e85a7dd4514093`. Test-line budget was related and is addressed by `38ed0145`.
- Exact-head CI `44096700963` completed with 11 failed jobs on merge `d6d9a9a5d34bf3951253a94b1ef2a76f6d1dc3b5`, actual base `6e38d6dc714da46ab482a0d6fe6889521ee22644`. The repaired test-budget gate passed. Seven jobs failed fetching Node24.22.1 before tests/types ran. The remaining failures are inherited runtime closure, stale inventory, Discord settlement and six UI cases. Final failure-report job `134109172203` compares job names without matching signatures or selected scopes; its labels alone do not establish attribution.
- New-base source tracing attributes the runtime-closure missing `runtime-worker-loader.mjs` to the base-introduced worker shim/build graph. Base and merge contain the same relevant owner code; exact PR head lacks that shim. No fresh base build is claimed. Stale session-fork inventory remains on the new base/merge while its file is absent; the relevant planner owners are unchanged from the earlier reproduced base failure.
- Discord wrong-delivered settlement is reproduced through the isolated Gateway on both `38ed0145` and unchanged main baseline `2a7ca163a57d77e8220965855329795791d7d5ec`: terminal worker, consumed requester input, one unidentified send, ambiguous-send warning, but recorded delivery status/disposition `delivered`. The determining producer, consumer and regression test are unchanged; their introduction predates the PR base. The baseline replay failed as expected (119.40s Vitest, 126.98s wrapper), with temporary diagnostics restored. Earlier local ingress failures were caused by loopback proxy routing; qualified runs use process-local loopback exemptions only. This is inherited, not repaired.
- All six current UI failures are reproduced in the observed 178-file lane prefix on both `38ed0145` and unchanged main `2a7ca163a57d77e8220965855329795791d7d5ec`: three chat-view contention assertions and three touch-prepend timeouts. Both runs reported 6 failed/2570 passed tests; complete failure sections are byte-identical and match CI. Relevant UI and test configuration are identical between the latest CI base and tested merge. Earlier focused/neighbor passes alone were not used as inheritance evidence. The underlying inherited state contaminator is not narrowed. Prior project-registration failure and original Gateway `chat.send` refusal retain their unresolved historical evidence; neither is a current failed job signature.
- Installed stable-to-candidate upgrade has not executed. Local setup is blocked by unavailable Docker/safe-temp permissions. Hosted `44092573275` rejected equal baseline/candidate2026.11.5 in preparation; both Node24/26 upgrade lanes were skipped. First-hop qualification `44099170595` was rejected by trusted workflow admission before any updater ran. These are setup/admission gaps, not updater proof or product failures. On November 17, 2026 at 15:03 UTC, after this gap was explained, Dallin explicitly requested merging. This records acceptance of the unrun upgrade proof, not a passing test or waiver of enforced security/review.
- Full live file previously reported 179 passed/1 failed: unchanged guarded-HTTP `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, reproduced on pinned parent. Existing widget703/700 max-lines violation has no growth. Remote testbox unavailable.

Dallin authorized admin merge for unrelated CI failures. Native evidence binds all 11 failed jobs to the exact head, run, tested merge and baseline, with hashed logs and determining source identities. The bounded history audit is not exhaustive historical semantic verification. An unmeasured Doctor performance-only delta remains deferred. Enforced security/review and writer authority remain in force; native publication and final website work do not gate core closeout.


## Conflict integration (November 17, 2026)

Merged main `7338e1c1e4c1bd2a664e1964c3cb360d556083b8` into the closeout as `2a6c9f228d39398a2d5a392b9afe5adff719fe17`. The only conflict was adjacent update-contract documentation additions; both are preserved verbatim. All other paths match Git's automatic merge result. The resolved document exactly equals main plus the unchanged closeout paragraph. Docs listing, focused formatting, and diff checks passed. Prior substantive review is reused for this mechanical integration; the CI and inherited-failure attribution above remain **prior-head evidence**, not CI for this new head. Current-head security approval and CI admission must be re-established before landing.

prs.title: improve(backup): use spare cores for gzip on larger hosts
prs.body:
Related: #183094, #199367

## What Problem This Solves

Large, compression-bound backups cannot use more than four cores even when the host has spare CPU capacity.

## User Impact

User impact: backups on hosts with seven or more available cores can use dedicated compression workers, leaving file reads off the shared gzip queue. Hosts with six or fewer keep the existing path, and archives remain standard `.tar.gz` files. More workers use additional peak memory and can use slightly more CPU; the measured tradeoff is shown below. No compression-level, integrity-check, format, configuration or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the dedicated-worker follow-up left by merged #199367, not a duplicate of its four-way libuv implementation. Above six cores, the existing worker pool compresses ordered 4 MiB members with `min(8, cores - 2)` workers. Owned buffers transfer to/from workers without detaching caller data; the existing stream retains bounded read-ahead, ordered errors and settlement, and closes its pool on success, failure or cancellation.

The worker is registered inline in the existing runtime manifest. Fixed-root POSIX relative paths replace manual prefix slicing, while one typed construction replaces three intermediate standalone namespace projections. Literal entry tuples retain the original inferred descriptor contracts rather than falling back to `any`. This keeps the existing manifest within its real 700-counted-line cap without a new manifest helper, copy dependency, cap exception or workflow mutation.

## Evidence

### Current integrated candidate

- Published head: `ef1ab2f699c6ecad14e00748380e118f6f7eb111`; source tree: `c4091ae96325fa61cedd4f9b8d4c9214f82232dc`.
- Integrated main `c531fd0b1339f53ec9530dfd5fed312944680a66` to resolve a real runtime-manifest conflict. The repair preserves main's worker-loader entry and helper parameter, alongside this PR's gzip registration and POSIX worker-name derivation. Original contributor ancestry is retained.
- Canonical independent Auto Review over the complete integrated candidate, **P0–P3**: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. An initial report's test concern was rejected against the existing explicit concurrency-2 failure test; the post-integration pass confirmed it.
- **55 focused tests passed** across gzip workers, gzip ordering, archive-stream cleanup, runtime worker URLs, benchmark instrumentation and standalone source entries. Real worker startup/exit failures, cancellation, bounded reads and caller-buffer ownership are covered.
- Targeted manifest types, lint, format and diff checks pass. All 123 current runtime descriptors preserve their expected worker names, including the new gzip worker and main's loader entry.
- The official source-run build passes. With isolated home/config/state, real `pnpm openclaw backup create --only-config --verify` exits successfully and reports `verified: true`; stock `gzip -t` accepts the archive. The built gzip worker is present at `dist/infra/backup-gzip.worker.js`.
- Current-head [CI attempt 2 passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44182271660/attempts/2), including [check-lint-core-5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44182271660/job/134417895584), the [selected-lane CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44182271660/job/134421284244), and the [combined CI/security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44191381383). Dependency and security-sensitive review statuses also pass. The original attempt's lint lane exceeded its 15-minute job budget, with no job log available even in the full run archive. The reconstructed actual lint workload passed locally in 76.8 seconds; one authorized job-only retry then passed on GitHub in 5m57s. Existing successful checks were reused. No source, lint rule, timeout, workflow, dependency or gate exception was changed, and the original timeout's cause remains unestablished.
- [ClawSweeper re-reviewed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199712#issuecomment-6899116741) and reported no actionable findings or before-merge items. This does not waive CI or human review requirements.
- Prior-head CI and package/performance evidence below are retained with their original source binding, not presented as current-head CI. No new compiled-standalone executable or comparative benchmark run is claimed.

### Prior-head correctness and packaging evidence

The following evidence belongs to original head `7755559c8a797ce40ff9b0b8be9b8b7c592c6ac7`: 98 focused cases passed, with real Node/Bun packaged success and worker-failure handling. That ten-file candidate passed targeted types, lint/format, strict 700-line checks, both Knip scans and P0–P2 review. Full details and limits follow.

Prior-head [full selected-lane CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43744983895/job/132913452687), with all 15 selected groups successful and no known-main-red exception; the security/dependency guard also passed. ClawSweeper's earlier review of that head reported no findings; the linked review comment now contains the newer integrated-head review. This is not human approval or merge authorization.

<details>
<summary>Source-bound correctness and packaging details</summary>

- Selected base: `5dbf569b4b8552253c37fac93b32bdaf87a872dc`; tested/reviewed source tree: `7835128e1bcd9ba543b64786d5dd3e643eb92842` (10 files).
- Fresh focused suites: **98 cases passed**, covering real worker count/order/buffer ownership, fallback, bounded reads, abort/error/native exit settlement, worker-host behavior, runtime resolution, archive stream cleanup, verified restore/database readability, compiled-worker fixtures and native dependency-free harnesses. The existing standalone-source suite now also guards against an `any` return-type regression.
- Canonical typechecker assertions prove exact old factory/plugin/standalone return signatures after excluding the new gzip property, bidirectional projection compatibility and no newly introduced `any`. Core production, infra tests and root-script test types pass.
- All **119 baseline descriptors and their order** remain identical. Across 45 plugin-directory selections at two module URLs, all 90 ordered standalone projections and 338 plugin-value reference identities match the baseline. The actual build-entry owner discovers the new worker.
- Strict native max-lines check at **700**: no diagnostic. Ordinary targeted lint/format, line-cap and suppression/environment ratchets, and both Knip scans pass without exemptions. Existing CI and wrapper definitions are byte-identical to the selected base; copied native closures load all 120 descriptors without any storage helper.
- Current generator regenerated runtime script assets and `--check` passes; both previously affected generated bundles are now byte-identical to the base, not hand-edited or copied from the archive.
- Fresh `qaRuntime` build and canonical runtime-only package integrity/import-graph check pass. Package SHA-256: `5d6849a2d0715e8fcaa14878141145082fd63840d4f6f101980406556435a0c9`.
- The actual extracted package runs `backup create --verify` successfully over a disposable 256 MiB workspace under Node 24.20.0 and pinned OpenClaw Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`; stock `gzip -t` accepts both archives. Removing the extracted worker or replacing it with native exit 23 makes **both runtimes exit 1 without publishing an archive**.
- Fresh full-candidate independent Auto Review: OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, **P0–P2**, `scoped-clean`, no findings, against the exact base/tree above. This was static review, not independent execution or human approval.

</details>

### Prior package CLI performance

Same revised package, Node 24.20.0/Linux, identical eight-core affinity, cold CLI processes and warm filesystem cache. A fresh committed `backup-verify-fixture.mjs <state> <workspace> --workspace-only` workload supplies 12,288 files / 768 MiB; no database inflation. One warmup per path, then five serial interleaved pairs. The committed measurement script constrains only the existing path to `BACKUP_MEASURE_GZIP_CONCURRENCY=4`; default selects six dedicated workers.

Acceptance rule recorded before the run: reduce archive-write median with every archive verified; report whole wall, CPU, RSS, size and host load separately. Additional memory is a visible tradeoff, not a free or universal speedup. No own heavy validation/build ran concurrently with the measured pairs.

| Metric | Four-way libuv | Six dedicated workers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Archive write median / p95 | 7.893 / 7.936 s | 6.925 / 6.995 s |
| Whole command median / p95 | 9.830 / 9.873 s | 8.861 / 8.921 s |
| Whole CPU median | 24.213 s | 24.613 s |
| Maximum process peak RSS median | 0.635 GiB | 0.781 GiB |
| Archive bytes median | 808,436,923 | 808,436,841 |

All ten measured archives verified. One-minute load during measured archive phases: 2.49–3.94. Archive medians improved 12.3% and whole-command medians 9.9% on this particular file-heavy workload; do not extrapolate a universal 2x gain.

The instrumenter measures real CLI phase boundaries, follows emitted parameter names and includes peak RSS; whole wall includes the launcher, CPU sums CLI/launcher totals, and RSS is the maximum process peak. SQLite/PostgreSQL capture is untouched. Supplied historical mixed-data results and the earlier 17-file implementation are not represented as measurements of this revised candidate.

### Limits

- Prior package execution reused workspace dependencies; a clean package dependency installation was not exercised. The integration worktree's frozen dependency installation succeeded.
- Standalone discovery/projection is qualified, but a compiled standalone executable is **not**: an earlier supported default-JIT build hit its 300-second cap before producing one. It was not repeated, and no compiled-mode success/startup/crash claim is made.
- Local actionlint setup was unavailable during earlier validation; this candidate makes no workflow change. Prior-head selected-lane CI and automated review are linked above; current-head CI and human maintainer review remain separate.

prs.title: fix(codex): model catalog requests fail through the inference relay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated model-discovery failures when native Codex sends a catalog GET through OpenClaw's inference relay. The relay currently rejects every non-POST request with a retryable transport failure.

## User Impact

Codex-backed sessions can retrieve their model catalog without spending startup or turn time retrying an unsupported method. The catalog request retains the requesting native account's credentials and upstream status.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow only bodyless `GET /models`, with either no query or one `client_version` argument, through the existing fixed-destination relay. Unsupported catalog request shapes return a terminal 400. Discovery keeps relay-lifetime and transport checks without requiring an inference turn; the existing host-held OAuth route restriction remains intact.

## Evidence

- Baseline: all seven new regressions fail on unchanged upstream with the expected HTTP 502 responses.
- Candidate: 44 tests pass in `inference-proxy.http.test.ts` and `inference-proxy.test.ts`, exercising real loopback HTTP/TLS and WebSocket transports, account headers, upstream errors, cancellation, and destination restrictions.
- Independent P0–P2 source review covered the complete change, including the extracted HTTP helpers and the unchanged destination, admission, and cleanup owners; no actionable findings.
- No universal latency reduction is claimed. This removes the observed unsupported-method retries; the historical native trace is not a benchmark of every account or Codex version.

- Formatting, targeted lint, core type checking, and focused Codex type checking pass.
- Validation used isolated local state. Crabbox was unavailable in this environment; no remote-test result is claimed.

### Native app-server proof added November 17

At @VACInc’s request, RoboClaw exercised the actual Codex 0.169.0 app-server through OpenClaw’s shipped RPC client and real loopback inference relay. The test logs into an isolated native ChatGPT account using synthetic credentials, lets the native process request its catalog, and checks `model/list` for a model absent from the bundled catalog. The external fetch boundary is mocked; no live account, backend entitlement, or live GPT-6.2 turn is claimed.

- **Before:** removing this PR’s two production-file changes causes native catalog refresh to receive HTTP 502; no request reaches the upstream boundary and the native discovery regression fails.
- **After:** the same test passes. Native Codex sends `GET /models?client_version=0.169.0`, preserves its synthetic bearer token and account header, and returns the remote-only model `relay-catalog-only` through `model/list`.
- The full relay-family run passed **88 tests**, with **1 optional live test skipped**. It includes guarded HTTPS/auth tests, existing POST/WebSocket coverage, and added disconnect/shutdown cleanup proof. Extension-test typecheck and targeted type-aware lint passed.

Reproduction source: [native catalog regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9fe8974589c5657ee79660a5e48de9c6ab84f368/extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-proxy.native.test.ts), in companion #200784. That checkout also carries the 0.169.0 runtime bump; it is not a claim that these additional tests are committed on this PR’s older base. Both production files in this PR, plus the upstream, dispatch, context, upload, and transport owners, were verified byte-identical between head `7ffffef8f91f28e625fd2b1e488272b2b3fb9c8f` and the tested checkout. This PR’s exact-head hosted CI gate and security/dependency checks are green.

Native test result summary:

```text
Before: loads a remote model catalog through the relay with native client version and auth — FAIL
After:  loads a remote model catalog through the relay with native client version and auth — PASS
Relay family: 6 test files passed; 88 tests passed; 1 optional live test skipped
```

Ben’s original implementation and commits remain unchanged. #200784 will rebase on main after this PR lands, removing the duplicate production change from that PR’s diff. The Codex version bump remains a separate, open-only PR.

### Landing assessment

A fresh independent P0–P3 review of this exact three-file candidate and its seven production owners completed with no actionable findings. No hostile behavior, credential exfiltration, or weakening of the existing destination/auth controls was identified in the reviewed changes.

ClawSweeper also reports no code findings; its remaining request is an unmocked live catalog-refresh run. That is a related integration-coverage limitation, not an unrelated CI failure. We do not treat it as a necessary additional prerequisite for this narrow relay repair: the real native-binary red/green test proves the rejected request path, while separate real-HTTPS transport tests cover forwarding, headers, upstream errors and network restrictions. The destination, native credential ownership and backend catalog contract are not replaced by this change. Live ChatGPT entitlement, live GPT-6.2 availability and a fully live end-to-end backend run remain unverified. This assessment does not claim ClawSweeper approved or waive any enforced GitHub check or required review.

prs.title: fix: use canonical Windows paths for release upgrade checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Windows packaged-upgrade checks can launch the published updater through a short temporary path while runtime retention records the corresponding long path. The archived Node 24 and Node 26 checks replaced the package successfully, then failed to import an old retained chunk.

## User Impact

Release operators get a canonical Windows lane root before the installation prefix and state paths are derived. This changes the release harness only, not the published updater or baseline package. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing macOS native-realpath normalization to Windows at lane creation, rather than normalizing only the later environment. Reuse the existing real-filesystem aliased-root regression for both platforms. The archives strongly implicate mismatched path aliases, but do not contain the baseline resolver map; this PR does not claim to repair arbitrary short-path launches outside the harness.

## Evidence

- The Windows canonical-root assertion failed before the implementation change (25 passed, 1 failed).
- After the fix, 31 focused upgrade-lane, lane, and Windows-installer tests passed. The regression enters through runUpgradeLane and uses native filesystem alias resolution; package operations and Gateway are mocked.
- Root-scripts targeted typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed with independently materialized frozen dependencies. Initial borrowed-dependency setup failures were resolved without changing package manifests or the lockfile.
- Actual Windows Node 24/26 baseline-to-candidate qualification remains required. Linux platform-mocked coverage is not that proof. An optional broader compiled-subprocess test did not execute because its initial borrowed-dependency build was missing workspace packages.
- Author inspected and simplified the change. No independent review was performed, per the operator’s explicit instruction; enforced GitHub/security gates remain required.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scheduled plugin commands keep running after the requester is removed from commands.allowFrom
prs.body:
Closes #188664

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an accepted requester-command schedule keeps running its plugin command on every occurrence after the requester is removed from `commands.allowFrom`, while a live command from the same sender is already refused.

## User Impact

User impact: after an operator narrows or empties `commands.allowFrom`, the next occurrence of a schedule whose requester is no longer listed is refused before any plugin code runs, with the occurrence error "Scheduled plugin command requester is no longer command-authorized; submit a new request." A recurring schedule stays enabled (re-listing the requester lets its next occurrence run) until cron's existing 10-failures-in-a-row limit disables it; a one-time one ends like any failed one. Like any failing job, the first refusal sends cron's failure notice to the owning conversation's agent (daily while it repeats).

- Re-checked: channel requesters (by their restored linked channel identity) and Gateway requesters signed in as a person (Control UI, including one reached through a remote-ingress plugin, browser copilot, TUI, CLI or another Gateway client). A person's occurrence uses the sender ids and channel account their live command was checked with (the profile id, plus the client id for a client that is not an operator UI) against the same list as live: `""` for an internal command, the channel's list for a command routed with an external origin (e.g. a TUI command delivered into a channel session), else `*`.
- Unchanged (they keep their original admission, because the occurrence has no identity it can re-check): a shared-token owner with no per-person command sender (its client id is not rechecked), a plugin's own Gateway requests, and a Gateway person's schedule accepted before this recheck existed. Channel reachability controls (a DM `allowFrom` list, `dmPolicy`, pairing) also keep their original admission; the docs say how to stop retained work then.
- Stored data: the operator recovery snapshot, its codec and the schedule envelope keep main's exact shape, so 2026.11.3 and earlier main builds read what this branch writes as they read what main writes. The one new value is private state on a person's requester-command schedule: the profile id, client id and route account its live command was authorized with; cron APIs can neither set nor read it.
- Upgrades: requester-command schedules shipped in 2026.11.5-beta.1 to beta.3, not in a stable release. A Gateway person's schedule created by a beta or a pre-fix main build keeps its original admission (no record); a channel one is re-checked when its requester identity is restored, and refused otherwise. A 2026.11.3 cron job with its recorded operator source loads unchanged.
- Downgrading to a pre-fix main build: it reads this branch's schedules unchanged, ignores the private value (running them with their original admission) and keeps it across rewrites; its cron job listing shows the value to callers who can read the job. A 2026.11.5 beta refuses to start on state written by this branch or by current main (newer state schema).
- No plugin SDK change, and live command authorization is unchanged.
- A third-party channel whose stable sender id differs from its phone number is re-checked by its id only, so a requester listed there only by phone number is refused (bundled WhatsApp and SMS report the same value for both). While a bundled channel's transport is not loaded, the occurrence still normalizes `provider:id` entries with the bundled plugin, so a re-listed `telegram:<id>` keeps running; a live command at that moment compares such entries as written. A non-bundled channel plugin that is not loaded cannot normalize them, so such an occurrence is refused until it is loaded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduled run passed a constant `isAuthorizedSender: true` into both the native-subagent requester authorization and command dispatch, so `commands.allowFrom` was never consulted after admission. Each occurrence re-checks the restored requester against `commands.allowFrom`, resolving the provider and list through the live command authorization code, and passes the checked value instead of the constant. For a Gateway person, the sender inputs are read at creation from the command context the live check reads (live adds the profile id after the client id, `src/auto-reply/sender-identity.ts:83`) and kept as private schedule state, outside the shared recovery snapshot. The client id is declared by the client at connect, but live matches on that same value, so the occurrence is never weaker than live. An occurrence uses the record only when it names the restored source's person, and refuses otherwise. A channel recovery that cannot restore its requester identity fails closed.

## Evidence

Tests (`node scripts/test-projects.mts <file> --maxWorkers=1`) on this branch:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-plugin.scheduled-turns.test.ts` (33/34; the failing row, `refuses a reset before command or input acceptance`, fails the same way on current main): a channel requester's occurrence is refused after the requester is narrowed out of / emptied from `commands.allowFrom` (the plugin command never runs, no input is committed, the schedule stays enabled) and runs while listed; a removed identity is refused at restore. The live command's sender inputs reach schedule preparation, and a requester record reaches the store's requester gate through `cron.add`. With main's production source the narrowed and emptied cases fail (`expected { status: 'ok' } to match { status: 'error' }`).
- `src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.gateway-recheck.test.ts` (14/14): the record is taken from the live command context, the snapshot decodes unchanged through the shared codec, and the restored requester decides as live `resolveCommandAuthorization` across provider / `""` / `*` matrices for an operator-UI person, a CLI person (listed by client id or profile id, refused when neither is) and a TUI person routed to an external channel under two accounts with a per-account alias. Only the stored source's person is recorded; a record that is not the restored person fails closed; a schedule stored without one keeps its admission. Remote Control UI and host-side persons, restored from JSON through the production remote-ingress recovery without the connection, decide as live; a remote owner has no record; a revoked grant refuses the restore.
- `src/cron/store/plugin-command-schedule.worker.test.ts` (26/26): the record is stored beside the unchanged envelope, survives a rewrite, is absent from the public job, must name the stored source's person, and cannot be authored.
- `src/auto-reply/command-auth.scheduled-recheck.test.ts` (4/4): a `provider:id` entry normalizes without a loaded transport, a different id still refuses, the `*` fallback, a wildcard list.
- Each of these changes makes a test fail: not storing the record or storing another person's; skipping its store guards or public-job removal; dropping the client id or route account from the record or the occurrence; ignoring the record at the occurrence or accepting another person's; checking an external origin on the internal list; re-checking a schedule stored without a record; dropping the requester at any step from the live command to the store, except the hand-off into the creation, which the built run below covers.

Built Gateway, persons signed in through a trusted proxy (a Control UI protocol client; a CLI client with a device-signed connect, approved with `device.pair.approve`) schedule with real `chat.send`; `config.patch` narrows; then a live command probe and a forced occurrence; plus a shared-token owner:

| step | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commands.allowFrom["*"]` narrowed to another id: live command | refused | refused |
| same, forced occurrence | runs, plugin command executes | refused with the error above, plugin command never runs |
| profile id re-listed: live + occurrence | both run | both run |
| CLI person, only its client id `cli` listed: live + occurrence | both run | both run |
| CLI person, narrowed to another id: live / occurrence | refused / runs | refused / refused |
| shared-token owner, narrowed: forced occurrence | runs | runs (unchanged) |

A build of this branch whose schedule preparation does not hand the record to the creation runs the narrowed occurrence again (ok, 1 tick), so the record is what refuses it.

Channel requester, built Gateway with the real Telegram plugin against a local Bot API: after narrowing `commands.allowFrom.telegram` to another id, a live command from the requester is refused; the forced occurrence runs on main and is refused here. The same on Telegram's servers (a test bot, commands typed by hand): narrowed, the forced occurrence runs on main and is refused here; re-listed, both run.

Restart, built Gateway: a slash command sent while the session is busy, or as a new session's first message, is not run again after a restart; a plain message queued behind the busy turn is. A plugin hook that rewrites a queued plain message into a slash command runs it live before the restart, its schedule carrying the person's profile id; nothing runs again after the restart.

Stored data: recovery sources and snapshots written by this branch and by main have the same keys and value types (values differ only in per-run ids), and the 2026.11.3 decoder accepts and rejects the same sources from both. A pre-fix main build decodes this branch's schedule unchanged, keeps the record across a rewrite, and lists it in the job's public state.

Upgrades, built Gateways: a cron job created by 2026.11.3 (the latest release) loads unchanged on this branch and keeps running after narrowing; a requester-command schedule created after the takeover is refused when narrowed and runs when re-listed. From 2026.11.5-beta.3: a person's schedule it created loads unchanged and keeps running after narrowing (no record), one created after the takeover is refused, and a Telegram schedule it created (local Bot API) runs listed, is refused narrowed and runs re-listed.

Prefixed entries, built Gateway: with `commands.allowFrom.telegram` written as `telegram:<id>`, narrowing refuses and re-listing runs, also after a restart with the Telegram plugin not loaded.

<details><summary>Result fields (redacted)</summary>

```
person, this branch: {"CA":{"live_ran":false,"status":"error","ticks":0},"CTL":{"live_ran":true,"status":"ok","ticks":1}}
person, main: {"CA":{"live_ran":false,"status":"ok","ticks":1}}
cli person (branch | main): CA {"status":"error","ticks":0} | {"status":"ok","ticks":1}; CTL ok, 1 tick | same
telegram, this branch: {"CA":{"status":"error","ticks":0},"CTL":{"status":"ok","ticks":1}}
telegram, main: {"CA":{"status":"ok","ticks":1}}
restart: {"ranBeforeStop":["S","R"],"ranAfterRestart":[],"plainRequestsAfterRestart":1,"eachScheduleHasProfileId":true}
2026.11.3 -> branch: {"oldUnchanged":true,"decodedSame":true,"oldNarrowed":"ok","newNarrowed":"error","newRelisted":"ok"}
2026.11.5-beta.3 -> branch: {"oldUnchanged":true,"oldNarrowed":"ok","newNarrowed":"error","ctl":"ok"}; telegram {"listed":"ok","narrowed":"error","relisted":"ok"}; back: "uses schema 40; this build supports 36"
stored shape vs main (parent / gateway / queued / snapshot): EQUAL SHAPE x4
2026.11.3 decoder, release-writer control (branch | main): ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED
```

</details>

Local format, type-aware lint, core and core-test typecheck, and the baseline ratchets pass.

Gaps: the channel runs other than the Telegram-servers run use a local Bot API. In-repo Gateway tests stop at the check; built-Gateway runs cover the occurrence. A route account and a remote Control UI person are covered at the restore and check level only. The Telegram-servers and prefixed-entry runs were not repeated on this head; they ran on commit 03d506ed002.

prs.title: fix(backup): release disk space when deleting staging databases
prs.body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw backup create` retains the disk space of deleted SQLite staging, snapshot, and verification copies until the process exits.

## User Impact

User impact: temporary disk space is released when backup removes each private database copy, instead of remaining pinned through the rest of a long backup. Archive format, integrity checks, source databases, and retention policy are unchanged; no migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

SQLite admission deliberately retains an identity descriptor after the last connection closes. Backup must retire that admission while the private file still exists, after its connections have closed and before unlinking it. This change does that for the online-copy staging file and recursively for backup/verification scratch under the existing exclusive lifetime token. Root token controls stay with their existing owner until its connection closes; nested payload files with the same basename are still retired.

The existing exclusive-copy implementation moves unchanged into its own module to keep the edited snapshot module within the repository's line cap. There is no new lifecycle owner or compatibility path. Simplification: the existing retirement owner handles cleanup; production delta is +37 net lines including the mechanical extraction, with 96 focused regression-test lines.

## Evidence

Current validation against refreshed main `5dbf569b4b8552253c37fac93b32bdaf87a872dc`:

- Red-before-green: the two new descriptor regressions failed on the unmodified production base, observing 1 deleted-open staging file and 2 deleted-open snapshot/verification files. Both pass with the repair.
- Strengthened scratch coverage includes a nested `payload/owner.sqlite` and proves a real competing SQLite reclaimer remains locked out at payload removal while the root control remains present.
- Focused scratch suites: 18 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Snapshot plus final descriptor regressions: 50 passed, 2 Windows-only cases skipped.
- Backup creation/verification consumers, including real create/verify/restore flows: 103 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped.
- Core production typecheck, infra-test typecheck, targeted four-file lint/format, line-cap ratchet, database-worker ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. The SQLite worker ratchet remains 166 live / 15 deprecated-only calls on both sides.
- Independent Auto Review, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, complete local candidate against the base above: no findings, `scoped-clean`. Changed owners and unchanged admission/walk/publication cleanup context were included. The review adapter refused the unchanged staging-token source as a sensitive filename; its internals were not independently inspected by that reviewer. Existing native custody regression and the new competing-reclaimer proof pass.

### CI follow-up

The first head (`55ce9b412fcd1be586d46d49ce386bfbd86910a3`) exposed a real runtime-source inventory omission: extracted trusted PR wrappers did not include the newly split copy helper. Commit `0d34aa30c3960a88827c0a5ab43edf41e33a47cc` adds that one module to `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`; no tests or guard contracts were weakened. The source-closure test was reproduced red locally, then the repaired eager-import/source-closure suites passed all 24 cases. Independent Auto Review of this one-line fix against that head is `scoped-clean` (P0–P2). `git diff --check` passes; the text inventory has no applicable formatter target.

Original CI evidence: [small-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43733126387/job/132870195581) reported the missing inventory entry and missing-module errors. [large-10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43733126387/job/132870195518) reported 17 private-provisioner injection failures under pinned Bun. Both are now passing on current head: [small-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43734997698/job/132876170191) and [large-10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43734997698/job/132876170192), with the latter logging all 17 provisioning cases passed (2 platform skips). These public job reads are bounded tails, not complete logs.

The provisioning failure is also causally qualified, not dismissed as baseline: a disposable copy made through the existing wrapper fixture ran the real private preload under pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` (Node child `24.20.0`). With the extracted helper absent, the preload fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and reproduces the exact `not every launched provisioner received its private store` assertion. Restoring that one module produces the real injection and preflight-store receipts; the deliberately argument-free provisioner then reaches its usage check. The preload imports the handoff lease, whose transitive chain reaches `sqlite-snapshot.ts` before recording injection. This explains both original failed lanes with the same inventory omission. No guard, fixture, or unrelated provisioning source was changed. The earlier local operation-lock failure is retained as a separate setup limitation, not baseline attribution. The repository failed-CI collector is unavailable here (`spawn gh ENOENT`); focused repository runners and public job evidence were used.

### Current-head built CLI proof

A fresh repository-owned `qaRuntime` build completed successfully in 56.4 seconds. Its dirty managed projection was source-compared to published head `0d34aa30c3960a88827c0a5ab43edf41e33a47cc` before and after execution; the build stamp records input signature `f2c3a4d2f7b8926d48b70617714316983a03fc012ce5b267ea97187c93e35d91` rather than pretending the projection's older Git HEAD is the published head.

The actual built CLI ran `backup create --verify --json --no-include-workspace` against baseline-initialized disposable state, including a 17.5 MB synthetic agent database with 16 MiB of benchmark payload. All five SQLite copies (19,017,728 output bytes total) completed; the 133,169-byte archive verified and the command exited 0. A passive preload sampled actual OS descriptors and inspected them at the CLI's verified-result write, before CLI finalization; it did not replace backup, SQLite, or cleanup operations or hold the process open:

```json
{"stage":"verified-result-before-cli-finalization","runtime":{"node":"24.20.0","bun":null},"samples":458,"maxOpenScratchDescriptors":10,"maxDeletedScratchDescriptors":0,"openScratchDescriptors":0,"deletedScratchDescriptors":0,"deletedScratchBytes":0,"archiveVerified":true,"archiveBytes":133169}
```

This is current shipped-entry-point behavior, not a mock harness or a Bun claim. The compatible Node 24.20.0 runtime emitted its normal security-patch warning; this proof does not qualify TLS or replace the recommended Node patch level. Sampling cannot establish that no shorter-lived descriptor ever existed; the final live-process observation establishes that no scratch descriptor remained at successful completion.

Limits: this Linux run does not repeat the contributor's historical macOS/APFS 945 MB disk-footprint/timing benchmark, nor claim those historical numbers as current proof. Descriptor checks use `/dev/fd` and are skipped on Windows. Broad cross-platform coverage remains with PR CI. No model/Gateway workflow is changed.

Contributor credit: original patch and investigation by Mitchell Etzel; scoped repair, additional coverage, and current validation performed with RoboClaw.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ac30b821-5414-4259-953b-dc9fccc11b0b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e06509d1-dd0a-4692-beae-20b5fb09ecca)

prs.title: fix(agents): subagents of scheduled runs get the guest toolsBySender["*"] entry
prs.body:
Closes #188441
Related: #178815 (broader consolidation of child authority; this change only restores the spawn snapshot for one case)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a subagent spawned by an isolated scheduled run gets the guest `toolsBySender["*"]` entry when it starts, even though the run itself does not apply sender policy (a run capped with `toolsAllow`, or a run of a job an owner created).

## User Impact

User impact: subagents (and their own subagents) of such runs now get the same sender policy as the run: the tool snapshot recorded when they were spawned, as released versions do. Current global, agent, provider, sandbox and sub-agent restrictions still apply.

The guest `"*"` entry no longer applies to these children in place of the run's policy, which has three visible effects, all matching the run itself:
- its denies no longer remove tools the run had;
- tools that only the `"*"` entry grants (for example an optional plugin tool in its `alsoAllow`) no longer reach these children, as they never reached the run;
- the children are no longer treated as sender-restricted: like the run, they may start helpers of other agents, and the sender-only confinement (working directory, agent and session-root pinning, ACP root rules, the delegated deny floor, the session permission policy) does not apply to them.

Unchanged:
- runs that apply sender policy themselves (for example a webhook run) and their subagents still get the `"*"` entry, like the run;
- children of turns that have a sender keep that sender's current entry;
- senderless work sent to such a child from any other session, from a later or retried run of the same job, or by any other turn opened on the run's own session (another job's `session:` target, a hook request naming that session key, an operator turn) still resolves current sender policy;
- runs on a shared or named session (`main` and `session:` targets, including names shaped like run keys) never record the exception;
- children spawned before this change keep today's behavior.

Not changed (same as `main`, no regression):
- turns placed on a worker environment do not record the exception yet: their tool authority is prepared before the run is admitted, so their children keep today's behavior;
- visible children (`sessions_spawn` with `visible: true`, or `sessions.create`) do not carry it: their creation path does not persist the record;
- uncapped runs on CLI backends (tools served over the Gateway MCP loopback) do not record it: that surface resolves a senderless turn with `when-sender-id`, so it is not marked;
- ACP children the run spawns directly (`runtime: "acp"`) get no sub-agent envelope from a scheduled run (as on `main`), so the record is not read for them;
- a capped run whose own turn has a group restriction records a sender restriction instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #157806, a child's admission that carries its requester's origin resolves current requester policy again from that origin. A scheduled run's origin has its run session key but no sender, so the lookup fell through to `"*"`, whether or not the run applied sender policy, and nothing a child's later admission can read recorded which it was.

The spawning turn now records it next to the child's inherited snapshot, and a later admission keeps the snapshot only when the request comes from that same run occurrence: its own turn stamps its requester origin with its fresh per-run session key, so another turn opened on the same session (another job, a hook, an operator) never counts as the run.

Docs: the `nesting.md` tool-policy line now describes `main`'s behavior since #157806 (senderless work that carries a requester origin re-resolves current sender policy; released versions kept the snapshot for every senderless child run) and states this exception, which restores the snapshot only for a run's own work.

<details>
<summary>How the exception is recorded and checked</summary>

The record is `inheritedToolPolicySource: "scheduled-run"` together with `inheritedToolPolicyRunSessionKey`, the run's own per-run session. The host writes both only when the spawning turn resolved without sender policy, with no sender and no operator, on a per-run session that the isolated runner created fresh for this run. That last fact comes from the run's admitted scheduled execution context (set only for detached isolated or `current` runs whose run key is new), never from the shape of the session key. `sessions.patch` does not accept either field, plugin extension slots cannot claim their names (reserved), and patching a child's inherited allow or deny list drops the exception.

A later admission keeps the snapshot only when the request origin is that same run: senderless, no operator, its session key equal to the recorded one, and stamped by that run's own turn. The run's own turn stamps the requester origin it hands to its tools with its per-run session key (`scheduledRunSessionKey`, set only from the same host fact that records the exception, copied only from an already captured origin, never from flat request input); its sub-agents inherit that origin unchanged. The new check reads only the child's own row; it adds no parent or intermediate row reads (an explicit delegation grant keeps its existing lineage check), so compaction, model fallback or the post-prompt sync of the run session cannot invalidate an admitted child's prepared policy. Nested children receive the exception and the run key from their parent's own admission. Completion batches keep it only when every completing child records the same run. Any other origin-bearing admission drops it. `SessionEntry` (exported through the plugin SDK) gains the `"scheduled-run"` source value and the optional run key.

Housekeeping (line caps): `hasCliSessionReuseMetadata` moves unchanged from `run-prompt-executor.ts` to `run-cli-session.ts`; the new `sessions.patch` rows live in `sessions-patch.subagent-policy.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

Built Gateway from this branch and, for the `main` column, the same build with every changed source file swapped back to `main` (`b9dd04d047f`); scripted model; `toolsBySender: { "*": { deny: ["read"] } }`; capped runs use a `toolsAllow` that includes `read`. Each cell is what the run's child got when it called `read` on a sentinel file in that turn (offered and returned the file / refused / not offered).

| Turn that reaches run A's child | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run A's own turn spawns the child | not offered | **returned** |
| Run A's own turn sends the child more work (`sessions_send`) | not offered | **returned** |
| Grandchild spawned by that child | not offered | **returned** |
| Run A's run session rewritten while the child is admitted (compaction-style row rotation) | not offered | **returned** |
| Fresh child after upgrading from `2026.10.8`, `2026.10.9` or `2026.11.3` (the pre-upgrade child row stays unmarked) | not offered | **returned** |
| Another job whose `sessionTarget` is `session:<run A's key>` sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| A hook request naming run A's session key sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| A forced re-run of the job after run A failed (new run key) sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| Gateway restarted mid-run (run A aborted, never resumed), then a turn on run A's key sends to the child | not offered | refused (current `"*"` policy) |
| Operator `chat.send` on run A's key sends to the child | returned | returned |
| Job on a persistent `session:` target (not a per-run session) | not offered | not offered |
| Webhook-triggered run (applies `"*"` itself): its child | not offered | not offered |
| Group turn with a sender (the repo's QA-lab Telegram Bot API stub): its child | returned (sender's own entry) | returned |

"Refused" rows: the call is refused at execution with "read is not available in this turn" under the current `"*"` policy. Unlike `main`, where `read` is never offered, it stays listed because it was offered on the run's own earlier turn (definitions stay pinned within a session). Runs hosted by the Codex harness are not exercised end to end here.

- `src/agents/requester-tool-policy.test.ts`: the record (only a run's own turn on its fresh session; not a run-shaped key without the runner's fact, another session, sender policy, an operator, a sender or a group restriction), the check (child, nested child, blank sender kept; legacy child, a mark without its key, another session, the run's stamp on another session, a later run, operator, sender re-resolve), side effects, origin-free resume, completion batches, own-row capability reads, and a prepared read replayed after the run's row is rewritten.
- Stamp rows: `requester-origin.test.ts` (only from a captured origin, carried only for the same session), `conversation-capability-profile.test.ts` / `tool-resolution.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` (only the run's own turn on its fresh session stamps), `gateway-caller-context.test.ts`, `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts`, `mcp-http.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` (callers and loopback calls keep the stamped origin).
- `codex-subagent-tool-policy.test.ts`: the Codex harness's retained requester facts for a run child name only the child's row.
- Spawn rows (native; ACP via `acp-spawn-policy.test-support.ts`, mutant only): run key and exception persist only together. Execution context rows: the fresh run session is exposed only for a detached run on its own fresh session. `sessions.patch` rows (`sessions-patch.subagent-policy.test.ts`): a patched ceiling drops the exception, never a sender restriction.
- RED: each changed test file run alone against `main`'s production source fails its new rows on their assertions in 8 files, e.g. `keeps the sender snapshot for a child of a senderless scheduled run`: `expected { allow: undefined, deny: [ …(2) ] } to be undefined` (`main` applies the `"*"` deny to the child). `requester-origin.test.ts`, `execution-context-admission.test.ts` and `isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts` call helpers `main` does not have, so they fail on the missing helper rather than on a behavioral assertion and their rows are covered by the mutants below; `codex-subagent-tool-policy.test.ts` passes on `main` by design (it pins that a run child's harness facts name only the child's row).
- Mutants: 30 single-condition mutants of the fix (each dropping one check of the record, the occurrence check, the stamp or a carrier; three re-anchored after the code moved) each turn the intended row red; none survives.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt on the touched files, `check:test-lines-ratchet` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Test cost: +871 test lines; the 471 over the 400-line allowance are recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/scheduled-run-child-tool-snapshot.txt` (rows on each owner of the record, the run-key check and the stamp; the table above is the end-to-end proof). Per-file test time (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`), base -> head: `requester-tool-policy.test.ts` 11.2 -> 12.4 s (+38 tests), `isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts` 27.3 -> 30.8 s (two rows on the real isolated runner); the other changed files within 0.5 s of base, including `conversation-capability-profile.test.ts` (44.1 -> 43.6 s, over 30 s on `main`) and `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts` (29.9 -> 29.8 s, with the three caller rows folded in instead of a new file); new files `tool-resolution.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` 12.0 s, `mcp-http.scheduled-run-origin.test.ts` 12.9 s, `sessions-patch.subagent-policy.test.ts` 10.7 s (mostly transform of the Gateway modules they test). CI seconds once available.

prs.title: feat(update): allow explicit retirement of backed-up session archives
prs.body:
Closes #186088

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot intentionally retire retained session-import archives when import proof is unavailable or archive identity changed, even after preserving an independent backup.

## User Impact

Operators can retire an exact, complete archive group using a byte-verified independent raw backup and separate `--accept-history-loss` consent. Ordinary cleanup stays conservative. Updates shows retained storage sizes, reasons, and recovery guidance only when requested.

Selected originals may contain unique history absent from SQLite. Retirement permanently removes them, preserves previous import evidence in v5 receipts, and does not promise automatic backup restoration or supported downgrade. Recovery/update-owner acceptance of this opt-in retention and older-reader contract remains required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance/disposal owner performs the explicitly authorized retirement; no alternate deletion owner or automatic retention policy is added. Integration with current main preserves live-writer cleanup, byte-verified surviving-duplicate redirects, and settlement of already-unlinked pending claims. Async snapshot preparation no longer consumes the bounded synchronous inventory allowance before the inventory starts; the existing entry, byte, and time limits remain unchanged.

## Evidence

**November 11 conflict refresh, candidate `3ba846a2bc8544aac1dc33299887f1cc6982aba1`:** integrated upstream main `ae651f116c7713295d6969b36bb1762ee0196edc`. The two conflicts were concurrent helper imports and generated protocol predicates; both imports are retained and the predicates are canonically regenerated. Upstream verified-update retention classification remains intact. No retirement-policy change or new runtime behavior is introduced by this refresh.

- **Fresh focused verification:** 87 tests across six files/four shards pass in 319.01 seconds wall time, including cold compiler preparation (archive cleanup, retirement receipts, inventory/disk usage, update-status helper and response ownership). Core/UI typechecks, canonical gateway-validator determinism, touched helper lint and formatting, max-lines ratchet, and scoped whitespace checks pass. The exact test-line grant now covers all 1,057 retained regression lines: 1,034 previously allocated plus a separate 23-line reconciliation; no scalar baseline increase or new test was added.
- **Source lint:** the supported source-focused type-aware configuration (`config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`) passes for all changed core production files. An earlier broader-configuration attempt stopped before linting when plugin-SDK declaration preparation exceeded300 seconds; that failed preparation is retained, not relabeled as a pass. Core and UI typechecking also pass. Exact-head CI still owns the remaining broad checks.
- **Independent integration review:** read-only native review of exact tree `9ababaa762ad92f0b1deca9efb4f1182fb3570e2` found no actionable integration defect. It checked both imports, UTF-16-safe truncation, generated recovery predicates, upstream verified-update retention/dependency protection, unchanged feature patch text, and independently counted the exact23-line allocation reconciliation. This is scoped integration review, not fresh full-feature certification. The earlier CLI autoreview attempt failed authentication before producing a verdict; that unavailable result remains recorded. No authentication or review policy was changed. Exact-head hosted CI remains pending.
- **Scope:** the built CLI, Gateway/UI and stable-upgrade receipts below belong to prior candidate `556fc60`; they are retained, not represented as fresh executions of this refresh. Recovery/update-owner policy acceptance remains outstanding. No merge, auto-merge, deployment, live-state change, or policy waiver occurred.

### Previously accepted candidate evidence

Prior candidate `556fc60f228c8a2437effe2c89926dc0ba1d0483` integrates main `3df96dfc805b01d5d16e12040ab519ab67c8d61f`. [Fresh immutable evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/51d0afd65d99acc6fb1bbe12896c0391500a5be7/README.md).

- **Normal built CLI:** conservative cleanup refuses both retained reason classes; explicit preview changes no state; selected retirement removes two files; replay removes zero. Active SQLite bytes, one session and three events remain identical; independent backup unchanged.
- **Latest-stable v2026.11.2 storage upgrade:** [new additive evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/d296dd6d076a361b4d31afb5a473eb51b50c8ea9/README.md) verifies the official package emits v3 receipts/schema 27 and candidate Doctor upgrades to schema 41. Supported config getters preserve nondefault timezone/update settings; sessions CLI and Doctor inspect the same session and three events. Independent backup bytes remain unchanged. Controlled interruption, resume and replay pass; three archives retired, replay removes zero. Pending/disposed candidate state is safely refused by older cleanup/restore; its exact shipped manifest reader independently rejects v5. This verifies storage/Doctor/cleanup and session inspection, not new conversational writes, the package updater or a service restart. The v2026.11.1 proof remains retained.
- **Actual built Gateway/UI:** all nine empty/retained/incomplete scenarios at 400/820/1280 px pass through real RPC. All 123 served assets match disk hashes; protected archive bytes stay unchanged. No mutation requests, page errors, recovery-section shifts, shell movement or horizontal overflow. Console warnings/errors (including blocked service-worker activity and 401/404 responses) are retained; this is not a clean-console claim. Nine screenshots inspected; the small unrelated Update status text shift remains in tablet/desktop observations.
- **Checks/review:** all 144 distinct storage/cleanup tests have passing receipts after the missing-await correction; 16 UI unit tests, core/UI types, scoped lint, line caps and test-line ratchet pass. The real-ledger empty-inventory regression passes without weakened assertions. Independent full-snapshot review plus final-delta and harness audits have no unresolved actionable finding. `pnpm build:runtime` passes, and all 26,549 launcher/dist artifact hashes stay identical through execution.

Synthetic isolated fixtures only; no original-reporter data or model/channel calls. Interruption is callback-based source-owner fault injection, not an OS kill. The official stable package and exact internal dependencies are integrity-verified; its other dependencies link read-only to the candidate install. Earlier failed harness attempts remain in the evidence. The build emits advisory UI gzip baseline excesses; that prior head’s hosted CI was green (89 passed, 44 skipped, zero failed/pending), including the aggregate gate. All 26,549 build artifact hashes remain identical before/after the additional v2026.11.2 run. Recovery/update-owner policy acceptance remains outstanding.

Historical mocked-Gateway capture, before the Recovery Storage feature was added:

![Updates before recovery-storage visibility](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5d9d860-8ed6-440c-b43f-81641d60d496)

Prior-candidate built Gateway/UI captures, with synthetic data:

![Current empty inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/51d0afd65d99acc6fb1bbe12896c0391500a5be7/gateway-ui/empty-400.png)
![Retained archive reasons and guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/51d0afd65d99acc6fb1bbe12896c0391500a5be7/gateway-ui/retained-400.png)
![Incomplete inventory remains explicit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/51d0afd65d99acc6fb1bbe12896c0391500a5be7/gateway-ui/incomplete-1280.png)

[Historical accepted proof and limitations](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/bc34ff469ef24177f29da1efeea567d6064636ff/README.md) remain retained as prior-head evidence, not relabeled as this run.
