prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.3 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, using the same minimatch options as the `extraPaths` matcher beside it in the memory host SDK (so patterns behave the same on Node and Bun), is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). **Portable glob matching (ClawSweeper's 2026-11-09 review on `05585b7`):** the exclusion matcher called `path.posix.matchesGlob`, which Bun implements with `Bun.Glob`: extglobs never match and wildcards match dotfiles, so `["memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md"]` excluded a report on Node but not on Bun. Main's #194912 had just moved the `extraPaths` matcher to minimatch for the same reason. `1463f6e` moves those minimatch options into one shared constant and uses it for `excludePaths` too, with compiled matchers cached per configured list. Results on Node are unchanged; on Bun they now match Node. Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main `11a13b6`: production +89/-21 in 15 files (including moving main's glob options into the shared constant); tests +159/-3; docs +16/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2654 -> 2658 on main `b03fd2f`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `c210875` (on main `c7152f3`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.3` from npm (installed with `--ignore-scripts`; the CLI runs without the package's install scripts). The branch CLI on `c210875` reports `2026.11.2` because main's version string trails the release. Earlier runs from 2026.11.2 on `1463f6e` and on `05585b7` (before the portable-matcher change), from 2026.11.1 on `6d9ace7` and from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.3 and existing data:** 2026.11.3 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.3, v27 -> v41), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.3, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.3 OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.279 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.272 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.266 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.260 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.254 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.3): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.3): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (c210875) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.3 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v41 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.3 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.279 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.272 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.266 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.260 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.254 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~1s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). - `internal.test.ts` "keeps generated dreaming reports out of default and overlapping extra paths" also lists files with `memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md`. With the old `path.posix.matchesGlob` matcher, `listMemoryFiles` under Bun still returns the report: on stock Bun 1.3.14 it lists `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md, memory/dreaming/light/report.md`, and with `1463f6e` only `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md`. On Node both matchers agree, so the Node run passes either way; the CI shard that runs this test (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-6`) sets up the pinned Bun 1.4.4 test runtime. **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +154, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and portable (Node/Bun) glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch merged main `11a13b6` at `2401ff9`, `1463f6e` adds the portable-matcher fix (its CI passed), `c210875` merged main `c7152f3`, `edb9fd1` merged main `aab88e3`, `fc2ef72` merged main `ba6147a`, `5985aa9` merged main `81ca4f4`, and `e768746` now merges main `b03fd2f`; earlier merges conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time, and the PR diff is unchanged. The v2026.11.3 proof above ran on `c210875`. `edb9fd1`, `fc2ef72`, `5985aa9` and `e768746` add only main's changes. In `5985aa9` and `e768746`, main's #195369 adds an embedding-cache hook to `manager-sync-base.ts` and #197128, #198348, #199226 and #199694 edit other entries in `schema.help.models.ts`; both files merge cleanly next to this PR's lines. In `edb9fd1`, main's #196480 changed session-export paging in neighboring memory-core sync files, which do not call the file listing, the exclusion matcher or the scope hash. Main's #194912 replaced `path.posix.matchesGlob` in the `extraPaths` matcher in `internal.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge kept both, and `1463f6e` then shares main's options with the exclusion matcher. Main's #139230 reworked dirty-index maintenance and the watcher's background sync in `manager-watch-ops.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge keeps this PR's one `excludePaths` line there, and `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts`, `watch-policy.test.ts` and `manager.watcher-config.test.ts` pass on `e768746`. Main's #191749 bounded the realpath deduplication at the end of `listMemoryFiles`; it merges cleanly because `excludePaths` filters files as they are collected, before that step. Main's #192488 moved the search manager types into `search-manager.types.ts`; this PR does not import them. Main's #193952 added provider name and icon help to `schema.help.models.ts`, which this PR also edits; both sets of entries merge cleanly. On `1cc43f3`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and so `ci-gate`) failed because main `bf10667` was over its own test-line ceiling by 137 lines; main's own scheduled job logged the same overage and passed only because that run added no test lines. Main `d1ffc39` got back under the ceiling, and the ratchet passes locally on `e768746` (net +154 test lines, covered by this PR's 154-line allocation). On `df4f9e6`, `check-prompt-snapshots` failed on three JSON prompt snapshots this PR does not touch: main's #192596 stopped formatting JSON snapshots without regenerating the committed ones (the content was identical, only the layout differed). Main fixed it in #192628, `5d93337` merged that fix, and `prompt:snapshots:check` passes locally on `e768746`. On `0a3aa17`, 19 CI jobs failed in setup before running any check because downloading the pinned Bun runtime from the `openclaw/bun` release returned HTTP 504; `pnpm test:ci-failed 188294` found no test failures, and CI on `5858e44` passed. Main rolled fs-safe back to 0.27.1 in #194589; `05585b7` merges that rollback, and `read-file.test.ts` passes locally (19/19). `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `config:docs:check` pass, and the touched tests plus `memory-files-worker.test.ts`, `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` and `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` (files main also changed) pass. `checks-node-changed` on `a63b2b5` failed in `plugin-sdk-package-contract-guardrails.test.ts` after main's #188833 referenced an untyped SDK entrypoint in a guide; main fixed it in #188937, and that test passes locally on `e768746`. prs.title: fix(matrix): keep explicit recovery available during deferred migration
prs.body:
Fixes #200790

## What Problem This Solves

After an unsafe Matrix crypto shutdown, a pending plugin migration could hide the documented recovery commands. Doctor and update repair required that recovery first, leaving operators unable to proceed through the supported CLI.

## User Impact

Operators can run `openclaw matrix doctor inspect [--json]` and `openclaw matrix doctor recover --account <id> --accept-snapshot-rollback` while a pending migration withholds Matrix. Recovery still requires explicit rollback consent, exactly one blocked account store, exclusive crypto ownership, and a valid replayable snapshot. Then run `openclaw update repair` (or `openclaw doctor --fix`) before restarting the Gateway.

Other Matrix commands remain withheld. Doctor/update repair and `--fix`, `--yes`, or `--force` never authorize snapshot rollback. The host CLI and plugin need this change together; upgrading the plugin alone does not add the route to older CLIs.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional `doctorContract.recoveryCli` declaration mounts exact subtrees under the plugin's existing CLI roots through the separate Doctor artifact. The existing CLI owner selects it only for the matching enabled plugin's structured migration refusal, preserving normal-root precedence and disabled, denied, quarantined, and ordinary-load-failure behavior. Registration receives a mounted Commander subtree and narrow plugin-bound state context, using existing source preparation and callback lifetime.

Both routes share the Matrix registrar and crypto recovery owner. The recovery helper no longer depends on full Matrix runtime access; no new state, migration ledger, lock, or crypto policy is introduced. The existing full/metadata loader gate remains intact. Production changes add 217 net lines; tests add 397 and docs add 68. The growth supplies the optional contract, admission, and owning-boundary regression proof.

## Evidence

Current head: `bfc5f3ef4fbc4ce4c7075d386d84472bcd7d8e6e`. Merged main: `b60b11474606ed85297eceae4a0a001ece69cd90`. Prior tested head: `b33cfb39f9cae8b174f413f9e6cf4081b40c6e27`.

The merge resolved only `docs/install/updating.md`: both the exact Matrix recovery paragraph and all upstream document content are retained. All 20 PR production/test files remain byte-identical to the prior tested head. This is a documentation-only conflict resolution; no trust boundary or API semantics changed.

- The committed real-registration regression fails on the base with Commander `unknown command 'matrix'` after synthetic state, obligation, and Doctor-detector setup succeeds. On the candidate it produces the actual inspect result and recovers a valid synthetic SQLite snapshot only with explicit consent. Inspect/refusals preserve the guard and obligation; recovery leaves deferred settlement to Doctor/update repair. No homeserver, real account, credentials, or real keys are used.
- The initial focused proof passed 118 tests across 11 named files. After CI repair, 70 tests across six named CLI/Doctor/Matrix snapshot files passed again, including actual registration, synthetic recovery, refusal safeguards, automatic Doctor non-recovery, and snapshot persistence (83.11 seconds including source compilation and three serialized shards).
- On the merged head, 41 tests across five named Matrix real-registration/recovery, CLI admission, manifest and Doctor contract files passed (59.48 seconds including source compilation and three serialized shards). The targeted native typecheck of nine source/test roots also passed. Document preservation, touched-document formatting and staged diff checks passed. Unaffected tests, typed lint and independent reviews remain prior-head evidence; no new independent review was needed for the mechanical paragraph union.
- [CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44181163298) caught a real store-contract mismatch and the new registrar assertion. Recovery now requires only bounded snapshot reads and sealing, shared by Doctor and normal runtime stores; retained-store options and V2 CAS stay with the operations that need them. Callable validation preserves registrar identity without the cast. No retention defaults, suppressions, or baseline exemptions were added.
- The repair passed a targeted native typecheck of nine named source/test roots plus ambient declarations, touched-file CI-core typed oxlint/format, and diff checks. The existing assertion parser reproduces the old file count `4 > 3` and verifies repaired `3 <= 3`; the full ratchet remains CI proof. Total test growth is 397 net lines, within the 400-line budget. Earlier export synchronization/check and inventory generation produced no additional changes.
- After simplification, shared autoreview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3) reviewed the complete repair delta against `18e2da0b01373655c87729b7399f7460618c3bf6` with the store and callback owners supplied, completing `scoped-clean` with no findings. This supplements the initial full-candidate review and is self-reported evidence, not CI attestation.

The new head's first CI run is pending. Full production/test type lanes, extension package declarations, and the full ratchet must validate this head in PR CI. Build/package generation, full SDK declaration/API diff, native/live Matrix behavior, and stable-upgrade testing were not run on the production Gateway host. Focused source/synthetic proof does not establish those results. No live state or Gateway service was changed.

Reported by @nikolay-bratanov

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix(codex): stop misreporting API quota as subscription exhaustion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex-backed chats claim that the user's subscription is exhausted when an API-key request fails because its API quota is exhausted.

## User Impact

The error now preserves Codex's explanation, including “Quota exceeded. Check your plan and billing details.” It uses neutral usage/quota wording and keeps reset-time guidance when Codex supplies it. No configuration migration is needed; credential selection and billing are unchanged.

The separate persisted history failure card still uses generic rate-limit wording. This PR fixes the detailed error surfaced by the run and live chat event.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native `usageLimitExceeded` represents API quota failures, subscription limits, and plans without Codex access. It cannot establish subscription exhaustion. The existing error owner retains the native cause separately from formatted guidance, including across the account-usage refresh. Structural HTTP 429 classification and evidence-based profile cooldowns are preserved. Related: #110381.

## Evidence

- **Single-run native-to-Gateway proof, completing ClawSweeper's request:** the real built Gateway launched the real pinned Codex 0.164.0 binary. Native Codex received an HTTP 429 `insufficient_quota` response, emitted `usageLimitExceeded`, and the same Gateway run produced the corrected `chat.state:error` and `agent.wait` output. The native app-server was not replaced or stubbed. The billing cause appears once; no subscription exhaustion or reset time is invented. See the redacted terminal excerpt below.
- **Red/green:** startup RPC and streamed terminal regressions both fail on base `0d2071eba04fc7a5b81f16854544e56baa6d23bf` because the billing explanation is missing. The authoritative-unexhausted-usage case also fails on base. All pass with the fix, including unavailable-usage and per-profile cooldown behavior.
- **Original-head validation:** 158 tests passed across the formatter, terminal projector, and attempt files; all 12 usage-limit cases passed again after the final ownership simplification. Format, focused lint, targeted TypeScript, test-line ratchet, diff checks, and the `qaRuntime` build pass. [CI passed on the reviewed head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41693291709).
- **Original-head independent review:** Codex autoreview found no actionable correctness or security defects. ClawSweeper also reported no code findings; this evidence update addresses its sole proof blocker. These original results apply to head `5b73f31a8b0c6ba7b37966abb40377de1fcafad4` (tree `a944b712e4f2668ea77d101b1e04c297c91a18be`).
- **Current conflict repair and CI repair:** Head `05a66c5de413ac91e5dac2b23f692d97584d7359` (tree `8d76b7f1de225a1b6042fdfcf14608d35a67b1d2`) retains the integration of main `c531fd0b1339f53ec9530dfd5fed312944680a66` and the contributor's ancestry. Both native-quota and model-policy-denial regression groups are preserved. [The previous integrated-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44179752236) exposed a stale bounded-turn assertion expecting subscription-exhaustion wording. The committed repair now requires both neutral quota guidance and the original native cause; production behavior is unchanged by this repair.
- **Current-head local verification:** 83 tests passed across bounded-turn, rate-limit formatter, and terminal-error projection; all 19 quota entry-point cases passed. Targeted lint and TypeScript, diff checks, and normal commit hooks passed. Dependencies were installed in the isolated task checkout with the frozen lockfile and pinned pnpm 12.15.0, providing required oxlint 1.89.0 without modifying dependency pins or shared installations. Independent P0–P3 review of this exact tree found no actionable findings. [ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192165#issuecomment-6612544797), found no findings or before-merge items, and accepted the proof reuse after inspecting the integration and test-only repair.

<summary>Single-run end-to-end proof: real Gateway and native Codex, simulated HTTP backend</summary>

The external HTTP backend alone is simulated. The run uses a fresh HOME/CODEX_HOME and isolated Gateway state, a dummy native API key, and Codex's supported `model_catalog_json` configuration containing only `synthetic-quota-proof`. The catalog schema is the same as the existing [native fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5b73f31a8b0c6ba7b37966abb40377de1fcafad4/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts#L108). Native Codex uses its custom HTTP Responses provider with WebSockets disabled. An observer records native stdout without changing protocol bytes. No app-server response is supplied by a fixture.

This corrects the earlier experiment's setup: its requested model was absent from the native catalog and it used the wrong Gateway provider prefix. No production capability checks were changed or bypassed.

prs.title: improve(ui): give form controls one surface standard across themes
prs.body:
Form controls in the Control UI now share one look. Selects, text fields, segmented controls, sub-tabs, switches and select menus take their fill and edge from the theme's own text colour laid over the surface they sit on, the same way row hover and selection already do. On the default dark theme the controls no longer sink into the card or show a blue-violet outline, and every built-in theme and light mode follows without values of its own.

Focus is now a neutral edge with a soft ring instead of the accent. Sizes, radii, spacing, icons, markup and behaviour are unchanged; only colours move.

The standard, as a share of the theme's `--text` over the host surface:

- Select triggers: fill 6%, edge 10%; on hover fill 8%, edge 16%. Value text `--text-strong`, chevron and placeholder `--muted`.
- Text inputs and textareas: fill 8%, edge 16%. Text `--text-strong`, placeholder `--muted`.
- Focus on any field: edge `--text-strong` at 55% and a 3px ring at 12%. Invalid fields keep their error colour.
- Segmented controls: track fill 6%, edge 10%. Idle items `--text`, hover `--text-strong`. The selected item has a 14% fill, a 16% inner hairline and `--text-strong` text.
- Sub-tabs: idle `--text`, active `--text-strong`; the underline is unchanged.
- Switches: off track 18% with no border, knob `--text-strong` on and off; the on track keeps the accent.
- Select menus: same background, a 16% edge, and an 8% fill on the highlighted and chosen rows.
- Disabled controls keep their current opacity.

The values live once in `base.css` as `--control-*` properties next to `--surface-hover` and `--surface-selected`, and the shared control rules read them. The Beacon and CRT themes set their own field focus edge (accent) and CRT sets its own selected segment; those theme values still apply.

Evidence is from the mock Control UI at 1440 px wide. Themes and modes were set with the Appearance page's own theme cards and Color mode control.

prs.title: improve(ui): list portals in a section sidebar
prs.body:
Portals now has a section sidebar, like Automations and Dashboards. It lists every portal with its title and port, and the open portal's row is selected. Choosing a row opens that portal, and coming back to Portals in the same tab reopens the last one.

Beside that sidebar the page is the open portal: its title, then its port and description, then the preview in one card that fills the rest of the page. The card's top bar keeps the address link and the close button; the frame sits inset below it. The page no longer repeats the portal list there.

Where the sidebar does not stand beside the page (sidebar closed, phone layout, native embed), the page keeps its list and layout as before. With no portals, the page shows its usual header and the existing empty content.

prs.title: fix: improve scrolling in touch dashboard panels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dashboard content that cannot stay in view when scrolling an iPad side panel, and prevents expanded Auto widgets overlapping during drag or resize previews.

## User Impact

Gesture previews retain the spacing of expanded Auto widgets without raising the Fixed resize limit.

**Historical practical iPad follow-up PASS at c7decbdf on the reported device (November17): restored split, independent feeds and Auto→Fixed→Auto. This is not all-device certification or a new physical-device trial of the gesture repair.** Auto-height HTML widgets can grow taller on touch layouts so more content scrolls with the board, instead of inside an oversized iframe. The original singleton-page viewport fix is retained.

Existing fixed-height widgets keep their saved sizes. Switching a very tall Auto widget to Fixed can shrink it to the existing fixed-size limit; switching to a fine-pointer mouse layout can also restore compact sizing. The reporter explicitly accepted this tradeoff on November 12. Fixed widgets and documents beyond the larger bound can still scroll internally.

**The previous 6ddce47 iPad grid result remains FAIL / unchanged versus its baseline**, separately from its tall-page improvement. No merge or deployment is authorized. The requester authorized taking this PR out of draft on November17; exact-head CI/review are followed separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

One existing board owner shares the effective content-fit policy across grid allocation, exact card height and gesture previews. Coarse-pointer layouts reuse the existing 240-row document bound; fine-pointer layouts retain the ordinary 20-row bound. There is no new touch relay, schema, configuration, permission, or dependency change.

## Evidence

### November 17 gesture-preview repair — published and locally verified

The fresh review identified a P2 overlap when dragging or resizing among tall Auto widgets on touch layouts. The repair makes initial rendering and gesture construction share the same effective sizing policy, preserves expanded neighboring Auto spans through drag/resize previews, and retains the existing 20-row Fixed resize target limit. **Published repair head:** [`417b7f69d6944339ba3a6ef7752ca098918f34e3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/417b7f69d6944339ba3a6ef7752ca098918f34e3). The before comparison is c7decbdf.

- **Red/green:** the full Control UI with native Chromium CDP touch reproduced approximately 583 px of card overlap on c7decbdf, then passed with the repair. Both drag and resize initiation, pointer movement and cancellation retain separated neighbors and unchanged Auto heights; the resize visibly advances to five rows. A separate pure-grid regression protects expanded drag spans and the 20-row Fixed target bound.
- **Passed:** 11/11 fullscreen E2E (25.43 s invocation), 39/39 board-owner/grid tests (3.71 s), and 26/26 real-Chromium board browser tests (6.86 s); targeted UI-component and UI-E2E typechecks, lint, formatting, controller and test-line guards, and production UI build. CI seconds and new-head CI are not yet available. Build size-budget warnings remain advisory; no bundle baseline was raised.
- **Scope and simplification:** one effective content-fit decision now serves rendering and gestures; no duplicate policy, new manager, cache, configuration, or dependency. This follow-up adds 17 net production lines and 90 net regression-test lines, with a separate 90-line allocation. The full-app check covers event/renderer wiring and geometry; the grid check independently guards resize-limit semantics.
- **Independent review:** a user-approved independent read-only OpenClaw reviewer completed a P0–P2 narrative review of the complete frozen 11-file, +639/−34 candidate against base `8569bd9edfadb9d08539083cae19b3680ef49b3c`, with no findings. Applicable Solid guidance was read in full. The reviewer assessed supplied source text; actual checkout correspondence, test execution and build receipts were verified by the implementing agent, not independently executed by that reviewer. This is not helper-validated Auto Review or machine scoped-clean status; two native Auto Review attempts ended interrupted without a report. Historical physical Safari evidence below stays pinned to c7decbdf, not this gesture repair; no new physical-device run is claimed.
- **Current-head gates:** [CI run 44154860288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44154860288) is attached to `417b7f69d6944339ba3a6ef7752ca098918f34e3`. A completed ClawSweeper assessment naming that same head and this final description is required before a maintainer-ready claim; older c7decbdf receipts do not certify this repair.

Before — starting the touch drag places the following cards inside the first Auto card:

![Before: touch drag preview overlaps expanded Auto widgets](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fcef571-4aae-49ed-b325-433cf1c8692d)

After — the same native touch interaction keeps the Auto footer, Fixed card and following Auto card separated:

![After: touch drag preview preserves expanded Auto widget spacing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d56da05b-aeed-495f-99d8-fa5fefe95c25)

The inspected 480×781 crops show only synthetic dashboard content and were also delivered to the originating conversation.

### Original touch-sizing experiment — historical c7decbdf stage

- **Before this experiment:** `6ddce47fac561860377eaaea68b094db3986c211`. **After:** `c7decbdf1a06fef89346ec221f79bee44ec97453`. Original PR/merge base: `8569bd9edfadb9d08539083cae19b3680ef49b3c`.
- **Red/green at the real UI boundary:** the before implementation retains 3,825px of inner-document scroll and fails the touch-fit assertion. The experiment reaches the final marker with trusted Chromium touch gestures through the real Control UI and native nested sandbox frames. The fixed-height control remains 260px; a fresh fine-pointer context retains ordinary inner scrolling. This does not prove the WebKit root cause or physical Safari correctness.
- **Passed locally:** full dashboard E2E **11/11**, board browser **26/26**, board unit **27/27**, owning UI-component and UI-E2E typechecks, targeted lint, formatting/whitespace, and Control UI build. E2E invocation 22.59s / tests 10.862s; added touch/fine cases 2.153s/1.170s. Browser/unit invocations 5.20s/3.13s. New-head CI and CI seconds are not claimed.
- **Original touch-sizing Auto Review (historical c7de stage):** OpenClaw engine, complete local snapshot against the pinned base, helper-selected **P0 scope**, scoped-clean with no findings. This is not a full-priority or Safari certification. The exact 200 net regression lines have their own allocation.
- **Warnings retained:** the successful build reports advisory bundle-budget overruns; no budget baseline was raised. Existing suites emit development strict-read/pointer-capture notices. An unsupported mid-context pointer-emulation attempt was replaced by independently verified native coarse/fine contexts, not counted as pointer-transition coverage.
- **Physical update:** November12 split/expanded improvement is retained; the November17 report and selected telemetry close restored split, independent feeds and Auto→Fixed→Auto on the stated device. The recovered actual JSON is fully parsed and the three direct clip links are archived below. Current-head CI and a completed fresh ClawSweeper review—not draft-skipped jobs—determine maintainer readiness.

### November 17 practical iPad follow-up — requested functional checks PASS

[Qualified report](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/a90a5876fc32f88178dcd20287d9d309a5495f9c/ui/src/e2e/side-panel-scrolling.physical-ipad-20261117.md) and [selected mark/feed readings](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/a90a5876fc32f88178dcd20287d9d309a5495f9c/ui/src/e2e/side-panel-scrolling.physical-ipad-20261117.readings.json), pinned at `a90a5876fc32f88178dcd20287d9d309a5495f9c`. The physical trial used `c7decbdf1a06fef89346ec221f79bee44ec97453`; no product edits or stylesheet substitution were made for that trial. The later gesture-preview repair is qualified separately above.

The reporter confirms **iPad Pro 13-inch M4, iPadOS 27.2.1, no mouse/trackpad**. The recovered actual Safari export is independently parsed and verified as **1,958 samples / ten marks**, collected **2026-11-17T15:52:45.328Z**, with `finePointer=false`, `maxTouchPoints=5`, 1376×867 CSS px, DPR2 and scale1 at all marks. Safari's desktop-style Macintosh/MacIntel UA is retained as recorded; it is not independent hardware/OS attestation.

| Requested check | Outcome on the reported device | Bound evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Candidate grid restored split | **PASS** | Marks2/3 show first/second Auto markers reachable. Mark3 outer board11908/max11908, remaining0; relevant earlier touchends precede marks2/3 by1.034s/3.137s. |
| Independent nested feeds | **PASS** | Mark6: each feed1658/max1658. Full-stream feed windows have recorded board and reported document-root offsets 0: 82/127 inner-scroll rows, or 83/128 total rows including one touchend each. |
| Auto→Fixed→Auto | **PASS, including the accepted smaller fixed bound** | Marks5/7/8/10: Auto iframe pairs5582/5582 →1308/5582 →1308/1308 →5582/5582. Final markers return after Auto is restored. |
| Separate Fixed control | **Iframe-height invariant supported** | All 1,940 recorded Fixed-control iframe geometries have height 220px, including every mark. This is NOT a total-card-height invariance claim. |

**Accepted Fixed-mode limitation retained:** at mark 9, both now-fixed document roots are at4274 with remaining0, but the outer board is still0 with892 remaining. Fixed mode still has internal scrolling. Do not claim those fixed-card footers are visible at that mark or that pinning makes all content fit the visible panel.

Roboclaw now independently parsed **all 1,958 actual sample records**, checked exact input bytes/SHA-256, source and baseline bindings, chronological sample times, ten mark identities, reason counts, input facts, the two full feed intervals, sizing transitions and every recorded Fixed-control iframe height. All 30 selected marked-widget payloads were compared to the original preceding stream messages, including their explicit ages. The original compact JSON was read without rewriting sample values or reconstructing telemetry. Earlier cross-frame readings remain asynchronous—not simultaneous mark-time measurements. Touchend telemetry is present; no video touch indicator independently exposes the physical release instant.

**Full-stream qualifications:** all ten marked trials are 1376×867, with DPR 2/scale 1, finePointer=false and maxTouchPoints=5. The stream also contains three unmarked 1032×1211 resize observations at 15:52:22.689Z; no portrait acceptance is claimed. The inherited fixture field `testDate` remains 2026-11-12, while `collectedAt` and every actual sample timestamp are November17. Those original values are retained, not silently corrected.

The reporter's inspected clip ranges are restored split19–40s, independent feeds54–70s, and Auto→Fixed→Auto74–113s. Each is a disclosed same-source-frame dashboard+toolbar composition, with private browser/chat/audio/source metadata removed. The full compact JSON keeps sample values unchanged, with only two top-level private origins redacted and an explanation added; file hashes are in the pinned report.

**Artifact recovery complete:** all four reattached files are present/readable and match the pinned byte counts and SHA-256 values. Roboclaw independently decoded the three actual videos and inspected sampled frames across restored split, feeds and sizing transitions; their dashboard+same-frame-toolbar composition is preserved. The exact, unmodified clips are now directly attached to this GitHub PR below. The full compact JSON (3,590,379 bytes) is retained in the linked work session and was programmatically inspected in full; the public companion readings remain the concise review surface. prs.title: improve(ui): give the Systems desktop more room with a collapsible health strip
prs.body:
On the Systems page the selected device is now the page title, with its status dot and device facts (for example "This computer · macOS 26.5") on the line under it. The Stats and Device details buttons stay at the right. The page no longer repeats the generic Systems title and subtitle, including its Learn more link, because the section sidebar already names the section.

Load, memory, disk and backups now sit in one row of equal cards directly under the device. One caption line follows: the volumes link on the left, the sample time on the right, and a small chevron that collapses the row.

Collapsed, the row becomes a single quiet line with the load, memory used of total and disk available of total. Clicking it expands the row again. This browser remembers the choice, and the buttons report their state with `aria-expanded`.

The desktop viewer sits in its own card with the theme's large corner radius and takes the rest of the page height. When the row is collapsed, the viewer grows into the space. Its toolbar keeps every control.

In the Systems sidebar, each device row shows the name on one line and its existing device fact under it. The group labels no longer show a count.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`) at 1440×900. Connected uses the `session-design` fixture, which serves a synthetic Gateway desktop. Connecting uses the default fixture, where the desktop never finishes connecting.

prs.title: improve(ui): seat the open sidebar on the rail with rounded corners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An open sidebar meets the rail at a straight vertical divider.

## User Impact

The open sidebar sits on the rail as a panel: the rail's surface runs behind it and shows through its rounded top and bottom rail-side corners, where a 1px hairline follows the curve. The radius follows the theme's corner scale; the content side stays square; the rail, colors and a closed sidebar are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

CSS only. Checked in light and dark: the hairline follows the curve and no sidebar content leaks past the corners; a page without a sidebar keeps the rail's divider and the rail stays 52px wide.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock at the end of the series, so the after image can show later parts too.

Top of the sidebar before and after (2x) (left: main, right: after):

![Top of the sidebar before and after (2x)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c4ed59a-20fc-4b4c-b7d6-cd6815275821)

Full window before and after (left: main, right: after):

![Full window before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e075d21-2433-4729-92a7-0143c20e624e)

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes at this PR's head.
- The unit tests of the files this PR touches pass at its head; the full UI unit suite passes at the end of the series (one failure also on main: a Workboard German relative-time string, "vor 1min", from the local ICU).
- `dashboard-website` and `sidebar-customization` UI e2e pass at this head.
- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.

Side rail series, part 16 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200012; review only this PR's commits.


## Update: e2e repair

The full Control UI e2e run on the stack found tests this PR broke or product gaps it introduced; this PR now carries their fixes:
- fix(ui): keep the rail's surface under imported palettes
- fix(ui): draw the sidebar panel's hairline without moving its content
- test(ui): measure sidebar row insets inside the panel hairline


## Update: review follow-up

- improve(ui): soften the sidebar panel corners — radius 22px to 18px.

## Maintainer verification

Reviewed the complete rebased stack while retaining the maintainer-approved visual design. The integrated candidate passed 558 unit/browser tests and 20 bundled browser E2E cases, including sidebar peeking, section navigation, Automation filters/history and native plugin navigation. The final removal of unused wiring and fixtures received focused checks afterward. Visual acceptance is the maintainer's previously completed hands-on run on the integrated local Gateway; these additional checks do not claim a second live-Gateway campaign.

## Final bundle-size comparison

Measured with the repository's production comparator against base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`, using the same installed toolchain. The optimized candidate is `baebb54ec1dbaca6c6424075f6d0bfa6f480ca1d`.

| Metric | Base | Stack before optional-code cleanup | Optimized stack |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat boot JS, gzip bytes | 1,324,943 | 1,339,806 | 1,330,444 |
| New Session boot JS, gzip bytes | 815,765 | 830,872 | 821,376 |
| Initial-entry JS, gzip bytes | 91,013 | 91,599 | 91,599 |

The cleanup removes the eager Automation filter UI/text dependency from the sidebar header. Chat still makes 21 boot JS requests and New Session 17, unchanged from the base. Total CSS is 684 gzip bytes smaller; total shipped JS is 9,779 gzip bytes smaller. The remaining boot cost is 5,501 bytes for Chat and 5,611 for New Session. These are delivery-size measurements, not a runtime latency benchmark.

The existing largest-JS and route-boot byte ceilings still fail. They have not been changed or bypassed. The final focused tests passed (21 UI cases and 10 browser cases) after the cleanup, in addition to the earlier integrated 558-case and 20-E2E-case run.

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

Vyctor approved the measured JavaScript byte cost for this navigation stack. These cumulative measurements compare this layer with paired main base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`. Each cap equals the original main cap plus the measured delta, preserving existing headroom without adding another margin.

| Metric | Cumulative gzip delta | Cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest JS asset | +4,803 B | 577,243 B |
| Chat boot JS | +5,501 B | 1,331,081 B |
| New Session boot JS | +5,611 B | 822,243 B |

CSS ceilings, request counts, startup ceilings and gate logic are unchanged. Byte measurements are delivery-size evidence, not latency measurements.

<!-- navigation-landing-review:start -->
### Maintainer validation

Reviewed and rebased this layer on predecessor `7338e1c1e4c1bd2a664e1964c3cb360d556083b8`; current head is `6c94013c6cf49a80fec50569c46bf3f7eaef3c57`. The own-layer tree, original human authors and signatures were checked. UI typechecking passed on this candidate. Previously verified functional and integrated visual proof was reused where inputs are unchanged; the maintainer also exercised the integrated stack on a real Gateway.

The Pages menu loads its own row and pin styles through its existing lazy component, without changing declarations or adding any request during Chat/New Session startup. The official paired check passed: largest shared CSS 58,977 B vs 59,102 B baseline (and 59,229 B with the original corners); total CSS 1,733,823 B raw, down 6,340 B. Both startup byte budgets and the relative CSS budget pass. Pin/unpin and reload passed in Chromium; stylelint, format and diff checks passed.

The maintainer authorized sequential CI bypass after repairing known PR-caused failures. Hosted CI may still be running; this is not a claim of full hosted CI success. The unrelated owner-approval timing failure is tracked separately in #200810.

On phones, the **Set up a model** button leaves a large blank space before Dictate. The direct setup action added in [#200640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200640) no longer matches the model picker's existing alignment rule. ## What Changed

Extend the existing New Session alignment rule to the setup button. Desktop layout stays unchanged. Update both empty-catalog tests to use the setup action while preserving their spacing, unavailable-effort, and no-session-mutation checks. Available-model spacing still checks opening and closing the popover; its fixture now selects its own non-reasoning model so an unrelated effort control does not sit between the measured controls.

## Validation

- Scheduled baseline: [UI5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44179757082/job/134381748605) and [UI7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44179757082/job/134381749126) at `c531fd0b` fail on obsolete empty-catalog selectors.

- Final behavior coverage: 13/13 across the two affected E2E files, combining 11 unchanged passing cases with a focused rerun of the 2 corrected available-model fixtures. No repeat of passing cases.
- Local proof uses macOS/Node 26.13.0 and the existing production-bundle E2E wrapper. The four current picker modules and changed files were temporarily overlaid on a qualified native checkout; this is scoped owner-input proof, not a whole-current-tree run. The local locator timeout is 10s versus 30s in CI.
- Targeted format, type-aware lint, and CSS lint passed. This resolves the earlier ad-hoc typecheck setup gap; no browser cases were rerun.
- Full final-source independent review: no findings (0.96 confidence).

## Visual Evidence

Mocked Gateway, dark theme, matching empty-catalog state. Before uses the frozen base CSS; after applies this alignment rule. Captures use the qualified owner-input overlay described above.

prs.title: fix(ui): guide Chat to setup when no model is connected
prs.body:
Closes #200323
Closes #200325

## What Problem This Solves

With no model connected, Chat could show an unconfigured default as selected and let users send a message that ended in a misleading authentication error.

## User Impact

Chat guides users to model setup and preserves their unsent draft instead of sending a request that cannot succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A default model name does not mean a model is usable. Setup detection now uses completed catalog and account information. Configured models with authentication errors or cooldowns, and catalogs still loading, retain their existing behavior rather than being mistaken for an unconfigured installation.

## Evidence

Verified on the exact source tree published as [f2e7969](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f2e7969f62a4149443b98243a75a408a43e828df):

- The unconfigured flow preserves the draft, disables send, makes no chat request, and opens model-provider settings. Authentication-error, cooldown, and pending-catalog cases pass.
- 222 unit tests, 38 browser tests, and 33 bundled end-to-end tests pass. Production build, targeted typecheck, lint, and formatting pass.
- The [CI performance check passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44184876057/job/134399823207). [Full CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44184876057) completed with failure. The unresolved [checks-ui (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44184876057/job/134399823254) failure is the inline-output assertion (0 messages, expected 1). The unchanged file passed five isolated runs on this head and five on main `3481cbc`; this did not establish the cause or prove flakiness.

Browser tests use synthetic Gateway responses, not live provider sign-in.

Reported and reproduced by @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_dn793l)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: feat(ui): list a plugin section's pages in its own sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A plugin page with child items, such as Workboard and its boards, put every child in the rail's pages menu, so the menu grew with every board and Workboard had no list beside its page.

## User Impact

Workboard (and any plugin navigation item with children) gets a sidebar of its own: the item, then each board, each with a pin toggle. The pages menu lists only Workboard. Only the rail item that shows the open page is marked, and a pinned board marks itself over a pinned Workboard. Reloading on Workboard restores its saved sidebar.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the navigation contract's `parent` field and adds nothing Workboard-specific. One rule decides whether a plugin navigation item is current. The sidebar views now come from one list that the boot snapshot format reads, so a new view is saved without a second edit.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock at the end of the series, so the after image can show later parts too.

Workboard before and after (left: main, right: after):

![Workboard before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/302b00f8-bea6-44c1-9529-6ac61c908a26)

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes at this PR's head.
- The unit tests of the files this PR touches pass at its head; the full UI unit suite passes at the end of the series (one failure also on main: a Workboard German relative-time string, "vor 1min", from the local ICU).
- `dashboard-website` and `sidebar-customization` UI e2e pass at this head.
- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.

## Known Gap

Reloading directly on Workboard shows its sidebar about 100 ms after the first paint, because whether the page has a section is known only once the plugin registry arrives. It belongs with the boot-order follow-up.

Side rail series, part 15 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200011; review only this PR's commits.


## Update: e2e repair

The full Control UI e2e run on the stack found tests this PR broke or product gaps it introduced; this PR now carries their fixes:
- test(ui): pin a board from the Workboard sidebar in the routing e2e

## Maintainer verification

Corrected current-page marking for plugin children addressed by query parameters. With both parent and child pinned, only the matching child is current; a parent-only pin still represents the section. The regression failed before the correction and all 11 focused navigation cases passed afterward. UI/test types, lint, formatting and independent review passed.

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

Vyctor approved the measured JavaScript byte cost for this navigation stack. These cumulative measurements compare this layer with paired main base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`. Each cap equals the original main cap plus the measured delta, preserving existing headroom without adding another margin.

| Metric | Cumulative gzip delta | Cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest JS asset | +4,803 B | 577,243 B |
| Chat boot JS | +5,501 B | 1,331,081 B |
| New Session boot JS | +5,611 B | 822,243 B |

CSS ceilings, request counts, startup ceilings and gate logic are unchanged. Byte measurements are delivery-size evidence, not latency measurements.

<!-- navigation-landing-review:start -->
### Maintainer validation

Reviewed and rebased this layer on predecessor `53d9315577659fbb97daeb2ca5409492679b29bf`; current head is `56c85fe660e6df985a73cf1250b618dcc983f08c`. The own-layer tree, original human authors and signatures were checked. UI typechecking passed on this candidate. Previously verified functional and integrated visual proof was reused where inputs are unchanged; the maintainer also exercised the integrated stack on a real Gateway.

Plugin-section classification is memoized on the registry revision and active plugin, preserving the single commit observer without repeating registry scans on unrelated sidebar updates. Existing plugin/selection cases, types and controller guard passed.

The maintainer authorized sequential CI bypass after repairing known PR-caused failures. Hosted CI may still be running; this is not a claim of full hosted CI success. The unrelated owner-approval timing failure is tracked separately in #200810.

prs.title: perf(sessions): shorten cold transcript writer holds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background cold transcript archival held the per-agent SQLite writer while converting an entire large session to navigation rows and removing its search index. Queued transcript appends could not run until that work committed.

This completes the original implementation in this PR and retains its commits. Publication is atomic per session: every archive chunk is durable before the cold marker becomes visible. Readers select that complete archive immediately. Navigation payload cleanup and FTS deletion then use separately admitted transactions capped at **256 rows**, with feedback targeting 20 ms. Embedded child blobs are cleared one chunk per transaction. Each unit rechecks the cold marker; queued foreground writes can run between units, and restoration cancels further cleanup. Read-only selection discovers interrupted cleanup, including sessions whose FTS rows are already gone.

Unqualified transcript projections reconcile through their existing owner before archive preparation. Idle maintenance stays read-only. No schema, index, configuration, retention, cache, or data-format change.

Cold operations now use distinct `session.cold.batch`, `.restore`, `.sweep`, and `.maintain` transaction labels. Their existing statement attribution records native `statementExecutionMs` separately from `callbackOtherMs`; legacy `sqlMs` included application work and cannot alone identify the cost of SQL execution.

## Evidence

Predeclared rule: five serial, interleaved A1/A2/B cycles from identical closed synthetic fixtures; both A arms use pinned main `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110`. B must beat both controls on maximum writer hold and p99 append queue wait. A throughput or CPU regression of 20% or more blocks landing. SQL-work target is 50 ms, with a fixed row ceiling rather than a promised elapsed deadline under arbitrary I/O stalls. Report every sample.

Fixture: **37.30 GiB**, 2,401 sessions, 6.05 million events. One eligible session has 50,000 events and 220,291,661 raw UTF-8 bytes; 2,400 hot siblings have 2,500 events each. Actual maintenance runs alongside 100 transcript appends, scheduled at 5 ms intervals after archival begins. The initial 200-append setup exceeded the existing 128-pending-task pool capacity and is retained as failed setup, not accepted timing evidence. No production data or systems were accessed.

Host: Apple M3 Ultra, 512 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1, APFS. This reproduces database scale, not btrfs or a particular production I/O-pressure tail. Payloads are deliberately compressible; this is not an incompressible-file stress result. Workspace files are not traversed by this flow. Fresh cloned fixtures and fresh processes are used; warm-up precedes timing, and host load is recorded for every run.

| Metric | A1 | A2 | B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Maximum cold writer hold (ms) | 1517.59 | 1505.59 | 103.88 |
| Maximum native SQL in a cold unit (ms) | 1181.09 | 1168.94 | 14.92 |
| Median per-run p99 append queue wait (ms) | 2018.00 | 2005.00 | 171.00 |
| Median complete maintenance pass (ms) | 15126.45 | 15086.69 | 16954.00 |
| Aggregate sessions/min | 3.95 | 3.89 | 3.57 |
| Median process CPU (seconds) | 16.97 | 16.29 | 18.29 |
| Sampled lifetime allocations, separate profile runs (GB) | 14.824 | 14.822 | 15.838 |

Writer hold includes COMMIT and excludes BEGIN wait. Append queue wait sums the preparation and mutation admissions belonging to each real append; it is not just the final write admission. Complete-pass throughput includes preparation, publication, cleanup and page reclamation. B lowers maximum cold hold about 93% and median p99 queue wait about 91%. Throughput is 8–9% lower and CPU 8–12% higher, within the declared threshold. Commit latency dominates B's longest holds; its largest native-SQL unit is 14.92 ms.

Separate instrumented A/A/B runs captured 28 allocation and CPU profiles per arm, with files verified for every observed transaction thread before teardown. Allocation sampling includes collected objects and startup/warm-up; these are allocated-byte estimates, not retained heap or latency measurements. B allocates about 7% more. Cold-owner CPU samples total 1.72 / 1.79 / 1.45 seconds; total process CPU still rises because separately admitted units add commit/admission work.

The earlier 128-row candidate was rejected: it reduced holds but increased median CPU 23% against A2. The 256-row ceiling roughly halves cleanup transaction count while preserving short native-SQL units. Its complete results remain retained alongside the accepted series.

<details>
<summary>All five samples per arm</summary>

| Arm | Max cold hold per pass (ms) | Complete pass (ms) | Per-pass p99 append queue wait (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | 1432.5, 1515.3, 1439.8, 1439.7, 1517.6 | 14192.4, 16256.0, 15126.4, 14910.3, 15511.1 | 1929, 2390, 1987, 2174, 2018 |
| A2 | 1477.5, 1401.9, 1444.1, 1418.7, 1505.6 | 16076.1, 13634.1, 14500.8, 15086.7, 17823.2 | 2153, 1949, 1980, 2053, 2005 |
| B | 82.8, 80.7, 93.6, 103.9, 84.9 | 17025.5, 16883.4, 16954.0, 17318.0, 15757.9 | 167, 171, 183, 182, 160 |

At five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum. No samples were discarded.
</details>

## Correctness and validation

The navigation regression fails on pinned main (eight unbounded updates instead of the bounded update, with untouched rows required to retain their exact payloads). Statement-attribution regression cases also fail on main. Tests cover interrupted navigation and FTS cleanup, restart with no FTS rows remaining, atomic rollback, exact restoration after partial cleanup, embedded-chunk recovery, foreground admission between units, and idle read-only maintenance.

Local proof is green: 66 focused backend tests (cold storage, crash recovery, admission, search worker, and native-SQL diagnostics), 17 affected Control UI browser tests, 4 transcript-search UI e2e tests, `pnpm check:changed --base ea94eb3bd38e2`, changed-script lint/format, and `git diff --check`. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean on the final staged implementation and profiling fix. The frozen-target follow-up at `419235050498c31ba7f24e576212c431ea36626b` also passes 32 consumer tests, the tooling test typecheck, shell syntax, `pnpm check:changed --base 1268ef13`, and scoped-clean Codex review through P2. It changes no runtime storage code, so the A/A/B and affected UI proof remain applicable. Hosted CI and ClawSweeper must qualify the exact final head before landing.

## Limits and implementation cost

Foreground restoration remains one atomic transaction and can still be long. File verification remains inside archive publication; statement attribution now exposes that application cost separately. Archive preparation still holds a long read snapshot, and recovery discovery can scan completed cold navigation rows outside writer admission; this PR does not claim to bound every read or every filesystem delay. Existing primary keys support the bounded write ranges, so no index proposal is required for this fix.

Production TypeScript delta against main is +309 lines, including the original PR's implementation. Growth implements the shared bounded cleanup operation, recovery selection and admission flow; extraction of the existing mutation adapter into its own file is mechanical. There is no second state owner or durable cleanup queue.

Reproduction uses the committed scripts (all directories must be new synthetic paths):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-cold-writer.mjs --prepare --state-dir <seed>
node scripts/perf/session-cold-writer-padding.mjs <seed> 2400
# Clone the closed seed for each run. Add --source-root <pinned-main> for A1/A2.
NODE_OPTIONS=--import=./scripts/perf/session-cold-writer-observer.mjs node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-cold-writer.mjs --state-dir <copy> --flow --appends 100
# Separate instrumented A/A/B runs: existing output directory, all-thread CPU/allocation profiles.
OPENCLAW_COLD_WRITER_PROFILE_DIR=<profiles> NODE_OPTIONS=--import=./scripts/perf/session-cold-writer-observer.mjs node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-cold-writer.mjs --state-dir <copy> --flow --appends 100
```

Existing-data compatibility: pre-fix main `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110` created and archived two synthetic sessions with 3,000 events. The candidate restored those persisted archives with an identical SHA-256 over transcript bytes, navigation, metadata and search rows, and unchanged settings. Additional running-Gateway and stable-to-candidate state-upgrade proof is recorded below. Frozen-target detection now accepts both old and bounded navigation call shapes, preserving the legacy archival distinction from #190716; both Docker consumers have red-before/green-after regression cases.

### Running Gateway and stable-data upgrade

Built exact head `419235050498c31ba7f24e576212c431ea36626b` with `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`. An isolated running Gateway received `sessions.storage.run` and concurrent `chat.inject` RPCs: **10,003 events / 45,272,371 bytes archived, 122 foreground appends completed, 27 appends completed between the archived session’s 82 cold write transactions**. Observer classification was restricted to the archived session ID so foreground FTS inserts were not counted as cold work. Subsequent RPC restoration preserved every original transcript byte and timestamp. This is product-boundary correctness/interleaving proof, not another latency benchmark.

The published **2026.11.5** Gateway imported synthetic sessions, archived two of them in its older archive format, and retained disabled cold-storage settings with the seven-day policy. After a clean stop, the candidate Gateway started on that same state, served all histories, and restored both archives through `chat.inject`; all nine original events and timestamps and the selected configuration sections survived exactly. Both Gateways stopped cleanly. This tests the persisted-state upgrade through a binary switch, not the package updater itself.

Main’s package version is 2026.11.4, behind the published baseline. The initial direct start correctly refused a downgrade. For the proof only, a separate copy of the exact built artifact was relabeled to 2026.11.5 with the existing `stampFixtureVersion` helper used by `published-driver.mjs`; commit/build identity and compiled code were preserved. No downgrade override, source version change, release, or live-state access was used. The initial stable harness also correctly exposed the legacy no-hot-row archive dialect; the final verifier checks exact restored data rather than imposing current navigation layout on stable.

Sanitized proof output:
```json
{"gatewayRpc":true,"events":10003,"rawTranscriptBytes":45272371,"concurrentAppends":122,"appendCompletionsBetweenColdTransactions":27,"coldTransactions":82,"exactRestoration":true}
{"baseline":"2026.11.5","candidate":"419235050498c31ba7f24e576212c431ea36626b","settingsUnchanged":true,"archivedSessionsRestored":2,"originalTranscriptEventsPreserved":9,"gatewayUpgradePassed":true}
```

prs.title: improve(ui): polish rail and sidebar navigation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several rough edges remained after the section sidebars: the pages menu did not show where you are, Sessions sat in the pages menu, phone headers differed from desktop, Plugins and Skills grabbed focus, dashboards had no author, and a chat opened after a page without a sidebar kept the Dashboards list.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled full release validation stops during frozen-source admission before its validation jobs can run. The trusted sparse checkout omits the current bundle-MCP client, which admission reads with lazy Git fetching disabled.

## User Impact

Restores the scheduled validation preflight. No runtime behavior or admission policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Include the single required client file in the existing trusted sparse checkout. The regression applies the actual workflow's sparse patterns to a filtered local clone, runs the admission entry point, and checks that the committed client identity was read.

## Evidence

- [Failed nightly child](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44179969185/job/134381376091): `frozen admission: unable to read selected source (cat-file)`.
- An isolated source-object fixture reproduces that error when the client blob is absent. Adding only that blob makes the same admission request pass.
- The failing revision and the frozen repair base have identical admission owners, checkout configuration, and client blob.
- The committed regression fails on the baseline with that exact error (9.07s) and passes with the fix (7.00s).
- Workflow checks, targeted type-aware lint, the tooling test typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh full-owner independent review found no actionable issues.
- Full nightly validation is not rerun; ordinary exact-head PR CI remains required.

prs.title: feat(ui): replace the Automations table with its sidebar and Run history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An open automation was hard to follow: choosing another one in the sidebar only moved the highlight, a linked automation was never marked, the detail header showed raw cron, a failed automation opened on its history, one-day intervals read "Every 1 day", and the sidebar read only the first 200 automations while the page hides its own list beside it.

## User Impact

Choosing an automation in the sidebar opens it and marks it; Automations always starts over when chosen again; the detail header reads the cadence ("Daily · Next in 10h") and the description as a subtitle; automations open on Settings with the failure in the banner and a Review run link; whole hours, days and weeks read Hourly, Daily and Weekly; the sidebar lists every automation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixes and polish on top of the Automations sidebar. The page records the open automation as section memory and the sidebar marks what the page has open, instead of keeping its own highlight.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock at the end of the series, so the after image can show later parts too.

An open automation before and after (left: main, right: after):

![An open automation before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7f1874e-d6cb-44fc-816c-df35b3cdf8bc)

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes at this PR's head.
- The unit tests of the files this PR touches pass at its head; the full UI unit suite passes at the end of the series (one failure also on main: a Workboard German relative-time string, "vor 1min", from the local ICU).
- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.


## Update: Automations table removed

The Automations page no longer has a table. The list lives only in the sidebar, whose header filter already carries the table's filters; the page shows the open automation or an empty state.
- A "Run history" row under "New automation" opens every automation's runs (`?activity`), the old table's Activity tab.
- The iPad app opens /automations with no web sidebar, so in the native embed the page renders the sidebar's own list.
- Gone with the table: its search, tabs, row controls, starter suggestions, the manual Refresh button and the `?session=` filtered view (nothing links to it). Failed reads show Retry in the empty state.
- E2E tests reach automations through the sidebar; 18 cron e2e files pass at this head. Tests that only covered the table were deleted.

Side rail series, part 13 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199833; review only this PR's commits.


## Update: e2e repair

The full Control UI e2e run on the stack found tests this PR broke or product gaps it introduced; this PR now carries their fixes:
- feat(ui): offer the Automations table's filters in the Automations sidebar filter
- test(ui): expect cadence words in the automation detail header e2e
- test(ui): open a failed automation on its settings in the attention e2e

Moved to an earlier PR or folded into another commit:
- fix(ui): switch between automations from the Automations sidebar




## Update: no sidebar without an automation

With no automation in the agent's scope, Automations now shows only the rail beside its "No automations yet" empty state and its New automation button; the sidebar (with New automation and Run history) returns once an automation exists. An agent picked in the sidebar's filter keeps the sidebar, so the filter stays reachable.

- feat(ui): show only the rail beside Automations without an automation
- New `cron-filters` e2e case: no automation → `.shell--nav-page-hidden` and no visible sidebar; it fails without the shell rule.
- Tests that opened Run history or New automation from the sidebar without an automation now use `?activity` or the empty state's button; `cron-select-values` gets one automation so it keeps using the sidebar. The rail-peek instant-open case now opens People.
- All 21 Automations/sidebar e2e files pass at this head (81 tests).

## Maintainer verification

The compact sidebar inventory now keeps read failures visible and retries the same inventory owner. The native embedded list exposes the existing shared filters again, with the same options and state, and uses the existing loading boundary. Regression checks reproduce the failures before the fix and verify retry, filtering, reset and focus afterward. Removed unused sidebar-reporting wiring, the retired table's exported helper surface and fixtures, and two stale E2E inventory entries. Current main's deliberately retired transcript reader stays removed; run history remains. The integrated stack passed 558 unit/browser tests and 20 bundled E2E cases; the final cleanup additionally passed 38 shell/navigation/history tests, the permission-revocation case and the focused settings-header browser case. Independent reviews found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

Vyctor approved the measured JavaScript byte cost for this navigation stack. These cumulative measurements compare this layer with paired main base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`. Each cap equals the original main cap plus the measured delta, preserving existing headroom without adding another margin.

| Metric | Cumulative gzip delta | Cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest JS asset | +3,615 B | 576,055 B |
| Chat boot JS | +4,128 B | 1,329,708 B |
| New Session boot JS | +3,997 B | 820,629 B |

CSS ceilings, request counts, startup ceilings and gate logic are unchanged. Byte measurements are delivery-size evidence, not latency measurements.

<!-- navigation-landing-review:start -->
### Maintainer validation

Reviewed and rebased this layer on predecessor `3a0ca90b383a2f7fd6d55529f968053231aacf87`; current head is `bb451408b1fc810c9d6c719edf0aa10087e7eecc`. The own-layer tree, original human authors and signatures were checked. UI typechecking passed on this candidate. Previously verified functional and integrated visual proof was reused where inputs are unchanged; the maintainer also exercised the integrated stack on a real Gateway.

The section-location comparison now uses the existing signal updater instead of a separate untracked read. The controller guard and 45 existing owner cases passed.

The maintainer authorized sequential CI bypass after repairing known PR-caused failures. Hosted CI may still be running; this is not a claim of full hosted CI success. The unrelated owner-approval timing failure is tracked separately in #200810.
