prs.title: fix(codex): doctor --fix removes an appServer.command that points into a missing plugin generation
prs.body:
Related: #181037
Complementary prevention (merged): #191693

## What Problem This Solves

Recovery only: older cleanup versions may already have deleted the managed Codex generation referenced by `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command`. The merged prevention fix #191693 keeps configured generations on disk, but cannot restore files already deleted.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then restart the Gateway. Doctor removes only the stale command override so normal managed binary selection resumes (or `OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN` applies). This may select a newer Codex binary. Other app-server settings, including arguments, remain unchanged. Plain Doctor previews the repair through its existing normalization flow.

Existing generation pins, unrelated custom executables, and non-missing filesystem errors remain untouched. No runtime fallback or cleanup changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the repair with the Codex plugin's existing Doctor normalizer. Recognize only the historical `openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-<16 lowercase hex>` directory layout beneath the state directory's `npm/projects`, and remove the override only when the generation stat returns `ENOENT` or `ENOTDIR`.

The historical name is deliberately frozen recovery data, not a second implementation of future install naming. This removes the hash-helper dependency, duplicate containment check, and nested exception scaffolding without adding SDK surface or state. Tests use an independent historical fixture and consolidate repeated setup and assertions.

Limits: no recovery of arbitrary custom paths, pinned non-default npm roots, relative command paths, external state-directory symlink aliases, or missing binaries inside an otherwise existing generation. No claim that updating alone applies this unpublished plugin repair; direct Doctor recovery is the supported scope.

## Evidence

- Simplified head: `090cc4fea9b5`; original contributor head: `5e9100d477b2`.
- Credential-free Linux ARM64 container, Node 24.22.1, frozen dependency install; no host state or credentials mounted. Tests ran with networking disconnected.
- Focused recovery and sibling Doctor suites: **60/60 passed**, two Vitest shards in 129.43s. After cleaning leftover source files from the reused image, the recovery suite was rerun: **21/21 passed**, 66.96s wrapper / 61.51s Vitest, dominated by compilation. The subsequent final change only adds required braces to a test conditional and adjusts its line allocation.
- Both primary recovery cases fail on pre-fix `c147613091ca` because the command remains configured; they pass with the repair.
- Targeted production/test TypeScript check passed using the repository test config with the two touched files as roots. Targeted source-backed lint: zero warnings/errors (23.4s). Pinned formatting, pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review: no P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed the full `c147613091ca..be697c268f72` range: no correctness/security findings. Final delta since that review is only the test braces and 122→124 line allocation; no production changes.
- Initial package-boundary validation encountered stale source files in the reused image; these were removed before the final focused checks. No successful full repository build is claimed.
- No new live Doctor/Gateway/model/channel or latest-stable updater run was performed. The contributor's earlier live evidence below is prior-head evidence, not a claim of current-head execution. Hosted CI is pending the push.

Compared with the original revision: production additions 62 → 44; regression test lines 394 → 124. The 124-line test allocation covers missing-generation recovery, managed selection, idempotency, preservation of settings and working pins, custom-path boundaries, symlinks, and filesystem-error distinctions.

**Live run on the current head: stable 2026.11.3 writes the state, `4087062` repairs it** (2026-11-14; Linux x64, Node 24.22.1). Added after the hosted review of `4087062da5d5`; the bullet above saying that no new live run was performed and that hosted CI was pending predates this run, and hosted CI on `4087062` has since passed (`ci-gate`). `4087062` merges main at `928c118f64db` into `090cc4fea9b5`; the four files of this PR are byte-identical in both. `openclaw@2026.11.3` was npm's latest stable release at each recorded checkpoint (`npm view openclaw dist-tags` reported latest 2026.11.3 when the sign-in window opened and at the end of the run). This head also identifies as 2026.11.3 (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (4087062)`), so the two builds differ by commit, not by version string. The candidate was a fresh clone of `4087062` (fetched by commit id), installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and built with `pnpm build` in an isolated directory. Test-host adaptation: the host also runs an unrelated, older OpenClaw Gateway as a system service under another account, and because of it this head's installed-service check refused to migrate the isolated state; every command of this head in this run, including its Gateway, therefore set `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT=openclaw-gateway-r5p-absent.service`, a unit that does not exist, so that check did not consider that service. That service was not changed, and the setting is unrelated to the Doctor repair under test. One isolated `HOME`, so the state directory is `<home>/.openclaw`; the Gateway listened on loopback with token auth; one real OpenAI OAuth sign-in (device code); the Telegram turns came from a self-created test bot in a private chat, with plain-text messages sent by hand; the CLI turns used `openclaw agent` through the Gateway, not `--local`. Redacted output is in the collapsed block below.

- **Stable writes the state.** `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> openclaw@2026.11.3 --allow-scripts=openclaw` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)`), then `openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3 --accept-capabilities`, which installed a flat managed project. The stable CLI wrote the Gateway, Telegram, tool-policy, and agent-runtime settings and the `appServer` keys `transport: "stdio"`, `homeScope: "agent"`, `mode: "guardian"`, `sandbox: "read-only"`, `approvalPolicy: "on-request"`, `requestTimeoutMs`, and `args`. At this point neither the stable CLI nor the plugin install had written `appServer.command` or `plugins.load.paths`.
- **Stable works before the stale override.** After sign-in, with the stable Gateway running, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli` asked the model to remember the code word `cw-9235c2ad` and returned `CLI-PRE-OK`. After Telegram pairing, a message asking the bot to remember `tg-ab3117bc` was answered with `TG-PRE-OK`.
- **The stale override.** The Gateway was stopped, and the stable CLI set `appServer.command` to `<home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex`. The path was written by hand, not left behind by an update or a cleanup, and no directory existed at it while the stable build ran.
- **Before (stable 2026.11.3).** `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` keep the command: the preview listed no removal and left the config file byte-identical, and both runs printed core Doctor's existing custom-command warning (`Custom Codex app-server command bypasses OpenClaw's managed exact-version binary.`); `--fix` applied stable Doctor's own repairs (its output reports the agent roster, the `openai/gpt-6-astra` model entry, two session titles, a plugin-registry refresh, the OAuth directory, and three disabled skills, with two `Updated config` writes) and left `appServer.command` and the other `appServer` keys unchanged. With the stable Gateway running again, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli-stable` exits 1 with `Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex or its working directory was not found`. A Telegram message asking for `STABLE-OK` got no reply within 3 minutes, and the Gateway logged `[telegram] dispatch failed: CodexAppServerSpawnError: Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/…`, then `spooled update <id> failed; keeping for retry`.
- **Which Codex plugin this head ran.** Two Codex plugins with the same version were present: the npm-installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3` in the state, which does not contain the removal message, and the copy bundled with this head's build at `<src>/dist/extensions/codex`. In a source checkout, a compiled bundled plugin under `dist/extensions` ranks ahead of a same-id npm install regardless of version; only a `plugins.load.paths` selection ranks higher (`resolveDuplicatePrecedenceRank`, `src/plugins/manifest-registry-build.ts:151-183`, compared at `:455-470`). Observed in this run: after the hand-off, this head's `openclaw plugins inspect codex --json` reported `plugin.origin` `bundled` and `plugin.rootDir` `<src>/dist/extensions/codex`, with the npm copy listed only under `diagnostics`; Doctor printed `Kept bundled plugin "codex" from the OpenClaw source build; …`, and the CLI warned `duplicate plugin id detected; global plugin will be overridden by bundled plugin (<src>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js)`; the Gateway on this build logged `duplicate plugin id detected; global plugin will be overridden by bundled plugin (<src>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js)`; and the removal message appears in this build's copy but in no file of the npm copy.
- **After (this head, same state).** The stable Gateway was stopped, an empty directory was created at the seeded generation path, and the same `HOME` was handed to this head's build.
  - First repair, generation present: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` ran this build's pending database migrations (state database v23–v40, listed under "Doctor changes"; agent database schema v27 -> v42; pre-migration SQLite backups saved under `<home>/.openclaw/state/` and `<home>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/`) and kept `appServer.command`, since the generation directory existed; the `appServer` subtree was byte-identical. Config changes in this run: none (the config diff was empty).
  - The empty generation directory was then removed by hand, standing in for an older cleanup that deleted it.
  - Preview: `openclaw doctor` lists `Removed plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command; it pointed into an OpenClaw-managed Codex plugin generation that no longer exists. …` as a pending change and leaves the config file byte-identical.
  - Repair: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` writes it. The only `appServer` change is the removed `command`; all config changes in this run: `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command` removed, `meta.migrations.skillLibraryToolSplit` and `meta.migrations.skillWorkshopPlugin` added, and `wizard.lastRunAt` updated by Doctor's run metadata.
  - Restart: the Gateway started on this build; the Codex app-server line was `Codex app-server: using bundled 0.164.0 (no codex on PATH)`.
  - Turns: in the same CLI session, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli` asked for the code word and returned `cw-9235c2ad`. In the same Telegram chat, the stable-phase message that the stable Gateway had kept for retry was answered with `STABLE-OK` after the hand-off (22:09 +09:00 in the Telegram client), before the follow-up was sent and with no other message sent to the bot in between; the follow-up was then answered with `tg-ab3117bc` (about 9 s after the Gateway received the message); no spawn error was logged after either reply.
- **Preview before migration.** On a separate state written by 2026.11.3 with the same kind of command and no directory, this build's `openclaw doctor` and `doctor --lint` exited 1 because the state-database migration had not run yet (`OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; …`, `… Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix.`), `doctor --json` reported `ok: false` with the pending migrations, and none of them listed the removal; `doctor --fix --yes` ran the migrations and removed the command in the same run. So the first Doctor command after the hand-off above was `doctor --fix --yes`, and the preview ran after it. The migration step is not part of this change.
- **Existing data still loads and works (data-model compatibility).** This head first upgraded the stored data (state database v23–v40; the agent database, which holds the sessions and the auth profile, schema v27 -> v42) and then used the state written by 2026.11.3 without a new sign-in, pairing code, or token: the CLI connected with the stored Gateway token. The CLI session and the Telegram chat that 2026.11.3 wrote before the hand-off were continued after the repair, and the code words given there were answered (above); the Telegram update that the stable Gateway had spooled for retry was processed and answered by this head after the hand-off. After the Gateway stopped, this head's `openclaw models auth list --provider openai --json` showed the one OpenAI profile from the stable-phase sign-in (OAuth, not expired), `openclaw pairing list telegram` showed no pending request, and `openclaw sessions --json` listed the two CLI sessions (`r5p-cli`, `r5p-cli-stable`) and the Telegram session. The npm-installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3` was left in place: the `npm/projects` listing was identical before and after this head's Doctor runs, and Doctor did not remove the install record.

Focused tests on `c147613091ca` (Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, Vitest on Node), `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`:

- New `extensions/codex/doctor-contract-api.stale-app-server-command.test.ts`. It removes a command under a missing Codex generation (plain, `~` and `..` spellings, a dangling generation symlink, `ENOTDIR`, and together with another legacy-key repair); the removal keeps the other `appServer` keys, does not mutate the input, is idempotent, and the repaired config resolves to managed command selection. - `autoreview` (Codex, local mode against `c147613091ca`, priorities P0–P2): scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.95)", no accepted or actionable findings.
- Not run: `pnpm test:contracts:plugins` and `pnpm test:contracts:channels`, since no shared plugin or channel interface changed.

**Not covered:**

- **Writer.** The step that wrote the override in the reported update is not identified. A full-text search of every file in these scopes found no code that writes `appServer.command`: non-test `extensions/codex/**` sources at v2026.10.10-beta.1, v2026.10.10-beta.3, and main; at beta.1 and beta.3, `src/cli/update-cli/**`, `src/commands/doctor/**`, `src/infra/update*`, `src/flows/doctor*`, `src/system-agent/**`, `src/**` files with `codex` in the name, and filename-selected files in `src/plugins/**` and `src/config/**`. - **Same update.** The repair does not apply during the update that retires the generation: that update's Doctor passes run before the Gateway restarts, while the retired generation is still on disk (the pass before plugin convergence also defers plugin-owned config repair), and the cleanup deletes it only after the restart. It is expected to apply on the next `openclaw doctor --fix` after that cleanup (the same-state run under **Evidence** shows this with the bundled plugin), or in a later update's post-plugin Doctor pass once the Codex plugin's pending data/settings upgrade completes (not exercised).
- **Other shapes.** Flat or non-generation project layouts under the npm root are not matched. `OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN` pointing into a removed generation is not changed; it is an environment variable, not config.
- **Live proof (2026-10-30, head `5e9100d`).** No passing published-driver × candidate cell: upstream's cell (`scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/published-driver.mjs`) updates to the candidate root package, which excludes `dist/extensions/codex/**`, and its config sets `plugins: { enabled: false }` with no `plugins.entries.codex`, so there is no `appServer.command` for this plugin's Doctor normalizer to repair there, and `scripts/lib/ci-published-driver-update-plan.mts` does not schedule it for pull requests. The update succeeded and `appServer.command` was kept. The Doctor run before plugin convergence deferred the Codex plugin's config repair (`shouldDeferConfiguredPluginInstallRepair`; the update output reported `Plugin "codex" data/settings upgrade is unfinished: Package convergence must wait until the updating parent releases its install records. Your existing data and settings have been kept. …`); the update's plugin step then replaced this head's 2026.10.7 with the published 2026.10.9 (`Repaired plugin "codex".`), which does not contain this change; and the `post-plugin doctor` step that followed exited 0 with the command still in place. So this adapted run did not exercise the repair from an unpublished Codex plugin during an update. The upgrade evidence above is the same-state sequence instead: the stable CLI installed from npm wrote the state, and a source build of this head took it over, not `openclaw update`. Only the Codex plugin bundled with this head's source build was exercised (`plugins inspect codex`: origin bundled, `<worktree>/dist/extensions/codex`; Doctor printed `Kept bundled plugin "codex" from the OpenClaw source build` and the Gateway skipped the npm-installed 2026.10.8 copy (`plugin requires plugin API >=2026.10.8`), which does not contain the removal message); the npm-packed form of the candidate `@openclaw/codex` was not exercised in that sequence. The generation lifecycle was simulated by hand: the missing generation path was written into config by hand; no directory existed at it during the stable phase; an empty directory was created there before the hand-off, standing in for an old generation still on disk after an update, and it was removed after the first repair, standing in for the retained-generation cleanup. None of this came from an update rotation, and the reported beta.1 → beta.3 sequence was not reproduced. The Telegram turns used a self-created test bot in a private chat (BotFather Threaded Mode on), with plain-text messages sent by hand rather than through the `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill, which drives a leased Telegram Test Server user; the CLI turns used `openclaw agent` through the Gateway, not `--local`. The current-head run under **Evidence** does not depend on `openclaw update` or on the adapted run above: it is the same-state hand-off from an npm-installed 2026.11.3 to a source build of `4087062`.
- **Preview before migration.** On the state written by 2026.10.8, this build's `openclaw doctor`, `doctor --json` and `doctor --lint` reported the pending state-database migration (`state database schema migration pending`) and did not list the `appServer.command` removal; `doctor --fix --yes` ran the migration. So the first Doctor command after the hand-off was `doctor --fix --yes`, and the preview above ran after it. The migration step is not part of this change.

**Open question:** should the update that retires a generation also prevent this first failure? That would mean treating a generation that is retired but still on disk as stale. Possible owners are core's retained-generation cleanup or the update-time Doctor; this PR does not choose between them.

prs.title: fix: make a newly installed Gateway available in the terminal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After installing a native Gateway, opening a terminal and running `openclaw` can fail to find the command or use a different profile. A fresh named-profile macOS installation also leaves its bundled command out of the shell's search path.

## Intended User Impact

A fresh installation should establish a discoverable, profile-bound terminal command. Later installations must preserve the established default and operator-managed launchers, including configured profiles whose Gateways are offline. Explicit profile arguments and environment overrides remain supported. No existing state is migrated and no running Gateway or app is restarted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Install the terminal launcher only after successful service installation, and let fresh bundled named-profile installations establish the default when no selection exists. Preserve first-install ownership rather than switching defaults based on live reachability or the app's current selection. Existing selections should receive a contextual command instead of being silently replaced.

prs.title: fix: show provider usage for model API key SecretRefs
prs.body:
Closes #150173

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw status --usage` and Gateway `usage.status` can omit a provider when its configured model API key is a SecretRef. A failed credential lookup could also interrupt the entire CLI status report.

## User Impact

Operators can see usage with their existing SecretRefs. If one lookup fails, status keeps reporting available usage and includes a diagnostic without the resolver’s raw error. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI status resolves only the configured provider API keys within its existing time budget, keeping the original config available for fallback. Uncertain subprocess cleanup still stops the command. Managed Gateway usage continues to check the captured credential owner at request time.

Thanks to @alex-strattab for the report, @Samay10 for the original investigation in #150192, and @meska for the Z.AI store report.

## Evidence

- On Node 24.22.1, all **74 tests across six files** passed (70.37 seconds across three repository test shards). The new regression failed before the fallback change and passes now; it also verifies that uncertain cleanup still fails the command. Online JSON coverage verifies that scan and usage diagnostics both reach the output.
- Core and command/infra test typechecks, scoped lint and formatting, test-line/timeout/mock guards, the unified runtime build, and the CLI bootstrap import guard passed. The test allocation is exactly 275 net lines for the credential, deadline, cleanup, and output regressions; it uses the upstream budget restored by #196432.
- Independent source review verified the follow-up. Earlier built loopback evidence for [CLI and Gateway usage and the deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187360#issuecomment-6489445493) and [managed credential checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187360#issuecomment-6490298252) remains scoped to the revisions recorded there. Callers that already hold independently resolved plaintext config remain outside the managed snapshot’s revocation guarantee.
- Hosted CI and maintainer review for this head are separate from the local checks.

### Built CLI fallback proof

Node 24.22.1, repository `cliStartup` build, head `ee435a893be7652c4f41c04e86b3f5ebd8423ab5`. The CLI command was `openclaw status --usage --agent main --json` with an isolated config and synthetic credentials.

The missing-env case leaves a configured environment SecretRef unset. A separate loopback Gateway protocol fixture returns a malformed `secrets.resolve` reply to exercise the preparation-error fallback in online JSON (`collection.source=gateway`, `gateway.reachable=true`). The real CLI emits the generic diagnostic and retains healthy OpenRouter usage from two native loopback HTTP requests. The raw resolver error and fixture credentials are absent from CLI output.

```text
malformed-response exit=0 secrets.resolve=1 diagnostics=1 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
missing-secret exit=0 secrets.resolve=1 diagnostics=2 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
healthy-control exit=0 secrets.resolve=0 diagnostics=0 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
```

These three product CLI cases passed locally. A subsequent Node 24.22.1 rerun compiled and verified the full test fixture graph and passed all 72 cases across five files in three repository Vitest shards. The same 72 cases and the required checks passed in hosted CI for this head.

AI-assisted implementation and verification.

prs.title: fix: preserve gateway administrator permissions across native UI clients
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An authenticated native-app administrator could receive caller-scoped automation inventory and “not found” for another conversation’s job, despite holding Gateway admin authority. The invariant is **same authenticated administrator, same effective scopes and policy, same Gateway permissions**, regardless of Control UI or native UI client. Rendering features remain separate.

## User Impact

User impact: native UI administrators can inspect and repair existing automations across conversations with the same effective scopes and policy as browser administrators. Caller-only caps, requester isolation, and live revocation remain enforced. The [maintainer direction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194443#issuecomment-6935746079) endorses native UI administrator parity; security approval is evaluated separately for each head.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse shared authenticated UI-admin classification for fresh-turn automation admission and durable recovery, without labeling native clients as Control UI or granting direct-local execution.
- Retain recorded automation-admin delegation across scheduled recovery and repair/notice continuations. Legacy browser grants remain compatible; historical native snapshots without recorded delegation are not upgraded.
- Preserve scope intersections, principal-only snapshot contracts, exact-device reconnect custody, requester identity, and the existing authorization gates for provider-review acknowledgment, dashboard reads, task suggestions, and signed-in mentions.
- Retain deployment caller caps, tool policy, fresh/direct-turn and exact-run binding, and live authority/revocation checks through the final effect. Browser origin checks and transport-specific rendering remain separate.

## Evidence

### Current selected-CI-planner repair — November 17, 2026

Current head: `0c556757a1f98d9ea265d3612b2d833cdf086c3f`, parent `c9258372212581d58b3454b9c4911a02fe1365c9`. The integrated-main baseline remains `2b9b23b9f3afbd8ebb233c097e13b847df0b73a3`; no additional main refresh or ancestry rewrite was performed.

The selected plugin-reload child already had a two-worker limit but retained the full row’s redundant two-worker job default. Exact environment comparison then stranded it from compatible serial work. The existing one-job, 32-class, serial, shortest-60-minute, exact-target-scope contract is deliberate and remains unchanged; no policy decision or weaker assertion was needed.
- The **12-line owning-producer repair** drops that default from the selected projection only when **every retained child explicitly pins an equal or narrower limit**. This respects the executor’s `min(job, child)` intersection: a job cap above an unpinned or wider child remains authoritative. Other environment values, process boundaries, worker limits, memory floors, timing identities, prices, capacity rules, and deadlines are preserved. Native authorization production code and both recovery test registrations are unchanged.

- **Red/green proof:** the original actual CI merge `2bda603d…` fails while its exact main parent passes. Applying the final repair makes that same merge’s serial-sharing regression pass under the checksum-pinned Bun fork. Candidate-snapshot checks pass **220 planner/selection/command tests across four files**, plus the executor worker-ceiling case; the tooling caller type graph and both targeted lint groups pass. Final formatting and test budget pass. These are batched snapshot checks, not a single all-green command or remotely executed new-commit-SHA claim. The three checked Git blobs exactly match this signed commit.
- [Guarded snapshot validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d7cb1bf17ca776b7bda0b6db662bdb12) retains an initial formatter-only failure after the tests/types/lint passed. No failure was hidden or converted into a waiver.
- Fresh independent **canonical autoreview, Codex, P0–P2: scoped-clean**, with the full planner, caller, capacity, and actual executor contracts supplied. Simplification keeps one projection owner and removes stale derived policy rather than adding another scheduler or compatibility layer.

```text
21:21:47 [model-fallback/decision] stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted

```

prs.title: feat(ui): name the Users section People and add remote access
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Users section mixes navigation and people without separation, and OpenClaw ID remote access is only reachable from the pages menu.

## User Impact

The section is named People; Remote access (OpenClaw ID) sits under Activity with the same visibility it had before; an ONLINE or USERS heading separates the people list.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves the existing remote access page into the section without changing who can see it.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock at the end of the series, so the after image can show later parts too.

Activity and the People sidebar before and after (left: main, right: after):

![Activity and the People sidebar before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e2c4ba6-15f4-44c5-9be5-3672d7b0bebf)

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes at this PR's head.
- The unit tests of the files this PR touches pass at its head; the full UI unit suite passes at the end of the series (one failure also on main: a Workboard German relative-time string, "vor 1min", from the local ICU).
- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.

Side rail series, part 9 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199829; review only this PR's commits.

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

Vyctor approved the measured JavaScript byte cost for this navigation stack. These cumulative measurements compare this layer with paired main base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`. Each cap equals the original main cap plus the measured delta, preserving existing headroom without adding another margin.

| Metric | Cumulative gzip delta | Cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest JS asset | +3,023 B | 575,463 B |
| Chat boot JS | +3,410 B | 1,328,990 B |
| New Session boot JS | +3,402 B | 820,034 B |

CSS ceilings, request counts, startup ceilings and gate logic are unchanged. Byte measurements are delivery-size evidence, not latency measurements.

<!-- navigation-landing-review:start -->
### Maintainer validation

Reviewed and rebased this layer on predecessor `f9b458f86684ee81006e67ab609cfb827a80c8aa`; current head is `6936e2314c3fc7a3d8e735a07518886bc811509c`. The own-layer tree, original human authors and signatures were checked. UI typechecking passed on this candidate. Previously verified functional and integrated visual proof was reused where inputs are unchanged; the maintainer also exercised the integrated stack on a real Gateway.



The maintainer authorized sequential CI bypass after repairing known PR-caused failures. Hosted CI may still be running; this is not a claim of full hosted CI success. The unrelated owner-approval timing failure is tracked separately in #200810.

prs.title: improve: explain package baseline drift during updates
prs.body:
Related: #200756

## What Problem This Solves

A Windows beta.2 → beta.4 update can pass candidate validation and then refuse package replacement with only “Baseline package scan failed | Package rollback tree changed during verification.” The report does not identify the entry or stat fields needed to investigate the refusal.

The original Windows mutation remains unidentified. This PR adds necessary diagnostics; it does not claim that the reported update now succeeds.

## User Impact

Local failure output and `openclaw update status --json` diagnostics retain the first mismatching package-relative entry, changed stat field names, and primitive before/after values. An unavailable original inode instead reports the entry and `ino=0`, including when both observations have zero inode. Equal values are not described as changed fields.

Public failure reports retain only closed field-name or unavailable-inode classifications, without the entry, installation path, or values. Existing status text bounds still apply. The integrity decision and refusal remain unchanged. This change must be present in the installed updater; staging a newer candidate cannot change an older updater’s scan.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing inspection already has the stat observations. One private error formatter now serves initial inode inspection and the final rescan through `PackageIntegrityMismatchError`, existing local diagnostics, failure facts, and the public redaction owner. There is no additional scan, retry, schema, or protocol.

Comparisons still cover `dev`, `ino`, `mode`, `uid`, `gid`, `nlink`, `size`, `mtimeNs`, and `ctimeNs`, with the original nonzero-inode requirement. Atime is not compared. The beta.2 tag source has the same refusal and comparison.

Pr-simplify retained one formatter because both inspection points need the same diagnosis. Against the original base, the change is +55 net production lines, +108 test lines, and +10 documentation lines; the repair delta adds +18, +33, and +2 respectively.

## Evidence

- On base `4764444d3c278e159117131eaffe10d290dba99b`, the real-temp-package drift regression still refused the controlled change but failed the diagnostic assertion with the opaque message. The unchanged control passed. The new initial zero-inode diagnostic also failed on prior head `e1e5488e7cb84da17fc7a33eb73408623d3b00be` for missing classification.
- All **147 tests passed** across the four named files below (41.58 seconds total wrapper wall time). The tests retain first-entry/value assertions and the unchanged nonzero control, and exercise zero inode at initial observation and both retained/current zero inode at final inspection. Local diagnostics name the private relative entry and zero inode; public reports retain the closed reason and omit the private entry. Existing multiple admitted hash, timeout, refusal-order, and settlement tests passed.
- The previous head’s [check-test-types-core-3 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44176773576/job/134373722748) reported TS2532. A real runtime assertion now narrows the observed failure step before reading its facts. Its exact `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json` type config **passes locally** under a 90-second timeout.
- Touched-file CI-core typed oxlint, format check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent local autoreview of the repair delta against `e1e5488e7cb84da17fc7a33eb73408623d3b00be`: **P0–P3, scoped-clean, no findings**. The reviewed bytes are commit `2a108a20a10398cf8d242059cc3f68d50223c175`; the reviewer used supplied source and proof without independently rerunning tests.

Limits: Linux diagnostic proof only. The zero-inode controls deliberately alter stat observations; they do not establish that Windows returned zero. No native Windows root-cause reproduction, published-driver upgrade success, or packaging/release validation is claimed. Broad proof and CI seconds await the new head’s CI. No attribution to atime, antivirus, or a particular writer.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/package-update-swap.integrity.test.ts \
  src/infra/package-update-integrity.test.ts \
  src/infra/package-update-swap.bounds.test.ts \
  src/logging/diagnostic-support-redaction.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

Reported by @DonnieFi.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix: stop listing chat attachments the Files panel can't open
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/gateway/server-methods/session-touched-files.ts:47` (`addTouchedFile`) recorded every `read` path as a workspace file, including `media://inbound/<id>`. The `read` tool opens that reference from the attachment store, but the Files panel resolved it under the workspace root (`<root>/media:/inbound/<id>`), so it listed an entry that always answered `session file not found`.

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent reads a file you uploaded to the chat, the session Files panel lists it a second time under **Session files**, with a missing marker. Clicking that entry shows "Couldn't open file / session file not found", even though the attachment is fine.

## User Impact

User impact: the Files panel no longer lists an attachment entry it can never open. The chat attachment entry itself is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The list of files a session touched now skips attachment-store references. It uses the check the `read` tool already uses to recognize them, so the panel and the tool agree. The listing, the relevance marks and the preview all read from that list. Nothing else is filtered: remote URLs, `data:` text, file URLs and filenames that contain a colon (such as `report:2026.txt` or `data:notes,2026.txt`) behave as before.

This builds on @li-y-w's first fix in this PR. Their commits stay on the branch. Their filter in `workspace-files.ts` is replaced by this narrower check where the list is built, which also settles the review finding about `data:` filenames that contain a comma. Their test file was removed on `main` (#162670), so the regression case now sits in `sessions-files.test.ts` with the other touched-file cases.

## Evidence

Real Control UI against an isolated Gateway (built `dist`) with a deterministic model fixture. A chat message carries an uploaded PNG, and the model calls `read` with the attachment's `media://inbound/<id>` reference.

- Before (`main` e5b1ad9f320d): Session files lists `fixture-photo---<id>.png` with a missing marker; clicking it shows `session file not found`. `sessions.files.list` returned `{"path":"media://inbound/fixture-photo---<id>.png","kind":"read","missing":true}`.
- After (this branch): Session files lists only the unchanged chat attachment entry `fixture-photo.png`; the broken row is gone.
- Focused test: the touched-file case with a `media://inbound/...` read fails on `main` (`expected length 3 but got 4`) and passes here (`sessions-files.test.ts`: 51 passed).

Screenshots (before/after, inspected): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151100#issuecomment-6960409763

Thanks @li-y-w for the report and the first fix.

No Control UI code changes, so the Control UI bundle size is unchanged.

Merge danger: two-way door. One read-side filter, no stored state or contract change. Blast radius: the Control UI Files panel only.

prs.title: fix: use collapse control in sidebar clearance tests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar clearance tests still click the selected Sessions/avatar control to collapse navigation. Since [#199824](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199824), that control opens the agent menu when Sessions is already expanded, so four clearance cases fail before checking their geometry.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The tests exercise the current navigation controls and continue checking collapsed-rail clearance and control reachability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the two obsolete toggle clicks with the existing dedicated sidebar collapse button. All collapse-class, geometry, focus, and reachability assertions remain unchanged; no production code, waits, or thresholds change.

## Evidence

- [Scheduled failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44179757082/job/134381749126): four collapsed-navigation cases expected `shell--nav-collapsed` after clicking the avatar.
- Unchanged local baseline reproduced all four failures; the expanded-navigation control passed (73.21 seconds).
- With the two action replacements, the entire file passes: **9/9 tests**, including mobile, attachment, stacked-tab, and focused-control coverage (18.31 seconds).
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh full-source review found no actionable P0–P3 issues.

Local browser proof used the qualified native dependency checkout with the 13 frozen navigation/icon owner files and this test overlaid from `ae6b903359e3d80a55c87794b3bfc04eb59119e7`; every overlay was restored afterward. This is bounded owner proof, not a claim that the entire current UI source graph ran locally. PR CI provides the broader exact-head check.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): keep quoted tool arguments parseable in exports
prs.body:
Related: #113709.

## What Problem This Solves

Trajectory JSON and JSONL exports can become malformed when quoted tool arguments contain token-like text, even though the export command reports success.

## User Impact

Diagnostic exports remain parseable while preserving default, configured-pattern and registered-secret masking, native-value serialization behavior and benign values. No configuration migration is required. Thanks to @nimarosa for isolating the escaped-quote case and @alfred429 for the installed-exporter report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final support-file pass uses the existing JSON scalar editor for JSON and JSONL; plaintext retains its existing path. Configured patterns keep their capture context and bounded scanning. Native-value origins remain with the serialization owner.

The current revision normally merges official main `1d72ad079047f85d881e521a03e67a86e17c5f3a` into author revision `0d024b2d259a3c1b6cb860872380f8d2b1ee2100` to address a named failing UI gate. All eleven introduced file blobs remain byte-identical to that author revision; this follow-up contains no manual product or test edits. The earlier configuration-form capability repair is now common with main and is no longer part of this PR's delta.

The Activity failure came from a stale contract: [the canonical session-visibility change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196446) replaced blanket denial of another person's Activity with filtering to sessions readable by the caller. A person without readable sessions therefore returns a successful empty list. The failing fixture created that person without a session but still expected the removed blanket-denial alert. [The upstream fixture retirement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197058), commit `d04c6ab44ad0694365727b6f5ef9e587970b2214`, removes that obsolete fixture and its matching 193-LF allocation while retaining other denial, retry, revocation and visibility coverage. This revision integrates that official fix.

## Evidence

Current author commit `4d91083e0fcda4d936d4c66631db3004f26823b0`, tree `98cd5deeb7549a510294b89b106c09af5b9b1d09`, has parents `0d024b2d259a3c1b6cb860872380f8d2b1ee2100` and `1d72ad079047f85d881e521a03e67a86e17c5f3a`. The tested and independently reviewed tree equals the committed tree. Actual branch prerequisites are Node **24.22.1**, pnpm **12.15.0** and the repository's pinned Bun test runner.

- **Original failed entry point:** an unchanged-source warm-cache run on the old actual CI merge `f960d37374b0baa37be93d5dd48739a81bb09936` reproduces the original Activity locator timeout at line 137. The wrapper took **219.738 seconds**. A separate first cold run exhausted the existing setup deadline before that assertion and is retained as an invalid product control; no timeout, assertion or access scope was weakened. The private fixture disabled model providers and used synthetic isolated state.
- **Current distinct cases:** **176 cases across 12 files pass**: 148 logging/export/session-visibility cases across nine files, five Skills cases in their original full file, and 23 clipboard/person-reference browser cases across two files. Their wrappers took **627.017**, **29.057** and **217.717 seconds**, respectively. Counts exclude duplicate reporter summaries and old-source diagnostic replays.
- **Current static checks:** production types and all five affected consumer graphs pass, including logging, UI pages, Gateway methods and UI E2E. Typed production/test lint, format, mock-export, line-cap and whitespace checks pass.
- **Native test-line budget:** **6,663,922 / 6,663,928**, leaving **6 LF**. The current proposal grows tests by exactly 44 LF, funded by the unchanged original 44-LF record. No supplemental grant, shared scalar, other author allocation or failure exception was added.
- **Runtime build:** `pnpm build:runtime` exits 0 in **551.838 seconds** on the frozen candidate tree. It builds the runtime and UI and reports restored CLI-startup metadata. This is candidate-tree build evidence; build metadata was generated before this commit. The report-only UI asset lane reports total CSS overages (gzip 319.3 versus 318.9 KiB; raw 1647.1 versus 1642.8 KiB). Strict asset-budget success is unclaimed.
- **Independent review:** a fresh desktop reviewer inspected the complete eleven-file proposal, affected owners and callers over read-only SSH, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewer did not execute tests or provide maintainer security approval. No Codex CLI was run on the remote host.
- **Retained earlier CLI proof:** the eight critical logging/export product and test inputs are byte-identical to the previous author revision. Earlier normal-CLI export proof below retains its original commit, date and scope; it is not a new CLI, installed-upgrade, live-provider or platform execution on this revision.

The prior [87-job natural CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42965879876) remains **failure** on its original `0d024b2` author / `f960d37` tested merge. Its repaired configuration-form cases and native budget passed. Its **Skills failure remains unclassified**: five full-file cases pass on both the old CI tree and the current integration, but these bounded runs do not reproduce the original Bun shard order and do not prove a product fix, inherited failure or flakiness.

The former Activity route-loss hypothesis is withdrawn: the public diagnostic snapshot intentionally omits unrecognized person paths, while its matching private snapshot retains the route. The public RPC ring also omits parameters and source attribution. Neither projection proves loss of navigation or identifies an Activity RPC. No navigation fix was introduced on that basis.

The [natural CI for this author revision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43070352850) completed **success** on attempt 1 with **88 terminal jobs: 60 successful and 28 skipped**. Its checkout is actual tested merge `d47ae86e725a1927b8c28b2ffcb41c11dc614133` of official main `85b3c4a4cf8018018b65f82bcf6fdc30b5351e91` and author `4d91083e0fcda4d936d4c66631db3004f26823b0`, with tree `97201b431972023d659b92c685b2d12d070fa38f`; checkout logs and the merge's raw parents agree. The native test-line job passes at **6,664,346 / 6,664,361**, leaving **15 LF**. This is separate from the earlier local candidate-tree budget and its 6-LF margin.

All three selected UI unit jobs and all five selected UI E2E jobs pass. The real-Gateway UI E2E job is skipped by this run's plan; neither that skip nor the current passing Skills shard proves the cause or repair of the old unclassified Skills failure. The old 87-job failure retains its original author, tested merge and result.

The Actions `openclaw/ci-gate` job succeeds. The separate classic `openclaw/ci-gate` status is **failure**, and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` is **pending**, because a maintainer must approve this current revision. Dependency review succeeds with no dependency changes. Natural CI success does not satisfy that owner approval. Any applicable upgrade and platform acceptance remain separate. No approval command, manual rerun, upstream merge, release or real operator-Gateway acceptance is claimed.

prs.title: fix(active-memory): warning repeats on every turn when the memory provider lacks private transcript recall
prs.body:
Closes #198437

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory logs the same "does not support protected private transcript recall" warning on every eligible turn when Remember across conversations is on and the memory slot owner does not support it.

## User Impact

User impact: operators see the warning once per memory provider and agent instead of on every turn. Later repeats go to the debug log. Recall behavior does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Whether the slot owner supports protected transcript recall is fixed by config, so repeating the warning adds nothing. The plugin keeps a set of provider and agent pairs it has warned about; the first skip warns, later skips log the same line at debug. The set lives in the plugin registration, so a plugin reload or config change that re-registers Active Memory warns again. The other skip warning ("... is unavailable"), which depends on the turn's tool authority, is unchanged.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on `c8df4c6e6226bc6f29c20730a7a0456fca451722`:

- Independent Astra cross-layer review found no actionable correctness or compatibility findings. The unchanged current-main owner still contains the repeated warning, so the fix remains needed.
- Local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6-astra`, P0–P2) reviewed the complete committed range `eae12351406e4cfee0b800e5f2006ae24e0e1578..c8df4c6e6226bc6f29c20730a7a0456fca451722` with plugin-registration lifetime context: complete, scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper tooling was unavailable; the existing exact-head hosted ClawSweeper review reports no findings.
- [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43499117236) passed. Inspected [changed-extension job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43499117236/job/134315467260) logs verify all 96 index tests, including the new warns-once regression, and 249 tests across the Active Memory lane. Actual tested merge `acf95e9a4d51d9a100ca40c25ab169f49be6fa26` includes this exact PR head.
- The real-Gateway before/after evidence below remains contributor-produced; it was not independently repeated. No untrusted PR code was executed on the Team host.

Implementation remains by @etzelm; additional review and landing were requested by @VACInc.

Real Gateway, before and after. Both builds came from source (`pnpm build`) and ran as an isolated local Gateway on loopback, each with its own state dir, config, and token. The model and the LanceDB embeddings came from the repo's QA `mock-openai` server, so no provider keys were used.

Setup, identical on both builds:

- `plugins.slots.memory: "memory-lancedb"`. LanceDB does not declare `supportsPrivateTranscriptRecall`.
- Active Memory is enabled with `agents: ["personal"]`.
- `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations: true`.
- Three private turns to agent `personal` over Gateway `chat.send` on session `agent:personal:main` (webchat, direct). The turns are neutral messages with no recall intent.
- Logging at debug.

| Build | Version | `does not support protected private transcript recall` at WARN | same line at DEBUG | recall runs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main `eae12351406` | OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (eae1235), macOS arm64 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| this PR `c8df4c6e622` | OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (c8df4c6), macOS arm64 | 1 | 2 | 0 |

Gateway log excerpt, this PR (redacted):

```
WARN  13:33:14 [plugins] active-memory: the current memory provider does not support protected private transcript recall; skipping Remember across conversations
DEBUG 13:33:43 [plugins] active-memory: the current memory provider does not support protected private transcript recall; skipping Remember across conversations
DEBUG 13:34:14 [plugins] active-memory: the current memory provider does not support protected private transcript recall; skipping Remember across conversations
```

Unit coverage:

- New test in `extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`: three turns with an unsupported provider produce one warning and two debug lines, and recall stays skipped. It fails on main at `eae12351406` and passes with this change.
- `extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`: 96 of 96 pass, including the existing "fails closed without product recall for an unsupported memory provider" case.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on both changed files.

prs.title: fix(postgres): chat history slows under concurrent reads
prs.body:
Closes #188956
Related: #197313, #190001 (#197313 tracks the repeated read snapshots inside each history page, which #190001 addresses)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on PostgreSQL, `chat.history` requests queue behind two history workers when several clients load history at once, so tail latency grows with concurrency while the CPU sits mostly idle.

## User Impact

User impact: concurrent `chat.history` on PostgreSQL waits much less for a history worker. Re-measured on current `main` (medians of 8 interleaved runs per build): at 8 concurrent clients p50 drops from 19.6 to 12.02 ms, p99 from 54.31 to 31.76 ms, and throughput rises from 378.1 to 622.95 requests/s; at 32 clients p99 drops from 163.13 to 103.1 ms. Single-client p50 is unchanged; single-client p99 rose from 15.08 to 17.07 ms over all runs (14.87 to 15.13 ms in the quieter block). SQLite keeps its current lane size.

Cost, measured on the same runs (medians of 8 runs per build):

- Memory: during concurrent history reads the Gateway runs up to two more transcript isolates (about 57 MiB of heap each). Peak transcript-worker heap rose from 334.1 to 453.6 MiB and peak Gateway RSS from 2,764.9 to 3,153.1 MiB. The extra isolates retire after the pool's existing idle timeout: 45 s and 100 s after load both builds ran the same number of transcript isolates with about the same heap (45 s: 229.4 vs 242.8 MiB; 100 s: 223.8 vs 227.8 MiB). RSS at 100 s was 2,106.1 vs 2,324.7 MiB.
- PostgreSQL connections: backends for the runtime role peaked at 23 on base and 25 with the change; both were back to 13 after 100 idle seconds. Each extra history isolate can retain up to two idle transports for three minutes; the documented budget (`isolates × (active + 2)`) now notes up to four history isolates.

**Decision for review:** should PostgreSQL history use up to four workers, accepting the cost above? This revises the two-worker reader cap from #167295 and #169110 for one lane on one engine.

- (a) Accept four workers for PostgreSQL history (this PR). Cost: up to two more isolates (about 120 to 124 MiB of worker heap and about 320 to 390 MiB of peak RSS across the two benches below) and two more peak backends, only while history load is concurrent; single-client p99 from 15.08 to 17.07 ms over all runs (14.87 to 15.13 ms in the quieter block). On a host whose CPU is already saturated by other work, the extra workers did not help p99 (see Evidence, block 1).
- (b) Keep two workers. PostgreSQL history keeps queueing: 5.57 ms of queue wait per worker request at 8 clients, 13.34 ms at 16.
- (c) Make the larger lane opt-in with a setting. No default cost, but it adds a config surface for an internal pool size, and the default keeps the queueing.
- (d) A cap of eight. Measured on an older `main` (see Evidence): lower queue wait at 16 clients, at about two and a half times the extra memory and with more backends.

Recommended: (a). The extra workers exist only on PostgreSQL agent stores and only under concurrent history reads, they retire through the existing idle timeout and cleanup owners, and SQLite, transcript search and every other lane keep the current cap. The memory bound stays fixed (at most four history isolates on any host), and the latency it buys is the symptom #188956 reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

On PostgreSQL a history worker spends most of a request blocked in `Atomics.wait` on bridge replies, so sizing the lane like a CPU-bound reader leaves requests queued while CPU is free. The history lane on PostgreSQL agent stores now gets two workers per CPU above one, capped at four (two on a two-CPU host). Transcript search, the other transcript lanes, and every SQLite lane keep the existing reader size from #167295 and #169110. No new setting.

The database engine is installed during boot, after the lane module is imported, so the history pool now resolves its size on first use instead of at import. Production code: +47/-7 lines ignoring whitespace (the pool options block is re-indented inside the first-use constructor); tests +117; docs +9/-4.

Scope: this closes #188956 (the queueing in front of the history workers). The transaction round trips inside each page are #197313, addressed by #190001; the two touch different files and are measured separately.

## Evidence

Evidence files: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/assets/pg-r2-l3d-history-reader-lane-evidence/current-main-2026-11-07 (paths below are relative to it; method, host and store in `README.md`). The earlier bench on `31866655fd6` stays at the root of the same branch.

Acceptance rule: through a running Gateway on PostgreSQL, at 8 or more concurrent clients, queue wait per worker request and p50 drop, throughput rises and p99 at 8 clients drops; single-client latency holds; the memory and backend cost is reported, and the extra isolates retire once history load stops.

- **Tests** on this head merged into current `main` `078033289a3`: a per-engine sizing table (`src/infra/worker-pool-sizing.test.ts`) and a lane test that installs the engine after importing the lane, as boot does (`src/config/sessions/session-history-lane-sizing.test.ts`: PostgreSQL 4, SQLite 2, search 2). Both pass, as do the consumer suites for the transcript lanes, the search worker, reconcile readiness, the chat history worker and worker-pool preparation: 12 files, 161 tests (`tests/unit-head.log`). On `main` the sizing table fails because the resolver does not exist, and the PostgreSQL lane case gets 2 instead of 4 while the SQLite case passes (`tests/unit-base-red.log`). `pnpm check:changed` on the merged head passes every check except two repo-wide audits that fail the same way on plain `main` `078033289a3`: changelog attributions (bot credits in `CHANGELOG/` files) and the dead export scan (`scripts/lib/control-ui-gesture-probe.ts`, `src/process/command-reservation-census.ts`) (`tests/check-changed.log`, `tests/base-changelog-attr.log`, `tests/base-deadcode.log`). CI on `987348094eb` was green.
- **After merging `main` `4a0e45492b8`** (head `3e55cf3ef68`): `main` dropped the history worker's `prewarmHistory` option (#198512), so the lazy pool no longer passes it; sizing is unchanged. The sizing table, the lane test and the consumer suites above plus the prewarm and history worker lifecycle suites pass: 14 files, 169 tests. One test in `session-transcript-worker-lanes.test.ts` (`releases pressure subscriptions after native settlement and rearms reopened lanes`, added on `main` by #197510) fails on this head and on plain `main` `4a0e45492b8` alike, 3 of 3 runs each on a macOS arm64 host. `pnpm check:changed` passes every step except the dead export scan, whose findings are all in files this PR does not touch.
- **Closed-loop `chat.history` bench on current `main`**: base `main` `078033289a3` vs this head merged into it, both built with `pnpm build`. A fresh Gateway on PostgreSQL 17.11 per run, seeded through its own RPCs with 200 sessions (170 sessions across 6 agents with 2 to 4,675 messages each, plus 30 imported Claude CLI sessions with tool rows hidden between visible turns). Limit 100, 45 s per arm, 16 runs (8 per build) in two interleaved blocks (base head head base base head head base). No run was dropped. Medians over all 16 runs (`bench/block-all/medians.tsv`; every run in `bench/block-all/arms.tsv`; raw scrapes in `bench/runs/`):

| arm | p50 / p95 / p99 ms | p99 range | requests/s | queue wait per worker request | handler mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 client, base | 6.09 / 10.69 / 15.08 | 12.85 to 51.11 | 156.4 | 0.0 ms | 5.19 ms |
| 1 client, fix | 6.00 / 11.02 / 17.07 | 11.9 to 106.71 | 154.4 | 0.0 ms | 5.27 ms |
| 8 clients, base | 19.6 / 31.82 / 54.31 | 28.99 to 161.47 | 378.1 | 5.57 ms | 19.46 ms |
| 8 clients, fix | 12.02 / 19.64 / 31.76 | 20 to 230.82 | 622.95 | 1.23 ms | 10.1 ms |
| 16 clients, base | 37.66 / 54.15 / 88.16 | 58.52 to 200.55 | 411.8 | 13.34 ms | 37.21 ms |
| 16 clients, fix | 24.6 / 42.92 / 66.77 | 45.72 to 499.74 | 606.65 | 6.73 ms | 23.41 ms |
| 32 clients, base | 71.04 / 96.61 / 163.13 | 90.84 to 421.36 | 431.7 | 28.54 ms | 72.43 ms |
| 32 clients, fix | 48.48 / 84.22 / 103.1 | 66.74 to 578.74 | 634.25 | 17.02 ms | 47.23 ms |

Queue wait is `openclaw_worker_queue_wait_seconds{kind="sessionTranscript"}`; handler mean is `openclaw_gateway_rpc_handler_seconds{method="chat.history"}`. The host is shared, and the wide p99 ranges come from runs under other load, so the two blocks are also reported separately:

- Block 2 (`bench/block-b2/`, started only below a 1-minute load of 12; arms at load 4 to 25): p99 at 1, 8, 16 and 32 clients 14.87 / 30.47 / 68.2 / 115.94 ms base vs 15.13 / 25.1 / 64.69 / 88.53 ms fix; p50 at 8 clients 18.11 vs 11.73 ms, throughput 431.6 vs 651.05 requests/s. At 16 clients p99 is about even while p50 drops from 35.98 to 24.6 ms.
- Block 1 (`bench/block-b1/`, load 6 to 55): p50, throughput and queue wait improve at 8, 16 and 32 clients as above, but p99 does not improve consistently: 69.65 vs 73.11 ms at 8 clients, 147.19 vs 113.72 ms at 16, 198.87 vs 281.24 ms at 32. The worst fix tails are `pg-head-r1` (the highest 1-minute load in the bench, 37 to 55) and `pg-head-r2` (load 25 to 33, started with 25% of host memory free); the other two fix runs in the block have p99 21.7 and 36.16 ms at 8 clients. When the host's CPU is already saturated, extra workers add little.

- **Moved the wrong way**: memory and backends (see User Impact: +120 MiB peak transcript heap, +388 MiB peak RSS, +219 MiB RSS 100 s after load, +2 peak backends); single-client p99 15.08 to 17.07 ms over all runs (14.87 to 15.13 ms in block 2; p50 6.09 to 6.00 ms over all runs, 5.71 to 5.94 ms in block 2; single-client p95 10.69 to 11.02 ms over all runs) and 19.35 to 33.27 ms in block 1 (driven by `pg-head-r2`, single-client p99 106.71 ms); single-client throughput 156.4 to 154.4 requests/s over all runs (163.6 to 155.65 in block 2); and in block 1, under the heaviest host load, p99 at 8 clients 69.65 to 73.11 ms and at 32 clients 198.87 to 281.24 ms. In the pair bench on current `main`, single-client p95 12.75 vs 10.47 ms (+22%), p99 21.33 vs 12.85 ms and throughput 136.4 vs 159.0 calls/s (-14%) (`pair-bench/medians.tsv`). These are part of the decision above.
- **Memory and connections** (`bench/block-all/memory-medians.tsv`, per run in `memory.tsv`): see User Impact. Heap and isolate counts come from the Gateway's worker metrics, sampled by the 30 s diagnostic heartbeat; RSS and backend counts are sampled every 2 s.
- **SQLite**: the lane size is unchanged by construction (the resolver returns the existing reader size for every non-PostgreSQL agent engine; covered by the sizing table and lane test). The earlier bench on `31866655fd6` measured SQLite p50, throughput and transcript isolates unchanged; not re-measured here.
- **Cap of four vs eight** (earlier bench on `31866655fd6`, 3 runs each, `bench/medians.tsv` and `bench/memory-medians.tsv` at the branch root, rows `base-a`, `fix4` and `fix8`): eight gave 0.07 ms queue wait at 8 clients and 1.66 ms at 16, at +325 MiB peak transcript heap, +974 MiB peak RSS and 27 peak backends over `base-a`, against +120 MiB heap, +382 MiB RSS and 25 peak backends for four (`fix4` over `base-a`).

- **Pair bench on current `main` `82210a2bbdb0`** (`pair-bench/`): four builds from one `main` (`main`, `main` + #190001, `main` + this PR, `main` + both), four runs each in interleaved order, PostgreSQL 17.11, closed-loop `chat.history` at 1, 8, 16 and 32 clients. Gate results on the same `main`: unit 12 files / 162 tests pass with this PR (the new sizing and lane tests fail on plain `main`); with both PRs unit 28 / 386 and PostgreSQL conformance 15 / 165 pass. Medians of 4 runs, this PR vs `main`: at 8 clients p50 13.84 vs 19.65 ms, p99 26.26 vs 46.48 ms, 555 vs 385 calls/s, queue wait per worker request 1.06 vs 5.28 ms; at 16 clients p50 29.21 vs 41.94 ms, 507 vs 362 calls/s; at 32 clients p50 58.09 vs 79.41 ms, p99 88.81 vs 199.78 ms, 545 vs 372 calls/s. At 1 client p50 is 6.31 vs 6.01 ms and p99 is noisier (12.12 to 60.43 ms across runs vs 11.74 to 23.23 ms on `main`; the two highest runs had the highest arm-start load of this build's four runs, 13.1 and 17.9 in `pair-bench/arms.tsv`). Cost: peak Gateway RSS 2789 vs 2468 MiB (+321 MiB), peak transcript worker heap 456 vs 332 MiB (+124 MiB), peak transcript workers 8 vs 6, peak PostgreSQL backends 23 vs 21; 100 s after load, 4 workers vs 3 and the same 13 backends. With #190001 as well, p50 is the same at 16 and 32 clients (29.57 and 58.06 ms) but p99 is higher (81.27 vs 67.81 ms, 128.55 vs 88.81 ms). At 8 clients the pair has p50 15.21 ms, p99 55.06 ms and 480.2 calls/s: p99 is above this PR alone (26.26 ms) and also above `main` (46.48 ms), and throughput is below this PR alone (555.25 calls/s) in all four paired runs (`arms.tsv`), so host load does not explain it. The cost comes from #190001 on this dense-page store (history worker time per request 3.741 vs 3.229 ms at 8 clients, `pair-bench/worker-time.tsv`) and is reported there.

### Gaps

- The bench store is synthetic, written through the Gateway's own RPCs, because `main` does not admit a `pg_restore` of a production store. Its shape follows the production bench in #188956.
- Shared host: the p99 tails in block 1 are dominated by other load (per-arm load in `arms.tsv`). Two fix runs (`pg-head-r2` in block 1, `pg-head-r8` in block 2) started while another job held most host memory; both are kept.
- At 16 clients and above the four-worker lane queues again (6.73 ms per worker request at 16, 17.02 ms at 32). A cap of eight removes most of that at a higher memory cost.
- Memory figures needed one measurement-only line, applied identically to both builds: the diagnostic heartbeat publishes its memory sample every 30 s instead of only after agent activity (`scripts/instrument-*.diff`). Isolate counts and heap cover every transcript lane, not only history, and 30 s sampling can miss the exact peak. RSS was watched for 100 s after load here; the earlier 300 s pair on `31866655fd6` (`bench/runs/pg-*-idle-r1` at the branch root) showed no lasting RSS difference with the same isolate count (1,676 vs 1,745 MiB at 300 s).
- Transcript search on PostgreSQL also blocks on bridge replies and keeps its two-worker cap; not measured here.
- The bench host is shared (1-minute load 4.2 to 13.8 at run start, `pair-bench/run-order-and-load.txt`, and 3.8 to 22.2 at arm start, `pair-bench/arms.tsv`). Tails at 1 and 8 clients move with that load; medians at 8 or more clients do not. Idle retirement past 100 s was not sampled in the pair bench; the earlier bench above covers it.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let manifest configSignals test a config value
prs.body:
Closes #197882

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors cannot hide a tool while its config flag is `false`, because manifest `configSignals` can only test whether a value is present. The tool is still offered to the model.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can list a tool only while a feature is actually on, for example `"equals": { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true }`, so the model no longer sees tools the plugin will refuse to run. Existing manifests behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each `configSignals` entry now accepts an optional `equals` map from a dot path to a literal string, number, or boolean. It follows the issue triage: literal equality only, with inequality left out until a plugin needs it. The issue is marked as needing a product decision; this PR implements the recommended contract so that decision can be made on concrete code.

The contract, stated in the docs and covered by tests:

- **Missing value:** a missing or `null` path fails. Comparison is strict, so `"true"` does not equal `true`.
- **Overlays:** paths are read from the same effective config as `required`, after `overlayPath`. With `overlayMapPath`, each map entry is checked on its own, so `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry.
- **SecretRefs:** never resolved. A path holding a SecretRef does not equal any literal, even when the secret has that value.
- **Older hosts:** they ignore `equals` and drop a signal that has nothing else, so the tool falls back to its other config or auth signals, and with none it stays listed, which is today's behavior. The docs tell plugins that rely on `equals` to set `openclaw.install.minHostVersion`.
- All fields of one signal must pass together. `required`, `requiredAny`, and `mode` are unchanged, so `false` still counts as present for `required`.

Generation provider metadata shares the same evaluator, so it gets the same field. Docs cover the field, its rules and a flag-gating example.

## Evidence

Real agent turns from the shipped CLI: `openclaw agent --local --model claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5 --json`, each with a fresh isolated state dir and config, `tools.profile: "full"`, and a small fixture plugin that registers two tools unconditionally:

- `kb_search`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", equals: { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true } }]`
- `kb_status`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", required: ["knowledgeBase.enabled"] }]` (presence only, unchanged control)

Prompt: list every tool whose name contains `kb_`, then call `kb_search` once if it is available, otherwise reply "kb_search unavailable". The tool columns come from the run's own tool list (`meta.systemPromptReport.tools.entries`, the tools sent to the model):

| Build | `knowledgeBase.enabled` | Tools sent | `kb_search` | `kb_status` | Model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (`92e16d25ce01`) | `false` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |
| main (`92e16d25ce01`) | `true` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |
| this branch | `false` | 61 | not sent | sent | listed only `kb_status`, replied "kb_search unavailable" |
| this branch | `true` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |

On main, `equals` is an unknown field, so the signal is dropped and the model can call `kb_search` while the flag is off. The presence-only `kb_status` stays listed in every run, because `false` counts as configured. On this branch the only difference between the two flag values is `kb_search`.

Redacted model reply, this branch, `knowledgeBase.enabled: false`:

```text
kb_status
mcp__openclaw__kb_status

kb_search unavailable
```

(The Claude CLI runtime also exposes OpenClaw tools under `mcp__openclaw__` names, so the model lists each tool twice.)

Regression tests (red on main, green here):

- `src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.test.ts`: on main 7 failed, 23 passed (30). Covers `true`, `false`, the string `"true"`, `null` and a missing path; `overlayPath`; `overlayMapPath` where `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry; and a SecretRef that is never resolved.
- `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts`: on main 1 failed, 65 passed (66). Loads a real manifest: the normalizer keeps `false` and `0`, trims paths, and drops non-scalar values, empty paths and a signal whose only `equals` entry is invalid.

Checks run on this branch (based on main `92e16d25ce01`):

- `pnpm test` on the two files above plus consumers (`tools.optional`, `tools.inspection`, `manifest-command-aliases`, `tool-policy`, `tool-policy-pipeline`, `tools-effective-inventory` (6 files)): 13 files, 286 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`, `pnpm build`: pass.
- `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-categories.test.ts` fails on main `92e16d25ce01` and on this branch with the same message, `perplexity: expected exactly one purpose category`. The perplexity manifest has listed two categories since #195641; this branch does not touch it.

Risks: low. The field is optional and additive, and no existing branch of the evaluator changed. Older hosts drop the unknown field and fall back to the tool's other signals, which is today's behavior; the docs point plugin authors to `openclaw.install.minHostVersion`.
