prs.title: feat(plugins): let an operator run a memory plugin beside the memory slot owner
prs.body:
Closes #198445

## What Problem This Solves

A memory plugin that does not own `plugins.slots.memory` is disabled before it registers anything, so an operator cannot keep memory-core and also run an external memory plugin.

## User Impact

An operator can set `plugins.entries.<id>.memory.sidecar: true` to load that memory plugin beside the slot owner. The mode is an explicit operator opt-in. The plugin keeps its hooks, tools and corpus supplements. The slot owner keeps `memory_search`, the memory runtime, the recall grant and memory lessons. A turn now carries a host-minted memory audience when a loaded sidecar can use it, so a sidecar that routes recall and retain by audience works next to memory-core. Configs without the setting load and behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registrar already strips slot-owner fields from a memory capability registered by a plugin that is not the owner (the dreaming sidecar relies on this), so the missing piece was the load decision. The setting is per plugin entry, so an operator accepts the cost of a second memory system for each install. `openclaw plugins enable` keeps the current slot for a sidecar entry, so enabling one does not replace memory-core.

Every sidecar lookup reads `plugins.entries` through the canonical policy id, so a manifest id such as `MiXeD-memory` matches its lowercase entry `mixed-memory`. Root help admits a sidecar only when the normalized memory slot is not `none`.

Memory audiences are minted by the host, not by plugins. The embedded runner minted one only when the slot owner was a native provider, so next to memory-core (a legacy runtime) a sidecar saw no audience and skipped recall and retain. The gate is now: native slot owner, or at least one loaded memory plugin that is not the slot owner and has `memory.sidecar: true`. The audience comes from the same `resolveMemoryAudienceFromEntry` call with the same owner, sender and lineage checks, so it grants nothing a native owner would not. A config with no sidecar entry returns before any registry read, so legacy-only turns still take no session lease and read no lineage. The other native-only paths (project memory bootstrap, post-compaction refresh, memory flush) talk to the slot owner's provider and are unchanged.

Config surface: `plugins.entries.*.memory` and `plugins.entries.*.memory.sidecar` are counted once per plugin entry, so the generated plugin path count in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` rises from 5080 to 5454. No other config paths change.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

- `PluginEntrySchema`: `memory.sidecar` (boolean), with label and help text.
- `normalizePluginsConfig`: `entries[id].memorySidecar`; `isMemorySidecarEnabled` reads it by canonical policy id.
- `resolveMemorySlotDecision`: `sidecar` parameter; enabled and not selected when the slot names another plugin; still disabled for `slots.memory: "none"`; a case variant of the owner id is not a sidecar.
- Callers: runtime loader, config validation, CLI root descriptors, plugin root contributions.
- `applySlotSelectionForPlugin`: drops the `memory` kind for a sidecar entry, so enable does not move the slot.
- `hasLoadedMemorySidecar` (`src/plugins/memory-state.ts`): true when a loaded `memory` plugin other than the slot owner has `memory.sidecar` on; never loads a plugin.
- `resolveEmbeddedAttemptMemoryAudience`: mints when the owner is native or `hasLoadedMemorySidecar` is true.
- docs/plugins/manifest.md: one line on the setting.

</details>

## Evidence

Builds: main `4cffd43ee04`, this branch before the audience change (`a3fca384bdb`) and with it (`e4597199264`), built from source. The external plugin is `@etzelm/openclaw-memory-hindsight` 0.9.0 from npm (manifest id `hindsight-native`, kind `memory`, `slotMode: sidecar`). `hindsightApiUrl` points at a loopback mock that logs every request and answers recall with one canned memory (`PROOF-CANARY-7731: the operator's test color is teal.`); no real credentials.

The head `44125d5382a` merges main (`4a0e45492b8`) on top of `e4597199264`, with one import reordered for the current formatter. On that merged tree, the 94 tests in the changed test files pass and `pnpm config:docs:check` is OK.

Chat turns: each build ran as an isolated scratch Gateway (own HOME, state dir, config, loopback port and token) with the repo's QA mock-openai server as the model, `plugins.slots.memory: "memory-core"`, and two `chat.send` turns on `agent:main:main`.

| Run | `plugins inspect hindsight-native` | `tools.catalog` | `memory.status` provider | Requests at the Hindsight mock | Canary in the model prompt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, plugin enabled, no `memory.sidecar` | disabled: `memory slot set to "memory-core"` | `memory_search`, `memory_get` | `memory-core` | none | no |
| `a3fca384bdb`, `memory.sidecar: true` | loaded | + `hindsight_recall`, `hindsight_reflect`, `hindsight_retain` | `memory-core` | none (`auto-recall skipped: this session has no memory audience`) | no |
| `e4597199264`, `memory.sidecar: true` | loaded | + `hindsight_recall`, `hindsight_reflect`, `hindsight_retain` | `memory-core` | per turn: `POST .../memories/recall` and `POST .../memories` (retain) | yes, both turns |

Gateway log, `e4597199264`:

```
[plugins] memory-hindsight: running as a sidecar beside memory-core; memory_search and memory_get stay with it
[plugins] memory-hindsight: auto-recall source=fresh
```

No `no memory audience` lines appear. The `hindsight_*` tool factories return null only for the sessionless `tools.catalog` call, which has no audience by design, and not during the turns. The model sees a compact tool list in this setup (`tool_search`, `tool_describe` and core tools), so neither `memory_*` nor `hindsight_*` tools are listed directly and no tool call was exercised.

Upgrade from the latest stable release (npm `openclaw@2026.11.3`), one scratch HOME and state dir:

- Stable: `onboard --non-interactive`, `plugins install` and enable of the 0.9.0 plugin, slot kept on memory-core, `config validate` passes, Gateway starts healthy with `memory.status` provider `memory-core`, `doctor --non-interactive` exits 0.
- Branch on the same state and config, without `memory.sidecar`: `config validate` passes with the config unchanged. The state written by stable needs `doctor --fix` before the Gateway serves sessions (the agent database schema moved on main), and `doctor --fix` exits 0. After it, `doctor --non-interactive` exits 0, the plugin stays disabled (`memory slot set to "memory-core"`), and the Gateway starts healthy with `memory.status` provider `memory-core` and no `hindsight_*` tools.
- Branch with `config set plugins.entries.hindsight-native.memory.sidecar true`: `config validate` and `doctor --non-interactive` exit 0, the plugin is loaded (`enabled in config`), the Gateway lists `hindsight_*` beside `memory_search` and `memory_get`, and `memory.status` stays `memory-core`.
- Round trip: `config get plugins.entries.hindsight-native.memory` returns `{"sidecar":true}` before and after an unrelated `config set logging.level info`. The file on disk keeps `"memory":{"sidecar":true}` and `config validate` still passes.
- Stable 2026.11.3 refuses the same state dir afterwards because the branch (main) state database is at schema 40 and stable supports 22.

Tests (`pnpm test` on the changed test files): 84 passed across `loader.memory-sidecar`, `config-state`, `slot-selection` and `plugin-root-contributions`. The case-variant slot check asserts a literal decision (`{ enabled: false, reason: 'memory slot set to "mixed-memory"' }`). Audience gate: `attempt-memory-audience.sidecar.test.ts` (native owner granted; legacy owner without sidecar none, with no lineage read or lease; legacy owner with a loaded sidecar granted; sidecar setting off or plugin not loaded none; a turn the owner checks deny stays denied) and `memory-state.sidecar.test.ts`. The new tests fail on `a3fca384bdb` (3 failed: `expected undefined to deeply equal { kind: 'owner-private', ... }` and `hasLoadedMemorySidecar is not a function`) and pass with the change; with the neighbouring audience and memory-state suites, 93 passed.

`pnpm check:changed` on `44125d5382a`: every step passes except the dead export scan. Its findings are all in files this branch does not touch (for example `src/agents/runtime/index.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-session-state.ts`, `src/shared/subagent-completion.ts`, `extensions/google/provider-catalog-runtime.ts` and test-support files under `src/gateway/`, `src/tts/` and `ui/src/`).

Not covered: a model-initiated `hindsight_*` tool call during a turn (the mock model does not call tools here), and a real Hindsight server (a loopback mock stands in).

prs.title: fix(plugins): scheduled command turns keep failing after the plugin is disabled or uninstalled
prs.body:
Closes #186957

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin's scheduled command turns keep failing after the plugin is disabled or uninstalled in a running Gateway, each one spending an attempt, until `maxRuns`, the deadline or the 10-failure auto-disable stops the schedule.

## User Impact

User impact: a schedule whose plugin was disabled or removed ends at its next occurrence instead of going through repeated-failure handling. Its command does not run in this case, before or after this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each occurrence already refused this case, but only the "another live instance replaced the plugin" refusal ended the schedule; the others went through ordinary failure handling. Now, if the current (non-retired) plugin registry no longer lists the plugin, or lists it disabled, the schedule ends the same way. A plugin that is still enabled but has no live instance (still unloading, or a registry swap) keeps the ordinary refusal and retries, as documented.

Parent conversation resets are out of scope: since #199512 a scheduled plugin command follows its parent conversation to the current transcript.

The scheduled command turns docs page names the case.

## Evidence

Each tree ran as a built Gateway (`createOpenClawTestInstance`) with a WebChat operator client, shipped RPCs only (`chat.send`, `plugins.setEnabled`, `config.patch`, `cron.list`, `cron.runs`) and a local stub model. Runs: `main` at `2e1b61901c5` twice and this branch at `5ee333af574` twice. Each run's assertions are gated on the side it expects.

| Case (`every` 2 s, `maxRuns: 3`, one healthy run first) | `main` (2/2) | this branch (2/2) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin disabled with `plugins.setEnabled` | refused at +1.6 s / +2.0 s (`no longer available from its original loaded plugin`); still enabled, next run armed | refused at +1.7 s / +2.0 s (`plugin was disabled or removed; the schedule ended`); disabled, no next run, no auto-disable |
| Plugin removed from `plugins.load.paths` / `plugins.entries` with `config.patch` | refused at +1.8 s (both runs), same error; still enabled, next run armed | refused at +1.8 s (both runs), same as above |

In every run the schedule's command ran once before the change and not after it. On both sides the Gateway then sends its notice about the failed run to the conversation that owns the schedule, and that turn reached the stub model: on `main` a repair request (the schedule is still enabled), on this branch the plain failure alert (the schedule has ended).

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: scheduled command turns whose plugin was disabled or uninstalled in-process keep failing and spending attempts.
- Real environment tested: Linux, source checkout, Gateway started from the built `dist`, isolated state directory and port, a configured plugin loaded from `plugins.load.paths`, operator device client over WebChat.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: a Vitest e2e driver (not committed) that starts the built Gateway and drives the cases in the table through the RPCs listed above, run twice on `main` and twice on this branch.
- Evidence after fix:

```
plugin disabled (plugins.setEnabled), cron.runs:
  before:   ok
  +1.7 s:   error  Scheduled plugin command's plugin was disabled or removed; the schedule ended.
  job:      enabled false, nextRunAtMs none, autoDisabled none   (2 of 3 runs used)
plugin removed (config.patch):
  +1.8 s:   error  Scheduled plugin command's plugin was disabled or removed; the schedule ended.
  job:      enabled false, nextRunAtMs none, autoDisabled none
```

- Observed result after fix: the schedule ends at its first refused occurrence and its command does not run again.
- What was not tested: an npm-installed plugin removed with `plugins.uninstall`. The test plugin is path-loaded, which `plugins.uninstall` refuses; the removal goes through the same in-process plugin reload. The repeated-failure auto-disable path, which these schedules no longer reach.

Tests: `commands-plugin.scheduled-turns.test.ts` adds two cases (plugin disabled, plugin removed), which fail on `main` and pass here. With this branch the file passes 29 of 30; the other one is the existing reset row, which fails the same way on current `main`. `plugin-command-scheduled-run.test.ts` adds three registry cases: a plugin absent from the current registry, or listed disabled without its instance, ends the schedule; absent from a retired registry stays an ordinary refusal.

`tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt` on the touched files, `lint:docs` and docs formatting are clean.

prs.title: fix(media): image descriptions use the ChatGPT OAuth route when OpenAI has no API key
prs.body:
Related: #165961

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: image descriptions fail with `No API key found for provider "openai"` when OpenAI is connected only through ChatGPT OAuth and the Codex plugin is not enabled.

## User Impact

User impact: `view_image` on its configured-model route, inbound image pre-analysis and `openclaw infer image describe` can use a ChatGPT OAuth login. Existing API-key setups, required-worker image workflows and other providers keep their current behavior. No config change or migration is needed. A backport to 2026.8.x is a separate release decision, not part of this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A model such as `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` has two routes: the Platform API and ChatGPT. The image runtime resolved the model first, which returned the Platform route, and then asked for credentials scoped to that route. A ChatGPT OAuth profile is rejected on the Platform route, so the request failed before the credential could select its own route.

The image runtime now uses `prepareModelWithCredentials`, sharing credential selection and materialization with the simple-completion runtime without adopting sessionless-helper admission policy. The selected credential determines the route. The shared credential owner accepts the caller's auth store and can re-resolve the model for the selected account, passing its credential mode and profile ID so profiles held only in the supplied store still work. Existing AWS credential handling, cancellation and resource ownership remain in place.

The follow-up correction separates this credential work from `prepareSimpleCompletionModel` admission. It preserves previously working API-key image descriptions when `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile` is set, including the configured-model image-tool route. Genuine sessionless helpers still enforce their required-worker policy and worker authority. There is no bypass flag, new grant, configuration requirement or tighter image admission rule.

## Evidence

### Current correction: `c331e5025867c738f761bb0070d31f983ee7c23f`

[Final isolated compatibility proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1c7f4edf9315b86f8af766ef71dfb765):

- Two new required-worker/API-key image cases fail on incoming `fc0076433b4ce1b704eb78c95cef5f5e8ac81654` and pass with the correction; the existing OAuth cases pass in both runs.
- The exact final corrective patch passed 46 tests across four files, covering image routing, helper admission, worker authority and prompt-prefix stability. Targeted formatting, type-aware lint and scoped typecheck passed.
- An earlier run passed 179 tests across 12 files before type-only and formatting cleanup. This is separate from the 46-test final-patch run.
- The committed corrective diff matches the tested patch byte-for-byte. Mitchell's original commits are preserved; the correction includes VACInc co-author credit.
- Independent local full-range source review of `5328b2754d84472b6c6e05fe80c2fc4513fd7e2e..c331e5025867c738f761bb0070d31f983ee7c23f` found no actionable P0–P2 findings. That review is not runtime execution or a current-head hosted ClawSweeper review.

**Current-head gates:** [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44170022422), including its aggregate CI gate, passed at `c331e5025867c738f761bb0070d31f983ee7c23f`. The exact-head security review passed. The [completed hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199299#issuecomment-6885717851) reports no code findings but retains a **live-proof hold**.

**Remaining proof:** run a real worker-backed Gateway turn invoking the configured-model `view_image` route with API-key credentials and configuration retained from v2026.11.5. The interrupted managed attempt recovered stable-version output and candidate installation/build evidence, but no worker-backed image turn or retained-configuration behavior completed. Mocked-provider tests and prior-head live OAuth output do not close this gap. Landing remains blocked; no current-candidate live success is claimed.

### Independent real-account proof on the prior head

[@jjjhenriksen's live verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199299#issuecomment-6889339328) tested `fc0076433b4ce1b704eb78c95cef5f5e8ac81654` in a disposable Linux ARM64 environment with genuine ChatGPT OAuth, no OpenAI API key and Codex disabled. The shipped `openclaw infer image describe` failed on stable 2026.11.3, succeeded on the PR with fresh state, and succeeded reusing stable-created state without a configuration change. Network diagnostics confirmed HTTP 200 from the ChatGPT `/backend-api/codex/responses` route.

This is prior-head live CLI evidence, not new-candidate E2E: fresh state imported an existing credential rather than performing interactive sign-in; the upgrade scenario switched executables rather than exercising the auto-updater. It did not prove a Gateway tool turn or inbound-image flow. The comment records 172 passing tests across nine files, its build/runtime substitutions and cleanup.

### Original contributor fixture proof on the prior head

The following evidence was captured by @etzelm before the corrective commit. Product code was identical at `dfe1d5450ea` and `fc0076433b4`; it does not claim execution at the current head.

Setup: a shipped embedded agent turn (`openclaw agent --local`) in isolated state/home, with a fixture ChatGPT OAuth profile (fake token), Codex disabled and no OpenAI API key. A local chat stub calls the shipped `view_image` tool, while TLS stubs for `chatgpt.com` and `api.openai.com` record routing. Configured image model: `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`.

```sh
sh e2e-165961/run-agent.sh
NODE_OPTIONS="--require preload.cjs" pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --message "Look at red.png" --json --timeout 120
```

Before, with the two changed product files restored to merge-base `5328b2754d8`, `view_image` failed with `No API key found for provider "openai"`; no image request reached either network stub. After the original fix, the tool returned `FIXTURE-DESCRIPTION: a small red square on a white background.` The image request used `POST /backend-api/codex/responses` on the ChatGPT route with an account header. A separate later `/v1/embeddings` call was background memory indexing, not the image request. Both embedded-agent commands exited 1 because of the deliberately minimal final answer from the chat fixture; this is not an overall successful-process claim.

The same original fixture through `openclaw infer image describe --file red.png --model openai/gpt-5.6-luna --json` failed on base and succeeded on the ChatGPT route after the fix. This fixture used a network stub, not a real account or Gateway process; the independent real-account proof above is separate.

### Original tests and review

The contributor's two-account case in `image.runtime-profile.test.ts` is red without credential-scoped model re-resolution and green with it. `src/media-understanding/image.auth-routing.test.ts` exercises `describeImageWithModelCore` with the real OpenAI provider plugin, auth planner and SQLite auth store, for both agent-owned and caller-supplied stores: red on base, green with the fix, red with the fix reverted.

On the prior head the contributor reported passing changed-file checks and media/image/PDF/simple-completion/TTS and provider consumer suites; the app-lint step lacked swiftlint 0.65.1. Those results are historical, not a waiver for current-head CI. Existing mock-based image tests use a single-route provider where OpenAI route selection is not under test.

The contributor's local ClawSweeper review of `5328b2754d8..fc0076433b4` reported no findings after auth-store and account-resolution fixes. The prior hosted review requested removing helper-only assertions from the sibling module's unit test; that file was removed. Neither prior-head review replaces current-candidate review.

## Contributor credit

Original fix and fixture evidence: @etzelm (Mitchell Etzel). Independent prior-head live verification: @jjjhenriksen. Current compatibility repair, review and landing requested by @VACInc. Original commits are preserved, and the correction retains VACInc co-author credit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3c8836ba-3b35-476e-bb49-38a97e37a956)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3528b093-44eb-445f-8ea2-de4de691f050)

prs.title: fix(acp): configured Claude binding goes offline when thinking is adaptive
prs.body:
<!-- template: .github/pull_request_template.md at upstream main 1fff14f6019 -->

Fixes #165731

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a configured ACP binding, such as Claude, is reported unavailable and its messages are dropped when the inherited thinking level (the default `adaptive`) is not one of the values the adapter accepts for `effort`.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who leave `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` at `adaptive` keep a working Claude ACP binding and get replies. The binding stays on the thinking level it already accepted. `/acp set thinking adaptive` still reports the adapter's rejection.

Risk: a configured thinking level that the adapter refuses by value is not applied to that binding. The refusal shows only in verbose logs, and the level is tried again on each readiness check with the same result. The bindings doc now says so.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconciling an existing binding applies the configured thinking level through the live setter. The adapter answers `Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive` and the whole binding was reported unavailable. A refused thinking value now keeps the accepted level and the binding stays online. Unsupported-control errors and every other failure still fail the binding, and explicit commands are untouched. The pre-turn replay already tolerates this rejection since #113935, so it is not changed.

No new config option, no SDK or manager API change. The bindings doc is updated.

This builds on #166078, which found the reconcile path and the idea of keeping the accepted level while leaving explicit commands strict. This change keeps the tolerance inside binding reconciliation, so the plugin-facing manager setter gains no parameter, and adds proof through a real adapter.

## Evidence

Base 1fff14f6019, head e5caa63788d.

- Maintainer verification: a fresh independent cross-layer review and local autoreview of `1fff14f6019cc12177e54e265d07ee8de38a6695..e5caa63788d78eeb0f091564dfd0563a8a1302b9` found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Local autoreview completed with full selected-range coverage; it did not execute the adapter or tests. [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43666110280/attempts/2) passed, including the binding-rejection regression and lifecycle, accepted-control, runtime-config, recovery and channel-consumer tests. Its logged checkout was merge `1980d134901d5c98de0ce7f3f6b6c5ce5adca49b`, with parents `78d3696be484dcaa3415205f0c42bfadce0d5fd4` and the exact PR head. The authenticated adapter output below remains contributor-produced, not independently repeated by the maintainer.
- Real adapter: isolated Gateway, real `claude-agent-acp` 0.99.1 on a Claude subscription login (no API key), `thinkingDefault: adaptive`. The adapter lists `default, low, medium, high, xhigh, max` for `effort` and answers `adaptive` with `Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602)`.
  - Base: reconciling an existing binding (accepted level `high`) with the inherited `adaptive` returns `ok: false` with that error, so admission drops the message.
  - Head: the same reconcile returns `ok: true`, the binding keeps `high`, and the next message gets a reply.
  - A fresh `adaptive` binding replies on both base and head. The pre-turn replay already tolerates the rejection.
  - Not covered: no real channel plugin. The binding spec is built the way the compiler builds it. The lifecycle and manager are the shipped code.
- Tests: the new binding test fails on the base with `ok: false` and the issue's error text, and passes with the fix. Reverting only the lifecycle change turns it red again. A second case checks that an explicit `thinking` command still rejects `adaptive` and keeps the accepted level. 50 tests pass across the new file and its consumers (binding lifecycle, accepted controls, runtime config, persistent bindings, manager).
- Gates: `pnpm check:changed` passes at the head (ratchets, format, typecheck, dead-export scan, lint). `git diff --check` is clean.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `--local-range` (Claude runner on a Claude subscription login), base 1fff14f6019, head e5caa63788d, full committed range, complete and checkout access verified. Outcome: no findings, patch is correct, rating D (proof D, patch B) after 2 rounds. The proof tier is low because the local range review cannot see the real adapter run above. Round 1 at an earlier head had one P2 (a redundant pre-turn filter), which was removed. Remaining findings: none.

Implementation by @etzelm. Additional review and landing requested by @VACInc.

## Runtime output

Same harness on both commits: isolated Gateway, real `claude-agent-acp` 0.99.1 on a Claude subscription login (no API key), `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault: adaptive`. Session ids are redacted.

Base 1fff14f6019:

```
$ OPENCLAW_PROOF_ACP_ADAPTIVE=1 pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/acp-claude-adaptive-effort.proof.live.test.ts
[proof] config thinkingDefault=adaptive
[proof] ensure binding (accepted thinking high): {"ok":true,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>"}
[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=high -> accepted
[proof] reply 1: BINDING-OK-1
[proof] adapter effort option: current=high choices=default,low,medium,high,xhigh,max
[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=adaptive -> REJECTED Agent rejected session/set_config_option for "effort"="adaptive": Invalid params: Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602).
[proof] ensure binding (inherited thinking adaptive): {"ok":false,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>","error":"Agent rejected session/set_config_option for \"effort\"=\"adaptive\": Invalid params: Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602). | -32602"}
[proof] binding reported unavailable: configured-binding admission drops the message
```

Head e5caa63788d:

```
$ OPENCLAW_PROOF_ACP_ADAPTIVE=1 pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/acp-claude-adaptive-effort.proof.live.test.ts
[proof] config thinkingDefault=adaptive
[proof] ensure binding (accepted thinking high): {"ok":true,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>"}
[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=high -> accepted

[proof] adapter set_config_option effort=adaptive -> REJECTED Agent rejected session/set_config_option for "effort"="adaptive": Invalid params: Invalid value for config option effort: adaptive (ACP -32602).
[proof] ensure binding (inherited thinking adaptive): {"ok":true,"sessionKey":"<binding-session>"}
[proof] reply 2: BINDING-OK-2
```

The binding stays online and answers the next message. The new test asserts the accepted level stays `high`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): work started by a cron run dies when the parent run ends
prs.body:
Closes #185961

## Decision for maintainers: cron reassignment

**Behavior change:** with this PR, children spawned by a cron-root run keep running after the parent run returns, **including when that cron job is later reassigned or deleted**. Today they die when the parent returns, whether or not anything was reassigned. That is the reported bug, and the reason the issue asks where the child's lifetime should start.

- Children still stop on `/stop`, on aborting the parent with its descendants, and on a reset of the requesting session (the existing requester-wide subagent cleanup), the same as children of a main session.
- The cron root's own session stays fenced, which is what #161085 protects: a child writes only to its own session, and its completion report runs as a new run in the cron key with its own fresh fence.
- If children should also stop when the cron job is reassigned, each child would need to hold a cron-root lease for its whole life. This PR does not add that; I'm happy to follow up if you prefer that design.

Jobs a cron-root run starts with the cron tool (`action: "run"`, second fix below) need no decision: the started job is its own cron run and holds its own cron-root lease and fence, so dropping the caller's fence changes no lifetime policy.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: work started by a run in a cron job's base session (`agent:<id>:cron:<job>`) fails with "Guarded request authority is no longer active" once that run ends:

- sub-agents it spawns die, and their completion reports never reach the cron session;
- a job it starts with the cron tool (`action: "run"`) that outlives the tool's wait (60 s by default) fails on its first provider request after the parent returns.

## User Impact

User impact: children spawned from a cron-root run keep working after the parent run returns, and their results are delivered back to the cron session, the same as children of a main-session run. Jobs a cron-root run starts with the cron tool finish normally even when the parent run ends first.

## Why This Change Was Made

A stable cron root fences its own provider requests for the life of its run (#161085): the run's prompt executes inside `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`, which marks the fence inactive when the run returns. `sessions_spawn` runs inside that prompt and launches the child through the in-process `agent` dispatch. The child's queued work captures the async context, so the child, and later its completion-report turn, inherit the parent's fence and fail on their first provider request after the parent returns.

The in-process `agent` handoff (`withInProcessGatewayDispatch`) already starts accepted autonomous runs outside two caller-owned scopes, the caller's transcript writer and its operator tool authority, because they "must not retain the caller's … authority after that invocation closes". This change adds the caller's request fence to that list, through `runOutsideGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` in `fetch-request-authority.ts`. The child then establishes its own fences when it runs, like any other run.

The cron job launch (`launchCronRunQueueResult` in `src/cron/service/run-queue.ts`) has the same gap: it already drops the caller's operator tool authority because "the launch owns its lifetime beyond the request acknowledgement", but a `cron.run` from a cron-root run's tool call launches the job inside that run's fence. The launch now also starts outside the caller's request fence, through the same helper; the job then sets up its own fence when its agent turn runs.

The request store can also carry a per-request egress check (`beforeRequest`). A run installs it only around its own provider stream call (`attempt-stream-settle.ts`), not while tools execute, so none is active when `sessions_spawn` hands off and none is dropped.

## Evidence

On unchanged `main`, both the mock-model Gateway runs and the live runs with a real Anthropic model show the reporter's exact error chain: the child's next provider request fails with "Guarded request authority is no longer active", the completion-report turn into the cron session fails with the same error, and the Gateway logs `Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure)`. With this change, the child finishes and its report reaches the cron session in both.

### Gateway regression (built Gateway process, local mock model)

`test/gateway-cron-root-subagent-spawn.e2e.test.ts` (new, one case) starts the built Gateway with a local OpenAI Responses mock. An `agent` request on `agent:main:cron:child-lifetime` spawns one child with `sessions_spawn`; the child's provider replies are held until the parent's `agent` request has returned. The case requires the child's second provider request and the report turn into the cron session to both arrive. Tool search is off so `sessions_spawn` is a direct tool, as in the existing `cron-isolated-spawn-only-child-delivery` QA scenario. Unchanged `main`, Gateway log (ids shortened):

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent:agent:main:cron:proof-job error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=spawn sessionKey=agent:main:subagent:3966…
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:cron:proof-job runId=announce:v1:…
[agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed for run e0da64e0… err={"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","message":"Guarded request authority is no longer active.",…}
[warn] Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure) run=e0da64e0… requester=agent:main:cron:proof-job
```

Mock-model Gateway runs of this scenario: unchanged `main` failed 4 of 4 with the chain above (the child never reaches the model); with this change 9 of 9 passed. Those counts come from a longer local version of the test; the committed case is that scenario trimmed to its core assertions (the committed case waits on the child's own run with `agent.wait`: on unchanged `main` it fails as soon as that run ends with `status: "error"`, 1 of 1; with this change it passes 2 of 2 in about 20 s).

### Live run (real Anthropic model)

Same built Gateway with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, reached through a local recording proxy that holds the child's first reply until the parent's `agent` request has returned. The parent was asked to spawn one child and reply `SPAWNED`. The child was asked to read a file and reply `LIVE-CHILD-OK`. Three runs on each side, cron key `agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime`: `main` failed 3 of 3 as below; with this change 3 of 3 completed and delivered the report (in two of them the child answered with a sentence instead of the exact marker word, but its run finished and the report arrived). Excerpts from the first pair:

Unchanged `main`: the model's reply to the child's first request (a `read` call) arrives, then the child's second request fails inside the Gateway before it leaves, and the report turn fails on the fence:

```
response role=parent tools=[sessions_spawn] … response role=parent text="SPAWNED"
parent run returned status=ok
response role=child status=200 tools=[read]
[model-fetch] error provider=liveproxy api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-5-5 elapsedMs=0 sessionKey="agent:main:subagent:4f9c…" requestNumber=2
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime runId=announce:v1:…
[warn] Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure) … requester=agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime
```

With this change:

```
parent run returned status=ok
response role=child status=200 tools=[read]
response role=child status=200 text="LIVE-CHILD-OK"
response role=report status=200 text="The live-child task finished successfully and returned exactly LIVE-CHILD-OK. …"
[agent] run announce:v1:agent:main:subagent:1978…:b355… ended with stopReason=stop
```

No "Guarded request authority" line in that Gateway log.

### Job started with the cron tool (one-off Gateway run, not committed)

Same built Gateway and mock model. A cron-root `agent` run creates a job with the cron tool and starts it with `action: "run"` and a 1 s wait; the mock holds the job's provider replies until the parent's `agent` request has returned. Unchanged `main`, the job's `cron` `finished` event, 62 ms after the parent returned:

```
{"action":"finished","status":"error","completionStatus":"failed","error":"Guarded request authority is no longer active.",…}
```

With this change the job finishes with `status: "ok"` after two provider requests, 5 of 5 runs (about 17 to 20 s each, mostly Gateway startup). This stays out of the committed tests: the unit case below covers the same contract without a second Gateway boot.

**Unit (cron launch):** `src/cron/service.run-queue.test.ts` › `starts a manual run outside its caller's request fence` runs `cron.run(id, "force")` inside a request fence and requires the job runner to see none. It fails on `main` (the runner sees the caller's fence) and passes here.

**Unit (agent handoff):** the existing launch case in `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.authorization.test.ts` now also runs the launch inside a request fence and requires the launched run to see none (both tool-authority variants). It fails on `main` (the launched run inherits the fence) and passes here.

**Consumers:** 17 related test files (every `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.*` suite, `server-plugin-subagent-runtime*`, `subagent-spawn.in-process-gateway`, `subagent-announce-completion-delivery`, `fetch-guard.authority`, `attempt-execution-phase`): 164 of 164 pass. One fork-transport timeout under a loaded host passed 3 of 3 on rerun; that test reads through `sessions.get`, not the changed `agent` path. For the cron launch: `src/cron/service` and `service.run-queue.test.ts`, 536 of 537 pass on current `main` plus this PR; the one failure (`ops.gateway-mutations.test.ts` › `leaves durable state unchanged when its caller is revoked during validation`, a 10 s `cron.add` timeout) fails the same way on unchanged `main`, 3 of 3.

Test lines are net +134 against `main`: two root-cause unit tests that reuse existing setup (the agent-handoff case extends the existing launch case; the cron-launch case uses `service.run-queue.test.ts`'s service and command-job helpers; +10 and +26, both fail on `main`) plus one Gateway case (98 lines, reusing the shared Gateway test-instance and mock-model helpers) for the report turn into the cron session, which no unit layer reaches; ClawSweeper's review of the issue asked for exactly this regression. The Gateway case takes about 22 s, mostly Gateway startup; the cron-tool path is shown by a one-off Gateway run in the body instead of a second committed Gateway case. Main's shared test-line ceiling has since filled, so `config/test-lines-allocations/cron-child-request-fence.txt` records exactly these 134 lines.

**Stopping a detached child** (existing coverage, rerun on this change): `subagent-control.accepted-stop.test.ts`, `subagent-control.commands.test.ts` and `subagent-announce.requester-settle-cancel.test.ts` pass (92 tests with the launch test). Locally, aborting the child (`sessions.abort`) or resetting the cron root (`sessions.reset`) after the parent returns stopped the child before its next provider request (2 of 2 each; the child sent no further request).

**Operator revocation** (one-off proof run, not committed): the cron-root parent was started by an operator connected with its own device. After the parent returned, an admin revoked that device's operator token (`device.token.revoke`), then the held child was released. 2 of 2 runs on this change; the child never reached the provider:

```
02:42:55.560 [gateway] device token revoked device=8483… role=operator
02:42:55.582 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent:agent:main:cron:child-lifetime error="Session turn no longer owns controller admission" taskKind=spawn runId=100e39c3…
agent.wait → {"status":"error","stopReason":"rpc","providerStarted":false}; provider requests from the child: 0
```

**Checks:** `pnpm check:changed` on the change: typecheck, format, lint, line-cap, test-line, assertion and mock ratchets pass. Its remaining failures do not involve this change: Knip reports unused exports in untouched files (`extensions/knowledge/src/conversation-access-view.ts`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-manifest-comparison.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-cleanup.ts`), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run on the test host (`rg` missing).

Proof artifice: the Gateway runs use a local mock OpenAI Responses server (or, for the live run, a recording proxy in front of the real model) that holds the child's or job's replies until the parent's `agent` request has returned; operator revocation was triggered by an admin call; unit tests run inside a hand-made request fence.

Not tested: a cron job woken by `sessions_send`, and the CLI-runtime (`claude-cli`) parent path. Both reach the child through the same `agent` handoff. For the cron-tool path: a started job whose target is the main session (it queues behind the caller's turn, so on `main` it always starts after the fence has closed; the change covers it the same way, but no run shows it), `runMode: "due"`, and a real model.

Follow-up, not in this PR: `runOutsideOperatorToolGatewayAuthority` has other callers. Chat dispatch, channel startup and plugin services start with no request fence. Session maintenance can run inside a cron-root turn; whether its work can outlive that turn is not traced here.

prs.title: fix(github): let PR contributors continue work across sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes credited contributors being blocked from continuing a publisher-authored PR when they move to a different conversation.

## User Impact

A verified linked GitHub account already credited as an author, coauthor or committer on the PR can import it and append changes to the original branch across conversations. No new role, grant, configuration or migration is required. Existing private-repository access, session authority, publisher permission and remote-head checks remain in place. Refusals retain the existing advice to use the original publication conversation or ask a full-write maintainer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared PR eligibility check previously recognized the PR author or the current conversation’s publication receipt, but not the human contributors behind a bot-authored PR. It now checks GitHub-recognized numeric account identities on the current PR commits, only when the PR author is the selected publisher. PR-body mentions and unpublished local trailers do not grant access.

This changes the shared eligibility owner used by inspection, preparation, publication and imported-PR actions. It does not change workspace custody/recovery or grant merge permission. Docs and tool guidance describe the same eligibility; repeated guidance is consolidated without adding prompts or permissions.

## Evidence

- Final head `d8002540ef6bab32d042476198c9e5b110cbe229` passed [CI run 44181148596](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44181148596), with no failed jobs, and [the final Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44183867924). It merged as [bc1e334](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bc1e334da0819f83d5aaaf5c0513a325439b9fa4). No failed-CI exception was used.
- After @VACInc updated the branch from main, a fresh independent P0–P3 review of the complete eight-file delta and seven current owner/caller contexts found no actionable issues. All 64 preparation and refresh integration tests passed on that exact head, covering upstream preparation changes, private access, saved work and publication recovery. The diff check passed.
- Cross-session coauthor publication and registered-action preparation regressions cover appending to the original PR and importing its exact head without a prior session receipt. Earlier focused validation passed 170 tests, including existing author/operator, private-access, saved-workspace, pagination and changed-head cases; follow-up integrated validation passed 117 tests.
- [ClawSweeper’s recovery-advice finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200236#issuecomment-6927955101) is resolved. Both raw/tool regressions failed before the fix, then all 43 inspector cases passed. ClawSweeper revision 3 found no actionable issues on the preceding head; the independent final-head review additionally covered main’s updated preparation context.
- Tool guidance is shorter than the pre-change version in all three modes: host by 95 characters, managed by 146, child-only by 45. Earlier scoped validation passed all 31 tool tests, 15 prefix-stability tests, six current prompt snapshots, publication-boundary type-checking, lint and formatting. No new prompting, role, grant, configuration or upgrade requirement was added.
- Read-only live lookups on [#190124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190124) and [#199842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199842) recognized the existing contributor and rejected an unrelated account. No live cross-session write or private-repository end-to-end operation was performed.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: feat(ui): give each rail section its own sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every rail section opens the same Sessions sidebar, so Dashboards, Users, Automations and Customize have no list of their own beside their pages.

## User Impact

Pages open from a rail menu (⋯). Dashboards, Users (with Activity), Automations and Customize each show their own sidebar, however their page is reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces per-section sidebars and the pages menu; later PRs in this series fill each section's list.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock at the end of the series, so the after image can show later parts too.

Dashboards before and after (left: main, right: after):

![Dashboards before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/831fce8d-93a9-4a32-8591-e96a1790148f)

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes at this PR's head.
- The unit tests of the files this PR touches pass at its head; the full UI unit suite passes at the end of the series (one failure also on main: a Workboard German relative-time string, "vor 1min", from the local ICU).
- `dashboard-website` and `sidebar-customization` UI e2e pass at this head.
- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.


## Update: Dashboards stays a gallery

Dashboards no longer gets a section sidebar. It stays the gallery (grid or list, search, author filter, display menu), now held in the same 1120px page column as Usage, and the rail's pages menu still opens it.
- Each card and list row has a three-dots menu with "Pin to the sidebar" / "Unpin from the sidebar", which puts the dashboard on the rail like other pins.
- With no dashboards, the gallery shows a sample dashboard illustration, "No dashboards yet", and a New session button.
- The navigation catalog's dashboard list and the boot snapshot's dashboard rows are gone with the sidebar; pinned dashboards resolve their row on their own.
- E2E run: dashboard-gallery, dashboards-list-demand (one dashboard request per tab), dashboard-website, session-list-row-events.

Side rail series, part 4 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199824; review only this PR's commits.


## Update: e2e repair

The full Control UI e2e run on the stack found tests this PR broke or product gaps it introduced; this PR now carries their fixes:
- test(ui): start recovered-search e2e tests beside the Sessions list
- test(ui): measure the default rail pins in the rail pitch e2e
- test(ui): drop the Dashboards case from the sidebar scroll e2e
- test(ui): expect no Sessions child read beside the Dashboards sidebar in the row-event e2e
- test(ui): drop the Sessions row check on Activity in the identity links e2e
- test(ui): reopen the pages menu before reading plugin selection in native navigation e2e
- test(ui): follow the gallery's own query beside the Dashboards sidebar list
- test(ui): read the closed pages menu's Dashboards item in the gallery e2e
- test(ui): reopen the session for its Sessions list in the identity links e2e
- test(ui): leave Systems through a page without a sidebar in the Systems e2e

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

Vyctor approved the measured JavaScript byte cost for this navigation stack. These cumulative measurements compare this layer with paired main base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`. Each cap equals the original main cap plus the measured delta, preserving existing headroom without adding another margin.

| Metric | Cumulative gzip delta | Cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest JS asset | +3,025 B | 575,465 B |
| Chat boot JS | +3,221 B | 1,328,801 B |

## What Problem This Solves

While you dictate in the Control UI, a bright highlight keeps circling the composer's border. It repeats what the voice indicator in the composer already shows, the motion never stops at the edge of the main input, and a maintainer reported it made him dizzy. In practice it shows up as a faint arc moving along the top edge rather than a clear state signal.

## User Impact

The composer stays still while you dictate. The voice indicator and the Stop and Send buttons show that the mic is listening.

## Why This Change Was Made

The circling border is one pseudo-element with its own gradient, keyframes and reduced-motion override in `ui/src/styles/chat/composer.css`. This removes that block and nothing else: the dictating composer keeps its light-mode frame and the incognito dashed edge. The corner-shape test drops its case for the removed pseudo-element.

Production: 51 lines removed. Tests: 1 case removed, no tests added.

## Evidence

Composer while dictating, same mocked Gateway, viewport and crop on both sides (Chromium, light theme).

prs.title: improve(ui): show dictation status beside Stop and Send so the composer keeps its height
prs.body:
Closes #200694

Stacked on #200234 (voice timeline). This branch contains #200234's commits, merges of current main, and three commits on top; review only `improve(ui): show dictation status in the composer's button row`, `improve(ui): keep pending-transcript status beside Stop and Send on phones` and `fix(ui): keep the one-line phone composer's status row while transcripts are pending`. Merge #200234 first.

## What Problem This Solves

Starting dictation in the Control UI adds a row with the voice bars (and "Listening…" on wider screens) above the draft, so the composer grows and the draft jumps when dictation starts and again when it stops.

## User Impact

User impact: on desktop and tablet widths the composer keeps its height when you start or stop dictating. The dictation status appears in the bottom row, beside Stop and Send.

## Why This Change Was Made

- During dictation the bottom row hides the model and speed pickers and keeps only Stop and Send. The dictation status fills that free space instead of opening a row of its own. This applies to the chat composer, the new-session page and side chat.
- The status row wrapper that only dictation used is removed with its styles, including its ease-in, since the status has no row of its own to ease in.
- After Stop, pending transcripts keep the status visible (with its announcements) while the pickers return. In the narrow phone toolbar the status then sits just before Stop and Send instead of leading the row.
- The one-line phone composer (empty draft) has no free cell, because its draft cell shows the transcript. There the status keeps its own row between any replies or attachments and the draft, for as long as the status shows, including while transcripts are still pending after Stop.
- Known limit: at phone width with a draft, the composer gets 8px shorter when dictation starts, because the hidden model picker's closed box is 44px tall while the row's buttons are 36px.

## Evidence

The Control UI ran with a mocked Gateway and a fake microphone. Each image shows #200234's head on the left and this branch on the right, typing on top and dictating below.

Desktop, 1000px: the composer stays 88px tall (on #200234 it grows from 88px to 117px).

![Composer at desktop width, before and after: typing, then dictating](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b008e4201b3713c2a47ba2c6638b2c9591b78966/images/2026/11/270f2384-6b54-4ce6-9ffe-0ef9c09111e1.png)

Phone, 390px, with a draft: the bars sit beside Stop and Send (on #200234 the composer grows by 24px; here it shrinks by 8px).

![Composer at phone width, before and after: typing, then dictating](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/b008e4201b3713c2a47ba2c6638b2c9591b78966/images/2026/11/414e38d0-e2f6-4eb2-a61e-8e4d82f829d6.png)

Phone, 390px, empty draft, stopped before the transcript arrives: the status keeps its own row above the draft and buttons. The left side shows the layout with that row tied to capture instead of the visible status, where the status overlaps them.

![One-line phone composer after Stop with a transcript pending, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/836256746b5975d44f0fc9351942a20a063d34fe/images/2026/11/0d9565ce-a4d9-4a14-b03c-637607b24f46.png)

Tests:

- The guest dictation browser test checks that the desktop composer keeps its height once listening starts. It fails on #200234 (117px instead of 88px) and passes here.
- A phone browser test stops dictation from an empty one-line composer before any transcript arrives and checks that the status overlaps neither the draft nor the buttons. It fails with the row tied to capture and passes here.
- Dictation browser suite (`browser-dictation-status.e2e.test.ts`): 14 passed. It covers the chat and new-session composers, transcripts that arrive after Stop, and a 320px composer with the long microphone permission hint, which wraps beside Stop and Send.
- Unit tests for dictation, the chat composer, chat view, goals and the new-session composer: 223 passed. `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`: 59 passed (three cases timed out once under heavy machine load and passed on rerun).
- UI typecheck (app and tests), lint and format are clean on the changed files.
- Not covered: side chat was not run in a browser, and no real microphone was used.

prs.title: improve(ui): show the voice level as a timeline across the composer
prs.body:
Closes #200233

## What Problem This Solves

While you dictate or use Talk in the Control UI, the voice level shows as seven bars that pulse together in a small fixed spot, so it reads as one block going up and down rather than as your voice.

## User Impact

User impact: while you dictate or talk, a strip of fine bars shows your recent speech sliding in from the right across the free width of the composer. Pauses show as gaps, and silence settles into a row of dots. On phones the strip alone shows that dictation is listening.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Dictation and Talk share one level meter. It draws a timeline: each new level enters on the right and slides left, and both ends fade out. Bars are 2px wide on a 4px pitch, and their number follows the width the meter gets.
- Dictation: "Listening…" comes first and the timeline fills the rest of the status row, and its shimmer sweeps every 4s. On phone widths the label is hidden and the timeline alone shows listening. When dictation starts, the status row eases in (height and opacity, 0.18s) instead of pushing the draft down in one frame. This applies in the chat composer, the new-session page and side chat.
- Talk: the timeline grows with the composer's width up to 160px, and phone-width composers keep it at 56px. While Talk runs, the model and speed pickers sit further left to make room.
- Connecting sweeps a highlight across the dots, thinking drifts two slow waves across the bars, and with reduced motion each state keeps its own still shape: an even row of short bars while listening, taller bars in the middle while thinking, and dim dots while connecting.
- The Talk benchmark's `--trace` layer snapshot now records the meter host and its canvas instead of the seven bar spans it used to expect.
- Audio capture, levels and settings are unchanged.

## Evidence

The Control UI ran with a mocked Gateway and a fake microphone. Main and this branch got the same made-up speech levels.

Light, 1000px:
![Before and after, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/32622310b6426310735ef029731f26f21a7012f7/images/2026/11/b7fd9673-c5d7-4594-bff7-5dffdb4d6c20.png)

![Before and after, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/32622310b6426310735ef029731f26f21a7012f7/images/2026/11/1ba186d5-c5c2-48b1-bc8d-f052ee046299.png)

![Before and after, phone width](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/32622310b6426310735ef029731f26f21a7012f7/images/2026/11/836519ad-b101-4a57-92ec-badac5b0bca2.png)

Entering dictation, 900px, played 10 times slower (before: the row appears in one frame; after: it eases in):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ebd6f46-53ee-4d90-85fe-ca2ef4f09555

"Listening…" shimmer, 900px, label enlarged 2x (2.4s sweep before, 4s after):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43c95aaa-f26a-4f96-9f70-c130a9d2f6b8

Dictation on a phone, 390px (the label is hidden and the timeline fills the row):

Tests: the meter, canvas, chat view, composer and dictation unit tests pass (165), and so do the dictation, Talk and microphone browser suites (13, 11 and 2) and the responsive chat layout test (59). The phone dictation test now expects the label hidden and the timeline in the row; it fails on the previous head (`expected true to be false`) and passes here. `scripts/bench-control-ui-talk.ts --trace --states speaking` against a production bundle of this branch failed before the benchmark fix (`Expected seven Talk meter spans, found 0`) and now completes, recording the host and canvas layers. The Control UI performance check passes against base 9323fb9 (total CSS raw +50 B). Typecheck, lint and format are clean. In the browser, Talk was checked at 1000, 760, 660, 600, 520 and 390px, with the default and a long model name, with no control pushed out of the row or overlapping another. Dictation was checked in the chat composer, the new-session page and side chat. Not covered: a real microphone, and recordings of the connecting and thinking states.

Both are fixed on this branch with a regression test each; the review was not rerun on the final head 903a34c.

prs.title: fix(agents): long provider error messages stall the Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one failed model request whose error message carries a long run of id-like text (letters or digits joined by `-`, `.`, `:` or `/`) freezes the whole Gateway for about 20 seconds and makes that failed turn take 11 to 29 seconds longer.

## User Impact

User impact: a provider, proxy or local model server that answers with a large error body no longer blocks other sessions, channels, the Control UI or `/healthz` while OpenClaw classifies and logs that error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three checks on the provider failure path start with an id-like pattern and then look for a fixed part after it. On a long id-like run without that fixed part, the engine walks to the end of the run from every position in it, so the cost grows with the square of the run length:

- the Ollama retirement check in `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` (`<id> was retired at <date> ... (ref:`), used by failover classification, error observation and the auth-key rate-limit check
- the same retirement wording in the run failover policy
- the `x-api-key: ...` style header pattern in the diagnostic credential redaction that projects every provider error

The streaming transport reads up to 64 KB of an error body, and one failure classifies and projects the message several times. In the run below the redaction runs on the Gateway main thread, and the retirement checks add their time to the failed turn.

Each check now finds its fixed part first (` was retired at ...`, or the credential header name and its colon) and then looks back over the id or header prefix with the same pattern. They accept exactly the same inputs as before, the redacted text is byte-identical, and each character is scanned a bounded number of times. In the failover policy the retirement wording moves out of the shared alternation into its own check with the same word boundaries.

## Evidence

Gateway from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run`), loopback, `/v1/chat/completions` enabled, with a mock OpenAI-compatible provider on loopback that answers HTTP 400 with the named error message. A separate process requests `/healthz` every 100 ms during the turn.

| Checkout | Provider error message | Turn | Longest `/healthz` wait | Gateway stall report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main `cb8c849` | prose control, 64,000 chars | 2.7 s | 77 ms | none |
| main `cb8c849` | `-a` repeated, 64,000 chars | 31.2 s | 20,369 ms | `main-thread stall: elapsedMs=17715 task="gateway:http"`, profile in `redactCredentialText` |
| main `cb8c849` | `a:` repeated, 64,000 chars | 13.8 s | 511 ms | none |
| this branch | prose control | 1.7 s | 109 ms | none |
| this branch | `-a` repeated | 1.8 s | 315 ms | one 324 ms report |
| this branch | `a:` repeated | 1.6 s | 67 ms | none |

The `a:` run leaves the credential header pattern fast (`:` ends its run), so its 11 extra seconds on main come from the retirement checks alone. Each turn made exactly one provider request on both checkouts. The branch rows come from two Gateway runs of the same commit `4175774`.

Rebased on main `fe3df80d15` (2026-11-17) after #200073 and #199234 added tests at the same place in `live-model-errors.test.ts` and `credential-redaction.test.ts`. Both sets of tests are kept, and the source changes are unchanged. The three test files pass (40 tests) on the rebased head.

With only the two retirement checks fixed, the same `-a` turn still blocked `/healthz` for 18.7 s, and the Gateway stall profile pointed at `redactCredentialText` under `projectProviderError`. That is why the credential header pattern is part of this change.

Single calls on a 64,000-character `-a` run:

| Helper | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isModelNotFoundErrorMessage` | 3,915 ms | 2.8 ms |
| `classifyFailoverReason` | 4,151 ms | 43 ms |
| `isApiKeyRateLimitError` | 3,885 ms | 13 ms |
| `buildApiErrorObservationFields` | 7,485 ms | 91 ms |
| `redactDiagnosticText` | 3,737 ms | 45 ms |
| `projectProviderError` | 14,009 ms | 210 ms |

Differential fuzzers compared old and new results on 600,000 random strings per check. The strings mix id characters, spaces, newlines, quotes, partial and complete retirement suffixes, the other model-not-found phrases, and credential header names with and without `x-` style prefixes. They found 0 differences in `.test()` results for both retirement checks and 0 differences in `replace()` output for the header pattern (about 15,000 of those strings were redacted).

Commands run on this branch:

- `pnpm test src/agents/live-model-errors.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.test.ts packages/ai/src/utils/credential-redaction.test.ts packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all passed. The three new tests fail on main (2,228 ms, 2,375 ms and 17,917 ms against their 500 ms bound) and take a few ms here.
- `pnpm test src/agents/failover-error.test.ts src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failure.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts src/agents/payload-redaction.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 297 passed. These include the existing Ollama retirement fixtures and the provider error redaction consumers.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: OK with the 33-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/provider-error-retired-model-scan.txt`.

prs.title: fix(e2e): run update repair before the next update in the installed-recovery lane
prs.body:
Related: #200680

## What Problem This Solves

The Docker lane `pnpm test:docker:package-installed-recovery` is red on `main` in all 7 cuts. Each cut kills an update during package publication, recovers it with the printed package-activation helper, and then expects a plain `openclaw update` to succeed. That update now refuses:

> Update <id> has unfinished recovery; reconcile it before starting another update. The update lease store no longer holds that update's lease, so this update cannot show that its processes are gone. Run openclaw update repair, then retry openclaw update.

The refusal is intended. #200680 made a plain update settle a killed run's recovery only when it can show the run's processes are gone. In this lane the helper's own claim retired the dead updater's lease, and the candidate replaced the original version without being verified, so the update names `openclaw update repair`. The lane's expectation predates that gate.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The installed-recovery lane now follows the operator flow the docs describe (`docs/cli/update/how-updates-run.md`, "Replacing the package directory"): after the helper, run `openclaw update repair` once, then `openclaw update`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- At the end of each cut, after the helper archives the completed custody, the driver runs `openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart --json`. It asserts:
  - exit 0, `mode: "finalize"`, `coreUpdate: "completed"`, and status `ok` or `warning`;
  - exactly one reconciled run ID (the cut's killed update);
  - the installed version and launchers are unchanged by the repair.

  The next update then runs with all of its existing assertions. Repairing inside each cut also keeps the driver's all-cuts mode coherent: every killed update is settled before the next cut starts another update.
- The host diagnostics receipt validates the exact command sequence, so `update-repair` is now a per-cut command and a required step in a passing receipt. The command cap goes from 10 to 11 to fit it in the non-helper cuts.
- The diagnostics test checks three receipts: a complete receipt is accepted; a receipt without the next update is rejected; a receipt without `update-repair` is rejected. Against the old `diagnostics.mjs`, the complete and missing-repair cases fail; with this change all three pass.

No product code changes. No assertion, cut, or test was removed.

## Evidence

- **Red on `main` (`f2f1edd7e9f`, local Docker, all 7 cuts, fail-fast off):** every cut passed `displacement` through `archive-completed`, then `next-update` exited 1 with the refusal quoted above.
- **Measurement (repair inserted, nothing else changed):** in all 7 cuts `openclaw update repair` exited 0 with `mode: finalize`, `coreUpdate: completed`, and exactly one ID in `reconciledRuns`. That ID was the killed run that Doctor had reported as abandoned moments earlier. `next-update` and `next-update-status` then passed in every cut. `status` is `warning` only because Doctor reports fixture advisories: the Codex plugin is disabled, Skill Workshop is off, and agent database path repair was skipped.
- **Green on Linux (Crabbox, AWS `c7a.8xlarge`, lease `cbx_813d5b75f537`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_00e451fa0c10279bde1c939dbf39939a)):** `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_ALL_FAIL_FAST=0 pnpm test:docker:package-installed-recovery` with a fresh package build from source `b6439a96d4e` (this diff; the head was later rebased onto unrelated `main` commits). All 7 cuts pass, and the command exits 0. The command took 78m53s, of which the lane pool took 62m30s.
- **Green on macOS (local Docker Desktop, base package tarball reused):** 6 of 7 cuts pass end to end in 41m23s. On macOS, `partial-previous` passes every driver step, repair and next update included, then fails at the access-reader container check. That check expects `readdir("/private")` to throw `EACCES` for an unrelated uid, and Docker Desktop bind mounts do not enforce host permissions. The same check passes on Linux above.

<details>
<summary>Checks and notes</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-installed-recovery.test.ts test/scripts/upgrade-survivor-installed-recovery-diagnostics.test.ts`: 46 passed, 5 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `keeps shared evidence readable through restrictive umask`, which fails identically on `main` on this macOS host.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, `pnpm tsgo:all`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main --no-merge-base`: pass. These ran on the first revision. The second revision changed the same three files the same way and passed CI.
- The `main` movement since the red run was checked. The update-CLI changes in it are an include-config refusal message and an `extended-stable` explicit-tag path, and neither reaches this lane's single-file `stable` fixture. The rest is UI, iOS, agent-tool, and autoreview files. The Linux run built the package from a post-movement base (`a7f5a0e295e`).

</details>

**Not proven here:**
- The autoreview helper does not run on this machine. A separate read-only reviewer reviewed the diff instead. Its should-fix findings were addressed: repair runs per cut, a negative receipt test was added, and the version and launcher are checked after repair.
- The driver's all-cuts mode (no cut selected) is not run by any lane and was not run here. In that mode, if the repair's Doctor wrote config bookkeeping, the next cut's full-bytes config check would fail. Whether repair writes config was not observed.
- The `older-runtime` installed-recovery lane is outside this family and was not run.

prs.title: fix(security): webhook content with long blank runs stalls the Gateway
prs.body:
Related: #104038

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a webhook body that contains a long run of blank lines freezes the whole Gateway for about 20 seconds, and the hook request is then refused with HTTP 503.

## User Impact

User impact: hook content such as an email body or a webhook payload with long blank or repeated runs is admitted like any other body. Other channels, the Control UI and `/healthz` keep responding while it is scanned.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before a hook turn starts, `detectSuspiciousPatterns` runs its prompt-injection monitoring patterns over the whole hook body. Four of those patterns rescan the same line or whitespace run from every later position, so their cost grows with the square of the run length:

- `^\s*System:\s+` restarts at every line start of a blank run
- `system\s*:?\s*(...)` lets two whitespace quantifiers split one run in every possible way
- `\]\s*\n\s*...` does the same around the first newline
- `\bexec\b.*command\s*=` rescans the rest of the line from every `exec`

Each rewritten pattern matches exactly the same inputs and scans the body once. The `System:` check starts at the last line start before the marker, the optional colon no longer sits between two overlapping whitespace runs, the bracket check stops its first whitespace run at the newline, and the `exec` check starts only at the first `exec` of a line (a later `exec` can only see a subset of the same tail).

The scan still covers the whole body, so a marker in the middle of a large body is still reported. This is the monitoring contract that the bounded head and tail window in #104038 gave up.

The warning log lists the matched pattern sources, so the four rewritten sources read differently in that log line. Nothing else consumes them.

## Evidence

Gateway from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run`), loopback, hooks enabled with a test token, mock OpenAI-compatible model on loopback. Each body is POSTed to `/hooks/agent` with `waitForCompletion: true` while a separate process requests `/healthz` every 100 ms.

| Checkout | Body | Hook response | Longest `/healthz` wait | Gateway stall report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main `cb8c849` | prose control, 233,622 chars | HTTP 200, run ok | 123 ms | none |
| main `cb8c849` | `start`, 120,000 newlines, `end` | HTTP 503, run did not start before admission timeout | 21,609 ms | `main-thread stall: elapsedMs=21544 task="gateway:http"`, profile in `src/security/external-content.ts` |
| this branch | prose control | HTTP 200, run ok | 125 ms | none |
| this branch | `start`, 120,000 newlines, `end` | HTTP 200, run ok | 184 ms | none |
| this branch | blank runs, `exec` line, `system` plus spaces, `]` plus newlines | HTTP 200, run ok | 243 ms | none |

Equivalence of each rewritten pattern with the original was checked with a differential fuzzer over 600,000 random strings built from the tokens these patterns care about (`System`, `exec`, `command`, `]`, `[user]:`, colons, spaces, tabs, `\r`, `\n`, U+2028, U+2029, NBSP and others). It found 0 differences in `.test()` results for all four patterns. Single-pattern timing on 64,000-character inputs:

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 64,000 newlines, `System:` check | 5,724 ms | 0.8 ms |
| `exec ` repeated, `exec` check | 1,401 ms | 0.4 ms |
| `system` then 64,000 spaces | 6,024 ms | 0.3 ms |
| `]` then 64,000 newlines, bracket check | 6,835 ms | 0.3 ms |

Commands run on this branch:

- `pnpm test src/security/external-content.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 12 passed. The new test fails on main (33,619 ms against its 500 ms bound) and passes here (24 ms).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: OK with the 18-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/hook-content-pattern-scan.txt`.

prs.title: fix(tests): keep tunnel redial deadlines pending
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Swift server-key redial test can fail with a deadline error instead of the expected connection refusal. Its fake clock completes every sleep immediately, including the five-second connection deadline.

## User Impact

This is a test-only repair. It keeps the redial and refused-verification coverage reliable without changing transport behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing cancellation-aware waiter for the injected clock, matching neighboring refusal tests. The connection refusal now determines the result; the losing deadline is canceled. All key, dial-count, error, and shutdown assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- [Main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44169263969/job/134344575930): the redial case expected `.closed` but received `.deadline`.
- Reproduced the same failure in the unchanged 20-test `OpenClawIDNodeTunnelTests` suite. With this one-line change, all 20 tests passed in 1.071 seconds, including the affected redial case.
- The complete Swift package tree used for the sandboxed macOS proof matches the frozen base `91070099ea62e36470fa359222e87019fd91003a`. The candidate test file matches this commit. Xcode 27.2 built the test targets; the incremental candidate build completed in 12.10 seconds.
- SwiftFormat, strict SwiftLint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed `91070099..0cb61c0d3273` and found no correctness or security findings (confidence 0.96). Its review was source-only; the execution evidence above was collected separately.

<details>
<summary>Focused execution output</summary>

Before:

```text
every redial reverifies the server key and A refusal never dials
Expectation failed: expected error ".closed", but ".deadline" was thrown instead
Test run with 20 tests in 1 suite failed after 1.079 seconds with 1 issue.
```

After:

```text
Test run with 20 tests in 1 suite passed after 1.071 seconds.
```

</details>

## CI follow-up

Exact-head [CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44175194420) completed with one underlying failure: the [Android 16 KiB lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44175194420/job/134365799612) could not resolve its test dependencies after Maven Central returned HTTP 429 for the Kotlin Compose Gradle plugin. The aggregate gate failed as a result. Android instrumentation tests did not execute in that lane.

The actual CI checkout was merge `a4ae6847cd0f9ca67feba14ea04e8e2634b42d8e`, with ordered parents `4764444d3c278e159117131eaffe10d290dba99b` and this PR head. Its Android and workflow trees exactly match that main baseline. The failure is an external dependency-download limit, unrelated to the Swift test-clock change.
