prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background reviews and plugin forks of sandbox-required managed-worktree chats can fail with `Local sandbox managed workspace owner changed` before reaching the model. Tool-free forks began taking this path in #200545; every caller of the shared fork runner is affected.

## User Impact

Sandboxed forks can review the source conversation using its existing private workspace. Host-executed forks keep their durable workspace behavior. No configuration, schema, protocol, or public Plugin SDK change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareSessionFork` selects the durable project workspace (`src/agents/session-fork-run.ts:175`), which the runner previously also passed to sandbox preparation. When that checkout is outside the managed worktree, the projection owner's containment check correctly refuses it (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.ts:634`).

Fork execution now uses `resolveIngressWorkspaceOverrideForSessionRun` (`src/agents/spawned-context.ts:94`), the same recorded-workspace contract ordinary turns consume (`src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts:277`). The existing sandbox-policy owner selects this only for sandboxed managed-worktree runs. There is no registry-path derivation or second workspace owner, and the projection guard is unchanged.

I checked #190158 and its predecessor #189302: the durable workspace replaced Workshop-only ambient plumbing and kept review context out of disposable worktrees. This change retains it for policy preparation and the SessionManager/transcript cwd; the parent's pinned prompt and request replay are preserved. Cancellation, source fences, admission, and plugin authority checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

The existing transport harness now exercises the public `subagent.forkSession` API, real embedded runner, real managed-worktree registry and real projection owner with a durable project workspace outside the worktree. Only the external container backend and loopback model transport are fixtures. Both variants receive `fork-ok`; the required-sandbox variant also persists its workspace projection. The existing stranger-access denial, parent thinking, pinned prompt, and history assertions remain.

`pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugin-subagent-runtime.fork-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

- Base: **1 failed, 1 passed**. Required sandbox fails with `Local sandbox managed workspace owner changed` at `resolveLocalWorkspaceOwner`; host execution passes.
- Fix: **2 passed**, 18.90 s Vitest wall time (21.21 s wrapper); test bodies total 9.99 s. CI timing will be available in the PR checks.

Validation: `pnpm tsgo:core`; gateway-server test-shard typecheck; focused oxlint; focused format check; `git diff --check`; `pnpm build` (2m 47.4s).

The patch adds 17 net production lines, 48 net test lines and five documentation lines. The test growth supplies a real managed-worktree fixture and external backend fixture within the existing harness; it proves the failure through model transport without duplicating the test setup or mocking workspace ownership. No test-line ceiling or allocation was changed.

Codex autoreview against base `91070099`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings on the final local change. The first preparation was rejected because the running build created a temporary declaration file; after that input settled, the complete review succeeded. No review guard was bypassed.

Sibling checks passed: session-fork policy/result tests (4), prompt-prefix stability (15), plugin fork authority/cancellation (9), and both real Gateway plugin-fork E2E suites (8). Total: 36 sibling tests.

CI attempt 1: four check jobs failed during runner setup, before tests or static checks, because the external Git package source returned HTTP 503. The affected jobs are `checks-node-changed-1`, `checks-node-changed-3`, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-1`, and `checks-node-compact-small-1`. Their setup inputs are unchanged by this patch. [Representative failed setup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44175095146/job/134365280071). Attempt 2 reran only the failed jobs and their aggregate gate; all four replacement test shards passed. The HTTP 503 setup failure did not recur.

## Why This Change Was Made

Match the boot editor to the existing mobile three-line cap and width-specific padding. Let decorative loading messages yield space at both landscape widths, and remove the obsolete whole-frame scroll cap. The live composer and handoff logic remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the exact [main CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44169263969/job/134344576560) on the unchanged boot HTML: frame height changed from 112px to 140px at handoff.

prs.title: fix: keep transcript backfill probes from blocking conversation appends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background transcript-facts coverage checks can reserve the single SQLite writer even though they only read. A slow probe then holds up new conversation events behind it.

## User Impact

Conversation appends no longer wait behind backfill discovery or coverage probes for writer admission. Actual backfill batches retain foreground priority, pacing, cursor resumability and transactional coverage checks. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic request-class list does not decide admission. Both reads were sent through the publication store, which always reserves the canonical writer. Move them to the existing session-history reader pool and delete the writable commands; open the write client only for a real batch. Read pacing uses its own elapsed request time. Existing write pacing already includes admitted preparation/commit/reply time, yields to queued foreground work and backs off on busy errors.

This also fixes discovery, the sibling read with the same routing error. Projection maintenance can mutate state and stays on the writer. Production code grows by 64 lines to wire the typed reader protocol; there is no new cache or scheduling owner.

## Evidence

The real scheduler regression fails on baseline `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110` because discovery/probes claim writer reservations. With the fix, covered probes finish while a real foreground actor append is queued behind a held writer; releasing the barrier commits the append. Seven backfill tests preserve completion, `afterPosition`, interleaved mutation and restoration behavior. Startup/idle consumers add 15 passing tests, writer admission 34, command census 2. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Five serial A1/A2/B groups used identical harness bytes, fresh clones of a synthetic 35.02-GiB, 3.2M-event, 12,481-session database, and 1,000 measured actor appends per arm. Median probe writer occupation: **177 / 155 / 0 ms**. Foreground queue maxima across groups: **56–289 / 49–389 / 0–1 ms**; median total queue wait per 1,000 appends: **185 / 163 / 0 ms**. Median process CPU: **1941 / 2091 / 2075 ms**. Separate sampled host allocations: **222.5 / 225.7 / 222.5 MB**. All controls and adverse results are retained; no CPU improvement is claimed. Reproduction harness and fixture instructions are included. This partial-pass macOS workload does not prove btrfs commit latency, readiness, or whole-database completion time.

Chromium transcript browser tests: 32 passed. UI E2E: 12 passed, one inherited WebKit history test failure. The failure reproduces on the exact baseline above (30 messages instead of 190). Commit `99eb4aa8ce76a5e6d47ac6f5d672499fcb10cf4f` changed the test's WebKit action from wheel scrolling to `Home`; restoring only that wheel action on the baseline passes. This main test regression is recorded for separate repair. No UI runtime imports were introduced.

`pnpm check:changed` and `pnpm build` passed. ClawSweeper reviewed the final head with [zero findings and no open items](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200794#issuecomment-6960696530). The [synthetic reservation and tick trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200794#issuecomment-6960872523) provides inspectable transport evidence. Exact-head PR CI remains the landing gate.

prs.title: fix(sessions): load chats with sparse transcripts on the embedded runtime
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A conversation with large gaps in its stored transcript sequence can fail to load when an agent resumes it on the embedded runtime. Load navigation pages from the rows that exist so the read can finish and the turn can continue.

## What Problem This Solves

Resuming a conversation can return `Session entry changed during read` before making a model request. Retrying the same turn can reproduce the error even while the store is idle.

## User Impact

The embedded runtime can use existing conversation history with sparse sequence numbers. Model routing, session identity, and existing transcript storage are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Build the navigation cache from occupied pages on a cold read. On subsequent reads, check the receipts for those pages and discover pages for new rows when reading the appended suffix. Existing validation of transcript rewrites and concurrent writes stays in place.

### Root Cause

The reader registered a scoped write receipt for every 512-position range through the highest raw sequence, including ranges with no rows. A sparse sequence could consume the bounded receipt cache and retire the session and transcript receipts captured by that same read. On an isolated snapshot of an affected transcript, the receipt cell identities changed on all three attempts while the scoped write revisions, schema revision, and database identity stayed constant. The writer-admitted retry consequently failed the same validation.

### Regression attribution

Source history points to #196484 (`261b24e6bc8`), which changed transcript acceptance from a database-wide write revision to scoped session and transcript receipts. #174435 introduced scanning page numbers from zero through the highest sequence. #176646 bounded receipt retention. Together, those changes let a read retire its own validation cells without a committed write. A historical bisect was outside the verification done here.

## Verification

### Real behavior proof

- Base `0b1c20f3acc`: a synthetic transcript with messages on either side of a gap fails in the production SessionManager and SQLite worker with `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError`.
- Candidate: the same regression reads both messages, then reads the complete context after appending a follow-up. The existing same-session and unrelated-session writer scenarios also pass.
- An isolated copy of an affected transcript reproduced the error on the base and loaded successfully with the candidate using the same model-context reader.
- Synthetic cold read work count derived from the fixture and page size: **7,813 → 2** scoped navigation page lookups per attempt. The worker regression finished in 10.17 s on the failing base and 1.66 s on the candidate, including fixture setup. Those are single test observations with different terminal outcomes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted lint and format, and `git diff --check` passed.

<details>
<summary>Focused command</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-transcript-context-read.worker.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-model-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

### Follow-through verification — 2026-11-17

Verified unchanged head `d5ec470478fecb783ba6927871753cfca43fec11`:

- Independent autoreview of the entire candidate through P3 completed with a validated `scoped-clean` result and no actionable findings. No hostile behavior identified in the reviewed changes.
- Full runtime build completed successfully, including native declarations, plugin assets, CLI bootstrap checks, and runtime postbuild checks.
- **45 focused tests passed** across the transcript worker, SQLite model-context, and bounded-context suites.
- **25 additional tests passed**: actor entry/transcript residency suites plus a task-local sparse-boundary variant. The variant warms the context at sequence `4_000_255`, then appends into the previously absent next page and verifies complete context.
- A task-local sparse-prefix proof passed: a same-generation rewrite of a discarded prefix row produces the same compact prefix counts/bytes and model context as an independently cold-seeded read. Two initial proof-fixture errors (cold reads do not expose compact prefix facts, and the row API returns parsed events) were corrected; no production change was needed.
- A task-local end-to-end proof passed through a real isolated Gateway and the embedded runtime, with a synthetic persisted sparse transcript and a loopback Responses model. Both historical messages and the resumed input reached the provider, and the expected reply completed. The test uses the normal Gateway/runtime path, not the minimal-Gateway fixture.
- Repeated the committed sparse regression with only the production page reader reverted to the pinned base: it failed with `SessionEntryChangedDuringReadError`. Restored the exact candidate reader afterward; candidate-focused and end-to-end proof above passed.

The extra proof fixtures are task-local verification artifacts, not permanent CI-suite additions. No production or committed-test changes were needed during follow-through. Exact-head CI and hosted reviewer results remain separate landing gates; local proof does not waive them.

### What was not tested

A live Telegram session and an external model-provider round trip were not rerun. The completed round-trip proof uses an isolated Gateway, synthetic persisted history, and a loopback model fixture.

## Evidence

The change removes per-page scan cursors and eliminates page creation for gaps. The existing transcript snapshot still owns rewrite receipts, append bounds, and cached prefix accounting. Production diff: +35 / −30 lines. Regression: +63 lines.

The earlier interrupted build and inconclusive autoreview were superseded by the completed follow-through verification above. The committed regression is `loads bounded model context across large transcript sequence gaps`.

prs.title: fix: let Doctor reclaim updater runtimes on Macs running node hosts or the app
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each OpenClaw update keeps a private copy of the running runtime (about 3.7 GB here) and relies on later updates or `openclaw doctor --fix` to delete copies nothing uses. On a Mac that runs node-host services or the macOS app, that cleanup never deletes anything. Every copy is refused with "other OpenClaw processes are still running", so one copy accumulates per update. On the reporting Mac, nine had built up since 2026-10-30.

## User Impact

On macOS, updates and `openclaw doctor --fix` can now reclaim abandoned updater runtimes while node hosts, the macOS app, its node worker, and helper programs the Gateway started are running. A process that references the copy still keeps it, and so does a CLI process whose command cannot be identified. The Doctor or updater doing the cleanup must contain this fix. It also reclaims copies left by older updaters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Without a path reference, the census counted every OpenClaw-looking process as a possible holder of every copy, because an updater creates its copy in-process before anything references it. Only the Gateway family was exempt. On the reporting Mac, the census (run read-only against a dummy path) named these as holders. All had readable working directories, and none were reported as "unknown":

- **Node-host services:** `node openclaw.mjs … node run` launchers, plus the CLI child each starts, whose process title erases its argv to `openclaw`. The node command never runs the updater.
- **The macOS app:** `OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw` matched the CLI-name rule case-insensitively. The native app starts every CLI command, `update` included, as a separate child.
- **The app's node worker:** titled `openclaw-node-worker`.
- **Non-OpenClaw helpers:** `op daemon`, `keyboxd` and `adb` inherited `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER` from the Gateway service environment. The Darwin reader passed the marker for every executable. Linux reads it only for JS runtimes.

The fix stays inside the census owner and the Darwin command reader:

- `node`, alongside `gateway`, counts as a command that never updates.
- The `openclaw-node-worker` title and the macOS app bundle's native executable count as non-updaters.
- A title-erased `openclaw` child counts as a non-updater only when its live parent's intact argv names a non-updating command. Respawn and node-host launchers keep their argv for exactly this purpose.
- The Darwin reader reports the service marker only for JS runtimes, matching Linux.

What still retains a copy:

- Any argv, cwd or executable reference to the copy.
- A title-erased CLI under any other parent, including a titled Gateway, whose `update.run` spawns one.
- `update` and `doctor` launchers.
- Update workers.

Platform scope: the command and launcher rules also apply on Linux and Windows, where the same processes exist. The app and marker rules apply only on macOS. The handoff branch is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Behavior checked.** The repro uses a private temp dir as the projection root, a fixture package root with the real retained-runtime marker, the real `maintainRetainedUpdateRuntimes` cleanup as Doctor calls it, and processes the test spawned. The host's other processes stay visible, so the cleanup still refuses because of unrelated live update work on the host. The table shows which of the test's own PIDs the refusal names.

Base `d0a5dbb9c13`, unmodified census and reader (red):

```text
BLOCKS   node-run launcher (intact argv)
BLOCKS   non-JS helper with inherited OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER
BLOCKS   OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw
BLOCKS   title 'openclaw-node-worker'
BLOCKS   node-run CLI child (title 'openclaw')
BLOCKS   CONTROL holder: cwd inside the copy
BLOCKS   CONTROL CLI of unknown command (title 'openclaw', non-launcher parent)
other host PIDs listed: 28
```

This branch (green):

```text
ignored  node-run launcher (intact argv)
ignored  non-JS helper with inherited OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER
ignored  OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw
ignored  title 'openclaw-node-worker'
ignored  node-run CLI child (title 'openclaw')
BLOCKS   CONTROL holder: cwd inside the copy
BLOCKS   CONTROL CLI of unknown command (title 'openclaw', non-launcher parent)
other host PIDs listed: 13
```

**Tests.** Each new or changed case fails on base and passes here:

- **Native macOS census test** with real processes. Every fixture runs the signed Node binary, exec'd through symlinks named `helper` and `OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw`. The Darwin reader reports a symlink exec's own path as the executable. No signed binary is copied or re-signed, because relocated copies fail code-signature validation and Gatekeeper rejects them.
  - Released: the node-run launcher and its title-erased child, the marker helper, the app-bundle image, and the node worker.
  - Retained: a cwd holder, a title-erased CLI under a shell, and Node spoofing the app path through `argv0`. An app-shaped argv alone does not exempt a JS runtime.
- **Census unit tests**, cross-platform (mocked Linux):
  - Exempt: the node launcher and its title-erased child, and `openclaw-node-worker`.
  - Still holders: a title-erased child of an `update` launcher, a title-erased child of a titled Gateway, and an `update` launcher.
- **Census unit test, mocked Darwin:** the app is released, but a title-erased bundled-runtime CLI the app starts stays a holder.
- **Darwin reader unit test:** `op daemon` with an inherited marker no longer reports it. JS runtimes still do.

**Results.**

- Focused suites pass: 188 tests across the census (unit, native, Windows, missing-command), the Doctor retained-runtime flow, update retained-runtime, and the Darwin command reader (unit and native).
- `oxlint --type-aware` is clean on the touched files.
- The core type check reports one error, in the untouched `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-websocket.ts`.
- `check-changed` passes every lane except the type-check and lint wrappers, which refuse this checkout's shared pnpm virtual store ("Declaration input escapes checkout"). I ran the linter and type checker directly instead.
- Autoreview (branch mode, through P3) is scoped-clean.

**Known gaps.**

- Gateway-family helpers outside the existing exemption still count as possible updaters: `service-child-relay`, `service-child-group-anchor`, the OpenClaw ID tunnel child, `tailscale-route-owner`, and spawn-broker `sqlite-readonly-location` workers. With a Gateway running, they can still block reclamation. Exempting them needs per-entrypoint proof that they never reach the updater in-process, so I left that for a follow-up.
- A title-erased CLI whose launcher has exited (reparented to launchd) stays conservative.
- The census does not inspect open files, which is unchanged. On the reporting Mac, node services that started before an update still map pre-update native modules whose only remaining link is inside a copy. Deleting that copy does not affect them. Their disk space is freed when those processes exit.
- No full packaged update was run.

Related: #200657 (Linux equivalent, merged) and #195162 (foreign-account unreadable cwd on Linux, a different rule; no overlap).

prs.title: fix: require consent for cross-version repair migrations
prs.body:
Fixes #200774

## What Problem This Solves

Running a newer package's `update repair` through npx can migrate databases while an older OpenClaw installation still owns the Gateway. The older release then cannot read them, and restoring configuration alone does not recover it.

## User Impact

Standalone repair names the consequence, verified backup locations, and restore instructions when a positively identified older installation cannot read the pending schema targets. Unattended runs require the existing `--yes`; healthy interactive capture uses the existing confirmation prompt. Declining restores the original managed service without switching its package.

If backup verification would require repairing live session data, an unconsented run refuses before that repair and explains the existing `--yes` retry. It preserves session windows, transcript history, FTS rows, and schema versions without claiming a verified backup group. Explicitly consented runs retain Doctor's supported repair and recovery-backup behavior.

Ordinary update finalization, same-installation, same-version, and schema-compatible repairs retain their behavior. Unknown identity or missing version/schema metadata retains existing behavior; this is an accepted edge case.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repair's parent uses its existing lifecycle ownership fact to check admission under offline maintenance before candidate Doctor's verified continuation. Ordinary finalization does not enter this repair-specific check. A narrow capture policy in the existing backup owner prevents its integrity-failure retry from repairing live session rows before consent; normal Doctor callers keep the existing default.

Existing flags, identity facts, backup formats, schemas, and wire protocols are preserved. The repairing CLI must contain this fix. The recovery documentation explains that cross-version database migrations require restoring backups to return to an older release.

## Evidence

- Original main baseline: 5 new regression cases failed and 4 controls passed, including refusal-time service replacement.
- Round-two boundary reproduction against `f9e82c3bb2d62759aca9290fb71b8f35442f6c1b`: ordinary finalization and unconsented orphan repair both failed; the explicit-consent orphan control passed. These exercise public callers and the real integrity/backup/repair owners with the existing schema-26 agent fixture.
- Fixed: **100 tests pass** across the complete repair/finalization file (26), backup owner, schema migrations, and installation suites (74). This includes all prior version/identity controls, real normal orphan migration, recovery-backup history preservation, and original-service restoration.
- Required touched-file core-leaf type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass.
- One fresh independent delta autoreview (Codex, P0–P2), against `f9e82c3bb2d62759aca9290fb71b8f35442f6c1b`: **scoped-clean**, no remaining actionable findings. The reviewer inspected supplied source and did not independently execute tests.
- pr-simplify retained the existing lifecycle and backup owners, with no duplicate repair-mode state. Round-two delta: production +40/−25 lines; tests +91/−5. The necessary growth proves and enforces the pre-consent data boundary.

Local cost: the changed repair/finalization file takes 99.45 seconds in Vitest (133.28 seconds including cold worker preparation); the three owner suites take 84.62 seconds (86.38 seconds including preparation). CI seconds are not yet available. The repair composition is needed to expose the continuation, public-caller scope, and refusal-time restoration failures; a helper-only test would miss them.

## Limits

Native-service and candidate child-process I/O are simulated; SQLite preflight, integrity, backup, repair, and maintenance owners are real. The mixed-backup control supplies PostgreSQL backup facts. No live macOS/npm released-version upgrade or PostgreSQL server recovery was run: this production host prohibits heavy proof, and configured remote proof lacked credentials before allocation. PR CI supplies broad proof.

Reported by @cbhawthorne84

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix: keep the permissions popover content-sized
prs.body:
Fixes #200635

## What Problem This Solves

In the native macOS app, opening **Full access** in an empty Main session without configured models stretches the five permission options almost to the window height. The reported Dashboard WKWebView window is 1240 × 794.

## User Impact

User impact: permission options stay compact without changing permission behavior, available modes, or the model picker.

**The reporter’s native macOS retest passed.** [Daniel’s verification and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200644#issuecomment-6956443723) use macOS 26.6.2, packageable main `3447bee`, and the exact CSS from `cdfec2d` at 1240 × 794 with an empty Main session and no models. Compact size, pointer selection, keyboard opening/navigation, numeric shortcuts, Escape, and outside-click dismissal passed. This is native evidence for the CSS change, not a native execution of the later main-refresh tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

[WebKit bug 328749](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=328749) documents the matching failure: a `position-area` grid stretches its automatic rows to the available block height, while the same content in a wrapping flex container remains content-sized.

Keep the shared Menu's flex layout and wrap the full-width permission options below the heading and Learn more link. Remove the grid and the ineffective `max-content` override. Existing anchor placement, viewport limits, keyboard order, and selection ownership stay unchanged; there is no JavaScript sizing workaround or browser detection.

## Evidence

- **Main refresh (2026-11-17):** merged `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110` into the existing PR without rewriting history; new head `0030121d10b51b48e072f5c6000b605fde053a19`. The feature delta remains the same two files. Repeated `pr-simplify`, all nine PR E2E tests, targeted format/Stylelint/Oxlint/TypeScript, and whitespace checks passed on the refreshed tree. The published tree matches the tested tree exactly. This starts fresh CI after the known Dashboard-menu flake tracked in #200660; no Actions rerun was requested.
- **Nine bundled Chromium E2E tests passed**, including 1240 × 794 with the native Dashboard chrome flags, 390 × 794 mobile editing, permission refresh/selection, new-session defaults, and existing picker interaction checks. The bundled UI build passed.
- Layout checks cover compact panel/rows, placement above the trigger, and heading/link alignment. Keyboard checks cover Learn more → first option, the Full access shortcut, Escape, and focus restoration.
- Linux WebKit source-mode checks also passed at both widths. Panel heights were 324.75 px desktop and 375.14 px mobile; option rows were 52.39–69.19 px.
- **Linux is not a native red/green reproduction:** the previous grid and even WebKit's reduced testcase remain compact in the available Linux engine. The reporter’s macOS before/after check and the upstream Safari report establish the regression evidence; see the native verification linked above. Constrained-height clipping was not qualified.
- Targeted format, Stylelint, Oxlint, TypeScript, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `pr-simplify` completed: removed the grid sizing path and ineffective height override; reused the shared flex menu with no new markup, state, positioning owner, or runtime dependency. Whole-PR delta: CSS +10/−4, tests +80/−0.
- Fresh independent source review of the revised diff found no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is not native-fix certification. The shortcut test selects the already-current Full access mode; separate permission-refresh tests cover changing permissions.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and exact checks</summary>

Base: `5230147ebfe95e1717987f1f82e18280829614eb`. Previous published candidate: `cd237e8291403e7d7b31b901de74e6115276c253`. Replacement head: `cdfec2d2e8860d96fd0d80e2fb90cbc49cfeafa2`. Refreshed base: `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110`; current head: `0030121d10b51b48e072f5c6000b605fde053a19`.

Native retest: build this head, confirm the served permission menu uses `display: flex` and wrapping rows, open an empty Main session with no models in a 1240 × 794 Dashboard window, then open Full access. Verify compact rows, selection, keyboard navigation, and dismissal.

## Summary

The alternative SQLite filename backup tests isolated OpenClaw state but still used the worker-wide temporary directory for backup scratch maintenance. It keeps scratch outside archived state and restores environment and worker custody during cleanup. All seven cases and their archive, restore, and warning assertions remain unchanged. No production behavior changes.

## Validation

- Controlled real-filesystem proof: an owned ambient scratch directory with a foreign sentinel makes the original ordinary `.db` case fail its existing empty-warning assertion; the changed fixture passes and leaves the sentinel unchanged. The actual backup and maintenance owners run in both cases.
- All seven existing alternative-filename cases pass with the candidate.
- Targeted formatter, type-aware lint, and scoped TypeScript check pass; `git diff --check` passes.

The test, both shared fixture modules, archive/scratch/SQLite owners, backup commands, and relevant test configuration match the frozen source. This is scoped owner proof, not a replay of the entire Linux CI cohort.

The separately reproduced production retirement-reservation warning remains a follow-up; this change does not suppress warnings or change filesystem/native requirements.

prs.title: fix: open model setup directly when no models are available
prs.body:
Fixes #200612

## What Problem This Solves

When the available model list is empty, opening the model control shows a large blank picker with a search field instead of taking the user to setup. This also happens on a clean installation with automatic account selection, even when no provider or account has been configured.

## User Impact

User impact: after the model list finishes loading and is confirmed empty, users can select **Set up a model** directly from the composer to open model-provider setup.

Loading, error, offline, restricted, locked, and pending-provider states retain their existing behavior. Personal/shared account recovery and other session targets keep the picker. No Gateway changes, configuration changes, or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing setup action and translated label rather than adding another setup flow. The shared model control chooses between the direct button and the picker in both existing chats and the new-session composer.

The earlier revision incorrectly treated the presence of any account section as a reason to retain the picker. The Gateway returns automatic account selection even before the first account is configured. The setup condition now accepts that selection while retaining the picker for a specifically selected personal or shared account.

The new-session page already shows its full-page setup action when no default model exists. The composer regression therefore also covers an empty available-model list with a configured default, where the shared picker is actually mounted.

## Evidence

Reproduced the reported automatic-account state before this repair: no models or configured default, no pending providers, and a successful catalog response opened the oversized empty picker. With the repair, the same existing-chat state opens **Add an account** directly. The new-session composer also opens setup directly by keyboard, and the existing full-page setup path remains working.

- All 246 focused unit/component tests across ten files passed.
- All 22 Chromium production-UI browser tests across the two PR suites passed with synthetic Gateway responses. The existing screenshots remain applicable because the bundle repair does not change the rendered controls.
- UI chat test typecheck, production UI typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent read-only source review of the lazy shortcut, row registration, and focus relocation found no actionable correctness issues. Existing assertions remain intact.

Native macOS/WKWebView has not been rechecked on the repaired head. The supplementary Linux WebKit attempt timed out, so it is not passing evidence. The [hosted control-ui-performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44166170430/job/134333815071) passed on b0a2172fb6ef5a108fd48c411b0d761b9cd0bccf. This verifies the performance gate, not the status of every CI job. The separate permissions-popover issue is outside this change.

### Bundle-size repair

The [d30492d performance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44159700439/job/134310927958) fails on PR-added JavaScript. Daniel supplied the full-log comparison: largest ordinary JavaScript gzip is 572,366 bytes on base and 572,537 bytes on the candidate, against an unchanged 572,440-byte cap. Chat boot gzip is 1,325,469 -> 1,325,640 bytes, against a 1,325,580-byte cap. New-session boot is 815,913 -> 816,084 bytes. Both boot paths gain 171 bytes; request counts remain 21 and 17. Startup JavaScript and all CSS are unchanged. The CSS headroom warning also occurs on base; it does not explain these PR-added failures.

## What Problem This Solves

The rail mixes the agent, sessions, search and new-session controls in ways that are hard to read, and its default pins do not match what people open most.

The agent avatar is the Sessions item and returns to the last session; New session lives in the Sessions header; search sits above Home in the footer; pins start as Automations, Customize and Usage below the separator; the drop zone is calmer; the sidebar closes with the mirrored Panels icon.

## Why This Change Was Made

A series of small rail changes that share the rail and its menus, kept in one PR so the new rail reads as a whole. Tests and the website-dashboard and sidebar-customization e2e tests follow the default pins and the avatar Sessions item.

## Evidence

- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.

## Known Gap

A browser that saved an empty rail before this change keeps its own list until the profile's preferences arrive, so its default pins can appear a moment after the first paint. The boot-order fix belongs to main and is follow-up work.


## Update: test types

The rail test now reads each view button through its attribute, which the UI test typecheck requires.

Side rail series, part 3 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199823; review only this PR's commits.


## Update: e2e repair

The full Control UI e2e run on the stack found tests this PR broke or product gaps it introduced; this PR now carries their fixes:
- test(ui): wait for the Sessions item's return to chat in the shell presentation e2e
- test(ui): pin Dashboards, not the default Usage pin, in the read-only appearance e2e

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

| Largest JS asset | +2,608 B | 575,048 B |
| Chat boot JS | +2,418 B | 1,327,998 B |
| New Session boot JS | +2,591 B | 819,223 B |

Current head `f827d011bfd082723bdbe935d7650d26e0bb9033` also repairs three obsolete CI expectations without changing production UI:
- Menu tests verify that menus remain on screen beside the rail, open correctly, dismiss with Escape and restore trigger focus, without fixing their vertical placement.
- Presence tests distinguish intentional setup navigation from person-row actions and still reject navigation caused by presence updates.

On the corrected source, 112 focused tests and all 3 bundled rail E2E scenarios passed, as did component-test typechecking, focused lint, formatting and diff checks. Independent review found no remaining issue in the correction. Hosted CI for this exact head is still pending.

## What Problem This Solves

The scheduled message lifetime regression can time out before its mocked provider boundary is entered on a cold, loaded test worker. Its five-second wall-clock race measures preparation speed rather than the delivery-lifetime contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `awaitGateBeforeSettlement` helper to wait for the provider boundary while still rejecting an operation that settles prematurely. The provider, cancellation, delivery outcome, and transport assertions are unchanged. Remove the now-unused timeout-ratchet entry.

## User Impact

Test-only change; no runtime behavior changes. This fix is split out of #169438 because the recorded timeout happened before the provider call, not during that PR's post-send history commit.

## Evidence

- Original failure: the first direct-send case timed out with `Scheduled provider boundary not reached` before the mock provider was entered.
- The repaired suite passed all 18 cases in the prior focused run, and all 18 cases passed again during the broader transcript-owner proof.
- No new local run was performed for this split-only commit; the source test and helper change are unchanged from those passing runs. Hosted CI validates this independent head.

## Known limits

This removes an incidental five-second race; it does not alter the test runner's overall timeout or any production deadline.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): reduce filesystem stalls after commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changed sandbox commands in large local workspaces create and retire a filesystem snapshot for each checkpoint. On btrfs, snapshot creation can force filesystem-wide transaction work, while recursive retirement adds metadata work that competes with other Gateway writers.

## User Impact

Changed command checkpoints now pause their own guest while saving an immutable Git result, then resume before canonical publication. Command completion still waits for acceptance, unchanged commands remain pause-free, and later guest writes remain available for the next checkpoint. No configuration, schema, dependency, or host changes are required.

Owner accepts +~290 ms guest pause per changed command checkpoint (APFS measurement; btrfs unmeasured) in exchange for removing per-checkpoint btrfs snapshots/removals (2/2 → 0/0 per trace; −21 LOC), because each snapshot forces a global btrfs transaction commit on Team (production evidence: 11:40–12:10 PST Gateway SQLite waits 9–19.6 s, RPC p99 52 s).

The owner will verify guest pause p50/p99 on btrfs using `Local workspace unpause` logs after deployment. Revisit this trade-off if p99 exceeds 3 seconds. This PR does not deploy or change the host.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing direct-capture and pause owner for ordinary command checkpoints. Remove the inventory-size/probe-duration snapshot selector and its plumbing (−21 production LOC). Reconciliation retains its existing snapshot, fallback, recovery, and bounded asynchronous retirement paths. The relevant tests now exercise snapshots at that remaining owner.

The unchanged probe already skips identical-content rewrites, identical atomic replacements, and ignored-output churn. An empty journal or unchanged Git commit alone cannot establish that guest files are unchanged. A time-based checkpoint skip would violate read-after-command acceptance; waiting for a timer would add completion latency.

Source inspection confirms that the btrfs branch of `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.27.1 already issues one snapshot ioctl. This removes snapshot requests rather than replacing a per-file copy with an already-existing native snapshot. Retirement renames the capture before recursively removing it; it does not copy dependencies into the retired directory.

## Evidence

A/A/B used a synthetic 62,000-file, 1,100,004,000-byte projection: 22,000 eligible files and 40,000 dependency files. The ten-step trace included reads, identical rewrites, ignored dependency/artifact churn, one source edit, an identical atomic replacement, and one deletion. Every step verified canonical content/deletion and retained dependency content. All arms produced identical results.

| Per ten-step trace | A1 | A2 | B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Snapshot requests | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| Recursive capture removals | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| Unchanged steps skipping capture | 8/8 | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| Guest pauses | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| Total guest paused time, ms | 0 | 0 | 576 |
| Owner time including awaited cleanup, ms | 24,867 | 21,984 | 3,117 |
| Process CPU, ms | 22,157 | 19,267 | 4,288 |

The B pauses were 284 and 292 ms. These are APFS measurements with the same synthetic runtime in all arms. Btrfs eligibility was simulated at the checkpoint boundary; native APFS copy/removal still ran. Counts represent owner snapshot requests, each mapping to one ioctl on btrfs; actual btrfs ioctls/writeback were not measured. Native btrfs capacity was unavailable. APFS inode changes and shared-host load affect these timings, so counts and identical results are the portable proof. CPU excludes native child processes; allocation and physical bytes written were not measured.

Validation:

- All 13 focused checkpoint/reconciliation tests passed, including interrupted acceptance, later writes, nested-subvolume fallback, retirement overlap, and failed-removal retry.
- The large-workspace regression fails at snapshot creation with the unchanged production files and passes with this change. Run it with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-projection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'checkpoints large workspaces without creating disposable snapshots'`.
- `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` passed on the uncommitted candidate against its parent, including TypeScript, lint, formatting, dead-export scans, and ownership guards. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2. The committed diff matches the reviewed candidate exactly.
- No changed module is imported by `ui/src`. No provisioned-copy or base-refresh change.

The existing `scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts --mode turn-loop` workload supports the native ten-command/two-edit follow-up; its filesystem qualification and cleanup-accounting instructions are in the adjacent Markdown guide. The APFS trace above was a local instrumented fixture, not a native-btrfs benchmark run.

prs.title: fix(github): reduce disk writes during workspace base refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing a GitHub publication base rebuilt two complete temporary repository checkouts, even when only a handful of files changed. Their object copies, file writes, scans, and recursive deletion created avoidable disk contention inside the Gateway.

## User Impact

Base refreshes keep the same manifest and staged result while writing substantially less temporary data. Native preparation now follows the caller's cancellation through the existing worker/Git execution owner. No configuration, schema, dependency, or sandbox-container changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest worker inventories the two Git trees one directory level at a time, prunes excluded subtrees through the existing inclusion owner, borrows the existing immutable object store, and materializes only entries that cannot reuse the accepted baseline. The existing exclusion, source-overlay, manifest serialization, and result-staging owners still decide the output. Symlinks and changed files use native checkout conversion; attribute-content changes deliberately materialize the eligible files to preserve Git's conversion semantics. Gitlink directories, saved workspace edits, and build-cache inputs retain their existing behavior.

Runtime code grows by 172 lines: the private Git index and selective materialization replace the two general-purpose checkout calls. This is the cost of preserving native checkout attributes and pruning excluded subtrees before expanding their contents without introducing another cache or changing the manifest/staging contract.

## Evidence

A synthetic repository with 62,000 files and 1.116 GB of file payload produced identical raw manifests, build-cache inputs, and staged commit OIDs in both baseline arms and the candidate. Five interleaved samples per arm, after warmup, measured the manifest preparation, staging, and cleanup owners:

| Metric | A1: original | A2: original | B: selective materialization |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median total wall time | 70.405 s | 70.066 s | 1.799 s |
| Median owner time before cleanup | 66.799 s | 66.485 s | 1.797 s |
| Median cleanup time | 3.606 s | 3.581 s | 0.0015 s |
| Median process + native Git CPU | 209.309 s | 208.166 s | 1.627 s |
| Main-isolate V8 allocations | 5.219 GB | 5.196 GB | 1.031 GB |
| Native-command peak RSS | 1.142 GB | 1.142 GB | 71.0 MB |
| Temporary files created/deleted, separate census | 124,043 | 124,043 | 24 |
| Temporary logical bytes, separate census | 6.745 GB | 6.745 GB | 24.3 MB |

The interleaved run covers the directory-pruning implementation. After the final native-header accounting correction, five candidate-only replay samples still produce the same hashes: median 1.986 s wall, 1.855 s CPU, and 1.055 GB V8 allocation. This is a final-source confirmation, not another interleaved control set.

Both controls agree within 0.5% in median wall time and 0.6% in CPU. Census uses retained control measurements and a rerun final-candidate measurement; the final interleaved run independently confirms the same retained file/byte counts. Census includes intermediate pack spools and staging input, but excludes file overwrites, the identical persistent staged pack, and filesystem amplification; it is a logical-write lower bound, not device-level IO. Allocation is the main-isolate V8 counter, not native allocation. Measurements use local APFS; they do not reproduce btrfs transaction stalls or prove production latency.

A 5,000-file delta also matches exactly: temporary census falls from 6.476 GB / 124,043 files in each control to 114.5 MB / 10,004 files. A separate representative refresh matches across renames, deletions, executable modes, symlinks, gitlinks, directory/file replacements, newline filenames, excluded paths, and build-cache inputs, and correctly marked staged-input exceptions versus unowned lookalikes. Native attribute content/type tests preserve checkout conversion. prs.title: fix(macos): app quits with a generic credential alert when a separately managed Gateway blocks migration after an update
prs.body:
Related: #187000

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after an in-place app update, the macOS app shows the generic "client credentials need recovery" alert and quits when a local Gateway it does not manage (extended-stable channel, a channel install policy, or an independently managed or write-disabled service) is still running and blocks the required credential migration.

## User Impact

User impact: the app now explains which owner keeps that Gateway's version and reports the known credential-maintenance conflict, with **Retry** / **Quit OpenClaw**. It does not infer version incompatibility from contention or unconditionally recommend an upgrade/downgrade. Resolve the reported conflict through the Gateway's management tool; change versions only if recovery identifies incompatibility. It still never stops, replaces, or migrates under such a Gateway. Credential preparation failures with any other cause keep the existing generic alert. Background (`--background-only`) launches print the same guidance and quit, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the credential migration owner knows why preparation failed, so it now marks the one case this alert explains. When a required migration's maintenance admission is refused because a process with lock role `gateway` holds the state, `prepareStartupClientCredentials` throws `ClientCredentialGatewayHeldError`, and `openclaw doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` reports `error.code: "client_credentials_gateway_held"`. The app runs that command with `--json` and shows the Gateway-owner alert only for that code **and** an excluded local Gateway service. Everything else, including invalid config and the runtime-pin conflicts proposed in #191436, keeps the generic recovery alert. Legacy preparation before admission is validate-only, so the alert can accurately report stopping before the required maintenance. The earlier draft's "nothing was changed" claim for every failure is gone.

The stale-service detection from #190162 (remote primaries hosting a local Gateway) now returns one pure `admission` decision (`notHosted`, `excluded(reason)`, `admitted`), and `managedRepairGatesOpen` is derived from the new `managedRepairExclusion`, so existing gate callers behave the same.

Overlap: #191468 (merged) touches only `GatewayEndpointStore`. #191436 (open) edits `startup-client-credentials.ts` and the same docs paragraph. The overlap is textual only: its pin-migration failures are not Gateway-held, so they correctly keep the generic alert.

## Evidence

**Real CLI against a real isolated Gateway.** Private `HOME`/state/config, named profile `mgre2e`, port 34781, never the operator's Gateway:
- With `pnpm openclaw gateway run` holding state (pid 19622, role `gateway`) and a required migration (receipt device mismatch, the remount case), `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` exited 2 with `"code": "client_credentials_gateway_held"` and the contention message naming that holder.
- Same running Gateway, unrelated failure (invalid config): exit 2, **no** code (`Cannot prepare client credentials with invalid config …`).
- After stopping that Gateway, the same command exited 0 with `{"ok": true}`, and the receipt returned to `complete` with the original device. This is the CLI side of **Retry**.

**Original-head regression evidence** (`c7e792e3b2d3`), red on the base and green with the fix:
- `startup-client-credentials.test.ts`: "attributes a required migration refusal to the Gateway only when a gateway holds state" uses a real state-owner lock. The `gateway` case fails without the fix, and the `agent-embedded` case proves non-Gateway holders are not attributed. Suite: 22/22.
- `register.maintenance.test.ts`: the coded JSON failure envelope and exit 2. Suite: 39/39.
- Swift, private `HOME`/state/`TMPDIR`: `ClientCredentialStartupTests` (`--json` arguments, only the Gateway-held code yields `GatewayHeldError`, owner-specific recovery text) and `StaleGatewayServiceReplacementTests` (the #190162 hosting matrix plus owner exclusions): 11/11.

**Original-head gates** (`c7e792e3b2d3`):
- `swift build` for the app product and the test targets passed.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, oxfmt, oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` all pass.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports only 2 existing file-length violations in untouched files (`DashboardManager.swift`, `GatewayConnection.swift`).

**Original-head review:** local autoreview (Codex), committed range `d894035c7829..c7e792e3b2d3`, `--max-priority P2` with the owning sources as context: `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings (0.88). An earlier P0-only pass was also clean.

**ClawSweeper finding follow-up** (`dddadc75e57f`):
- Removed the unsupported incompatibility diagnosis and unconditional version-change advice from the alert and docs. Receipt reconciliation after a remount can require exclusive maintenance without changing the credential layout.
- Removed the unused app-version argument and the wording-only helper test; error attribution, cancellation, and bundled-owner tests remain. No detection or service-lifecycle behavior changed.
- Current checks passed: `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` (app and test targets), targeted SwiftFormat, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, docs oxfmt, and `git diff --check`.
- Native tests were not rerun on the operator desktop; the macOS guide requires OS-level isolation or a disposable runner. The earlier 11-test result above is prior-head evidence and includes the now-removed wording test. Subsequent explicitly authorized isolated native proof is recorded below.

**Native app validation on a prior head (`dddadc75e57f`):**

Performed natively with explicit operator authorization, in a fresh OCM environment: separate HOME/CFFIXED_USER_HOME, state/config/profile, bundle identity, test LaunchAgent, and port 34781. No copied operator credentials or channels. A sandbox guard denied app access to the operator state and writes to operator preferences/LaunchAgents, and blocked connections to the live Gateway ports. App metadata pins the tested commit.

- Stable `2026.10.10` service: the actual app showed the owner-preserving maintenance alert with Retry / Quit. Retrying while the service held state returned to the alert without migration. After stopping only the test service, Retry completed migration; the native credential socket returned the original synthetic device ID, public/private keys, and creation time. Test config remained unchanged.
- Compatible runtime: the test service ran the PR app's bundled runtime. A synthetic receipt device mismatch represented remount maintenance (not a real filesystem remount). The real app showed the same corrected maintenance alert without asserting version incompatibility. Retry while held returned to the alert. After stopping only this test service, Retry repaired the receipt; native credential admission preserved the original identity/keys and config.
- Operator config and Gateway LaunchAgent hashes remained equal to their pre-test values. The live Gateway restarted independently during the interrupted agent run, so continuous PID preservation is not claimed; no test command stopped or modified that service.

**Merged head (`58359d17191c`):** merged current `main` and fixed the Quit hang.

- Conflict resolution: `doctor --client-credentials` keeps both `prepareRuntimePins: true` from `main` and this PR's coded failure. The docs text moved to the new **Credential recovery** section.
- Quit fix: both credential-startup alert paths now use `AppDelegate.requestTermination()` instead of calling `terminate` on the main dispatch task.
- Isolated OCM run, same guards, app metadata pinned to this commit: with the test Gateway holding state and a synthetic receipt device mismatch, process sampling shows the app in `retryAfterExcludedGatewayFailure` → `NSAlert.runModal`. The bundled CLI exits 2 with `client_credentials_gateway_held`.
- Passing: `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` and `register.maintenance.test.ts` (64/64), app packaging, oxfmt, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports 5 violations, all in files this PR does not touch.
- Native test targets do not compile on `main`: `GatewayEndpointStoreTests.swift` calls the now-throwing `_testLocalConfig` without `try`. This PR does not touch that file. With a temporary local `try!` patch, not committed, the test targets built.

- Real alert clicks, same isolated OCM run on `58359d17191c`, pressed through the Accessibility API with the alert's actual text and controls read back:
  - **Retry** while the test Gateway held state: the alert returned and no migration ran.
  - **Quit OpenClaw**: the app exited in about 2 seconds. This is the path that hung on `dddadc75e57f`.
  - **Retry** after stopping only the test Gateway: the receipt returned to `complete` with the real device, and the native credential socket returned the original device ID, public/private keys, and creation time. Test config unchanged.
- Operator config and Gateway LaunchAgent hashes matched before and after.

**Remaining gaps:**

- **Visual screenshots remain missing.** `AppActivation.presentAlert` sets `alert.window.sharingType = .none`, so captures of the real alert are blank. No mockup or blank image is offered as proof.
- The alert's **Details** line uses `detail.suffix(300)`, so it can start mid-word (observed: "e directory."). The actionable end of the message is intact.
- Successful Retry is proved at the real app credential socket, not full chat/model connectivity. The full native suite remains CI-owned.

prs.title: fix(release): backport extended-stable updater targeting repairs
prs.body:
## What problem does this PR solve?
The 2026.10.33 release qualification cannot upgrade the published 2026.9.37 extended-stable executable through a --tag override. Separately, the blanket restriction prevents one-off explicit package targets for newer extended-stable installations.

## Changes
Backport the three reviewed main fixes onto extended-stable/2026.10.33, preserving the existing release repairs:
- #200708, source 84dd10b2777bc3e23c5dfef7e35902e9b8499d8f: use the already-shipped loopback registry selector for the old 9.37 executable and serve the exact candidate archive. Adapt only the release branch's existing driver invocation, without importing newer main-only follow-up scenarios.
- #200726, source 5484e18dab2bbed35a930a2bdc3842e3965797e0: remove the blanket extended-stable --tag rejection. Without an explicit target, retain verified selection; with one, retain the existing version/schema/runtime/ownership compatibility path and saved channel. Keep package --tag main refusal.

- #200751, source da5ebcbad8b03705cab92e180410cb4b307fc656: select the existing frozen baseline from candidate release-train classification when a staging or empty ref lacks canonical branch context. Production patch is identical to main; only the older release test layout was adapted.

Dallin explicitly approved these repairs and publication only after qualification. This PR does not publish or waive failures.

## Scope and risk
Target release v2026.10.33: core openclaw, all npm-publishable official plugins, and matching Docker extended-stable artifacts. No npm latest, native application, ClawHub, or website publication. No SDK export, schema, dependency, migration, or config-default changes; the explicit-target policy change is intentional and authorized. No private security material is introduced by these public backports. Existing release inventory and security decisions are unchanged. Revert the three commits to restore prior behavior if needed.

## Evidence
- Main policy regression red on prior runtime; three focused cases green on main.
- Release-branch selector helper: 10/10 tests passed, syntax/format/type-aware lint passed; independent adaptation review scoped-clean.
- Release-branch policy: 3/3 selected CLI cases passed (29 unrelated cases filtered), covering explicit target, default verified selector, and Git-install refusal. Type-aware lint: zero errors; format and diff checks passed. Independent adaptation review scoped-clean.
- Original FRV44116511839 evidence is retained, not reclassified as green. Its first infrastructure retry produced unsealable GitHub ghost jobs; canonical cancellation confirmed all children terminal. Stale-binding Bun and live-cron assertions remain unwaived. Node stale-binding suite 8/8 passing does not replace Bun proof.
- Real managed-service upgrade and full qualification remain required on the landed exact candidate. No release-success claim based on unit tests.

Base before backports: 834ce75f75f0099b608f54001150800d1ccd2aa1. Staging head: 0f467336353ed4c4d7ce7da5c2763511d65399f7. Trusted release tooling remains separately pinned; no change to accepted waiver scope.


## Current integration gate
Original hosted run 44147820548 exposed a staging-context defect: it selected npm latest 2026.11.5 and hit the schema 36-to-22 refusal. That original failure and artifact remain retained. The repair from #200751 is now backported at 0f467336353ed4c4d7ce7da5c2763511d65399f7. All 41 release workflow-plan tests and 21 baseline-owner tests pass; type-aware lint and formatting pass. Independent adaptation review is scoped-clean, with no P0–P2 findings. Production workflow patch identity matches the landed main fix. Fresh exact-head hosted gate 44154338064 is running; no unchanged retry or failure waiver. Full release qualification remains required after integration.


### UI failure investigation and bounded recovery

At exact head `0f467336353ed4c4d7ce7da5c2763511d65399f7`, integration run `44154338064` attempt 1 failed only the UI shard and its aggregate gate. The original failure was a timeout waiting for `system.info` in the connection-settings E2E test; it remains recorded, not waived or claimed fixed.

Bounded local reproduction used the original 795-pattern include list, shard 2/8, and three workers. It completed with 414/415 tests passing, including all 12 sidebar tests and the original failing connection case. The one local failure was a different terminal-width assertion (99 columns versus at least 125); that test passed in the original CI run. Local Node 26 differs from CI Node 24. Local browser font setup was repaired without source changes; that local issue is not attributed to CI. No speculative product patch or weakened assertion was retained.

Working classification: suspected intermittent UI readiness/timing failure, not a proven deterministic updater regression; precise root cause remains unresolved. Under the maintainer's explicit bounded-retry authorization, perform at most one initial retry of the failed UI job and its dependent gate on this unchanged head, preserving the original attempt. A green retry is qualification evidence, not proof of a repair; a repeated failure requires renewed investigation, not an automatic retry loop.

Fixes #200773

## What Problem This Solves

After a global npm update, `openclaw doctor --fix` can fail to reinstall managed plugins with `EALLOWSCRIPTS`. An inherited `npm_config_allow_scripts=openclaw` reaches the project-scoped install, where npm rejects it even with `--ignore-scripts`.

## User Impact

Managed plugin installs and Doctor repairs can complete when this global-install setting is inherited. Lifecycle scripts remain disabled, and global core installs retain their existing allow-scripts behavior. No migration or operator configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the inherited setting to the shared project-install environment reset set. Its existing case-insensitive reset covers lowercase, uppercase, and mixed-case keys for every safe-install caller. The fix adds one production line, without npm-version detection or another policy owner.

The candidate performing plugin installation or Doctor repair must contain this fix; it does not change an already-running older installer. Existing managed plugin projects are preserved.

## Evidence

Real npm reproduces the reported error through `createSafeNpmInstallEnv` and its real `createNpmProjectInstallEnv` owner. With the fix, each casing installs successfully, writes its lockfile, and leaves the preinstall/install/postinstall marker absent. The sibling global-install test retains `--allow-scripts=openclaw` for both supported flagged policies.

- Verified on main/base `ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110` before editing production: **142 passed, 3 failed**; all three failures were the new real-npm `EALLOWSCRIPTS` cases.
- Same six named files with the fix: **145 passed, 0 failed**, 6 files. Every case passing on the base remained green.
- Touched-file type-aware oxlint, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pr-simplify`: existing owner retained; +1 production line and +36 net test lines.
- Independent Codex autoreview, local candidate against the base above, P0–P3, complete env-owner and fixture context: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The reviewed candidate is committed as `344f190ea0beda463bc6ca942fd28852bd25651f`.
- Named-run wall time: 70.91s including worker preparation; Vitest duration 29.67s. Changed test files: safe-package-install 2.150s and update-global-lifecycle 0.134s. CI timings pending.

<details>
<summary>Source audit and focused commands</summary>

The main/base reset set at [`npm-install-env.ts:19`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110/src/infra/npm-install-env.ts#L19) omits allow-scripts; its case-insensitive deletion at [line 337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110/src/infra/npm-install-env.ts#L337) therefore preserves the inherited value. [`safe-package-install.ts:29`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ea94eb3bd38e29d17df08a957a08fa2866355110/src/infra/safe-package-install.ts#L29) composes that owner with script-disabled installation.

Inherited environments reach managed plugin installation at `src/plugins/install-managed-npm.ts:294`, peer planning and host-peer repair at `src/infra/npm-managed-root.ts:644,808`, package-directory installation at `src/infra/install-package-dir.ts:529`, and Git plugin installation at `src/plugins/git-install.ts:355`. Plugin uninstalls also consume the same safe environment. No project-install allow-scripts CLI flag or OpenClaw-written allow-scripts npmrc entry was found. Managed npmrc inputs are copied unchanged (`src/plugins/install-managed-npm-state.ts:34`, `src/infra/npm-managed-root.ts:615`); package-directory installation temporarily hides its staged npmrc. The separate native prebuild repair already strips this inherited setting (`scripts/lib/fs-safe-prebuild.mjs:206`).

Explicit allow-scripts flags belong to the global core path (`src/infra/update-global.ts:214,1144`, `scripts/install-policy.sh:279`, `scripts/install.ps1:1822`). Those paths are unchanged.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_SERIAL=1 \
OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1 timeout 240s pnpm test \
  src/infra/npm-install-env.test.ts src/infra/safe-package-install.test.ts \
  src/infra/npm-managed-root.test.ts src/infra/install-package-dir.test.ts \
  src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts src/infra/update-global-lifecycle.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=default

timeout 120s pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --threads=1 \
  --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json \
  src/infra/npm-install-env.ts src/infra/safe-package-install.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-global-lifecycle.test.ts

timeout 30s pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/npm-install-env.ts \
  src/infra/safe-package-install.test.ts src/infra/update-global-lifecycle.test.ts
```

</details>

Limits: real-npm proof uses the repository-pinned npm 12.2.1 on Linux with Node 26.12.1. The reporter's parent environment, exact macOS/npm 11.17 combination, and a full Doctor upgrade flow remain unverified. The named install.npm-spec suite mocks npm execution; the regression above executes real npm at the shared environment boundary. No Gateway e2e, upgrade matrix, or check:changed run was performed; broader proof is left to PR CI as requested.

Reported by @cbhawthorne84

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why this is needed

An MCP server that is sometimes down, but otherwise valid, should not block upgrades or leave the Gateway unstable. Today it does: Doctor reports the outage as an error, so a Doctor-gated start or update stops, and someone has to SSH in to fix it. A warning is reasonably safe here, because the outage does not block OpenClaw itself. The Gateway runs without that server's tools, as it already does at runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP code now keeps a typed reason for "the remote service is unavailable" from catalog collection through startup backoff. The pagination code gives a typed deadline error. Classification uses the transport and structured error fields, never the server's message text. Doctor keeps the strongest finding when one server is seen in several agent contexts, so a warning cannot hide an error.

The change reuses the existing catalog-projection code and does not add a new manager, setting or stored data. Update-time probe deferral, OAuth inspection, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Before: published `openclaw@2026.11.5` (current stable on npm). After: this PR head `42571b615c3`, built from `7c6f38d4da6` (upstream/main on 2026-11-18). Real built CLI and Gateway, fake MCP servers on loopback, throwaway HOME and state dir. Ubuntu 26.04, Node 26.10.0.

**Doctor CLI.** `node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning|error`. Exit codes: warning threshold / error threshold.

| Case | Before (2026.11.5) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy server (remote or stdio) | no finding; exit 0 / 0 | no finding; exit 0 / 0 |
| Remote outage: connection refused, HTTP 503, HTTP 401, hang past the 10 s deadline | error; exit 1 / 1 | warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 0 |
| Remote invalid catalog (bad tool entry, repeated cursor) | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Stdio failure: crash at start, missing executable, invalid catalog | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Remote 503 and stdio crash in one config | error + error; exit 1 / 1 | error + warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 1 |

**Doctor-gated Gateway start, same state dir, upgrade from current stable.** The remote MCP server answers every request with HTTP 503. A small supervisor script runs `openclaw doctor --lint --json --severity-min error` and starts `openclaw gateway run` (random loopback port, token auth) only if that exits 0. The same temp state dir is used first by `openclaw@2026.11.5`, then by this build.

| Build | Doctor gate | Gateway |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw@2026.11.5` | error on the remote server, exit 1 | not started |
| This PR head | no error finding, exit 0 (the outage is a warning at the warning threshold) | started, `gateway health` returned ok |

The second build reused the first build's state dir and its settings. I did not compare state files byte for byte. Not the `openclaw update` command.

**Tests.** `pnpm test` on the 5 touched or related files (4 shards, `--maxWorkers=2`): all pass (12 + 55 + 11 + 11 tests), including the Doctor stdio tests. Test lines are now +398 against the allowance of 400 (it was +483): I cut duplicate cases (legacy SSE POST, insufficient-scope, 401 SSE, a cause-less cycle case and a last-good-catalog test). The remaining tests still cover each classification rule and the strongest-severity rule.

Not tested: real `openclaw update`, real third-party servers, OAuth, legacy SSE, TLS, human-readable Doctor output, Windows, macOS, a live production Gateway.
