prs.title: fix: keep worker previews loading during activity updates
prs.body:
Closes #200673

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a worker website preview can load the page but fail concurrent scripts, styles, images, or WebSocket connections with HTTP 502. Recording activity for one connection temporarily fences attachment reads used to authorize another connection.

## User Impact

Worker preview connections wait for the pending write and then check access again. Actual revocation and portal closure still reject access. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the inventory owner's existing settlement promise in a typed pending-mutation error. The worker portal carrier waits for that promise and retries connection admission, including when the dispatch authorization callback encounters the mutation. Retry occurs before the stream is returned to carry application requests, so it does not replay HTTP requests.

This keeps the attachment activity digest and idle-cleanup guards intact. It adds no polling timer, arbitrary delay, or authorization bypass. The carrier preserves the original dispatch authorization exception instead of losing it behind a generic dispatch failure.

The source change adds 37 and removes 8 production lines, plus 158 test lines. The added cases cover publication settlement, discovery/dispatch contention, revocation, and closure.

## Evidence


**Real browser and complete package build proof for the published candidate:** [redacted request log, build results, and reproducible scripts](https://gist.github.com/SeveHo/d9b4cdc7459f88b3836303997370fc24/002989b1d61d87715f550c752e7fe6f6976d38d7).

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| 10 fresh browser contexts, cache disabled through CDP, app responses `no-store` | 820 HTTP responses, all HTTP 200 |
| Failed requests / HTTP 502 / browser script errors during those runs | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Per-run asset and fetch checks | 16 scripts, 8 stylesheets, 24 rendered images, 32 completed fetches |
| Real WebSocket echo | Passed in all 10 runs |
| One button click and one POST per run | App effect counter advanced exactly from 1 through 10 |
| Negative control after the successful runs: stop the exact node process | Portal returned HTTP 502 while the app still returned HTTP 200 directly |

The test used a real isolated Gateway, a real enrolled node host, SQLite attachment publication, the node stream broker, and Chromium. A supported `device` profile attached the node to a persistent conversation. A real admitted admin agent turn opened `portal` through `dispatch_action`; the existing repository model fixture supplied only that tool selection. No synthetic pending-mutation error, fake settlement promise, mocked transport, or package-file workaround was used.

Gateway and node ran as separate processes on one Linux host. This is proof of the candidate's real Gateway/node connection path, not Hetzner provisioning, ingress from another machine, or access from a particular remote user's browser. The published log removes origins, IP addresses, bearer URLs, credentials, and headers. Its SHA-256 is `fa926b5fb9fea289edf2fc4e5198729f592cbc495e15f2402edbbc9fb302316c`. The source patch was checked before and after execution against the published candidate. The attachment reached `destroyed` through the native API, and the isolated test processes were stopped.

- Regression proof on base `bb45ba99390c80784ca50d1b07f150b72cd57b7d`: all five new cases failed; the other 25 selected tests passed. This used the new test files and error declaration with the original carrier/projection behavior.
- Fixed candidate: all 70 tests passed across the carrier, projection, worker store, and HTTP/WebSocket proxy suites, including idle-cleanup guards.
- Targeted type-aware lint passed on all five changed files. Production and affected Gateway test type checks passed. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The only subsequent change removed two redundant default type arguments from a test, as requested by lint.
- **Full package build passed:** `pnpm build:package` completed from a clean checkout of `53887cdcd8321240abd253b91ff0e7ecc55095f9` on an isolated Hetzner CPX42 through Crabbox 0.83.2. It exited 0 in 6m 59.65s, including unified declarations (3m 9.3s), all 105 local plugin builds, package exports, and the Control UI. The frozen dependency install passed. Source SHA and clean status were verified before installation and after the build. The evidence artifact includes the exact script, phase output, and execution record. Native cleanup confirmed successful server deletion and server absence.
- ClawSweeper reports sufficient behavior proof, no actionable code findings, and readiness for maintainer review. [Hosted product CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44121053823) is awaiting upstream maintainer approval (`action_required`, no jobs started); this is not a passing CI result. The candidate has not been deployed to the operator's running Gateway.

<details>
<summary>Commands and environment</summary>

Tests used Node 24.21.0 on Linux x64; lint, type checks, and build used Node 24.22.1 with pnpm 12.15.0. Repository wrappers used their documented Node/oxlint/oxfmt fallback because downloading the pinned Bun fork failed.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/portal-node-carrier.test.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/store-projection.test.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/store-worker.test.ts \
  src/gateway/portals/portal-http-proxy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/store-errors.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/store-projection.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/portal-node-carrier.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/store-projection.test.ts \
  src/gateway/worker-environments/portal-node-carrier.test.ts

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json --incremental
pnpm build:package
```

Test result: 4 files, 70 tests passed in 305.78 seconds. The full package build passed with exit 0 from the clean published candidate. The source patch SHA-256 was verified as `3e715a5392efdb6ea27bec106c01f1087c883bb4b632fa46fcda6ccc18aa6e49` before and after the browser proof and package build.

</details>

prs.title: fix(android): realtime Talk hangs up when a navigation prompt or notification sound plays
prs.body:
Closes #181710

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk hangs up with "audio focus lost" as soon as another app plays a short sound, for example a navigation prompt or a notification.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk now keeps going while you drive with navigation on or when a notification sound plays. During the prompt Talk gets quieter and stops listening, then carries on. A ringing or active phone call still ends Talk, and now so do VoIP calls that ring or use the microphone in call mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

The focus listener in `RealtimeCommunicationAudio` treated every focus change except `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN` as fatal. Navigation apps grab transient focus for each prompt (on my phone it arrives as `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, not just `..._CAN_DUCK`), so every "turn left" ended the session.

Now a transient loss keeps the session and marks Talk as interrupted until `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN`:

- Microphone frames are dropped through the existing capture gate, so the prompt itself doesn't reach the provider as user speech.
- `RealtimePlayout` lowers its track volume to 20 %. Android never auto-ducks speech, so the app has to do it. The playout owner applies the gain on every write and on every periodic poll, which also covers audio that's already buffered.
- I chose ducking over `AudioTrack.pause()` on purpose. The playout's stall detection, write timeouts and mark timing all assume a playing track, and pausing would have meant reworking that.

Calls take transient focus too, and Talk shouldn't keep talking over a call. So while focus is lost, Talk still ends when a call shows up through any of these signals:

- a telephony mode (`MODE_RINGTONE`, `MODE_IN_CALL`, `MODE_CALL_SCREENING`) for regular phone calls,
- an active player with `USAGE_NOTIFICATION_RINGTONE`, which covers ringing in most VoIP apps,
- another app's `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` capture, which VoIP apps start once a call is answered. Talk's own recorder is excluded by its audio session ID; unprivileged apps get anonymized recording configs, but those keep the session ID and source ([`anonymizedCopy`](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/media/java/android/media/AudioRecordingConfiguration.java)).

These can arrive before or after the focus loss, so the focus, mode, playback and recording callbacks all check again. The loss is reported only once. No new permissions are needed.

Known limits:

- VoIP detection is best effort. An app that neither plays a ringtone nor captures with `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` only interrupts Talk instead of ending it, and a ringtone preview while Talk is interrupted would end it.
- Ducking still lets Talk's speech be heard quietly under the prompt.

## Evidence

- Real phone, navigation running ([screen recording, 29 s](https://github.com/mcdax/openclaw/releases/download/talk-focus-proof-181713/talk-focus-before-after.mp4)): with the current app, starting navigation during Talk immediately shows "Sprachfunktion fehlgeschlagen: audio focus lost" and the session ends. With a debug build of this branch, navigation starts while Talk is active and Talk keeps listening and answers normally. The Gateway only saw a normal `session.closed` in the failing case, no server error.
- Real phone, phone call during Talk ([screen recording, 18 s](https://github.com/mcdax/openclaw/releases/download/talk-focus-proof-181713/talk-call-ends-talk.mp4)): same debug build of this branch (`2026.8.2-debug`). Realtime Talk is listening, then a call to the carrier voicemail is placed from the same phone. As soon as the call connects, Talk ends with "Sprachfunktion fehlgeschlagen: audio focus lost", so a transient focus loss during a call still ends Talk. The VoIP path (ringtone or another app's `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` capture) is covered by the tests below, not by a device recording.
- A build that only tolerated `..._CAN_DUCK` still dropped at the prompt, which is why transient losses are handled too.
- New tests: transient loss interrupts without ending Talk; a call ends Talk once, whether the mode change comes before or after the focus loss; a VoIP ringtone or foreign voice capture ends Talk while Talk's own capture does not; buffered speech is ducked without new writes and restored afterwards; mic frames are held back while focus is lost.
- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.voice.*'`: 280 passed. `:app:ktlintCheck` and `:app:lintPlayDebug` are clean and `:app:assemblePlayDebug` builds.

prs.title: feat(ui): rename Plugins to Customize and move Templates into it
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins, Skills, Skill workshop and Templates are one place to shape the agent, but the hub is named Plugins, Templates sits apart, and Apps clutters the Pages catalog.

## User Impact

The hub is named Customize and holds Plugins, Skills, Skill workshop and Templates; Apps is gone from the Pages catalog.

## Why This Change Was Made

Renames the hub and its navigation entry, moves Templates under it, and drops Apps from the catalog. A saved `route:templates` pin is dropped by the existing pin normalization; Templates stays reachable from Customize.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock at the end of the series, so the after image can show later parts too.

Customize before and after (left: main, right: after):

![Customize before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf6e2ddd-fb0c-49e9-be98-3e626ccb06cc)

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes at this PR's head.
- The unit tests of the files this PR touches pass at its head; the full UI unit suite passes at the end of the series (one failure also on main: a Workboard German relative-time string, "vor 1min", from the local ICU).
- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.

Side rail series, part 2 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199822; review only this PR's commits.

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

Vyctor approved the measured JavaScript byte cost for this navigation stack. These cumulative measurements compare this layer with paired main base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`. Each cap equals the original main cap plus the measured delta, preserving existing headroom without adding another margin.

| Metric | Cumulative gzip delta | Cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest JS asset | +2,370 B | 574,810 B |
| Chat boot JS | +2,390 B | 1,327,970 B |
| New Session boot JS | +2,390 B | 819,022 B |

CSS ceilings, request counts, startup ceilings and gate logic are unchanged. Byte measurements are delivery-size evidence, not latency measurements.

### Landing validation

prs.title: fix: stop showing a running Linux Gateway service as last exit 0
prs.body:
Root cause: src/daemon/systemd-runtime.ts:186 (and the D-Bus reader at src/daemon/systemd-loaded-runtime.ts:243) copied systemd's `ExecMainStatus`/`ExecMainCode` into the last exit even while the main process was still running, when systemd holds both at 0, so `openclaw gateway status` and onboarding printed `last exit 0, reason 0` for a Gateway that had never exited.

Scope: this PR fixes one defect, the false `last exit 0` diagnostic that #200671 was filed on ("startup failure exits 0"). It does not close #200671. The rest of that report is not a defect in this code path: the startup-failure path already exits nonzero (`src/cli/gateway-cli/run.ts:881`, 1 or 78), restarting on any exit is the deliberate `Restart=always` service policy, and a fresh Gateway outgrowing a 1 GB host below the 2048 MiB heap floor is a separate memory/performance question.

## What Problem This Solves

On a low-memory Linux host, a systemd-managed Gateway that keeps getting killed and restarted shows `Runtime: running (pid …, state active, last exit 0, reason 0)`. That reads as "the Gateway exits cleanly and systemd keeps restarting it", which is how #200671 was filed. The Gateway never exited 0: every restart in the journal was `code=killed, status=9/KILL` (out of memory). The 0/0 is systemd's placeholder for a main process that has not exited yet.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway status` and the onboarding readiness summary no longer claim a running Gateway last exited with 0. Real exits (for example `last exit 9, reason 2` after a kill, or the status after a stop) are still shown.

## Why This Change Was Made

systemd resets `ExecMainCode` to 0 when it starts a new main process and sets it only when that process exits. Both systemd readers now report the last exit only when `ExecMainCode` is non-zero. The startup-failure exit path itself is unchanged: it already exits 1 (or 78 for config refusals), and `Restart=always` restarts on any status by design.

## Evidence

Reporter's flow (`openclaw onboard --non-interactive … --install-daemon`) in a Debian 12 container with systemd as PID 1, Node 24.22.1, 906 MiB RAM + 511 MiB swap (cgroup limits), building this branch and its base inside Linux.

Base (1f3524eec31a):
```text
systemctl --user show: ActiveState=active SubState=running ExecMainCode=0 ExecMainStatus=0 NRestarts=5
journal: openclaw-gateway.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL   (every restart)
openclaw gateway status: Runtime: running (pid 645, state active, sub running, last exit 0, reason 0)
```

Candidate (this branch):
```text
systemctl --user show: ActiveState=active SubState=running ExecMainCode=0 ExecMainStatus=0 NRestarts=7
openclaw gateway status: Runtime: running (pid 1161, state active, sub running)
control, during auto-restart: Runtime: unknown (state activating, sub auto-restart, last exit 9, reason 2)
control, after stop:          Runtime: stopped (state inactive, sub dead, last exit 9, reason 2)
```

Regression tests in `src/daemon/systemd-loaded-runtime.test.ts` cover both readers (systemctl show and D-Bus); they fail on the base with `lastExitStatus: 0` / `lastExitReason: "0"` and pass here.

Thanks @DonnieFi for the detailed Raspberry Pi report.

Merge danger: two-way door. Display only; no state, config or contract change. Blast radius: Linux systemd Gateway status and onboarding summaries.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep assistant answers out of the collapsed Worked fold
prs.body:
Related: #180490

## What Problem This Solves

On main, a completed Control UI turn collapses into one "Worked" line, and that line swallows **about a third of Claude's answers** (and those of other models that don't label commentary) along with the tools.

The fold hides every assistant text group that is not the run's last reply, unless the provider labels it as commentary. So an answer followed by any tool call (saving a note, updating a file) is hidden, and only the short closing line stays visible. A steered run that produces two replies shows only the last one.

This affects **every model that does not label its commentary**, not just Claude: as far as we know, everything except OpenAI models. Fresh GLM-5.3 Flash and DeepSeek v4.1 Flash runs on current code store their text with no phase label (examples below). Claude is where it shows most, because it routinely answers and then calls a tool to record the result.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isCollapsibleWorkGroup` treated every unphased assistant text group as completed work unless it owned the turn's final reply. That is a guess: an absent phase is unknown, not commentary, and `toolUse` is an execution stop reason, not a narration label (Claude often answers and then calls a tool to record the result).

The runtime prompt added in #159416 (refined in #178108) tells models that "Commentary is optional progress and may be hidden" and asks them to repeat every pending answer in the final response. That works for providers that tag commentary natively (OpenAI): their commentary really is throwaway progress, and the answer carries a final-answer label, so important messages stay visible.

It cannot help models that do not tag commentary, or streamed turns with no definitive final answer. The instruction does not create phase labels, so the UI still cannot tell an answer from progress, and generation ending or a later tool call does not establish that earlier text was commentary. Unlabeled text must not be folded on that assumption, hence this change.

The change adds one guard: an assistant text-only group is collapsible only when every message in it resolves to explicit `commentary` through the existing `resolveAssistantReplyPhase` (provider phase, text signatures, keyed stream-fallback commentary). Everything else is unchanged: one Worked line per turn, the same partition and ownership logic, tools and reasoning still fold, and providers that label commentary (OpenAI/Codex, Muse Spark) fold exactly as before. No CSS, renderer or layout change.

**Intentional change to existing behavior.** Main currently treats any assistant text without a phase label as narration and folds it. That assumption holds for providers that tag commentary natively, such as OpenAI, which is what the existing tests and runtime prompt (#159416, #178108) are built around. It does not hold for providers that never send a phase, where it hides real answers (34% in the replay below). This PR deliberately reverses that default. Maintainer sign-off on this behavior change is requested.

Key points for review:
- **An absent phase is unknown, not commentary.** Folding is now driven only by an explicit commentary label (provider phase, text signature, or keyed stream fallback), never by a missing one.
- **Natively tagged providers are unchanged.** OpenAI/Codex (and Muse Spark) commentary folds exactly as before.
- **OpenClaw's own rows still fold.** Host-generated assistant rows (provider `openclaw`, e.g. publication receipts) are identified with the existing `isTranscriptArtifactProvider` and fold as on main; only model-authored text is affected.
- **Layout is unchanged.** One Worked line per turn, the same rows in the same positions; every tool call still folds, and expanding Worked shows rows in transcript order.
- **Prompt guidance cannot substitute for labels.** Asking models to keep commentary throwaway does not give the UI a way to tell an untagged answer from progress.

## User Impact

**Hidden answers go from about 1 in 3 to zero.** The Worked line still collapses only the work: same count, same positions, every tool call still inside it. Expanding it shows tools between the answers they came between, as on main.

Trade-off: short unlabeled status lines (for example "Build passed; tests running now.") are now visible too, in their chronological place, for models that do not natively tag their commentary.

## Evidence

| Measure | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Answers hidden in the collapsed fold (1,474 sampled text blocks, two blind classifiers) | **34%** (25% if status lines count as narration) | **0%** |
| Turns that hide at least one answer | about **1 in 5** | **0** |
| Unlabeled assistant text blocks hidden (962 sessions, presentation replay) | 4,874 | **0** |
| Worked rows (same replay) | 3,483 | 3,483, **zero** differences in position, key, reply owner or duration |
| Tool cards inside Worked | 35,164 | 35,164 |
| Rows revealed, rendered A/B in the real Control UI (979 sessions) | | **4,051** across 432 sessions |
| Previously visible rows lost / sessions gone blank | | **0 / 0** |
| Expanded rows: same IDs and text, by session | | **979 / 979** |

**Method.** Every Claude Code session on one workstation (about 3 Oct to 11 Nov 2026) was replayed through main's real history import and presentation code (`840105308d2`, default View settings), then rendered on two otherwise identical scratch Gateways with and without this change. *Answer* means text that tells the user something (a result, explanation, decision, question or status), even if it also says what happens next.

**Screenshots** (synthetic conversation, same data and settings on both builds).

One streamed turn: three long answers between tool batches, ending with a notes-file write.

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Collapsed | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/before-collapsed.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9faab0a8ae958afc581c1c0b706b6ff69e4dfd8f/after-collapsed.png) |

Steered turn: both builds split the turn at the steer and show the pre-steer answer; after it, main hides both answers and this PR shows them. Expanded order is identical.

**Other models** (real runs on the synthetic workspace; the prompt asks for findings before each further tool call so the turn has this shape). Neither model's stored text carries a phase label.

**Tests.** New regressions (answer then tool then closing line; a steered two-reply run; explicit commentary still folds; an unlabeled model answer stays visible while an OpenClaw publication receipt in the same turn still folds; tools and reasoning still fold; Worked row count and position unchanged) fail on stock and pass patched. On current main (`f7c48defb85`): UI typecheck passes; `ui/src/pages/chat` plus tool-call grouping: 8,912 passed, 3 skipped, 5 failed. Four are native-drop undo tests that fail identically on unmodified main; the fifth (an inline mock reset) passes 3/3 in isolation on both main and this branch. Existing main tests are unchanged apart from neutral fixture names.

prs.title: fix(codex): chat rows that arrive during a native turn are never sent to Codex
prs.body:
Related: none found (no open or closed issue or PR covers this).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat message that arrives while a Codex turn is running is never sent to Codex, because the next turn thinks the thread already saw it.

## User Impact

User impact: Codex now gets every chat message exactly once. Before, a message saved during a running turn (and not steered into it) was silently lost for Codex on the next turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

After a turn, the thread binding stored "history seen up to <turn end time>". A row saved mid-turn has an older time, so the next turn skipped it.

Now the binding also stores the exact chat row that was sent with the turn (thread id, run id, row key). The next turn resumes after that row. Rows steered into that run are skipped. If the row is not found (for example, history was compacted), the old time check is used, so nothing gets worse.

Size: 4 files, about 60 lines of code plus one test.

## Evidence

### 1. Built Gateway, real client path, fake Codex app-server

Built with `pnpm build`. The built Gateway runs on a loopback port with a temp HOME and state dir. The Codex plugin talks to a small fake app-server process (a copy of the repo's own refusal fixture, plus a "hold turn 1" switch). No OpenAI call, no credentials. The test drives the Gateway with `chat.send` and `agent.wait` over its WebSocket client.

Steps:
1. `chat.send` "FIRST-REQUEST". The fake app-server holds turn 1 open.
2. While turn 1 runs, a user row is written into the Gateway's own SQLite transcript. It is not steered into turn 1.
3. Release turn 1. Stop and start the Gateway, so the next turn resumes the stored native thread.
4. `chat.send` "SECOND-REQUEST". Count the row text in what the app-server receives after `thread/resume` (`thread/inject_items` and `turn/start`).

| | Plain main (`5cbed85ff94`) | This PR (`47b8294779d`) |
|---|---|---|
| Row stored during turn 1, seen by Codex after resume | 0 times (lost) | 1 time |
| "SECOND-REQUEST" sent | yes | yes |
| Requests after resume | `thread/inject_items`, `turn/start` | `thread/inject_items`, `turn/start` |

Both runs used a fresh `pnpm build` of that exact source.

### 2. Stored data from the current stable release

Stable is `openclaw@2026.11.5` and `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.5` (the Codex plugin is a separate package in stable). I ran the real stable binding codec from the published package next to this PR's codec, on the same stored record shape:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Binding written by stable (no `transcriptCoverage`), read by this build | loads, field is absent, `historyCoveredThrough` kept, so the old time check is used |
| Binding written by this build (with `transcriptCoverage`), read by stable | loads, the unknown field is dropped, thread id and time kept |
| This build writes then reads `transcriptCoverage` | round trip is exact |
| Malformed `transcriptCoverage` in storage | binding still loads, field ignored |

So an upgrade keeps existing bindings. A downgrade also loads the binding; it only forgets the new field, and the old time check applies again.

### 3. Unit and static checks (unchanged since the last review)

- New test is red on base: `expected [ Array(1) ] to have a length of 2 but got 1`. Green here.
- `run-attempt.bounded-continuity`, `session-binding`, `run-attempt`, `run-attempt.durable-context`, `run-attempt.generation-finalization`: 5 files, 181 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the 4 files.

### Not tested

- A real Codex app-server binary. The app-server is a fake. Real Codex behaviour on `thread/resume` was not run.
- The host row in section 1 was written straight into the Gateway's SQLite transcript. I did not find a Gateway call that adds an unsteered user row during a running turn. `chat.inject` adds an assistant row, and the resume projection did not render that row in this run, so it is not a valid probe.
- A full stable Gateway writing a real binding, then this build reading it. Section 2 uses the stable codec, not a full stable Gateway run. Codex is an external plugin in stable, so this needs a plugin install step that I did not do.
- The "steered row is not sent again" and "row not found, use old time check" paths have no new test. A turn run without a user-turn recorder keeps the old time check.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep bootstrap completion in long sessions
prs.body:
Related: #154923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, the workspace instructions are sent again in a long session, even though the first full turn already completed.

## User Impact

Long sessions keep skipping the workspace instructions after the first turn, as the setting promises. Reset and compaction still re-arm the instructions. Short sessions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The check for "full bootstrap already done" only read the last 500 transcript events. Once the marker was older than that, the check said "not done" and the instructions were injected again.

Now the check asks the transcript reader for the latest marker, reset or compaction on the active branch. The query uses the existing projection snapshot and read fence. It reads only small navigation data and does not unpack message bodies. It reads `customType` with the existing guarded `jsonLastStringValue` helper, so it works on SQLite and PostgreSQL, keeps the last-duplicate-key rule of `JSON.parse`, and does not fail on JSON-valid entries that PostgreSQL cannot store as `jsonb` (for example an escaped NUL). There is no new schema, writer or database connection.

#154923 made the marker get written. This PR fixes how the marker is found again later.

## Evidence

Two proofs. Both use the built product (`pnpm build`), a temp HOME and a temp state dir. Table 1 is a small script on SQLite. The script uses a temp HOME and a temp state dir, makes a real session with `SessionManager` and calls the built `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn`. SQLite only.

| Session | main | this PR (`8c7906f732c`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| marker, then 5 messages | true | true |
| marker, then 501 messages | **false** | true |
| reset, marker, then 501 messages | **false** | true |
| marker, 501 messages, then reset | false | false |
| no marker, 501 messages | false | false |

Table 2 is the shipped path: a built Gateway on a random loopback port, `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, a fake local OpenAI-compatible model server, and `openclaw agent --session-key ... --json` as the client. Steps: two turns, stop the Gateway, append 520 user messages to the same session, start the Gateway again, send a third turn. A completed full-context turn writes one `openclaw:bootstrap-context:full` entry. A turn that injects context again writes another one, so the entry count shows whether the instructions were injected again.

| Step | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| after turns 1 and 2 | 1 entry | 1 entry |
| after 520 more messages | 1 entry | 1 entry |
| after turn 3 | **2 entries** (injected again) | 1 entry (skipped) |

The main build for table 2 was this branch with the changed source files taken from `upstream/main` (it also pulled in a few unrelated newer files). Scripts: fake server, driver and appender are available on request.

Tests (focused files, run with `--maxWorkers=2`):

- Red on main, green here (numbers from the first push; re-run after the rebase: bootstrap, memory-history, maintenance-read and the PostgreSQL conformance file all pass on SQLite, 49 passed and 31 passed, 12 PostgreSQL-only cases skipped). `bootstrap-files.test.ts`: 2 new tests fail on main, 39 of 39 pass here. `session-actor-memory-history.test.ts`: 7 new tests fail on main, 23 of 23 pass here.
- Core type check, test type check shards, oxlint and format check pass on the touched files.

<details>
<summary>Exact script output</summary>

Before (main):

```
as-expected | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=true | marker, then 5 messages (expect true)
UNEXPECTED  | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | marker, then 501 messages (expect true)
as-expected | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | marker, 501 messages, then reset (expect false)
UNEXPECTED  | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | reset, marker, then 501 messages (expect true)
as-expected | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | no marker, 501 messages (expect false)
```

After (this PR): all five rows as expected (true, true, false, true, false).

</details>

Not tested:

- PostgreSQL was not run on my machine (no PostgreSQL here). I added a case to `session-transcript-portability.conformance.test.ts` (a marker followed by a custom entry holding an escaped NUL). It passes on SQLite. It runs on PostgreSQL only in the repo's PostgreSQL conformance CI, and I did not see it red there before the fix.
- The Gateway run used a fake model server, not a real provider. It did not cover reset or compaction through the Gateway (unit tests cover them).
- A cold-storage restore test was left out to keep the test file under its line cap.

## What Problem This Solves

A rejected Workshop experience review loses the source correlation and collapses every anchor mismatch into the same error. Operators cannot distinguish a rewritten completed turn from an unavailable anchor projection after the queued candidate is discarded.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop provider fallback for unavailable transcript projections
prs.body:
Related: #153976.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes provider fallback attempts and failure attribution when a local session transcript projection is rebuilding.

## User Impact

The original storage error stops the turn without consuming another configured provider candidate. There is no configuration or stored-data change. This does not wait for rebuilding, retry the user's message, or improve rebuild speed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the existing projection exception to the existing runtime-coordination classification. That owner already stops fallback for local failures, including errors preserved through provider-looking wrappers. The change leaves failure wording, visibility and recovery ownership in place.

The hydration recovery proposed in #164843 addresses a separate wait/retry boundary. This change only prevents a storage error that reaches fallback from being treated as a provider failure.

## Evidence

A direct Node 26.5.0 probe calls the real `runWithModelFallback` owner with two synthetic candidates and the actual storage exception, in isolated state with no provider transport. On both unpatched main `38c85c2fe23` and the real published OpenClaw 2026.10.5 package, the direct exception and a provider-looking `503` wrapper execute two candidates and report a provider failure. With this fix, each executes once, reports no provider failure or fallback step, and preserves the identical original error. The wrapper previously lost that error in aggregate fallback failure.

The two regression cases extend the existing fallback-owner table; they add no test-only production seam. The full touched suite passes 51/51 with the official agents-core Vitest config on Node 26.5.0 (296.16 seconds wall on the local Mac). A focused run of the two new cases also passes (2/2; 92.70 seconds wall). The owner boundary is needed to verify that neither another candidate nor provider-failure callbacks run; a classification-only test would miss that behavior.

Targeted formatting, typed lint, the owning `agents-other` test typecheck and `git diff --check` pass.

No new state, policy, configuration, retry owner or recovery path was added; the production delta is one error-classification entry. Gateway-entry evidence with a local fake provider is in the next section. No live provider request, channel or production transcript is used or claimed.

## Gateway-entry proof at the current head — 2026-11-16 (UTC)

Built the exact head `f45f5ff9995a47ad512f65dc5e7e7adbbb816711` (`pnpm build`, Node 26.5.0, macOS) and ran it as a loopback-only Gateway with isolated state, no messaging channels, and two model candidates (`mock-primary/primary-model`, fallback `mock-backup/backup-model`) served by a local fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint that records each requested model. The head still merges cleanly into `main` at `687dc6c99a32`.

**Trigger (induced on purpose, not a natural production occurrence):** after a few normal turns, the test session's projection was marked for rebuild (`UPDATE session_transcript_index_state SET needs_rebuild = 1`, the state that the repository fixtures use and that the session-table migration sets on upgrade), and one stored, non-leaf event of that session was made undecodable, so the rebuild fails and the projection stays unavailable. A slow rebuild alone does not reach the fallback decision on this head, because the turn waits for the rebuild within its time limit. The error reaches fallback only when the rebuild ends and the projection is still unavailable, which is the state induced here. Every run used:

```
openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:<test-session> --message "<text>" --json --timeout 60
```

| Build | Fallback decision | Candidate attempts | Error returned to the caller |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR head (two runs) | `chain stopped: reason=local_runtime_coordination` | 1 | `Session transcript projection is rebuilding: <session-id>` |
| Same build with only this PR's entry removed from the two built bundles (restored afterwards, SHA-256 checked) | `candidate_failed reason=unknown next=mock-backup/backup-model` | 2 | same text |

The fake endpoint received no model requests in either variant, because the failure happens while the session is opened. After the stored event was restored, the next turn on the PR head completed normally with `mock-primary/primary-model` (one model request).

Limits: the failure is induced as described. The caller-visible error text is the same in both variants; the difference is the extra candidate attempt and the fallback decision. The provider-looking 503 wrapper is covered only by the owner-level probes, not at the Gateway entry. No live provider, channel or production data was used.

<details>
<summary>Gateway log excerpts</summary>

PR head (excerpt):

```
[sessions/transcript-index] session transcript reconcile failed agent=main error=Expected double-quoted property name in JSON at position 18 (line 1 column 19)
[diagnostic] lane task error: ... errorName=SessionTranscriptProjectionUnavailableError taskKind=turn ... modelFallbackCandidate=true
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=local_runtime_coordination candidate=mock-primary/primary-model errorName=SessionTranscriptProjectionUnavailableError
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Session transcript projection is rebuilding: <session-id>
```

CLI result: `{"ok":false,"origin":"gateway","error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"Session transcript projection is rebuilding: <session-id>"}}`

Control, entry removed (excerpt):

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: ... errorName=SessionTranscriptProjectionUnavailableError taskKind=turn ... modelFallbackCandidate=true
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=mock-primary/primary-model candidate=mock-primary/primary-model reason=unknown next=mock-backup/backup-model
[sessions/transcript-index] session transcript reconcile failed agent=main error=...
[diagnostic] lane task error: ... errorName=SessionTranscriptProjectionUnavailableError taskKind=turn ... modelFallbackCandidate=true
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Session transcript projection is rebuilding: <session-id>
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier owner-level probes and branch history (2026-11-05)</summary>

### Additional current-stable owner probe

Repeated against the actual published OpenClaw **2026.10.10** fallback runner in isolated state. The direct `SessionTranscriptProjectionUnavailableError` and the same exception wrapped by a provider-looking 503 error each execute **two candidates before the fix**, and **one candidate after it**, propagating the identical original error. An ordinary provider 503 still executes the backup candidate, and the existing `ActiveTurnClaimError` still stops after one.

The candidate probe loads the same single classification-name addition through a process-local module load hook; the installed package on disk remains unchanged. All four candidate scenarios pass. An initial probe used an incorrect shortened exception name and failed; that probe was corrected against the actual public diff before the passing run. This is fallback-owner execution with synthetic candidate callbacks, not Gateway-entry or natural-conversation acceptance. Gateway-entry evidence was added in the section above; natural-conversation acceptance is not claimed.

### Conflict resolution against main

Resolved the conflict by merging pinned main into this PR branch, preserving both histories. prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The Slack-owner decision remains whether to expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current submission section below owns the latest head and CI status; maintainer edits remain enabled. Owner acceptance is still outstanding.

The historical [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. Package integrity and the scope are recorded in the [release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621). This is not a new live Slack incident or a claim that existing documented defaults were silently changed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. No new review command or redundant behavior replay was added for this mechanical integration.

prs.title: fix: keep quiet Auto Review calls alive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An Auto Review that runs quietly for more than fifteen minutes can lose the entire reply with `Reply operation stalled` and `no_activity`, including when called inside Code Mode. The review is still within its parent run's lifetime, but the watchdog has no deadline for it.

## User Impact

Users can let long reviews finish within the parent run's budget without losing the turn to the quiet-tool watchdog. Stop, parent timeouts, per-pass limits, and authority revocation retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The watchdog uses `(deadlineAtMs ?? lastProgressAtMs) + quietWindow` ([owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5e6bbeddb9fb9/src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.ts#L594)). Auto Review's execution at `extensions/autoreview/src/tool.ts:237` previously published neither a deadline nor progress. #200670 preserved nested host-exec deadlines, but Auto Review had no deadline to preserve.

The embedded tool wrapper now honors the existing `getExecutionTimeoutMs` contract generically and publishes its result through `recordDiagnosticToolExecutionDeadline` (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts:471`). The admitted execution owner's deadline getter is bound at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.ts:213` and carried through both direct tool construction and the catalog hook context. Auto Review returns the remaining parent budget through that contract (`extensions/autoreview/src/tool.ts:236`). This preserves #175529's policy that the parent owns the review's total lifetime; the Code Mode parent receives the nested liveness allowance through the existing owner.

For an unlimited parent, the watchdog allowance is tool start plus the existing `DEFAULT_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (48 hours). This is only a liveness allowance: it adds no abort timer. A quiet hang remains recoverable after the allowance plus the fifteen-minute quiet window. Watchdog policy is unchanged, core has no tool-name special case, and there are no new public plugin-SDK exports.

The existing execution owner supplies its deadline getter through internal construction options. Necessary growth against the base is 35 net production lines, 8 documentation lines, and 102 test lines; the two cases protect distinct finite/unlimited lifetime behavior.

## Evidence

Two fake-timer cases use the actual Auto Review tool inside the subscribed Code Mode bridge. Both survive past 900 seconds with the parent `exec` still pending, remain alive just before allowance plus quiet window, and are reaped with `no_activity` just after it. Existing per-pass, cancellation, parent-timeout, and prompt-prefix tests pass.

- Red on base `5e6bbeddb9fb9` (repeated after the clock repair): `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/agents/code-mode.bridge.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps quiet nested Auto Review'` → **2 failed, 23 skipped**, both receiving `AbortError: Reply operation stalled`, `staleReason: no_activity` at the first quiet window.

prs.title: fix: keep mobile chat drafts above composer actions
prs.body:
Fixes #200728

## What Problem This Solves

At short phone viewport heights, the chat composer can place its action row over the draft during an active run. At 360×240 and 375×240, the focused empty editor overlaps Stop, and a long draft overlaps Send.

## User Impact

Users can read and scroll their draft without it running beneath the action row. No configuration changes or migration are needed. A sendable draft shows Send rather than Stop; this change does not alter that behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The older landscape layout caps and scrolls the whole composer and makes its footer sticky. Native mobile composers already size the editor against the available pane, so applying both sizing systems causes the overlap.

Exclude native-mobile descendants from all five legacy landscape rules, including the textarea/input/CodeMirror child rule. Keep the original declarations and specificity for standalone session-rail, command-palette, and other legacy composers.

## Evidence

- Updated the unchanged fix to include main `bab767eeea3eeec51d30ca60ab7d8a015902fcdf`. The managed publisher preserved history with a merge commit rather than a linear rebase.
- On that base: 11 composer/keyboard browser E2E tests and 15 mobile component tests pass. Targeted typecheck, oxlint, stylelint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The production UI bundle builds.
- Two retained regressions failed on the original main reproducer `a3f553e2f17e9b1c29cfa2ebe9295c65dbf70167` and pass with the fix. They cover focused Stop, resting side-by-side Stop, and a long scrollable draft with Send at both widths.
- Earlier expanded Chromium verification measured 94 states: widths 360/375, layout heights 640/420/320/240, simulated visual-viewport reductions and keyboard close. Main overlapped in 12 states, all at layout height 240; the final selector correction had zero overlaps. At both failing widths, the fixed editor ends 8 CSS px above the action button. Taller and visual-viewport-only reductions did not reproduce the overlap.
- Completed pr-simplify: retain the existing native-mobile sizing owner and remove the competing legacy rules only in that layout. Production delta is +10/−5 lines; +105 test lines protect the observed overlap, side-by-side layout, and draft scrolling without new production helpers or state.
- Independent source-snapshot and final-selector review found no actionable correctness issues, including standalone consumers. The fix is patch-identical after the base update. The additional local Auto Review attempt was interrupted without a terminal report; it is not claimed as a passing review.

**Size check:** `pnpm ui:check-performance` fails on both the candidate and untouched main for the same three budgets. A same-toolchain baseline build measured largest CSS gzip at 59,191 B on main and 59,218 B with the fix (+27 B; ceiling 58,315 B). Total CSS remains within its fixed ceiling: 336,479 → 336,506 B gzip. Both builds have 21 chat-boot JS requests (limit 20) and 1,325,671 B chat-boot JS gzip (limit 1,325,580 B). No budgets were changed. The archive-based comparison first exhausted the sandbox temporary filesystem; attribution above comes from serial builds in the task workspace with the sole production change removed and then restored.

**Not verified:** physical phones, Safari/WebKit, native keyboards, a real Gateway/model run, or the attachment/reply triggers in related #151843. Browser verification uses the real bundled UI with mocked Gateway acknowledgments and streaming.

### Clean comparison

User-supplied 375×240 long-draft/Send captures for this issue; exact capture commits were not supplied. Before is the reported main behavior; after shows the same local fix before this patch-identical base update.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: lower draft lines obscured by composer actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ac447cd5b640e79d5db6d556af976187c0679c94/images/2026/11/56b24009-0145-40f1-b287-6bccb7effdeb.png) | ![After: last draft line visible above Send](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ac447cd5b640e79d5db6d556af976187c0679c94/images/2026/11/e6f7e8ba-5f00-4b42-bb2f-6ce07690381f.png) |

### Annotated comparison

The same clean captures with labels in an added margin; the captured UI is unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: obscured lower draft lines highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39390fb7-6532-4dc8-ad8c-0541f4b21603) | ![After: visible last draft line highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1e213d7-ad99-4253-bfc8-a04b1c077f5e) |

prs.title: chore(ui): capture missing Dashboard menu click evidence
prs.body:
Extend failure diagnostics for Dashboard menu clicks whose browser event sequence is missing.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6a1b6fef-8de4-46d1-8db7-8a8e43aa305c)

Related: #200660, #200378

## What Problem This Solves

Dashboard menu selections still sometimes time out with the root menu open. The new chronology in two failures after #200660 records opening settlement but no pointer, click, selection, or hide sequence, leaving the production cause unproven. This explicitly requested diagnostics-only follow-up does **not fix the flake**.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Future E2E failures will include the selected item's geometry and hit target, surface interaction styles, and bounded input-path identities. No production code, action timeout, hidden wait, retry, or assertion changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observer already uses document capture and includes pointer/click/focus targets outside the menu. Extend that existing observer with redacted target and composed-path identities, plus one best-effort sample immediately before the click command: item box/center, `document.elementFromPoint`, surface transform and individual scale/translate, pointer events, and inert state. Facts are emitted only on failure. The sample has the existing 500 ms diagnostic deadline and an explicit availability flag; a late sample must not be treated as pre-click evidence.

The production investigation found the 0.95→1 opening scale transition, but no evidence of a coordinate miss or intercepted hit in these incidents. Opening explicitly clears surface inertness, and the inspected chat document listeners do not explain the missing entire input sequence. A production change would still be speculative.

## Evidence

- [Check 134249206000](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44142325296/job/134249206000): Focus → Expand Dashboard, not Restore split. One observed DOM owner, opening→open at 232 ms, after-show at 233 ms, no recorded input/selection/hide/replacement; zero dropped events.
- [Check 134215877308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44132938445/job/134215877308): Restore split. Same observed DOM identities, native toggle at 18 ms, opening→open and after-show at 280 ms; zero dropped events, no recorded input/selection/hide/replacement.
- Node/jsdom: **4/4 observer tests and 29/29 failure-capture consumer tests pass**. New cases cover document capture outside the host despite earlier `stopPropagation`, bounded redacted paths, and immutable pre-click geometry/style evidence after later state changes. The two new cases fail against the original observer for the missing diagnostic fields/method.
- Changed observer suite: 1.60 s Vitest / 2.63 s wrapper wall time, 122 ms test callbacks. Failure-capture consumer: 1.70 s Vitest / 2.81 s wrapper. Per-test CI seconds were not read; the selected UI CI jobs passed.
- Touched-file strict typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Production delta: 0; test/support delta: +177/−6. Simplification keeps the existing observer, ring, cleanup, and failure-facts owner.
- Independent shared Auto Review (Codex default, P0–P2), complete local candidate against `7ee8a43d29fb18e37fada7426afd7e056f1950ea`: **scoped-clean**, no findings. Static review ran no commands or tests.
- Browser proof: automatic exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44157678289) passed all selected `checks-ui-e2e` jobs and all three UI unit shards. Fresh rollup: 50 successful / 64 skipped, none failed or pending; `openclaw/ci-gate` and security-sensitive review are SUCCESS; no local browser/container/broad suite and no CI rerun. Passing CI validates the diagnostics integration, not a flake repair or execution of the future failure branch. The sample precedes Playwright's own scrolling/actionability work and does not claim to be its eventual dispatch point. Document capture cannot observe another frame's events or events stopped before reaching that listener.

If `OPENAI_API_KEY` or another API-key credential is available, it now serves image generation instead. An explicit request with no usable credential fails before any network call with "OpenAI image generation is not included in the Free ChatGPT plan. Upgrade the plan, or configure an OpenAI API key to use the OpenAI Images API." Paid plans, unknown plans and API-key setups are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Free plan has no image tool on any Codex model, and the native Codex image route returns 403 for it (probes in #174733). OpenAI's Codex client makes the same call: `image_generation_available()` returns false for `PlanType::Free` ([openai/codex#34850](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/34850), [`spec_plan.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0a0a9b6c8f2153205ee31eea8e5bbaeb9a3ef5f7/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs#L360-L378)).

Agent tool discovery and credential selection decide image availability in core, through the provider's model auth policy. That is the hook #159920 uses to keep Sign in with ChatGPT credentials out of media requests, and live testing showed a plugin-only check never reaches it (`image_generate` stayed in the agent's tool list). So this PR adds the plan already stored on OAuth credentials to the secret-free policy context as `planType`, and the OpenAI policy rejects `image-generation` for a Free plan. `chatgptPlanType` is written at login and on every token refresh from the access token's claim, so an upgraded account is picked up without signing in again. Like Sign in with ChatGPT, a Free sign-in is filtered before selection, so an independently authorized credential keeps working. Only an exact `free` plan is gated; a missing or unknown plan keeps today's behavior.

In the plugin, the Codex route check passes the stored plan. When a Free sign-in is the only credential, an explicit request names the plan instead of reporting a missing credential. A Free plan in the token claim is still checked before the Codex request, for logins that never stored a plan. The route helpers moved unchanged from `image-generation-provider.ts` into a sibling `image-generation-auth-routes.ts` to stay under the line-cap ratchet.

Review follow-ups:

- The earlier plugin-side Free-plan veto is gone, so a Free Sign in with ChatGPT profile can no longer hide a working `OPENAI_API_KEY` route (P1). Sign in with ChatGPT handling from #159920 is unchanged; the Free rule sits beside it in the same policy and reuses its filter-before-selection intent.
- The new test mocks pass the real module exports through (P2); `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` passes.

## Evidence

Live, Free ChatGPT account (`chatgpt_plan_type: free`, stored as `chatgptPlanType: "free"`), Ubuntu aarch64. Before = released 2026.10.4 (383c124); after = this branch (d462be6), packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`. Both ran against separate copies of the same existing install's state, so the stored login from the 2026.10.4 install was read as-is (the copy for the branch was migrated with `openclaw doctor --fix`); the live gateway and its state were not touched.

Agent tool discovery, `openclaw agent --local --agent clawd --message "Reply with just: ok" --json`, tool names from the run's tool report. Both runs used the built-in runtime with `tools.toolSearch: false` and Code Mode off so every tool appears in the report (the host's installed Codex plugin targets 2026.10.4):

| | Tools | `image_generate` |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 62 | offered |
| After | 62 | not offered (`github_read` and `github_search` are new on main) |

Explicit request, `openclaw infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-2 --prompt "a small red cube on a white background" --json`:

- Before: `OpenAI Codex image generation failed (HTTP 400): Tool choice 'image_generation' must be specified with 'tools' parameter.`
- After: `OpenAI image generation is not included in the Free ChatGPT plan. Upgrade the plan, or configure an OpenAI API key to use the OpenAI Images API.` (no request sent)

API-key control (macOS, this branch, throwaway state with a synthetic Free ChatGPT OAuth login):

- Without `OPENAI_API_KEY`: the same Free-plan message.
- With `OPENAI_API_KEY`: `"ok": true`, `gpt-image-2`, 1024x1024 PNG generated through the Images API; the Free login was skipped by credential selection.

No paid ChatGPT account was available for a live paid control; paid and unknown plans are covered by the tests below.

Tests:

- New cases fail without the policy rule and pass with it: Free plan hidden from `image_generate` discovery; Free plan skipped in credential selection so `OPENAI_API_KEY` serves the request; a pinned Free login fails with the plan reason; the Codex image route ignores a stored Free plan; the OpenAI policy rejects `free` (any case) only for `image-generation`.
- Controls that pass both ways: Plus and unknown plans keep the tool; Free plus an `api_key` profile or `OPENAI_API_KEY` keeps it; Free with `embedding` or no capability stays compatible; a paid token still sends the `gpt-6-astra` Codex request.
- Focused suites (`image-generation-provider{,.auth,.free-plan}.test.ts`, `provider-auth.contract.test.ts`, `image-generate-tool.auth.test.ts`, `model-auth-availability.native.test.ts`): 106 passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`: typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, line-cap ratchet, plugin boundaries and the other guards pass. Three steps fail on current `main` without this PR's files: new max-lines suppressions in `ui/src/pages/*`, the advisory core test shard root budget, and unused exports in unrelated `src/` files. `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` passes.

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): batch direct-chat text and media bursts into one agent turn
prs.body:
Closes #200753
Related: #146117, #146178, #106458

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp users who send a burst like "look at this" + two photos + a voice note + "what do you think?" get several fragmented replies, because inbound debounce batches text but flushes media immediately.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can opt in with `channels.whatsapp.debounceMedia: true` so direct-chat text, photos, videos, voice notes, documents, and stickers sent within the `messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp` window reach the agent as one turn, with every attachment and every voice-note transcript. The default is unchanged (`false`); groups, quoted replies, locations, and control commands such as `/stop` still dispatch immediately.

```json5
{
  messages: { inbound: { byChannel: { whatsapp: 20000 } } },
  channels: { whatsapp: { debounceMedia: true } },
}
```

The toggle appears on the WhatsApp channel page in the Control UI as **WhatsApp Batch Media With Text**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Following the direction in #106458 (a WhatsApp-owned configuration rather than a cross-plugin debounce hook), the policy stays inside the WhatsApp plugin:

- `debounce-policy.ts` decides whether a message may wait. Media waits only when the account enables `debounceMedia` and the conversation is direct; captions keep the control-command bypass. The window keeps its single owner, `messages.inbound.byChannel.whatsapp`.
- A batch that holds media carries ordered `batchedParts` (each caption paired with its own attachment) instead of promoting the last entry's media, so attachment metadata stays with its source message, which is the risk the core text-only guard documents.
- `processMessage` transcribes each uncaptioned voice note of a batch in place, loading the STT runtime once and transcribing concurrently, and marks those media indexes as transcribed so core STT does not repeat them. The default core policy only processes the first attachment, so this also keeps a second voice note from going unheard.
- Dispatch and group history read attachments through one helper (`listWhatsAppInboundMedia`).

Groups stay excluded on purpose: group mention gating transcribes each voice note before admission, and batching would hide a spoken mention.

Config surface: the channel baseline grows by two intentional paths, `channels.whatsapp.debounceMedia` and `channels.whatsapp.accounts.*.debounceMedia` (regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`: channel 4005 → 4007). The root key is in the common Settings tier so the toggle is visible without "advanced".

Accepted edge case: if a media download takes longer than the window, the earlier text flushes alone and the media starts its own turn. Nothing is dropped; with realistic windows (several seconds) this is rare.

## Evidence

**Live proof on a real linked WhatsApp account** (gateway built from this change applied to v2026.11.5, real agent and model, window 20 s, `debounceMedia: true`; this branch carries the same commit rebased onto `main`, where only generated files conflicted and were regenerated). Identifiers redacted:

```text
+0s   inbound message  textLength=0   mediaType=image/jpeg
+3s   inbound message  textLength=21
+9s   inbound message  textLength=21
+18s  inbound message  textLength=22  mediaType=image/jpeg
+27s  inbound message  textLength=0   mediaType=audio/ogg; codecs=opus
+48s  Inbound message <sender> -> <bot> (direct, image/jpeg, image/jpeg, audio/ogg; codecs=opus, 268 chars)
+66s  cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=<model> durationMs=10818   <- single reply
```

The agent transcript for that turn contains both images, the framed voice-note transcript, and the voice-note media marked `transcribed: true`.

**Control UI** (isolated gateways, synthetic config, fake number):

| Before (v2026.11.5) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giovanna-z/openclaw/pr-assets/whatsapp-debounce-media/pr-assets/whatsapp-debounce-media/before-whatsapp.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giovanna-z/openclaw/pr-assets/whatsapp-debounce-media/pr-assets/whatsapp-debounce-media/after-whatsapp.png) |

**Tests** (each new test fails on the base commit and passes here):

- `debounce-policy.test.ts`: media waits only with the toggle, only in direct chats, never for quoted replies or caption commands; the toggle resolves per account.
- `monitor-inbox.debounce-policy.test.ts`: a real inbox burst of text + captioned photo + voice note flushes once, in arrival order, with each caption paired to its attachment and all three read receipts sent.
- `process-message.audio-preflight.test.ts`: two voice notes in one batch are both transcribed, placed in arrival order, and the dispatched context marks exactly those media items as transcribed. The test's context mock now passes through the real prepared `media` list instead of rebuilding it from a single `payload.media`.

Local checks on this branch (rebased onto `main`): `pnpm test:extension whatsapp` (102 files, 1058 tests passed), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm config:channels:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, schema and tier tests, oxfmt, and oxlint on the changed files.

Gaps: `pnpm test:contracts:channels` did not run locally, because its runner requires a full build that exceeds the test host's memory while the live gateway is running; I'm relying on PR CI for that lane. Groups and multi-account linked proof were not exercised live (groups keep the existing behavior).

Follow-up, out of scope: merging `channelStructuredContext` across text-only batches (the P1 noted in #116353). This PR merges it only for batches that hold media, where each attachment's native context must survive.

Note on #146178: that PR batches images only. This one also covers voice notes (with per-note transcription), video, documents, and stickers, and adds live linked-account proof. Happy to consolidate in whichever direction maintainers prefer.

AI-assisted: yes. Implemented with Claude Code; the co-author reviewed the change and ran the live WhatsApp test.

prs.title: fix(nostr): DMs through a relay are lost after its connection drops
prs.body:
Closes #174073

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Nostr channel stops receiving DMs through a relay for the rest of the Gateway's life after that relay's WebSocket closes (a relay restart, a crash, a network blip).

## User Impact

User impact: when a relay connection drops, the channel subscribes to it again (after 10 s, backing off to once a minute) and receives the DMs sent through it, including ones the relay stored while the socket was down. No configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each relay's DM subscription in `startNostrBus` is opened once, at startup. When one closes, the bus only reports `Subscription closed`. With two or more relays (the default) the channel keeps reporting connected, so the health monitor never restarts it, and every DM through the dropped relay is lost. nostr-tools' own reconnect does not cover this on Node: the socket fires `error` before `close` and nostr-tools turns reconnects off for a socket that had connected. So the bus now resubscribes a relay itself after an unexpected close, and never during shutdown or abort.

Rebased onto current `main`, where the per-relay subscription moved into `nostr-bus.ts`. The replay and admission rules follow the review:

- **Where a resubscription starts.** It replays from when that relay's subscription closed (or, if it closed before its EOSE, from where it started), minus the bus's 120 s lookback, and never later than the existing durable cursor's transient-rejection ceiling. A DM that was rejected for a retryable reason (rate limit, backpressure) therefore stays inside the replay even after newer DMs were accepted. Never earlier than the startup baseline.
- **Replay does not use up admission.** Events the bus already stored durably in this process are skipped by every relay subscription before admission (nostr-tools `alreadyHaveEvent`, a bounded set of 4096 ids; rejected events are never added, so they are retried). An event that still reaches durable admission and turns out to be a duplicate hands its rate-window slot back, so even an id that fell out of that set cannot starve a new DM.

## Evidence

A Gateway from source (this branch, `pnpm build`), the Nostr channel and a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider in a Linux container, against three **strfry** relays in Docker. A second key ("alice") DMed the bot through relay 2 only and watched all three relays for replies. After a warm-up turn, relay 2 was restarted (`docker restart`); probe-102 was sent 6 s later, while relay 2 was back but before any resubscription, so the relay stored it.

| | main (`356931bbd`) | this PR (`426d852d4`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| probe-101 (before the restart) | answered in 1 s | answered in 1 s |
| probe-102 (stored on relay 2 during the outage) | **no reply** | answered in 5 s, from the resubscription's replay |
| probe-103, probe-104 (after) | **no reply**: relay 2 disconnected at 13:34:54 and was never subscribed again | answered in 1 s each |

Trace from the PR run (all UTC):

```
# alice
13:11:35.741Z  DROP: docker restart ns-relay2
13:11:41.771Z  sent probe-102 via relay2 only     <- relay2 is back, the Gateway is not subscribed: stored on the relay
# Gateway
13:11:36.092   [nostr] [default] Disconnected from relay: ws://host.docker.internal:7002
13:11:36.114   [nostr] [default] Nostr error (subscription): Subscription closed: relay connection failed
13:11:46.141   [nostr] [default] Connected to relay: ws://host.docker.internal:7002/   <- resubscribed 10 s later
# scripted provider
13:11:46.539Z  turn 3 -> pong: probe-102           <- the stored DM reached the agent from the replay
# alice
13:11:46.775Z  reply "pong: probe-102" after 5s
13:12:26.601Z  reply "pong: probe-103" after 1s
13:13:11.726Z  reply "pong: probe-104" after 1s
```

Tests (`pnpm test`, Linux, Node 24.22.1):

- `nostr-bus.reconnect.test.ts` (new): the real bus and nostr-tools pool against a loopback relay that stores DMs and replays them for each REQ's `since`; only the resubscribe backoff runs on a controlled clock.
  - the relay drops the socket; the bus resubscribes just behind the outage (not the hour since startup) and receives the next DM;
  - **replayed history does not use up admission:** with a 10-event window, six handled DMs are replayed on resubscribe and four new DMs still arrive, with no `rate_limited` rejection;
  - **a rate-limited DM stays in the replay:** a DM stamped 200 s back is rate-limited, a later DM is accepted, and the resubscription still starts at or before the limited DM, which then arrives.
- `nostr-state-store.test.ts`: a duplicate admission hands its rate-window slot back.
- On main all four fail. With each safeguard removed in turn, its test fails: no id skip and no refund fails the burst test; no transient ceiling fails the rate-limited one (`since` 1793017805 > 1793017724).
- `nostr-bus.reconnect`, `nostr-state-store`, `nostr-bus.inbound`, `nostr-cursor`: 41 + 6 passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passes; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the old behavior without touching stored state. Blast radius is the Nostr channel's relay subscriptions and its inbound admission count. A relay that keeps closing is retried once a minute, and a real EOSE resets the backoff; that includes a relay that refuses the DM subscription outright (for example strfry's default `auth-required` for kind 4), which is now retried once a minute with a log line each time. The duplicate refund only applies to events the durable queue already holds, which append nothing.

Not covered: a socket that dies silently and never closes. Nothing detects it, before or after this change; #174073 describes it as a separate follow-up.

prs.title: fix(agents): persona disappears after large inline avatar updates
prs.body:
Related: #127507 (remaining identity/avatar path; the ordinary workspace editor limit was fixed separately).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent loses its persona and custom identity instructions after saving a supported large inline avatar.

## User Impact

A supported 2 MiB avatar stays available for display while the agent continues receiving its name, persona, and instructions before and after the avatar field. Stored identity and avatar bytes remain intact. Ordinary workspace files and projected identity text retain their 2 MiB limits. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model receives a text projection with the inline image omitted. Identity publication and raw sandbox copies use the existing bounded 4 MiB identity allowance. Raw files and prepared identity text share the existing cache byte budget.

The implementation follows the canonical bootstrap file reader and preserves parallel read settlement, prompt order, source identities, and live workspace revocation. Extra-file discovery moves unchanged into its own module to keep the existing oversized workspace module from growing, retaining main's complete-file glob matching.

## Evidence

**Review target:** `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, comparison base `27f243756a45f02724b70597803571e2f0e1d020`. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159), including the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127820963084) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127823558387), passed. GitHub associates those checks with this exact head; the CI execution used the merge commit documented below.

| Revision | Evidence and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Current `8c251978` | 13 focused tests across projection, raw sandbox copy, and bootstrap cache; production-source filesystem probe preserves persona and exact raw copy, rejects an oversized ordinary file, and checks managed glob selection. Current-head hosted CI passed. |
| Previous `3034a560` | 224 tests, one existing skip, core typecheck and typed lint passed. Its CI ratchet failed on inherited debt. The recorded full-index PR patch is byte-identical to the current patch; this does not make its CI green. |
| Historical `4fd20c3` | Built Gateway/agent CLI and real host-model generation preserved four persona facts with a 2 MiB inline avatar. Separate base/candidate probes demonstrated the original loader and copy failures. These executions belong to that historical revision. |

The current candidate's recorded full-range independent review covers all 15 changed files, including the discovery extraction, bounds, cache, and publication owners, with no actionable findings. Its retained full-index diff SHA256 is `c76627e0c35fe7241bf1818f41e63e98807af184814b6ca211de00941b8ade0b`. This description update adds no code or new test execution. The [November 11 hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173124#issuecomment-6192419182) now covers `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, with sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. Its 4/6 proof assessment explicitly retains the historical-revision and model-bridge limitations below.

**Proof limits:** No full Gateway/model E2E was rerun on `8c251978`. The historical real-model proof used a manually orchestrated host-model bridge, not a genuine external Responses service compatibility test. Historical builds skipped declaration emission; skipped CI lanes are not build/test proof. The failed historical ratchets and unavailable local autoreview remain recorded below.

<details>
<summary>Retained verification records, commands/observations, and historical limitations</summary>

The ordinary built Gateway, normal agent CLI, CLI parser, and Gateway RPC paths are used. For the multi-megabyte update/save parameters only, a task preload replaces a short `--params` placeholder with JSON file contents before the unchanged CLI parser; this avoids Linux's single-argument size limit. CLI proof invocations provide the same `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning` Node flag that the CLI normally adds during startup, avoiding a second OS spawn after large JSON expansion.
