Independent host-session review of the complete 15-file committed range `6b9a762375a4044ce7b69a626fa13d36c8f63738..4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c` found no supported P0/P1/P2 findings. It independently matched all changed-file bytes and 21 runtime source hashes to the commit, and inspected the actual primary HTTP request, storage, session and cleanup observations. The full-index committed diff SHA256 is `179c31c174551d7f93be598ed59f9d64fc4c6525a8c324bd57beb8ee5a7c6fde`.

Local autoreview remains unavailable: the previously attempted helper rejects its configured `stream_max_retries` before sending a provider request. No successful autoreview of this final range is claimed; the independent source review above is the review actually performed.

Setup failures are retained separately: the first offline build needed two existing lock-pinned Darwin native asset archives; preparing the build owner's cache with SHA-512-verified archives allowed the isolated build to complete. The first CLI proof stopped before the update RPC with `E2BIG` during startup respawn; supplying the normal Node flag corrected the proof transport. Earlier proof and reviews on `c56a0e8d8d778478b950c11e2c9b6fde90d05b2c` remain historical; they do not establish validation of the conflict-repair candidate. Maintainer edits remain enabled.

### Historical red-on-base and candidate comparison (4fd20c3)

The same two probes ran through the canonical Vitest runner in separate detached source views: baseline `6b9a762375a4044ce7b69a626fa13d36c8f63738` and published candidate `4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c`. A second supported build completed on the clean published `4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c` HEAD (289 seconds, supported declaration-emission skip). prs.title: fix: keep memory notes that start with a CR or CRLF line break exactly as written
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory note is saved and the new text starts with a CR or CRLF line break, OpenClaw adds an extra LF in front of it. The saved file then has a line break that was not in the text. This can happen on the host and in the sandbox.

## User Impact

User impact: memory notes that start with CR or CRLF are now saved exactly as written. Notes that start with LF, and notes that start with any other text, behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a leading LF was seen as "already starts on a new line". Now a leading CR counts too. This is done in the host append, the sandbox append and the text given to the provenance record. Nothing else changes.

## Evidence

Tests (`src/agents/agent-tools.memory-flush-append-write.test.ts`): two new cases, run for host and sandbox, so 4 new tests. On plain `main` (7ee8a43d29f) 4 fail and 16 pass. With this change all 20 pass. The neighbouring `agent-tools.memory-flush-writer.test.ts` also passes (32 tests in both files). `tsgo:core`, format and lint pass for the touched files.

Real code, before and after: I ran the real `projectMemoryFlushTools` write tool from source with `tsx` (not a built `dist`) against a temp workspace, for host and sandbox. The sandbox used the repo's test bridge that writes to the host disk, not a container. The file starts as `Saved` with no final newline. Bytes in hex:

| Added text | Before (main) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `\n- note\n` | `53 61 76 65 64 0a 2d ...` | same |
| `\r- note\r` | `53 61 76 65 64 0a 0d 2d ...` (extra `0a`) | `53 61 76 65 64 0d 2d ...` |
| `\r\n- note\r\n` | `53 61 76 65 64 0a 0d 0a 2d ...` (extra `0a`) | `53 61 76 65 64 0d 0a 2d ...` |

Host and sandbox gave the same bytes. The text passed to the provenance record matched the file bytes in every case.

<details><summary>Full output</summary>

Before:
```
host    delta=CR   file : 53 61 76 65 64 0a 0d 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d   expected=false
host    delta=CRLF file : 53 61 76 65 64 0a 0d 0a 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d 0a   expected=false
sandbox delta=CR   file : 53 61 76 65 64 0a 0d 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d   expected=false
sandbox delta=CRLF file : 53 61 76 65 64 0a 0d 0a 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d 0a   expected=false
```
After:
```
host    delta=CR   file : 53 61 76 65 64 0d 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d   expected=true
host    delta=CRLF file : 53 61 76 65 64 0d 0a 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d 0a   expected=true
sandbox delta=CR   file : 53 61 76 65 64 0d 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d   expected=true
sandbox delta=CRLF file : 53 61 76 65 64 0d 0a 2d 20 6e 6f 74 65 0d 0a   expected=true
```
</details>

Not tested: a full `pnpm build` and a running gateway; a real container sandbox; the full test suite (CI runs it).

prs.title: fix: keep one missing archived transcript from blocking every update
prs.body:
Related: #200594 #200659

## What Problem This Solves

Updates that rehearse Doctor on a private copy of your state now copy your cold (archived) session transcripts into that copy. Since #200659, if even one archived transcript file referenced by your database was already gone (deleted by hand, lost in a restore, or a dangling link), the update refused before doing anything, and every later update refused the same way. Separately, on Windows the rehearsal shared the live archive files through hard links, and removing those links on a filesystem without POSIX delete semantics (for example an SMB share) clears the live file's read-only attribute.

## User Impact

User impact: one lost archive file no longer blocks every update. The rehearsal mirrors your state as it is: a missing archive stays missing, the snapshot reports a warning that names it, and only a Doctor repair that actually reads that archive fails, exactly as it would on your live state. On Windows the rehearsal never shares an archive file with your live state.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Missing payloads: inventory sizing and the snapshot projection now treat a missing archive file (including a dangling symlink) as missing instead of refusing. Corrupt archives still copy as-is and still fail their integrity check when read, so nothing broken is hidden.
- Windows: archives are always copied, never hard-linked. Native proof on Windows Server 2025 with Node 24.22.1: removing a hard link on local NTFS leaves the live file untouched (libuv uses POSIX delete), but on an SMB share libuv's fallback delete clears the read-only attribute of the shared file. A private copy avoids that on every Windows filesystem. Released updaters already budget a full copy of these bytes, so no space accounting changes.
- No schema, protocol, or config change. The released parent's capacity field is unchanged.

## Evidence

Live update proof on Crabbox AWS Linux. Each lane installed published 2026.11.4, seeded one file-backed cold transcript archive with released 11.4 code (database row `storage=file` confirmed), then deleted the archive file before updating:

| Lane | Update | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Base: main with #200659 (`9bf980ed4a1`) | 11.4 → main, CLI | **Refused** after 97 s: `Update state snapshot failed ... ENOENT ... during plugin inventory ... stat .../sessions/cold/<archive>.jsonl.zst`; stays on 11.4 |
| Fix | 11.4 → fix, CLI | Succeeded (285 s, readyz 200); update JSON carries the warning `1 referenced cold transcript archive file(s) are missing (first: ...)` |
| Fix | 11.4 → fix, managed `update.run` | Succeeded (333 s, Gateway core ready); same warning in the update status detail |
| Fix, archive left in place | 11.4 → fix, CLI | Succeeded (268 s, readyz 200) |

The fix package was built from `8deffc38ee1`. The final head `715db3a63d3` only widens the same check to the repo's `isMissingPathError` (ENOENT or ENOTDIR) for a dangling link whose target path runs through a regular file.

Windows (native, Windows Server 2025, Node 24.22.1): a hard link to a read-only live file, then the rehearsal directory removed with `fs.rm`. On local NTFS the live file stays read-only (libuv uses POSIX delete). On an SMB share (`\\localhost\C$`) the live file becomes writable, because libuv's fallback delete clears the read-only attribute of the shared file. With a private copy, both stay read-only. The Windows proof covers the file-system behavior; a full Windows update lane was not run for this change.

Regression tests: on base sources 3 of 6 fail (snapshot refuses a missing archive, inventory refuses, the Windows projection shares the inode). With the fix 7 of 7 pass, including a new dangling-link case. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.

Reviews: autoreview scoped-clean (P2) on `715db3a63d3`; independent Codex review: no findings. Earlier rounds found the dangling-link and Windows test-assertion gaps, both fixed.

Production LOC: +66/−26 across the worker and its caller (net state.ts 0; tests +114/−39; docs +7/−3).

prs.title: fix(codex): attach a request over the turn cap instead of losing its middle
prs.body:
Related: #200514, #200690

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server rejects any turn over 1,048,576 characters (`MAX_USER_INPUT_TEXT_CHARS` in codex-rs). Since #200690, a current request over that cap keeps its head and tail and loses its middle. Anything that appears only in the middle is gone, and the model answers from what remains.

Large requests come from hooks (up to 1 MiB since #200514), the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (20 MiB bodies), channel messages, pastes and cron messages.

## Fix

- **New host capability, `fitCurrentInput`.** It is a generic harness host capability, so there are no new Plugin SDK exports. The Codex attempt calls it right after its connection is ready, with the Codex turn cap and the connection's own `prepareInputAttachments`.
- **Over the cap, and the run may read files on this host:** the full request is saved as an inbound attachment (`current-request.txt`). The model sees the request's head and tail, which keep the instruction and both untrusted-content markers. It also sees a marker saying the visible part is incomplete and that it should search the attachment before answering, plus the attachment path.
- **Placement is the connection's decision.** It already refuses local paths for a sandbox, remote execution, non-stdio transport, a remote workspace root, restricted tools or a non-full permission mode, and prefers a registered remote attachment binding.
- **Otherwise:** only the middle is cut, as in #200690.
- **Transcript:** keeps the original (`transcriptPrompt`). There is no change to stored turns, schema or retention; the file follows the operator's existing inbound attachment retention.
- **Visible outcome:** each case logs `current input oversize: chars=… budget=… action=attached|cut`.

**Scope, after local review.** Earlier revisions also estimated a token budget from the model window and fitted requests for the built-in runtime. A chars-per-token estimate cannot prove token overflow. Fitting below the hard cap could drop content that fit, and the built-in runtime has its own token-aware overflow handling. This version acts only past a runtime's hard per-turn text cap, so nothing that worked inline changes.

## User Impact

On the Codex runtime, a request over 1 MiB stays usable: the agent can search the full text instead of guessing from its start and end. Requests within the cap and the built-in runtime behave as before.

## Evidence

Real Gateways from source with real models on the Codex runtime, `POST /v1/chat/completions`.

**1. 3 MB request.** A 2,948,079-character meeting transcript. The instruction is at the top ("Kenji Sato states the budget codeword. Reply with ONLY that codeword"). The codeword `HERON-5150` appears once, at the 49.9% offset.

| model | `main` 9aed362 | this PR, final head |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-5.4 | `Fire`, `Fire`, `ClawRouter` (0/3) | `HERON-5150` ×3 (3/3) |
| gpt-5.4-mini | `armed`, `Fire`, `Fire` (0/3) | `HERON-5150` 1/3 (`armed`, `done`) on an earlier head with the same staging path |

- The log shows `current input oversize: chars=2948079 budget=1048576 action=attached`.
- The Codex rollout shows the agent opening `…/media/inbound/current-request---….txt`, parsing it, and printing the matching segment.

**2. 2 MiB request whose instruction is only at the top** ("reply exactly ZEBRA-4217"), gpt-5.4-mini, final head: `ZEBRA-4217`, `action=attached`.

**Tests:**

- `src/agents/harness/current-input-budget.test.ts` covers three cases:
  - unchanged within the cap;
  - attached: the saved file holds the full original, and the instruction and both markers stay inline;
  - cut-only when staging returns nothing.
- Passing: `src/agents/harness/` and every `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt*.test.ts` (11 shards), `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `check:test-types`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check`.

**Not covered / accepted:**

- gpt-5.4-mini is unreliable at finding a middle-only fact through the attachment (1/3). The docs say so.
- Requests over the 5 MB inbound media cap fall back to the cut.
- Each retry of the same oversized turn saves its own copy.
- The Codex-side head/tail cut from #200690 stays as the guard for prompt decoration that still exceeds the cap.
- The built-in runtime's handling of an oversized single message stays a separate, token-aware follow-up.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep the instruction when an oversized request is fitted
prs.body:
Related: #200514

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex runtime accepts at most 1 MiB of text per turn (`MAX_USER_INPUT_TEXT_CHARS` in `codex-rs/protocol/src/user_input.rs`). `fitCodexProjectedContextForTurnStart` enforces that cap. When the current request alone was over the cap, it was cut with the same helper used for older history, which keeps only the tail (`[truncated N chars from older context]`).

For a current request, the head is the part that matters. The instruction, the opening `<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT>>>` marker and its safety note were all removed. Only the closing marker and the run's trailing guidance survived. The model then answered whatever the tail suggested, and the run still finished `ok`.

Found while reviewing #200514. On its first revision an 8 MiB hook body made the agent ignore the hook and run unrelated tool calls. #200514 now caps hook bodies at 1 MiB, but any route can send a request over the cap: the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, chat, cron messages or large pasted text.

## Fix

The three places where a current request can exceed the cap now keep its head and tail and cut the middle, with a visible `[truncated N chars from the middle of the current request]` marker:

- the request range itself;
- the preserved input when there is no projected history;
- the request and hook text after the history.

Projected history keeps its current tail-first truncation. The kept tail keeps its source position, so history image groups inside it still map. One existing test asserted the old tail-only result for an oversized request; it now checks that the request header and tail both survive. The `preserved` case of the image-mapping test is removed: production only maps images when there is a projected context range (`run-attempt-prompt.ts`), so the range-less preserved path cannot carry images.

## User Impact

A request over 1 MiB on the Codex runtime still loses its middle, but the model now sees the instruction, both untrusted-content markers and a marker saying how much was cut.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway from source, real model** (`openai/gpt-5.4-mini` on the Codex runtime), `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a 2,097,270-character message. The instruction at the top says "Ignore the meeting transcript below. Reply with exactly ZEBRA-4217 and nothing else." The transcript contains a different codeword near its end.

| build | trial 1 | trial 2 | trial 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` 3b61a7c | "Got it — I have the transcript context. What would you like me to do…" | "I'm missing the actual question here…" | "…including the codeword **OSPREY-2208**. What would…" |
| this PR | `ZEBRA-4217` | `ZEBRA-4217` | `ZEBRA-4217` |

The Codex rollouts show `[truncated 1048739 chars from older context]` on `main` and `[truncated 1048760 chars from the middle of the current request]` here. Prompt tokens are 238k on both builds.

**Tests:** `keeps the instruction and both content boundaries of an oversized current request` covers the three fitting paths. It fails on `main` (the result starts with `[truncated … chars from older cont…`) and passes here. `context-engine-projection.test.ts` passes. `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass.

**Not covered:** the app-server suite has one failure, `dynamic-tools.test.ts` › `bounds high-cardinality validation errors returned to Codex`. It fails the same way on `main` 3b61a7c and does not involve this file. Five native app-server tests timed out during a run on a host at load ~100, then passed when rerun alone.

**Not in this change:** an operator log line when a request is cut. A `warn` from this module did not show up in the scratch Gateway's console or file log during the E2E runs, even though the code path ran, so it is left out until that log path is understood.

prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:

Avoid implementation details such as:

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: on Windows machines without the Visual C++ redistributable, OpenClaw's native process helpers fail to load. `openclaw doctor` reports `proc-safe: load-failed` (`ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`), and process identity, process census, Job-object supervision and AppContainer token checks are unavailable.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: on a clean Windows x64 or ARM64 install, the process helpers load with no separate VC++ runtime install. Doctor reports `proc-safe: loaded`, and the creation-time PID-reuse guard, process census, Job-object kill-on-close supervision and token queries work. No config, API or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

`@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.2's Windows natives import `VCRUNTIME140.dll`, which a clean Windows install doesn't have. 0.6.0 includes openclaw/proc-safe#40: the Windows x64 and ARM64 natives link the VC runtime statically and keep the OS-serviced UCRT. This PR adopts 0.6.0.

0.4.2 → 0.6.0 is additive for OpenClaw: no breaking entries in the changelog, and the typed API only gains an opt-in Job-child stdin pipe and a Linux `filesystem-launch` subpath. No OpenClaw call site changes. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` gets a reviewed exact-version release-age exception that expires seven days after publish, matching earlier fs-safe bumps.

The same release also changes two other platforms:
- **Linux:** glibc 2.28–2.33 hosts now load the native instead of using the existing `/proc` fallback.
- **macOS:** identity reads for protected processes such as `login` now come from validated kernel records. The native ancestry walk can therefore continue past Terminal's `login`, so the `ps` fallback from #193164 isn't reached in that case. Ancestry results stay the same or become more complete. The fallback is kept because it still covers the case where both native interfaces deny access.

fs-safe has the same VC++ dependency. Its hybrid-CRT fix isn't released yet and will follow separately.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For visual web/macOS/iOS/Android changes, follow
the PR visual-proof standard and its screenshot delivery gate:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/media.md#pr-visual-proof
Keep the clean before/after pair visible first, then the annotated pair.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Head `65dabc2f958bcf38183d8310e6fb2c902e030d96` on base `d29fad4e3e687dedf683e38ec35b12cb85510637`.

**Clean Windows x64 guest, before and after.**
- **Guest:** Hyper-V Win11 build 29683 with no VC++ runtime. Before and after the runs there was no `VC\Runtimes\x64` key, and every `vcruntime140*`/`msvcp140*`/`concrt140`/`vccorlib140`/`vcomp140` DLL failed LoadLibrary with 126. Only Node 24.22.1 was added.
- **Build:** one OpenClaw tarball built from this head with `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog` (SHA-256 `B15256DA…2C239838`, matched on the guest).
- **Installs:** npm-installed twice. `before` adds an npm override back to `@openclaw/proc-safe` 0.4.2, which loads its nested `proc-safe-win32-x64-msvc@0.4.2`. `after` is this head's own dependency, 0.6.0. proc-safe is the only variable.

| Probe, from the installed `openclaw` dependency tree | before (0.4.2) | after (0.6.0) |
|---|---|---|
| `getProcSafeNativeStatus({ probe: true })` | `reason=load-failed`, `loadErrorCode=ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` | `reason=loaded`, `win32-x64-msvc@0.6.0` |
| `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/native-status --severity-min info --json` | `warning: proc-safe: load-failed` | `info: proc-safe: loaded` |
| `readProcessIdentity(self)` / a child's identity and parent | `helper-unavailable` | ok / ok, parent = probe |
| `listProcesses({ pids: [self], includeCommand: true })` | `helper-unavailable` | ok: identity and `node.exe` |
| `readCurrentAppContainerSid()` | `helper-unavailable` | `null` (not contained) |
| `WindowsJob.create({ killOnJobClose: true })`, spawn, then close | `helper-unavailable` | child admitted (`processIds` = [child]) and gone after close |

Both Doctor runs also report `fs-safe: load-failed`, which is out of scope here and is why Doctor exits 1 in both. The probes ran over SSH as a local administrator at High integrity in session 0, and none of these operations depend on the session or integrity level.

**ARM64 (static only, no ARM64 guest).** PE imports of the exact registry natives:
- `proc-safe-win32-{x64,arm64}-msvc@0.4.2` import `vcruntime140.dll`.
- `@0.6.0` import no VC runtime DLL (no delay imports either) and still use the UCRT `api-ms-win-crt-*` set.

**Local checks on Windows (x64, Node 26.13.0).**
- The canonical package build passed, including `check-cli-bootstrap-imports`.
- `node scripts/check-openclaw-package-tarball.mjs --require-bundled-workspace-deps <tgz>`: "OpenClaw package tarball integrity passed." The packer's 300 s wrapper timed out on this host; the direct run took 635 s.
- `pnpm test` over all 47 non-e2e test files that import proc-safe. These pass: daemon (3 files), process and supervisor (9, 1 skipped), `shared/pid-alive`, cli and update-handoff, and infra. The infra files include doctor native-status, process census (including `.windows`), restart-stale-pids ancestry, managed-service handoff identity/native/process, Windows process start, AppContainer spawn, process-respawn and update continuation.
- Failures seen locally are Windows-host artifacts in code this PR doesn't touch, and Linux CI is the broad proof:
  - tooling tests that assert `/` path separators, or whose fixtures omit `src/shared/deferred.ts`;
  - `doctor-health.fleet-preflight`: a temp-dir EPERM and a 120 s timeout under host load;
  - `doctor-maintenance.admission-activation`: the SQLite read-only worker rejects the Windows file-URL path (`ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH`);
  - `chrome.internal`: browser executable detection fails on this host, and identity is mocked in that test.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` (root-package surface, all lanes) passes, including typecheck of all projects, format, the dependency pin guard, plugin boundaries and package patch guard. Three items did not pass, none caused by this diff:
  - The npm package-lock guard hit Windows' command-line length limit.
  - The Plugin SDK surface budget is over (163 > 162 entrypoints). Its inputs are identical on base; this diff only changes the proc-safe dependency line.
  - Lint: `oxlint:core` timed out at 902 s on this host, and two `max-lines` hits are in unchanged test files that are already over 1000 lines on base (`extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts`).

**Local ClawSweeper review.** `clawsweeper review --local-range` over `d29fad4e3e68..65dabc2f958b`, with this description:
- Completed, decision `keep_open` at high confidence.
- Patch correct (0.93), no review findings, security cleared.
- Real-behavior proof rated sufficient (`live_output`).
- Rated platinum hermit overall, for proof and for patch, with no rank-up steps.

prs.title: fix(telegram): record each final answer's delivery outcome in debug logs
prs.body:
Related: #189765, #49889, #111064

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram final answer leaves no Gateway log record of how it was delivered when it is edited into the streaming preview, and on current main a final sent as a new message leaves none either.

## User Impact

User impact: with the Gateway file log at debug level (`logging.level: "debug"`, or `OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL=debug`), each text final handled by `deliverFinalAnswerText` writes one line to the Gateway log naming how it settled; under `--verbose` the line is also printed to the console. Default INFO output is unchanged, and delivery behavior is unchanged.

`telegram final delivery outcome=<kind> chat=<id> [message=<ids>] [reason=<suppression reason>]`

Kinds: `preview-finalized` (the answer's preview stream holds the final: edited into a visible preview, or, for a final under the 30-character preview threshold, sent by the stream as its first message), `preview-finalized-partial` (the preview shows the final but a follow-up step failed; `telegram final reply failed` also fires), `preview-retained` (`reason=adapter_returned_no_identity`), `sent` (the lane's normal send path, for example with streaming off), `skipped` (for example `channel_transform`, `cancelled_by_message_sending_hook`, `no_visible_result`). The kind is the lane's own delivery result, logged as is. The line carries ids and the suppression reason only, no message content.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main removed the routine Telegram success lines on 2026-10-16: `telegram outbound send ok` in #174260 (`e2bdc7a2b71`) and `telegram text delivery ok` in #174402 (`dcd28a06c67`). Since then a final edited into the preview and a final sent as a new message both settle with no success line at any level; only failures are logged.

Earlier versions of this description said those per-message lines "still fire" next to the outcome line. That was wrong: both removals are ancestors of this PR's base and of current main.

#189765 (2026.10.9) is the kind of current-release report the #49889 closure asked for: finals and native-command replies left no success line, a delivered answer looked lost, and the user got it twice. ClawSweeper's review there recommends keeping default logs quiet and improving debug diagnostics, so this PR now writes the outcome line through `logVerbose`, the path the Telegram extension already uses for verbose diagnostics in this file (`telegram progress discard failed`, the lane deliverer's `log`). `logVerbose` (`src/globals.ts`) returns early unless `--verbose` is on or the file log level is `debug`, then writes a debug record through the Gateway logger and prints to the console only under `--verbose`. If you would rather have this at INFO, it is a one-line change back to `turn.runtime.log`, and the `(info)` test case flips.

The line is written where each text final settles, in `deliverFinalAnswerText`: the [formatter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e90dd3e3b3ef687f9ab473681d85c8547ec35619/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts#L457), the [early `channel_transform` skip](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e90dd3e3b3ef687f9ab473681d85c8547ec35619/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts#L497) (the recovered transcript final leaves nothing to send), and the [settled result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e90dd3e3b3ef687f9ab473681d85c8547ec35619/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts#L550).

Not covered: finals that bypass `deliverFinalAnswerText` (media-only finals, status notices), native-command replies such as `/model` (the other half of #189765, sent from `bot-native-command-builtins.ts`), finals dropped before delivery, non-final preview finalizations, and the reasoning lane.

Overlap: #165510 is open and touches other files. #170069 was closed without merging, so the earlier note about its follow-up finals no longer applies.

## Evidence

Head `e90dd3e3b3e`: `6ef53a3bc78` merges main `2e24ab71b14793899f62ba255e2a327efaf5a79b` into `e633886c9f1c` with no conflicts, then `e90dd3e3b3e` moves the line to `logVerbose` and updates the tests. Against that main: 3 files, +181 (20 production lines, 159 test lines, a 2-line test-lines allocation).

Local, macOS, 2 Vitest workers. Correction: these ran on the local default runtime, which since #172625 is OpenClaw's pinned Bun, not Node 26.12.1 as this line said; the Node re-run is the first bullet.

- Re-run on Node 26.12.1 (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`), merged onto main `3855c896edd`: `bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts` 17 passed.

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts`: 17 passed (17).
- Same tests with `bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts` from the previous head `e633886c9f1c` (INFO through `runtime.log`): 8 failed, 9 passed. The `(info)` and `(debug)` preview cases fail with `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called` (it received `telegram final delivery outcome=preview-finalized chat=123 message=1001`); six outcome cases fail with `expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]` because the line never reaches the Gateway log.
- Same tests with only the early-skip call removed: 1 failed, 16 passed, the new `channel_transform` case.
- Same tests with main's `bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts`, which has no outcome line: 7 failed, 10 passed. The `(info)` case passes there, as it should.
- 10 Telegram dispatch test files (this one, `delivery-transcript`, `fallback-topic-media`, `progress-card`, the four dispatch `telegram-http` suites, `lane-delivery`, `lane-delivery.presentation`): 149 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm run tsgo:all`: exit 0. `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the 2 changed files: exit 0. Line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets against `2e24ab71b14`: OK.
- Test-lines ratchet against `2e24ab71b14`: net delta +159, matched by `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-final-delivery-outcome.txt` (159). It still exits 1, "over by: 443", which is main's own overage at `2e24ab71b14` (6,420,146 test lines against a 6,419,703 ceiling). Main has been over its ceiling since `2a32ab046f2` (#191638), so that check fails for any PR that adds tests until main is back under.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts` 64.1 s (cold worker cache, 23.4 s of it compiling) and 28.0 s wall, 17.0 s and 17.2 s of tests. CI run 41607418127, Bun: `bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts` 40.7 s Vitest duration, 13.7 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-extensions-config`).

The Gateway run below uses a local fake Bot API; a short live Telegram run follows it.

### Gateway run at this head (2026-11-09)

A real Gateway from a built `dist`, a local fake Telegram Bot API that grammY talks to as its transport, and a scripted Responses provider. Base: main `3855c896edd`. Head: this PR merged onto that main, since the branch is about 2,350 commits behind (`git merge-tree --write-tree 3855c896edd e90dd3e3b3e` = `c61c6ed8331`, no conflicts; its diff from main has the same patch-id as this PR's diff). Gateway: `node dist/index.js gateway run` on Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64; Vitest also on Node. `logging.file` points at a file read back after each run, and `OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL` is unset.

Two bot accounts, three DMs one at a time:
- `streaming.mode: "partial"`, a streamed answer: preview `sendMessage` 9001, then two `editMessageText` to 9001, the last one with the full answer.
- Same account, a 12-character answer: `sendMessage` 9002.
- `streaming.mode: "off"`, a 12-character answer: `sendMessage` 9003.

Outcome lines, debug and info run twice per build, `--verbose` once:

| build | `logging.level` | `--verbose` | outcome lines in the Gateway file log | on the console |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | debug | no | 0, 0 | 0, 0 |
| main | info | no | 0, 0 | 0, 0 |
| main | info | yes | 0 | 0 |
| this PR | debug | no | 3, 3 | 0, 0 |
| this PR | info | no | 0, 0 | 0, 0 |
| this PR | info | yes | 3 | 3 |

This head at debug, from the Gateway file log:

```
2026-11-09T02:04:53.084-05:00 telegram final delivery outcome=preview-finalized chat=777 message=9001
2026-11-09T02:04:54.714-05:00 telegram final delivery outcome=preview-finalized chat=777 message=9002
2026-11-09T02:04:57.403-05:00 telegram final delivery outcome=sent chat=777 message=9003
```

- Each of those is a DEBUG record tagged `verbose` whose source frame is `logVerbose`.
- The debug file log works on main as well (149 and 148 DEBUG records in its two runs); it just has no outcome line.
- At info the file log has 164 records in all four info runs, main and this head, none of them an outcome line.
- With `--verbose` at info the console prints the 3 lines, and the file log picks them up as INFO through console capture.
- The fake Bot API saw the same 5 calls in all 10 runs, and `chat.history` read back 3 user and 3 assistant messages each time.

`preview-finalized` means the answer's preview stream holds the final, not that an earlier preview was edited. The 12-character answer on the partial account is under the 30-character preview threshold, so no preview went out while it streamed. At the final, the stream's `stop()` sends it as the stream's first and only message (9002; the fake API saw no edit and no delete for that turn), and the line reads `outcome=preview-finalized message=9002`. `sent` is the lane's normal send path, which the account with streaming off takes.

Not covered: real Telegram, Linux, group chats, media and native-command finals, and the `preview-retained`, `preview-finalized-partial` and `skipped` kinds at the Gateway level (the lifecycle tests above cover those).

### Live Telegram at this head (2026-11-10)

A throwaway bot in a DM, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1: one isolated Gateway built from main `9a5df3d60f1` with this PR's head and four of my other PR heads merged in (no file touched by two of them), on the real Telegram Bot API, with QA Lab's scripted mock provider (head `e90dd3e3b3e`), `logging.level: "debug"`.

- `streaming.mode: "partial"`: the reply streamed into a preview message and the final was edited into it. Gateway log: `telegram final delivery outcome=preview-finalized chat=<id> message=7`.
- After `openclaw config patch` set `streaming.mode: "progress"`, the next DM turn: `telegram final delivery outcome=sent chat=<id> message=9`.
- Not run live: the INFO leg and a main-side control. Both are in the Gateway run above.

### After-fix proof (production, 2026-10-13/14)

Recorded before this change moved the line to debug level, on a v2026.10.1 build with local patches whose `bot-message-dispatch-delivery.ts` change matched this PR's INFO version line for line. It was deployed on 2026-10-13 to two gateways.

- Gateway A: 3 Telegram accounts, `streaming.mode: "partial"`. 33 outcome lines since the restart: 8 `preview-finalized`, 25 `sent`.
- Gateway B: replies through the message tool only. 11 outcome lines, all `sent`.

One turn from gateway A, chat id and bot name redacted:

    2026-10-14T12:58:44.039-04:00 [telegram] Inbound message telegram:group:<group> -> @<bot> (group, 39 chars)
    2026-10-14T12:59:03.228-04:00 [telegram] final delivery outcome=preview-finalized chat=<group> message=46883

Telegram's sent-message record for 46883 (`plugin_state_entries`, namespace `telegram.sent-messages`) was created at 12:59:03, the same second. No other send line exists for that turn, and on current main none would exist for a `sent` final either.

prs.title: fix: managed nodes fail to start when a sandbox restricts IPC
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent can start its OpenClaw workspace node under Strands Box and still get stuck before the node connects to its Gateway. The node launcher and its child exchange JSON over Node's native IPC channel. In a Linux ARM64 Box running Node 24.22.1, the parent never received the child's first bootstrap message. The same programs completed the handshake when run directly.

## User Impact

A compatible OpenClaw package can now start and restart a managed workspace node in a sandbox that restricts descriptor reception. The parent retains ownership of executable selection and the child's lifetime. Standard input, output and error stay available to the workload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher protocol only needs JSON. This change carries those messages over a bounded, length-prefixed byte stream on an inherited socket. The launcher checks the selected package's manifest before choosing this transport. Older packages, Bun and Windows continue to use native Node IPC. This ports [the earlier draft](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186282) to current node enrollment and resume handling.

## Evidence

- Ran the focused launcher suite on macOS ARM64 with Node 24.22.1. All 17 tests passed. The default Bun lane passed 16 and skipped the Node-specific test.
- On Linux ARM64, exercised the OCE-pinned launcher and its node-renewal changes against stock Strands Box at `d5278f29972f7bf2f688e3fa76511d3a29705f33`. The original launcher passed directly and failed in Box before the first acknowledgment. With the port applied, both runs rejected an invalid restart request, accepted valid restart arguments, and started a fresh child with the approved arguments and stale access settings removed. The fixture exercised the real launcher and client using synthetic inputs.
- Checked both mixed-version directions with the native package selector. The old/new and new/old pairs completed the handshake over Node IPC. The new/new pair completed it over the byte stream.
- Formatting, focused lint and the launcher client's strict TypeScript check passed. Complete OCE deployment and Gateway enrollment are being qualified separately.

prs.title: test(qa-lab): replayed plugin media paths stay text in the next provider request
prs.body:
Closes #168610
Related: #101866

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: nothing fails when a media path from a plugin tool registered under a core tool name, replayed from Telegram history, reaches the next provider request as an image or file input or with its text rewritten.

## User Impact

User impact: no runtime change. QA Lab gains a Crabline Telegram regression on the final provider request for replayed media references, and a mock-provider directive that scripts exact tool calls. The Crabline dependency patch gains Telegram reply ingress, used only by QA, so that regression can send its second turn as a reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR used to expect replay to rewrite the plugin's path to `[unverified media reference removed]/generated/...`, the behavior #101866 proposed. That expectation was wrong. #101866 was closed unmerged on October 31, and the [closing comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101866#issuecomment-6541917131) found that on main replayed references stay literal text, produce no `input_image` or `input_file` payloads, and leave stored rows unchanged. It asks that a follow-up preserve stable conversation bytes and start from a final-provider-request regression. This PR is that regression.

`telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history` installs a run-owned, non-bundled plugin that registers `music_generate` and returns a PNG under the state media directory. No music provider is configured, so the plugin's tool is the one that runs. The state media directory is a local media root, so the prompt image loader would accept that file. Turn 1 calls the tool and replies with the path through the real Telegram plugin. The last provider request on turn 2 must have:

- no `input_image` or `input_file` part anywhere in `input`, and `imageInputCount` 0;
- the turn 1 reply, byte for byte, as the bot's own `(you):` line in the Telegram chat window of the current turn's runtime context, and separately in the earlier assistant message.

Turn 2 is a Telegram reply to the bot's turn 1 message. Since #183190, an existing plain Telegram DM carries its history in the session transcript and leaves the chat window out of the turn's runtime context; replies, topics, groups and fresh DMs keep it (`shouldSuppressPersistedDmChatWindowContext` in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.session.ts`). Sent as a plain DM, turn 2's request has no window line for the reply. On the reply path the window is the plugin's own (`Conversation context (chronological, selected for current message)`), which names the bot's messages `<first_name> (you)` (`buildTelegramSelfSenderName` in `extensions/telegram/src/group-history-window.ts`), so the check matches `(you): ` followed by the exact reply. The reply quote, `[Replying to: "..."]`, carries the same text without that prefix.

`QA tool plan:` works as before: the mock calls each listed tool in order with the given arguments, then replies, and `{{media:N}}` becomes the first media path the Nth result carried. It now sits at the end of main's scripted automation chain, so `server.ts` is identical to main.

- Removed: the placeholder expectation and its `path.sep` suffix; the unmanaged control path, which only made sense for selective redaction; the `server.ts` hunk, which after merging main grew it from 2251 to 2253 counted lines against the line-cap ratchet; and the `exec_command` ordering case with its cron argument checks, which test the cron planner rather than this change.
- Still protected: a plan never preempts a scripted cron turn, plan order and media substitution, undeclared tools, drive-rooted Windows paths, and Code Mode `wait`.
- Delta against main `5767fe7aae6`: no production code. qa-lab mock +119/-2; tests +155/-1 (`server.tool-plan.test.ts` +124, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/qa-tool-plan-directive-168610.txt`, and the Crabline reply case +31/-1); qa-lab reply mapping +43/-1 (`crabline-telegram-replies.ts` +33, `crabline-transport.ts` +10/-1); scenario +240; Crabline patch +125; `patches/README.md` +2; `pnpm-lock.yaml` 4 patch-hash lines.

Crabline patch: Crabline 0.2.0's Telegram server had no reply ingress. Admin inbound never set `reply_to_message`, the server kept no sent messages to quote, and its `sendMessage` events did not carry the assigned `message_id`, so the harness could not name the bot's message. For Telegram only, `patches/@openclaw__crabline@0.2.0.patch` now keeps accepted sends, `editMessageText` results and admin inbound messages by chat and `message_id`, records `messageId` on accepted send events, and turns an admin inbound `replyToMessageId` into a Bot API `reply_to_message` (without a nested reply), refusing an unknown target with `message to be replied not found`. The bridge forwards `OpenClawCrablineInboundInput.replyToId` as that field. prs.title: fix(ui): point gateway-token errors at the secret source and #token= link
prs.body:
## What

This replaces advice to run `openclaw doctor --generate-gateway-token` in the Control UI auth-required step, its English string, and the CLI and gateway error messages. The new text points at the configured secret source and the `#token=` fragment link already supported by the Control UI.

The old advice is destructive in practice: it rotates the gateway token, disconnecting other session pages and daemons that still hold the old one. The common cause of 'unauthorized: gateway token missing' is simply that this browser has no token saved in session storage. The supported fix is a `#token=<token>` fragment link, which the UI accepts and strips. No token is printed and no query parameter is used.

## Changes

- `ui/src/components/login-gate-feedback.ts`: remove the `--generate-gateway-token` command from the auth-required step.
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-login.ts`: `login.failure.authRequired.stepGenerate` now distinguishes 'this browser has no token saved' from 'no token configured', points at `gateway.auth.token` and the `#token=` link, and warns that generating a new token disconnects other sessions.
- `src/commands/gateway-auth-token.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-gateway-auth.ts`, `src/gateway/auth.ts`, `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/auth-messages.ts`: the same non-destructive guidance in the CLI, doctor, startup and WebSocket close messages.
- Three tests updated to assert the new strings.

Generated translation caches are intentionally excluded: the repo's i18n tooling says to commit only the English source and let the post-merge refresh translate.

## Proof

- 11 of 11 login-gate UI tests pass; the three updated source tests pass.
- `oxlint` is clean on all nine changed files.
- The WebSocket close message is 107 bytes, under the 120-byte limit.
- Three independent reviews at the wall: spec clean, security clean, bug and lint clean on the diff.

## Scope note

Other copies of the phrase remain in the wizard, security audit, known-weak secret path, macOS probe and docs. They are deliberately outside this patch to keep it small and reviewable; a follow-up can cover them.

prs.title: fix: use the release predecessor in staged upgrade checks
prs.body:
Related: #200734

## What Problem This Solves
Manual release-gate checks for an extended-stable candidate can select the newer npm latest as their upgrade starting point when run from a staging branch. For 2026.10.33 this selects 2026.11.5, creates schema 36, and correctly refuses to install the schema-22 candidate. The check never reaches the intended upgrade from 2026.9.37.

## User Impact
No installed-user behavior changes. Release operators can run the same meaningful predecessor-upgrade check from a PR staging branch as from the canonical release branch. Schema compatibility safeguards and existing release waivers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Recognize the candidate package's existing release-train classification as well as the branch context, then call the existing baseline resolver. This avoids adding PR API lookups or manufacturing a canonical branch context. Stable candidates still use npm latest; cache write authorization is unchanged. The repair is five added/two removed workflow lines, with the existing executable regression parameterized for canonical, staging, and absent context.

## Evidence
- Red before repair: staging and absent-context cases selected 2026.11.5 rather than captured 2026.9.37; canonical context passed.
- Green: all 29 workflow-plan tests and all 20 baseline-owner tests passed. The tests execute the actual workflow shell.
- Type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Independent local review: scoped-clean, zero P0–P2 findings. Lead separately inspected the unchanged baseline/classification owners; author simplification pass retained the existing owner with no new helpers or state.
- Original failing hosted gate 44147820548 / job 134272939031 and its artifact are retained. This is a deterministic harness repair, not a retry or waiver.
- Real hosted published-driver upgrade and full release qualification remain required after integration; focused tests are not a publication verdict.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let plugin forks read, ls and run owner exec under the session's policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A plugin can fork a chat with `runForkedTurn` and reuse its prompt cache, but the fork could only run tools the plugin registered itself. A fork that needs to look at the project (read a file, list a folder, run `rg`) had no way to do it: `read`, `ls` and `exec` are core tools, and `runForkedTurn` refused every core tool. This blocks porting pi-better's `/better`, whose helper reads the code before rewriting a prompt.

The same check had a hole the other way: a plugin could list a core tool id such as `exec` or `write` in its manifest's `contracts.tools`, register a tool by that name, and get it accepted. That grant widens the chat's tool profile, and at run time the name resolves to the core tool.

## User Impact

- A plugin fork may run `read`, `ls` and `exec` when the chat's own tool policy already allows them. They are never added to that policy: a chat on the `messaging` profile still refuses them.
- `exec` in a fork runs only on the owner's turns, and a fork never asks for exec approval: a command the agent's exec approvals would ask about is denied, and no approval request is created. Allowlist entries ("Always allow") and full-permission exec apply as for the chat's own turns.
- `through` is optional: without it the fork reads through the chat's latest message, as `forkSession` already does.
- A manifest may claim a core catalog id only when the catalog marks it plugin-built (`browser`, `canvas`, `memory_search`, `memory_get`, `skill_workshop`, `code_execution`, `x_search`).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One path, no new policy.** `read`, `ls` and `exec` passed in `tools` skip the plugin grant and go straight to the fork's existing run-time allow list (`toolExecutionAllow`), after the existing `prepareSessionFork` policy check. Every chat tool stays listed in the request, so the provider serves the cached prefix; other calls still return "not available in this background run".
- **Owner-only exec.** `exec` is not on `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS`, so `runSessionFork` keeps it out of the allow list unless the anchored turn's requester is the owner.
- **No approval cards from a hidden run.** Tool assembly sets the existing `nonInteractiveApproval` rule (already used by swarm collectors and worker placement) for session-fork runs. YOLO (`security=full`, `ask=off`) never reaches approval; allowlist entries are the agent's and match on the same workspace. An agent with `askFallback: full` or `allowlist` is still denied in a fork rather than run unattended.
- **Loophole.** The catalog now records which ids a plugin builds (`pluginBuilt`, on the 7 ids bundled plugins declare), and `resolvePluginSubagentToolsAlsoAllow` accepts a declared catalog id only when it is marked. This fails closed: every core-built id is refused, including `sessions_create`, `skills_search` and `skills_read`, which have no factory family, and any core tool added later without the mark. A contract test pins the marked set to the ids bundled plugin manifests declare.
- `process` is never offered to a fork.

The forked-turn e2e was over the file line cap, so its Gateway fixture moved to `gateway-plugin-forked-turn.test-support.ts` and the new case has its own file.

## Evidence

**Red on `main`, green here.** New case `gateway-plugin-forked-turn-session-tools.e2e.test.ts`. Run on `main` with every assertion soft, each case fails for its own reason: the owner fork with `read`/`ls`/`exec` is refused before running; a fork without `through` fails; non-owner `exec` never runs; the unmatched `exec` never reaches `approval_required`; the plugin claiming `write` is accepted (`ok: true`); the plugin claiming `exec` on a `messaging` chat settles instead of being refused and makes 2 extra model calls. On this branch: `read` returns the file, `write` returns the refusal as a tool result and creates no file, owner `exec` runs, non-owner `exec` is refused, the unmatched `exec` under `allowlist`/`on-miss` returns `approval_required` with `exec.approval.list` empty, both claims are refused.

**Unchanged suites:** `gateway-plugin-forked-turn.e2e` (7), `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, Skill Workshop (16 files), `session-fork-run`, session model-context limits, `server-plugins`, `agent-tools.runtime-plugin-tool-grant`, fork transport.

**Live, real providers** (source Gateway, recording proxy; pi-better's `/better` ported as a plugin that forks with `read`, `ls`, `exec`). Per provider: turn 1 with the plugin disabled, turn 2 enabled, `/better`, turn 3 while the helper works, turn 4 disabled again.

| | Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` | OpenAI `gpt-5.6-luna` |
|---|---|---|
| Parent requests across plugin off → on → off: same system / tools / cache key, history only extends | yes (5 requests) | yes (6 requests) |
| Helper request 1: same system / tools / cache key as the parent's last request, history prefix kept | yes, 7 / 7 | yes, 12 / 12 |
| Helper request 1: cache read / input | 19,176 / 20,222 (94.8%) | 11,599 / 12,224 (94.9%) |
| The chat's own turn 3, from the same cache: cache read / input | 19,176 / 19,773 (97.0%) | 11,599 / 11,886 (97.6%) |
| Helper requests 2–4: cache read / input | 97.3–98.9% | 98.6–99.5% |
| Tools the helper ran | `ls`, `exec` | `ls`, `read` |
| Turn 3 started and finished while the helper was running | yes | yes |

The helper's first request reads exactly as many cached tokens as the chat's own next turn: everything turn 2's request cached. The uncached part is the chat's last reply (a response, so no request had cached it yet), the per-turn runtime context, and pi-better's ~2 KB helper task, about 1,040 tokens on Anthropic. Only the helper task is new because of the fork. On this ~19k-token chat that is 5%; on a chat with 60k–150k tokens of history the same suffix is 1–2%.

**SDK impact.** `runForkedTurn` gains no field; `through` becomes optional and `tools` accepts `read`, `ls` and `exec`. `plugin-sdk-impact` (ClawHub, 2,663 eligible releases: 2,239 complete, 422 partial, 2 failed; bundled source at `main` `7b0a97a4c96e`): `runtime.subagent.runForkedTurn` has 0 public consumers and 1 bundled (Skill Workshop, own tool only, unchanged). `manifest.contracts.tools` declaring `exec`, `read`, `ls`, `write`, `edit`, `process` or `apply_patch`: 0 public, 0 bundled for each, so the stricter claim rule breaks no observed plugin. Coverage is incomplete, so this is not proof of no use. Advisor (`forkSession`) is unchanged.

prs.title: chore(build): report memory on admission refusal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A build can refuse its required heap before any tests start, but its error only reports the selected heap. The Telegram shard in [this Plugin Prerelease run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44139325837/job/134238721228) refused 4279MB against the existing 4352MB minimum without recording the memory inputs needed to investigate the constraint.

## User Impact

No runtime or build-admission policy changes. Developers get bounded memory details when the build refuses to start.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fatal CLI branch reports the existing memory-capacity fields, current-process RSS, and at most eight cgroup current/peak rows without paths. The record is explicitly sampled **after refusal**: it does not identify the original limiting sample. Diagnostic failures preserve the original refusal; the heap floor, reserve, cleanup, and compiler behavior remain unchanged. This is a visibility improvement, not a capacity fix.

## Evidence

- The extended existing fatal-admission test fails on the base because the record is missing; it passes with the change. It reaches `runTsdownBuild`, verifies the original refusal, and confirms no output cleanup or compiler launch.
- The full owning file passed 94/94 tests (1.16s test run; 1.76s wrapper) under the pinned Bun route on macOS. The qualified donor matched frozen dependency inputs and relevant owners; this is bounded source-overlay proof, not a whole-current-tree result.
- Owning test-root-scripts typecheck, targeted typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The final `Number.NaN` style correction was rechecked with lint/format; it does not alter the tested behavior.
- Full-source local review found no actionable findings. No Linux admission sample or additional hosted run has been collected for this change.

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose active cron snapshot revisions in agent hooks
prs.body:
### Main synchronization · November 17

Merged main `7c6f38d4` into `1169f7e6a123`. The CLI hook-context import now preserves both the cron snapshot projection and main's authorized prompt-build types. The 410 regression lines use 10 allocation credits beyond main's new 400-line allowance.

Git diff whitespace and the test-line counts were checked on the merge tree. Runtime tests are pending hosted CI.

Related: #113441 (Automation identity and definition revision in hook context).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins observing scheduled agent runs cannot distinguish the definition that started an active run from a job edited while that run is still executing.

## User Impact

Plugin developers can correlate prompt and lifecycle events with the cron executor's original definition revision without importing private engine modules or re-reading current job configuration.

This is a contract proposal, ready for maintainer review, for the product/security owner decision requested in #113441. The new optional metadata is diagnostic provenance; it does not grant action approval or replace existing run and tool authority. Tool-hook identity and broader automation envelopes remain outside this proposal. There are no new configuration keys, persistent stores, or migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made
