prs.title: fix(gateway): repair state_meta local policy receipts on legacy-main rekey
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When a named profile had run its own standalone gateway before joining the shared multiplexer, its local creation receipts and API binding receipts were written under `agent:main:*`, regardless of the profile name. `hermes sessions repair-profiles --legacy-main rekey --apply` rekeys `sessions.session_key` to the target namespace (`agent:<profile>:` or `agent:main~:` for a profile literally named `main`), but previously left `sessions.origin_json`, the `state_meta` session receipts (`gateway.local_policy.v1:<session_id>` and `gateway.api.binding.v1.<session_id>`), and `gateway_routing` pointing at the old route.

When Hermes Desktop resumes a historical local conversation, `owned_receipt` in `gateway/session_local_recovery.py` compares the stored receipt route with the dynamically computed multiplexed route. The mismatch raises `ValueError('route mismatch')` and surfaces to the client as `storage_unavailable` (`JsonRpcGatewayError: storage_unavailable`).

This PR generalizes the repair to every named profile, makes the three-table update atomic, and protects named-profile legacy state and local routes during `repair-profiles`:

1. `rekey_legacy_main_sessions` in `persistence/sqlite/admin/profile_repair.py` (`SQLiteProfileRepairAdmin`) now reconciles `sessions` (`session_key`, `profile_name`, `origin_json`), the `state_meta` local policy and API binding receipts (`POLICY_PREFIX` and `API_BINDING_PREFIX`), and every scoped `gateway_routing` row (including `entry_json`) in one write transaction. Repeated runs are no-ops and never append a second namespace.
2. The `gateway_routing` route key is derived from the stored session and receipt routes, so custom and `local-<hash>` chat IDs are covered alongside standard `{sid}` chat IDs.
3. `gateway/session_local_recovery.py:_checked_entry` now promotes legacy `agent:main:local:` receipts at read time for any named profile, not only the profile named `main`. Promotion requires the route suffix, `entry.session_key` and origin profile to agree; every other mismatch still refuses. The durable receipt is not rewritten.
4. `RepairPlan` in `hermes_cli/sessions_repair_profiles.py`:
   - Uses `profile_is_standalone()` and treats `gateway.standalone: true` profiles as islands: no `--legacy-main` rekey/move and no routing-row move or delete.
   - Skips named-profile `agent:main:*` rows during `mislabelled` scanning so default `--apply` (`--legacy-main report`) does not relabel them to `default` before an explicit `--legacy-main` decision.
   - Keeps unscoped (`scope=''`) local/API routing rows in their owning named profile store under multiplexing instead of classifying them as `routing_stray`.
5. Regression coverage was added in `tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_repair_profiles.py` and `tests/gateway/test_local_receipt_missing_profile.py`, including three-table atomicity/idempotency, API binding receipt rekeying, a named profile other than `main`, a profile literally named `main` (`agent:main:` -> `agent:main~:`), `report`-mode `mislabelled` protection, multiplexed `scope=''` local routes, standalone isolation, and an ended legacy receipt restored on first touch.

> Note: the branch was rebased onto the current `main` at `f7e2898aae` (ported to the `persistence/` layout). The current head is `ef3feea774`, with two commits in this PR.

## Related Issue

Fixes #143150
Refs #143547 (Lane 9 / LC-28)
Related: #151311, #156373

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `persistence/sqlite/admin/profile_repair.py`:
  - In `SQLiteProfileRepairAdmin.rekey_legacy_main_sessions`: update `sessions.session_key`, `profile_name` and `origin_json`; update `state_meta` receipt `route`, `entry.session_key` and `entry.origin.profile` for both `POLICY_PREFIX` and `API_BINDING_PREFIX`; and move every scoped `gateway_routing` row for the rekeyed routes in the same write transaction.
  - Rewrite `gateway_routing.entry_json` along with its `session_key` so the routing index cannot keep a stale route after the session row has moved.
  - Keep the operation idempotent: a second run finds no legacy keys and changes nothing; a `main`-named profile is rekeyed to `agent:main~:` without accumulating tildes.
  - Treat an existing target routing key as authoritative and drop the legacy duplicate instead of raising on the unique key.
- `gateway/session_local_recovery.py`:
  - Add `_promote_legacy_local_route()` and call it from `_checked_entry` when the stored route differs. It handles any named profile whose legacy route is `agent:main:local:*`, but only when the expected route is the exact namespaced twin and the receipt's entry/origin still agree.
- `hermes_cli/sessions_repair_profiles.py`:
  - Use `profile_is_standalone()` from the profile's own `config.yaml`; skip legacy-main rekey/move and routing rows for `gateway.standalone: true` profiles.
  - Skip named-profile `agent:main:*` rows in `mislabelled` findings so default `--legacy-main report` preserves their `profile_name`.
  - Keep `scope=''` local/API routing rows in their owning profile store during `_scan_routing`.
  - Re-read the source routing row at apply time so a legacy-main rekey performed earlier in the same run is moved under its new key rather than re-adopting the old key.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_repair_profiles.py`:
  - Add a three-table atomicity/idempotency test covering `sessions`, `state_meta` and multiple routing scopes.
  - Add an API binding receipt (`gateway.api.binding.v1.`) rekey and idempotency test.
  - Add a named `main` profile test (`agent:main:` -> `agent:main~:`) with a hashed chat ID and repeated `--apply` runs.
  - Add tests for `report`-mode `mislabelled` protection on named-profile `agent:main:*` chats and keeping `scope=''` routes in the named profile store under multiplexing.
  - Add a standalone-profile isolation test alongside a normal profile that is still repaired.
- `tests/gateway/test_local_receipt_missing_profile.py`:
  - Add legacy-main read-time promotion coverage and an ended-receipt restore-on-touch case.

## Known Limitations / Follow-up

This PR includes the preventive fix for the root cause described in #151311: profile-local `scope=''` routes are no longer classified as routing strays or moved out of their owning store, and legacy routes are rekeyed in place during the owning profile's repair.

It does not restore routing rows that were already displaced by an earlier repair run or migrate `sessions.json` mirrors. Those retrospective migrations require backups, ambiguity checks, and integrity validation, and remain separate follow-up work.

## How to Test

1. Create a profile that previously ran standalone, with a local session stored under `agent:main:local:*` and a matching `gateway.local_policy.v1:*` receipt.
2. Open or resume that chat after the profile joins the shared gateway. Without the patch it returns `storage_unavailable` with `route mismatch`; with the patch it opens and keeps the profile's current route.
3. Run `hermes sessions repair-profiles --legacy-main rekey --apply` twice. The first run rewrites all three tables; the second run reports no repairable findings and changes nothing.
4. Set `gateway.standalone: true` on a profile, rerun the repair, and confirm its history and routing index are untouched.

Local verification on Windows 11 (build 26100 / x86_64):

prs.title: fix(batch): keep tool-search bridge trajectories
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #123817.

The batch trajectory merger previously validated `tool_stats` against a module-import-time snapshot of registered tools. Tool Search bridge tools are synthesized separately, and plugins/MCP servers can register tools after import. Valid trajectories could therefore be incorrectly discarded as corrupted.

### Changes

- Resolve the registered tool names at merge time instead of relying on a stale import-time snapshot.
- Include inline executor names and Tool Search bridge names in the valid-tool set.
- Keep the existing behavior for ordinary registered tools.

### Regression coverage

- Tool Search bridge trajectories survive batch merging.
- A tool registered after `batch_runner` import survives merging.
- Inline executor tools that bypass the registry survive merging.

### Testing status

The regression tests are committed. GitHub Actions currently report `action_required` for this fork PR, so upstream CI still needs maintainer approval.

The change is limited to trajectory merge validation; normal tool registration and execution are unchanged.

prs.title: catalog: update hermes-dreaming to 3.8.8
prs.body:
Update the hermes-dreaming entry from 3.8.6 (merged in #150681) to released 3.8.8, pinned to a0bda14bb6d6205f185ddb2bad24d4e36039b33c (tag `v3.8.8`). All README/image URLs use this immutable commit.

3.8.7 and 3.8.8 are fixes from a code review of 3.8.6 — ways the nightly pass dropped a true update, or a whole night, without saying so:

- **Rejections and dedupe.** A human's rejection of a fact no longer silences a newer value of it (another number, time, weekday, month or name); a fact whose text is the beginning of a memory entry with a different number ("thread 43" / "thread 437 …") is a conflict to ask about, not "already in memory".
- **Dates.** A time written with a dot ("at 10.30") is no longer read as a date; a date without a year takes its year from the day the fact was stored, not the year closest to today.
- **Robustness.** A fact store that cannot be read (empty file, not a database, an older table) no longer ends the whole pass: the memory-file review runs and an alert `fact_store_unreadable` says why. Database paths are opened as read-only file URIs: a `#` in a path cut `?mode=ro` off and opened another file for writing. A broken extraction cursor restarts at the current time instead of going `backfill_days` back. A voice reply corroborates. The judge reads `.env` as python-dotenv does.
- **Loss alerts.** A memory-loss alert is raised again after a night no agent turn answered; 3.8.8 makes the forget sweep remove a forgotten fact from those alerts' entry previews too.

Disclosure changes: a memory-loss alert (with the 60-character previews that already name lost entries in the report) is now also kept in the dream's seen state in `$HERMES_HOME/cache` until an agent turn answers it; the forget sweep cleans it. No change to defaults, network behaviour, credentials, tools, hooks or env vars; the nightly prompts are unchanged.

Validation: CI on the 3.8.8 merge commit passed, 12/12 (unittest on Python 3.9/3.11/3.13/3.14 with and without PyYAML, provider integration, lint, `hermes plugins validate`, the core contract). `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/hermes-dreaming.yaml`: OK. Every pinned URL returns 200.

Compare: https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/compare/21878d3ec8752283dd7ee69a803c63bb989c1740...a0bda14bb6d6205f185ddb2bad24d4e36039b33c

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(dashboard): sort the Sessions page by last activity (Refs #155919)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Sessions page lists sessions by when they were created, not by when they were last used. A conversation you return to over several days slowly sinks as new sessions appear, and with cron jobs enabled each run adds a row, so the chat you actually use can end up well past the first page. The sidebar's Recent Sessions list already requests `order=recent`, so the page and the sidebar show different orders for the same data.

The page never set an order, so `api.getSessions` used its default of `created`. This PR makes the page's query options (`sessionQueryOptions` in `web/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx`) include `order: "recent"`. Both the history list and the 5-second overview poll use those options, so both now sort by last activity. The existing source filters, including the default Chats view that leaves out automation sources, are unchanged. Search is unaffected because `/api/sessions/search` does not take an order.

The overview poll decides when to refresh the history list. It used to compare only the id at the head of its response. With recent ordering that is not enough: if the top session and an older one are both active inside one 5-second window, the head id stays the same while the sessions behind it swap places, and the history list kept the old order. The poll now compares the ordered ids of everything it fetched (`sessionsSignature` in `web/src/lib/session-refresh.ts`), so a reorder anywhere in the fetched page triggers the existing silent refresh. The first poll still only sets a baseline and an empty response still never triggers a reload.

Before: a chat started on 27 Oct and used a few minutes ago can sit at row ~130 of 212, behind sessions created after it. After: it is near the top, matching the sidebar, and stays in the right place when other sessions are active at the same time.

## Related Issue

Part of #155919. This covers the ordering defect in the title and in the issue's first proposal. The issue's comment also describes inert Overview rows, the Overview list excluding active sessions, and the unpersisted view choice. Those are separate page changes and are not part of this PR, so the issue should stay open for them.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `web/src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx`: the page's query options now carry `order: "recent"`, and the overview poll compares the ordered ids it fetched instead of only the first id.
- `web/src/lib/session-refresh.ts`: adds `sessionsSignature` and updates the docs of `shouldRefreshSessions` to describe the signature it compares.
- `web/src/lib/session-refresh.test.ts`: covers the signature, including a swap behind an unchanged head.
- `web/src/pages/SessionsPage.test.tsx`: one test asserts every `getSessions` call asks for `recent`. A second drives the overview poll with an unchanged head and a reordered tail and checks that the history list is fetched again.

## How to Test

1. Create a few sessions, then continue an older one so its last activity is newer than the rest.
2. Open Dashboard → Sessions → History.
3. The continued session is at the top, in the same order as the sidebar's Recent Sessions. Before this change it stayed in creation order.

Automated, from `web/`: `pnpm exec vitest run src/lib/session-refresh.test.ts src/pages/SessionsPage.test.tsx`.

Validation run: those two files pass (15 tests). The new reorder test fails on the previous head-id comparison (the history list is not fetched a third time) and passes with this change. `tsc -b . --noEmit` is clean and `eslint` reports no errors on the four changed files; the one warning is an existing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning in `SessionsPage.tsx` that this PR does not touch. prs.title: fix(desktop): isolate perf-harness messaging platforms and attach on Wayland
prs.body:
**Stack 1/6:** Targets `main`.

- The harness copied configuration and credentials into its scratch home unchanged. That started a second set of messaging adapters; Photon sidecars fought over port 8789 and disrupted the live gateway.
- Seed `platforms.<name>.enabled: false` for the listed core adapters and discovered bundled platform directories. Explicit disables outrank environment and auth activation; provider credentials remain available.
- Apply the same seeder to isolated launches and cold-start samples. This is not a general sandbox for arbitrary third-party plugins.

```js
// scripts/perf/lib/seed-home.mjs
for (const name of platformNames) {
  const block = platforms[name]
  platforms[name] = { ...(block && typeof block === 'object' ? block : {}), enabled: false }
}
```

| Config loader on the same seeded user configuration | Enabled platforms |
|---|---|
| main: verbatim copy | `discord`, `photon`, `telegram` |
| candidate: explicit disables | none |

- On the affected Linux/Wayland launch, Electron's platform-selection relaunch left the parent holding the CDP port. The harness saw an empty target list until its 120 s timeout.
- Pass `--ozone-platform=wayland` on the initial harness launch in a Linux Wayland session, avoiding that relaunch.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Harness
  participant E as Electron
  H->>E: spawn with ozone platform and CDP port
  Note over E: No platform-selection relaunch
  H->>E: discover renderer target
  E-->>H: page target and perf driver
```

**Next in stack:** https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153066

prs.title: fix(mcp): send YAML-typed header values and stdio args as text
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

An MCP server whose config carries an unquoted scalar never connects, because YAML types the value before Hermes reads it:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  versioned:
    url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    headers:
      Notion-Version: 2022-06-28   # datetime.date
      X-Api-Version: 2             # int
      X-Debug: true                # bool
  local:
    command: python
    args: [-m, server, --port, 8080, --verbose, true]   # int, bool
```

- HTTP: `_prepare_run` hands `dict(config["headers"])` to the content-type preflight and `_http_endpoint` hands the same values to the Streamable HTTP / SSE client. httpx (and the SDK's httpx2) accept only str or bytes, so the first request raises `TypeError: Header value must be str or bytes, not <class 'datetime.date'>` on every connect attempt. Date-shaped version headers (`Notion-Version`, `X-GitHub-Api-Version`, `anthropic-version`) hit this whenever they are written unquoted.
- stdio: `_run_stdio` passes `config["args"]` to `StdioServerParameters`, which takes `list[str]`, so `--port 8080` fails with `ValidationError: args.3 Input should be a valid string [input_type=int]`.

One helper, `_config_text`, renders a value as the text the user wrote: strings (including rendered `${VAR}` values), bytes and None are left alone, dates are written in ISO form, bools as `true` / `false`, other scalars with `str()`. `_configured_headers` and `_configured_args` apply it, and the preflight, the HTTP transport and the stdio launch read through them. A header with an empty (None) value is not sent, the same rule `normalize_extra_headers` applies to provider headers. The stdio args are converted before the OSV preflight and the cached npx swap, so those checks see the same argv the server gets.

## Related Issue

No issue or PR found for headers or args. The `env` side of the same YAML typing problem is #85223 (PRs #85277, #118205); this change leaves `env` to those.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/mcp_tool_config.py`: `_config_text`, `_configured_headers`, `_configured_args`.
- `tools/mcp_tool_transport.py`: `_http_endpoint` and `_run_stdio` read headers and args through them.
- `tools/mcp_tool_server_run.py`: the preflight call in `_prepare_run` does the same.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_typed_config_values.py`: configs loaded with `hermes_yaml`. Checks the headers `_connect_inputs` returns, runs the real preflight from `MCPServerTask.run()` against a local HTTP server that records the request headers, and runs `_run_stdio` up to a real `StdioServerParameters` to check the args it receives.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_typed_config_values.py`: all three tests fail on `main` (the `TypeError` and `ValidationError` above) and pass with this change.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp*.py tests/tools/test_osv_check.py`: 102 files, 939 passed, 1 skipped.
3. `python scripts/check`: 12 checks, ok.

Tested on Linux (Python 3.14.6).

prs.title: feat(skills): three-way merge bundled updates with manual conflict review
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Today a bundled skill the user has edited is frozen: `hermes update` skips it, and every later upstream improvement is withheld until the user diffs and re-baselines by hand (#135035).

This reconciles instead, with a three-way merge. The recorded upstream content is the base, the user's copy is "ours", the new bundled copy is "theirs".

- Conflict-free merge: applied, origin hash re-baselined.
- Conflict: the user's copy is left untouched, and the update is queued for review.
- Review with `hermes skills resolve <name> [--accept merged|local|upstream]` (curses picker when interactive). Accepting records the new upstream as the base for later updates.
- Pending state lives under `$HERMES_HOME/skill-updates/`, outside the active skills tree. Files are merged as bytes, so CRLF/BOM files survive.

Covers mechanisms 1 and 2 of #135035; the additive `user/` extension (3) is not included.

## Related Issue

Refs #135035

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `tools/skills_sync_merge.py` (new): byte-preserving merge, pending-update state, resolve
- `tools/skills_sync.py`: sync calls the merge instead of skipping user-modified skills
- `hermes_cli/skills_merge.py`, `subcommands/skills.py`, `skills_hub.py`: `hermes skills resolve`
- `update_cmd_maint.py`, `update_completion.py`: list pending reviews after `hermes update` and offer to resolve them; on Windows the completion child keeps the parent's console when interactive (CREATE_NO_WINDOW would swallow the keys)
- Docs: skills guide, CLI reference, source-update-completion
- Tests: `test_skills_sync_merge.py`, `test_bundled_skill_merge.py`, `test_skill_review_console_windows_live.py` (+ small updates to existing update/sync tests)

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_skills_sync_merge.py tests/hermes_cli/test_bundled_skill_merge.py tests/hermes_cli/test_skill_review_console_windows_live.py tests/tools/test_skills_sync.py tests/tools/test_skills_runtime_cache.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_modified_notice.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_post_commit_followups.py tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_hub.py`
2. Edit a bundled skill, bump the bundled copy in a different region, run `hermes update`: the change merges. Bump the same lines: the update is reported as pending and `hermes skills resolve <name>` walks through it.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature

prs.body:
**Stack 2/6:** Depends on https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153065. Targets that branch; review the incremental diff.

- `sharedPrimaryRoute` swallowed rejection and its 20 s timeout as `false`. Callers interpreted that as a separate backend and attempted another connection lookup.

- Record failed background lookups in the existing dial-failure cooldown. Apply the same rejection rule to `ridesPrimaryBackend` when the primary is local; preserve the remote-primary fallback.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[Resolve profile route] --> S{Result}
  S -->|shared| P[Use primary socket]
  S -->|separate| D[Dial secondary]
  S -->|error or timeout| F[Surface failure]
  F -. removed fallback .-> D
```

- Ordinary local profiles share one multiplexing gateway; this change adds no process pool or idle TTL.
- Remove unused `openSecondaryCount` and correct stale prewarm, gateway-field, timeout and cron-lifecycle documentation.
- **Retry behavior changes:** a failed route lookup leaves no secondary socket entry, so there is no background reconnect ladder for that attempt. The user must retry. The companion profile-switch UX change adds an inline Retry action but is not required for this fix.

prs.title: fix(tools): cap the pre-exec guard wait at 90s, and test the ceiling
prs.body:
fix(tools): cap the pre-exec guard wait at 90s, and memoize only a confirmed identity verdict

The guard deadline had a floor and no ceiling: a long command's own timeout became the
guard's budget, so with a wedged identity probe a 420s command waited 420s before the
refusal — while the refusal itself is identical either way. The ceiling bounds that at 90s.

The root cause of the wedge is the supervised-gateway identity probe, which does real
filesystem and kernel-process work and is called on EVERY terminal command, so each
abandoned guard thread parks in the same `open()`. Memoize it — but **only a confirmed
True**, per `@kvnloo`'s review of the earlier attempt (#151792): the gateway PID file is
written after the process starts and can briefly name the previous pid, so freezing an
early False would answer "not the gateway" for the rest of the process's life and silently
disable the self-kill/ownership guards (#113667). The negative path is still free — the
`_HERMES_GATEWAY` marker test returns before any gateway import — so re-probing it costs
nothing per call, while the positive path (the one that actually did the I/O) is paid once.
A probe that raised is never cached either.

Evidence from `~/.hermes/logs` on 2026-11-16, before the cap was in effect there: 241 guard
refusals (each is logged twice; 362 raw records), 191 of them (79%) longer than 90s — 446
records at 180s, worst 420s — and 661 minutes of dead wall clock. A 420s refusal cannot
happen when `min(guard_timeout, 90)` is live, which is how the cap was confirmed absent
rather than merely ineffective.

Two test files, both two-sided:

- `test_terminal_pre_guard_cap.py` pins the sizing rule, not the constants' existence. With
  the ceiling all five pass; with the ceiling removed — reproducing the code this replaces —
  exactly the three ceiling tests fail and the two floor tests still pass.
- `test_supervised_gateway_verdict_cache.py` is the control for the memo. Against the parent
  commit, `test_transient_false_does_not_freeze_the_verdict` fails with "a cached False
  survived a pid file that now names this process" and `test_unsupervised_launch_is_not_memoized`
  fails on a memoized negative, while the five that pin the positive-path memo pass. With
  this change all 7 pass, and 12 pass together with the cap tests (7.66s).

prs.title: fix(model): a direct alias without base_url still uses its own key_env/api_key
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A `model_aliases:` entry that names a built-in provider and its own credential, but no `base_url`, silently ignores that credential:

```yaml
model_aliases:
  personal:
    model: claude-opus-5-5
    provider: anthropic
    key_env: ANTHROPIC_PERSONAL_TOKEN   # second Anthropic account
```

`/model personal` returns success, but the request goes out with the **default** provider's credential (here, the Claude Code login), so it's billed to the wrong account and nothing says so. In `_resolve_switch_credentials` the alias's own key is only applied inside the `if da.base_url:` branch (`_apply_direct_alias_endpoint`). An alias with no URL never reaches it.

This PR applies the alias's own `api_key`/`key_env` on the provider's normal endpoint when no `base_url` is set. When the alias declares a key that isn't set, the switch now fails with a clear message instead of falling back. Without that, the declared key is the only signal of which account the user meant, and falling back bills the other account silently.

Aliases that declare no credential are unchanged: they still use the provider's resolved key.

## Related Issue

No existing issue that I found. Related but different: #83612 / #83793 (URL-bearing aliases inheriting the default key) and #126534 (persisted alias picks). Both keep the alias-key logic gated on `base_url`, so they don't cover this case.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`: in `_resolve_switch_credentials`, add a branch for direct aliases with no `base_url` that declare `api_key`/`key_env`. It uses `direct_alias_api_key()` (env reads stay profile-scoped) and fails closed when the key is unset.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_alias_credentials.py`: new `TestBuiltinProviderAliasOwnCredential` with three cases: the alias `key_env` is used and handed to the validation probe; an unset `key_env` fails and never probes with the default key; an alias without its own key keeps the default credential.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_alias_credentials.py -q` passes (59). On `main`, `test_key_env_is_used_without_base_url` and `test_unset_key_env_fails_closed` fail.
2. Manual: log in with Claude Code (default account), add the alias above with a second account's `claude setup-token` in `ANTHROPIC_PERSONAL_TOKEN`, then `/model personal`. Before this change, usage lands on the default account. With an invalid token it still answers, because the alias key is never sent.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [x] Tests pass: the alias credential file plus every `tests/hermes_cli/` test matching `model_switch or alias or provider` (1749 passed, 7 skipped). I didn't run the full `pytest tests/`.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Arch Linux (Omarchy), Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A (no config keys changed; `key_env` on aliases is already documented)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A

prs.title: perf(desktop): reduce streaming and terminal hot-path work
prs.body:
**Stack 4/6:** Depends on https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153067. Targets that branch; review the incremental diff.

- Preserve settled transcript identity through reconciliation and runtime normalization; deduplicate tool calls only on cache misses.
- Patch the live tail, use reference comparisons on live publishes, and retain the full preservation path for view-only assistant errors.
- Avoid unchanged metadata writes and activity notifications; keep one deadline timer per watchdog, with silence deadlines and event timestamps on the same monotonic clock.
- Move microphone levels into a recorder-owned nanostore, batch preview-console updates per frame, and isolate splitter-height subscriptions.
- Keep terminal backlog in capped chunks; read the composer prefix without cloning DOM and take conversion undo snapshots only on Space.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D[Gateway delta] --> F[Flush scheduler]
  F --> T[Patch live tail]
  T --> V[Identity-preserving view sync]
  V --> R[Reuse settled runtime rows]
  R --> A[assistant-ui / Streamdown]
  F -. hidden, no voice consumer .-> H[250 ms floor]
  F -. visible or voice consumer .-> C[40 ms base floor]
```

- Visible base floor: 33 → 40 ms. Hidden streams use a 250 ms floor; voice consumers retain responsive updates.
- `session.info running=false` drains queued text before settling a live turn; superseded-turn orphan handling is preserved.
- Identity caches require immutable published rows and arrays. Reconciliation uses weak references so earlier streamed snapshots remain collectible.

- No blanket renderer-speedup claim: final whole-stack measurements show a strong terminal-backlog improvement, near-parity prose CPU, and worse dense-fence frame p95 despite lower script work. These are not incremental measurements against this PR’s parent.
- [Whole-stack measurements and remaining limits](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153070#issuecomment-6844735970).

**Next in stack:** https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153069

prs.title: feat(codex): offer catalog-backed extended context for GPT-6.2
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Offer `gpt-6.2-astra-900k` and `gpt-6.2-sol-900k` in the Codex picker when the account catalog publishes a larger `max_context_window` than the base model's `context_window`. The existing `-900k` suffix is a local opt-in with a 900,000-token ceiling, not a claim that every subscription accepts that many tokens. Both aliases send the original model ID on the wire. Bare selections and global compression settings are unchanged.

## Related work

#157141 registers the base models and explicitly excludes extended-context aliases. This PR depends on that base-model registration for the new reasoning/parameter contracts; it normalizes context aliases to the registered base identity rather than duplicating the model registry. #146757 adjusts the legacy verified-window heuristic; these two entries use the provider's explicit maximum instead. [Tibo's Codex example](https://x.com/thsottiaux/status/2089082893804896524) explains the opt-in on an earlier model; it is not a source for the 6.2 limits.

## Verification

- Regression failed on unchanged main before implementation. The follow-up tests exercise `/model` validation with fresh and stale catalogs and reject unknown variants without inventing a provider limit. Nine relevant test files passed locally: 405 tests, zero failures, using the canonical runner with an explicit Python 3.11 test interpreter on Windows. Repository lint checks passed all 22 checks using Python 3.14. Remote CI is awaiting contributor-workflow approval; this is not a remote-CI or full-suite pass.
- Used synthetic short requests through the Hermes Responses transport. Both aliases resolved to 872,000 and completed on their respective base models. Bare Astra stayed at 272,000; bare Sol stayed at 500,000. No full-window load test was performed.
- Native Codex CLI 0.169.0 also completed one ephemeral, read-only session on each base model with `-c model_context_window=1000000 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000`. Both returned `OK` with no tool calls. User config and project instructions were excluded. This confirms the native settings are accepted, not that a million-token input fits, and does not justify overriding the account's published maximum in Hermes.
- Reproduce with `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_models.py tests/hermes_cli/test_model_validation.py`.

## Review follow-up

Synthetic regressions now cover catalog outages, credential/endpoint isolation, custom Codex proxy maximums, offline cache/default hints, and exact base reasoning registrations. The catalog-outage and proxy-window regressions failed before their fixes. The cached maximum is reused only for the credential and endpoint that supplied it; another account or endpoint gets a conservative fallback. Offline compatibility hints do not offer the new extended variants. Provider and model-picker documentation now explains these differences from legacy verified variants.

## Activation and validation

The aliases require the updated code in the process that owns the chat. Opening a PR or launching a newer CLI client does not patch an already-running gateway. After installing, restart the gateway handling the session. An unrecognized alias is a local Hermes support check, not evidence of a 272K server-enforced limit; the rejection message now states that distinction. No launch scripts, user settings, or service changes are included.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add /resume --all-sources that matches /sessions all
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`/sessions all` and `/resume` are sibling commands that disagreed about what "all" widens.

`_handle_sessions_command` passes `include_all_sources=cross_origin`, so an admin sees every source. `_list_titled_sessions` (the list `/resume` prints and the list a numbered `/resume <n>` resolves against) only cleared `session_key` and left `sources=(platform,)` pinned — so `/resume --all` could never list, or resolve a pick number for, a desktop, CLI or other-platform session. The two also ordered differently (`LAST_ACTIVE` vs `STARTED_AT`), so even same-platform rows sat at different numbers in each list.

This adds an explicit flag rather than redefining `--all`:

- `--all` keeps its current, test-pinned meaning — this platform, any chat (`test_bare_resume_admin_all_preserves_same_platform_widening`).
- `--all-sources` (aliases `--alls`, `--all_sources`, `--all-src`) delegates to the **same** `query_session_listing` call `/sessions all` makes — cross-origin key, every source but `tool`, named rows only, current session included — so the two surfaces cannot drift apart by construction and a pick number means the same session in both.

Flag parsing also now stops at the first positional word (the convention `parse_session_listing_args` already documents), so a title containing `--word` is never misparsed as a flag, and an unknown flag answers with the flag list instead of falling through to `No session found matching '--alls 2'`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #107911 — gateway `/resume <number>` resolving against a different scope than `/sessions all`.
Fixes #41220 — Telegram `/resume` surfacing cross-source (Desktop/CLI) sessions.

Related: #146798 (ordering). The `--all-sources` path resolves numbers against exactly the list `/sessions all` prints, so that half is fixed there. The platform-scoped numbered pick still ranks by lineage activity rather than root `started_at`, which is deliberate per #114271 (a compressed lineage must sit where the user last touched it), so I did not change it in this PR.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/slash_commands_session.py`
  - `RESUME_ALL_SOURCES_FLAGS` / `RESUME_KNOWN_FLAGS` + `_resume_flags()` — leading `-`/`--` tokens, stopping at the first positional; `_strip_resume_name` strips the known set.
  - `_list_titled_sessions(..., all_sources=False)` — admin `--all-sources` delegates to the new `_list_sessions_all_sources()`, which calls `query_session_listing` with `/sessions all`'s exact arguments and shapes the rows as pick entries.
  - Threaded `all_sources` through `_resolve_resume_target` (numeric picks), `_resume_access_denied_reply` (the admin override), and `_resume_listing_reply` (declined-flag notice).
  - Unknown flags now return a named error instead of a title lookup.
- `locales/en.yaml` — `gateway.resume.all_sources_requires_admin`, `gateway.resume.unknown_flag`.
- `tests/gateway/test_resume_command.py` — two tests: `--all-sources` returns the identical rows and order as `/sessions all` (plus the `--alls` alias and the unknown-flag reply), and a non-admin `--all-sources` stays chat-scoped with the notice.
- `website/docs/reference/slash-commands.md` — documents both widening flags on `/resume`.

## How to Test

1. Configure an admin (`platforms.telegram.allow_admin_from: ['<your id>']`), restart the gateway, then from Telegram send `/sessions all`.
2. Send `/resume --all-sources` (or `/resume --alls`) — the same titled rows appear in the same order.
3. Send `/resume --alls 2` — it resumes the session that row 2 of `/sessions all` names, cross-source included.
4. `/resume --all` still lists only this platform (unchanged), and `/resume --all-sources` from a non-admin still stays chat-scoped with the declined-flag notice.

Driving the real handlers against a throwaway `state.db` (Telegram + desktop + CLI rows seeded):

```
/sessions all          → 1. CLI Gamma  2. Desktop Beta  3. Telegram Alpha
/resume --all-sources  → 1. CLI Gamma  2. Desktop Beta  3. Telegram Alpha   (identical)
/resume --alls         → identical to --all-sources
/resume --all (old)    → 1. Telegram Alpha only                       (unchanged)
numeric pick 2         → ds1 (Desktop Beta)
non-admin --all-sources→ chat-scoped + notice
unknown flag           → ⚠️ Unknown flag `--nope` for `/resume`. + flag list
```

## Prior art

Three open PRs touch this neighbourhood; flagging them so maintainers can dedupe:

- #107920 (`fix(gateway): make cross-platform session indexes resumable`) — same bug, untouched since September.
- #76774 (`fix(resume): unify session-source visibility across all resume surfaces`) — broad unification, 12 files.
- #146812 (`fix(gateway): share one numbered listing between /sessions and /resume`) — currently `CONFLICTING`.

This PR is deliberately the narrow version: no existing behaviour changes (the `--all` semantics and last-activity ranking on platform-scoped paths are preserved), and the new path is one delegation to the query `/sessions all` already uses.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) — see Prior art above
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the changed tests — **could not run locally**: this checkout is a packaged install without the dev payload, so importing `gateway.run` (needed by the test fixture) trips `tests/home_io_guard.py` against the real hermes home; every test in that file fails that way, including untouched ones. I verified behaviour by driving the real handlers directly instead (output above) and both new tests collect cleanly.
- [x] `just check` passes — `just` is not installed on this machine, so I ran the same checks via `python scripts/check`: **22 checks, ok** (code health 0 blocking, 0 advisory).
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

prs.title: fix(gateway): recognize bracketed NO_REPLY as intentional silence
prs.body:
Fixes #157236.

A reply consisting only of `[NO_REPLY]` can be delivered to chat because the gateway recognizes `NO_REPLY` but not its bracketed form. In the regression test, the real gateway stream consumer sends the marker when it arrives as `[NO`, `_RE`, `PLY]`.

This adds `[NO_REPLY]` as an exact silence alias and holds partial matches while streaming. It does not extend autonomous prefix matching to `[NO_REPLY]` followed by prose, and normal text mentioning the marker still reaches the adapter.

## Test plan

- On upstream base `730d593fe3c6facd0e9c7a3fa2b6009f3b742c8e`, the new regression file produced 3 failures and 1 passing control before the fix.
- After the fix, the official runner passed 70 tests across the new regression and the related response-filter, stream-consumer, gateway-silence and delivery-filter suites. `python scripts/check --staged` passed all 22 checks.
- The regression uses a simulated platform adapter. The full test suite and a live Telegram end-to-end run were not performed.

The original tested commit and its author attribution are unchanged.

## Update nvidia-switchyard to 0.1.1

Bumps `plugin-catalog/nvidia-switchyard.yaml` from 0.1.0 to 0.1.1 (repo SHA `34046b28541098fcd1b88181a3143f91a19bdc37`, previously `114c3e12c1`).

**Commits adopted** ([114c3e12c1...34046b2854](https://github.com/NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing/compare/114c3e12c1931d86cf75affc6c6ec5754865d107...34046b28541098fcd1b88181a3143f91a19bdc37)):

- [`060fb90fd4`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing/commit/060fb90fd45e3e968339b86f6a7109f1ee1e1f96): a cloud tier set up as a Custom URL to `api.openai.com` now defaults to the Responses API, as Hermes itself reaches OpenAI. Over Chat Completions, OpenAI's reasoning models refuse the tools Hermes sends, so every cloud turn failed with HTTP 400. A format set with `--cloud-format` is kept. The setup check now sends one tool, so a model that refuses tools is reported at Save.
- [`2a9363dbb7`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing/commit/2a9363dbb7407c5a200109acb46590c82edd6dd9), [`34046b2854`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing/commit/34046b28541098fcd1b88181a3143f91a19bdc37): version 0.1.1 in the plugin's three manifests.
- [`a700d98d93`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing/commit/a700d98d93acd045bd6eea52f333a6b906303f3e) (NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing#2): the plugin is renamed **NVIDIA Switchyard** in its manifests, provider profile, sidebar, page and dashboard tab, and its page wording is simplified. Wording and layout only: routing, setup and saved settings are unchanged.
- [`65bb732216`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing/commit/65bb7322162156feafb08fd867fe32bce7ff9a00) (NVIDIA/switchyard-local-first-routing#1): Hermes picks its model-specific system-prompt guidance (tool-use enforcement, execution guidance) by the chat's model name, which behind Switchyard is `switchyard/<preset>` and matches none. The plugin now adds the blocks Hermes would give each tier's own model to that tier's requests, right after the steer-channel note where Hermes places them. If Hermes's prompt doesn't have that note exactly once, the request is sent unchanged.

**Entry changes:**

- `version` 0.1.0 → 0.1.1, matching `plugin.yaml` at the pin.
- `title` and the description's opening follow the rename.
- The disclosure gains: "adds to each tier's system prompt the model-specific guidance Hermes gives that tier's model".
- Screenshot URLs move to the new pin. The images themselves are unchanged in this range.
- `capabilities` is unchanged: no hooks, middleware, tools or env vars are added or removed in this range, and no dependency changes (`nemo-switchyard==0.4.0a1`).

**Validation:** `catalog_validate_pinned_entries.py` passes at the new pin, with `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` from current `main`.

- Security scan: safe. Desktop surface: inside the plugin SDK.
- Rule 9: the private-import warnings go from 21 to 28. All 7 new ones are in `guidance.py`: `agent.system_prompt._model_gate` and six names from `agent.prompt_builder` (the guidance texts, their model lists and `STEER_CHANNEL_NOTE`). They're read inside a `try`, so a Hermes without them sends the request as it came. The public seam that replaces them, model-specific prompt text for aliased model names, is part of #154621; the plugin moves onto it in a later SHA bump once it ships.

**Tested** on Windows 11 ARM64 with Hermes Desktop and the CLI: install over the previous pin and a fresh install, the setup page, the model menu, routing through local, cloud and VGR presets, and removal. The Responses fix was then tested at this pin with the CLI: an `api.openai.com` cloud tier with no saved format runs on Responses and answers with Hermes's tools; an explicit `--cloud-format openai_chat` is kept, and setup reports OpenAI's refusal; VGR routing is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(memory): follow-ups to #149763 from @GottZ's review
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Forks get the right gate. Before: Review fork: prune withheld; Opt-out child: archives to memory; Gate docs: gaps unnamed. After: Review fork: prunes, like compaction; Opt-out child: follows parent opt-out; Gate docs: gaps named. Change: _checkpoint_exempt_fork(), parent.skip_memory.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84bcd0e9-849e-47bf-9d6d-6b070e876a86)

## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #149763. It carries @GottZ's findings from [his review there](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149763#pullrequestreview-5794210188), which he rated low and suited to a follow-up, so #149763 kept its approval at `55a7b84292`. #149763 has since landed on `main` as rebased copies, so the commit list here still starts with its nine original commits and GitHub reports conflicts. This PR's own commits are the six from `b03638f21e` on. The branch needs an update from `main` before it can merge.

With `compression.checkpoint_required` armed:
- the detached review and `/btw` forks had their proactive prune withheld, with a warning that the session halts, although their compaction is exempt. Both gates now use one predicate, `_checkpoint_exempt_fork()`;
- a delegate child of an `--ignore-rules` or `--safe-mode` session loaded the memory provider and archived its transcript into memory the session had opted out of. That isn't intended: subagents now follow the session's opt-out at every depth and fail closed at their first compaction, as the session does.

Points to review:
- `b03638f21e` moves the inline exemption for persistence-isolated forks (#133032) into `_checkpoint_exempt_fork()` with the same truth table, and the prune gate uses it.
- `e0a3a1b246` keyed the child on the parent's memory manager; `78a96dd157` keys it on the recorded opt-out instead, because a parent with built-in memory only has no manager either. `9a9be995f9` carries that opt-out down the delegate chain as `_memory_opt_out`, because a delegate child's own `skip_memory` only says the gate was off where it was built ([@GottZ's review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/149791#pullrequestreview-5797373744)). Read the three together.
- `685636a35a` documents what the gate still leaves out, including the `preview.restart` helper agents, which fail their first compaction under the armed gate on `main` too. Their fix changes how those agents are built, so it's separate. `445041c822` drops two leftovers of the #149265 split.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to #149763. Related: #149265 (the parked superset), #136488 (turns the prune on by default).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_proactive_prune_checkpoint_gate.py tests/agent/test_fork_memory_under_checkpoint_gate.py \
  tests/agent/test_proactive_prune_loop_wiring.py tests/agent/test_pre_compress_checkpoint_contract.py
```

I tested on Linux arm64 at `9a9be995f9`, on top of `55a7b84292`:
- 63 test files that touch the changed code: 838 passed, 0 failed. `scripts/check` passes against `55a7b84292`.
- Each new test fails on the commit before its fix: the detached fork's prune ran 0 times before `b03638f21e`, the `--ignore-rules` child got `skip_memory=False` before `e0a3a1b246`, the built-in-only parent's child got `skip_memory=True` on `e0a3a1b246`, and a gate-off child's grandchild under the armed gate got `skip_memory=True` on `78a96dd157`.

Not run: the full suite, the update from `main`, a real `preview.restart` run or plugin-host process, macOS, Windows.

prs.title: feat(gateway): let the Bot Chat replace the messaging home channels
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Bot Chat as your home. Before: Cron, no origin: lands in Telegram; Gateway notices: ping Telegram; /sethome: messaging chats only. After: Cron, no origin: Bot Chat turn; Gateway notices: Bot Chat notes; /sethome: works in Desktop. Change: gateway.home: bot-chat.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/017958dc-5ca4-40ce-8d1e-d40a030a2386)

## Video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e0e3c77-9311-4825-bd9d-fc57ccd814d8

The Webapp on this branch's head in a scratch profile, recorded with a real browser and pointer. It shows `/sethome` from the app's slash palette, then a `--deliver all` job whose result lands in the Bot Chat as a turn, then the "Gateway online" note after a planned restart. Mock model, scripted input, 51 s, sped up 1.4x for the first chat and 4x during the cron wait. No messaging platform is connected, so the Telegram side is not shown.

## What does this PR do?

Cthulhu asked on Discord for the gateway to be the "home" for messages: with Desktop and the Webapp he never wants anything auto-delivered to Telegram, but Telegram is the `/sethome` destination. Desktop and the Webapp aren't messaging channels, so following Teknium's point, the home here is the profile's canonical Bot Chat.

With `gateway.home: bot-chat` (or `/sethome` typed in any Desktop/Webapp chat):

- a cron job with no origin delivers into the Bot Chat as a turn (the existing `bot-chat` lane), and `deliver=all` includes it;
- gateway notices (online after a planned restart, state.db / cron-store / low-disk warnings, unauthorized-sender hints) are written into the Bot Chat as notes, with no model call;
- the platform home channels no longer get origin-less results or these notices. `deliver=all` still includes them alongside the Bot Chat (`deliver=bot-chat` reaches the Bot Chat only). An explicit `deliver=telegram` and jobs created in a Telegram chat are unchanged, and `/sethome` in a messaging chat takes the home back.

Points to review:

- Notices are notes through the Bot Chat authority's FIFO (`gateway/bot_chat_home.py`); cron stays a turn so it queues while the gateway is down.
- No shutdown note: the authority refuses admissions once the gateway drains, and the app already shows the disconnect.
- `/sethome` is last-wins between local and messaging chats; the setting is per profile, read under each profile's scope.

The first commit moves the shutdown broadcast out of the over-cap `gateway/run_shutdown.py` unchanged.

## Related Issue

Related to #76780, #69809, #143037.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_cron_bot_chat_home.py tests/gateway/test_bot_chat_home.py tests/gateway/test_bot_chat_home_notices.py
```

Manually: in a Desktop chat run `/sethome`, check `gateway.home: bot-chat` in `config.yaml`, then restart the gateway (`hermes gateway restart`); the "Gateway online" note appears in the profile's Bot Chat, not in Telegram.

Tested on Linux (arm64). A real `hermes gateway run` in a scratch `HERMES_HOME` with a planned-restart marker wrote the online note into a newly created Bot Chat. Recording the video surfaced two bugs, fixed here with tests: the online note was refused when the Bot Chat already existed, and the app's slash palette did not offer `/sethome`. Not covered: mobile push (the Webapp has no service worker, so a closed tab still gets no alert).

issues.title: cli-tools.test.ts "no vercel" guard fails once /add-vercel is applied
/add-rtk: mount to /usr/local/bin/rtk is rejected by mount security
issues.body:
**Skill:** `.claude/skills/add-rtk/SKILL.md`, Step 3

Step 3 mounts the host binary into the container at an absolute path:

```bash
ncl groups config add-mount --id <group-id> \
  --host ~/.local/bin/rtk \
  --container /usr/local/bin/rtk \
  --ro
```

Mount security rejects absolute container paths. `isValidContainerPath` in `src/modules/mount-security/index.ts` (around line 282) says:

```ts
// Must not be absolute (it will be prefixed with /workspace/extra/)
if (containerPath.startsWith('/')) {
  return false;
}
```

`add-mount` accepts and stores the entry, but `validateAdditionalMounts` drops it at every spawn with:

```
Additional mount REJECTED … reason="Invalid container path: \"/usr/local/bin/rtk\" - must be relative, non-empty, and not contain \"..\""
```

A relative path wouldn't help either: valid mounts land at `/workspace/extra/<containerPath>`, which is not on `PATH`. Either way `rtk` is missing inside the container. The Step 4 `PreToolUse` hook runs `rtk hook claude`, so every Bash call then hits a missing-command hook.

**Repro:** follow `/add-rtk` on a fresh install, then send the group a message. `logs/nanoclaw.log` shows the `Additional mount REJECTED` warning, and `which rtk` inside the container finds nothing.

**Suggested fixes (pick one):**
- Install rtk in the image (a pinned GitHub-release tarball in the Dockerfile, or `cli-tools.json` if an npm build exists), and drop the mount step.
- Mount it under `/workspace/extra/rtk/` and have the hook call the absolute path `/workspace/extra/rtk/rtk hook claude`.
- Add an allowlisted way to mount a single binary onto `PATH`.

We hit this in a downstream fork and now bake rtk into the image. That has worked across ~40 groups.

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.11.0-rc.1 (280cae014), same code on main at ab9551f01

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

An update with `/update-nanoclaw` changed agent-runner source on a host with no Bun, and nothing typechecked the new source before it went live.

Validate skips the check when `bun --version` fails and records that it was deferred (`scripts/update/transaction.ts:519-534`). The image build never runs it: `container/Dockerfile:90` copies only `agent-runner/package.json` and `bun.lock`, and the Dockerfile has no `tsc` step. The source is mounted into the container at spawn (`src/container-runner.ts:1323-1326`), so cutover's `container/build.sh` runs fully from cache and checks nothing.

Bun is not a host requirement, so most installs take this path. The deferral has been there since the transactional updater landed (8772ec977).

### What did you expect?

Validate checks the staged agent-runner source before cutover, or says plainly that it was not checked. The skill refresh already runs the pinned Bun through pnpm when the host has none (`scripts/update-skills.ts:60`, version from `pinnedBunVersion`), and validate could do the same for `bun install` before its `tsc` run.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. On a Linux host with no `bun` on `PATH`, run `/update-nanoclaw` across a range that changes `container/agent-runner/src/` (v2026.11.0-beta.4 to rc.1 does).
2. Read the `validation` list in the transaction's `state.json`: it has the line in the logs below.
3. Cutover's `container/build.sh` is fully cached and the image ID does not change. Nothing ran `tsc` against the new source.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, x86_64

### Install or update path

Something else

### Docker version

29.9.2

### Channel or interface

Not channel-specific

### Agent provider

Not provider-specific

### Agent model

Not model-specific.

### Relevant redacted logs

```shell
container typecheck deferred to image build (Bun unavailable on host)
```

### Last version that worked

Never. A hand check of this update inside the image passed (`tsc` clean, `bun test` 682 pass, 0 fail), so nothing broke this time; nothing would have caught it if it had.

issues.title: [bug] Updates don't rebuild per-group images: groups with installed packages keep the old agent image
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

`cab10bbc` (origin/main, 2026-10-11), updated from `88eb1766` via `/update-nanoclaw`

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

After `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilt the agent image, an agent group with packages (`packages_apt: ["ffmpeg","ghostscript"]`, installed earlier via `install_packages`) kept running its old per-group image:

- `nanoclaw-agent-v2-<slug>:latest` was rebuilt (Claude Code 2.1.296, Agent SDK 0.3.296).
- `nanoclaw-agent-v2-<slug>:<agent-group-id>` was still the image built the day before on the old base. A freshly spawned container for that group reported `claude --version` → `2.1.281`.
- Only `ncl groups restart --id <group> --rebuild` fixed it.

Why, from the code:

- Spawn uses the group's tag whenever one is set: `image: containerConfig.imageTag || CONTAINER_IMAGE` (`src/container-runner.ts`, `composeSessionSpec`).
- `buildAgentGroupImage` records the base it layered onto (`LABEL dev.nanoclaw.derived-from=<base image id>`), but nothing compares that label with the current base.
- The update controller's image step builds or pulls only the base (`scripts/update/transaction.ts`: `container/build.sh` / `pull`). It never rebuilds derived group images.

Impact: every group that has ever installed a package silently misses agent-image updates (Claude Code CLI, Bun, Agent SDK and other runtime deps) after each update. The agent-runner *source* is a shared live mount while its dependencies are baked into the image. So such a group can also run new runner code against old dependencies. The update reports success, and the base image looks current.

### What did you expect?

After an update that changes the base image, each group's derived image is rebuilt (or rebuilt lazily at its next spawn) on the new base, or the update at least lists the stale groups and the `--rebuild` command.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. In a group, `install_packages({ apt: ["jq"] })` and approve, so the group gets `nanoclaw-agent-v2-<slug>:<group-id>`.
2. Bump a pinned CLI in `container/cli-tools.json` (or update to a release that does) and run `/update-nanoclaw` (or `./container/build.sh`).
3. Message the group, then `docker exec <its container> claude --version`: it shows the old version. `docker image inspect <group image> --format '{{index .Config.Labels "dev.nanoclaw.derived-from"}}'` differs from the current base image id.

Possible fixes:

- At spawn, compare `dev.nanoclaw.derived-from` with the current base id and rebuild if they differ (the label already exists for this).
- Or have the update's image step rebuild every group whose `packages_apt`/`packages_npm` is non-empty, before restart.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Raspberry Pi OS (Debian 12), Linux 6.18 arm64

### Install or update path

`/update-nanoclaw` (local image build)

issues.title: [bug] "Re-run setup to get a fresh code" does not work: a re-run skips the hardened image question

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

8e52b12

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

On a fresh install I said yes to "Enable Echo's hardened agent image? Open the perks dashboard in your browser?". Setup printed the portal link and a code. The code was not approved in time (it stopped working after roughly five minutes), and setup printed:

```
▲  That sign-in code expired before it was approved. Re-run setup to get a fresh code. Skipping this step for now.
```

It then went on to build the sandbox locally. I stopped the installer and re-ran `bash nanoclaw.sh`, as the message says. After "Standard setup" and "Fresh agent" it went straight to "Preparing your assistant's sandbox…". The hardened image question was not asked, so there was no fresh code.

The expired sign-in is recorded as an answer. `.env` now contains `NANOCLAW_HARDENED_IMAGE=false`, and `chooseImageSource()` returns early when `imageSourceDecided()` is true. Deleting that line and re-running brings the question back.

Where this comes from:

- `setup/registry-login.ts:864`: `new LoginError('That sign-in code expired before it was approved.', 'Re-run setup to get a fresh code.')`
- `setup/portal.ts`: `signInThroughPortal` → `skippedSignIn` → `beginPortal` returns `null` → `runImagePortal` runs `if (!client) { if (!options.apply) writeImageSource('local'); return; }`
- `setup/lib/registry-state.ts`: `writeImageSource` writes `false` on purpose so a resumed run does not re-prompt.
- A comment in `setup/auto.ts` says a skipped or failed sign-in is written to `.env` and the question is not asked again. So the skip is by design, and the hint text contradicts it.

### What did you expect?

Either the re-run asks the question again and issues a fresh code, as the message promises, or the message says what actually gets a fresh code.

Possible fixes: treat an expired code as "not answered" (`clearImageSource()` instead of `writeImageSource('local')` for that case), or keep the behaviour and change the hint. Separately, the portal path prints no expiry time for the code, and five minutes is short for a first sign-up.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Fresh checkout on a machine with no NanoClaw account. Run `bash nanoclaw.sh`, choose Standard setup and Fresh agent.
2. Press Enter at the hardened image question, then do not approve the code. Wait about five minutes for it to expire.
3. Stop setup and run `bash nanoclaw.sh` again with the same options.
4. Observe that the hardened image question is not asked and `.env` has `NANOCLAW_HARDENED_IMAGE=false`.

### OS version and CPU architecture

Debian 13, x86_64 (unprivileged LXC on Proxmox VE 9)

### Install or update path

Standard setup with nanoclaw.sh

### Docker version

Docker 29.10.0

### Channel or interface

Not channel-specific

### Agent provider

Not provider-specific

### Agent model

_No response_

### Relevant redacted logs

```shell
▲  That sign-in code expired before it was approved. Re-run setup to get a fresh code. Skipping this step for now.
```

### Last version that worked

_No response_

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-antigravity with its own payload
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-antigravity`, a provider skill that runs agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) and Gemini models, switchable per group with `ncl groups config update --provider antigravity`.
- **Problem**: there is no way to run a NanoClaw agent on Gemini through Google's own agent harness; OpenCode reaches Gemini models but not Antigravity's tools, planning and conversation store.
- **Fix**: a provider skill shaped like `/add-cursor`. All code and tests live in the skill's `payload/`; apply wires the five provider barrels and adds a pinned, sha512-checked `agy` 1.5.8 to the agent image. Auth is a Gemini API key held only by the credential gateway; the container sees a placeholder.
- **Out of scope**: Google-account (OAuth) sign-in, which Google's terms do not allow from a third-party harness; a generic manifest for native binaries (see "Core changes" below).

<details>
<summary>Core changes outside the skill, and why</summary>

agy is a native Go binary that is not published on npm, so `container/cli-tools.json` (npm only) cannot install it. The block has to run as root, before the setuid sweep and `USER node`, and is best placed above the often-bumped layers so a lockfile or Claude Code bump does not re-download 265 MB. No existing hook does that, so this PR adds one:

- `container/Dockerfile`: an empty `# >>> nanoclaw:provider-binaries` / `# <<< nanoclaw:provider-binaries` marker region just above `# ---- agent-runner deps`. With nothing installed it changes no layer.
- `docs/skill-directives.md`, `scripts/skill-directives.ts` (comment), `docs/skill-guidelines.md`, `docs/skills-model.md`: one line each naming the region as the native-binary path.
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts`: the scratch root gets a stub Dockerfile carrying the region, the same way it already stubs `cli-tools.json`.

Alternatives considered: a prose-only Dockerfile edit like `/add-mnemon` breaks setup's deterministic provider install (`setup/providers/install.ts` fails on any step it cannot apply); appending at end of file with `USER root`/`USER node` breaks on remove, which deletes by line and would also delete core's own `USER node`. A `json-merge` manifest for native binaries (url + sha512 per arch) would be cleaner long term but is a bigger core feature. I'm happy to split the marker into its own PR first, or to rework it into a manifest, if you prefer.

Other edits: the `registry-skills.yml` matrix entry, the provider list in `skill-descriptor.test.ts`, `.github/skill-pins/not-covered.json` (regenerated; `AGY_VERSION=1.5.8` now appears as a hand-checked binary pin), and README (Antigravity listed next to Codex, Cursor and OpenCode).
</details>

## Related work

No issue. It is a self-contained provider skill in the `/add-cursor` shape (#4107), so it can be reviewed directly; nothing changes for installs that don't apply it.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run skill-pins:check`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint` -> pass (lint: 0 errors)
- `pnpm test` -> pass: 345 files, 5082 tests
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts add-antigravity` -> pass: apply, host and container typecheck, payload tests (vitest 102, bun 87), provider-contract verifier (9/9), image build (agy 1.5.8 amd64, `cli.tar.gz: OK`), byte-exact remove, re-apply
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts --combined-providers` -> pass with codex, cursor and opencode (vitest 288 passed, bun 462 passed)
- Live end-to-end on Linux x64 (Docker, Iron Proxy gateway, CLI channel, real Gemini key): two turns in one session; resume after `ncl groups restart` (new container, `--conversation` reused, earlier codeword recalled); the `conversations/` archive written with both exchanges; inside the container `ps` shows agy and no claude; the gateway saw only Google hosts (0 Anthropic requests); REMOVE.md restored the tree byte-exact and re-apply reproduced it. The real key was found nowhere in container env or filesystem, the image, logs, process args or the checkout. An earlier run of the same setup also covered file and shell tools, MCP `send_message`, `ask_user_question`, and a 12-case scripted eval against the live API.
- arm64: (a) native GitHub `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner ([run](https://github.com/kennethleungty/nanoclaw/actions/runs/44118483750)): apply/remove, image build, all tests (bun 759 pass), and agy reaching the Gemini API from the arm64 image. (b) QEMU-emulated arm64 on x64: full NanoClaw chat behind the gateway (reply, resume, tools, MCP, `ask_user_question`). Both ran before the installer switched from `TARGETARCH` to `uname -m`, so (c) the final 5-line block was rebuilt for arm64 under QEMU on the pinned base image: arm64 tarball selected, sha512 OK, `agy --version` 1.5.8 on aarch64 as `node`. A mismatched `AGY_VERSION` stops the build before any download.
- Live on a real chat app, behind OneCLI: a long-running downstream install (2026.10.0 core, OneCLI 1.42 gateway, Telegram channel, GCP e2-small x86_64). That core predates the Dockerfile region and the exchange archive (#4105), so both were backported first, plus the provider list in `skill-descriptor.test.ts`. The skill's own pre-flight check then passed and its directives applied cleanly (host build, runtime typecheck, payload tests, verifier 9/9, image build with agy 1.5.8). The key went in through `setup/index.ts --step provider-auth antigravity` at the masked prompt and landed in OneCLI as a project-scoped secret for `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` with `x-goog-api-key` injection. Then the group was switched with `ncl groups config update --provider antigravity`:
  - Messages sent from the Telegram mobile app were answered by agy. In the session container `agy … --model gemini-4-hydrogen-medium --conversation <id>` was running, and there were 0 `claude` processes.
  - The container env held only `GEMINI_API_KEY=nc-antigravity-placeholder`, and OneCLI logged only Google hosts (`generativelanguage`, `play`), with 0 Anthropic requests.
  - The conversation resumed across a model change and `ncl groups restart`, and one `conversations/` archive covered both turns.
  - `agy models` from inside the container, through the gateway, listed the slugs the key can use.
  - Replies arrived about 11 s after the Telegram message on `gemini-4-hydrogen-medium`, including a cold container start.
  - On current `main`, OneCLI also records the connection for the group's provider from `provider: 'antigravity'`, the same target shape as `/add-cursor`, asserted in `setup/providers/antigravity.test.ts`.
- Apple Silicon: Docker Desktop runs the same `linux/arm64` image as the native arm64 runner and the QEMU runs above, and the skill's host-side code is plain TypeScript with nothing platform-specific.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-antigravity skill: run agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (Gemini models) with a Gemini API key held by the credential gateway.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Credentials:** the Gemini key goes only to the credential gateway, through `getCredentialStore().connection()` with a `GatewayCredentialTarget` that sets `provider: 'antigravity'`. Containers get `GEMINI_API_KEY=nc-antigravity-placeholder`, which agy sends as `x-goog-api-key`; the gateway swaps it for the real key on the wire. The key is never in `.env`, container env, argv, mounts or logs. The live runs scanned for it and found it nowhere.
- **Supply chain:** one exact build (1.5.8, execution id 4602374149505024) downloaded from `storage.googleapis.com`, a sha512 pinned per architecture and checked with `sha512sum -c` before extraction, a `--version` check that fails the build, and auto-update forced off. The tarballs are byte-identical to the assets on Google's GitHub release.
- **Egress:** model domains are `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` and `play.googleapis.com` (agy telemetry, which 1.5.8 cannot turn off in API-key mode). Requests from antigravity groups pass without an approval card; with Iron Proxy, model domains are allowed install-wide (as for other providers).
- **Permissions:** agy runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and its terminal sandbox off (it needs user namespaces, which Docker's seccomp profile blocks), so the container is the boundary, as with the other providers. The image still ends as `node`, with no setuid binaries.
- **Prompt injection:** per-session instructions go in-band as a `<nanoclaw_system_context>` block in agy's first turn. Core's formatter escapes `<` in inbound text, so a chat message cannot forge that block.

## Skill delivery

- **Apply:** the pre-flight check refuses a core without the provider contracts, the credential-connection seam, the exchange archive or the Dockerfile region, and leaves no partial change. Apply then copies 21 payload files (host, container and setup provider code, their tests, and `container/install-antigravity.sh`). It appends one import to each of the five barrels (`src/providers`, `src/provider-contracts`, `container/agent-runner/src/providers`, `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts`, `setup/providers`) and adds the 5-line Dockerfile block inside the region. It then rebuilds the image and host and runs the copied tests.
- **Remove:** `REMOVE.md` reverses each step; every appended line is unique to this skill. After removal the checkout is byte-identical to before (checked by `test-registry-skills.ts`).
- **Fresh clone:** `test-registry-skills.ts` applies the skill to a fresh clone, builds, tests, removes and re-applies it, alone and combined with codex, cursor and opencode.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Codex ChatGPT sign-in works without a Codex CLI on the host, and no longer warns about `/tmp`.

- **Problem**: with no `codex` on PATH, setup asks for `npm install -g @openai/codex`, which fails with EACCES on a root-owned npm prefix. The throwaway `CODEX_HOME` was in `/tmp`, where Codex refuses its helpers and warns.
- **Fix**: npx fetches the image's exact pin from `container/cli-tools.json` into the npm cache, running in an empty private project. Setup checks that the binary reports the pin, then runs it directly, with no global install and no sudo.
- **Sign-in home**: `data/codex-login/<random>`, git-ignored with mode 0700, and never `~/.codex`. On a signal, setup stops the login before removing the home, using SIGKILL after 3 seconds or on a second signal. A killed run's leftovers are swept after an hour.
- **Fails closed**: a pin that isn't strict semver never reaches npx. If npx is missing or fails, setup names the API-key option and OpenAI's installer (`… | sh -s -- --release <pin>`, no sudo), with npm second. The installer writes to `~/.codex/packages` and the shell profile, but sign-in still uses the throwaway home.

<details><summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

- **Sign in inside the agent image** (OpenCode): Codex binds its browser callback to `127.0.0.1` inside its own process, so a container's port forward can't reach it. Only device pairing would work.
- **`pnpm dlx`** (Cursor's Bun helper): this would work too. npx was the call made on #3791, because it covers both sign-in methods with no Docker step.

</details>

## Summary

Makes setup verify systemd linger without launching interactive PolicyKit authentication.
