prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a group mount of a folder NanoClaw keeps for itself from silently stopping that group's agent from starting.

- **Problem**: only NanoClaw may mount its runner code, skills, plugins and instruction files, and its key and certificate folders (`data/session-materials`, `data/gateway-trust`). The driver's guard enforces that. But `ncl groups config add-mount` stores such a mount without complaint, and the guard then refuses every start. The only trace is a once-a-minute warning, and the person gets no reply.
- **Fix**: the guard's rule moves into `requiredMountClass` in `drivers/types.ts`. `validateSpec` and `add-mount` both call it, so there is one rule, not a copy. `add-mount` judges the path the way the mount check resolves it, and refuses a reserved path with the reason. For install content it suggests mounting a copy; for keys and certificates it just refuses.
- **Fix**: a start refused with `denied-by-policy` or `spec-invalid` also logs an error naming the cause, on each attempt (about once a minute per stuck session). The existing retry warning is unchanged, because installed skills anchor on that exact line.
- **Out of scope**: a mount of a parent folder, such as the whole checkout, read-write. That needs a new guard rule and changes behavior for some installs, so it comes as its own PR.

## Related work

No issue. Found in a live install's logs, where two sessions went silent for about 10 minutes after a group mount of the runner code.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests fail on main and pass here: `add-mount` refuses each reserved folder, stores nothing, and suggests a copy only for install content; a policy refusal keeps the warning and adds the error. A retryable failure logs no error.
- Existing guard tests (`drivers/`, `mount-composition`) pass unchanged against the shared function.
- Full suite: 330 files pass. 6 files hit 5 s timeouts under load and pass alone; `onecli-detection.test.ts` fails locally on the previous head too (a local pnpm issue). `tsc`, eslint and prettier are clean.
- No existing line is edited in `wakeContainer`'s failure path or in `groups.ts`'s imports, so downstream skills that patch those lines still apply.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a FIFO (or symlink, or directory) at the group's Claude `settings.json` from wedging every container start.

- **Problem**: `writeMemorySessionHook` read `~/.claude/settings.json` with `readFileSync` and rewrote it with `writeFileSync`. That directory is the group's persistent, agent-writable `.claude-shared` mount, so a FIFO there blocked runner startup forever, on every respawn, before the poll loop started. A symlink was read and written through.
- **Fix**: open with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and require a regular file. A refused entry is logged and left alone, as the host's `prepareClaudeMemorySettings` already does, so the session still starts (without the memory hook). Writes go through a sibling temp file and `rename`, never truncating in place, and are skipped when nothing changed.
- **Out of scope**: a size cap on the file; moving hook registration to the host.

## Related work

No issue. Found by an automated review of a downstream fork; the code is unchanged from upstream.

## Summary

An agent tagged in a thread gets the thread's earlier lines it never saw, read back from the chat, on the channels the install lists in `NANOCLAW_PLATFORM_HISTORY` (for example `NANOCLAW_PLATFORM_HISTORY=slack`).
- **Problem**: a wiring that wakes on tags drops the thread's other lines, and a new thread session has seen nothing, so the agent answers the tag without the conversation it was pulled into.
- **Fix**: right after the existing backfill, the router reads the thread through the channel adapter and writes the lines the session has not seen as one `<thread-history>` row before the message.
- **Off by default**: unset or empty, `backfillPlatformHistory` returns at once and routing runs today's code. The operator names the channel types; core names none.
- **Out of scope**: the channel's top-level lines (next PR in this stack), any agent tool, `ncl sessions history`.

```mermaid

  look: neo
---

    the chat's top-level timeline`"]
    b4["`**Thread lines not addressed to Pip**
    never reach it`"]
    b3["`**Pip sees**
    timeline + the tag`"]
    b1 -- "routes" --> b2 -- "writes rows" --> b3
    b4 -. "dropped" .-> b3
  end
  subgraph after["After, with NANOCLAW_PLATFORM_HISTORY=slack"]
    direction TB
    a1["`**Tag in a thread**
    Alex: @Pip can you look?`"]
    a2["`**Backfill**
    unchanged`"]
    a3["`**Thread look**
    adapter.readHistory, 1.5 s budget`"]
    a4["`**Keep unseen lines only**
    exact match by platform id,
    sender allowed in this chat`"]
    a5["`**Pip sees**
    timeline + one thread-history row + the tag`"]
    a1 -- "routes" --> a2 -- "then" --> a3 -- "newest 100 lines" --> a4 -- "one row" --> a5
  end
  before ~~~ after
  classDef same fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,color:#24292f
  classDef gone fill:#ffebe9,stroke:#cf222e,color:#24292f
  classDef added fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#24292f

  class b4 gone
  class a3,a4,a5 added
  style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4
  style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4
  linkStyle default stroke:#8c959f
```

<details><summary>How it decides</summary>

- **When**: only when lines can be missing: the session was just created, or the wiring does not take every message (not `mention-sticky`, not `accumulate`, not pattern `.`).
- **Reader**: new optional `ChannelAdapter.readHistory(platformId, threadId, { limit })`. The Chat SDK bridge implements it with the chat library's `history.thread.list` and refuses a thread whose `channelIdFromThreadId` is not the chat. Core checks whether the method exists, never a channel name.
- **Which lines**: the newest 100, minus everything the session already has, matched exactly by platform message id: messages it holds, lines an earlier block showed, rows the backfill seeded, its own delivered replies, and the message itself. The agent's lines from anywhere else stay and show as `you`.
- **Senders**: a line whose sender the chat's access rules refuse is left out (`wouldAdmitSender`: the access gate's rule plus the wiring's `sender_scope`, read only: no dropped-message row, no approval). The block says how many were left out, even when nothing else remains, so the agent can say so instead of guessing.
- **Once**: the row id is keyed by the message id, and a look that finds this message's block already written adds nothing.
- **Time**: a 1.5 s budget, because a person is waiting for the reply. The message never waits longer. A read that runs past it is left to finish and writes its block when it lands; the block then rides with the next message. While it runs, the thread starts no second read.
- **Old windows**: a full window that does not contain the message is not the thread's newest lines, so no block is written.
- **Mailbox**: `MailboxTimelineMessage` and `MailboxHistoryMessage` gain an optional `platformMessageId` (the SQLite mailbox reads it from `delivered`); the backfill keeps it on the rows it seeds. Mailbox implementations that do not return it still compile.

</details>

**Platforms**
- Verified: Slack.
- Read, not verified, and found wanting. Listing one of these turns on what is described here, so they are not recommended:
  - Discord: a top-level mention's thread id is the channel itself, so it would read the channel's lines as if they were the thread.
  - GitHub: the adapter returns a PR's oldest comments first. Past 100 comments the window misses the message, and no block is written.
  - Teams: Graph pages hold 50 messages and need read permissions most bot installs lack, so the read likely fails, with a warning per tag.

**Known limits**
- A brand-new conversation pays one platform read even when its thread holds only the message itself (the bare Slack call measured about 0.2 s).
- Display names: on a cold name cache the chat library looks up each uncached author. A long read misses the budget, and its block follows on the next message.
- Slack threads longer than about 200 lines: the adapter's backward read returns a window that ends near line 200, which misses the message, so no block is written.
- Two messages in one thread within one read (roughly 0.2 to 1.5 s apart) can land in a different order than they were sent.

## Related work

No issue. Near #4247 (attachments on echo and backfill rows) and #4395 (copies in `ncl sessions history`); neither overlaps these lines. Safe to review directly: nothing changes until an install lists a channel.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes ten CLI scripts actually run when the checkout path has a space in it or is reached through a symlink.

- **Problem**: they decided whether they were the entry point with ``import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}` ``. `import.meta.url` is percent-encoded and symlink-resolved; `argv[1]` is neither. - **Out of scope**: other CLIs that use `pathToFileURL(argv[1])` without realpath (space-safe, symlink-unsafe); a shared `isEntryPoint` helper.

No issue. Each changed site is the same one-line expression, so it can be reviewed directly.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Follow-up to #4418: the three non-blocking points from its review. Nothing changes on the normal install path.

- **A broken Node ran twice**: `check_node` ran `node --version` again only to read its error. The one run now sends stderr to the log, and the screen line is read back from there.
- **Installer output kept twice**: corepack's and npm's output went to the log and into a variable. It now goes to the log only; the first error line is read from what the log gained during the try. If the log's lines cannot be counted, no error line is shown, never an older one.
- **`~/.local` diagnosis trimmed**: the check of which part of the path is in the way is gone. When `mkdir` fails, setup names the folder it tried, shows `mkdir`'s own error line and gives the log path.

`setup.sh` gets 4 lines shorter. On Ubuntu 26.04, whose `mkdir` names no path, a file at `~/.local` now reads:

```
Could not install pnpm: /home/x/.local cannot be created:
  mkdir: Already exists
Fix that, then re-run setup. mkdir's full output is in /home/x/nanoclaw/logs/bootstrap.log
```

Known limits:

- A Node that cannot start: what it printed on stdout goes into the log after its stderr, so the two are not in time order there.
- The `mkdir` line does not say which part of the path is in the way, such as a file or a dangling link higher up.

## Related work

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): apply media-failure note at the inbound boundary (follow-up to #2895)
prs.body:
## What

Follow-up to #2895 (merged). A high-effort review of that PR surfaced a regression on the approval-answer path, plus a minor cleanup.

## The bug

`appendMediaFailureNote` was applied to `content` **before** the pending-question slash-command handler. When an approver answers a pending question with a slash command carried as an image caption (e.g. `/approve`) and the image download fails, `content` becomes `"/approve\n[image could not be downloaded]"`. The handler does `cmd = content.trim().toLowerCase()` and exact-matches against the option commands, so the answer no longer matches: the approval is silently dropped, `pendingQuestions` is not cleared, and the raw text is forwarded to the agent. Narrow trigger (slash answer + media + download failure), but a real regression of a sensitive path.

## Fix

- Apply the media-failure note at the inbound `text` boundary, leaving `content` pristine for the slash-command and bot-message matching above.
- Tighten the empty-message guard so a message carrying only a *failed* download still survives (`failures.length === 0` added to the skip condition) — preserving the original intent of #2895.
- Swap an em-dash for a hyphen in a new comment.

The `appendMediaFailureNote` unit tests from #2895 still cover the helper itself; this change only moves where it is applied.

prs.title: fix(container): rebuild a group's image when the agent image under it changes
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Groups with extra packages now move to the new agent image after an update, instead of running the old one until someone runs `--rebuild`.

- **Problem**: a group that used `install_packages` runs its own image, built `FROM` the agent image once. Updates and setup rebuild only the agent image, and spawn prefers the group's image, so the group keeps the old CLI, SDK, Bun and agent-runner `node_modules` under fresh agent-runner source, with no warning.
- **Fix**: compare the group image's `dev.nanoclaw.derived-from` label with the current agent image id, and rebuild on a mismatch (or a missing label or image). The host checks every group in the background at start, and each spawn starts a check without waiting for it. One image job runs per group at a time; a failed rebuild keeps the old image, logs the `--rebuild` command, and waits for the next agent image change. A pin to any other tag is left alone, a re-pin made during a rebuild holds, and a group still pinned to its own image after all its packages were removed keeps that image.
- **Out of scope**: removing the replaced group image (disk), and containers already running, which keep their image until they exit.

## Related work

Closes #4076

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/container-runner.stale-group-image.test.ts`, 11 tests with a stub `docker`: stale, fresh, missing label or image, foreign pin, no packages left, re-pins, three spawns share one check, failed build, startup pass, spawn not held. The spawn test fails without the spawn call, and the no-packages test without its early return. Full suite 4955 pass, and the 25 load timeouts in 8 `scripts/`, `setup/` and skill files (untouched here) pass when rerun alone; `tsc` clean.
- Real install on Proxmox (Debian 13 LXC, `./container/build.sh` as the update runs it): unpatched main reproduces the bug; with the fix the startup pass rebuilt the group image within 10 s of restart, and with the host running a spawn started the rebuild and the next container ran the new image with its package.
- Real Docker: a group image built on a v2026.10.0 agent image moved from Claude Code 2.1.280 / SDK 0.3.280 to 2.1.321 / 0.3.321.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Groups that installed extra packages now move to the new agent image on their own after `/update-nanoclaw` or an image rebuild: NanoClaw rebuilds their image in the background when it starts or when the group next runs, and the group's next container uses it, so `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild` is no longer needed after an update. If you built a group's image by hand under the group's own tag, give it your own tag and pin that with `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --image-tag <tag>`, because NanoClaw now rebuilds the group's own tag.
```

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The host now opens two files in container-writable folders with `O_NONBLOCK`, so a named pipe (FIFO) under either name can no longer make the open wait. The log now names a file that was refused.

- **Problem**: two host functions open a name inside a folder the agent container can write, using `O_NOFOLLOW` but not `O_NONBLOCK`:
  - `readGroupPersona` reads `instructions.prepend.md` in the group folder on every spawn.
  - `prepareSpawnFile` opens `append-open-close` provider files, such as Codex's `auth.json`.

  `O_NOFOLLOW` stops symlinks, not FIFOs. A synchronous open of a FIFO with no peer waits on the host's event loop. The regular-file check after it never runs.
- **Fix**: add `O_NONBLOCK` to both opens.
  - The persona read's `fstat().isFile()` check then refuses the FIFO and leaves the persona out, now with a warning naming the file.
  - The spawn-file open of a FIFO with no reader fails with `ENXIO`, so only that group's start fails. A new `fstat().isFile()` check also refuses a FIFO that something reads.
  - A refused spawn file now fails with an error that names it and says to remove it, not a bare `ENXIO` or `ELOOP`.
- **Out of scope**: what the host reads or writes. Only how these two files are opened changes.

## Related work

No linked issue. Maintainer fix; the diff and its tests are the review surface.

prs.title: fix(channels): close and reopen a code fence when a long reply is split
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a long reply split mid-code-block from rendering the rest of the code as plain text.

- **Problem**: `splitForLimit` in `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` cuts long replies at the platform limit (Discord 2000, Telegram 4000, Slack, Mattermost) without tracking code fences. When a cut lands inside a fenced block, the code in the next message renders as plain text and the prose after it gets fenced instead.
- **Fix**: when a chunk ends with a fence still open, close it at the end of the chunk and reopen it — same marker and info string — at the start of the next one, the same approach `splitCardText` already uses for cards. Room for the closing marker is reserved before cutting, so no chunk exceeds the limit, and only the line break at the cut is dropped, so the next line's indentation (code) survives. Text with no open fence at the cut splits exactly as before.
- **Out of scope**: card splitting (already handled); inline code spans.

## Related work

No issue. Found by reading `splitForLimit`; every channel with a length limit goes through this path, and the two new tests reproduce the broken rendering on `main`, so the change is safe to review directly.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now gives OneCLI's local database its own password instead of the fixed fallback in OneCLI's compose file.

Data stays in its volume, and OneCLI's two containers (app and database) are recreated once; a second run changes nothing. `/update-nanoclaw` does not run setup, so the release note asks updating installs to run that command once.
- **Safety**: it refuses, changing nothing, when recreating OneCLI from `~/.onecli` would change more than the password (an image, a port, a mount or a setting), and says what to save first. Image-tag and port settings that setup saves after OneCLI starts (as on macOS) are accepted, and so is another tag of the same local image. A run cut off midway is finished by the next one.
- **Out of scope**: remote gateways, which setup leaves alone.

prs.title: fix(portal): end a refused cell dial at once instead of after 10 s
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A refused portal dial now shows up in the log at once as `dial_failed`, not 10 s later as `handshake_timeout`.

- **Problem**: on Node 22, a refused WebSocket upgrade fires `error` but never `close`, and `readyState` stays at CONNECTING. The link's `error` listener was empty and only `close` dropped the socket, so each refused dial waited out the 10 s handshake timer and was logged as a timeout. On Node 26 `close` 1006 follows at once, but nothing was logged.
- **Fix**: an `error` before `open` is a failed dial. It is logged as `dial_failed`, the socket is dropped once, and the link retries on the usual backoff. On Node 26 the `close` that follows finds the socket already gone, so there is no second reconnect. An `error` after `open` still leaves the drop to `close`, which carries the close code (a 4403 still stops the link).
- **Out of scope**: why the cell refuses a ticket the portal just issued. That is on the portal side. Node's WebSocket does not expose the HTTP status, so the host can log that a dial failed, not why.

## Related work

Part of #4427: this fixes the misleading log. The link itself waits on a portal-side fix.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 4 new tests in `src/community-portal/link.test.ts`: `error` alone (Node 22) and `error` then `close` 1006 (Node 26) each give one `dial_failed`, one reconnect, the same backoff, and no handshake timeout. Both fail on `main`. `error` after `open`, then `close` 1006 or 4403: one drop, and 4403 still stops the link.
- `vitest run src/community-portal src/modules/community-portal` → 55 pass. `tsc` and `prettier --check` clean.
- Live, the real link code against `wss://portal.nanoclaw.dev/cell/link` with a bogus ticket, 13 s each:
  - Node 22.23.5, `main`: `handshake_timeout` at 10.0 s, 2 dials.
  - Node 22.23.5, this branch: `dial_failed` at 0.7 s, then retries at 1.3 s, 2.7 s and 6.6 s. No `handshake_timeout`.
  - Node 26.13, this branch: `dial_failed` at 1.1 s, 4 dials and 4 events, so no double reconnect. `main` retried but logged nothing.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Daniel's follow-ups from his #4202 and #4213 approvals.

- **Problem**:
  - On a fresh Arch image, `pacman -S jq` fails with "target not found". The jq note then names 5 skills, but 13 run jq.
  - After a provider install on a Mac with no service, "not installed" prints twice.
  - A host build with type errors still writes its JS to `dist/`, and the next restart loads it.
- **Fix**:
  - On a never-synced pacman, jq needs a full system upgrade. Before the sudo ask, `nanoclaw.sh` says so and asks "Run the full system upgrade now? [y/N]". Only `y` or `yes` runs `pacman -Syu --needed jq`. On a no (the default), setup installs nothing and shows the jq note; with no terminal, or for a non-root user without sudo, it doesn't ask and does the same. A host that has synced is never upgraded. The answer goes to `logs/setup.log`.
  - The note names skills as examples; a test keeps it true.
  - `restartHost` drops `restart.sh`'s stderr only on exit 2 (no service).
  - Both host builds in a provider install use `--noEmitOnError`, and so does the rebuild command setup prints when its own fails.
- **Out of scope**: #4213 follow-up 3 (OpenCode needs one more restart after auth).

## Related work

Follow-ups to #4202 ([comment](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4202#issuecomment-6771411298)) and #4213 ([comment](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4213#issuecomment-6771412357)). prs.title: fix(chat-sdk): resume a split reply at the part that failed
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A retry of a long reply now starts at the part that failed, so the parts already posted are not posted again.

- **Problem**: the bridge splits a long reply into parts. If part 3 of 5 failed, the retry started again at part 1, so the user saw parts 1 and 2 twice. On a rate-limited channel the repeats used up the budget the failed part needed.
- **Fix**: delivery passes the adapter a delivery id made of the session id and the outbound row id (`OutboundMessage.deliveryId`); a row id alone is unique only within one session. The bridge stores how many parts of that row are posted in its SQLite state store. A retry, even after a restart, resumes there, returns part 1's id, and does not resend part 1's files. A changed text or limit starts over. The record outlives the last part (7-day TTL), so a retry after a failed delivery ack posts nothing. A store error falls back to posting from part 1, as before.
- **Out of scope**: backing off before a retry (#4227). A part that fails every attempt still fails the message after 3 tries, with the earlier parts posted once.

## Related work

Follow-up to #4366 (closed): its three "today:" tests are inverted here or kept as plain contracts. Touches the same loop as #4227; whichever merges second rebases.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge-split.test.ts` (new, 17 tests): resume after a failed part, a part failing every attempt, files across a retry, a restart that closes and reopens a file-backed database, a failed ack, a failed progress read. 7 of them, plus the delivery and registry id tests, fail on `main`.
- `src/delivery.test.ts` runs the real host loop, channel registry and bridge: when `markDelivered` fails after every part landed, the retry posts nothing more (fails on `main`); two sessions whose rows share an id each post their whole reply.
- The split, delivery, registry and state test files pass (57 tests); `pnpm run typecheck`, Prettier and `eslint` are clean on the changed files.
- E2E (Proxmox LXC, real Discord channel, live agent, 6-part reply, a proxy failing the 3rd post once with a 503): on `main` the channel shows part 1 three times and part 2 twice, the repeats hit Discord's real 429, and the reply gave up without part 6. On this branch the retry logged `Resuming a split reply ... posted=2` and posted parts 3-6; each part appears once.

## User and release impact

A long reply that fails part-way is no longer posted again from the start on retry; it resumes at the part that failed.

prs.title: feat: add extension points for context at a session's wake
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds extension points so a skill can give a waking session more context without editing core lines. None of them does anything by itself. With nothing registered, routing works as today, and three small things change: seeded rows gain one field, two mailbox reads do one lookup per row, and the prompt gains one line (see "User and release impact").
- **Problem**: a skill that wants to put context in front of the agent when a message wakes it (for example, lines it reads back from the chat) has to edit `src/router.ts`, the container's formatter and the agent's prompt text. Those edits break on upstream changes.
- **Fix**: four small seams, each usable on its own:
  - `ChannelAdapter.readHistory`: an optional reader of a thread's or a chat's newest lines, implemented once in the Chat SDK bridge.
  - `registerWakeContext(name, provider)`: modules register providers. The router runs them once in the wake branch, after the cross-session backfill, and writes their blocks before the message.
  - A generic context block in the container: `<tag about="...">`, so a new block needs no formatter or prompt edit.
  - An optional `platformMessageId` on the two outbound mailbox reads and on the rows the backfill seeds.
- **Why core, given CONTRIBUTING**: these are extension points, not a feature. Each is the smallest generic piece a skill cannot add from outside: the router call and the order of a session's writes, the container renderer, the adapter method on the bridge, and the delivered id that only the mailbox has. Features that use them belong in skills.

```mermaid
---
config:
  look: neo
---
flowchart LR
  subgraph before["Before"]
    direction TB
    b1["`**Engaged message**
    wakes a session`"]
    b2["`**Backfill**
    cross-session timeline`"]
    b3["`**Message written**
    container wakes`"]
    b1 -- "routes" --> b2 -- "then" --> b3
  end
  subgraph after["After"]
    direction TB
    a1["`**Engaged message**
    wakes a session`"]
    a2["`**Backfill**
    unchanged`"]
    a3["`**gatherWakeContext**
    registered providers, one 1.5 s budget`"]
    a4["`**Context rows**
    one per block, tag + about`"]
    a5["`**Message written**
    in arrival order, container wakes`"]
    a1 -- "routes" --> a2 -- "then" --> a3 -- "blocks ready in time" --> a4 -- "before" --> a5
    a3 -. "none registered: returns at once" .-> a5
  end
  before ~~~ after
  classDef same fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#8c959f,color:#24292f
  classDef added fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#24292f
  class b1,b2,b3,a1,a2,a5 same
  class a3,a4 added
  style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4
  style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:4 4
  linkStyle default stroke:#8c959f
```

<details><summary>What each seam guarantees</summary>

- **readHistory(platformId, threadId | null, { limit })**: the newest lines, oldest first. Each line has its id, time, sender, whether a bot or this bot wrote it, its thread, and its text. The text is what an inbound message of that line would carry, including what the channel's `extractRawText` recovers. The bridge reads through the chat library's `history.thread.list` and `history.channel.listMessages`, and refuses a thread whose `channelIdFromThreadId` is not the chat named. Core checks whether the method exists, never a channel name.
  - A line also carries `raw`, the platform's own message. An inbound message's platform fields are read inside the bridge, by hooks the channel registers (`extractRawText`, `extractReplyContext`), and then dropped. A history line goes to host-side code instead, so `raw` lets that code read a platform-specific field itself. It never reaches the session (see the stored shape below).
- **registerWakeContext(name, provider)**: a provider gets `{ agentGroup, session, mg, wiring, created, trigger }` and returns blocks `{ key, tag, about, lines, state? }`.
  - **Budget**: all providers share one 1.5 s budget per waking session, because a person is waiting for the reply. A message that wakes two agents can wait twice. A block that misses the budget is written when it lands and rides with the next message.
  - **Isolation**: a provider that throws costs only its own blocks. While a provider's call for a session is running, later wakes of that session skip it.
  - **Once per message**: each block is one `session-echo` row with `trigger=0`, keyed by session, provider name, block key and message id. A redelivered message adds nothing.
  - **Stored shape**: core stores the block's fields and nothing else, so a field a provider adds (a line's `raw`, for example) never reaches the session. A malformed block or line is dropped on its own.
  - **Message order**: while a provider is registered, a session's messages are written in the order they arrived, so a message waiting for its context is not overtaken. A failed write, or any way out of delivery before the write, does not hold up the next message.
  - **Commands**: a slash command gets no context, because the runner runs a command only when nothing comes before it.
- **Context block**: the container renders `<tag about="...">` with one `<line sender time>` per line. `state` is never rendered: it stays on the row for the provider to read back at a later wake. The tag must match `^[a-z][a-z-]{0,39}$`: core drops any other, and the container never renders one as a block. Sender, text and `about` are escaped. One generic line in the agent's prompt explains `about`.
- **platformMessageId** (optional on `MailboxTimelineMessage` and `MailboxHistoryMessage`): read from `delivered`, so a provider can tell which messages a session already has. A mailbox implementation that omits it still compiles.

Precedent for a seam with no in-tree caller: `registerSessionCreatedHook` is already in main with no in-tree registrant. #3926 (an optional bridge hook) proposes the same shape.

</details>

## Related work

No issue. Builds on the cross-session context backfill: the backfill keeps the platform's id on the rows it seeds and is otherwise unchanged.

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/wake-context.test.ts`, through the real `routeInbound`, central DB and session mailboxes, with registered test providers:
  - nothing is written but the message when providers have nothing;
  - each block is one row before the message, in registration order;
  - a slow provider costs neither the message nor another block, its block follows, and it is not run again meanwhile;
  - a later message is written after an earlier one that is still waiting for its context, and a message that leaves before its write does not hold up the next;
  - only the block's fields are stored, and a malformed block or line costs only itself;
  - a slash command runs no provider;
  - two providers' blocks stay apart under one key;
  - a throwing provider costs only its own block;
  - a block is written once per message, and a tag that could carry markup is dropped.
- `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge-history.test.ts`: lines mapped through the real chat library, thread and top level. A line's text includes what the channel's raw-text extractor recovers. A thread of another chat is refused without a read.
- `src/mailbox/sqlite/sqlite.test.ts` and `src/modules/cross-session-context/backfill.test.ts`: the delivered id on both outbound reads, and on the rows the backfill seeds.
- Container: the block renders with escaped content and without `state`, and a block with a bad tag is never rendered as one.
- Every existing test passes unchanged: host `src` (2439) and container (682). `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, the container typecheck and `format:check` are clean.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

<!-- Maintainers own CHANGELOG.md — do not edit it in this PR. -->
- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

With nothing registered, exactly three things change for every install:
- rows the backfill seeds gain one field, `platformMessageId`, when the platform's id is known;
- `getTopLevelOutbound` and `getOutboundHistory` do one indexed lookup per row on `delivered`;
- the agent's prompt gains one line: "Any other tagged block carries an `about` attribute that says what it holds."

## Security and trust boundaries

- **What a provider can reach**: blocks are written only into the waking session, as context rows that never wake a container and are never fanned out. Core does not limit which chat a provider reads: a provider is host code and can name any chat to `readHistory`. The bridge refuses a thread that is not in the chat named.
- **What is stored**: only the block's fields. `raw` and any other field a provider adds never reach the session's database, which the agent can read.
- **Markup**: a block's tag is checked in core and in the container, and every value inside is escaped.
- **The wake**: providers share one budget, and a failing or hanging provider never holds the message past it. A later message never overtakes one that is waiting.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops recurring tasks from growing a session's `inbound.db` by one full copy of the task payload per run.

- **Problem**: every re-arm copies the full content (prompt + script) into the next occurrence, and finished occurrences are never trimmed. Size grows as payload × runs, without bound. On a real install, one 21 KB prompt on a `*/10` cron reached 238 MB over 11k runs.
- **Fix**: inside the existing `armNextTask` transaction, the content of the series' older finished occurrences (`completed`/`failed`, recurrence already cleared, `seq` below the new occurrence) is replaced with `{"superseded":true}`.
- **Why rows stay**: `getTaskStats` (runs, failed runs, last run) and `trailingFailedRuns` (script-failure auto-pause) count rows by status. Deleting rows would change both; replacing only the payload changes neither.
- **Why nothing notices**: once a later occurrence exists, every content reader resolves to the newest row of the series: `getTask`, `listLiveTasks`, `findTaskBySeriesSlug`, `updateTask` (future rows only), and the re-arm itself (it reads the just-completed row before compacting). Retries only touch `pending`/`processing` rows. `sessions history` already renders task rows as empty text, because task content has no `text` field.
- **Existing installs**: a series' backlog is compacted on its next re-arm. No migration is needed.
- **Out of scope**: reclaiming file size. SQLite reuses the freed pages, so the file stops growing. `VACUUM` is left to the operator.

<details><summary>Only observable difference</summary>

`ncl tasks get <id>` with the row id of a *superseded* occurrence (not the series id) now shows an empty prompt. The series id and the live occurrence still show the full content.
</details>

## Related work

No existing issue. Searched open and closed issues and PRs for inbound.db growth, retention, prune and recurring tasks. #3289 / #3291 are about the pending backlog, not finished rows.

Open PRs in the same area, all compatible:
- #3696 and #3741 add fields to task content. They read them from the just-completed row at re-arm time, or from the live row at spawn. Neither row is compacted.
- #2915 and #3247 touch the pre-`armNextTask` recurrence path.
- #3594 is container-side.

Happy to rebase whichever lands second.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/mailbox/sqlite/arm-next-task.test.ts` -> 7 passed. 5 are new:
  - a payload is kept once per series, and every row, `getTaskStats` and `trailingFailedRuns` are unchanged;
  - a cancelled series keeps its payload;
  - a pre-existing backlog is compacted on the next re-arm;
  - other series and non-task rows are untouched;
  - when the insert fails, the compaction rolls back with the pair.
- Same file without the one-line call in `armNextTask` -> the two compaction tests fail. The three guard tests still pass, as intended.
- `pnpm run build` -> ok.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 4242 passed, 1 skipped. The clean base had 4237 passed, 1 skipped, so the 5 new tests are the only change.
- Copy of the 238 MB production `inbound.db`, through `wrapSqliteInbound`:
  - stats identical before and after;
  - 203 MB of pages freed;
  - first re-arm 105 ms, which compacts 11k rows once;
  - steady-state re-arm 8 ms.
- Live install, same patch:
  - after the next sweep re-arm, all 11,072 finished rows of the series hold the marker;
  - the pending occurrence keeps its full 12 KB payload;
  - `ncl tasks get <series>` shows the full prompt and an unchanged `completed_runs`;

prs.title: fix(setup): ask the image question again after a failed sign-in
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

After a sign-in code expired, setup said "Re-run setup to get a fresh code", but a re-run never asked the hardened image question again.

- **Problem**: a sign-in that ended without approval (code expired, timed out, a service down) took the same path as a "no" and wrote `NANOCLAW_HARDENED_IMAGE=false`. Setup reads that as an answer, so the next run skipped the question.
- **Fix**: only a real "no" settles the question: No at the prompt, a decline in the browser, a cancel, or a perk the account is not offered. A sign-in, device registration or browser step that fails or runs out puts the `.env` line back as it was before the step. That includes the `true` a saved sign-in writes when a later part of the step fails.
- **Hints**: every "re-run" or "retry" hint now leads back to the question. A browser decline says how to undo it. The sign-in prints how long the code lasts.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - A broken self-hosted registry config (no browser sign-in, or unreachable) is asked again on every re-run until someone answers No.
  - Setup's own re-runs can ask again in the same install. fail()'s retry of the container step asks the question. A run past the container step, the sg-docker re-exec included, shows the Echo reminder once.

## Related work

Fixes #4426

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Fixes two OneCLI 1.45 doc gaps left after #4215: when an Allow overrides an Ask, and what an agent should do on `access_restricted`.

- **Overlap rule (`/add-onecli` SKILL.md)**: #4215 said only tools sharing one exact host, method and path override each other. But the gateway checks Allow tools first, and a pattern ending in `*` matches deeper paths, so an Allow tool lets through the requests of any Ask or Never tool it covers (GitHub `get_repo` on Allow: `list_issues` on Ask is never held). The section says so and points to the patterns (`permission-definition` shows only IDs).
- **Agent guidance (`onecli-gateway` container skill + `instructions.md`)**: agents were told to show `connect_url` and retry. On 1.45 a key saved through that link is attached to no agent, so the retry answers `access_restricted`. Agents now read the error code first, use `secret_url` for API keys, explain that an admin must attach the credential, and warn that the first retry may fail. `credential_not_found` now reads "nothing matched", since a saved key whose path pattern misses the URL answers it too.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The WhatsApp link step now treats `creds.json` as a link only when it holds a finished pairing (`account`), and says to clear `store/auth/` only for creds that parse without one.

- **Problem**: #4387 took any saved `me` as a finished pairing, but a requested code saves `me` too. So a close right after pairing said "before linking" and to clear a good link, and a rerun after an unused code said "already authenticated".
- **Fix**:
  - Paired = `account` in the saved creds (only a real pairing writes it), or `isNewLogin` on this connection.
  - After a close that follows pairing, the step waits up to 5 s for creds writes, then reads `creds.json` once: `account` → saved ("probably saved" if a write still runs); none → clear `store/auth/`; unreadable → rerun to check.
  - A rerun judges one read of `creds.json` (re-read for up to 1 s while it isn't valid JSON): `account` → skipped; other creds → "no linked device" (Baileys would log in as that `me`); still not JSON → stop the service, rerun; can't open → fix permissions.
  - SKILL.md matches each message.
- **Out of scope**: 401 and 408 closes.

## Related work

Follow-up to https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4387 (merged as d3384a9c5). No issue.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/whatsapp-auth.test.ts` → 29 pass, QR and pairing-code: reruns over an unused code or a cut-short, just-rewritten or unopenable `creds.json`; the 515 reconnect and closes around it; creds writes that fail, hang or still run.
- 18 fail on `main`'s source. Undoing any one part turns a test red, except chaining only the latest write (Baileys already orders writes, so that only adds log noise).
- `vitest run setup/` → 934 pass, 14 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` and Prettier clean.
- Existing links keep working: in Baileys 6.17.16, 7.0.0-rc.9 and rc14 only a finished pairing writes `account`, nothing removes it, and sending needs it.
- Live on macOS with real WhatsApp, no phone: the QR comes up; a forced old version gets a real 405 and "before linking". Via `setup/index.ts`: code-only `creds.json` → "no linked device", paired → skipped, cut-short → "not valid JSON" after 1 s, mode 000 → "could not be opened (EACCES)".
- A live, working install on Baileys 7.0.0-rc14 has `account` in its `creds.json`.
- Not run live: a new pairing, the 515 restart and closes after it (need a phone). The success path (`open`, and the reconnect after a 515) is the same code as on `main`.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Follow-up to #4358: peer cleanup should retire only the services setup wrote, and never delete a live one.

- **Problem**: since #4358, setup stops and deletes any `nanoclaw*` or `com.nanoclaw*` service that starts this checkout under another name, even a hand-written one. Dead-service cleanup reads only the unit file, so a unit changed with `systemctl edit` whose drop-in starts a live entry is deleted as dead, and its `.service.d/` is left behind (same on main).
- **Fix**: the same-checkout retire needs a name setup writes (`com.nanoclaw-v2-<slug>` or `nanoclaw-v2-<slug>`); on systemd, also no `<unit>.service.d/` and a loaded ExecStart that starts this checkout. A unit is dead only when every ExecStart in its file, its `*.conf` drop-ins and `systemctl --user show` names a missing entry, and it goes with its drop-in folder.
- **Out of scope**: units in `/etc/systemd/system`; with no user bus, drop-ins outside `<unit>.service.d/`.

## Related work

Follow-up to #4358. Covers the follow-up in [this review](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4362#pullrequestreview-5919760010).

- exe.dev VM with a real systemd user manager and drop-ins from `systemctl --user edit`; `setup --step service` on main, on `b31a08ea7` and on this head. Two units whose drop-ins start a live checkout (one in `/etc/systemd/user`) were deleted before and keep running now. Dead units with drop-ins now go with their folders. <!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Follow-up to #4341: the three points from its approving review, plus gaps found while reviewing this branch.

- **Owner cannot be kept**: a root-owned docker credential helper in a bin directory the user can write stayed stale, and the install at sign-in failed with EPERM (a regression from #4341). Both replace it again, as the user's own 0755 file. Other chown failures still stop the write; now tested.
- **Needless rewrite**: a helper that matches what setup would write, and can run, is no longer rewritten before every pull.
- **Linked source**: a helper linked to another checkout's `setup/registry/credential-helper.mjs` was rewritten at its target, a tracked file. The link is now replaced with a copy; the source is never written. A source is known by its first line or its place in a checkout, because `main` has written its header into such files since #4341.
- **Not executable**: a helper hard-linked to a 0644 source was replaced by one docker could not start. The old mode is kept and made runnable.

## Related work

prs.title: fix(add-onecli): fail setup when gateway readiness rejects
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Make OneCLI setup exit non-zero when its gateway readiness check fails.

- **Problem**: `run()` rejects after emitting `STATUS: failed`, but the shared logger handles unhandled rejections without setting a failing exit code. Setup can therefore exit 0 and let the skill driver continue.
- **Fix**: catch rejections at the OneCLI CLI entry point, log the error, and set `process.exitCode = 1`.
- **Coverage**: launch the real setup CLI against loopback fixtures for a 404, a dropped `/v1/health` connection, and a healthy gateway. The tests use a disposable HOME and a fake OneCLI CLI.

## Related work

Closes #4408.

#4303 changes the entry-point path guard and leaves `void run(...)` unchanged. This changes the invocation inside that guard; the adjacent edits may need coordination.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Against unchanged main at `c0ec12952e8d9a4ebbd869015010daac804d5d11`, `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/readiness.test.ts` -> 2 failed, 3 passed. Both failing gateways emitted `STATUS: failed` but exited 0.
- With this fix, the same file -> 5 passed. Failed readiness exits 1; healthy readiness exits 0.
- `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts setup/gateways setup/installer-shell.test.ts scripts/skill-apply.test.ts scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts scripts/skill-directives.test.ts scripts/skill-pins.test.ts` -> 639 passed in 18 files on Node 22.22.0 and Node 24.18.0, macOS, fresh clone.
- Host `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc` -> pass.
- Separate strict TypeScript check of `setup.ts` and `readiness.test.ts` -> pass; the root tsconfig does not include these files.
- Prettier on both changed files and `pnpm run format:check` -> pass.
- `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors, 209 warnings in unchanged `src/` files.
- `git diff --check` -> pass.
- Live OneCLI installation, Linux, and the full repository/container suites were not run. The CLI regression exercises reuse; the shared entry-point catch also handles rejected remote and fresh-install runs.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
OneCLI setup now exits with failure when the gateway readiness check fails, so setup cannot record a failed gateway check as a successful installation.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

No credential, permission, or network policy changes. The fix makes the process exit code reflect the readiness failure already reported by setup.
