releases.name: v2026.11.0-rc.1
releases.body:
NanoClaw 2026.11.0-rc.1 is the first release candidate of 2026.11.0: the build we expect to ship as stable unless testing finds a problem, so no more betas come before it. The November release takes the place of 2026.10.1, which never becomes a stable release; its two release candidates stay published, and everything they brought is in this entry. Installs on the `beta` channel get this release candidate; `stable` stays on 2026.10.0 until 2026.11.0 is published. Since 2026.11.0-beta.4, OneCLI installs give OneCLI's database its own password with one command (see below), groups that installed extra packages move to the new agent image on their own, setup asks the hardened-image question again after a sign-in that did not finish and names the real cause when Node or npm is broken, a long reply that fails part-way resumes at the part that failed instead of starting over, `/update-skills` refreshes `slack-agent-flow`, and agents no longer misread a OneCLI `access_restricted` error. Since 2026.11.0-beta.3, fetching the pre-built image works again after a Node upgrade, the WhatsApp link step stops at once when WhatsApp refuses the connection and tells a finished pairing from a requested code, setup keeps using the Node version it checked, Claude agents start fresh when their saved conversation is gone, and a long Slack reply cut through an emoji now posts. Since 2026.11.0-beta.2, gateway approval cards mark anything they shorten, an approval card changes only after NanoClaw accepts the click, long Slack replies are sent as several messages, and installs that set `NANOCLAW_INSTALL_ID` use it in the shell scripts and the installed service. Since 2026.11.0-beta.1, locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2, `/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops on a lockfile conflict at the first update of a default install, setup installs jq when it's missing so channel setup works on WSL and minimal Ubuntu images, setup restarts NanoClaw after it installs a provider, mention-sticky threads no longer wake the agent for chatter it was never mentioned in, answered question cards keep their question text on every channel, and setup warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine. Since 2026.10.1-rc.2, a stuck channel send no longer silences a conversation, agents can put KPI fields, a table and charts in cards, setup on Linux and WSL asks for your password in the open before it installs Node or Docker, setup on Linux reaches Docker right after it adds you to the docker group, setup names the NanoClaw account a machine is signed in to and lets you switch it, Discord server messages that @mention someone reach the agent, agent reactions reach Telegram, Mattermost recovers by itself from a short outage at startup, the OneCLI upgrade guide deletes the Dial key only when it has to, and locally built agent images clear every known High and Critical advisory that had a fix. Since 2026.10.0 it moves OneCLI to 1.45, where new agent groups get only their model key and other keys go to the groups you choose, makes the webhook server listen only on this machine by default, applies egress lockdown to agents that were already running, asks for Node's October 2026 security releases, and lets Claude agents read PDFs; Google Chat now checks that its webhooks come from your app. It also lets agents create other agents from templates, adds Cursor as an agent provider, and moves locally built agent images to Claude Code 2.1.321 with Claude Haiku 5.5. Eight changes need action from some installs, among them the OneCLI upgrade, the OneCLI database password, the webhook address and two new Google Chat settings, so check the section below before you update.

### ⚠️ Before you update

- [BREAKING] **Chat SDK channels move to adapter 4.41.1, which fixes Telegram messages with links that were never delivered.** Affected: installs where `grep -o '"@chat-adapter/[a-z]*"' package.json` prints anything (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, GitHub, Linear). Fix: `/update-nanoclaw` refreshes installed channels; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one. Google Chat: @mentions in spaces now need `GOOGLE_CHAT_BOT_USER_ID=users/<id>` in `.env` (DMs work without it; without it the log says "Google Chat botUserId is not configured" at startup): once the app has replied to you in a DM, list that DM's messages with the Chat API (`spaces.messages.list`), copy the `sender.name` of a message whose sender `type` is `BOT`, and restart the service. Slack agent-to-agent rooms: a sibling bot now arrives as `slack:bot:U…` instead of `slack:bot:B…`, so approve each sibling bot once more. Check: each channel answers a test message. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>` ([rolling back](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading#rolling-back)).
- [BREAKING] **Iron Proxy installs that connected Codex with ChatGPT before this release must sign in to Codex again.** Detect, from the NanoClaw folder (works while the service is stopped): `f=data/session-materials/iron-control/codex.json; [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '"mode":"chatgpt"' "$f" && ! grep -q '"accountId"' "$f" && echo affected`. Once running, an affected install's Codex agents answer only with the failure notice ("Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer") and the agent container log shows `selected workspace missing from routing discovery`. Why: Codex 0.156 and later check the login's workspace id, and older Iron logins never recorded it. Fix: `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`, then check that a Codex agent answers. OneCLI installs are affected only when the vault holds several ChatGPT logins or one without a recorded id; the host log then says "OneCLI login stand-in keeps its placeholder account id": delete the extra or stale login (`onecli secrets list`, then `onecli secrets delete --id <id>`), run the same command, and grant the new secret to each agent that had the old one, as `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install describes. Rollback: return to the previous release.
- [BREAKING] **Forks and hand-made templates: the template code moved and `templates/` is now ignored by git.** Affected: fork code that imports `cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate` or `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` from `setup/templates.ts` (it stops compiling), forks that edit the `GROUP_SCOPE_RESOURCES` line or the stamper's `ensureContainerConfig` line, forks that point setup at their own template library, and anyone who keeps a hand-made template in `templates/`. Why: templates fetched by setup or by an agent are install state and must not block `/update-nanoclaw`, and setup now lists a library from its `index.json`. Fix: import `cloneRegistry` and `listTemplatesFromDir` from `src/templates/library.ts` and `await cloneRegistry()`; `copyTemplate` is gone, so call `ensureTemplateLocal`; a fork that changed `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` edits `LIBRARY_REPO` (`owner/repo`) and `LIBRARY_BRANCH` in `src/templates/library.ts` instead; re-anchor fork edits on the new lines; keep a new hand-made template in git with `git add -f templates/<ref>`; give your own library an `index.json` at its root in the same shape as `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates` (`{ "schema": 1, "categories": { "<category>": [{ "ref": "<folder>", "name": "...", "description": "..." }] } }`). Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and setup's library picker lists your templates ([building templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/building)). Rollback: revert this release; fetched templates then show as untracked in `git status`, so delete them or `git add` the ones to keep.
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: upgrade the gateway to 1.45.0 and the `onecli` CLI to 2.11.0, where agents get only the keys you grant them.** Detect: the gateway's `/api/health` reports a version older than 1.45.0, or `unknown` (Iron Proxy installs skip this). Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs, so do not skip past it. Fix: before restarting, follow `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install ([the same guide on GitHub](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-onecli/payload/docs/onecli-upgrades.md)); it backs up the gateway database, stops if the conversion would delete your rules, and covers the CLI binary. If you use `/add-dial-tool`, run the guide's Dial check before you pull; it deletes the Dial key only when the upgrade could hand it to agents you kept away from Dial (see the Dial item below). Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential, and on a 1.42 gateway new groups still get every key until you upgrade. To give a group a tool, re-run that tool's skill (for example `/add-vercel`) and pick the group; with `/add-tavily-tool`, re-run its Phase 5 so paid-key upgrades attach the key. `/add-vercel`, `/add-tavily-tool` and `/add-dial-tool` refuse a gateway that is not 1.45. If your Claude key in OneCLI is not named `Anthropic` (or your Codex key `Codex` or `openai`), new groups get no key: run that provider's login again after upgrading (`pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step gateway-auth claude`, or `codex`). Check: `/api/health` reports 1.45.0 and a new agent group answers. Rollback: restore the database backup the guide takes.
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: give OneCLI's database its own password. `/update-nanoclaw` does not do this for you.** Detect: `[ -f ~/.onecli/docker-compose.yml ] && { ! grep -q '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.' ~/.onecli/.env 2>/dev/null || grep -Eqx "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=[\"']?(onecli)?[\"']?[[:space:]]*" ~/.onecli/.env; } && echo affected`. Remote gateways and Iron Proxy installs are not affected. Why: OneCLI's database still used the fixed default password from OneCLI's compose file. Fix, from the NanoClaw folder: `pnpm exec tsx .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/postgres-password.ts`. It saves a random password in `~/.onecli/.env`, sets it on the database and restarts OneCLI once; your data stays. If it prints "Not changed", fix what it names (usually a setting to save in `~/.onecli/.env`) and run it again. Check: a second run prints "OneCLI's database already has its own password", and once the update has finished, an agent answers. Rollback: none needed; the previous release keeps working with the new password.
- [BREAKING] **The webhook server now listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.** Tunnels and reverse proxies on the same machine keep working. Affected: a proxy on another machine, or anything in Docker on Linux that calls back to the host, such as a Mattermost server; webhooks stop arriving, and the log shows `Webhook server started host="127.0.0.1"`. Fix: set `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0` (or one interface's IP address; a name such as `localhost` stops the host at startup) in `.env` and restart. Check: a message on that channel gets an answer. Rollback: the same setting restores the old behavior.
- [BREAKING] **Google Chat installs need two new settings, or the channel does not start.** Google Chat now verifies that webhooks come from your Workspace add-on Chat app, using `GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL` and `GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER` (digits) in `.env`; `/update-nanoclaw` brings the new adapter but cannot ask for them. Detect: the log says "Google Chat needs GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL and GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER (digits) in .env to verify webhooks". Fix: re-run `/add-gchat`, which keeps your existing values and asks for the endpoint URL, the project number and the bot user id for @mentions in spaces, or set both values by hand and restart. The Chat app must be a Google Workspace add-on, and converting an app to one cannot be undone. Check: a test message gets an answer. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>`.
- [BREAKING] **Custom skills and forks: a card's response handler must say what the click did.** Affected: your own skill or fork code that registers a response handler for card clicks, or that calls `finalizeReject` with a reason. Detect: a response handler that returns `true` still compiles, but its card no longer changes and the host logs `legacy_true`; a `finalizeReject` call with a 4th string argument no longer compiles. Why: a card may show only what the host decided. Fix: return `'accepted'`, `'refused'`, `'closed'` or `'ignored'` (or `false` to pass the click on), and pass a reject reason as `finalizeReject(approval, session, userId, { reason })`. Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and a clicked card changes. Rollback: return to the previous release; handlers that return `true` then redraw as before.
- **`/add-dial-tool` users: run the upgrade guide's Dial check before upgrading OneCLI.** It reads only, and says `delete` only when the gateway has not converted yet (1.43 or older) and the upgrade could remove what keeps agents away from Dial, such as `Dial: blocked agents`, or when it cannot read all the rules that decide; a gateway already on 1.44 or later keeps its Dial key and its grants. When it says `delete`, the guide's `--delete` command removes the key; re-run `/add-dial-tool` after the upgrade, which gives the Dial key only to the agent groups you choose, and new groups get Dial only when you add them. NanoClaw's `ONECLI_PROJECT_ID` and the `onecli` CLI's project (`onecli config set project`, or `ONECLI_PROJECT`) must match or both be unset: when they differ, the re-run stops and writes nothing to OneCLI. An agent group name with a line break no longer changes which groups keep Dial.
- **Update Node to its October 2026 security release.** Setup now requires Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 or newer and refuses the end-of-life 23 and 25; locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.5 (Node's November 2026 security release), pinned by digest, and hardened installs get it with a later image. NanoClaw keeps running on an older Node; re-running setup picks a Node that meets the minimum, and stops only when it finds none. After `/update-nanoclaw`, run `bash setup/install-node.sh`, then re-run `bash nanoclaw.sh` so the service uses the new Node. If Node comes from nvm, fnm, volta or asdf, update it there.
- **Egress lockdown now covers agents that were already running when it was turned on**: they restart on the locked network when the host restarts. If the lockdown network exists but is not internal (only a network made by hand, or a setting that points at an ordinary one), agents no longer start and the host log says "Refusing to spawn with open egress". Fix: list what is attached with `docker network inspect nanoclaw-egress`, detach it (`docker network disconnect nanoclaw-egress <container>`), then `docker network rm nanoclaw-egress`; the next agent start recreates it as internal. Iron Proxy installs name it `nanoclaw-egress-<slug>`, and `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_NETWORK` can set another name.
- **Locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, where Claude Haiku 5.5 replaces Haiku 4.5.** They are the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2. On the Anthropic API, Claude Code's background requests and groups set to `haiku` move to Haiku 5.5, which costs a tenth of Haiku 4.5's price for prompts up to 100K tokens. Hardened installs keep Claude Code 2.1.280 and Haiku 4.5 until an image for this release is listed.
- **Hardened installs move to the image built from v2026.10.0.** A pull now takes the image listed in `agent-images.json` on `main` for the newest release in the install's history, so a new hardened image reaches installs without a new release. Betas and release candidates never get an image of their own, so this release candidate uses v2026.10.0's (Claude Code 2.1.280, newer than the old pinned build), and the pull's "agent-runner lock drift" warning is expected. `main` lists a newer build of that image, made on 2026-11-14, so `/update-nanoclaw` pulls it again. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step registry -- --refresh` to move onto it ([hardened runtime](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/guides/echo-hardened-runtime)).
- **Codex groups with no model set start new threads on GPT-6.1 Sol.** `/add-codex` now pins `@openai/codex` 0.162.1; existing threads keep their model. To stay on the old one, run `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --model gpt-6-astra`, then `ncl groups restart --id <group-id>`.

### ✨ New

- **Agents can create other agents from templates.** Ask for one in chat, pick from `ncl templates list` or the public library, and the agent builds it. Setup's template library list now shows what each template does ([using templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/using-templates)).
- **Cursor is an agent provider.** The new `/add-cursor` skill runs Cursor's Agent SDK, and setup offers Cursor in the provider picker; it needs a locally built agent image ([providers](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/extend/providers)).
- **Setup waits for a slow first reply instead of failing.** The first-chat check waits 2 minutes, then asks whether to keep waiting, and shows each stage (sandbox, agent runtime, model) with its time, so local models that take minutes to load no longer fail setup. Runs without a terminal now stop after 2 minutes instead of 30 seconds.
- **Agents on slow local models are no longer cut off mid-turn.** Raise `NANOCLAW_ABSOLUTE_CEILING_MS` (default 30 minutes) or `NANOCLAW_CLAIM_STUCK_MS` (default 60 seconds) in `.env`; the host log names which one fired. Restart the service after a change; installs that set neither are unaffected ([environment variables](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/reference/environment-variables)).
- **Agents can put KPI fields, a table and charts in a `send_card` card.** Slack draws them natively and Teams shows a chart as a table; WhatsApp Cloud doesn't show tables or charts yet, and Mattermost doesn't show charts, so agents put those numbers in text there. The linked-device WhatsApp channel (`/add-whatsapp`) doesn't show cards at all. A card's whole text, title and description included, may be up to about 12,000 characters; `send_card` refuses a longer card with the reason, so the agent can send a smaller one. Channels have lower limits of their own, such as 4,096 characters for a whole card on Telegram, and 150 for the title and 3,000 for the description on Slack; a card over them can be cut off or not posted.
- **Early test builds are now called betas.** They are tagged `vX.Y.Z-beta.N`, and `-rc.N` (release candidate) is kept for the last build or two before a release. The `beta` channel offers the newest beta or release candidate that is newer than stable, and `stable` never offers either. `/update-nanoclaw` reads this rule from `main`, so beta installs on 2026.10.1-rc.2 get this release candidate as they are.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **Setup tells you when your assistant's first reply failed.** Instead of saying the assistant is ready (for example after a bad API key), it shows the agent's error, names the log files and links the troubleshooting docs; `pnpm run chat` exits with code 4 on a failure notice. When an agent has no error of its own to share, every channel's failure notice now reads "Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer" and links the troubleshooting docs.
- **Setup on Linux and WSL asks for your password up front.** It asks in the open, right before it installs Node or Docker, instead of hiding the sudo prompt behind the progress spinner. On WSL, the docker-group message now tells you to run `wsl --shutdown`.
- **Setup on Linux reaches Docker right after it adds you to the docker group.** The service kept the groups it started with, so it could not open Docker and kept restarting; setup's workaround needs the `acl` package, which stock and minimal Ubuntu lack. Setup now installs `acl` on apt systems, gives your user access to Docker until Docker restarts, and starts the service without a crash wait; a reboot (or `wsl --shutdown` on WSL) makes it last. If it still can't reach Docker, setup prints the commands to run.
- **Setup names the NanoClaw account this machine is signed in to.** At the hardened image and managed Slack steps it asks "Continue as <email>" or "Use a different account", so switching no longer means deleting `account.json`. A first sign-in prints a short code in the terminal: approve only if the sign-in page shows the same code.
- **Setup asks about the hardened image again after a sign-in that did not finish.** If the sign-in code expired or a service was down, setup used to save "build locally" and never ask again, even though it told you to re-run. Now only a real "no" is saved.
- **Channel setup works on WSL and minimal Ubuntu images.** Setup now installs jq when it's missing, so Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup work there. Slack and Discord setup now stop when the API reply has no id, instead of saving an empty one.
- **Setup restarts NanoClaw after it installs a provider.** `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth <provider>` now restarts NanoClaw after installing a provider, so Codex, Cursor and OpenCode work without a manual host restart. The restart runs before sign-in, so an OpenCode install or re-auth that sets a new endpoint needs one more `bash setup/lib/restart.sh`.
- **Setup warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine.** They would never reply, so setup prints the `GATEWAY_BASE_URL` line to set.
- **Agents no longer lose or repeat a reply around `send_message`.** An agent that sent something with `send_message` and then left its answer unwrapped is shown what it already sent and asked to finish, and an exact repeat is not sent twice. On streaming providers, a reply sent with `send_message` and followed by plain closing text costs one extra model turn.
- **Agents reply in the language of the message they are answering**, unless you ask for another one. They no longer pick a language from earlier history, other people's messages or the timezone.
- **A stuck channel no longer silences agents.** NanoClaw stops waiting on a send after 60 seconds, logs `Message delivery passed its deadline`, and keeps delivering that conversation's later replies until 3 of its sends are stuck at once; chats wired to share one session (`agent-shared`) count as one conversation. A stuck message is retried if its send fails, and marked failed if there is still no answer an hour later. Other conversations keep going while up to 8 are stuck; with more, their replies can wait a minute or more.
- **Fewer failed agent runs.** On Docker Desktop, a message that arrives while an agent is replying no longer fails the run, and "Permission denied" replies to admin-only commands are sent directly to the chat. On every install, `ncl` and agent tools no longer hit intermittent "database is locked" errors.
- **Mention-sticky threads no longer wake the agent for chatter it was never mentioned in.** A thread keeps going without a mention only after the agent was woken there. A message sent while the thread's first mention is still in its admin-command check (such as `/clear`) no longer wakes the agent: it is dropped under `ignored_message_policy='drop'` (the default) and kept as context under `'accumulate'`. The gap is near zero unless the role lookup is slow, as with a remote database.
- **Approval cards appear where you are waiting and are easier to read.** When an agent in a thread of your own DM asks for approval, the card and its "Reject with reason" prompt appear in that thread. Cards show command arguments and agent-to-agent messages in a code block, and names and the install reason quoted on one line. An approval an agent asks for, or an `ask_user_question`, whose title and question together run over 2,000 characters is refused, and the agent is told the limit so it can shorten it; `ask_user_question` also returns an error within seconds of the host giving up on delivering its card, instead of waiting out its 300-second timeout.
- **Answered question cards keep their question text** on every channel, not just Discord.
- **Gateway approval cards show the action in the card text and mark anything they shorten.** Card text is no longer cut at a fixed length: a shortened value ends with "… N more characters not shown", and left-out details are counted. Card text shows as typed on Slack, Google Chat and Discord. On Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud a card too long to show whole is refused instead of cut: nothing is approved, and the approver is told the request was not shown. `/update-nanoclaw` brings the channel side; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one.
- **An approval card changes only after NanoClaw accepts the click.** A click from someone who can't answer the card leaves its buttons in place. WhatsApp, iMessage and the local web chat confirm an answer only after it is accepted; a refused answer leaves the question open. On Discord, clicks on cards from a durable approval gateway are now recorded (they were ignored), a stalled click acknowledgement no longer holds later events in its channel, and a decided gateway approval card no longer keeps its buttons. `/update-nanoclaw` brings the channel side; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one.
- **The background service finds the tools it was installed with.** On macOS it now includes `/opt/homebrew/bin` and the Node.js folder, so Apple Silicon installs using Homebrew or Apple Container no longer crash at start; on Linux it includes the Node.js folder (for example from nvm). Existing installs get it by running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step service` once.
- **Installs that set `NANOCLAW_INSTALL_ID` now use it in the shell scripts and the installed service.** The shell scripts (image build and pull, restart, skill steps) and the launchd or systemd service that setup installs use the id, and an invalid value stops them with a clear error. On Linux without systemd, `start-nanoclaw.sh` keeps the id too, and re-running setup with a new id replaces the checkout's old service instead of leaving it running. It retires only a service with a name setup writes (`nanoclaw-v2-…`) that starts this checkout and has no `systemctl edit` drop-in, or a service whose program no longer exists. Any other `nanoclaw*` service is left alone. An existing install gets the id into its service and `start-nanoclaw.sh` by running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step service` once.
- **`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops at its validate step on installs with Slack.** The skill refresh now credits each channel import to the skill that adds it, so it stops looking for Slack skills that don't exist. The fix comes with the update itself.
- **When `/update-nanoclaw` cannot refresh an installed skill, the error names each failed skill** and its error, instead of a generic message.
- **`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops on a lockfile conflict at the first update of a default install.** It now regenerates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the agent-runner `bun.lock` when they are the only merge conflicts. After a manual merge, take the new lockfile and run `pnpm install --lockfile-only` (for `bun.lock`, `bun install --lockfile-only` in `container/agent-runner`).
- **Discord: Approve on an approval card now approves.** Button clicks were misread, so approvals were recorded as rejections and answers to questions came back garbled.
- **Discord: server messages that @mention someone reach the agent.** Chat SDK adapter 4.41.1 dropped every server message with an @mention, including ones that mention the bot; `/add-discord` and `/update-nanoclaw` now apply a patch with the upstream fix. After a manual merge, rerun `/add-discord`.
- **Agent reactions reach Telegram and other Chat SDK channels.** They failed with "message to react not found" and were dropped after three tries.
- **Errors the Chat SDK hits while handling an incoming message show in the NanoClaw log** instead of being dropped silently.
- **Mattermost recovers by itself from a short outage at startup.** When the server, or a proxy in front of it, is unreachable or answers with a server error, it tries 3 more times, waiting 2, 5 and then 10 seconds, instead of staying offline until NanoClaw is restarted; after a longer outage, restart NanoClaw once the server is back. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-mattermost`.
- **Slack: long replies are sent as several messages instead of failing.** Slack refuses a message over 12,000 characters, so a reply over 10,000 is now split. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-slack`.
- **Fetching the pre-built sandbox image works again after a Node upgrade.** It failed with "error getting credentials" once Node was upgraded or replaced. The docker credential helper now finds Node on its own, and setup and `/update-nanoclaw` rewrite a helper from an older version.
- **The WhatsApp link step gives a clear answer.** When WhatsApp refuses the connection, the step stops at once, shows the reason and asks you to clear `store/auth/` and try again, instead of waiting two minutes and reporting a timeout. It also tells a finished pairing from a requested pairing code: a rerun after an unused code no longer says "already authenticated", and when the connection drops right after pairing, the step says whether the link was saved and asks you to clear `store/auth/` only when it was not.
- **Setup keeps using the Node version it checked.** An older Node in `~/.local/bin` or npm's global folder can no longer take over `pnpm install` or the background service. When the Node on PATH cannot start or npm is broken, setup names the real cause instead of ending without a message or saying it needs root, and `migrate-v2.sh` finds the pnpm that setup put in `~/.local/bin`.
- **Claude agents start fresh when their saved conversation is gone.** When Claude Code has deleted a chat's saved conversation (after 30 idle days by default), the next message gets a normal reply from a new session, instead of a "No conversation found with session ID" error and a lost message.
- **Long replies sent in parts resume at the part that failed.** A retry, even after a restart, picks up after the parts NanoClaw recorded as posted instead of starting over, and a cut no longer splits a single emoji character (on Slack, that stopped the rest of the reply from posting). An emoji built from several characters, such as a flag or a skin tone, can still be split between parts, but each part posts.
- **`ncl groups restart --id <other group>` restarts that group.** Run by a global-scope agent, it restarted the agent's own session instead.
- **Setup's verify step says why a background Slack install failed**, and passes again once a later Slack setup has connected and wired a chat.
- **Discord and Matrix: updates and re-runs apply the adapter patch.** `/update-nanoclaw` no longer fails on a Discord install older than adapter 4.41.1, and re-running `/add-discord` or `/add-matrix` on an existing install now applies the adapter patch.
- **`/update-skills` refreshes an installed `slack-agent-flow`**, and re-applying a skill adds the lines an append block gained since the install.
- **Discord: an approval card that times out or closes with nobody clicking no longer keeps its buttons.** `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-discord`.
- **Mattermost: a connection that never finishes opening no longer hangs.** If the server accepts the connection but never finishes the WebSocket upgrade, the adapter gives up after 10 seconds and retries, instead of hanging until NanoClaw restarts. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-mattermost`.
- **WhatsApp: a voice note is marked as a voice note**, not as an audio file, so the agent can tell the two apart. The file itself still does not reach the agent, as with all WhatsApp media; a fix is in review. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-whatsapp`.
- **Stopping an agent container no longer logs a false "session realization failed: unknown"** while Docker is still finishing its own removal. A session network that can't be removed keeps the session's claim and is retried, instead of leaking silently.
- **Clearer logs.** Idle containers stopped after 30 minutes log at info, not warn, so the warning log shows only stops that interrupt a message, and a failed container stop logs Docker's own error. GitHub, Linear and Resend log a warning when a message that waited behind a busy conversation is skipped or expires.
- **A refused portal connection is logged right away.** On Node 22 the host waited 10 seconds and logged `handshake_timeout`. It now logs `dial_failed` at once and retries on its normal schedule.
- **The OneCLI docs match OneCLI 1.45.** `/add-onecli` explains what OneCLI 1.45 can allow, ask or block per agent, and the templates guide no longer promises automatic key injection or approval holds on host, method and path. When OneCLI answers `access_restricted`, agents no longer retry a connect link or say the key is stored: they ask an admin to check that the app is connected (another Google app on the same host can cause the error), then connect, attach or reconnect it. `/add-onecli` warns that an Allow tool can let through requests of an Ask tool it covers.
- **Claude agents can read long PDFs you send them.** Installs that build their own agent image get it from the image rebuild in `/update-nanoclaw`. Hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Groups that installed extra packages move to the new agent image on their own.** After `/update-nanoclaw` or an image rebuild, NanoClaw rebuilds their image in the background when it starts or when the group next runs, and the group's next container uses it, so `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild` is no longer needed after an update. If you built a group's image by hand under the group's own tag, give it your own tag and pin that with `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --image-tag <tag>`, because NanoClaw now rebuilds the group's own tag.
- **Google Chat attachments reach the agent.** On channels whose message ids contain `/`, such as Google Chat, files were dropped and the agent saw only the file name. When someone shares a file from Google Drive, the agent now says it can't open Drive files and asks for the file to be pasted or dragged into the chat.
- **Resend email replies are sent.** Agent replies and the "Connect yourself" hello failed with `Invalid thread ID format`; they now go out, and a reply lands in the email thread the person last wrote in. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`.
- **Installing extra packages for an agent works when NanoClaw lives in a folder whose name has a space.** Setup and uninstall now stop only this install's own host process.
- **Smaller fixes.** An agent reads its own replies from other threads of the same chat as its own, not as another agent's; `ncl groups delete` also removes the group's host bookkeeping rows, and agents that could message it stop listing it right away; creating an agent from a template no longer fails when an agent that has not run yet holds that name; a Slack bot set up for channels only no longer sends you an FYI each time it turns away a DM; `ncl messaging-groups delete` also removes the group's wirings, its own sessions and pending approvals instead of failing with a foreign key error, and removing iMessage uses it; creating an agent refuses a name whose group folder would be invalid (too long, or reserved such as "Global") before anything is written, and says why; setup accepts Anthropic's newer API key types (`sk-ant-usr`, `sk-ant-svc`), which must be scoped to one workspace; Linux Signal setup installs signal-cli 0.14.9, which fixes sends to new contacts hanging (rerun `setup/install-signal-cli.sh`, then restart the service); when `ncl` can't reach the host, it also shows the restart command for Linux without systemd (for example WSL); and the `/add-dashboard` dashboard keeps updating when a transcript grows past about 512 MB and no longer re-reads every transcript each minute (rerun `/add-dashboard` to get it).

### 🔒 Security

- **`/add-resend` installs a Resend adapter with no known advisories.** The pin moves from 0.1.1 (4 moderate findings through `uuid`) to 0.3.0, and `/update-nanoclaw` moves existing email installs to it (after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`). The webhook now answers before the message is processed, so a message that fails is not retried, and replies are sent as HTML with a plain-text part that drops link targets.
- **Signal setup checks the signal-cli download's sha256** before installing it.
- **OneCLI setup keeps keys off the command line.** Setup now gives keys to the `onecli` CLI through a private temporary file or stdin, and hides them in error messages. If setup ever failed while saving your Anthropic key or OneCLI API key, rotate that key and delete the old files in `logs/setup-steps/` and `logs/setup.log`.
- **Dial setup no longer leaves the account token readable by other users on the machine** while it pins the default sender number.
- **Registry sign-in opens your browser only for a plain https link**, and says so when it starts no browser. On WSL without `wslview` or `xdg-open` it no longer tries `cmd.exe`; open the link it prints instead.
- **Text that task scripts and webhooks put in an agent's prompt can no longer pose as text NanoClaw wrote.** Script output, webhook bodies, task prompts and attachment types can no longer close the block they sit in.
- **Locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.5, Node's November 2026 security release.** `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image. Setup's minimum Node stays the same.
- **Approval cards on Google Chat and Discord show request text as typed.** On Google Chat a card's own labels are bold, so a line of request text can't pose as one, and a line in an agent's message that starts like a label, such as `*Action:*`, stays as typed. On Discord, `*`, `_` and `~` in request text show as typed, so they can't turn code into links, mentions or spoilers. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-gchat` or `/add-discord`.
- **Locally built agent images move to Bun 1.4.4, which no longer trusts the revoked eMudhra certificates.** `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Locally built agent images clear every known High and Critical advisory that had a fix.** The image ships npm 11, pnpm 10.34.9, a fresh build of its Node base and updated agent-runner libraries. `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Re-applying a template to an agent (restamp) can no longer be pointed outside its group folder.** It refuses, with an error, to write a context file or skill through a folder in the group folder that was swapped for a link, and checks template file names more strictly. On a Mac this needs the NanoClaw folder on an APFS or HFS+ disk (the usual Mac disk); on other disks these writes are refused.
- **Hardened how the host opens files in agent folders.**

### 🔧 For custom installations

- **Custom container code that reads `inbound.db`** through `openInboundDb()` or `getInboundDb()` (`mailbox/sqlite/connection.ts`) must use `readInbound((db) => ...)`: `openInboundDb()` is gone, and `getInboundDb()` now works only in tests.
- **Custom mailbox stores that create storage on first write**: a new thread or conversation now gets its earlier context there. The default SQLite store was not affected.
- **`CLAUDE.md` matches the code again.** Coding agents get the right session folder and image tag, and know a group's `CLAUDE.md` is rewritten on every start: standing instructions go in `instructions.prepend.md`.
- **`/add-codex` ships its provider inside the skill**, so installs and forks no longer need the providers branch; on an older core its instructions tell you to update core first. Codex archives pick up core's header fix (the thread-id line no longer renders as a heading).
- **Provider skills can archive exchanges through core.** Use `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/exchange-archive.ts`; refreshing `/add-codex` deletes the old copy in `providers/exchange-archive.ts`, so a custom provider that imports it must switch.
- **Skills can add context when a message wakes an agent, without editing core.** Register a provider with `registerWakeContext` (`src/wake-context.ts`): blocks it returns within a shared 1.5-second budget are written before the waking message, as `<tag about="...">`, a later block rides with the next message, and a slash command gets none. Channel adapters gain an optional `readHistory` (the Chat SDK bridge has it), and the mailbox's outbound reads carry an optional `platformMessageId`. With nothing registered, routing works as before and the agent's prompt gains one line about the `about` attribute.
- **A gateway credential can target one exact path on a host.** The provider credential seam moves to version 2: a custom provider skill that requires exactly version 1 must accept 1 or later, a skill that sets `path` must require 2, and a custom gateway must declare `connectionPaths: true` to accept path-scoped credentials.
- **The agent image no longer installs `cron-parser`** or its `luxon` dependency (about 4.9 MB); scheduling still runs on the host. Custom container code that imported them must add them back.
- **Forks that pointed the `versions.json` agent-image pin at their own mirror** must move that reference to `NANOCLAW_AGENT_IMAGE_REF`, because the `agent-images.json` list now comes first.
- **Forks no longer run the agent-image refresh workflow**, which failed every 6 hours outside `nanocoai/nanoclaw`.
- **OpenCode: `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` and `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_COUNT` are gone**; they never took effect.
- **Forks: keep `@chat-adapter/discord` at 4.41.1.** A newer adapter needs a newer `chat` than core pins, so `pnpm run build` fails. If pnpm stops with `ERR_PNPM_UNUSED_PATCH`, run `pnpm add @chat-adapter/discord@4.41.1` or re-run `/add-discord`; to remove Discord, follow its `REMOVE.md`. `/add-discord`'s troubleshooting now gives the same fix, instead of keeping a newer adapter that doesn't build.

  • Core: Fix build crash when ref reachability check fails mid-request - #36181, thanks @​shilman!
  • Core: Restore the change-detection CTA in the sidebar - #36214, thanks @​ghengeveld!
  • TanStack: Support both interpolatePath signatures - #36333, thanks @​BaconMan1168!
  • Telemetry: One tools-command record per invocation with CLI toolset and tool names - #36210, thanks @​kasperpeulen!

v10.6.0

10.6.0

New skills architecture for agentic workflows

Storybook 10.6 contains hundreds of fixes and improvements:

  • 💻 CLI bindings for agent tools/skills

  • 🟢 Vue MCP/skills support and improved docgen/snippets (experimental)

  • ⚡ Improved performance and reduced bundle size
  • Addon MCP: Stop silently dropping composed refs from MCP composition - #36077, thanks @​kasperpeulen!
  • Addon Vitest: Pin storybook/test in optimizeDeps so its CJS-only deps are prebundled - #35572, thanks @​Nic-Polumeyv!
  • Addon Vitest: Report test runs with failures as failed tool outcomes - #36080, thanks @​kasperpeulen!
  • Addon Vitest: Resolve story test globs against the project root - #36103, thanks @​kasperpeulen!

  • Angular Vite: Resolve tsConfig against the workspace root - #36026, thanks @​ndelangen!
  • Angular-Vite: Run Compodoc on demand - #35776, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!
  • Angular: Add an in-process docgen analyzer, replacing Compodoc under the flag - #35805, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!
  • Angular: Bind only what the component accepts in story snippets, and report the rest - #35943, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!
  • Angular: Decide the migration's zone.js import from the dependency tree - #36008, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!
  • Angular: Declare story args the snippet markup binds by name - #35895, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!
  • Angular: Declare style preprocessors as optional peers and name the missing one - #36098, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!
  • Angular: Derive required inputs from Compodoc's own flag - #35758, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!
  • Angular: Extract Compodoc parsing into its own package - #35749, thanks @​valentinpalkovic!

prs.title: fix(artifacts): support CSV encodings and in-app Windows links
prs.body:
## Summary

修复 Windows 下 GBK CSV 中文预览乱码，以及正文中的 `C:/.../products.csv` 链接误调用系统打开方式的问题。现在正文链接进入应用内预览，CSV/TSV 支持自动识别和手动编码切换，预览不写回原文件。

## Related Issue

用户反馈：Windows 11 中相同内容的 GBK CSV 显示乱码，而 UTF-8 CSV 正常；暂无关联 issue 编号。

## Changes Made

- 严格按 BOM / UTF-8 解码，必要时尝试 GB18030；提供自动、UTF-8、GB18030（兼容 GBK）、UTF-16 LE/BE、Big5 选项及解码失败提示，保留编号前导零。
- 按会话和文件隔离编码选择，切换文件、编码或刷新时隐藏过期内容，阻止旧异步读取结果覆盖当前预览。

prs.title: fix(openclaw): skip async provider catalog builders when indexing max tokens
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclawModelCatalog` indexes model max tokens by calling every `build*Provider` export from the runtime's `provider-catalog.js` with `process.env`. OpenClaw's `buildHuggingfaceProvider` is `async` and expects an API key string, so `discoveryApiKey?.trim()` threw inside the async function. The resulting rejected promise escaped the synchronous `try/catch` and surfaced as an unhandled rejection (`TypeError: discoveryApiKey?.trim is not a function`), which fails the Vitest run even when all tests pass.

An async builder's promise never contributed to the index (it has no `.models`), so calling it only risked live-discovery network work and stray rejections.

## Changes
- Skip `AsyncFunction` builders before calling them.
- If a regular builder still returns a thenable, absorb its rejection and skip it.
- Regression test with a fake runtime: sync builder is indexed, async builder is never called, rejecting thenable builder produces no unhandled rejection. The test fails on the old code with the same `trim` error.

## Behavior
No change to indexed max tokens: async builder results were never indexed. No IPC, storage, or OpenClaw config changes.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test -- openclawModelCatalog openclawConfigSync` (224 passed, no unhandled errors)
- [x] `npm run compile:electron`
- [x] ESLint on touched files

prs.title: fix(openclaw): extend plugin archive extraction timeout on every platform
prs.body:
## Summary
Installing `@openclaw/discord@2026.8.1` fails on macOS with `extract tar timed out after 120000ms`. `ensure-openclaw-plugins` then stops, so every plugin after it (wecom, weixin, popo, nim, bee, email) is missing from the runtime.

## Root cause
The time goes into OpenClaw's `@openclaw/fs-safe` archive extraction, not the disk. For each file it re-runs `realpath`/`lstat` on every ancestor and fsyncs both the file and its directory. Measured on an Intel Mac (macOS 12) with the 5,774-file Discord archive:

| Extractor | Time |
|---|---|
| fs-safe 0.5.6 (pinned via OpenClaw 2026.8.1), native or JS path | ~146–153 s |
| fs-safe 0.28.1 (latest) | ~58 s |
| system `tar` | ~2 s |

The run made about 533k `realpath`, 751k `lstat`, and 11.5k fsync calls. The existing patch raised the default only on Windows (900 s) and left 120 s elsewhere. Upstream OpenClaw 2026.11.4 still defaults to 120 s on every platform, so this is not fixed upstream either.

## Changes
- `openclaw-plugin-archive-windows-timeout.patch`: `DEFAULT_PLUGIN_ARCHIVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 900_000` on every platform. The filename is unchanged to avoid renaming its references.
- `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs` strong-validation snippets and the patch test updated to match.
- `ensure-openclaw-plugins.cjs`: build wrapper timeout is 20 min on every platform (was 5 min outside Windows), so it stays above the runtime's 15 min archive budget and does not interrupt cleanup.

## Electron / runtime notes
- Affects packaged apps too: runtime plugin installs go through the same `installPluginFromArchive` default, so slower Macs installing large plugins will no longer hit the 120 s limit.
- Requires rebuilding the OpenClaw runtime (`npm run openclaw:runtime:host`) to take effect locally.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run openclaw:patch`: all 98 patches applied with strong validation
- [x] `npm run openclaw:runtime:host` on macOS x64: discord and all later plugins installed
- [x] `npm test -- openclawPatches ensure-openclaw-plugins` (130 passed)

prs.title: fix(artifact): restrict localfile protocol to sandboxed local media
prs.body: ## Summary Fixes #3096. The `localfile://` handler served any absolute path with any type. Tested on Electron 43, app pages and inline artifacts can display files through it but cannot read their bytes (CSP blocks `fetch`; the scheme is not CORS-enabled, so canvas reads are tainted). The real exposures were: - `.html` / `.svg` files were served as active documents with the `localfile://local` origin, whose script can `fetch` any file on disk. HTML file previews (served without CSP) could frame such a document. - On Windows, `localfile://local//host/share/a.png` resolved to a UNC path, so the main process would open an SMB share (NTLM credential leak). A fixed root allowlist does not fit: the scheme displays images and videos the user or agent references anywhere on disk (chat markdown, media artifacts, image editor). This PR restricts what the scheme serves instead: - Serve only image, video and audio extensions; documents and unknown types return 403. - Every response carries `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; ...` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so a framed or opened file gets an opaque origin with scripts off. `` / `

issues.title: [Feature]: Plugin-facing theme extension point (semantic token override layer)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Console theme system added in #7741 lets **users** pick a palette (6 built-ins) and customize accent / hover / background / surface / radius. But **plugins** still have exactly one theme knob: `window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.set(pluginId, { colorPrimary })`. Plugin authors who want deeper theming (backgrounds, glass / `backdrop-filter`, full palettes) have no official hook, so they end up injecting CSS.

Proposal (for discussion): add a **plugin-facing semantic token override layer**, built on QwenPaw's *own* semantic tokens rather than the upstream UI library's raw tokens — so plugins can theme deeply **without coupling to upstream upgrades**.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Problem / Motivation

1. **Plugin theming is one-dimensional today.** The plugin theme API only accepts `colorPrimary` (see `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` and `plugins/hostSdk/install.ts` → `themeFieldMap`). Everything else is unreachable from a plugin.
2. **The marketplace already proves both the demand and the fragility of the workaround.** Appearance plugins such as *QwenPaw Skin Studio*, *background-wallpaper*, and *No Glass (Flat UI)* all describe themselves as "pure frontend, zero-dependency" — i.e. they inject CSS and poke the DOM directly. That breaks whenever the Console's markup or styles change.
3. **Why not simply expose the upstream tokens?** Because `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` deliberately keeps the public surface stable *"across vendor upgrades"* — exposing the upstream UI library's raw tokens would couple every plugin theme to that library's token names. The layer worth opening is **QwenPaw's own semantic layer**, part of which already exists (see #7682).

## Proposed Solution

Two steps, in order:

1. **Own the layer.** Make the Console's theming go through **QwenPaw-owned semantic tokens** (semantic role names → mapped internally to whatever the underlying UI library expects). #7682 ("use semantic tokens in SettingsCenter") is already a step in this direction.
2. **Open the layer to plugins.** Add a plugin API to override those semantic tokens, with the same disposable / registration semantics as the rest of the plugin SDK, e.g.:

```js
const dispose = window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens("my-plugin", {
  "surface":         { light: "#ffffff", dark: "#1f1f1f" },
  "chat.background": { light: "#fafafa", dark: "#111111" },
  // ...any semantic token; both light & dark required, so an override
  // never goes illegible when the user flips the color scheme.
});
```

Because plugins override **QwenPaw's semantic names**, an upstream library upgrade only changes QwenPaw's internal mapping — plugin themes keep working. That removes the exact risk that motivates keeping the surface closed today.

Happy to start with a **minimal first cut** (e.g. the handful of tokens the Console already uses for surface / background / border / text) and grow from there, rather than a big-bang "full skin system".

## Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo — each plugin injects CSS.** Works, but fragile and duplicated; breaks on Console changes; no clean restore. (This is what marketplace appearance plugins do today.)
- **Expose the upstream UI library's raw tokens directly.** Rejected — couples plugins to upstream token names and contradicts the existing "do not expose vendor config" design intent.
- **Only widen the current scalar list** (accent / surface / radius / …). Helps a little, but still cannot reach backgrounds / glass / full palettes.

## Additional Context

- Related: #7741 (merged — 6 palettes + accent/hover/background/surface/radius), #7406, #5909, #6312 (superseded by #7741), #7287 (external frontend gateway — `not_planned`).
- **Reference design**: DeepSeek Harness ships exactly this — `ctx.theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)` plus a `ThemeDefinition` type (alias-token overrides, light + dark required), documented as *"Third-party themes can register alias-token overrides through `ctx.theme`."*
- Marketplace plugins currently working around this: `@osier-yi/qwenpaw-dream-skin`, `@levodoubt/background-wallpaper`, `@erickcharles/qwenpaw-no-glass`.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

---

### 中文摘要

Console 的主题系统（#7741）让**用户**能换 6 套预设、自定义 accent / 背景 / 表面 / 圆角；但**插件**目前只有一个主题接口 `chat.theme.set(id, { colorPrimary })`。插件想深度定制（背景、毛玻璃、整套配色）没有官方入口，只能注入 CSS —— 市场里的外观类插件（Skin Studio、背景壁纸、去玻璃化）都是这么干的，Console 一改版就失效。

建议：**在 QwenPaw 自己的语义 token 层上加一个面向插件的覆盖接口**（而不是暴露上游 `AgentScope Runtime WebUI` 的原始 token）—— 这样上游升级时插件主题不受影响（只需 QwenPaw 内部重新映射）。愿意在讨论通过后提 PR，可先做最小版本。

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub model gateway instantly fails for Anthropic/MiniMax presets — provider_headers() calls missing request_headers()
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (latest release). Also present on `main` @ 19363e6069fb (2026-11-13): `src/qwenpaw/hub/model_service/provider_setup.py` is unchanged.

## Description

In QwenPaw Hub, any organization-model connection that uses the built-in `anthropic`, `minimax`, or `minimax-cn` preset fails instantly. The admin **Test** button returns HTTP 502:

```json
{"error": {"message": "Invalid or incomplete response from the upstream model.", "code": "hub_upstream_error"}}
```

and the request ledger (`hub_model_requests`) records `error=upstream_failed` with created→completed deltas of only **10–50 ms** — the request never leaves the Hub process (a TLS handshake to the upstream alone takes ~140 ms).

**Root cause:** `hub/model_service/provider_setup.py::provider_headers()` unconditionally calls `preset.request_headers()`:

```python
def provider_headers(connection: dict) -> dict:
    preset = supported_presets().get(connection.get("provider_id"))
    return preset.request_headers() if preset is not None else {}
```

but `AnthropicProvider` and its subclass `MiniMaxProvider` do not implement `request_headers()`. Enumerating all 31 presets returned by `supported_presets()`, exactly three lack the method:

| provider_id | class | request_headers |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic | AnthropicProvider | missing |
| minimax | MiniMaxProvider | missing |
| minimax-cn | MiniMaxProvider | missing |

All other presets (OpenAI/OpenRouter-derived) implement it. The resulting `AttributeError` is swallowed by `ModelGateway.call`'s generic `except BaseException`, settled as `upstream_failed`, and surfaced as a generic 502 — so it looks like a network/provider outage even though the upstream is perfectly healthy.

**Related PR(s):** #7779 (feat(hub): add model gateway, member governance and usage dashboard) introduced this code path.

**Security considerations:** none (no credentials involved in the failure path).

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Linux x86_64 (fnOS NAS)
- **Install method:** venv (fnOS app package)
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run QwenPaw Hub 2.3.0 and sign in as admin.
2. In organization model management, create a connection using the `minimax-cn` preset (MiniMax China), base URL `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`, with a valid API key.
3. Publish a model on that connection (e.g. `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` or `MiniMax-M3`).
4. Click **Test** (`POST /api/hub/admin/models/{model_id}/test`).

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** instant 502 `hub_upstream_error` ("Invalid or incomplete response from the upstream model."). Every recorded attempt fails identically in 10–50 ms (34/34 over 5 days in our ledger). Same failure with the `anthropic` preset.
- **Expected:** the test succeeds. A direct `POST https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages` from the same host with the same key and model returns HTTP 200 in ~1.4 s (verified independently with curl and urllib; `MiniMax-M3` and `MiniMax-M2.7` also return 200).

## Logs / Screenshots

Raw traceback, captured by instrumenting `ModelGateway._prepare` (the gateway normally hides it behind the generic 502):

```
File ".../site-packages/qwenpaw/hub/model_service/gateway.py", line 169, in _prepare
    **provider_headers(connection),
File ".../site-packages/qwenpaw/hub/model_service/provider_setup.py", line 78, in provider_headers
    return preset.request_headers() if preset is not None else {}
File ".../site-packages/pydantic/main.py", line 1110, in __getattr__
    raise AttributeError(f'{type(self).__name__!r} object has no attribute {item!r}')
AttributeError: 'MiniMaxProvider' object has no attribute 'request_headers'
```

## Additional Notes

- **Suggested fix:** make `provider_headers()` defensive, e.g.
  ```python
  fn = getattr(preset, "request_headers", None)
  return fn() if callable(fn) else {}
  ```
  or implement `request_headers()` on the `Provider` base class / `AnthropicProvider` so all presets satisfy the contract.
- **Workaround:** create a *custom* connection without `provider_id` (protocol `anthropic`) with the same base URL and key — `provider_headers()` returns `{}` when no preset matches, bypassing the crash.
- Runtime-level (personal) MiniMax providers are **unaffected**; only the Hub model-gateway path is broken.
- Duplicate check: searched issues for `request_headers`, `MiniMaxProvider`, `provider_headers`, `upstream_failed`, `minimax hub`, `hub model failed` — no existing report of this bug. #7445 is a different problem (local/LAN URL reachability from containerized runtimes).

issues.title: [Bug]: Subagent completions incorrectly trigger the "Reply completion" desktop notification
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`). Also verified against `main` (`__version__ = "2.3.1b1"`) — `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py` is identical there, so the bug is not yet fixed upstream.

## Description

With Console → Notifications → "Reply completion" enabled, **a desktop notification ("The agent has finished a reply") is also fired every time a subagent finishes** — i.e. when the main agent calls `spawn_subagent`, `submit_to_agent`, or `chat_with_agent`.

The user only cares whether *their own* turn has finished. A subagent is an internal child task of the main agent; its completion should never produce a user-facing reminder.

When one task dispatches several subagents (especially with `batch` or `background=true`), the user receives multiple unrelated "The agent has finished a reply" notifications in quick succession — often while the main task is still running — which is misleading and looks like their request has already been answered.

**Related PR(s):** None

**Security considerations:** None (notification noise only; no auth, config, or credential exposure)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

> The event is published by the backend; the frontend only renders it. The root cause is backend-side, so only Core is checked. The `systemNotifications.conversation` toggle itself behaves correctly.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0
- **OS:** Linux (Docker container on a 6.6 kernel host)
- **Install method:** Docker (`agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In Console → Settings → Notifications, enable "Desktop notifications" and the "Reply completion" (`conversation`) category, and grant browser notification permission.
2. Send the main agent a task that makes it spawn a subagent, e.g.:
   - "Use `spawn_subagent` to count files in directories A, B and C separately, then summarize."
   - or let it call `submit_to_agent` / `chat_with_agent` to talk to another agent.
3. Keep the Console tab in the background (or minimized) and watch system notifications.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** One "The agent has finished a reply" notification per subagent completion. N subagents → N notifications, sometimes before the main task finishes. Also reproduces with `spawn_subagent(background=true)` and `batch` mode.
- **Expected:** The "Reply completion" notification should fire only when a turn **initiated directly by the user** completes. Subagent runs, background child tasks, and inter-agent internal calls must not trigger it.

## Logs / Screenshots

The notification is published unconditionally at the end of `stream_one()` in `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py` (~lines 545–556; identical in v2.3.0 and `main`):

```python
if (
    not err_msg
    and last_response is not None
    and last_response.status == RunStatus.Completed
    and session_id
):
    publish_notification(
        category=f"conversation",
        agent_id=getattr(self._workspace, f"agent_id", f"default"),
        title=f"QwenPaw",
        body=f"",
        session_id=notification_session_id,
    )
```

A comment in the same function states that `stream_one` is **the single executor for every path**:

> `stream_one is the single console executor for the web streaming, background-task, and terminal CLI paths`

Subagent requests travel through the very same path via `POST /console/chat` and `POST /console/chat/task`:

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py`
  - `stream_agent_chat()` / `collect_final_agent_chat_response()` → `POST /console/chat`
  - `submit_agent_chat_task()` → `POST /console/chat/task`

So a finished subagent also satisfies `status == RunStatus.Completed` and also reaches `publish_notification`.

## Additional Notes

### Root cause

1. `stream_one()` publishes the notification **without inspecting the request origin** — any completed response triggers it.
2. The codebase already has a way to identify subagents; this call site just doesn't use it:
   - `spawn_subagent` sets `_spawn_subagent: True` in `request_context` (`_build_spawn_request_context` in `agent_management.py`), with session ids shaped like `sub-xxxxxxxx`;
   - `_chat_registration_fields()` in `app/routers/console.py` uses it to tag the chat with `source: "subagent"`;
   - `services/session_thinking.py`, `app/approvals/service.py`, and `hooks/request_setup/contextvars_hook.py` all read the same flag.

### Suggested fix

Filter before publishing the `conversation` notification:

```python
request_context = getattr(request, "request_context", None) or {}
is_internal_call = (
    isinstance(request_context, dict)
    and request_context.get("_spawn_subagent") is True
)
if not err_msg and not is_internal_call and last_response is not None and ...:
    publish_notification(...)
```

### Coverage gap worth noting

Checking only `_spawn_subagent` is **incomplete**:

- `chat_with_agent()` / `submit_to_agent()` go through `build_agent_chat_request()`, whose `request_context` currently carries only `root_agent_id` — **no** `_spawn_subagent` — with session ids shaped like `{from}:to:{to}:{ts}:{uuid}`.
- Those paths would therefore still leak notifications. Either:
  - **(a)** add a shared internal-call flag (e.g. `_agent_internal: True`) in `build_agent_chat_request()` and check both, or
  - **(b)** additionally check the session-id prefix (`sub-` / `:to:`) at the publish site as a fallback.

### Related issues (not duplicates)

- #7107 [Feature]: System notification when a response or task completes while the Console/Desktop app is not focused — the feature this notification implements; this issue is an edge-case defect in that implementation.
- #5797 [Feature]: 定时任务结果弹窗提醒应加开关 — about a user-facing toggle for cron reminders; unrelated.
- #6084 Desktop 任务完成或审核请求的弹窗通知 — feature request; does not cover subagent filtering.

---

## 中文版（Chinese）

### QwenPaw 版本

2.3.0（Docker 镜像 `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`）；同时已核对 `main` 分支（`__version__ = "2.3.1b1"`）的 `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py`，问题代码一致，说明上游尚未修复。

### 描述

当 Console 的「桌面通知 → 回复完成（Reply completion）」开启后，**子智能体（`spawn_subagent` / `submit_to_agent` / `chat_with_agent`）完成任务时也会弹出「Agent 已完成一轮回复」的桌面通知**。

用户只关心自己发起的对话轮次是否完成。子智能体属于主智能体的内部子任务，其完成不应产生面向用户的提醒。

在一次主任务派发多个 subagent（尤其是 `batch` 或 `background=true`）时，用户会在短时间内连续收到多条互不相关的「Agent 已完成一轮回复」，实际到手时主任务往往还没结束，容易被误导为「我的请求已经答完了」。

**关联 PR：** 无

**安全影响：** 无（仅通知噪音，不涉及权限、配置或凭据暴露）

### 影响组件

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

> 说明：通知事件由后端发布、前端仅负责展示，根因在后端，故只勾 Core。前端 `systemNotifications.conversation` 开关本身行为正常。

### 环境

- **QwenPaw 版本：** 2.3.0
- **操作系统：** Linux（Docker 容器，宿主机内核 6.6）
- **安装方式：** Docker（`agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`）
- **Python 版本：** 3.11

### 复现步骤

1. 打开 Console → 设置 → 通知，开启「桌面通知」与「回复完成」（`conversation`）类别，并允许浏览器通知权限。
2. 向主智能体发送一个会让它调用子智能体的任务，例如：
   - 「用 `spawn_subagent` 分别统计 A、B、C 三个目录的文件数，再汇总」
   - 或直接让它 `submit_to_agent` / `chat_with_agent` 与其他智能体通信
3. 保持 Console 页面在后台（或最小化），观察系统通知。

### 实际 vs 预期

- **实际：** 每个子智能体完成时都会弹出一条「Agent 已完成一轮回复」。N 个子智能体 → N 条通知（甚至主任务还在跑就先弹了）。`spawn_subagent(background=true)` 与 `batch` 模式下同样会弹。
- **预期：** 只有**用户直接发起**的那一轮对话完成时才弹「回复完成」通知；子智能体、后台子任务、跨智能体内部调用的完成不应触发该通知。

### 日志 / 截图

通知由后端在 `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py` 的 `stream_one()` 尾部无条件发布（约第 545–556 行，v2.3.0 与 `main` 一致）：

```python
if (
    not err_msg
    and last_response is not None
    and last_response.status == RunStatus.Completed
    and session_id
):
    publish_notification(
        category=f"conversation",
        agent_id=getattr(self._workspace, f"agent_id", f"default"),
        title=f"QwenPaw",
        body=f"",
        session_id=notification_session_id,
    )
```

而 `stream_one` 的函数注释里明确写着它是**所有执行路径的统一入口**：

> `stream_one is the single console executor for the web streaming, background-task, and terminal CLI paths`

子智能体的请求同样经由 `POST /console/chat` 与 `POST /console/chat/task` 走这条路径：

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py`
  - `stream_agent_chat()` / `collect_final_agent_chat_response()` → `POST /console/chat`
  - `submit_agent_chat_task()` → `POST /console/chat/task`

因此子智能体跑完同样满足 `status == RunStatus.Completed`，同样会 `publish_notification`。

### 补充说明

#### 根因定位（供参考）

1. `stream_one()` 发布通知前**没有区分请求来源**，只要响应完成就发。
2. 系统里其实已经有识别子智能体的机制，只是这一处没用上：
   - `spawn_subagent` 的 `request_context` 带 `_spawn_subagent: True`（`agent_management.py` 的 `_build_spawn_request_context`），session id 也是 `sub-xxxxxxxx` 形态；
   - `app/routers/console.py` 的 `_chat_registration_fields()` 已用它把 chat 标记为 `source: "subagent"`；
   - `services/session_thinking.py`、`app/approvals/service.py`、`hooks/request_setup/contextvars_hook.py` 等多处也都在读这个标记。

#### 建议修复方向

在 `stream_one()` 发布 `conversation` 通知前增加过滤，例如：

```python
request_context = getattr(request, "request_context", None) or {}
is_internal_call = (
    isinstance(request_context, dict)
    and request_context.get("_spawn_subagent") is True
)
if not err_msg and not is_internal_call and last_response is not None and ...:
    publish_notification(...)
```

#### 需要注意的覆盖盲区

仅判断 `_spawn_subagent` **覆盖不全**：

- `chat_with_agent()` / `submit_to_agent()` 走 `build_agent_chat_request()`，其 `request_context` 目前只有 `root_agent_id`，**不带** `_spawn_subagent`，session id 形如 `{from}:to:{to}:{ts}:{uuid}`。
- 因此这两个工具触发的通知仍会漏过过滤。建议二选一：
  - **(a)** 在 `build_agent_chat_request()` 里也补上统一标记（如 `_agent_internal: True`），过滤时一并判断；
  - **(b)** 在发布处同时判断 session 前缀（`sub-` / `:to:`）作为兜底。

#### 关联 issue（不重复）

- #7107 [Feature]: System notification when a response or task completes while the Console/Desktop app is not focused —— 本通知功能的需求来源，本 issue 是其实现的一个边界缺陷。
- #5797 [Feature]: 定时任务结果弹窗提醒应加开关 —— 讨论的是 cron 提醒开关，与本问题不重复。
- #6084 Desktop 任务完成或审核请求的弹窗通知 —— 需求类，未涉及子智能体过滤。
