issues.title: [Bug]:  [2.3.0] WeChat channel cannot start (`ACCOUNT_IN_USE`) and successful sends are reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Environment

| item          | value                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| QwenPaw       | 2.3.0 (PyPI latest at time of report; no 2.3.1 available)    |
| agentscope    | 2.0.10                                                       |
| openai SDK    | 2.33.0                                                       |
| Python        | 3.12.13                                                      |
| OS            | Linux (Manjaro, x86_64), systemd system service              |
| wechat plugin | `wechat` 0.1.0.dev0 (bundled with 2.3.0, `publish: false`)   |
| Channel setup | single agent `default`, wechat enabled with an existing iLink bot token (`bot_token`, no `bot_token_file`) |

## Bug 1 — WeChat channel never starts: `ACCOUNT_IN_USE` (critical)

### Symptom

On every boot (6+ restarts, always identical — unrelated to restart count):

```
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'wechat' Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py:1076 | Failed to start new workspace instance for default: Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'wechat' failed: default@...:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
```

The plugin then gets unregistered (`Unregistered channel 'wechat'`), so the workspace no longer has a wechat channel at all and the bot is silently offline.

`GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `404 {"detail": "Channel 'wechat' is not running."}`

### Traceback

```
manager.py:1602  start_one
manager.py:1671  _start_one_unlocked
manager.py:1342  _reserve_channel_auth
wechat_auth_custody.py:117  _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence
    raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

Line 117 is the loop that treats **another agent profile** as a competing owner of the same WeChat credential:

```python
scopes, others = evidence
for runtime_key, configured, other_scopes in others:
    if (
        configured or any(lease.key == runtime_key for lease in leases)
    ) and (scopes.intersection(other_scopes)):
        raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

### Root cause

`_read_wechat_auth_evidence()` skips "myself" with a case-sensitive id comparison:

```python
for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
    if agent_id == workspace_id:
        continue
```

but the workspace id that `manager._reserve_channel_auth()` resolves and passes in is **`Default`** (capital D), while the profile key in `config.json` is **`default`**. The guard therefore never skips itself and evaluates `default` as "another profile". Instrumenting the guard shows the conflict is with the very same workspace, with identical scope hashes:

```
BLOCK workspace_id=Default other=<WORKING_DIR>/.copaw/workspaces/default
      configured=True lease_hit=True overlap=True
      own=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
      other_scopes=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
```

Note also that with `bot_token_file` left empty, `wechat_auth_scopes()` derives the token paths from `WORKING_DIR`, so **any** profile is guaranteed to hash to the same scopes — meaning a second (even dormant, non-wechat) agent profile is enough to trip this check once the id comparison fails.

### Suggested fix

Normalize identity instead of comparing raw strings; e.g. casefold both sides and/or compare resolved workspace directories. A `workspace_dir` parameter is already available at both call sites.

```python
if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
    continue
if own_dir is not None and Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve() == own_dir:
    continue
```

## Bug 2 — Plugin recovery deadlocks on a leaked custody-only lease (critical)

### Symptom

After the plugin has been probed once in a process, it can never be (re)enabled:

```
ERROR loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: ...
POST /api/plugins/wechat/enabled {"enabled": true}
→ 500 {"detail": "Failed to update plugin enabled state: Plugin 'wechat' recovery failed; needs_restart: Recovery has runtime resources; unload first"}
```

`POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` returns `clean: true, quiescent: true`, yet the next enable still fails, and the `_recovery_blocked` entry is never cleared for the lifetime of the process.

### Root cause

`loader._has_runtime_custody()` is just `bool(registry.runtime_owners.leases(plugin_id))`. Probe reservations are made with `custody_only=True` and **no stop adapter**, and `RuntimeOwners._invoke()` refuses to attest a stop for them:

```python
async def _invoke(entry):
    if entry.stop is None:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

`release()` then returns `False` for that lease, so the entry stays in `_entries` forever → recovery sees "runtime resources", blocks, and caches the error.

### Suggested fix

A custody-only reservation owns no process, so it can always be released:

```python
if entry.stop is None:
    if entry.custody_only:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
    return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

## Bug 3 — Successful sends reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`; replies dropped (critical)

### Symptom

Inbound works and the agent produces a reply, but the user never receives it:

```
INFO  channel _consume_with_tracker: chat_id=... session=wechat:...        (message received)
INFO  builder: built agent for session=wechat:... model=...
INFO  Usage for session wechat:...: {'input_tokens': 142422, 'output_tokens': 102}
ERROR base.py:1040 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
WARNING isolated_proxy.py:637 | Channel diagnostic: RESPONSE_FINISH_FAILED
qwenpaw.app.channels.isolated_proxy.ChannelDeliveryError: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
```

`qwenpaw channels send --channel wechat ...` fails the same way (`500` on `/api/messages/send`).

### Reproduction of the platform side

Calling the iLink API directly with the same bot token and the stored `context_token`:

```
POST https://ilinkai.weixin.qq.com/ilink/bot/sendmessage
{"msg": {"to_user_id": "...@im.wechat", "message_type": 2, "message_state": 2,
         "context_token": "<token>", "item_list": [{"type": 1, "text_item": {"text": "test"}}]},
 "base_info": {"channel_version": "0.1.0"}}

→ HTTP 200  {"message_id": <MESSAGE_ID>}
```

**A successful send returns only `message_id` — no `ret`, no `errcode`.**

### Root cause

`plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py:406`:

```python
@staticmethod
def _check_result(response, sent):
    if not isinstance(response, dict) or not (
        {"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()
    ):
        raise WeChatDeliveryError(
            "PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN",
            side_effect_possible=True,
        )
```

Every successful send is therefore classified as an unknown result and the reply is discarded (the proxy also marks `_reply_unknown`, so there is no retry).

### Suggested fix

Accept `message_id` as success (and/or fall back to the HTTP status):

```python
if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
    return
```

## Bug 4 — `top_k` / `repetition_penalty` from per-model `generate_kwargs` crash the model call (major)

With an OpenRouter model whose stored `generate_kwargs` contain `top_k` and `repetition_penalty`:

```
TypeError: AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'top_k'
  File ".../openai/resources/chat/completions/completions.py", line 2714, in create
```

OpenAI-compatible endpoints generally expect these in `extra_body`; the SDK signature does not accept them as top-level kwargs. Removing them from the model's `generate_kwargs` (`PUT /api/models/{provider}/models/{model}/config`) fixed it. Suggestion: filter known-unsupported keys into `extra_body` in the OpenAI-compatible wrapper instead of passing them through.

## Observation (not necessarily a QwenPaw bug)

While testing, `openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` repeatedly returned an empty stream while its connection test reported `status=available, verification=live`:

```
WARNING retry_chat_model.py:1201 | LLM stream failed (attempt 1/4):
        LLM stream for openrouter:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free produced no content
```

Switching the agent's chat model to `deepseek-custom/deepseek-flash` produced normal replies, so this looks model/provider-specific, but the retry loop silently consumed 4 attempts without surfacing a user-visible error.

## Minimal patch set that made the channel usable (for reference)

```diff
--- a/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
 def _read_wechat_auth_evidence(config, workspace_id, working_dir,
+                               workspace_dir=None):
     for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
         if agent_id == workspace_id:
             continue
+        # NEW: the resolved workspace id may differ in case from the profile key
+        if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
+            continue
+        # NEW: or point at the very same workspace directory
+        if workspace_dir is not None and (
+            Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+            == Path(workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+        ):
+            continue

--- a/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
     async def _invoke(entry):
         if entry.stop is None:
+            if entry.custody_only:
+                return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
             return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")

--- a/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
+++ b/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
     def _check_result(response, sent):
         if not isinstance(response, dict) or not ({"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()):
+            if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
+                return
             raise WeChatDeliveryError("PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN", side_effect_possible=True)
```

After these three changes (plus removing `top_k`/`repetition_penalty` from the model's `generate_kwargs`):

- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `{"channel":"wechat","status":"healthy"}`
- plugin → `status: active, diagnostics: ["channel_validation_passed"]`
- inbound messages are consumed, replies are delivered, no `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

## Additional notes

- A zero-downtime agent reload (triggered by any config change) can leave the previous wechat channel handle undelivered: subsequent `POST /api/config/channels/wechat/restart` returns `CHANNEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` indefinitely, and a stale `shared_worker.py` keeps polling (reported `platform_state: connected`) while its messages no longer reach the app. Killing the stale worker unblocks the drain.
- Plugin source edits require `POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` + `enabled=true` to take effect; `channel restart` fails with `SOURCE_REVISION_MISMATCH`.
- With a large wechat session (142k input tokens per turn) replies take 60–90 s end-to-end, which may be close to the iLink reply window.

issues.title: perf: prefix cache instability from unsorted tool schemas and interleaved env_context fields
issues.body:
## Problem

The LLM prefix (KV) cache misses unnecessarily on repeated turns due to two sources of
non-determinism in the prompt construction:

1. **Tool schema ordering** — `ToolRegistry.filter()` iterates `self._descs.values()` in dict
   insertion order. This is stable within a process but not across restarts or plugin load-order
   changes. Tool schemas are the largest prefix segment in the LLM request (~3,000-8,000 tokens).

2. **Env context field interleaving** — `build_env_context()` emits per-session dynamic fields
   (session_id, date, working_dir) interleaved with static fields (About, GitHub, Docs, Important
   hints). Every call changes the dynamic fields, shifting all subsequent tokens including the
   static hint block that should be cache-stable.

Both issues cause the prefix cache to invalidate on segments that should be reusable across turns.

## Root Cause Analysis

Six potential prefix cache instability sources were identified:

| # | Source | Status | Impact |
|---|--------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Tool schema ordering (dict insertion order) | **Fixable** | High — ~3-8K tokens |
| 2 | env_context dynamic fields interleaved in static content | **Fixable** | Medium — ~150-400 tokens |
| 3 | Memory tool injection (post-toolkit) | Low — same manager in practice | Low |
| 4 | Coding mode project_dir | Low — worktree paths are rare | Low |
| 5 | Continuation summary shifts (scroll compression) | Intentional design | N/A |
| 6 | Tool result folding (`[scroll folded]` markers) | Intentional design | N/A |

Items 5 and 6 are documented architectural decisions in the Scroll memory system.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Sort tool schemas** by name in `ToolRegistry.filter()` — one line (`out.sort(key=lambda d: d.name)`)
2. **Split static/dynamic sections** in `build_env_context()` — static prefix (About/GitHub/Docs/Important) first, dynamic tail (OS/date/session_id/working_dir) last

Both changes are verified to be on the critical path from `AgentBuilder.build()` through to the LLM API request.

## Verification

- Tool schemas: `list_tools()` → `ToolRegistry.filter()` (sorted) → `PolicyGuardedTool` wrapping → `Toolkit` → `AgentScope.Agent` → `tools` param in LLM request
- Env context: `build_env_context()` → `EnvContextContributor` (priority=90, last contributor) → system prompt tail

issues.title: [Bug] Agent switch deletes the agent's last session (lastChatIdByAgent) and makes historical sessions unclickable - 2.2.1-beta.2
issues.body:
## Summary

Two concrete defects in the console's session bookkeeping that fire on **every agent switch**. They are independent of the "always start on a blank conversation" behaviour discussed in #7687 — I understand from the reply there that landing on a blank chat is intentional, so the sections below are about **state loss** and a **dead interaction**, not about that design choice. (Design feedback of my own is at the bottom, clearly separated.)

**Environment:** QwenPaw Desktop **2.2.1-beta.2**, Windows 10 (AMD64). Console bundle built **2026-09-10 17:48:28**: `index-8OrhnpZF.js` + chat chunk `index-BAFRWhpS.js` (71,879 B). I also compared tags `v2.2.1-beta.2...v2.2.1` on GitHub: it contains **0 `console/` file changes** (the only diff is README/version/release-notes), so this applies to **2.2.1** as well. Line numbers below are from tag `v2.2.1`'s `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` (byte-identical to `v2.2.1-beta.2`).

## 1. The agent's "last session" record is **deleted**, not skipped

The switch effect (L2719-2723) creates a draft-shaped local id on every switch:

```ts
sessionApi.preferredChatId = null;
sessionApi.lastActiveChatId = null;
navigate(CHAT_BASE_PATH, { replace: true });
sessionApi.userInitiatedCreate = true;
void sessionApi.createSession({});   // id like 1789094161754-iyotsc2
```

and `onSessionCreated` (L2667-2673) then persists it. But the store treats draft-shaped ids as **delete** signals:

```ts
setLastChatId(agent, id) {
  if (/^\d+-[a-z0-9]+$/.test(id)) { delete lastChatIdByAgent[agent]; return; }
  /* else: record */
}
```

⇒ Every agent switch **erases `lastChatIdByAgent[agent]`**. That forms a self-reinforcing loop — *no memory → draft id created → memory deleted* — so an agent that is switched to but not messaged in can never regain its last session. Verified in `localStorage["qwenpaw-agent-storage"].state.lastChatIdByAgent` (read out of the WebView2 leveldb): the entries are either real UUIDs or missing entirely; the agents missing there are exactly the ones that were never messaged while sitting on the blank chat.

Suggested fix: on a draft-shaped id, **skip** the write (`if (isDraftId(id)) return;`) instead of deleting the existing record.

## 2. Historical sessions become unclickable while a draft is active

`onSessionSelected` (L2588-2594) returns early as soon as the active chat is an unresolved local draft:

```ts
if (sessionApi.lastActiveChatId && sessionApi.isUnresolvedLocalSession(sessionApi.lastActiveChatId)) return;
```

After a switch, clicking a conversation in the sidebar does nothing — there is **no manual way back** to the previous session, which is what makes defect 1 so visible in practice.

## 3. A message sent right after a switch is silently registered as a new chat, and the backend then rejects tool calls

`%USERPROFILE%\.qwenpaw\qwenpaw.log`:

```
Auto-registered new chat: c463285d-… -> 1789094161754-iyotsc2
tool_calls.py:91 session_id mismatch: url=1789094161754-iyotsc2 backend=<real session uuid>   # 10+ occurrences within one minute
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open agent A and go into one of its existing conversations.
2. Switch to another agent (B).
3. Switch back to A and **send a message immediately**.
4. The message appears in a **new conversation** (title auto-generated from the first line); the original conversation shows no trace of it, and per defect 1 the agent's last-session record has been erased.

## Minimal fixes I would suggest

1. In the switch branch, restore `getLastChatId(selectedAgent)` when it is a real backend id — this is what the 2026-08-31 build (`index-DeBQK-i1.js`) did — and fall back to a blank chat only when there is none.
2. `setLastChatId`: never `delete` for a draft-shaped id; skip the write.
3. Don't return early from `onSessionSelected` for draft ids (or give the user an explicit way out of the blank chat).
4. Never send with a draft id as the session target: resolve/register first, so the `session_id mismatch` rejections stop.

*(No upstream change was made here; to validate 1–3 I string-patched my own installed console chunk off-line. Happy to share the diff if useful.)*

## Design feedback (separate from the bug report)

Even granting "always start the newly selected agent on a blank conversation", the practical effect is a loss of continuity: after switching agent — or simply reopening the app the next day — you cannot continue where you left off, and per defect 2 you cannot even click your way back. The 2026-08-31 build restored the agent's last session instead. If the blank start is deliberate, a per-agent "remember the last conversation" option (default on) would solve this without changing your intended first-run behaviour.

## 中文小结

切智能体时会**删掉该 agent 的"上次会话"记录**（草稿形 id 在 store 里是 `delete` 而不是跳过），同时"草稿态守卫"会让侧栏的历史会话**点不动**，所以切回来直接发消息就会被静默 `Auto-registered` 成一条新对话、原对话被一分为二，后端还会成片 `session_id mismatch` 拒绝工具调用。这三条与 #7687 里"切过去落在空白对话"的设计无关（那部分我接受），建议按上文 4 条最小改动修一下；另外希望能把"记住上次会话"作为可选项。谢谢！

issues.title: Creator: Windows source-intelligence write path still derives its directory from the raw source_id (write-side root cause split from #8547)
issues.body:
## 背景

从 #8547 的修复 PR(xuanrui-L/QwenPaw#254)CR 中拆出的**写侧根因**。#8547 修的是读/导入侧,本 issue 跟踪写侧。

## 问题

Windows 上 Creator 素材理解(source-intelligence)的写路径仍拿 raw `source_id`(形如 `source:<uuid4 hex>`,生成点 `services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:3282`)当落盘目录分量:

- `services/source_analysis/service.py:2077-2082`:`relative_uri = PurePosixPath("assets", "source-intelligence", job.source_id, f"{job.intelligence_version_id}.json")`
- publish 时 `AssetFileStore` 按该 `relative_uri` mkdir 父目录

`:` 是 Windows 非法字符,因此 Windows 上**新建素材理解、或对导入项目的素材重跑理解**,publish 阶段 mkdir `source:<id>` 会失败。读路径不受影响(一律经 `IndexedFile.relative_uri` 解析,见 `services/media/source_observation.py:401`、`services/file_agent_runtime/driver.py:9384`、`services/project_files/assets.py:412`)。

代码路径推断,未 Windows 真机复现;复现成本不高,建议认领时先补一条 Windows 矩阵的发布用例。

## 与 #8547 的关系

- #8547 / PR #254 修的是**解包侧**:Windows 提取归档时把含非法字符的成员名 sanitize 成合法名,并把 `IndexedFile.relative_uri` 重写到与落盘一致;逻辑标识(source_id、`sources.items` 键、`order`)不动。
- 写侧根因非该 PR 引入,也不被该 PR 解决。PR body 中"落盘路径只经 relative_uri 解析"的论断已按 CR 修正为**仅读路径成立**。

## 建议修法(二选一,认领时定)

1. **publish 时 sanitize**:`AssetFileStore` 落盘前统一映射非法字符,并把 sanitized 结果写回 `relative_uri`,保持注册表与落盘一致(与 PR #254 的解包侧 sanitize 复用同一函数,保证幂等);
2. **生成点不再拿 raw source_id 当路径分量**:目录名改用 uuid/hash 形态,`source_id` 仅保留为逻辑标识。需要为存量 `relative_uri` 做迁移或兼容读。

方案 1 改动面小、与现有 sanitize 一致;方案 2 更彻底但带迁移成本。

## 验收标准

- Windows 真机/CI:新建素材理解、对导入示例素材重跑理解,publish 均成功;
- Linux/macOS 导出、Windows 导入的归档,`relative_uri` 与落盘路径一致,导入后写路径可继续追加文件。

## 关联

- #8547(读/导入侧症状)
- xuanrui-L/QwenPaw#254(读/导入侧修复)
- 历史读侧修复 `4f71f44e5`(#165,1.1.2 发布)与回归点 `f6ed7362c`(#185 重构 example_routes 时丢失 sanitize)
- 另一独立动作(不在本 issue 范围):按 #165 复审结论重建并重传 `cat-perspective-0803` 归档(合法目录名 + 更新 manifest sha256),让内置示例的运行时重写变 no-op,顺带绕开"在途事务归档 + Windows 导入"时重写改变语义 etag 致 recovery 基线失配的窄边缘(`services/project_files/recovery.py:419/461`)。该动作需要 OSS 发布权限。

[qwenpawmail-mcp] Add save_draft tool: write to Drafts without sending
issues.body:
### Feature Request: `save_draft` tool

**Problem**

qwenpawmail's `send_message` / `reply_message` / `forward_message` all send immediately via SMTP — there is no draft mode and no way to write a message into the Drafts folder without sending.

For agent workflows where the user wants the agent to *draft* an email for later human review, the only current options are writing drafts to local files (invisible in the mailbox) or risking premature sending. The internal IMAP APPEND in `imap_ops.py` is only used as a fallback for `move_message` and is not exposed as a tool.

**Proposed solution**

Add a `save_draft(folder, to, subject, body, cc)` tool that:

- Builds an RFC822 message and appends it to the Drafts folder via IMAP APPEND with the `\Draft` flag
- Does **not** send via SMTP
- Returns the UID (parse `APPENDUID`) so callers can fetch/update the draft later

This mirrors how `get_message(folder, uid)` already works, and lets users review and send drafts from webmail or a mail client.

**Notes**

- APPEND is supported on the providers qwenpawmail targets (verified end-to-end, including fetch-by-UID and cleanup).
- `encode_folder()` in `imap_ops.py` can be reused.
- On some providers, SEARCH does not index freshly APPENDed messages, so returning the UID is important.

issues.title: [Bug]: Invalid batch task values can dispatch sibling subagents before failing
issues.body:
## Description

`_spawn_batch()` checks task presence using `str(spec.get("task", "")).strip()`, but later dispatches the original value unchanged. Consequently, null, numbers, lists, and objects pass the batch preflight.

With `[{"task": "valid sibling"}, {"task": null, "fork": true}]`, the valid sibling can be submitted and the fork API called before the invalid item fails with `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable`.

Source: [`src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c8025df92a9200fc5094ac7c9957a4031db0a241/src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py), specifically `_spawn_batch()` and `_spawn_forked_subagent()`.

## Evidence and limitations

I reproduced this using the current upstream functions extracted unchanged via Python AST, with HTTP submission and the fork API stubbed. The observed output was:

```text
[1/2] submitted

[2/2] ERROR: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable
['normal sibling submitted', 'fork API called']
```

Separate checks showed that `null`, `123`, `[]`, and `{}` all pass the task preflight and reach the submission payload unchanged.

No real subagents or worktrees were created, no external requests were dispatched by the reproduction, and all task text and paths were synthetic. This is an isolated control-flow reproduction, not a full application or live-server test. The potential real-world impact is partial batch execution and a fork request occurring before invalid input is rejected, not a demonstrated security-boundary bypass.

## Proposed scope

Validate every batch item's task as a non-empty string before any dispatch, with regression tests asserting zero submission and zero fork calls for invalid batches. Existing valid strings and JSON-array batch compatibility would remain unchanged.

Would this focused fix be welcome? I can prepare the PR.

AI assistance disclosure: this investigation and report were prepared with AI assistance. The isolated reproduction described above was executed; full application tests have not yet been run.

prs.title: fix(console): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in chat Markdown
prs.body: ## What problem this solves `**中文。**后面` and `__中文！__后面` never parse: CommonMark only accepts a closing delimiter run that is right-flanking, and a run preceded by CJK punctuation and followed by a CJK letter is neither right- nor left-flanking. The renderer therefore shows the raw markers instead of bold text. Earlier commits in this PR repaired the string before parsing. Following the review, this revision drops that approach entirely: the fix is an instance-level marked tokenizer, and the Markdown source is never rewritten. ## Scope Type: C (new renderer behaviour, no data or protocol change) | Input | Stock | This PR | In scope | |---|---|---|---| | `**甲。**乙` | literal markers | `甲。乙` | yes | | `__甲。__乙` | literal markers | `甲。乙` | yes | | `**甲，**乙` … `**甲？**乙` | literal markers | `甲，乙` | yes | | single `*甲。*乙` / `_甲。_乙` | literal | unchanged | no | | ASCII punctuation before the closer (`**甲.**乙`) | literal | unchanged | no | | ASCII follower (`**甲。**b`, `**甲。**1`) | literal | unchanged | no | | nested or unbalanced runs (`***甲。***乙`) | stock result | unchanged | no | | CJK punctuation after the closer (`**甲。**，`) | stock result | unchanged | no | | fenced code, inline code, HTML | verbatim | verbatim | protected | | link label and image alt | verbatim | verbatim | protected (`inLink`) | | link `href` / `title`, image `src` / `alt` / `title` | unchanged | unchanged | asserted | | tables | literal in cells | emphasis in cells | ordinary inline text | Everything outside the rows that change returns the stock tokenizer result, so unsupported shapes keep the stock renderer's behaviour. ## How it works `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.ts` registers one `tokenizer.emStrong` override: - it runs only when the source starts with `**` or `__`; - it looks for a closing run whose preceding character is CJK punctuation and whose following character is a CJK letter, within a 4096-character body; - on a hit it returns a `strong` token whose body keeps the punctuation (`甲。`), so no character moves; - on anything else it returns `false`, which makes marked fall back to the stock tokenizer. `console/src/components/ChatMarkdown/ChatMarkdown.tsx` is a local counterpart of the SDK's Markdown component. The SDK builds its `config` internally and never forwards one, so the only way to register an instance-level extension without touching global tokenizer prototypes is to compose the same pieces ourselves: math, footnotes, citations, streaming cursor, media, link handling, HTML sanitisation and the code-block slot are all preserved, and the only difference from the SDK is the extra extension. `AssistantMarkdown` renders through it and no longer rewrites the text; `vite.config.ts` inlines the SDK subpaths the wrapper imports so the unit tests resolve them the same way the app does. ## Evidence - `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.test.tsx` renders the real `XMarkdown` component and asserts DOM output: 20 tests, including the agreed punctuation family, the follower family, protected regions, repeat-render stability, streamed-versus-complete equality and a non-amplification guard against stock `marked`. - `console/src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx` and `HostBubbles.render.test.tsx`: 22 tests pass, covering the streamed code-block pipeline that this component reuses. - Benchmark (same process, best of three, stock `marked` versus stock plus the extension): | shape | bytes | stock | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | `**甲。**乙` repeated | 2,800 | 5.8 ms | 3.1 ms | | `**甲。**乙` repeated | 11,200 | 9.0 ms | 7.9 ms | | `**甲。**乙` repeated | 44,800 | 35.0 ms | 17.3 ms | | `- [a](` repeated | 2,800 | 6.1 ms | 6.6 ms | | `- [a](` repeated | 11,200 | 10.8 ms | 9.9 ms | | `- [a](` repeated | 44,800 | 42.7 ms | 46.5 ms | | mixed CJK paragraph | 7,600 | 4.4 ms | 2.8 ms | | mixed CJK paragraph | 30,400 | 15.9 ms | 8.0 ms | | mixed CJK paragraph | 121,600 | 68.8 ms | 35.4 ms | ## Test scope - Target: `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.test.tsx` (20 passed) - Neighbour: `console/src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx`, `HostBubbles.render.test.tsx` (22 passed) - `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint and prettier pass on the changed files.

prs.title: feat(providers): extract local model management into plugin
prs.body:
## Description

Extract local model management into a Plugin Provider. The plugin owns model downloads, llama.cpp installation and service lifecycle. The host keeps model selection and unified inference.

- Preserve existing users' configuration and model files.
- Move download dependencies into the plugin and import them lazily.
- Reuse plugin registration, dependency preparation and lifecycle management.

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose the semantic colour roles to plugin themes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#8071 asks for a plugin theme extension point. #8422 landed the first slice:
six roles (`bg`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `border`, `text`,
`text-secondary`). Those cover the page frame, but not the semantic colour
surface a theme actually has to touch — a plugin that wants its own accent,
status colours, or the lower-contrast text and border tiers still has to reach
into raw `--app-*` names, which this closed API deliberately rejects.

This PR widens the closed set to the 31 semantic colour roles that
`console/src/styles/tokens.css` already defines and the console already
consumes, and keeps the compatibility story honest:

- the original six roles keep their current minimum SDK version, so plugins
  that already call `overrideTokens` are unaffected;
- the new roles sit behind `sdk.version >= 1.2.0` plus a `themeTokens`
  capability, so a plugin cannot silently depend on a role that an older host
  does not know.

Group 2 from #8071 (fifteen shape and layer roles: radius, shadow,
focus-ring, scrollbar, fill) stays out of this PR and is left for a separate
discussion, as requested.

## Evidence

Every role below is already read by the console. No component was changed and
no new colour was invented — this only opens roles that exist.

| family | role | representative consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface | `surface-subtle` | `layouts/index.module.less:324` |
| surface | `surface-sunken` | `components/RenderableCodeBlock/index.module.less:122` |
| surface | `shell-bg` | `layouts/dockableSidebar.module.less:13` |
| text | `text-tertiary` | `layouts/dockableSidebar.module.less:36` |
| text | `text-quaternary` | `layouts/index.module.less:254` |
| border | `border-subtle` | `layouts/index.module.less:53` |
| border | `border-strong` | `layouts/sidebarA.module.less:99` |
| accent | `accent` | `App.tsx:421` |
| accent | `accent-hover` | `App.tsx:422` |
| accent | `accent-soft` | `App.tsx:423` |
| status | `success-bg` | `components/LoopInput/index.module.less:57` |
| status | `warning-border` | `components/Chat/ToolCards/shared/offloadBanner.module.less:11` |
| status | `error-text` | `tauri/BackendLoadingPage.module.less:52` |

Both schemes are exercised rather than assumed: `themeTokens.test.ts` asserts
each role lands in the `:root` block with its light value and in the
`html.dark-mode` block with its dark value.

## Self-review

1. Overlapping registrations — `install.test.ts` keeps the existing
   "stacks per token and falls back on dispose" case, and the new semantic
   roles go through the same stacking path.
2. Switching scheme or preset while an override is active —
   `themeTokens.integration.test.ts` keeps "wins over the preset's inline
   `--app-surface` in both schemes" and "restores the preset when the plugin is
   unloaded".
3. Cleanup — "removes the element once every override is gone" and
   `disposeAll(pluginId)` both still clear the new roles.
4. Invalid input — a role missing one scheme and a genuinely unknown name both
   still throw; the unknown-name case now uses `not-a-role` so it does not
   accidentally test a role that became valid in this PR.
5. Backward compatibility — `sdk.version: 1.0.0` stays valid for the original
   six roles; `1.1.0` with `themeTokens` is rejected with a clear message;
   `1.2.0` with `themeTokens` is accepted.

## Test scope

- Console: `src/plugins` — 34 files, 462 passed, including the five
  capability-gate cases and the seven `pluginSdk` cases.
- Python: `tests/unit/app/routers` 161 passed and
  `test_plugins_router_lifecycle.py` 115 passed, including the new
  `test_frontend_list_reports_declared_sdk`; `tests/unit/plugins` passed with
  `test_theme_tokens_capability_gates_on_sdk_version`.
- `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint, prettier and pre-commit on the touched files.
- Browser: `python scripts/verify_theme_tokens.py` from `console/` (values in
  the follow-up section below).

## Coordination with #8764

#8764 also moves `SDK_VERSION` to `1.2.0` and touches
`src/qwenpaw/plugins/frontend/index.d.ts`. This PR needs the same version slot.
Whichever lands first, the other rebases onto it — the two changes are additive
and share only that version line, so the rebase is mechanical.


## Review follow-up

Two points from review are addressed on `156a6a26`.

**The gate now covers undeclared usage.** `validate_sdk` used to run only when
a plugin declared `themeTokens`, so a plugin could use a new role while
declaring nothing at all. `/frontend_plugin` now carries `sdk_version` and
`sdk_capabilities`, and `chat.theme.overrideTokens` consults that declaration
for every extended role: no declaration, an older version, or a missing
capability each throw with the role, the plugin, what is required and what was
declared. A manifest that cannot be read is treated as undeclared, so the check
fails closed. The original six roles keep their 1.0.0 minimum and need no
declaration.

**Components now demonstrate it.** The earlier assertions only read the
stylesheet text an override produces, which is an intermediate representation.
`console/theme-verify.html` plus `console/src/themeVerify/main.tsx` mount the
real `BackendLoadingPage`, and `console/scripts/verify_theme_tokens.py` drives
that page through Playwright and reads `getComputedStyle`. The measured values
equal the declared override in both schemes (page background, card surface,
card border, accent button, error text, secondary text). Stacked registrations
walk back 176 → 160 → default across two `dispose()` calls, and the page
returns to its pre-override colour once everything is disposed. The same public
call with an undeclared plugin throws in the browser too, so the gate is not a
test-only guard.

Third-party scope is documented in `plugins/frontend/README.md`: this is a
colour surface, not a full UI theme. Only the listed roles participate, and
layout, spacing, typography, iconography, chart palettes and markup that
hardcodes `rgb()`/`rgba()` do not follow the override.

prs.title: fix(providers): read a gateway-reported status from the error text
prs.body:
## Description

`extract_status_code()` reads a status from the exception's `status_code`, `code`, `response`, and `body`/`details` fields, and falls back to the message text for one narrow gateway format — `Streaming response failed: [503] ...`.

An OpenAI-compatible gateway that fails mid-stream can instead report the status only inside the message text, for example `status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)`. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError` for such a response: no `status_code`, no `response`. The real status is present in the text, but the fallback does not recognise that shape, so `classify_model_error()` returns `unknown` — no same-model retry, no cross-model fallback, and the turn or scheduled job dies. The same upstream failure wrapped as a real HTTP 502 is `transient` and does fall back, so identical failures behave differently only because of how the gateway phrased them.

This adds one more narrow pattern for gateway error text, keeping the same deliberate narrowness the existing fallback documents: only `4xx`/`5xx` are read, so a success code quoted in a message (`expected status_code=200`) is never mistaken for a failure, and unrelated three-digit numbers in provider messages are still ignored.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8505

**Security Considerations:** None — this only affects how a provider error is classified, never what is sent to a provider.

prs.title: fix(scroll): recognize url-referenced media in tool-result folding
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat session accumulates enough turns to trigger context compression, historical completed tool results are inspected by `ScrollContextManager._tool_result_fold_candidates()` to collapse long or media-carrying results into compact pointer stubs (`[scroll folded] ...`).

Previously, `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` only checked for `source.get("type") == "base64"` or `source.type == "base64"`. URL-referenced media blocks (`source.type == "url"`), such as video, audio, or image outputs generated by `send_file_to_user` and similar tools, were not recognized as inline media. Consequently, these media tool results failed the `has_media` check and, having short text captions (<= 200 chars), were skipped by `_tool_result_fold_candidates()`.

As a result, uncollapsed media blocks were carried over across turns and re-spliced verbatim into rebuilt request payloads after compression. Subsequent model API requests failed repeatedly with errors such as `400: Video count 2 exceeds limit 1 per request`, permanently hanging the session for that channel.

This change extends `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` to recognize `source.type == "url"` with non-empty URL values for both dictionary-based and object-based sources.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8474

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the issue happens

In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`:

```python
    @staticmethod
    def _tool_result_has_inline_media(block: Any) -> bool:
        ...
        for item in output:
            if ScrollContextManager._block_type(item) != "data":
                continue
            source = (
                item.get("source")
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                else getattr(item, "source", None)
            )
            if isinstance(source, dict):
                if source.get("type") == "base64" and source.get("data"):
                    return True
            elif getattr(source, "type", None) == "base64" and getattr(
                source,
                "data",
                None,
            ):
                return True
        return False
```

When a tool output provides a data block with a URL source (`source={"type": "url", "url": "https://..."}`), `_tool_result_has_inline_media` returned `False`.

In `_tool_result_fold_candidates`:

```python
    has_media = self._tool_result_has_inline_media(block)
    if (
        not has_media
        and self._tool_result_text_chars(block) <= _PRE_TRIM_MIN_CHARS
    ):
        continue
```

Because `has_media` was `False` and media tool results generally have little or no text characters (`<= 200`), the block was skipped and never folded. During context compression and payload rebuild, the raw media block remained in the active payload.

## The change

1. In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`, `_tool_result_has_inline_media` now also checks:
   - For dict sources: `source.get("type") == "url" and source.get("url")`
   - For object sources: `getattr(source, "type", None) == "url" and getattr(source, "url", None)`
2. In `tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py`:
   - Added `test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources` to test both base64 and URL sources across dict and object representations as well as negative cases.
   - Added `test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length` to verify that tool results carrying URL media bypass the text length restriction and fold into pointer stubs under context pressure.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_hung_completion_callback_does_not_block_new_messages
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]
23 passed in 0.49s
```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app
3118 passed, 1 skipped, 12 warnings in 58.77s
```

One caveat worth stating plainly: the baseline run pins the module source with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a pristine checkout. The venv's editable install points at the patched worktree, so simply `cd`-ing to the unmodified tree would still have imported the patched code and produced a false green — that happened on the first attempt and the baseline above is from the corrected invocation.

Lint: `black`, `flake8` and `mypy` are clean. `pylint`, run with the full argument list from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, scores **10.00/10 with zero findings on both the unmodified and the patched tree** — I have not pasted a terminal transcript for that one because I did not capture it to a file, and I would rather say so than manufacture the output.

prs.title: fix(hub): expose request_headers on AnthropicProvider presets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hub model connections that use the built-in `anthropic`, `minimax` or `minimax-cn`
preset fail instantly with HTTP 502 `hub_upstream_error`, and the request never
leaves the Hub process.

`hub/model_service/provider_setup.py::provider_headers()` calls
`preset.request_headers()` for every presets-based connection, but
`AnthropicProvider` never defined that method (`OpenAIProvider` and
`OpenRouterProvider` do). Because `MiniMaxProvider` subclasses
`AnthropicProvider`, three of the 31 presets returned by `supported_presets()`
raise `AttributeError: 'AnthropicProvider' object has no attribute
'request_headers'`.

`ModelGateway` catches it with its generic `except BaseException`, settles the
ledger row as `upstream_failed`, and surfaces
`Invalid or incomplete response from the upstream model.` — so a broken call
site looks like a provider outage even though the upstream is healthy.
`provider_headers()` returns `{}` for custom connections, which is why only
preset-based connections are affected.

Fixes #8718.

## Change

Implement `request_headers()` on `AnthropicProvider`, mirroring the existing
implementations on `OpenAIProvider` and `OpenRouterProvider`:

```python
def request_headers(self) -> dict:
    """Return provider headers for an externally owned HTTP transport."""
    return self._build_default_headers()
```

`MiniMaxProvider` inherits the method, so all three affected presets are fixed
by one definition.

I did not add a `getattr` fallback in `provider_headers()`: that would silence
the crash while silently dropping attribution and session headers for any
future preset that forgets the method. Keeping the contract callable makes a
missing implementation fail in tests instead.

## Evidence

Before the patch, calling `provider_headers({"provider_id": ...})` for every
preset:

| provider_id | class | result |
|---|---|---|
| anthropic | AnthropicProvider | `AttributeError` |
| minimax | MiniMaxProvider | `AttributeError` |
| minimax-cn | MiniMaxProvider | `AttributeError` |
| openai | OpenAIProvider | `{}` |
| openrouter | OpenRouterProvider | headers returned |

After the patch all 31 presets return a dict.

The new regression test is parametrized over `supported_presets()`, so it covers
every built-in preset rather than only the three known-bad ids:

- unpatched tree: `3 failed, 69 passed` (fails exactly for anthropic, minimax, minimax-cn)
- patched tree: `72 passed`

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/providers/test_hub_provider_reuse.py` — 72 passed
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/providers` — 1191 passed, 1 skipped
- Pre-commit: all hooks passed (ast, docstring-first, encoding, private key,
  whitespace, trailing commas, mypy, black, flake8, pylint)

prs.body:
## Description

With "Reply completion" notifications on, every subagent that finishes raises "The agent has finished a reply", often while the user's own turn is still running. `ConsoleChannel.stream_one` publishes the `conversation` notification for every completed turn, and subagents (`spawn_subagent`) and inter-agent calls (`chat_with_agent` / `submit_to_agent`) go through the same `/console/chat` and `/console/chat/task` path.

prs.title: fix(channels): hide internal scaffolding at the display boundary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two different families of model-facing bytes are persisted as ordinary
assistant text and therefore reach the user verbatim:

1. **Framework-injected context** — the `<system-info>` /
   `<system-notification>` notes and the other `system-*` notices the runtime
   prepends to a turn. The channel renderer has switches for structured
   thinking and tool blocks, but those switches only match structured block
   types, so injected text is forwarded unchanged. The same bytes come back
   from `GET /chats/{id}`, so reloading a conversation re-exposes them even
   after the live stream was clean. The matcher also recognised only two of
   the notice names while the host emits five, so `system-warning`,
   `system-reminder` and `system-error` were forwarded whole.

2. **Reasoning a model inlined into plain text** — some models write a
   `<thinking>…</thinking>` block into the text block, or emit a truncated tail
   that ends in a bare `</thinking>` with no opening tag *(observed on two
   separate occasions: a whole `<thinking>` block around an `IncompleteRead`
   error, and a 436-character block containing a partial reasoning sentence
   followed by a bare closing tag and the actual reply)*. Those bytes sit in
   the same text block, so no display switch reaches them either.

`tag_parser.text_contains_think_tag` / `extract_thinking_from_text` exist but
have no call site anywhere in `src/qwenpaw/`, so inline reasoning is never
converted into a structured `REASONING` block in the first place; the display
boundary is the last place where it can be dropped.

## Why the display boundary

Fixing the parser per provider would leave the same hole for every provider
that behaves differently, and a truncated tail (closing tag without an opening
tag) cannot be reliably reconstructed into a structured block at all. The
renderer is the one place every path — live channel streaming and HTTP history
replay — passes through, so both exits are handled by one rule set.

## What is covered, and what is not

Covered:

- balanced `think` / `thinking` / `analysis` / `reasoning` blocks;
- a bare closing tag with no opening tag — when a reply follows the tag the
  reasoning head is dropped, and when the tag ends the message only the
  trailing reasoning paragraph goes, so the reply written before it survives;
- `system-*` notices under any name, closed either by their own tag or by a
  shortened one (`</notification>` closing `<system-notification>`);
- a cut-off `<parameter …>` tool shell that opens the message *or* a
  paragraph — anchoring to the start alone missed 49 of the 51 occurrences
  observed in the corpus, because a model that narrates before calling a tool
  leaves the shell mid-message;
- a message that is nothing but scaffolding produces no message at all, rather
  than falling back to the `[Message type: …]` placeholder;
- quoted mentions (inline backticks and fenced code) are never modified, so
  prose that discusses the tags survives.

Not covered, deliberately:

- an opening tag that never closes: every observed sample (7 messages) was a
  reply *discussing* the tag rather than leaking reasoning, so truncating at
  the opener deleted real replies and the rule was removed;
- reasoning prose with no tag at all — it has no anchor, so any regex would
  damage ordinary replies; separating it requires the parser to keep reasoning
  out of the text block, which is a separate change;
- a scaffold block with no closing tag anywhere (1 sample), left untouched as
  damaged data.

## Evidence

Targeted:

```
tests/unit/agents/context/test_serialize.py       71 passed
tests/unit/app/channels/test_renderer.py          53 passed
tests/unit/app/chats/test_utils.py                51 passed, 1 skipped
```

Both call sites are load-bearing — removing either one turns its tests red:

prs.title: fix(loop): record tool calls appended to one reply message
prs.body:
## Description

`DoomLoopGate` never fired on 2.3.0. agentscope 2.0.10 appends every iteration's blocks to the same assistant message and uses `state.reply_id` as its id, so `_auto_record_from_ctx` — which treated the message id as a per-iteration cursor — recorded only the first snapshot of a reply. With the default `window_size=3`, the warning could fire only when that first snapshot already held 3 identical calls, and the `after=4 / stop` stage was unreachable.

A reply is not always a single message either: when a warning is injected, `check_pending_gates()` appends a user continuation message and the next reasoning step opens a new assistant message that reuses the same `reply_id`. Neither the message id nor a per-message block count can tell which calls were already recorded, so this revision tracks the `id` of every recorded tool-call block for the turn and records only ids it has not seen yet. Every iteration contributes its own calls, and re-checking an unchanged snapshot stays a no-op. (Thanks to @lalaliat for pointing out the message-count gap in review.)

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8700

prs.title: fix(local_models): parse llama.cpp build numbers without false updates
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8125 (follow-up to #7633).

`LlamaCppBackend.has_update()` compared the pinned release tag against the
installed runtime by parsing the digits after a leading `b`:

    return int(latest_version[1:]) > int(await self.get_version())

That only ever worked for the old `version: 8514 (406f4e3f6)` output. Since
llama.cpp v0.4.0 the server prints `version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10853, commit
9dcf84e5a)`, so `int()` raised, the bare `except` fell through to `return
True`, and QwenPaw decided an update was available. The downloader then
reinstalled the pinned CPU-only `b8744` over a newer user-installed build,
which removed its Vulkan `ggml-vulkan.dll` and left `llama-server` crashing at
startup with a symbol-table mismatch.

This PR adds a small `_parse_llamacpp_build_number()` helper that understands
every version shape llama.cpp has shipped (`8514 (406f4e3f6)`, `b8744` /
`b10839`, and `0.4.0-dev (build 10853, ...)`), uses it in `get_version()` so
callers always compare build numbers, and makes `has_update()` return `False`
(with a warning) when either version can't be recognized instead of defaulting
to `True`. An unknown version must never trigger a reinstall that overwrites
what the user already has.

The change is deliberately small and stays inside the version-parsing path; no
other behaviour is touched.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8125

**Security Considerations:** none — this only changes how a local runtime
version string is compared before the update prompt appears.

prs.title: docs(heartbeat): document runtime semantics of silence, concurrency, and reloads
prs.body:
## Description

Docs-only change to `website/public/docs/heartbeat.en.md` and `heartbeat.zh.md`.
The heartbeat page documents how to *configure* heartbeat but not the runtime
behavior users hit after enabling it. This adds a `## Runtime semantics` section
(before `## Heartbeat vs cron jobs`) covering the five behaviors from the issue,
and corrects two stale sentences.

What the new section documents:

- **Nothing to report is not filtered** — `main` (default) runs but never
  delivers; `last` streams every event (staying quiet is the model's job);
  `inbox` writes one entry (`heartbeat_result` / `heartbeat_timeout` /
  `heartbeat_error`). A tick is skipped silently when outside `activeHours`, or
  when HEARTBEAT.md is missing/empty; `last` with no recorded dispatch degrades
  to a run without delivery.
- **Overlapping runs** — the job leaves the APScheduler default
  `max_instances=1`, so an overlapping tick is **skipped, not queued**
  (`misfire_grace_time` 60s); ticks bypass the channel queue and the cron
  per-job concurrency limit and always use session `main`; concurrent runs on
  `main` are not serialized *with each other* and the later session save wins.
- **Own-message drop** — many bundled channels drop inbound events from the
  agent's own account (Matrix compares `event.sender` to the agent's user id;
  DingTalk skips `is_bot` messages; Mattermost compares the sender to the bot
  id). Not every channel does this.
- **HEARTBEAT.md vs the AGENTS.md heartbeat section** — HEARTBEAT.md is read per
  tick and becomes one user message tagged `request_context.source="heartbeat"`
  (which also skips auto-memory search); the `<!-- heartbeat:start/end -->`
  AGENTS.md section is kept without markers when heartbeat is on and stripped
  entirely when off.
- **Config changes apply without a restart** — a Console save reschedules the
  job; a direct `agent.json` edit is picked up by the config watcher (~2s) and
  re-registers it.

Also: notes the 30-minute fallback when `every` is present but
empty/unparsable/non-positive, and replaces the hedged "some setups may need a
restart" sentence.

One factual correction to the issue's own analysis: session load/save is not
lock-free — `save_session_state` is guarded by a per-path lock
(`src/qwenpaw/app/chats/session.py`). The real caveat is that concurrent runs on
the same session are not serialized *with each other* (last-write-wins), which
is what the new text says.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8082

**Security Considerations:** None — documentation only.

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under
my direction and review.

prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2006 - Telegram bot name concatenated to message without space

## Problem

When a bot_prefix is configured (e.g., \"George\"), the bot name was concatenated directly to the message text without any separator, resulting in:
- **Actual output:** `Georgehello how are you`
- **Expected output:** `George  hello how are you` (with space)

## Root Cause

In `console/channel.py` line 411, the bot_prefix was concatenated directly to the message text without any separator:
```python
self._safe_print(f"{self.bot_prefix}{p.text}")  # Missing space!
```

## Fix

Add two spaces between bot_prefix and message text (consistent with other places in the codebase like `base.py` line 730 and `console/channel.py` line 454):
```python
self._safe_print(f"{self.bot_prefix}  {p.text}")
```

## Testing

✅ Python syntax check passed (`python -m py_compile`)

## Impact

- Fixes message formatting when bot_prefix is configured
- Minimal change, low risk

prs.title: feat(memory): allow a separate model for ReMeLight memory writing
prs.body:
## Description

`ReMeLightMemoryManager` currently injects the agent's main model into ReMe's `as_llm` component before every memory-writing job (`auto_memory` / `auto_dream` / `daily_paper` / `auto_fin`), so memory writing always consumes the same (often expensive) model used for chatting.

This PR adds an optional `memory_model` slot to `reme_light_memory_config`, so memory writing can run on an independent, lighter model:

- Uses `{"provider_id": "...", "model": "..."}` as the canonical format; a string is treated as a bare model name that inherits the main model's provider, including version-tagged names such as `qwen2.5:7b`.
- When unset, behavior is unchanged (main model is used).
- If dedicated-model construction fails (including non-`ProviderError` SDK exceptions), the manager logs a warning and injects the usable main model. Runtime failures before output can also fall back to that model. Main-model failures still propagate. Image jobs exclude the main-model fallback unless it has confirmed image support.
- The injected model is refreshed before every LLM job, so config changes take effect without a restart.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7664

**Security Considerations:** `memory_model` stores only a provider/model reference; no credentials are written to `agent.json` (API keys stay in the provider store).

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

Not applicable — no channel code paths are touched.

- [ ] **Optional**: Unit tests in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` for complex internal logic

## Testing

Verified with `agentscope==2.0.10` and `reme-ai==0.4.2.0`:

- Backend memory/configuration/fallback/model-factory media/startup suites: **982 passed**, with one existing unawaited-coroutine warning.

- `tsc -b --noEmit`: passed.

- Prettier checks for changed Console files and both website configuration documents: passed.
- The missing-key regression exercises actual Gemini SDK construction and verifies successful main-model injection and ReMe startup. No live model-service calls were made during this verification.

- Merged `main@45c754ee` and resolved the Console, backend, and bilingual documentation conflicts.
- Preserved image-support requirements, per-model image resizing, actual-model returns, and LLM-job locking.
- The Console uses `buildEligibleProviders()`, filters unconfigured providers, preserves stale selections, and explicitly displays inherited-provider selections without changing their saved configuration.
- Model-slot resolution uses direct typed field access.

prs.title: feat(advisor): improve worker-advisor collaboration
prs.body:
## Description

Advisor guidance can miss the worker's effective system constraints or recommend an action before the evidence needed for that decision is available. This draft carries the worker's current system instructions into advisor requests and updates the guidance to make recommendations conditional on relevant evidence and prerequisites.

- Capture the effective worker system messages on every model call and forward them without truncation to opening plans, consultations, and interventions.
- Record each advisor attempt, including the submitted messages, source hashes, outcome, response, and available usage.
- Refine the advisor and consultation prompts around decision-relevant evidence, confirmed observations, proportionate checks, authorized disclosure, and conditions the worker can apply locally.
- Include the frozen P3 implementation's provenance and a `Pcurrent → P3` version pointer. Relative to P1, P3 changes only `ADVISOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT`; this upstream diff also includes the inherited context-forwarding, audit, and consultation changes.

**Related Issue:** None linked; submitted as a draft for design and implementation discussion.

**Security Considerations:** Effective worker system instructions are forwarded to the advisor, and the local audit transcript stores full request messages and replies. The advisor cannot execute tools. Prompt guidance about private data does not enforce an outbound disclosure boundary: a sender-side privacy filter is not implemented. These data flows require review before production adoption.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Breaking change

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend — Advisor Mode middleware and prompts
- [x] Documentation — experiment version and validation records

- [x] I ran relevant tests locally and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated

## Testing

- **Passed:** 163 advisor-related tests covering middleware, mode, triggers, configuration, and runtime middleware assembly.
- **Passed:** `git diff --check` and Flake8 on the three modified implementation files.
- **Passed:** all 3,400 runtime source files match the frozen experiment snapshot; the rendered advisor prompt and version-pointer hashes match.
- **Blocked:** the full pytest suite stops during collection because `dingtalk_stream` is missing from the available environment.
- **Unavailable:** `pre_commit` is not installed in the available environment.
- **Known formatting difference:** Black 23.3.0 requests two quote-style changes in `prompts.py`. The original frozen bytes are retained in this draft; the other two implementation files pass.

Exact commands and limitations are recorded in [P3-validation.json](https://github.com/jinglinpeng/CoPaw/blob/2ebc2cdf6b2ea94c7fe1b19857430ae648f450e8/docs/experiments/P3-validation.json).

## Evidence

The focused run used the existing test dependencies with this checkout's `src` first on `PYTHONPATH` and isolated QwenPaw working/state directories:

```text
python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/unit/modes/test_advisor_middleware.py \
  tests/unit/modes/test_advisor_mode.py \
  tests/unit/modes/test_advisor_trigger.py \

163 passed in 2.42s
```

The frozen implementation was used for two 600-task AutomationBench collaboration arms: 1,197 episodes completed normally and 3 model terminal errors were retained. These counts establish the recorded run coverage, not a claim of consistent quality improvement. Raw task trajectories and credentials are not included in this PR.

prs.title: feat: access local QwenPaw through the shared Platform Web App
prs.body:
## Description

Add Platform-backed Web App access to local QwenPaw. Users connect a cloud account from Console, scan a QR code to sign in on their phone, and switch between cloud and connected workspaces.

The phone loads the selected Runtime's own versioned Console, including its existing model, thinking, and mode controls. A shared workspace menu and refresh action are available across Console pages. Manual recovery obtains a fresh Console grant while keeping the selected workspace and route. Runs remain on their Runtime across Relay replacement, using the existing Console reconnect path instead of resubmitting messages. Includes Hub user isolation, reconnect and upgrade handling, a compact experimental indicator, and English/Chinese guides and launch posts.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #7378.

**Security Considerations:** QR sign-in authorizes the full Platform account through a short-lived, single-use ticket and desktop confirmation. Hub connections remain scoped to the owning user's Runtime. Platform credentials stay out of the isolated Console; forwarded routes and bodies are bounded, with flow control and explicit cancellation. Displayed and copied diagnostics redact temporary Console credentials.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Ready for review

Scoped checks pass. Full-repository lint is not claimed as clean; existing errors in unchanged frontend files remain outside this change.

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [x] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh console` and it passes
- [ ] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery)
- [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py`
- [x] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/`

Official channel plugins are unchanged. The new Platform access integration coverage is in `tests/unit/app/test_platform_web_access.py`.

## Testing

1. Start a supported standalone or Hub Runtime, open Console, and connect a cloud account from the workspace menu or phone dialog.
2. Generate a QR code, open it on a phone, complete desktop confirmation, and verify cloud/connected workspace selection. Test the in-app-browser handoff before authorization.
3. At a mobile viewport, open the existing model/thinking and loop-mode controls. Switch between owned nodes from the header and Settings menu; check uploads and history isolation.
4. Refresh from Settings and verify the selected workspace and route remain intact. In a disposable development environment, make the entry or Chat module unavailable, restore it, and verify manual recovery.
5. Verify cross-account access is rejected, disconnecting stops access, background recovery does not resend messages, and an upgrade reloads the matching Console.

## Evidence

- Cancellation/dispatch ownership has a deterministic regression check: the previous build released the run quota while encoding was paused, then dispatched the canceled request when encoding resumed. The fixed build dispatches nothing when cancellation wins; when dispatch wins, subscriber cancellation keeps the run quota until a genuine completion report. Both orderings passed ten repetitions. A canceled reconnect also preserves the existing run and sends no new operation. Encoding work retains a body credit until it unwinds.

- Related Python integration tests and Console channel contracts passed. The current recovery checks include 111 existing Console tests; type checks, scoped lint/formatting, Console/Website production builds, Monaco CSS, and initial-bundle budgets pass.
- At 375px, the workspace, refresh, terminal, and file controls stay on one row; action buttons retain 44px touch targets. Existing model/thinking and loop-mode menus open normally.
- Real entry-script and Chat-module fault injection passed: retries stop, recovery remains available, manual refresh obtains a new grant, and diagnostics hide that grant. Refresh also preserves the Settings route.
- Two connected nodes with distinct Console build identifiers passed resource integrity, uploads/previews, early SSE delivery, history recovery, grant renewal/revocation, and account isolation. Cloud destination selection uses the existing backend resolver and passed ownership/routing checks; a real cloud deployment remains untested.
- The companion data plane now runs separately from account/control requests. With a model fixture that kept all five runs active, a single account used two nodes while 250 Console resources returned 200 with matching SHA-256 in 4.13 seconds, including a 7,021,308-byte file. The slowest four-API control probe took 1.13 seconds. Control requests, stop, upload limits, grant revocation and cross-node isolation passed. Disconnecting a subscriber preserves the logical run quota; genuine completion or stop releases it.
- Companion access checks rejected unauthenticated, foreign-account, foreign-origin, revoked-grant, and cross-node requests. Invalid credential probes were rate-limited while a valid owned grant remained usable. The relevant companion backend suites and scoped Python lint/type checks passed. The current Runtime integration subset has 19 passing tests; the companion backend has 51 passing checks.
- Staging browser verification confirmed a real model reply and conversation recovery. Staging HTTPS/HTTP/2 resource reads at concurrency 32 also passed integrity checks.
- Relay transport profiling used six 4-vCPU/4-GiB replicas (12,000 stream slots and a 512 MiB buffer budget per replica for this fixture) and three independent load processes on the isolated development host: 10,000 synthetic users, five active streams each, 2 frames/s and 1,040 bytes/frame, with a three-minute soak and a one-minute regression of the final build. All 50,000 streams remained active, with zero errors, approximately 99 MiB/s and p99 at or below the 50 ms histogram bucket. A separate 5,000-stream/20-frames-per-second profile also passed. These tests cover the data plane; they exclude public TLS/SLB, real agents and model-provider capacity.
- With the long-running model fixture, owner-crash recovery took 1.43 seconds and graceful drain migration took 5.77 seconds, including the planned drain delay. The running task retained its logical run lease; reconnection replayed the existing task, and stop released the quota. Slow-reader, maximum 8 MiB upload, stale-epoch, one-use-ticket and legacy-socket admission checks passed. Empty reconnect responses and delayed Runtime reports cannot release a still-running task slot; reservations are acquired after queue admission and completion is reported independently of the HTTP stream.
- **Open acceptance item:** a previous staging 250-request burst produced 143 successes and 107 Nginx HTML 503 responses; invalid-grant requests reproduced failures before Relay execution. This refactor has not been released or retested there. Public-ingress behavior and production capacity remain unverified.

Screenshots are hosted on GitHub and referenced by the guides; image files and development plans are excluded from the final diff:

- [Local Console workspace menu and phone entry (demo environment)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99a956a4-8e86-4b74-903f-e76ba134ba03)
- [Shared Console model/thinking controls at a mobile viewport (demo environment)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41b91808-9712-4541-b3de-e762dd5b958d)

## Additional Notes

Keep this PR in draft until the staging ingress 503 investigation, real cloud deployment switching, and physical-device installation/browser-handoff acceptance are complete. Browser viewport checks are not iOS, Android, or HarmonyOS device certification.

Requires a compatible companion Platform frontend/backend deployment, including the separate Relay service and updated Nginx routes. The autoscaling manifest also needs the cluster custom-metrics adapter. Its default budget is 4,096 stream slots per replica with an HPA stream target of 2,500; the six-replica transport fixture used explicit higher limits. Kubernetes HPA execution and public-ingress capacity have not been certified by these local tests. Runtime users continue to configure a single Platform URL. Older Runtimes without Web App protocol support must upgrade. Each supported Runtime supplies its own Console; there is no need to build every historical frontend into Platform.

This revision changes only the companion Relay data plane. Public ingress/TLS/SLB and Kubernetes HPA execution still require staging acceptance. An unsynchronized load-generator teardown produced a 250 ms tail for the remaining shard after two other shards disconnected together; the steady-state rerun uses a shared start/end barrier and snapshots results before teardown. This is recorded separately from the steady-state capacity result.

The cancellation fix was rebuilt and rerun with a coordinated three-generator measurement window: all 50,000 active streams held for three minutes, with zero errors, about 99 MiB/s, p95 at the 5 ms histogram bucket and p99 at the 50 ms bucket. All six replicas returned to zero stream slots and buffered bytes. The 51 relevant Java tests and 19 Runtime Python tests passed, along with maximum-upload, slow-reader, quota, reconnect, owner-crash and planned-drain checks. The current five-task/250-resource test completed in 6.04 seconds; its slowest four-API probe took 1.88 seconds. Owner-crash recovery was 1.36 seconds; planned drain migration took 25.27 seconds including the configured spread-out closing delay, while the task remained running.

prs.title: fix(providers): use declared Responses thinking-off control
prs.body:
## Description

When `disable_thinking=True` reaches the OpenAI Responses adapter, inherited `reasoning` settings are removed. The adapter previously restored `reasoning.effort=none` only for a hard-coded list of model names, even when another model's declared `ThinkingControl` supports turning reasoning off.

Pass the model's declared off mapping into the Responses adapter. A declared native control that supports off now sends `reasoning.effort=none`; unknown or unsupported controls still do not receive guessed parameters, and the existing documented-model fallback remains.
