prs.title: fix(gateway): record the canonical OIDC certificate actor
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** The OIDC enrollment route used to prepend `oidc:` to a principal ID that already carries that prefix. It now copies the validated principal ID into the certificate ledger. The route test compares the complete stored actor with the identity derived from the test issuer and subject.
- **Scope boundary** This changes attribution on newly issued OIDC client certificates. Existing actor labels stay in the ledger as recorded. Operators can list either spelling and revoke certificates by device.
- **Blast radius** Consumers that filter the raw actor field should recognize both historical and current spellings. The operator guide shows both.
- **Linked issue(s)** Closes #12333. Follows the certificate issuance flow introduced in #12317.

### What this does, simply

When an operator looks up a certificate issued during sign-in, its actor now matches the user's OIDC principal exactly. Older certificates can still be found and revoked with their device ID.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The enrollment test needs a runner that allows local TCP listeners.
- **Interface(s) exercised** Gateway OIDC certificate endpoint and operator CLI.
- **Setup / preconditions** Use the gateway crate's existing local OIDC and mTLS fixtures.
- **Steps to run** Run `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib previously_unknown_human_bootstraps_without_pairing_or_enroll_listener`. The test drives sign-in and reads the issued SQLite row.
- **Expected on this branch** The row's actor equals `PrincipalId::for_oidc(issuer, subject)`.
- **Prior behavior on master** The row prepends `oidc:` to that ID a second time.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change** The gateway crate's route test covers the authenticated writer. The runtime ledger suite covers the SQLite read and revoke paths.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any** The local WireMock fixture could not open a loopback port. The named enrollment and historical-row regressions both passed on the signed PR head in the hosted Linux Test job. [Linux Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44242085049/job/134592156654)
- **Commands run and tail output**
  - `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib historical_oidc_actor_remains_listed_and_revocable_by_device` reported `1 passed; 0 failed`.
  - Running all `security::cert_ledger::tests::` in that compiled test binary reported `45 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib previously_unknown_human_bootstraps_without_pairing_or_enroll_listener` compiled the regression. WireMock reported `Failed to bind an OS port for a mock server` and `PermissionDenied` before reaching the assertion.
  - `cargo build --locked --offline -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime,plugins-wasm --bin zeroclaw` passed. The binary reported `zeroclaw 0.9.0 (v0.9.0-12-g12672f024e)`.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` passed. The docs quality gate reported `Summary: 0 error(s)`. The docs link gate passed its six tests and found zero added links.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the ledger's read and revocation queries. Actor text is display metadata. A reopened database returned a historical actor exactly as written, and device revocation marked its fingerprint revoked.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact plain-text output. The changed field is an operator-visible string.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path** The SQLite suite, gateway test, and operator CLI were built from `12672f024e` on `cda933e6b9`. The signed head `8131bff862` applies the same patch on updated master `115a03b517`. The hosted Linux enrollment run passed on this head. The CLI used an isolated configuration, English locale, and a temporary ledger containing both actor forms.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence** From `zeroclaw security list-client-certs --json`, the `device_id` and `actor` fields for the two synthetic rows were:

  ```text
  device-current     oidc:https%3A//issuer.example:subject
  device-historical  oidc:oidc:https%3A//issuer.example:subject
  ```

- **Action or changed state and observed result** Running `zeroclaw security revoke-client-cert --device device-historical` removed only that device from the active list. Its original actor remained readable in the reopened ledger.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why** The full workspace suite is left to CI. The local runner cannot exercise the route's network fixtures.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The changed value is the existing authenticated human principal used for certificate attribution.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The database schema accepts both strings. External exact-match filters that need the full device history should check both forms.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? The operator CLI's actor field reflects the corrected value for new OIDC entries. Command syntax is unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users No migration. Device ID and fingerprint remain the supported revocation keys.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path** Revert the implementing commit. Both forms of already-recorded entries remain valid after rollback.
- **Feature flags or config toggles** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms** A newly issued OIDC certificate contains a second `oidc:` prefix, or an operator cannot find an active historical device by its certificate listing.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A.

prs.title: feat(gateway): move plugin webhook admission and dedup into a core ingress
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`7666a52abf`). **Depends on #11339** (the reservation store move); the branch merges #11339 at `59875788c1`, and its changes show in the diff until it lands. #11318 (plugin webhook golden frames and CI leg) landed on 2026-11-03 as `ee8a753dff` and is part of the base now.
- **Restacked onto #11339 (maintainer decision on this PR):** #11339 lands first and moves the reservation store into `zeroclaw-api` with no behavior change. This PR now uses that store, `WebhookReservationStore`, instead of a store of its own, and keeps the ingress (route lookup, queue admission, the deadline) in `zeroclaw-infra`. On top of #11339 it makes the dedup behavior change described under **Behavior change** below.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-03 (`e40a47518f`):** merges master `ee8a753dff`, which is #11318 squash-merged, so #11318's changes no longer show in this diff; the merge also brings the 77 master commits since this branch's previous base `24938afc6d`. The four conflicts were all in files #11318 added or edited (`.github/workflows/README.md`, `golden_frames.rs`, the plugin backend change filter and its test): master's version of each is exactly #11318's final content, and this branch's version is that content plus the lines this PR adds on top of it, so every conflict resolves to this branch's side. #11339 stays merged at `59875788c1`.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-08 (`f3b02467e6`, `988d9bffe4`):** merges master `7666a52abf`, which brings the 45 master commits since `ee8a753dff`: #12270 (the relay serves a daemon's dashboard at a per-node host), #11406 (macOS broad roots refused in the filesystem channel), #11964 (orphaned remote sessions retired), #11965 (opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in), #12232 (principal-unaware tools withheld from non-admins), #11149 (cron approval and authority enforced at the write), #12239 (current authority held through session effects), #11218 (schema v4 migration), #12213, #12157, #12233, #12114, #12273 (vodozemac 0.11.2) and a batch of test-only and docs commits. One conflict, in `src/main.rs`: #12270 hoists the `GatewaySupervision` construction out of the gateway call so it can attach the relay dashboard ingress, and this branch hands that constructor the core `PluginWebhookIngress` in place of the registry; the merged closure clones the ingress, builds `supervision` from it, applies master's `with_dashboard_ingress` step and passes `supervision` to `run_gateway_with_plugin_webhooks`. Against this branch the merged file changes exactly as master did (278 added, 28 removed) and against master exactly as this branch did (14 added, 5 removed). A second, semantic conflict surfaced in `cargo check`: master's new `relay_dashboard_ingress` integration test builds its `GatewaySupervision` with a bare `PluginWebhookRegistry`, which this branch's constructor no longer accepts; `988d9bffe4` builds that test's `PluginWebhookIngress` from the fixture config's idempotency settings, the way `run_gateway` does. #11339 stays merged at `59875788c1`.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-10 (`3f132f42f3`):** merges master `a11a5ce5b4`, which is #12244 (scoped dashboard chat through the core on a shared RPC client, carrying the `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` extraction and `zeroclaw-rpc-client` that #11320 and #11322 build on) and #12359. One conflict, the CI README: #12244 extends the Installer Drift row with the OpenRPC drift check and this branch extends the Plugin gateway ingress row beneath it, so the merged file keeps master's Installer Drift row and this branch's ingress row (one changed line against each parent). #11339 stays merged at `59875788c1`.
- **Fix of 2026-11-13 (`c69d072224`, `addaf1fcc1`):** the Security job's `cargo audit` fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0538, published after master's last Security run: `quinn-udp` 0.5.14 can spin its receive loop after a truncated datagram on the targets that read one datagram per call (macOS without the fast datapath, the BSDs, illumos), and master's lockfile pins the same version. `c69d072224` bumps it to 0.5.16, the patched release inside quinn's semver range; because that `cargo update` also let the resolver move nine unrelated `windows-sys` edges to older majors, `addaf1fcc1` puts those back so the net lockfile change is quinn-udp's own entry (version, checksum and its `windows-sys` edge). Master needs the same one-line bump.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-17 (`faeaff79c5`):** merges master `e59e65f04e`, the 29 commits since `a11a5ce5b4`: v0.9.0 (#12377), #12419 (quinn-udp 0.5.16 on master, so the 2026-11-13 entry below now matches master's), #12392 (rustix for RUSTSEC-2026-0486), #12516 (zip for RUSTSEC-2026-0548), #12417 (the plugin wake-dispatch exception row), #12281 (SOP cancel treats a forwarded loopback address as non-local), #12151, #12149, #12115, #12237, #12379, #12352, #12368, #12363, the web dependency bumps and fixes, and docs. One conflict, the gateway's `lib.rs`: #12281 adds `request_is_local` directly above `normalize_max_keys`, which this branch moves to `zeroclaw_infra`, so the merged file keeps master's new function and this branch's move. Against this branch the file gains exactly master's 32 added lines (the function and its test), and against master it shows exactly this branch's own change. #11339 stays merged at `59875788c1`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Channel-plugin webhook dispatch was split between the gateway handler (route lookup, queue admission, the 10 s deadline) and the gateway's idempotency store (message dedup), both reached through in-process handles. A gateway in another process could reach neither. This moves all four into one core-owned service with a single entry point, so the next PR can expose it over RPC unchanged.
  - `zeroclaw-infra`: new `plugin_webhook` module. `PluginWebhookIngress` owns the route registry, per-route queue admission, the deadline counted from enqueue, and message dedup in #11339's `WebhookReservationStore`, with the same owner, in-flight, rollback and generation-fencing semantics as before. `dispatch(request, cancel)` returns a typed outcome; dropping or cancelling it cancels the worker's copy of the request.
  - `zeroclaw-api`: shared limits and path grammar, the route owner (`PluginWebhookOwner`), a validating `PluginWebhookRequest` (redacting `Debug`; header names limited to what `http`'s `HeaderName` accepts, values to what `HeaderValue::to_str` yields), and `PluginWebhookOutcome`. Routes now carry their owner.
  - `zeroclaw-gateway`: the `/plugin/{path}` handler is an HTTP adapter over `dispatch` with a pure outcome-to-response mapping. The idempotency store keeps only the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay path.
  - The gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store keeps #11339's `WebhookReservationStore` backing, with a store of its own for each gateway run.
- **Behavior change (dedup, on top of #11339):**
  - **Lifetime:** plugin webhook dedup lasts for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run. A gateway restart inside the generation keeps it; a reload or daemon restart still clears it.
  - **Budget:** plugin deliveries get a committed-key budget of their own (`gateway.idempotency_max_keys`), no longer shared with `/webhook` and `/sop/*`. A burst of generic keys can no longer push out plugin keys, or the reverse. The worst case is twice that many committed keys across the two stores.
  - **Key:** dedup keys include the owning plugin and channel alias, so two instances never collide and a path that changes owner starts clean. #11339's pinned unscoped key no longer applies.
  - Tests that pinned the old behavior in #11339 (per-run lifetime, shared budget, unscoped key) are replaced by `plugin_webhook_dedup_state_outlives_a_gateway_router`, `plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets` and `dedup_key_separates_every_identity_component`. #11339's store tests stay in `zeroclaw-api`.
- **Follow-up from the review, not in this PR:** a per-owner share of the dedup budget, #11565.
- **Webhook paths stay out of failure logs (`fc5f3e95b9`, from Audacity88's review of #11322):** some vendors use an unguessable webhook path as their shared secret, and log records are persisted as written. The ingress's `plugin_webhook_route_closed`, `plugin_webhook_reply_dropped`, `plugin_webhook_unauthorized`, `plugin_webhook_invalid` and `plugin_webhook_unavailable` records and the gateway's `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` record no longer carry the path; the owner's plugin and channel alias still identify the route. `dispatch_logs_route_and_worker_failures_by_owner_without_the_path` and `plugin_webhook_bounds_record_keeps_a_secret_path_out` send requests to secret-shaped paths and assert that no record contains them. The gateway's `plugin_webhook_rate_limited` record still logs the path, as on master. #11320 merges the same commit, so #11322 carries it too.
- **Scope boundary:** No other HTTP-visible change: the PR 1 plugin webhook golden frames replay byte-identical. No WIT, config schema, `zeroclaw-plugins`, or `zeroclaw-channels` change. No RPC surface (next PR).
- **Blast radius:** plugin webhook ingress in the supervised and standalone gateway; the gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store (same behavior, #11339's implementation, its own budget); route publication in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/plugin_runtime.rs` (mechanical: routes gain an owner, and the grammar and queue depth come from shared definitions; no new functionality, so no holding-crate exception row is needed for it).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000.

### What this does, simply

When a chat platform calls a channel plugin's webhook, several things have to happen before the plugin sees the request: find which plugin owns the URL, check its queue has room, start a deadline, and make sure a message the platform retries is not delivered twice. That work was spread across the web gateway. This PR puts it in one place in the core, so a gateway running as its own process can later ask the core to do it.

One thing changes on purpose. The core remembers delivered message IDs for as long as the daemon runs its current configuration, not just while one gateway process lives, so restarting the gateway no longer forgets them; reloading the config still does. Plugin messages also get their own memory, so a flood of other webhooks cannot make the core forget them, and each plugin channel's IDs are kept apart. This only suppresses platform retries; it is not a security check, which stays with each plugin's signature verification.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the PR 1 golden frames replay the public HTTP contract byte-identical, and the root e2e test drives a real WASM guest through the ingress.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (plugins gateway ingress)` (gateway plugin webhook tests and golden frames), `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with the real guest, runtime plugin admission tests), `Test` (infra and api units, gateway default-feature tests), `Lint`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-api` alone does not compile on master (its manifest lacks tokio's `time` feature, which `channel.rs` uses); the api tests run through workspace feature unification, as in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `98e1666b31`: this PR on master `a0f70b7925` with #11339 `59875788c1` merged; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
test result: ok. 292 passed ; test result: ok. 331 passed   (api includes #11339's store tests; infra includes plugin_webhook::*)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib
test result: ok. 636 passed ; test result: ok. 653 passed   (includes plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --test golden_frames plugin_webhook   (x2)
test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; fixtures unchanged
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --test golden_frames -- --include-ignored
test result: ok. 12 passed
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e
test result: ok. 5 passed (includes a_repeated_message_id_is_delivered_once_through_the_core_ingress)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime::
test result: ok. 17 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-gateway [--features zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm] --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings ; cargo clippy --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings (all three)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check ; bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh ; bash scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh ; docs quality gate on the changed docs
clean ; passed ; pass ; 0 errors
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each caught by the new tests: a longer or shorter deadline, the wrong log level, key or alias, dropping `"` from the allowed header-name bytes, removing the header-name length bound, and one eviction assertion. A 256-byte sweep compares the header-name rule with `http::HeaderName` byte by byte.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Log path redaction (`fc5f3e95b9`, head `a63bcc6f89`):** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib plugin_webhook` (17 passed), `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib plugin_webhook` (15 passed), and clippy on `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-infra` and `zeroclaw-gateway` with and without `plugins-wasm` (no warnings). Mutation check: putting the path back into either record fails its test.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-03 (head `e40a47518f`):** on the merged tree: fmt; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib plugin_webhook` 17 passed; gateway lib `plugin_webhook` with `plugins-wasm` 15 passed; the plugin webhook golden frames 5 passed against the recorded fixtures; gateway clippy with `plugins-wasm`, and infra plus api clippy, (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed; the root `architecture` target 82 passed; `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` 5 passed; `plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh` and `windows_test_scope.test.sh` pass; the docs quality and link gates on the changed docs. The parallel runtime gate script (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6010 tests, and the channels suite, 2051 tests, at 16 threads) was green on its second run. On the first run one runtime pass failed master's `tools::delegate::tests::background_agentic_delegate_persists_localized_semantic_empty_error`, whose background task has five seconds to get through a retrying provider wrapper and three empty completions and took longer under the 16-thread load; this PR does not touch that tool or its test (its only runtime change is `plugin_runtime.rs`), the test alone passed five times in about 1.7 s each, and the delegate test module passed three times at 16 threads.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-08 (head `988d9bffe4`):** on the merged tree: fmt; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift` (the first run failed on master's new `relay_dashboard_ingress` test until `988d9bffe4`); `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib` 350 passed; gateway lib `plugin_webhook` with `plugins-wasm` 15 passed; the plugin webhook golden frames 5 passed against the recorded fixtures; gateway, infra and api clippy and the root crate's clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed; the root `architecture` target 86 passed; `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` 5 passed; `plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh` and `windows_test_scope.test.sh` pass; the docs quality and link gates on the six changed docs files. The parallel runtime gate script (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6177 tests, and the channels suite, 2058 tests, at 16 threads) green on the first run.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-10 (head `3f132f42f3`):** on the merged tree: fmt; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib` 350 passed; gateway lib `plugin_webhook` with `plugins-wasm` 15 passed; the plugin webhook golden frames 5 passed against the recorded fixtures; gateway, infra and api clippy and the root crate's clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed; the root `architecture` target 90 passed; `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` 5 passed; `plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh` and `windows_test_scope.test.sh` pass; the docs quality and link gates on the six changed docs files. The parallel runtime gate script (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6199 tests, and the channels suite, 2059 tests, at 16 threads) green on the first run.
- **Fix of 2026-11-13 (head `addaf1fcc1`):** lockfile-only: `cargo metadata --locked` accepts the result, and the net change against `3f132f42f3` is the three lines of quinn-udp's entry; no Rust source changed, so the hosted CI on this head is the build and test evidence for the bump.
- **Refresh of 2026-11-17 (head `faeaff79c5`):** on the merged tree: fmt; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` with and without `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib` 350 passed; gateway lib `plugin_webhook` with `plugins-wasm` 15 passed; the plugin webhook golden frames 5 passed against the recorded fixtures; gateway, infra and api clippy and the root crate's clippy (`--all-targets`, `-D warnings`) clean; `runtime-composition-consumer` 10 passed; the root `architecture` target 90 passed; `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` 5 passed; `plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh` and `windows_test_scope.test.sh` pass; the docs quality and link gates on the six changed docs files. The parallel runtime gate script (three passes each of the runtime suite, 6233 tests, and the channels suite, 2059 tests, at 16 threads) green on the first run.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace clippy with `ci-all` is left to CI. The comment hygiene gate did not run locally for the redaction commit (this machine's ripgrep cannot load its pcre2 library); CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (plugin secrets stay in the guest; header values pass through as before). The new and moved failure records leave out the webhook path, which some vendors use as their shared secret.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The ingress re-validates every request with bounds that are supersets of what the HTTP layer admits, so nothing new reaches the guest.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for HTTP clients and plugins. Intended behavior changes, relative to #11339 (which keeps today's behavior):
  - Dedup lives for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run, so it survives gateway supervisor restarts; it still starts empty after a daemon reload or restart. In plain terms: restarting the gateway no longer lets a platform's retry of an already-delivered message through.
  - Dedup keys include the owning plugin and alias, so a path that changes owner starts clean.
  - Plugin dedup has its own capacity (from `gateway.idempotency_max_keys`) instead of sharing the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` store; the worst case is twice that many committed keys across both stores. In plain terms: heavy traffic on one kind of webhook no longer makes the other kind forget recent message IDs.
  - Dedup remains best effort: a key can still be displaced inside its TTL once the plugin store is full, and it is not replay protection (the plugin docs now say so).
  - Outcome logs (`plugin_webhook_unauthorized`, `plugin_webhook_invalid`, `plugin_webhook_unavailable`) now come from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook` with plugin and channel alias, and no longer the path. New WARN keys `plugin_webhook_route_closed` and `plugin_webhook_reply_dropped` replace two silent 503 paths. A request outside the ingress bounds gets 400 `invalid webhook` with `plugin_webhook_request_invalid`, also without the path (the HTTP listener's own header and URI limits normally refuse such a request first).
  - Rust API: `PluginWebhookRegistry::get` returns a `PluginWebhookRoute`; `GatewaySupervision::new` takes `Arc<PluginWebhookIngress>` in place of #11339's registry and per-run store, so #11339's `zeroclaw_gateway::plugin_webhook_reservations` and `IdempotencyStore::shared` are removed; `zeroclaw_gateway::IDEMPOTENCY_MAX_KEYS_DEFAULT` moved to `zeroclaw_infra` (no workspace users). Experimental crates.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. No persisted state, WIT, or config changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `plugins.enabled = false` or a build without `plugins-wasm` disables plugin webhook routes, as before.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_*` error keys from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook`; duplicate deliveries after a gateway restart would indicate dedup regressions; golden-frame drift in the plugin gateway CI leg.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject updates to fields owned by declarations
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** The cron store refuses attempts to patch a declarative job's command, name, schedule, session target, allowed tools, or memory setting. The daemon reads those values from the declaration on startup. A successful database update used to disappear at the next sync.
- **Scope boundary** The refusal occurs inside the existing transaction, after the ownership and authorization checks and before any patch fields are applied. It reports the exact `config.toml` key in all five built-in CLI locales.
- **Blast radius** CLI, RPC and tool callers that use the shared cron update path. Runtime-created jobs retain their existing update behavior.
- **Linked issue** Closes #9770. Related #9350. Draft for the existing assignee to review; #10836 separately covers reassignment when a declaration changes owner.

### What this does, simply

If a schedule was declared in a config file, changing it in the database cannot survive a daemon restart. The command now points the operator to the setting the daemon actually reads, and leaves the whole row intact if part of the request is refused.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The store regression materializes a declaration, tries each field, and runs startup reconciliation. The component regression exercises the real CLI against a materialized job.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change** The cron store suite covers synchronization, transactions, and existing job ownership rules. The component suite checks the exit code, error message and stored command at the CLI boundary.
- **Known CI coverage gap** The local CLI build used `agent-runtime` with default features disabled. Storage behavior is shared with gateway builds.
- **Commands and output** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib cron::store::tests::` passed 106 tests. `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime --test component cron_delivery_cli` passed four. Workspace formatting, diff checks and both docs gates passed.
- **Beyond CI** On the original store a forbidden command edit returned a successful job row. On the fixed store, all six attempts fail before a companion update to `enabled` can change the row. The same patches succeed for an imperative job. An independent `enabled` update still succeeds for a declarative job.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact plain-text output. A fixture that materializes a genuine declarative row supplied the temporary SQLite database for both operator checks.
- **Tested revision and interface** The signed branch head `5364ed0ce9` has tested tree `dc053c12da`. Binary tested: `zeroclaw 0.9.0 (v0.9.0-15-g5ec3ded5f8)`, `zeroclaw cron update decl_job --agent default --command 'echo edited'`.
- **Exact output** English: `Error: Edit [cron.decl_job].command in config.toml and restart the daemon to update this declarative job.` French: `Error: Modifiez [cron.decl_job].command dans config.toml et redémarrez le démon pour mettre à jour cette tâche déclarative.`
- **Action and observed result** Both commands exited 1. The stored command was still `echo declarative`.
- **Other checks** The regression exercises the existing reconciliation function directly, without starting a background scheduler.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the change? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced or changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Callers that relied on a successful response for a transient edit must update the declaration instead. The CLI flags and stored schema are compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? A config-owned patch now exits 1 with the key to edit.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps? Edit the named field in `[cron.<id>]` and restart the daemon to apply it.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback** Revert this PR on a review branch. The store will again accept transient edits to these declarative fields until the next sync.
- **Feature flags or toggles** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms** A valid patch on an imperative job fails, or a refused mixed patch modifies the declarative row.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A.

prs.title: feat(web): manage write-only plugin TLS credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch is `master`.
- Add a write-only operator panel under Config → Storage → Secrets for credentials already referenced by a plugin TLS profile.
- Reuse the canonical encrypted plugin configuration and existing host-mediated TLS authorization. The catalog returns instance, property, destinations and configured state.
- This is the first implementation slice of Related #12373. The broader catalog, reversible disable, and references usable by other consumers are open design work. This PR leaves the issue open.

### What this does, simply

An authenticated operator can provision a PEM value for a configured plugin TLS profile without putting the value in a chat. Rotation and deletion use the existing configuration commit path. New connections continue to use the existing instance and destination checks.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- Pair the dashboard, enable encryption with an initialized key, and configure a plugin TLS profile referencing a schema-declared secret.
- Open Storage → Secrets → Plugin TLS credentials. Set, replace, refresh and delete a synthetic PEM value. Inspect the responses and verify they contain only metadata or configured state.
- On master, the dedicated panel is absent.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --tests -j2` completed successfully.
- Web TypeScript type checking passed. The four existing read-only configuration UI regression tests passed.
- Rust formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Added a real config-router test for scoped-principal rejection, missing key, encrypted persistence, duplicate creation, replacement and deletion. The gateway test exposed a deletion failure. The follow-up persists only the selected credential and tests that neighboring ciphertext and the TLS profile survive. The current-head gateway test is pending CI. A Chrome walkthrough of the real WebUI with a synthetic API passed create, replace, refresh, delete, and draft clearing on cancel. This browser test did not use a live gateway.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new route requires a current authenticated administrator. It accepts only existing TLS binding slots.
- New external network calls? No.
- Credential handling changed? Yes. Bounded request bodies carry write-only values. The route requires encryption and an existing key, returns metadata with no-store, and emits mutation metadata without the submitted value.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the diff or fixtures? No.
- Model-visible inputs or prompt injection surface changed? No.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config, env or CLI surface changed? No. The API and dashboard gain a panel for existing bindings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

Revert this change to remove the panel and route. Values already saved remain standard plugin configuration. Restore a known-good encrypted configuration backup to undo a credential rotation or deletion, and retain the corresponding encryption key. Watch for unexpected 403, 409 or 412 responses on the new route and for connection failures after credential edits.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.

- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 10; reference implementation `921b8ee993a0b2439a0c2c41cb84337270942a06`. Depends on #12450.

### What this does, simply

The terminal setup and configuration screens need to edit the same connections and models that the backend resolves. This change switches Zerocode to exact registry keys and adds connection/model editing, replacing the old provider-profile workflow. The exact-head ZeroCode edit/save/reopen workflow has been verified with the matching daemon and synthetic data; the reopened registry shows the persisted model and masked credential.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the interactive workflow below supplements the passing required CI gate.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `tui`, exercised interactively at `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c` with the matching daemon; English locale, xterm 160 columns × 50 rows.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits. Use an isolated V5 configuration with a synthetic `openai.demo.gateway` connection, a `chat.demo.gateway` model and an enabled agent referencing that model and a supervised risk profile. Build ZeroCode and its matching daemon together.
- **Steps to run:** Run `cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins`; launch `target/debug/zerocode --config-dir <isolated-config-dir>`. Open Config → Provider registry → providers.registry. Change `models["chat.demo.gateway"].model` from `gpt-synthetic-before` to `gpt-synthetic-after`, press Ctrl+S, then press Enter to reopen the registry.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The TUI reads and writes V5 registry documents, preserves complete model names and reports edit failures without discarding the draft.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The TUI edits provider-family tables and derives selections by splitting profile references.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c`, CI Required Gate, Test, Lint and Zerocode RPC Boundary pass. These cover compilation, automated tests and RPC boundary checks. The actual terminal interaction is covered separately by the exact-head evidence below. The report-only risk workflow fails on file-evidence/head binding.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** This manual run covers registry editing, Ctrl+S persistence, reopening, dotted keys and credential masking. Quickstart and chat model selection were not manually exercised in this run; no old #9809 screenshot is substituted for the ZeroCode result.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0, no formatting diff. `git diff --check`: exit 0, no whitespace errors. `cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins`: exit 0, both binaries built in this worktree’s `target` directory.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran the actual ZeroCode registry edit/save/reopen sequence against the matching local daemon. Parsed the persisted TOML independently and confirmed the literal dotted model key holds the updated value; the credential was not replaced by the mask, and the terminal capture does not contain the stored credential. No provider inference request was made.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Direct screenshot of the reopened actual xterm/ZeroCode interface, using synthetic data. Captured with ImageMagick `import` on an isolated Xvfb display; the UI was not reconstructed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `904b56d40d7849f69ee6aff31952fd141949723c`; `tui`, 160×50 terminal, November 16, 2026. [Evidence and reproduction record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/README.md). Evidence files are on a standalone fork branch and do not change this implementation PR’s diff.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Direct reopened-editor screenshot](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/zerocode-registry-reopened.png), [save-result capture](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/saved-terminal.txt), [reopened-editor capture](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/reopened-terminal.txt).

  ![Actual ZeroCode registry after Ctrl+S and reopening: updated dotted-key model and masked credential](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/8ceccb989b7eff9bac4090242db52288568293aa/zerocode-registry-reopened.png)

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Ctrl+S returned `Saved "providers"`. Reopening displayed `"model": "gpt-synthetic-after"` under the intact `chat.demo.gateway` key, `"api_key": "***MASKED***"` and `No pending edits`. The saved TOML independently contains the updated model value. Result: PASS.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full test/clippy matrix was run; the existing required CI covers it. A local build and focused real TUI interaction were performed to fill the reviewer-identified evidence gap.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No additional permissions.

prs.title: fix(sop): keep terminal runs closed in SQLite
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Install a SQLite trigger when the SOP store opens. It rejects a write that changes `sop_runs.terminal` from 1 to 0, including the update in an older writer's upsert.
  - Cover fresh databases and an existing database whose legacy writer already has the file open. Document what that writer will see during a mixed-version upgrade.
- **Scope boundary:** This change guards updates of the terminal flag. Run creation, normal completion, idempotent terminal writes and retention deletes keep their current behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Processes sharing the durable SQLite SOP run history, including older daemons or CLIs. The in-memory store has no schema migration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11947. Follow-up to #11861.

### What this does, simply

**Release note.** When an updated daemon or CLI opens an existing SOP `runs.db`, it installs the guard without rewriting the stored runs. An older process sharing that file gets a SQLite constraint error if it tries to mark a finished run active again. The run retains its terminal state and history.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The tests open real SQLite databases and issue the older writer's SQL directly on a separate connection.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Local tests exercise the SQLite store, its WAL-backed file initialization and the application-level terminal and revision guards.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The mixed-version check executes the older SQL directly through SQLite. A full previous-release daemon was not started.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - With only the two regression tests applied to the base, `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib sop::store::sqlite::tests` reported `15 passed; 2 failed`. Both failing assertions received `Ok(1)` for a write that reopened the terminal row.
  - On the submitted tree, `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib sop::store::` reported `34 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: both exited 0.
  - `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` for the SOP guide: `Summary: 0 error(s)`. `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` reported `Ran 6 tests`, `OK`, and zero added links.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran the same transition matrix directly through Python’s SQLite driver on a fresh database and an upgraded database. Normal updates (0→0, 0→1, 1→1) succeeded. An older connection attempting a 1→0 UPSERT received `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_TRIGGER`; every stored field matched the pre-write row.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This is a database constraint.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The 34 store tests ran at `6a9ef3d308`. The signed commit `eb3f598814` replays the same patch on `115a03b517`. The raw SQLite transition tests also passed on the integrated tree, including the legacy writer on an upgraded database.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** A rejected raw write returns `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_TRIGGER`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Reopening the database installed the guard with the older connection still open. A rejected upsert left the original revision, terminal flag, timestamp and JSON intact.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace testing was left to CI. This change touches one SQLite schema and its operator documentation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Existing databases, valid writes and readers are compatible. Older writers attempting to reverse a terminal flag now receive a SQLite constraint error.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: Opening the store installs the guard automatically. Update older processes sharing the file if they still attempt the refused transition.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this commit. An installed trigger persists across binary rollbacks. To restore the old database behavior, stop all updated writers, back up the database, and run `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_sop_runs_keep_terminal;` on that database. Reopening with the updated binary reinstalls the guard.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A legacy write trying to reopen a finished SOP run receives `a terminal SOP run cannot be reopened`.

N/A.

prs.title: fix(sop): preserve a completed step when cancellation wins the write
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** A driver can finish a step and lose the race to persist it when another engine requests cancellation. When the adopted row is that cancellation of the same step attempt, carry the newly recorded step result through the refusal and append it to the adopted run before writing the terminal cancellation. The maintenance retry uses the same rule.
- **Scope boundary** The change carries one locally executed result. The stored run supplies its history prefix, current step, status, revision and cancellation request. If multiple unseen row revisions have elapsed, the same step number alone cannot prove it is the same attempt. The stored history wins in that case. No database schema changes.
- **Blast radius** SOP result handling after a refused driver write, and maintenance finalization of a requested cancellation.
- **Linked issue(s)** Closes #11948. Follow-up to #11861.

### What this does, simply

A step can finish at the same moment another process cancels its run. Operators could then see a cancelled run whose history omitted work the step had already done. The cancellation now retains that result when the stored step and revision confirm it belongs to the same attempt.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The SQLite regressions establish the ordering of the writes deterministically.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change** The runtime library's SOP engine tests cover dispatch, terminal writes, maintenance retries, and durable cancellation. The regression tests use independent engine instances and SQLite. They also assert the run-detail projection from a reopened database.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any** The race is injected at the store boundary. The tests run locally without a production daemon, network, provider, or external tool.
- **Commands run and tail output**
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib remote_cancel` on the original implementation with strengthened regression checks: `2 passed; 3 failed`. Both driver write paths and the maintenance path omitted the expected result.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib sop::engine::tests::` on the repaired implementation: `254 passed; 0 failed`.
  - Removed only the stored-revision guard and ran `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib remote_cancel_after_another_visit`. The regression found `["late result"]` where the authoritative later attempt had no recorded result. Restoring the guard restored the passing engine suite.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Examined both write paths and the persisted histories. Refusing a write only carries the first new result beyond the committed prefix when the next durable revision requested cancellation of that step. The terminal writer keeps the recorded cancellation actor and reason, and persists the final state and audit event together.
- **Visual interface evidence** N/A. This corrects the step history available through the existing SOP run detail interface.
- **Tested revision and interface** Local test commit `1fe8f47534` exercised the SQLite run store and run-detail projection. Signed head `0eb12e70ca` replays the same patch on master `bec292f667`. The maintenance test reopens a file-backed SQLite store after two maintenance ticks and reads the finished run again.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence** The persisted run-detail projection includes exactly one step with number `1` and output `"one"`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result** The finish-write case includes `(1, "one")` then `(2, "two")`. The refused dispatch includes `(1, "one")`. Maintenance records `"one"` once. A later attempt retains its own evidence when an older driver returns.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why** Full workspace CI is left to GitHub. Local validation covered all tests in the affected SOP engine module.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No change to credential storage or processing. Step output may contain sensitive data. The transient refusal carries the already-recorded result privately to finalization. Debug formatting omits this payload, and the existing run-detail redaction continues to apply.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing rows and API shapes remain compatible. A cancelled run can include the result of the step its driver actually executed.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback** Revert the change to `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/sop/engine.rs` and redeploy. Existing completed run histories remain readable.
- **Feature flags or config toggles** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms** A cancelled run lacks the just-completed step after a competing write, contains a duplicate result, or includes a late result from a different step attempt.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Activate canonical registry admission and backend consumers, promote V4 configuration to V5, materialize complete models for routing/fallback/switching, and wire secret-safe registry editing. Registry types, native protocols, chat transport and reflection are prepared in #12454, #12455, #12456 and #12457.
- **Scope boundary:** V5 admission, persistence/editor wiring, canonical model construction and backend consumer/lifecycle cutover. Activation and affected consumers remain together so no intermediate revision clears profiles that active consumers still read. Zerocode and Web follow separately.
- **Blast radius:** Config persistence and secret handling; provider construction; agent/session lifecycle; memory, speech and decision consumers; channel/gateway/RPC dispatch.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 9; reference implementation `921b8ee993a0b2439a0c2c41cb84337270942a06`. Depends on #12457.

### What this does, simply

The preceding layers prepare independent registry types, native capability protocols, chat transport and generic reflection. This layer activates those components: V4 input is promoted at the V5 admission boundary, backend consumers resolve exact model references, and routing, fallback and switching build complete target bindings. Configuration activation and dependent consumers stay together to avoid a partially switched runtime. This remaining cutover is still large; the preparatory layers make their own architectural boundaries independently reviewable.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the migration or interactive workflow below supplements passing current-head CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `cli`. Not exercised interactively at this revision.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits; use the repository toolchain and existing test fixtures.
- **Steps to run:** Run workspace Quality Gate, migration and registry edit tests, provider protocol tests, runtime route/switch/fallback/refresh tests and feature-matrix checks; exercise `zeroclaw config migrate` with a V4 backup.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** V4 configuration becomes V5 connections/models; internal consumers resolve exact model keys; switching/fallback materializes all target configuration and a failed update preserves the previous binding.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Master stores provider-owned profiles and consumer-specific capability settings, and has no canonical decoupled registry.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Earlier green runs are historical only. Current-head workspace CI is required after the review fixes; no current-head all-green claim is made.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The separate PR-risk reporter failed its head-bound evidence capture. Live CLI/migration verification remains pending; passing CI does not establish the two old-configuration migration restrictions identified in review. Original #9809 CI does not validate intermediate stack revisions.
- **Commands run and tail output:** At `7457ad9664`, `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets` passed. Expanded config unit suite passed 2,085 tests, including the final fallback and timeout regressions. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and the changed-line docs quality gate passed. Existing Rust-toolchain deprecation/unused-dependency warnings were not changed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Addressed previous-head split dependency errors (retained embedding factory, complete timeout helpers, deferred dispatch-dependent sampling, and secret-test trait import). New-head execution remains pending. Compared the integrated provider and UI trees byte-for-byte with the saved pre-split snapshot. Preserved the frozen V4 fixture. Corrected previous-head CI failures caused by unnecessary TOML rewriting; the existing comment-preservation and atomic-save assertions remain intact. New-head execution is pending. Inspected ownership, imports and the incremental diff against the parent. Runtime/network behavior has not been re-executed locally.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Pending: CLI Quickstart and configuration command output require exact-head verification before interface sign-off.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `b46ac874c036def0c6da63856eb0200492c8ec5f`; source formatting only.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** No interactive action performed; current-head CI passed, while manual runtime checks remain pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Cargo build/test/clippy were intentionally skipped at the author’s request to use GitHub CI instead of repeated heavy local compilation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes; existing capability selection is represented in the new registry. Existing admission boundaries remain in force.
- New external network calls? Yes; native capability adapters use the selected connection and protocol. No additional allowlist bypass is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; connection credentials and sensitive headers use the existing encrypted persistence and masked edit contracts.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes; shared extraction policy is selected per materialized model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Migration, registry editing and provider selection cross configuration trust boundaries. Preserve ciphertext, use masked compare-and-swap edits, validate references before installation, and keep the previous binding when construction fails. Provider output remains subject to runtime tool admission.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Older files are converted at the migration boundary; the new internal API and persisted V5 shape replace profile-owned construction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; connections, models, presets, fallback references and configuration editing use the V5 shape.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Back up the existing configuration and run `zeroclaw config migrate`. Inspect the resulting connections/models and exact model references. V1-V3 first migrate through the frozen V4 step, then V4-to-V5. Install the dependent clients before the complete interactive rollout; restore the V4 backup for a V4 downgrade.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert merged children before this layer. Restore the pre-upgrade V4 backup when returning to a V4 binary; retain memory identity checks and never downgrade by editing only the version number.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this repository grants this author read-only access. These fork PRs therefore target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent; merge parents first and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 remains the reference PR and is not superseded or closed.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/d9820d99da0366e2f32c0ecc571ec95c6014aa4b...b46ac874c036def0c6da63856eb0200492c8ec5f).



### Review fixes (2026-11-17)

- Preserve V4 primary selection and non-strict text tools; strict policy follows named models, routes and fallback targets, with conflicting agent policies refused. Materialize fallback connections even when a canonical model shadows legacy input.
- Preserve non-streaming versus streaming timeout semantics with `api.stream_request_timeout_secs`; keep Grok subprocess deadlines bounded.
- Reject registry saves when disk edits diverge, compare stored references without resolving external secrets, and avoid blocking chat sessions for speech-only edits.
- Compare legacy embedding identity against the actual endpoint digest, and normalize image recovery using the served fallback model policy.
- Follow-up native Azure/Bedrock/Gemini timeout wiring is in #12455 and propagated to descendants. Follow-up `96a2d022fd` regenerates only the V5 fixture and fixes the recovery test setup and Clippy condition; `3e7455f7f0` fixes strict Clippy fixture initialization. Placement exception and fresh head-bound Quickstart evidence remain review items; this update does not claim maintainer approval.

- **What changed and why** In a build without the gateway, the four gateway-backed SOP administration commands now direct the operator to the standard build. The CLI-only exit-code health check asks the configured local daemon for its health snapshot and accepts only `components.daemon.status == "ok"`. The request has a five-second deadline.
- **Scope boundary** The changes apply to builds with the agent runtime and without the gateway. Gateway-enabled builds retain their HTTP health probe and SOP administration routes.
- **Blast radius** CLI-only health checks and the `sop pending`, `logs`, `approve` and `deny` commands. The localized `status --help` text explains what a healthy CLI-only daemon means.
- **Linked issue(s)** Closes #12097. Builds on merged #11975 and #11976.

### What this does, simply

These commands used to look for a web gateway even when the installed binary could only run a local daemon. A health check now asks that daemon directly. Commands that need the web gateway tell the operator which build provides it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The CLI-only build job includes the real executable, a loopback listener on the configured gateway port, and on Unix a local IPC fixture that serves healthy and unhealthy replies.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change** The existing CLI-only lane runs binary and component tests without the gateway. Its component checks hold the gateway port open while running all four SOP verbs and checking an absent daemon. The Unix IPC fixture checks which local methods the binary calls and observes both exit codes.
- **Known CI coverage gap** On the signed PR head, the hosted CLI-only build ran both `sop_admin_and_exit_code_status_do_not_contact_the_gateway_port` and `status_exit_code_reads_the_local_daemons_health` successfully. The local runner could not bind its socket fixtures. [CLI-only build](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44245807800/job/134604360145)
- **Commands run and tail output**

From the resulting test executables, the daemon health predicate passed (`1 passed; 0 failed`) and the CLI-only command/status component checks passed (`2 passed; 0 failed`). The unfiltered unit selection also reached two existing updater mocks that need a listening socket; the sandbox refused their binds.
  - `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime,gateway` — finished successfully.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` — exited 0.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Executed all four SOP verbs, the absent-daemon exit-code check, and `status --help` in isolated configuration directories. Confirmed the local-daemon help in English, Spanish, French, Japanese and Simplified Chinese. The previous CLI-only binary tried the configured gateway for every SOP verb.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact plain-text output.
- **Tested revision and interface** CLI-only executable built with Rust 1.96.1 from local commit `446ca674a8` (tree `cbe1395bb8`, identical to the signed PR commit `be0a804ce4`). The executable identified itself as `zeroclaw 0.9.0 (v0.9.0-15-g446ca674a8)` before the command checks. The output below uses the English locale.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence**

  ```text
  Error: This ZeroClaw build has no dashboard or web gateway (CLI-only build). To use them, install the standard build: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/master/install.sh | sh
  ```

  ```text
  --format <FORMAT>          Output format: "exit-code" exits 0 when the local daemon answers health with daemon status "ok", and 1 otherwise.
  ```

- **Action or changed state and observed result** All four SOP commands returned exit 1 with the same diagnostic as `gateway start`. The CLI-only status probe returned exit 1 with an absent socket. The daemon health predicate accepted an `ok` daemon and rejected missing, starting, error and unknown states.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why** Local sandbox policy prohibited binding both TCP and Unix listeners. The two socket tests were compiled for execution on the hosted CLI-only lane.

- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Standard builds keep their current endpoint behavior. In a CLI-only build, the health check now requires a responding local daemon with a healthy daemon component.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Existing CLI-only commands use the behavior described above. Their names and arguments remain compatible.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. Install the standard build to use the gateway-backed SOP commands.

prs.title: fix(auth): explain how to recover a reused Codex refresh token
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** The OpenAI OAuth response parser retains the HTTP status and response body as a typed error. On an explicit `auth refresh`, a confirmed reused-token 401 now produces a recovery instruction in the CLI's selected language.
- **Scope boundary** The command suggests reimporting a current Codex CLI login, explains how to target a named profile, and offers sign-in for other operators. Reimport remains an explicit operator action.
- **Blast radius** The formatter is called from the OpenAI Codex refresh flow. Other failures preserve their existing error text and retry classification.
- **Linked issue(s)** Closes #9492.

### What this does, simply

If another client has already used a profile's refresh token, retrying that same token cannot repair the profile. The CLI now points operators who imported a Codex login to the command that refreshes ZeroClaw's copy. The command takes no automatic action with the other client's credentials.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The regression uses synthetic provider responses. It can be run offline and requires no real account.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change** The providers suite passes synthetic HTTP responses through the same token parser and CLI error formatter used by refresh. The runtime suite formats the message from each of the five built-in Fluent catalogs.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any** A live OAuth account was not used to consume a single-use token. The upstream code and the issue provide structured and message-only forms of the refusal.
- **Commands run and tail output**
  - `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib codex_refresh_reimport_hint`: `1 passed; 0 failed`. The test checks six inputs: a reused-token code, the reported message with no code, a revoked-token code, an unrelated invalid grant, malformed text, and a 429.
  - Running all OpenAI OAuth parser tests and the shared retry policy tests in the resulting binary: `16 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib codex_refresh_reimport_hint_preserves_the_command_in_every_locale`: `1 passed; 0 failed` across English, Spanish, French, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The refresh flow still returns before updating the stored profile when the provider refuses the token. The test preserves the original error on a different provider failure and preserves a retryable classification on a 429.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact plain-text output from the CLI's Fluent formatter with the recovery command.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path** Signed PR commit `df534d2570`, identical tree to the tested commit `1396fe8edc`, CLI refresh diagnostic. The regression is in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/auth/openai_oauth.rs`; locale coverage is in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/i18n.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence** English and French diagnostic text, rendered in separate processes using the exact committed i18n module and locale tables:

  ```text
  Error: This OpenAI Codex refresh token was already used. If you imported your Codex CLI login, run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json` again. For a named profile, add `--profile <name>`. Otherwise, sign in again.
  Error: Ce jeton de renouvellement OpenAI Codex a déjà été utilisé. Si vous avez importé votre connexion depuis la CLI Codex, relancez `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`. Pour un profil nommé, ajoutez `--profile <name>`. Sinon, reconnectez-vous.
  ```

- **Action or changed state and observed result** A synthetic consumed-token response selected the localized instruction. The unrelated responses retained their original error. The synthetic fixture read no credential files.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why** Full workspace testing is delegated to CI. No live provider request is needed to verify this diagnostic.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? The authentication operation and storage are unchanged. For this recognized refusal the CLI emits a local diagnostic in place of the provider response body. It displays the documented import command and never executes it.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The command still reports failure for a consumed token.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Its diagnostic text changes for this refusal. Invocation and exit semantics stay the same.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users None.

## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** A tab now invalidates outstanding cookie-session checks when it signs out or receives a sign-out notification. The refresh and startup paths check whether a sign-out occurred before applying the response.

- **Linked issue** Closes #12106.

### What this does, simply

If a dashboard session check takes longer than signing out, its answer belongs to the previous session. The tab now keeps the sign-out screen visible when that answer arrives. During startup it records the sign-out generation when the session request begins, so an earlier sign-out followed by a genuine new sign-in is respected. A subsequent sign-in from another tab can still restore the session.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

prs.title: fix(providers): honor Retry-After in nonstreaming chat requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** Nonstreaming HTTP chat failures carry a parsed `Retry-After` delay to `ReliableModelProvider`. A valid delay-seconds or HTTP-date header on 429 and 503 responses takes precedence over the older error-text hint. Invalid or missing headers fall back to the existing behavior.
- **Scope boundary** This covers the common provider HTTP error builder, OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic typed errors, and custom error paths in Azure OpenAI, Gemini, GLM, Ollama, Hailo-Ollama, and Telnyx. Streaming still uses its existing `StreamError` contract. Model catalog requests and credential acquisition are outside this change.
- **Blast radius** Nonstreaming model invocations that encounter a throttled or temporarily unavailable provider. Successful responses and error display text keep their established behavior. The existing limits are 30 seconds for a retry backoff and 60 seconds for a cross-call rate-limit cooldown.
- **Linked issue(s)** Related #11768. This draft covers nonstreaming chat requests; streaming remains open. The quota reset information in #11895 comes from response bodies and remains a separate change.

### What this does, simply

A busy provider can ask ZeroClaw to wait before retrying. Previously its HTTP header was discarded, so ZeroClaw could retry too soon. A provider asking for four seconds now gets a four-second retry delay, even if an older delay appears in the response body. A quota that requires operator action still fails promptly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)
