prs.title: fix(install): verify Windows prebuilt release checksums
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, at `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Resolve one release tag, then download the Windows archive and `SHA256SUMS` from that tag. Require one exact asset entry and a matching SHA256 before extraction.
  - Use one PowerShell helper for `setup.bat --prebuilt` and the generated Windows guide. Missing, malformed, duplicate or mismatched checksums stop installation. A failed download also stops this mode.
  - Add offline tests under PowerShell 5.1 and 7 to the existing required Windows job. Helper-only changes now select that job.
  - Set the bundled helper process execution policy explicitly so the batch entrypoint works when the inherited policy is Restricted. User/machine policy settings are unchanged; organizational Group Policy still takes precedence.
- **Scope boundary:** Windows x86_64 prebuilt installation only. No change to Unix installers, release publishing, signing, PATH policy or the existing Rust prerequisite check in `setup.bat`.
- **Blast radius:** The Windows batch entrypoint, its shared helper, the generated PowerShell guide and Windows CI selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12122.

### What this does, simply

The Windows installers currently extract a downloaded archive without checking its release checksum. This checks the checksum first. If it fails, the archive is not extracted and the existing install is left alone. Both files come from the same resolved release, so a change to `latest` between requests cannot mix releases.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for additional manual checksum testing: the checked-in offline fixtures exercise the hash and extraction path, the complete documented failure path and the real batch entrypoint. A live release installation and binary startup are not claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current-head [run 41359345404](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404) passes [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125008855004), [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125006156219), [Installer Drift](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125006156522) and the [required Windows job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41359345404/job/125006301814). Both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and 7 checksum steps pass in that job. Test, Lint, targeted Windows Clippy and Docs Style pass. The Windows log confirms the real batch fixture passes under inherited Restricted policy in both steps. This covers the original true-rebased repair and the two-file launch correction.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The full generator and required Windows checks pass on this corrected head. The checksum suites use synthetic archives and mocked downloads, including the Restricted-policy launch case. They do not run an installed ZeroClaw binary, persist a user PATH change, or reproduce organization-enforced Group Policy/App Control.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1
pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1
# Each shell:
PASS setup.bat --prebuilt under Restricted policy: checksum mismatch, exit 1, no extraction, source fallback or PATH write
PASS 22 checksum cases, explicit tag and 3 invalid tags; all network calls mocked

bash scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.test.sh
Required Windows package ownership: pass
Required Windows gate consistency: pass
windows test scope contract tests: pass

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check xtask/src/generate/docs.rs
git diff --check
bash -n install.sh
# exit 0

bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

  The link gate's six unit tests and changed-link collector passed under Linux. No invalid local targets were found. Optional `lychee` validation was unavailable. The repository comment-hygiene filter passed on the changed supported source files.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial passes checked same-tag URLs, exact and duplicate manifest entries, fail-before-extraction behavior, temporary-file cleanup, batch error propagation, generator/helper parity and CI selection. Two disposable mutation controls failed as intended: removing the hash comparison and changing the archive URL back to `latest`. The October 31 release inventory listed both the Windows archive and `SHA256SUMS`; neither asset was executed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output. No layout or rendering change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 8c7dd665ca80f1c7eddd6e549381bf113bba7278; Windows, PowerShell 5.1 and 7, scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1. Both complete checksum suites and the revised actual-batch case pass. The test failed before the launch correction with running scripts disabled; it now reaches checksum refusal and returns 1 without installation side effects. Other selector/generator/source controls above ran at the preceding rebased commit, whose helper, generator and CI-selection code are unchanged.

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The output above includes the observed batch failure and fixture results. The helper prints `SHA256 verified: zeroclaw-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip (v1.2.3)` for a valid synthetic archive.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A valid archive replaces the fixture payload. Corrupt or unverifiable input leaves the existing fixture unchanged, removes temporary downloads and stops before PATH or Quickstart. The batch process returns 1.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace generator, Cargo tests and Clippy were not duplicated locally in the sparse source checkout; the current-head hosted Installer Drift, Test, Lint and required Windows checks supply that evidence. Earlier Linux link tests and changed-link collection remain historical evidence for unchanged links; optional `lychee` validation was unavailable. No live installation or new private CI job was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No new file-system scope.** The helper uses process-only `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`; it does not modify user/machine execution-policy settings or override organizational Group Policy. Downloads use a unique temporary directory; the install destination is unchanged. [Execution-policy scopes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_execution_policies?view=powershell-5.1).
- New external network calls? **Yes.** Both routes fetch the manifest. The batch route resolves the release through the public GitHub API instead of the previous `gh`/mutable-URL fallback. Asset URLs use one validated version tag.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** No credentials are required or added.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Downloads stay on the existing GitHub release boundary. Missing or invalid verification data fails closed. A checksum is not a signature: this does not protect against an attacker who can replace both the archive and its manifest.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for the former automatic fallback and standalone copies of `setup.bat`.** Valid prebuilt archives install as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No new installer flags or application configuration.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Keep `setup.bat` with `scripts/install_windows_prebuilt.ps1` from the same checkout or unpacked source archive, or use the self-contained PowerShell guide. If a prebuilt download or checksum fails, select `--dist` explicitly to build from source. The existing `setup.bat` Rust prerequisite is unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed commit through a reviewed PR. This restores the unverified Windows extraction paths; use a source build while a replacement fix is reviewed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SHA256 mismatch`, a missing/invalid `SHA256SUMS` entry, a download error or a missing helper causes an error before installation. `setup.bat` prints `Setup failed` and returns 1.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This does not supersede another PR.



## Review status — 2026-11-17 UTC

Head 8c7dd665ca80f1c7eddd6e549381bf113bba7278 has APPROVED submissions from [@Audacity88](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12166#pullrequestreview-5763421507), [@IftekharUddin](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12166#pullrequestreview-5821068825), [@tidux](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12166#pullrequestreview-5898428126). These are other reviewers' submissions, separate from my self-review. The required gate currently reports success for this head. This does not replace a fresh integration, policy and dependency check before merge; the shared dependency work in #12505 and #12101 must be considered there. No new test run is claimed by this record update.

### What this does, simply

If the price of cached tokens depends on a missing input price, the dashboard and CLI should not treat those tokens as known to be free. The ledger now records how many lacked a price, alongside the dollar amount ZeroClaw could calculate.

Follow-up to #12114 for #12280: `authorize_sop_cancel` used `forwarded_client_ip` and treated a loopback result as local, so a trusted forwarded `127.0.0.1` (loopback peer or remote peer) could cancel without pairing. The rate-limit path already refused that case.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, at `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require the existing read-policy check before `file_upload` or `file_upload_bundle` reads a file for its configured HTTP endpoint. A write-only sibling grant no longer permits uploads; a read grant now suffices.
  - Require read access before `file_edit` opens the existing target. Its existing write check remains. Denied edits cannot reveal match counts or indentation diagnostics.
  - Add permission-matrix and loopback HTTP regressions. Confirm that `file_write` still permits a write-only deposit. Document the contract.
- **Scope boundary:** Five files; no policy state, dependencies, schema, tool registration or transport changes. This does not add descriptor-based race hardening or change hard-link handling.
- **Blast radius:** Uploads and edits under per-agent file grants. The existing `SecurityPolicy` remains the source of truth.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12144. Related #11997; this does not replace its separate `send_via` work. Includes the merged #12129 Security-gate dependency repair through the true rebase.

### What this does, simply

A write-only grant lets one agent leave files for another without reading that agent's existing files. These three tools used the write permission to authorize operations that read content. This repair checks read permission before that content is opened. Uploads require read access; edits require both read and write access. A plain file deposit still needs only write access.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Independent Core Team/CODEOWNER security review remains required before merge. Current-head native Linux CI executes all four access-tier regressions, including the Unix symlink case.

- **Interface(s) exercised:** The production tool API (`Tool::execute`) and a loopback HTTP upload endpoint. No `web`, `tui`, `cli` or messaging `channel` attribution is claimed by this test harness.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A supported Rust toolchain and the normal test dependencies. Fixtures create isolated workspaces, synthetic content and loopback servers; no provider credentials or external destination are needed.
- **Steps to run:** Run the two commands below. For A/B verification, copy only `crates/zeroclaw-tools/tests/file_access_tiers.rs` into a clean checkout of the base revision and run the first command there with production files unchanged.

  ```sh
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --test file_access_tiers -- --nocapture
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib file_ -- --nocapture
  ```

- **Expected on this branch (after):** Three tests pass on Windows; Unix also runs the symlink case. Write-only uploads make no HTTP request. Edit attempts return the same policy denial for exact, absent, repeated and indentation-only matches. The file stays unchanged. Read-capable uploads and read/write edits succeed; write-only deposits still succeed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Historical Windows execution against base 1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29 gave one pass and two failures: a write-only upload sent the file, and a write-only edit changed it. The separate bundle-only negative control also detected the missing read guard. Those controls were not rerun on the current base.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current-head [run 41358936353](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353) passes [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125007642064), [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125004913334), [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125004913544) and [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41358936353/job/125004913539). I checked the Test log: all four file_access_tiers regressions pass, including the native Unix symlink case, as do 122 existing file-tool tests. The checkout merges this head into b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855; merge snapshot 49c0aa0396269f1b83f248706bd98da58196578b. The one-commit range-diff is unchanged. Three same-head Core review submissions are recorded below; final integration remains separate.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-head Linux Test covers the access-tier matrix and Unix symlink regression. Windows Application Control blocked the local test executable after compilation; zero local tests ran on this head. The earlier Windows execution and mutation controls below remain historical evidence for the unchanged patch. No live-agent, external upload or full OIDC acceptance run is claimed.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tools --test file_access_tiers -- --nocapture
      Finished test profile
      Running tests/file_access_tiers.rs
  could not execute process ... (never executed)
  An Application Control policy has blocked this file. (os error 4551)

  cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
  # package scope; exit 0
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  git diff --check
  # exit 0
  npx --offline markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 docs/book/src/agents/internals.md
  Summary: 0 error(s)
  ```

  Two warnings come from unchanged Windows-gated config fields, `DockerRuntime.resolved_launcher` and `NativeRuntime.resolved_shell`. Their definitions and platform gates match the base; no suppression is added.

  Historical execution on 28ab00fb521abe14719bb82e978c4adde9b0f05b: the Windows access-tier suite passed three tests; the existing file suite passed 125 tests. The unpatched baseline failed two of the three regressions. Restoring only the bundle's old write guard made the upload regression fail; source was restored afterward. That unchanged-patch control was not rerun after the current Windows execution block.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes traced canonical policy, registry wrappers, grant unions, reads and final network/file effects. A denied later bundle item must produce zero requests; write-only edit refusal precedes content diagnostics; read-only uploads and write-only file deposits remain valid controls. No new policy state is added. No live agent, provider or external upload was run, and no full OIDC acceptance is claimed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: file authorization at the tool API; no renderer, layout or focus behavior changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 5c82d3d2e3aef1a0deeb9f3c6086f72008d2ecbd; production tools and `crates/zeroclaw-tools/tests/file_access_tiers.rs`. Current local evidence is compilation and static checks; execution is blocked as recorded above. Historical executed controls are identified separately.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Relevant current command output and historical execution counts are above. The checked-in regressions record loopback requests and verify returned denials and unchanged file content.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Current-head hosted fixtures verify that write-only grants produce zero upload requests and no content-derived edit diagnostic. Read grants allow uploads, combined read/write grants allow edits, and write-only file deposits remain supported. A denied later bundle item sends no partial upload; a workspace symlink does not grant read access to its write-only target.

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** After Windows Application Control refused the test executable, I did not run the broader local suite or a fresh mutation control. Current-head upstream Linux Test supplies the executed regression and workspace evidence. No policy bypass, extra private CI job, live-agent test or external upload was run. macOS runtime execution remains outside the completed validation. The review record is listed below. No new documentation links were added.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, a correction to access scope:** read-only grants now allow these read-side uploads, while write-only grants no longer allow uploads or edits. The configured endpoint and network policy remain unchanged. Tests assert both allowed and denied effects.
- New external network calls? **No.** The existing upload calls are gated before reading; regressions use loopback only.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** No new credential path. The repair prevents these tools from reading content under a write-only grant.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** The new refusal reuses the existing policy diagnostic and exposes no file contents.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The access-scope change is explicit above. Existing deployments that relied on the incorrect write-only behavior must grant read access deliberately; the repair does not infer it.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for callers that used write-only grants to upload or edit; that behavior is the defect being removed. Read-only uploads now work.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.** Existing grant values are reused.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Keep `Write` for deposit-only workflows and use `file_write`. If an agent must inspect and edit a sibling's files, change that sibling grant to `ReadWrite` after reviewing the trust boundary. Use `Read` when only reading/uploading is intended. Do not broaden unrelated grants.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this change's landed commit through a reviewed PR. This restores the reported read leak, so prefer a targeted correction if a regression appears.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Existing per-agent `Read`, `Write` and `ReadWrite` grants control intended access.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Upload/edit tools return `Resolved path escapes workspace allowlist` for a write-only sibling. That is expected after this repair; failures with a correct read/read-write grant would be a regression. The tool result must contain no content-derived edit diagnostic on denial.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. No PR is superseded and no contributor branch is modified.


## Review status — 2026-11-17 UTC

Head 5c82d3d2e3aef1a0deeb9f3c6086f72008d2ecbd has APPROVED submissions from [@Audacity88](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12151#pullrequestreview-5763383509), [@IftekharUddin](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12151#pullrequestreview-5821069570), [@tidux](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12151#pullrequestreview-5898425123). These are other reviewers' submissions, separate from my self-review. The required gate currently reports success for this head. prs.title: fix(mcp): confine SSE endpoints and redirects to the server origin
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Validate each resolved SSE message endpoint before a write starts. A server can no longer send configured headers or JSON-RPC content to another origin through an endpoint event.
- Bind SSE GET and POST redirects to the same origin. Reject URL credentials and report sanitized origins without query strings or userinfo.
- **Scope boundary:** SSE transport destination validation and its documentation. HTTP transport, stdio, CA trust, tool authorization, DNS pinning and gateway admin authorization retain their existing behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Remote MCP servers configured with `transport = "sse"`. Same-origin relative/absolute endpoints and redirects remain supported.
- Fixes #12146. #12129 merged as f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7. This branch now contains that dependency repair through a single true rebase onto master 4c9edcf33716381b2c3455649cbd0f3e6b3a38b1; its two-file patch is unchanged.

### What this does, simply

An MCP server can tell the client where to send its next message. The client now checks that address against the server URL the operator configured. A different scheme, host or effective port is refused. HTTP redirects cannot bypass this check. The refusal happens before credentials or content reach the other destination.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Local HTTP fixtures exercise the production transport and record requests at the destination; no real server or credential is needed. The commands below run these checks.

### How I tested

Rebased revision: d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a. Fresh local validation on Windows x86-64, Rust 1.97.1, 2026-11-01. Exactly one own commit, with parent 4c9edcf33716381b2c3455649cbd0f3e6b3a38b1. `git range-diff` reports the original repair and this rebased commit as equivalent. No source edits followed validation.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib mcp_transport::tests::
87 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0

cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0 (no tools-crate warnings)

npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

The changed-link collector also passed: zero added links in the edited document. Test/dev debug info and incremental compilation were disabled; builds used two jobs.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a, [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860/job/124719523203) and [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860/job/124717381898) pass. [Run 41262135860](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860) also passes Test, Lint, MSRV, Linux build, Windows compilation and targeted Clippy, macOS compilation, Docs Style and Installer Drift. Path-gated skips are not runtime execution evidence. The old b09f760f72 run is historical evidence only. The same-head review submissions are recorded below; final integration and merge-policy checks remain separate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The hosted required gate is complete and passes; same-head review submissions are recorded below. The local tests use loopback HTTP fixtures; no live external MCP service or native macOS execution was performed. A macOS compile job does not establish runtime execution.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial self-review passes and a final reread covered endpoint-to-write ordering, redirects, URL normalization, error privacy, the constructor policy and non-SSE compatibility. The checks happen before headers, pending-sender registration and the write outcome marker. These passes are not independent approval. Historical negative control on b09f760f72: removing the two new guards made both capture tests fail because a foreign server received a request; restoring them passed all 87 tests. That mutation control was not repeated on the unchanged rebased patch; the 87-test result above is fresh on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No CLI, TUI or web rendering or interaction code changed; the network boundary is exercised directly.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The revision above; `SharedMcpTransportConn::send_and_recv` through real loopback HTTP servers, with synthetic `Authorization` and `X-Api-Key` headers. Tests are in `mcp_transport.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test summaries above. Five new tests cover origin rules, refused endpoint/redirect destinations, and accepted same-origin endpoint/redirect controls.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Foreign destinations received zero requests with the fix. Accepted destinations received the configured headers and returned the JSON-RPC result. Refused endpoints left no pending sender or post-write outcome marker.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full workspace or live-service run; the focused transport module includes existing TLS, cancellation, fallback and response-limit controls. The locked test run fetched missing cached dependencies; Clippy then used offline resolution.

Two existing Windows warnings remain in unchanged `zeroclaw-config` files: `resolved_launcher` in `platform/docker.rs` and `resolved_shell` in `platform/native.rs`. Their reads are Unix-only. No warning suppression was added.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** SSE credentials and payloads stay on the configured origin. Redirects receive the same check; URLs with credentials are refused. Errors name only sanitized origins.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** This validates server-controlled transport metadata.

This changes a network credential boundary. Independent Core Team/CODEOWNER security review is required; this submission is not self-approval.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for servers that advertise another origin or use URL credentials. Same-origin endpoints and redirects remain supported.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A server with an incompatible endpoint or redirect has an error chain containing `MCP SSE endpoint must use the configured server origin ...`. The error identifies both origins and omits URL credentials and query strings.

Head d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a has APPROVED submissions from [@Audacity88](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12149#pullrequestreview-5763390781), [@IftekharUddin](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12149#pullrequestreview-5821069782), [@tidux](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12149#pullrequestreview-5898424032). prs.title: fix(channels): pace native polls with outbound messages
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Queue native polls with ordinary sends, final replies and final draft edits for the same recipient. Previously a poll posted immediately even when that recipient already had a message waiting.
  - Use the same Tokio clock for the pacing deadline and the existing Tokio sleep, so the test can advance each interval deterministically.
  - Return the inner channel's delivery result. If the queue drops a poll, return an error so the poll tool can report the failed post.
  - Drop a waiting poll when its caller cancels. If delivery already started, let the worker finish it and release the recipient for subsequent sends.
- **Scope boundary:** The change is in the channel pacing wrapper. An interval of zero still returns the original channel, and unsupported channels keep their existing fallback.
- **Blast radius:** Channels that support native polls and have outbound pacing enabled, including WhatsApp Web. Polls to different recipients use independent queues.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11050. Follow-up to #10984.

### What this does, simply

An operator can set a minimum time between replies to the same chat. A poll now waits its turn alongside messages sent ahead of it. If the channel rejects the poll or the queue is full, the tool reports that it could not post it.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Decode a Windows file-move failure with `WIN32_ERROR::from_error` and pass the underlying Win32 code to `io::Error::from_raw_os_error`. The removal path can then recognize `ErrorKind::NotFound`.

If someone removes a plugin’s directory outside ZeroClaw, they can still need to remove its installation record. prs.title: feat(web): add paired-device voice settings and chat controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Add opt-in browser dictation and narration in agent chat, with paired-device voice preferences and a localized guide under Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio.
- Save microphone, recognition mode, language, voice, speed and automatic narration on the authenticated paired-device record, not browser storage. Operators can select another paired device's record without changing the current browser's identity.
- Add one global `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` setting in that same voice screen: default 15 seconds, accepted range 0â€“300, with 0 disabling automatic submission. It applies to every device/conversation and uses the existing authenticated configuration property API.
- Speak rendered Markdown text rather than hidden delimiters; omit only a trailing crab signature. Preserve meaningful literal code punctuation. Formatting-only replies do not block the continuous reading queue.
- **Scope boundary:** browser speech APIs, paired-device preferences, one gateway configuration field and normal chat submission. No server STT/TTS backend, microphone-audio upload endpoint, new identity or external service is added.
- **Blast radius:** web Config/chat, existing device-registry migration, gateway configuration and same-origin microphone Permissions Policy.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable microphone and speaker controls next to the composer. Recognition starts only when the user clicks the microphone and grants browser permission. Local recognition is the default and never falls back online automatically; browser-service recognition is an explicit choice.

Dictation appends final recognized text to the draft. After the global silence interval, capture stops and final results are accepted before the normal send path is invoked once. Empty captures, hidden/cancelled chats, disconnected/busy sessions and stale conversation requests do not auto-send. A browser ending recognition early still honors the remaining silence interval. Local slash commands remain for manual submission. Set the global value to 0 for manual sending only.

The speaker reads a reply once, stops it, or enables continuous reading through a hold/Shift+Enter gesture. Automatic reading skips restored history and consumes unreadable formatting/signature-only replies so later responses can play. Changing the speech text never changes the displayed/stored response.

<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at 9a9f6a1be. Combined voice controls with scoped chat while retaining operator-only image uploads. Voice submission honors the existing canSend/first-conversation path. A regression drives the actual voice callback through a restricted account's first WebSocket conversation, verifies exactly one message after session_start, and verifies that file uploads remain unavailable. Canonical API generation, the auth suite, all 31 voice tests, and the production build passed. Five gateway voice authorization tests also passed, including revocation during a write. This update was validated locally; earlier installed-browser evidence below describes its recorded revisions.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces:** web Config and agent chat; authenticated gateway configuration/device APIs.
- **Preconditions:** HTTPS or localhost, a paired browser, browser/OS speech support; select a locally available voice to test playback.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio. Enable dictation/narration, select language/voice and try the sample.
  2. Change global silence to 15, dictate and pause: verify exactly one send after the interval. Test 0 (manual only), another value, empty capture, manual stop, conversation switch and hidden chat. Confirm the same value appears on another paired device.
  3. Read a response with headings, emphasis, lists, a link and a horizontal rule. Formatting must not be spoken; code such as `apt-get --yes` must retain literal punctuation. A final crab signature is silent, but a crab in the body remains content.
  4. Enable continuous reading; place `---` or a signature-only reply before another readable answer. The latter must play. Restored history and trim notices remain silent.
  5. Reload settings and switch the device selector: per-device choices remain isolated, while the silence timeout stays global. Revoke a technical device and confirm its voice API refuses access. No voice preference storage key is added to browser storage.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: no online fallback. Browser-service mode and online voices remain explicit choices.
- **Expected after:** documented opt-in controls, durable per-device voice choices, one adjustable global silence deadline and readable narration.
- **Before on master:** these browser speech controls and preference APIs are absent.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Earlier layout revision:** 61aeff4bb (global silence, narration fixes and responsive settings/toolbar spacing); the corresponding integrated candidate uses the same feature changes.
- **Latest checks actually run:** 24 voice tests passed; configuration default/range test passed; canonical `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` passed; integrated TypeScript check and production WebUI build passed. The checks exercise the actual component speech-submission callback, global property save, zero-disable, final-results ordering, activity resets, empty/hidden/cancelled capture, early recognition end, signature filtering and continuous queue progress.
- **Historical baseline checks:** gateway paired-device tests (14), security-header tests (5), auth/session/UI tests and format/diff checks passed at earlier documented revisions. These are not reattributed to the new head.
- **CI status:** current head includes master755bc9a4e. Its SQLite exception was approved and merged by maintainers in#12321; this PR does not introduce its own exception. The functional/layout source and installed bundle remain unchanged by that policy-only merge. Current-head CI is authoritative. The independent PR's shared SQLite advisory remains tracked by #12320; the checkout-only #12322 bridge was removed here after its registry-publication limitation was found. No advisory ignore was added. The preceding head's 32-bit check failed during runner `apt install` timeouts, before checking this code.
- **Coverage limits:** component tests simulate speech APIs. Actual microphone hardware, audible OS voice output, language pack downloads and browser-provider network behavior require device testing. New browser validation/deployment results will be reported separately, not inferred from unit tests.
- **Installed-browser validation:** synthetic microphone transcript, actual WebSocket/model completion, exactly one automatic send after **15,131 ms**, technical conversation deleted, global field verified at15 in Browser Voice and Audio; a nondefault16-second value was saved, verified on disk/after reload, then restored to15. Actual microphone hardware/audio playback are not claimed.
- **Responsive layout follow-up at61aeff4bb:** label above the numeric input (8px gap), separate help and save row (16px gap), and nonshrinking40px microphone/speaker buttons. Verified the installed UI at1280px and390px wide; both controls remain visible. The layout-only static update preserved configuration and binary and did not restart the daemon.

![Current desktop voice settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-desktop.png)

![Historical mobile layout before the global controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-mobile.png)

- **Earlier functional-field evidence (before the spacing follow-up):** cropped from the installed UI matching the feature changes at3f70b1efc; the evidence branch adds only this image, without changing the reviewed feature head.

![Global browser voice silence setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6423d16e3db0b77a369c815b7839f81bbe79d357/.pr-evidence/web-voice-global-silence-live.png)

- **Visual evidence provenance:** the following captures were originally recorded at 6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae and retained at the evidence revision below. They show the prior device selector, guide and controls; they do not show the newly added global field.

![Paired-device selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-devices-other-desktop.png)

![Settings and usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-desktop.png)

[Mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-mobile.png) Â· [Portuguese guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-pt.png)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Permissions:** same-origin microphone/on-device recognition is permitted; microphone and narration default disabled per device. Browser consent and user initiation are still required. Global silence defaults to 15 only after dictation is explicitly started.
- **External calls:** optional browser language-pack downloads, explicitly selected online recognition/voices; no microphone audio reaches the gateway.
- **Credentials:** own-device routes resolve the existing paired bearer under the live pairing guard; other-device management uses existing operator authorization. Global timeout reads/writes use the existing config property API and its authorization/validation. No credential is returned or logged by this feature.
- **Personal data in fixtures/docs:** none; synthetic content only.
- **Model-visible text:** recognized text follows the existing user draft/send path; no approval bypass or additional execution capability.

## Compatibility (required)

- **HTTP/config:** existing paired records receive disabled voice defaults; the new global field defaults to 15 when absent. Its range is validated on configuration writes/load. Rust struct-literal callers may need the new field or `..Default::default()`.
- **Config surface:** `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs`; existing device preference routes remain per-device. No new environment variable or transport endpoint.
- **Toolchain floor:** unchanged.
- **Upgrade:** build matching gateway/WebUI, enable desired device controls and adjust the global interval in Browser Voice and Audio. Cookie-only sessions without a paired-device identity cannot edit device preferences.

## Rollback

- Disable automatic sending by setting global silence to 0; microphone/narration/continuous reading can be disabled independently in the voice screen.
- For binary rollback, restore a verified prior binary; remove the new configuration key if rolling back to a version rejecting unknown fields. The nullable device-preference column can remain. Preserve state and credentials rather than blindly restoring an old database after accepted work.
- Observable failures: Config save/load errors, browser capture/playback errors or preference-API refusals. Global-setting load failure disables automatic submission rather than guessing a deadline.

### Localization

The existing voice guide/device strings retain their ten-language translations and English fallback. The six new global-setting strings are provided in English and Portuguese; other locales use the existing English fallback.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
Continuous reading now checks readiness, listening and speaking before parsing a queued Markdown answer. Added a regression demonstrating no repeated DOM conversion while the parent rerenders during playback; it fails before the fix and passes after. All 32 voice tests pass; the integrated WebUI production build passes.

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

## Authenticated browser evidence

A paired Windows operator completed the real spoken-input, single automatic send and audible-reply check in Chrome and Edge on integrated revision `77c0b647d`. The [operator acceptance](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880263250) and [screenshots](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880323951) are available. The settings capture shows local dictation selected. The operator did not record browser build numbers or the recognition mode used for each recorded round trip.


## Current mobile interface and playback ownership

The screenshot below renders the production `BrowserVoiceSettings` component and stylesheet from PR commit `610484335` in a headed Chrome viewport at 390 CSS pixels. Device, voice and API data are synthetic. The image shows the reading-voice selector and the speech-speed row. Current head `1f331f278` changes only the navigation wording in the book relative to the capture.

![Mobile Browser Voice and Audio settings with a reading voice and speech speed control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/850c9a854fb577686c5d6448914df6658ffb8278/.pr-evidence/web-voice-settings-mobile-610484335.png)

For the earlier evidence, integrated build `77c0b647d` used the paired voice changes through `bf0093778`, whose themed-dropdown patch has the same stable patch ID as integrated commit `ec761ae6f`. That build predates `2a70a0f90` and `fec38c9b9`. The older image above is historical. This update removes the nine stale captures from the PR branch and stores the new capture on a separate evidence ref.

```text
npm run test:voice
✔ stopping one pane does not cancel playback owned by another pane
✔ manual playback in a second pane shows the playback busy message
ℹ tests 34
ℹ pass 34
ℹ fail 0
```

The headed browser also opened the authenticated settings route on Jarvis and confirmed it remained accessible after reload. The screenshot is from the isolated PR fixture. The production check verified navigation and rendering.

The shared Security findings are tracked in #12505 (chrono and chrono-tz) and #12101 (zip 9.0.5). This voice PR does not alter the workspace dependency graph or advisory policy.

Depends on #12265. Merge the runtime exception record before this change.

## Summary

Base branch: `master`.

Refuse repeated identical tool calls before dispatch and retain completed results for the tools-free closeout. Closes #11866.

### What this does, simply

Repeated calls stop before another side effect. The final closeout retains completed results and current upstream result-aware recovery.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

Run `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::turn`, including the closeout token-calibration capacity regression, and the current-head CI matrix.

### How I tested

The [CI Required Gate passed](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43785704095/job/133037511106) at `39ea9adf8d7d3cae13e150af2d6d0f1ab960c125`; closeout fixtures include its required capability_binding and keep_tool_context_turns fields. The Landlock job exhausted runner disk with full debug information; job-local DEV/TEST debug level 1 preserves debug lines and the same runner, permissions, test selection and assertions. The rerun passed. Production-composition runtime turn validation is recorded separately.

Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

No new permissions, external network destinations, persistent state, configuration, or authority grants. The refusal gate narrows dispatch, while closeout retains only turn-local results under existing limits.

- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: No
- New external network calls: No
- Secrets/credentials handling changed: No
- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.
- Untrusted model-visible content changed: Yes — retained tool results enter the bounded final closeout under existing context and policy limits.

## Compatibility (required)

Backward compatible at the documented tool-loop boundary. No configuration or toolchain-floor change.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the refusal/closeout change. No persistent-state migration is required. Observe repeated-call refusal and final-summary capacity errors; do not infer successful external effects from a retained result alone.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.

## Pending Core Team decision

Core Team placement approval and its recorded bounded exception remain required. The proposed scope is the repeated-call pre-dispatch refusal and tools-free closeout at the existing turn owner, with destination the planned kernel agent-loop owner. Review at that extraction design review, or before expanding refusal criteria, execution authority or retained state. This PR does not grant itself an exception.

SQLite scope correction: #12322 remains draft pending a published Matrix storage dependency (matrix-org/matrix-rust-sdk#7456). Its workspace-only bridge was removed from this PR; registry compatibility is preserved and #12320 remains the shared advisory tracker. No SQLite waiver is added here.

prs.title: feat(runtime): log reported context usage and budget trims
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `enforce_reported_budget` receives the provider's own `reported_input_tokens` for responses with provider-reported input usage that reach enforcement — the measured count of what a request actually cost — compares it against `max_context_tokens`, trims history if it is over, and then discards the number.
  - Adds a **DEBUG `context_usage`** record on every enforcement call with reported input usage with the reported tokens, the budget, and an `over_budget` flag. Emitted whether or not the budget is exceeded, so the distribution is observable rather than only the overruns.
  - Adds a **WARN `context_budget_trim`** record when history is actually dropped, with the reported tokens, the budget, and the dropped/kept counts.
  - Logging only. No control flow, config surface, or trimming behaviour changes.

### Why this is worth a patch

Without it, sizing `max_context_tokens` means reconstructing the prompt by hand — and that silently answers a different question. A reconstruction cannot see the trimming this function has already applied, so it reports what the prompt *would* have been rather than what was sent, and overstates usage against a budget that is in fact enforced. I made exactly that mistake on a live deployment: a hand-reconstructed prompt came out 12% over the configured budget and I concluded the budget was too small, when usage had been bounded correctly the whole time and the number I had was not a measurement.

Trimming also had no log record of its own. `TurnEvent::HistoryTrimmed` reaches the UI and `ObserverEvent::HistoryTrimmed` reaches telemetry, but neither lands in the daemon log an operator greps after the fact — so "did history get dropped during that session?" was unanswerable after the fact on a deployment without an observer backend.

- **Scope boundary:** does not change when trimming happens, what it drops, or any default. Does not add a config key or touch the existing `TurnEvent` / `ObserverEvent` payloads.
- **Blast radius:** one DEBUG record per enforcement call with reported input usage; event construction has a small cost even when DEBUG is filtered out and one WARN record per actual trim, which is already an exceptional event.
- **Linked issue(s):** None
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `agent`, `runtime`, `observability:log`, `risk:low`, `size:XS`, `topic:agent-loop`

### What this does, simply

Agents keep earlier messages as context for later model requests. When the provider reports input usage, these logs show that measured count beside the configured budget. If budget enforcement drops messages, a separate record shows how many were dropped and how many turns remain. The change does not alter when trimming happens or what it removes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — one command shows the new record.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: cli` and `channel`; the function is on the shared turn path.
- **Setup / preconditions:** any agent with `max_context_tokens` set.
- **Steps to run:** `RUST_LOG=debug zeroclaw --verbose daemon`, then send a turn.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a `context_usage` record when a response supplies input usage and reaches budget enforcement carrying `reported_input_tokens`, `context_token_budget`, `over_budget`. Drive a session past the budget and a `context_budget_trim` WARN appears with the dropped/kept counts.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** neither record exists; `reported_input_tokens` is read and discarded, and a trim leaves nothing in the daemon log.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust build/lint/test jobs cover `zeroclaw-runtime`, the only crate touched.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```console
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --locked
11 suites, 5011 passed, 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That the added record sits before the early return so the under-budget case — the common one — is still reported; a record placed after it would only ever fire on overruns, which is the case an operator already knows about.
- **What I did NOT verify, and why no test was added:** no new log-capture assertion was added. Existing module tests cover over-budget trimming, within-budget no-op, and disabled-budget no-op; the early return, trim path, and both existing events are untouched.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full-workspace `cargo test` not run; the change is confined to one function in one crate.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No** — the records carry integer counts only, never message content.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — nothing added reaches the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`. The DEBUG record is filtered unless the recording level enables it, with a small event-construction cost even when disabled; the WARN record only fires where a trim already occurred.

prs.body:
## Summary

- Strip stale `reasoning_content` from retained Anthropic tool-call messages after tool-context collapse removes earlier transcript rows.
- Apply the transformation only to the provider-facing collapsed copy; preserve durable conversation history and all other providers.
- Add a regression test that retains reasoning on ordinary assistant messages while removing it from Anthropic tool-call carriers.
- Scope boundary: this does not change tool-call payloads, user-visible answer text, history persistence, or non-Anthropic requests.
- Blast radius: Anthropic requests after configured tool-context collapse; saved transcripts remain unchanged.
- Linked issue: Fixes #12401.

### What this does, simply

prs.title: fix(runtime): count and send the collapsed view in the budget projection and the final summary
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11297 builds each ordinary request from a collapsed copy of the history: turns older than the newest `keep_tool_context_turns + 1` are sent without their tool rows. Two other paths that estimate or build a request from the history still used the full history. @Audacity88 named both on #11297 as a follow-up, and Greptile raised them as P1s there.
    - **Terminal budget projection** (`enforce_reported_budget`): it counted older tool rows the next request leaves out, then dropped whole turns until that larger count fit. A tool-heavy session could lose earlier prompts and answers whose collapsed form fit the budget.
    - **Final-summary request** (`finish_after_max_iterations`): when the iteration allowance ran out, the summary request resent the older tool output the collapse had hidden, and its trim check counted it.
  - **One view for every path.** A new `ToolContextRetention` holds the retention setting and the known tool names. `request_view` applies the same `collapse_tool_context_older_than` the request build uses, and both paths now go through it:
    - `enforce_reported_budget` projects the collapsed view for `tokens_before`, for every whole-turn drop decision and for `tokens_after`. The raw pre-selection counts every row, so it now runs only when the collapse hides nothing; when it hides rows, the projection loop alone selects the drops. With nothing collapsed, the path is unchanged.
    - `finish_after_max_iterations` prepares the summary request from the collapsed view, before the first count and after every trim. When the provider omits `input_tokens`, the display-only estimate it reports is of that dispatched request, not of the full history.
  - The working history itself is still never collapsed, as before.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The terminal projection collapses the current history with the configured retention. The next turn adds its own user turn, which moves one more older turn out of the window. The projection doesn't simulate that: it can count one turn's tool rows that the next request will drop, which errs towards trimming slightly early, never late.
  - No change to the ordinary request build, to the retention setting, or to what the collapse itself removes.
- **Blast radius:** `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/mod.rs` (the view type, `enforce_reported_budget`, three call sites) and `turn/max_iter.rs` (one parameter, two preparations). It only changes behaviour when `keep_tool_context_turns` hides rows and `context_token_budget` is set, or when a turn ends on the iteration limit. Two approved PRs touch the same functions: #10597 adds logging inside `enforce_reported_budget`, and #11868 edits `finish_after_max_iterations`. Whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11297

### What this does, simply

To keep requests small, older tool output is left out of what is sent to the model. Two places still counted or resent that hidden output: the check that decides when to forget old turns, and the final "summarize what you did" request at the iteration limit. The first forgot turns it didn't need to; the second sent back output that was meant to be left out. Both now see the same trimmed view the normal request does.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional.
- **Setup:** `keep_tool_context_turns = 1`, a positive `context_token_budget`, a provider that reports usage.
- **Steps:** a session of several turns with large tool output each.
- **Expected after:** earlier prompts and answers stay while their collapsed request fits the budget; a run that hits the iteration limit sends a summary request without the older tool output.
- **Before:** whole earlier turns are dropped as the full history grows past the budget, and the summary request carries every old tool result.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-runtime` runs the new and existing budget and max-iteration tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** I could not run the `zeroclaw-runtime` lib tests locally; the test binary needs more memory than this machine has. Clippy compiled them, and CI runs them.
- **Commands run and tail output** (worktree at `f0cddc7dd4`, on master `cda933e6b9`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    ok
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings       ok
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-runtime            ok
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                        passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** New tests:
  - `reported_budget_counts_the_collapsed_request_not_hidden_tool_output`: six tool-heavy turns, a budget between the collapsed request and the full history. With the retention, nothing is dropped; counted in full (the old behaviour), whole turns are dropped.
  - `reported_budget_still_trims_when_the_collapsed_request_is_over`: a budget below the collapsed request still trims and leaves the breadcrumb.
  - `graceful_summary_sends_the_collapsed_view_of_older_turns`: with four tool turns and `keep_prior_turns = 1`, the summary request leaves out turns 1 and 2's tool output but keeps their answers, keeps turns 3 and 4 whole, and the working history keeps every row. With usage tracking on and no `input_tokens` from the provider, the accepted summary's estimate is below the full history's.

  The existing budget and summary tests pass a retention that keeps every row (`ToolContextRetention::keep_all`, test-only), so they exercise the unchanged path.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the runtime lib tests, for the memory reason above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The summary request now sends less of the earlier tool output, not more.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With nothing collapsed, both paths behave as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; or set `keep_tool_context_turns` high enough that nothing is collapsed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `keep_tool_context_turns`, `context_token_budget`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a `HistoryTrimmed` event whose counts don't match the sent request, or a final summary that still carries older tool output.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add host-mediated agent wake dispatch (dispatch.wake)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` interface `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` (`wake(target-agent, prompt) -> result<_, dispatch-error>`) and gated `import dispatch;` on `world tool-plugin` (`wit/v0/tool.wit`), gated by `PluginPermission::AgentDispatch` (`agent_dispatch`).
  - Adds `AgentWakeBackend` / `AgentWakeService` on `PluginHostServices` (`zeroclaw-plugins`), `OptionalImports::dispatch` linker gating + coherence checks, `PluginState::wake_agent` (enforcing `ToolExecute` call-frame phase, host-call budget, grant, and target/prompt grammar), and host-owned `WasmTool::caller_alias`.
  - Adds operator grant fields `PluginEntryConfig::{dispatch_agents, dispatch_rate_per_min}` in `zeroclaw-config` (default-closed `[]` and `30`/min, strict alias/padding/bounds validation), `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` in `zeroclaw-api`, and `manifest_owns_instance_state` row seeding so `agent_dispatch`-only manifests receive a `[[plugins.entries]]` row on install.
  - Implements `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/plugin_wake.rs` and wires `plugin_host_services_with_wake` / `register_plugin_tools` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` under the ADR-016 exception approved in #12417: live-config target authorization, `MAX_PLUGIN_WAKE_DEPTH = 2`, per-instance continuous token bucket, per-`(instance, target)` wake coalescing, `AgentExecutionCapability` admission, `TaskKind::PeerInbox` durable `TaskRecord` registration/settlement, and `CostTracker` scoping.
  - **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):** Increments the hardcoded `wit/v0/` input-inventory assertion in `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`Run runtime plugin admission regressions`, line 1241) from `17` to `18` to account for the new `wit/v0/dispatch.wit`, matching the `expected_inputs` update in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/r5_namespace_tests.rs`. No workflow triggers, runner labels, permissions, pinned actions, secrets, or step logic changed.
  - Adds `tool-dispatch-fixture` WASM guest + `dispatch_plugin_e2e`, unit tests across all touched crates, and documentation (`plugin-protocol.md`, `plugin-manifest-fields.md`, `writing-a-tool-plugin.md`, `CHANGELOG-next.md`).
- **Scope boundary:** `tool-plugin` world only; `channel-plugin` and `memory-plugin` do not import `dispatch`. No synchronous plugin-to-agent RPC, no ambient target grants, no edits to `send_message_to_peer.rs`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` changes only the 1-line `len(inputs) != 18` inventory count. `wit/v0` remains experimental (no `.frozen` marker); `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` keeps existing `wit/v0` plugins linking unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Additive WIT import, optional `PluginEntryConfig` fields, `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool`, runtime adapter wiring, and the `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` inventory entry in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` / `r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Default-closed (`dispatch_agents = []`) until an operator explicitly grants target aliases for an `agent_dispatch` plugin.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12416, Related #12417

### What this does, simply

Tool plugins run in a fresh store per call with no network listener or access to the agent loop. This adds a gated `dispatch.wake(target-agent, prompt)` host import so an operator-authorized tool plugin can nudge a target agent into an asynchronous turn—coalescing burst wakes onto at most one queued follow-up turn, capping recursion at 2 hops, and enforcing live per-instance rate limits and target allowlists. It also updates the runtime plugin admission step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and its matching `r5_namespace_tests.rs` list) to expect 18 WIT input files instead of 17 now that `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` exists.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; automated WASM component E2E (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and runtime mock-provider coalescing/panic/cost tests (`plugin_wake`) exercise the full boundary directly.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI runs workspace format, clippy (with CI's pinned toolchain), `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-plugins`, `zeroclaw-runtime` (including the `r5_namespace_tests` fixture-receipt proof), architecture runner-label checks, and docs/links checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s explicit `--test` list in the plugin-component job does not yet enumerate `dispatch_plugin_e2e` (though `cargo test` for `zeroclaw-runtime` unit tests runs `wasm_tool_dispatch_reaches_the_runtime_backend_end_to_end`). Local `dispatch_plugin_e2e` was run explicitly below.
- **Commands run and tail output (on head `f72f78a8ff` / prior `8ac25c5f9b` before the 2-line inventory update):**


- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Verified compiled `tool-dispatch-fixture` (`wasm32-wasip2`) end-to-end through both `WasmTool` (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` (`wasm_tool_dispatch_reaches_the_runtime_backend_end_to_end`).
  - Verified under local `rustc 1.99.0` that `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings` surfaces only pre-existing lints in untouched files (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/{upload,dispatch}.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`) and zero warnings in `plugin_wake.rs` or `tools/mod.rs`.
  - Note: in default parallel execution on an earlier run, pre-existing `component_logging::tests::plugin_log_queue_enforces_byte_bounds` flaked once on shared queue bytes; under `--test-threads=1` all 478 `zeroclaw-plugins` lib tests pass.

The command tails above are from `f72f78a8ff`. Interface: WIT `zeroclaw:plugin/dispatch` + `PluginEntryConfig` + `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend`.

- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `dispatch_agents = []` on the affected `[[plugins.entries]]` rows in live config; new plugin wakes are denied without a rebuild. For a code rollback after merge, revert the merged PR commit.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): classify incomplete terminal responses
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Treat incomplete Anthropic responses and semantic-empty terminals as typed failures, not successful blank or partial answers. Validate buffered envelopes and SSE framing, terminal reasons, content-block lifecycles, and execution-bearing tool input.
  - Preserve the first incomplete cause, observed usage, and opaque reasoning state through provider parsing and downstream consumers. Valid signed/redacted reasoning remains available for later provider reuse without becoming final display text.
  - Carry typed recovery and chargeability policy through Reliable and the runtime. The changed typed-terminal paths reject replay after immutable output, client-tool activity, provider-executed work, or cancellation; retain the documented pre-send connection, exact image-replacement, and sole-candidate exceptions.
  - Bind final failure and serving-provider identity to the same physical attempt. Reconcile terminal usage field by field, account rejected work once, and attribute successful fallback to its actual serving route. Preserve combined usage for direct unscoped structured calls, while scoped runtime calls retain accepted and rejected usage separately. Derive missing accepted-summary input estimates from the finalized sanitized request, floored at known cached input; estimates remain display-only.
  - Deliver localized terminal failures through CLI, ordinary turn/RPC, SOP, and delegation. Settle completed rejected-attempt usage when provider-backed work is cancelled, times out, or its future is dropped; controlled summary exits flush the existing usage-event projection before returning. Isolate the real peer-execution cost regression in an exact subprocess and wait for its durable terminal task before asserting accounting.
- **Scope boundary:** No OAuth/authentication, credentials, provider-default, gateway/config-schema, deployment, Matrix-adapter, telemetry-schema, or generic response-metadata changes. No paid/live provider calls. OpenAI-compatible output-limit classification remains a separate slice. The SOP accounting change is a narrow fix for usage lost at cancellation/timeout; broader SOP lifecycle architecture is deferred rather than folded into this PR. The peer-test correction does not change production cost-tracker policy.
- **Blast radius:** Provider API/parsers; Reliable/Router recovery and attribution; ordinary runtime turn, history, accounting, RPC, SOP and delegate delivery; direct CLI error output; external Rust consumers of changed public error types.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9421. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9421

### What this does, simply

A provider can finish an HTTP request without finishing the answer: it may exhaust its output/context budget, pause, refuse, return malformed tool data, or return no usable answer. Those outcomes should not be reported as success. This PR preserves their cause and usage all the way to the caller and restricts recovery of these typed outcomes so an already visible answer or tool operation is not silently repeated. Any text already streamed remains visible as partial output; the turn still ends as incomplete, not as an accepted final answer. An unchanged generic outer context-overflow recovery path can still restart after visible output when it recognizes an overflow diagnostic; that pre-existing limitation needs a separately scoped follow-up and is not claimed fixed here.

Merged #11625 records the original bounded runtime holding-crate exception. The additional production accounting changes in `src/agent/turn/mod.rs` still require the separate Core-approved scope record proposed in #11816 to land before #9447 merges. A pending proposal, green CI, or earlier approval does not grant that additional scope or establish merge readiness.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11625
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11816
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9447

**Separate upstream advisory:** Greptile notes that manual Stable-docs promotion can copy pages without refreshing their SEO tags. The promotion script and deployment workflow are unchanged by this PR relative to `master`, so remediation is outside this PR's scope. Greptile requests a fix before merge; the advisory remains unresolved for maintainer consideration.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9447#issuecomment-6047185780

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A - deterministic buffered/SSE, recovery, accounting, and production-CLI fixtures cover the contract without credentials or paid/live requests.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43370549463) and [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43370549463/job/131709280754) passed for `ed53b1521f04c4a7737fba8237f076ee9dd5a94d`. The run covers provider tests, repeated runtime/channel tests, lint, security, and selected platform/feature checks. The rollup has 48 successes, ten expected conditional skips, and no failures or pending checks; skipped jobs are not claimed as executed coverage.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The ten conditionally skipped hosted jobs did not execute.
